"A bitter pill to swallow" means a fact, situation, or outcome that is very unpleasant and painful to accept, but you have no choice — you must accept it.
A blessing in disguise is something that seems bad or unfortunate at first, but turns out to be good or beneficial in the end.
When you do something a cappella, you perform it using only human voices — with zero musical instruments.

When you call a person "a cog in the machine", you mean: They are one small, unimportant part of a very large organization or system. They follow instructions and do their assigned task, but have no real power, voice, or influence over the bigger picture.
When something is "a dime a dozen," it means that thing is so common and easy to find that it has little or no special value.
Something that has both a benefit and a drawback. The same thing that helps you in one way hurts you in another way.
A dressing-down is a harsh, thorough scolding — a sharp verbal telling-off that someone in authority gives to a person who has made a serious mistake, behaved badly, or failed to meet expectations.
When you say something is "a far cry from" something else, you mean the two things are very different from each other — so different that the gap between them feels large and significant.
A force to be reckoned with
When you call someone or something "a force to be reckoned with," you mean they are so powerful, capable, or impressive that no one can safely ignore them or take them lightly.
A foregone conclusion is an outcome or result that is so certain and predictable that it feels like it has already been decided, even before it actually happens.
A fortiori is an adverb meaning "with even stronger reason" or "all the more so." You use it when a conclusion is even more obviously true than something you've already established.

"À la carte" describes a system where you select individual items from a list of separate options, with each item carrying its own separate price or value, rather than receiving a fixed, pre-packaged combination.
A leopard can't change its spots
This idiom means that a person cannot truly change their fundamental nature, character, or personality — especially their bad habits or negative traits.
A question that is open to debate with no clear answer, or one that no longer matters because circumstances have changed.
A priori knowledge is knowledge you can arrive at through reason alone, without needing to go out into the world and observe or experience anything.
A person who brings warmth, happiness, and positive energy to the people around them — just like a single beam of light brightens a dark day.

A red herring is something — a clue, a fact, an argument, or a piece of information — that is misleading or distracting. It pulls your attention away from what actually matters and points you in the wrong direction.
A rude awakening is the sudden, shocking experience of discovering that something you believed, hoped, or assumed was completely wrong — and that the truth is much harsher than you expected.
A sudden, unexpected insult or act of disrespect — something that feels deeply unfair or hurtful, especially when you expected the opposite.

"A slap on the wrist" means a punishment that is far too mild or light for the seriousness of the wrongdoing. When someone does something bad and receives only a tiny, almost meaningless consequence, we say they got "a slap on the wrist."
A spoonful of sugar helps the medicine go down
A small pleasant thing can make something unpleasant much easier to accept. The sugar does not replace the medicine; it simply makes the experience less awful.
"A stone's throw away" means a very short distance. If something is described as being "a stone's throw away," it simply means it is very close — nearby, not far at all.

"A storm in a teacup" means making a huge fuss about something that is actually very small and unimportant. It describes a situation where people get very upset, angry, or excited over a trivial matter — treating a tiny problem as if it were a massive crisis.
To be taken aback means to be suddenly and noticeably surprised or startled by something you did not expect — so much that you don't quite know how to react right away.
An abacus is a hand-operated tool used for doing arithmetic — counting, adding, subtracting, multiplying, and dividing — without pen, paper, or a calculator.
An abalone is a type of sea creature — specifically, a large marine snail — that lives in the ocean and is known for two things: its delicious, edible flesh and its strikingly beautiful shell.
To abandon something or someone means to leave it permanently — and not come back.
Abandoned means completely left behind and no longer cared for, with no intention of returning.

Abandonment is the act of leaving someone or something behind — permanently, or with no real intention of coming back or taking care of it. It also describes the state of having been left in that way.

Abandonment issues refer to a deep, persistent fear that the people you care about will leave you — and a pattern of thoughts, feelings, and behaviors that stem from that fear. It is not just about being sad when someone leaves.

To abase someone means to lower their dignity, worth, or status — to make them feel small, shameful, or inferior. It strips away their sense of self-respect, either in their own eyes or in the eyes of others.
Abasement means the state or act of being degraded, humiliated, or made to feel deeply inferior. It is about a fall — not a physical one, but a fall in dignity, pride, or standing.
To abash someone means to make them feel suddenly embarrassed, ashamed, or self-conscious — especially in a way that causes them to lose their confidence or composure right in that moment.

Abashed means feeling suddenly embarrassed, self-conscious, and a little ashamed — usually because something happened that exposed you, caught you off guard, or made you feel small in front of others.
To abate means to become less intense, less severe, or to reduce in strength or degree. Think of it as something "turning down its own volume."

Abatement means a reduction, decrease, or lessening of something — usually something negative, burdensome, intense, or problematic. It can also mean the complete stopping or elimination of that thing.
An abattoir is a place — a building or a large facility — where animals are brought to be killed so that their meat can be prepared and sold as food.

An abbey is a building — or, more accurately, a complex of buildings — where a group of religious people called monks (men) or nuns (women) live together as a community, cut off from ordinary society, dedicating their lives to God through prayer, work, and study.
To abbreviate something means to make it shorter by leaving out parts of it — while the shortened result still clearly stands for the original and is understood to mean the same thing.
To abdicate means to formally and deliberately give up a position of power, authority, or responsibility — especially one that you were officially holding and were expected to keep.
Abdication is the act of formally and deliberately giving up a powerful position, role, or important responsibility — especially one that you were expected to keep and carry out.
Abdomen is a noun that refers to a specific section of the body — the region situated between the chest and the hips.

Abductive reasoning is the mental process of looking at something you observe and choosing the simplest, most plausible explanation for it — even when you can't be 100% certain that explanation is correct.

An abecedarian is a person who is at the very beginning of learning something — so much so that they are essentially at the "A, B, C" stage. Think of a child who has just started school and is learning to read letter by letter.

Aberrant describes something that strays away from what is normal, expected, or standard. If something is aberrant, it has departed from the usual pattern — and that departure is noticeable, significant, and typically unwelcome.
An aberration is something that is noticeably different from what is normal, expected, or typical. Think of it as a "deviation from the usual pattern."
To abet someone means to encourage, support, or assist a person in doing something wrong or harmful. It is almost always used in the context of wrongdoing — crime, dishonesty, or bad behavior.
Abetment is the act of helping, encouraging, or supporting someone else in doing something wrong — especially something illegal or harmful.

Abeyance means a state of temporary suspension — when something still exists, but is currently inactive, paused, or not being acted upon, and is waiting (sometimes indefinitely) to be revived or resolved.
To abhor something means to feel a deep, intense hatred or disgust toward it — so strong that it almost feels like a physical reaction of revulsion. It is not just disliking something.
Abhorrence is a feeling — a deeply powerful, negative emotion. When someone feels abhorrence toward something, they don't merely dislike it or even hate it in an ordinary way.

Abhorrent means something that causes an intense, deep feeling of disgust, hatred, or moral outrage — something so wrong or offensive that it fills you with a strong urge to pull away from it. When you find something abhorrent, you don't just dislike it.
To abide something means to be able to tolerate it — to stand it, accept it, or put up with it.
To abide by something means to follow it, respect it, and act in accordance with it — especially when it comes to rules, laws, decisions, or agreements.
When something is abiding, it means it has lasted for a very long time — and continues to last — without weakening, fading, or disappearing.
Ability means the power to do something. It is the answer to the question: "Can this person actually do this thing?"
"Abject" means something bad has reached its absolute lowest, most complete, and most hopeless extreme — with all dignity stripped away.

An abjuration is a formal, solemn, and often public declaration in which a person officially and completely rejects or gives up something they previously believed in, belonged to, or were loyal to — typically under oath.

To abjure something means to formally and solemnly declare that you are rejecting or giving it up — usually something you once believed in, were loyal to, or claimed as your own — and committing yourself to never returning to it.

The word ablaze essentially means intensely lit up — whether by real fire, by brilliant light and color, or by a powerful emotion burning inside a person. Think of it as a word that captures something burning or glowing with great intensity.

When "ablaze" is used as an adverb, it modifies a verb — it tells you how something is burning, shining, or feeling. It means "in a fierce, blazing state" or "in a way that resembles a powerful fire."

Abligurition means extravagance, especially in matters of food and drink. More specifically, when you squander your money on treats and comfort foods, you are engaging in abligurition — excessive spending on food and drink.
Ablution means the act of washing the body, particularly as a formal, ritual, or ceremonial act.

To abnegate something means to deliberately and consciously give it up, reject it, or deny it — especially something of real importance or value. The key word is deliberately. This is always a chosen act, never an accident.

Abnegation means the act of giving something up or denying yourself something, usually deliberately and willingly. That "something" is typically a desire, a comfort, a pleasure, a right, or a personal interest.
An abnormality is something that noticeably differs from what is normal, expected, or typical — such as an unusual feature, condition, or instance.

"Aboard" as a preposition means on, inside, or within a vehicle — specifically a large vehicle built to carry people or goods from one place to another, like a ship, a plane, a train, or a spacecraft.
An abode is simply the place where a person lives. It is another word for someone's home — the physical place they stay in, sleep in, and return to as their own.
To abolish something means to officially and permanently put an end to it — to wipe it out of existence completely, usually through an authoritative decision.

Abolition means the complete and official ending of something — especially a harmful, unjust, or widely accepted practice, system, law, or institution. When something is abolished, it is not merely paused, reduced, or changed.

An abolitionist is a person who campaigns to completely and permanently end a practice, system, or institution that they consider morally wrong — especially one that is widely accepted or even legally protected by their society.
Abominable means something is so extremely bad, morally disgusting, or deeply unpleasant that it triggers a powerful feeling of horror, hatred, or revulsion in you. It is not just bad.
Abominably means in a way that is shockingly, disgustingly, or deeply unacceptably bad. It is the adverb form of the adjective abominable, and it is used to describe how something happens or is done.
To abominate something means to hate it with the deepest, most intense disgust you can imagine. It is not casual dislike. It is not ordinary hatred.

An abomination is something that causes a feeling of extreme disgust, hatred, or moral outrage — something so deeply wrong, offensive, or repulsive that it feels like a violation of everything that is right and decent.

"Aboriginal" describes something — a people, a language, a culture, a plant, or an animal — that has existed in a particular place since the very beginning, before anything or anyone else arrived there.

The word abortion refers to the ending of something before it reaches its natural completion. Think of it as a process that stops in the middle — something that was growing or developing gets cut short before it is fully formed or finished.
Describes something that was begun or attempted but failed or was cut short before it could reach its goal — an effort that tried but didn't make it.
To abound means to exist in very large numbers or amounts. When something abounds, there is a lot of it — more than enough, plentiful, everywhere you look.
Above means at a higher level or position than something else. Think of two things, one placed higher than the other — the one that is higher is "above" the other.
"Above all" means "most importantly" or "more than anything else."

"Above and beyond" means doing more than what is expected, required, or asked of you. It describes effort, work, or behavior that goes past the normal standard — past what is considered "enough" or "sufficient."

When something is aboveboard, it is completely honest, open, and transparent, with absolutely nothing hidden, secret, or sneaky about it. There are no tricks, no hidden agendas, no shady motives — everything is out in the open for anyone to see and examine.

To abrade something means to wear away, scrape, or damage a surface by rubbing it against something rough or hard. The key ingredient is friction — two surfaces in contact, where one gradually damages the other.
Abrasion means one of two closely related things: the act of scraping or wearing something away by rubbing, or the damage (a wound or a worn-down surface) that results from that scraping.

Abrasive means something that rubs, scrapes, or irritates — either physically against a surface, or emotionally against a person's feelings. Think of it as the quality of being rough in a way that causes friction and discomfort.

An abreaction is the sudden, intense release of emotions that were locked up inside a person — emotions that were originally tied to a painful or traumatic memory that they had buried deep in their mind, often without realizing it.
When people or things are abreast, they are lined up next to each other, at the same level, all facing the same direction. Nobody is ahead, and nobody is behind — they are perfectly parallel.

To abridge something means to make it shorter by carefully cutting parts out — while making sure the most important content, the overall meaning, and the spirit of the original are all still preserved.

When something is abridged, it means it has been shortened from its original, fuller version — by cutting out parts of it — while still keeping the essential content, main ideas, and overall structure intact.

A shortened version of a book or other written work that keeps its essential content while cutting the less important parts. It can also mean the act of shortening something, or a reduction of rights.
When you are abroad, you are physically present in a country that is not your home country.

To abrogate something means to formally and officially cancel, abolish, or do away with it — typically a law, rule, agreement, treaty, or established right — so that it no longer has any force or effect.

Abrogation means the official, formal cancellation or abolition of something — such as a law, a treaty, a right, a contract, or an agreement — by someone who has the recognized authority and power to do so.
Happening suddenly and unexpectedly, without a smooth lead-up or transition. Of a person's manner, it means brief and curt to the point of seeming rude.
Abruptly means in a sudden, unexpected way — without warning, without preparation, and without a smooth or gradual transition.
An abscess is a pocket of pus that forms inside the body — in a tissue, an organ, or beneath the skin — as a direct result of infection.

Abscission is the deliberate, controlled separation of a part from a living organism — specifically, the process by which something naturally detaches and falls away on its own, as a planned, biological event, not by accident or damage.
To abscond means to secretly and suddenly run away — especially to escape punishment, legal trouble, debt, or some other consequence.
Absence means the state of not being somewhere, or the state of something not existing or not being present.
To absent oneself from something means to deliberately stay away from a place or situation where you are expected to be present.
Your body is in one place, but your mind is somewhere else — so you keep forgetting things, missing what's happening around you, and doing things without fully realizing it.
Absenteeism is the habit or pattern of regularly staying away from a place where you are expected or required to be — most commonly a job or a school — often without a good or valid reason.
The word absolute captures one central idea: something that is complete, total, and exists without any limits, exceptions, or conditions attached to it.
Absolutely means completely, with no exceptions, to the fullest possible degree.
Absolution means the formal, official release of a person from guilt, sin, blame, or punishment. It is not just a feeling of relief — it is an act performed by someone with the authority to grant it.
A system of government in which one ruler — almost always a king or queen — holds complete, unlimited power. More broadly, the belief in something being total and unconditional, with no exceptions.

To absolve someone means to formally or officially declare that they are free from blame, guilt, responsibility, sin, or an obligation. Think of it as lifting a heavy burden off someone's shoulders — a burden of fault or duty.

To take in a liquid or other substance so that it becomes part of you, as a sponge absorbs water. Figuratively, to take in information, or to hold someone's full attention, as in "absorbed in a book."
When a person is described as absorbed, it means their mind is so completely and deeply focused on one thing that the rest of the world has faded away.
Something is absorbing when it is so deeply interesting and engaging that it takes over your complete attention — not just some of it, but all of it.
Absorption is the process of one thing drawing something inside itself — taking it in fully, so that what was outside becomes part of what's inside.
To abstain means to deliberately and consciously choose NOT to do something — especially something you could do, might want to do, or are expected to do.
Abstemious describes a person who deliberately chooses to eat and drink very little — someone who consciously holds back from overindulging, even when more is freely available.
Abstention means the deliberate, conscious choice to hold yourself back from doing something — especially something you are fully able to do, entitled to do, or even expected to do.

Abstinence means the deliberate, conscious choice to hold yourself back from doing something — especially something that is pleasurable, tempting, or that you are capable of doing — either for a period of time or permanently.

Abstinent means deliberately choosing to stay away from something — usually something that gives pleasure or satisfaction — through personal self-control. A person who is abstinent can do something, but chooses not to.
Existing only as an idea or concept in the mind, with no physical form — like love, justice, freedom, or time. You cannot hold it, see it, or point to it directly.
An abstract is a brief, condensed summary of a longer piece of writing — most often a research paper, scientific study, academic article, or legal document.

Abstract Expressionism is an art movement where artists use non-recognizable shapes, colors, and marks — rather than pictures of real things — to express raw inner emotions, unconscious thoughts, and psychological states.
When a person is described as abstracted, it means their mind has quietly withdrawn from the world around them and is deeply occupied with their own inner thoughts.
An abstraction is a concept, idea, or representation that has been deliberately stripped of specific, concrete details — leaving behind only the essential qualities that apply broadly.

Abstruse describes something that is very difficult to understand because it is deeply complex, highly specialized, or obscure — the kind of thing that makes most people's brains feel like they've hit a wall.
So unreasonable, so illogical, or so wildly out of place that it cannot be taken seriously.
Absurdism is the philosophy that begins exactly here — at the uncomfortable collision between the human hunger for meaning and the universe's total refusal to provide it.

Absurdity means the quality of being so wildly unreasonable, illogical, or out of touch with reality that it almost defies belief — often to the point where it feels laughable, even if it also happens to be frustrating or serious.
Abundance means a very large amount of something — so large that there is more than enough of it.
Abundant means present in very large quantities — so large that there is more than enough.
To abuse one's medication means to use a medicine in a way that is different from how a doctor prescribed it or how the manufacturer intended it to be used.
Abusive means causing harm, hurt, or wrongful treatment to someone — through actions, words, behavior, or the misuse of power.
To abut means to touch something at its edge or border — to be right next to it with no gap in between, sharing a common boundary line.
As an adjective, "abutting" is used to describe one thing in relation to another thing it directly touches at an edge or boundary.
A place, group, or situation that is full of lively, excited activity, talk, or energy — humming with life like a beehive.
Abysmal means extremely and shockingly bad — so bad that it hits the very bottom of any acceptable standard. It is not used for things that are just a little bad, or even moderately bad.

An abyss is a space, gap, or depth so enormous and so deep that it feels like it has no bottom — like it goes on forever into darkness. The single most important idea packed into this word is immeasurable, terrifying depth. Not just "very deep."
Academe means the world of higher education and scholarly life — universities, colleges, research institutions, and everything that happens within them.
Academia refers to the world of higher education and formal scholarship.
Relating to schools, colleges, universities, and formal scholarship. It can also mean purely theoretical — interesting to discuss, but with no practical importance.

An academic advisor is a trained professional at a school, college, or university whose entire job is to help students make smart, informed decisions about their education — from what courses to take, to what degree to pursue, to what career path to consider.

Academic integrity is the commitment to being honest, fair, and responsible in all academic work — whether that's writing an essay, taking a test, conducting research, or collaborating with classmates.

An academy is a place or an organization dedicated to learning, training, or the pursuit of excellence in a particular field. It almost always carries a sense of seriousness, prestige, or specialization — it is not just any ordinary school or group.

To accede means to agree to something, or to formally take up a position of power. It always appears with the word "to" — you accede to something. That little detail matters a lot: "accede" by itself is incomplete. It always needs a target.
To accelerate means to go faster, or to make something go faster or happen sooner.
Acceleration means the process of something speeding up, or the rate at which it does so.
The word accent has several related meanings, all tied to one central idea: something that stands out from the rest by being given more emphasis, prominence, or distinctiveness.
To accentuate something means to make it more noticeable, more prominent, or more striking than it would otherwise appear.
Accept means to take something in or agree to something willingly. The key word here is willingly. You are not forced. You are not tricked. You choose to receive it, believe it, or say yes to it.

Acceptance means receiving, agreeing to, or making peace with something — whether that's an offer, an idea, a person, or a painful reality. It is the state of saying "yes" rather than "no," of letting something in rather than pushing it away.
An acceptance letter is an official written document in which one party says "Yes, I agree" to another party.
Accessible means able to be reached, entered, used, or understood — without significant barriers.

The word accessory describes something — or someone — that plays a supporting, secondary role. An accessory is not the main thing. It exists alongside the main thing, helping it, completing it, or enhancing it — but it is never the central focus.

When you do something accidentally, you did it without meaning to. You did not plan it. You did not want it to happen. It happened by chance, through a mistake, or through some unforeseen cause — not through your conscious choice.

Acclaim means enthusiastic, widespread public praise and admiration that people express for someone or something — usually in response to an outstanding achievement, an impressive performance, or a remarkable creation.
To acclaim someone or something means to praise them openly, enthusiastically, and with great admiration — usually in front of others or as part of a shared public response.

When something or someone is acclaimed, it means they have been publicly and enthusiastically praised by a large number of people — especially by people whose opinion carries weight, like experts, critics, or the general public at large.

Acclamation is the loud, enthusiastic, collective approval or praise that a group of people expresses together — through cheering, clapping, or shouting — to show that they strongly agree with or admire something or someone.
To acclimate means to gradually get used to a new or unfamiliar condition — whether physical, environmental, or situational — until it no longer feels difficult, uncomfortable, or strange.
To acclimatize means to gradually get used to something new — a new place, a new environment, a new situation, or new conditions — so that it starts to feel normal and manageable.
An acclivity is an upward slope — the rising face of a hill, a mountain, or any piece of ground that goes up. It is the inclined surface you see and feel beneath your feet as you climb.
An accolade is a recognition of excellence given to someone by others. It is a way of saying, publicly or formally: "What you did was outstanding, and we want to acknowledge it."
To provide enough room for people or things, as in "the hotel accommodates 300 guests." It also means to adjust or make special arrangements to meet someone's needs, or to adapt to a new situation.
Accommodating describes a person who is willing to adjust themselves — their plans, preferences, or behavior — to fit the needs or wishes of others.
A place where a person can sleep, live, or stay, especially temporarily. It can also mean an adjustment or arrangement made so that someone's needs can be met.
Accompaniment means something that goes along with something else — something that exists alongside a main thing, usually in a supporting or complementary role.
Accompany means to go with, exist with, or occur alongside something or someone. The central image is always "together" — one thing moving or existing in parallel with another.
An accomplice is a person who helps someone else do something wrong or illegal — not the main person committing the act, but someone who plays a supporting role in it.
To accomplish something means to successfully carry a task, goal, or objective all the way through to its completion — through intent and effort.

When you call someone accomplished, you mean they are highly skilled at something — not just decent, not just average, but genuinely excellent, with a level of mastery that earns real respect and admiration.
An accomplishment is something you have successfully done, especially something that took effort, skill, or time. It is the result of trying to do something and actually doing it well.
Accord is about two or more things being lined up, matched, or in agreement — whether that's people agreeing on something, ideas matching each other, or a decision aligning with a set of values.

When you accord something to someone, you give or grant it to them — but it's a specific kind of giving. The thing being given is almost always intangible: respect, recognition, trust, importance, rights, a privilege, a welcome, or status.
Accordance is a noun that means agreement, harmony, or alignment between two or more things — where one thing matches, follows, or conforms to another.

"According" as an adjective means in alignment with, in agreement with, or in harmony with something else. It describes a relationship where two things correspond to each other — where one thing fits, matches, or conforms to another.

"Accordingly" is a word that connects what you do (or what happens) to a situation or piece of information that came before it. It always looks backward at something already said or known, and uses that as the reason or justification for what comes next.
To accost someone means to approach them and address them in a bold, intrusive, or aggressive way — especially when they haven't invited the interaction and don't welcome it.
To account for something means to explain why it happened. It can also mean to make up a particular amount or share, or to keep track of something.
To explain or give a reason for something. It can also mean to make up a particular amount, to keep track of something, or to take something into consideration.
Accountability is the obligation to own your actions, explain them, and accept the consequences that come from them — whether those consequences are good or bad.

When someone is accountable, it means they are in a position where they are required to answer for their actions, decisions, or results — and they must face whatever consequences follow from those actions.

Accountancy is the professional field — the entire discipline — that deals with managing, recording, and making sense of money-related information for individuals, businesses, governments, or any organization.

An accountant is a trained professional whose job is to handle financial information — that means everything related to money: tracking it, recording it, organizing it, analyzing it, and reporting it accurately.

The organized system of recording, measuring, and reporting financial information — showing whether a business makes a profit, what it owes, and what it is worth. It is often called "the language of business."
To accoutre someone means to fully equip or outfit them with everything they need — the clothing, gear, weapons, tools, or accessories — for a specific role, occasion, or activity.
An accoutrement is an extra item — a belonging, accessory, or piece of equipment — that goes along with something or someone, completing a full picture rather than being the main thing itself.

Accoutrements are the extra items, accessories, or pieces of equipment that go along with a particular activity, role, or way of life. They are never the main thing — they are always the accompanying things.
An official stamp of approval from a trusted, independent authority, certifying that an institution, organization, or program meets a defined set of standards.

When something or someone is described as accredited, it means they have received official recognition and approval from a trusted authority — because they have been carefully checked and confirmed to meet a specific set of required standards.

Accretion means the gradual growth of something through the slow, continuous addition of material from the outside, layer upon layer, over time. It refers both to the process of that buildup and to the result — the mass or thing that has formed because of it.

To accrue means to build up gradually over time as a natural result of something. When something accrues, it doesn't appear all at once — it accumulates slowly, steadily, and often automatically in the background.
When something is accrued, it means it has been steadily building up over a period of time — quietly, gradually, automatically — as a natural result of time passing or an ongoing activity.
The cultural and psychological change that happens when two distinct cultures come into sustained, direct contact — as people pick up new habits, language, and ways of thinking.
To accumulate means to gradually build up a large amount of something over a period of time, either by actively collecting it or by simply letting it pile up on its own.
Accumulation means the gradual building up of something over time — layer by layer, piece by piece, until you have a large amount or a significant mass.
Accuracy means how close something is to what is true or real.

Accursed describes something — a person, place, object, or situation — that is either under a curse or is so deeply hateful, horrible, or frustrating that it feels like a curse. It is a word dripping with strong negative emotion.
An accusation is a statement that someone has done something wrong, bad, or illegal — without it necessarily being proven true.

When something is accusatory, it carries the sense that someone has done something wrong — or that you believe they have. It doesn't necessarily mean someone is formally charged with a crime. It means the feeling or suggestion of blame is in the air.

To accuse someone means to openly say or claim that a person has done something wrong, bad, or illegal. When you accuse someone, you are pointing directly at them and stating that they are responsible for a wrongdoing.

To accustom someone to something means to make them so familiar with it — through repeated experience over time — that it no longer feels strange, uncomfortable, or difficult. The thing becomes normal to them.

Accustomed as an adjective carries the idea of familiarity built through habit or repeated experience. Something that is accustomed is not new, not surprising, and not uncomfortable — it has become normal.

To ace something means to do it outstandingly well — not just to pass, not just to do okay, but to perform at an excellent or near-perfect level. Think of it as going beyond success into impressive success.

When someone has an ace up their sleeve, it means they have a secret advantage, resource, or plan that they are keeping hidden — ready to use at just the right moment, especially when things get difficult or competitive.

Acephalous means "without a head" or "lacking a head." It describes something — a creature, a group, a piece of writing — that is missing the part we'd normally think of as the "head" or leading authority.
Acerbic means sharp, biting, and harsh — particularly in the way someone speaks, writes, or expresses themselves.
Acerbity means a sharp, harsh, biting quality — in either taste or, more commonly, in someone's words, tone, or manner of behaving toward others.
"Acetic" means of, relating to, or derived from acetic acid — the sharp, sour-smelling acid that is the active chemical in vinegar.
To "ache for" something or someone means to want or miss them so deeply that it feels almost like a physical pain inside you.

An achene is a type of fruit — but almost certainly not the kind of fruit you're picturing. Forget apples and oranges. In botany, a "fruit" simply means the structure that develops from a flower's ovary and contains a seed.
To achieve something means to successfully reach a goal or get a desired result through effort or work.

An achievement is something you have successfully done after putting in real effort — especially something that was difficult, required skill, or took time. It is the end result of working toward a goal and actually reaching it.
An Achilles' heel is a single, critical weakness in an otherwise strong person, system, or thing — one that can cause serious harm or total failure despite all other strengths.
Achromatic means without color — describing anything that is completely free of hue and exists only as white, black, or shades of gray in between.

"Acid" as an adjective always conveys one core idea: sharp, biting, and capable of cutting or burning. Everything else flows from this idea — whether you're talking about taste, chemistry, someone's words, or even colors.
Rain, snow, sleet, or fog that is unusually acidic due to pollution in the atmosphere is called acid rain.
When we say something is an "acid test," we mean it is a final, decisive challenge or test that proves beyond any doubt whether something — or someone — is truly genuine, good, or capable.
The experience a person has while under the influence of LSD.

When we say something is acidic, we mean it contains, or behaves like, an acid. An acid is a type of substance with specific chemical properties — it's reactive, it has a sharp sour taste, and it can break down or corrode other materials when strong enough.
Acidification is the process by which something becomes more acidic over time. The word describes a change — a shift toward acidity — rather than a fixed state.
Slightly sour, tart, or sharp in flavour — like a green apple. Used of a person's speech or manner, it means sharp, biting, and a little sarcastic.
Acknowledge means to accept that something is real, true, or valid — and in many cases, to show that acceptance through words or actions.

An acknowledgement is what happens when someone recognizes something and shows — through words or actions — that they have recognized it. It is the act of saying, openly and clearly: "I see this. I know this is real. I am not ignoring it."
When you say something is at its acme, you are saying: It has climbed as high as it can possibly go. Nothing surpasses it. It represents the finest, most complete version of itself.
Acne is a common skin condition in which the tiny openings on your skin — called pores — get blocked or clogged, causing bumps, spots, and blemishes to form on the surface of the skin.

An acolyte is someone who closely follows, assists, or serves another person — usually someone with more power, authority, or status. Think of it as a helper, a devoted follower, or an apprentice who stands beside a more important figure and supports them.

Acoustic means relating to sound or the sense of hearing. If something is described as acoustic, it has a direct connection to sound — how sound is produced, how it travels, how it is heard, or how it behaves in a space.
The way sound behaves in a particular room or space — how clearly it can be heard. Acoustics is also the branch of science that studies sound.

Acquaint means to make someone familiar with something or someone they didn't know before. Think of it as bridging a gap — moving a person from a state of not knowing to a state of being familiar with.
An acquaintance is someone you know, but not very well. They are not a stranger, and they are not a close friend — they sit comfortably in the middle.

"Acquainted" describes a state of partial knowing — having some familiarity with someone or something, but not deeply. Picture a scale in your mind. On the far left is total ignorance — a complete stranger, a topic you've never heard of.
To acquiesce means to accept or go along with something without fighting it, even though you may not fully agree with it or like it.
Acquiescence is the act of quietly going along with something — accepting it, allowing it, or letting it happen — without openly agreeing to it, but also without resisting or objecting to it.
Acquiescent describes a person who accepts, agrees with, or goes along with something — without arguing, resisting, or pushing back — even when they may not be fully happy about it.
To acquire something means to come to have something that you did not have before — through some kind of process, effort, or experience.

When "acquired" describes something, it means that thing was not there from the start — it came later, through experience, exposure, learning, or some kind of process. It wasn't natural, inborn, or original. It was gained over time.
When something is called "an acquired taste," it means something that most people do not like the first time they experience it, but can gradually come to enjoy after repeated exposure over time.
Acquisition means the act of getting something, or the thing that was gotten. That's the simplest way to put it.

Acquisitive describes a person (or group) who has a strong, constant desire to get and keep things — especially money, possessions, or power. Think of someone who always wants more, who is always reaching out to grab and hold onto things.
Acquisitiveness is the strong, persistent desire to get and own things — whether money, objects, power, knowledge, or anything else of value.
To officially declare someone not guilty of a crime. To acquit yourself well also means to behave or perform in a particular way, especially under pressure.
An acquittal is an official legal decision that a person accused of a crime is not guilty.

When a person is described as acquitted, it means a court of law has officially declared them not guilty of a crime or charge they were accused of. The legal process examined the available evidence and concluded that guilt was not sufficiently proven.
Acrid describes something that has a sharp, bitter, and harshly unpleasant smell or taste — the kind that doesn't just bother you mildly, but actually irritates your nose, throat, or eyes. It stings.

Acrimonious describes a situation, relationship, argument, or exchange that is filled with deep bitterness, sharp anger, and resentment — the kind where people are not just disagreeing, but are being hurtful, hostile, and mean-spirited toward each other.
Acrimony is a harsh, biting bitterness that comes out in the way people speak to each other or treat each other — especially during a disagreement, conflict, or breakdown of a relationship.

Acrophobia is an intense, overwhelming fear of heights. It is classified as a specific phobia — a type of anxiety disorder where a person experiences extreme fear in response to a particular thing or situation.
"Across the board" means something that applies to everyone or everything in a group, equally and without exception.
On the other side of the road, directly opposite where you are or where something else is.

When you describe something as acrostic, you mean that it is a piece of writing — most often a poem — in which the first letters of each line, read from top to bottom, spell out a hidden word, name, or message.
An acrostic is a piece of writing — most often a poem — where certain letters from each line, read from top to bottom, spell out a hidden word, name, or message.
To act on something means to do something because of it. The thing you "act on" is the reason, the trigger, or the cause of your action.
To express difficult feelings like anger, pain, or anxiety through bad behaviour instead of talking about them. It can also mean to perform a story or scene by acting it.
"Act up" always means that something or someone is behaving in a way that is wrong, unusual, or problematic — and causing trouble because of it.

An action figure is a small, human-shaped toy — almost always made of plastic — that represents a specific character from a movie, TV show, comic book, video game, or real life. The word "figure" simply means a model shaped like a person or creature.
To activate something means to cause it to start working or functioning. Before something is activated, it already exists — but it is dormant, idle, switched off, or simply waiting.

Activism is the practice of taking deliberate, active steps to create change — usually in society, politics, the environment, or the economy. The single most important word in understanding activism is "active."

An activist is a person who takes deliberate, sustained action to bring about change — usually in society, politics, the environment, or human rights. The key word here is action. Many people hold opinions about what is wrong with the world.
A person who performs a character in a film, play, television show, or other performance. In a broader sense, an actor is any person or group that takes part in an event or situation.
Actuality means the state of something being real — the condition of truly existing as a fact, rather than being imagined, assumed, theorized, or merely appearing to be so.
Relating to the mathematical and statistical assessment of financial risk and uncertainty — especially the risk that uncertain future events (like death, illness, or accidents) will cost money.

An actuary is a trained professional who uses mathematics, statistics, and financial theory to measure, analyze, and manage risk — specifically, the financial risk that comes from uncertain future events.
Actuate is a formal verb with two closely related meanings — one used for machines and devices, and one used for people and their motivations.
Sharpness, keenness, and precision — whether in how well you see and hear, or in how quickly and clearly you think.
Acumen is the ability to quickly and sharply understand a situation and make smart, effective judgments about it — especially in a practical, real-world context.

Every single meaning of "acute" connects back to one idea — sharpness. Whether it describes pain, a person's mind, a medical condition, or a geometric angle, "acute" always signals something pointed, intense, or precise — never dull, mild, or vague.
When something is felt or noticed acutely, it is not just felt strongly — it is felt in a piercing, cutting, impossible-to-ignore way.
Created or done for one particular purpose or situation only, rather than planned in advance, as in "an ad hoc committee."
When you do something ad hoc, you do it without prior planning, in direct response to a situation as it happens, rather than following a pre-existing system, rule, or schedule.
A flawed argument in which someone attacks the person making a point instead of the point itself — going after their character, past, or motives rather than what they said.
Endlessly; without end. When something continues ad infinitum, it keeps going and going with no stopping point.

Ad libitum means "freely, according to one's own desire, without restriction or limit." When something is done ad libitum, the person doing it has complete freedom to decide — how much, how long, how fast, how often, or whether to do it at all.
Ad nauseam is a Latin phrase that means "to the point of causing nausea" — or in plain English, to a sickening, unbearable degree of repetition or excess.
An adage is a short, well-known saying that expresses a truth about life — one that people have found so wise and so accurate that they have been repeating it for generations.
As an adjective, adagio means slow, graceful, and calm — describing music, a section of music, or a type of movement in dance that is performed at a deliberately unhurried, dignified pace.

When you use adagio as an adverb, it means "in a slow, smooth, and graceful manner." It is primarily a musical instruction, telling a performer how to play a piece of music — slowly, calmly, and with a sense of ease and dignity.

When someone is adamant, they have made up their mind completely — and nothing will change it. No argument, no pressure, no plea, no negotiation. They are not just firm or confident. They are immovable.
Every meaning of adamantine flows from a single image: something so impossibly hard that it simply cannot be broken, cut, pierced, or changed.
When someone does something adamantly, they do it with total, unshakeable firmness — a complete refusal to change their position, no matter what arguments, pressure, or circumstances they face.
To adapt means to make a change — either to yourself, or to something else — so that it fits a new situation, purpose, or environment better than it did before.

Adaptability is the quality of being able to adjust yourself — your thinking, behavior, or approach — when your situation changes or when something unexpected happens. It is not an action you take once.
When something or someone is adaptable, it means they are capable of changing or adjusting themselves to suit new, different, or unexpected conditions — and doing so successfully.
Adaptation means a change made so that something fits better into a new situation, environment, or purpose.
Adaptive describes something — a person, a system, a behavior, a process — that is able to change itself in response to new or different conditions in order to function better or survive.
To make a bad situation even worse, especially in a way that feels unfair, embarrassing, or disrespectful.
"Add to" means to make something greater, larger, or more intense by putting something on top of what already exists.
To calculate a total. It also means to make sense or seem believable — when the facts don't add up, something seems wrong.
To come to a particular total when everything is combined. It also means to result in or amount to something, as when small efforts add up to a big change.
An addendum is a piece of extra information that is added to a document, book, contract, email, or any piece of writing — after that writing has already been completed or finalized.

An addict is a person who is so strongly and repeatedly drawn to something — a substance or a behavior — that they feel they cannot stop, even when it is clearly hurting them. The key idea is loss of control.
Addiction is a condition in which a person feels a powerful, uncontrollable urge to repeatedly do something — or keep using a substance — even when it is clearly causing them harm.
"Additional" means added on top of something that already exists. It describes something that comes beyond what was already there, already mentioned, or already expected.
An additive is a substance that is added to something else — usually in small amounts — to change it, improve it, or give it a quality it wouldn't naturally have on its own.
To addle means to confuse someone's mind so completely that they can no longer think clearly or in an orderly way.

When something is addled, it is confused, muddled, and unable to function clearly. Think of a brain that is scrambled — thoughts that won't line up properly, a mind that can't think straight. That is the heart of what "addled" means.
The word address refers to a specific point of contact — a place, a location, or a way to reach something or someone.

The verb "address" means to direct something — your words, your attention, or your action — purposefully toward someone or something. That single idea is the thread that ties all its meanings together.
An addressee is the specific person, group, or organization that a communication is meant for — the one to whom a letter, email, package, document, or any form of communication is formally directed.
To adduce something means to bring it forward — a fact, an example, a piece of evidence, or a reason — specifically to support an argument or claim you are making.
When you call someone adept, you are saying they are highly skilled at something — not just okay at it, not just decent, but genuinely, impressively good. The word carries a sense of admiration.

Adequacy is the state of being enough — enough to meet a need, fulfill a requirement, or satisfy a standard. When something has adequacy, it means it does the job it is supposed to do. It covers what is needed. It is not falling short.
When something is adequate, it means it is just enough — it meets the required standard, fulfills the need, and does the job. Nothing more, nothing less.
"Adequately" means in a way that is good enough for the purpose — not more, not less, but just enough.
A brain-based condition in which a person struggles to regulate their attention, impulses, and activity levels in a way that most people do naturally and automatically.
To stick firmly to a surface. More often, to adhere to a rule, belief, or plan means to follow it closely and faithfully.
"Adhere to" means to follow something closely, consistently, and faithfully — without breaking away from it or making exceptions.

Adherence means the act or quality of faithfully and consistently sticking to something — a rule, a plan, a belief, a standard, a schedule, a diet, or any principle that requires you to stay committed to it over time.
An adherent is a person who believes in, follows, and supports a particular idea, cause, religion, philosophy, or movement — and sticks with it faithfully.

Adhesion means the sticking of one thing to another thing. More precisely, it refers to the force, condition, or process by which two surfaces or substances are held together — often surfaces that are different from each other.
An adhesive is a substance that makes two things stick together. When you put an adhesive between two surfaces and press them, it grips both surfaces at the same time — holding them joined.
Adipose means relating to, consisting of, or containing fat — specifically the soft, yellowish fat stored inside the bodies of animals and humans. It is a scientific and medical term.

"Adjacent" means directly next to something, typically sharing a side, edge, or border with it. Think of two things sitting right beside each other with nothing in between — that is the essence of "adjacent."

When two things adjoin, they are sitting directly next to each other and sharing a common boundary — a wall, a fence, a border line, or an edge. There is no gap between them. They are literally touching along one side.
Something is adjoining when it is directly next to something else and the two things physically share a common boundary — a wall, a fence, a border, or an edge — between them.

To adjourn means to officially bring a formal gathering — such as a court session, a parliamentary debate, or a business meeting — to a close, either temporarily or permanently. The key idea is that this closing is deliberate and declared.
The formal suspension of a meeting, trial, or official proceeding — either until a later, fixed time, or with no set date to return.
To adjudicate means to make an official, authoritative decision about a dispute, case, or competition — after carefully hearing and examining all sides of it.

An adjunct is something — or someone — that is added to a main thing but is not an essential or permanent part of it. It plays a supporting, secondary role. Without the adjunct, the main thing still works perfectly fine.
An adjuration is a deeply solemn, serious appeal or command — one that carries extraordinary urgency and moral weight. It is not a casual request, not a polite ask, and not an ordinary order.

To adjure someone means to urgently and solemnly urge, appeal to, or command them to do — or not do — something. It is never a light or casual request. It always carries a sense of gravity, seriousness, and high stakes.
To adjust means to make a small, careful change to something so that it becomes more correct, more comfortable, or more suitable for a purpose.
Something is "adjustable" when it can be changed, moved, set, or modified — and it was designed or intended to be that way. The central idea is the capability for controlled, deliberate change.
An adjutant is a military officer who serves as an administrative assistant and right-hand man to a senior commanding officer.

If something is adjuvant, it means it is helping, assisting, or boosting something else — but crucially, it is not the main thing doing the work. It plays a supporting role that makes the primary thing more effective.
Administration refers to the act of managing, organizing, and running something — whether that something is an organization, a process, a substance, or even an estate.
"Administrative" means relating to the management and organization of something — whether that something is a company, a government, a school, or any institution.
"Admirable" describes someone or something that genuinely deserves respect, deep approval, and a feeling of looking up to it.
Admiration is a warm, pleasant feeling you get when you see or think about someone or something that you find genuinely impressive, excellent, or worthy of praise.

To admire someone or something means to look at them or think about them with a feeling of genuine pleasure, respect, and appreciation — because you find them impressive, excellent, or beautiful in some way.

An admirer is a person who looks at someone — or occasionally something — and feels a deep, genuine sense of appreciation, respect, and wonder. The admirer sees a quality, talent, achievement, or trait and is genuinely moved by it.
When you "admit" something, you are saying out loud a truth that you were holding back, resisting, or perhaps even hiding — and now you are finally releasing it.
Something that is added to and mixed into another substance, or the mixture that results. Figuratively, a small mixed-in element or trace, as in "an admixture of fear and hope."

To admonish someone means to firmly but calmly tell them that they have done something wrong, or to warn them not to do something wrong. Think of it as a serious, caring correction — not a screaming rage, but not a gentle whisper either.
An admonishment is a firm, serious verbal warning or correction directed at someone because their behavior is wrong, inappropriate, or likely to cause problems.
An admonition is a serious, earnest warning or piece of cautionary advice given to someone — usually to stop them from making a mistake, to correct their behavior, or to urge them to be more careful.

Something admonitory is anything that carries a warning, a caution, or a gentle rebuke — it signals to someone that they are doing something wrong, or that they need to be more careful, or that they should stop a certain behavior.
Ado means unnecessary fuss, commotion, or trouble surrounding something — especially when that fuss seems bigger than it needs to be.
Adobe refers to a type of building material — specifically, a brick made from a mixture of earth, water, and usually some kind of fibrous material such as straw or grass.

Adolescence is a noun that refers to the period of life between childhood and adulthood — the years when a person is no longer a child but has not yet fully become an adult. It is a stage of growth, change, and transition that every human being goes through.
When you use "adolescent" as an adjective, it means relating to, belonging to, or typical of the period of life between childhood and full adulthood.
Adopt always carries one central idea: Taking something that exists outside yourself — and making it officially or personally your own, through a conscious and deliberate choice.
Adoption means the act of taking something (or someone) that was not originally yours and choosing to make it your own — permanently and willingly.

To adore someone or something means to love them deeply, warmly, and with great admiration. It's not just a gentle fondness — it's a strong, heartfelt feeling where you find the person or thing truly wonderful, even close to perfect in your eyes.
To adorn something means to make it more beautiful or attractive by adding something to it. That "adding" part is the heart of the word.
When something is adorned, it has been made more beautiful or attractive by adding decorative elements to it.
Adornment means anything that makes something — or someone — look more beautiful, attractive, or impressive. Think of it as decoration with a sense of care and intention behind it.
Adrenaline is a natural chemical your body produces on its own. It is made in your adrenal glands — two small, triangular-shaped glands that sit on top of your kidneys, one on each side.
A sudden, powerful surge of energy, excitement, and alertness caused by your body releasing adrenaline, usually in moments of danger or thrill.
Floating without control, anchor, or direction, like a boat whose rope has been cut. Used of a person, it means lost, aimless, and without purpose or support.
Floating freely with no steering, anchor, or fixed destination, carried along wherever the wind and current take it.

Adroit means being exceptionally skilled and clever — doing something with ease, quickness, and grace, whether that involves using your hands and body, or using your mind to handle a tricky situation.
Adroitness is the quality of doing something — whether with your hands or your mind — with impressive skill, speed, and ease, especially when the situation is difficult or tricky.
To adulate someone means to admire, praise, or flatter them in an extreme, excessive way — so much so that it goes beyond what is natural, honest, or dignified.
Adulation means excessive, over-the-top praise or admiration given to someone — far more than what they actually deserve, or far more intense than what is considered normal or appropriate.
To adulterate something means to secretly mix a cheaper, inferior, or harmful substance into something, making it impure, weaker, or less genuine — while it still looks like the original thing.
Something is adulterated when it has been made impure by secretly mixing a foreign, cheaper, or harmful substance into it.

Adulterous is an adjective that describes anything related to, involving, or characteristic of adultery — which is when a married person has a sexual or romantic relationship with someone other than their spouse, while the marriage is still active.
Adultery is when a married person willingly has sex with someone who is not their husband or wife.
To outline something broadly, without filling in the details. It can also mean to give a faint early hint of something that is to come.
Adumbration refers to something incomplete, shadowy, or partial — a trace or hint of a larger, fuller thing. It is not the thing itself. It is the early, dim, rough version of it.
To move forward, especially with purpose, as in "the troops advanced." It can also mean to make progress or develop, to help something succeed, to put forward an idea, or to lend money ahead of time.
Advancement means the act or process of moving something forward toward a better, higher, or more developed state — or the result of that movement.

An advantage is anything that puts you in a better position than others — or makes it easier for you to succeed at something. Think of it as a head start, an extra tool, or a favorable condition that works in your favor.

Advantageous describes something that gives you an advantage — meaning it puts you in a better, stronger, or more favorable position, either compared to where you were before, or compared to someone else. If something is advantageous, it works in your favor.
Advent means the arrival or coming of something important, significant, or long-awaited. It doesn't just mean something "showed up."

Adventitious describes something that does not naturally or originally belong where it is found. It came from the outside, appeared by chance, or showed up in an unusual place — rather than being an inherent, built-in part of something.

When we say someone or something is adventurous, we mean they are willing to try new, unknown, exciting, or risky things — and often, they actively seek those experiences rather than just tolerating them.
An adversary is a person, group, or force that actively works against you — someone who opposes your goals, challenges your position, or stands on the opposite side of a conflict or competition.
Adverse means harmful, unfavorable, or working against you (or something). When something is adverse, it creates difficulty, causes damage, or pushes against a desired outcome.

Adversity means a situation of serious difficulty, hardship, or suffering that a person (or group of people) faces in life. It is a condition — a state of things being hard, painful, or unfavorable — that challenges you in a significant way.
An advert is a message that someone creates and puts out in public to get people's attention — usually to persuade them to buy something, use a service, apply for a job, or support a cause.
Advice is something you say to another person to help them decide what to do or how to handle a situation. It is a recommendation — a suggestion about the best or wisest course of action.
Advisable means worth doing or sensible to do in a given situation — specifically because it is the wise, safe, or smart choice under the circumstances.
To advise someone means to tell them what you think they should do — usually because you have more knowledge, experience, or expertise than they do in that area.
When something is described as advisory, it means it exists to give advice, guidance, or recommendations — but it carries no power to force anyone to act on that advice.

An advisory is an official announcement or notice — issued by an authority or expert body — that informs people about a potential risk, danger, or important situation, and typically recommends what they should do about it.
Advocacy means actively speaking up for, supporting, or fighting for a cause, a person, a group, or an idea — especially when it matters and when it might make a difference.
An advocate is a person who actively and openly supports a cause, an idea, or another person — especially by speaking up for them, defending them, or pushing for change on their behalf.
To advocate means to actively and openly speak in support of something or someone — to argue for it, promote it, or defend it, especially when you believe in it strongly.

An adze is a hand-held cutting tool used for shaping, smoothing, or hollowing out wood. Think of it as a close cousin of the axe — but with one important difference that changes everything about how it works.
Protection, backing, or authority from a powerful, prestigious, or official source. Something done under the aegis of an organization is done with its support.
Aerial simply means "of, in, or from the air." Whenever something exists in the air, happens in the air, or is viewed from high up in the air, you can describe it as aerial.
An aerie is the nest of a large bird of prey — most commonly an eagle, but also hawks, falcons, and ospreys.
Aerobic means requiring oxygen, using oxygen, or relating to the presence of oxygen. Whenever you see this word, your first instinct should be to think: oxygen is involved here.
When you describe something as aerodynamic, you mean it is shaped or designed in a way that allows air to flow over and around it smoothly and easily, with as little resistance as possible.
Aerophobia is the intense, persistent, and irrational fear of flying or air travel.

An aesthete is a person who loves beauty deeply, seriously, and almost above everything else — and who has trained themselves to notice, appreciate, and seek out beauty in a way that most people simply don't.
"Aesthetic" means relating to beauty, or to how something affects you when you experience it through your senses — and whether that experience is pleasing or artistically meaningful.
Aestheticism is the belief that beauty is the highest value in life, and that art, beauty, and sensory pleasure are more important than moral lessons, practical usefulness, or social purpose.
Aesthetics means the study, principles, and experience of beauty, art, and sensory pleasure — and what makes something feel pleasing, moving, or meaningful to us.

Affability is the quality of being warm, friendly, and easy to approach or talk to. It describes a person's natural way of making others feel welcome and at ease — especially people they're meeting for the first time or don't know well.
The word affable describes a person who is friendly, warm, and genuinely easy to talk to.

The word affair refers to a matter, situation, event, or piece of business — something that is happening, has happened, or needs to be dealt with. Think of it as a general-purpose word that covers a wide range of situations.

An affectation is a way of behaving, speaking, or presenting yourself that is fake and put-on — something you do deliberately to seem more impressive, sophisticated, cultured, or interesting to other people, even though it is not natural to you at all.

When we call someone or something "affected," we mean the behavior, speech, or manner being described is not natural or genuine — it is deliberately put on, like a costume worn over the real personality.
Affection is a warm, gentle feeling of fondness and care that you have toward someone or something.
Affectionate describes someone — or something — that openly and warmly shows love, fondness, and care toward others.
Afferent means carrying or conducting something toward a central point or structure.
An affidavit is a written statement of facts that a person declares to be true under oath.

To affiliate means to officially connect or formally associate one person, group, or organization with another — usually in a way that is recognized, structured, and carries some mutual purpose or benefit.
Affiliation means a formal or recognized connection between a person (or an organization) and a larger group, body, or cause.

Affinity means a natural pull, attraction, or feeling of closeness toward something or someone — a pull that feels almost built-in, as if it comes from deep inside you rather than from effort or outside pressure.

To affirm something means to say it is true — but not just casually. When you affirm something, you say it with clear confidence, full conviction, and a sense of deliberate purpose. There is always a backbone to the word. It is never weak or lukewarm.
An affirmation is a positive, confident declaration that something is true — or the act of making such a declaration.

"Affirmative" means expressing, confirming, or belonging to the "yes" side of things. When something is affirmative, it asserts that something is true, agrees with something, or gives approval. It is the direct opposite of "negative."
Affirmative action is the active effort to improve employment, educational, and other opportunities for members of groups that have been subjected to discrimination.
To affix something means to attach it deliberately and securely onto a surface or another object, so that it stays there.
Afflatus means a sudden, powerful burst of creative inspiration — specifically one that feels as though it has been sent to you by a divine force, a god, or some higher power beyond yourself.
To afflict someone or something means to cause them serious suffering, pain, trouble, or distress — often in a way that is persistent, heavy, and hard to escape.

When someone is described as afflicted, it means they are suffering from something serious — a disease, a painful condition, deep emotional distress, or a difficult circumstance that causes real, significant hardship. The word is not used for minor troubles.

An affliction is something that causes a person deep pain, suffering, or distress. It is a burden — a condition, illness, or situation that weighs heavily on someone and makes their life genuinely difficult.
Affluence means the state of having a lot of money, material possessions, and financial resources — essentially, being wealthy and living very comfortably as a result of it.
Affluent means having a large amount of money, possessions, and financial resources — in short, being wealthy.
When you can afford something, you have enough money for it. When you can't afford it, you don't.
An affray is a noisy, violent fight or brawl that happens in a public place — and that is frightening or alarming to ordinary people who happen to witness it.
An affront is an action, a remark, or a piece of behavior that openly and boldly insults someone — in a way that attacks their dignity, honor, or self-respect.
To affront someone means to openly and deliberately insult or offend them in a way that attacks their dignity.
An afghan is a warm, cozy blanket — typically hand-knitted or crocheted (meaning it's made by looping yarn together using needles or a hook, rather than woven on a loom).
An aficionado is a person who has a deep, long-standing passion for something combined with substantial knowledge about it. Think of it as the sweet spot where love and expertise meet.
Away from home or the usual area. Far afield means a long way off — or, figuratively, far from the subject or point being discussed.
"Afloat" describes something that is floating on the surface of water — held up, not sinking. But here is what makes "afloat" special: this image of not going under travels far beyond water.
When something is afoot, it means it is currently happening, in progress, or being actively planned — especially when the thing in question feels significant, mysterious, or somewhat secretive.
When you use the word aforementioned before a noun, you are pointing your reader back to something you have already named or talked about earlier in the same piece of writing or speech.
"Afresh" means again, but starting completely from the very beginning — as if you are doing something for the first time, with a clean slate, leaving everything from before behind.
"Aft" means toward the back of a vessel — a ship, a boat, a submarine, or an aircraft. That single idea is the heart of this word.
"After" as a preposition always expresses the same fundamental idea: one thing follows another. Whatever noun or phrase comes right after "after" is the reference point.
Despite what was expected, as in "it didn't rain after all." It is also used to give a reason that supports what you've just said: "Let him sleep — after all, he's been working all night."
Late at night, after the time when television channels are allowed to show programmes unsuitable for children, such as violence, strong language, or sexual content.
Afterglow always refers to a warm glow — or a warm feeling — that lingers even after the thing that caused it is gone.
The afterlife is the belief or idea that some part of a person — their soul, spirit, consciousness, or essence — continues to exist in some form after their physical body dies.

Aftermath means the situation, conditions, and consequences that exist after a significant — and usually difficult or damaging — event. It is the changed reality you are left with once something major has happened.
A smaller earthquake that follows a larger one in the same area. Figuratively, an aftershock is a lasting effect or consequence of a shocking event.
An aftertaste is a taste that stays in your mouth after you have finished eating or drinking something. It is the flavor that lingers — that remains behind — even after the food or drink is gone.

An afterthought is something — an idea, a comment, a detail, an addition, or even a person — that is only considered, remembered, or included after the main thinking, planning, or action is already complete. It was not part of the original thought or plan.
"Against all odds" means succeeding or achieving something even though the chances of success were very low or almost impossible.
"Against the clock" means working as fast as possible to finish something before a deadline or before time runs out.
When something is "against the grain," it means it goes against what feels natural, comfortable, or normal — either to a person, or to a group of people, or to society as a whole.

Agape means wide open — but not just any kind of open. It describes an opening that is hanging open, gaping, often in a way that feels almost uncontrolled or involuntary. Think of a mouth that has dropped open so wide that you look almost frozen in place.
Every meaning of "aged" connects to a single central idea: time.

"Ageing" as a noun means the process of becoming older, and the changes that come with it. It is the name we give to something that happens gradually and continuously over time — not a single event, but an unfolding process.

An ageing population is a population in which the average age of people is rising over time. In practical terms, this means the share (percentage) of older people in a country or region is growing, while the share of younger people is shrinking.
Ageism is the word for prejudice, stereotyping, and discrimination directed at a person — or a group of people — solely because of their age.
Agency is always about who or what has the power to act, cause, or make things happen.
Agenda means a list of things that need to be dealt with. It is always forward-looking — it's about what is to be done, not what has already been done.

An agent is always the one doing the acting. No matter the context — everyday life, science, grammar, philosophy, or technology — the word "agent" always points to the active party, never the passive one.
An agent provocateur is a person who secretly infiltrates a group — usually a political, activist, or criminal group — and deliberately stirs up trouble from within.

Aggiornamento means the act of bringing something — especially a large, established institution or set of ideas — up to date with the modern world. It is a deliberate, thoughtful process of renewal and reform, not a radical overthrow.

To agglomerate means to come together — or to bring things together — into a single large, dense mass or cluster. That whole tends to feel bulky, dense, and somewhat haphazardly formed — not neatly arranged.
An agglomeration is a large, clustered mass of many things — often varied things — that have come together or been gathered together to form a single, bigger whole.

To agglutinate means to stick things together into a single clumped or unified mass — or, in reverse, to become stuck together that way. The key image is of many separate, individual things binding to each other to form one larger, joined cluster.
To aggrandize means to make someone or something appear — or actually become — greater, more powerful, more important, or more impressive than they truly are or deserve to be.
