Aggrandizement means the act of making someone or something appear — or actually become — greater, more powerful, more important, or more impressive, either in reality or in the eyes of others.
Aggravate means to make something bad even worse, or in informal use, to annoy or irritate someone. Those are its two meanings, and both are widely accepted today.

When a person is aggravated, they feel irritated, bothered, or exasperated — not just mildly annoyed, but noticeably and somewhat strongly so. The feeling often builds up because something keeps happening, keeps going wrong, or feels unfair or unnecessary.
Aggravation means one of two closely related things: 1. The act of making a bad situation even worse; 2. A feeling of irritation and frustration, or the thing that causes it.

An aggregate is a whole that is made up of many individual parts collected or grouped together. Think of it this way: you take several separate things, bring them together into one unified group or total, and that combined result is the aggregate.
To aggregate means to gather many separate things and bring them together into one combined whole or total.

Aggregation is the noun that describes two closely related things: the process of collecting many separate individual items together into one larger whole, and the result of that process — the whole itself that gets formed.

Aggression means hostile, forceful behavior that is directed at someone or something with the intent to dominate, harm, intimidate, or overpower. It is the noun that names the act, quality, or pattern of being aggressive.
Ready or likely to attack or confront others, as in "aggressive behaviour." It can also mean forceful and determined, as in "an aggressive sales campaign," or, of a disease, spreading quickly.

Aggressiveness is a noun that names a quality — specifically, the quality of approaching things with force, intensity, boldness, or a strong drive to push forward, dominate, or win, often without holding back.

To aggrieve someone means to cause them to feel wronged, hurt, or treated unjustly. When you aggrieve someone, you don't just make them sad — you make them feel that something unfair has been done to them.
When someone is aggrieved, they feel that they have been treated unfairly or wrongly — and they are upset, hurt, or resentful because of it. It is a specific kind of emotional pain.

Aghast means being so deeply shocked or horrified by something that you are momentarily frozen — overwhelmed, speechless, unable to react normally. It describes a moment when something hits you so hard that your mind and body briefly stop.
Agile means able to move, think, or respond quickly, easily, and with great control — without being clumsy, slow, or rigid. Think of it as the opposite of being stiff, sluggish, or stuck.

Agility means the ability to move, think, or adapt quickly, easily, and with great control. It is not just about speed. It is about being swift and smooth, swift and accurate, swift and in control — all at the same time.

Agita means a feeling of anxiety, stress, worry, or nervous unease — the kind of unsettled, on-edge feeling that something stressful causes you. It is an informal word, used in everyday speech rather than formal writing.

Agitate means to disturb something from a state of calm — whether that "something" is a person's mind, a physical substance, or a society. Think of it as the opposite of "settle." When you agitate something, you shake it up, stir it up, or work it up.
When a person (or animal) is agitated, they are in a state of being deeply unsettled, worried, or emotionally stirred up — to the point where they cannot stay calm or still.

A state of anxious, restless worry or nervous excitement, as in "she paced the room in agitation." It can also mean public campaigning to stir up support for a cause, or the shaking or stirring of a liquid.
An agitator is something — or someone — that stirs things up. That single idea of "stirring" runs through every use of this word.

Aglow describes something — or someone — that is radiating a warm, beautiful light or glow. Think of it as a single word that captures that soft, luminous quality you see in something that shines gently from within or is bathed in warm light.
Agnostic means "not claiming to know" — specifically about something that is genuinely uncertain, difficult to prove, or considered beyond the reach of human knowledge.

An agnostic is a person who holds the position that whether God — or any divine, supreme, or supernatural being — exists or doesn't exist is something that is not known, and may never be knowable by human beings.
The view that it is impossible, or currently impossible, to know whether God or any divine power exists.
Agog means being in a state of intense eagerness, excitement, or curiosity — especially when you are waiting for something to happen, be revealed, or be experienced.

To agonize means to suffer deeply — in your mind, your emotions, or your body. It is not a mild or passing discomfort. When you agonize, you are in real, intense pain — the kind that grips you, consumes your thoughts, and doesn't let go easily.
When someone is agonized, they are experiencing or visibly showing extreme, overwhelming pain — not a mild ache, not ordinary sadness, but a pain so intense that it takes over their entire being.

When something is agonizing, it causes extreme, almost unbearable pain or suffering — either in the body, or in the mind and emotions. It sits at the very top of the scale of pain and distress. It is far beyond just "painful" or "upsetting."
Agony means extreme, intense suffering — either physical, emotional, or both. It is not ordinary pain or discomfort. It is pain at its most overwhelming, most unbearable level.

An agony aunt is a person — almost always a woman — whose job is to receive letters or messages from members of the public who are going through personal problems, and to respond to those problems with advice, comfort, and guidance.

Agoraphobia is an anxiety disorder in which a person feels intense fear and distress in situations where they believe escape would be difficult, or where help might not be available if they were to panic or feel seriously unwell.
When something is described as agrarian, it relates to farmland — its use, its ownership, and the kind of life and society that is built around it.

Agree means to be of the same mind as someone, or to say yes to something. Think of it as two things coming together and fitting — two opinions matching, two people accepting the same idea, or two facts lining up.
Pleasant, pleasing, or enjoyable. When used of a person, it means willing to agree to something, or friendly and easy to get along with.
Agriculture is the human practice of deliberately growing plants and raising animals to produce food, materials, and other useful things.

An agronomist is a scientist who specializes in finding the best ways to grow crops and manage the soil they grow in, so that farmers can produce more food, more efficiently, and with less harm to the land.
Aground means: onto or on the ground at the bottom of a body of water, in a way that stops a vessel from moving.
An ague is a specific kind of fever — one that does not just burn steadily, but arrives in attacks that repeat themselves in a pattern.

A quantum effect in which a charged particle such as an electron is influenced by an electromagnetic potential even when it travels only through regions where the electric and magnetic fields are zero.
When you say someone or something is "ahead of their time," you mean that their ideas, work, or way of thinking was too advanced, too modern, or too innovative for the era they lived in.
To be ahead of the curve means to be more advanced, innovative, or forward-thinking than most other people or organizations.
"Ahead of time" means doing something before the expected, scheduled, or required moment.

Aid means help given to someone who genuinely needs it. When a person, group, or country is struggling and cannot fully manage on their own, whatever is provided to make things easier or better — that is "aid."
To aid means to help someone or something achieve a goal, overcome a difficulty, or function better. It always involves one thing making progress or success easier for another.
An aide is a person whose job is to help or support another person, especially someone in a position of authority, responsibility, or need.
An aide-de-camp is a military officer who works as a close personal assistant to a very senior officer — such as a general or an admiral — or to a head of state, a viceroy, or a governor.
An aide-mémoire is anything — most often a written document or a physical object — that helps you remember something you might otherwise forget.
To ail means to be sick, unwell, or in poor condition — or, when something is troubling a person or thing, to cause discomfort or distress to them.

Ailing means in a weak, poor, or deteriorating state — most commonly due to illness or some other serious problem. When you call someone or something "ailing," you are saying that they are not well, not strong, and not functioning as they should be.
An ailment is a health problem — something that is wrong with your body or, less commonly, your mind — that makes you feel unwell, uncomfortable, or unable to function normally.

An ailurophile is a person who loves cats. Not just someone who thinks cats are "okay" or "kind of cute," but someone who genuinely adores them — someone who feels a deep fondness, warmth, and affection specifically for cats.
An ailurophobe is a person who has an intense, irrational fear of cats.
Aimlessly means doing something without any goal, purpose, or direction.

To "air one's dirty laundry" means to publicly reveal private, embarrassing, or shameful personal matters that most people would prefer to keep secret — especially family conflicts, personal failures, or scandalous information.
Airborne means "in the air" or "carried by air." Anything that has left the ground and is now moving through, floating in, or being transported by air can be described as airborne.
In a light, casual, carefree way — as if the matter carries no weight at all, sometimes in a way that brushes off something serious.
To airlift something (or someone) means to transport them by aircraft — but not in the ordinary sense of booking a flight.

When someone puts on airs and graces, they are behaving as if they are more important, more sophisticated, or more refined than they really are. It means pretending to be of a higher class or status through fake, showy, or snobbish behavior.
When a place is described as airy, it means it has plenty of fresh air moving through it. It feels open, not cramped or stuffy. There are usually big windows, high ceilings, or good ventilation.
An aisle is a long, narrow walkway or passage that runs between two rows of things — such as seats, shelves, or benches — allowing people to walk through easily.

When something is ajar, it is slightly open — not fully open, and not fully closed, but somewhere in between, leaning toward closed. Think of a door that someone forgot to shut all the way, leaving just a small gap. That door is ajar.

"Akimbo" describes a specific position of the arms. When someone's arms are akimbo, both hands are placed firmly on the hips (or waist), and both elbows are bent and pointing outward — away from the body.
Akimbo is an adverb that describes a very specific body position. It almost always appears in the phrase "arms akimbo."
Akin means similar in nature, quality, or character.

Al dente is an adjective used to describe food — most commonly pasta, but also vegetables, rice, and legumes — that has been cooked until it is just tender on the outside but still has a slight firmness, a tiny bit of resistance, when you bite into it.
Alabaster is a naturally occurring stone — a mineral that comes out of the earth. It is not man-made. People have been digging it out of the ground, carving it, and using it for thousands of years.
Alacrity means doing something quickly and eagerly — with a kind of bright, willing enthusiasm. It is not just speed, and it is not just willingness. It is both, fused together into one feeling.

Something is alarming when it causes a sudden, serious feeling of worry or fear — specifically because it signals that something is wrong, dangerous, or getting worse. Think of the word "alarm" inside it.
Alarmingly means in a way that causes alarm — that is, in a way that makes you feel worried, anxious, or even a little frightened about something.
An alarmist is a person who exaggerates danger, risk, or bad news — causing unnecessary fear, worry, or panic in others — when the situation does not actually justify that level of alarm.

"Alas" is a word you say — or write — to express sorrow, regret, or disappointment about something sad or unfortunate. It signals that what you are about to say (or just said) is unhappy news, a painful truth, or an outcome you wish were different.
An albatross is a large seabird. When people say "albatross" in a straightforward, literal way, they are referring to this real creature.

If something is an albatross around your neck, it is a heavy burden — a problem, mistake, or responsibility that: Follows you everywhere and won't go away; Constantly causes you trouble or shame; Holds you back in life, work, or relationships; Is something you cannot easily escape or get rid of.

Albite is a naturally occurring mineral — a solid, crystalline substance found in the Earth's crust. It belongs to one of the most important and widespread mineral groups on Earth, called the feldspar group.

Alchemy means the process of transforming something ordinary, base, or worthless into something precious, powerful, or extraordinary — often in a way that feels almost magical or impossible to fully explain.
The adjective "alcoholic" has two closely related meanings, and both of them revolve around the same thing: alcohol — specifically the kind found in drinks like beer, wine, and spirits.

An alcoholic is a person who is addicted to alcohol — meaning they have lost control over their drinking and cannot reliably stop or limit it, even when they want to, and even when it is causing them serious harm.

Alcoholism is a serious, long-term medical condition in which a person has a powerful, uncontrollable urge to drink alcohol — and cannot stop, even when drinking is clearly destroying their health, relationships, work, and life.

An alcove is a small, recessed section built into or carved out of a larger space — most commonly a room or a wall. Think of it as a sheltered "pocket" or "nook" that is set back from the main area around it.
An alderman is an elected or appointed member of a city's or town's governing council — essentially, a local politician who helps run the affairs of a municipality (a city, town, or borough).
Something is aleatory when it depends on chance, luck, or a random event — when its outcome cannot be predicted or controlled, and is left to uncertainty rather than design or intent.
To alert someone means to make them aware of something important so they can pay attention, be prepared, or take action.
Alfalfa is a plant grown primarily to feed animals, but it also has uses in human food and health.

Alfresco simply means in the open air or outdoors. When you describe something as alfresco, you are saying that it happens outside, under the open sky, rather than inside a building or a covered space.
When you do something alfresco, you do it outside, in the open air — out in the open, under the sky, rather than inside a building.

An alga (plural: algae) is a living organism that makes its own food using sunlight — similar to how plants do — but it is not a plant. It is a simpler, more ancient form of life that lives mostly in water.
Algae are living organisms that make their own food using sunlight — just like plants do — but they are not plants.

An algorithm is a precise, ordered set of steps that, when followed correctly, solves a specific problem or completes a specific task. Think of it as a detailed recipe — not for food, but for getting anything done systematically.

An alias is a name that a person goes by that is not their real, official name. It is an alternative name — a second (or third, or fourth) name that someone uses instead of, or alongside, their true identity.
An alibi is proof — or a claim — that a person was somewhere else when something bad happened, which means they could not possibly have done it.
To alienate someone means to make them feel like a stranger — disconnected, unwelcome, or pushed away — from a person, a group, a place, or even from themselves.

When someone feels alienated, they feel like they do not belong — like they are an outsider looking in. They feel cut off, separated, or disconnected from something that they are supposed to be a part of.
Alienation is the state of feeling like an alien — not literally from outer space, but in an emotional, social, or philosophical sense.

"Alight" as an adjective means on fire or glowing with light. It describes something that is actively lit up — whether by real flames, by bright light, or even by a strong emotion radiating from within a person.
Of a bird or insect, to come down and settle on a surface. Of a person, to step off a bus, train, or other vehicle.
Aligned means "properly arranged so that things match up, point in the same direction, or agree with each other."
Alignment means the condition of things being correctly lined up, positioned, or arranged in relation to each other.

"Alike" means similar — two or more things or people share the same, or nearly the same, qualities, features, or characteristics. When you say two things are "alike," you are saying they noticeably resemble each other in some meaningful way.

Alimentary means relating to food, nourishment, or the process of feeding and digesting food. Whenever something is described as "alimentary," it is connected in some way to how living things take in food and process it to sustain life.
Alimony is money that one spouse is legally required to pay to the other after a marriage ends — whether through divorce or legal separation.

"Alkaline" is an adjective used to describe a substance that is chemically the opposite of acidic. It means a substance has a pH greater than 7 — placing it on the basic side of the chemical spectrum.
"All along" means "during the entire time" — from the beginning to now, or from the beginning to some specific point in the past.
Suddenly and without warning. It can also mean at the same time, with everything happening together.

When someone says "I'm all ears," it means they are ready and eager to listen to you completely. They are giving you their full, undivided attention. Nothing will distract them — they are focused entirely on what you are about to say.

"All hell breaks loose" means that a situation suddenly becomes completely chaotic, out of control, and overwhelming. In a single moment, everything goes wrong at once — there is noise, confusion, panic, anger, fighting, or total disorder.

When someone says "it's all in a day's work," they mean that something — no matter how difficult, dangerous, unusual, or impressive it may seem to others — is just a normal, expected part of their job or routine. It's a way of saying, "This is just what I do.
"All in all" means "considering everything together — both the good and the bad — here is my final conclusion."
When something is "all the rage," it means it is extremely popular right now — a big trend that almost everyone is excited about, talking about, buying, or doing.
Nevertheless; even so. Despite what was just said, this other thing is still true — as in "the film got terrible reviews, but I enjoyed it all the same."
"All told" means "in total" or "when everything has been counted and included."
"All walks of life" means people from every kind of background — different jobs, social classes, education levels, income levels, ages, cultures, and life experiences.
If the final result of a situation is good, then the difficulties, problems, or stress along the way don't matter anymore.
"All-encompassing" is an adjective that means covering, including, or dealing with absolutely everything — leaving nothing out.

When you use all-out before a noun, it means something is done using the absolute maximum amount of effort, force, energy, or resources — with nothing held back. Not 70%. Not 90%. One hundred percent. Everything available is being used.

When something covers every part, side, or area — leaving nothing out — you can call it "all-round." Think of a circle: it has no gaps, no missing sides. The word "all-round" carries exactly that image.

To allay something means to reduce or calm a negative feeling — to make it less intense, less troubling, or less pressing. Think of it as turning down the volume on something uncomfortable inside someone's mind or body.
An allegation is a claim that someone has done something wrong — but without proof (yet).
To allege something means to claim or state that something is true — especially something serious like a wrongdoing, a crime, or a misconduct — without having proven it yet.
"Alleged" means claimed to be true, but not yet proven.
According to what has been claimed, but not yet proven to be true.

Allegiance is a noun that means loyal support, commitment, and faithfulness that a person gives to someone or something they feel strongly bound to — such as a country, a leader, a group, a cause, or a set of beliefs.

Allegorical is an adjective that describes something — usually a story, painting, film, or any creative work — that operates on two levels at the same time: a surface level (what it literally shows) and a deeper level (what it actually means).
An allegory is a story — or a poem, painting, or any other creative work — that operates on two levels at the same time.

An allergy is a condition in which a person's immune system reacts abnormally — and harmfully — to a substance that is completely harmless to most other people. That substance is called an allergen. The word "allergy" is a noun, and its plural is allergies.
To alleviate something means to make a bad, painful, or difficult situation less intense, less severe, or easier to bear — without completely removing or solving it.
Alleviation means the act of making something bad, painful, or difficult feel less severe — without fully removing it.
An alley is a narrow passage — a long, tight space that allows you to move from one place to another. Think of it as a corridor, but outdoors or inside a specific building.
An alliance is a relationship between two or more parties — people, groups, organizations, or countries — who agree to work together to achieve a shared goal or protect their shared interests.
Alliteration is the repetition of the same starting sound across two or more nearby words in a sentence or phrase. When those opening sounds match and appear close together, that's alliteration.

To allocate means to officially decide that a specific amount of something — usually a resource like money, time, space, or people — will be set aside and directed toward a specific purpose or recipient. It is not a casual or accidental act.
The act of dividing something up and giving portions of it to different people or purposes, or the share that is set aside for someone or something, as in "the budget allocation."
To allot something means to officially give or set aside a specific portion of something — time, money, space, tasks, or any other resource — for a particular person or purpose.

An allotment is a specific share or portion of something that has been officially divided up and assigned to a particular person or group. The key word here is officially — an allotment is never a random or accidental piece of something.
Describes a mineral grain that has failed to develop its own natural geometric shape, and instead has an irregular outline imposed on it by the crystals growing around it.
When something is described as allotted, it means it has been officially set aside and given to someone, or reserved for a specific purpose — usually as a fixed, limited share or portion.
An allottee is a person who has been officially given a share or portion of something through a formal process of distribution.
"Allow for" means to make room for something — either in your plans, your thinking, your calculations, or in the structure of a system, design, or rule.

Allowance refers to something — money, a quantity, a margin — that is officially given, set aside, or permitted for a specific purpose. Think of it as a defined "slice" of something that someone is entitled to or that a system permits.

An alloy is a material made by melting two or more elements together — where at least one of those elements must be a metal — to produce a new, single, uniform material that has different (and usually superior) properties compared to any of its individual ingredients on their own.
To allude to something means to refer to it indirectly — to hint at it, suggest it, or bring it up without fully stating it or naming it openly.
Allure is a deep, magnetic, almost irresistible pull that something or someone has over you. It's not plain, ordinary attraction — it's stronger than that, and often more mysterious.
To allure someone means to attract them in a powerful, almost irresistible way — through a sense of charm, beauty, mystery, or the promise of something wonderful. It's not just regular attraction.

Something alluring is so powerfully and mysteriously attractive that it pulls you toward it almost like a magnet. You feel a strong urge — almost a craving — to get closer to it, have it, experience it, or know more about it.

An allusion is an indirect, passing reference to something outside the text — a person, a place, an event, a book, a myth, a historical moment, or anything from the broader world of human knowledge — made without fully explaining it.

Something is allusive when it hints at or indirectly refers to something else — a person, a place, a story, an event, a piece of art — without directly naming or explaining it. It points sideways at something rather than pointing straight at it.
Alluvial describes anything that was deposited, shaped, or formed by flowing water — most commonly a river or stream.
An ally is a person, group, or country that stands on your side — especially when things are difficult — and actively supports you, helps you, or works together with you toward a shared goal.
To ally means to deliberately join or unite with someone — a person, a group, an organization, or a country — in order to work toward a shared goal or to support each other.

Your alma mater is the school, college, or university that you attended and graduated from. Simple as that. When someone says, "Harvard is my alma mater," they mean Harvard is the school where they studied and got their degree.
An almanac is a book — usually published once a year — that packs together a wide variety of useful facts, data, and predictions all in one place.
An almond mom is a mother who imposes unhealthy eating habits and harmful expectations about weight and body image onto her children, especially daughters.

Alms means money, food, clothing, or any other goods given freely to poor or needy people out of charity or compassion. If you hand a coin to a beggar on the street, or give food to a homeless person, what you are giving is alms.
Aloft means high up in the air — well above the ground, raised to a considerable height, or suspended in the open sky.

"Along the lines of" means roughly similar to, in the general style/manner of, or something like. It tells the listener or reader: "What I'm about to say is not exact — it's a general idea, a comparison, or an approximation."
Alongside means at the side of something or someone — either physically (in space) or figuratively (in relationship, cooperation, or time).

When someone is aloof, they are deliberately distant — emotionally, socially, or both. They keep themselves apart from people or situations, showing little warmth, interest, or involvement. They are present, but they don't really connect.

Aloofness is the quality of keeping yourself emotionally and socially distant from the people around you — not physically, but mentally and emotionally. An aloof person is present in the room but feels unreachable.
Alpenglow is the warm, rosy-pink or reddish-orange light that you see glowing on the tops of mountains during twilight — in the few minutes just before sunrise or just after sunset.
An altar is a special, dedicated surface or structure — usually a raised table, flat platform, or block — that is set aside for religious, spiritual, or ceremonial purposes.

To alter something means to make a change to it — but not a total or sweeping change. The thing you alter stays fundamentally the same thing; it is simply adjusted, modified, or revised in some specific way.
A second version of yourself — a different identity, like a bold stage persona, that exists alongside your everyday self. It can also mean a very close and trusted friend.

An alteration is a change made to something that already exists — where the thing is modified in some way but is not completely replaced or destroyed. After the alteration, the original thing is still recognizably itself, just different in one or more ways.

An altercation is a heated, noisy, and angry argument between two or more people. It is a verbal clash — a moment where people are loudly disagreeing, often with raised voices, sharp words, and visible emotion.
Alterity means otherness — the quality or state of being "the other," of being fundamentally different from a point of reference, which is usually a self, a group, or a dominant perspective.

When something alternates, it switches back and forth between two things repeatedly, in a pattern. Think of a see-saw: one side goes up, then the other, then the first again, then the other again — neither side stays up permanently.
"Alternately" means in turns — two things keep switching back and forth, one after the other, in a repeating pattern.
When "alternative" is used as an adjective, it describes something that is not the main, standard, or usual thing — but a different option that could be used instead.
An alternative is one of the possible options you can choose from when you are in a situation where a decision must be made.
An altimeter is an instrument that measures altitude — meaning, how high something is above a reference point, usually sea level (the average surface level of the ocean).
Altitude means the height of something measured above a fixed reference point. That reference point is almost always sea level — the average surface level of the world's oceans.

Altruism is the genuine care for the well-being of others, acted upon without seeking any personal reward. When someone demonstrates altruism, their driving force is simply this: I want this other person (or creature) to be better off.
When you describe someone or something as altruistic, you mean that it is focused on the well-being of other people, with no expectation of personal gain or reward in return.
Alumnus means a person who has studied at and graduated from a particular school, college, or university. If you went to Harvard and finished your degree there, you are a Harvard alumnus.
A progressive, irreversible brain disorder that slowly destroys memory, thinking, and the ability to carry out everyday tasks.

An amalgam is a mixture of different things that come together to form a single, unified whole — but with a very important twist: the parts making up the mixture are noticeably distinct from each other, and you can still sense each of them within the result.

To amalgamate means to combine two or more separate things into a single, unified whole — not just to put them side by side, but to merge them so thoroughly that the result functions as one new entity.
An amalgamation is the combining of two or more separate things into one single, unified whole.
An amanuensis is a person whose job is to write down exactly what another person says, or to copy out a piece of writing by hand on someone else's behalf.

To amass something means to gradually build up a very large amount of it over time. Think of it like slowly filling a giant container — piece by piece, bit by bit — until you've collected an impressive, substantial quantity.
Amatory means relating to, expressing, or characteristic of romantic love or sexual desire.
In Greek mythology, a member of a nation of fierce women warriors. Today the word is used for a tall, strong, and powerful woman.

An ambassador is a person who officially represents one country, organization, or entity in its dealings with another. Think of them as a trusted spokesperson and messenger — someone empowered to speak, act, and negotiate on behalf of whoever sent them.

When "amber" is used as an adjective, it describes a specific, warm color — a rich golden-yellow with an orange tinge. Picture honey in a glass jar held up to sunlight, or the glow of a sunset just before the sky goes dark. That warm, luminous color is amber.

Ambidextrous describes a person who can use both their right hand and their left hand equally well — or nearly equally well — to perform tasks that normally require skill and control, such as writing, drawing, throwing, or playing a musical instrument.
Ambience means the overall feeling, mood, or atmosphere that a place gives you — the invisible but very real sense of "what it is like to be there." It is not one single thing you can point to.

When something is ambient, it belongs to the surrounding environment — it's already there, spread throughout a space, coming from no single identifiable source. It wraps around you. It's the background condition of a place.
Ambiguity is the quality of something having more than one possible meaning, interpretation, or outcome — and the situation gives you no clear way to tell which one is correct or intended.
Something is ambiguous when it can be understood or interpreted in more than one way, and it's genuinely unclear which way is the correct or intended one.

The word ambit means the scope, range, or extent of something — specifically, the boundaries within which something operates, applies, or holds influence. It describes the full reach of a thing, and just as importantly, where that reach ends.
Ambition is a strong, deep, internal desire to achieve something significant — success, power, a great goal, or a higher position in life — combined with the drive to actively work toward it.

When we call someone ambitious, we mean they have a strong, burning desire to achieve something great — whether that's success, power, wealth, fame, or a specific important goal. An ambitious person is not content with where they are right now.
Ambivalence is the state of having two genuinely opposite feelings, desires, or attitudes toward the same person, thing, or situation — both at the same time.

When you are ambivalent about something, you have two opposing feelings about it at the same time — and both feelings are genuinely real and strong. You are not simply confused or undecided. You simultaneously want something and don't want it.

To amble means to walk slowly and in a relaxed, unhurried way — not because you're tired or weak, but because you simply have no reason to rush. You're at ease. You're comfortable. You're moving at whatever pace feels pleasant to you in that moment.
In Greek and Roman mythology, the food of the gods, said to make them immortal. Today it means any food or drink that is exceptionally delicious.

Ambrosial means divinely delightful — so extraordinarily pleasing to the senses (especially taste and smell) that it feels like something beyond the human world, something worthy of the gods themselves.
The word ambulatory essentially revolves around one central concept: walking and movement.
An ambush is a surprise attack carried out by people (or animals) who were hiding and waiting for their target to come close, then striking suddenly when the target least expects it.
To ambush someone means to suddenly attack them after secretly hiding and patiently waiting for them to arrive.

To ameliorate something means to make a bad, painful, or unsatisfactory situation better than it currently is. Not perfect — just better. The key thing to understand is that this word is exclusively used for things that are already negative or problematic.
Amelioration is the process of making a bad, difficult, or unsatisfactory situation better — especially when that improvement happens gradually, over time, or through deliberate effort.

Amenable means open to something — not resisting it, not refusing it, but being willing to accept it, go along with it, or be affected by it. Think of it as a door that swings open rather than one that stays shut.
Amends means something you do — an action, gesture, or effort — to repair the harm, hurt, or damage you have caused someone.
To amend something means to make a specific change to something that already exists — usually to fix, improve, or update it.
When something is described as amended, it means it has been officially or deliberately changed, corrected, or updated — but it has not been thrown away and replaced with something entirely new.

An amendment is a formal change, correction, or addition made to something that already exists — most often a document, a law, or an agreement — without completely replacing or throwing away the original.

An amenity is anything — a feature, a service, a facility, or even an agreeable quality — that makes a place, situation, or experience more comfortable, convenient, or enjoyable. Think of it as the "nice extras" that go beyond what is merely necessary.

An amethyst is a beautiful purple gemstone. More specifically, it is a type of quartz — one of the most common minerals on Earth — but what makes amethyst special is its striking purple or violet color.

Amiability is the quality of being friendly, warm, and pleasant — the kind of natural, easy-going goodness that makes a person genuinely nice to be around. When someone is amiable, amiability is the name we give to that quality they possess.
Amiable describes a person who is genuinely friendly, warm, and pleasant to be around — someone who has a naturally good-natured personality that makes others feel comfortable and at ease.
Amiably means in a friendly, pleasant, and good-natured way. When someone does something amiably, they do it with easy, relaxed warmth — not forced, not stiff, just naturally cheerful and agreeable.

Amicable describes a quality of friendliness, goodwill, and cooperation — specifically in a situation where there could be tension, conflict, or disagreement, but the people involved choose to handle it calmly and respectfully instead.

Amicably means doing something in a friendly, peaceful, and cooperative way — especially when there is a disagreement, a separation, or a conflict involved, yet people choose to handle it without hostility or bitterness.
"Amid" means "in the middle of" or "surrounded by."
"Amidst" means being surrounded by something, or being in the middle of something — whether that "something" is a physical environment, a group of things, a situation, or an atmosphere.
When something is amiss, it means something is wrong, not right, or not as it should be.
"Amiss" means in a wrong, faulty, or unsatisfactory way — in a way that is not how it should be, not as expected, or not as it was supposed to turn out.

Amity means a state of friendly, peaceful, and warm goodwill between people or groups. It describes a relationship where both sides genuinely like, respect, and wish well for each other — not just tolerating one another, but actively being on good terms.
"Ammo" is an informal word for ammunition — the supply of things that a weapon fires, shoots, or launches in order to cause damage or destruction.

Bullets, shells, and other objects fired from weapons. Figuratively, facts or arguments that can be used to support your case or attack someone else's, as in "the scandal gave her opponents ammunition."
Amnesia is a condition in which a person loses the ability to remember things — either things that happened in the past, or the ability to form new memories going forward, or both.
Amnesiac means relating to, caused by, or characteristic of amnesia — or simply, having amnesia.

Amnesty is an official decision made by a government or authority to forgive a group of people for something they did wrong — and to completely wipe away any punishment those people would otherwise have faced.
"Amok" is an adverb that is almost always used in one specific phrase: run amok (sometimes spelled run amuck).
Amoral means outside of morality entirely — not caring about, not governed by, and not even capable of thinking in terms of right and wrong.
"Amorally" means doing something in a way that has no connection to right or wrong at all — not choosing to do wrong, but simply not engaging with the question of right or wrong in the first place.
Amorous is an adjective that describes feelings, behavior, or expressions that are driven by romantic love or sexual desire — or both at once.
Amorphous means without a definite, fixed shape or clear structure. If something is amorphous, it doesn't have neat, well-defined edges or a firm form you can point to and describe precisely.
Amortization means the process of gradually reducing something large — a debt or a cost — by spreading it into smaller, regular pieces over a set period of time, until it is completely gone.
To amortize something means to pay off or absorb a large financial amount gradually, in smaller pieces, spread out over a period of time — instead of dealing with it all at once.
To add up to a total, or to be the same as something, as in "the bill amounted to fifty dollars" or "his reply amounted to a refusal."

An amphibian is an animal that lives a double life — part of its life in water, and part on land. In fact, the word captures exactly this idea: these are creatures that belong to both worlds, not fully one or the other.
An amphitheater is a large, open venue designed so that a big crowd of people can watch an event happening in a central area.
Ample means more than enough — enough with comfort to spare.
Amplification means the process or result of making something greater than it already is — whether that means louder, stronger, larger, more detailed, or more widespread.
An amplifier is anything — most often an electronic device — that takes something weak or small and makes it stronger or bigger, while keeping its original nature intact.

Amplify means to make something bigger, stronger, louder, or more powerful than it already is. Think of it as turning up a dial — the thing itself doesn't change in nature, only in its intensity or reach.
Amplitude means how far something swings away from its resting, neutral position — and by extension, it's a measure of the size, intensity, or extent of something.
Amply means in a way that is more than enough — generously, fully, and with room to spare.
To amputate means to surgically cut off a limb or body part from a person's (or animal's) body.
An amulet is a small object that a person keeps or wears because they believe it has the magical power to protect them from harm, evil, bad luck, illness, or danger.

To amuse someone means to cause them to feel gentle pleasure through something funny, entertaining, or pleasantly interesting. When something amuses you, a quiet smile crosses your face, or a soft chuckle escapes you.

When you feel amused, you are experiencing a gentle, pleasant feeling of finding something funny or entertaining. It is a light, comfortable, relaxed kind of enjoyment — the kind that makes you smile quietly or let out a soft chuckle.

An about-face is a complete, total reversal — a full 180-degree flip in direction, opinion, decision, or behavior. Not a small adjustment. Not a partial change. A complete switch from one position to the exact opposite.
"An arm and a leg" means a very large amount of money — so much that it feels unreasonably or shockingly expensive. When something "costs an arm and a leg," it means it is extremely expensive.

An open secret is something that is supposed to be a secret — but in reality, almost everyone already knows about it. The people involved may still treat it as a secret officially, but the information has quietly spread around until it's common knowledge.
An anachronism is something — an object, a word, a custom, a technology, a person, or an idea — that appears in the wrong time period. It doesn't belong to the era it's associated with.
Anachronistic describes something that is out of place in time — it exists in, or is used in, a time period where it simply does not belong.
An anaesthetic is a substance — almost always a drug — that is given to a person to deliberately block their ability to feel sensation, especially pain. Think of it as a "feeling switch."
An anagram is a word or phrase that you get by rearranging all the letters of another word or phrase.
Analgesia is the state of being unable to feel pain, or having pain significantly reduced, while remaining fully conscious and aware of your surroundings.
When you describe something as analgesic, you are saying that it has the ability to reduce or relieve pain.

An analgesic is any drug or substance that relieves pain. If you take a pill when you have a headache and the pain goes away, that pill is an analgesic. The word is simply the medical and scientific name for a painkiller.

"Analogical" is an adjective. It describes anything that involves, relies on, or is built from analogy — the act of comparing two different things because they share a similar relationship, structure, or pattern.
Analogous means similar in function, role, or relationship — even if the two things being compared are very different in nature, origin, or appearance.

An analogue is something that closely corresponds to or parallels something else — usually by performing the same function or filling the same role — while being different in its nature, origin, or form.
An analogy is a comparison between two different things that share a similar pattern, relationship, or way of working — used to explain something, clarify an idea, or support an argument.
Analysis means breaking something complex into smaller parts and studying each part carefully to understand the whole thing better.

"Analytical" describes a quality — of a person, a skill, a method, or a piece of writing — that involves breaking something complex into smaller parts in order to understand it fully, deeply, and accurately.

To analyze something means to study it carefully by breaking it down into its smaller parts, examining each part closely, and then understanding how those parts connect — so that you end up with a deep, clear understanding of the whole thing.
Anaphylactic describes something related to a sudden, severe, whole-body allergic reaction that can be fatal if not treated immediately.
An anarchist is a person who believes that society should have no rulers, no governments, and no systems of forced authority over people.
Anarchy means the absence of a ruling authority — a situation where there is no government, no leader, no laws, and no one officially in charge of maintaining order.
Something or someone that is strongly disliked or completely unacceptable, as in "violence is anathema to her." In religion, a formal curse or excommunication.
Anatomy is about structure — what something is made of, how its parts are arranged, and how those parts connect and relate to each other.
An ancestor is any person from whom you are directly descended — meaning someone who was born before you, and from whom your family line flows down to you.
When you describe something as ancestral, you mean it belongs to, comes from, or is connected to your ancestors — the people in your family who lived before you.

Ancestry means the full line of people from whom you are descended — your parents, their parents, their parents, and so on, going back through time as far as you can imagine. Think of it as your family going backwards through history.
A heavy object dropped from a boat to the bottom of the water to stop it drifting. Figuratively, a person or thing that gives stability, or a news presenter who leads a broadcast.
An anchorage is a sheltered area of water where ships are safe to drop anchor and stay for a period of time. Think of it as a parking spot for ships — but in the sea, river, or harbor.
Ancient means belonging to a very distant past or having existed for a very, very long time — so long that it feels like an entirely different world from the one we live in today.
Ancillary means "providing support to something more important, while being less important than it."

When a piece of music — or a section within it — is described as andante, it means the music should be played at a calm, flowing, walking-pace speed. Not rushed. Not dragging. Just a steady, unhurried movement forward.
An andiron is one of a pair of metal supports placed inside a fireplace to hold the logs (firewood) up off the floor of the hearth.
Androgynous means combining both masculine and feminine qualities at the same time — not fully one, not fully the other, but a genuine blend of both.
When something is anecdotal, it means it is based on personal stories, individual experiences, or informal accounts — rather than on careful, systematic research, data, or scientific evidence.
An anecdote is a short, real story about a specific event or experience, usually involving a particular person.

Anemia is a medical condition in which your blood does not have enough healthy red blood cells — or does not have enough of a substance inside those cells called hemoglobin — to carry the right amount of oxygen to the rest of your body.
Having anemia — a lack of healthy red blood cells, leaving a person pale and tired. Figuratively, weak, thin, and lacking the strength or energy something should have.
A sea anemone is a soft-bodied ocean animal with a ring of tentacles that make it look like a flower. An anemone is also a garden plant with bright, cup-shaped flowers.

Anesthesia is the deliberate, controlled, and temporary loss of sensation in the body — most importantly, the loss of pain — that is brought on by specific drugs administered by a medical professional.
Anew is an adverb that means "again, but with a fresh start" — often with the sense of doing something over in a new or different way, rather than simply repeating it in the exact same way.
Resembling an angel — beautiful, pure, and innocent in appearance, or exceptionally kind and well-behaved in behaviour.
To angle for something means to try to get what you want, but indirectly — through hints, flattery, clever maneuvering, or subtle behavior — rather than simply asking for it openly and directly.

Anglophobia means a strong dislike, fear, hatred, or deep prejudice directed at England, English people, English culture, or anything associated with England or the English-speaking British world. A person who holds these feelings is called an anglophobe.
Angst means a deep, heavy feeling of anxiety, worry, or unease — often about life, the future, or your place in the world.
Anguish is a severe, intense form of emotional or mental pain — the kind that overwhelms a person so completely that it feels unbearable. It is not ordinary sadness or worry.

Anguished describes someone — or something — that is showing or experiencing deep, overwhelming emotional or mental pain. This isn't ordinary sadness or discomfort. It is severe inner suffering, the kind that feels almost unbearable and is difficult to hide.
Having sharp corners or angles, as in "an angular design." Of a person, thin and bony, with sharp features, as in "an angular face."
An animadversion is a harsh, critical remark that expresses strong disapproval of someone or something.

To animadvert means to criticize something formally and openly, or to pass a critical remark or judgment on something. Think of it as deliberately turning your attention toward something and then commenting on it with disapproval or fault-finding.

"Animate" means alive or living. When you call something animate, you are saying it has life. A dog is animate. A human being is animate. A tree is animate. A rock, a chair, a river, a plastic bottle — these are not animate.
Animate means to bring to life — or more broadly, to fill something with life, energy, or movement.

The word animated at its heart means full of life and energy. Think of the difference between a person staring blankly at a wall versus a person who is laughing, waving their hands, and talking with sparkling eyes. The second person is animated.
Describes a mechanical figure built to look like a real creature or person and made to move as if alive, powered by motors and electronics hidden inside it.

Animism is the belief that everything in the world has a spirit or a soul — not just humans and animals, but also trees, rivers, mountains, rocks, the wind, the rain, and even ordinary objects like a stone or a cooking pot.
Animosity means a strong, active feeling of hostility or bitter dislike toward someone or something.

At its most common, animus means a strong feeling of hostility, dislike, or ill will directed at a specific person, group, or thing. It is not just mild dislike — it carries a sense of deep-seated, often personal antagonism.
The ankh is an ancient Egyptian symbol that looks like a cross, except that instead of having a plain top arm, it has an oval loop (like a teardrop or a handle) sitting on top of it.

"Annals" is a noun that refers to the formal, written historical record of events — essentially, documented history. It is almost always used in its plural form. You will rarely, if ever, see the singular "annal" in everyday writing or speech.

To anneal something means to heat it to a very high temperature and then allow it to cool down very slowly and gradually. This is done deliberately, under controlled conditions, to make the material stronger, tougher, more flexible, and easier to work with.

An annex is an addition to something that already exists — something secondary and supplementary, always attached to or associated with a main, primary thing. The annex is never the center of anything; it is always the extra.
To annex something means to take control of a place or territory and permanently absorb it into your own country, state, or domain — making it officially "yours."
Annexation is the act of one country, government, or authority formally taking over a territory and making it their own, permanently and officially.

To annihilate something means to destroy it so completely that it effectively ceases to exist. Not just damage it. Not just break it. But wipe it out entirely — leaving nothing, or next to nothing, behind.

Annihilation means the complete and total destruction of something — so thorough that it leaves nothing behind. It comes from the verb annihilate, and when you turn it into a noun, it names the act, event, or result of that total destruction.

An anniversary is a day that comes back every year on the exact same date as a meaningful past event. The idea is simple: something important happened on a specific date, and every year when that date returns, it is called the anniversary of that event.

At its most essential, to annotate means to add your own notes, comments, or explanations to a piece of content — a book, a document, an image, a piece of code, anything — without changing the original content itself. The notes you add are called annotations.

An annotation is a note, comment, or explanation that is added to a piece of existing content — such as a book, a document, an image, a piece of code, or a dataset — in order to explain, clarify, describe, or add information about that content.
To announce something means to make information known to people — usually publicly, officially, or to a group — often for the first time.

To annoy someone means to cause them a feeling of mild irritation, impatience, or displeasure. When you annoy someone, you make them feel bothered — not deeply hurt, not furious, but uncomfortable in a nagging, "I wish this would stop" kind of way.
Annoyance describes a mild, uncomfortable feeling — a kind of low-level dissatisfaction or displeasure that arises when something bothers, disturbs, or irritates you. It is not intense anger or rage.

An annuity is a financial arrangement in which a person receives a series of regular payments — typically monthly, quarterly, or yearly — either for a fixed period of time or for the rest of their life.

To annul something means to officially and completely wipe it out — not just stop it, but declare that it has no legal force whatsoever, often treating it as though it never existed in the first place.
An annulment is an official declaration — made by a court, a legal authority, or a religious institution — that something never validly existed in the first place.
When something is described as anodyne, it means it is so carefully designed to be safe, inoffensive, and unlikely to upset anyone that it ends up being dull, empty, or meaningless.

To anoint someone means to deliberately apply oil — or sometimes another liquid — to a person's body, usually as a meaningful, ceremonial act. But the word almost never stops at just the physical action.

Anointing is the act of deliberately applying oil — or sometimes another substance — to a person or object as a meaningful, intentional gesture. The word always implies that this is not just a casual, accidental, or practical act. It is purposeful.
Anointment means the act of anointing — that is, the act of applying oil or a sacred liquid to a person (or sometimes an object) as part of a ceremony.
Anomalous means departing from what is normal, expected, or standard. If something is anomalous, it doesn't fit the established pattern that everything else around it follows.
An anomaly is something that does not fit the normal pattern. It is a thing, event, person, or situation that stands out because it is different from what is expected or usual in its surroundings.

Anomie means normlessness — a condition where the shared rules, values, and moral standards that normally hold a society together have broken down, weakened, or become unclear, leaving people without clear guidance for how to live, what to aim for, and how to relate to one another.
"Anon" means soon, shortly, or in a little while. It tells you that something is going to happen — but not at this exact moment. A small delay is expected, and then the thing will occur.
Anonymity is the state of being unknown or unidentifiable. When someone has anonymity, their true identity — who they actually are — is hidden from others.
When something or someone is described as anonymous, it means their identity — most importantly, their name — is either unknown or not revealed to others.

An anorak is a waterproof or windproof jacket with a hood attached. Its most recognizable feature is that it is usually a pullover style — meaning you slide it over your head to wear it, instead of zipping or buttoning it up the front like a coat.
To be held responsible for something and face the consequences, as in "they will answer for their crimes." It can also mean to vouch for someone or something.
Antagonism is a state of active opposition between two things — people, groups, forces, or ideas — that are fundamentally working against each other.

An antagonist is someone or something that actively works against someone or something else. Think of it as the force of opposition — the thing standing in the way, pushing back, or creating conflict.
Antagonistic means actively working against something or someone — showing opposition, resistance, or hostility that goes beyond simple disagreement. The key word here is actively.

To antagonize someone means to say or do something that makes them feel hostile, angry, or opposed to you — essentially, to turn someone against you, either by irritating them repeatedly or by actively working against their interests.
An ante is something you must put in — usually money — just to be allowed to participate in something, before anything has actually started.
Antebellum is an adjective that means "belonging to, existing in, or characteristic of the period before a war."
To antecede means to come before something — in time, in order, or in sequence.

Antecedence means the state or fact of coming before something else — in time, in order, or in sequence. If something has antecedence, it simply means it occupied the "before" position. It came first.
When "antecedent" is used as an adjective, it means coming before something else — in time or in order — and being meaningfully connected to what follows.
An antecedent is simply something that came before something else — and that earlier thing has a meaningful connection to what follows it. Think of it as "the thing that went first."

An antechamber is a small room that sits directly in front of, and leads into, a larger and more important room. It is a space you must first enter — or wait in — before you are permitted to pass through into the main room beyond it.
When you say A antedates B, you mean A is older than B — it existed or happened first.
Something antediluvian is so incredibly old or outdated that it seems to belong to a completely different world — one that has long since vanished.

"Anterior" means situated at or toward the front. It describes where something is positioned — specifically, that it is in the front relative to something else, or closer to the front than something else.
An anteroom is a small room that you pass through — or wait in — before entering a larger, more important room beyond it. Think of it as a room that guards the entrance to another room.
An anthem is a song that stands for something — a country, a group, a cause, a movement, or even a feeling. It is not just any song.
An anthology is a carefully chosen collection of creative works — such as poems, short stories, essays, songs, or films — gathered together into one single place.
The idea that the universe's laws and constants must be compatible with conscious life, because otherwise no one would be here to observe them.
The proposed name for the current period of Earth's history, in which human activity has become the dominant influence on the planet's climate and environment.
Something is anthropoid when it looks or is structured like a human being — but is not actually human.
"Anthropological" means relating to the study of human beings — their origins, cultures, societies, behaviors, biology, and evolution.
An anthropologist is a scientist who studies human beings — not just people alive today, but humans across all of time, all over the world, and in every aspect of their lives.
Anthropology is the study of human beings — not just one part of being human, but all of it. It asks a very big question: What does it mean to be human?
Anthropomorphic describes anything non-human that has been given, assigned, or portrayed with human qualities.
Anthropomorphism is the act of giving human qualities to something that is not human.

To anthropomorphize something means to treat a non-human thing — an animal, an object, a natural force, a god, or even an idea — as if it were human. You give it human qualities: human feelings, human thoughts, human motivations, or even a human personality.
An antibiotic is a medicine that either kills bacteria or stops bacteria from growing, so that your body's immune system can finish clearing an infection.

An antibody is a tiny, Y-shaped protein made by your immune system whose entire job is to find, grab onto, and help destroy foreign threats — such as bacteria, viruses, toxins, and other harmful substances — that enter your body.
To anticipate means to think ahead about something that hasn't happened yet — and very often, to act on that thinking. It lives in the future.
Anticipation is the mental and emotional experience of thinking about a future event before it happens — and feeling something because of it.
"Anticipatory" describes something that happens, exists, or is felt before an expected event — driven entirely by the expectation of that event.

Anticlimactic describes something that fails to deliver the payoff that the buildup promised. It's the feeling of being let down after a lot of anticipation — when the expected exciting peak turns out to be flat, underwhelming, or just... nothing special.

An anticlimax is a sudden, disappointing drop from something exciting, tense, or important down to something trivial, ordinary, or underwhelming — especially when that drop comes right after a long buildup of expectations.

Antics means silly, playful, or foolish behaviors and actions — the kind that make people laugh, shake their heads, or both. These actions are usually exaggerated, over-the-top, or attention-grabbing.
An antidote is something that works against a poison or something harmful — neutralizing it, stopping it, or reversing the damage it causes.
Matter made of antiparticles — mirror images of ordinary particles with the opposite electric charge. When matter and antimatter meet, they destroy each other in a burst of energy.
An antioxidant is a substance that protects your body's cells from a type of internal damage caused by harmful, unstable molecules called free radicals.
If you are antipathetic toward something or someone, you have a strong, deep-seated feeling of dislike or aversion toward it. It goes beyond a casual "I don't like this."
Antipathy means a strong, deep feeling of dislike or aversion toward someone or something.
"Antipodal" means completely and utterly opposite — as far apart from each other as two things can possibly be.
"Antipodes" refers to a pair of places on Earth that are positioned at the exact opposite ends of the globe from each other — as far apart as any two points on Earth can possibly be.

When you describe something as antiquarian, you are saying it is related to the study, collection, or deep appreciation of old, rare, and historically significant objects — things like ancient artifacts, old manuscripts, rare coins, or especially old and rare books.

An antiquarian is a person who has a deep love for, studies, and often collects old and rare things from the past — things like ancient coins, old manuscripts, rare books, historical documents, antique objects, and artifacts.

When you call something antiquated, you are saying that it is so old that it no longer belongs in the modern world. It has aged past the point of being useful, fitting, or sensible in today's context. The world has moved on, but this thing hasn't.
"Antique" describes something that is genuinely old — old enough to belong to a clearly different era of the past — and because of that age, it is typically valuable, rare, or worth preserving.

An antique is a man-made object from the distant past — something old enough to be considered a piece of history — that people collect and value today because of its age, craftsmanship, rarity, beauty, or the story it carries.
The ancient past, especially the era of the great ancient civilizations such as Greece, Rome, and Egypt. It can also mean great age, or an object surviving from ancient times.
The word antiseptic has two layers of meaning — a literal one rooted in medicine and hygiene, and a figurative one used to describe people, places, writing, and atmospheres.
Antisocial means acting in ways that harm, disturb, or work against the wellbeing of other people and society as a whole.
If someone or something is antithalian, it means they are opposed to, or strongly disapproving of, fun, laughter, festivity, and merriment.
Antithesis means the direct, exact opposite of something. Think of it as the furthest possible point away from something — not just different, but the complete reverse.
Antithetical means directly and completely opposed to something — not just different from it, but fundamentally in conflict with it, to the point where the two things cannot truly coexist.

An antler is a large, branching, bone-like structure that grows out of the top of the head of certain animals. Think of it as a natural "tree" growing out of an animal's skull — with a main trunk and multiple branches sticking out from it.

"Antsy" is an informal adjective that describes two closely related feelings that usually appear together: A feeling of restlessness — your body can't keep still; you feel a strong urge to move, get up, or do something.
An anvil is a large, very heavy block — traditionally made of iron or steel — that is used as a solid working surface for shaping hot metal.
Anxiety is a feeling of worry, unease, or nervousness about something uncertain — usually something that has not happened yet, but might.

Anxious describes a state of mental unease — a feeling that something could go wrong, might already be going wrong, or is simply uncertain. When you are anxious, your mind is unsettled, often occupied with "what if?" thoughts.
When you are in serious trouble, you accept any help or solution available, even one you would normally reject.

When something is anyone's guess, it means that nobody knows the answer, outcome, or truth about it. The situation is so uncertain or unclear that no person — not even an expert — can say what is true or what will happen.
Apace means quickly, rapidly, or at a fast speed — especially when describing something that is continuously moving forward or progressing without slowing down.

Apartheid is a system in which a government officially divides its citizens into racial groups and then treats those groups with extreme, deliberate inequality — not through carelessness or informal bias, but through laws written into the books and enforced by the full power of the state.
If someone is apathetic, it means they have little or no interest, feeling, concern, or enthusiasm about something — or sometimes about everything in general.

Apathy is a complete absence of feeling, interest, or concern about something — or about everything in general. A person experiencing apathy doesn't feel excited, sad, angry, curious, or motivated. They simply feel... nothing. They don't care.

An ape is a type of large, intelligent, tailless primate — meaning a mammal that belongs to the same broad group as monkeys, lemurs, and humans. The single most important thing to know about apes: they have no tail (or only a tiny, non-functional stub).
To ape someone means to copy or imitate them — their behavior, gestures, speech, style, or mannerisms. But it's not just any kind of copying.

An aperture is a controlled opening or hole through which something — most commonly light — passes. It is not just any crack or gap. The word implies that the opening is intentional, and crucially, that its size matters.

Apex means the single, absolute highest or topmost point of something. Think of it as the very tip — not just anywhere near the top, but the one precise point where something reaches its maximum height or peak and can go no further.
Aphasia is a medical condition in which a person loses — partially or completely — the ability to use language, as a result of damage to the brain.

An aphorism is a short, sharp statement that captures a general truth about life, people, or the world — expressed so precisely and cleanly that it sticks in your mind long after you first encounter it.
Expressed in short, clever, memorable statements that capture a general truth — like an aphorism.

An apiarist is a person who keeps, raises, and takes care of bees — specifically honeybees — usually in man-made structures called beehives. A simpler, more everyday word for the same person is a beekeeper.

An apiary is a place where beehives are kept and managed. Think of it as a dedicated "home base" or "station" for a collection of beehives. Just like a library is a building that houses books, an apiary is a location that houses beehives.

Apiculture is the practice of keeping, managing, and caring for honeybees in order to benefit from them — most commonly to collect honey, but also for other products they produce and services they provide.
Aplenty means "in great amounts," "in more than enough quantity," or "abundantly."
Aplomb means calm, confident composure — especially when you are under pressure, facing a difficult situation, or when things are going wrong around you.

The word apocalypse has two distinct but deeply connected meanings: 1. A divine revelation — a great truth being uncovered or revealed, especially from God. 2. A catastrophic, world-ending event — the total destruction or collapse of the world, or of life and civilization as we know it.

The word apocalyptic is an adjective. It describes something that is either related to the total destruction or end of the world, or that resembles what such an end might look, feel, or sound like — massive, overwhelming, devastating beyond recovery.

When you call something apocryphal, you are saying that it is a widely told story, claim, or quote that is probably not true — or at least cannot be verified — even though many people believe it and repeat it as if it were fact.
The word apogee means the farthest or highest point something reaches — either in a literal, physical sense or in a figurative sense.
When you describe someone or something as apolitical, you mean they exist outside the world of politics — they are not involved in it, not interested in it, and take no political side or position.

Apologetically means doing something in a way that shows you feel sorry, regretful, or guilty — usually because you believe you've done something wrong, caused an inconvenience, or failed to meet someone's expectations.
An apologia is a formal, reasoned defense of something — your beliefs, your actions, your decisions, or your character.

An apologist is a person who defends, justifies, or argues in favor of a particular idea, belief, cause, person, or system — especially when that thing is being criticized, doubted, or attacked by others.
To apologize means to express to someone that you are sorry for something you said, did, or failed to do — something that hurt them, wronged them, disturbed them, or caused them trouble in some way.

An apologue is a short story with a moral lesson at its heart, where the characters are typically animals, plants, or objects — not human beings. The whole point of an apologue is to teach something about right and wrong, good judgment, or wise conduct.
"Apoplectic" means overwhelmingly, explosively furious — so angry that a person seems to be on the verge of losing all physical and mental control. It is not used for ordinary anger.

Medically, apoplexy refers to what we today call a stroke — a sudden, severe event inside the brain where a blood vessel either bursts or gets blocked, cutting off the blood supply to part of the brain in an instant.

Aposematism is the biological strategy where a living creature uses a conspicuous, attention-grabbing signal to warn potential predators that attacking or eating it would be a bad idea — because it is toxic, venomous, foul-tasting, or otherwise harmful.
Apostasy means the deliberate, complete abandonment of a belief, faith, religion, or cause that a person once deeply held and publicly committed to.

When "apostate" is used as an adjective, it describes a person — or something belonging to that person — who has openly abandoned a belief, faith, religion, or ideology that they once genuinely held and committed to.
An apostate is a person who was once a committed member or believer of a religion, ideology, or cause — and then deliberately abandoned it, often publicly and completely.

An apostle is someone who is chosen and sent out on an important mission — specifically to spread a belief, message, or cause to others. The word almost always carries a sense of authority, purpose, and pioneering spirit. An apostle isn't just a believer.
An apothecary is a person who prepares and sells medicines. Think of them as the pharmacist of the old world — except they did far more than just hand you a box of pills.
An apothegm is a short, sharp, and clever saying that expresses a truth or a piece of wisdom — and it comes from a specific, identifiable person.
Apotheosis means the elevation of something or someone to the highest possible level — so high, it feels almost divine or sacred.
To apotheosize something or someone means to elevate them to the highest possible status — so high that they are treated almost as a god, or as the absolute, supreme ideal of their kind.
If something is apotropaic, it is meant to ward off evil, harm, or bad luck — especially evil of a supernatural kind, like malevolent spirits, curses, or the "evil eye."
To appall someone means to cause them to feel a sudden, strong combination of shock, horror, and deep disgust — all at once. It's not just about surprising someone.
Appalled describes the feeling you get when something shocks you so deeply — because it seems so wrong, cruel, offensive, or unacceptable — that you can barely believe it is actually happening.
Appalling means so bad that it causes shock, horror, or disgust. It describes something that doesn't just make you feel unhappy or uncomfortable — it hits you hard. It disturbs you.
Appallingly means "in a way that causes shock, horror, or deep disgust" — or, when used as an intensifier, "to an extremely bad and disturbing degree."
Apparatus means a collection of parts, tools, instruments, or components that work together as a unified whole to perform a specific function.
Clearly visible or obvious. It can also mean seeming to be true, but possibly not really so — as in "an apparent accident."

Apparently signals that something seems to be true, but the speaker is not stating it as a definite fact. It creates a gap between "what appears to be" and "what definitely is." The speaker is stepping back slightly from a claim, rather than owning it fully.
An apparition is a ghostly figure or image that appears suddenly — something seen that feels unreal, supernatural, or deeply unsettling.

To appeal means to reach out — either because something pulls you toward it, or because you are reaching out to someone for help or intervention. This "reaching" quality runs through all its meanings.
When something is appealing, it has a quality that attracts you toward it — it draws your attention, interest, or desire. It makes you think "I like this," "I want this," or "This is good."
Appear carries one underlying idea: something comes into awareness — whether it physically comes into view, shows up in a place, gives off an impression, or comes out into the world.
To appease someone means to calm them down or satisfy them — especially when they are angry, upset, or making demands — by giving them what they want.

Appeasement is the act of giving an aggressive, threatening, or demanding person or group what they want — not because it's fair or right — but specifically to calm them down, avoid a fight, or prevent a bigger conflict from breaking out.
An appeaser is a person who tries to avoid conflict or keep the peace by giving in to someone's demands — even when those demands are unfair, unreasonable, or threatening.
Appellate means relating to, or having the power to hear and decide, appeals in a legal context.
