An appellation is simply a name or title given to someone or something. When you call something by a particular name — whether that name is official, descriptive, or honorary — that name is its appellation.
To append something means to add it to the end of something that already exists.

An appendage is something that is attached to a larger, more important main thing — and is considered secondary to it. It is not the center. It is not the core. It is the thing that hangs off the core, sticks out from it, or is connected to it.

The word appendix refers to something that is attached to or added onto something larger and more important — something that belongs to the main thing but is not the main thing itself. Think of it as a "hanger-on."
To appertain means to belong to, relate to, or be a natural and proper part of something.

Appetency means a deep, natural, instinctive desire or craving for something. It's the kind of longing that doesn't feel like a choice — it feels like it comes from within you, almost like a built-in pull that your nature generates on its own.
Appetite is a natural desire or craving for something — most often food, but also for anything else that you want or enjoy deeply.
To applaud means to show that you approve of, appreciate, or are impressed by something or someone.

When someone is the apple of your eye, they are the person you love, treasure, and cherish the most in the world. They are your most precious person — the one you care about deeply and protect with all your heart.
When someone says two things are "apples and oranges," they mean those two things are so different from each other that comparing them is unfair or pointless.
An appliance is a device or machine that is purpose-built to perform a specific, practical task — usually to make everyday life easier, more comfortable, or more efficient.

When something is applicable, it means it is relevant, suitable, or fitting for a specific situation, person, or case — in other words, it actually applies to that situation. Think of it as asking: "Does this belong here? Does this fit this situation?"

An applicant is a person who formally requests something — usually an opportunity, a position, a benefit, or a permission — from an authority or organization that has the power to grant or deny it. The key word here is formally.

"Application" is a word that wears many hats. It has five distinct meanings in English, but they all share a single underlying idea: directing something toward a target — whether that's a request, a substance, a skill, an effort, or a tool.
An appliqué is a decorative piece of material — almost always fabric — that is cut into a shape and then attached onto the surface of another, larger piece of material.
Every meaning of "apply" shares one central idea — bringing something into contact with something else, with a purpose.
To appoint someone means to officially choose them for a specific role, job, or position — and to give them that role through an act of authority.
An arrangement to meet someone at a particular time and place, as in "a doctor's appointment." It can also mean the act of choosing someone for a job, or the job itself.
Apposite means perfectly suited, strikingly fitting, or precisely right for a particular situation or purpose.

An appraisal is a careful, considered judgment about something — its value, quality, condition, or nature. It is not a careless glance or a snap decision. It is a deliberate, thoughtful assessment formed after giving something proper attention.

To appraise something means to carefully examine and judge its value, quality, or condition. The judgment is not a quick, casual glance — it is a deliberate, thoughtful assessment. When you appraise something, you are essentially asking: "What is this worth?
Appreciable means large enough, or significant enough, to be noticed or felt.
To recognize and enjoy the true value or quality of something, or to be grateful for it. It can also mean to fully understand a situation, or to increase in value over time.

"Appreciation" is always about recognizing and acknowledging value or worth. Something — a person's kindness, a piece of music, a house, a difficult situation — has value, and you see that value clearly.
To catch and arrest someone suspected of wrongdoing. In formal or literary use, it can also mean to grasp or understand something.
A feeling of worry or unease about something that might happen in the future. It can also mean the arrest of a suspect, or understanding of something.
If you are apprehensive, you are feeling worried, uneasy, or slightly fearful about something that might happen in the future.
An apprentice is a person who is learning a skilled trade or craft by working directly under the close supervision of someone who is already a qualified expert in that field.

An apprenticeship is a formal, structured arrangement in which a person learns a skilled trade or profession — not by sitting in a classroom, but by actually doing the work, side by side with an experienced expert, over a set period of time.
To apprise someone means to inform or notify them about something — to make sure they know about a fact, a situation, or a development.
Approach means to move closer to something or someone — but not all the way there. There is always a sense of moving toward, of getting nearer, rather than arriving.
"Approachable" means easy to reach, talk to, or engage with — without fear, nervousness, or difficulty. Think of the word "approach," which means to come near to someone or something.

Approbation means approval — but not just any quiet, internal approval. It means approval that is expressed, shown, or officially given. It is the act of endorsing something or someone with clear, positive recognition.
Appropriate means suitable or fitting for a specific situation, person, place, time, or purpose.
When "appropriate" is used as a verb, it means to take something and make it your own — either by claiming it, using it, or officially setting it aside for a purpose.
"Appropriately" means in a way that fits the situation perfectly — in a manner that is right, suitable, and correct for the specific circumstances at hand.
Appropriation means the act of taking something and making it your own — setting it aside for a particular person, group, or purpose.
Approval means a positive response toward something or someone — a signal that says "yes, this is good" or "yes, you may go ahead."
To approve means to say "yes" to something — either officially, or in your own mind and heart.
To approve of something or someone means to think that it is good, right, or acceptable. It is your personal judgment — your inner feeling or opinion — that something meets a standard you believe in.
When something is approximate, it is close to the real or exact value, but not perfectly precise. It is a "nearly right" answer — good enough to be useful, but not 100% accurate.
To approximate means to come close to something — without reaching it exactly.
An approximation is something — a number, a value, a description, or an answer — that is close to the real or exact thing, but not perfectly identical to it.

An appurtenance is something that belongs to or goes along with something more important — not as the main thing itself, but as a secondary thing that is naturally attached to it, associated with it, or considered part of it.
Apricity is the warmth of the sun that you feel on your skin during cold weather, especially in winter.
When something is described as apropos, it means it is perfectly fitting and remarkably relevant to the situation, topic, or moment at hand.
"Apropos" as an adverb means at exactly the right moment, in a way that fits perfectly with what is already happening or being discussed.

When something is apt, it means it fits the situation so well that you couldn't have chosen better. Think of it as a "perfect match" — like a key that fits a lock exactly, with no wiggling, no forcing, just a clean fit.
Aptitude means a natural ability to learn or do something well — an inborn quality that makes a person pick up a particular skill faster and more easily than most other people.
Aquaplaning is the dangerous loss of control that happens when a vehicle's tires ride on top of a thin layer of water on the road instead of gripping the road itself.
An aqueduct is a structure built to carry water from one place to another, especially over a long distance.
Aqueous means of, relating to, containing, or dissolved in water — in short, water-based.
An aquifer is an underground body of water stored inside rock, gravel, or sand.
Aquiline means resembling or characteristic of an eagle — specifically the sharp, curved, prominent quality of an eagle's beak.

An arabesque is a style of ornamental design made of flowing, interlacing curves and lines, typically inspired by plant forms — curling vines, spiraling stems, leaves, and flowers — all woven together into a continuous, repeating pattern.
Arable is an adjective used to describe land or soil that is suitable for growing crops.
An arachnid is any animal that belongs to the scientific group called Arachnida.
An arbiter is a person (or sometimes a thing) who has the final say on something. Their decision is accepted as the highest authority — no one above them gets to overrule it.
"Arbitrarily" describes how something is done. Specifically, it means doing something without a clear reason, rule, or principled basis to justify the choice.

Arbitrary describes something done or decided without a clear reason, logic, rule, or principle behind it — something that could just as easily have been done differently, because there's nothing solid backing the choice.

To arbitrate means to act as a neutral, independent person (or panel of people) who steps in between two sides that are in a dispute, listens carefully to both of them, and then makes a final, binding decision to resolve the conflict.
A way of settling a dispute outside court, in which both sides agree to accept the decision of a neutral person called an arbitrator.
A shaded garden structure made of a light wooden or metal frame covered with climbing plants, forming a leafy shelter.

Arboreal means relating to trees, or more specifically, living in or among trees. If something is described as arboreal, trees are at the center of its existence — its home, its highway, its dining table, its shelter.
Arborescent means tree-like in structure, shape, or growth pattern.
An arboretum is a carefully designed outdoor space — somewhat like a park or garden — that is dedicated specifically to growing, displaying, and studying trees and other woody plants.
An arc is a curved line or curved path — smooth, bent, and shaped roughly like a portion of a circle. Think of the letter C, or the shape of a crescent moon. That kind of curve is an arc.
A row of arches supported by columns, or a covered walkway lined with shops. It is also a place with coin-operated games for entertainment.
Arcadian is an adjective that describes something — a place, a way of life, or a scene — that is ideally peaceful, simple, and close to nature.
Deep secrets, mysterious knowledge, or hidden truths that are known only to a few people — usually because they require special study or insight to understand.
If something is arcane, it is so obscure, mysterious, or deeply specialized that only a very small number of people can truly understand it.
When someone is being arch, they are being deliberately, self-consciously playful in a knowing, clever, and slightly superior way — often with a teasing or ironic edge.

An arch is a curved structure that spans — that is, bridges over — an opening or a gap. Picture a rainbow, or the letter U turned upside down. That graceful, rising-and-falling curve is the defining image of an arch.
Archaeology is the scientific study of human history and prehistory through the discovery, careful digging, and analysis of physical objects and remains that people left behind.
Something archaic is so old that it no longer fits naturally into modern life.

An archaism is a word, phrase, or expression that was once a normal part of everyday language but is no longer used in ordinary modern speech or writing. It belongs to an older time in a language's history.
An archenemy is not just any enemy — it is someone's chief, most important, and most dangerous enemy.
The word archeological simply means "relating to, or having to do with, archeology."
An archaeologist is a scientist who studies human history and human behavior by finding, digging up, and carefully examining objects and structures that people left behind in the past.
Archaeology is the scientific study of past human life and culture through the discovery, careful recovery, and analysis of the physical things people left behind.

"Archetypal" describes something that is the perfect original model — or the most defining, essential example — of its kind. Something so purely and completely representative of a category that it practically is the definition of that category.

An archetype is the original model or master pattern from which all similar things are shaped, measured, or derived. It's the definitive "first version" — the source template that everything else is based on.
An archipelago is a group of islands that are clustered together in a body of water, usually an ocean or a sea.
A trained professional who plans and designs buildings. More broadly, the person who designs or creates a plan, system, or idea, as in "the architect of the peace deal."
The adjective architectural simply means "of, relating to, or having to do with architecture."

Architecture is the art and science of designing and constructing buildings and other physical structures. Notice that it combines two things: art (creativity, aesthetics, beauty) and science (technical knowledge, engineering, safety).

"Archival" is an adjective. It always connects back to one central idea: archives — collections or places (physical or digital) where valuable records, documents, photographs, films, letters, maps, or data are carefully stored and preserved for the long term.
An archive is a collection of records, documents, or other materials that are preserved because they have lasting value — and also the place where those materials are stored and managed.

To archive something means to deliberately preserve it — to take it out of everyday, active use and store it safely in an organized way, so it can be found and referred back to in the future, even though it isn't immediately needed right now.

Archness is the quality of being deliberately playful, teasing, or mischievous in a knowing and self-aware way — with a subtle sense that the person doing it believes they are being very clever about it.
"Arctic" is an adjective that has two closely related meanings — a literal one and a figurative one. Both meanings revolve around one central idea: extreme, severe coldness and harshness.
"Ardent" describes a feeling — or a person's quality of feeling — that is intensely strong, deeply passionate, and almost burning in its force.

"Ardently" is an adverb — a word that describes how an action is done. Its meaning is: with deep, sincere, burning passion and intensity. When someone does something ardently, they do it with their whole heart fully engaged.
Ardor means a strong, burning intensity of feeling — most often passion, enthusiasm, or devotion toward someone or something.
Arduous means extremely difficult, demanding, and exhausting — requiring a great deal of effort, energy, and endurance to complete.

An argosy is a large, grand merchant ship — one that carries a rich, valuable cargo across the sea. Think of it as a great sailing vessel loaded with treasure, goods, or precious wares, gliding majestically across the ocean. It isn't just any ship.

Argot is a special, private vocabulary — a set of words, phrases, and expressions — used by a specific group of people, particularly to communicate among themselves in a way that outsiders cannot easily understand.
To disagree with someone and express it, often angrily. It can also mean to give reasons in support of or against a position, calmly and logically.
A heated disagreement between people. It can also mean a set of reasons given to support or oppose an idea.

When we say a person is argumentative, we mean they have a strong, deeply ingrained tendency to argue, disagree, or pick fights — often even when there is no real reason to. It's not about one single argument they had.
An aria is a song for a single voice, accompanied by instruments, found in large-scale musical works like operas, oratorios, and cantatas.
Arid means extremely and persistently dry — so dry that very little, if anything, can grow or survive.

Arise means to come into existence or to appear — specifically when something that wasn't there before suddenly becomes present, noticeable, or relevant. Think of it like something surfacing or emerging from nowhere.
Aristocracy means rule by a privileged, elite group — a small class of people who hold power, wealth, and high social status, usually because of the family they were born into.
Belonging to or typical of the aristocracy, the highest social class, made up of noble families who inherited their wealth, land, and titles.
At its most essential, arithmetic is the branch of mathematics that deals with numbers and the four basic operations you can perform on them: addition, subtraction, multiplication, and division.

Arm-twisting means using pressure, force, or threats — not physical, but social or emotional — to make someone do something they don't really want to do. It is the act of pushing or pressuring a person until they give in, even against their own wishes.
An armada is a large, powerful fleet of warships sailing together as one organized force.
Armament means weapons and military equipment, especially those belonging to a country, an army, or a military vehicle like a warship or fighter jet.

An armchair critic is a person who freely judges, criticizes, or offers opinions about something — but has no real experience, hands-on involvement, or deep knowledge of the thing they are criticizing.
"Armed to the teeth" means to be extremely well-equipped — carrying as many weapons as possible, or more broadly, being fully and thoroughly prepared with everything you could possibly need.
An armistice is a formal, mutual agreement between two or more warring sides to completely stop all fighting, usually while a more permanent solution — like a peace treaty — is being worked out.
An armoire is a large, tall, freestanding wooden cabinet used primarily for storing clothes, but also for other household items like linens, bedsheets, towels, or even electronics like a TV.

Armor is a protective covering — something worn on the body, or placed on an object, to shield it from physical harm. Its purpose is simple: to stop or reduce damage from attacks, blows, or other threats.
An arms race is when two or more rivals keep trying to out-build each other in weapons or power, each side responding to the other's growth, in a cycle that has no natural stopping point.
An aroma is a distinctive, pleasant smell — one that is rich, noticeable, and often inviting. It is the kind of smell that fills a space and makes you stop to notice it.

When something is described as aromatic, it has a strong, distinctive, and typically pleasant smell — the kind that fills a room, greets you immediately, and is hard to ignore. The word is not used for faint or forgettable smells.
"Around the clock" means continuously, for 24 hours a day, without any break or stop.

When people say something is "around the corner," they mean it is going to happen very soon. It is not here yet, but it is so close that it feels almost visible — just like something physically sitting around the bend of a road.
Arouse means to bring something that was inactive, hidden, or dormant into an active state — to "wake it up" and make it present and felt.

An arpeggio is what happens when, instead of playing all the notes of a chord at the same time, you play them one at a time, in quick flowing succession — either going upward (from the lowest note to the highest) or downward (from highest to lowest).

Arrabbiata simply means angry or furious. It describes a person (or animal) who is in a real, felt state of anger — not mild, quiet irritation, but genuine, visible anger. Think of a person with a raised voice, a clenched jaw, or a flushed face.

To arraign someone means to formally bring them before a court of law and officially charge them with a crime — and then ask them, right there in front of the judge, whether they are guilty or not guilty.
One of the first steps in a criminal case, when the accused is brought before a judge, formally told the charges, and asked to plead guilty or not guilty.

Arrant means complete, total, and absolute — but here's the critical catch: it is only ever used with bad or negative things. It's a word that takes something already negative and cranks it up to the maximum possible degree.

Array means a collection of things arranged in an organized, ordered way — and often an impressive one. It's not just a random pile or a simple list. An array has a sense of purposeful arrangement and usually notable size or variety.

To array something means to arrange it in a neat, orderly, and often visually impressive way — deliberately, with purpose. Think of it as arranging things so they can be clearly seen, properly organized, or used effectively.

Arrears (always used in plural form) refers to money that was supposed to be paid by a certain time, but wasn't. It is the unpaid amount that has piled up because someone fell behind on their financial obligations.
Arrest means to stop something completely and hold it in place. This single core idea runs through every use of the word — whether it's a person, a process, or even attention.

If something is arresting, it is so powerfully striking that it stops you — it seizes your attention the moment you encounter it and holds it there. You don't look away easily. You don't walk past it casually.
Lacking a regular, predictable rhythm — unsteady and irregular in timing, as with an arrhythmic heartbeat.
When you travel somewhere and you get there, you arrive at that place.

An arriviste is a person who claws their way to the top of society or their profession with naked, shameless ambition — often by being fake, manipulative, or ruthless — and who others look down on for it, even when they succeed.

Arrogance is the attitude of a person who believes they are far more important, more capable, or more valuable than they actually are — and who shows this belief in a way that is offensive or dismissive to others.

When someone is arrogant, they believe they are better, more important, or more capable than other people — and they show this belief through how they behave. It's not just a private feeling; it comes out in the way they treat others.
To arrogate means to claim or take a right, power, or privilege for yourself — when you have absolutely no legitimate basis to do so.
An arroyo is a dry, channel-like ditch or gully carved into the ground by water — but here's the key: it holds little or no water most of the time. It only fills up temporarily when heavy rain hits.
Arsenal means a large stock of weapons and military equipment — either the place where they are stored or made, or the collection of weapons itself.

Arson is the crime of deliberately setting fire to property — such as a building, vehicle, forest, or any other structure — with the intent to destroy or damage it. The single most important word in understanding arson is deliberately.

An artery is a tube-like blood vessel — a hollow channel inside your body — that carries blood away from the heart and delivers it to the rest of the body. That single direction (away from the heart) is the defining feature of every artery.
Artesian describes underground water that is naturally trapped under pressure, causing it to rise on its own — sometimes all the way to the surface — when a well is drilled or a crack opens.

"Artful" describes someone or something that is cleverly cunning — achieving goals through skill, smartness, and often a touch of slyness rather than through straightforward, honest means. Think of it as being impressively clever in a slightly sneaky way.
Arthritis is a medical condition in which one or more joints in the body become inflamed, causing pain, swelling, stiffness, and reduced ability to move.
An arthropod is a type of animal. Specifically, it belongs to the largest group of animals on Earth — a group so big that it contains more than 80% of all known animal species.

When you describe someone as articulate, you mean they are very good at expressing their thoughts, ideas, and feelings clearly and effectively in words — whether they are speaking or writing. That is the heart of it.
To articulate something means to express an idea, thought, or feeling in clear, precise, well-chosen words — in a way that another person can genuinely understand.

Articulation is about making something clear, distinct, and well-connected — whether that "something" is a thought, a sound, a body part, or a mechanical structure. Think of it as the opposite of vagueness, blur, or disconnection.
An artifact is something that exists because of human involvement. Either humans deliberately made it, or it unexpectedly appeared as a side effect of something humans did.
Artifice means a clever trick or crafty scheme used to deceive or manipulate — but it can also mean the deliberate, calculated skill and technique behind something constructed, like a work of art.
"Artificial" describes something that was made or produced by human beings, rather than coming into existence on its own through nature.
Artillery refers to large, heavy, powerful weapons — such as cannons, howitzers, and rocket launchers — that fire explosive projectiles (shells or rockets) over long distances.
An artisan is a person who is highly skilled at making things by hand.
Artisanal describes something made by a skilled person using their hands, craft knowledge, and careful attention — rather than being churned out by machines in a factory.
An artist is a person who creates works of art — things made to express ideas, feelings, beauty, or meaning, rather than simply to serve a practical purpose.
Artistic means relating to, involving, or characteristic of art or the qualities associated with art — such as creativity, beauty, imagination, and skilled expression.

Artistry means the exceptional skill, creativity, and elegance that a person brings to something they do — so much so that the result feels not just correct or competent, but truly beautiful, impressive, and deeply human.

When someone is artless, they are completely genuine — they don't perform, pretend, calculate, or manipulate. They simply are what they are, and they say what they feel, openly, without any attempt to create an impression or deceive anyone.

When you call someone or something arty, you are saying that they are very strongly associated with art, creative culture, and an unconventional, bohemian way of life — but with a hint that this interest is a bit exaggerated, showy, or pretentious.
Arugula is a type of leafy green plant that people grow and eat as a vegetable. It belongs to the same plant family as cabbage, broccoli, and mustard.
"As it stands" means "in its current state" or "the way things are right now."

"As luck would have it" is an idiom used to describe something that happened purely by chance — not because of anyone's planning, skill, or effort, but simply because fate or coincidence decided it that way.
This idiom is used to say that a person or thing represents the highest possible degree of a particular quality. In simple terms, it means "extremely" or "as much as possible."

"As the crow flies" means the shortest straight-line distance between two points, measured directly through the air, ignoring all roads, rivers, mountains, buildings, or any other obstacle that stands in the way.
To ascend means to move upward — to go from a lower position to a higher one. Think of it as the opposite of "descend" (go down).
Ascendancy means the state of having dominant power, control, or influence over others.
"Ascendant" describes something — a person, a group, an idea, a technology, a movement — that is rising in power, influence, or importance. Think of the verb "ascend," which means to climb upward.

"Ascending" means going upward, rising, or increasing — moving from a lower point, level, or value toward a higher one. The single most important idea locked inside this word is: starting low, moving high.
Ascension means the act or process of going upward — rising from a lower place, level, or state to a higher one.
Ascent means the act of going upward — a movement, journey, or progress from a lower point to a higher one. Think of it as the story of rising.

To ascertain something means to find out a fact with certainty through deliberate effort. When you ascertain something, you don't stumble upon it by accident — you actively investigate, check, or inquire until you can say with confidence that you know it.
Something or someone ascetic deliberately avoids pleasure, comfort, and luxury — choosing a life of strict self-denial, usually for a spiritual, moral, or philosophical purpose.

An ascetic is a person who deliberately chooses to live a life of extreme simplicity and self-denial — giving up physical pleasures, comforts, and desires on purpose, usually to achieve a deeper spiritual or religious goal.

Asceticism is the deliberate, voluntary practice of denying yourself physical pleasures, comforts, and worldly indulgences as a way of achieving a higher goal — most often spiritual growth, self-mastery, moral purity, or closeness to the divine.
An ascot is a type of neckwear — a wide, flat, soft piece of cloth worn around the neck, usually tucked inside the collar of a shirt or draped loosely over it.

When you ascribe something to someone or something, you are making a connection between two things — pointing at a source, a cause, or a creator and saying: "This came from there" or "That happened because of this."
When something is aseptic, it means it is completely free from harmful microorganisms — bacteria, viruses, fungi, and other microscopic living things that can cause infection or contamination.
Ashamed means feeling a painful inner sense of shame — a heavy, negative feeling about yourself because of something you did, said, thought, or are.
Very pale and grey, like ash, usually from shock, fear, or illness — as in "her face went ashen."
Ashore means on land or onto land — but only when that land is being contrasted with water or a vessel (a ship, boat, etc.).
When you say something aside, you are stepping away — even if just for a moment — from the main conversation, story, or topic, to say something that is separate from it.
Asinine means extremely stupid or foolish — not in a mild or forgivable way, but in a way that is so obviously dumb that it shocks or frustrates the people witnessing it.
"Ask after" is a phrasal verb. It means to inquire about someone's well-being, health, or current situation — typically by asking a third person on their behalf.
"Ask around" means to ask several different people the same question — usually because you are looking for information, a recommendation, or help, and you are not sure who has the right answer.

When you look at someone or something askance, you are looking at them with suspicion, distrust, or disapproval. You are not accepting them straightforwardly. Instead, you are eyeing them with doubt, caution, or quiet judgment.
In a way that is not straight, not level, or not properly aligned — tilted or turned to one side.
One particular part, feature, or side of something larger, such as a situation, problem, or plan.
An aspen is a type of tree. More specifically, it is a medium-to-large deciduous tree (meaning it sheds its leaves every autumn) that belongs to the poplar family.
Harshness or sharpness in someone's tone or manner. It can also mean roughness of a surface, or the severity of difficult conditions.
An aspersion is a damaging or unfair remark about someone — specifically one that attacks their character, honesty, or reputation.

Asphalt is a thick, dark, sticky substance used primarily to build and pave roads, driveways, parking lots, and similar surfaces. It is one of the most widely used construction materials in the world.

To asphyxiate means to cause a living being to lose consciousness or die because their body is being deprived of oxygen — or more precisely, because the body's normal exchange of oxygen and carbon dioxide has been severely disrupted or stopped.

Asphyxiation is the condition that occurs when the body is deprived of enough oxygen to survive. The word refers both to the process of being cut off from oxygen and to the state that results from it.
An aspirant is a person who strongly wants to achieve something big — a high goal, an important position, a title, or a prestigious status — and is actively working toward it.
A strong hope, goal, or ambition to achieve something meaningful.

"Aspirational" means connected to a strong desire to achieve something better — a better life, a higher status, greater success, or a goal that feels just beyond your current reach but worth striving for.
To aspire means to strongly want to achieve something great, important, or meaningful — and to be genuinely motivated to work toward it.
When you call someone aspiring, you mean they deeply want to become something — usually a specific profession or a prestigious role — and they haven't become it yet, but they are reaching for it.
Assail means to attack something or someone — but not just any ordinary attack. The word carries a strong sense of force, intensity, and being overwhelmed.
Something is assailable when it has weaknesses or flaws that allow it to be attacked, challenged, or questioned — and those attacks have a reasonable chance of succeeding.
An assailant is a person who physically attacks someone else. If someone punches, stabs, shoots, or in any way violently attacks another person, that attacker is called the assailant.

An assassin is a person who deliberately and secretly kills a specific, carefully chosen target — almost always someone who is important, powerful, or well-known, such as a political leader, a president, a king, a general, or a public figure.
To assassinate someone means to deliberately and intentionally kill a person who is important, famous, or powerful — usually for political, religious, or ideological reasons.
An assay is a careful, scientific test performed on a substance to find out what it contains, how much of something is in it, or how potent (strong or active) it is.
To test a substance, such as a metal or drug, to find out what it contains and how pure it is. In literary use, it means to attempt something.

Assemblage means a collection of things or people that have been brought together in one place or for one purpose. Think of it as the result of gathering — the finished "pile" or "group" that exists after things have been assembled.
"Assemble" means to bring separate things or people together into one place, or to put separate parts together to make one complete whole.

The most common meaning of assembly is a group of people who have come together in one place for a shared reason. The gathering is usually deliberate — people are there for a specific event or purpose — and it's temporary.
An assembly line is a way of making a product where the work is broken into small, simple steps, and each step is done by a different person (or machine) in a fixed sequence.
Assent means agreement — specifically, the act of agreeing to, accepting, or approving something that has been proposed, stated, or put forward, usually by someone else.
To assent means to agree with something, or to say "yes" to something — but not in a casual, offhand way.
To assert something means to state it firmly and confidently, as though you are certain it is true — whether or not you offer any proof.

An assertion is a confident, direct statement that someone makes, declaring something to be true. When you make an assertion, you are not asking a question, not expressing doubt, and not making a suggestion — you are declaring something as a definite fact.
When you describe someone as assertive, you mean they confidently and directly express their thoughts, feelings, needs, and opinions — while still being respectful toward others.

Assertiveness is the quality of being able to express your thoughts, feelings, needs, and opinions confidently, clearly, and directly — while at the same time respecting the rights and feelings of the other person. Both parts of that sentence matter equally.
An asservation is a serious, emphatic, and sincere declaration that something is true — made with strong personal conviction.
To assess something means to carefully look at it, study it, and form a judgment about it — its condition, quality, value, importance, size, or extent.

An assessment is a careful, considered judgment about something — what it is, what it's worth, how good it is, how serious it is, or what condition it's in. It is both the process of examining something closely and the conclusion you reach after doing so.
An assessor is a person who carefully examines something — a property, a situation, a person's performance, or a claim — and makes an official judgment or determination about it.
An asset is anything valuable that you own or control — something that works in your favor, either by holding worth, generating money, or making your situation better.

To asseverate means to state or declare something with great earnestness, sincerity, and emphasis — essentially, to insist firmly that something is true, and to do so with your full personal conviction behind it.
An asseveration is a serious, sincere, and emphatic declaration that something is true — made with great conviction, but without a formal oath.
Assiduity means the quality of giving constant, careful, and dedicated effort to something over a long period of time.
Someone who is assiduous works extremely hard, consistently, and with close, careful attention — without slacking off, cutting corners, or giving up partway through.
To do something assiduously means to do it with careful, steady, and persistent effort over time — giving it your full attention and not slacking off, even when it gets tedious or difficult.

Assign means to officially and deliberately direct something — a task, a role, a resource, or a meaning — toward a specific person, place, or purpose. It always implies a sense of authority, intention, and specificity.
The word assignment has several meanings, but they are all connected by one central idea: something that is given, directed, or transferred to a specific person or place, with a clear purpose.
Assimilate means to take something in and make it a true, working part of something else — or to be absorbed into something larger until you truly become part of it.
Assimilation means the process of absorbing something new into something that already exists — and making it blend in so completely that it becomes a natural part of the whole.
To assist means to help someone do something. But there is a key nuance that separates it from a simple, plain "help": when you assist someone, you are playing a supporting role, not the leading one.
Assistance means help — any action, effort, resource, or support given to someone so that a task becomes easier, a problem gets solved, or a need gets met.

An assistant is a person (or sometimes a tool or system) whose role is to help someone else do their work more effectively. The assistant is not the main person in charge — they are the supporting person.
An associate is a person who is connected to you — or to an organization — through shared work, a shared purpose, or a shared membership.

To associate means to connect two or more things together — either in your mind or in the real world. When you associate A with B, you are saying that A and B belong together in some way, that they are linked, related, or connected.

Association is about connection — a link between people, things, or ideas. Every meaning of this word, no matter how different the context, comes back to that one idea: something is connected to something else.

Assonance is the repetition of the same or similar vowel sounds in words that are close to each other in a sentence, line, or passage — while the consonant sounds around those vowels can be completely different.
When something is described as assorted, it means it consists of several different types or kinds, all brought together as one collection or group.
An assortment is a group or collection of things that belong to the same general category but are different from one another in type, kind, size, color, flavor, or some other quality.

To assuage something is to make a painful, uncomfortable, or intense feeling less severe. Think of it like turning down a dial — the feeling doesn't always disappear entirely, but its grip loosens and it becomes more bearable.
To believe something is true without proof. It can also mean to take on a role or responsibility, or to adopt a particular appearance or manner.
An assumption is something you believe to be true without proof.

Assurance is about removing doubt. Whether it comes from another person or from within yourself, assurance is what makes you feel certain, calm, and free from worry. Think of it as the opposite of uncertainty. It fills the gap where doubt used to be.
To assure someone means to tell them something clearly and confidently so that they feel certain — and no longer worried or doubtful. You are giving them your word.

"Assuredly" means certainly, without any doubt, or in a confident manner. When someone uses this word, they are making a firm, confident statement — one that leaves no room for uncertainty or question.

When something is assuring, it gives you a sense of confidence, safety, or certainty. It takes away your doubt, worry, or fear — even if just a little — and makes you feel that things are okay, or that something is true and reliable.
An asteroid is a natural, solid object — made of rock, metal, or a mixture of both — that orbits the Sun, just like Earth does, but is far too small to be called a planet.
A long-term disease of the airways in which they become inflamed, narrowed, and partly blocked, making it difficult to breathe.
Astigmatism is a common eye condition in which vision is blurred or distorted because the eye's surface or internal lens is not shaped perfectly, causing light to focus incorrectly inside the eye.

Astir is an adjective that describes a state of movement, activity, or wakeful energy. When something or someone is astir, they are no longer still, quiet, or asleep — they are up, moving, and active.
To astonish someone means to fill them with such a great and sudden sense of wonder and disbelief that they can barely process what they are seeing, hearing, or experiencing.

Astonished describes a feeling of very strong, sudden surprise — the kind of surprise that is so powerful it briefly overwhelms you, sometimes leaving you speechless, wide-eyed, or frozen for a moment.

Astonishing describes something that causes a very strong feeling of surprise and wonder — so much so that it's hard to believe or fully take in. When something is astonishing, it goes far beyond what you expected. It stops you in your tracks.
When something surprises you so strongly that it almost shocks you — like it's hard to believe it's even real — that's when you use astonishingly.
To astound someone means to surprise them so powerfully and so deeply that they can barely process what just happened. It is not a mild or ordinary kind of surprise.

Astral means of or relating to the stars. Think of the night sky — those distant, glowing points of light. Anything described as "astral" has a connection to that world: the stars, the heavens, or the vast space above us.
Away from the correct path or direction. To go astray means to get lost or wander off — or, figuratively, to do something wrong.
With one leg on each side of something, as in sitting astride a horse or bicycle.
Causing skin or body tissue to tighten and shrink, as in "an astringent lotion." Of taste, sharp and dry. Of remarks, harsh and severe, as in "astringent criticism."
An astronomer is a scientist who studies everything that exists beyond Earth's atmosphere — stars, planets, moons, galaxies, black holes, comets, and the universe itself.

The word astronomical is built on the word astronomy — the science of studying outer space: stars, planets, galaxies, black holes, and the universe as a whole. So "astronomical" simply means of or relating to astronomy.
Astronomy is the scientific study of everything that exists beyond Earth's atmosphere — the entire universe and all the objects within it.

Astrophysics is a branch of science that uses the laws of physics and chemistry to understand how everything in the universe — stars, planets, galaxies, black holes, and even the universe itself — actually works.
If someone is astute, it means they are very good at quickly and accurately understanding situations, people, and information — and they know how to use that understanding wisely to their advantage.

Astutely means doing something in a way that shows sharp, clever, and perceptive thinking — especially the kind of thinking that helps you quickly understand a situation, spot things others miss, and use that understanding wisely and practically.
Asunder means "into separate parts" or "apart from each other," describing something that has been split, divided, or broken completely — often with force or great intensity.
Protection given by a country to someone who has fled danger or persecution in their own country. The word was also once used for a hospital for people with mental illness.

An asylum seeker is a person who has fled their home country because they fear serious harm — such as persecution, violence, or torture — and has arrived in another country asking for protection and the legal right to stay safely.
Asymmetric describes something where the two sides, parts, or parties involved are not equal, not balanced, and do not mirror each other.
Something is asymmetrical when its two sides, halves, or parts do not match or mirror each other.

When we say someone is "at a crossroads," we mean: They are at a critical point in their life, career, or situation where they must make an important decision that will significantly shape their future.

If you are "at a loose end," it means you have nothing particular to do at a given moment. You feel idle, bored, or a little restless because you have no task, plan, or purpose to occupy yourself with.
The idiom "at a premium" is used in two closely related ways: 1. Something is scarce (hard to find) and therefore highly valued.
Continuously, without a break — as in "she worked for ten hours at a stretch." It can also mean only with difficulty or if you are generous in your judgement.
To keep someone or something at arm's length means to deliberately maintain a certain distance from them, to avoid becoming too close or involved.
"At best" means in the most favorable situation possible or even if everything goes as well as it can.

"At death's door" means to be so dangerously ill or critically injured that death feels very close — almost certain. When someone is described as being "at death's door," they are in an extreme, life-threatening condition where survival is not guaranteed.
To take something "at face value" means to accept it exactly as it appears, without questioning it, doubting it, or looking for a deeper or hidden meaning.
Free and not yet caught, as in "the escaped prisoner is still at large." It can also mean as a whole, in general, as in "society at large."
In great detail or for a long time, as in "she explained her decision at length." It can also mean eventually, after a long time.
To be at loggerheads with someone means to be in a strong, stubborn disagreement with them — a situation where two people or groups simply cannot agree, and neither side is willing to give in.

To be at odds with someone or something means to be in disagreement, conflict, or contradiction with them or it. When two things or people are "at odds," they do not match, agree, or go well together. There is a clash between them.
"At one fell swoop" means doing something all at once, in a single decisive action, often suddenly and with great force or impact.
When someone says "at your own risk," they mean: "You are free to do this, but if anything goes wrong, it is entirely your problem. No one else will be responsible for what happens to you."

When someone is at their wits' end, they are so frustrated, confused, or overwhelmed by a problem that they have completely run out of ideas on how to deal with it. They have tried everything they can think of, and nothing has worked.

"At sixes and sevens" means being in a state of confusion, disorder, or disarray. It can describe either a situation that is messy and disorganized, or people who are in disagreement or cannot get along.
At the drop of a hat
"At the drop of a hat" means immediately, without any hesitation, and without needing any special reason or advance notice.
"At the eleventh hour" means at the very last moment — so late that you almost ran out of time, but something still happened just before it was too late.
To achieve or gain something while something or someone else suffers or is sacrificed, as in "speed at the expense of quality."
In the most leading, advanced, or important position in a field, movement, or activity.
In charge of something; leading and controlling an organization or group, like a person steering a ship.
When you are at the mercy of someone or something, it means you are completely under their power or control, and you cannot do anything to protect yourself or change your situation.
"At will" means "whenever you want, however you want, without needing permission or giving a reason."
In its most precise definition: atavism is the reappearance, in an individual organism, of a characteristic that belonged to a distant ancestor but had been absent in all the generations in between.

Atavistic describes something that is a throwback to an ancient, primitive past — a trait, behavior, instinct, or tendency that seems to have skipped generations and suddenly reappeared from a far earlier time in our evolutionary or ancestral history.

An atelier is a private workshop or studio where a skilled artist, craftsperson, or designer does their work. Think of it as a dedicated creative space — but one that carries a specific sense of mastery, care, and prestige.
Atheism is the absence of belief in the existence of God or gods.
An atheist is a person who does not believe that any god or gods exist.
Atheistic is an adjective that means relating to, characterized by, or based on atheism — the view that God or gods do not exist.
An athlete is a person who participates in sports, physical games, or bodily exercises — especially one who does so with skill, training, and serious dedication.

Athletic describes someone or something that shows the qualities of a person who is physically trained, strong, fit, and capable — someone whose body is built and conditioned for physical activity and sport.
"Athwart" fundamentally means "across" — specifically, crossing something from one side to the other, often at a right angle, and often in a way that blocks or cuts against the main direction.
A book of maps. In Greek mythology, Atlas was a giant forced to hold up the sky on his shoulders.
Creating a strong mood or feeling, often of mystery or beauty, as in "atmospheric music." It also means relating to the air surrounding a planet.

An atoll is a ring-shaped island — or a chain of small islands arranged in a ring — made entirely of coral, sitting in a tropical ocean, with a calm, shallow body of water called a lagoon trapped inside it.
A powerful electron microscope that can show the arrangement of individual atoms in a material — far beyond what any light microscope can see.
To atomize something means to break it into the tiniest possible pieces — so tiny that the result is a mist, a fine spray, a powder, or individual separate fragments.
Describes music that has no tonal centre, or "home note" — so it never settles into a familiar key and does not resolve in the way most music does.

To atone means to actively do something to make up for a wrong you have committed. It's the act of trying to repair the moral, emotional, or spiritual damage caused by your mistake or bad action — not just by feeling sorry, but by doing something about it.
Atonement means the act of doing something to make up for a serious wrong you have committed.
Atop means on the very top of something. When one thing is atop another, it is resting on, sitting on, or placed on the highest surface or highest point of that other thing.

Atrabilious describes someone who is gloomy and bad-tempered at the same time. Think of a person who is not just sad, and not just irritable — but both, wrapped together into one sour, brooding disposition.
A large, open central space in a building, often with a glass roof. In the heart, an atrium is one of the two upper chambers that receive blood.
Atrocious means shockingly and extremely bad — so bad that it causes a strong reaction of horror, disgust, or outrage in any decent person who witnesses it.

An atrocity is an act of shocking, extreme cruelty — something so brutal, violent, and morally horrifying that it deeply disturbs anyone who hears about it. It is not just "something bad." It is something so severely wrong that it stuns the human conscience.

Atrophied describes something that has wasted away, shrunk, or become significantly weaker — not because it was always weak, but because it was once normal or strong and then deteriorated over time due to lack of use, nourishment, or stimulation.
Atrophy means the wasting away, shrinking, or weakening of something — a slow, gradual decline that happens when something is not being used, nourished, or stimulated the way it needs to be.

To atrophy means to gradually waste away, shrink, or weaken — to slowly become less than what something once was. It describes a process of decline that happens quietly, over time, when something stops being used, fed, or exercised enough.

Attached means joined to something or someone — physically, emotionally, or officially. The exact nature of that "joining" depends on the context, and the word carries several distinct but related meanings.
The theory that the emotional bond between a young child and their caregiver shapes how that person relates to others, handles emotions, and feels safe for the rest of their life.

An attaché is a specialist official who is attached — that is, assigned and connected — to a diplomatic mission, such as an embassy or consulate, in a foreign country. Think of an embassy as a team sent by one country to live and work inside another country.

An attack is a sudden, aggressive, or forceful action directed at a target — with the aim of harming, defeating, damaging, or overcoming it. The target can be a person, a place, an idea, a body, or even a problem.
To attain something means to successfully reach or achieve something — especially after putting in effort, time, or going through a process to get there.

"Attainment" has two closely connected meanings that work together: The first is the act or process of successfully reaching something — a goal, a level, a standard — especially after putting in real effort over time.

An attempt is an act of trying to do something. When someone makes an attempt, they put in effort toward a goal — but the key thing is: the result is not certain. They might succeed, or they might fail.
When you attempt something, you try to do it — but with a very important detail baked in: you are not sure you will succeed. There is a real possibility of failure, and you know it.
"Attend" is a rich word with several meanings, but one thread ties them all together: being present — with your body, your attention, or your care.

Attendance means the fact of being present somewhere. When you physically go to a place — a school, a meeting, a concert, a church service — the act of being there is called your attendance. Think of it as the opposite of absence.
An attendant is a person who is present at a place as part of their job — specifically to help, serve, assist, or take care of people or things there.

Attention is the act of directing your mind toward something. Think of your mind like a flashlight in a dark room. Whatever that flashlight is shining on — that thing is receiving your attention. Everything else in the room is in the dark, ignored.
If someone is attentive, it means they are paying careful, focused, and active attention — either to what is happening around them, to what someone is saying, or to what another person needs.

Attentively means doing something with full, focused, and engaged attention — without letting your mind wander, without getting distracted, and with genuine care for what is happening in front of you.

To attenuate something means to make it weaker, thinner, or less intense — to gradually reduce its strength, force, or effect. When something attenuates, it doesn't disappear completely; it simply becomes a lesser, diminished version of what it was.

Attenuated describes something that has been reduced in strength, force, thickness, or intensity — something that still exists in its original form, but in a much weaker, thinner, or diluted state compared to what it once was or what it could fully be.
Attenuation means the gradual weakening or reduction of something as it travels, spreads, or passes through something else.
To attest means to declare or confirm that something is true, real, or genuine — either by being a witness to it, or by serving as evidence of it yourself.
Attire means clothing, particularly clothing that is worn for a specific purpose, occasion, or setting.
To attire someone means to dress them — or yourself — in clothing that is special, formal, fine, or carefully chosen for a particular occasion.
An attitude is a settled, ongoing mindset — a lens through which you see and respond to something.

The word attorney means a person who is officially authorized to act on behalf of someone else. Think of it this way: when you cannot — or choose not to — handle something yourself, you appoint someone to step into your shoes and act for you.

"Attraction" describes a pull — the force, feeling, or quality that draws someone or something toward another. Think of a magnet. The invisible force pulling a piece of metal toward the magnet is attraction.

Attributable means able to be traced back to a source, cause, or origin. When something is described as attributable to something else, it means that "something else" is the explanation — the reason it exists, happened, or turned out the way it did.
An attribute is a quality, feature, or characteristic that belongs to — and helps describe — a person, thing, or concept.

To attribute something to someone (or something) means to point to a source — to say or believe that a particular person, thing, or reason is where something came from, who made it, or why it happened.
Attribution means the act of identifying the source, cause, or creator of something — essentially saying "this came from here" or "this happened because of that."
Attrition means the slow, gradual process of wearing something down — reducing its strength, size, or numbers — through continuous pressure, friction, or repeated loss over time.
To attune something or someone means to bring them into a state of harmony, sensitivity, or alignment with something else.

When you are attuned to something or someone, you are so deeply and sensitively aware of it that you can instantly notice its smallest signals, changes, needs, or patterns — and you respond to them naturally and correctly.
Not matching the usual, expected pattern for its kind; out of the ordinary.
Au courant means being fully up to date and well-informed about the latest developments in something.
Au fait means being well-informed and up-to-date about something, to the point where you can handle, discuss, or engage with it competently.

An au pair is a young person from a foreign country who comes to live with a family in another country, helps take care of the children and does some light household work, and in return receives a free place to stay, meals, and a small amount of spending money.
Auburn is an adjective that describes a specific shade of color — a rich, warm reddish-brown. It is not purely red, and it is not purely brown.

An auction is a method of selling something where the price is not fixed in advance. Instead, interested buyers compete against each other by placing bids — each one offering to pay a certain amount of money for the item.
To auction off something means to sell it publicly to the person who offers the highest price.

Audacious describes a person, action, plan, or idea that is strikingly bold, daring, and willing to go far beyond what is normal, expected, or socially acceptable — in a way that surprises, shocks, or impresses people.

Audacity means a bold, daring willingness to do something that most people would hesitate to do — because it's risky, difficult, shocking, or socially out of line. Think of it as a kind of fearless, over-the-top boldness that makes people stop and stare.
Audible means able to be heard. If a sound is audible, it simply means that your ears can detect it — it is real, present, and loud or clear enough to register as sound.
Audience means a group of people who receive something — a performance, a speech, a piece of writing, or any form of communication. The "something" could be delivered live, broadcast, or published.

An audiophile is a person who is deeply passionate about high-quality sound reproduction — meaning they care intensely about how music and audio actually sounds when it is played back through speakers, headphones, or other equipment.

An audit is a careful, official, and independent examination of something — usually financial records, accounts, processes, or systems — conducted to check whether everything is accurate, honest, and in order.
To audit something means to carefully and officially examine it to check whether it is accurate, honest, and following the rules.

An audition is a live tryout — a short performance or demonstration that someone gives in front of a person (or a group of people) who are evaluating whether that person is the right fit for a role, a position, or an opportunity in a performance-based field.
An auditor is a person who carefully and officially examines records — especially financial records — to check whether they are accurate, honest, and following the correct rules and laws.
An auditorium is a large, purpose-built room or hall designed to hold an audience — a group of people who have come to watch, listen to, or attend something happening on or near a stage.

Auditory is an adjective that means relating to the sense of hearing, or anything connected to the process of hearing sound. Whenever you see this word, it is pointing to something that has to do with ears, sound, or the act of listening.

An auger is a tool designed to bore holes into a material — usually wood, soil, or ice — by rotating and simultaneously pulling out the loosened debris as it goes deeper. Think of it as a drilling tool with a built-in cleanup mechanism.
To augment something means to make it larger, stronger, or more complete — by adding to what already exists.
Augmentation means the act or process of making something larger, greater, stronger, or more complete — by adding to it.
Made greater, larger, or more powerful by having something added to it.
Augmented Reality is technology that adds digital things — images, text, sounds, or 3D objects — on top of what you see in the real world, in real time.
To augur means to be a sign of something that is likely to happen in the future. When something augurs a certain outcome, it acts as an early signal or indicator pointing toward that future.
Relating to omens, signs, or the prediction of future events — especially when those signs are interpreted by someone with special authority to do so.
An augury is a sign or omen that is believed to hint at what will happen in the future.
Commanding deep respect and admiration because of an impressive, almost overwhelming sense of dignity, importance, or grandeur.

An aura is an invisible quality, feeling, or energy that seems to radiate outward from someone or something — surrounding them like an invisible cloud. You don't touch it. You sense it, feel it, or perceive it.
Aura farming means doing things with deliberate coolness, confidence, or mystique — often to elevate your social status or gain attention — while making it all look completely effortless.

Aural simply means relating to the ear or the sense of hearing. If something is "aural," it involves sound being received and processed through your ears. That's the whole foundation of the word — ear, hearing, listening.
Aureole means a ring, glow, or radiance of light that surrounds something — like a glowing border or halo that wraps around an object or figure, setting it apart from everything else.

An aurora is a natural light display that appears in the sky, usually seen near the Earth's polar regions — the far north and the far south. It looks like glowing, dancing sheets, ribbons, or curtains of colored light floating high up in the night sky.
The adjective auroral means of, relating to, or resembling an aurora.

Auscultation is the act of carefully listening to sounds produced inside the body — specifically sounds made by internal organs — as a way to assess whether those organs are healthy or showing signs of a problem.

"Auspices" appears almost exclusively in one particular phrase: under the auspices of. This phrase means under the protection, sponsorship, guidance, and authority of someone or something — typically a respected or powerful organization.
Something is auspicious when it is a favorable sign that good things are likely to happen.
Austere means noticeably stripped of warmth, comfort, luxury, or decoration — and doing so with a kind of deliberate, serious rigidity.

Austerity means a state of severe simplicity — cutting away everything comfortable, pleasurable, or excessive, and living or operating with only what is strictly necessary. Think of it as deliberate tightening, stripping things back to the bare minimum.

An auteur is a filmmaker — almost always a director — whose movies carry such a strong, unmistakable personal stamp that we think of the films as their creative work, in the same way we think of a novel as belonging to the writer who wrote it.
Authentic means real, genuine, and exactly what it claims to be — not fake, not copied, not pretended.
To authenticate something means to prove — or to confirm — that it is genuine, real, and exactly what it claims to be.

Authenticity is the quality of being real, genuine, and true — not fake, not copied, and not pretended. When something or someone has authenticity, it means they are exactly what they claim to be, nothing more and nothing less.

When we call something or someone authoritarian, we mean they demand strict, unquestioning obedience — and they use power, control, or force to get it, rather than earning people's willing cooperation.

Authoritarianism is a system of governing — or the belief in such a system — where one person or a small group holds power in an absolute or near-absolute way, with little or no genuine accountability to the people being governed.
When something or someone is described as authoritative, it means they carry a kind of weight.
Authority means the recognized right to make decisions, give orders, or be trusted — and to have others accept that right and act accordingly.
To authorize something means to officially give permission for it to happen — or to officially give someone the right to do something.
Authorship means the fact or condition of being the creator of something — most commonly a written work like a book, article, poem, or script, but sometimes also a theory, idea, or plan.
Autism (also called Autism Spectrum Disorder, or ASD) is a condition that affects how a person's brain develops and works.
An autobiography is a book — or a long written account — in which a person tells the story of their own life, written by themselves, in their own words.
An autocracy is a system of government in which one single person holds complete and unlimited power over an entire country.
An autocrat is a ruler who holds complete, unlimited power over a country or a people — and who answers to no one.

Autocratic describes a person, a leadership style, or a system where one single person holds all the power and makes all the decisions — alone, without asking for anyone's opinion, and without allowing anyone to question or challenge them.

An autodidact is a person who has taught themselves — someone whose knowledge or skills were not gained through a formal school, university, or teacher, but through their own independent effort and curiosity.
A type of novel in which the author writes about their own real life but freely invents, exaggerates, or rearranges parts of it — a deliberate blend of autobiography and fiction.
Autoimmune describes anything related to a situation where your own body's defense system turns against your own body.
To automate something means to set up a task or process so that it runs on its own — without a person needing to do it manually each time.
"Automatically" means in a way that happens by itself, without someone needing to do it manually or think about it each time.
Automation is the use of technology — such as machines, software, or systems — to perform tasks on their own, with little or no human effort required each time.

An automaton is anything — a machine, a device, or even a person — that operates on its own, carrying out a set of actions automatically, without needing a human to guide it step by step in real time.
Autonomous means self-governing — able to make your own rules, decisions, and choices, and act on them freely, without being controlled or directed by an outside force.
Autonomy means the freedom and ability to govern yourself — to make your own choices, live by your own rules, and direct your own life without being controlled by someone else.

An autopilot is a system — usually electronic or mechanical — that automatically controls a vehicle, keeping it on a steady course without the human operator having to do it manually, moment by moment.

An autopsy is a thorough, systematic medical examination of a dead human body, performed by a specially trained doctor, to find out why the person died, how they died, and what the state of their body was at the time of death.
Autumn is one of the four seasons of the year. The four seasons, in order, are: spring → summer → autumn → winter. Autumn comes after summer and before winter. It is the third season of the year.
Autumnal is an adjective that means of, relating to, or characteristic of autumn. It describes anything that belongs to autumn, feels like autumn, or reminds you of autumn.

When you describe something as auxiliary, you are saying that it provides extra support to something more important or more central. It is not the main thing — it is the helper, the backup, the supplement. Think of it as the sidekick, not the hero.

An auxiliary is something — a person, a group, a device, or a word — whose entire purpose is to support, assist, or back up something else that is the main or primary thing. It is never the star of the show. It exists in service of another.
Avail, as a noun, means use, benefit, help, or practical effectiveness — specifically, whether something actually works or produces a useful result.
Avail means to be of use, help, or benefit to someone. The word always carries this central idea: producing a useful result or advantage.
"Avail oneself of" means to make use of something that is available to you — especially an opportunity, a resource, a service, or an offer.

Availability is a noun that captures a single, powerful idea: the state of something — or someone — being ready to be used, reached, or obtained. It answers the question: "Can I get it, use it, or access it when I need it?"

An avalanche is a massive, sudden, and violently fast flow of snow — and sometimes ice, rock, or soil — that breaks loose from a mountain or steep slope and rushes downward at tremendous speed, destroying or burying everything in its path.

When you describe something as avant-garde, you are saying it is experimental, unconventional, and ahead of its time — particularly in fields like art, music, film, fashion, literature, architecture, or even thinking and ideas in general.
Avarice means an extreme, obsessive greed for wealth and material possessions. It's not just wanting money — nearly everyone wants money. Avarice is a far more intense, darker version of that desire.

Avaricious means having an extreme, obsessive, and never-satisfied greed — specifically for money and material wealth. A person who is avaricious doesn't just want wealth; they are consumed by the desire to acquire it and hold onto it.
An avatar is a visible form or representation that something invisible, abstract, or powerful takes on — a body or image through which something makes itself known or present in the world.

To avenge someone or something means to punish a person who did something wrong — not randomly, but specifically because they hurt you or someone you care about. The punishment is a response to that wrongdoing.

To aver means to state something with firm, confident conviction — to declare that something is true, and to stand fully behind that declaration. When you aver something, you are not guessing, not suggesting, and not hedging.
When different amounts balance each other out over time, resulting in a middle level overall — as in "my good and bad months average out."

Averse means having a strong personal feeling of dislike, reluctance, or opposition toward something. When you are averse to something, you want to avoid it — not because something external is stopping you, but because something inside you resists it.
An aversion is a strong, deep feeling of dislike or disgust toward something — so strong that it makes you want to stay away from it, avoid it, or refuse to have anything to do with it.

When you avert something, you take deliberate action to stop a serious, negative event before it actually occurs. The key idea is that the bad thing was approaching — it was on the verge of happening — and someone stepped in to stop it.
Avian simply means "of, relating to, or characteristic of birds."
An aviary is a large, enclosed space specifically built to house birds, where the birds can fly around freely inside it. Think of it as a giant "room" or "house" built for birds to live in.

Aviation means the practice, science, and industry of flying aircraft. It is the entire world of human-made flight — from the moment a plane lifts off the ground to the moment it lands, and everything that makes that possible.
Avid means having a very strong, enthusiastic interest in something — to the point where you actively and eagerly pursue it. When someone is avid about something, they don't just like it casually.
An intense, almost hungry eagerness or enthusiasm for something. In science, avidity is the overall strength with which an antibody binds to its target.
When you do something avidly, you do it with great eagerness, enthusiasm, and passionate desire. You don't just like doing it — you crave doing it.

An avocation is an activity — usually a hobby or a secondary pursuit — that someone engages in alongside their main job, primarily for personal enjoyment, passion, or fulfillment. It is something you do in addition to your regular work, not instead of it.
To avoid like the plague means to stay away from someone or something as completely and strongly as possible. Not just a little bit — but totally, deliberately, and with great effort.
Avoidance is the act or practice of deliberately keeping away from something, someone, or a situation — or making sure something does not happen.
To avouch something means to declare it to be true with full confidence and personal responsibility.

To avow something means to openly, boldly, and frankly declare or admit something — especially your own beliefs, opinions, feelings, or personal stance — without shame, without hesitation, and without being forced to do so.

An avowal is a willing, open, and frank declaration in which someone publicly states what they believe, feel, or stand for — especially on a matter of importance. It refers both to the act of making such a declaration and to the declaration itself.

When something is described as avowed, it means it has been openly, publicly, and explicitly declared by the person themselves. The person hasn't hidden it, denied it, or kept it private — they have come forward and stated it clearly for the world to know.
Avowedly means in a way that has been openly and boldly declared by the person themselves.

When you describe someone as avuncular, you mean they behave like a warm, kind, friendly uncle — someone who is approachable, gently wise, good-humored, and makes you feel comfortable and cared for, without being strict or demanding.
To await something means to wait for it — knowing or expecting that it will come. It is not a restless, uncertain kind of waiting. It is a calm, expectant kind.
Awareness is the state of knowing, noticing, or being conscious of something. It is the mental condition of having something on your radar — of recognizing that it exists, is happening, or is true.
Covered or flooded with water. Figuratively, having a great amount of something, as in "the city was awash with rumours."

Awe is a powerful feeling you get when you encounter something so grand, so vast, so beautiful, or so overwhelming that it seems far beyond ordinary experience. It stops you in your tracks. It makes you feel very, very small — and yet, strangely moved.

Something that is awe-inspiring causes you to feel a powerful emotion called awe — a deep mix of wonder, amazement, and sometimes even a little fear, all at the same time. When something is awe-inspiring, it stops you in your tracks.
Awestruck means being completely overwhelmed by a feeling of deep wonder, admiration, and amazement — so much so that you are almost frozen, speechless, or stunned by it.
Awful means extremely bad, unpleasant, or of very poor quality. It describes something that makes you feel strongly negative — disgusted, unhappy, shocked, or horrified.

"Awkward" describes anything that doesn't fit smoothly or comfortably — a clumsy movement, an embarrassing social moment, a hard-to-handle object, an inconvenient time, or a person who doesn't quite know how to act.

Awkwardness is the quality or state of something — or someone, or a moment — being awkward. It means a lack of ease, grace, or smoothness. Whenever something doesn't flow naturally, feels uncomfortable, or is difficult to handle, that's awkwardness.
