An awl is a small, simple hand tool designed to punch or pierce holes into materials. That's its one job — making holes. It does not drill, cut, or screw anything. It simply pushes through a material and creates a hole by forcing the material apart.
An awning is a roof-like cover — usually made of thick fabric or metal — that is attached to the outside wall of a building and sticks out over a window, a door, or an open area like a patio.

AWOL stands for Absent Without Leave. When someone is described as AWOL, it means they have disappeared from a place where they were expected or required to be, without asking for or receiving permission to leave.

Awry means away from the correct, expected, or intended direction — either physically (something is crooked or twisted to one side) or, far more commonly, figuratively (something has deviated from how it was supposed to go).
To suddenly and decisively get rid of something — to cancel a plan, cut a service, or dismiss someone from their job.
When someone "has an axe to grind," it means they have a hidden personal motive, a selfish reason, or a private agenda behind what they are saying or doing.
An axiom is a statement that is accepted as true without needing proof, and that serves as the starting point from which other truths are built.

Axiomatic is simply the adjective form of axiom. So when something is described as axiomatic, it means it has the quality of an axiom — it is so obviously and universally true that it needs no proof, no argument, and no debate.
An axle is a straight rod or bar — usually made of metal — that passes through the center of one or more wheels and holds them in place while allowing them to spin.

Azure describes a specific shade of bright, clear, sky-blue. Not just any blue — a particular one. Think of a perfect, cloudless sky on a sunny day at noon, when the sky looks its most vivid and pure. That exact color is azure.
The philosophical view that past, present, and future are all equally real, and that "now" is not special — events are simply ordered as earlier or later than one another.
Babble means to make a continuous flow of sound that is either hard to understand, hard to follow, or simply never-ending.
A babel is a loud, chaotic mixture of voices, sounds, or languages all happening at once — so tangled together that nothing can be clearly understood.
A sudden, large increase in the number of babies born, especially the one that followed World War II, between about 1946 and 1964.
A baby boomer is a person who was born during a sudden, dramatic increase in birth rates that happened in many countries — especially the United States — after World War II ended in 1945.

A bacchanal is a wild, frenzied, out-of-control celebration — one driven heavily by excessive drinking, loud excitement, and the complete abandonment of self-restraint or social rules. It's not just a lively party.

Bacchanalian is an adjective that describes wild, unrestrained, drunken celebration or behavior — the kind where people completely abandon self-control and give themselves over entirely to drinking, pleasure, and excess.
A bachelor is an adult man who is not married.
To "back the wrong horse" means to support, choose, or invest in the person, plan, idea, or option that ultimately fails or loses.
To support someone or confirm what they say. It can also mean to make a spare copy of computer data, to move backwards, or for traffic to come to a standstill.

When you describe something as back-of-the-envelope, you mean it is a quick, rough, and informal calculation, estimate, or plan — one that gives you a good enough answer without going into precise detail.
When two or more things happen one immediately after the other — with no gap, no pause, and no break between them — you describe them as back-to-back.
Backbiting is the act of saying cruel, harmful, or negative things about a person who is not present in the conversation.
Backbreaking describes physical work or effort that is extremely hard, exhausting, and punishing on the body — so brutally demanding that it feels as though it could literally break your back.
The background or setting against which events take place, as in "the talks took place against a backdrop of violence." Literally, it is a painted cloth hung at the back of a stage.
A backer is a person (or an organization) who supports someone or something — usually by providing money, influence, or active help — so that person or thing can succeed.
When a plan or action backfires, it has the opposite effect to what was intended, often harming the very person who started it.

When something is backhanded, it means it appears to be one thing on the surface — usually something positive or harmless — but secretly carries the opposite meaning underneath. It is a statement, gesture, or action that hits you from an unexpected angle.
A secret payment given to someone to persuade them to do something dishonest; a bribe.
Backing means support — but it's a very specific kind of support. Think of it as the thing that stands behind something else to give it strength, stability, or help.
A strong, widespread negative reaction from many people against a change, decision, or someone's actions.
A backlog is an accumulation of unfinished work, unmet demands, or unfulfilled tasks that have piled up because they couldn't be handled fast enough — and are still waiting to be dealt with.
To backpedal means to retreat from something you previously said, promised, or committed to — to go back on your own words or decisions, usually because of pressure, criticism, or backlash.

To backslide means to return to bad behavior, bad habits, or wrong ways after you had already improved or made progress. In simpler words: you were doing well, then you slipped back into doing badly again.
A backstop is a last-resort safety mechanism — something positioned behind all other plans and measures, whose sole job is to make sure things don't completely collapse if everything else fails.
A backup is something you have in reserve — kept ready in case the main thing fails, gets lost, or needs help.

The word backward always points to something going in the opposite of the expected, natural, or forward direction — whether that is a physical direction, the direction of time, the direction of progress, or the direction of social confidence.

In its physical sense, a backwater is a body of water — usually a section of a river, a pool, or a small channel — where the water is slow-moving or completely still, because the main current of the river doesn't flow through it.

Bad blood means deep, long-lasting feelings of hostility, hatred, bitterness, or resentment between two or more people or groups. It's not about a quick, small argument that people forget the next day.
"Bad faith" means deliberate insincerity — acting as though you mean something when you don't, or pretending to engage honestly while secretly working against that very engagement.

When you describe someone as bad-tempered, you mean that they get angry, irritated, or annoyed very easily — often over small things that most people would not react to so strongly. A bad-tempered person does not need a big reason to become upset.

A badass is a person who is deeply impressive — someone who combines toughness, high skill, fearlessness, and a cool, unshakeable confidence. When you call someone a badass, you are paying them a high compliment.
A villain or bad guy in a story or film. In modern slang, a baddie is a confident, attractive, and stylish woman.
A badge of honor is something — a difficulty, a criticism, a scar, a habit, a label — that a person wears proudly, even though it might seem negative or painful on the surface.

A badger is a wild animal — a medium-sized mammal that lives in forests, grasslands, and farmlands across Europe, Asia, and North America. It is related to weasels, otters, and wolverines, though it looks quite different from all of them.

To badger someone means to repeatedly pressure, pester, or annoy them — usually by asking for something over and over, or pushing them to do something — and refusing to stop even when they resist or say no.
Badinage is playful, witty, back-and-forth conversation — the kind of light, teasing, clever talk that happens between people who are relaxed and comfortable with each other.

To baffle someone means to confuse them so completely that their mind goes blank — they simply cannot understand, explain, or make sense of something, no matter how hard they try. It's not mild confusion. When something baffles you, you hit a hard wall.

When someone is baffled, they are completely unable to understand something — no matter how hard they try. Their mind hits a wall. They look at something, think about it, turn it over in their head, and still cannot make sense of it.

Something is baffling when it is so confusing or puzzling that you simply cannot make sense of it — even after genuinely trying. It goes beyond ordinary confusion. With ordinary confusion, you might struggle for a moment, then figure it out.
A bagatelle is something small and unimportant — barely worth your attention.

The word baggage is built on one consistent image: things you carry with you. Whether it's a suitcase stuffed with clothes or a heart weighed down by old wounds, baggage is always about what you bring along — sometimes by choice, sometimes not.
A baguette is a long, thin loaf of bread that originally comes from France. It is one of the most recognizable breads in the world, and it is a symbol of French food culture.
Money paid to a court so that an accused person can be released from custody until their trial, as a guarantee that they will return.
When a boat takes on water and risks sinking, you bail — you scoop or pour the water out using a bucket, cup, or anything available. You can say bail or bail out.
To rescue a person, company, or country from serious difficulty, especially by giving them money. It also means to jump out of an aircraft by parachute, or to abandon a commitment.
A bailiff is an official who is given authority by a higher power — a court, a judge, or a landowner — to carry out specific duties, usually involving enforcement, order, or management.
A bailiwick is a person's own particular area — the specific domain where they are skilled, responsible, or in charge.

A bailout is a rescue. It happens when someone — or something — is in serious trouble and an outside party steps in to save them by providing money or other support. Think of it as a lifeline thrown to someone who is drowning financially.

Bait is something that is deliberately offered or placed to attract a living creature — an animal or a person — toward a trap, danger, or desired outcome that is hidden from them. The bait itself appears desirable, appealing, or harmless.
To bait always means to use something as a lure — to draw out a reaction, catch a creature, or trap a person.

Bait and switch is a deceptive tactic where someone attracts you with an appealing offer (the bait), and then, once they have your attention or commitment, replaces it with something worse (the switch).
A bake-off is a baking competition. People compete against each other by making baked goods — breads, cakes, cookies, pies — and a judge (or a panel of judges) decides whose creation is the best.

Baklava is a sweet dessert pastry — a baked food item eaten as a treat or after a meal. It is one of the most well-known and beloved sweets across the Middle East, Central Asia, and the Mediterranean region.
A balaclava is a type of tight-fitting garment that you wear on your head. It covers your entire head — including your face and neck — leaving only a small part of your face open.

A balancing act is the skill — and the ongoing effort — of managing two or more competing demands, responsibilities, or forces at the same time, without letting any one of them collapse or cause the others to fail.
Balderdash means language — spoken or written — that is complete nonsense: foolish, exaggerated, or simply untrue, yet presented as if it means something or deserves to be taken seriously.
In a direct, plain, and blunt way — with nothing added to soften what is being said.
A large, tightly pressed block of loose material such as hay, straw, cotton, or paper, tied with wire, twine, or netting so that it holds together.
Baleful means something that is threatening, menacing, and full of evil intent — something that warns you, either through its expression or its very nature, that harm or misfortune is coming.
To balk means to suddenly stop and refuse to do something, or to show strong reluctance to proceed with it.
To balkanize something means to break it apart into smaller, mutually hostile pieces that are weaker, dysfunctional, and unwilling or unable to cooperate with one another.
Balky means stubbornly refusing to move, act, or function the way you want or expect.
A ballad is a story told in the form of a song or poem.
Ballast means heavy material added to something in order to make it stable. Think of it as "stabilizing weight."
A forensic finding that two bullets or shell casings were fired from the same gun, based on the unique microscopic marks every gun leaves on its ammunition.

A ballot is the method or means by which people make a choice — privately, fairly, and officially — especially when deciding on something important like who should lead a country, a company, or an organization.
When used as an adjective, "ballpark" means approximate — not exact, but in the right general range.
A ballpark figure is a rough, approximate number — an educated guess that is close enough to be useful, but not meant to be exact.
Ballyhoo means loud, exaggerated, and over-the-top publicity or hype — the kind deliberately designed to make something seem far more exciting, important, or impressive than it actually is.
A balm is something that soothes and heals. That one idea — gentle, healing relief — runs through every use of this word, whether it describes a real physical substance or a feeling.

When used to describe weather, air, a breeze, or a climate, balmy means pleasantly warm, mild, and soft — the kind of gentle warmth that feels comfortable and agreeable on your skin. Not hot. Not cold. Just right, and soothing.

A balsam is a thick, naturally occurring, sweet-smelling substance that oozes out of certain trees and plants — either on its own, or when their bark is cut or wounded. Think of it like tree sap, but more aromatic and more medically useful.
A railing along the edge of a staircase, balcony, or terrace, made up of a row of short decorative posts with a rail along the top.

To bamboozle someone means to trick or deceive them, usually in a clever, sneaky, or confusing way. The person being bamboozled ends up believing something false, doing something they didn't intend to do, or simply having no idea what just happened to them.
To ban something or someone means to officially declare that it is not allowed. Think of it as a formal "No" that comes from a person or group that has the power to enforce it.
A mathematical theorem showing that a solid ball can, in theory, be cut into a finite number of pieces and reassembled into two balls each identical in size to the original.
If something is banal, it is so ordinary, predictable, and overused that it feels completely empty of meaning or interest.
Banality means the quality of being so ordinary, predictable, and unoriginal that it becomes dull, flat, and devoid of any real meaning or freshness.
If something is banausic, it is purely mechanical, routine, and practical — the kind of thing that requires no real thinking, no creativity, and no intellectual or artistic effort.
A bandanna is a large, square piece of cloth — soft, thin, and lightweight. It is usually made of cotton, though sometimes silk.
A bandwagon is a popular trend, movement, cause, or activity that keeps attracting more and more people simply because it is already popular.

Bandwidth is the capacity of a channel to carry things at once. Whether the channel is a wire, a radio signal, or a person's mind, bandwidth asks the same question — how much can flow through this at the same time?
When people bandy words, insults, jokes, or accusations with each other, they are throwing them at each other in a rapid, back-and-forth way — the way players hit a ball to and fro.

Bane means something that causes serious harm, misery, or ruin — something that makes life significantly worse, either by constantly irritating and troubling you, or in its more severe sense, by destroying or even killing.
Baneful means causing serious harm, ruin, or destruction. If something is baneful, it doesn't just hurt a little — it damages, corrupts, poisons, or devastates.
"Bang for your buck" means getting a lot of value, benefit, or results for the money you spend.
Excellent; first-rate (American). In British slang, to bang someone up means to put them in prison.
A bangle is a type of ornament — specifically, a stiff, circular ring worn around the wrist (and sometimes the ankle).

To banish someone means to officially force them to leave a place — usually a country, kingdom, or community — as a punishment, and to strictly forbid them from ever coming back. The key idea is: you are removed, and you are not allowed to return.
Banishment is the act of officially and forcefully sending someone away from a place — usually their own country, city, or community — and ordering them never to return. It is a punishment.
A banister is the railing structure along the side of a staircase — the thing you reach out and hold onto when you walk up or down stairs to keep yourself steady and safe.
"Banjo-eyed" means having eyes that are wide open and bulging — the way a person's eyes look when they are struck by extreme surprise, shock, or amazement.
A bank is an organization — usually a building or a company — that deals with money on behalf of people and businesses.
To keep money in a bank, or to have an account with a particular bank. To bank on something means to rely on it. Of an aircraft, to bank is to tilt while turning.

"Bank on" is a phrasal verb that means to rely on, trust, or feel very confident about something or someone. When you "bank on" something, you are so sure about it that you are willing to make plans or decisions based on it.
To bankroll something means to provide the money needed to make it happen.
Bankrupt means being completely and officially unable to pay back the money you owe to others.

Bankruptcy is a legal status — officially recognized by a court of law — in which a person or organization is formally declared unable to repay the money they owe to others. It is not about being temporarily tight on cash.
A banner is something that displays a message or represents an identity — visually, through text, images, or symbols.
A banquet is a large, formal, and elaborate meal shared by many people, held to celebrate or mark a special occasion.

A banshee is a supernatural female spirit from Irish and Scottish Gaelic folklore. She is not a ghost of a dead person — she is a type of fairy or spirit being that exists in her own right. Her one and only purpose is to announce that someone is about to die.
Banter is playful, teasing conversation between people who are comfortable with each other. It is light-hearted, witty, and friendly — nobody is genuinely trying to hurt anyone.

When something is described as bantering, it means it has the quality of being playfully teasing, lightly witty, and good-humored — like a friendly back-and-forth exchange where people joke around with each other without any real harm or serious intent.
Baptism is a religious ritual that uses water on a person. The water is applied either by fully dipping the person in it, pouring it over their head, or sprinkling it on them.

A baptism of fire is a first experience that is extremely difficult, intense, and testing — one that throws a person into the deep end right from the very beginning, often with little time to prepare.

To baptize someone means to perform a sacred ritual in which water is used on a person as a symbol of spiritual cleansing, a new beginning, and formal entry into a religious community — most commonly, Christianity.

"Bar" is one of the most versatile nouns in English. It carries many distinct meanings, but if you look carefully, almost all of them connect to a core image: something long, rigid, and solid — or something that divides, blocks, or measures.
To officially prevent someone from doing something or entering somewhere, as in "he was barred from the club." It can also mean to block a way or opening.

"Bar none" means without any exception, whatsoever. It is used to say that something or someone is the absolute best (or most extreme) — and that no person, thing, or situation in the world can challenge that claim.
The most fundamental meaning of barb is a sharp point that curves or angles backward from the tip of something. Think of a fishhook.
A barbarian is a person who is considered uncivilized, violent, crude, or morally primitive — usually by the standards of another group, culture, or society that sees itself as superior and refined.

Barbaric means something is shockingly cruel, brutally violent, or so uncivilized that it offends our sense of basic human decency. It describes behavior or actions that feel deeply wrong — the kind that make people say, "How could anyone do that?"
A state of extreme cruelty, brutality, and lack of civilization. It can also mean a word or expression that is badly formed or considered incorrect.

Barbarity means extreme cruelty, savage violence, or brutally uncivilized behavior — the kind that shocks your moral conscience and makes you feel that the person or group responsible has lost all sense of humanity and decency.
"Barbarous" describes something — an action, a behavior, a treatment, or a person — that is savagely cruel, brutal, and shockingly lacking in human compassion or moral decency.
Of a remark or comment, deliberately hurtful and cutting, often in a way that is clever or indirect. Literally, having sharp backward-pointing spikes, like barbed wire.

A bard is a poet — but a special kind of poet. Not just someone who writes a poem for fun or scribbles a few lines in a diary. A bard is a celebrated, skilled poet whose work is considered important, powerful, or artistically great.

Bare describes something that has been stripped down to its most basic state — without a covering, without additions, and without anything extra. Think of it as the opposite of "full," "covered," or "decorated."
"Bare minimum" means the least amount of something that is absolutely necessary — not one drop more, not one step extra.

To bare one's soul means to reveal your deepest, most private feelings, thoughts, fears, and truths to another person — completely and honestly, holding nothing back. It is an act of total emotional openness and vulnerability.
Barefaced means doing something wrong — especially lying or cheating — openly, shamelessly, and without even trying to hide it.
Barely means only just — something is true, but only to the smallest possible degree. It sits right at the edge, almost at zero, but not quite.
"Barest" is the superlative form of the adjective "bare." This means it takes the meaning of "bare" and pushes it to its absolute extreme — to the furthest possible degree.
A barfly is a person who spends an excessive amount of time at bars, drinking. Not someone who occasionally goes out for a drink with friends — but someone who seems to live at the bar.

A bargain is fundamentally about two people reaching an agreement — usually an agreement where each person gives something and gets something in return. Think of it as a settled deal between two sides, where both have agreed on the terms.
To bargain means to talk with another person — back and forth — in order to reach an agreement, especially about price, terms, or conditions.

Bargaining is the process of two or more parties discussing and negotiating with each other to reach an agreement — especially about price, terms, or conditions — where each side tries to get the best deal possible for themselves while giving the other side enough to make the deal happen.
A bargaining chip is anything — an object, a piece of information, a privilege, a resource, or even a person — that gives you leverage in a negotiation.
When you "barge," you move into a place or situation in a way that is forceful, sudden, and rude — without caring about the people around you, without asking permission, and without being invited.

To barge in means to enter a place, a conversation, or a situation suddenly, rudely, and without being invited or asked. The person who barges in has no regard for what is already happening — they just push themselves in, interrupting or disturbing others.
A barista is a person whose job is to prepare and serve coffee-based drinks — especially espresso and espresso-based drinks — typically working at a café, coffee shop, or espresso bar.
The tough, protective outer covering of a tree's trunk and branches. A bark is also the short, loud sound a dog makes.

Barmy means crazy, foolish, or mentally unhinged — but almost always in a light-hearted, informal way. When you call someone or something barmy, you're saying they are absurd, ridiculous, or a bit mad.
A barnacle is a small marine animal — meaning it lives in the sea — that permanently glues itself to hard surfaces and spends its entire adult life completely stuck in one place.
When you call something barnstorming, you mean it is thrillingly impressive, full of wild energy, and done with spectacular skill.
The Barnum Effect is the very human tendency to believe that a vague, general personality description was written specifically for you, when in reality it could apply to almost anyone.
An instrument that measures air pressure, used to forecast the weather. Figuratively, something that reflects changes in a situation, as in "a barometer of public opinion."
Barometric is an adjective. It simply means "relating to atmospheric pressure" — the pressure that the air around us exerts on everything it touches.
The adjective baroque has one central idea: elaborate, ornate, and richly complicated — often extravagantly so. Everything else about this word branches out from that core.

A barrack is a large building — or a group of buildings — built specifically to house soldiers. Think of it as a military dormitory: a place where troops eat, sleep, and live while they are stationed at a base or post.

A barrage is a large, overwhelming, and continuous flood of something that comes at you all at once — so much, so fast, and so forcefully that it becomes very difficult, or even impossible, to handle, escape, or properly respond to.
Forbidden or not allowed, as in "he was barred from entering." It can also mean having bars, as a barred window does.
To barrel means to move very fast, with force, and often without full control — like something heavy charging forward that would be difficult to stop.

Barren means completely unable to produce anything — no life, no results, no richness, nothing of value. Think of a vast, dry, cracked desert where nothing grows, no animal lives, and nothing useful can come from the land.

A barrette is a small device worn in the hair to hold it in place. Think of it as a hair clip — something you fasten onto a section of hair to keep it from falling into your face or to style it a certain way.
A barricade is a temporary structure or arrangement of objects placed across a path, entrance, or open space to block people or vehicles from getting through, or to protect the people behind it.

A barrier is anything — physical or non-physical — that blocks, prevents, or limits movement, access, or progress between two sides. Think of it as something that stands in between, making it difficult or impossible to get from one side to the other.
"Barring" means "except for" or "unless [something] happens." It introduces a single thing that you are mentally setting aside before making your main statement.

A barrio is a neighborhood — a defined section or district of a city or town where people live. Think of how any large city is divided into smaller areas, each with its own character and community. Each of those areas can be called a barrio.

A barrister is a specific type of lawyer whose primary job is to argue cases in court on behalf of a client. While the word "lawyer" is a broad umbrella term for anyone trained in law, a barrister is a specialized kind of lawyer — a courtroom specialist.

To barter means to exchange goods or services directly with another person — without using money. Instead of paying cash for something you want, you give something of yours in return, and both of you walk away with what you needed.
A barterer is a person who trades goods or services directly for other goods or services — without using money.

A bas-relief is a type of artwork — specifically a type of sculpture — where figures, shapes, or designs are raised slightly above a flat background surface. The figures are not floating freely in space like a standalone statue.
Basalt is a type of rock — specifically, a dark-colored rock formed when lava (molten rock that erupts from a volcano) reaches the surface, flows out, and cools down and hardens.
When "base" is used as an adjective, it means morally low, shameful, or dishonorable.
"Base" means the lowest part of something, or the foundation on which everything else rests.
Having no basis in fact, evidence, or sound reasoning, as in "baseless accusations."
A baseline is a starting point or reference point that you use to measure, compare, or judge everything else against.

Baseness is the quality of being morally low, dishonorable, or contemptible. When you say someone displays "baseness," you mean their actions or character fall far below the standards of decency, honor, and integrity that we expect from a good person.

Bash means to hit something hard. But it's not just any hit — it carries a sense of real force, often with a blunt or heavy object, and sometimes a sense of clumsiness or lack of control. Think of it as a solid, heavy, thudding kind of blow.
Bashful describes a person who is shy and easily made to feel self-conscious or embarrassed — especially around other people.
"Basic" means relating to, or forming, the foundation of something — the most essential level, the starting point, the simplest or most stripped-down version of a thing.
A large, oblong hall with a high central aisle and rounded end. In the Catholic Church, a basilica is a church given special status by the Pope.
A basin is anything that is shaped like a bowl: hollow in the middle, with raised edges all around.
When you identify the basis of something, you are identifying its root — the thing it cannot exist without.

To bask means to stay in a warm, pleasant situation and enjoy it fully — soaking it in with a feeling of deep comfort and pleasure. The key idea is passive enjoyment: you are not doing anything active. You are simply receiving something good and savoring it.
When you call someone or something a basket case, you mean they are so overwhelmed, broken down, or dysfunctional that they can barely function at all.
The lowest range of musical sound, or the instrument or voice that plays or sings it. A bass is also a type of freshwater or sea fish.
Bass-ackward (as an adverb) means doing something in completely the wrong order, in the exact opposite of the sensible or correct way, or in the most illogical, mixed-up manner imaginable.
A bassinet is a small, cosy bed made specifically for newborn babies and very young infants.

A bassoon is a large musical instrument that belongs to the woodwind family — the group of instruments in an orchestra that are traditionally made of wood and played by blowing air through them (like the flute, clarinet, and oboe).

At its most literal, a bastard is a person born to parents who were not married to each other at the time of their birth. The word historically referred to a child considered "illegitimate" — meaning their birth fell outside the boundaries of legal marriage.

When you bastardize something, you take something that was originally good, pure, genuine, or in its proper form — and you corrupt it, weaken it, or degrade it, usually by mixing it with something inferior, changing it carelessly, or stripping away what made it authentic.
To baste means to spoon, brush, or pour liquid over food — usually meat — while it is cooking, especially while it is roasting in an oven or grilling over heat.
A bastion is a stronghold — a place, person, or thing that powerfully protects and preserves something, especially when that something is under threat or disappearing from the world around it.

To "not bat an eyelid" means to show absolutely no reaction — no surprise, no shock, no discomfort, and no emotion — even when something unusual, disturbing, or dramatic happens right in front of you.
A bat mitzvah is a Jewish coming-of-age milestone for girls. The phrase comes from Hebrew and Aramaic and means "daughter of the commandment."
A batch is a group of things of the same kind that are made, collected, or handled together, at one time.
To hold back or reduce something, as in waiting "with bated breath." Of a hawk, to bate is to beat its wings and try to fly off its perch.
Describes something that drops suddenly from the grand or serious to the trivial or silly, or that is so falsely emotional it feels cheap rather than moving.
Bathos is the jarring, often humorous effect created when something grand, serious, or emotionally weighty is suddenly undercut by something trivial, silly, or absurdly mundane.
A short, thin stick used by a conductor to direct music, passed between runners in a relay race, or carried by a police officer.
A battalion is a large unit of soldiers in an army. Think of it as one of the standard "building blocks" that armies are organized into.

A batten is a long, narrow, flat strip of a rigid material — almost always wood, though sometimes metal, fibreglass, or plastic. Picture a short wooden plank, then imagine it sliced lengthwise into a much thinner, narrower strip. That strip is a batten.
"Batten down the hatches" means to prepare yourself for a difficult, dangerous, or challenging situation that is coming. It is a call to take protective action before trouble arrives — not after.

To batter something means to hit it hard, repeatedly, and with great force — usually to the point of causing serious damage. It is much stronger and more violent than simply "hit" or "strike." A single blow is never battering.

Battered describes something — or someone — that has taken a lot of rough, damaging treatment and shows clear signs of it. The single most important thing to understand about this word is that the damage isn't from one quick accident.

A battery is a device that stores chemical energy and converts it into electrical energy when needed. Inside a battery, chemicals react with each other in a way that pushes electrons through a circuit, producing electric current.

When you describe someone as battle-hardened, you mean they have become tough, experienced, and unshakeable because they have been through many difficult, dangerous, or painful situations — and those experiences have permanently changed them for the stronger.
A battleground is a place — or a situation — where a serious, intense conflict takes place between two or more opposing sides.

A battlement is a defensive wall structure built along the very top edge of a castle, fort, or tower. It looks like a row of alternating raised blocks and open gaps — like a crown with square teeth, or like the top edge of a chess rook (the castle piece).

"Batty" means slightly crazy, eccentric, or foolish in a mild, harmless way. It's an informal word used in everyday speech to describe someone whose thinking or behavior seems a little odd, irrational, or out of touch with common sense.

A bauble is a small, shiny, decorative object that looks attractive but has little or no real value. Think of something that catches your eye, maybe even makes you say "oh, pretty!" — but when you pick it up and think about it, it's essentially worthless.

Bawdy describes something that deals with sex in a humorous, crude, or playfully naughty way. When something is bawdy, it is openly sexual — but the key word is playfully. Bawdy humor is not meant to shock or disgust you.

To bawl means to cry in a way that is loud, messy, and completely unrestrained. It is not quiet, gentle, dignified weeping — it is full-force, open-mouthed, sometimes ugly crying, often with loud wailing sounds.
When "bay" is used as an adjective, it describes a specific shade of reddish-brown. Think of the warm, rich color of dried autumn leaves, or dark rust — that is the general territory of "bay."

A bayonet is a long, pointed blade — essentially a large knife, dagger, or spike — that is designed to be attached to the front end of a rifle, converting the firearm into a combined weapon: a gun and a spear at the same time.
A bayou is a slow-moving — sometimes almost completely still — body of water found in flat, low-lying land. Think of it as a lazy, sluggish stretch of water that barely seems to flow at all.
The idiom "to sunset" (and therefore "to be sunset") means to deliberately bring something to a planned, graceful end.
"Be that as it may" is a phrase you use to acknowledge a point someone made — or a fact that exists — while signaling that it doesn't change your conclusion or what you're about to say next.

To say someone "is tightly wound" means that person is extremely tense, anxious, uptight, or unable to relax. They are very high-strung — easily stressed, easily irritated, and quick to overreact even to small things.
A beachhead is a position you fight to secure in unfamiliar or hostile territory, specifically so you can use it as a base to push further forward from there.
A beacon is anything — a light, a fire, an electronic signal, or even a person or idea — that exists to guide, warn, or inspire others, usually from a distance.
Of eyes, small, round, and shiny, with a sharp, watchful look — often suggesting suspicion or greed.
A beam is a narrow, focused stream of light that travels in a straight line from a source. It doesn't scatter randomly — it goes in one clear direction.
When a person beams, they are not just smiling — they are radiating joy from their whole face. It is a big, open, glowing smile that is impossible to hide.

Beaming describes a face, smile, or person showing a wide, bright, glowing expression of happiness — one so strong and full that the joy seems to shine outward, the way a ray of light shines from a lamp. It is not just "happy." It is visibly, radiantly happy.

Beamish means radiantly cheerful — full of bright, glowing happiness that shows on a person's face and in their entire manner. Think of someone whose smile is so wide, so warm, and so natural that their whole face seems to shine. That person is beamish.

Bean soup theory, also known as the bean soup effect or the "what about me?" effect, describes the phenomenon where someone who is not part of a target audience demands that content be adjusted to fit their personal tastes or situation.

"Bear" is one of the most versatile verbs in English. It has a single soul — the idea of holding or carrying something — but that idea stretches in many directions depending on what is being held: a physical weight, an emotion, a child, or even a direction.
To move quickly towards someone or something in a threatening way. It can also mean to put strong pressure on someone, or to press down hard.
Of an effort or plan, to finally produce a good result, as in "years of research bore fruit."
"Bear in mind" means to remember something important, especially while you are thinking, deciding, or doing something.
"Bear out" means to confirm, support, or prove that something is true.
To "bear the brunt" means to suffer the worst, heaviest, or most damaging part of something unpleasant.

"Bear witness to" means to see something happen with your own eyes, usually something significant. It also means to serve as proof or evidence of something. These are its two main meanings, and understanding both will give you full command of this phrase.
Bearable describes something that is unpleasant, painful, or difficult — but not so bad that you cannot handle it. It means: you can endure it. You can get through it. It won't destroy you.

A bearer is anyone — or anything — that carries, holds, or brings something. Think of the verb "to bear" not in the animal sense, but in its meaning of to carry or hold. A bearer is simply the one doing that carrying or holding.
The way a person holds and carries themselves. To have a bearing on something means to be relevant to it. A bearing is also a direction measured by compass.
"Beast" describes a living creature with raw, untamed power. Depending on context, it can mean a wild animal, a cruel person, a remarkably skilled individual, or even a powerful machine.
Beat is one of the most versatile verbs in English. It carries many meanings, but they all share a common thread: force applied repeatedly, or the act of overcoming something.

To "beat a hasty retreat" means to leave a place or situation very quickly, usually because you want to avoid something uncomfortable, dangerous, or embarrassing. The key idea is speed and urgency — you are not just leaving, you are rushing away.

To beat somebody to the punch means to do something before someone else does it, especially when both people want to do the same thing. It's about being faster or quicker than another person and, as a result, getting an advantage over them.
"Beat to a pulp" means to hit someone (or something) so hard and so many times that they are completely, utterly destroyed — reduced to a broken, helpless, unrecognizable state, just like pulp.
When you describe something as beat up, you mean it is in poor, rough, worn-out condition — clearly damaged or deteriorated because of heavy use, rough treatment, or simply a long, hard life.

"Beatific" describes a look, smile, or expression — or the state of being — that radiates deep, serene, glowing bliss. Not ordinary happiness, but a kind of happiness that seems so pure, so peaceful, and so complete that it almost looks otherworldly.
To beatify someone means to officially declare, in the Roman Catholic Church, that a deceased person is holy enough to be honoured with the title "Blessed."

"A beating" describes something that happens repeatedly and with force — whether that's hitting, pulsing, or overpowering. This single idea branches into three distinct meanings depending on the context.

Beatitude means a state of perfect, supreme happiness — but not just any kind of happiness. It is a deep, serene, almost otherworldly kind of bliss and blessedness, typically of a spiritual or divine nature.
A woman's boyfriend or male admirer. In old-fashioned use, a beau is also a man who cares greatly about fashion.

To beautify something means to make it more beautiful or attractive than it already is. You take something — a place, an object, a person, or even yourself — and you improve how it looks so that it becomes more pleasing to the eye.
To becalm a ship is to leave it stranded and motionless because the wind has died completely.

To be at someone's beck and call means to be always available and ready to do whatever that person wants, the moment they want it — without question, without delay, and without your own needs or schedule mattering much.

To beckon means to signal someone — using a movement of your hand or finger — to come toward you or to follow you. It is a silent, physical invitation. You are not speaking; you are using your body to say "come here" or "follow me."
When you say something is becoming, you mean it is attractively suitable — it looks good on someone because it fits them well.

Bed rotting refers to the act or practice of staying in bed all day (or for a prolonged amount of time), especially when feeling stressed or overwhelmed, but also sometimes just for the pleasure of doing so.
To bedaub something means to smear, coat, or cover it messily and thoroughly with a wet, sticky, or dirty substance — like paint, mud, grease, or anything thick and gooey.
To bedevil something or someone means to cause persistent, ongoing trouble, frustration, or suffering that is hard to escape or solve.

To bedizen something or someone means to decorate or dress them up in a way that is flashy, showy, and overdone — but in poor taste. The decoration isn't elegant or refined. It's excessive, cheap-looking, and garish.
Dressed up or decorated in a showy, excessive, and tasteless way.
Bedlam means a situation or place of complete chaos, wild noise, and total disorder — where everything seems to be happening at once and nothing is under control.

To bedraggle something or someone means to make them wet, dirty, and untidy — typically by soaking them in rain, dragging them through mud, or exposing them to messy, wet conditions. The result is a sorry, limp, disheveled state.

Bedraggled describes something — usually a person or an animal — that looks wet, dirty, messy, and exhausted all at once, typically because they have just been through something rough, like a rainstorm, a long difficult journey, or a tough physical struggle.
Bedrock is the solid, hard layer of rock that lies beneath the Earth's surface — underneath all the loose material like soil, sand, gravel, mud, and clay that we walk on every day.

Bedside manner refers to the way a doctor (or any healthcare professional) interacts with a patient — their tone, attitude, warmth, communication style, empathy, and overall behavior during an appointment or treatment.

"Beef up" is a phrasal verb that means to make something stronger, bigger, more powerful, or more effective. The core idea is always about adding more — more strength, more resources, more content, or more force — to something that already exists.

Beefy means large, solid, and powerfully built — with a strong sense of bulk and substance behind it. Think of a thick slab of beef: heavy, dense, and substantial. That physical quality is exactly what this word captures when it's applied to people or things.
A beeline is the most direct, straight path between where you are and where you want to go — the shortest possible route, with no wandering, no detours, and no distractions.
To befall means for an event — usually something bad or unfortunate — to happen to someone or something, typically beyond their control.
To befit something or someone means to be right, appropriate, or suitable for them — especially given who they are, what their role is, or what the occasion demands.

Befitting means appropriate or suitable for a particular person, role, occasion, or situation — but with a specific added weight: it carries the sense that something matches the dignity, importance, or character of whatever it refers to.

To befog something means to make it unclear, hard to understand, or confused — exactly like how real fog on a road makes it difficult to see ahead. When something is befogged, it is covered in a kind of mental or perceptual "cloud" that blocks clarity.
"Beforehand" means doing or knowing something earlier than the moment it is actually needed, used, or expected.

To befoul something means to make it foul — that is, to make it dirty, disgusting, polluted, or morally corrupt. Think of it as the act of taking something and contaminating it so badly that it becomes repulsive or ruined.
To befriend someone means to deliberately act as a friend toward them — to reach out, show kindness, and build a friendly connection with them, especially when they need it.
To befuddle someone means to confuse them so thoroughly that their mind feels foggy, jumbled, and unable to think clearly.

When someone is befuddled, their mind is confused and foggy — they cannot think clearly, make sense of what is happening, or put their thoughts together in an organized way. It is not just mild confusion.
To assume the very thing you are trying to prove, so that the argument goes in a circle. In modern everyday use, it often simply means to raise or invite an obvious question.
To beget something means to cause it to exist — to be the direct source from which something else is produced or born. Think of it as a stronger, more deliberate version of the word cause.
A beggar is a person who asks strangers or the general public for money, food, or other basic necessities — not as a one-time request to a friend, but as a regular or habitual way of surviving.

To begin means to do the first part of something — to take an action, or to enter into a state, that was not happening before. It marks the exact point where something moves from not existing or not happening into existing or happening.
Begrudge captures a very specific and deeply human feeling — a quiet mixture of resentment, envy, and reluctance. The word has two closely connected meanings.

When someone does something begrudgingly, they do it — but they really, truly did not want to. And even as they do it, there is a quiet storm of resentment, irritation, or bitterness sitting right beneath the surface.
To beguile someone means to charm or captivate them so powerfully that they are completely drawn in — sometimes in a delightful way, sometimes in a deceptive way.

When someone is beguiled, they have been so pleasantly charmed by something — a person, a place, a story, an idea — that they are completely captivated by it. Their attention is fully captured, and they are in a kind of delightful spell.

If something is beguiling, it is so charming, attractive, or fascinating that it pulls you in — almost like a spell. You find yourself drawn to it, captivated by it, unable to look away or stop thinking about it.

Behalf means the interest, representation, or benefit of a person or group. Think of it as a stand-in word for someone — it signals that an action is connected to a person who is either not present, not speaking, or not acting themselves.

A behemoth is something — a creature, an organization, a machine, or anything really — that is so enormous in size, power, or scale that it feels almost overwhelming just to look at or think about. It's not just "big." It's incomprehensibly big.
A behest is a command, order, or strong directive — especially one that comes from someone in a position of authority or power. When someone issues a behest, they are not merely asking or suggesting.
"Behind the scenes" means the things that happen in private, out of public view, that most people don't get to see — even though those things are very important to the final result.

To behold something means to see it — but not in a casual, everyday way. When you behold something, you are seeing it with your full attention, often with a feeling of wonder, awe, or deep admiration.

If you are beholden to someone, it means you are in a position where you feel you owe them something — not necessarily money, but a sense of duty, loyalty, or obligation — because they have helped you, supported you, or done something significant for you.
A person who sees or observes something — especially in the saying "beauty is in the eye of the beholder," meaning beauty depends on who is looking.
To behoove someone to do something means that it is necessary, proper, or in their best interest to do that thing.

To belabor something means to spend far more time, words, or effort on it than is necessary or useful — to keep repeating, explaining, or emphasizing something long after it has already been understood or resolved.
Belated describes something that has arrived or happened after the time it was expected, needed, or appropriate. It means: this should have come earlier, but it didn't.
A belay is essentially a secured safety system — a point, setup, or act that holds something (usually a person) from falling or drifting away. Think of it as an anchor of control.
To belay, concretely, means to manage the rope in a controlled way so that: As the climber moves up, you feed the rope out gradually, keeping just enough slack for them to move freely.

To belch means to force gas out of your stomach and up through your mouth, producing a loud, rough sound in the process. It is the same thing as "burping," though belch tends to sound more forceful and unpleasant than burp.

To beleaguer someone means to subject them to constant, relentless trouble, pressure, or attack — coming from multiple directions at once — leaving them feeling overwhelmed, trapped, and unable to escape or recover.
A belfry is a tower — or the topmost section of a tower — specifically built or used to hold large bells. Think of the tall, pointy tower you see rising above old churches, cathedrals, or town halls.

"Belie" means to contradict or give a false impression of something. It describes a mismatch — a gap between what appears to be true and what is actually true, or between what is claimed and what the evidence shows.
To belittle someone means to make them feel small, unimportant, or worthless — either by what you say, how you say it, or how you treat them.
A result in physics showing that no theory based on hidden local properties can reproduce all the predictions of quantum mechanics — implying that nature is stranger than Einstein believed.

Bellicose describes someone — or something — that is eager, ready, and inclined to fight or cause conflict. It is not just about being angry or upset. It is specifically about having a strong, active urge to argue, quarrel, or go to war.

Bellicosity means a strong, eager inclination to fight, argue aggressively, or cause conflict. It is the quality of being warlike, hostile, and confrontational — not just occasionally, but as a consistent, defining attitude.
Belligerence means an aggressive, hostile, and combative attitude — a readiness and eagerness to fight, argue, or cause conflict.

If someone is belligerent, they are openly hostile, aggressive, and ready — even eager — to fight or argue. It goes far beyond simply being upset or in a bad mood. A belligerent person has a combative attitude.

To do something belligerently means to do it in a way that is aggressively hostile and ready to fight — either physically or verbally. When someone acts belligerently, they are not just angry or upset.

To bellow means to make a very loud, deep, and powerful sound — either with your voice or, in the case of an animal, with whatever sound it naturally produces. Think of the loudest, most forceful sound a person or a large animal can make. That's a bellow.
A bellows is a device built to move air — specifically, to draw air in and then push it out in a controlled stream.
A bellwether is a person, place, company, or thing that leads the way — and because it leads, watching it gives you an early, reliable signal of where everyone else is headed next.
Belongings refers to the personal, physical things that you own — the items that are yours.

When you describe someone or something as beloved, you mean it is deeply and tenderly loved — not just liked or appreciated, but held very close to the heart with great warmth and lasting affection. It is a word that carries emotional weight.

If someone does or says something below the belt, it means they have acted in an unfair, cruel, or hurtful way — especially during an argument, a fight, or a competition. It means they crossed a line that decent, fair people shouldn't cross.
"Belt out" is a phrasal verb that means to sing, say, or shout something very loudly, powerfully, and with great energy or enthusiasm.
To bemoan something means to openly express sadness, regret, or dissatisfaction about it — usually about something you feel is unfortunate, unfair, or already beyond your power to change.

To bemuse someone means to confuse or puzzle them, leaving them in a mild state of bewilderment — that foggy, slightly lost feeling you get when something doesn't quite make sense to you and you're not sure how to process it.

Bemused means mildly confused, puzzled, or bewildered — usually in a quiet, gentle way. A bemused person hasn't understood something, and that moment of not-understanding has left them with a slightly dazed, faraway look. They're not upset or alarmed.
A benchmark is a fixed reference point — a known, agreed-upon standard that you use to measure, compare, or judge something else.

To bend over backwards means to try extremely hard to help someone or to make something happen, often to the point where you are putting yourself out of your way or making things difficult for yourself.
A period of wild, uncontrolled drinking or partying, as in "he went on a three-day bender." It can also mean a tool used for bending materials.
Beneath means lower than something else — either in a real, physical sense (where something actually is), or in a more abstract sense (how something compares in value, worth, or dignity).
A benediction is a formal, spoken blessing — words of goodwill, divine favor, or protection — pronounced over a person or a group, typically at the close of a religious service or solemn ceremony.

A benefaction is a generous act of giving — money, help, or support — done out of genuine goodwill and a sincere desire to do good for someone or something. It is always a free, voluntary act. Nobody is forced into a benefaction.
A benefactor is a person who helps someone else — or a group, organization, or cause — by giving something of real value, most commonly money, but also resources, opportunities, or support.

A benefice is a church office — a position held by a clergyman such as a priest, rector, or vicar — that comes permanently bundled with both religious responsibilities and a legal right to income from property attached to that office.

Beneficence means the active practice of doing good for others. It is not simply the wish, the feeling, or the intention that you want others to be well — it is the actual doing of something that helps, improves, or enriches another person's life.
Beneficent describes someone (or something) that actively does good for others — not just someone who wants to do good, but someone who actually does it, generously and meaningfully.

When something is beneficial, it means it produces a positive effect or a good result for someone or something. In other words, it brings about something good — it helps, improves, or adds value in a meaningful way.

A beneficiary is a person — or sometimes an organization — that receives something valuable from another person, a document, a system, or a situation. That "something valuable" could be money, property, rights, services, or simply an advantage.

A benefit is anything good that you gain, receive, or experience — something that helps you, improves your situation, or makes things better for you in some way. Think of it as "the good stuff that comes to you."

Benevolence means a genuine desire to do good for others and to promote their well-being. A person who has benevolence in their heart doesn't just avoid hurting people — they actively want others to be happy, safe, and flourishing.
Benevolent means genuinely wishing well for others and showing it through kindness, generosity, or helpful action.
Benighted means being in a state of deep ignorance — especially a kind of ignorance that is so thick and stubborn that the person or group doesn't even realize they are ignorant.

Benign means not harmful. If something is benign, it may look concerning or feel significant, but it does not cause damage, danger, or suffering. Think of it as the opposite of threatening. A benign thing is either gentle, or safe, or both.
Benignant means kindly, gentle, and gracious — especially when shown by someone in a position of power or authority toward those who are beneath them or under their care.
Benignity means the quality of being kind, gentle, and warmly favorable toward others — a deep, steady goodness of character that shows itself through warmth, mildness, and care.
A benison is a blessing — specifically, a solemn, spoken blessing that one person formally bestows on another. It is not just a warm feeling of goodwill kept silently in someone's heart.
The most basic, literal meaning of bent is something that was once straight but is now curved, twisted, or angled out of its normal shape — usually because a force was applied to it.

When someone has a bent for something, it means they have a natural inclination and ability toward that thing — a pull from within that feels built-in and effortless. It's not just that they can do something well.
"Bent on" means to be completely and firmly determined to do something, especially in a way that is hard to change or stop. When someone is "bent on" something, their mind is fully made up.
To bequeath something means to formally leave it to someone after you die, through a legal document called a will (also called a "last will and testament").

A bequest is something — money, property, or a valued possession — that a person officially leaves to someone else through their will. A will is a legal document in which a person states what should happen to their belongings after they die.
To berate someone means to scold or criticize them very harshly and angrily — and to keep doing it, not just for a moment.
To bereave someone means to cause them to lose a loved one through death. It captures the act of being robbed — cruelly and permanently — of someone you deeply love.

Bereaved describes a person who has lost a loved one through death. When someone you deeply love — a parent, a child, a spouse, a close friend — dies, you become bereaved. It means you are now living with the painful absence of that person.
Bereavement is the state of deep sadness and loss that a person goes through after someone they love dies.
Completely without something important, as in "bereft of hope." Used alone, it means deeply sad and lonely after losing someone or something.
A beret is a type of hat — specifically a soft, round, flat hat with no brim.
Berserk means wildly and dangerously out of control — behaving in a frenzied, explosive way with no restraint, usually because of a powerful emotion like rage, excitement, or fear.
A bed built into a ship or train. It is also a place where a ship ties up in port. To give someone a wide berth means to stay well away from them.

To beseech someone means to ask them for something with great urgency and deep sincerity — not a casual ask, not a polite request, but a heartfelt, desperate plea. When you beseech someone, you are not simply hoping they will say yes.
To beset someone or something means to trouble, attack, or surround from all sides, in a way that is persistent and hard to escape.

When something is described as "besetting," it means it persistently and repeatedly troubles a particular person — specifically as a fault, weakness, or struggle that they cannot seem to shake off or overcome. It is their characteristic, enduring flaw.
When someone is beside oneself, they are in such an extreme state of emotion that they feel almost out of control — as if they have lost their usual calm, rational self completely.
To besiege means to surround something or someone completely and overwhelm them with force or pressure, leaving them with no easy way out.

To besmirch someone means to damage or ruin their good reputation by saying bad, harmful, or false things about them. When you besmirch someone, you are attacking their character or their name — not physically, but in the eyes of other people.
Besotted means being so deeply and intensely in love with, or fascinated by, someone or something that you lose your ability to think clearly or see their flaws. You are completely under their spell.
To bespatter something means to splash or scatter drops of a dirty or wet substance all over a surface or a person, covering it with many messy spots or specks.
When something bespeaks a quality, it doesn't announce it loudly or explicitly — it silently signals it, the way evidence points to a conclusion.
Bespoke means something made specifically for one particular person, designed exactly to their personal needs, preferences, and requirements — not produced in bulk for the general public.
The past tense of "bespeak," meaning to show or be a sign of something, as in "his trembling hands bespoke fear." As an adjective, bespoke means made to order for a particular customer.

A best practice is a method, technique, or way of doing something that has been proven — through experience, research, and repeated testing — to produce the best results compared to all other known ways of doing the same thing.

Bestial means having the qualities of a wild beast — not a pet or a domesticated animal, but a savage, uncontrolled creature that acts purely on raw instinct, with no reason, no compassion, and no moral sense whatsoever.

A bestiary is a type of book — specifically, a collection of descriptions of animals, both real and imaginary, where each animal is paired with a moral or spiritual lesson drawn from its behavior or nature.

To bestir means to rouse yourself — or someone else — into action, especially after a period of being inactive, lazy, slow, or idle. Think of it as mentally and physically shaking off sluggishness and pushing yourself to get moving and do something.

To bestow something means to give it to someone. But it is not just any ordinary giving. It is a special, deliberate, and generous act of giving — where the thing being given carries real weight, honor, or significance.

To bestride something means to position yourself over it with one leg on each side — to straddle it. Picture a cowboy swinging onto a horse: one leg crosses over, both legs hang down on opposite sides, and the horse sits directly beneath them.
A bestseller is a product — most often a book — that has been bought by a very large number of people, making it one of the top-selling items of its kind during a given period of time.
When you say "you can bet your bottom dollar" on something, you mean you are absolutely, completely, 100% sure about it. There is no doubt in your mind whatsoever.

To betide means to happen to someone — particularly something bad or serious that comes upon a person, almost like fate delivering a consequence. Think of it as a more dramatic, formal way of saying "to befall" or "to happen to."

To betoken something means to be a visible sign of it — to indicate, suggest, or reveal that something exists, is true, or is about to happen. The word describes the relationship between a sign and what that sign points to.

Betray means to turn against someone who trusted you. When you betray a person, you do something that harms them or works against their interests, even though they believed you were loyal, honest, and on their side.
Betrayal is the act of breaking someone's trust in a way that harms them, especially when that person never expected you to hurt them because they believed you were loyal, honest, or on their side.
To betroth someone means to formally promise them in marriage — or to be formally promised to someone in marriage.

A betrothal is a formal, public promise between two people to marry each other. Think of it as the official declaration — the moment when two people (or their families) solemnly commit that a marriage will happen.

If someone is betrothed, they are formally and officially promised in marriage to another person. It means they are engaged to be married — but with a stronger, more solemn weight to it than the everyday word "engaged."
"Better off" means in a more favorable, comfortable, or advantageous situation than before, or than someone else, or than would otherwise be the case.
Between a rock and a hard place
In a situation where you must choose between two options that are both bad or difficult, with no easy way out.
A beverage is any liquid that a person drinks. If you can pour it into a glass or a cup and drink it, there's a good chance it can be called a beverage.
A bevy is a group of people or things — usually a notably large and impressive one — where all the members of that group are of the same kind.
To bewail something means to express deep, intense grief or sorrow about it — usually in an open, outward way. Think of it as crying out in anguish over a loss, a misfortune, or a painful situation.
To beware means to be alert and cautious because something is dangerous, harmful, or likely to cause trouble.
To bewilder someone means to confuse them so deeply that they feel completely lost — mentally stuck, unable to understand what's happening, or unsure what to think or do next.
When someone is bewildered, they are so confused and surprised at the same time that their mind cannot figure out what is happening or what to do next.

Bewildering describes something that causes a deep sense of confusion and disorientation — something so complex, strange, or overwhelming that your mind genuinely struggles to process or make sense of it.
Bewilderment is the feeling of being so confused that you cannot make sense of something — as if your mind has gone completely blank and the situation in front of you simply does not compute.
To bewitch someone means to put them under a witch's spell — to use magic to take control of their mind, feelings, or actions.
Something is bewitching when it is so powerfully attractive, charming, or fascinating that the effect feels almost magical — as if it has cast a spell on you.
"Beyond" points to whatever lies on the far side of a boundary, limit, or point — whether that boundary is physical, related to time, related to quantity, or related to what you are capable of.

If someone's behavior is "beyond the pale," it means their behavior is so unacceptable, so offensive, or so morally wrong that it has crossed the line of what decent society can tolerate. It is not just rude or bad — it is shockingly out of bounds.

A bias is a lean — a tilt of the mind toward or against something, someone, or some idea — that shapes the way you think, judge, or make decisions, often without full fairness or complete information.
When someone or something is biased, it means they are unfairly tilted in one direction — leaning toward one side, person, or idea — in a way that makes balanced, fair judgment impossible.

A bibelot is a small, decorative object that you keep or collect because it is beautiful, unusual, or charming — not because it does anything useful. It just sits there and looks lovely, or interesting, or delightfully odd.
A bibliography is a list of written sources — such as books, articles, journals, or websites — connected either to a specific piece of writing or to a specific subject.
A bibliophile is a person who loves books deeply — not just as a pastime, but as a genuine passion. Think of it as the word for someone who doesn't just read books, but truly cherishes them.
Bibulous is an adjective that describes someone who drinks alcohol excessively or who has a strong habit of drinking.

Bicameral is an adjective that describes something — almost always a law-making body — that is divided into two separate chambers or houses, each with its own members, its own powers, and its own distinct role.
To bicker means to argue with someone about something small and unimportant, usually in a repeated, back-and-forth, slightly childish way.

A bid is an attempt to get something, usually by offering something in return — most often money, effort, or a proposal. Think of it as raising your hand and saying, "I want this, and here's what I'm offering."
When you bid on something, you are announcing how much money you are willing to pay for it — usually in a competition against other buyers. The person who offers the most wins the item.
Biddable describes a person, animal, or group that is naturally easy to direct, control, or tell what to do — and that willingly goes along without resistance or argument.
A bidder is a person (or a company) who offers a price to try to buy or win something, usually in a situation where several people are competing for the same thing.
The orders or wishes of someone who expects to be obeyed, as in "she always does her mother's bidding." It also means the offering of prices at an auction.

To bide means to wait or to remain somewhere. That's the foundation. But the word carries something extra that plain "wait" does not — a sense of patience with purpose. When you bide, you are not fidgeting or rushing.
To bide one's time means to wait patiently for the right moment to act.
"Biennial" describes something tied to a two-year cycle. It has two closely related meanings, depending on context.
A bier is a flat, portable frame or platform used to carry a coffin — or sometimes a dead body — from one place to another, usually during a funeral.
To bifurcate means to split into two separate branches or parts.
Bifurcated means divided or split into exactly two distinct parts, branches, or sections.
A bifurcation is a splitting of one thing into two distinct branches, paths, or parts. Think of it as a fork — one thing arrives, and two things leave.

"Big cheese" is used to describe a very important, powerful, or influential person — usually in an organization, company, or group. It refers to someone who is at the top, who makes the big decisions, and whose words carry a lot of weight.
Something genuinely important or significant. Said sarcastically — "big deal!" — it means the opposite: that something is not impressive or important at all.
Big fish in a small pond

A "big fish in a small pond" refers to a person who is very important, powerful, or well-respected — but only within a small or limited environment. The moment that person steps outside that small world, they may become quite ordinary or even unnoticed.
The "big picture" means the overall view of a situation — the full, broad understanding of something, as opposed to getting lost in the small, specific details.

A bigot is a person who holds strong, unreasonable hatred, dislike, or prejudice toward a particular group of people — and stubbornly refuses to question, reconsider, or let go of that attitude, no matter what.
Bigoted describes a person — or their words, actions, and attitudes — that show strong, unreasoning prejudice and intolerance toward a group of people simply because of who those people are.

Bigotry is the stubborn, closed-minded intolerance of people who are different from you — especially people who belong to a different group based on things like race, religion, ethnicity, gender, sexual orientation, nationality, or political belief.

A bigwig is an important, powerful, or highly influential person — someone who holds a top position, commands great authority, or carries significant weight in a particular field, organization, or society.
Bilateral is an adjective that describes something involving exactly two sides, parties, or groups — where both sides are actively participating, mutually committed, or equally affected.
A partial dislocation of a joint, occurring on both sides of the body at once.
A bildungsroman is a type of novel.
A bitter, yellowish-green fluid made by the liver that helps digest fat. Figuratively, bile means bitter anger and resentment.

Bilingual means involving, using, or able to use two languages. It comes from the prefix "bi-" (meaning two) and "lingual" (relating to language). When something or someone is described as bilingual, two languages are at the center of it.
Bilingualism is the ability of a person — or a group of people — to use two languages effectively in daily life. The word itself is a noun, meaning it names a concept, a state of being.

The word bilious is built around the idea of something being unpleasant in a way that makes you feel sick — physically, emotionally, or visually. It can describe a feeling in your body, a person's bad mood, or even an ugly colour.
To bilk someone means to cheat or defraud them — typically by deceiving them to get money, goods, or some benefit, and then failing to give them what they were rightfully owed or promised in return.
A document showing how much money you owe for something. A bill is also a proposed new law, a banknote (American), or a bird's beak.
A billboard is a very large, flat board or panel used to display advertisements or messages to the public in outdoor spaces.
A billet is a place — usually a room or house — where a soldier or military personnel is temporarily lodged, often in a civilian's home rather than a military base.
Billiards is a word that refers to a family of indoor games where players use a long stick — called a cue — to hit balls across a large, flat, cloth-covered table.

Billingsgate means foul, obscenely vulgar, and abusively crude language — the kind of language that is not merely rude or blunt, but spectacularly offensive and low. It refers to coarse verbal abuse at its most unfiltered and gutter-level extreme.
A billow is a large, swelling, rounded mass of something soft or fluid — something that rises, expands, and rolls in big, full curves.
To billow means to swell, puff out, or rise in large, full, rounded shapes — usually because air or wind is pushing something outward, or because something light and airy is expanding upward.
Billowing describes something that is swelling outward in large, rounded, rolling waves or masses — usually because wind or air is filling and pushing it from the inside or below.
To bimble means to move — usually on foot — at a slow, relaxed, unhurried pace, with no particular destination or urgent purpose.
A bimester is a period of exactly two months.
Binary means "consisting of, relating to, or built upon exactly two things."
Bind means to hold things together so they cannot easily come apart or move freely. That single idea — of joining, fastening, or restricting — runs through every meaning of this word.
When something is binding, it means you must follow it. You have no legal or moral choice to ignore it, walk away from it, or pretend it doesn't exist.
To binge means to do something — almost always something pleasurable or addictive — in a way that is excessive, unrestrained, and concentrated into a short burst of time.
Biochemical means relating to the chemical processes, substances, and reactions that occur within, or are produced by, living organisms — such as humans, animals, plants, bacteria, and fungi.
When something is biodegradable, it means nature can break it down on its own, naturally, over time — turning it back into simple, harmless substances that the Earth can absorb and reuse.

Biodiversity means the total variety of life on Earth — every plant, animal, fungus, bacterium, and any other living organism. Think of it as a measure of how rich and varied life is on our planet, in a given region, or even in your own backyard.
A biofuel is any type of fuel that is made from living things — or from materials that were recently alive. The word "bio" simply means "life," so a biofuel is literally a life-sourced fuel.
Biographical is an adjective. You use it to describe anything that is about the life of a real person — their story, their experiences, their journey from birth through their life.
A biography is a written account of a real person's life, created by someone other than that person.
Biological means "relating to life, living things, or the processes that occur within them."
A biologist is a scientist who studies living things. If something is alive — or was once alive — a biologist is interested in it.
