Bioluminescence is the ability of a living organism to produce and emit light from its own body through a chemical reaction happening inside it.

Something described as bioluminescent is a living organism — or something belonging to or produced by one — that generates and emits its own visible light through a chemical reaction happening inside its body.
The word biomass is made of two simple ideas stuck together: life and mass (weight/matter). So biomass simply means the material that makes up living things, or that once did.

A biome is a large region of the Earth that is defined by its climate and the specific community of living things — mainly plants, but also animals, fungi, and microorganisms — that have naturally adapted to survive in that climate.

When you describe something as biometric, you are saying that it involves the measurement or use of the unique biological or physical characteristics of a person's body to recognize, verify, or identify who that person is.
Bionic describes something that combines a living body with electronic or mechanical technology — specifically in a way that replaces or dramatically enhances a natural biological function.
A biopic is a movie that tells the life story of a real person who actually existed.
The biosphere is the total, global system of all life on Earth — every living thing that has ever existed on this planet, along with the physical spaces those living things occupy and interact with.

Biotechnology is the use of living things — such as bacteria, cells, plants, or animals — and their natural biological processes, to create products or develop solutions that benefit people and the world.
When two groups of people who usually disagree with each other come together and agree on something, that agreement is called bipartisan.
A biped is any living creature that walks, runs, or moves primarily on two legs.
Bipedal is an adjective used to describe any creature — or thing — that moves on two legs as its main, natural way of getting around.
Bipedalism is the condition of moving around primarily on two legs, in an upright, vertical posture — with the body held tall and straight above the legs.
To bisect something means to divide it into two equal parts — to cut right through the middle so that both resulting pieces are the same size.
A bishop is a high-ranking official in many Christian churches — someone who holds authority over a group of churches and the priests or ministers who serve them.

A bison is a very large, heavy, wild animal with hooves, horns, and a thick shaggy coat. It is one of the biggest land animals in the world. Think of it as a massive, wild relative of a cow — much larger, much stronger, and built completely differently.
A rich, thick, creamy, and completely smooth soup, often made with shellfish. It is also unglazed white pottery.
A bit part is a very small, minor role that an actor plays in a film, TV show, or theatre production. The role is so tiny that it barely matters to the overall story.
A rude, informal way of telling someone you don't care what they think and want them to leave you alone.

To "bite one's tongue" means to stop yourself from saying something you really want to say — usually because saying it out loud would be hurtful, inappropriate, cause trouble, or make a situation worse.
"Bite the bullet" means to force yourself to do something painful, difficult, or unpleasant — even when you really don't want to — with courage and without complaining.
When cold weather or wind is described as biting, it means it is so sharp and fierce that it feels like it is literally cutting into your skin. It is not just "a little cold."
"Bitter" has several distinct but related meanings. It describes something that is harsh, sharp, and unpleasant — whether it's a taste, a feeling, a situation, or even the weather.
In a way that shows deep pain, anger, or resentment, as in "she wept bitterly" or "they argued bitterly." Of weather, it means extremely cold.
The word bitterness describes a sharp, harsh, and deeply unpleasant quality — whether that quality exists in a taste, a feeling, an experience, or even the weather.
Bittersweet describes something that makes you feel happy and sad at the same time — not one after the other, but both emotions together, in the same moment, woven into each other.
A bivouac is a temporary, makeshift camp set up outdoors — usually for just one night — with little to no proper shelter. Think of it as sleeping rough in the open: no cabin, no hotel, often no tent.
Bizarre means strangely unusual to a striking, almost shocking degree — so unusual that it feels hard to explain, hard to believe, or just deeply out of place in the normal world.

To blab means to say things you are not supposed to say — to reveal private information or secrets carelessly, without thinking. The person who blabs lets words escape their mouth when they should have stayed quiet.
To blabber means to talk too much — in a way that is pointless, rambling, or foolish — OR to carelessly reveal information (secrets, private details) that was supposed to stay quiet.
A black hole is a region in space where gravity is so overwhelmingly strong that nothing — not matter, not light, not any signal of any kind — can escape from it once it falls in.
A black market is any place, network, or system where people buy and sell goods or services illegally — meaning outside the rules and oversight of the government or official authorities.
To suddenly lose consciousness for a short time. It can also mean to have all the lights or power go out, or to hide something by covering it in black.
A black sheep is a person who is considered the odd one out, the troublemaker, or the embarrassment of a family or group.

To blackball someone means to deliberately exclude or reject a person from a group, organization, community, or profession — usually as a collective act by a group of people who decide that this person is no longer (or never to be) welcome.
A blackguard is a deeply dishonest, morally corrupt, and contemptible person — someone who has no sense of honor, decency, or conscience.

To blacklist someone or something means to put them on a special list of people or things that are rejected, banned, or blocked — and then to treat them accordingly by refusing to deal with them, hire them, allow them, or trust them.

When you blackmail someone, you make a threat against them to force them into giving you what you want. The threat usually sounds like this: "Do what I say — or I will expose your secret, cause you harm, or ruin you."

A blade is something that is thin, flat, and usually longer than it is wide — like a strip or a sliver. Think of a flat piece of metal, a leaf of grass, or the wing of a fan. That flat, slim shape is what ties all the meanings of "blade" together.
Blameless means deserving no blame. A blameless person is one who did nothing wrong, is not responsible for something bad, and cannot fairly be criticized or held at fault for an outcome.
When a person blanches, their face suddenly loses its color — it goes white or very pale.
Lacking strong, interesting, or stimulating qualities — such as food with little flavour, or something dull and uninspiring.
To blandish someone means to use flattery, sweet talk, and charming, pleasing words or actions to gently persuade them into doing what you want.
A blandishment is a flattering word, a charming compliment, or a pleasing action that someone uses to gently persuade or coax another person into doing something.
When people use "blank cheque" as an idiom, they are no longer talking about money or banking at all.
To cover something completely and evenly over a wide area, as in "snow blanketed the city."
A blanket ban is a complete, total prohibition on something that applies to everyone, everywhere, in all situations — with no exceptions allowed.

When you do something blankly, you do it with absolutely nothing showing — no expression, no emotion, no understanding, no reaction. It is the adverb that describes an empty, expressionless, or uncomprehending way of doing something.

To blare means to produce a sound that is very loud, harsh, and hard to ignore. It is not just any loud sound — it is the kind of sound that forces itself into your ears whether you want it to or not.
Blarney is smooth, charming, flattering talk that sounds pleasant but is not completely sincere or truthful.

To blaspheme means to speak about God, a divine being, or anything considered sacred in a way that is deeply contemptuous, mocking, or disrespectful. It is not merely disagreeing with a religion or doubting its teachings.

Blasphemous is an adjective that describes something — a word, an action, a piece of art, a joke, a statement, or a behavior — that shows deep disrespect, contempt, or irreverence toward God, holy figures, sacred objects, or religion itself.

Blasphemy is the act of speaking, writing, or behaving in a way that deeply disrespects, insults, or shows contempt for something considered sacred — most commonly God, a religion, holy figures, or sacred objects.
A sudden, powerful rush of air or wind, or a violent explosion. Informally, a blast is a very enjoyable experience, as in "the party was a blast."

When you describe someone as blasé, you are saying they are unimpressed, indifferent, or unbothered by something — not because the thing is genuinely boring, but because they have experienced it so many times that it has lost its ability to excite or impress them anymore.
When something is blatant, it means it is so completely obvious and out in the open that it is impossible to miss — and it is done without any shame, guilt, or attempt to hide it.

Blatantly means doing something in a way that is completely open and obvious — with no attempt to hide it, no shame, and no care for what others think. It almost always describes something that is wrong, bad, or inappropriate.

To blate means to make a bleating sound — the weak, wavering cry that a sheep, lamb, or calf makes. Think of a young lamb calling out to its mother: that soft, trembling "baa" is what blating sounds like.
Blather is long, rambling talk or writing that sounds like a lot is being said, but when you really pay attention, almost nothing meaningful is there.
To blather means to talk at great length in a foolish, empty, or pointless way. When someone blathers, they keep going on and on, producing a stream of words that carry little to no real value.

Blaze captures the idea of something that is intensely bright, vivid, and impossible to ignore. Whether it is fire, light, color, or emotion — a blaze is never quiet or subtle. It is always powerful, striking, and demanding of attention.
To blaze means to burn very brightly and strongly — not a gentle, quiet burning, but fire that is big, intense, and dramatic.
To blaze a trail means to be the first person to do something new and important, making it easier for others to follow in your footsteps later.

A blazon is a precise, formal verbal description of a coat of arms — written in a strict, specialized language that tells you exactly what the coat of arms looks like, piece by piece, in a specific order.
To blazon something means to display it very boldly and publicly, or — in a specialized technical context — to describe a coat of arms in precise, formal language. Those are its two main senses.

To bleach something means to remove or strip away its color, making it white, off-white, or much lighter than it originally was. You are not painting over the color or covering it up — you are actually destroying the color itself, from within the material.

Bleaching is the process of removing or destroying color from something, making it appear white, lighter, or colorless. Think of it as the opposite of dyeing — while dyeing adds color, bleaching takes it away.

Bleak describes something that is cold, bare, and completely without warmth, comfort, or hope. Picture a grey, windy, empty field in winter — no shelter, no colour, nothing welcoming anywhere you look. That feeling is bleakness.
"Bleak" describes something that is bare, cold, and empty of anything warm, hopeful, or comforting. It always carries two feelings at once: harshness and hopelessness.
In a way that is cold, bare, and cheerless, or without hope.

Bleary describes eyes — or vision — that are unfocused, watery, and hazy, usually because of tiredness, lack of sleep, or some other physical strain. When your eyes are bleary, they cannot see clearly. Things look foggy and dull rather than sharp and bright.
When a sheep or goat makes its characteristic cry — that soft, wavering, high-pitched sound — it is said to bleat. This is the word's primary, literal meaning.
To bleed someone dry means to take everything from someone — especially their money, resources, energy, or strength — until absolutely nothing is left.
A blemish is a small mark, spot, or flaw that spoils the appearance or quality of something that is otherwise good, clean, or attractive.
To blemish something means to damage or spoil it in a way that leaves a visible flaw or mark — making it less perfect, less attractive, or less pure than it was before.

To blend means to combine two or more things together so smoothly that they form one unified whole — and in that process, the hard boundaries between the individual parts begin to disappear or become difficult to notice.
"Blend in" means to mix into a group or environment so well that you are not noticed or do not stand out.
A blessing is something good — good that is given, received, wished for, or recognized. It almost always carries a feeling of warmth, gratitude, and specialness.
A blight is anything that causes serious harm, decay, or destruction — leaving something much worse than it was before, often in a way that is difficult or impossible to reverse.

To blight something means to severely damage or destroy it — especially in a way that ruins its health, its future, or its ability to grow and thrive. When something is blighted, it does not just get a small setback or a temporary knock.

When something is blighted, it has been severely damaged or ruined — especially in a way that destroys its ability to grow, thrive, or reach its potential. The damage isn't minor or temporary. It is deep, lasting, and often tragic.

Blind means unable to see. A person who is blind cannot perceive light, shapes, or images through their eyes — either partially or completely. The condition can exist from birth or develop later due to illness or injury.
An area your eye cannot see, such as the part of the road a driver cannot see in the mirrors. Figuratively, a subject or weakness a person fails to notice or understand.
Without being able to see. Figuratively, without thinking, questioning, or understanding, as in "blindly following orders."

To blindside someone means to hit them, attack them, or shock them from a direction or angle they never saw coming — leaving them completely unprepared, stunned, and unable to defend themselves or react in time.

A blip is something small, brief, and quickly passing — whether it's a tiny spot of light, a short sound, or a minor event that doesn't change the bigger picture. The word carries a strong sense of smallness and fleetingness.

Bliss means a state of complete and perfect happiness — the kind where nothing feels missing, nothing is wrong, and you feel entirely at peace with the world. It is not just happiness. It is happiness at its highest, fullest, most undisturbed form.
Blissful means experiencing or expressing a state of complete, perfect happiness — the kind of happiness that fills every part of you, leaving no room for worry, sadness, or stress.
A blister is a small, raised bubble of fluid that forms on the surface of your skin. Think of it like a tiny water balloon sitting just under the outermost layer of your skin.
It describes something so extreme in its intensity that it almost feels like it burns.

Blithe means cheerfully unconcerned — having a light, carefree attitude, as if nothing in the world is troubling you. Think of someone who floats through life like a leaf in a gentle breeze: easy, unworried, unbothered.
When someone does something blithely, they do it in a cheerful, carefree way — as if they have not a worry in the world.
Blithesome means having or showing a bright, carefree, lighthearted kind of happiness — the sort of joy that feels effortless, natural, and completely free of worry or heaviness.
A blitzkrieg is a method of warfare built on one simple but devastating idea: attack so fast, so hard, and so unexpectedly that the enemy collapses before they can even respond.
A blizzard is a very severe winter storm. But here is the most important thing to understand right away: a blizzard is not just heavy snowfall.

Bloat means excessive, unwanted swelling or expansion — a condition where something has grown bigger than it should be, filled with stuff that doesn't belong there or isn't needed. The key word is excessive. Bloat isn't just "big."
A bloc is a group of countries, political parties, or people who come together and act as a united force because they share a common goal, interest, or belief.

A blockade is when one party deliberately seals off or surrounds a place — like a city, a country, a port, or a region — to cut off its supply of essential things: food, fuel, weapons, trade goods, or people.
A blockage is anything that blocks, stops, or slows down the movement of something through a space, path, channel, or system.
A blockbuster is something — most often a film — that is a massive, overwhelming success. We're not talking about something that is merely popular or well-liked. A blockbuster is a phenomenon.

Blocking means the act of stopping, obstructing, or deliberately placing/positioning something. This core idea — of halting, holding in place, or arranging — runs through every field where this word appears, though each gives it its own precise flavor.

Blond is an adjective that describes a light yellow or golden color. Think of the warm, pale yellow color of wheat fields, or the golden color of straw — that range of light, yellowish color is what "blond" captures.
Bloodcurdling describes something that is so terrifying, so intensely horrifying, that it produces a violent, immediate, physical reaction of fear in you.
Bloodshed means the killing or wounding of people through violence, especially when it happens on a significant scale.
The bloodstream is the continuous, flowing movement of blood through your body's network of tubes — called blood vessels — at any given moment.
If someone is bloodthirsty, they have a strong, eager desire to kill, hurt, or see violence — and they actually enjoy it or want it. The key idea is not just violence itself, but a craving for it.

Bloom refers to a flower, specifically one that is open or in the process of opening. Think of a single rose fully opened on a bush, or the way cherry trees burst into pink flowers every spring — each of those individual flowers is a bloom.
When something blooms, it opens up, develops fully, and reaches a state of beauty or greatness — often after a period of quiet growth.

To blossom means to open up and become something more beautiful, fuller, or more complete than before. It describes a transformation — a gradual, natural development from a smaller or hidden state into something wonderful and fully alive.
A spot or stain of ink or other liquid. Figuratively, something that spoils or damages a reputation, as in "a blot on his record."

When a liquid — most commonly ink — falls on a surface like paper or cloth and spreads into a messy, irregular patch, it blots that surface. The word captures both the accident and the result: something that was clean now has a dark, spreading mark on it.
Put together literally: a blot on the landscape is something so ugly or out of place that it ruins an otherwise beautiful natural scene — just like an ink stain ruins a clean piece of paper.
To cover something so completely that it can no longer be seen, as when clouds blot out the sun. It can also mean to deliberately erase a painful memory from your mind.
A blotch is a large, messy, irregularly shaped mark or patch that appears on a surface or on skin.
To bloviate means to talk or write for a long time in a pompous, self-important way — while actually saying very little of real value.
A blow is a forceful impact delivered to something or someone — by a fist, a weapon, a hammer, or any hard object.
"Blow away" means wind or air forcefully moves something from one place to another, or carries it out of sight.

When someone "blows their own trumpet," it means they are praising themselves, boasting about their own achievements, or drawing attention to how great they are — usually in a way that other people find annoying or unnecessary.

To blow something out of proportion means to treat a small or minor problem as if it were much bigger, more serious, or more important than it actually is. In other words, it means to exaggerate or overreact to something.
When a problem, argument, or scandal blows over, it gradually fades and is forgotten without causing serious harm.
To "blow the whistle" means to expose or report someone's wrongdoing, dishonesty, or illegal activity — usually to a person in authority or to the public.
To explode, or to destroy something with an explosion. It can also mean to suddenly become very angry, to fill something with air, or to enlarge a photograph.

A blowhard is a person who talks loudly and endlessly about how great, smart, knowledgeable, or important they are — but whose big talk is mostly empty air. The word captures two things at once: the volume of their talking and the hollowness behind it.

"Blowing" as an adjective describes something that is being moved, carried, or driven through the air by wind — or something that is actively and noticeably producing or experiencing strong air movement.
When a tyre suddenly bursts. Informally, a blowout is also a big party or lavish meal, or an easy, one-sided victory.
Blubber is the thick, soft layer of fat that sits just beneath the skin of certain sea animals — most famously whales, but also seals, walruses, and dolphins.

To blubber means to cry loudly, messily, and in an uncontrolled way — so hard that your body shakes, your face scrunches up, your nose runs, and you can barely speak properly. It is not quiet, elegant crying.
A bludgeon is a heavy, thick stick used as a weapon to beat or strike someone.
To bludgeon someone means to hit them hard and repeatedly with a heavy object — or, in a figurative sense, to force or pressure someone aggressively into doing or accepting something.
The most fundamental meaning of blue is a color — the color of a clear daytime sky, deep ocean water, or a sapphire gem. It is a cool, calm color.

When you do something "until you are blue in the face," it means you do it for a very long time, repeatedly, and with great effort — but it makes no difference. The result does not change. Nobody listens. Nothing works. All that effort is completely wasted.
When you call something blue-collar, you are describing work, workers, or anything connected to jobs that primarily involve physical or manual labor, skilled trades, or operating machinery.
The word bluegrass has two distinct meanings as a noun: one refers to a type of plant, and the other to a genre of music. Both are deeply connected to the American state of Kentucky.
A blueprint is a detailed, precise plan that shows exactly how something should be built, created, or achieved — step by step, piece by piece, with nothing left vague or to guesswork.

When someone says they "have the blues," they mean they are feeling sad, low, or gloomy. It is not quite full-on depression — it is more like a soft, lingering unhappiness. You feel a bit flat, unmotivated, or melancholic.

To bluff means to pretend you are in a stronger, more confident, or more capable position than you actually are, in order to trick someone into believing it — and to gain some kind of advantage as a result.
A blunder is a mistake — but not just any mistake. It is a mistake that is serious, embarrassing, and avoidable, usually caused by carelessness, poor judgment, or a shocking lack of thought.
To blunder means to make a serious mistake — usually because of carelessness, poor judgment, or not thinking carefully enough before acting.
When something physical is described as blunt, it means its edge or tip is dull — worn down or never sharp to begin with. It cannot cut, pierce, or slice cleanly the way a sharp object can.
To blunt something means to reduce its sharpness, strength, or power — to make something that was once forceful, intense, or effective become weaker and less powerful.
Bluntness is the quality of saying exactly what you think or feel — directly, plainly, and without softening your words to protect someone's feelings.

To blur means to make something unclear, or to become unclear — so unclear that the edges, details, or differences are hard to see, think about, or understand. Think of it as the opposite of "sharpening."
A blurb is a short piece of writing that describes something — usually a book, a film, a product, or a person — in a way that makes it sound appealing and worth your attention.
Blurred describes something that is not clear, not sharp, or not well-defined — something whose edges, details, or divisions are difficult to make out.
To blurt something means to say it suddenly, without thinking first — especially when you probably should have kept it to yourself.
To blurt out something means to say it suddenly, without thinking first, and without being able to stop yourself.
To blush means for your face — especially your cheeks — to turn red or pink because of an emotion. It's your body's visible reaction to how you feel inside.
To bluster means to speak or behave in a loud, aggressive, and threatening way — but without real power, substance, or follow-through behind it.
Blustery most commonly describes a type of weather — specifically, weather dominated by strong, rough, gusty wind. Not a gentle breeze. Not even a steady strong wind.
A large, non-venomous snake that kills its prey by squeezing it. A boa is also a long, fluffy scarf made of feathers.
A flat, rigid piece of wood or other hard material. A board is also a group of people who control a company or organization, or the meals provided by a hotel.
A boardroom is a room inside a company or organization that is specifically designed and reserved for important, high-level meetings — particularly meetings held by the board of directors.

To boast means to talk about yourself — or something connected to you — with too much pride, making yourself sound better, more impressive, or more important than others might think is necessary or appropriate.

Boastful describes a person who talks about themselves — their achievements, possessions, abilities, or experiences — in an excessive, show-off way, usually to make others see them as impressive or superior.
A bobbin is a small spool — a cylindrical object with wider rims on each end — around which thread, yarn, or wire is wound for storage and controlled release.
Bodacious is an informal adjective that means something (or someone) is so impressively bold, remarkable, or outstanding that it demands your attention and admiration.
"Bode" means to be a sign of something that is likely to happen in the future.
If something bodes well, it means it is a good sign that something positive will happen in the future.

A bodega is a small, independently owned neighborhood store — the kind of place you duck into quickly to grab a snack, a drink, a can of soup, a pack of cigarettes, or a bottle of hot sauce at 11 PM. It's not a supermarket and it's not a fancy specialty shop.
A bodice is the upper portion of a woman's garment — specifically, the section that covers the torso from the shoulders or neckline down to the waist. Think of any dress you have ever seen.
The adjective bodily simply means "of, relating to, or belonging to the physical body."

Body language is the use of physical behavior, movements, expressions, and postures to communicate feelings, attitudes, intentions, and reactions — either consciously (on purpose) or unconsciously (without realizing it).

A bog is a type of wetland — a piece of land that is permanently waterlogged, soft, and spongy. Think of it as ground that is so soaked with water that it behaves almost like a very thick liquid rather than solid earth.
To bog down means to slow down so much that you can barely make progress — or stop making progress altogether — usually because of something heavy, complicated, or overwhelming.
"Bog-standard" means completely ordinary, plain, and basic — with nothing special, extra, or impressive about it.

A bogeyman is an imaginary, frightening creature — a monster that does not actually exist in reality, but lives powerfully in people's minds, especially in children's fears. Think of it as the ultimate "made-up thing to be scared of."

When something boggles you, it overwhelms your mind so completely that you struggle to fully understand or accept it. Your brain, in a sense, hits a wall. You're not simply surprised — you're stunned to the point where thinking clearly becomes difficult.

"Boggling" describes something so extreme, vast, or complex that your brain struggles to fully process or comprehend it. When something is boggling, it doesn't just surprise you — it overwhelms your ability to think clearly about it.

Boggy describes land (or a surface) that is soft, wet, and spongy — land that sinks or squelches under your weight because it is soaked with water and made of loose, waterlogged soil or decayed plant matter.
Bogus means not real, not genuine, or not what it claims to be. It describes something that is fake, false, or designed to deceive — something that pretends to be real but isn't.

Bohemian describes a person, lifestyle, or atmosphere that is free, creative, and unconventional — one that deliberately rejects the ordinary rules, routines, and expectations that most of society follows.
A person who lives an unconventional, artistic, free-spirited life outside the norms of mainstream society.
"Boil down to" means to reach the most essential, fundamental truth of something after removing all the complexity, details, and noise around it.
When a liquid boils over, it rises and spills over the top of its container. Figuratively, when emotions or tensions boil over, they suddenly erupt into anger or violence.

Boiling as an adjective means something has reached — or feels like it has reached — a state of extreme, intense heat. Think of a pot of water on a stove when it's bubbling and steaming violently: that is literally boiling.
Boisterous describes a person, group, or behavior that is loudly energetic, lively, and somewhat unrestrained — usually in a cheerful, high-spirited way.

Bold means not holding back. Whether it describes a person, an action, a decision, or even a visual design, "bold" always carries the idea of something that steps forward confidently, stands out clearly, and does not shrink or hide.
With courage, confidence, and openness — without fear or hesitation. It can also mean in a way that is strikingly clear, as in "a boldly coloured painting."
Boldness is the quality of being willing to act, speak, or behave in a strong, confident, and courageous way — especially in situations where most people would hesitate, stay quiet, or play it safe.

A bollard is a short, sturdy, vertical post — thick and strong, firmly fixed in place. Think of it as a small but solid pillar, usually no taller than your waist, designed to either stop things or tie things.
To bolster something means to strengthen or reinforce it, especially when it is already there but feels weak, shaky, or not convincing enough.
A bolt is a metal rod — usually made of steel — with a flat or rounded head on one end and a spiral groove (called a thread) on the other end.
When a person or animal bolts, they run away very suddenly — often out of fear, panic, or the desire to escape. The key idea is surprise + speed. It's not a planned, calm exit. It's an abrupt dash.
"A bolt from the blue" means something that happens suddenly and completely without any warning — something so unexpected that it shocks or surprises you deeply.
A hypothetical, self-aware brain that forms spontaneously from random fluctuations in the universe, used by physicists to test theories about the nature of reality.

To bombard something or someone means to hit a target with a large, continuous, relentless stream of something — so much and so fast that the target feels overwhelmed, under siege, and unable to escape.

Bombardment means the act of hitting something continuously, heavily, and repeatedly — whether with physical weapons, particles of matter, or even non-physical things like words, questions, or messages.

Bombast is language — spoken or written — that sounds grand, powerful, and impressive, but is actually hollow and empty underneath. It is big words, dramatic statements, and inflated claims that carry very little real meaning or truth.
Bombastic describes language — speech or writing — that sounds grand, powerful, and deeply impressive on the surface, but is actually hollow and empty underneath.
A shocking piece of news that comes completely unexpectedly. A bombshell is also used informally for a strikingly attractive woman.

A bon mot is a short, clever, and witty remark — one that is not just funny, but brilliantly phrased. It's the kind of thing someone says in conversation that makes everyone stop, smile, and think, "That was perfectly said."
A bon-bon is a small, sweet confection — in other words, a bite-sized candy or sweet treat. Think of it as a tiny little piece of something sweet that you can pop into your mouth in one or two bites.

"Bona fide" means genuine, real, and authentic — exactly what something or someone claims to be. When you call something bona fide, you are saying: this is the real thing, not a fake, not an imitation, not a trick.

A bonanza is a sudden, large source of great wealth, profit, or something extremely valuable and desirable. Think of it as a moment or a situation where good things — usually money or resources — flow in much, much more than expected or than usual.

A bond is something that connects, holds, or ties things together — whether those things are people, objects, atoms, or agreements. Think of it as an invisible or visible "link" between two or more things.
To bond means to join or connect things — or people — so closely that they become firmly tied to each other.
Bonding means the process of forming a strong connection or union between two or more things — whether those things are people, atoms, materials, or legal/financial entities.

A bone is one of the hard, rigid pieces that form the internal framework inside the body of a human or animal. All these bones together make up the skeleton — the structural "scaffolding" that holds your body up and gives it its shape.

A "bone of contention" is a specific issue, topic, or matter that causes disagreement or argument between two or more people (or groups). It is the central point around which a conflict or dispute revolves.
When someone says "I have a bone to pick with you," it means they are unhappy about something you did or said, and they want to talk about it, discuss it, or sort it out.
Bonhomie means a warm, easy, cheerful friendliness — the quality of being genuinely good-natured in a way that makes everyone around you feel comfortable and welcome.
Bonkers is an informal adjective that means crazy, wildly irrational, or completely absurd.
A bonus is something extra — something you receive on top of what you were already supposed to get. It goes beyond the normal, the expected, or the agreed amount.
So thin that the bones show, as in "bony fingers." Of fish, it means full of small bones.
A booby trap is a hidden danger that is triggered by the victim themselves, usually without any warning.
A boogeyman is an imaginary, frightening creature — a monster — that does not actually exist in reality. It is not a specific-looking monster with a fixed shape or face.
"Boogie" refers to a type of lively, rhythmic music — specifically, an upbeat style of blues music originally played on the piano, often called boogie-woogie.
Bookish describes a person who loves books deeply — someone who reads a lot, studies a lot, and feels most at home in the world of books and ideas.

Bookkeeping is the practice of systematically recording every single financial transaction of a business — every penny that comes in and every penny that goes out — in an organized, consistent, and accurate manner.
A booklet is a small, thin book with relatively few pages, usually held together with staples, stitching, or glue, and covered with a soft paper cover rather than a hard one.
A bookmark is a tool — physical or digital — that marks a specific spot so you can return to it easily later, without having to search for it all over again.

A boom is a sound that is loud, low-pitched, and heavy — the kind of sound that you can almost feel in your chest. It is not a sharp, high-pitched noise like a squeak or a crack. It is deep and powerful, like it comes from something massive.
"Boom" as a verb has two main branches of meaning — one about sound and one about rapid growth. Each branch has a natural extension. At the heart of every meaning is one idea: force and power.
A repeated pattern in an economy of a period of rapid growth and prosperity followed by a sudden collapse.
Of a plan or action, to come back and harm the person who started it, as in "the scheme boomeranged on him."
Of a sound, loud, deep, and powerful, as in "a booming voice." Of a business or economy, growing quickly and very successfully.
A boon is something that is extremely helpful, beneficial, or welcome — something that makes a situation, a life, or the world noticeably better.
A boondoggle is a project or activity that wastes money, time, and effort while producing little or no real, useful result — yet is often dressed up to look like meaningful, important work.

A boor is a person who is rude, crude, and socially unpleasant — someone who lacks basic manners and the social awareness to behave decently around others. The word is a strong, somewhat formal insult.
Boorish is an adjective used to describe a person or their behavior as rough, rude, and unpleasant — in a way that shows a complete lack of good manners, sensitivity, and social awareness.

To boost something means to push it upward — either literally (physically) or figuratively (in terms of amount, power, strength, or quality). Think of it as giving something a lift — making it go higher, grow bigger, or become better than it was before.
A "booster" is anything (or anyone) that raises, strengthens, or supports something that already exists.
A booth is a small, enclosed or partially enclosed space or structure built for a specific, limited purpose.
When something is described as bootleg, it means it is illegally made, copied, or sold — without the permission of the person or company who has the legal right to make or sell it.
A bootlegger is a person who produces, transports, or sells something — usually goods or media — illegally, specifically without government permission and without paying the required taxes or fees.
Bootless means producing no result; achieving nothing; completely useless or futile.
To bootlick means to try to win the favor of someone powerful by being excessively flattering, agreeable, and submissive — not out of genuine respect, but purely for personal gain.
To bootstrap something means to build, start, or improve something using only what you already have — your own resources, efforts, or existing tools — without relying on outside help.

Booze means alcoholic drinks — any drink that contains alcohol and has the power to make a person drunk if they consume enough of it. Think of beer, wine, whiskey, vodka, rum, gin, or any other drink in that category.

The noun border means an edge or a dividing line between two areas. When used as a verb, the idea stays the same at heart — it means something acts as a border, sits at the edge of something, or comes very close to a certain state or quality.
It describes something that sits right at the edge between two categories, two conditions, or two judgments, making it genuinely difficult to decide which side it belongs to.
To drill a hole or tunnel through something. It also means to make someone feel weary through dullness. "Bore" is also the past tense of "bear."

Boreal means of or relating to the north — specifically, the far north of our planet. When you see this word describing something, it is telling you that thing belongs to, comes from, or is characteristic of the cold, northern parts of the Earth.
Born with a silver spoon in one's mouth
When we say someone was "born with a silver spoon in their mouth," we mean that person was born into a wealthy, privileged family.
A borough is a town, district, or area that has its own local government — or one that has been given a special official status by a higher authority (like a national or state government).
To borrow a page from someone means to copy or adopt their method, strategy, or idea — usually because it worked well for them and you want to use it yourself.
Borscht is a type of soup. More specifically, it is a hearty, cooked soup that is most famous for being a deep, vivid red or purple-red color.
Boscage means a thick, dense mass of trees and shrubs growing together — essentially a small, bushy woodland or a heavy thicket.
An exotic state of matter that forms when certain particles are cooled almost to absolute zero, so that they stop behaving as individuals and act together as one single quantum "super-particle."

"Bosh" means nonsense — talk, writing, or ideas that are foolish, empty, and completely without substance or truth. When you call something "bosh," you're saying it is so hollow and worthless that it doesn't even deserve to be taken seriously.
Bosky means covered with, or full of, trees, bushes, and shrubs — thick with wild plant growth.
A person's chest, especially a woman's. Figuratively, the bosom of something is a place of safety and closeness, as in "the bosom of the family."

To boss someone around means to tell people what to do in a rude, controlling, or bossy way — especially when you have no real right or authority to do so, or when you do it more than is necessary or acceptable.
Botanical simply means "of, relating to, or involving plants."

A botanist is a scientist who studies plants — professionally, deeply, and systematically. It is their job (or life's work) to understand everything about the plant world: what plants are, how they work, how they grow, where they live, and why they matter.

Botany is the branch of science that is dedicated to the study of plants — what they are, how they work, how they grow, where they live, and how they relate to other living things and the environment.
To botch something means to do it so poorly, carelessly, or clumsily that the result is ruined, messy, or a complete failure.

Botched means badly and carelessly ruined during execution — especially when the task required skill, care, or precision, and the person either lacked that skill, was negligent, or made serious errors that left things damaged or completely failed.
A reaction to a situation, such as a crisis or emergency, that is handled so badly that it fails or makes the problem worse.
Bother means to cause some kind of trouble or discomfort — whether that trouble is emotional (annoyance, worry), physical (pain), social (interrupting someone), or mental (making an effort).
To hold your feelings or emotions tightly inside yourself instead of expressing them.
A bottleneck is a single point in a process, system, or flow where things slow down, get restricted, or get stuck — and because of that one narrow point, the entire system is held back.
The final total on a company's financial statement, showing its profit or loss. More generally, the bottom line is the most important fact or conclusion in a situation.
To reach the lowest point of a decline and stop falling any further, as in "prices have bottomed out."

Bottom-up describes any process, approach, or system where things start from the lowest level — from individuals, small parts, or fine details — and move upward toward the big picture, the leadership, or the whole.

A boudoir is a woman's private room — a personal, intimate space in a home where she can withdraw from everyone else. Think of it as a room that belongs entirely to her: a place to dress, rest, reflect, write letters, or simply be alone.
A bough is a large, main branch of a tree — one of the big, thick arms that grow outward from the trunk.

Bouillon is a clear, thin, savory liquid made by simmering ingredients — such as meat, fish, poultry, vegetables, or bones — in water, and then straining everything out so that only the flavored liquid remains.
A boulder is a very large, naturally occurring rock. It is so large that a single person cannot lift it, and it typically requires heavy machinery (like a crane or bulldozer) to move it.
To recover and return to a good condition after something bad, difficult, or painful happened.

A bouncer is a person who is hired to stand at the entrance of a place like a nightclub, bar, pub, music concert, or private party. Think of them as the "gatekeeper" — they decide who is allowed inside and who is not.
"Bound" as an adjective has several distinct meanings. Something that is "bound" is never completely free — it is always connected, restricted, or pointed somewhere.

"Bound for" means "heading toward a destination" or "on the way to a place." When you say something or someone is bound for somewhere, you are saying that their journey has a clear, definite target — a specific place they are going to reach.
"Bound up with" means that two things are so deeply and closely connected to each other that you cannot fully understand, think about, or separate one without the other.
A boundary is a line, point, or limit that marks where one thing ends and another begins. It separates two things from each other.
A bounder is a man who behaves in a dishonourable, unscrupulous, or socially unacceptable way — particularly someone who violates the standards of decent, gentlemanly conduct.
Boundless means having no limits, no edges, and no end. It describes something so immense, so great, or so wide that you cannot find — or even imagine — where it stops.
"Bountiful" means large in amount, more than enough, and generously given. Think of it as a combination of two ideas packed into one word: a lot of something, and a warm, generous spirit behind it.

Bounty is a word about giving generously — but it has stretched over time to cover a few closely related ideas. In every single meaning, something valuable is being offered, given, or received, usually in a large or generous amount.
The word bouquet has two distinct, well-established meanings. Both share a common thread: the idea of many things coming together to form something pleasing.
Typical of the comfortable, property-owning middle class and its values, tastes, and attitudes, often used to suggest a dull concern with respectability and money.
A member of the middle class, especially someone who owns property or a business and lives a comfortable, conventional life.
The bourgeoisie refers to a social class — specifically, the class of people who own property, businesses, and capital, and who sit above the working class in society's economic hierarchy.

A bout is a distinct, concentrated period of something — a stretch of time where something happens with noticeable intensity before it ends. Think of it as a clear episode with a beginning and an end.

A boutique is a small shop — but not just any small shop. It's one that sells a carefully chosen selection of specialized, fashionable, or high-quality goods, and where the experience of shopping feels personal and curated rather than mass-market and generic.

A boutonniere is a small, carefully arranged decoration made of one or a few flowers — sometimes with leaves, small berries, or other delicate greenery — that a person wears pinned to the front of a jacket or suit.
Relating to cattle. Used of a person, it means slow, dull, and placid, like a cow.
A bovine is any animal that belongs to the cattle family — a group of large, plant-eating, hoofed mammals. Think of a cow, a bull, a buffalo, or a bison. Each of these is a bovine.

"Bow out" means to withdraw from something voluntarily and gracefully. It means to step aside, quit, or leave a role, situation, competition, or responsibility — usually in a calm, dignified, and respectful way.

To bowdlerize something means to remove or alter parts of a book, film, play, or any creative work because someone considers those parts offensive, indecent, or morally inappropriate — and to do so in a way that is excessive, overzealous, and damaging to the original work.
A pleasant, shady place under trees or climbing plants in a garden or wood.
To greatly surprise or impress someone, as in "I was bowled over by the view." Literally, it means to knock someone down.
To surround someone so that they cannot move or escape. Figuratively, to restrict someone's choices so that they feel trapped.
A boy is a male child — a young person who is male and has not yet grown into an adult. This is the word's most fundamental and common meaning.
A boycott is when a person or a group of people deliberately refuse to buy, use, support, or participate in something — as a way to protest against it and pressure it to change.
To boycott something means to deliberately refuse to buy, use, or participate in it — as a way of protesting against it or pressuring it to change.

To brace means to make something firm and steady so it can resist pressure, force, or a difficult impact. Think of it as the act of preparing something — your body, your mind, or a physical object — to hold strong against something coming at it.

Something or someone that is braced is in a firm, steady, ready state — prepared to withstand a force, a blow, or a difficulty. The key feeling behind the word is deliberate firmness under anticipated pressure.

A bracero is a Mexican laborer — specifically a male one — who travels to the United States to work, usually doing physically demanding, low-wage jobs in agriculture or on railroads. The word is used in both Spanish and English.

When something is bracing, it hits you with a sharp, fresh energy that wakes you up, clears your head, and makes you feel alive and alert. It is stimulating — but with an edge. Think of it like a splash of cold water on your face in the morning.

Bracken is a type of large, wild fern — one of the most common and widespread plants on Earth. It belongs to the genus Pteridium, and you'll find it growing in fields, hillsides, moorlands, open woodlands, and heathlands across almost every continent.

The most concrete meaning of "bracket" is a piece of hardware used to support or hold something up. Picture a rigid piece of metal or wood shaped like the letter L. The short side is fixed to a wall, and the long side sticks out horizontally.
Of water, slightly salty, as found where a river meets the sea.
To brag means to talk about yourself — your achievements, your possessions, your talents, or your life — in a way that makes you sound better, more impressive, or more special than others.
Braggadocio means empty, exaggerated boasting — the kind of loud, puffed-up self-promotion that has little or no truth behind it.

A braggart is a person who constantly, excessively, and annoyingly boasts about themselves — their achievements, skills, wealth, possessions, looks, or experiences — usually to make others feel impressed or inferior.
To braid means to take three or more separate strands and weave them over and under each other — in a specific, repeating crossing pattern — until they form a single, unified structure.
The large-scale departure of highly skilled and educated people from one country to another, usually where pay and conditions are better.
The word brain-dead describes a state of complete mental absence — either literally (the brain has permanently stopped working) or figuratively (someone is being extremely stupid or mindless).
A brainchild is an original idea, plan, invention, project, or creation that came directly from one particular person's mind — and that person is considered its creator or "parent."

When you brainstorm, you rapidly generate as many ideas as possible about a topic or problem — freely, openly, and without stopping to judge whether each idea is good or bad. The goal is quantity first, quality later.
In common, everyday language, a brainwave is a sudden, clever idea that arrives in your mind unexpectedly — especially one that solves a problem you've been struggling with.
When you describe food as braised, you are saying that it was cooked using a specific two-step method — first seared in hot fat, then slowly cooked in a small amount of liquid inside a covered pot.
A bramble is a wild, prickly plant — specifically, a shrub with tough, thorny or spiny stems that tends to grow in a wild, tangled, spreading way.

"Branch out" is a phrasal verb. It means to go beyond what you normally do and try something new, different, or wider in scope. It describes the act of expanding your activities, interests, skills, or focus into areas you haven't explored before.
A brand is a mark that identifies something and sets it apart from everything else. Everything else the word means grows from this one core idea.
The creation and promotion of a distinctive name, image, and identity for a product or company. Literally, the act of burning an identifying mark onto an animal's skin with a hot iron.
To brandish something means to wave or hold up an object in a bold, dramatic way — usually to threaten someone, or to show it off confidently and aggressively.
Brash means being overly bold, loud, and self-confident in a way that is rude, tactless, or unpleasant to others.

When someone says "let's get down to brass tacks," they mean: "Let's stop wasting time on unimportant things and focus on what really matters — the core facts, the real issue, or the most essential and practical details."
Bravado is a show of boldness or confidence that is exaggerated, put on, or not completely genuine — often used to hide fear, weakness, or self-doubt, or to impress and intimidate others.
When you describe someone — or something they do — as brave, you mean they chose to face something frightening, dangerous, painful, or very difficult, and they did it anyway.
Bravery is the quality of being willing to face danger, pain, fear, difficulty, or something deeply uncomfortable — and choosing to act anyway, despite feeling that fear.
Bravura is the quality of doing something with brilliant, dazzling skill — performed in a bold, confident, and often showy way that leaves people in awe. It is not just about being good at something.

A brawl is a rough, noisy, and chaotic fight — usually between a group of people, or at least more than one person — that happens in a public or semi-public place. It is unplanned, messy, and out of control.
To brawl means to fight physically in a rough, noisy, and disorderly way. It is not a calm, controlled, or organized fight.
Physical strength and muscle, as in "brains and brawn." In British cooking, brawn is also a type of pressed meat made from a pig's head.

Brawny describes someone who is physically strong and visibly muscular. When you call a person brawny, you are saying two things at once: they have large, well-developed muscles, and those muscles give them real, impressive physical power.

A bray is the loud, harsh, grating cry that a donkey makes — that unmistakable "hee-haw" sound. It is the standard, accepted word for a donkey's call, the same way "bark" is the word for a dog's sound or "roar" is the word for a lion's sound.

To bray most fundamentally means to make the loud, harsh, grating cry that a donkey (or mule) makes. You know that rough, almost comical "hee-haw" sound a donkey produces — that is called braying. When a donkey does this, you say the donkey brays.
Brazen means doing something wrong, rude, or socially unacceptable in a completely open and bold way — with absolutely no shame, guilt, or embarrassment.

To brazen it out means to face an embarrassing, accusatory, or difficult situation with bold, shameless confidence — without admitting guilt, backing down, or showing any sign of shame, even when you know you are wrong or have been caught.
A metal container on legs that holds burning coal or charcoal, used for heating or cooking outdoors.

A breach is a break — a moment or result of something being broken, torn open, or violated. That one idea — a break — stretches across physical, legal, and social situations, and that is why this word appears in so many different contexts.
To breach something means to break through something that was supposed to hold, or to break something that was supposed to be kept.
Your main source of income or living, as in "teaching is my bread and butter." It can also describe something basic and everyday, as in "bread-and-butter issues."

A breadcrumb is a tiny fragment or crumb that breaks off from a piece of bread. When you bite into a crusty baguette, slice a loaf, or pull apart a roll, the little bits that fall onto your plate or your lap — those are breadcrumbs.

Breadth means width — the measurement of how far something extends from one side to the other. If you measure a swimming pool and find it stretches 10 meters from the left wall to the right wall, that 10 meters is its breadth.
A breadwinner is a person who earns money to financially support their family or household.
"Break a leg" is a way of wishing someone good luck — but without actually saying "good luck."
When a machine breaks down, it stops working. When a person breaks down, they lose control of their emotions and cry. It can also mean to fail, or to divide something into smaller parts.
To break even means to reach a point where your gains and your losses are exactly equal — so you end up right back where you started, with no profit and no loss.
To enter a building illegally by force. It can also mean to interrupt a conversation, or to use new shoes or equipment until they become comfortable.
To end a relationship, discussion, or agreement suddenly. It can also mean to stop talking, or to separate a piece from something by snapping it.
When something such as war, fire, or disease breaks out, it starts suddenly. It can also mean to escape from prison, or for spots to appear on the skin.
To publicly disagree with, or act against, the group, organization, or authority you belong to — especially when others in that group are staying silent or going along.

To "break the ice" means to do or say something that helps people feel more comfortable and relaxed, especially in an awkward, tense, or unfamiliar social situation — like when strangers first meet, or when a conversation feels stiff and uneasy.
To do something in a completely new and different way that has not been done before.
When two people in a romantic relationship decide to stop being together, they "break up." The relationship that was once "whole" has now "come apart."
The word breakdown comes from the idea of something falling apart, failing, or being divided into smaller pieces.
Breakneck means so dangerously fast that something could go terribly wrong.

A breakthrough is a sudden, significant achievement or discovery that solves a difficult problem — one that had been blocking progress for a long time. Think of it like a wall that nobody could get past.

Breakup describes the ending or falling apart of something that was once together — whether that "something" is a relationship, an organization, a physical object, or even a season. The key idea is always: unity → separation.

Breaststroke is one of the four major swimming strokes — a specific, defined way of moving your body through water to travel forward. The other three are freestyle (front crawl), backstroke, and butterfly.
Someone or something that is pleasantly new, different, and refreshing, especially after a long period of something dull or tiresome.
To watch or supervise someone so closely that it creates pressure and discomfort. It can also mean to be close behind someone in a race or competition.
To breathe new life into something means to make something old, tired, boring, failing, or forgotten become fresh, exciting, active, and full of energy again.
Breathless means that someone is struggling to breathe normally, usually because of physical effort or a medical reason.
Breathtaking means something is so overwhelmingly impressive, beautiful, surprising, or extreme that it almost steals the air from your lungs — even if just for a split second.
The word breech has a few distinct but related meanings, all of which circle around the same central idea: the back end or rear-bottom part of something.
Breeches are a type of clothing for the lower body — think of them as trousers, but ones that stop just below the knee rather than going all the way down to the ankle.
Breed means to cause something new to come into existence from something that already exists — whether that "something new" is a living baby animal, a type of creature, a feeling, or a situation.
"Breeding" refers to the process of producing new life — whether that's animals giving birth, plants producing seeds, or humans deliberately controlling which animals or plants reproduce.
A breeding ground is a place or a situation where something grows, multiplies, and spreads very easily — because the conditions there are perfectly suited for it to do so.

A breeze is a gentle, light wind — the kind that is mild, pleasant, and refreshing. It is not a storm. It is not a gust. It is simply calm, moving air that you can feel on your skin without it being harsh or violent.
Breezy describes something that feels light, fresh, and effortless — like a gentle wind that moves through on a pleasant day.
"Brethren" is simply a formal, old-fashioned plural form of the word "brother." It means "brothers" or "fellow members of a group."
A book containing the daily prayers, psalms, and readings that Catholic priests and other clergy are required to recite at set times each day.
Brevity means the quality of using few words or taking little time — of being short and to the point, without saying more than is needed.
Brew means to create something by letting things slowly mix, combine, or develop over time — usually involving heat, soaking, or a gradual buildup.
When "brewing" is used as an adjective, it describes something bad (or at least serious) that is quietly developing in the background — not fully here yet, but clearly on its way.

To bribe someone means to secretly offer them money or something valuable so that they will do something in your favor — something they are not supposed to do, or something that goes against their duty, rules, or conscience.

Bribery is the act of giving or offering something valuable to a person — usually someone in a position of power or authority — to secretly influence their decision or behavior in your favor. It also covers the act of receiving or asking for such a thing.

Bric-a-brac refers to a random collection of small, miscellaneous objects — typically decorative — that people keep around their homes, usually displayed on shelves, mantlepieces, windowsills, or inside cabinets.

Bricks and mortar are the two essential materials used to construct physical buildings. Without mortar, the bricks would just be a loose pile. Without bricks, the mortar has nothing to hold together. They depend on each other.

A bridesmaid is a woman or girl who is chosen by a bride to be part of her wedding and to support her throughout the wedding experience. Think of a bridesmaid as a bride's closest helper and companion during one of the most important events of her life.
A bridge is something that spans a gap to create a connection where one didn't exist before. Everything this word means — whether physical, figurative, or technical — flows from this single idea.
"Bridge the gap" means to reduce or eliminate a difference, disconnect, or divide between two things so they can come closer together or work together better.
A bridle is a set of straps and fittings placed over a horse's head that gives a rider or handler direct control over the horse's movements — where it goes, how fast it moves, and when it stops.
To show sudden anger or offence, typically by stiffening and pulling the head back, as in "she bridled at the suggestion." Literally, it means to put a bridle on a horse.
Simply: fitted with a bridle. A bridled horse is a horse that has its bridle on — it is physically equipped with the restraining headgear and is under control.
When something is brief, it is short — either in time or in words.
To brief someone means to give them the key information they need, before they do something or deal with something.
A briefing is a focused session — or a document — in which someone gives a person or a group the key information they need to know about a particular situation, task, or event.
"Briefly" always signals shortness — but there are two kinds of shortness it can refer to: shortness in time, and shortness in expression (words used).

A brig is a sailing vessel with exactly two tall vertical poles (called masts) and a specific sail arrangement. The sails on both masts hang horizontally from crossbeams — stretched sideways like a wide, rectangular sheet.

A brigade is an organized group of people who come together with a shared purpose or goal. The word almost always suggests that the group has some structure to it — not just a random collection of people, but people who are working in a coordinated way.
A brigand is an armed robber and outlaw, typically one who is part of a gang, and who operates in wild or remote places like mountains, forests, or rural countryside.
Brighten means to make something brighter, or to become brighter. Think of it as the action of adding or gaining brightness — more light, more colour, more happiness, or more hope.

Brilliance means an exceptional, striking, standout quality — whether that quality is light, intelligence, talent, or the execution of something remarkable. Think of it as the noun form of "brilliant," which itself means outstandingly impressive.
Brilliant means something that stands out powerfully — either because it shines with intense light, bursts with vivid color, or rises far above ordinary quality, intelligence, or talent.
The word brim has two distinct but related meanings. Both meanings share the same core idea: the top or outermost edge of something.
To brim means to be so completely, absolutely full of something that it reaches the very top edge — and is on the verge of spilling over, or is just barely contained.
Filled right to the top, almost overflowing. Figuratively, full of a feeling or quality, as in "brimming with confidence" or "eyes brimming with tears."
Brimstone is simply sulfur — a naturally occurring, bright yellow mineral found in the earth. It's the same substance chemists today call sulfur.
Brindled describes a coat or surface that has a warm base colour — such as brown, tan, or grey — streaked or patched with darker markings.
Brine is water with a very high amount of salt dissolved in it — much saltier than ordinary drinking water, and generally saltier than typical seawater as well.
"Bring about" means to cause something to happen or to make something happen, especially a change, a result, or a new situation.
When you "bring down" a number, a price, a temperature, or any measurable level, it means to make it lower or smaller.

When you "bring forward" an event, meeting, appointment, or deadline, you reschedule it to happen sooner than originally planned. You are pulling it closer toward the present — that is the "forward" part.
"Bring home the bacon" means to earn money to support yourself or your family. It can also mean to achieve success in a broader sense — like winning a competition or completing a challenging task.
"Bring out" means to cause something to move from a hidden, inner, or stored state to a visible, active, or public state.
To make someone regain consciousness after fainting. It can also mean to persuade someone to change their mind and agree with you.
To bring someone to account means to make a person face the consequences of their wrong actions and explain or answer for what they did.

When something is "brought to a head," it means a situation — usually a problem, conflict, or tension that has been quietly building up for a long time — is finally forced to reach its critical, decisive point.
"Bring to bear" means to apply something — a skill, power, resource, influence, or knowledge — in a focused and purposeful way toward a goal or target.
"Bring to light" means to reveal something that was previously hidden, unknown, or secret — and make it known to others.
To "bring to the table" means to offer or contribute something valuable — such as a skill, idea, quality, experience, money, or resource — to a group, situation, or discussion.
When you bring up a child, you take care of them, educate them, and guide them from childhood until they become an adult.
It is the extreme edge of something, the final point before a major change begins.
Brinkmanship is the deliberate act of pushing a dangerous situation right to the very edge of disaster — as a strategy to force your opponent to back down.
Briny means having a strong, sharp saltiness — specifically the kind you associate with the sea, ocean water, or a concentrated salt solution.
Brio means a lively, energetic, and spirited quality — the kind of vibrant confidence and enthusiasm that makes someone or something feel alive and exciting.

A bris is a Jewish religious ceremony in which a newborn baby boy is circumcised — meaning the foreskin (the small fold of skin at the tip of the penis) is surgically removed. But it is much more than a medical procedure.
Brisk means lively, quick, and full of energy — in a fresh, invigorating way.
A bristle is a short, stiff, coarse hair or fiber — the kind that is firm enough to stand upright or resist bending, rather than being soft and floppy.
When an animal bristles, its hair or fur suddenly shoots upward and outward — becoming stiff and spiky, like bristles.
Covered with stiff, rough hairs, like an unshaven chin. Used of a person's manner, it means easily irritated and quick to take offence.
Brittle describes something that is hard, but breaks suddenly and completely when force or pressure is applied — without bending, stretching, or warning first.
To broach something means to bring up a topic for the first time in a conversation — especially when that topic is sensitive, awkward, uncomfortable, or has been difficult to raise.

Broad means wide — but it carries a sense of generous, open, impressive width rather than just any measurement of width. Think of a broad river: it doesn't just measure a certain number of metres. It feels expansive, open, and imposing.

When something is described as broad-based, it means it draws from, covers, includes, or is supported by a wide range of things, people, groups, or areas — rather than being limited to just one or a few.
Broadband is a type of high-speed internet connection that can carry large amounts of data very quickly, and stays connected all the time without needing to "dial in" each time you use it.
To broadcast something means to send out information, audio, or video to a large number of people at the same time, usually through a medium like television, radio, or the internet.
Broaden means to make something wider — or to become wider. Think of a narrow path that gets wider as you walk along it. That path is broadening.
Before understanding the idiom, you need to understand the key word in it — horizon.

"Broadly" comes from the adjective "broad," which means wide, large in range, or not narrow. As an adverb, "broadly" carries exactly those same qualities into action or description: it means in a wide, general, or non-specific way.
A fierce verbal or written attack, as in "a broadside against the government." Historically, it was the firing of all the guns on one side of a warship at once.
Brocade is a type of fabric — a cloth — that has a pattern built into it during the weaving process, resulting in that pattern being slightly raised above the surface of the fabric.

A brochure is a small, printed paper document that gives information about something — usually a product, a place, a service, or an organization — in a way that is short, attractive, and easy to read.
A strong regional accent, especially an Irish or Scottish one. A brogue is also a sturdy leather shoe with decorative punched holes.

To broil means to cook food using direct, intense heat. The key word here is direct — the heat doesn't surround the food from all sides (the way an oven bakes bread); it blasts at the food from one direction, typically from above, at a very high temperature.

A broker is a person or company whose job is to act as the middleman between two parties — typically a buyer and a seller — and help them complete a deal. The broker brings them together, facilitates the transaction, and earns a fee for doing so.

When you broker something, you are the person in the middle — the one who brings two or more parties together and works to get them to agree on something. You are not one of the main parties in the deal.
A remark or idea that is so dull and overused that it has lost its meaning — a tired cliché meant to soothe. In chemistry, a bromide is a compound of bromine.

A bronco is a wild or only partially tamed horse — one that has not been fully trained to accept a rider or human control. The word almost always refers to horses found in the open ranges and plains of the American West.
A brooch is a decorative ornament — a piece of jewellery — that you attach directly to your clothing.

When you "brood," you sit with something heavy in your mind and just... stay there. You think about something sad, painful, or troubling — again and again — in a dark, silent, withdrawn way. You don't move on from it. You don't solve it.
Brooding is the act of sitting with something deeply — either physically, like a bird sitting over its eggs, or mentally, like a person sitting inside their own dark thoughts.
A brook is a small, shallow, naturally flowing stream of fresh water.
To tolerate or allow something, almost always used in the negative, as in "she would brook no argument."
Brotherhood means a deep, warm bond between people — a feeling that you belong together, that you care for each other, and that you would stand by each other no matter what.
A brouhaha is a loud, excited, and chaotic commotion — a big noisy fuss — that erupts among a group of people, usually because of something controversial, shocking, or scandalous.
The forehead. It can also mean an eyebrow, or the top of a hill or slope.

To browbeat someone means to intimidate, bully, or pressure them psychologically — through stern looks, a harsh tone, repeated criticism, or relentless pressure — in order to make them do what you want, feel inferior, or back down from their position.
A brownie is a small, rich, chocolate baked good, usually cut into a square or rectangular piece. It is denser and heavier than a cake, and has a deep chocolate flavor.

"Brownie points" are imaginary credits or rewards that a person is said to "earn" when they do something good, helpful, impressive, or pleasing — especially to make someone like them more, think better of them, or get into their good books.
Browse means to look through a collection of things in a relaxed, unhurried, and casual way — without a strict plan or a specific target in mind. You're not hunting for one particular thing.
A bruise is a dark, discolored patch that appears on the surface of something — most often human skin — after it has been hit or struck hard, without the surface being cut open or broken.

When something hits, presses, or impacts a surface with enough force to cause hidden damage — damage that you can feel or see, but that doesn't break the outer layer open — that action is called bruising.
To bruit something means to spread a piece of news, a rumor, or a report widely among people — usually in an informal, word-of-mouth way, and often before anything has been officially confirmed.
Brumal means of, relating to, or characteristic of winter. It's a single-word way to say "wintry" — but with a richer, more deliberate feel.
Brume means mist or fog — specifically the kind that is thick, heavy, and low-hanging, the sort that wraps around a landscape like a grey blanket and makes it difficult to see clearly.
Brunt means the main force, worst impact, or heaviest burden of something difficult or harmful.
A brush is a tool that has: a handle (the part you hold), and bristles attached to one end — stiff fibers made from hair, nylon, plant fibers, wire, or similar materials.
"Brush aside" means to refuse to take something seriously, to dismiss it quickly, or to treat it as if it is unimportant or not worth your attention.
To dismiss or ignore something or someone casually and rudely, as if it doesn't matter. Literally, to remove dust or crumbs from something by brushing it.
A brushstroke is the mark or trace that a paintbrush leaves on a surface in a single, continuous movement.
Brusque means being abrupt, short, and blunt in the way you speak or behave toward someone — to a degree that can feel rude or cold, even if you don't mean it to be.

When someone does something brusquely, they do it in a way that is short, abrupt, and lacking any warmth or softness. There are no pleasantries, no gentle tone, no padding — just a blunt, sharp delivery that feels almost impatient or dismissive.
When you call something brutal, you are saying it crosses a line. It doesn't just hurt — it overwhelms. It doesn't just disappoint — it devastates. It isn't simply strict — it is merciless.
Brutality means extreme cruelty or violence that causes serious pain, suffering, or harm — especially when it is far beyond what is necessary or acceptable.
With extreme cruelty or violence. It can also mean in a completely direct and unsoftened way, as in "brutally honest."
When you use "brute" as an adjective, you are describing something that is raw, unthinking, and stripped of all intelligence, skill, or refinement.

Brute force is the method of solving a problem by trying every possible option, one by one, until you find the correct answer — relying purely on raw computational effort (or physical effort) rather than strategy, intelligence, or cleverness.
Brutish means behaving like a brute — like a wild animal rather than a thoughtful, feeling human being.
"Bubbling anger" refers to a slow, steady build-up of anger that is being held inside, not yet released.

When a liquid is described as bubbly, it simply means it contains bubbles — the fizzing, sparkling kind you see in soda, sparkling water, or champagne. The liquid feels alive, light, and active because of those rising bubbles.
