"Bubonic" is an adjective that means relating to, caused by, or characterized by buboes. Everything hinges on that one word — bubo. A bubo (plural: buboes) is a lymph node that has become severely swollen, painful, and inflamed due to a bacterial infection.

A buccaneer is a type of seafaring raider or pirate who operated specifically in the Caribbean Sea, mainly during the 17th and 18th centuries. They were known for attacking and plundering ships and coastal towns — most often those belonging to Spain.
To buck means to resist, push against, or refuse to go along with something. Think of it as a stubborn force going in the opposite direction from what is expected or required.
To "buck the trend" means to do the opposite of what most people, things, or situations are doing — especially when everyone or everything else is moving in one clear direction.
"Buck up" is a phrasal verb with two closely related core meanings: 1. To become more cheerful, positive, or confident — especially after feeling sad, discouraged, or defeated.
To fasten something with a buckle. It also means to bend or collapse under pressure — and figuratively, to give in, as in "he finally buckled under the strain."
"Buckle down" means to start working seriously, with strong focus and full effort — especially after a period of being lazy, distracted, or avoiding a task.

Bucolic describes something that is pleasantly and peacefully rural — evoking the beauty of the countryside, nature, open fields, grazing animals, fresh air, and a calm, simple way of life far away from the noise and rush of cities.
A bud is the small, tightly closed, rounded growth that appears on a plant — on its stems, branches, or tips — before it fully opens up into something bigger.

When "budding" is used as an adjective, it describes a person who is in the early stages of developing a skill, talent, or career, and who already shows clear signs of becoming successful or excellent in that area.
To budge means to move slightly, or to cause something or someone to move slightly — especially when there is resistance, difficulty, or stubbornness involved.

A budget is a plan for money — specifically, a plan that shows how much money you have, how much money you expect to receive, and how you intend to spend or use it, all within a specific period of time (like a week, a month, or a year).
Relating to a budget — a financial plan for how much money is available and how it will be spent.
Budgeting is the process of creating and managing a plan that decides, in advance, how money will be received and how it will be spent over a set period of time — usually a week, a month, or a year.
A buff is a person who has a deep, passionate interest in a particular subject and has built up a lot of knowledge about it.
Something that sits between two things and reduces the impact, clash, or tension between them, as in "a buffer zone."

A buffet is a way of presenting and eating a meal where all the food is laid out on a long table or counter in advance, and guests walk along it, serve themselves whatever they want, in whatever quantity they like, and then sit down to eat.
When something buffets something else, it hits it repeatedly with force, knocking it around roughly. The key word here is repeatedly — it is not a single clean strike.
A buffoon is a person who behaves in a ridiculous, clownish, or embarrassingly foolish way — someone whose silly or stupid actions make people laugh at them, not with them.
Buffoonery means silly, clownish, ridiculous behavior — the kind that looks undignified, embarrassing, or absurdly foolish, especially when the situation calls for seriousness or decorum.
To repeatedly annoy or bother someone. It can also mean to secretly install a hidden microphone to listen to someone's conversations.

A bugaboo is something — real or imaginary — that causes a person (or a group of people) persistent fear, worry, dread, or anxiety. Often, that fear is exaggerated or out of proportion to how genuinely threatening the thing actually is.
Something that you particularly dread or find persistently annoying, as in "noise is my biggest bugbear."

A buggy is a small, light vehicle — one that carries people (sometimes goods) without being heavy, bulky, or complex. The word appears in several distinct contexts, each describing a different kind of small vehicle.
To "build bridges" means to create or restore a positive connection between people, groups, or organizations that are divided, in conflict, or simply unfamiliar with each other.
To use something that already exists — a skill, a success, or an idea — as a foundation for further progress.
To gradually increase or become stronger, as in "tension built up." It can also mean to praise someone so much that people expect great things of them.
"Build-up" describes a process of gradual growth — things coming together, piling up, or intensifying little by little over time. It is never about something happening all at once.

When something is described as "built-in," it means it is already included as a permanent, inseparable part of something else — present from the very beginning, not added later, not separate, and not optional.
The word bulb describes something with a rounded, swollen shape — wide and full in the middle or at one end, often narrowing toward the other end. Think of the shape of an onion.
Bulbous means rounded and swollen in shape, like a bulb.
When something bulges, it swells or pushes outward from a surface, forming a rounded lump or bump in a place that is normally flat, straight, or smooth.
"Bulk" always revolves around the concept of large size, large volume, or large quantity.
A bulkhead is a strong dividing wall built inside a structure — such as a ship, aircraft, spacecraft, or even a tunnel — to separate one section from another.
Something is bulky when it is large in size and takes up a lot of space in a way that makes it difficult or inconvenient to carry, move, store, or handle.
To flatten or destroy something with a bulldozer. Figuratively, to force someone into doing something, or to push a plan through without considering others.

A bulldozer is a massive, extremely powerful machine used in construction and earthmoving work. Its entire purpose is to push things out of the way using brute force — soil, rocks, rubble, trees, sand, debris, or even entire structures.
A bulletin is a short, official (or semi-official) piece of information — written or spoken — that announces something important, current, or urgent to an audience.
Strong enough to stop bullets, as in bulletproof glass. Figuratively, so strong that it cannot be challenged or defeated, as in "a bulletproof argument."
Bullion refers to precious metals — primarily gold or silver — in their raw, physical form, typically shaped into bars or ingots, and valued purely by how much they weigh and how pure they are.
Bullish means being optimistic, confident, and expectant of growth or success — specifically the belief that something is going to rise, improve, or get better.
A bullock is a male bovine (cattle) that has been castrated — meaning its reproductive organs have been surgically removed. More specifically, it is typically a young castrated male.

When used as an adjective, "bully" means excellent, first-rate, or very good. It is a word of strong, enthusiastic approval. When someone describes something as "bully," they are saying it is outstanding, admirable, or of high quality.
A bully is a person who uses their power, strength, or position to repeatedly hurt, frighten, humiliate, or control someone who is weaker or less able to defend themselves.
To bully someone means to repeatedly use your power or strength to frighten, hurt, or control a person who is weaker than you — or who cannot easily fight back.
Bullying is the repeated, intentional act of hurting, threatening, or controlling another person who finds it difficult to defend themselves.

In its oldest and most direct sense, a bulwark is a solid defensive wall or fortification — something built to physically protect a place from attack. Think of the heavy stone ramparts of a medieval fortress, or earthen walls built around a military camp.
To bumble means to do something — or move through something — in a clumsy, confused, and disorganised way, making mistakes along the way and generally failing to do things smoothly or competently.
When you call someone bumbling, you are saying that they act in a clumsy, confused, and ineffective way.
If someone is bummed, they feel disappointed, sad, or let down — usually because something bad happened, something didn't go as planned, or they received unwelcome news.
A bump is something that sticks out or rises up from a flat surface — a small, rounded raised area that doesn't belong to the smoothness around it.
To meet someone by chance. Literally, it means to accidentally walk into someone or something.

When "bumper" is used as an adjective, it means exceptionally large, plentiful, or impressive — well beyond what is normal or expected. It describes something so abundant or so successful that it genuinely stands out.

A bumpkin is a person from the countryside or a rural area who comes across as simple, naive, unsophisticated, or socially awkward — especially when compared to people from cities or towns. The word carries a mild sense of looking down on someone.
If someone is bumptious, they are unpleasantly full of themselves — loudly, pushily, and sometimes embarrassingly so.

A bundle is a collection of things brought together into one unit. The items inside a bundle are tied, wrapped, or grouped so tightly that they can be carried, stored, or treated as a single thing — rather than as separate, scattered pieces.

To bundle means to gather separate things together and treat them as one unit — usually by tying, wrapping, or grouping them. Think of taking scattered sticks and binding them tightly with rope. Those loose sticks have now been "bundled."
When you call someone "a bundle of nerves," you mean that person is extremely nervous, anxious, or tense — so much so that their whole being seems to be consumed by worry or fear.

A bungalow is a type of house. What makes it special — and different from most other houses — is that it is built on only one floor. Everything you need: bedrooms, kitchen, living room, bathroom — all of it is on the ground level.

To bungle something means to do it so badly, clumsily, or carelessly that you ruin it or fail at it — especially when the failure was entirely your own fault because of your incompetence, lack of skill, or lack of care.
A narrow bed built into a wall or stacked above another, as on a ship or in a dormitory. Informally, bunk also means nonsense.
A bunker is a strong, enclosed, often partially hidden space — built either to protect something or to store something.
Bunkum is talk, writing, or ideas that are empty, hollow, or foolish — the kind that might sound meaningful at first but actually contains very little or no real substance, truth, or value.
Strings of small, colourful flags or fabric used as decorations for celebrations. A bunting is also a type of small songbird.
In its most physical sense, to buoy something means to literally keep it floating on water — to hold it up on the surface so it doesn't go under.
To make someone feel more cheerful, confident, or hopeful. It can also mean to keep a price or level high, or to keep something afloat.

Buoyancy is the upward pushing force that a fluid (a liquid or a gas) exerts on any object placed inside it. It is the force responsible for making things float, or for making things feel lighter when they are submerged in a fluid.
Cheerful and optimistic. It can also describe an economy or market that is strong and rising, or something able to float.

Burble describes a soft, gentle, continuous, flowing sound — most naturally the sound of water moving over stones in a shallow stream. It's not the loud crash of a waterfall or the angry rush of a flood.
A burden is anything — physical, emotional, financial, or moral — that is heavy, difficult, or hard to carry or bear. The word always carries a sense of weight, strain, and difficulty.
The burden of proof is the obligation on a person who makes a claim to provide sufficient evidence to support that claim. If you make the claim, you carry the burden. It is your job to prove it.
When something is burdensome, it is so difficult, demanding, or troublesome that it feels like a heavy weight pressing down on you — one that is hard to carry and hard to escape.
An office or government department that handles a particular kind of work, as in "the Federal Bureau of Investigation." A bureau is also a chest of drawers or writing desk.
A bureaucracy is a large, formal system of rules, procedures, departments, and officials that is used to manage and run a big organization — like a government, a company, a hospital, or a university.

A bureaucrat is a person who works as an official within a large, formal system — most commonly a government, but also large organizations like corporations, universities, or international bodies — and whose job is to carry out the rules, procedures, and policies of that system.
Involving too many complicated rules, forms, and procedures, so that things move slowly and inefficiently.

To burgeon means to grow, expand, or develop rapidly and vigorously — especially after a slow or quiet start. Think of it as the moment something "takes off" and begins flourishing with real energy and momentum.
Burgeoning describes something that is growing, expanding, or developing rapidly — and usually, it also implies that this growth is relatively new and full of energy and promise.

A burgher is a full, official citizen of a town or city — specifically one who holds recognized legal rights within that town. Think of it this way: not everyone who lived in a medieval or early modern town was a burgher.
A burglar is a person who enters a building without permission in order to commit a crime inside — most commonly, to steal things.
Burglary is the act of entering a building illegally — without permission — with the intention of committing a crime inside.
To burgle a place means to illegally enter a building — usually by breaking in — with the intention of committing a crime there, most commonly theft.

Burial means the act of placing a dead body into the ground and covering it with earth. It is what happens when a person (or an animal) dies and their body is put into a grave — a hole dug in the ground — and then the hole is filled back up.
Burlap is a type of fabric — but not the soft, comfortable kind you'd wear as clothing. It is a coarse, rough, loosely woven textile made from the fibers of plants, most commonly the jute plant.
Burlesque is a style of comedy built on one simple trick: mismatch.
Burly is an adjective used to describe a person — almost always a human being — who has a large, heavy, and solidly muscular body, giving a strong impression of physical power and toughness.
To permanently destroy a relationship or connection, so that going back becomes impossible.
When a building burns down, fire destroys it completely. When a fire or candle burns down, it gradually becomes smaller as the fuel is used up.
Burn the candle at both ends

When someone says a person is "burning the candle at both ends," they mean that person is exhausting themselves by doing too much, resting too little, and living at a pace their body and mind simply cannot sustain.
When you use burning as an adjective, you are always describing something with an extreme, intense quality — like fire itself. Fire is powerful, impossible to ignore, and demands immediate attention.

A "burning issue" is a topic, problem, or matter that is so urgent, important, and pressing that it absolutely cannot be ignored or delayed. It demands immediate attention — just like a fire that you cannot walk away from.

To burnish something means to rub a surface repeatedly and firmly until it becomes smooth and bright. The rubbing itself — the friction of something hard and smooth pressing against a surface — is what creates the shine.

Burnished describes a surface that has a rich, smooth, glowing shine — the kind that looks like it has depth and warmth to it, not just a flat glitter. It is not a harsh, blinding glare. It is more like a glow that seems to come from within the surface.

As a noun, "burnout" describes the state of being completely used up — physically, mentally, and emotionally — usually because of prolonged stress or overwork. It is not just being tired after a long day.
A state of complete physical and emotional exhaustion caused by long-term stress or overwork. To burn out means to become exhausted in this way.

A burrow is a hole or tunnel that an animal digs into the ground to live in. Think of it as an underground home — one that the animal makes itself, using its claws, snout, or body to push and scrape the earth away.

To burrow means to dig a hole or tunnel into the ground — usually by pushing the earth aside with your body, claws, or hands. Picture a rabbit using its front paws to push through soil, moving deeper and deeper underground. That action is called burrowing.
To "burst into" something means to begin doing something suddenly, quickly, and with great force or energy.
To suddenly catch fire and start burning strongly.
To burst someone's bubble means to destroy someone's happy illusion, false belief, or unrealistic excitement by telling them the truth or harsh reality.
Bury one's head in the sand
To "bury one's head in the sand" means to deliberately ignore a problem, danger, or uncomfortable truth instead of facing it.

To "bury the hatchet" means to end a conflict and make peace with someone. When two people or groups "bury the hatchet," they agree to stop fighting, forgive each other, and move forward without holding onto old grudges or anger.
A busboy is a junior restaurant worker whose main job is to clear and clean tables after customers finish eating, so that the table is ready for the next guests.

Bushcraft is the set of skills, knowledge, and practical abilities that allow a person to live comfortably and safely in a wild, natural environment — using almost entirely what nature itself provides, with little or no reliance on modern tools, gadgets, or pre-packaged supplies.
A bushel is a unit of measurement used mainly to measure quantities of dry goods — things like grain, fruits, and vegetables.

To busk means to perform in a public place — usually on a street, in a park, or in a subway/train station — and hope that people passing by will stop, watch or listen, and drop some money as a voluntary tip.

A buskin is a thick-soled boot that reaches up to the calf or knee, laced up the front. Think of it as something between an ankle boot and a knee-high boot — sturdy, raised, and dramatic in appearance.
"A busman's holiday" describes a situation where you spend your free time — your day off, weekend, or vacation — doing the same kind of work you do in your regular job.
A sculpture of a person's head, shoulders, and upper chest. It can also mean a woman's chest measurement, a police raid or arrest, or a total failure.

Bustle refers to a scene of busy, energetic, often noisy movement — usually involving many people rushing around, doing things, going places. It is the feeling and atmosphere of a place that is alive with activity.

To bustle means to move around quickly and energetically in a busy, active way. But it's not just speed — it's a particular kind of movement: brisk, purposeful, and full of energy, often with a sense of many things happening at once.
Bustling describes a place or scene that is full of energetic activity, movement, and noise — usually because many people are present and actively doing things at the same time.
A busybody is a person who is nosy and interfering — someone who sticks their nose into other people's lives, affairs, and private matters without being invited or asked to do so.
The masculine energy, confidence, and self-assured strength associated with butch identity in LGBTQ+ culture.
"Butt in" means to interrupt or force yourself into a conversation, situation, or activity where you were not invited and where your involvement was not asked for.
When someone is the butt of the joke, they are the person (or thing) that everyone is laughing at — not laughing with, but laughing at. They are the target.
A butte is a tall, isolated hill with steep, nearly vertical sides and a small, flat top, standing alone on an otherwise flat or open landscape.
To butter someone up means to flatter someone in an exaggerated, insincere way — with a hidden goal of getting something from them.

"Buttoned-up" describes a person, place, or organization that is tightly controlled, formal, and closed off — not relaxed, not open, and not expressive. Think of someone who keeps everything neat, guarded, and proper, never letting their guard down.

To buttonhole someone means to stop them — often when they're clearly on their way somewhere or are busy — and trap them in a conversation they didn't ask for and probably don't want. You corner them.
A structure of stone or brick built against a wall to support it. Figuratively, something that supports or strengthens something else, as in "a buttress against inflation."

To buttress something means to strengthen or reinforce it so that it holds up more firmly — especially against pressure, doubt, or challenge. Think of it as adding extra support to something that might otherwise be questioned, weakened, or fall apart.

"Buxom" is an adjective used to describe a woman who has a full, rounded, and voluptuous body — especially a large, prominent bust (chest). Think of a woman who is plump and curvy in a way that looks healthy, lively, and physically robust.
To accept or believe in an idea, plan, or belief, often completely. Literally, to buy a share in a business.
To accept the basic assumption behind an argument, question, or story as true.
All the meanings of "buzz" as a noun connect to one core idea: something that is alive, active, and vibrating with energy.
A buzzkill is a person, thing, event, or piece of information that suddenly ruins a good mood, kills excitement, or drains the fun and energy out of a situation.
A buzzword is a word or phrase that becomes extremely popular and fashionable within a specific group of people, a profession, or in society at a certain point in time.
Buzzworthy means "interesting or exciting enough to make many people talk about it."
"By all accounts" means according to what everyone says, or according to all the information available.

"By all means" is a phrase used to say "yes, absolutely" or "of course" — but with warmth, enthusiasm, and zero hesitation. It is a polite, emphatic way of giving someone permission to do something or encouraging them to go ahead with something.
"By and large" means "in general" or "on the whole."
By any stretch of the imagination
This idiom means "even if you try as hard as possible to believe or imagine something."

"By chance" means that something happened without being planned, intended, or expected. It was not arranged. Nobody made it happen on purpose. It simply happened on its own, due to luck, fate, or randomness.
"By dint of" means "by means of," "through the use of," or "as a result of."
"By far" means by a great amount or by a large margin.

"By fits and starts" means doing something irregularly — in short, sudden bursts of activity, followed by stops, pauses, or periods of doing nothing — and then picking it up again, only to stop again.

"By hook or by crook" means by any means necessary — whether the method is easy or hard, fair or unfair, conventional or unconventional. When someone says they will do something "by hook or by crook," they are expressing strong determination.

"By leaps and bounds" means very quickly and in large amounts. It describes something that is growing, improving, or progressing at a remarkably fast and significant rate — not slowly, not steadily, but in big, dramatic jumps.
"By means of" simply means "using something" or "through the use of something" to achieve a result or goal.
"By no means" is a phrase that means "absolutely not," "definitely not," or "not at all."
"By someone's reckoning" means "according to someone's calculation, estimate, or judgment."

"By the by" means incidentally or as a side note. You use it when you want to bring up something that is not the main topic of your conversation — something extra, something off to the side, something you just want to slip in.
"By the same token" means for the same reason or on the same basis. You use it to connect two ideas that are linked by the same logic, the same evidence, or the same underlying principle.
"By virtue of" means "because of" or "as a result of" — but with a specific flavor. It points to a quality, characteristic, position, status, or right that causes or allows something to happen.

A by-product is something that is produced as a result of a process, but is not the main thing you were trying to produce. It is a secondary output — it appears alongside the main result, almost as a "bonus" or "side effect" of doing or making something else.

"Bygone" means belonging to a period of time that has already passed and is now completely over. When you call something "bygone," you are saying it existed in an earlier era — and that era is now firmly in the past, not coming back.
Bygones refers to things that happened in the past — specifically, past events, past quarrels, past mistakes, past offenses, or past wrongs between people.

A bylaw is a rule or regulation made by a group, organization, or local authority — not by a national or central government — that applies only to those who belong to that group or live within that local area.
A byline is a short line of text in a published piece of writing — such as a newspaper article, magazine feature, or online post — that tells you who wrote it.

To bypass something means to go around it, avoid it, or skip it — particularly when it is something that normally stands between you and where you want to go, or something that you would normally be expected to deal with.

A bystander is a person who is present when something happens but is not directly involved in it. They are simply there — watching, observing, or just nearby — but they are neither causing what's happening nor are they the one it's happening to.
The tendency for people to be less likely to help someone in need when other people are present.
A person or thing so strongly associated with a quality that they become its best-known example, as in "the company became a byword for greed."
"Byzantine" describes something that is extremely complicated, tangled, and difficult to understand or navigate — often to a frustrating, almost absurd degree. It's not just "complicated."

Béchamel (also spelled bechamel) is a smooth, creamy, white sauce used in cooking. It is one of the most important and widely used sauces in Western cuisine, particularly in French and Italian cooking.

A bête noire is a person, thing, task, or situation that someone particularly dislikes, dreads, or finds deeply irritating — and keeps encountering or dealing with repeatedly. It is their specific source of strong aversion, frustration, or discomfort.
A cabal is a small, secret group of people who secretly plot together to gain power, control, or some advantage — usually for their own selfish benefit, and almost always against someone else.
"Cabalistic" describes something that is secret, mysterious, and understood only by a small inner circle of people — as if it belongs to a hidden world that outsiders are not allowed into.

A cabinet is a piece of furniture — a box-like structure, usually made of wood or metal, that has doors, drawers, or shelves inside it. Its main purpose is to store things neatly and keep them out of sight.

Caboodle means the entire collection of things or people — every single item or individual in a group, without leaving anything out. Think of it as a word that means "the whole lot" or "everything included."

Cacao is a word with a few closely related meanings, all of which revolve around one thing: a tropical tree and everything that comes directly from it — its fruit, its seeds, and the raw natural substance inside those seeds that eventually becomes chocolate.
A cache is a stash — a collection of things deliberately set aside in a specific spot so they can be accessed quickly when needed.
Cachet means a quality of prestige, distinction, or special status that makes a person, place, thing, or institution admired, respected, or desirable — especially in the eyes of others.
To cachinnate means to laugh very loudly and without restraint — the kind of laughter that bursts out of you uncontrollably, fills the room, and cannot be easily stopped or quieted.
To cackle means to make a particular kind of loud, sharp, broken sound — either the sound a hen makes, or, more commonly in everyday usage, a specific type of laugh that sounds like that hen.
When something is described as cackling, it is producing — or characterized by — a sharp, high-pitched, broken sound, most commonly a laugh. This laugh is not smooth or flowing.
Cacophonous is an adjective that describes sounds which are harsh, jarring, and unpleasant to hear — sounds that clash and grate on your ears rather than flowing smoothly or sounding pleasing.
A cacophony is a harsh, jarring, deeply unpleasant mixture of sounds that clash together all at once.

A cad is a man who behaves in a dishonorable, selfish, or unkind way — especially toward women — while knowing full well that what he's doing is wrong. He lacks basic decency, integrity, and respect for others.

A cadaver is a dead human body — specifically one that is being used, or intended to be used, for scientific study or medical training. It is not simply any dead person; the word carries a precise, clinical meaning tied to the world of medicine and science.

"Cadaverous" is an adjective used to describe someone — or something — that looks like a corpse. Not simply unwell or tired, but corpse-like: deathly pale, gaunt, hollow, and drained of all visible life.

Caddish describes behavior that is dishonorable, selfish, and deeply ungentlemanly — especially the way a person (almost always a man) treats others, particularly women, in a way that is unfair, dishonest, or morally cheap.
Cadence means a rhythmic flow or pattern — a sense of regular rise and fall, beat and pause, speed and pace that you can feel in sound, movement, or even events.

A cadenza is a solo passage in a musical piece — usually a concerto — where one performer plays alone, without any accompaniment, to display their skill and artistry. Think of it as a spotlight moment.
A cadet is a person who is officially enrolled in a training program to become an officer — most commonly in the military, but also in the police or similar uniformed services.
To cadge means to get something from someone by asking for it — without paying for it, without earning it, and without offering anything in return.
A cadre is a small, select group of people who are specially trained, highly capable, and deeply committed — and who form the essential core of a larger organization.
A caesura is a pause or break that falls within a line of poetry — not at the end of a line, but somewhere in the middle, where the reader naturally stops for a beat before the line continues.
Containing caffeine, as in "caffeinated drinks." Informally, full of energy from drinking coffee.
A caftan is a long, loose, flowing garment — think of it as a full-length robe or dress that drapes over your body with a lot of freedom and airiness.

When you describe someone as cagey, you mean they are deliberately careful and guarded — especially about sharing information, revealing their thoughts, or committing to something. A cagey person doesn't give you straight, open answers.

A cairn is a pile of stones stacked on top of each other by a person, on purpose. It is not a natural rock formation — it is deliberately built by human hands, usually out of rough, unshapen rocks found nearby.
To cajole someone means to persuade them to do something — not by forcing them, threatening them, or paying them — but by being sweet, flattering, and persistent.
Cajolery is the act of persuading someone to do something — not by forcing them, not by arguing logically, but by using sweet talk, flattery, charm, and gentle coaxing.
Calamitous means causing or involving a great disaster, enormous suffering, or severe destruction. When something is calamitous, it is not just bad — it is devastatingly, overwhelmingly bad.

A calamity is a serious event that causes great harm, suffering, or loss — to a person, a group of people, or an entire society. Think of it as a disaster that hits hard and leaves real damage behind.

To calcify means to harden through the build-up of calcium. When something calcifies, it gradually becomes stiff and rigid because calcium — a naturally hard mineral — accumulates inside it and turns it solid.
To calculate means to work something out carefully and deliberately — usually using numbers or logical thinking — to reach a specific answer or conclusion.
When something is calculated, it means it was done on purpose, after careful thought, with a specific goal in mind.
A branch of mathematics that deals with how things change, such as speed or growth. It can also mean a system of reasoning, or a hard deposit, like a stone, in the body.
A caldera is a large, bowl-shaped hollow in the ground formed when a volcano partially collapses into itself after a massive eruption.
A caldron is a very large, deep, heavy pot — the kind used for boiling huge amounts of liquid or cooking large quantities of food over an open fire.
A young cow or bull, or the young of some other large animals such as elephants and whales. The calf is also the fleshy back part of the leg below the knee.
The quality, ability, or standard of someone or something, as in "a player of the highest caliber." Literally, the inside width of a gun barrel, or the size of a bullet.
To calibrate something means to carefully adjust it so that it is accurate, correct, and works exactly as it should — usually by comparing it to a known standard or a specific goal.
When something is described as calico, it means it has patches or blotches of multiple contrasting colors — typically three or more — arranged in an irregular, uneven way across a surface.

Caliginous means dark, murky, and misty — the kind of thick, heavy darkness that feels almost physical, like it has texture and weight to it. Think of a dense fog rolling over a swamp at midnight, or a cave so deep that your torch barely makes a dent.

Calisthenics is a type of physical exercise where you use your own body weight — and nothing else — to build strength, fitness, and flexibility. No dumbbells, no machines, no gym required. Just your body and gravity working against each other.
A calk is a small, sharp, pointed metal projection — essentially a spike or a cleat — that is fixed onto the bottom of a horseshoe or the heel and sole of a work boot.
A "call" is an act of reaching out — with your voice, a signal, a request, or a decision — directed at someone or something.
When something calls forth something else, it causes it to come out — from inside a person, a situation, or the world — often something that was hidden, sleeping, or waiting to appear.
To visit someone briefly, to ask someone to do or say something ("The teacher called on me"), or to draw on a quality or resource ("She called on all her courage").
Calligraphy is the art of beautiful, decorative handwriting.
If someone is callous, they show a complete lack of sympathy or concern for the pain, suffering, or feelings of other people — and importantly, they don't feel bad about it either.
Callousness is the quality of being completely unfeeling and indifferent toward other people's pain, suffering, or distress — even when you are fully aware of it.

Callow means inexperienced and immature in a naive, unsophisticated way — typically because a person is young and hasn't yet been shaped by real-world experience. A callow person hasn't faced enough of life to develop good judgment, depth, or wisdom.
A callus is a patch of skin that has become unusually thick, hard, and rough because of repeated rubbing, friction, or pressure. It is your body's way of protecting itself.
Callused means having developed a hardened, toughened quality — either on your skin or, figuratively, inside yourself emotionally.

Calorific means relating to, or producing, heat and energy. More specifically, it describes how much energy a substance (food or fuel) releases — either when your body burns it for energy, or when it is literally set on fire.
A calque is a word or phrase in one language that was created by translating another language's word or phrase piece by piece into native-sounding parts.
To calumniate someone means to deliberately make up false, damaging lies about them and spread those lies to others in order to destroy their reputation.
Calumnious describes something — a statement, an accusation, a remark, a campaign — that tells lies about a person with the specific goal of damaging their reputation.
Calumny is a false and malicious statement made about a person with the deliberate intention of damaging their reputation.
Camaraderie is the warm, comfortable feeling of friendship, trust, and loyalty shared among a group of people.
The word cameo always carries one essential idea: something small, but striking and distinct — standing out clearly from its surroundings.
Camouflage is any method, pattern, color, or disguise that makes something blend into its surroundings so that it becomes difficult — or impossible — to notice.
A place where people live temporarily, usually in tents or simple shelters. It can also mean a group of people who share a particular opinion, as in "the two camps disagreed."
A campaign is an organized, planned series of actions carried out over a period of time, all working toward a single specific goal.
A campus is the total physical space — all the land and buildings together — that belongs to and is used by an institution, most commonly a school, college, or university.
Campy describes something that is wildly exaggerated, theatrical, and over-the-top in a way that feels deliberately artificial — and that's exactly what makes it entertaining.

When someone says a situation is "a can of worms," they mean it is a complicated problem that — once you get involved with it — creates many more problems, complications, or conflicts that are difficult to manage or resolve.

A canal is an artificial waterway — a long, narrow channel that humans dig into the ground and fill with water. The single most important thing to remember about a canal is that it is man-made, not natural.

A canapé is a tiny, bite-sized piece of food made up of two essential parts: a small, firm base and a topping placed on it. Think of it like a miniature open-faced sandwich — except it is far smaller, more refined, and is never a meal by itself.
A canard is a false story or claim — one that is made up, has no solid basis in fact, and yet gets repeated and spread around as if it were true.
Cancerous means relating to, characteristic of, or affected by cancer.
When someone is candid, they tell you the truth openly and directly — even when that truth is uncomfortable, awkward, or not what you want to hear.
A candidate is a person who is being considered or evaluated for something — a job, a position, an award, an exam, or any kind of selection process.
Candor is the quality of being genuinely open and honest in what you say, especially when the truth is difficult, uncomfortable, or sensitive.
A dog, or any member of the dog family, such as a wolf or fox. A canine is also one of the four pointed teeth next to your front teeth.

A canister is a rigid, cylindrical container — round like a tube or a drum — that has a removable lid or cover. It is designed to store, hold, or carry something safely inside, whether that something is a solid, a powder, a liquid, or a gas.

A canker is a destructive sore, wound, or area of decay that eats into living tissue — and crucially, it doesn't stay put. It tends to spread, grow worse, and damage more than just the spot where it started. Think of it as a kind of rot that creeps.
"Canned" has a few related meanings, all connected by a single core idea: something that was made in advance, stored, and is ready to be used at any time — rather than being freshly made right now.
Cannibalism is the act of eating the flesh — and sometimes other body parts — of a member of one's own species.
A cannoli is a classic Italian pastry dessert — something you eat as a sweet treat, most famously from the island of Sicily in southern Italy.

A cannonade is a long, heavy, and continuous burst of cannon fire — not just one shot, but many cannons firing again and again, repeatedly, over a stretch of time, creating a thunderous, relentless storm of destruction.
Shrewd and careful — sharp in judgement, especially in money or business, and not easily fooled.

A rule or principle accepted as authoritative, or the works of literature, music, or art accepted as the most important, as in "the literary canon." In fiction, it means the official story. A canon is also a member of the clergy at a cathedral.
Canonical means officially accepted, standard, and authoritative.

When "canonical" becomes the noun canonicals, it almost always refers to one specific, concrete thing: The official vestments — robes and ceremonial garments — that clergy are required by church law to wear when performing religious duties.

To canonize something or someone means to officially declare them to be of the highest, most authoritative status — to formally place them in a special, elevated category that a recognized authority or community accepts as final and definitive.

To canoodle means to kiss, hug, and cuddle with someone in a romantic and affectionate way — in a soft, playful, and tender manner. It describes the whole cozy bundle of sweet physical closeness between two people who are romantically drawn to each other.
A canopy is something that spreads out above you and covers what is below it — like a ceiling, but one that is not necessarily built from solid walls.
Hypocritical talk that sounds moral or sincere but isn't meant. It can also mean the special language or jargon of a particular group.

Cantankerous describes a person who is bad-tempered, grumpy, and genuinely difficult to get along with — someone who argues, complains, and causes trouble regularly, often over small or unimportant things.

A cantata is a piece of music that is sung — not just played on instruments. It is a composition for one or more singers, accompanied by instruments, divided into several distinct sections, and built around a central theme or text.
A canteen is a room or building inside a school, office, factory, hospital, army base, or any large institution where employees, students, or members go to buy and eat food.

A canter is a specific way a horse moves — a smooth, rhythmic, rocking pace that is faster than a trot but slower than a gallop. It is one of the natural gaits (ways of moving) that a horse uses, and it sits right in the middle of the speed range.
A cantilever is a beam, plank, slab, or any structural element that is anchored firmly at only one end, while the other end sticks out freely into the air — with nothing supporting it from below.
The raised, curved part at the back of a horse's saddle.
A canto is a major division of a long poem — think of it as the "chapter" of a poem.
Canvas is a type of strong, tough, heavy fabric — a thick woven cloth. Think of it as the opposite of something delicate like silk. Canvas is rugged, durable, and built to hold up under pressure.
To canvass means to go around actively and systematically talking to people — either to ask for their votes or opinions, to examine something thoroughly, or to seek something (like sales or support).
Capacious means having a large amount of space inside — able to hold, contain, or store a great deal. When you call something capacious, you are saying that it has an impressive internal capacity.

Capacity refers to the maximum that something or someone can hold, do, or be. But this single idea branches into several distinct meanings depending on context. Every meaning shares one unifying thread: a limit, a boundary, or a maximum potential.

A caparison is an ornamental covering — a large, richly decorated cloth — that is draped over a horse. Not just any plain saddle blanket, but a grand, elaborate, often floor-length cloth that covers most of the horse's body: neck, back, sides, and flanks.
A daring, amusing, or illegal adventure, especially a robbery. It can also mean a playful leap, or the small pickled flower bud used in cooking.
A capillary is an extremely narrow tube — so narrow that it sits at the boundary of what you can see with the naked eye.

Capitalism is an economic system in which private individuals or companies — rather than the government — own the resources and tools used to produce goods and services, and where most economic decisions are driven by the pursuit of profit through free markets.
The use of capital letters in writing. In finance, it is the total market value of a company's shares.
To capitulate means to stop resisting and give in — but only after you have been resisting for some time.

Capitulation means the act of giving up resistance and surrendering to someone or something — especially after you have been fighting, struggling, or holding your ground for a significant period of time.
Capoeira is a Brazilian martial art that is uniquely blended with dance, acrobatics, and live music — all at the same time.

A caprice is a sudden, unplanned desire, decision, or change of mind that has no strong or logical reason behind it. It comes from a feeling or a mood — not from careful thinking. It is, essentially, a whim.
Capricious describes someone or something that changes suddenly, unpredictably, and without any clear or logical reason — driven purely by impulse or mood.
To capsize means to overturn a boat or other watercraft in water — that is, to flip it upside down or onto its side so that the bottom faces up and the deck faces down (or sideways).

A capsule is a small, self-contained shell or container that encloses something inside it — protecting it, preserving it, or keeping it neatly packaged. Think of it as a tight little "wrapper" around something.
A caption is a short piece of text that is attached to something visual — most commonly an image, photo, illustration, chart, or video — to explain, describe, or give context to what you are seeing.
If someone is captious, they have a habit of finding fault with people and things — but not in a fair, helpful, or constructive way.
To captivate someone means to powerfully attract and hold their complete attention — in a way that feels almost magical, almost impossible to resist.
When someone is captivated, their attention and interest have been so completely taken over by something that they cannot easily pull away from it. They are fully absorbed — held, as if by a spell.
Captivation is the state of being completely held by something — your attention, your feelings, and your focus all locked onto it so powerfully that you can barely pull yourself away.
When something or someone is captive, it means they are held by an outside force and cannot freely leave or escape.

Captivity is the state of being held or kept somewhere by force, where you cannot leave freely. When someone or something is in captivity, they are under the control of another — trapped, confined, unable to go where they wish or live as they naturally would.
A captor is a person who captures and holds another person — or sometimes an animal — against their will and keeps them from leaving freely.

A carabiner is a metal loop — shaped roughly like a stretched oval or the letter D — that has a small, hinged gate built into one of its sides. That gate is spring-loaded, meaning it stays closed on its own and snaps back shut the moment you stop pressing it.

A carafe is a container used to hold and serve liquids — most commonly water, wine, juice, or coffee. Think of it as a serving vessel that sits on a table so that people can pour from it into their own glasses.

To caramelize something means to heat it until its sugar content transforms — changing color, flavor, and texture in a very specific way. The word is used in cooking, and it describes one of the most important flavor-building techniques in the kitchen.

A carapace is the hard, protective shell or shield that covers the back and upper body of certain animals. Think of it as nature's built-in armor — a tough outer casing that the animal is born with and carries for life.
A unit of weight for gemstones, equal to 200 milligrams. It is also a measure of the purity of gold, where 24 carats is pure gold.
A caravan is a group of people — and sometimes animals or vehicles — traveling together, especially across a long, dangerous, or remote stretch of land. The key element is the together part.

A carcass is the dead body of an animal. That is its most basic, everyday meaning. When a lion kills a zebra on the savanna and eats its fill, what remains — the lifeless body of the zebra — is called a carcass.

Carcinogenic is an adjective. When you describe something as carcinogenic, you are saying that it has the ability to cause cancer — or more precisely, that it is capable of initiating or promoting the uncontrolled growth of cancerous cells in a living body.
A card is a small, flat, rectangular piece of stiff paper or thin plastic. That's the physical object the word originally describes.

Cardiac simply means "relating to the heart." Whenever you see or hear this word, it is telling you that whatever is being described has something to do with the heart — its structure, its function, its health, or its disorders.
Cardinal means of the highest, most fundamental importance — the kind of importance where everything else depends on it or flows from it.
A senior official in the Catholic Church, ranked just below the Pope. A cardinal is also a red North American songbird.
A cardiologist is a medical doctor who specializes in the heart and the network of blood vessels connected to it — the arteries, veins, and capillaries that carry blood throughout your body.

To careen means to move forward rapidly while at the same time tilting, lurching, or swaying side to side — in a way that feels unstable, uncontrolled, or dangerously close to losing balance entirely.
A career is the long journey of a person's working life — the entire path of work someone builds and travels over many years, usually within one field or a closely related set of fields.
Carefree means being free from worry, anxiety, or the weight of responsibilities — and feeling light, easy, and happy as a result.

A carer is a person who looks after someone who cannot fully look after themselves. The person being looked after usually needs help because of old age, illness, disability, or a mental health condition.
A caress is a gentle, slow, loving touch — the kind that communicates warmth, tenderness, or deep affection through physical contact.

The word caretaker is built on two simple ideas: care (looking after, protecting, maintaining) and taking (actively doing it, taking on the responsibility). A caretaker is someone who takes on the responsibility of looking after something or someone.

Careworn is an adjective that describes a person who looks visibly tired, aged, and worn down — not from physical labor or a single rough night — but from carrying the weight of prolonged worry, stress, or hardship.
A caribou is a large deer that lives in the cold, icy regions of the world — mainly the Arctic and sub-Arctic areas of North America (Canada, Alaska), as well as parts of northern Europe and Asia.
A caricature is a depiction of a person or thing where certain features are deliberately exaggerated or distorted, usually to make a point, create humor, or offer criticism.
A caricaturist is an artist who draws exaggerated portraits of people, usually for humor, entertainment, or to make a sharp point about that person.

A carillon is a large musical instrument made entirely of bells — specifically, a carefully tuned collection of cast bronze bells housed inside a tower, designed to be played as a unified instrument to produce music.
When you use carmine as an adjective, you are describing a specific shade of red — not just any red, but a deep, vivid, rich red that leans slightly toward purple or blue.
Carnage means the violent killing of a large number of people, resulting in a scene of widespread death, blood, and destruction. The word does not describe just one death or even a few deaths.
Carnal means relating to the body and its physical desires, as opposed to the mind or the spirit. Think of it as the opposite of "spiritual" or "intellectual."
Carnality is the state or condition of being heavily absorbed in, or driven by, the desires of the physical body — especially sexual desire — rather than the mind or spirit.
A carnivore is a living thing — almost always an animal — that eats meat as its primary or sole source of food. "Meat" here means the flesh of other animals.
Carnivorous is an adjective that means meat-eating — that is, describing any living thing that feeds primarily on the flesh of other animals.
A carousal is a loud, lively, and wild celebration — specifically one centered around drinking a lot of alcohol and being rowdy and merry with other people.
To carouse means to drink alcohol enthusiastically and excessively, with a group of people, in a loud, cheerful, and wildly social way — often for a long stretch of time.
To carp means to complain or find fault in a petty, persistent, and often irritating way — especially about small or unimportant things.
A condition in which a nerve in the wrist is squeezed, causing numbness, tingling, and pain in the hand and fingers.

A carpetbagger is a person who moves into a new place — a city, a state, or a region — not because they genuinely care about that place or its people, but purely to exploit opportunities there for their own benefit.
"Carpeted" always conveys one central image: a surface that is completely and evenly covered — with no gaps, no bare patches. That's the thread running through every use of this word.
Carping describes a style of criticism that is petty, excessive, and fault-finding — focused on picking out minor flaws in a nagging, unreasonable way, rather than offering anything helpful or fair.
Carping means the act of complaining or finding faults repeatedly, in a petty and irritating way — especially about things that are small, unimportant, or unavoidable.
A carrel is a small, private study space designed for one person to sit, read, and work quietly — and it is found almost exclusively inside libraries.
Carrion is the dead, rotting flesh of an animal.

Carsick describes how you feel when riding in a moving car makes you feel sick — specifically nauseous (an uncomfortable urge to vomit), dizzy, or generally unwell. It is the unpleasant physical reaction your body has to the motion of a car.

Carte blanche means complete and unlimited freedom to do whatever you decide, with no restrictions, no need for approval, and no questions asked — because someone in a position of authority has fully handed over that power to you.
A group of separate businesses, countries, or criminal organizations that agree to act together to control a market, prices, or territory for their own benefit.

Cartilaginous simply means "made of, consisting of, or relating to cartilage." If something is described as cartilaginous, it is either built from cartilage, or it strongly resembles cartilage in its nature and texture.
A cartographer is a person who makes maps. If someone's job or skill is to create, design, or draw maps — of countries, oceans, cities, mountains, or anything else — that person is a cartographer.
Cartography is the science and art of making maps.
A caryatid is a sculpted figure of a woman — carved in stone — that stands upright and acts as a column, holding up the roof or ceiling of a building on her head.
A waterfall, especially one of several small falls flowing down in stages. Figuratively, a large amount of something that comes all at once, or a chain of events where each one triggers the next.
To flow or fall downward in large amounts, like a waterfall. Figuratively, to pass from one stage to the next in a chain.
Cashmere is an exceptionally soft, fine, and warm fiber — and the fabric made from it — that comes from a specific type of goat called the cashmere goat (also known as the Pashmina goat).

The Casimir effect is a real, measurable attractive force that spontaneously arises between two uncharged, conducting objects placed extremely close together in a vacuum — caused not by any charge, magnet, or gravity, but purely by the strange quantum nature of "empty" space itself.

A cask is a large, strong container — shaped roughly like a cylinder, but with sides that bulge slightly outward in the middle — traditionally made of wood, and used for storing or aging liquids, especially alcoholic drinks like wine, whisky, rum, or beer.

A casket is a box in which a dead person's body is placed for burial or cremation. It is rectangular, has a lid, and is usually made from wood or metal. The inside is padded and lined with soft fabric, often silk or velvet, to give it a dignified appearance.

A casserole is a type of deep, heavy cooking dish. It usually has thick walls, a flat bottom, and comes with a tight-fitting lid. It is designed to go inside an oven and withstand long hours of heat without cracking or warping.
A cassette is a small, sealed case — usually made of plastic — that holds some kind of material (most often a thin magnetic tape) neatly wound inside it.
A cassock is a long, plain garment worn by members of the Christian clergy — priests, ministers, deacons, and others who hold religious office in the church.
All the actors in a film, play, or show. It is also a hard covering that holds a broken bone in place, or a mould used to shape something.

To cast means to send something outward — away from yourself, or away from a source. Think of it as a directed release. That one idea — sending something outward — is the thread running through every use of this word.

A caste is a fixed social group that you are born into, and that you cannot leave or change for your entire life. Your caste is inherited — meaning it passes down from your parents to you automatically, just like your eye color.
To castigate someone means to criticize or scold them very severely and harshly, usually because they have done something morally wrong, irresponsible, or unacceptable.

Castigation is the act of criticizing someone — or something — very severely and harshly, usually because they have done something wrong or unacceptable. It is not gentle, mild, or polite criticism. It is sharp, forceful, and deliberate.

A castle in the air is a dream, plan, or wish that sounds wonderful but has no real chance of coming true. It is something that exists only in your imagination — a fantasy that is not grounded in reality.
To castrate means to surgically remove the reproductive glands — most commonly the testicles (in a male).
"Casual" describes something that is relaxed, informal, and low in intensity or seriousness. Think of it as the opposite of "formal," "serious," or "deliberate."

"Casually" is an adverb, which means it describes how an action is done. When someone does something casually, they do it in a relaxed, informal, and unconcerned way — as if it requires no special effort, no formality, and no big deal.
A casualty is a person who has been killed, injured, or otherwise harmed as a result of an accident, a disaster, a war, or any other violent or dangerous event.
Clever but misleading reasoning used to justify something morally questionable. Originally, it meant resolving moral problems by studying the details of each individual case.
A cataclysm is a sudden, violent, and massive event that causes enormous destruction and fundamentally changes things — often forever. It is not just a bad event.
Cataclysmic describes something that is extremely violent, massively destructive, and so powerful that it fundamentally — and often permanently — changes the world or situation it hits.
A catacomb is an underground burial place made up of a network of tunnels and chambers carved into rock or earth, where human bodies or their remains are stored.

Catalepsy is a medical condition — or more precisely, a symptom — in which a person's body suddenly becomes rigid and freezes into a fixed position, while the person loses the ability to voluntarily move or respond to the world around them.

A catalyst is something — a substance, a person, an event, or an idea — that causes or speeds up a significant change, but with one special quality: it is not consumed or permanently destroyed in the process.
A catapult is a large, powerful machine built to throw heavy objects — such as stones, boulders, or other projectiles — over long distances with great force.
A medical condition in which the lens of the eye becomes cloudy, causing blurred vision. It can also mean a large, powerful waterfall.

A catastrophe is a sudden, severe event that causes massive destruction, widespread suffering, or total failure — something so devastating that it fundamentally changes a situation, often in ways that are very hard or impossible to undo.

Catastrophic describes something that causes enormous, devastating damage, destruction, or harm — on a scale so large and so severe that recovery is extremely difficult, takes a very long time, or may even be impossible.

Catatonia is a medical and psychiatric syndrome — meaning it's a recognized cluster of signs and symptoms, not a standalone disease — in which a person loses normal voluntary control over their movements, speech, and responsiveness to the world around them.
Catatonic describes a state in which a person is physically still and mentally cut off from the world around them — as if their mind and body have both pressed "pause" at the same time.
A catcall is an unwanted shout, whistle, or remark made in public — directed at a person, usually a stranger — that comments on their body or appearance in a sexual or objectifying way.
To "catch someone's drift" means to understand the general meaning, hint, or intention behind what someone is saying — especially when they haven't said it directly or completely.
A catch-22 is a situation where you are trapped because you need A to get B, but you also need B to get A — so no matter what you try, the rules themselves make it impossible to win.
A catchphrase is a short, memorable expression that becomes strongly connected to a specific person, character, brand, or cultural moment — and gets repeated over and over again by many people.
A catechism is a structured set of questions and answers designed to teach the core beliefs and principles of a religion.
Categorical means absolute, unconditional, and without any exceptions or qualifications whatsoever.

When someone says or does something categorically, they are doing it in a way that is completely, absolutely, and unconditionally — with no exceptions, no "ifs," no "buts," no room for doubt, and no possibility of being partially true or partially false.
To categorize something means to look at it, decide what type of thing it is, and place it into a group with other similar things.
A category is a group of things that share one or more common features, and are therefore treated as belonging together under one label.
Cater means to provide something that someone needs or wants — whether that is food at an event, or products and services tailored to a specific group of people.
A catered lunch is a midday meal that is professionally prepared and delivered (or served) by a hired food service, rather than being cooked at home or ordered individually by each person eating it.
A caterwaul is a loud, harsh, shrill, wailing sound — the kind that is unpleasant and almost painful to hear. It is not just any loud noise.
To caterwaul means to make a loud, harsh, shrill, and deeply unpleasant wailing or screeching sound.
Catharsis is a powerful emotional release — a purging of feelings that were bottled up inside — that leaves you feeling cleansed, lighter, or relieved afterward.
Cathartic describes something that helps you release pent-up emotions — and leaves you feeling emotionally cleansed, lighter, or relieved as a result.

A catheter is a thin, flexible tube that is inserted into the body — through a natural opening or a small incision — to either drain fluid out of a body part, deliver fluid or medicine into a body part, or keep a passage open.

When you see "catholic" written in lowercase and used as an adjective (not referring to the religion), it means having broad, wide-ranging tastes, interests, or sympathies — being open to and inclusive of many different kinds of things.

A catnap is a short, light sleep — one that lasts only a few minutes, or at most around 20 to 30 minutes. It is not a full, deep sleep. It is a quick rest that you take to refresh yourself, usually during the day.

Catty describes a person, remark, or behavior that is subtly cruel, spiteful, and mean-spirited — especially when it involves making nasty comments about other people, often behind their backs or in an indirect, sneaky way.
A catwalk is the long, narrow, raised platform that fashion models walk along during a fashion show, so that the audience seated on both sides can see the clothes up close.

When a group of people who share the same political goals or affiliations meet privately to talk things through, coordinate their strategy, or make a collective decision before a bigger, more public meeting or vote — that is what it means to caucus.

A caudillo is a powerful, authoritarian leader — typically military or political — who rules mainly through personal force, personal loyalty, and personal charisma, rather than through laws, institutions, or the democratic will of the people.

A cauldron is a very large, deep, round pot — the kind used for cooking or boiling a big quantity of liquid or food, especially over an open fire. Think of it as the biggest, heaviest cooking pot you can imagine, but older and more dramatic.
Caulk is a soft, paste-like sealing material used to fill small gaps, cracks, or joints between two surfaces — especially where they meet at a seam or edge.
Causal means relating to, involving, or expressing a cause — that is, anything connected to why something happens or what makes something happen.

Causality is the principle that every effect has a cause — and more specifically, it refers to the relationship between a cause and its effect. It's the idea that things don't just happen randomly; something makes them happen.
Causation is the relationship between a cause and its effect — it describes the fact that one thing brings about, produces, or is responsible for another thing.

A causeway is a raised, solid road or path that is built across water, marshy ground, swamps, or any low and wet area of land — so that people and vehicles can travel safely from one side to the other.
Of words or remarks, harshly and bitterly sarcastic in a way that stings, as in "a caustic comment." Of a chemical, able to burn or corrode living tissue.

Causticity means the quality or degree of being caustic — of having the power to burn, corrode, or cut. The word has two main lives: one in the physical world, and one in the world of language and personality.

To cauterize something means to deliberately burn or destroy a small area of body tissue — using heat, electricity, extreme cold, or a chemical — in order to achieve a specific medical purpose, most commonly to stop bleeding or prevent infection.
Cautionary means intended to warn someone — to alert people about danger, risk, or bad consequences so they can avoid them.
Cautious describes someone (or something) that is carefully aware of possible risks or dangers and acts in a way that avoids them. A cautious person doesn't rush.
A cavalcade is a long, impressive procession or sequence of things — people, vehicles, or events — moving or unfolding one after another, often in a grand or striking way.

When someone is cavalier, they treat something serious as if it doesn't matter much — with a breezy, dismissive attitude, as if they're too important or too relaxed to bother giving it proper care or respect.

Cavalry refers to a group of soldiers who fight while riding, rather than walking. Historically, this meant soldiers on horseback. In modern times, it means soldiers in fast-moving armored vehicles, like tanks.
A cave is a natural hollow space inside the earth or inside a rock formation — such as a hillside, a cliff, or a mountain — that is large enough for a person to enter.

When something caves, it collapses inward or gives way under pressure. That single idea — giving way under pressure — is the heart of this word, whether you're talking about a physical structure or a person's will.
To collapse inward, as a roof or tunnel does under weight; or to give in after resisting ("He finally caved in to their demands").

A caveat is a warning or caution that you attach to something — a statement, a plan, an agreement, a piece of advice — to say: "This is true or valid, but there's something important you need to know that limits it, changes it, or could affect it."

A caveman is a prehistoric human — one of the very early members of the human species (or closely related species) who lived thousands to millions of years ago, long before cities, schools, governments, or any form of modern civilization existed.

A cavern is a large, hollow space found underground or deep inside a rock formation — essentially, a very big cave. Think of it as a giant empty room that nature carved out over thousands of years, hidden beneath the earth.
Huge, deep, and hollow, like a cave — often feeling dark, empty, and echoing.
Caviar is the salt-preserved eggs of a sturgeon — a large, ancient species of fish. These eggs, also called roe, are carefully harvested, lightly salted, and packaged as a food delicacy.
To cavil means to raise small, petty, or unnecessary objections to something — especially when those objections are unfair or beside the point given how good the overall thing actually is.

A cavity is a hollow space or empty area that exists inside something solid. Think of it as a "hole within" — not a hole you can see from outside by looking at a flat surface, but a space that is enclosed or sunk into a solid material.

To cavort means to move around in a wild, energetic, and playful way — jumping, leaping, skipping, or bouncing with obvious excitement and joy, often without much care for looking graceful or dignified.
To cease means to stop — either something stops happening on its own, or someone deliberately brings something to an end.
Ceaseless means never stopping. Something that is ceaseless continues without any pause, break, or end. It keeps going and going, relentlessly, with no interruption.

To cede something means to formally and officially give it up to someone else — usually something significant like land, power, rights, or control — often because you are forced to, pressured to, or have agreed to do so through a treaty or deal.
A celebrant is a person who officially leads or performs a ceremony.
To celebrate means to do something special to mark an important or happy occasion — and to express joy about it.

When we call someone or something celebrated, we mean that they are widely known and widely praised — admired by many people, especially for being exceptionally good at something or for having outstanding qualities.

A celebrity is a person who is widely known and recognized by a very large number of people — typically because of their work or presence in a public field such as acting, music, sports, or politics — and who receives significant, ongoing attention and interest from both the public and the media.

Celerity means extreme swiftness or speed, especially in movement or action. When someone or something acts with celerity, they act with impressive, often urgent quickness — wasting no time whatsoever.
Celestial means "of or belonging to the sky, outer space, or heaven." It describes things that exist above the Earth — in the sky, among the stars, or in a divine realm.
Celiac simply means "relating to the abdomen" — specifically, the cavity inside your belly that houses your digestive organs (stomach, intestines, liver, etc.).
Celibacy is the deliberate choice to abstain from sexual activity and, in many cases, from marriage — and to maintain that choice as a long-term or even lifelong commitment.
When someone is described as celibate, it means they have made a deliberate, conscious choice to abstain from sexual activity. The key idea here is choice — celibacy is always voluntary.
Celluloid is a type of hard, lightweight, and slightly flexible plastic material — in fact, one of the very first man-made plastics ever created.
A cemetery is a piece of land that is set aside specifically and permanently for burying the bodies of dead people.

A cenotaph is a memorial structure — something like a monument, a tomb, or a large stone marker — that is built to honor a person or a group of people who are not actually buried there. The structure is completely empty.
A person or official body with the power to examine books, films, news, or other content and remove or block anything considered offensive, dangerous, or politically unacceptable.
Censorious describes a person who is excessively and harshly critical of others — someone who is always quick to find faults, point out flaws, and pass moral judgment.

Censorship is the act of blocking, suppressing, or controlling information, speech, art, or any form of communication — usually by someone in a position of power — so that other people cannot freely access, share, or express it.

Censure means strong, formal, and official disapproval of someone's behavior, expressed openly and on the record by a person or group with authority. It is not quiet disappointment. It is not a private complaint.

To censure someone is to formally and openly express strong disapproval of them — usually by an authority, group, or institution — because they did something considered wrong, unethical, or unacceptable.
A census is an official count of all the people living in a country — or sometimes a smaller area like a city or region — done at a specific point in time.
A cent is a very small unit of money. Specifically, it is one hundredth (1/100) of a larger currency unit.
A centaur is a creature from ancient Greek mythology — meaning it is entirely imaginary, not a real animal. It does not exist in the real world, only in stories, art, and legends.
A scale of temperature on which water freezes at 0 degrees and boils at 100 degrees. It is the same as Celsius.
The adjective centrifugal describes anything that is directed, moving, or tending to move away from a center point — especially when that movement is caused by spinning or rotation.
A centrifuge is a machine that spins a mixture at very high speed in order to separate its components from one another based on how heavy or dense they are.
Centripetal means directed or moving toward a center.
A centrist is a person whose political beliefs sit in the middle of the political spectrum — not leaning strongly to the left, and not leaning strongly to the right.
A centurion was a professional military officer in the ancient Roman army who commanded a unit of soldiers called a "century."

A cephalopod is a type of animal — specifically, a highly advanced, soft-bodied sea creature without a backbone. The group includes the octopus, squid, cuttlefish, and nautilus. These are the animals you are referring to whenever you use the word cephalopod.
Relating to the brain. Used of a person or work, it means intellectual and logical rather than emotional or instinctive.
To cerebrate simply means to think — to use your mind actively, to engage in mental activity or reasoning.
Cerebration simply means the act or process of thinking. It refers to the mind being at work — processing ideas, forming thoughts, reasoning through problems, or making sense of information.
The cerebrum is the largest part of the human brain.
Ceremonial describes anything that is related to, used in, or fitting for a ceremony — a formal, structured event held to mark something important or significant.

When you call something or someone ceremonious, you mean they are marked by a great deal of formal ritual, pomp, and elaborate procedure — often to a degree that feels stiff, exaggerated, or overdone.
A ceremony is a formal event — or a set of formal actions — that follows a fixed, agreed-upon order, performed to mark an important moment. It is not just any gathering or happening.

Certification is the official act — or the result of that act — by which a trusted, authoritative body confirms that a person, product, process, or organization meets a defined set of standards or requirements.

When something or someone is described as certified, it means an official authority has examined them, verified that they meet specific standards or requirements, and formally declared them to be what they claim to be.
To certify means to officially declare, confirm, or guarantee that something is true, correct, genuine, or meets a required standard — and to do so with authority and responsibility.
Certitude means the state of being completely and unshakably certain about something — a deep, inner sense of knowing that leaves no room for doubt whatsoever.

Cerulean means a specific shade of blue — the bright, clear, vivid blue of a cloudless sky on a perfect sunny day. When you look straight up on a calm, clear afternoon and see that rich, open blue overhead, you're looking at cerulean.
Cessation means the stopping or ending of something. When something that was happening — an action, a process, an event, or a state — comes to a stop, that stopping is called a cessation.
Cession means the formal, deliberate act of giving up something — and handing it over to someone else.
A cesspool is a large, sealed underground pit or tank that collects and stores human sewage — that is, the waste that goes down your toilet (urine, feces, and dirty water).
When used as an adjective, cetacean means of, relating to, or characteristic of the group of sea mammals that includes whales, dolphins, and porpoises.

A chador is a large, full-length garment — essentially a big piece of cloth — that some Muslim women, particularly in Iran, wear over themselves when they go out in public or enter sacred spaces like mosques and shrines.
To make skin sore by rubbing against it, as in "the straps chafed her shoulders." Figuratively, to feel irritated or impatient because of restrictions, as in "chafing at the rules."
Of skin, sore and red from being rubbed. Figuratively, irritated or annoyed.
In its most concrete sense, chaff is the dry, worthless husks of grain — the part that gets discarded, blown away, and left behind while the good grain is kept.
