Chafing is the soreness, rawness, or irritation that develops on skin when it is rubbed repeatedly against something — another patch of skin, a piece of clothing, or any surface.
Chagrin is a specific mix of two feelings at once: embarrassment and disappointment, stirred together into one uncomfortable emotion.
Chain mail is a type of flexible armor made by linking thousands of small metal rings together to form a continuous mesh — like a fabric, but made entirely of metal.

A chaise longue is a type of furniture — a long, padded chair that extends far enough forward for you to fully stretch out your legs while sitting or reclining. Think of it as a hybrid between an armchair and a bed.

A chalice is a special type of drinking cup. But not just any cup — think of it as a grand, ceremonial cup used for important rituals or formal occasions. It is the kind of cup that signals that something significant is happening.
Challah is a special type of bread deeply rooted in Jewish tradition.
A challenge is anything that demands effort, skill, or courage from you — something that isn't easy, but isn't necessarily impossible either. It sits in the space between "too easy" and "too hard."

A chamber is an enclosed, contained space — a room, compartment, or hollow area that is set apart from its surroundings and often serves a specific, dedicated purpose. Think of it as a space that is somewhat sealed off, private, or structurally defined.

The word chameleon captures one powerful idea: something that changes itself to fit its surroundings. This word has two layers of meaning — a real, living creature, and a way to describe people or things that behave like that creature.
Champ is simply a casual, shortened form of the word champion. That's the most important thing to understand about it.
A champion is someone who has competed against others and won, earning the top position in their field.

A championship is something connected to being the best — or to finding out who is the best. The word carries this idea of supreme excellence, and from that single core, it branches into a few closely related meanings.
A chancellor is a high-ranking official who holds significant authority — in a government, a university, a court of law, or a religious institution.
Chancy describes something that involves significant uncertainty and risk, where the outcome depends heavily on luck or chance — and where things could very easily go wrong.
A small, slow wobble in the Earth's rotation, which causes the North Pole to wander in a small circle over a period of about 14 months.

A changeling is a creature from old European folklore — specifically, it is a being secretly left behind in place of a human child that has been stolen away by supernatural creatures, most commonly fairies.
To channel means to direct something in a controlled, purposeful way along a specific path or toward a specific use.
A chant is a group of words or phrases that are spoken or sung out loud, repeatedly, in a steady rhythm. The repetition and the rhythm are what make it a chant — not just the words themselves.

Chaos means a state of complete disorder, confusion, and unpredictability — a total breakdown of structure and control, where nothing is organized, nothing follows a clear pattern, and nobody is successfully managing what's happening.

Chaotic describes a situation, place, person, system, or event that is in a state of complete disorder, confusion, and lack of control — where things are happening unpredictably, randomly, or all at once in a way that is impossible to manage or make sense of.

Chaparral is a specific type of wild, natural landscape — one dominated by a dense, tangled mass of low-to-medium-height shrubs, bushes, and woody plants. It is not a forest with tall trees, and it is not an open grassland.

A chapbook is a small, thin booklet — typically just a handful of pages long — that is cheap to make and easy to carry around. Think of it as a miniature book, the kind you could slip into your pocket.
A theatrical act in which a performer twists a single ring of felt into dozens of different hat shapes, one after another, to portray different characters.

A chapel is a small place dedicated to Christian worship. Picture it as a quieter, more intimate version of a church — a space where people go to pray, attend religious services, or find spiritual comfort.

A chaperone is a responsible person — usually older or in a position of authority — who accompanies and supervises others (typically younger people) in a social setting, with the purpose of keeping them safe, well-behaved, or out of trouble.

To chaperone someone means to go with them to a social event or public place and watch over them — ensuring they are safe and behaving appropriately. You are not just "going along." You are taking on a responsibility.
A priest, minister, or other religious leader who gives spiritual care within an institution such as a hospital, prison, school, or the armed forces.
A chapstick is a small stick of soft, waxy balm that you rub directly onto your lips to keep them moist, smooth, and protected.

To char something means to burn it partially — just enough that its surface turns black and brittle — without burning it completely to ash. The thing still exists. It still has its shape. But its outer surface has been scorched into a layer of black carbon.
To characterize something means to describe it by focusing on its most important, defining qualities — the features that make it what it is, or that make it stand out from other things.
A pretence or show that is obviously false, intended to make something seem real or true when it is not. Charades is also a party game of acting out words without speaking.
The verb charge has many meanings, but they all share one underlying idea: directing something — force, energy, money, or authority — toward a target.
A slight difference in the way the laws of physics treat matter and antimatter, which may explain why the universe is made almost entirely of matter.

Charisma is a powerful, magnetic personal quality that some people naturally possess, which makes others feel drawn to them, captivated by them, and eager to listen to, trust, or follow them — often without being able to fully explain why.
When we say someone is charismatic, we mean they have a powerful, almost magnetic quality that naturally draws people toward them.
In its most common, everyday sense, charitable describes someone — or something — that gives help, money, time, or resources to people who need it, without expecting anything in return.
Charity is about giving something freely to someone who needs it — without expecting anything back. That "something" can be money, help, food, or even just kindness and a fair judgment.
A charlatan is a person who pretends to have skills, knowledge, or expertise that they do not actually possess, usually to trick people into giving them money, trust, or power.

The most important and widely used meaning of charm is a special quality in a person — or sometimes a place or thing — that naturally draws other people in, makes them feel pleased, and wins them over.

A charter is a formal, written document that officially grants something — rights, powers, permission, or authority — from one party to another. Think of it as an official "you are now authorized to do or have this," put in writing and made legally binding.

Chary means being very careful and cautious — either about doing something, giving something, or trusting something. A chary person holds back. They don't rush in. They think carefully before they act, give, or commit.
Chase means to go after something or someone quickly, with effort and intention — because you want to catch it, reach it, or stop it from getting away.
A chasm is a deep, wide gap or opening — the kind that dramatically splits something into two separate sides with a vast empty space in between.
A chassis is the structural frame — the underlying skeleton — of a vehicle, machine, or device. It is the rigid, load-bearing foundation onto which all the other parts are mounted or attached.

Chaste means exercising restraint or purity in sexual behaviour. A chaste person avoids sexual activity that is considered inappropriate — either by abstaining from sex altogether, or by being faithful and modest within the bounds of a committed relationship.

To chasten someone means to correct, discipline, or humble them — in a way that makes them better. The word carries a very specific flavour: the pain or difficulty involved is not meant to destroy or merely punish, but to improve.
To chastise someone means to scold, criticize, or punish them sharply because they have done something wrong.
Chastisement means the act of punishing or severely scolding someone in order to correct their behavior.

Chastity is the quality of being pure, disciplined, and restrained in sexual behavior. It means choosing not to engage in sexual activity that falls outside the moral, religious, or personal standards a person holds.
A chateau is a large, grand French country house or castle — the kind of magnificent, sprawling building that historically belonged to French royalty, nobility, or very wealthy landowners.
A chattel is any item of personal property that you own — something that belongs to you and can be moved, bought, sold, or transferred. Think of it as "stuff you own that isn't land or a building."

To chauffeur someone around means to drive a person from one place to another, often to multiple destinations, repeatedly, or on a regular basis. The person doing the driving is acting like a personal driver — taking someone wherever they need to go.

Chauvinism is the strong, excessive, and usually irrational belief that your own group is superior to another group — and that because of this superiority, the other group deserves less respect, fewer rights, or lower status. It is never a neutral word.

A chauvinist is a person who has an excessive, blind, and unshakeable belief that their own group is superior to all others — and who, based on that belief, looks down on, dismisses, or treats people from outside their group as lesser or less deserving.

To cheap out means to deliberately choose a cheaper, lower-quality option at a moment when quality actually matters — and as a result, disappointing people, causing problems, or producing a poor outcome.
A cheapskate is a person who strongly dislikes spending money — not because they can't afford it, but because they simply refuse to part with it, even when they clearly should.
To check means to look at something carefully to make sure it is correct, safe, true, or in good condition. This is the central idea behind almost everything this word does.
Of someone's past, marked by periods of trouble or scandal as well as success, as in "a checkered career." Literally, having a pattern of squares of alternating colours, like a chessboard.
"Cheeky" describes a person or behavior that is a little bold, slightly disrespectful, or pushes a boundary — but in a playful, light-hearted way that makes it hard to stay angry about.

To cheese someone off means to annoy, irritate, or frustrate someone — to make them feel fed up or displeased. When you cheese someone off, you do something that gets under their skin and puts them in a bad mood.
Cheeseparing describes someone who is extremely and pettily unwilling to spend money or share resources — even when they can afford to be more generous.

A chemise is a simple, loose, straight-hanging garment for the body — one with almost no shaping, no tight waistline, no structural complexity. Think of a soft tube of fabric that drapes straight down from the shoulders. That simplicity is what defines it.
Chemotherapy is a medical treatment that uses powerful chemical drugs to destroy or stop the growth of cancer cells in the body.
A soft, thick, fuzzy yarn, or the velvety fabric made from it, often used for blankets, cushions, and upholstery.
Of a person's past or history, marked by periods of trouble, failure, or scandal, as in "a chequered career." Literally, having a pattern of squares of two colours.
The faint blue glow given off when a charged particle travels through a material such as water faster than light itself moves through that material.

A cherub is a type of angel. But this word carries two very different images depending on where you encounter it — the original religious one and the popular artistic one — and they look almost nothing alike.

Cherubic is an adjective that describes someone — usually a person's face, appearance, or expression — that looks sweet, innocent, round-cheeked, and angelically cute, much like the classic image of a baby angel.
To "chew the fat" means to have a long, relaxed, friendly conversation — usually about nothing very serious or important.
In art, the use of strong contrasts between light and dark to create a sense of depth, volume, and mood on a flat surface.

When you call something or someone chic, you mean they are stylish and elegant — but in a very specific way. Chic is not just "good-looking" or "fashionable." It means a kind of refined, sophisticated style that looks effortless.
A chicane is a tight, S-shaped series of bends or obstacles that is deliberately placed on a road or racetrack to force drivers to slow down and navigate carefully.

Chicanery means using clever, sneaky tricks and deceptive talk to mislead or manipulate someone — usually to get what you want or to escape blame. It is dishonesty with a layer of cleverness on top of it.

A chickpea is a small, round, edible seed that grows inside the pod of a plant called the chickpea plant (Cicer arietinum). It belongs to a group of plants called legumes — the same family as lentils, peas, and beans.
To chide someone means to express disapproval of their behavior by speaking to them about it — to tell them, in words, that what they did or said was wrong, unwise, or disappointing.
Chiffon is a type of fabric — a textile, a cloth. But not just any cloth. It is one of the most delicate, lightweight fabrics that exists.
A chiffonade is a collection of very thin, delicate, ribbon-like strips made from leafy vegetables or fresh herbs.

A chignon is a specific type of hairstyle — a smooth, neat knot or roll of hair that is pinned or twisted up at the back of the head, most commonly at the nape of the neck (the lower back part of the head, where it meets the neck), though it can also sit a little higher.
A chihuahua is a breed of dog. More specifically, it is the smallest recognized dog breed in the entire world.
To chime in means to join a conversation that is already happening by adding your own comment, opinion, or thought.

Something hoped for that is impossible to achieve; a wild dream or illusion. In Greek mythology, the Chimera was a fire-breathing monster with the head of a lion, the body of a goat, and the tail of a snake.
Something is chimerical when it is so wildly imaginary and detached from reality that it could never actually exist or come true.
A chink is a very small, narrow opening — a thin gap or crack — in something that is otherwise solid or closed. Think of it as a tiny slit that breaks through a surface.

Chintz is a type of cotton fabric — but not just any plain cotton. It has two defining qualities that set it apart: a colorful printed pattern (almost always floral or nature-themed) and a smooth, slightly shiny surface finish called a glaze.
Chintzy is a word that captures a specific kind of cheapness — either in a person's behavior (being stingy with money) or in the quality/appearance of a thing (looking cheap, flimsy, or low-quality).
A small piece broken off something hard, or the mark left behind. A chip is also a thin crisp slice of potato, a tiny electronic circuit, or a token used in gambling.

When someone has a chip on their shoulder, it means they carry a persistent feeling of anger, resentment, or bitterness — usually because they believe they have been treated unfairly, disrespected, or looked down upon at some point in their life.
Chipper means cheerful, lively, and in good spirits. When someone is chipper, they are in a bright, happy mood — and they show it actively through their energy, their voice, and their behavior.

Chiromancy is the practice of reading a person's character, personality, and future by closely examining the lines, shapes, and physical features of their hands — especially the palms. It is also commonly called palmistry or palm reading.
A chiropodist is a trained and qualified healthcare professional who specializes in the care, diagnosis, and treatment of problems related to the feet and lower legs.

Chiropractic is a form of healthcare that focuses on diagnosing and treating problems related to the musculoskeletal system — the bones, joints, muscles, and connective tissues of the body — with particular emphasis on the spine.

A chirp is a short, sharp, high-pitched sound. Think of the quick little sound a small bird makes in the morning — that brief, bright tweet — that's a chirp. It is not a long, drawn-out sound. It is not deep or booming. It is small, quick, and light.
To chirp is to make — or to say something in — a short, sharp, high-pitched sound. Think of a small bird singing in the morning: the sound is quick, light, and bright. That is a chirp.
A chisel is a hand tool used to cut, carve, or shape hard materials like wood, stone, or metal.

Chitchat is light, casual, friendly conversation about small, everyday, unimportant things. It is the kind of talking people do simply to be sociable — not to solve a problem, share important news, or discuss anything serious.

Chivalrous describes a person who is deeply courteous, honorable, kind, and considerate — especially someone who goes out of their way to show respect, care, and protection toward others, often in a noble or gentlemanly manner.
The ideal code of conduct of medieval knights, including courage, honour, and protecting the weak. Today, it usually means polite and considerate behaviour, especially by men towards women.
Chlorpromazine is a prescription medication used primarily to treat serious mental illnesses — especially schizophrenia — by calming abnormal brain activity.

"Chockablock" means so completely crammed or stuffed full that there is almost no empty space left. It describes something packed to its absolute limit — not just full, but bursting full, with things pressed tightly together and barely any breathing room.
Choice refers to the act, result, or freedom of selecting one thing from two or more possibilities. It always involves picking — consciously and deliberately — from a set of available options.
A choir is an organized group of people who sing together as one unit. The key word here is organized — a choir is not just any bunch of people who happen to be singing at the same time.

To choke back something means to stop a strong emotion or reaction from coming out, even though it is very difficult to do so. You feel something powerfully — like sadness, anger, or laughter — but you force yourself to hold it in and not let it show.

A choke hold is a grip applied around a person's neck that cuts off either their air supply, their blood supply to the brain, or both — causing them to become helpless, unconscious, or in extreme cases, to die.
When something is described as choking, it means it is so thick, dense, strong, or overwhelming that it blocks or tightens the ability to breathe — or feels like it does.
Anger or irritability. In old medicine, choler was yellow bile, one of the four bodily fluids believed to control a person's mood.
Cholera is a serious infectious disease that attacks a person's digestive system — specifically the small intestine — and can cause extreme, life-threatening dehydration very rapidly if not treated.

Choleric means having a hot, quick temper — the kind of person who gets angry fast, often over things that wouldn't bother most people, and whose anger tends to be intense and visible. If someone is choleric, they don't simmer quietly; they flare up.

Something that is choppy is broken into small, uneven, irregular pieces or movements — lacking smoothness, flow, or steadiness. It gives a sense of something that keeps getting disrupted instead of moving in one continuous, controlled way.
Choral means relating to, written for, or performed by a choir — a group of singers who sing together.

A chore is a routine task that must be done regularly, but is generally considered dull, tiresome, or unpleasant. It is not something you do for fun or because you love it — it is something you do because it needs to be done.
To choreograph something means to carefully plan, design, and arrange every movement, step, or action in a sequence so that the whole thing comes together in a smooth, deliberate, and controlled way.
Choreography is the art of planning and arranging dance movements — deciding which movements a dancer (or a group of dancers) will perform, in what order, to what rhythm, and in what space.
A chortle is a specific type of laugh — one that is joyful, gleeful, and a little triumphant. It is louder than a chuckle and more uncontrolled, but it is not a full roar of laughter.

To chortle means to laugh in a way that is breathy, gleeful, and full of deep satisfaction — often with a soft snorting quality mixed in. It is the sound of someone who is not just amused, but truly, warmly delighted.
All meanings of chorus share one unifying idea: many things — voices, sounds, or people — coming together as one unified whole.
A Christmas cracker is a festive cardboard tube wrapped in brightly colored, decorative paper, with each end twisted closed so it looks a bit like a giant wrapped candy or a large bon-bon.

The word chromatic is an adjective that essentially means "relating to color" or, in music, "relating to all possible notes within an octave." It has two major areas of meaning — one in the world of color and light, and one in the world of music.

Chronic describes something that has lasted for a long time, keeps coming back, or shows no sign of going away. Think of it as the opposite of a quick, passing problem. If something is chronic, it has settled in and made itself at home.
A chronicle is a written record of events arranged in the order in which they happened — from the earliest to the most recent. Think of it as a timeline put into words.
To chronicle something means to record events carefully, in detail, and in the order they happened — over a period of time.

Chronological is an adjective that describes things arranged in the order they happened in time, starting from the earliest and moving toward the most recent. It is all about time sequence — what came first, what came second, what came after that, and so on.

A chronology is a list or record of events arranged in the order they happened — from the earliest event to the most recent. The key idea is time order. A chronology answers one simple question: "What happened, and when?"

A chronometer is an exceptionally precise and accurate timekeeping instrument — essentially a clock or watch, but one that is built and tested to a far higher standard of accuracy than an ordinary timepiece.

A chrysalis is the protective shell-like casing that a caterpillar seals itself inside while it transforms into a butterfly. Think of it as a natural "transformation chamber" — a temporary home where one of nature's most dramatic changes takes place.

Chthonic means of or relating to the underworld — specifically, the realm of the dead beneath the earth. It also carries the broader sense of being deeply, primordially connected to the earth itself, its darkest and most hidden depths.
A chuckle is a soft, quiet laugh — one that stays low and controlled, never bursting out loudly. It's the kind of laugh you make when something amuses you, but not enough to make you laugh out loud.
Chuffed means feeling very pleased, happy, or proud — usually because something good happened to you or you received a compliment, achieved something, or got some good news.
A close friend (informal), as in "an old chum from school." Chum is also chopped-up fish thrown into the water as bait to attract fish or sharks.
When fishermen "chum" the water, they throw a mixture of chopped fish, fish blood, fish guts, and other messy, smelly organic matter into the water.
Chummy means very friendly and informal with someone, in the way that close friends are with each other.
A chump is a person who is foolish, naive, or easily tricked — someone who gets taken advantage of because they lack good judgment or street smarts.
Thick, solid, and heavy, as in "a chunky sweater." Of food, containing thick pieces. Of a person, broad and stocky.
A churl is a person who is rude, mean-spirited, or unpleasant — specifically someone who behaves badly in situations where decency, generosity, or good manners would normally be expected.
Churlish means being rude, ungracious, and unpleasant in a grumpy, sullen way — especially in a situation where basic politeness or generosity is expected from a decent person.
To stir or move liquid violently, as when making butter from cream. Of the stomach, to feel sick and unsettled from anxiety. To churn out means to produce large amounts of something quickly.
"Churning" describes something that is in a state of violent, turbulent, swirling movement — not calm, not still, but forcefully mixed up, tossed around, and agitated in a continuous, restless way.
A churro is a long, ridged stick of fried dough, sweet and golden, that is eaten as a snack or a treat.
A chutney is a thick, flavoured condiment — something you eat alongside food, not as food on its own. Think of it as a bold, concentrated mixture that adds punch, sweetness, heat, or tang to a meal.

Chutzpah means extreme boldness or audacity — the kind that makes others think, "How dare they?!" It describes a person who does something shockingly brazen, with zero shame or embarrassment, as if the outrageous thing they're doing is completely normal.

A cicada is a type of insect — specifically, a medium-to-large winged insect found in forests, woodlands, and warm regions across almost every continent on Earth. There are over 3,000 known species of cicadas in the world.
Something is described as ciliated when it has cilia — tiny, hair-like structures projecting from its surface.
The original, literal meaning of cinch is a strong, tight strap that wraps around a horse's belly to keep the saddle firmly in place.
To cinch something means to pull something tight and hold it firmly in place — to secure it so it won't slip, loosen, or escape.

Cinematic means "relating to cinema" — that is, relating to movies and filmmaking. But this is only the starting point. The word's real power comes from a richer, figurative meaning that goes far beyond just talking about films.

A cipher is a specific, rule-based system for transforming a normal, readable message into a scrambled, unreadable one — and then back again. The purpose is secrecy: only someone who knows the rules of the cipher can decode the message and understand it.
Circadian is an adjective that means relating to a biological cycle that repeats approximately every 24 hours.

A circlet is a thin, smooth band — usually made of metal like gold or silver — worn around the head as a decorative ornament or as a symbol of rank and status. Picture a large ring, sized for your head, resting on your forehead and going all the way around.
A route or path that goes around and returns to where it started. An electrical circuit is the complete path that electricity flows around. A circuit is also a regular series of events or venues.
Circuitous means indirect — taking a longer, more winding path to reach a destination or a point, instead of going straight there.

To move continuously around a system, as blood does through the body. It also means for news or rumours to spread from person to person, or to pass something around among a group, as in "circulate a memo."

Circulation means the continuous, ongoing movement of something through a system — where that something travels along a path, spreads out, and often comes back around to where it started. Think of it as things flowing rather than sitting still.
Circumlocution is the act of saying something in a roundabout, indirect way using more words than necessary, when the same idea could have been expressed much more simply and directly.
To circumnavigate something means to travel all the way around it in a complete loop, returning to where you started — OR — to find a clever way around something that's blocking or restricting you.
When you circumscribe something, you place limits on it. You define a space — often a figurative one — within which something must stay. Whatever falls outside that space is off-limits.
Circumspect means being carefully watchful in all directions before you say or do something — thinking through every possible angle, consequence, and risk so that you don't make a careless mistake.

Circumspection means the quality of being very careful and thoughtful — especially before making a decision, taking an action, or saying something important. It means pausing to consider all possible risks, consequences, and angles before you proceed.
A circumstance is a fact, condition, or event that exists around a situation and affects how it happens, how it's understood, or how it's judged.
Based on surrounding facts that suggest something is true but do not prove it directly, as in "circumstantial evidence."
To circumvent something means to find a clever, indirect way around it — instead of going through it, dealing with it head-on, or breaking it directly.

Circumvention is the act of getting around something — usually a rule, a law, a system, or an obstacle — without directly breaking it or confronting it head-on. Instead of going through something, you go around it, cleverly and often secretly.
A cistern is a container — usually large — designed specifically to collect and store water (or sometimes another liquid). Think of it as a reservoir that holds liquid until it is needed.

A citadel is a strongly built, heavily fortified structure — essentially a fortress — placed at the highest or most defensible point within or right beside a city. It is designed to be the last and strongest line of defense when a city is under attack.
A citation is a formal reference that points to the source of a piece of information, a quote, an idea, or an achievement. Think of it as a signpost that says: "This came from here."
When you cite something, you officially point to it — you bring it forward as evidence, support, or acknowledgment of where something came from.

When we say someone is citified, we mean they have taken on the habits, attitudes, appearance, and ways of life that are typical of people who live in cities — often to the point where they seem out of place in a rural or country setting, or have noticeably left behind their rural roots.
Civics is the study of what it means to be a citizen — your rights, your duties, and how the government and society you live in actually work.

When someone is described as "civil," they are behaving politely enough — not rude, not hostile — but not necessarily warm or genuinely friendly either. "Civil" describes the baseline of acceptable social behavior. It's the floor, not the ceiling.
A civilian is a person who is not a member of the military — not a soldier, sailor, airman, or any other armed forces personnel.

Civility is the quality of treating other people with basic politeness, respect, and decency — especially in a shared social space, in public life, or when you are dealing with people you disagree with, dislike, or simply don't know.
A civilization is a large, complex, and organized human society that has developed advanced systems for people to live together, work together, and build a shared way of life.
To civilize someone or a group means to raise or develop them to what is considered a higher, more educated, more refined, or more socially organized state of existence.
Clabber is milk that has naturally soured and thickened on its own, turning into a soft, lumpy, gel-like mass — without anyone doing anything to it deliberately.
Clad means covered — either by clothing (worn on a person) or by a material (layered over a surface). Think of it as a more literary, formal, or elegant way of saying "dressed in" or "covered with."
Claim means either to state something as true or to say something belongs to you — both with a sense of asserting, insisting, or putting yourself forward.
Clairvoyance is the supposed ability to know or perceive things that cannot possibly be known through your ordinary five senses — sight, hearing, touch, taste, and smell.

If someone or something is described as clairvoyant, it means having the ability to perceive things that go completely beyond the reach of normal human senses — things that cannot be seen, heard, touched, tasted, or smelled in any ordinary way.

A clairvoyant is a person who claims to have the supernatural ability to perceive information about people, objects, events, or situations that cannot be known through the five ordinary senses — sight, hearing, touch, taste, and smell.
Clamant means urgently and insistently demanding attention — so loud, pressing, or forceful that it simply cannot be ignored.
To clamber means to climb something in a clumsy, effortful way — using both your hands and your feet (or your whole body) to pull yourself up, over, or through something difficult.

Something is clammy when it feels unpleasantly damp, cold, and slightly sticky all at once. It is not just wet. It is not just cold. It has a specific, uncomfortable combination of all three — and that combined feeling is what "clammy" captures.
Clamorous describes something or someone that is loud, noisy, and impossible to ignore — but not just "loud" in a simple way.
A loud, confused noise made by many people shouting at once. It can also mean a strong, widespread demand or protest, as in "a clamour for change."
To clamp down on something means to take strong, strict action to stop, control, or limit something — especially something that is considered harmful, illegal, or problematic.
A clan is a large group of people who are all connected to each other through a shared ancestor — a common person in the distant past from whom everyone in the group descends.
Clandestine means done in secret — especially because it is forbidden, disapproved of, or would cause serious trouble if discovered.
Clangor means a loud, harsh, metallic ringing or banging sound — especially one that is continuous, repeated, or fills the air. It is not just any loud noise.
Clap means to strike two flat surfaces — most often your two palms — together sharply to produce a sound. That sharp, quick sound is central to almost everything this word means.

A clapper is something — or someone — that produces a sharp, striking sound by hitting one surface against another. Think of it as a "thing that claps." That one idea connects all its different meanings.
Claptrap is talk or writing that sounds impressive or convincing on the surface, but is actually empty, meaningless, or dishonest underneath.
To clarify something means to make it clearer — to remove the fog of confusion, vagueness, or misunderstanding surrounding it, so that it becomes easy to understand.

When something is described as clarion, it means it is loud, sharp, ringing, and brilliantly clear — the kind of sound or message that cuts right through everything around it and demands your full attention immediately.

Clarity means the quality of being clear — completely free from confusion, vagueness, blurriness, or doubt. When something has clarity, it is easy to understand, see, or grasp. Nothing about it is muddled or ambiguous.

To clasp something means to hold it tightly and securely by wrapping your fingers, hands, or arms around it. It's not a loose or casual hold — it's a firm, close, enclosing grip, the kind where the thing you're holding feels locked in place.

A classic is something — usually a creative work like a book, film, piece of music, or painting — that is widely recognized as being of the highest quality and has stood the test of time. Both parts matter equally.
Classy means having style, elegance, and good taste — in a way that feels natural, confident, and effortless.
A clatter is a loud, sharp, rattling noise made when hard objects repeatedly strike each other or hit a hard surface — usually quickly, one after another. It's not a single sound.
To crash into someone or something with a loud, clumsy collision.
Claustrophobia is an intense, overwhelming fear of being in small, enclosed, or confined spaces — or in situations where a person feels trapped, unable to escape, or cut off from open air.
The word "claustrophobic" describes either a person who fears enclosed spaces, or a place/situation that feels dangerously small, cramped, or suffocating.
The clavicle is a bone in your body — specifically, the bone most people call the collarbone.

A claw is a hard, sharp, curved nail found at the tip of an animal's toe or finger. Think of it like a human fingernail — but much tougher, much sharper, and curved like a hook. Claws are made of keratin, the same material your own nails are made of.
To claw is to scratch, tear, dig into, or grab at something using sharp nails, claws, or fingertips — with force, urgency, and often desperation.
To claw back something means to recover or take back something that was given away, lost, or taken from you — usually with considerable effort, and often through deliberate action or force.
To "claw one's way" means to achieve something or move forward through enormous effort, struggle, and determination — especially when there are many obstacles in the way.
A natural, fine-grained earth that is soft and easy to shape when wet, and becomes hard and permanent when dried or fired, as in pottery and bricks.

A clear conscience is the peaceful, calm feeling inside you when you know that you have done nothing wrong — that you have acted honestly, kindly, and fairly, and that you have no reason to feel guilty or ashamed about anything.
To empty a room or space by removing everything you don't want. Informally, it also means to leave a place quickly.
To explain or resolve a confusion or problem. It can also mean to tidy a place, for the weather to become fine, or for an illness to go away.
An open area of land inside a forest, where there are no trees. In banking, clearing is the process of transferring money between banks.
Cleavage means a split, a crack, or a division — especially one that happens along a natural line of weakness or a natural boundary.
To split or cut something apart with force, as with an axe. Strangely, it can also mean the opposite — to stick closely to someone or something, as in "cleave to one's beliefs."

A cleft is a narrow crack, split, or opening in something solid — the kind of gap that appears when a surface or object has been divided or split apart, but not completely separated into two separate pieces.

Clemency means showing mercy and leniency toward someone who deserves punishment — choosing to be kind, gentle, and forgiving instead of strict and harsh, especially when you have the power to punish severely but decide not to.

"Clement" essentially means mild and not harsh. That single idea — mildness, gentleness, the absence of severity — is the heart of this word. It branches into two distinct but closely related uses: one about people, and one about weather.

To clench means to tighten or press a part of your body firmly and forcefully, holding it in a stiff, locked position. Think of it as the body's way of gripping itself — muscles tightening inward, pressing together hard.

A clerestory is the upper portion of a wall in a building that rises above the roofs of the lower sections beside it, and is pierced with windows to let light (and sometimes air) flood into the interior below.
Clergy refers to the group of people who are officially appointed, ordained, or recognized as religious leaders within a religion or a religious institution.
A clergyman is a man who has been officially appointed or ordained to carry out religious duties as his profession or calling.

A cleric is a person who has been officially appointed or ordained to serve as a leader or official within a religion. Think of a priest in a church, an imam in a mosque, a rabbi in a synagogue, or a monk in a monastery — all of these people are clerics.
Relating to office work, such as typing, filing, and keeping records. It can also mean relating to the clergy, as in "a clerical collar."

When you call someone or something clever, you mean they show a special kind of sharp, quick thinking — the ability to understand things fast, solve problems in smart ways, and come up with ideas that others might not think of easily.
A cliché is a phrase, idea, or image that was once fresh and powerful, but has been repeated so many times that it has lost all its original strength and meaning. It has gone stale.
A client is a person, group, or organization that receives a service from someone else — usually a professional or a business — often in exchange for money.
Clientele means the entire group of customers or clients that a business or professional regularly serves.
Forming the most intense, exciting, or important part of a story or series of events, as in "the climactic scene."
Climate change refers to significant, long-term shifts in global temperatures and weather patterns — affecting the entire Earth, not just one region.
When something climaxes, it reaches its highest, most intense, or most important point — after building up toward it.

A clime is a region, land, or tract of the earth — particularly one thought of in terms of its atmosphere, weather, or overall character. Think of it as a "place with a distinct feel," where that feel is shaped largely by its climate and natural quality.

To hold on tightly to someone or something, as in "the child clung to her mother." Figuratively, to refuse to give up a belief or hope, as in "clinging to the past." It also means to stick closely to a surface.

A clinic is a place where people go to receive healthcare — to see a doctor, get a checkup, ask for medical advice, or get treatment for a health problem. Think of it as a smaller, more focused version of a hospital.
In its most precise, technical sense, "clinical" means relating to the direct observation, diagnosis, and treatment of patients — as opposed to work done in a laboratory or based on theory alone.

A clinical trial is a carefully controlled scientific study conducted on human beings to find out whether a medical treatment — such as a drug, vaccine, surgery, medical device, or therapy — is safe and effective before it becomes available to the general public.

Clinomania is an excessive, obsessive, and often uncontrollable desire to stay in bed — not because your body genuinely needs rest, but because of a powerful, deep, almost irresistible compulsion to remain lying down, even when life is calling you to get up.
Something clinquant glitters or shines in a flashy, dazzling way — but the shine is superficial, cheap, or imitative rather than genuinely valuable.
A short extract from a film or recording. A clip is also a small device that holds things together, such as a paper clip or hair clip.

"Clipped" means cut short — made shorter than it naturally would be, in a way that feels deliberate, sharp, and often a little abrupt. That core idea of "cutting short" runs through every use of this word.
A tool for cutting hair or nails. Historically, a clipper was a fast sailing ship.

A clique is a small, tight group of people who are very close to one another — but who also, importantly, make it difficult for outsiders to join them. Think of it as a social circle with a locked door.

A cloak is a long, loose outer garment — essentially a large piece of fabric that drapes over your shoulders and hangs down, wrapping around most of your body. Think of it as a wearable blanket shaped into clothing.

To cloak something means to hide, cover, or conceal it — but not in a simple or obvious way. It specifically implies hiding something so well that it becomes hard to detect, see through, or recognize for what it truly is.

Clobber means to hit someone or something very hard. But in everyday use, it has grown well beyond just physical hitting — it covers any situation where something is struck, defeated, damaged, or attacked with overwhelming force.

A clod is a compact, solid chunk of dirt, soil, or clay. Think of it as a piece of earth that has stuck together and hardened into a rough, irregular lump — not a smooth, round ball, but a dense, blocky mass.
A covered walkway around an open courtyard in a monastery, cathedral, or college, with arches on the courtyard side.

Cloistered means sheltered and cut off from the outside world — living or existing in a way that keeps you enclosed, protected, and separated from the wider experiences, realities, or influences of ordinary life.
Close-knit describes a group of people who are deeply and strongly connected to each other.

A clot is a thick, lumpy mass that forms when a liquid — especially blood — changes from a flowing state into something semi-solid. Think of it this way: if you leave warm milk out for too long, it starts to curdle and form thick, gooey lumps.
Power and influence, as in "political clout." Informally, it also means a heavy blow with the hand.
Cloven means split into two parts, especially along a natural line or groove running down the middle.
A clown is a person whose purpose — or behavior — is to make others laugh, usually through exaggerated silliness, foolishness, or absurdity. Everything else about it grows from this core.
"Cloying" describes something so excessively sweet, rich, sentimental, or overwhelming that it has stopped being pleasant and crossed into something suffocating, sickening, or irritating.

A club is a thick, heavy stick — usually wider or heavier at one end — used for hitting. This is one of its oldest meanings. Think of a blunt weapon someone might carry into battle, or the kind of primitive tool you'd picture early humans using.
Club foot is a birth defect where a baby's foot or feet turn inward. When you look at the foot, the bottom often faces sideways or even upward.
Clueless means having absolutely no knowledge, understanding, or awareness — either about a specific topic, or about what is happening around you.

Clumsy means lacking smoothness, control, or care — in the way someone moves, acts, speaks, or does things. The result of being clumsy is usually accidents, mistakes, or outcomes that look rough and unpolished.
A cluster is a group of similar things that are gathered closely together — in the same place, at the same time, or connected in some meaningful way.
To clutch something means to hold it very tightly — usually with your hand or fingers — in a way that shows urgency, fear, anxiety, or desperation.

Clutter is a collection of things that are messy, disorganized, and spread around in a way that makes a space feel crowded, chaotic, or difficult to use. It's what happens when too many things pile up in a place with no real order to them.
To clutter something means to fill a space with too many objects in a messy, disorganized way — so much so that the space feels crowded, hard to use, or difficult to move through.
When you co-opt something or someone, you pull it into your group or system and make it serve your purposes — usually in a way that strips it of its original independence.
A coadjutor is a person officially appointed to assist someone in a position of authority — and who is simultaneously designated to succeed that person when they eventually leave their role.
A coagulant is a substance that causes a liquid to clump, thicken, or solidify — turning it from a free-flowing liquid into a gel, clot, or solid mass. The process it triggers is called coagulation.

To coagulate means to change from a liquid (or something liquid-like) into a thicker, semi-solid, or solid clumped mass — usually triggered by something like heat, a chemical reaction, or a biological process happening inside the body.
Coagulation is the process by which a liquid transforms into a thick, gel-like, or solid mass. Think of it as a liquid "deciding" to firm up and clump together under certain conditions.
For separate things to come together and gradually merge into a single, unified whole.
A coalition is a group of people, organizations, or countries that come together and agree to work as one unit — but only for a specific purpose or period of time.
The word coarse always points to one of two things: something that is rough and unrefined in a physical sense, or someone whose behavior or language is rough and unrefined in a social sense.

To coast means to move forward or make progress without putting in any real effort — because something else is doing the work for you. That something could be gravity, momentum, or a past advantage you built up earlier.
The word coat has three distinct but connected meanings. All of them share one underlying idea: a covering layer that goes on top of something else.
To coax means to gently and patiently persuade someone — or carefully handle something — using softness and skill rather than force or commands.

A cobbler is a craftsperson whose job is to repair and restore footwear — shoes, boots, sandals, and similar items. When your shoe sole comes apart, the heel wears down, or the leather cracks, you take it to a cobbler.
The coccyx is the small, triangular bone at the very bottom of your spine. You might already know it by its everyday name: the tailbone.

A cockade is a small decorative badge or ornament — usually made from ribbons, folded cloth, or feathers — shaped into a rosette (a circular, flower-like shape) or a neat knot. It is traditionally pinned or fastened onto a hat, cap, or helmet.
A cockerel is a young male chicken — specifically, a male that is less than one year old. Once that same bird reaches one year of age or becomes sexually mature, it is no longer called a cockerel.

When "cocktail" is used as an adjective, it means relating to, suitable for, or characteristic of a cocktail party — a type of stylish, social gathering where people stand, mingle, sip drinks, and have light conversation.
A cocktail is a drink made by mixing two or more ingredients together, where at least one of those ingredients is usually an alcoholic spirit such as vodka, rum, gin, whiskey, or tequila.
Cocky means having an excessively high opinion of yourself — being so confident in your own abilities or importance that it becomes irritating, off-putting, or disrespectful to the people around you.

A cocoon is a snug, closed protective case that certain insects spin around their own body — usually made of silk thread — inside which the insect rests and silently transforms into a completely different creature.
To wrap someone in a soft, warm, protective covering, or to shelter them from the outside world, as in "she cocooned herself from the news."

A coda is a deliberate, self-contained closing section — something that comes at the very end, after the main body of something is already complete, specifically to wrap it up, resolve it, and give it a sense of finality. It is not just "the last part."
To coddle someone means to treat them with too much care, protection, or gentleness — so much so that it ends up doing them more harm than good.
A codger is an informal word for an old man — typically one who is a bit odd, quirky, or set in his ways.
A codicil is a legal document that makes changes to a person's existing will — without throwing the whole will away and rewriting it from scratch.

Codification is the process of taking rules, laws, or principles — which may exist in scattered, informal, or inconsistent forms — and organizing them into a single, clear, systematic, and official written collection called a code.

To codify something means to take rules, principles, or ideas that exist in a scattered, informal, or unclear state, and organize them into one clear, official, and structured system — usually in written form.

To coerce someone means to force them to do something they don't want to do — not necessarily by grabbing them physically, but by putting them in a position where they feel they have no real choice. The key mechanism behind coercion is a threat.
Coercion is the act of forcing someone to do something — or stop doing something — against their genuine will, by using threats, pressure, or force.
Coercive describes anything — a behavior, a tactic, a system, a person, a relationship — that uses force, threats, or pressure to make someone do something they would not freely choose to do.
When two or more things are described as coeval, it means they belong to the same period of time — they came into existence at the same time, existed during the same era, or are of the same age.
To coexist means to exist at the same time and in the same space as something or someone else — and to keep existing alongside them, with neither one eliminating or replacing the other.

A coffer is a strongbox — a heavy, sturdy chest with a lock, designed to store things of great value: money, gold coins, jewels, important documents, or contracts. Think of it as a safe from the pre-modern world.

A cog is one of the small, tooth-like projections that stick out from the edge of a rotating wheel. Imagine a circular disc with a row of little rectangular bumps all around its rim — each one of those bumps is a cog.
A cogent argument, reason, or explanation is one that is so clearly expressed and so well-supported by logic and evidence that it becomes very hard to argue against.
To cogitate means to think deeply, carefully, and seriously about something. It is not a word for quick, passing thoughts.
Cogitation means deep, careful, and serious thinking.
When something is described as cognate, it means it is related to something else through a shared origin.
A cognate is a word in one language that is related to a word in another language because both of them descended from the very same word in a shared ancient ancestor language.

Cognition means the set of mental processes by which your mind takes in information, makes sense of it, stores it, and uses it. In the simplest possible terms: cognition is everything your mind does to know things and think about things.
Cognitive describes anything related to the mental processes by which you acquire, understand, process, store, and use information.
The mental discomfort you feel when you hold two conflicting beliefs, or when your actions clash with your values — which pushes you to change your thinking or justify your behaviour.
A cognitive verb is a verb that describes a mental process — something that happens inside the mind rather than in the physical world.
Cognizance means conscious awareness or knowledge of something — specifically, the state of having noticed, registered, and acknowledged something in your mind.

Cognizant means having clear, active awareness or knowledge of something. When you are cognizant of something, you don't just vaguely sense it in the background — you consciously, deliberately recognize and acknowledge it.
A cognomen (plural: cognomina or cognomens) is an additional name given to a person — beyond their basic first and family name — that identifies them more specifically.
People with deep knowledge and refined taste in a particular field, such as art, music, or wine.
To cohabit means to live together in the same home, especially as a romantic couple, without being married.

To cohere means to stick together or hold together as a unified whole. Separate parts connect, bond, or align with each other so well that they stop feeling like isolated pieces and start functioning as one complete, consistent thing.
Coherence means the quality of fitting together logically and consistently as a clear, unified whole.

Coherent means holding together in a clear, logical, and unified way. When something is coherent, its parts connect to each other — they make sense together, they don't contradict each other, and they form a solid, unified whole.
An idea whose defining features fit together logically without contradicting each other — unlike, for example, "a square circle."

Cohesion means the quality or state of sticking together as a unified whole. When the parts of something hold together tightly — rather than falling apart or feeling disconnected — we say that thing has cohesion.

Cohesive describes something made of multiple parts that stick together well, connect naturally, and work as a single, unified whole. The parts don't just exist together — they belong together. They support and strengthen each other.

A cohort is a group of people who share something in common — usually a shared experience, a shared characteristic, or a shared point in time. Think of it as a cluster of people who are linked by something that defines them as a group.
To coif means to style, arrange, or dress someone's hair — typically in a deliberate, careful, and often polished or elegant way.

A coiffure is a hairstyle — specifically, the way a person's hair has been carefully styled, arranged, or set into a particular shape or form. It refers to the finished look of someone's hair as a deliberate creation.

A coin is a small, flat, usually round piece of metal that is officially made and issued by a government, and used as money. It has a fixed monetary value stamped on it, and people use it to buy things, pay debts, or make change.

When two things coincide, they occupy the same point — the same moment in time, the same position in space, or the same place in thought (i.e., they agree). The word always signals that two separate things have ended up at the same point together.

A coincidence is when two or more things — events, facts, or circumstances — happen at the same time or come together in a way that is surprising or striking, but without any connection, cause, or plan behind it. Nobody arranged it.

Coincident means "occupying the same point in time or space." When two things are coincident, they line up — either they happen at the same moment, exist at the same location, or match each other in some meaningful way.

Something is coincidental when two or more events happen together, around the same time, or in a strikingly similar way — but purely by chance. No one planned it, no one caused it, and one event did not lead to the other.
A colander is a bowl-shaped kitchen tool full of small holes. You use it to drain liquid away from food. Think of it as a strainer or a sieve built in the shape of a bowl.

A "cold war" is a state of deep hostility and intense rivalry between two countries (or groups) that never breaks out into direct, open fighting. They are enemies — but they don't shoot at each other directly.

When we say an animal is cold-blooded, we mean its body temperature is not controlled from the inside. Instead, its body temperature changes depending on how warm or cold the surrounding environment is.
Colic is a noun that refers to a type of severe, cramping pain in the belly (abdomen).

Colicky means relating to, caused by, or affected by colic — a condition involving sharp, cramping pain, usually in the belly. It can describe a person (especially a baby), an animal, or a type of pain.
To collaborate means to work together with one or more people toward a shared goal, where everyone involved is actively contributing.
Collaboration is the act of two or more people working together toward a shared goal — where each person contributes their effort, skills, or ideas, and the result is something they build jointly.
A collage is a work of art — or any composition — made by taking separate, pre-existing pieces of material and sticking them together onto a flat surface to create one unified whole.
To suddenly fall down or fall apart, as in "the bridge collapsed." Figuratively, to fail suddenly, or, of a person, to fall down from illness or exhaustion.
When you collate something, you bring together separate pieces of information, documents, or items from multiple different sources, and arrange them into a single, organized whole.
Secondary, indirect, or accompanying, rather than the main thing. Collateral damage is unintended harm caused to people or property during an attack.

When someone lends you money, they're taking a risk — the risk that you might not pay it back. To protect themselves from that risk, they may ask you to put something valuable "on the line." That something is collateral.

"Collation" is a word with several distinct meanings. What ties them all together is a core idea of bringing things together carefully — whether to compare them, arrange them, describe them, or simply offer them as a gathering of something.

A colleague is a person you work with — but more specifically, someone who belongs to the same professional world as you. It could be someone at your workplace, or someone in the same field or profession as you, even if they work somewhere else entirely.
Collect means to bring things together into one place, or to cause them to come together — whether that's objects, people, information, money, or even your own scattered thoughts.

When you say someone is collected, you mean they are calm, composed, and in full control of themselves — especially in a situation that is difficult, stressful, or emotionally overwhelming. They haven't lost their head. Their thoughts aren't scattered.
Something is "collective" when it belongs to, is done by, or involves a group of people treated as a single whole — rather than as separate individuals.

College-ruled is an adjective used to describe paper — typically in notebooks, notepads, or loose-leaf sheets — that has horizontal lines printed on it with a specific, standardized amount of space between each line.
When something is described as collegial, it means it has the quality of mutual respect, cooperation, and equality among people who work or function together.
To collide means to come into forceful, sudden contact with something — to crash or smash into it.
A collier is a coal miner — a person who works underground in a coal mine, physically cutting and extracting coal from the earth.
A collision is an event in which two or more things forcefully come together and strike each other. It is the noun for that moment of impact — the event itself, not the things involved in it.

A collocation is a pair or group of words that naturally and habitually belong together in a language — words that native speakers automatically reach for as a unit, without needing to think about it.
Colloquial describes language — words, phrases, or an entire style of speaking or writing — that belongs to everyday, informal conversation.

A colloquy is a conversation — but not just any conversation. It is a serious, purposeful, and often formal exchange of words between two or more people. Think of it as a conversation that has weight to it.
To collude means to secretly work together with someone to do something dishonest, unfair, or harmful — usually to trick, cheat, or disadvantage a third person, group, or system.
Collusion is a secret agreement between two or more people or groups who work together — usually behind closed doors — to deceive, cheat, or harm others, almost always for their own benefit.

Collusive is an adjective that describes any action, agreement, behavior, or relationship that involves secret cooperation between two or more parties to deceive someone else, gain an unfair advantage, or cause harm to a third party.
A punctuation mark (:) that introduces a list, an explanation or a quotation; also the main part of the large intestine.
A colonel is a high-ranking military officer — a leader who commands a large group of soldiers and has earned significant trust, experience, and authority within the armed forces.

A colonnade is a row of columns — evenly spaced, standing in a line — that together form a covered walkway or support a structure above them. Think of it this way: one column is just a pillar. Two columns side by side is still just a pair of pillars.
A colony is a place, group, or settlement that exists somewhat separately from where it originated — but is still connected to, or controlled by, that origin in some way.

Coloratura is a word used in classical vocal music — primarily opera — and it refers to elaborate, ornamental passages in a song or aria where a singer performs rapid, dazzling vocal acrobatics that go far beyond simply singing a straightforward melody.

Colossal means extraordinarily large — so large that it creates a feeling of awe, shock, or disbelief in the person witnessing or thinking about it. It doesn't just mean "big." It means overwhelmingly, almost unbelievably big.

A colossus is something — most often a person, a statue, or an organization — that is so enormously large, powerful, or important that it dwarfs everything around it. The word carries a strong sense of awe-inspiring dominance. It doesn't just mean "big."
A state of deep, prolonged unconsciousness in which a person is alive but cannot be woken and does not respond to anything around them.
Comatose describes a person who is in a coma — a state of deep, unresponsive unconsciousness from which they cannot be woken up.
Combat means a fight — but not just any fight. It is a serious, intense struggle between two opposing sides that are actively trying to defeat or overpower each other.
To combat something means to actively fight against it, work hard to stop it, or take deliberate action to reduce its power or harmful effects.

A combatant is a person who actively fights in a war or armed conflict. The key word here is actively — a combatant is not just someone present near a war, but someone who directly participates in the fighting itself.
Combative means eager or ready to fight, argue, or strongly oppose — whether physically or verbally.
When you describe something as combustible, you mean it is capable of catching fire and burning.
To break into pieces, as in "the old book came apart." Figuratively, a person, plan, or relationship that comes apart fails or falls into chaos.

"Come down with something" means to become ill or to start getting sick. When you "come down with something," you are catching a disease or illness — usually one that is not life-threatening, like a cold, the flu, or a fever.
When something comes full circle, it means a situation has gone through a long journey of changes and has finally returned to where it originally started — completing a cycle.
"Come to grips with" means to face something difficult and begin to deal with it, understand it, or accept it.
When a person, team, trend, or anything else was once doing well, then fell into failure, difficulty, or obscurity — and then rises again — that return to success is called a comeback.

Comely means pleasant or attractive to look at — but with an important flavor to it. It doesn't just mean someone or something looks good. It implies a wholesome, gentle, modest kind of attractiveness. Think of it as the opposite of flashy or dramatic beauty.
If you describe something as comestible, you are saying it is appropriate to consume as food — that it can be safely eaten without harm.
A comestible is simply any item that can be eaten — any food, any edible thing. If you can put it in your mouth, chew it, and swallow it safely as nourishment, it is a comestible.
Comeuppance means a punishment or consequence that someone truly deserves because of their own bad behaviour.
Comity means courteous, respectful, and considerate behavior between people or groups — especially a mutual, voluntary agreement to treat each other with goodwill and dignity.
A comma is the small, curved punctuation mark that looks like this: ,
To command means to exercise authority — whether over people, things, attention, or resources. The word always carries a sense of power, control, or earned status. It is never passive or humble.

A commandant is a person who is officially in charge of — and holds full authority over — a specific military place or institution. Think of it as the top boss of a particular place, not of a moving army or fleet, but of a fixed location or organized body.

To commandeer something means to take it by force or authority, for your own use or for an official purpose, without asking for the owner's permission — and usually without giving them a choice in the matter.

A commandment is a rule or order that you are expected — or required — to obey. It is not a request, not advice, and not a suggestion. It is a firm directive handed down by someone in authority, and it carries real weight.
To commemorate something means to do something special to honor and keep alive the memory of an important person, event, or moment from the past.
When something is commemorative, it means it was made, designed, or done specifically to honor and keep alive the memory of an important person, event, or moment from the past.
To commence means to begin or to start something. When something commences, it moves from a state of not yet happening into a state of actively happening.

To commend someone means to praise them sincerely, express formal approval of them, or recommend them to others as being worthy. It is more than just saying "good job" — when you commend someone, you are putting your own credibility behind them.

When something is commendable, it means it deserves praise and positive recognition. It tells you that a person's action, effort, quality, or behavior is good enough — and noticeable enough — to be acknowledged and appreciated by others.

A commendation is an act of formal, public praise given to someone because they did something exceptionally well, went beyond what was expected of them, or showed outstanding qualities like bravery, skill, or dedication.

"Commensurate" describes a relationship between two things where one is at exactly the right level or degree in proportion to the other. When two things are commensurate, they are balanced and appropriately matched.
A comment is a remark or observation that someone makes about something — a person, a situation, an idea, an event, or a piece of work.
When you comment, you say or write something that expresses your thoughts, observations, or opinion about something.

A commentary is a piece of spoken or written content in which someone explains, describes, or shares their thoughts and opinions about something else — an event, a text, a situation, a work of art, or anything happening in the world.
A commentator is a person who watches, listens to, or reads something — and then explains, describes, or gives their opinion about it to an audience.

Commerce is the large-scale, organized activity of buying and selling goods and services. It is the engine that keeps an economy moving — every time a product is made, transported, purchased, or exchanged for money, commerce is happening.
Commercial describes anything that is connected to or driven by commerce — the activity of buying and selling goods or services to earn money. Think of commerce as trade and business for profit.
To commiserate means to express sympathy and share in someone's sorrow, disappointment, or bad luck — often in a mutual, back-and-forth way.

Commiseration is the act of expressing sympathy and sharing in someone else's sorrow, grief, or disappointment. When you offer commiseration to someone, you are essentially saying, "I feel sorry about what happened to you, and I share in your sadness."

The word commissary has two broad branches of meaning: it can refer to a person delegated to act on behalf of a higher authority, or — more commonly today — to a place where food, supplies, or provisions are stored and distributed.
The word commission has several distinct meanings, but they all share a common thread: authority given to someone to do something, or something that results from that authority.
A commissioner is a person who has been officially given the power and responsibility to do a specific, important job — usually by a government, an organization, or some other authority above them.

A committee is a small group of people who are selected from a larger organization or body, and given the responsibility to handle a specific task, make decisions on a particular matter, or look into something — on behalf of that larger group.
The process of turning something that was not previously bought and sold — such as culture, care, or personal data — into a product with a price.
To turn something into a product that can be bought and sold, especially something that was never meant to be treated that way.
Commodious means spacious and comfortable — having generously enough room for people or things to fit, move, and function with ease.

A commodity is a basic, useful good — usually a raw material or a primary product — that can be bought, sold, and traded. Think of things like wheat, gold, crude oil, copper, coffee beans, natural gas, or cotton.
Common purpose means a shared goal or aim that a group of people hold together and work toward collectively.
"Common sense" means basic, practical judgment that helps you navigate everyday life without needing special training, a textbook, or an expert's advice.

When something is commonplace, it means it is so ordinary, familiar, and frequently seen or heard that it no longer feels special, surprising, or worth noticing. It blends into the background of everyday life.
A political community or state organized for the good of all its people. The Commonwealth is also an association of countries that were once part of the British Empire.

A commotion is a sudden burst of noisy, disorderly, and confused activity — usually in a shared space — that disrupts what was happening normally and draws people's attention. Think of it as noise + movement + disorder, all happening at once, unexpectedly.
Communal describes something that belongs to, is shared by, or involves a group of people together — rather than one person alone.
A commune is a group of people who choose to live together, share their resources, and run their lives cooperatively. It goes far beyond simply being neighbors.

To commune with something or someone means to connect with them at a deep, intimate level — sharing thoughts, feelings, or a sense of unity that goes far beyond ordinary conversation. It is not simply talking.

If something is communicable, it means it is capable of being passed on from one to another. Think of it as something that doesn't stay with just one person — it moves, spreads, or travels across to someone else.
To communicate means to share or exchange information, ideas, feelings, or messages with someone — in a way that the other person actually receives and understands it.

Communion means a deep, intimate sense of sharing and togetherness — a connection so strong that it feels like two or more things (people, a person and God, people and nature) have become one in spirit, feeling, or purpose.

A communiqué is an official written or spoken announcement made by an authority — such as a government, a military, or an international organisation — to share important information with the public or with other official bodies.
Communism is a political and economic system built on one central belief: that society works best when everything is owned collectively by the people as a whole, rather than by private individuals.
A person who supports communism, a system in which land, factories, and other major resources are owned by the community as a whole rather than by private individuals.
Commutation means the act of replacing one thing with another — specifically, swapping something more severe, burdensome, or complex for something lighter, simpler, or more convenient.

"Commute" carries one deep idea: exchanging one thing for another — swapping, replacing, or moving between two things repeatedly. This core idea shows up in every meaning of the word, even though those meanings look quite different on the surface.

A commuter is a person who regularly travels between two places — almost always between their home and their workplace or school — and then travels back again. This back-and-forth trip happens repeatedly, typically every day or several days a week.
Small and neatly designed to take up little space, as in "a compact car." It can also mean closely packed together, or, of a person, small but strong and solidly built.

Companionable describes a person — or sometimes an animal, a thing, or even an atmosphere — that is pleasant, easy, and comfortable to be around. If someone is companionable, they make a good companion.
Companionship is the warm, comfortable feeling of being with someone and not feeling alone.

A compartment is a separate, enclosed section within a larger space or container. It is not a standalone thing — it always exists inside something bigger, and it is divided off from the rest of that bigger thing by walls, partitions, or some kind of barrier.
Dividing something into separate sections that are kept apart from one another. In psychology, it means mentally separating conflicting thoughts or feelings so they don't clash.
To compartmentalize means to separate something into distinct, isolated sections — and to keep those sections from mixing with or affecting each other.
Compassion is the warm, caring feeling you get when you see someone suffering, combined with a genuine desire to help ease that suffering.
If someone is compassionate, it means they genuinely feel concern for a person who is suffering or going through a hard time, and they are moved to help or comfort that person.
Compatibility is the quality or state of being able to exist together, work together, or function together without causing problems, conflict, or failure.
When two or more things are compatible, it means they can exist, work, or function together without causing problems or conflict. They fit together. They don't clash.
A compatriot is a person who comes from the same country as another person.
To compel means to force someone to do something in a way that leaves them no real choice.

"Compelling" means something has a kind of force or pull over you — so much so that you feel almost unable to resist it. It could pull your attention, pull your belief, or pull you toward action. The key word is force.

Compendious describes something that is both brief AND complete at the same time. It packs a large amount of essential information into a small, tight space — nothing important is missing, yet nothing is wasted either.

A compendium is a carefully gathered collection of information about a particular subject, presented in a complete yet compact way. Think of it as a "everything you need to know, all in one place" kind of resource.

To compensate means to make up for something. Think of a scale — when one side is heavier, you add weight to the other side to balance it. That act of balancing, of making things even again, is the spirit of "compensate."
When we say something is compensated, we mean it has been corrected, balanced out, or paid back — the deficit has been addressed.
Compensation means something given or received to make up for something else — a loss, a harm, an effort, a weakness, or a service rendered.
