Competence is the ability to do something well enough — to meet the required standard for a task, role, or situation. It means you have the right combination of knowledge, skill, and judgment to handle something reliably and effectively.
When you call someone competent, you are saying they have the ability, knowledge, and skill needed to do a particular job or task to a satisfactory standard.
Competition describes what happens when two or more parties try to win or achieve the same thing — and only one, or a limited few, can actually succeed.
A compilation is a single thing created by gathering and putting together many separate pieces.
To compile something means to gather material from multiple different sources and bring it all together into a single, organized whole.

Complacency is a state of being too comfortable and satisfied with how things are, to the point where you stop trying to improve, stop being careful, or stop noticing problems — even when you really should.

Complacent describes a person who feels so satisfied with how things currently are — with themselves, their situation, or their performance — that they stop paying attention, stop trying to improve, or stop watching out for problems.
When someone does something complacently, they do it with a quiet, self-satisfied feeling — a sense that everything is perfectly fine and there's nothing to worry about.
To complain means to express unhappiness, dissatisfaction, or annoyance about something — to say, out loud or in writing, that something is wrong, unfair, painful, or not good enough.

Complaisance is the quality or habit of being too eager to please others — a disposition to go along with what other people want, even when it means setting aside your own preferences, opinions, or better judgment.

Complaisant describes a person who is eager and willing to please others — someone who gladly goes along with what other people want, accommodates their wishes, and makes others feel comfortable and satisfied, often putting other people's desires before their own.

A complement is something that completes something else — it fills in what is missing to make a whole, or it pairs so perfectly with something else that together they become better, fuller, or more complete.

When you say that A complements B, you mean that A and B fit together so well that each one makes the other better, or that together they form something more complete and satisfying than either could be alone.
When two (or more) things are complementary, they work together in a way that makes each other better, fuller, or more complete — because each one supplies what the other is missing.
"Complex" describes something that has many parts, layers, or factors — and crucially, those parts are all connected to and dependent on each other.
The natural colour, tone, and texture of a person's skin, especially on the face. It can also mean the general character of something, as in "the political complexion of the government."
Compliance means the act of doing what you are told, expected, or required to do — following a rule, a request, a standard, or a law.
If someone or something is compliant, it means they follow the rules, meet the required standards, or do what they are asked to do — without resistance, argument, or refusal.

To complicate something means to make it harder, messier, or more difficult to deal with — by adding something to it that wasn't there before. That something could be a new problem, a new fact, a new condition, a new emotion, or a new obstacle.
Something is complicated when it has many parts, steps, layers, or moving pieces — and because of that, it becomes hard to understand, explain, solve, or deal with.
When someone is complicit in something wrong or harmful, they share in the moral responsibility for it — even though they may not have done the harmful thing directly.

Complicity means being involved in a wrongdoing that someone else committed — not necessarily as the main person who did it, but in a way that helped it happen, allowed it to happen, or made it easier for it to happen.
A compliment is something kind and positive that you say to someone — specifically to express praise, admiration, or approval of them, their qualities, their actions, or something they own.
Expressing praise or admiration, as in "complimentary remarks." It also means given free of charge, as in "complimentary drinks."

To comply means to do what is required of you by an external rule, law, instruction, or request. The key idea is simple: something or someone outside of you sets a requirement, and you act according to it.
A component is a part — a single piece — that belongs to a larger whole. It is one of the individual building blocks that, when combined with other parts, makes up something complete.
To behave or conduct yourself in a particular way, as in "she comported herself with dignity." To comport with something means to agree with it.

Comportment means the way a person carries and presents themselves — both in how their body looks and moves, and in how they act and behave. Think of it as the total impression you leave on others through your physical presence and your conduct combined.
"Compose" always involves bringing separate elements together deliberately to create something unified and ordered. That single idea runs through every meaning of this word.

When someone says "compose yourself," they are telling you to calm down, regain control of your emotions, and return to a state of being collected and dignified — especially after something upsetting, shocking, scary, or emotionally overwhelming has happened.
When you describe a person as composed, you mean they are calm, in control of their emotions, and steady — particularly during a situation that is stressful, difficult, emotional, or upsetting.
"Composedly" means in a calm, steady, and self-controlled manner — especially in a situation that is difficult, stressful, or emotionally charged.
"Composition" comes down to one central concept: the act of putting parts together to make a whole, the result of that act, or the way something is made up of its parts.

Compost is a dark, crumbly, rich material made from rotted organic matter — things like food scraps, leaves, and plant waste — that has broken down naturally over time. Think of it as nature's own recycled fertilizer.
Composure is the quality of being calm, emotionally steady, and in control of yourself — especially when you are under pressure, facing something difficult, or feeling strong emotions inside.
A compote is a dish of fruit that has been gently cooked in a sweetened liquid — typically a simple syrup made of sugar and water.
A compound is a fenced or walled piece of land that contains a group of buildings, treated as one secure, self-contained unit.
To comprehend something means to fully and deeply understand it — not just on the surface, but completely, in a way where it truly makes sense in your mind.
Comprehension means the act or ability to understand something fully — to grasp its meaning, take it in mentally, and make sense of it.
When something is comprehensive, it covers everything — or at least everything that matters. It is so complete and thorough that nothing important has been left out.
To compress something means to reduce it — to make it take up less space, less time, or less volume than it normally would. Think of it as squeezing or pressing something into a smaller, denser form.
"Comprise" means "to consist of," "to contain," or "to be made up of."
A compromise is a middle-ground agreement where every person or side involved gives up something they want, so that everyone can get at least some of what they want.
To settle a disagreement by each side giving up part of what it wants. It can also mean to weaken or damage something, such as safety, a reputation, or one's principles.
A compulsion is a powerful force — either coming from inside you or outside you — that pushes you to do something, often making it feel impossible to resist or refuse.
Compulsive means driven by a powerful inner urge that is very hard — or even impossible — to control.
Something is compulsory when you must do it — not because you want to, but because a law, rule, or authority requires you to. You have no real choice. If you don't do it, there will be consequences.

Compunction is the uneasy, guilty feeling you get in your conscience when you have done something wrong — or when you are about to do something wrong and some inner voice tells you that you shouldn't.
Compunctious describes someone who is feeling a deep, conscience-driven guilt or remorse about something they have done wrong — or are about to do wrong.
To compute means to work out an answer through a step-by-step process — especially by using mathematical operations, logical rules, or a fixed method.
A medical scan that uses X-rays and a computer to create detailed cross-sectional images, or "slices," of the inside of the body.

A comrade is a person who is bonded to you — not simply through personal liking, but through a shared struggle, shared purpose, or shared experience. The bond is one of solidarity: you are "in it together."
A trick to deceive someone, usually to get their money. A con is also a disadvantage, as in "pros and cons," or informally, a prisoner.
To concatenate means to join or link things together, one after another, forming a single connected chain or sequence.

Concave means curved inward, like the hollow of a bowl. When a surface or shape is concave, it dips inward rather than bulging outward. Picture holding a bowl right-side up — the inside surface you see is concave. It curves inward, toward a center point.

To conceal something means to deliberately hide it — from someone's eyes, from someone's knowledge, or from someone's awareness. When you conceal something, you make sure it is not seen, not found, or not known.
To concede means to admit or give up something, even when you don't want to. The most important feeling hiding inside this word is reluctance — you're not happily agreeing or freely giving.
An excessive, unrealistic sense of your own talent, importance, or attractiveness. In literature, a conceit is an elaborate, clever metaphor.

When we say someone is conceited, we mean they have an excessively high opinion of themselves — of their looks, intelligence, talent, or importance — and they make sure others around them know it. It is always a negative word.
Something is conceivable if the human mind is capable of imagining it, picturing it, or accepting that it might exist or happen — even if it hasn't happened, isn't happening, and may never happen.
"Conceivably" means "in a way that is possible to imagine."

"Conceive" always refers to the moment something begins to exist — either in your mind, or in the body. Whether it's an idea, a vision, or a new life, conceiving is the act of bringing something into existence for the very first time.
When you concentrate on something, you aim your full mental energy at it. Your mind stops jumping from thought to thought. Distractions fade out. You are fully locked in on one thing.
Made stronger by removing water or other substances, as in "concentrated orange juice." It can also mean focused intensely in one place or on one task, as in "a concentrated effort."
Concentric describes two or more shapes — usually circles, but also spheres or other rounded forms — that are different in size but share the exact same center point.
"Conception" always points to the very beginning of something — the moment it first comes into existence, either in the physical world or in someone's mind.
Relating to, involving, or existing as concepts (ideas) rather than as something physical, tangible, or real in the world.

"Concern" means something that matters — to you, to someone, or to the world. The word is flexible and carries several related meanings, but no matter which one you encounter, it always points to something that has weight, importance, or relevance.
To be about or apply to someone or something, as in "this rule concerns everyone." It can also mean to worry someone, or to involve yourself in something.
"Concerted" means something done in a deliberate, planned, and serious way — and very often, by multiple people or groups working together in a coordinated manner toward the same goal.
A concession is always about giving something — something you didn't have to give, but chose to (or were pressured to).

A conch is a large, spiral-shaped sea shell — one of the most recognizable shells in the world. It comes from a group of sea creatures called marine gastropods (a type of snail that lives in the ocean).
A concierge is a person whose entire job is to help someone else — usually a guest, a resident, or a client — by handling requests, making arrangements, and solving problems on their behalf.

To conciliate someone means to win over their goodwill — to take deliberate action that turns someone's hostility, suspicion, or unfriendliness into a positive, cooperative attitude. You're not forcing them to change. You're not just being polite.
Conciliation means the act of reducing hostility, cooling down anger, or settling a disagreement — by making opposing parties feel heard, respected, and willing to cooperate with each other.
Conciliatory means intended to reduce conflict, calm tension, or make peace with someone — by showing friendliness, understanding, or a willingness to compromise.
Concinnity means the elegant, skilful fitting together of parts so that everything harmonises beautifully as a whole.

When something is concise, it expresses everything that needs to be said — using as few words as possible. Nothing important is left out. Nothing unnecessary is included. Every single word earns its place.
Concision is the quality of expressing an idea using only the words that are truly needed — not one word more, not one word fewer. It means being brief and clear and complete, all at once.

A conclave is a private, secret meeting held by a small, select group of people — usually powerful or important ones — for the purpose of making a serious decision. The key idea baked into this word is that the meeting is closed off from the outside world.
To bring something formally to an end, as in "she concluded her speech." It can also mean to decide something after thinking about it, or to finalize an agreement.

Conclusion carries one fundamental idea: the point where something ends or settles. Whether it's the end of a story, the end of a thinking process, or the end of a negotiation — a conclusion is where things finally close up and come to rest.

Something is conclusive when it settles a question completely and finally — leaving no room for doubt. It doesn't just support an idea; it proves it so firmly that no reasonable person can argue against it anymore. The matter is closed.
To concoct something means to create or produce something by cleverly combining or putting together multiple parts or elements.
A concoction is something you create by mixing several different things together, especially when the mixture is unusual, creative, experimental, or improvised.
Something is concomitant when it naturally and inevitably comes along with something else — not by coincidence, but because the two things are bound together by their very nature.
Concord means a state of agreement, peace, and harmony — between people, groups, or even things. Think of it as the opposite of conflict.
Concordance means agreement — a state where two or more things match, align, or are consistent with each other. Think of it as things being "on the same page."
A concordat is a formal, official agreement — essentially a treaty — made between two powerful parties that lays down the terms of how they will deal with each other on important matters.

Concourse describes a large, open space — or sometimes a gathering of people — where many things or individuals come together and flow in one place. Think of it as the opposite of a narrow, closed-off passage. A concourse is wide, open, and built for scale.

The adjective concrete means real, specific, and clearly defined — the opposite of something vague, general, or purely theoretical. The single best way to unlock this word is through its direct opposite: abstract.
A concubine is a woman who lives with a man and shares a sexual and domestic relationship with him — but is not his wife.

Concupiscent means filled with strong sexual desire or lust. If you describe a person, a look, or a feeling as concupiscent, you are saying it is driven by intense, often raw, carnal longing — a hunger of the flesh.
To concur means to agree with someone or something, especially after thought or consideration. It is simply a more formal, precise word for "agree."

Every use of "concurrence" is built on one idea: things coming together. Whether it's opinions aligning, events overlapping in time, or forces joining up — the word always points to some kind of togetherness.

"Concurrent" means happening, existing, or taking place at the same time. When two or more things are concurrent, they overlap in time — they run alongside each other rather than one coming after the other.
"Concurrently" means at the same time — two or more things happening together, running side by side, overlapping in time, rather than one finishing and then the next beginning.
A concussion is a type of brain injury. It happens when your head receives a sudden, powerful hit, jolt, or impact — causing the brain to shake rapidly back and forth inside your skull.
Condemn means to make a strong, serious, and final-sounding judgment that something or someone is bad, wrong, guilty, or unacceptable. It is never a mild word.
Condemnation means a strong, serious, and often final declaration that something or someone is wrong, unacceptable, guilty, or unfit. It goes far beyond ordinary criticism or disapproval.
Condense means to make something smaller, shorter, or more concentrated — without losing what is most important about it.
To condescend means to treat someone as though they are less intelligent, less important, or less capable than you — and to let that belief show in the way you speak to them or act toward them.

If someone is condescending, it means they behave toward others as if they are superior — smarter, more important, or more capable — and they make that feeling obvious in the way they talk or act. A condescending person, in short, talks down to people.

Condescension is the attitude or behavior of someone who acts as if they are superior to another person — and then shows that feeling by the way they speak, behave, or treat that person, making the other person feel small, lesser, or looked down upon.

Condign means fully and fittingly deserved — particularly when referring to a punishment or consequence. If a punishment is condign, it means the wrongdoer got exactly what they had coming. Not too harsh, not too light. Just right. Justice, served precisely.
A condiment is a food substance that you add to other food — usually just before eating or while eating — to make it taste better, more interesting, or more suited to your preference.
The state something is in, as in "the car is in good condition." It can also mean an illness, a requirement that must be met, or, in the plural, the circumstances surrounding something.

Something is conditional when it depends on a condition — a requirement, a circumstance, or a rule that must be met first. It doesn't stand alone or hold automatically. It comes with a built-in "but only if..." attached to it.
To condole means to express sympathy and sorrow to someone who is going through a painful experience — most often the loss of a loved one.
When you express a condolence, you are essentially saying: "I know you are in pain, I feel for you, and I share in your grief."
A building or complex divided into individually owned units, such as flats, while the shared areas are owned jointly by all the unit owners. It also means one such unit.
To condone something means to accept, overlook, or let pass something that is wrong — without objecting to it, punishing it, or trying to stop it.
Conducive means making something more likely to happen by creating the right conditions for it.
Conduct means the way a person behaves — particularly how they act in situations where their behavior can be noticed, judged, or measured against some standard.
To organize and carry out a formal activity, as in "conduct an experiment." It also means to direct an orchestra, to behave in a particular way, or to allow heat or electricity to pass through.
A conduit is anything that allows something to pass through it from one place or person to another. Think of it as a middle path — a channel, a pipe, or a go-between.
To unconsciously invent false memories to fill gaps in what you remember, while sincerely believing they are true. In older use, it means simply to chat.

Confabulation is when someone sincerely states something false — a memory, an explanation, a story — not because they are lying, but because their brain automatically invented it to fill a gap, and they genuinely believe it to be true.

A confection is a sweet food item — but not just any sweet. The word carries a sense of careful crafting and skill. It suggests something that has been put together with deliberate effort, often with beauty or pleasure in mind.
Confectionery refers to the world of sweet foods — the kinds of things made primarily from sugar. Think of it as an umbrella word that covers a whole category of sweet treats.

A confederacy is a formal union of independent parties — people, groups, or states — who voluntarily join together to work toward a shared goal, while each member keeps its own independence and continues to govern or manage itself.

A confederate is someone who is joined together with another person or group for a shared purpose. Think of it as a partner, an ally, or someone on your side — united by a common goal, plan, or cause.

When people confer, they come together to talk — not casually or randomly, but with a clear purpose. The conversation is deliberate, focused, and usually aimed at reaching a decision, solving a problem, or sharing important information.

To confess means to openly admit or say something true — especially something you have been keeping inside, something you feel guilty about, something embarrassing, or something that was wrong. The key idea is that what you are saying is hard to say.

A confidant is a person you trust so deeply that you are willing to share your most private thoughts, secrets, fears, and personal troubles with them — and you feel completely safe doing so, because you know they will keep what you tell them private and will not judge you for it.

A confidante is a person you trust so deeply that you feel safe sharing your most private thoughts, secrets, fears, worries, and personal problems with them — knowing with full confidence that they will keep everything to themselves and not judge you.
To confide means to share something private, personal, or secret with someone — because you trust them.

Confidence means a feeling of trust or certainty — either in yourself, in another person, in a situation, or in a piece of information. Think of it as the opposite of doubt. When you have confidence, you are not shaky or unsure; you are settled and assured.

When you are confident, you have a strong, settled belief — either in yourself, or in something being true or likely. It is the feeling of being sure without being shaky. You are not guessing nervously. You are not pretending. You genuinely believe.
Something is confidential when it is meant to be kept private and shared only with specific, trusted people — not with the general public or anyone outside a defined circle.
Confidentiality is the quality or condition of keeping certain information private — shared only with specific people who are supposed to have it, and protected from everyone else.
Configuration means the particular way in which the parts of something are arranged or set up in relation to each other.

Confine means to keep someone or something within a limited space or boundary, so they cannot go beyond it. Think of it as drawing a line — real or imaginary — around something and saying: "You stay within this. You don't go beyond it."
When something or someone is confined, it means they are restricted within limits — they cannot move freely beyond a certain boundary or range.

Confinement means the state of being kept within limits and not allowed to go beyond them. Think of a boundary drawn around you — a wall, a rule, a situation — that prevents you from moving freely or going where you wish.

"Confines" means the borders, limits, or boundaries that mark the outer edge of a space or area — the invisible (or visible) lines that define where something ends and beyond which you cannot or should not go.
Something is confining when it limits your freedom — your freedom to move, act, or express yourself — in a way that feels tight, uncomfortable, or suffocating.
To confirm something means to make it certain — to move it from a state of doubt, possibility, or unofficial status to a state of certainty, truth, or official reality.
Confirmation means the act of making something certain, or something that proves a thing is true or settled.
The tendency to notice, remember, and favour information that supports what you already believe, while ignoring or dismissing information that contradicts it.

To confiscate something means to take it away from someone using your official power or authority — typically because the item is forbidden, illegal, dangerous, or being misused, or as a form of punishment.
Confiscation is the act of someone in authority officially taking away a person's belongings or property — usually without paying for them, and usually because a rule, law, or order has been broken.

A conflagration is a large, destructive, out-of-control fire — one that spreads widely and causes serious damage. Think of a wildfire tearing through thousands of acres of forest, or a historic city burning to the ground. That is a conflagration.
To conflate two things means to merge or combine them into one — treating them as if they are the same thing, when in reality they are two separate, distinct things.
Conflation is the act of merging two or more separate, distinct things together and treating them as if they are one and the same — when in reality, they are different and should be kept apart.
A conflict is a serious clash or struggle between two or more sides that want different things, believe different things, or cannot coexist peacefully.

When two things conflict, they are directly opposed to each other in a way that makes it impossible — or very difficult — for both to be true, happen, or exist at the same time without causing a problem.

Confluence means the coming together of two or more things into a single point or place. Think of it as a meeting — but a very specific kind. In a confluence, things don't just cross paths and go their separate ways.
To conform means to adjust yourself, your behavior, or something else so that it matches, fits, or agrees with a rule, standard, pattern, or expectation.
Conformation means the shape or structural arrangement of something — how its parts are put together and organized in space.
A conformist is a person who follows the rules, beliefs, behaviors, and expectations of the group around them — without seriously questioning whether those things are right or wrong, good or bad.

Conformity means going along with something — matching it, agreeing with it, or fitting into it. That "something" could be a rule, a standard, a norm, an expectation, or what a group of people does or believes.

"Confound" means to throw something into disorder — it can throw your understanding into disorder (leaving you baffled), throw your expectations into disorder (proving them wrong), or throw the distinction between two things into disorder by blurring them together.

When someone is confounded, they are so deeply confused that they are almost frozen — unable to think clearly, respond quickly, or make sense of what is happening. It goes beyond just being "a little puzzled."

To face someone or something directly, especially to deal with a problem or challenge, as in "confront your fears." It also means to accuse someone face to face, or, of a problem, to present itself to someone.

A confrontation is a direct, open clash or face-to-face encounter between two or more people (or groups) who are in disagreement, opposition, or conflict with each other. The key word here is direct — a confrontation brings a tension out into the open.
When someone or something is described as confrontational, it means they tend to directly face, challenge, or oppose others — often in an aggressive, forceful, or hostile way.
Confuse means to make something unclear — either in someone's mind, or between two things. Think of it as the opposite of making things clear.
Confusion is the state of not being able to understand something clearly, or the state of a situation being unclear, mixed up, or disordered.
To congeal means for a liquid (or something soft and flowing) to slowly thicken and turn into a solid or semi-solid mass — typically because it cools down.

Congealed describes something that was once liquid — flowing, pourable, or fluid — but has since thickened, stiffened, or turned semi-solid. This usually happens because the substance cooled down, or because it was simply left undisturbed for too long.
Congee is a type of thick, creamy porridge made from rice. It is one of the most widely eaten dishes in Asia and is beloved as a comfort food across many cultures.

Congenial means pleasantly suited or agreeable — either to a person's taste, personality, or nature, or simply pleasant and enjoyable in a general sense. Think of it as describing a perfect, comfortable "fit" between a person and something or someone else.

Congeniality is the quality of being warm, friendly, pleasant, and genuinely easy to be around. When someone possesses congeniality, they make other people feel welcome, comfortable, and at ease — almost effortlessly.

Congenital describes anything that is present in a person from the moment of birth. If a condition, trait, or characteristic is congenital, the person didn't develop it later in life — they came into the world already having it.
"Congested" describes a place, space, or passage that is so full or blocked that things cannot move through it freely — or can only move with great difficulty.
Congestion means a state where something is so overcrowded or blocked that things can no longer move or flow properly. Think of it as a "traffic jam" — but not just for vehicles.
A long-term condition in which the heart cannot pump blood as well as it should, causing fluid to build up in the lungs and other parts of the body.
To conglomerate means to gather, collect, or mass together into one unified whole — especially when the things coming together are varied, diverse, or different from one another.

A conglomeration is a collection of many different, varied things that have been gathered or grouped together into one mass or whole — things that may not naturally belong together and are often loosely, randomly, or unsystematically assembled.

To congratulate someone means to tell them that you are happy about something good that has happened to them or something they have achieved. You are sharing in their joy and letting them know you recognize their good news or success.
When someone says "congratulations are in order," they mean: "This situation deserves congratulations. It is the right and appropriate moment to congratulate someone."
To congregate means to come together in one place as a group. It describes people, animals, or things gathering or assembling at a particular spot — often in noticeably large numbers.

Congregation means a group of people or things that have come together in one place. Think of it as a gathering — but not a random one. The word carries a sense of people (or things) assembling with a shared purpose or reason.
Relating to the United States Congress, the national law-making body made up of the Senate and the House of Representatives.
Congruence means the state of things matching, aligning, or agreeing with each other perfectly — with no gap, conflict, or mismatch between them.
In agreement or harmony with something, as in "actions congruent with her beliefs." In geometry, describing shapes that are exactly the same size and shape.
Congruity means the quality or state of things fitting together properly — matching, agreeing, or being in harmony with each other.
Congruous means fitting naturally and harmoniously with something else — describing two or more things that match, align, or belong together in a way that feels right, logical, or expected.
A conifer is a tree or shrub that produces cones as part of its reproductive process. Pine trees, spruce trees, fir trees, cedars, cypresses, junipers, and redwoods are all conifers.

A conjecture is a belief or conclusion you reach through reasoning or observation — but without full, solid proof. Think of it as an educated guess: not a random stab in the dark, but not a proven fact either.
To conjecture means to form an opinion or reach a conclusion based on incomplete information — without having full proof or solid evidence to back it up.

To conjoin means to join two or more separate things together into a single, connected whole. When things are conjoined, they are brought together and united — they go from being separate to being linked, bonded, or combined as one.

When two (or more) things are described as conjoined, they are joined together so closely — so intimately — that they function, exist, or appear as a single unit. It is not a loose or temporary connection.
Conjugal is an adjective that means relating to marriage and the intimate bond shared between two spouses.

To conjugate means to systematically change the form of something — usually a verb — to show different information about who is doing the action, when it happens, how many people are involved, and other such details.
A conjuncture is a specific moment in time defined by a particular combination of circumstances, events, or forces that have all come together at once.
Conjure means to make something appear — in the real world, the spirit world, or the mind — through some kind of special power, skill, or effort. Think of a magician on stage.
Connect means to join two or more things so that they have a link between them — a link through which something can pass, flow, or be shared.
Joined or linked together, as in "two connected rooms." It can also mean related, as in "connected events," or having useful social or business contacts, as in "well connected."

When "connecting" is used as an adjective, it describes something whose job or quality is to serve as a link or bridge between two or more things, places, or people. The thing being described is not one of the two ends — it is the middle part that joins them.

Connection means a link or relationship between two or more things. Whether those "things" are physical objects, people, ideas, or systems — a connection is whatever joins them, ties them together, or makes them relevant to each other.
A conniption is a sudden, loud, and dramatic outburst of extreme emotion.
Connivance means secretly allowing something wrong to happen by deliberately doing nothing about it.
To connive means to be secretly involved in something wrong — either by quietly allowing it to happen, or by actively plotting it with others. The word always carries a sense of hidden dishonesty.

When you describe someone as conniving, you are saying they are a person who secretly schemes and plots to get what they want — usually for selfish reasons, and almost always through dishonest, manipulative means.

A connoisseur is a person who has such deep knowledge and refined taste in a particular subject — usually something related to art, culture, food, or pleasure — that they can judge quality with great skill and confidence.
An idea or feeling that a word suggests in addition to its literal meaning. "Slender" and "scrawny" both mean thin, but they have very different connotations.
When a word (or image, or symbol) connotes something, it means that word carries an extra layer of meaning — a feeling, an idea, or an association — beyond its plain, literal definition.
Connubial is a formal adjective that means relating to marriage or the relationship between a married couple.
To conquer something means to overcome it completely and gain control over it — usually through great effort, force, or determination.
Conquest means the act of defeating something or someone and then taking full control over them — usually through force, great effort, or determination.
Consanguineous is an adjective that describes people who are related by blood — meaning they share a common biological ancestor somewhere in their family tree.

Consanguinity is the state or condition of being related to someone by blood — meaning you and that person share the same ancestor somewhere in your family tree. If two people have consanguinity, they are blood relatives.
Your conscience is the inner sense inside you that judges your own actions, thoughts, and intentions as either right or wrong.

If someone is conscientious, it means they care deeply about doing things correctly, thoroughly, and to the best of their ability — especially when it comes to their duties, responsibilities, and how they treat others. They don't cut corners.

A conscientious objector (often shortened to CO) is a person who refuses to serve in the military — or to take part in war or killing — because doing so would violate their deeply held moral, ethical, or religious beliefs.
Awake and aware of your surroundings. It can also mean aware of something, as in "conscious of the risks," or done on purpose, as in "a conscious decision."
When you do something consciously, it means you are doing it with full awareness and on purpose — your mind is active, present, and fully knows what is happening.

Consciousness is the state of being awake, aware, and able to experience your own thoughts, feelings, and surroundings from the inside. It is what makes you present — mentally switched on, perceiving the world, and knowing that you are the one doing it.
To conscript someone means to officially force them to join the military against their will, usually because a government or authority decides it needs more soldiers and cannot get enough volunteers.

Conscription is the act of a government legally forcing its citizens — usually men of a certain age — to serve in the military, whether they want to or not. It is not a request. It is a legal obligation.

To consecrate something means to officially declare it as sacred or holy, and to set it apart from ordinary use, through a formal act or ceremony — usually one that carries deep religious or solemn authority.

When we call something consecrated, we mean it has been formally and officially made sacred or holy — usually through a religious ceremony performed by someone with the authority to do so (like a priest, bishop, or religious leader).
Consecration means the formal act of making something — or someone — sacred, holy, or officially set apart for a divine or deeply solemn purpose.
Consecutive means following one after another in a fixed order, with no gaps, skips, or breaks in between.
Consensual describes something that happens with the free, willing, and informed agreement of everyone involved.

A consensus is a general agreement reached among a group of people — not just one or two individuals, but a collection of people who have, through discussion or shared understanding, come to hold the same view or accept the same decision.
Consent means a genuine, voluntary agreement that someone gives — allowing something to happen to them, or permitting someone else to do something that involves them.
To consent means to willingly and freely say "yes" to something — to give your agreement or permission for something to happen, especially something that affects you directly.
A consequence is something that happens because of something else. It is the result, the outcome, the "what follows" from an action, a decision, an event, or a situation.
Consequent means following as a direct result of something. If one thing causes another, the second thing is consequent — it is the outcome that flows naturally from the first.
"Consequential" describes something that produces significant consequences — meaning it matters a lot, it carries real weight, and its effects ripple forward and change things in a meaningful way.
Consequently means "as a result of that" or "because of what just happened."
Conservation is the careful protection of something valuable so that it is not lost, wasted, damaged, or destroyed — either for the benefit of people alive today, or for future generations, or both.

A conservative is a person who believes in preserving what already exists — existing traditions, institutions, values, and ways of doing things — and who is cautious, even skeptical, about rapid or sweeping change.
A conservatoire is a specialist school or college dedicated to training students in the performing arts — most commonly music, but sometimes also dance, drama, or opera — at a professional level.
A conservatory is a specialized school where students are trained to a very high professional level in music, and sometimes in other performing arts like dance or drama.

To conserve something means to protect it from being wasted, lost, or destroyed — by using it carefully or by actively working to keep it safe and available. The word holds two closely linked ideas at the same time: don't waste it, and make sure it lasts.

Consider means to think carefully and deliberately about something. The key word is carefully — "consider" is not a quick, passing thought. It implies giving something real mental attention, turning it over in your mind before you decide, judge, or act.

"Considerable" means large, strong, or significant enough that it genuinely deserves your attention and cannot be brushed off as minor or trivial. It describes something that clearly sits above the ordinary or the negligible.

When you describe someone as considerate, you are saying that they think carefully about how their actions and words will affect other people — and they behave accordingly. A considerate person does not just act on impulse or think only about themselves.
Consign means to officially and deliberately hand something — or someone — over to a person, place, or fate. The key idea is intentional transfer, often with a sense of formality and permanence.

A consignment is a batch of goods that one person sends to another person — not to give away or sell outright, but specifically for the receiver to take care of, store, or sell on behalf of the original owner.

"Consist" is a verb that describes a relationship — specifically, what something is made of or defined by. It never stands alone; it always needs a preposition after it, and that preposition is either "of" or "in."
Consistency means staying the same — in behavior, quality, standards, or appearance — over time or across different situations.
Consistent means staying the same — either a person or thing reliably behaves the same way over time, or two things match and agree with each other without contradiction.
Consistently means in the same way, every time, without changing.
Consolation is the comfort, relief, or sense of solace that someone receives — or feels — after something painful, disappointing, or sad has happened to them.

To console someone means to comfort them emotionally when they are sad, upset, or suffering — especially after something bad has happened to them. When you console someone, you are not trying to fix the problem that caused their pain.
Consolidate means to bring things together into one stronger, more stable whole — or to make something that already exists more firm, secure, and solid.

Consolidation means the process of making something stronger, more secure, or more unified — either by combining separate things into one, or by firmly establishing and solidifying something that already exists.

Consonance means a pleasing sense of agreement, harmony, or compatibility between things. When two or more things are in a state of consonance, they fit together well — they don't clash, contradict, or create tension.
A consonant is a speech sound made by blocking or restricting the flow of air as it travels from your lungs, through your throat, and out of your mouth.
To consort with someone means to spend time with them regularly, as a companion or associate — especially in a way that is seen as wrong, suspicious, or socially unacceptable.
A formal group of companies, governments, universities, or other organizations that join together to work toward a goal too big for any one of them to achieve alone.
Conspicuous means very easy to notice — so noticeable that it is almost impossible to ignore or overlook.
A conspiracy is a secret plan, made by two or more people working together, to do something harmful, illegal, or dishonest.

A conspiracy theory is an explanation for an event or situation that claims it was secretly planned and carried out by a powerful group — usually a government, corporation, shadowy organization, or elite group — and that the "real truth" is being deliberately hidden from ordinary people.

A conspirator is a person who secretly joins with one or more others to plan or carry out something harmful, dishonest, illegal, or wrong. The word always implies a group — you cannot be a conspirator by yourself.
Suggesting that people are sharing a secret or plotting something together, as in "a conspiratorial whisper."
To conspire means to secretly plan with one or more other people to do something wrong, harmful, or illegal.

A constabulary is simply a police force — an organized, official body of police officers responsible for maintaining law and order in a specific area. If you know what a police force or police department is, you already understand the heart of it.
Constancy is the quality of remaining steady, faithful, and unchanged — no matter what time passes, what pressures arise, or what temptations appear. It is the noun form of the adjective constant.

A constellation is a named group of stars in the night sky that, when you connect them with imaginary lines, forms a recognizable pattern or shape — like a connect-the-dots picture drawn across the sky.
Consternation is a feeling of sudden shock, worry, and confusion that hits you all at once — leaving you troubled, unsettled, and unsure of what to do or say next.
A constituency is a group of people who are represented by someone — usually an elected official — or the specific geographic area where those people live.
A constituent is something — or someone — that is a part of a larger whole. It doesn't just exist alongside other things; it actively makes up or belongs to something bigger.

"Constitute" is a verb about identity — about what something is made of, or what something counts as, or what something has been formally made to be. These are its three distinct but closely related meanings.
The set of fundamental rules and principles by which a country or organization is governed. It can also mean a person's physical health and strength.
Relating to, allowed by, or in agreement with a constitution. Relating to a person's physical makeup, it means inherent or natural.
To constrain something or someone means to limit, restrict, or hold back what they can do — or to force/compel them to do something, often because of circumstances outside their control.
Restricted or limited, as in "constrained resources." Of behaviour, forced and unnatural, as in "a constrained smile."

A constraint is anything that limits what you can do, how far you can go, or what choices you have. It's a boundary — real or imposed — that keeps you within a certain range and stops you from going beyond it.

To constrict something means to squeeze, tighten, or narrow it by applying pressure from the outside — like pressing inward on something to make the space inside it smaller or the opening through it tighter.

Constriction means a squeezing, tightening, or narrowing of something — either the process of it happening, or the result of it having happened. Think of pressing a soft tube in the middle with your fingers. The tube becomes narrow and pinched at that spot.

Construction refers to the act of building something, or anything connected to that act — the process, the method, the result, or the industry. Think of it as a word that lives in the world of "putting things together" in a deliberate, planned way.

"Constructive" means building something up — improving a situation, helping someone grow, or moving things forward in a useful way. The clearest way to understand it is through its opposite: destructive tears things down, constructive builds them up.
To construe something means to interpret it — that is, to decide what it means, especially when the meaning isn't obvious or when it could reasonably be understood in more than one way.
An official sent by a government to live in a foreign city and help its citizens and trade there; in ancient Rome, one of the two chief magistrates.
The office in a foreign city where a country's government representative helps its own citizens abroad and issues visas to local people.

To consult means to go to someone or something to get information, advice, or guidance — especially when you need help from someone who knows more than you, or when you want someone's opinion before you act.

A consultation is a formal or purposeful meeting, conversation, or process in which one person (or a group) goes to someone with expertise or authority to seek advice, guidance, or an expert opinion about something specific.

To consume means to take something in, use it up, or destroy it — in a way that leaves less of it, or nothing at all. It is the opposite of creating or adding. When something is consumed, it is absorbed, depleted, eaten away, or overtaken.
When something is consuming, it takes over your mind, your time, your energy, or your emotions so completely that everything else fades into the background. It dominates you. It absorbs you entirely.

When you call someone or something consummate, you are saying it is the most complete, perfect, and masterfully skilled example of what it is — the absolute highest standard, with nothing missing and nothing left to improve.
To consummate something means to bring it to its fullest, most complete, and final state of realization — not just to finish it, but to make it truly whole and complete in the deepest sense.

Consumption means the act of using something up. When something is consumed, it is taken in, used, or spent — and after that, it is either gone or has changed form. Think of burning wood in a fire: the wood is consumed. The fire uses it up.
Tending to use up or drain resources heavily. In older use, suffering from tuberculosis, then called consumption.

"Contact" refers to a connection — the moment or state when two things (or people) meet, touch, or reach each other. Think of it as the point where a gap is closed, whether physically, socially, or through communication.

Contagion means the spreading of something harmful from one person, place, or thing to another. Think of it as the act and process of something bad jumping across from one host to the next, almost like a chain reaction.

Contagious describes anything that spreads automatically from one person (or thing) to another — often without people even trying to make it happen. Think of it as describing something that "jumps" from source to receiver.
A contaminant is any substance that is present somewhere it should not be, and because it is there, it makes that place, thing, or substance impure, harmful, or unfit for its intended use.
To contaminate something means to make it impure, unsafe, or harmful by introducing something unwanted into it.

To contemn something or someone means to regard them as completely worthless, inferior, or beneath you — and to show that attitude through the way you treat them. It's not just a feeling kept inside; it's an active expression of deep scorn and disdain.
To contemplate something means to think about it deeply, carefully, and for a sustained period of time. It is not a quick, passing thought.
Contemplation is the act of thinking about something deeply, carefully, and for a sustained period of time — usually in a calm, quiet, unhurried way.
Contemplative describes being absorbed in deep, quiet, sustained thought — especially about something serious, meaningful, or profound.

"Contemporary" means belonging to the same period of time. That period could be the present — right now, today — or it could be any other specific era in history. This one idea is the seed from which all meanings of the word grow.
A contemporary is a person who lives — or lived — during the same period of time as another person.

Contempt is the feeling that someone or something is so worthless, low, or beneath your standards that they don't even deserve your basic respect. It is one of the strongest forms of disrespect a person can feel.
Contemptible means deserving to be looked down upon with strong moral disgust and disrespect.

Contemptuous is an adjective that describes a person, look, tone, action, or attitude that shows deep disrespect and a strong sense that someone or something is worthless, inferior, or beneath notice.
In a way that shows you think someone or something is worthless and beneath your respect.
When you contend with something or someone, you are actively facing a challenge, a rival, or a difficult situation — and putting in effort to handle it.
A contender is a person, group, or thing that is competing for something — and, crucially, has a real, genuine chance of winning or achieving it.

To be content means to be peacefully satisfied with what you have or where you are in life — not craving anything more, not wishing things were different, just quietly at ease with your current situation.
To content someone means to make them feel satisfied — to give them a sense of "this is enough; I'm at peace with what I have."
Contented means feeling quietly happy and satisfied with your life or situation, exactly as it is — without wishing it were different, without craving more, and without feeling restless.

"Contention" has three distinct but connected meanings. All of them orbit a single core idea: some kind of struggle — a struggle between competing ideas, between people who disagree, or between rivals competing to win something.

Contentious means likely to cause, or already causing, strong disagreement or argument. When something is contentious, it's the kind of thing that makes people clash, raise their voices, or take firm opposing sides.

Contentment is a calm, quiet feeling of being happy and satisfied with what you already have, who you already are, or where you already are in life — without feeling a strong urge to want or need anything more.

Conterminous describes a relationship between two things. It tells you that two things either share the same boundary, or cover the exact same area or range. Think of it as a word about how two things "match up" spatially or in scope.
A contest is a competition between two or more sides, where each side actively tries to win, succeed, or prove itself better than the other.

When you contest something, you formally push back against it. You are saying, in effect: "I do not accept this. I believe it is wrong, unfair, or invalid — and I am going to do something about it." It is more than just a private feeling of disagreement.
A contestant is a person who enters and actively takes part in a competition — a contest where there is something to win, a result to be decided, or a title to be earned.
Context is the surrounding information, circumstances, or background that helps you understand something correctly.
Contiguity is the state of two or more things being directly next to each other — touching, sharing a border, or immediately following one another — with absolutely no gap between them.
Two things are contiguous when they directly share a border or boundary — they physically touch along an edge, with zero gap between them.
Continence is about control — specifically, the ability to hold back, restrain, or contain something when you could otherwise lose control of it. Think of it as the power of "keeping it in check."

When used as an adjective, continent means having strong self-control over one's own physical desires and urges — particularly the ability to restrain yourself from acting on impulses related to bodily pleasures.
A contingency is something that might happen in the future, but you can't be sure whether it will. It's a possible event or situation that you plan for — just in case.
Something is contingent when it is not certain or guaranteed — when it depends on conditions, or when chance has a say in whether it happens.

"Continual" describes something that keeps happening again and again, repeatedly, but with brief pauses or gaps in between. It is not something that runs non-stop, with zero interruption — that's a different word entirely.
Continuance means the fact or state of something keeping going, lasting, or remaining in existence over time.
A continuation is the act or state of something carrying on — going forward, extending further, or resuming after a pause, always while staying connected to what came before.

A continuum is a connected whole that flows from one end to the other with no gaps, no jumps, and no sudden breaks. Everything within it shifts so gradually into the next thing that you can never draw a clean dividing line between any two neighbouring points.

To contort means to twist, bend, or pull something — usually a body, a face, or a shape — into a strained, unnatural, or distorted position. The key idea is that the twisting goes beyond what looks or feels normal.
When something is contorted, it has been twisted, bent, or strained into an awkward, unnatural shape or position — one that looks forced, uncomfortable, or hard to make sense of.
A contortion is an extreme, unnatural twisting or bending — of the body, the face, or even an idea — into a position or shape that looks strained, distorted, or far beyond what is ordinary.

A contortionist is a person who can bend and twist their body into extreme, unusual positions that most people cannot achieve — positions that look physically impossible or deeply uncomfortable to the average person.
A contour is the line or edge that traces the outer shape of something — especially when that shape is curved or irregular.

When you call something contraband, you are saying that it is illegal to have, carry, trade, or move — either because the law forbids it outright, or because it was brought somewhere secretly without following legal rules (such as paying taxes or getting permission).
Contraband refers to goods or items that are forbidden by law — either to own, to trade, to carry, or to move from one place to another (especially across a border).
To become smaller or tighter, as muscles do when they work. It can also mean to catch an illness, to make a formal agreement, or to shorten a word.
To contradict means to say or show that something is the opposite of — or incompatible with — something else. When you contradict a person, you are not just disagreeing with them.
A contradiction is when two things are so directly opposite that both cannot be true, valid, or real at the same time.

Something is contradictory when it directly clashes with something else in such a way that both things cannot be true or valid at the same time. If two things are contradictory, accepting one means you must reject the other.
A distinction made by contrasting the opposite qualities of two things, as in "art, in contradistinction to science."

A contrail is a long, white, cloud-like streak that forms in the sky directly behind a flying aircraft — most commonly a jet plane at high altitude. It is essentially a man-made cloud, triggered by the plane's engines.
When "contralto" is used as an adjective, it describes a voice — or any sound — that carries the qualities of the lowest female singing voice: deep, rich, dark, and full in tone.
A contralto is the lowest type of female singing voice. It is a classification — a label that tells you where a singer's voice sits on the scale from high to low.

A contraption is a device, machine, or gadget — but not just any device. It's one that looks strange, overly complicated, or oddly put together. It's the kind of thing that makes you tilt your head and think, "What on earth is that thing?"

When you describe something as contrapuntal, you are saying that it contains two or more independent voices, lines, or threads that run simultaneously, each distinct and complete on its own, yet interacting with each other to create something richer together.

A contrarian is a person who deliberately takes the opposite position from what most people think, believe, or do — not out of stubbornness or to be difficult, but because they genuinely believe the popular opinion is wrong, or at the very least, worth questioning.
Contrast is the noticeable difference between two or more things when they are placed side by side, compared, or experienced one after the other.

"Contrast" as a verb is about difference — specifically, a difference that is clear, noticeable, and worth pointing out. The word is always about how two things are different from each other, never about how they are similar.
To contravene something means to go against it, conflict with it, or act in a way that directly breaks or violates it.
A contravention is the act of breaking or going against an established rule, law, regulation, treaty, agreement, or official order.
A contretemps is an unexpected, awkward, and usually embarrassing little incident — a minor mishap that suddenly disrupts the flow of events at an inconvenient moment.
To contribute means to give or add something — your money, time, effort, ideas, skills, or any resource — to something larger that is shared, built, or achieved together with others.
A contribution is something you give, add, or do that becomes part of something bigger than yourself.

Contrite means feeling deeply and genuinely sorry for something wrong you did — not just sorry you got caught, not sorry because of what it cost you, but sorry from within, because you know your action was morally wrong and it hurt someone or something that mattered.
Contrition is a deep, sincere feeling of sorrow and regret for something wrong you have done — paired with a genuine wish that you had not done it, and a real desire to do better.
Something cleverly invented or arranged, especially a gadget, a scheme, or a plot device that feels artificial or forced rather than natural.

To contrive something means to plan, create, or bring something about through deliberate, clever thinking — especially when conditions are difficult, resources are limited, or the method involves some calculation and effort.
Something is contrived when it has been deliberately created or arranged — but the effort and artificiality behind it are too visible. It doesn't feel natural, genuine, or spontaneous.

Control is about having the power to direct, limit, or manage something — to decide what it does, how much of it exists, or what happens to it. If you have control over something, you are the one steering it, holding it back, or setting the rules for it.

To control something means to have the power to decide what it does, how it behaves, or what happens to it. When you control something, you are the one steering it — the outcome depends on your decisions and actions.
Something is controversial when it causes strong disagreement among a significant number of people.
A controversy is a prolonged, public disagreement about a topic where people hold strong, opposing opinions and neither side easily backs down.
To controvert something means to argue against it or dispute its truth, typically using reasoning, logic, or evidence.
Contumacious means stubbornly and boldly refusing to obey authority — not out of confusion or fear, but out of open, defiant contempt.
Contumacy means stubborn, willful refusal to obey authority — most often, the authority of a court of law.

Contumely means harsh, contemptuous, and humiliating treatment or language directed at someone — the kind that doesn't just insult a person but deliberately degrades them, as if they are beneath the speaker's dignity even to acknowledge as an equal.

A contusion is a bruise. It is an injury to a part of the body caused by a hard blow or impact — but one where the skin is not broken or cut open. Everything that gets damaged happens underneath the intact skin surface.
A conundrum is a difficult problem or question that has no obvious, easy, or fully satisfying answer.
A conurbation is a large, continuous urban area that is formed when several towns or cities grow outward over time until they physically merge together into one sprawling built-up region.
To convalesce means to gradually recover your health and strength after a serious illness, injury, or surgery.

Convalescence is the period of time a person spends gradually recovering their health and strength after an illness, injury, or surgery. It is not the sickness itself, and it is not the final moment of being fully well again.
Convalescent describes someone — or something related to someone — who is recovering from an illness, injury, or surgery, but has not yet fully returned to normal health and strength.
A convalescent is a person who is recovering from an illness, injury, or surgery — but has not yet fully returned to normal health and strength.
Convection is the transfer of heat through the movement of a fluid — where "fluid" means any liquid or gas, because both can flow.
To convene means to come together as a group for a formal, organized meeting — or to cause such a gathering to happen.
Convenience means the quality of being easy, effortless, and without trouble. Something has convenience when it fits smoothly into your life — saving you time, effort, or difficulty.

Something is convenient when it fits your needs smoothly — it saves you time, effort, or trouble. It works well for you, right where and when you need it, without causing problems or requiring extra work.

A convent is a place where a group of nuns live together as a religious community. It refers to two closely connected things at once: 1. The building (or complex of buildings) where nuns live; 2. The community of nuns living there.
A way of doing things that is generally accepted as normal or correct, even though no law requires it. It is also a large formal meeting, or a formal agreement between countries.

"Conventional" describes something that follows the widely accepted, commonly practiced, or traditionally established way of doing things. It sticks to what most people in a society, field, or group consider normal, standard, or expected.

Conventional wisdom is any idea, belief, or explanation that most people in a society accept as true — not necessarily because it has been proven beyond doubt, but simply because it has been widely repeated, rarely challenged, and passed down over time.
To converge means to come together from different starting points toward a single point, place, or outcome.
The process of different things moving towards or meeting at a common point, idea, or result.
Conversant means well-acquainted with something — familiar enough with a subject to understand it, work with it, and talk about it in a knowledgeable way.

To converse means to talk with another person in a back-and-forth exchange — what we call a conversation. It's not just one person talking; both people are involved, listening and responding to each other. Think of it as two minds meeting through words.
Conversion means the act or process — or the result — of changing something from one form, type, function, state, or belief into another. It's not just any small adjustment or tweak.
A convert is a person who has changed their deeply held beliefs — moving away from one set of beliefs and genuinely adopting another. The word always refers to a person, not a thing or a process.
To convert something means to change it from one form, state, purpose, belief, or system into a completely different one.
Convex describes something that bulges or curves outward, away from its own center. Think of the outside surface of a ball. It pushes toward you. That outward-rounding quality is what "convex" means.
Convexity is the quality or state of curving outward — of bulging away from a center point, like the outside surface of a ball, the top of a dome, or the rounded back of a spoon.
Convey means to carry something from one point and deliver it to another — so that whatever is being "conveyed" successfully moves from a source to a destination.
Conveyance means the act of carrying or moving something (or someone) from one place to another, or the thing used to do that carrying.
A firmly held belief. A conviction is also a formal declaration by a court that someone is guilty of a crime.
To convince someone means to make them believe something is true — or to make them feel certain about it — usually by giving them reasons, evidence, or a strong argument.

When you describe someone as convinced, you are saying that they have a firm, settled belief about something — one with no real doubt behind it. Their mind feels made up. The belief isn't shaky or "maybe" — it feels solid and certain to them.
"Convivial" describes warm, friendly, and lively enjoyment in the company of other people — particularly in social settings like gatherings, meals, or celebrations.
Conviviality is the warm, lively, and cheerful friendliness that fills a room when people are genuinely enjoying each other's company.

A convocation is a formal, official gathering of people who have been called together by someone in authority, for a specific and important purpose. It is never a casual meetup. It always carries a sense of ceremony, seriousness, and official weight.

To convoke means to formally and officially call a group of people together for a specific meeting or assembly. When someone convokes a group, they are using their authority to summon people to gather, usually for an important and deliberate purpose.
If something is convoluted, it is twisted, tangled, or wound over itself in so many layers that it becomes extremely difficult to follow or make sense of.
A convoy is a group of vehicles, ships, or aircraft traveling together as one organized unit, usually for safety, protection, or coordination.
Convulse means to shake violently and uncontrollably — whether that's a body, a place, a society, or a group of people. The shaking is always sudden, powerful, and beyond normal control.
A convulsion is a sudden, violent, and uncontrollable event — one in which a body, a society, or even a situation is overtaken by an overwhelming force that it simply cannot resist or stop.
Sudden, violent, and uncontrolled, like a convulsion, as in "convulsive sobs" or "convulsive laughter."
In a hopeless situation, with no chance of success (informal slang), as in "if the teacher finds out, we're cooked." It can also mean exhausted or mentally drained.
The cold, clammy dampness of a surface, such as stone walls, before a change in the weather — a phrase made famous by the opening of the novel Dune.
To cooperate means to work together with one or more people toward a shared goal, where each person plays their part willingly and in harmony with the others.
When you describe someone or something as cooperative, you mean they are willing to work together, follow reasonable requests, and not cause unnecessary difficulty or resistance.
To coordinate means to organize two or more people, things, or activities so that they work together smoothly toward a shared goal.
Coordinated describes something — or someone — where multiple parts work together smoothly and effectively, each doing its own job in a way that fits with what the others are doing.
Copacetic means everything is perfectly fine, smooth, and satisfactory — with absolutely nothing to worry about.
To cope means to deal with something difficult in a way that allows you to manage or get through it. It is about handling a hard situation without being completely defeated by it.
The traditional explanation of quantum mechanics, which holds that a particle has no definite properties until it is measured, and that measurement itself determines the outcome.

Copious means "existing in very large, often impressively large, quantities." When you describe something as copious, you are saying there is a great deal of it — more than typical, and often more than expected.

A coppice is a small, managed area of woodland where the trees and shrubs are deliberately cut down to near ground level on a regular cycle — not to destroy them, but to encourage them to regrow. This regrowth is the heart of the whole concept.
A copse is a small, dense cluster of trees — bigger than a few scattered trees standing in a field, but much smaller than a forest or even a wood.
To copulate means to engage in sexual intercourse — the physical act in which two beings join their bodies together, typically for reproduction. The word applies to both humans and animals.
Copulation is the physical act of sexual union between two living beings — specifically, the joining of their bodies in a way that allows reproduction to occur.
Coquetry is the art of deliberate, playful flirting — done not out of genuine romantic feeling, but for the pleasure of attracting admiration and being desired.

A coquette is a woman who flirts with men to win their attention and admiration — but with no real intention of committing to them. She enjoys being desired and chased. The relationship itself doesn't interest her much; the thrill of being wanted does.
To coquette means to flirt with someone — but not in an innocent, warm-hearted way.

Coquettish describes a way of behaving that is playfully flirtatious — full of charming little tricks designed to attract someone's attention and interest, while deliberately keeping them guessing about how serious you actually are.

Cordial means warm, friendly, and genuinely pleasant — but in a polite, composed, and somewhat controlled way. It describes a kind of friendliness that feels sincere and heartfelt, not fake or forced, yet not wildly emotional or overly casual either.

Cordiality is the quality of being genuinely warm, friendly, and pleasant in the way you treat others. When someone shows cordiality, they make the people around them feel sincerely welcomed, at ease, and valued — not just tolerated or acknowledged.

Cordially means in a warm, friendly, and genuinely sincere way. When someone does something cordially, they do it with real warmth — not just surface-level politeness, but with an openness of heart that feels welcoming and authentic.

A cordon is a protective or restrictive ring or line formed around something — usually made up of people, vehicles, or physical barriers — whose purpose is to control who can enter or leave a particular area, or to protect something inside it.
The core is the innermost, central, or most essential part of something.
A cormorant is a large water bird found all over the world — on coastlines, rivers, and lakes. It is primarily known as a remarkably skilled diver and fish-hunter.

To corner means to trap someone or something so they have no escape and no good options left. Think of a literal corner in a room — it's a closed-off space where you can't move forward, left, or right.

A cornerstone is the single most important, fundamental element that everything else depends on. It is not just one of several important things — it is the essential piece. Without it, the whole structure falls apart.

The word cornice refers to a projecting, horizontal ledge or decorative strip running along the top edge of something — think of it as a "cap" or "crown" that sits at the upper rim of a surface, either sticking outward or running along a boundary.

The most common use of "corniche" in modern English refers to a road that runs along the edge or face of a cliff, a hillside, or a steep coastal slope. Picture a narrow road carved into the side of a mountain that overlooks the sea.

A cornucopia means an overflowing, generous abundance of good things — so much of something desirable that it feels almost overwhelming in the best possible way. Think of it as the opposite of scarcity.
When you call something corny, you are saying it is overly sentimental, clichéd, or unsophisticated in a way that feels a little embarrassing or cringe-worthy.
A corollary is a truth that follows so naturally and directly from another truth that it requires little or no additional effort to establish.
As a noun, "a coronary" is an informal, everyday word for a heart attack — specifically, the kind caused when one of the heart's own blood supply pipes gets blocked.
A coronation is a grand, formal ceremony in which a king, queen, emperor, empress, or any other monarch is officially crowned and publicly recognized as the ruler of a country or empire.

A coroner is an official whose job is to investigate deaths — specifically deaths that are sudden, unexpected, suspicious, or unexplained. Their central mission is to answer one critical question: How did this person die?
Corporal means relating to or directly involving the physical human body — not the mind, not the soul, not one's money or freedom, but the actual flesh-and-bones body.
If something is corporeal, it has a physical body. It takes up space in the real world. You could, at least in principle, reach out and touch it.

A corps is a group of people who are formally organized together to carry out a specific role, function, or mission. The members of a corps share a common purpose, operate as a unified body, and usually work within some kind of structure or authority.

A corpse is the dead body of a human being. The very moment a person dies, their physical body becomes a corpse. That's the single most important thing to know: the word refers to a human body that is no longer alive.

Corpulence is a noun that refers to the condition of being excessively overweight — having a body that carries a notably large and heavy amount of flesh or fat. It does not merely mean being a little chubby or slightly overweight.

Corpulent means very fat or heavily overweight. When you describe a person as corpulent, you are saying that their body is noticeably large and heavy — carrying a significant amount of excess flesh. It goes well beyond "a little chubby."
Corpus simply means a body — a collected, organized whole made up of many parts.

A corpuscle is a tiny, self-contained, discrete particle or small body — something so small it is invisible (or barely visible) to the naked eye, exists as a distinct individual unit, and functions as part of a much larger system.
A corral is an enclosed outdoor area — surrounded by a fence or a barrier — that is used to keep livestock (animals like horses, cattle, or pigs) safely contained so they cannot wander off or escape.
