To correlate means to show, find, or establish a connection between two things such that when one changes, the other tends to change in a related way. It means recognizing that two things move together in a pattern — they are linked.
A correlation is a relationship between two things — specifically, a pattern where changes in one thing are consistently associated with changes in another thing.

When two things are correlative, they belong together as a naturally matched pair — each one so closely tied to the other that you cannot fully understand, define, or even have one without the other. They are mutually dependent.
To match or be similar to something, as in "the figures correspond with our records." It can also mean to exchange letters or messages with someone.
Written communication, such as letters or emails, exchanged between people. It can also mean a close similarity or connection between two things.

A correspondent is someone who communicates with someone else from a distance — usually in writing, or by sending information regularly. Think of it as: a person on the other end of an ongoing communication.
"Corresponding" describes something that has a direct, specific match or connection with something else. There are always two things (or two sets of things) involved.

A corridor is a long, narrow passage that connects two or more places. Its defining purpose is to allow movement — it is a path between places, not a destination itself. Think of it as a channel or a throat through which people, things, or access must pass.
Something or someone is corrigible if they can be — or are willing to be — corrected, improved, or set right.
To corroborate something means to provide additional evidence, information, or testimony that confirms or supports a claim, story, or statement that has already been made.
When something is corroborating, it means it supports, confirms, or backs up something that was already said or claimed.
To corrode means to gradually eat away and destroy a material — usually from the surface inward — through a chemical reaction.

Something corrosive slowly and steadily destroys, eats away, or damages whatever it comes into contact with — often in a way that cannot be undone. The key word here is slowly. A corrosive thing does not smash or explode.
"Corrugated" describes a surface — or an object — that has been shaped into a series of regular, parallel ridges (raised parts) and grooves (sunken channels) that alternate evenly with each other.
"Corrupt" describes something — or someone — that has been spoiled, tainted, or made bad from a state that was once good, pure, honest, or properly functioning.
To corrupt something or someone means to take what was originally good, pure, honest, or working correctly — and damage or change it so that it becomes bad, dishonest, or broken.
Something is corruptible if it can be made dishonest, morally bad, or impure — especially through bribery, temptation, or harmful outside influence.

Corruption is what happens when something that was originally pure, whole, correct, or trustworthy gets spoiled, twisted, or damaged into a worse form — either gradually or by deliberate interference.

A corsage is a small, decorative arrangement of flowers — and sometimes ribbons, greenery, or other ornaments — that a person wears directly on their body as an accessory. Think of it as a tiny, wearable bouquet.
A pirate, especially one who raided ships in the Mediterranean, often with the backing of a government.

A cortege is a slow, formal, and solemn procession — a group of people (and often vehicles) moving together as one unit to honor or accompany someone. It is the group in motion, not just a crowd standing still.

Coruscant means flashing or sparkling with brilliant light — but not in a steady, constant way. The key idea is movement. The light dances, flickers, and shoots off in rapid little bursts. Think of it as light that is alive.
To coruscate means to flash or sparkle with light — specifically in quick, repeated bursts. If something coruscates, it throws off rapid, dazzling flashes of brightness.
"Cosmetic" means relating to or affecting only the outer appearance of something — not its true nature, deeper substance, or actual function.
Cosmic means "of, relating to, or belonging to the cosmos."
A cosmogony is an account, story, or theory that explains how the universe — or the world — came into existence. The plural is cosmogonies.

Cosmology is the study of the universe as a whole — its origin, its structure, how it has changed over time, and what its ultimate fate might be. Think of it as asking the biggest possible questions a human mind can ask: Where did everything come from?
Cosmopolitan means belonging to, comfortable with, or composed of the whole world — not just one place, one culture, or one way of life.
To cosset someone means to give them an excessive amount of care, comfort, and attention — far more than they truly need. Think of it as pampering someone to the point of spoiling them.
A costume is a set of clothing — and often accessories, makeup, or props — that a person wears to look like someone or something they are not in real life.
To get close and comfortable with someone, physically or socially, often to win their favour ("cosying up to the boss"). Also spelt "cozy up".

A coterie is a small, tight-knit, and exclusive group of people who share a common interest, taste, or purpose — and who tend to stick closely together, often in a way that makes it difficult for outsiders to join or be accepted.
A cotillion is either a specific type of group dance, or a formal social event (a ball) built around such dancing — especially one meant to introduce young people into society.

A cottage is a small, simple house, usually found in the countryside, a village, by the sea, or near a lake. It is not grand or spacious — it is modest in size, and that modesty is a defining part of what makes it a cottage.
A deep, steep-sided ravine carved by water, especially in the prairies of western North America, which is often dry except after rain.

Counsel means serious, careful advice — the kind given thoughtfully by someone who wants to genuinely help you navigate a difficult situation. It's not the quick, casual sort of advice a friend throws out ("just go for it!"). Counsel is weighty.
A counselor is a person whose job or role is to give guidance, advice, or support to someone who needs it.
To find the total number of things, or to say numbers in order. It can also mean to be important or valid, as in "every vote counts." To count on someone means to rely on them.
A person's face or facial expression, as in "a stern countenance." It can also mean approval or support.
To countenance something means to accept it, approve of it, or give it your moral support — especially when that thing is considered wrong, inappropriate, or controversial.
To counter something means to respond to it with an opposing action, argument, or measure — specifically to weaken, block, or defeat it.
Something is counter-intuitive when it goes against what your gut feeling, common sense, or natural instinct tells you should be true — and yet it actually is true.
To counteract something means to take action against it in order to reduce, weaken, or cancel out its effect.
When something is described as counterfeit, it means it is a fake copy of something real, made specifically to trick people into believing it is the genuine thing.
A counterfeit is a fake copy of something real and valuable, made specifically to trick people into believing it is the genuine thing.
To counterfeit something means to make a fake, unauthorized copy of something valuable or official, with the deliberate intent to trick people into believing that the fake is the real thing.
To countermand something means to cancel or reverse a previously given order or instruction — by issuing a new, opposing order in its place.
A counterpart is a person or thing that matches, mirrors, or corresponds to another person or thing — but exists in a different place, group, system, or context.

Counterpoint means two or more independent things — melodies, ideas, qualities, or perspectives — that are genuinely different from each other, yet are placed together in a way that makes each one richer and more meaningful.
To countervail means to act against something with equal or sufficient force so as to neutralize, offset, or balance it out.
Countervailing describes something that acts as an opposing force, pressure, or influence that works against another force in order to reduce, balance, offset, or neutralize it.
Countless means so many that it is impossible, or at least impractical, to count them.

A coup means a sudden, impressive, and decisive move — something done in one swift stroke that changes a situation dramatically. Think of it as the opposite of a slow, gradual process. A coup is sharp, fast, and its effects are immediate.
A coup d'état is the sudden, illegal seizure of a government's power by a small group of people — usually from within the country itself, and very often from within the government or military.
A coup de grâce is the final, decisive action that ends something — or someone — that was already weakened, failing, or suffering.
"Couple" as a noun has two main, closely related meanings: two people romantically involved, and a small number, usually two.
To couple means to join or connect two things together — not just placing them near each other, but creating a real, meaningful link between them so they work in relation to each other.

A couplet is a pair of two consecutive lines in a poem that belong together as a unit. The word "pair" is key — just like a pair of shoes, a couplet is always exactly two lines, never one, never three.

Courageous describes a person (or their actions, decisions, or words) that show courage — the ability to face something difficult, dangerous, painful, or frightening and still move forward, even when every part of you wants to run away or give up.
A courier is a person or a company whose job is to carry and deliver something — a letter, a document, a package, or any other item — from one specific person or place to another.

A court is a place — and an institution — where legal matters are formally decided. When someone is accused of a crime, or when two parties have a dispute, they go to court so that a judge (and sometimes a jury) can hear the case and deliver a judgment.
A court martial is a military court — a special legal tribunal that exists specifically within the armed forces to judge military personnel accused of breaking military law.
When we say someone is courteous, we mean they are genuinely polite, respectful, and considerate in the way they treat other people.
A courtesan is a woman who provided sexual companionship to wealthy or powerful men — kings, nobles, politicians, merchants — in exchange for money, gifts, fine housing, and a comfortable life.
A courtier is a person who is part of the inner circle surrounding a powerful ruler — a king, queen, emperor, or similar monarch — and who spends their time at the royal court.
Courtly describes a style of behavior that is very polished, refined, and elegantly formal — the kind of gracious, almost ceremonious politeness associated with royal courts and aristocratic life.
A courtroom is a room — usually inside a larger building called a courthouse — where legal cases are officially heard and decided.
A courtyard is an outdoor, open-to-the-sky space that is enclosed — fully or partially — by the walls of a building or by a group of buildings around it.

Couture means high-end, custom-made clothing — clothing that is designed and built specifically for one individual person, by hand, with extraordinary skill and the finest materials available. It is not clothing you pick off a rack in a store.
A cove is a small, sheltered area of water along a coastline, where the land curves inward to partially wrap around it — like a scoop or a pocket cut into the shoreline.
A covenant is a serious, solemn, and formally binding agreement or promise between two or more parties — one that carries a deep sense of duty, commitment, and moral weight.
A false explanation used to hide someone's real identity or activities. It is also the main article in a magazine, featured on its cover.
"Coverage" means the extent to which something is reached, included, protected, or reported on. It always answers the question: "How much of X is covered — and how well?"

A coverall is a one-piece garment — a single, continuous piece of clothing — that covers your entire body from your neck all the way down to your wrists and ankles. Think of it as a full-body suit that you wear on top of your regular clothes to protect them.
Covert means done or kept in a hidden, secret way — especially on purpose.
To covet something means to want it very, very badly — with a deep, aching, almost hungry kind of desire. But it goes further than just "wanting."

When something is described as coveted, it means it is deeply and intensely desired by many people — not in a casual, everyday way, but in a strong, almost aching way. People don't just want a coveted thing; they long for it, sometimes for years.
Covetous means having a strong, greedy desire to possess something that belongs to someone else.
A covey is a small, tight-knit group — most commonly used for certain birds, especially quail and partridges, but also sometimes for people.

A cow is a large, four-legged farm animal with hooves, a thick body, a long tail, and — in many cases — horns. You've almost certainly seen one, or at least a picture of one: a big, gentle creature that grazes on grass in fields and meadows.
A coward is a person who avoids danger, difficulty, or pain — not simply because they are afraid, but because they allow their fear to win when they really should not. The key word here is should.

To cower means to shrink your body and pull yourself down or backward because you are afraid or feel threatened. It is a physical reaction to fear — your body instinctively makes itself small, as if trying to disappear or protect itself.
A cowl is a loose, hood-like covering — something that drapes, curves, or wraps over something else to cover it. Think of it as a "hood" in the broadest possible sense.

A cowlick is a small patch of hair on a person's scalp that grows in a noticeably different direction from all the hair around it. Instead of lying flat and blending in smoothly, this section sticks up, swirls outward, or points in a direction of its own.
Coy means pretending to be shy, modest, or reluctant when you are actually not — or when you are deliberately choosing to act that way to achieve some effect.

A coyote is a wild, dog-like animal native to North America. It is a member of the same animal family as dogs and wolves, but it is its own separate species — not a stray dog, not a small wolf, but its own distinct creature.

To cozen someone means to trick or deceive them in a smooth, crafty way — usually to get something from them. It combines the ideas of cheating, swindling, and manipulation, all wrapped in a layer of slyness.
Cozy describes a feeling that is warm, comfortable, and pleasantly sheltered — a kind of small, gentle happiness that comes from being in a safe, soft, and welcoming place or situation.
To snuggle close to someone, or to become friendly with someone in order to gain an advantage ("He's been cozying up to the new manager").

When "crabbed" describes a person, it means they are chronically grumpy, harsh, and unpleasant to be around. A crabbed person is not just having a bad day — they carry a permanent cloud of ill-temper.

"Crabby" describes a person who is in a bad, irritable mood — easily annoyed, slightly grumpy, and unpleasant to be around. When someone is crabby, small things bother them more than usual, and they tend to snap, complain, or react with impatience.
When something hard — a wall, a glass, a road, a bone — gets damaged but doesn't fully fall apart, the thin visible line of damage is called a crack.

A crackdown is a sudden, firm, and forceful effort by people in authority — such as a government, police, or an organization — to stop, control, or punish something they consider illegal, harmful, or unacceptable.

When you describe someone or something as crackerjack, you mean they are exceptionally skilled, capable, or excellent — not just good, but outstandingly, impressively good. It signals that a person or thing is operating at the very top of its class.
A crackhouse is a building — usually a rundown house, apartment, or any abandoned structure — where people go to buy, sell, or smoke crack cocaine.
To hold something gently, carefully, and protectively — with your arms or hands forming a soft, curved shape around it, like a nest.
An activity that involves making things skilfully by hand, such as pottery or weaving, or the skill itself. It can also mean cunning, or a boat or aircraft.

To craft something means to make or create it — but not just casually or quickly. When you craft something, you make it with skill, care, and a lot of deliberate thought. Every choice you make during the process is intentional.

Craftsmanship refers to the high quality and care that goes into making something — the skill, precision, and dedication a person brings to their work, especially when that work involves creating or building something with their hands or through deep technical expertise.

Crafty means cleverly deceptive. It describes someone who uses their intelligence not openly and honestly, but in a sneaky, calculated way — usually to get what they want while hiding their true intentions from others.

A crag is a steep, rugged, jagged mass of rock — the kind that juts out sharply from a cliff, a mountain, or a rocky hillside. Think of it as nature's rough, uneven, and imposing rock projection: not smooth, not rounded, but broken, angular, and hard-edged.
Craggy describes something that is rugged, rough, and uneven in a sharp, rocky way — full of irregular bumps, ridges, and hard angles, rather than being smooth, gentle, or flat.
Cram means to force too much of something into a space that is too small for it. The key feeling behind this word is excess and force — you are pushing more than what fits comfortably.
Cramped describes a situation where there is not enough space — where things, people, or a body are squeezed tightly into an area that is too small for them.
A large machine with a long arm, used to lift and move heavy objects. A crane is also a tall bird with long legs and a long neck.
To crane means to stretch your neck forward, upward, or sideways in order to see something better.

If someone is cranky, they are in a bad mood — easily annoyed, irritable, and somewhat difficult to be around. A cranky person gets bothered by small things, may snap at others, complain, or just seem generally grumpy and unpleasant.

A cranny is a small, narrow crack or opening in a hard surface. Think of a wall that has developed a thin split in it over time, or a rock face with a tiny gap running through it — that gap, that little crack, is a cranny. It is not a big hole.
Crapulous describes a state of gross, shameless excess — specifically in eating and drinking — and the wretched physical feeling that follows from it.
When something crashes, it hits something else with a violent, damaging impact.

"Crass" describes behavior, comments, or attitudes that are offensively coarse, showing a shocking lack of basic sensitivity, decency, or intelligence — in a way that is painfully obvious and embarrassing to witness.
A crate is a sturdy, rigid container used to hold, protect, and transport things. Think of it as a tough, heavy-duty box — built not for elegance, but for strength and practicality.
A crater is a large, bowl-shaped hollow or pit in the ground or on the surface of something — wide at the top and curving downward toward the bottom, like an upside-down dome scooped into the earth.
A cravat is a type of decorative neckwear — a wide, soft piece of fabric that a man wraps, folds, or ties around his neck, typically over a shirt collar.

To crave something means to want it with an extreme, deep, almost urgent intensity. It is not a casual or mild want. It is the kind of want that feels powerful, persistent, and sometimes hard to control or ignore — almost like a hunger or a thirst inside you.

Craven means contemptibly cowardly — not just scared, but so shamefully and disgracefully lacking in courage that the cowardice itself becomes a moral failure. When you call someone craven, you are not simply saying they were afraid.
A crease is a line, ridge, or mark that forms on a flat, flexible surface when it is folded, pressed, bent, or squeezed. It is the visible trace that a fold or bend leaves behind.

When you call someone or something creative, you are saying that they have the power to produce something new, original, and imaginative — something that did not exist before, or a fresh way of doing something that already exists.
Credence means belief in, or acceptance of, something as true or real. When you give credence to something, you are choosing to believe it, trust it, or treat it as worth taking seriously.
A credential is anything that proves something about you — either who you are or what you are qualified to do.

A credenza is a long, low piece of furniture — essentially a storage cabinet — that sits flat against a wall. Think of it as a wide box, low to the ground, with a flat top and storage space (doors, drawers, or shelves) hidden below.

Credibility is the quality of being trusted and believed by others. When a person, organization, or source of information has credibility, people accept what they say as true and rely on what they do as dependable.

Credible means worthy of being believed. When something or someone is credible, you have solid, reasonable grounds to trust or believe them — not just a feeling, but actual backing from evidence, logic, track record, or expertise.

Praise or recognition for something you have done, as in "she deserves credit for the idea." It also means an arrangement to buy now and pay later, money in an account, or a unit of study at a college.

"To credit" means to give recognition or acknowledgment to someone or something. Think of it as pointing at someone or something and saying, "This belongs to you" — whether that's praise, an achievement, a quality, money, or even just the truth of a story.

Creditable means deserving of praise, respect, or acknowledgment. When you call something creditable, you are saying it is good enough — or better than good enough — to earn recognition and admiration.
A credo is a personal statement of core beliefs — a declaration of the things you believe so deeply that they shape how you live, work, and make decisions.
Credulity is the tendency to believe things too easily, too quickly, and without asking for good reasons or evidence.
Credulous means too willing to believe things, especially without questioning whether they are true or asking for proof.
A creed is a clearly defined set of beliefs or principles that a person or group holds as absolutely fundamental — the core convictions they live by, stand by, and identify with.

Every use of "creep" shares one central idea — movement that is slow, quiet, and gradual. Whether a person is sneaking across a room, a plant is growing up a wall, a price is rising over years, or a feeling is spreading through your body — it is all creep.

To cremate means to burn a dead body at extremely high temperatures until it turns into ash and bone fragments. It is one of the two most common ways humans deal with a person's body after they die — the other being burial (placing the body in the ground).
Cremation is the process of disposing of a dead human body (or sometimes an animal) by burning it at an extremely high temperature until it is reduced to ash and small bone fragments.

Crenellated is an adjective that describes something — almost always a wall, tower, or building — whose top edge is not smooth or flat, but instead has a repeating pattern of raised solid blocks alternating with open gaps or notches.
A crepe is an extremely thin, flat pancake. Unlike a regular pancake — which is thick, fluffy, and rises up — a crepe is paper-thin, soft, and slightly chewy.

Crepitation means a crackling, grating, or rattling sound — or a similar sensation felt through touch. Think of the sharp, dry snap of dry twigs breaking underfoot, or the crackle of a fire, or the grinding noise a rusty hinge makes.

Crepuscular means "relating to, occurring during, or resembling twilight." Twilight is that brief, soft-lit period that appears twice every day — once just before sunrise (dawn), and once just after sunset (dusk).
A crescendo is a progressive build-up — a steady increase in force, intensity, or loudness, leading toward a peak.
When you use "crescent" as an adjective, it means shaped like a crescent moon — that thin, curved, silvery slice of the moon you see in the sky just a few days after a new moon.

A crest means the highest point of something — the very top, the peak, the part that rises above everything else around it. Almost every meaning of this word connects back to this single idea of topmost-ness.

Crestfallen means feeling visibly sad, disappointed, and deflated — specifically because something you were hoping for or expecting didn't happen. It describes that hollow, sinking feeling when reality falls short of what you were counting on.
A very stupid person (an offensive insult). In outdated medical use, it referred to a person with a severe thyroid condition causing stunted growth and intellectual disability.
Extremely stupid. The word is offensive, as it was originally used for people with a severe thyroid-related disability.
A crevasse is a deep crack in a glacier or a large body of ice.
A crevice is a narrow crack or opening in a hard surface — one that is thin enough to be tight, but deep or long enough to actually be a space you can notice, look into, or put something inside.

Crimson describes a specific shade of red — one that is deep, rich, and vivid, with a slight lean toward blue or purple rather than orange. Think of it as red at its most intense and saturated, but with a cool, darker undertone.
When you cringe, your body or your mind pulls away from something — as a reflex, not a choice. It happens automatically, the moment something feels threatening, painful, or deeply uncomfortable.
To crinkle means to form many small, irregular, random-looking folds or wrinkles on a surface.
When you cripple something, you damage it so badly that it can no longer work properly — but you don't completely destroy it.
Crippling describes something so severe and damaging that it greatly weakens or disables the ability to function, survive, or move forward normally.
A crisis is a serious, dangerous, or very difficult situation that demands urgent attention, where the outcome is uncertain and a lot is at stake.
A crisscross is a pattern made by lines — or paths, or marks — that cross over each other in multiple directions, creating a network of intersections.
The standards or conditions used to judge, evaluate, or decide something. "Criteria" is plural; the singular is "criterion."
A criterion is a specific standard, rule, or factor that you use to judge, evaluate, or decide something.

A critic is a person who carefully studies, evaluates, and judges something — and then shares that judgment, usually in words. The key idea is that a critic does not just say "I liked it" or "I didn't like it."
"Critical" always points to something that deserves serious, careful attention — either because it involves judgment, because it is vitally important, or because it is at a dangerous turning point.
"Criticism" means the act of examining something carefully and expressing a judgment about it — whether it is good, bad, or somewhere in between.

To criticize means to look at something — a person's behavior, a piece of work, an idea, a decision, or anything really — and point out what is wrong, weak, or flawed about it. You are making a negative judgment and expressing it.

A critique is a careful, detailed examination of something — where you look at it closely, analyze how it works, identify what is strong about it, and point out what is weak, flawed, or could be better.

A croak is a low, rough, harsh sound — the kind that feels like it comes from deep in the throat and has a scratchy, raspy quality to it. It is never smooth or musical. Think of it as the opposite of a clear, clean sound.
Crochet is a handcraft that creates fabric or decorative objects by interlocking loops of yarn (or thread) using a single hooked needle.
A crock-pot is an electric kitchen appliance used to cook food slowly, using low heat, over a long period of time — typically anywhere from 4 to 10 hours.

Crockery is a collective word for the cups, plates, bowls, saucers, mugs, and similar items that you use when eating or drinking. These items are typically made from baked clay — such as earthenware, stoneware, porcelain, or china.

A croissant is a type of baked pastry — a light, flaky, crescent-shaped bread made primarily from dough that has been layered with a generous amount of butter. It is one of the most recognizable pastries in the world.

A crone is an old woman — not just any old woman, but one who is seen as ugly, withered, and unpleasant. Think wrinkled skin, a bony frame, a sharp or bitter manner. That is the picture the word paints.
A crony is a close friend or associate of someone — but not just any friend. The word carries a strong negative meaning.

Cronyism is when someone in a position of power gives jobs, contracts, favors, or opportunities to their close friends — not because those friends are the best or most qualified people for the job, but simply because they are friends.

"Crooked" describes anything that deviates from being straight, flat, level, or properly aligned. If something should be straight but isn't — if it bends, curves, leans, or sits at the wrong angle — it is crooked.

To croon means to sing in a soft, low, smooth, and gentle voice. The singing is quiet rather than loud, warm rather than sharp, and flows effortlessly — like honey poured slowly. The overall feeling is tender, intimate, and soothing.

Croquet is an outdoor lawn game in which players use long-handled wooden hammers (called mallets) to hit coloured balls across a grass field, trying to pass them through a series of small wire hoops stuck into the ground.

A cross is a shape made by two straight lines or bars that meet and intersect each other — one going up-and-down (vertical) and one going left-and-right (horizontal). Picture the plus sign (+), or the letter "t".
A crossbreed is a living thing — an animal or a plant — that is born from two parents who belong to different breeds or varieties of the same species.

A crosshair is a fine, thin line — or more commonly, a pair of two such lines crossing each other at their centers to form a "+" shape — used as a reference point for aiming, targeting, or aligning something precisely.

A crossing guard is a person whose job is to help people — especially children — cross a road safely. They stand at a specific spot on the road, stop the traffic when needed, and signal to people when it is safe to walk across.

A crosspiece is any bar, beam, plank, rod, or strip of material that is placed or fixed across something — usually running at a right angle to the main length or direction of the structure it belongs to.

A crossroads is a place where two or more roads meet and cross each other. Picture a simple "+" shape on a map — that intersection is a crossroads. When you're standing there, you can go straight, turn left, turn right, or go back the way you came.

When you call someone crotchety, you mean they are grumpy, irritable, and easily annoyed — but with an important extra layer: they also tend to hold odd, stubborn, and unreasonable opinions that they refuse to let go of. It's not just a bad mood.

To crouch means to lower your body toward the ground by bending your knees, while keeping your feet flat or on your toes, and your upper body leaning slightly forward. You are not sitting. You are not lying down.

"To crow" means to make a loud, triumphant sound — the kind that announces something good has happened. Whether it's an animal, a baby, or a person, crowing is always about expressing victory, joy, or pride out loud and boldly.
"A crowning glory" means the finest, most impressive, or most admirable part of something or someone — the ultimate highlight that stands above everything else.

When something is crucial, it means it is so important that the result of a situation — success or failure, good or bad — depends on it. It is the key deciding factor. If you remove or ignore a crucial thing, everything falls apart or goes wrong.
Shaped like a cross, or arranged in the form of a cross.
A situation of severe testing or difficulty that forces people to change or develop. Literally, a heat-resistant container used to melt metals.

Crucifixion is the act of killing a person by fastening them to a large wooden cross — either by driving nails through their wrists and feet, or by tying them with ropes — and leaving them there to die slowly and in agony.
In a natural, unrefined state, as in "crude oil." It can also mean simple and roughly made, as in "a crude shelter," or offensively rude, especially about sex, as in "crude jokes."
The state of being crude — rough and unrefined, or offensively vulgar. A crudity is also a crude remark or act.
Cruel describes someone or something that causes pain or suffering — and either doesn't care, or actually wants it to happen.
A cruet is a small container designed specifically for holding and pouring liquid condiments or seasonings at the dining table.
To cruise means to move in a smooth, relaxed, and effortless way — without strain, without rush, and without much resistance. Think of the feeling of gliding.
A crumpet is a round, flat, soft bread-like food that is very popular in the United Kingdom. It is not quite bread, not quite a pancake — it sits somewhere in between.

To crumple something means to press, squeeze, or crush it in a way that leaves it deformed — full of random, irregular folds and wrinkles — so that it loses its original smooth, flat, or upright shape.

A crusader is someone who fights passionately and persistently for a cause they deeply believe in — someone who doesn't just care about something, but actively and relentlessly works to change things, often in the face of opposition.

To press something so hard that it breaks or loses its shape. Figuratively, to defeat someone completely, to put an end to a protest by force, or to make someone feel deeply disappointed or humiliated.
Crust means a hard or firm outer layer that sits on top of, or around, something softer. That's the single idea that connects every use of this word.
A crustacean is a type of animal. Think of familiar creatures like crabs, lobsters, shrimp, and crayfish — these are all crustaceans.
A crutch is a physical support device used to help someone walk when they cannot walk properly on their own — usually because of an injury, surgery, or a physical disability.

The crux of something is its single most important, central point — the part that everything else depends on or revolves around. It's the essential piece that, if you miss it, you miss the whole thing.

A crypt is most commonly an underground chamber or room, especially one located beneath a church or cathedral. It is typically made of stone and is used as a place for burial — to lay the dead to rest.
Something is cryptic when it is mysterious, unclear, or has a hidden meaning that is genuinely difficult to figure out — and often deliberately so.

A cryptogram is a piece of writing — usually a message, sentence, or short text — that has been deliberately scrambled into a secret form using a specific system, so that it looks like meaningless gibberish to anyone who doesn't know (or hasn't figured out) that system.
Cryptography is the science and practice of securing information so that only the right people can read or understand it, while making it meaningless to everyone else.
Having the structure of a crystal. Figuratively, extremely clear and pure, as in "crystalline water" or "crystalline prose."
To crystallize means to form crystals, or to cause something to form crystals.

A cubicle is a small, enclosed or semi-enclosed space created by surrounding a limited area with walls or partitions, separating it from a larger surrounding space. The key ideas are: small, enclosed, and carved out of a bigger space.

Cubism is a style of art — and a revolutionary art movement — that began in the early 20th century (around 1907–1908), primarily in Paris. It was pioneered by two painters: Pablo Picasso (Spanish) and Georges Braque (French).
Cubist describes something that belongs to, is characteristic of, or resembles Cubism — one of the most revolutionary art styles in history, born in the early 1900s.
To cuckold a man means to make him the victim of his partner's sexual infidelity.

A cudgel is a short, thick, heavy stick used as a weapon to hit or beat someone. Think of it as a simple but brutal club — the kind a person would pick up, swing hard, and use to cause serious pain or injury.
To cudgel someone means to beat them hard with a heavy stick.

A cue is a signal — something that tells you it's time to act, or gives you information about what is happening or what is expected of you. Almost all of its meanings flow from this one central idea: a cue is a trigger.
A cuirass is a piece of body armor that protects the torso — the chest and the back — of a soldier or warrior.
A cuisine is a complete, living tradition of cooking that belongs to a particular group of people — a country, a region, a culture, or an ethnic community. It is not just a set of recipes.

A cul de sac is something — most often a road, but also a situation or a body part — that has only one opening and is closed off at the other end. Whatever enters must come back out the same way it went in.
Culinary is an adjective that means relating to cooking or the preparation of food.
"Cull" means to deliberately pick something out from a larger group.

When something is culminant, it is at its absolute highest point — its peak, its top, its most powerful or prominent moment. Think of it as a spotlight moment: everything has been building up, and right now, this thing is at the very top of its arc.
To culminate means to reach the highest or most important point of a process — usually after a long buildup — and then end or result in something significant.
A culmination is the final, highest point that something reaches after a long process of building up.
Culpability means deserving of blame for something wrong, harmful, or illegal.
If someone is culpable, it means they deserve to be blamed for something bad that happened — because they either caused it, allowed it to happen, or played a part in it.

A culprit is a person who is responsible for something bad — a crime, a mistake, or a problem. When something goes wrong and someone is to blame, that person is the culprit. The word carries a sense of fault and guilt.

"Cult" describes a group of people united by an intense, fervent devotion to something — a person, a belief system, an idea, or even a piece of art. The word is powerful precisely because it sits on a spectrum.
To cultivate something means to deliberately and patiently work toward its growth or development over time.

When someone is described as cultivated, it means they have developed their mind, tastes, and manners through years of education, reading, travel, and deep engagement with art, music, literature, and ideas.

Cultivation means the deliberate, sustained effort to help something grow, develop, or improve. It is never accidental — it always involves conscious care, attention, and repeated action over time. Think of it as the direct opposite of neglect.
Cultural means relating to culture — that is, relating to the shared way of life of a group of people.

Culture is the total shared way of life of a group of people — everything they believe, value, practice, create, and pass on to the next generation, not through biology or instinct, but through living together and learning from one another.

When we call a person cultured, we mean they have developed a deep, broad familiarity with the finer things of human civilization — art, literature, music, history, philosophy, theatre, and the ways of the world.

"Culturing" is the gerund form of the verb "to culture," which means it describes the act or process of deliberately growing living things — especially microorganisms — in a carefully controlled environment.
A culvert is a structure that lets water pass underneath something — most commonly underneath a road, a railway track, a path, or an embankment (a raised mound of earth).
If something is cumbersome, it causes difficulty, trouble, or inconvenience — either because it is physically awkward and hard to handle, or because it is overly complicated and slow to deal with.

Something is cumbrous when it is so large, heavy, or complicated that it becomes difficult and awkward to deal with. Imagine something that "weighs you down" or "gets in the way" — either physically or in a more abstract sense.
A cummerbund is a wide, pleated band of fabric that a man wears around his waist as part of formal attire.
Something is cumulative when it is built up gradually by adding one thing on top of another, over time, so that the total keeps growing with each new addition.
Cuneiform is the name given to one of the world's oldest writing systems — a method of writing that was invented and used by ancient civilizations in the Middle East for over 3,000 years.
Cunning means being clever in a sneaky, hidden, or deceptive way — using your intelligence not openly and honestly, but through tricks, schemes, and carefully hidden intentions to get what you want.
Cunning, as a noun, means the quality of being clever in a sly, sneaky, or deceptive way to get what you want — especially when others don't notice what you're really doing.
"Cunt" is one of the most heavily loaded words in the English language. It carries multiple meanings, and its impact varies dramatically depending on where in the world it is used.

Cupidity means an intense, excessive, and selfish desire for wealth, money, or material possessions. In plain terms, it is greed — a burning, consuming hunger to acquire more and more, usually in a way that is morally blameworthy.

A cupola is a small, dome-shaped structure that sits on top of something larger — usually on the roof of a building, on top of a tower, or on top of a military vehicle. Think of it as a little rounded "cap" or "crown" placed on top of something bigger.
A worthless, aggressive dog, especially a mongrel. Figuratively, a contemptible and cowardly man.
To curate something means to carefully select, organize, and present items from a larger collection, using your knowledge and judgment, with a specific purpose or audience in mind.
When you describe something as curative, you mean that it has the power or ability to cure — that is, to fully heal a disease, illness, or problem and restore someone to a healthy or normal state.
A curator is a person who carefully selects, organizes, and takes care of a collection — and then presents it meaningfully to others.

A curb is the raised border — usually made of concrete, stone, or granite — that runs along the outer edge of a sidewalk where the sidewalk meets the road. Imagine you are walking on a sidewalk and you want to cross the street.

When a smooth liquid — most commonly milk or cream — breaks apart into thick, lumpy solid bits floating in a thin, watery liquid, we say it has curdled. The solid bits are called curds, and the remaining watery liquid is called whey.
That ruined, lumpy, separated state is what curdled describes.
A cure is something that completely removes or eliminates a disease, illness, or problem — not just eases it, but actually gets rid of it.

A curfew is a rule or official order that restricts people from being in public spaces — streets, parks, or any outdoor area — during certain hours, usually at night. It is essentially a "stay indoors" command.

A curio is a small, unusual object that people find interesting or fascinating — often because it is rare, old, exotic, or just plain strange. It's the kind of thing you might pick up, turn over in your hands, and wonder about.

Curiosity is a strong, active desire to know, learn, or understand something. It is the inner feeling — almost like a pull or an itch — that makes you want to find out more about something unknown, puzzling, or interesting.
Eager to learn or know something. It can also mean strange or unusual, as in "a curious noise."
To curl up means to pull your body (or something) into a tight, rounded shape — like a ball or a C-shape — often for comfort, warmth, or rest.

A curlicue is a decorative, spiral-shaped curl or twist — a swirling, coiling line that loops or winds around in an ornamental, fancy way. Think of it as a curl that keeps going, turning in on itself, purely for the pleasure of looking elegant or elaborate.

A curmudgeon is a person who is consistently bad-tempered, grumpy, and difficult to get along with. They complain often, get irritated easily, and seem to find fault in almost everything and everyone around them.

If you describe someone as curmudgeonly, you are saying that they are bad-tempered, grumpy, and difficult to be around — and that this isn't a temporary mood, but a deeply fixed part of their personality. It is a character trait, not a passing feeling.

The word currant is a noun that refers to a type of small fruit — but here's the thing: it actually refers to two different kinds of small fruits that happen to share the same name. Understanding both will give you the complete picture.

The word currency comes down to one idea: something that flows and circulates through a community because people agree to accept it. Keep this mental image — of something flowing and being passed around — because it underlies both of the word's main meanings.

A current is a continuous, directional flow of something moving through a larger medium. The key word is flow — not random swirling, not a one-time gush, but a steady stream that keeps moving in a particular direction.
A curriculum is an officially planned set of subjects, topics, and learning experiences that an educational institution designs for its students to go through over a period of time.

A curry is a dish — or rather, a whole family of dishes — built around a richly spiced sauce or gravy. The spiced sauce is the heart of it. Almost everything else can change: the protein, the vegetables, the country it comes from, the thickness of the sauce.
A curse is something that brings harm, misfortune, or suffering. That "something" can be a word, a wish, a spell, or even a situation in life.
To curse someone or something means to direct something negative toward them using words — whether that is angry, offensive language, a wish for harm, or a magical spell.
Cursive is a style of handwriting in which the letters within a word are joined together in one continuous, flowing stroke — meaning your pen or pencil doesn't lift off the paper between letters.

Cursory means done quickly and without proper care or attention. When something is done in a cursory way, it is shallow and rushed — just enough to say it was done, but not enough to actually do it well.
Curt means being so short and brief in your words or manner that it comes across as cold, rude, or dismissive. It is not just about using few words.
To curtail something means to deliberately reduce it, limit it, or cut it short — making it smaller, briefer, or less than it was, or stopping it before it can fully run its course.
Curtailment means the act of reducing, restricting, or cutting something short — making it smaller, shorter, or less powerful than it was or than it was supposed to be.

Curtly means in a way that is very short, sharp, and unfriendly. When someone says something curtly, they use as few words as possible — not to be efficient or polite, but to show that they are annoyed, dismissive, impatient, or simply don't want to engage.

A curtsy is a formal gesture of respect and honor performed by a woman or girl. It is a way of physically showing reverence — that you recognize someone as important, superior, or worthy of deep honor — without using any words.
To curtsy is to perform a specific gesture of respect toward another person. You do this by bending both knees and lowering your body downward briefly, then rising back up.

When you call something curvaceous, you mean it has full, smooth, rounded curves that are visually appealing. The word almost always describes a woman's body — specifically one with noticeable, flowing curves at the bust, waist, and hips.

Curvature means the quality, state, or degree of being curved — in other words, how much something bends away from being perfectly straight (if it is a line or path) or perfectly flat (if it is a surface).
Cushy means something that is easy, comfortable, and pleasant — especially when it involves little effort, little stress, or more reward than you would normally expect for the work involved.
A cusp is a sharp, pointed tip — the kind you get when two curves or edges come together and meet at a single point. Think of the sharp tip of a crescent moon, or the pointed tip of a canine tooth.

"Cussed" means stubbornly difficult, contrary, and obstinate in a way that frustrates or annoys other people. A cussed person refuses to cooperate, refuses to budge from their position, and often seems to enjoy being troublesome.
The word custodial always comes from custody, which means the responsibility of keeping, watching over, protecting, or caring for someone or something.

A custodian is a person who has been given the responsibility to take care of, protect, and look after something — whether that's a physical place, a person, money, or even something as intangible as a cultural tradition.

Custody means the responsibility of keeping someone or something safe under your care and control. Think of it as a combination of two things: protection and authority. Whoever has custody has both the duty to protect and the power to control.
A custom is an established way of doing something that a group of people follows regularly, usually because it has been done that way for a long time.
When something is customary, it means it is the normal, expected thing to do based on a long-standing tradition or habit shared by a group of people.

"A cut above" means better than, superior to, or of a higher quality than others. When you say someone or something is "a cut above," you mean it stands out from the rest — it is noticeably higher in quality, skill, or class.
When you say two people are "cut from the same cloth," you mean they are very similar in character, personality, values, or behaviour — almost as if they were made from the same material.
To be "cut out for something" means to have the natural qualities, personality, and abilities that make you a perfect fit for a particular job, role, or activity.
"Cut short" means to end or stop something before it is finished — before it reaches its natural, expected, or deserved conclusion.

To "cut someone some slack" means to be less strict, less critical, or more forgiving toward someone — especially when they are going through a hard time, made a mistake, or are not performing at their best.
The idiom "cut to the bone" has two closely related meanings that share the same core idea: going to the most extreme depth possible.
When someone says "cut to the chase," they mean: skip everything unnecessary and get straight to the important point.
Cutaneous is an adjective with one core meaning: of, relating to, or affecting the skin. Any time you see the word "cutaneous," it is pointing to the skin in some way.
A cutlass is a type of sword — specifically, a short, heavy sword with a slightly curved blade that is sharp on one side only.
Cutlery means the set of tools — mainly knives, forks, and spoons — that you use to eat food at the table.

When you call something cutthroat, you mean it is so intensely and aggressively competitive that people are willing to harm, cheat, deceive, or destroy others just to come out on top. There is no mercy, no fairness, and often no ethics involved.
Something is cyclical when it follows a repeating pattern — a sequence of stages that plays out, comes full circle, and then starts all over again.

A cyclone is a large weather system in which winds rotate in a spiral pattern around a central point of low air pressure. Think of it like a giant whirlpool, but made of air instead of water — winds swirl inward and upward around a calm center.

A cygnet is a young swan — specifically, a swan in the early stage of its life, from the time it hatches as a chick until it grows into a fully mature adult swan. Think of it the way you'd use the word "puppy" for a young dog, or "kitten" for a young cat.
A cymbal is a percussion instrument — a round, thin, slightly curved metal disc that makes a ringing, crashing, or shimmering metallic sound when struck or clashed.
A cynic is a person who believes that people — at their core — are selfish, and that almost nothing anyone does is truly motivated by kindness, goodness, or genuine care for others.

Cynical means distrusting or doubting the good intentions of other people. A cynical person believes that people mostly act out of selfishness — even when they appear to be acting kindly, generously, or for noble reasons.
Cynicism is the belief that people are fundamentally selfish — that behind most human actions, especially those that appear good, generous, or noble, there is a hidden self-serving motive.
An ancient Greek philosophy which taught that virtue lies in living simply and naturally, rejecting wealth, power, and social convention. Today, cynicism means distrust of people's motives.
A cynophile is a person who loves dogs — deeply, genuinely, and enthusiastically.
A cynosure is a person or thing that powerfully attracts everyone's eyes, attention, and admiration — the one thing in the room (or in a situation) that everyone naturally focuses on.

The word czar always points to one central idea: a person with supreme, sweeping authority — someone who holds so much power over something that they are virtually unchallengeable in that domain. That is the thread that runs through every use of this word.

To dabble in something means to try it or do it occasionally and lightly, without going deep into it or becoming truly serious about it. Think of it as dipping your toe into a pool instead of jumping in and learning to swim.
Daft means silly, foolish, or lacking good sense. If someone calls an idea, a decision, or a person "daft," they are saying that it shows poor judgment or a clear absence of sensible thinking.

Daftly means in a silly, foolish, or slightly crazy way. When someone does something daftly, they are acting without good sense — behaving in a way that is absurd, unthinking, or just plain ridiculous.
A dagger is a short, pointed weapon that looks like a small sword. It has a sharp blade and a handle, and its defining purpose is stabbing — driving the pointed tip into something or someone.
A daguerreotype is a very early type of photograph, made on a shiny metal plate, produced using a specific process invented in the 1830s.
Dainty means delicately small, pretty, and refined. It describes something that is neat, fine, and elegant — but in a way that feels gentle and fragile, not bold or heavy.

A dainty is a small, choice, and particularly delicious thing to eat — something that feels special, refined, or a little bit luxurious. Think of it as a treat that stands apart from ordinary food because of how fine, delicate, or pleasing it is.

The simplest way to put it: A dais is a raised platform — a section of floor that has been built up higher than the rest of the room — where important or distinguished people stand or sit so that everyone else in the room can see and hear them clearly.
A dalliance is something that is casual, playful, and not serious — usually a romantic involvement, but sometimes a casual engagement with an activity or idea, or even a lazy wasting of time.

To dally means to treat something — whether it's time, a person, or an idea — in a casual, unhurried, and not-fully-serious way. There's always a sense of lightness, even carelessness, in the word. No urgency. No deep commitment.
Damage means harm or injury that makes something worse than it was before — reducing its quality, strength, beauty, usefulness, or value.
Damask is a rich, decorative fabric whose pattern is woven directly into the cloth itself — not printed on top, not embroidered, not dyed on later. The pattern is born from the weaving process.

As a noun, "a damn" means the tiniest, most negligible unit of care, concern, or value imaginable — essentially, the absolute minimum. It is almost always used to say that even this smallest possible amount is absent.
To damn with faint praise means to praise someone or something so weakly, so half-heartedly, that the so-called "praise" ends up harming them rather than helping them.
Damnation means being condemned — that is, being officially and finally judged as guilty or wicked, and sentenced to suffer as a result.
"Damned fortunate" means extremely lucky — and not just a little lucky, but strikingly, almost surprisingly lucky.

When something is described as damning, it means it is so powerfully negative or incriminating that it essentially proves someone is guilty, wrong, or deeply flawed — and there is almost nothing the person can say or do to argue against it.
"A damp squib" means something that was expected to be exciting, impressive, or successful, but turned out to be a disappointment.
When you dampen something, you add a small amount of water or moisture to it — enough to make it damp (slightly wet), but nowhere near soaking it.
A damper is something that reduces, controls, or stops something else — whether that's a mood, a flow of air, a sound, or physical movement.
Tiny flakes of dead skin shed by animals such as cats and dogs, the main cause of pet allergies. "To get your dander up" means to become angry.
To dandle means to gently bounce a baby or very young child on your knees or in your arms, in a loving and playful way.
A dandy is a man who is obsessively devoted to looking elegant, refined, and stylish — and who treats his own appearance almost like a work of art.
When something dangles, it hangs loosely and freely from a fixed point, with its lower end swinging or moving without anything supporting it from below.
Unpleasantly cold, damp, and stuffy, as in "a dank cellar."
When you call someone dapper, you are saying that they look very neat, well-groomed, and stylishly dressed — and that this look feels deliberate, polished, and put-together.

To dapple means to cover or mark a surface with scattered, irregular patches of light, shadow, or color — creating a broken, spotty pattern that is neither uniform nor random chaos, but something pleasantly in between.
Dappled describes a surface that has irregular patches or spots of different colors or shades scattered across it — most often a mix of light and dark areas sitting side by side.
Dare means to have the courage or boldness to do something — especially something that feels risky, frightening, or socially forbidden.
A daredevil is a person who deliberately does extremely dangerous things — things that most people would never attempt because the risk of serious injury or death is very real.
A dark horse is a person who is not well known or not expected to succeed, but who then surprises everyone by doing much better than anyone predicted — often winning or coming very close to winning.

To darn something means to repair a hole or a worn, thinning area in a piece of fabric — not by stitching the edges of the hole together like a wound, but by weaving new threads across the hole until the gap is completely filled in with a fresh patch of fabric.
A dart is a small, slim, pointed projectile — something designed to fly through the air and stick into a target. It is narrow, light, and has a sharp tip at the front.
"Dash" is a vivid, energetic word. It always carries a sense of speed, force, or sudden action. That quality runs through every meaning it has.

A dashiki is a type of garment — specifically, a loose, flowing top or shirt that covers the upper body from the shoulders down to roughly the hips or thighs. Think of it as a wide, comfortable tunic.
A dastard is a person who is both wicked and cowardly — but in a very specific, combined way. It doesn't just mean a simple coward, and it doesn't just mean an ordinary villain.
Dastardly means wicked and cowardly at the same time.
A database is an organized collection of data stored electronically so that it can be easily accessed, managed, and updated.
A datum is a single piece of information — one fact, one measurement, or one observation about something.

A daub is a rough, messy smear or blob of a thick, soft, or sticky substance — like mud, paint, or plaster — applied carelessly or clumsily onto a surface. Think of it as the opposite of a neat, precise stroke. It is untidy, uneven, and a little crude.
To daub means to spread or apply a thick, soft, or sticky substance onto a surface, usually in a rough, messy, or unskilled way.
To daunt someone means to make them feel afraid or discouraged — specifically in a way that shakes their confidence and makes them hesitant to attempt or continue something difficult.
Something is daunting when it seems so difficult, large, or demanding that it makes you feel discouraged, intimidated, or unsure whether you can handle it — even before you have fully tried.
Dauntless means impossible to frighten, discourage, or intimidate — no matter how dangerous, difficult, or overwhelming a situation gets.
A davit is a type of small, fixed crane — a mechanical arm — mounted on the edge of a ship, boat, or offshore structure.
To dawdle means to move, act, or do something much more slowly than necessary — wasting time when you should be going faster or finishing sooner.
Dawn is the moment — and the short period around it — when light first begins to appear in the sky, before the sun has actually risen above the horizon.
When something "dawns on someone," it means that a person suddenly realizes or understands something — often something they had not noticed, thought about, or figured out before.
"Day and age" means a period of time — specifically, the era or time in which we currently live.
When you daydream, your mind quietly slips away from what is happening around you — right now, in the real world — and begins to wander into an imaginary world of its own making.

"Days" is the plural form of the noun "day." To fully understand "days," you first need to understand what "day" means — and then see what changes (and what becomes possible) when we use it in plural.

A daze is a temporary state of mental fog and confusion in which a person cannot think clearly, respond normally, or fully grasp what is happening around them. Their mind is working, but slowly and poorly — as if something has scrambled it.

Dazzle means to overwhelm someone's senses — either their eyes with extreme brightness, or their mind with something breathtakingly impressive — to the point where they are momentarily stunned and cannot think or react normally.
When something is dazzling, it is so intensely bright, beautiful, or impressive that it momentarily overwhelms you — your eyes, your mind, or both. It stops you. It makes you stare.
De facto describes something that is true or real in practice, even if it is not officially declared, legally recognized, or formally established.
"De facto" means in reality, in practice, or as a matter of fact — describing what is actually true or what actually happens, even when it isn't officially, legally, or formally declared.
De jure describes something that is true, valid, or recognized according to law, official rules, or formal standards — on paper, by right, as things are supposed to be.
Required by fashion, custom, or etiquette, so that not doing it would seem improper, as in "a black tie is de rigueur at the gala."

To de-escalate means to intentionally reduce the intensity, tension, or severity of a situation — to bring something that is growing more serious, aggressive, or dangerous back down to a calmer, more manageable level.
A deacon is a person who holds a formal role of service and leadership within a Christian church.
Dead reckoning means figuring out where you are — or what is likely true — by using what you already know, rather than having direct proof or a clear view of the answer.

If someone is a dead ringer for another person, it means they look so incredibly similar to that person that you could almost mistake one for the other. The resemblance is not just "a little similar" — it's striking, almost unbelievable.
A deadbolt is a type of lock — specifically, a locking mechanism built into a door that uses a solid, thick metal bar (called the bolt) to keep the door firmly shut.
To deaden something means to make it become more like "dead" — to strip away its strength, sharpness, or intensity until it becomes weak, numb, or dull.
"Deadening" describes anything that makes a sensation, feeling, experience, or sound become numb, dull, muted, or hollow — like a flame slowly being smothered rather than blown out instantly.

A deadlock is a situation where everything has come to a complete standstill because two sides — whether they are people, groups, machines, or processes — are each blocking the other, and neither can move forward.

If someone is deadpan, they say or do something — often something funny, surprising, or absurd — while keeping their face and voice completely blank, flat, and serious. No smile. No raised eyebrow. No change in tone. Nothing.
Deafening means so extremely loud that it overwhelms your senses — a sound so powerful that it could temporarily hurt your ability to hear, or at least feels that way.

The verb deal has one unifying idea underneath all its uses: directing or giving something toward someone or something. That core idea stretches into several distinct meanings depending on context. Here is every important one.
A dearth means a serious and noticeable scarcity of something — a shortage so significant that it creates a real problem, or is at least worth pointing out.
A debacle is a sudden, total, and deeply embarrassing collapse or failure — one that is chaotic, very public, and often shocks the people involved and those watching.
To debar someone means to officially prevent them from doing something, going somewhere, or being part of something — usually by a rule, authority, or formal decision.
To debase something means to lower its quality, value, or dignity — to make it worse, cheaper, or less respectable than it originally was or should be.
Debasement means the act of lowering something's value, quality, or dignity — making it worse, cheaper, or less worthy than it originally was.

When something is debatable, it means it is open to argument — there is no clear, universally agreed-upon answer, and reasonable people can disagree about it. It sits in a gray zone: not definitely true, not definitely false.
When you debate something, you talk about it seriously with someone who holds a different view — each side presenting reasons and arguments to support their position.
A debauch is a specific event or occasion — a session, episode, or bout — in which a person or group throws aside all restraint and plunges into wild, excessive indulgence in physical pleasures.
To debauch someone means to corrupt them morally by drawing them into a life of excessive, sinful pleasure — particularly involving heavy drinking, sexual indulgence, and wild, reckless behavior.
Given over to excessive drinking, sex, and other physical pleasures, to the point of moral corruption.

Debauchery refers to excessive, wild, and morally unrestrained indulgence in pleasures — particularly those involving alcohol, drugs, sex, and other sensory gratifications — taken to an irresponsible, shameless, or harmful extreme.
A debenture is a document (a formal certificate) that represents a loan given to a company or government by an investor.
To debilitate something or someone means to weaken them so seriously that they can no longer function properly or at their normal capacity. It is not ordinary, mild weakening.

Something is debilitating if it makes a person severely and significantly weaker — in body, mind, or ability — to the point where living normally, functioning, or doing everyday things becomes very hard or even impossible.
When you call someone debonair, you are saying they are a special combination of three things at once: charming, confident, and effortlessly stylish. The key word here is effortlessly.
To debouch means to emerge from a narrow or confined space into a wider, open space.

To debrief someone means to question them carefully and systematically after they have completed a task, mission, or important event — in order to gather information about what happened, what they saw, what decisions were made, and what the results were.

A debriefing is a formal meeting or structured conversation that takes place after a significant event, task, mission, or experience — in which a person (or group) is carefully questioned or asked to report on what they saw, did, experienced, decided, and observed.
Debris refers to the scattered pieces, fragments, and remnants left behind after something has been broken, destroyed, or worn down.
A debt is something you owe to someone else — because they gave you something first, with the understanding (or agreement) that you will give it back or return the favour later.

To debunk something means to prove that a widely believed claim, story, or idea is false, misleading, or exaggerated — and to show this clearly, using facts, evidence, or reasoning, so that people can see it for what it really is.
A debut is the first time a person, thing, or group appears publicly — especially in a particular role, field, or capacity — in a way that is noticed, received, or witnessed by others.

A debutante is a young woman, usually from a wealthy or upper-class family, who is formally and publicly introduced to "society" for the very first time at a special event — most commonly a grand ball or ceremony. This event is called her debut.

Decadence is the state of falling into excessive self-indulgence, luxury, and pleasure-seeking — especially when this represents a decline from a previously higher standard of discipline, morality, or strength.
Decadent means excessively and self-indulgently devoted to pleasure and luxury, often in a way that signals moral weakness, decline, or a loss of discipline.
To decamp means to leave a place suddenly and often secretly, especially to avoid trouble, responsibility, or being caught. Think of it as slipping away rather than walking away openly.

To decant means to carefully pour a liquid from one container into another, usually slowly and gently, for a specific purpose — either to separate the liquid from unwanted solid bits that have sunk to the bottom, or simply to transfer the liquid into a more suitable container.

A decanter is a special container — almost always made of glass or crystal — used to hold and serve drinks like wine, whisky, brandy, or other spirits. It is not the bottle the drink originally came in.

To decapitate something or someone means to cut off its head. When the head is separated from the body — whether by a blade, a sharp tool, or any other means — that act is called decapitation, and the one performing it is said to decapitate.

Deceit is the act of deliberately making someone believe something that is not true. It is the practice of hiding the truth, creating false impressions, or tricking someone — usually to gain an advantage or to avoid a consequence.

Deceitful describes someone or something that deliberately creates a false impression in another person's mind. The key word here is deliberately — deceitful is never about accidents or innocent mistakes. It always involves a choice to mislead.
To deceive someone means to deliberately make them believe something that is not true.
To decelerate means to become slower, or to cause something to become slower. It is the direct opposite of accelerate (to speed up).
Decency is the quality of behaving in a way that is morally acceptable, respectful, and appropriate — toward yourself, toward others, and in line with what a society considers right and proper.

"Decent" is a word that broadly signals approval — that something or someone meets an acceptable, appropriate, or good standard. It is not the highest praise, and it is not criticism. It sits comfortably in positive territory.
Deception is the act of causing someone to believe something that is not true — knowingly and on purpose.

Something is deceptive when it creates a false impression — when it makes you believe something that is not actually true or accurate. The gap between what something appears to be and what it actually is — that gap is what makes it deceptive.

A decibel (written as dB) is a unit that measures the level or intensity of something — most commonly sound — using a special mathematical scale that compresses enormous ranges of values into manageable numbers.
Clearly and without any doubt, as in "the weather was decidedly cold." It can also mean firmly and decisively.

Deciduous describes something that sheds or falls off naturally at a specific time — not by accident, not because it's damaged, but as a normal, predictable part of its life cycle. Think of it as the opposite of permanent.
To decimate something means to destroy or damage a very large part of it — so much so that what remains is a shadow of what it once was.

To decipher something means to figure out what it says or means — but specifically when it is difficult, unclear, coded, or hard to understand. The key idea baked into this word is that the thing you're looking at is not immediately obvious.
Decisive means settling something firmly and clearly, with no room left for doubt or going back.

"Deck out" is a phrasal verb that means to decorate, adorn, or dress something (or someone) in an impressive, elaborate, or festive way. The idea is making something look special, eye-catching, or celebratory — going beyond the ordinary and adding flair.
To declaim means to speak in a loud, passionate, and dramatic way — the kind of speaking that feels like a performance or a powerful public speech, not an ordinary conversation.

A declamation is a formal speech delivered with theatrical power — one where how it is spoken matters just as much as what is being said. It is not everyday talking, not casual conversation, and not a simple explanation.
To declare something means to say it clearly, firmly, and with full intention — often so that others know it officially or as a matter of record.
In grammar, the set of different forms a noun, pronoun, or adjective takes depending on its role in a sentence, like "he," "him," and "his." It can also mean a gradual decline.

When you decline something, you say no to it — but in a respectful, gentle way. This is the key detail: the word carries a tone of politeness or formality. You're not slamming the door; you're closing it softly.
A declivity is a downward slope — a stretch of ground, surface, or terrain that tilts and descends from a higher point to a lower point.
To declutter means to remove things that are unnecessary, unused, or unwanted from a space or a system, so that only what you truly need or value remains.
To decode something means to take something that is hidden, scrambled, encrypted, or confusing — and convert it back into a form that is clear and understandable.

To decommission something means to officially and permanently take it out of active service. It is the formal process of retiring something that was previously in use — ending its working life in an organized, deliberate way.
Decomposition means the process of breaking something down into smaller, simpler parts.
To relax after a period of stress or pressure. Literally, it means to reduce the pressure on something, or for a diver to return slowly to normal air pressure.

To deconstruct something means to carefully take it apart — not physically, but mentally — in order to examine its individual pieces, understand how those pieces work, and question the assumptions or ideas that hold them together.

To decorate means to add things to something in order to make it look more attractive, beautiful, or festive. The key idea is simple: you take something that already exists, and you add to its surface or surroundings to improve how it looks.

When something is described as decorated, it means that extra things have been deliberately added to it — such as colors, patterns, designs, or objects — to make it look more attractive, beautiful, festive, or interesting.
Decorous describes behavior, speech, appearance, or conduct that is proper, dignified, and appropriate for the situation at hand.

Decorum means behaving in a way that is proper, dignified, and appropriate for a given situation. It is about matching your actions, words, and manner to what is considered respectful and socially acceptable in that moment.

To decouple two things means to remove the link between them so they no longer depend on each other, affect each other, or move together. Before decoupling, the two things were connected — what happened to one would influence the other.
A decoy is something — a person, an animal, or an object — that is deliberately made to look real or important in order to fool someone.

A decree is an official, formal order or decision made by someone in a position of high authority — such as a ruler, a government, or a court — that carries the force of law and must be obeyed by those it applies to.

To decree something means to officially and authoritatively declare that something must happen, must be done, or must be accepted as true — and that declaration carries the full force of the power of whoever is making it.

Decrepit describes something — or someone — that has become so worn out, weakened, and broken down over time that it is in a visibly poor, sad, and deteriorated state. Think of it as the result of age and neglect combining to do serious damage.

Decrepitude means the state of being so worn down, weakened, and broken — usually from old age or prolonged use — that functioning properly is no longer really possible. It is not just "being old" or "being a little tired."
To decry something means to openly and publicly criticize it in strong terms, usually to make others aware that you believe it is wrong, harmful, unfair, or bad.

To dedicate means to give something — your time, effort, energy, work, or even a physical space — fully and with genuine commitment to a particular person, purpose, or cause. The key word here is fully.
