When you call someone or something dedicated, you mean they are fully and consistently committed to a particular purpose, cause, or activity — giving it serious time, effort, and focus, without easily giving up.

Dedication means giving yourself fully to something — your time, energy, focus, and effort — because you deeply care about it. It isn't a quick burst of enthusiasm. It is a sustained, long-term commitment that doesn't fade easily when things get hard.

To deduce means to reach a conclusion by thinking logically from facts, evidence, or clues you already know. The conclusion you arrive at isn't guessed or invented — it follows naturally and necessarily from what you already have in front of you.
Something is deducible when it can be logically worked out from information you already have.
An amount taken away from a total, such as money subtracted from pay; or reaching a conclusion by logical reasoning from known facts.
Deductive is an adjective that describes anything related to deduction — a specific kind of reasoning where you start from general truths and work your way down to a specific, necessary conclusion.
Deductive reasoning is the process of reaching a conclusion that must be true, because it logically follows from things you already know to be true.

A deed is something that is actually done — a real, concrete action carried out in the world. It is not a thought, not a wish, not a plan, and not a promise. A deed has already happened. It exists in reality.
To deem something means to consider it, judge it, or conclude that it is a certain way.
Deep means going far from the surface toward the inside or the bottom. This is the single idea that connects almost every use of this word.
A deepfake is a fake photo, video, or audio recording — made using artificial intelligence (AI) — that looks and sounds so realistic that most people cannot tell it is fake.

To deface something means to deliberately damage or spoil the way it looks — especially its surface or outward appearance — by marking, scratching, writing, painting, or otherwise messing it up in a way that makes it look ugly, damaged, or difficult to read and recognize.
To defalcate means to secretly steal or misuse money that was entrusted to you by someone else. It is not ordinary theft. The person who defalcates is not a stranger who broke in and took something.
Defamation is the act of making a false statement about a person — and communicating it to others — in a way that damages that person's reputation.

Something is defamatory when it damages a person's reputation by making a false statement about them that is presented as a fact — not an opinion — and that statement is shared with at least one other person.

To defame someone means to make false statements about them — to other people — that damage how others think of that person. In short, you are harming someone's reputation by spreading lies about them.
What happens or is chosen automatically when no other choice is made, as in "the default settings." It is also a failure to pay a debt or meet an obligation, as in "a loan default."

Defeatism is an attitude — a way of thinking — in which a person accepts that they are going to fail or lose, often before the outcome has even been decided, and sometimes without putting up a real fight.
A defeatist is a person who believes, often before even really trying, that failure is unavoidable — so there's no point in trying hard or fighting back.
A defect is a flaw, imperfection, or problem in something — a point where a person, object, system, or plan falls short of what it is supposed to be.

This combination is what makes "defect" different from simply quitting or leaving. Quitting a job is neutral. Defecting is a betrayal of loyalty. You were sworn to one side — and now you're on the other.

Defection is the act of abandoning a group, country, organization, or cause that you previously belonged to — especially to join the opposing side, or to simply walk away from your loyalty altogether.
Something is defective when it has a flaw, fault, or imperfection that prevents it from working correctly or being what it is supposed to be.
A defector is a person who abandons the country, organization, political party, or group they originally belonged to — and goes over to the opposing or rival side.

To defenestrate someone means to throw them out of a window. The window is the crucial detail. You cannot "defenestrate" someone through a door, off a rooftop, or out of any other opening. The word is window-specific.
Defense means protecting something or someone from harm, attack, or damage.

When "defensive" is used as a noun, it almost always appears in one fixed phrase: "the defensive." You will rarely see it standing alone — it lives inside expressions like "on the defensive," "put someone on the defensive," or "go on the defensive."
When you defer something, you deliberately delay it. You're not cancelling it — you're pushing it forward on the timeline. Think of it as pressing a "pause" button on something.

Deference means respectfully yielding to someone else's judgment, wishes, or authority — particularly because you recognize that they know more, have more experience, or hold a position worthy of respect.
Deferential means showing respectful submission to someone else — their authority, their judgment, their experience, or their status.
Defiance is the bold, open refusal to obey someone or something that has power or authority over you — even when you know there could be consequences for doing so.
When someone is defiant, they openly refuse to obey, submit to, or be controlled by a person, rule, or force — and they do it boldly, without hiding or backing down.

Defiantly means doing something in a way that openly refuses to obey, submit, or back down — especially when facing authority, rules, pressure, or opposition. It describes the manner of doing something: boldly, stubbornly, and without fear of consequences.

A defibrillator is a medical device that delivers a carefully controlled electric shock to the heart in order to restore its normal, healthy rhythm when it has started beating in a dangerous, chaotic way.
A deficiency is a situation where there is not enough of something that is needed or expected. It's a gap — between what exists and what should exist.
Deficient means not having enough of something that is needed, expected, or required. It describes a shortfall — a gap between what exists and what should exist.
A deficit is a shortfall — a situation where you have less of something than you need, or where what comes in is less than what goes out.
To defile something means to make it impure, unclean, or corrupt — especially something that was previously pure, sacred, respected, or beautiful.

When something is definitive, it means it is so complete, thorough, and authoritative that it settles the matter for good — there is no need to look further, ask again, or revisit it. It is the final word on something.

To understand "deflate," start with its opposite: inflate means to fill something up with air until it expands. Deflate is the reverse — it means to let air (or gas) out of something so it shrinks, goes flat, or collapses.

Deflect means to make something change direction — to push, steer, or turn it away from the path it was originally on. The key idea is this: something is moving toward a point, and something else steps in and redirects it. It doesn't stop.
Deflection means the act of turning something away from its original path or direction — or the result of that turning. It can also refer to how much something has been turned.
To defoliate means to strip a plant, tree, or an area of vegetation of its leaves — either partially or completely. The result is a plant left bare, without its foliage.

Deforestation is the large-scale removal or destruction of forests — permanently or for a very long time — usually caused by human activity, so that the land can be used for something else or the trees can be sold.

A deformity is an abnormal shape, structure, or form — something that has been twisted, bent, distorted, or otherwise formed differently from what is considered normal. Think of it as something that should have a certain shape but doesn't.
To defraud someone means to deliberately trick or deceive them in order to take something valuable away from them — usually money, property, or a legal right they are entitled to.
To defray means to pay for a cost or expense, or to provide money that covers it — either fully or partially.

To defrock someone means to officially strip a member of the clergy — a priest, minister, monk, or similar religious figure — of their religious status, title, and the right to carry out their religious duties.
Deft means skillful, quick, and precise in the way you do something — and doing it with such ease that it almost looks effortless.
Deftly means doing something with skill, quickness, and ease — all at the same time.

When you describe something as defunct, you mean it no longer exists, operates, or functions — and it never will again. It is completely finished. Whatever it once was or once did, it is no longer. The thing is gone for good.
To defuse something means to remove or reduce the danger from it — to make a risky, explosive, or tense situation safe before it causes harm. Think of it as "taking the danger out of something."

To defy something or someone means to openly and boldly refuse to obey, follow, or be limited by them — even when you know you are expected to, or when there is a real force or authority pushing you to comply.
"Degenerate" means having fallen from a higher, better, or more complete state into a lower, worse, or simpler one.
Calling someone "a degenerate" means labeling them as a person who has fallen below the standard of decent, moral, or civilized behavior that society expects of a human being.
To degenerate means to gradually become worse than what it was before — to fall from a higher, better, or more orderly state into a lower, worse, or more chaotic one.
Degeneration means the process by which something gradually declines from a better, healthier, or more capable state into a worse, weaker, or more damaged one.

Degenerative describes something that involves or causes a slow, continuous, and typically irreversible breakdown — where something that once worked properly gradually loses its structure, function, or quality over time, and the body or system cannot repair it fast enough to stop the decline.

Degradation means the process of something — or someone — becoming worse, lower, or lesser than it was before. Think of it as a downward movement: from better to worse, from higher to lower, from stronger to weaker, from dignified to shameful.

Degrade means to make something or someone lower, worse, or lesser than what they were. Every use of this word — no matter the context — involves a downward movement: in dignity, in quality, in rank, or in physical condition.
Degraded describes something (or someone) that has been brought to a lower, worse, or lesser state than it was before — or lower than what is normal, expected, or respectful.
Degrading describes something that attacks a person's dignity — their sense of self-worth, their value as a human being — by treating them as lesser, inferior, or unworthy of basic respect.
To dehumanize someone means to treat them — or think of them — as if they are not fully human.
To dehydrate means to remove water from something, or to lose water from something.
Dehydrated means having lost too much water, or having had water removed from it.
Dehydration is the condition of not having enough water in your body (or in something else) to function properly.
Deification means the act of making someone or something into a god, or treating them as if they were a god.
To deify someone or something means to treat them as a god — to give them the kind of extreme worship, reverence, and unquestioning devotion that humans normally reserve only for a divine being.
To do something you consider beneath your dignity or status — usually reluctantly, and as if doing it is a great favor to the person receiving it.

A deity is a god or goddess — a supernatural, divine being that is believed to have powers far beyond those of any human or natural creature, and that is typically worshipped by people as a higher power.

Dejected means feeling sad, low-spirited, and without hope or energy — especially because something went wrong or didn't turn out the way you wanted. When someone is dejected, their spirit has been knocked down. They feel defeated inside.
Dejection is a feeling of deep sadness and low spirits — the kind that comes over you when something has gone wrong, disappointed you, or knocked the energy and hope right out of you.
A quantum experiment suggesting that a choice made after a particle has been detected can seem to affect how it behaved earlier — whether it acted like a wave or a particle.

Delectable means so deeply pleasing to your senses that it fills you with delight and satisfaction. When something is delectable, it doesn't just feel good — it feels wonderfully, almost irresistibly good.
Delectation means a feeling of great pleasure and delight — but not just any pleasure. It's the deep, savored, almost luxurious kind of enjoyment you feel when you are truly relishing something.
A delegate is a person who has been chosen by a group to represent them — to go somewhere, speak on their behalf, vote in their name, or carry out a specific task for them.
Delegation is the act of giving someone else the authority or responsibility to do something on your behalf.
To delete something means to deliberately remove it so that it no longer exists in its current place. It is always a conscious, targeted act — you choose a specific thing and make it disappear.
Deleterious means causing harm or damage. When something is deleterious, it hurts, damages, or destroys something — whether that's a person's health, a relationship, an environment, or a system.
Done on purpose, as in "a deliberate lie." It can also mean slow, careful, and unhurried, as in "deliberate steps."
When you deliberate, you think about something carefully, slowly, and seriously before making a decision.
Deliberately means doing something on purpose, with full awareness and conscious choice — not by accident, not by impulse, not carelessly.

Deliberation means the process of thinking carefully, seriously, and thoroughly about something — especially before making a decision or taking action. It is slow, purposeful thinking. Not rushed. Not careless.

The word delicacy has two broad types of meaning: one refers to a thing (a special food), and the others refer to a quality (how something looks, how fragile it is, how a situation must be handled, or how a person behaves).
"Delicate" describes something that is fine, subtle, or fragile — and almost always, it carries an underlying message: handle this with care.

When someone is delighted, they are feeling great joy and pleasure — a warm, genuine happiness that usually comes as a reaction to something good that happened, something someone said, or something they received or experienced.
When you delimit something, you fix or establish its boundaries — you draw a clear line that marks precisely where something begins and where it ends.
Delimitation means the act of establishing the boundaries or limits of something — deciding precisely where something begins and ends, what falls inside it, and what falls outside it.

To delineate something means to make it completely clear and precise — by carefully marking out its exact shape, limits, or features — so that no confusion remains about what it is, where it begins, and where it ends.
Delineated means clearly and precisely outlined or defined — in a way that leaves no blurriness, no overlap, and no confusion about where something begins and where it ends.
Delineation means the act of describing, defining, or marking out something with great clarity and precision.
A delinquent is a person — almost always a young person — who repeatedly behaves in ways that break rules, laws, or the basic standards of acceptable conduct in society.
When you call something deliquescent, you mean: it absorbs moisture from the surrounding air so aggressively that it eventually liquefies completely — melting into the very water it pulled in.
"Delirious" describes a state where a person's mind is no longer functioning in its normal, clear, controlled way — it has been overwhelmed by something.
Delirium is a sudden, serious state of mental confusion. When a person is in delirium, their mind temporarily stops working the way it normally does.

Deliverance means the act of being rescued or freed from something harmful, dangerous, or oppressive. It is the moment — or the process — of being saved from a situation that felt inescapable, threatening, or crushing.

"Delt" is an informal, shortened form of "deltoid" — specifically the deltoid muscle, which is the large, prominent muscle that wraps around the top of your shoulder and gives it its rounded, dome-like shape.

A flat, triangular area of land where a river splits into many channels before reaching the sea, as in "the Nile delta." It is also the fourth letter of the Greek alphabet (Δ), and in maths and science it stands for a change in a quantity.
When you describe something as deltoid, you mean it is roughly triangular in shape — specifically, shaped like the uppercase Greek letter delta, which looks like this: Δ.
When someone says "the deltoid", they almost always mean a specific muscle in the human body.

To delude someone means to make them believe something that is not true — and to make that false belief feel completely real to them. The person who has been deluded doesn't just make a small mistake or a quick error.
If someone is deluded, they believe something that is not true — and they believe it firmly and confidently, without realising they are wrong.
A deluge is an enormous, overwhelming flood of water — so massive and sudden that it causes serious destruction and is very difficult to escape or control.
To deluge someone means to overwhelm them with an extremely large amount of something — so much, all at once, that they struggle to cope with it.

A delusion is a false belief that a person holds with absolute, unshakeable conviction — even when clear, solid evidence proves that it is wrong, and even when no one else around them shares that belief.

When we call someone delusional, we mean they believe something that is clearly false or out of touch with reality — and they hold that belief firmly and unshakeably, even when the truth is staring them in the face.
When something is delusive, it creates a false belief in your mind — it makes you think something is real, true, or good when it actually isn't. The key is that the falsehood feels convincing.
Misleading and based on a false belief; creating a delusion, as in "delusory hopes."
Something is deluxe when it is of a higher, more luxurious, or superior grade than the ordinary or standard version of the same thing.

To delve means to search deeply and thoroughly into something — to go well beneath the surface of a topic, subject, question, or matter in order to understand it fully or discover something meaningful.
A demagogue is a leader — usually a political one — who gains power and popularity not through honest reasoning, good policies, or genuine solutions, but by manipulating people's emotions.

Demagoguery is when a politician (or any leader) tries to gain power and influence over people not by telling them the truth or making sound arguments, but by manipulating their emotions — especially their fears, anger, and prejudices.
A demand is a strong, firm claim for something — stated not as a polite question, but as something expected to be fulfilled. The person making it isn't hoping for a yes; they're insisting on one.

To demand something means to ask for it in a firm, forceful, non-negotiable way — as if you have the right to receive it and you expect it to happen without question. It is much stronger than simply "asking."
To demarcate something means to clearly establish and mark where one thing ends and another begins — to draw a firm, deliberate line that separates two things from each other.
Demarcation means the action of drawing a clear line to separate two things, or the line itself that separates them.
To demean someone means to treat them in a way that lowers their dignity, worth, or self-respect — to make them feel small, inferior, or unworthy of basic respect.

If something is demeaning, it lowers a person's dignity — it makes them feel small, worthless, disrespected, or less than human. It strips away a person's sense of self-worth, either in their own eyes, in the eyes of others, or both.

Demeanor is the overall impression a person gives to others through the way they outwardly carry themselves — their behavior, body language, facial expressions, tone of voice, and general attitude, all taken together.

Demented means having a severely disturbed or broken-down mind — a mind that has lost its grip on reality, reason, or normal functioning. Think of it as a mind that is no longer working the way a healthy mind should.

Dementia is not the name of a single disease. It is an umbrella term — a broad, general label — used to describe a serious, ongoing decline in a person's mental abilities that is severe enough to interfere with their daily life.
A fault, flaw, or disadvantage. At school or work, a demerit is a mark given against someone for bad behaviour.
Demesne means land that someone holds and uses directly for themselves — not land they rent out or hand over to others, but land they personally possess, control, and occupy as their own.

To demilitarize something means to remove all military presence, weapons, soldiers, and war-related equipment from a place or an organization — essentially stripping it of its military character and returning it to a peaceful, non-military state.

"Demise" means the death of a person, but it's not a word you'd use in casual conversation. It's formal, serious, and carries a quiet gravity to it. You'd find it in news reports, literature, speeches, and formal writing — not in a text to a friend.

A demo is a short form of the word demonstration. A demo is something — a presentation, a recording, a version of a product — that exists to show what something is like, without being the final or complete thing itself.

Democracy is a system of government in which the people of a country hold political power — meaning the authority to make decisions about how the country is governed ultimately belongs to the citizens, not to a single ruler or a small group.
When something is described as demographic, it relates to the measurable characteristics that define or describe groups of people within a population.
A demographic is a specific group of people who share one or more common characteristics.
Demography is the scientific study of human populations — who they are, how large they are, how they are structured, where they live, and how they change over time.

To demolish something means to destroy it completely and deliberately, so that nothing of it remains standing or intact. The single most important idea locked inside this word is totality — when something is demolished, it is not just damaged or weakened.

Demolition is the act of deliberately and intentionally tearing down, destroying, or breaking apart a structure — most commonly a building, a bridge, a wall, or any large physical thing that was built by people.
A demon is an evil supernatural being — a powerful, non-physical creature that exists in the unseen, spiritual world and that uses its power to harm, corrupt, deceive, or destroy humans.

A demoniac is a person believed to be possessed by a demon or evil spirit — meaning a malevolent supernatural being has taken up residence inside that person's body and is controlling or tormenting them from within.
The word demoniacal describes something that is either deeply, savagely evil — like a demon — or wildly frenzied and out of control, as if a demon has taken over.

To demonize someone or something means to portray them as evil, dangerous, or wicked — especially in a way that is unfair, exaggerated, or dishonest — in order to make others fear, hate, or distrust them.
Something is demonstrable if it can be shown to be true through clear evidence, facts, or proof — not just claimed, but actually proven and shown to others.
Demonstrate means to show something clearly, deliberately, and convincingly — in a way that makes it easy for others to see, understand, or believe.
A demonstration is the act of making something visible or clear to others — not by just saying it, but by actually showing it, doing it, or proving it.
The word demonstrator refers to a person or thing that demonstrates — meaning someone or something that actively shows, proves, or displays something to others.

To demoralize someone means to weaken their spirit, confidence, and will to keep going. It's not just making someone feel sad — it specifically attacks their inner drive, their belief that they can succeed, and their desire to keep trying.

Demoralizing is an adjective that describes anything — a situation, an experience, a person's behavior, an event — that causes someone to lose their confidence, motivation, hope, or will to keep going.
To demote someone or something means to move them to a lower rank, position, level, or status than the one they currently hold.
Demotic is an adjective that means of, belonging to, or characteristic of ordinary, everyday people — as opposed to a privileged, educated, or elite class.
To demur means to raise a mild objection, express hesitation, or show reluctance about something — usually in a restrained, polite way. When you demur, you are gently pushing back.

Demure describes a person who is quietly modest, gently restrained, and deliberately understated in the way they carry themselves. A demure person doesn't seek the spotlight, doesn't speak loudly or boldly, and doesn't show off.
To demystify something means to take away its confusion, complexity, or sense of mystery so that it becomes clear and easy to understand.
A den is a small, enclosed, private, and often hidden space — a tucked-away place that belongs to someone (or something) in a very personal way.

Denial means the act of refusing to accept, admit, or agree to something. Think of it as saying "no" — but not just to a request. You can deny a fact, a truth, a request, or even your own painful feelings.

To denigrate someone or something means to speak about them in a way that makes them seem less important, less worthy, or less valuable than they truly are — almost always unfairly and often with the clear intention of damaging how others see them.
Denigration is the act of attacking, belittling, or speaking negatively about someone or something — usually unfairly — in order to make them appear worthless, lesser, or bad in the eyes of others.

A denizen is an inhabitant — a person, animal, or plant that lives in, belongs to, or is closely associated with a particular place. Think of it as a slightly elevated, more expressive way of saying "a resident of" or "a creature of" somewhere.
A denomination is a named category or division within a larger group or system.

Denotation is the literal, direct, official meaning of a word — the plain, factual definition that points to something in the real world, completely stripped of emotion, personal feeling, or cultural suggestion.

To denote something means to directly stand for, represent, or indicate something else. When X denotes Y, X is a clear, direct pointer to Y — no guessing, no reading between the lines. It's a firm, explicit connection.
Denouement is the final resolution of something complex — the moment when everything that was tangled, tense, or uncertain finally gets sorted out, explained, and settled.
To denounce someone or something means to publicly declare that they are wrong, bad, harmful, or morally unacceptable — and to do so with force and conviction.
Closely packed together, as in "a dense forest" or "dense fog." Of writing, hard to understand because it contains a lot of complex ideas. Informally, of a person, slow to understand.
Density is the measure of how much "stuff" is packed into a given space.
To dent something means to push in a part of its surface so that it creates a small hollow or depression — usually by hitting, pressing, or knocking it with force.

Dentine is the hard, yellowish tissue that forms the main bulk — the core body — of a tooth. Think of a tooth as a layered structure: dentine is not on the outside, and not the very innermost part either.
To denude something means to strip it completely bare — to remove whatever naturally covers, protects, or clothes it, leaving it naked and exposed.
Denunciation means the act of publicly and strongly declaring that someone or something is wrong, bad, dangerous, or guilty.

Deny means to push something away — either by saying it isn't true, or by refusing to let someone have it. Think of it as a word that involves rejection or refusal, but the kind of rejection depends on the situation.
The moral view that some actions are right or wrong in themselves, regardless of their consequences — so that people have a duty to follow certain rules.

The word departure is rooted in the idea of leaving. Whenever someone or something leaves — a place, a situation, a way of doing things — that act of leaving is called a departure. But the word stretches well beyond just physically leaving a location.

To "depend" means that one thing needs, is controlled by, or can be trusted because of another thing. There is a connection between two things — one of them is not complete, safe, or functioning on its own without the other.
Reliable and trustworthy; able to be counted on, as in "a dependable friend" or "a dependable car."
To depict something means to represent it — to show what it looks like, or to describe it so clearly that a picture forms in someone's mind.

A depiction is a representation of something — a person, place, object, event, or idea — created through any expressive medium. That medium could be a painting, a drawing, a photograph, a film, a piece of writing, a sculpture, or even a verbal description.
To depilate means to remove hair from the body (or from any surface).

To deplete something means to use it up, drain it, or reduce it — often to a dangerously low level or until almost nothing is left. Think of a water tank with a slow leak. Drop by drop, the water level falls.
Deplorable means so shockingly bad or wrong that it deserves strong condemnation and causes a deep sense of disgust, sadness, or moral outrage.
To deplore something means to feel and express a strong sense of disapproval combined with sadness or regret about it.
To deploy something means to take it from a state of readiness and put it into active use — in a purposeful, strategic way — so it can do its job effectively.
Deployment means the act of putting something into active use in the real world, in an organized and intentional way, so that it can start doing its job.
To depopulate a place means to sharply reduce the number of people living there, often to the point where it becomes nearly empty or completely abandoned.
To deport someone means for a government to officially and forcibly remove a foreign national (a non-citizen) from its country and send them back to their home country or another country.

Deportation is the official act by which a government forcibly removes a foreign national — a person who is not a citizen of that country — from its territory and sends them back to their home country or another country willing to accept them.
Deportment means the way a person carries themselves — both physically and behaviorally — especially in front of others.
To depose someone means to forcefully or officially remove a ruler, monarch, or leader from their position of power — usually against that person's will.
To put something down somewhere, or to leave it there, as in "the river deposits silt." It also means to put money into a bank account, or to pay part of the price of something in advance.
A formal statement given under oath, to be used as evidence in court. It can also mean the removal of a ruler from power, or the laying down of sand and soil by water or wind.

A depot is a place where things are stored, kept, or managed in an organized way — and from which those things are distributed or dispatched when needed. Think of it as a base of operations for something.

Depraved means morally corrupt in a deep, extreme, and fundamental way. It describes a person, behavior, desire, or mindset that has gone far beyond ordinary wrongdoing — something that most decent people would find shocking, disgusting, or monstrous.
Depravity means a state of being deeply, profoundly morally corrupt or wicked.
To deprecate something means to express that you disapprove of it, consider it inferior, or want people to stop using it.
Deprecating means expressing disapproval, criticism, or a low opinion of something or someone — in a way that belittles or diminishes them.

Deprecation is the act of expressing that something is no longer approved of, no longer recommended, or no longer worthy of use — and signaling that it should be set aside in favour of something better.
Deprecatory means expressing disapproval or a low opinion of something, or showing that you are apologetic, humble, and trying to seem harmless.
To lose value over time, as in "new cars depreciate quickly." In formal use, it can also mean to belittle or dismiss something as unimportant.

Depreciation means the loss in value of something over time. That "something" is typically a physical object or a currency. A brand-new car is worth more on the day you buy it than it will be a year later, and even less five years after that.
Depredation means the act of causing serious damage, destruction, or loss — especially by attacking, plundering, or repeatedly harming something over time.

Feeling very sad and hopeless, especially over a long period. Of a place or economy, suffering from a lack of money and activity, as in "a depressed area." Of a surface, pushed down or lower than the area around it.

If something is depressing, it causes you to feel sad, hopeless, and emotionally heavy. It pulls your mood downward — not just for a second, but in a lingering way that makes things feel bleak, grey, or without hope.
Depression always means something has gone lower than its normal level — it has been pushed down, sunken in, or reduced.
Deprivation means the condition of not having enough of something that you genuinely need — something whose absence causes you harm, suffering, or prevents you from living or functioning normally.
To deprive someone means to take away something from them that they need, deserve, or already have — leaving them without it.
When we say someone or something is deprived, we mean they are seriously lacking things that people normally need or deserve in order to live a decent, healthy life.
Depth means how far something extends going inward, downward, or backward — away from the surface or the front. It is the measurement or quality of that inward distance.
To deputize means to officially give someone the authority to act in your place — or to be that person who acts in someone else's place.
A deputy is a person who has been officially given the authority to act on behalf of someone else — usually someone in a position of power or responsibility.

To deracinate something means to pull it up by its roots and tear it away completely from where it belongs. The key word here is roots — not just removing something from a place, but severing its deepest connection to that place.
To cause a plan or process to fail or go off course, as in "the scandal derailed his career." Literally, to cause a train to come off its rails.

To derange something means to throw it out of its normal, ordered, or proper state — to upset it, disturb it, and leave it in disorder or dysfunction. Think of it as the opposite of "arrange." If you arrange things, you put them into order.
Deranged means having a severely disturbed, disordered, or broken mind — so much so that the person has lost touch with reason, reality, or normal human behavior.
"Derangement" describes a state in which something that was once in proper order has been thrown into serious disorder or disruption.
A derby is a prestigious, important horse race — especially one that is run every year and has a long tradition behind it.

Derelict describes something that has been abandoned and has fallen into neglect and decay as a direct result of that abandonment. Those two ideas always travel together in this word: being left behind, and then deteriorating because of it.
A derelict is something — or someone — that has been abandoned and left to fall apart.

Dereliction means the act or state of abandoning something that should not be abandoned — whether that is a duty, a responsibility, or a physical place. There is always an element of neglect, failure, and sometimes wrongdoing attached to this word.

To deride someone or something means to mock them or ridicule them in a way that shows you think they are stupid, worthless, or not worth taking seriously. It is not just laughing with someone — it is laughing at them, often with contempt or scorn.
Derision is the feeling or act of thinking someone or something is completely ridiculous and worthless — and showing it, often by laughing at them, mocking them, or treating them with contempt.

Derisive means showing mocking contempt toward someone or something — treating them as if they are stupid, worthless, or ridiculous, and making that feeling obvious through your words, laughter, or expression.
So small or inadequate that it is ridiculous, as in "a derisory pay offer." It can also mean mocking.
The origin of something, or the process of developing it from a source, as in "the derivation of a word."

Something is derivative when it comes from something that already existed, rather than being genuinely and freshly original. The word's heart is in the verb "to derive" — meaning to take or get something from a source.

A derivative is something that comes from something else. If you take an original thing and build, transform, or develop something new out of it, that new thing is a derivative of the original. It always points back to a source.
To get something from a source, or to trace something back to where it came from.
A dermatologist is a medical doctor who specializes in diagnosing and treating conditions related to the skin, hair, and nails.
To derogate means to reduce, take away from, or diminish something of value, dignity, authority, or standing. It can also mean to belittle or speak disparagingly of someone or something.
When something is derogatory, it expresses a low, disrespectful opinion of a person or group. It puts them down, belittles them, or attacks their dignity.
A derrick is a type of machine designed to lift and move very heavy loads — things too heavy for people to move by hand. Think of it as a specialized crane.
Derring-do means bold, daring, heroic action — the kind that takes real courage and involves facing serious danger or risk with a spirit of adventure.
A derringer is a type of small, compact pistol (handgun) specifically designed to be easily hidden on a person's body.
A dervish is a member of a Muslim Sufi brotherhood — a spiritual community within Islam — who has dedicated their life to the pursuit of a direct, personal experience of God.

A descant is a separate melody sung or played above the main melody, at the same time as it. It is not the main tune. It is not a harmony in the ordinary sense (a harmony typically supports the melody from below or alongside it).
Descend means to move from a higher place to a lower place. It is the opposite of ascend (to go up).
A descendant is someone (or something) that comes from another person (or thing) through a continuous chain of connection over time.
The act of moving downwards, as in "the plane began its descent." It can also mean a downward slope, a decline into a worse state, or a person's family origins, as in "of Irish descent."

Descriptivism is the view that the right job of a scholar, scientist, or observer is to describe how something actually is in the real world — not to judge it, correct it, or tell people how it should be. The "something" depends on the field.
A descriptivist is someone who believes their role is to describe something as it actually is — to observe, record, and explain — rather than to judge it or declare how it should be.

To descry something means to manage to see it — particularly when it is difficult to see. This difficulty might be because the thing is far away, hidden in shadow, barely visible through fog or darkness, or simply very small against a large background.
To desecrate something means to treat a sacred or deeply respected thing in a violating, disrespectful, or damaging way — in a manner that destroys or corrupts its holy or special character.

Desecration is the act of treating something sacred, holy, or deeply respected in a way that is deeply disrespectful, offensive, or damaging — in a way that violates its dignity or destroys its special status.
The most famous example in history is the desegregation of the American South during the Civil Rights Movement of the 1950s and 1960s.
To desensitize someone means to make them less sensitive — less reactive, less affected, or less disturbed — by something, usually through repeated exposure to it.
When a place is deserted, it means it has no people in it — it is completely empty of human presence. You look around, and there is nobody there.

Desertification is the process by which land that was once fertile and productive — able to grow crops, support animals, and sustain communities — slowly degrades into dry, barren, desert-like land that can barely support any life at all.

Desertion is the act of leaving behind someone or something that you had a duty, obligation, or commitment to stay with — doing so deliberately, without permission, and (crucially) with no intention of coming back.
Deserts means what a person deserves — the reward or punishment that is exactly right and fitting based on what they have done.
To deserve something means you have a valid claim to it — not because of luck or someone's favor, but because your actions, behavior, or qualities have earned it or made you worthy of it.
To desiccate something means to remove all, or nearly all, of its moisture — drying it out completely and thoroughly. It is not ordinary, surface-level drying.
Desiccated means completely and thoroughly dried out — with all, or nearly all, moisture stripped away. It doesn't just mean "a little dry."
A desideratum is something that is seriously needed, wanted, or considered necessary — especially when it is currently missing. It is not a passing wish or a vague hope.
At the very center of the word design is one powerful idea: intentional arrangement. When something has been designed, it means it didn't happen by chance.
When you designate something or someone, you officially and purposefully choose them for a specific role, status, or purpose — and you make that choice clear and known. It's not a casual act.
To desist means to stop doing something — and to stop it deliberately and completely.
Desolate describes a state of complete emptiness — stripped of life, comfort, or hope. It is a strong, heavy word. It doesn't just mean "empty" or "sad." It means utterly empty. Deeply sad.

Desolation means a state of complete emptiness, bleakness, and lifelessness — whether in a place or in a person's inner world. It is not ordinary emptiness. It is a deep, heavy, overwhelming kind of emptiness — one that feels total and inescapable.

Despair means the complete, total loss of hope. Not a little hopeless — completely hopeless. It is the feeling that your situation is so bad, so permanent, and so beyond your control that things cannot get better. Ever.
To despair means to completely lose hope — to reach a point where you stop believing that a situation can ever get better, or that something you want is ever going to happen.
A desperado is a dangerous, reckless criminal or outlaw — someone who acts without fear of consequences, often because they feel they have absolutely nothing left to lose.

Feeling or showing hopelessness and a willingness to do anything to change a terrible situation, as in "a desperate attempt." It can also mean extremely serious, or having a great need or desire for something, as in "desperate for water."

Desperately describes doing something — or feeling something — with extreme urgency, intense need, or a sense that the situation is serious or even hopeless. It tells you how strongly or in what emotional state something is happening.
Desperation is the intense, overwhelming feeling you get when you are in a very bad situation and believe you have no good options left — or that time is running out fast.
When you call someone or something despicable, you mean they are so morally bad, so shameful in their behavior, that they deserve nothing but contempt and disgust from decent people.

To despise someone or something means to feel a deep, strong sense of hatred combined with contempt — the feeling that whoever or whatever you are looking at is completely unworthy, inferior, or beneath your respect.
To despoil something means to strip it of what makes it valuable, beautiful, or whole — usually through force, greed, or violence — and leave it in a ruined or emptied state.

Despondency is a deep, heavy state of sadness combined with a loss of hope. When someone is in despondency, they feel that things are going very badly and that things will not get better. It is not just feeling unhappy.
Despondent means feeling a deep, heavy loss of hope — usually about a specific situation — to the point where you feel like things will never get better no matter what you do.
A despot is a ruler — or any person in a position of authority — who holds complete, unchecked power and uses it in a harsh, cruel, or oppressive way.
If someone is despotic, they have total power over others and use it in a harsh, cruel, and selfish way — completely ignoring what others think, feel, or deserve.

Despotism is a system of rule — or a way of exercising power — in which one person holds complete, unlimited authority over everyone else, and uses that power in an oppressive, self-serving, or cruel way, with no accountability to anyone.

To destabilize something means to make it less stable — to weaken its foundations, disrupt its balance, or shake its security to the point where it might start to fall apart, lose control, or stop functioning properly.
A destination is the place or point that someone or something is meant to reach at the end of a journey or process.
Destined means certain to happen or to be, as if already decided by fate or some higher force before it even began. It is not just "probably will happen" — it is stronger and deeper than that.
Destiny means the idea that a person's life, future, or final outcome has already been decided — often by a higher power, the universe, or some force beyond human control.
Destitute means being so extremely poor that you lack even the most basic things needed to survive — things like food, water, shelter, clothing, and money.
Destitution means the state of being completely without the basic necessities of life — things like food, clean water, shelter, and clothing. It is not simply being poor or financially tight.
Destruction means the complete ruining or ending of something — to the point where it either no longer exists, or no longer works the way it used to.
Something is destructive when it causes damage, harm, or ruin — when it breaks down, tears apart, or wipes out something that existed before.
Desuetude means the state of no longer being used or practiced.

Desultory describes something done in a scattered, unfocused, and half-hearted way — jumping from one thing to another randomly, without a clear plan, purpose, or logical connection holding it together.
The root word is attach, which means to connect or fasten something to something else. So detached simply means the opposite — separated, not connected, or not involved.

Emotional distance — the state of being calm, uninvolved, and not personally affected by what is happening. It can also mean being separated from something, or a small group of soldiers sent on a special task.
Something is detailed when it includes many specific pieces of information — the small, fine, and particular facts — rather than just a broad or general overview.
To detain someone means to hold them and prevent them from leaving. The person being detained cannot walk away freely — they are being kept in place by someone with authority or power over them.

A detainee is a person who is being held in custody by an authority — such as the police, the government, the military, or immigration officials — but who has not yet been formally convicted of any crime, and often has not even been formally charged with one.

A detector is anything — a device, an instrument, or sometimes a person — whose job is to find out whether something is present, especially when that something is invisible, hidden, too small to see, or hard to notice with your natural senses.
Detention means the act of keeping a person (or sometimes a thing) held somewhere, stopping them from going free or moving on.
To deter someone means to discourage them from doing something by making them think the action is too risky, too costly, or not worth it.
A detergent is a substance used for cleaning — specifically, one that helps remove dirt, grease, oil, and stains from surfaces, fabrics, dishes, skin, or anything else that needs washing.
To deteriorate means to gradually become worse — in condition, quality, or state. Something that deteriorates doesn't collapse in an instant; it slowly, continuously slides downward over time.

Something is determinate when it is clearly defined, has fixed limits, and is fully settled — leaving no room for vagueness, ambiguity, or open-endedness. You know exactly what it is, where it begins and ends, and there is no uncertainty hanging over it.
Determination is the strong, steady inner resolve to reach a goal — even when things become hard, painful, or seem impossible.
Determine means to arrive at something fixed and definite — a clear fact, a firm decision, or a settled outcome.

When you describe someone as determined, you mean that they have made a firm, unshakeable decision in their mind to do something — and they refuse to stop or give up, no matter how difficult things become.
The philosophical belief that every event, including human choices, is fully caused by what came before it, so that nothing could have happened differently.
Deterrence is the act or effect of making someone choose not to do something by making them afraid of what will happen if they do it.

When something is described as deterrent, it means it discourages or prevents an action by making someone (or something) unwilling to attempt it — usually because it signals a threat, a consequence, or an unpleasant outcome.

A deterrent is anything — a threat, a consequence, a presence, or a measure — that discourages someone from doing something by making them feel that doing it is too risky, too costly, or too dangerous.

To detest something or someone means to feel an extremely strong hatred and disgust toward them. It is not mild dislike — it is a deep, intense negative feeling where the very thought or presence of something repels you.
If something is detestable, it is so bad, so morally wrong, or so deeply offensive that it fills people with intense hatred and disgust.

Detestation is a noun that describes an intense, deep feeling of hatred, loathing, and disgust toward something or someone. It sits at the very top of the scale of negative feelings — far beyond ordinary dislike, and even stronger than plain hatred.
To dethrone someone means to remove them from the highest position of power or dominance — to knock the person who is "on top" off their top spot.
To detonate means to explode suddenly and violently, releasing a massive burst of energy, heat, sound, and force in a split second.

A detonation is a sudden, extremely violent explosion — one that happens with overwhelming speed and force, releasing a massive amount of energy almost instantaneously. Think of it as the most extreme, fastest kind of explosion possible.

A detour is an indirect, alternative path you take when your usual, direct path is blocked, unavailable, or needs to be avoided — with the understanding that you will still eventually reach your destination, just not by the most straightforward way.

To detract means to take away from the value, quality, appeal, or importance of something. When something detracts, it makes a person, thing, or experience seem less good, less impressive, or less worthy than it would otherwise be.
Detraction is the act of reducing or taking away from someone's reputation, merit, or worth — most often through what you say about them.

A detractor is a person who speaks negatively about someone or something — typically with the effect (and often the intent) of making that person or thing seem less valuable, less impressive, or less worthy of respect.

Detriment means harm, damage, or disadvantage caused to someone or something. When something works to the detriment of a person or thing, it is hurting them, weakening them, or making their situation worse in some way.

Detrimental means causing harm, damage, or a negative effect to something or someone. When something is detrimental, it makes a situation, a person's condition, or an outcome worse than it would otherwise be.
Detritus is the word for the debris, waste, or leftover fragments that remain after something has been broken down, worn away, used up, or destroyed.
Deuce simply means the number two. That's the root idea running through almost every use of this word. But how it plays out depends on the context. Here's a full picture.

A deus ex machina is when a story introduces a sudden, unexpected solution — usually a character, event, object, or power — that appears out of nowhere at the last moment to rescue the hero or resolve the plot.

To devastate means to cause damage so severe and so complete that almost nothing is left intact — to reduce something to ruin. This is not ordinary damage. The word carries the weight of total, overwhelming destruction.
If something is devastating, it causes extreme damage, destruction, or distress — so much so that it is very hard to recover from, or the impact is deeply felt and long-lasting.
Devastation means a state of complete and overwhelming destruction or ruin. The key word here is complete — not partial damage, not some harm, but a thorough, large-scale wreckage of something.
Develop means to change from a simpler, smaller, or less complete state into a more complex, fuller, or more complete state — gradually, over time.
The process of growing, changing, or becoming more advanced, as in "child development." It can also mean a new event or piece of news, or a group of new buildings, as in "a housing development."
Deviance means the act, quality, or state of departing from what is considered normal, expected, or acceptable — usually by a group, a society, or some established standard.
"Deviant" describes something that strays from what is considered normal, standard, or acceptable within a particular group, society, or system.

To deviate means to move away from something that was expected, normal, planned, or established. That "away from" is the heart of the word — you always deviate from something. Think of it as leaving a path you were supposed to stay on.
A deviation is a departure or difference from something that is considered normal, standard, expected, or agreed upon.
To "play devil's advocate" means to argue for a side you don't personally believe in, just to test an idea, challenge a viewpoint, or push a discussion further.
Devious describes a person or behavior that is clever, indirect, and dishonest — someone who uses hidden, sneaky methods to get what they want, instead of being open and straightforward.
Deviousness is the quality of being sneaky, dishonest, and indirect in getting what you want — especially in a way that is hard for others to see or detect.
To devise something means to think it up carefully and cleverly — to come up with a plan, method, system, or solution through deliberate mental effort.
"Devoid" means completely without something — not just low on it, or barely having it, but having absolutely none of it. It describes a total, complete absence.
Devolution means the act of passing power, authority, responsibility, or property downward — from a higher level to a lower one, or from a central body to a smaller, more local one.
Devolve describes a downward movement — either of power/responsibility (passed down to someone else) or of quality/condition (sliding down into something worse).

When someone is devoted, they have a deep, sincere, and lasting commitment to a person, a cause, or an activity. They don't just care about it — they actively give their heart, time, energy, and effort to it, consistently and wholeheartedly.
A devotee is a person who is deeply and sincerely dedicated to something or someone — not casually, not occasionally, but with real, consistent commitment and passion.
Devotion is a deep, steady, and wholehearted commitment of your love, time, energy, and loyalty toward someone or something.

Devour means to eat something with great speed, hunger, and eagerness — consuming it entirely, leaving nothing behind. Think of a lion that hasn't eaten in days finally catching prey. It doesn't nibble. It doesn't pause.
Devout means deeply and sincerely committed — most often to a religion or a set of beliefs — in a way that is genuine, earnest, and visible in how a person actually lives their life.
When someone does something devoutly, they do it with deep, sincere, wholehearted feeling — not casually, not half-heartedly, but with their whole heart truly invested in it.

Dexterity means skill, ease, and precision in doing something — either with your hands and body, or with your mind. When someone has dexterity, they can perform tasks smoothly, quickly, and accurately, with very little effort or error.
If someone is dexterous, they perform skilled tasks — especially with their hands, but sometimes with their mind — with impressive ease, precision, and grace.
Diabolic means characteristic of the devil — and by extension, extremely evil, wicked, or cruel. When you call something diabolic, you are not just saying it is bad or wrong.
Diabolical means relating to or characteristic of the devil. Think of it as the adjectival form of "the devil."

A diadem is a type of crown — but not just any crown. Picture a circular band or ring made of gold, silver, or another precious material, decorated with jewels and gems, designed to sit around a person's head like a headband.

To diagnose means to carefully examine something — a person, a machine, a system, or even a situation — and then identify what is wrong with it and why. It is not just noticing that something is wrong.
A diagnosis is the identification of exactly what a problem is, arrived at after a careful study of evidence.
When something is described as diagnostic, it means it is related to — or useful for — identifying what something is, what's wrong, or what caused a problem.

A diagram is a drawing or visual representation that explains how something works, what something looks like, how parts are connected, or how a process unfolds — using lines, shapes, symbols, labels, and sometimes arrows.

A dialect is a specific variety, or version, of a language that a particular group of people use. Think of a language as a large umbrella. Under that umbrella, many slightly different versions of the same language exist, each spoken by a different community.
A dialectic is a process by which two opposing ideas clash, and through that clash, produce a deeper or truer understanding than either idea could reach on its own.

Something is "dialectical" when it involves two opposing ideas or forces in conflict with each other, and that conflict itself — rather than being a problem — is what produces a deeper truth, a richer understanding, or real change.

"Diametrical" describes opposition or difference that is total, absolute, and complete — with no middle ground, no overlap, and no room for compromise. When two things are diametrical, they sit at the exact opposite ends of a spectrum from each other.

Something is diaphanous when it is so incredibly thin, light, and delicate that you can see through it — or almost see through it. It describes a kind of beautiful, dreamy see-through quality, most often in fine fabric or cloth.

A diaphragm is always some kind of thin, flexible dividing structure — something that either separates two spaces, or moves/vibrates to serve a purpose. That one idea threads through every meaning of this word.
A large group of people who share a common homeland but have scattered and settled in many other parts of the world, while keeping a shared sense of identity.

A diatribe is a long, bitter, angry speech or piece of writing that attacks someone or something very harshly. It's not a simple disagreement or a polite critique — it's a forceful, sustained verbal assault charged with strong negative emotion.
Dicey means risky and uncertain in a way that could easily go wrong.
When you say something is dicey-looking, you mean it appears risky, unsafe, unreliable, suspicious, or questionable — purely based on how it looks to you at first glance.
A dichotomy is a division of something into two parts, groups, or ideas that are complete opposites of each other — and where the two sides don't overlap.
To waste time in a lazy, aimless way (vulgar slang). To dick someone around means to treat them unfairly, for example by making them wait or changing plans.
"Dictate" is about control flowing in one direction — from someone (or something) with authority or power, toward a person or situation that must follow.
A dictator is a ruler who holds complete, unlimited power over a country — and who holds that power by force or manipulation, not because the people freely and fairly chose them.
A dictatorship is a system of government in which one person — or sometimes a small group — holds absolute power over an entire country, with no meaningful checks on that power.
Diction has two distinct but related meanings. Both are in common, everyday use. You need to understand both to fully own this word.

A dictum is an authoritative statement — something said by a person (or institution) whose words carry weight, and therefore the statement is taken seriously or accepted as a guiding principle. Think of it as a "word from on high."
Didactic means intended to teach. When something is didactic, its main purpose is to instruct, educate, or convey a lesson — whether that lesson is moral, intellectual, or practical.

Didacticism is the quality or practice of being primarily focused on teaching, instructing, or delivering a moral lesson — especially when that focus becomes so dominant that it overshadows everything else, like the story, the beauty, or the entertainment value.

To die means to stop being alive. When a living thing — a person, an animal, a plant — permanently stops all the processes that keep it alive, it dies. This is the primary, most universal sense of the word.
Diesel is a type of fuel — a liquid made from crude oil (the thick, dark substance extracted from deep underground) — used to power certain kinds of engines.
A dietitian is a trained and officially recognized health professional who is an expert in food, nutrition, and how what you eat affects your body and health.
To differ means to be not the same, or to hold an opposing view. Everything else is just a variation of these two ideas.
Differentiate means to recognize, show, or create a difference between things.
When something is difficult, it means it takes a lot of effort, skill, or thought to do, understand, or deal with. It is simply the opposite of easy.
Diffidence means a lack of confidence in yourself — a quiet, inner feeling that you are not good enough, not capable enough, or not worthy enough to put yourself forward.

Diffident describes a person who lacks confidence in themselves — someone who holds back, stays quiet, and avoids putting themselves forward because deep down they doubt their own worth, abilities, or the value of what they have to say.
The entire meaning of diffuse rests on one central idea: spread out widely and thinly, rather than gathered or focused in one place.
To diffuse something means to spread it out widely from a central point, in all directions, so that it becomes less concentrated and more evenly distributed.

Diffusion means the process of something spreading outward — moving from a place where there is a lot of it to places where there is little or none of it, until it is spread more evenly. Think of it as "the natural act of spreading out."
To "dig at" someone means to say something critical, mocking, or sarcastic about them — often in a clever, indirect, or sneaky way, rather than through open, direct criticism.
When someone says "dig in," they are telling you to start eating without waiting — often enthusiastically and without formality.

To dig in one's heels means to stubbornly refuse to change your opinion, decision, or position — even when others are pressuring you, arguing against you, or giving you strong reasons to change your mind.
A digest is a collection of information that has been carefully condensed, organized, and made easier to read — drawn from sources that are often long, dense, or numerous.

To digest means to break something down into a simpler, usable form. Whether it's food, information, or a feeling — something complex goes in, and something simpler and absorbed comes out. That single idea connects all its meanings.
"Digital" describes something that works with, stores, or represents information as separate, distinct values — typically numbers.
A dignified person (or thing) has a calm, serious, self-respecting quality that naturally commands the respect of others — without demanding it.
To dignify something means to treat it as worthy of respect, seriousness, or importance — to give it a sense of weight or value that makes it feel elevated and significant.
A dignitary is a person who holds a high rank or an important official position, and who is treated with great respect and honor because of that position.
Dignity is the quality of being worthy of respect — from others, and from yourself.
To digress means to move away from the main topic you are supposed to be talking or writing about, and start discussing something else — something that is not directly related to the central point.

A digression is a temporary departure from the main topic — a moment when a speaker or writer wanders away from what they were originally talking about and goes off on a side path, before (sometimes) returning to the main point.
When something — a piece of writing, a speech, a conversation, or a person's way of communicating — keeps moving away from its main point and wandering into side topics, it is called digressive.

A diktat is an order, ruling, or set of terms that is imposed by someone in power on others who have no say in the matter whatsoever. The people on the receiving end cannot negotiate, argue, or refuse.
When something is dilapidated, it is in a state of serious decay and poor condition, usually because it has been neglected for a long time and not taken care of.
Dilapidation is the state of being badly damaged, broken down, or in serious disrepair — especially as a result of long-term neglect and the slow passage of time.

To dilate means to become wider or larger, or to make something wider or larger — especially an opening, a passage, or a hollow space in the body. Think of it as the opposite of shrinking or narrowing. When something dilates, it opens up and expands.
Dilation means the act, process, or result of something becoming wider, larger, or more open — or being deliberately made so.

Dilatory means tending to delay, slow to act, or deliberately causing delay. It describes someone or something that is dragging its feet — either out of laziness and habit, or on purpose as a strategy.

A dilemma is a situation in which you must make a choice between two or more options, but every option comes with a serious downside, cost, or consequence. No matter which option you pick, something bad, uncomfortable, or regrettable happens.

A dilettante is a person who engages with a subject — typically art, music, science, literature, or some intellectual field — but only at a shallow, surface level. They never put in the serious, sustained effort needed to truly master it.
Diligence means careful, steady, and consistent hard work — especially when applied over time and with attention to doing things well, not just getting them done.

Diligent describes a person who works with steady, careful, and thorough effort. A diligent person takes their work seriously, pays close attention to what they are doing, and keeps going until the job is done well — not just done quickly.

Diligently means doing something with careful, steady, and persistent effort — giving it your full attention, not rushing, not cutting corners, and not giving up just because it becomes difficult or boring.
To dilute something means to reduce its strength, concentration, or intensity — most often by mixing it with something else that is weaker or neutral.
To dim something means to make it less bright — to reduce its light or glow without completely switching it off. When something dims on its own, it becomes less bright by itself.
Dim-witted means not intelligent; slow to understand things; having a weak mind that struggles to grasp ideas.

A dimension is a direction in which something can be measured, or more broadly, a distinct aspect or feature of something. These two ideas — one concrete, one abstract — are the two main branches of the word.

To diminish means to become smaller, weaker, or less — or to make something smaller, weaker, or less. Think of it as something losing its size, strength, importance, or intensity — either slowly over time or because something else is causing it to shrink.
When something is diminishing, it is gradually becoming smaller, weaker, fewer, or less significant over time. The key word here is gradually — it's not a sudden drop, but a slow, ongoing decline.

Diminution means a reduction or lessening of something — in size, amount, strength, importance, or quality. It describes the process of something becoming smaller or less than it was before, or the result of that process.

When you describe something as diminutive, you are saying it is very small — noticeably, strikingly small, often smaller than you would normally expect something of that kind to be. It goes beyond just "small."

A dimwit is a person who is not very intelligent — someone who is slow to understand things, makes obviously foolish mistakes, or simply lacks common sense. When you call someone a dimwit, you are saying their thinking is dull and slow, not sharp or bright.

A din is a loud, prolonged, and chaotic mixture of sounds that is deeply unpleasant and hard to escape. It is not just one loud sound — it is many sounds clashing together all at once, continuing over time, creating a kind of overwhelming wall of noise.

To dine means to eat a meal — but not just any meal in any way. It carries the sense of eating in a deliberate, unhurried, and somewhat special or elevated manner. The most common context is a proper sit-down meal, often dinner or lunch.

A diner is a person who is eating a meal. Whether someone is eating at a restaurant, at a formal dinner party, or at a banquet hall, they can be called a "diner." This is the straightforward, literal sense of the word.
A dinghy is a small, open boat — typically light enough for one person to carry or drag, and small enough to seat just a few people (usually between one and six).
Something is dingy when it looks dirty, dull, grimy, and gloomy all at once — usually because it has been neglected for a long time. It's not just a little dirty.
"Dinky" is an informal adjective. It always refers to something small, but how that smallness feels — positive or negative — splits sharply between British and American English.

"Dint" is a word with two related meanings. One is older and refers to a physical mark; the other is the more famous one that you'll actually encounter in real life — and it lives almost entirely inside a single, fixed phrase: "by dint of."
A diorama is a three-dimensional scene — a carefully built, miniature (or sometimes life-size) representation of a real or imaginary place and moment in time.
A diphthong is a single vowel sound that glides — smoothly travels — from one mouth position to another, all within a single syllable.

A diploma is an official document issued by an educational institution — such as a school, college, or university — that certifies you have successfully completed a specific course of study or program.

Diplomacy is the skill or practice of handling difficult, sensitive, or high-stakes situations through careful communication and negotiation — rather than through force, aggression, or thoughtless bluntness.
A diplomat is a person who is officially sent by their government to represent their country in another country.

When we call someone or something diplomatic, we mean they are skilled at handling sensitive situations carefully — saying or doing the right thing in a way that avoids upsetting, offending, or creating conflict.
A dipshit is a stupid, foolish, or incompetent person — someone who consistently makes dumb decisions, says or does thoughtless things, or just doesn't seem to have basic common sense.

Dipsomania is a medical and psychological term for an uncontrollable, overwhelming, and compulsive craving for alcohol — one so powerful that the person experiencing it feels completely unable to resist it, no matter how hard they try.

A dipsomaniac is a person who has an overwhelming, uncontrollable urge to drink alcohol — not just someone who enjoys drinking or even drinks too much, but someone who is seized by a compulsion to drink that they feel powerless to resist.
Dire means extremely serious, severe, or urgent — so bad that it causes fear, demands immediate action, or signals that something terrible is happening or about to happen.
A direction is the line along which something moves, faces, or points. It answers the question: which way?

A directive is an official instruction that someone in a position of authority gives to people under them, telling them what to do or how to act. The key element is authority — a directive doesn't come from just anyone.
A directory is an organized list or collection that helps you find things.

A dirge is a slow, deeply mournful piece of music — or sometimes a poem — that expresses grief, especially over someone's death. Think of it as the musical sound of mourning. If sadness had a melody, a dirge would be it.
A disability is a condition — physical, mental, sensory, or cognitive — that significantly limits a person's ability to do certain things or participate in everyday life in the way most people do.
To disabuse someone means to free them from a wrong belief they are holding — to correct a mistaken idea in their head and replace it with the truth.

Disaffected describes a person — or a group of people — who used to feel loyal, content, or supportive toward something (a government, a company, a cause, a leader, an institution), but no longer do. Something changed.

Disaffection means a feeling of disappointment, loss of loyalty, and growing emotional distance toward something or someone you once believed in, supported, or felt a sense of belonging to — typically a government, an institution, a cause, an organization, or a leader.

When something is disagreeable, it causes discomfort, displeasure, or annoyance. It isn't just "not great" — it actively bothers you in some way. The unpleasantness can hit any of your senses or feelings.
To disappear means something that was there is no longer there — either because it can no longer be seen, or because it has stopped existing entirely.
To disappoint someone means to fail to meet what they hoped for, expected, or looked forward to — leaving them with a feeling of sadness or letdown.
Disappointment is the feeling you get when reality turns out to be worse than what you expected or hoped for. It is the emotional gap between what you wanted to happen and what actually happened.
Disapprobation means strong, serious disapproval — especially disapproval that carries a moral judgment.

When you disapprove of something, you think it is wrong, bad, unacceptable, or not the way things should be. You may not necessarily be angry — you simply feel that something falls short of what you consider right or appropriate.
Disarm means to remove the ability to cause harm — most directly by taking away weapons, but also, in a powerful figurative sense, by softening someone's hostility or resistance.
So charming, honest, or friendly that it makes people drop their suspicion or defensiveness, as in "a disarming smile."
In a way that makes people drop their suspicion or guard, through charm, honesty, or warmth, as in "disarmingly frank."
Disarray means a state of complete disorder, confusion, or untidiness — where things that should be organized, structured, or working properly have fallen apart or become messy.
To disassemble something means to take it apart, piece by piece, into its separate components — the individual parts that were originally put together to make it.

To disavow something means to openly and deliberately say that you have no connection to it — that you did not do it, do not support it, do not believe it, or are not associated with whoever is involved in it.
A disavowal is when someone publicly and deliberately says: "I have nothing to do with that. Don't associate me with it."
To disband means to officially break up a group so that it no longer exists as a unit, and its members go their separate ways.
To disbar someone means to officially and permanently strip a lawyer of their license to practice law, as a punishment for serious wrongdoing.
Disbelief is the state or feeling of not believing something — of refusing to accept, or being unable to accept, that something is true or real.
To disbelieve something means to actively think that it is not true — to mentally reject it as false or unreliable.
To disburse means to pay out money from a fund, account, or organized source — to the people or places it is meant for.
A disbursement is money that is officially paid out from a fund, account, or pool of money to someone or for a specific purpose.
To discard something means to deliberately get rid of it, set it aside, or throw it away — because you've decided it is no longer useful, needed, or valuable to you.
