To discern something means to perceive, identify, or recognize it — especially when it is not immediately obvious, not easy to see, or hidden among other things. It is the mental or sensory act of picking something out with care and sharpness.
Discernible means able to be noticed, perceived, or recognized — usually through careful observation or attention.

Discerning means having the ability to recognize quality, subtlety, and important differences that most people would miss or overlook. A discerning person doesn't just look — they see. They don't just listen — they truly hear.
Discernment is the ability to see clearly, judge wisely, and tell things apart — especially when it is not easy to do so.
The act of officially allowing someone to leave a hospital, prison, or the armed forces. It can also mean a liquid or gas flowing out of something, the release of electricity, or the firing of a gun.

To officially allow someone to leave a hospital or job, as in "she was discharged yesterday." It also means to let out a liquid or gas, to fire a gun, or to carry out or complete a duty, as in "discharging her responsibilities."

A disciple is a person who follows a teacher, leader, or thinker — not merely to learn facts or skills, but to absorb, believe in, and live by that person's teachings, ideas, or way of life. A disciple is deeply committed.
A formal step taken by an employer, school, or institution to correct or punish someone for breaking its rules, such as a warning, suspension, or dismissal.
"Discipline" is about control and order — either the control you exercise over yourself, or the control that rules and authority exercise over a group of people.

A disciplined person is someone who has strong control over their own behavior. They can make themselves do what needs to be done — even when it's hard, boring, or uncomfortable — consistently and without needing someone else to push them.
To disclaim something means to formally or deliberately deny any connection to it — to say, in effect: "This is not mine. I am not responsible for it. I do not own it. I do not believe it."
A disclaimer is a statement — written or spoken — in which a person or organization officially says: "I am not responsible for this" — or — "Don't take this as something I haven't said it is."
To disclose something means to make known information that was previously hidden, secret, or not publicly available.
To discombobulate someone means to confuse them, throw them off balance, or leave them in a flustered, disoriented state — so much so that they struggle to think clearly or respond normally.
When someone is discombobulated, they feel mentally confused, disoriented, and thrown off balance all at once — as if their mind has been scrambled or shaken up.

To discomfit someone means to make them feel mentally unsettled, flustered, or thrown off balance — to put them in a state of confusion, embarrassment, or awkwardness where they don't quite know how to react or what to do next.

Discomfiture is the feeling of being thrown off balance — a mix of embarrassment, unease, and being flustered — especially in a way that is visible to others or that disrupts your confidence and composure.
To discompose someone means to disturb their inner calm — to throw off their emotional balance, make them feel unsettled, flustered, or mentally agitated.
A state of being upset, flustered, or no longer calm and in control of yourself.

To disconcert someone means to disturb their calm, shake their confidence, or throw them off balance — not physically, but mentally and emotionally. When you disconcert someone, you disrupt the sense of ease, composure, or certainty they had a moment ago.

Disconcerted means feeling suddenly thrown off your inner balance — mentally or emotionally — because of something unexpected. When you are disconcerted, something has disturbed your sense of calm, comfort, or confidence.
Something is disconcerting when it makes you feel uneasy, unsettled, or thrown off balance — not physically, but mentally and emotionally.

Disconnect means to break or end a connection between two things. It is the direct opposite of connect. When you connect things, you bring them together or create a link. When you disconnect them, you undo that link.
Disconsolate means deeply, heavily sad — in a way that cannot be comforted or relieved by anything or anyone around you.

Discontent is the feeling of not being satisfied or happy with your current situation — a restless inner sense that things are not the way they should be, or that something important is missing or wrong.
To discontinue something means to permanently or indefinitely stop something that had been going on for a while — something that was regular, ongoing, or continuous.

Discord means a state of disagreement, tension, or conflict — typically between people, groups, or things that fail to come together peacefully. It describes a situation where, instead of harmony and cooperation, there is friction, clash, and division.
Clashing or out of harmony with something else, as in "a discordant note" or "discordant opinions."
A discount is a reduction in the usual or original price of something. It is the amount that is taken off the full price — not the final price you pay, but the part that has been removed.

When you discountenance something, you make it clear — through your words, attitude, or behavior — that you do not approve of it. The goal is often to discourage it, stop it, or signal that it is unacceptable.
To discourage someone means to make them feel less confident, less willing, or less hopeful about doing something — so that they either don't do it at all, or do it with less energy and belief.

Discourse means an extended, organized piece of communication — spoken or written — about a particular subject. The key word here is extended. Discourse isn't a single sentence or a quick remark. It's a sustained, developed treatment of a topic.
Discredit means the loss of trust, respect, or good reputation — either the process of losing it, or the damaged state that results.
To damage someone's reputation so that people stop trusting or respecting them. It can also mean to make an idea or claim seem false or unreliable.
"Discreet" describes a person or action that is carefully tactful and private — especially when handling sensitive, delicate, or confidential matters.
A discrepancy is a difference between two or more things that should match or agree with each other — but don't.
"Discrete" means separate, individually distinct, and not connected to or blending into anything else.

Discretion has two closely related meanings, and both revolve around one central idea: good judgment. One meaning is about how you behave (carefully and wisely), and the other is about the power you have (the freedom to make your own call).
Something is discretionary when it is not fixed, not forced, and not automatic — it depends entirely on the judgment and choice of the person or authority who has the power to decide.
Making careful distinctions; selective and discerning, as in "discriminate use of resources." It is the opposite of "indiscriminate."
Discriminate means to notice a difference and act on it — either by telling things apart, or by treating people differently based on some characteristic.

When we call someone discriminating, we mean they have the sharp ability to notice fine differences between things — and because of that, they have excellent, refined taste and judgment. They don't just accept anything that comes their way.

"Discrimination" simply means the ability to recognize and tell apart differences between things. This is the older, more neutral sense of the word, and it carries no judgment — it is actually a sign of intelligence and sharpness.
Wandering from one topic to another rather than following a focused, direct path. In philosophy, it also means proceeding by logical reasoning rather than intuition.
A discussion is a focused, back-and-forth exchange of thoughts between two or more people on a specific topic.
Disdain is the feeling that someone or something is so inferior, unworthy, or beneath your standards that they don't deserve your respect, attention, or serious consideration.
To disdain something means to look down on it as unworthy of your attention, respect, or effort — because you believe it is beneath you. It is a feeling of cold, superior contempt.

If someone is disdainful, they think a person or thing is so unworthy, inferior, or beneath them that it doesn't even deserve their respect or proper attention. They look down on it — not just with dislike, but with a kind of cold, superior contempt.
Disdainfully means doing or saying something in a way that shows you think a person or thing is worthless, beneath you, or undeserving of your respect.
To disembark means to get off a large vehicle — especially a ship or an airplane — after it has arrived at its destination.
"Disembodied" means existing separately from, or completely without, a physical body.
To disembowel something (a person or animal) means to cut open its belly and remove — or tear out — the intestines and other internal organs from inside the body.
Disenchanted means feeling disappointed and let down after realizing that something — or someone — is not as wonderful, perfect, or exciting as you once believed.
Disenchantment is the feeling of disappointment and loss of excitement that you get when something — or someone — turns out to be far less wonderful than you originally believed.
To disencumber something or someone means to remove whatever is burdening, weighing down, or getting in the way of that person or thing — so that they can move, act, or exist more freely.

To disenfranchise someone means to take away their right to participate — most specifically, their right to vote, but more broadly, their right to have a voice, power, or standing in any system that affects their life.

Disenfranchised describes a person or group that has been denied rights, power, or a meaningful voice — either by law, by the system, or by how society treats them. It carries a strong sense of being shut out, left behind, or rendered powerless.
Disenfranchisement means being stripped of your rights, power, or voice — particularly the right to participate in decisions that affect your own life.

To disengage means to separate, release, or pull away from something that was connected, involved, or locked together. Think of it as the act of undoing a connection — whether that connection is physical, mental, emotional, or social.
To disentangle means to separate, free, or sort out something that is twisted, knotted, mixed up, or tangled — so that it becomes clear, ordered, and free again.
To disfigure something means to badly damage or spoil its appearance — making it look ugly, distorted, or significantly worse than it originally did.
Disfigured describes something — most often a person's face or body — whose normal, natural appearance has been severely and visibly damaged or destroyed, usually permanently.
Disfigurement means the condition of having one's appearance — most often the face or body — seriously and visibly damaged or spoiled in a way that is permanent or long-lasting.

"Disgorge" means to forcefully release or expel something that was being held inside — whether from a body, a channel, a container, or an organization. The release is typically sudden, large in scale, or reluctant.

Disgrace means the loss of other people's respect, approval, or good opinion — usually because of something shameful, wrong, or deeply disappointing that someone (or something) has done or represents.
To disgruntle someone means to make them feel dissatisfied, displeased, and quietly resentful — especially because they feel they have been treated unfairly, let down, or ignored.
Disgruntled describes a person who feels a mix of anger, annoyance, and dissatisfaction — specifically because they feel they have been treated unfairly, let down, or ignored.
A disguise is anything used to change or hide someone's true appearance, identity, or nature — so that others cannot recognize or identify them correctly.
To disguise something means to change its appearance, nature, or character so that others will not recognize it for what it truly is.
Disgust is a strong, deeply unpleasant feeling of revulsion — a powerful inner reaction that says "this is wrong, offensive, or foul, and I want nothing to do with it."
A dish is a container — usually round, flat or slightly hollow — used to hold, cook, or serve food.
The state of being only partly or carelessly dressed, as in "she answered the door in dishabille."

If harmony is a smooth, calm river flowing in one direction, disharmony is what happens when the water starts moving in conflicting directions, creating turbulence. The different currents don't cooperate — they fight each other.
To dishearten someone means to cause them to lose their courage, hope, confidence, or enthusiasm — to make them feel like giving up or feel that there is no point in continuing.
Disheartened means feeling a loss of hope, courage, or confidence — usually after something disappointing has happened or after your efforts have failed to produce the result you wanted.

When something is disheartening, it causes a person to lose hope, enthusiasm, or the inner strength to keep going. It makes you feel deflated, discouraged, and beaten down — like the energy has been drained right out of you.

When you describe someone as disheveled, you are saying that their appearance is untidy and messy — like they haven't taken care of how they look, or like something has disturbed their neat appearance.

Dishonor is the opposite of that. It is the loss, destruction, or complete absence of that respect and dignity. When someone loses their honor — whether through a shameful act, a moral failure, or a humiliating event — the result is dishonor.
To disillusion someone means to destroy a belief they held that was false, idealized, or too good to be true — leaving them face-to-face with reality, which tends to be disappointing.
Disappointed and saddened after discovering that someone or something you believed in or admired is not as good as you thought.
Disillusionment is the feeling — and the state — of having a belief, an admiration, or a hope stripped away because reality turned out to be very different from what you thought.
A disinclination is a feeling of not wanting to do something, engage with something, or accept something. It is an inner pull away from something — a soft, quiet resistance that lives inside you.

A disinfectant is a chemical substance that you apply to surfaces, objects, or skin to kill or destroy harmful microorganisms — primarily bacteria, viruses, and fungi — that you cannot see with the naked eye.
Disinformation is false or inaccurate information that is deliberately created and spread to deceive people.
Disingenuous means pretending to be honest, innocent, or unaware, while actually being calculating and deceptive underneath.
To disintegrate means to break apart — not just into two or three pieces, but into many small fragments, or even into dust, powder, or nothing recognisable.

Disintegration is a noun. It refers to the process or the event of something breaking apart so thoroughly that it can no longer be recognized or function as what it once was. It is not just "breaking."
To disinter something means to dig it up from where it was buried — or, more broadly, to bring something hidden or forgotten back into the open.
"Disinterested" means impartial — having no personal stake, bias, or hidden agenda in the outcome of a situation.

Disjointed describes something whose parts do not connect or flow together properly. Instead of forming a smooth, unified whole, the parts feel broken apart, scattered, or out of sync with each other.
A disjunction is a separation or disconnect — a gap between two things that don't fit together, or that pull in different directions.
To dislodge something means to force it out of, or move it away from, the place where it is stuck, fixed, wedged, or firmly settled — especially when that thing doesn't come out easily on its own.
When something is dismal, it causes a heavy, sinking feeling — a sense that things are bleak, cheerless, and hopeless. It goes beyond simply being "bad" or "sad." Something dismal drains the spirit.
To dismantle something means to take it apart, piece by piece, until it no longer exists as a whole working thing.
Dismantled describes the state of something that has been deliberately taken apart, piece by piece, until it no longer exists or functions as a whole.

Dismay is a heavy, unsettling feeling you get when something bad, shocking, or deeply disappointing happens — especially when it catches you off guard or when the situation feels worse than you expected or can easily handle.
When someone is dismayed, they are feeling a sudden mix of shock, worry, and disappointment all at once — triggered by something unexpected and unpleasant.
To dismember means to cut, tear, or forcibly separate the limbs or parts of a body from the rest of it — leaving it broken into pieces rather than whole.

Dismemberment is the act of cutting off, tearing off, or otherwise separating the limbs — the arms, legs, or other body parts — from a body, whether human or animal. The result is a body that has been broken apart into separate pieces.

Dismiss means to send away, end, or shut out — whether you're sending a person away, ending something officially, or refusing to take something seriously. In almost every use, the person dismissing holds some authority or makes a deliberate, final decision.

When someone is dismissive, they treat a person, idea, feeling, or concern as if it is simply not worth their time, attention, or serious thought. Instead of engaging with it properly, they brush it aside — quickly, casually, and without real consideration.
Disobedient is an adjective that describes a person (or animal) who refuses to follow rules, orders, or instructions given by someone in authority — like a parent, teacher, boss, or the government.
To disobey means to deliberately refuse to follow a rule, an order, a law, or an instruction given by someone in authority.

To disorient someone means to make them confused and unsure about where they are, what is happening around them, or what they should think or do. It is the act of causing that lost, mixed-up, "wait — what's going on?" feeling in a person.
Disorientation is the state of being mentally lost — not in a physical forest, but inside your own awareness.
Confused and unsure of where you are, what time it is, or what is happening around you.

Something is disorienting when it causes you to feel confused, lost, or unsettled — when it makes you lose your grip on something you normally feel sure about, such as where you are, what is happening around you, what is real, or how things are supposed to work.
To disown someone means to formally and publicly cut all ties with them — to declare that you no longer acknowledge them as part of you, your family, your group, or your responsibility.
To disparage someone or something means to speak about them in a way that makes them seem smaller, less important, less capable, or less worthy than they actually are.
Disparagement is the act of making someone or something seem less valuable, less important, or less worthy than they actually are — usually through words.

When something is disparaging, it puts someone or something down — it makes them seem less valuable, less worthy, or inferior. A disparaging remark, comment, or attitude carries a sense of disrespect or dismissal toward its target.

Disparate describes things that are so fundamentally different from each other that they seem to belong to completely separate worlds. Not just different — but different in a deep, essential way that makes them hard to compare or connect.

A disparity is a significant, noticeable difference or gap between two or more things — especially when that difference involves an imbalance or inequality that feels unfair, surprising, or troubling.

When someone is dispassionate, they are calm, rational, and fair in the way they think about or judge something — and crucially, their personal feelings, emotions, or biases are not getting in the way of that thinking.
A dispatch is a piece of written communication — a message, report, or piece of news — that is sent urgently and officially from one place or person to another.
To dispatch means to send, handle, or deal with something quickly and with clear purpose. Think of it as doing something decisively — not lazily, not slowly, but with intention and efficiency.

To dispel something means to make it completely disappear — not by physically removing it, but by destroying its power over a person's mind. You dispel something by proving it wrong, addressing it directly, or shining a light on the truth.

Something is dispensable if you can remove it, get rid of it, or live without it — and nothing important falls apart as a result. It is not essential. It is not critical. The world (or the situation) carries on just fine without it.
A dispensary is a place where medicines, drugs, or other controlled substances are prepared and given out — or sold — to people who need them.
"Dispensation" is a word that always involves an authority of some kind — a church, a government, God, or an institution — making some kind of special arrangement.

Dispense means to give something out — but not in a casual, random way. It carries a sense of being controlled, measured, official, or systematic. When someone dispenses something, there is usually a system, a role, or an authority behind the act.
"Dispense with something" means to choose not to use something, or to get rid of something, often because it is unnecessary, inconvenient, or no longer needed.
To disperse means to spread out or scatter in multiple directions from one place, so that what was once gathered together is now spread apart.
Dispersed describes something that is spread out widely across a large area, rather than being gathered or concentrated in one place.

Dispersion means the spreading or scattering of things from a central point, or the state of being spread out across a wider space. Think of it as the opposite of things being bundled together — dispersion is when they fan out, drift apart, or scatter.
When someone is dispirited, they have lost their enthusiasm, hope, or inner drive — usually because of repeated disappointment, failure, or a situation that keeps beating them down.

Dispiriting describes something that causes you to lose your inner energy, hope, enthusiasm, or motivation. When something is dispiriting, it weakens your desire to try, to continue, or to believe that things will turn out well.
To push something out of the place it occupies, so that something else takes over that space or role.
In ordinary language, displacement means the act of something or someone being pushed out of its normal position or replaced by something else.
To play, frolic, or amuse oneself in a free, lively, and joyful way.

Disposable describes something that is meant to be used and then thrown away — it is not built to last, not meant to be kept, and not expected to be repaired or reused. The moment its purpose is served, it is discarded.

Disposal means the act of dealing with something definitively — removing it, settling it, or directing it in some way. The exact shade of meaning shifts based on context, but this central idea holds across all uses.

"Dispose" is about directing something or someone toward a particular outcome — whether that's getting rid of something, settling a matter, arranging things in a certain way, or influencing someone's attitude.
A person's natural character or temperament, as in "a cheerful disposition." It can also mean the arrangement of things, or the way something is dealt with or given away.
To dispossess someone means to forcibly take away their land, property, or home — leaving them without it.

Dispossession means the act of taking away something that someone owns, occupies, or has a rightful claim to — especially land, property, or a home — often by force, law, or power, and usually without the person's willing consent.
Disproportion is what happens when that balance breaks down — when one thing is too much or too little relative to another. It names the state of that mismatch, that imbalance of scale or degree.
Out of proportion — too much or too little relative to something else.
To disprove something means to demonstrate, through evidence or logic, that a claim or belief is false.

A disputation is a formal, structured debate or argument — usually between two or more people — where each side tries to defend their own position and challenge the other's, using logic and reasoning.
Disputatious means having a strong, habitual tendency to argue, debate, or challenge — often more than the situation actually calls for.

A dispute is a serious disagreement between two or more parties — people, groups, companies, or even countries — where each side holds a different view, claim, or position, and neither is willing to simply back down without a fight.

To disqualify someone means to officially declare that they are no longer allowed to participate in, compete for, or receive something — because they have either broken a rule, failed to meet a required condition, or have something about them that makes them unfit or ineligible.
Disquiet is a feeling of unease, worry, or inner disturbance — a quiet but persistent sense that something is not right, not settled, or troubling. It is the absence of peace in your mind.
Something that is disquieting causes a feeling of unease, anxiety, or worry — particularly the kind that settles into you and lingers.
Disquietude means a state of mental unease, restlessness, or anxiety — a feeling that something is wrong, uncertain, or troubling, and your mind simply cannot settle because of it.

A disquisition is a long, formal, and carefully organized piece of writing or speech that examines a subject in great depth and detail. Think of it as a serious, thorough investigation of a topic — put into words, either on paper or out loud.
Disregard means a lack of attention, care, or respect for something — treating something as if it simply does not matter, even when it does.

To disregard something means to deliberately pay no attention to it — to treat it as though it has no importance, no value, or no relevance to you, and therefore let it have no effect on what you think, say, or do.

When you call someone or something disreputable, you are saying that they are not respected or trusted by most people — and that this lack of respect is earned, because of bad, dishonest, or morally questionable behavior.

Disrepute means the state of being viewed poorly, distrusted, or looked down upon by people in general. When someone or something is in disrepute, they have lost the respect and good opinion of others — often publicly and widely.
Disrespect means a failure to treat someone or something with the honor, seriousness, or consideration they deserve.
To disrobe means to remove clothing — to undress.
To disrupt something means to break the normal flow or order of something that was running smoothly, causing it to slow down, stop, change course, or fall into confusion.

Disruptive means causing a break in the normal, smooth flow of something. Think of it this way: imagine a calm river flowing steadily. Now throw a large boulder into it. The water gets disturbed, the flow breaks apart, and nothing moves the way it did before.

Dissect means to carefully cut something apart in order to study it closely. Whether used literally or figuratively, the word always carries two key ideas together: cutting/breaking into parts, AND examining those parts closely.
Dissection is the act of carefully cutting something open or apart — piece by piece — so that you can study, understand, or examine what is inside it or how it is made up.
To dissemble means to hide your true feelings, thoughts, or intentions behind a false outward appearance.
To disseminate something means to spread information, knowledge, or ideas widely — to a large number of people or across a large area.
Dissemination means the act of spreading something widely so that it reaches many people or places.
Dissension means strong disagreement among people within the same group — disagreement serious enough to cause tension, conflict, or division between them.

Dissent means disagreement — but not just any ordinary disagreement. It specifically refers to the act of holding or expressing an opinion that goes against what the majority, an authority, or an official body believes or has decided.
To dissent means to hold and express an opinion that is different from — and opposed to — an officially accepted position, a majority decision, or the view of those in authority.

A dissenter is a person who disagrees with and openly refuses to accept an opinion, a decision, a belief, or a rule — especially one that is officially held, widely accepted, or supported by people in authority.

A dissertation is a very long, very detailed piece of writing that a person produces to earn an advanced academic degree — most commonly a doctoral degree (like a Ph.D.), and sometimes a master's degree.
When used as an adjective, dissident describes someone or something that openly disagrees with — and stands in active opposition to — an official, dominant, or authoritative position.

A dissident is a person who strongly and openly disagrees with the beliefs, rules, or actions of a powerful authority — most often a government, a political system, or an official institution — and who refuses to stay silent about it.
To dissimulate means to hide or disguise what you truly feel, think, believe, or intend — so that other people cannot see your real inner state.

Dissimulation means the act of hiding your true feelings, thoughts, intentions, or character — while outwardly appearing normal, calm, or even the opposite of what you actually are. It is the deliberate concealment of one's inner reality.
To dissipate means to gradually break apart, spread out, and disappear — or to cause something to do that.
Describes a person whose health, looks, and character have been visibly damaged by years of heavy drinking, gambling, and other excessive pleasures.

Dissipation describes the process by which something that was gathered, concentrated, or whole gradually breaks apart, spreads out thinly in all directions, and eventually disappears or becomes so weakened that it is effectively gone.
Living a life of excessive pleasure-seeking — drinking, gambling, or sexual indulgence — without moral restraint.
Dissolution means the process of something breaking apart, coming undone, or ceasing to exist as a whole thing.

Dissonance means a clash — a jarring lack of harmony between things that are forced together but don't fit. Think of it as the feeling of wrongness you get when things that should work together simply don't.

Dissonant means clashing, conflicting, or failing to fit together in a way that feels jarring or uncomfortable. Something dissonant doesn't belong, doesn't agree, or doesn't blend — it sticks out in a way that creates tension.
To dissuade someone means to talk them out of doing something — to use words, reasoning, or arguments to convince a person not to do something they were planning or seriously considering.
Dissuasion is the act of trying to convince someone not to do something — through reasoning, arguments, or appeals — rather than by force or rules.
A distaff is a simple, elongated stick or staff — usually around two to three feet long — that was used as a tool in the ancient craft of hand-spinning fiber into thread or yarn.
Distal means situated farther away from a point of reference — usually farther from the center of the body, the trunk, or the point where something attaches or originates.
"Distant" describes a significant gap or separation — between you and something else. That gap can be physical space, time, emotional closeness, or even mental attention.

Distaste is a feeling of mild dislike, disapproval, or aversion toward something. It's the quiet, controlled version of not liking something — not explosive anger, not deep hatred, but a noticeable sense of "I find this unpleasant or wrong."

To distend means to expand, stretch, or swell outward because of pressure coming from inside. When something distends, its walls, skin, or surface are being pushed outward by whatever is building up within it — gas, liquid, food, or any other substance.
To distill something means to take a large, complex, or mixed thing and carefully extract only the most pure, essential, and valuable part of it — leaving behind everything that is unnecessary.

Distillation is about taking something mixed or impure, applying a process, and ending up with something purer, more concentrated, and more essential. Everything non-essential is left behind. What remains is the core of what you were after.
A distillery is a place — a factory or a building — where alcoholic spirits are made using a process called distillation.
Distinct means something that stands clearly apart — either because it is clearly different from something else, or because it is clearly noticeable on its own.
Distinction carries two related but separate meanings. Both share the idea of something standing apart from something else — either because it is different, or because it is better.
Something is "distinctive" when it has a quality so noticeable and recognizable that it clearly sets it apart from everything else of the same kind.

To distinguish means to recognize or notice a difference. When you distinguish something, you are either: spotting what makes one thing different from another, or being the thing that creates that difference.

Distinguished means standing out from the ordinary in a quiet, admirable, and impressive way. It is not about being loud, flashy, or just popular. It is about being noticeably above average — in a way that earns genuine respect and admiration from others.
To distort something means to change it in a way that twists, bends, or warps it so far from its original, true form that it becomes inaccurate, misleading, or unrecognizable.
Something is distorted when it has been twisted, bent, or pulled away from its true, natural, or original form — making it look, sound, or feel wrong, warped, or inaccurate.
Distortion means a change or twist away from what something originally was, or what it truly is — in a way that makes it inaccurate, warped, or misleading.
To distract someone means to pull their attention away from what they are focused on, and redirect it toward something else.

When a person is distracted, their attention has been pulled away — either by something happening around them, or by thoughts inside their own head — so they cannot focus properly on what they are doing or what is in front of them.

A distraction is anything that pulls your attention away from what you are currently doing, thinking, or focusing on — especially when you did not intend for that to happen, or when you would rather stay focused.
Distrait means being mentally absent from your present surroundings because your mind is absorbed elsewhere — typically by worry, anxiety, or deep preoccupation with something troubling or consuming.
When someone is distraught, they are so deeply upset and emotionally overwhelmed that they can barely think clearly or keep themselves together. It is not just feeling sad, nervous, or worried.

Distress means a state of serious suffering or trouble — a condition where someone (or something) is experiencing pain, danger, anxiety, or hardship that is difficult or impossible to bear alone. It's not a mild feeling.

When you use "distress" as a verb, it means to cause someone pain, worry, or suffering — not physical pain from a punch or a cut, but the kind of pain that happens inside a person: emotional pain, mental anguish, or deep anxiety.
To distribute means to take something and spread it out to multiple people, places, or parts — moving it from one source to many destinations.
Distribution means the way something is spread out, shared, or delivered across multiple places, people, or points in time.
Something that interrupts peace, order, or normal functioning, as in "a disturbance in the night." It can also mean a riot or public disorder, or a mental or emotional disorder.

Disused describes something that was used regularly in the past but is no longer used today. The thing still exists — it hasn't been destroyed — but people have stopped using it, and it now sits idle.

A ditch is a long, narrow channel dug into the ground. Think of it as a man-made groove or trench carved into the earth, usually running in a straight line along the side of a road, field, or piece of land.

To dither means to hesitate — but not in a calm, thoughtful way. It means to be caught in nervous, flustered indecision, going back and forth without being able to commit to a choice. When someone dithers, they're not simply pausing to think carefully.
A ditty is a short, simple song — the kind that is easy to sing, easy to remember, and doesn't take itself too seriously. It's not a grand performance piece.
Diurnal has two closely related meanings: 1. Relating to, or happening during, the daytime; 2. Happening once a day, or recurring every single day.
A diva is either a supremely celebrated female performer — or a person who is outrageously demanding and difficult because they believe they are extraordinarily special.

To divagate means to wander away from where you are supposed to be — either physically off a path, or mentally off a topic. Think of it as straying. You start somewhere, and then you drift, you lose the thread, you end up somewhere else.
If you picture a neat, low bed where the "box" underneath the mattress is fully padded and covered in fabric, that is a divan bed.
To diverge means to move apart, go in different directions, or become increasingly different — usually starting from a common point or a shared path.

Divergence means the act, process, or result of moving apart, spreading outward, or becoming increasingly different. Think of it as the opposite of things coming together — it is things going their separate ways.
Moving apart from a common point, or becoming increasingly different, as in "divergent opinions."

Diverse means made up of many different kinds of people, things, or ideas — not just one kind, or types that are all very similar to each other. When a group is diverse, it contains rich, meaningful variety among its members.

A diversion means turning something away from where it was originally headed. Think of a river that normally flows straight, but someone builds a wall and forces the water to flow in a different direction. That act — and the new path — is a diversion.
Diversity means the presence of many different types, kinds, or varieties of things existing together in the same place, group, or system.
Divert means to deliberately turn something — or someone — away from its original path and send it in a new direction.
If something is diverting, it is pleasantly entertaining or amusing — it captures your attention in a light, enjoyable way and gives you a welcome break from boredom, routine, or serious matters.
Divest means to deliberately remove, strip away, or get rid of something — whether that something is money, power, property, or even an abstract thing like responsibility.
Divide means to take something whole and break it into two or more separate parts. Think of it as drawing a line — real or imaginary — through something so that what was one becomes many.
A share of a company's profits paid to its shareholders. Figuratively, a benefit that comes later from something you did, as in "the investment paid dividends."
Divination is the practice of trying to discover hidden knowledge — especially about the future, or about something unknown or secret — through supernatural or mystical means.
When "divine" is used as a noun, it refers to a person of the clergy or a theologian — someone who has dedicated their life to the study, teaching, or practice of religious faith.

To divine something means to discover or figure out something hidden, unknown, or unclear — not by being told directly, and not through obvious logic, but through a special kind of sensing, intuition, or supernatural power.
When something is divisive, it causes people to split into opposing sides. It creates sharp disagreement, tension, or conflict — pulling people apart rather than bringing them together.
Divisiveness is the quality of causing people to split into opposing groups that disagree with, resent, or conflict with each other.

A divot is a small chunk of earth — grass, soil, and roots all stuck together — that gets scooped or torn out of the ground, leaving a little hollow behind. Think of it as a bite taken out of the ground.
To divulge something means to reveal or share information that was previously private, secret, or confidential.
"Divvy up" means to divide something into portions and share those portions among a group of people.

To do a number on someone or something means to harm, damage, hurt, or have a strong negative effect on someone or something — physically, emotionally, or psychologically. It can also mean to deceive, manipulate, or trick someone in a harmful way.
An informal phrase: to kill someone, or to exhaust someone completely ("That hike really did me in").
"Do one's bidding" means to carry out someone's orders, wishes, or commands, usually because you are under their control, authority, or influence.
A docent is a person who leads guided tours and provides educational explanations at a place like a museum, art gallery, zoo, botanical garden, historical site, or science center.
Docile means naturally easy to control, teach, or manage. A docile person or animal tends to follow instructions without arguing, resisting, or causing trouble.
A docket is an official list or schedule of things that need to be dealt with. Think of it as a formal "to-do list" — but one that belongs to an institution, not a person.

A doctorate is the highest level of academic degree that a university can award to a person. Think of it as the final, most advanced certificate of learning and expertise in a particular field of study. There is no academic degree above it.

When we call someone or something doctrinaire, we mean they are rigidly, inflexibly devoted to a theory or set of beliefs — and they apply that theory mechanically, no matter what the real world is actually telling them.

A doctrinaire is a person who holds a set of principles or theories so rigidly that they insist on applying them to every situation — regardless of whether doing so actually works, causes harm, or flies in the face of reality.
A doctrine is a set of beliefs, principles, or rules that a group officially accepts, teaches, and follows.

A document is a piece of recorded information. The key word here is recorded — it means the information has been fixed in some form so that it can be preserved, referred to, shared, or used later. A thought in your head is not a document.
Based on or consisting of documents and factual records, as in "documentary evidence." It can also describe a film or programme that presents facts about real events.

A documentary is a film, video, or television program that is about real things — real events, real people, real places, or real issues. Nothing in it is invented for the purpose of entertainment. It is the opposite of fiction.

Documentation is any written, recorded, or organized material that captures information — so that the information can be understood, used, referred back to, or proven later. Think of it as "putting things down in a form that lasts and communicates."

Doddering is an adjective that describes a person — almost always an elderly one — who has become noticeably weak, shaky, and mentally slow due to old age. It paints a picture of someone whose body and mind are both clearly in decline.

"Doddery" describes a person — almost always an elderly one — who moves in a slow, shaky, and unsteady way. Think of someone who shuffles rather than walks, whose hands tremble slightly, and who looks as though they might lose their balance with each step.
To dodge something means to avoid it — quickly, cleverly, or both.
Dishonest or suspicious, as in "a dodgy deal" (British informal). It can also mean unreliable or in poor condition, as in "a dodgy knee," or risky and dangerous.
To doff something means to take it off or to remove it — most often a hat, but also other items of clothing or gear.

Dogged means refusing to stop or give up, no matter how hard things get. It describes a steady, grinding kind of determination — the kind that keeps a person going even when they are tired, failing, or facing something very difficult.
Doggedly means doing something with stubborn, relentless determination — continuing even when it is very difficult, painful, or seems hopeless.

Doggerel is a word for a specific kind of bad poetry — verse that is clumsily written, poorly crafted, and lacking real artistic skill. When someone calls a piece of writing "doggerel," they mean it as a criticism.

A dogma is a belief — or a set of beliefs — that is declared to be absolutely, certainly true by some authority, and that you are expected to accept without question, without proof, and without debate.

When you call someone or something dogmatic, you mean they hold their beliefs or opinions with such strong, unshakeable certainty that they refuse to consider any other point of view — even when faced with good reasons or evidence to think differently.

Dogmatism is the tendency to hold your beliefs as absolutely and certainly true — and to refuse to question, examine, or reconsider them, no matter what evidence, arguments, or perspectives are presented to you.
A dogsbody is a person who is given all the dull, lowly, and unwanted tasks that nobody else wants to do.
A doily is a small, flat, decorative mat placed underneath objects — either to make things look prettier or to protect a surface.
When someone or something is in the doldrums, it means they are stuck in a state of gloom, low energy, boredom, or stagnation — with little to no progress, excitement, or motivation happening.
"Dole out" means to give or distribute something to people, usually in small amounts, and often with a sense of control or carefulness.
Doleful means deeply sad, mournful, and full of sorrow — and expressing that sadness in a way that is clearly visible or clearly felt by others.
A dollop is a small, soft, rounded blob or lump of something — usually a thick, creamy, or semi-liquid substance. It is not a precise amount. It is a casual, rough, "eyeballed" quantity.

The simplest meaning: a dolly is just a doll — a toy shaped like a human figure, typically used by young children. It is a soft, affectionate word that small children and adults speaking to small children use.

Dolorous means deeply sad, mournful, or full of grief and suffering. It describes either a feeling of heavy sorrow inside a person, or the outward expression of that sorrow — the kind you can see or hear in someone's face, voice, or behaviour.
A dolt is a person who is noticeably slow-witted, foolish, or lacking in basic intelligence or common sense.
Doltish means stupidly slow to understand things, hopelessly dim-witted, and embarrassingly foolish in thinking or behavior.
"Domain" means a defined space, area, or territory that belongs to something or someone, or within which something operates, applies, or has authority.
The single most important thing to know about this word is that "domestic" always points to some kind of home.

Domestication is the long, gradual process by which humans take wild animals or wild plants and — over many generations — change them so that they live with humans, serve human purposes, and reproduce under human control.

A domicile is a person's permanent home — the place they legally and officially consider their fixed, primary place of residence. Think of it as the address the world officially recognizes as "yours" in the most permanent and legal sense.
Dominance means the state or condition of having power, control, or superior influence over others — or over a situation.

"Dominant" describes something — or someone — that has the most power, influence, or presence in a particular situation or group. It stands clearly above everything else around it. It controls, shapes, or overshadows the others.

Dominate means to have so much power, strength, or influence over someone or something that you clearly stand above all others. When something or someone dominates, they are not just ahead — they are far ahead.
Domination means having complete and powerful control over someone or something — in a way where the one being controlled has very little freedom, choice, or ability to resist.

To domineer means to control or order others around in a harsh, overbearing, and arrogant way — without any respect for their feelings, opinions, or rights. It is always about abusing power or authority, not simply having it.

Someone who is domineering wants to be in control of other people — and they push for that control in a forceful, aggressive way that leaves little room for others to have their own voice, make their own choices, or express their own opinions.
"Dominion" means complete, supreme, and unchallengeable authority or control over something or someone.

The domino theory is the belief that if one country falls under the control of a political ideology — especially communism — then the neighboring countries around it will also fall, one by one, like a row of dominoes toppling each other.
In British English, a don is a senior teacher, lecturer, or academic at a university — especially at famous universities like Oxford and Cambridge.
A sharp way of telling someone that they are wrong to think so highly of themselves, as in "don't flatter yourself — I wasn't talking about you."
"Don't meet trouble halfway" means do not worry about problems that haven't happened yet. Do not waste your mental and emotional energy suffering over things that might go wrong in the future.
"Don't sweat it" means don't worry about it or it's not a big deal. You say it to calm someone down when they are stressed, anxious, or feeling guilty about something.

To donate means to give something to someone or an organization freely, with no expectation of getting anything back in return. The giving is permanent — you are not lending, not selling, not trading. You are simply giving, out of goodwill.
When you say something is "a done deal," you mean it is completely decided, settled, and finished — and most importantly, it cannot be changed or reversed.
A donor is a person — or sometimes an organization or country — who gives something to someone else, usually to help them, and typically without expecting anything of equal value in return.

A doodle is a simple, casual drawing that a person makes without much thought or intention — often while their attention is completely focused on something else. It's not a planned artwork. It just... happens.

To doodle means to draw casually and without a specific plan or serious intention. It is drawing done in a relaxed, aimless, almost automatic way — not to create a finished piece of art, but simply because your hand feels like moving.

Doom means an unavoidable terrible fate — most often death, total destruction, or complete ruin. The single most important thing to understand about this word is the element of inevitability. Doom isn't just something bad that might happen.

If someone or something is doomed, it means a bad ending is certain — or nearly certain — and cannot be avoided. The bad outcome has, in a sense, already been decided. Nothing can stop it from happening.
A doomsayer is a person who constantly predicts that terrible things are going to happen — disasters, failures, collapse, or the end of something important.

The Doomsday argument is a philosophical thought experiment that claims: based purely on the fact that you exist right now, and nothing else, you can statistically estimate when humanity will go extinct.
A doozy is something that is strikingly extraordinary — something that stands out so strongly from the ordinary that it demands to be noticed or remarked upon.
Dopamine is a chemical messenger produced naturally inside your body.

A doppelganger is a double of a person — someone or something that is an eerie, striking copy of someone else. Think of it as a "second version" of a person that exists somewhere out there, looking and perhaps acting just like them.

The Doppler effect is the change in the frequency of a wave — sound, light, or any other wave — that an observer experiences because the source of the wave and the observer are moving relative to each other.

Doraphobia is a deep dread of touching the skin or fur of an animal. It is not just a mild dislike or discomfort — it is a genuine, intense fear that goes far beyond what most people would consider a normal reaction.

A dork is a person who is socially awkward, out of touch with what is considered "cool," and often unaware of — or completely unbothered by — this fact. The word is informal and belongs to everyday casual speech.

A dorm is a building where students live while they study at a college or university. It is simply a place provided by the school for students to stay in — their home away from home during their academic life.

Dormancy means a state of temporary inactivity — a pause in life, growth, or function. Something in dormancy is not dead, not destroyed, and not finished. It is simply waiting, held in a kind of deep stillness, until the right conditions return to wake it up.

Dormant describes something that is alive and real, but currently in a deep state of rest or inactivity — not doing what it normally does, not showing itself, yet fully capable of becoming active again when the right conditions arrive.

A dormer is a structure that pokes outward from a sloping roof, and it always contains a window. Think of it as a small "bump-out" or projection built into a slanted roof, with its own mini-walls and its own small roof on top — and a window facing outward.
A dormitory is a place designed for many people to sleep and live together, all under one roof.
Dorsal means "of, on, or relating to the back or upper surface" of a body or a body part.
The word dory has two completely separate meanings as a noun — one is a type of boat, and the other is a type of fish. Here's everything you need to know about both.
A dose is a specific, measured amount of something — most often a medicine, drug, or chemical — that is meant to be taken or given at one time.

A dossier is a carefully assembled collection of documents, records, and information all focused on one specific subject — most often a particular person, but sometimes an event, organization, or case.
Dotage refers to a period in a person's life — usually very old age — when their mind has grown weak, slow, or confused.
A dotard is an old person whose mind has become so weakened by age that they can no longer think clearly, reason sensibly, or function mentally as they once could.

To dote means to love or adore someone (or something) deeply — but not just normally deeply. It means your love and affection for that person is so strong that it almost goes beyond reason. You are completely, overwhelmingly fond of them.

To dote on someone means to love someone so deeply and so excessively that you lavish them with attention, affection, and care — often to the point where you overlook their faults or weaknesses completely.

When someone is doting, they love a person so deeply and so completely that they become almost blind to that person's faults. Their affection is not just strong — it is overflowing, soft, and forgiving to the point of indulgence.
To become even more committed to a risky position or belief, especially when others think it is wrong. The term comes from the card game blackjack.
A double whammy means two bad things happening together or one after another, creating a combined negative effect that is much worse than either one would have been alone.

A double-barreled adjective describes something that has two parts, two actions, or two effects — often happening together or aimed at the same target. The word carries a sense of doubled force, doubled purpose, or simply two-in-one.
Something is "double-sided" when both of its sides are usable, active, or meaningful — not just one. The word signals that neither face is blank, empty, or wasted.
A doublet is a snug, close-fitting jacket worn by men in Europe, roughly from the 1300s to the 1600s.

When you doubt something, you are not fully sure about it. You feel uncertain — your mind hasn't settled on whether something is true, real, correct, or trustworthy. You hold a question in your head rather than a firm answer.
A douche is a stream or jet of liquid — usually water or a water-based solution — that is directed into a part of the body to clean it from the inside.

Doughty means brave, strong, and determined — especially in a way that doesn't quit. A doughty person faces difficulty head-on, keeps going even when things get hard, and does not back down from a fight or a challenge.
A doula is a trained, non-medical support person who helps someone through a major life event — most commonly childbirth, but also the period after birth, or even the process of dying.

Dour describes someone (or something) that is stern, gloomy, and completely without warmth or humor. It is not just a bad mood — it is more like a permanent personality. A dour person carries a sense of harshness and joylessness about them at all times.

To douse something is to cover it or flood it with liquid — usually water — suddenly and thoroughly. Picture someone grabbing a bucket of water and throwing it over something all at once. That's the spirit of "douse."

A dovetail is a type of joint — a connection point used to join two pieces of wood together. It gets its name from its shape: it looks exactly like the spread tail of a dove. A dove's tail is narrow where it meets the body and fans out wider at the tips.

When two things dovetail, they fit together so neatly, precisely, and seamlessly that they almost seem designed for each other — like two puzzle pieces that click together without any gap, overlap, or wasted space.
A dowager is a widow who keeps the noble or royal title she had through her husband, even after he has died and someone else has taken over his position.

Something or someone that is dowdy looks dull, unfashionable, and lacking any sense of style — not because they are dirty or poor, but simply because their appearance feels old, boring, and out of touch with modern taste.

Down-at-heel is an adjective used to describe someone or something that looks shabby, poor, and neglected — as if they were once in a better condition but have since fallen into hard times and can no longer maintain a decent appearance.
Sad, discouraged, and low in spirits. Of eyes, looking downward, often in sadness or shame.
To downplay something means to make it seem less important, less serious, or less significant than it actually is.
The downside of something is the negative part of it — what's bad, what you lose, what could go wrong, or what you have to sacrifice.
If someone is downtrodden, they are treated so badly and kept so powerless — usually by people stronger, richer, or more powerful than them — that they can barely stand up for themselves.
A downturn is a period during which something — most often an economy, a business, or an industry — becomes weaker, worse, or less successful than it was before.
Soft, fine, and fluffy, like the small feathers of a young bird, as in "a downy chick" or "downy hair."
A dowry is the money, property, goods, or assets that a bride's family gives to the groom (or his family) at the time of marriage.
When someone dowses, they walk slowly over land while holding a forked stick, a pair of bent metal rods, or a pendulum.
A doze is a short, light sleep — the kind where you're not fully asleep, and you can be woken up very easily.
"Doze off" means to gradually and gently fall asleep, usually without planning to.
It describes something that is depressingly dull — either in actual color, or in character and feel.
Most people know "drab" as an adjective — describing something dull and lifeless. But as a noun, it carries distinct, specific meanings that are worth understanding carefully.
Draconian describes something — a law, a rule, a punishment, a policy, or a measure — that is excessively and unreasonably harsh or severe, far beyond what the situation actually calls for.
A first, rough version of a piece of writing. A draft is also a current of cold air in a room, or a written order for a bank to pay money.
To write a first version of something, such as a letter, law, or speech. It also means to select someone for compulsory military service, or, in sport, to choose a player for a team.

Drafty is an adjective used to describe an enclosed space — like a room, a house, a hallway, or a building — where cold air sneaks in through cracks, gaps, and openings, making the inside uncomfortably chilly even though you're technically "inside."
A dragnet is a method of capturing something — or someone — by casting a wide net and sweeping an entire area, so that nothing can easily escape.

Dragon fruit is a tropical fruit that grows on a type of cactus plant. It is widely known for its strikingly unusual appearance — it looks almost like something out of a fantasy story, which is likely why it was named after dragons.

Drama is about stories told through action and speech — performed by people, not just read on a page. From this core idea, the word has grown to cover several related meanings. Here they all are, clearly explained.
Dramatic is an adjective with three distinct meanings, all connected to the idea of drama — something intense, emotional, and larger than ordinary life. Here is each meaning explained fully.

Drastic means extreme, severe, and having a very strong or powerful effect. When something is drastic, it goes far beyond normal, moderate, or gentle — it is bold, forceful, and usually difficult to ignore or reverse.

To drat something means to mildly curse it — to direct a small, harmless expression of frustration or annoyance at something. Think of it as the verbal equivalent of lightly shaking your fist at something that has annoyed you.
A draught is something being drawn, pulled, or flowing. That one idea — of drawing or pulling — quietly connects all the different meanings this word carries.
At its deepest level, draw means to pull something, or to move something by pulling. Almost every meaning of this word grows from that one root idea.
Literally, "draw the blinds" simply means to close the window blinds or curtains — to pull them across so that people outside cannot see in, and to block light from coming through.

A drawl is a slow, stretched way of speaking where the vowel sounds inside words are held longer than usual — almost like the speaker is gently pulling the sounds out of their mouth instead of saying them cleanly and quickly.
To drawl means to speak in a slow, lazy-sounding way by stretching out the vowel sounds in your words, making them last much longer than they normally would.
"Drawn-out" describes something that lasts much longer than it needs to, or longer than feels natural and comfortable. The emphasis is not simply on length — it's on excessive length.
A dray is a low, flat, heavy cart — built specifically for hauling large, heavy loads from one place to another. Think of it as a strong, no-frills platform on wheels.

Dread is a deep, heavy feeling of fear about something bad that is going to happen — or that you believe is going to happen. It is not the fear you feel when something frightening is right in front of you. It is the fear you feel before it arrives.
To dread something means to feel a deep, heavy fear or anxiety about something that is going to happen — or that you think might happen — in the future.

Dreadful means extremely bad, unpleasant, or upsetting — so much so that it causes a heavy, sinking feeling inside you. Think of it as "bad" turned all the way up. It's not just bad; it's the kind of bad that makes you wince, recoil, or feel deeply disturbed.

"Dream" as a verb describes what your mind does when it steps away from present, practical reality — either involuntarily while you sleep, or deliberately when you let yourself imagine things you wish for.

Something is dreary when it is dull, gloomy, and depressing in a way that drags you down and makes the world feel heavy, colorless, and lifeless. It is not a sharp, sudden sadness — it is more like a gray fog that hangs over everything and refuses to lift.
To scoop mud, sand, or rubbish from the bottom of a river or harbour. To dredge up something means to bring back an unpleasant memory or fact from the past.
"Dredge up" means to bring back something from the past that was buried, forgotten, or deliberately left alone — usually something unpleasant, painful, or uncomfortable.
Dregs are the part nobody wants. They're what's left after all the good stuff has been used or consumed. They represent the lowest point — literally the bottom — of something.
To drench means to make something or someone completely and thoroughly wet — not just a little damp, but soaked all the way through, as if liquid has penetrated every part.
A dribble is a small, thin, slow trickle of liquid. It is not a flow, not a stream, not a splash — it is the tiniest, most sluggish version of liquid moving. Think of it as the opposite of a flood.
To drift means to move slowly and gently, carried by a force outside your control, rather than moving by your own effort or decision.
A drip is a single, small drop of liquid that falls from something. Think of a leaky tap, a melting ice cream cone, or rain falling from a leaf — each tiny drop of water that falls is a drip.
"To drive a wedge between" means to deliberately cause conflict, suspicion, or distance between two people (or groups) who were previously close or united.

Drivel is talk or writing that is so stupid, pointless, or empty that it has no real value whatsoever. It is content that wastes your time and insults your intelligence. Think of it as words that add up to absolutely nothing.

A droid is a robot — an artificial, mechanical being built and programmed by humans (or other intelligent beings) to perform tasks. What sets a droid apart from a simple machine or appliance is that a droid possesses some degree of artificial intelligence.
Droll means funny, but in a quiet, odd, and understated way — the kind of funny that makes you smile or give a small, surprised chuckle rather than burst out laughing.

Drollery refers to a particular kind of humor — one that is quiet, dry, gently odd, and quietly amusing. It is the quality of being funny in a whimsical, understated, slightly peculiar way, without being loud, obvious, or trying too hard.

A dromedary is a type of camel — specifically, the camel with one hump on its back. Its scientific name is Camelus dromedarius. That single hump is the most important detail: it is what sets the dromedary apart from the Bactrian camel, which has two humps.

To drone means to make a continuous, low, flat, unchanging sound — the kind that goes on and on at the same pitch and volume without rising, falling, or stopping. Think of the steady hum of bees around a flower, or the buzz of an airplane engine far overhead.
When someone drones on, they talk for a very long time in a dull, flat, and boring way — usually without noticing (or caring) that the people listening have lost interest.
To droop means to bend or hang downward from a position that was once upright or lifted — usually because of weakness, tiredness, heaviness, or a loss of energy or life.
When something is drooping, it is bending or hanging downward in a way that suggests weakness, heaviness, tiredness, or a loss of energy and support.

"A drop in the ocean" means a very small amount compared to what is actually needed or what actually exists. It describes something so tiny and insignificant that it makes practically no real difference to the bigger situation.
To "drop the ball" means to make a mistake by failing to do something you were responsible for, especially at an important moment. It means you let someone down by not doing your part properly.
Something worthless, especially among things of value; rubbish. Literally, the waste that rises to the surface when metal is melted.
A drought is a long period of time during which there is much less water — especially rainfall — than a place normally receives, causing serious shortages.
To drown out means to make a sound so loud that it completely covers another sound, making that other sound impossible to hear.
Drowsy describes a state where a person (or sometimes an animal) is not fully awake, but not fully asleep either — they are caught somewhere in between.
"Drub" has two closely connected meanings. Both share the same core idea: overwhelming, one-sided force.
A drubbing is a thorough, one-sided defeat or beating — one so complete that there is no doubt whatsoever about who won and who lost. It is not a close call, not a narrow loss, and not a fair fight.

A drudge is a person whose life is filled with hard, exhausting, and deeply boring work — the kind of work that is low-status, repetitive, and thankless. Nobody praises a drudge. Nobody notices a drudge.
Drudgery means hard, boring, repetitive work that feels exhausting and joyless — work you have to do, but that gives you no pleasure, no excitement, and often feels pointless or beneath you.

A drunkard is a person who drinks alcohol excessively and repeatedly, as a fixed habit in their life. The key idea here is habit — not someone who occasionally drinks too much, but someone for whom drinking heavily is a regular, ongoing pattern of behavior.
"Drunken" means affected by alcohol to the point where your thinking, behavior, or body no longer works normally.
A dryad is a female tree spirit from ancient Greek mythology.

To dub means to give someone or something a name, title, or label — usually one that is new, unofficial, or chosen to capture something special about them. It also has a few other distinct meanings in specific contexts.

Dubiety means doubt — but it's a richer, more layered word than plain "doubt." It refers to either: 1. A feeling or state of uncertainty in someone's mind, or 2. A quality of being doubtful or questionable that belongs to a thing itself.
Dubious is all about doubt. When something is dubious, there is a real reason to question it — to not fully trust it, not fully believe it, or not feel sure about it.
Dubiously means in a way that involves doubt — either someone is feeling doubt, or something is causing doubt (because it seems questionable or suspicious).

A ducat is a gold coin that was once used as real money across most of Europe. Think of it the way you think of a currency note today — except it was a small, round piece of solid gold, and its value came directly from the gold it was made of.
A duck is a medium-sized bird that lives in and around water. It is one of the most widely recognized birds in the world, found on almost every continent except Antarctica.

When we call a material ductile, we mean it can be pulled, stretched, or drawn out into a thin wire without snapping, cracking, or falling apart. The material changes its shape permanently under this pulling force, but holds together throughout the process.

Ductility is the ability of a material — almost always a solid, and most commonly a metal — to be permanently stretched, pulled, or drawn out into a longer or thinner shape without cracking or breaking.
A dud is something — or someone — that fails to do what it is supposed to do. It looks like it should work. It was meant to work. But when the moment comes, it simply doesn't. It lets you down.

Dudgeon means a strong feeling of deep offence, resentment, or wounded indignation. It describes the emotional state of someone who feels they have been insulted, disrespected, or treated unfairly — and who is very unhappy about it.

Due process means that the government must follow fair, established rules and procedures before it can take away your life, freedom, or property. It's essentially a guarantee that the state cannot act against you in an arbitrary, sudden, or unfair way.
A duenna is an older woman who is appointed to watch over, accompany, and protect a younger, unmarried woman — essentially a live-in chaperone and guardian rolled into one.

The word dugout is a noun that refers to things that have been made by digging out or hollowing out something — either the ground itself, or a solid object. It has three distinct, well-established meanings.

"Dulcet" describes a sound that is sweet, soft, and pleasing to the ear. Think of it as the opposite of harsh, sharp, or grating. A dulcet sound flows gently and smoothly, making the listener feel calm, soothed, or charmed.

Something is dull when it is less than it should be — less sharp, less bright, less interesting, less lively, less intense. Almost every meaning of this word carries the same spirit: something important is missing or reduced.

A dullard is a person who is notably slow-witted, unintelligent, or mentally unresponsive. When you call someone a dullard, you mean they are dim, thick-headed, and consistently fail to grasp things that most people would understand without much effort.
Duly means "in exactly the way it should be done — at the right time, in the right manner, and to the right degree."
To dumb something down means to make something simpler, easier to understand, or less intellectually demanding — usually so that a wider or less-educated audience can understand it.
To dumbfound someone means to shock or surprise them so completely and so suddenly that they are left speechless — unable to speak, move, or react, even for just a moment.
Dumbfounded means being so completely and overwhelmingly shocked or surprised that you are momentarily unable to speak, react, or even think clearly. It is not just ordinary surprise.
Dumbstruck means so shocked or amazed that you suddenly cannot speak.
A model or copy of something, used as a substitute, such as a shop mannequin or a practice weapon. Informally, a stupid person. In British English, a dummy is also a baby's rubber pacifier.
Dun describes a color — specifically, a dull, muted, grayish-brown. It sits somewhere between gray and brown, but without the warmth or richness of either. It is flat, faded, and lifeless-looking.

A dunce is a person who is considered slow to learn, dim-witted, or simply not very intelligent. When you call someone a dunce, you are saying that they struggle to understand things that most people grasp without much difficulty.
A dune is a hill or mound of loose sand that has been built and shaped entirely by wind.
Dung is the solid waste that comes out of an animal's body after it has digested food — in other words, an animal's feces or excrement.
A dungeon is a dark, underground prison room or cell — typically found beneath a castle, fortress, or large stone building — where prisoners are held captive, often in terrible conditions.

The Dunning-Kruger effect is a psychological phenomenon where people who know very little about something tend to overestimate how much they know, while people who know a lot tend to underestimate their own expertise.

A dupe is a person who has been tricked, deceived, or manipulated by someone else — usually without realizing it. The dupe is always the victim in the situation, not the villain. They are the one being fooled, while someone else is doing the fooling.
To dupe someone means to trick them into believing something false, or into doing something they would never agree to if they knew the truth.

When you duplicate something, you make an exact copy of it — a copy so precise that it matches the original in every important way. The result is two things that are essentially identical: the original, and its duplicate.
When someone is duplicitous, they are deliberately showing one face to the world while secretly having a completely different set of intentions, feelings, or loyalties underneath.
Duplicity means the act of deliberately deceiving someone by showing them one face while secretly having a completely different one.
Durable describes something that can last a long time and hold up well under regular use, stress, or the passage of time — without breaking down, wearing out, or losing its quality.
Durance means imprisonment — specifically, being forcibly confined or held captive, often for a long period and under harsh or degrading conditions.
Duration means how long something lasts — from the moment it begins to the moment it ends.
Duress means pressure, threats, or force used to make someone do something against their will.

Dusky means softly dark or somewhat dark — not completely black, not fully bright, but somewhere in that gentle, in-between zone. Think of the sky just after the sun sets. It's not night yet, but the brightness is fading.

A dustup is an informal word for a brief, heated conflict between people — one that flares up suddenly, gets intense for a moment, and then settles down. It sits somewhere between a sharp argument and a minor physical fight.

"Duteous" describes someone who faithfully and obediently performs their duties. If a person is duteous, they do what is expected of them — their responsibilities, obligations, and tasks — willingly, carefully, and without resistance.
Dutiful describes a person who reliably and conscientiously does what is expected of them — based on their role, their responsibilities, or their obligations to others.
"Dutifully" describes how a person does something — specifically, in a way that shows they feel a sense of duty, obligation, or responsibility to do it.
A duvet is a type of soft, thick bed covering — essentially a large, flat bag stuffed with filling — that you lay on top of yourself while sleeping to stay warm.
The word "dwarf" as a noun has three distinct, well-established meanings — one about people, one about mythology and fiction, and one about science.
To live in a place (formal or literary). To dwell on something means to keep thinking or talking about it, especially something unpleasant, as in "don't dwell on your mistakes."

To dwell on someone or something means to spend a long time thinking, talking, or writing about a particular person or thing — especially when doing so is unhelpful, unnecessary, or emotionally painful.

To dwindle means to gradually become smaller, fewer, or weaker over a period of time — often to the point of being nearly gone. Think of a candle burning down hour by hour. It doesn't disappear all at once.

When something is dwindling, it is gradually becoming smaller, fewer, weaker, or less — and the process is still happening. It hasn't reached zero yet, but it's heading that way, slowly and continuously.
