Dynamic means full of energy, constant movement, or ongoing change — as opposed to anything still, fixed, or passive. If something is dynamic, it is alive with activity. It doesn't sit still; it pushes, shifts, evolves, or drives forward.
"Dynamics" refers to the forces, interactions, and patterns that drive change, movement, or behavior in a system.
Dynamism means the quality of being full of energy, force, and constant activity that drives change and progress.
A dynamo is a machine that generates electricity by converting mechanical energy — the energy of physical movement — into electrical energy.
Relating to a dynasty — a line of rulers from the same family, with power passed down through generations.
A dynasty is a line of rulers — kings, queens, emperors, or other leaders — who all belong to the same family, and who hold power one after another, across multiple generations.
Dysentery is a serious infection of the intestines — specifically the large intestine (also called the colon) — that causes severe, painful diarrhea containing blood and mucus.
Not working in a normal or healthy way, in a manner that causes harm or problems, as in "a dysfunctional family."

Dyslexia is a learning difference — a condition that affects a person's ability to read, spell, and write accurately and fluently, despite having normal or above-average intelligence and receiving proper education.
Dyspepsia simply means indigestion — but it's the formal, medical word for it.
Bad-tempered and irritable, as in "a dyspeptic critic." Literally, suffering from indigestion.

Dysphoria is a noun that describes a state of deep inner discomfort, unease, and dissatisfaction — a feeling that something is profoundly wrong, either with yourself or with your situation. It goes beyond ordinary sadness.
A dystopia is an imagined society — a community, a city, a country, or even an entire world — where life is deeply miserable, unjust, and oppressive for the people living in it.

When we call something dystopian, we mean it describes, resembles, or belongs to a society that appears to be deeply, systemically broken — a world where life has gone terribly wrong, not just for one person, but for an entire society or civilization.
A low neckline on a dress or top, or the part of a woman's neck, shoulders, and upper chest that it reveals.
Décolleté describes a garment — most commonly a dress, gown, or blouse — whose neckline is cut significantly low, leaving the neck, collarbones, upper chest, and upper part of the breasts exposed.

Déjà vu is the sudden, strange feeling that something you are experiencing right now has happened to you before — even though you know (or at least suspect) that it probably hasn't, or you can't figure out when it did.

In its noun form, détente means the relaxation of strained or hostile relations between parties, especially between countries or political powers, achieved through diplomacy, negotiation, and a mutual willingness to reduce conflict.
An eager beaver is a person who is extremely enthusiastic, hardworking, and always ready and willing to do things — often more than is expected of them, and sometimes even before being asked.
An ear is the organ on either side of your head that allows you to hear sounds. Every human being has two ears — one on the left side of the head and one on the right.

Ear-splitting describes a sound that is so extremely loud and sharp that it feels physically painful to your ears — almost as if the sound could tear or "split" your ears apart. It is always negative or alarming in feeling.

An earful is something that fills your ears — not literally, but figuratively. It refers to a large amount of spoken words directed at you, and those words are almost always something you'd rather not hear.
To earmark something means to officially set it aside for one specific purpose — and only that purpose.
To earn something means to receive it because you did something to deserve it — through work, effort, behavior, or merit.

To "earn one's keep" means to work hard enough, contribute enough, or be useful enough to justify the food, shelter, money, or opportunity that someone gives you. In short: you are worth what you cost.

When someone is earnest, they are deeply sincere, serious, and genuinely committed to what they are saying or doing. They are not joking. They are not pretending. They are not putting on a performance.
When you do something earnestly, you do it in a way that is genuinely serious, sincere, and deeply felt — with your whole heart behind it, not half-heartedly or casually.

Earnestness is the quality of being completely sincere, deeply serious, and genuinely committed — in what you say, what you feel, or what you do. When someone shows earnestness, they are not playing around, not pretending, and not performing for an audience.
Earshot is a noun that describes the distance within which a sound — especially a person's voice — can be heard.
Unable to leave the ground or the Earth, as in "earthbound creatures." Figuratively, unimaginative or ordinary. Of a spacecraft, travelling towards the Earth.
Earthenware is a category of pottery — that is, objects made from clay and hardened permanently by baking them in very high heat.

"Earthly" means belonging to the Earth or to life on Earth. But the word is flexible — what you contrast "earthly" things against changes its exact meaning. There are two distinct uses, and understanding each one fully is the key to mastering this word.
When something is earthshaking, it is so massively important, powerful, or significant that it changes the way things are — it turns the world (or at least someone's world) upside down.

"Earthy" has a few distinct but connected meanings. All of them radiate from one central idea: the earth, the ground, the soil beneath your feet — and everything that is raw, real, and unpolished about the natural world.

When you use ease as a verb, it always carries one of two related ideas: reducing something unpleasant or intense, or moving something slowly and carefully. Both senses share the same spirit — gentleness, gradualness, and the removal of harshness or force.
To gradually reduce or lessen in strength or intensity, as in "the rain eased off." To ease off on someone means to stop pressuring or criticizing them.
"Ease up" means to reduce pressure, intensity, effort, speed, or strictness. When someone or something "eases up," they are doing less, pushing less hard, or becoming less intense than before.

An easel is a freestanding, upright stand or frame designed to hold something flat — like a canvas, a painting, a sign, or a display board — in a vertical or near-vertical position, either so someone can work on it, or so others can see it clearly.
This idiom is used to say that talking about doing something is much simpler than actually doing it.
"Easy come, easy go" is a proverb — a short, well-known saying that carries a piece of wisdom about life.
Used to tell someone to do something slowly and carefully, without rushing.
"Easy on the eye" (also said as "easy on the eyes") means that something or someone is pleasant and comfortable to look at.

If someone is easygoing, they are calm, relaxed, and flexible. They don't get stressed over small problems, they don't get annoyed easily, and they don't put heavy pressure on themselves or on others.
To gradually damage, weaken, or destroy something over time, as rust does to iron or worry does to a person's peace of mind.
To "eat crow" means to admit that you were wrong about something, especially when it is deeply embarrassing or humiliating to do so.

To "eat humble pie" means to admit that you were wrong, accept humiliation, and apologize — especially after you were very confident, boastful, or arrogant about something that turned out to be incorrect or unsuccessful.

"Eat into" is a phrasal verb. It has two closely related meanings: 1. To gradually reduce or use up something (the most common, figurative meaning); 2. To physically erode or corrode something (the literal meaning).
To suffer deeply from sadness, longing, or jealousy. Said playfully — "eat your heart out!" — it means "be jealous of this."
To "eat one's words" means to admit that something you said was wrong and to take it back — usually because real life has proven you incorrect.
When you tell someone to "eat up," you are telling them to finish all the food in front of them.
Eaves are the lower, overhanging edge of a roof — the part that projects outward beyond the wall of a building.

To eavesdrop means to secretly listen to a conversation that you are not supposed to hear — one that was not meant for you. The people talking do not know you are listening. That secrecy is what makes it eavesdropping.
An eavesdropper is a person who secretly listens to a conversation that was not meant for them — one they were never invited or permitted to hear.
The movement of the tide going out to sea. Figuratively, a decline, as in "at a low ebb" or "the ebb and flow of life."
To ebb means to gradually decrease, fade, or weaken — especially after having been strong or full at some earlier point. Think of it as the slow draining away of something.
When people say something has an "ebb and flow," they mean: It naturally rises and falls, increases and decreases, or strengthens and weakens over time — in a repeated, cyclical pattern.

When "ebony" is used as an adjective, it describes a color — specifically, a very deep, rich, intense black. But calling it just "black" undersells it. Ebony black is not a flat, dull, or faded black.
Ebony is a noun that refers primarily to a type of wood — but not just any wood. It is one of the rarest, hardest, and most beautiful woods in the entire world.

Ebullience is a powerful, overflowing cheerfulness and enthusiasm that is so strong it visibly spills out of a person. It is the quality of being bubbling over with energy, excitement, and joy — the kind that is hard to contain or hide.

Ebullient describes a person who is overflowing with enthusiasm, excitement, and high spirits — so much so that it radiates outward and becomes nearly impossible to contain. It's not just happiness. It's happiness that bubbles over.

When you call someone or something eccentric, you mean they behave, think, or exist in ways that are noticeably outside what most people consider normal — but in a way that feels harmless, personal, and genuinely their own. It is not random strangeness.
Eccentricity is the quality of being noticeably unusual, unconventional, or different from how most people think, behave, or live — and doing so consistently, as a natural part of who you are.

When something is described as ecclesiastic, it means it belongs to, relates to, or comes from the Christian Church as a formal, organized institution — its structure, its officials, its rules, or its official practices.
An ecclesiastic is a person who holds an official position within a Christian church. Think of it as a formal, elevated word for a church official or a member of the clergy.
Ecclesiastical means relating to the Christian Church, its organization, its clergy, or its affairs.
An echelon is a level or rank within a structured system — especially one that has multiple layers arranged from lower to higher, like rungs on a ladder.
An echo chamber is an environment — online or in real life — where a person only ever encounters ideas, opinions, and information that agree with what they already believe.
Echolocation is a natural ability that some animals have to figure out where objects are — and how far away they are — by sending out sounds and then listening to the echoes that bounce back.
When something is eclectic, it means it is made up of, or draws from, many different sources, styles, or ideas — rather than coming from just one single tradition or following one clear system.

Eclecticism is the practice of freely selecting and combining the best ideas, methods, or styles from a wide variety of sources — rather than pledging loyalty to any single system, tradition, or school of thought.
An eclipse is an event in which one object in space moves into the shadow of another — or passes directly in front of another — causing a block of light.
To eclipse something means to make it appear dim, insignificant, or invisible — by being so much bigger, brighter, or better that the other thing simply fades into the background.
The path that the Sun appears to follow across the sky over the course of a year, as seen from the Earth.

Ecocide means the large-scale, severe destruction of the natural environment — destruction so massive that entire ecosystems are killed off, collapsed, or left unable to support the life that depends on them.
Relating to the relationships between living things and their environment, as in "an ecological disaster."
An ecologist is a scientist who studies the relationships between living things and the world around them.
Ecology is the branch of science that studies the relationships between living organisms and the world around them — both the living and non-living parts of that world.
To economize means to use something — most often money, but also resources, time, or effort — carefully and without waste, so that you use less of it than you otherwise would.

"Economy" has two distinct core meanings — one about a vast system, and one about a personal quality — plus a third, everyday use that flows from both. Understanding all three will let you recognize and use this word confidently in any context.

An ecosystem is a community of living things — plants, animals, fungi, bacteria, and every other organism — interacting with each other and with their non-living surroundings (like water, soil, sunlight, and air) as one working system.

Ecotourism is a special kind of travel to natural places — such as forests, mountains, oceans, wetlands, and wildlife habitats — that is done responsibly, with a genuine effort to protect those places and benefit the local people who live near them.
Ecstasy means an overwhelming feeling of joy, happiness, or pleasure so intense that it almost takes over your whole mind and body.

When someone is ecstatic, they are feeling an overwhelming, almost uncontrollable joy — a happiness so powerful and intense that it feels like it's bursting out of them. It sits at the very top of the happiness scale. This is not quiet, gentle happiness.
Ecumenical means universal, worldwide, or broadly inclusive — especially in the spirit of bringing different groups together rather than keeping them apart.
Eczema is the name for a group of inflammatory skin conditions that cause dry skin, itchiness, rashes, scaly patches, blisters, and skin infections.
Edacious means consuming or devouring greedily and in large quantities. It describes anything — a person, an animal, or even a force of nature — that devours with intensity and little restraint.

Edamame is a food — specifically, it refers to young, immature soybeans that are harvested while they are still green and soft, before they fully ripen and harden into the dry, yellowish soybeans used to make tofu, soy milk, or soy sauce.
An eddy is a circular, swirling movement of a fluid — most commonly water or air — that spins in the opposite direction to the main current flowing around it.
Of water, air, smoke, or dust, to move in a swirling circular pattern, often against the main flow.

"Edge one's way into" means to enter a place, group, conversation, or situation slowly, carefully, and in small steps — especially when the space is tight, the situation is difficult, or there is some kind of resistance or challenge involved.
"To get a word in edgewise" means to manage to say something when someone else is talking a lot. Literally, with the edge facing forward.

When someone feels edgy, they are in a state of inner tension or anxiety — as if they are balanced right at the edge of their patience. An edgy person is restless, easily startled, and quicker than usual to snap or react sharply.

Edible means safe and suitable to be eaten by humans. When you call something edible, you are saying that a person can put it in their mouth, chew it, swallow it, and digest it without it causing harm.
An edict is an official command or order issued by a person or body that holds authority — such as a ruler, a government, or any powerful figure — that everyone under their power is expected to obey.
Edification means the process of improving a person's mind, moral character, or spiritual understanding through instruction, knowledge, or meaningful experience.
An edifice is a building — but not just any building. It is a large, grand, and imposing one. The word suggests something that is substantial, solid, and commands attention simply by existing.

When a person is edified, they are in a state of having been genuinely enriched — intellectually, morally, or spiritually — by something they experienced, heard, or read. They feel uplifted and improved as a person because of it.

To edify someone means to improve their mind, character, or soul — to leave them wiser, morally stronger, or spiritually richer than they were before. Think of it as uplifting someone through knowledge or wisdom.

If something is edifying, it improves you as a person in some meaningful way — it makes you wiser, morally better, more thoughtful, or more informed after you've experienced it. It doesn't just entertain or distract you. It lifts you up.
To editorialize means to mix your personal opinions into something that is supposed to be purely factual or neutral.

To educe something is to draw it out from where it already exists — to bring it to the surface, whether that "something" is a hidden quality, a latent ability, or a conclusion buried within a set of facts.

Eerie describes something that feels strangely unsettling in a mysterious, hard-to-explain way — often suggesting the presence of something supernatural, ghostly, or deeply "off" about the world around you.

To efface something means to wipe it out so completely that little or no trace of it remains. Think of it as a deep, thorough erasure — not just hiding something, but making it as though it barely existed.

Effacement means the act of making something disappear — of wiping it away so completely that it leaves no trace, or barely any trace at all. Think of it as the noun form of "erasing," but stronger and more total than ordinary erasing.
To effect something means to bring something into existence or to make something actually happen.

Successful in producing the intended result, as in "an effective treatment." It can also mean actually in use or operating, as in "effective from Monday," or existing in fact though not officially, as in "effective control."
"Effects" is the plural form of the noun effect. To truly understand "effects," you need to start with "effect."
Something is effectual when it actually achieves the specific result it was meant to achieve. Not just "it did something" — but "it did the exact thing it was supposed to do."

To effectuate something means to make it actually happen — to take action that successfully causes something to occur or come into existence. When you effectuate something, you don't just plan it, hope for it, or talk about it. You actively bring it about.
When someone calls a man or boy effeminate, they mean he has qualities, behaviors, or an appearance that are traditionally associated with women rather than men.

To effervesce means to bubble. More precisely, it means to produce small bubbles of gas that rise rapidly to the surface of a liquid and escape into the air. That process — that lively, fizzing, bubbling action — is effervescing.

Effervescence is the state or quality of bubbling, fizzing, or sparkling — either in a liquid, or in a person's personality. Think of it as the noun form of the idea: the thing itself, not just an action.
Bubbly and full of energy and enthusiasm, as in "an effervescent personality." Of a liquid, fizzing with small bubbles of gas.
Effete means weak, worn-out, and drained of real strength or vitality — but with a specific flavor that makes it more cutting than just "weak."

Efficacious means capable of producing the result it is meant to produce. When something is efficacious, it doesn't just try to work — it actually does work, and it works in the exact way it was supposed to.
Efficacy means the power or ability of something to produce the result it is meant to produce.
Efficient means achieving a result without wasting time, energy, effort, money, or other resources.

An effigy is a physical object — such as a statue, a carved figure, a dummy, or a model — that is deliberately made to represent a specific, real person. The key word here is represent. An effigy isn't just any random figure or sculpture.
Efflorescence means a blooming, a bursting forth, or a reaching of peak beauty and development. Think of it like a flower opening up at its most glorious moment.

Efflorescent means in a state of blooming, blossoming, or bursting into full expression. Think of a flower bud that has opened up completely — that moment of peak, radiant unfolding is what this word captures.

Effluence means a flowing out — something issuing, streaming, or radiating outward from a source. Think of it as the opposite of something flowing in: effluence is always moving away from an origin point, spreading outward into the surroundings.
Liquid waste, such as sewage or factory wastewater, that is discharged into a river or the sea.
An effluvium is an unpleasant, often invisible stream of vapor, gas, or smell that drifts out of something — usually something that is decaying, rotting, or producing waste.
Effort is the energy — mental, physical, or both — that you consciously put into doing something. It is the active application of your ability, attention, or strength toward a task or goal.
Effrontery means bold, shameless rudeness or disrespect — the kind that shocks people because the person doing it acts as if normal rules of decency and respect simply don't exist for them.
Effulgence means a brilliant, powerful, radiant glow of light — the kind that feels like it is pouring outward and flooding everything around it with brightness and splendor.
Effulgent means shining with a powerful, radiant, and overwhelming brightness. It describes light that doesn't just glow softly — it floods outward, filling everything around it with brilliance.
An unrestrained outpouring of words or feelings, as in "effusions of gratitude." In medicine, it is an abnormal build-up of fluid in the body.

Effusive describes someone who expresses their feelings — especially warm, positive ones like praise, admiration, gratitude, or affection — in an abundant, overflowing, and unrestrained way. When a person is effusive, they don't hold anything back.
Based on the belief that all people are equal in worth and deserve equal rights, treatment, and opportunities, whatever their background, wealth, gender, or race.
Egalitarianism is the belief that all human beings are fundamentally equal and deserve to be treated as equals — not just in theory, but in practice, through real structures, laws, and systems.

To egg someone on means to urge, push, or encourage a person to do something — especially something they are hesitant to do, or something risky, foolish, or mischievous. Think of it as adding fuel to a fire that is already burning.
If someone has egg on their face, it means they are embarrassed or humiliated — especially because they did or said something foolish, and other people witnessed it or found out about it.
Eggnog is a sweet, thick, creamy drink traditionally made from a mixture of eggs, milk or cream, sugar, and spices — most commonly nutmeg, and sometimes cinnamon or vanilla.
Ego means the "I" inside you — your sense of being a self. It is the inner voice that says "I exist. I am someone. I matter."

Egocentric describes a person who is so focused on themselves — their own thoughts, feelings, needs, and point of view — that they have genuine difficulty stepping outside their own perspective to see the world through someone else's eyes.
Egoism is the belief — or principle — that the self, its needs, goals, and wellbeing, comes first. An egoist places their own interests at the center of everything they think and do.

Egomania is a noun that describes an extreme, obsessive fixation on oneself — one's own needs, desires, feelings, importance, and opinions — to a degree that is excessive, unhealthy, and damaging to relationships and the world around that person.

An egomaniac is a person who is so completely and obsessively wrapped up in themselves — their own importance, their own needs, their own opinions — that other people barely exist in their world. It is not just someone who is a little self-centered.
When you describe someone or their behavior as egomaniacal, you are saying they are dominated by an excessive, out-of-control preoccupation with themselves.
Egotism is the habit of thinking, talking, and behaving as if you are the most important person in the world — and that almost everything is about you.

Someone who is egotistical is excessively focused on themselves — their importance, their achievements, their opinions, and their image — to a degree that they genuinely show little real interest in, or regard for, other people.
Egregious means outstandingly bad — so bad that it stands out sharply and cannot be ignored, excused, or explained away.
A shockingly bad and conspicuous example of something, as in "an egregious display of arrogance."
Egress means a way out, or the act of going out. If you understand those two things — a place of exit, or the action of exiting — you understand egress.
An egret is a type of bird — specifically, a wading bird closely related to herons. Most egrets are known for their striking pure white feathers, though a few species have darker coloring.

"Eidetic" describes something related to mental images that are unusually vivid, sharp, and detailed — so clear in the mind that they almost feel like actually seeing the thing right in front of you, rather than just remembering it.
An eidolon is an image of something that looks real but isn't truly real. Think of it as a phantom double — a copy, shadow, or ghost of something, rather than the thing itself.
To say something suddenly and forcefully; to exclaim (now rare). In biology, it means to eject semen from the body.

An ejaculation, in this sense, is a short, sharp burst of speech — a sudden, spontaneous cry or exclamation that someone lets out, usually driven by strong emotion such as surprise, shock, joy, or alarm.
Ejection means the act of forcing someone or something out of a place, or the process of being forced out. It always involves movement — something or someone goes from inside to outside.
To eke out a living means to barely manage to survive. To eke something out means to make a small supply of something last longer by using it carefully.
To eke out something means to manage to get or achieve something with great difficulty, usually with very little to work with.

When you describe something as elaborate, you are saying that it is highly detailed, carefully built or planned, and more complex than what is ordinary or simple. It is the opposite of plain, basic, or bare.
To elaborate means to explain something in greater detail — to take a basic idea and expand it, develop it, or fill it in more fully so that it becomes clearer and more complete.
Elaboration means the act of adding more detail, depth, or explanation to something — or the result of doing so.
To elapse means for a period of time to pass from a starting point to an ending point. When time elapses, it has moved forward and is now gone.
Something is elastic if it can be stretched, squeezed, or bent — and then springs back to its original shape or size on its own once you stop applying force.
Elated means feeling extremely happy and excited, almost to the point where you feel like you are floating on air.
Elation is a feeling of extreme happiness and excitement, usually caused by something wonderful that has just happened.

Your arm has two main parts: the upper arm (from your shoulder down to the middle) and the forearm (from the middle down to your wrist). The elbow is the joint — the bending point — right in the middle where these two parts meet.

"Elbow grease" means hard physical effort or hard work, especially the kind where you have to scrub, polish, rub, or push with a lot of force. It is not a real substance. It is just a colorful, creative way of saying "put in real, muscular effort."
Enough space to move around comfortably. Figuratively, freedom to act or make decisions without restriction.

An elder is a person who is older than others, and — most importantly — who is respected because of that age. The word carries a sense of dignity. It's not just about age; it's about the wisdom, experience, and authority that come with age.
An older, highly experienced and respected politician or leader whose advice is valued, especially after they have retired from office.
Eldritch means strange and frightening in a way that feels completely unnatural — as if it belongs to a world beyond our own.
Electioneering is the noun that describes all the activities a person, political party, or group carries out in order to win an election.
An elective is a course or class that you choose to take — as opposed to one you are required to take.
An electorate is a group of people who have the right to vote. Think of it as the "voting group."

An electric dipole is a system of two equal and opposite electric charges — one positive (+q) and one negative (−q) — separated by a small distance. But the implications of this simple setup run deep through all of physics, chemistry, and technology.

To electrify something means either to literally pass electricity through it or connect it to electricity, or — in a much more common, figurative way — to fill someone or a group of people with sudden, powerful excitement, the way an electric shock jolts your body.
When you describe something as electrifying, you mean it causes a sudden, powerful rush of excitement, thrill, or energy — so intense that it almost feels like an electric shock running through you.
Energy that travels through space as waves of electric and magnetic fields, including light, radio waves, microwaves, and X-rays.

Eleemosynary means relating to, or characterized by, charity — specifically the giving of money, goods, care, or services to people in need, purely out of generosity, with no expectation of anything in return.
Elegance is the quality of being pleasingly beautiful, graceful, and refined — in a way that feels effortless, simple, and perfectly right. Nothing about it is overdone, nothing is missing.
Elegant describes something that achieves its purpose — or simply exists — in a way that feels exactly right: refined, pleasing, and effortless, with nothing unnecessary and nothing missing.

Elegiac describes a particular kind of sad, reflective mood — one that is gentle, beautiful, and deeply tinged with a sense of loss. It is the feeling of mourning something — a person, a time, a place, a way of life — while also treasuring the memory of it.
To write or speak about someone who has died or something that has been lost, in a mournful and reflective way.
An elegy is a poem — or sometimes a piece of music — that expresses deep sadness and grief, most commonly written in memory of someone who has died. It is a work of mourning.
"Element" means a fundamental part — something basic that makes up a larger whole, or something essential that cannot be broken down further in a given context.

Elementary means belonging to the most basic, foundational level of something — the starting point, the simplest layer, the bare foundation before anything complex begins. Think of it as describing the "ground floor" of any subject, skill, or idea.

"Elephant in the room" refers to a problem, issue, or uncomfortable truth that is obvious to everyone present, but which nobody is willing to bring up or talk about — usually because the topic feels awkward, embarrassing, painful, or socially risky.
Enormous, heavy, and clumsy, like an elephant, as in "elephantine proportions."
Elevate means to move something or someone to a higher level — but "higher" doesn't just mean physically upward. It can mean higher in position, rank, quality, importance, or even mood.
Elevated means raised above what is considered normal, standard, or ground level — whether physically or in terms of quality, status, importance, or measurable quantity.
Elevation is about height — either literal, physical height, or a figurative "raising up" of something in rank, status, or quality. All its different meanings grow from this central idea.

The eleventh hour means the last possible moment before something ends, a deadline passes, or a situation becomes impossible to change. It refers to a point in time that is so late that any later and it would be too late.
When you call something or someone elfin, you are saying it has the qualities of an elf — but not the scary or monstrous kind.
To elicit something means to draw out or bring out a response, reaction, feeling, or piece of information from a person — something that was already inside them, waiting to come out.
To leave out a sound or syllable when speaking, as in "I'm" for "I am." It can also mean to omit or skip over something, or to merge things so their differences disappear.
Meeting the conditions needed to do or receive something, as in "eligible to vote." An eligible bachelor is a man seen as a desirable person to marry.
To eliminate something means to completely remove it, get rid of it, or put an end to it — so thoroughly that it no longer exists or no longer plays any role in a situation.

Elision is the act of leaving something out — specifically, cutting away a sound, syllable, or sometimes an entire passage — to make speech, writing, or thought flow more smoothly or efficiently. The thing that gets cut is the elision.
When you call something or someone elite, you mean they are among the absolute best — not just good, not just great, but at the very top of their group.
The elite refers to a small, select group of people who are considered the best, most powerful, or most privileged within a larger group or society.

Elitism is the belief or attitude that a small, select group of people — called "the elite" — are inherently superior to ordinary people, and therefore deserve more power, privilege, status, or influence over society.

When you call something or someone elitist, you are saying it reflects — or is shaped by — the belief that certain people are inherently superior to others and therefore deserve more power, privilege, access, or influence.

An elixir is a special liquid that is believed — or claimed — to have a powerful, almost magical effect on whoever drinks it. Think of it as a "wonder liquid." That core idea of a powerful, transformative liquid runs through every meaning of this word.

An ellipse is a closed, flat curve that resembles a stretched circle — like a circle that has been gently squished from two sides, or what people loosely call an "oval." It is a single, smooth, continuous loop with no corners or sharp edges.
Ellipsis means leaving something out. Both of its meanings — and it has two — grow from this single root idea.
Oval-shaped, like a stretched circle. Of speech or writing, using so few words that the meaning is hard to understand.
Elocution is the art and skill of speaking clearly, correctly, and expressively — especially in front of an audience. It is entirely about how you speak, not what you say.
To elongate something means to make it longer — specifically, to stretch or extend it along its length so that it becomes more drawn out than it was before.
Elongated means stretched out or extended in length, making something longer and thinner than it normally is — or longer than the typical shape of that kind of thing.
To elope means to secretly run away with the person you love in order to get married — typically without telling your parents or family, and often without their approval.
Eloquence is the quality of expressing ideas through language — spoken or written — in a way that is clear, beautiful, and powerfully moving.

When we say someone or something is eloquent, we mean it expresses ideas in a way that is clear, powerful, beautifully worded, and deeply moving — all at the same time. It goes far beyond simply "speaking well."
To elucidate means to make something clear and easy to understand — especially something that was previously confusing, complex, or difficult to grasp.
Elucidation means the act of making something unclear, complex, or confusing much easier to understand — essentially, shining a light on it so that it becomes clear.
Elude means to slip away from someone or something. Think of it as the act of something or someone escaping a grasp — whether that grasp is physical, mental, or emotional.
Elusion is the act of successfully avoiding, escaping from, or slipping away from someone or something — usually through skill, cleverness, or quickness.
Something elusive is very difficult to find, catch, achieve, or define — and crucially, it seems to keep slipping away just when you're getting close to it.
Elysian describes something so perfectly beautiful, peaceful, and blissful that it feels like paradise — almost too wonderful to belong to the ordinary world.

Elysium means a place or state of absolute, perfect happiness and bliss — a paradise so complete that nothing in it causes any pain, worry, or suffering. Think of it as the ultimate, ideal version of joy and peace.
An em dash is a punctuation mark that looks like this: —

To emaciate means to cause a person or animal to become dangerously thin and weak — so thin that their body looks visibly wasted, with bones pushing against the skin. It describes an extreme, serious kind of thinness, not just being slim or lean.

Emaciated describes a person or animal that is extremely, dangerously thin — so thin that it is alarming to look at, and so thin that it clearly signals something is seriously wrong with their health.

Emaciation is the condition of being dangerously and extremely thin — so thin that the body appears skeletal, with bones visibly jutting out beneath the skin, and with a near-total loss of body fat and muscle mass.
Emanate means to come out from a source and flow or spread outward into the surrounding space.
An emanation is something that flows out from a source — like a stream flowing out of a spring.

To emancipate someone means to free them from a form of control, restriction, or oppression that has been holding power over them — especially when that control is formal, legal, social, or deeply systemic.
Emancipated means freed from control, restriction, or oppression — and now living in that state of freedom.
Emancipation means the act or process of being freed from some form of control, restriction, or oppression that was unjustly or forcibly placed on someone.
An emancipator is a person who frees other people from some form of control, oppression, or restriction that they are trapped in — especially when those people cannot free themselves on their own.
To emasculate means to strip away power, strength, or essential force from someone or something — leaving it (or them) weakened, ineffective, or diminished at its very core.

Emasculation means the act of stripping something or someone of their power, strength, or essential force — leaving them weakened, diminished, or ineffective. Think of it as the process of cutting away what makes something strong, authoritative, or potent.
To embalm a body means to treat it with special preserving chemicals so that it does not decay — or at least decays very slowly. Think of it as a way of "pausing" the natural breakdown of the body.
An embankment is a long, raised mound or ridge of earth, rock, gravel, sand, or similar solid material that humans deliberately pile up and compact to form a stable, elevated structure.

An embargo is an official ban — a formal "stop" order — placed on the movement of goods, services, or information. Think of it as a wall that a government (or authority) deliberately builds to block something from flowing in, out, or both.

When a government (or authority) embargoes something, it officially bans or blocks trade, movement, or the release of something. Think of it as an authority putting up a firm, legal wall and saying: "This shall not pass."

Embark means to begin something — but not just anything. It specifically carries the feeling of stepping into something significant, like a journey. Think of a sailor walking onto a ship before a long voyage.
"Embark upon" means to begin or start something significant, new, or ambitious.
To embarrass someone means to cause them to feel uncomfortable, self-conscious, and awkward — usually because something about them has been exposed, noticed, or spotlighted in a way they didn't want.

An embassy is the official office that one country sets up inside another country to represent itself. Think of it as a government's "branch office" in a foreign land — a place where the home country conducts its official business abroad.

When we call someone or something embattled, we mean they are facing serious trouble, heavy criticism, or strong opposition from multiple sides at the same time — and the pressure is ongoing, not just a brief moment of difficulty.

To embed something means to place it firmly and deeply inside something else, in a way that it becomes a fixed, integral part of that thing — not just sitting on top or loosely attached, but truly built in.
Embedded means fixed firmly inside something else, in a way that makes the two feel like one unified whole — not just touching, not just resting on top, but genuinely enclosed within.
To embellish something means to add extra details to make it more attractive, impressive, or interesting — details that may or may not be entirely true or necessary.

An embellishment is something extra that is added to make something look better, sound more interesting, or feel more impressive — but it is not necessary for the thing to exist or function. It is a decorative addition, a flourish, an ornament.
An ember is a small, glowing piece of partially burned material — usually wood or coal — that remains after a fire has burned down or is dying out.
Embers are the small, hot, glowing pieces of burned material — such as wood or coal — that remain after a fire has died down or is nearly finished burning.
To embezzle means to secretly steal money or property that someone else has trusted you to look after.
Embezzlement is a type of financial crime where a person steals money or property that they were trusted to take care of — but that never truly belonged to them.

To embitter someone means to fill them with a deep, lasting feeling of resentment, anger, and disappointment — usually because life has treated them unfairly, or because someone has hurt or wronged them badly.

Embittered describes a person who has developed a deep, lasting feeling of anger, resentment, and disappointment — not because of something that just happened, but because of painful experiences that have built up over time and have permanently changed how they feel about life, people, or the world.

To emblazon something means to display or decorate a surface with a name, symbol, image, or design — but not in a quiet or modest way. It means doing so boldly, prominently, and conspicuously, so the result is immediately visible and impossible to ignore.

An emblem is a visual symbol — an image, a design, a badge, or a physical object — that officially and publicly represents something larger than itself: a country, an organization, a religion, a cause, or an abstract idea.
When something is emblematic, it works as a perfect symbol or a shining example that represents something much bigger than itself.

Embodiment means the visible, real, or concrete form of something that is normally abstract or invisible. It is what happens when an idea, quality, or value stops being just a thought and becomes fully expressed in a person, an object, or an action.

To embody something means to give a concrete, visible, or real form to something that is otherwise abstract — an idea, a quality, a value, or a feeling. It also means to be the fullest, most perfect example of that thing.
To embolden someone means to give them the courage, confidence, or bravery to do something they might otherwise hesitate to do — or not do at all.
When someone is emboldened, they have gained a feeling of courage, confidence, or daring that pushes them to do or say something they might not have done before.

To emboss something means to press or stamp a design, pattern, or lettering onto a surface so that it rises up above the surrounding flat area. The result is a raised, three-dimensional effect that you can both see and feel with your fingertips.

When something is embossed, it means it has a raised design, pattern, or text on its surface — meaning part of the surface sticks out slightly, like a bump or a ridge, above the flat background around it.
To embrace something or someone means to hold it close — either with your arms, or with your heart and mind.
To embroider means to add decoration to something — either to a piece of cloth using needle and thread, or to a story using extra details.
Embroidery is the art or craft of decorating fabric — or sometimes leather, paper, or other materials — by stitching patterns, pictures, or designs onto its surface using a needle and thread.
To embroil someone means to pull them into a messy, complicated situation — especially a conflict, argument, controversy, or serious trouble — in a way that is hard to escape from.
An embryo is a living thing in its very first, earliest stage of development — before it has grown into a recognizable form of what it will eventually become.
Embryonic means in the very earliest stage of development — existing, but not yet fully grown, shaped, or mature.
An emcee is a person whose job is to officially host and run an event. They are the one standing in front of an audience, speaking, guiding, and keeping things moving from start to finish.

To emend means to correct errors in a written text. When someone emends a text, they examine it carefully, identify mistakes or corruptions in the words or passages, and fix them to make the text more accurate and reliable.
An emendation is a correction made to a written text — specifically, a deliberate change that fixes what is believed to be an error in something that was written down.
To emerge means to come out into the open from a place where you were hidden, enclosed, or not yet visible — and in doing so, become seen, known, or noticeable for the first time.
In the early stages of coming into existence or being noticed, as in "an emergent technology." In science and philosophy, describing properties that arise from a whole but not from its parts alone.
Having retired from a position but keeping the title as an honour, as in "professor emeritus."

An emeritus is a person who has retired from an important professional role — most often at a university or other institution — but has been officially allowed to keep their title as a mark of honor and respect for their years of distinguished service.

If something is emetic, it means it has the power to cause vomiting. In other words, when a person swallows or is exposed to something emetic, it triggers the body to forcefully expel the contents of the stomach through the mouth.

An emetic is any substance — a medicine, chemical, or naturally occurring agent — that causes a person or animal to vomit when it is swallowed or administered. That's it at its heart: something that makes you throw up, either by design or as a known effect.
To emigrate means to leave your own country and go to live in another country, usually for a long time or permanently.
Eminence means standing notably above others — whether in reputation, achievement, rank, or even physical height.

"Eminent" describes a person who is widely respected and clearly stands out above others — especially in a professional, intellectual, or creative field — because of their exceptional achievements, skills, or qualities.
Eminent domain is the power of a government to take privately owned property for public use, even if the owner doesn't want to sell, as long as the government pays the owner a fair price for it.
Very; to a high and obvious degree, as in "eminently suitable" or "eminently reasonable."
An emir is a title given to a ruler, prince, or high-ranking leader — primarily in Arab and Muslim societies, both historically and in the modern world.
An emissary is a person who is sent by someone — usually a leader, a government, or an organization — to go to another person or place and carry out a specific mission on their behalf.

Emission means the act of sending something out from a source, or the thing that is sent out. Think of it as a release — something moves from the inside to the outside, or from a point of origin into the surrounding environment.
To emit something means to send it out or give it off from a source, outward into the surrounding environment.
The word emollient means softening and soothing — reducing harshness, roughness, or irritation. Think of it as the opposite of something rough, abrasive, or aggravating.
An emollient is a substance — usually a cream, lotion, ointment, or oil — that softens, soothes, and protects the skin by restoring its smoothness and helping it retain moisture.
An emolument is any payment, benefit, or financial advantage that a person receives as a result of holding a job, office, or position of authority.
To emote means to express your emotions outwardly — through your face, your voice, your body language, your tears, or any visible or audible sign that lets the world know what you are feeling inside.
An emotion is a complex inner experience that arises inside you in response to something — a situation, a thought, a memory, or an event — and shapes how you feel, think, and act in that moment.
When something is emotive, it means it stirs up strong feelings in people — or it is designed to do so.
To empanel means to officially select and enroll a group of people to form a jury or a formal panel, so they can carry out a specific duty — most commonly, to decide the outcome of a legal case.

When we say someone is empathetic, we mean they have the ability to truly understand what another person is feeling — not just by observing it from the outside, but by genuinely stepping into that person's shoes and feeling it from within their world.
To empathize means to understand and share what another person is feeling — not just to recognize their feelings from the outside, but to genuinely step inside their experience and feel it with them.

Empathy is the ability to understand and share the feelings of another person — to step inside someone else's emotional experience and genuinely feel what they are going through, not just observe it from the outside.

An emperor is a person — historically almost always a man — who holds the absolute highest level of political power and authority over a vast territory called an empire. Think of him as the supreme ruler, the top of the top.
Special importance or attention given to something to make it stand out, or extra force given to a word when speaking.
To emphasize something means to give it special importance or attention — to make it stand out as more significant than the things around it.
Emphatic means expressed or done with such force, strength, and clarity that it leaves absolutely no room for doubt, question, or misunderstanding.
When you do or say something emphatically, you do it with great force, strong feeling, and absolute certainty — leaving no room for doubt or misunderstanding.
An empire is a large collection of different territories, countries, or peoples that are all ruled and controlled by a single, central power — usually one powerful ruler or one dominant government.
Empirical means based on real-world observation, experience, or evidence — rather than on theory, assumption, or pure reasoning alone.
The belief that all real knowledge comes from experience and observation through the senses, rather than from reason or theory.

An emporium is a large, impressive store or shop that sells a wide variety of different goods — all in one place. Think of it as a grand, well-stocked shop where you can find many kinds of things rather than just one specific type of product.
To empower someone means to give them the power to do something — and that "power" can take many forms.

When someone is empowered, they have the power, confidence, and freedom to act, decide, or take control — either because they feel it within themselves, or because someone has officially given them that authority.
Empowerment means the process of gaining — or the state of having gained — power, control, confidence, or freedom to act in your own life or in society.
Relating to the highest heaven or the sky; heavenly and sublime.

When you describe something as empyrean, you are saying it belongs to, relates to, or has the quality of the highest possible heaven — a place of absolute purity, divine light, and supreme elevation far beyond anything in the ordinary world.

The empyrean means the highest heaven — the supreme, ultimate realm that exists at the very top of everything, far beyond the world we see, beyond the sky, beyond the stars. Not just a heaven, but the highest of all possible heavens.

The word emu most commonly refers to a large, flightless bird that is native to Australia. It is one of the most recognizable animals in the world and is a national symbol of Australia — it appears on the country's coat of arms.

To emulate someone or something means to try to equal or surpass them by following their example. It combines two ideas at once: admiring someone enough to model yourself after them, and striving to reach — or even exceed — their level.
Emulation means the act of trying to match or even surpass someone or something you admire — and doing so by studying and imitating them closely.
When you are emulous, you are driven by a powerful desire to equal or surpass someone else — to match their achievements, their qualities, or their success, and ideally go one step further.

To emulsify means to combine two liquids that naturally refuse to mix — most commonly oil and water — into a single, smooth, stable mixture by breaking one of them into impossibly tiny droplets that are evenly spread throughout the other.
All together, as a single group, rather than one by one, as in "the committee resigned en bloc."
An en dash is a punctuation mark — a small horizontal line — that sits between two things to show a connection, a range, or a relationship between them. It looks like this: –
En famille means in the company of one's family — doing something with family members, together as a unit, in a private and relaxed home-like setting.
All together, in a large group at the same time, as in "the staff resigned en masse."
In passing; casually or incidentally, as in "she mentioned it en passant." In chess, it is a special move in which a pawn captures an enemy pawn that has just moved two squares past it.
"En route" simply means "on the way" or "in the process of traveling to a place."

Enact means to make something real and official through a deliberate, authoritative action. It is about taking something that exists as an idea, a plan, or a proposal — and bringing it into formal existence.
"Enamel" always refers to a very hard, smooth, glass-like coating or material — something that forms a tough outer layer to protect what's underneath and often looks shiny or glossy.
To enamor someone means to fill them with a strong feeling of love, admiration, or deep fascination toward a person or a thing.

To be enamored means to be filled with a deep, powerful feeling of love, admiration, or fascination — toward a person, a thing, or even an idea. It goes far beyond simply liking something. When you are enamored, you are captivated.

To encamp means to settle into a temporary place by setting up a camp. When a group of people stop at a location — pitching tents, arranging their supplies, and preparing to stay for a while — they encamp there.

An encampment is a place where a group of people set up temporary shelters and live together for a period of time — usually outdoors, and usually in tents, makeshift structures, or simple materials rather than permanent buildings.
Encapsulate means to enclose something completely within something else, or to express the full essence of something in a compact, efficient form.
Enceinte means pregnant — that is, a woman who is carrying a baby inside her womb.

When something enchants you, it captures you so completely — so powerfully and pleasurably — that you feel almost spellbound by it. You're swept away. The world around you fades. You are, in a beautiful sense, helpless against its pull.
"Enchanted" always carries the idea of magic — either real, literal magic, or a feeling so powerful and wonderful that it feels like magic. That is the thread connecting every use of this word.
When you call something enchanting, you are saying it is so beautiful, so delightful, and so captivating that it feels almost magical — like it has cast a spell on you.
A feeling of great delight and fascination, as if under a spell. Literally, an enchantment is a magic spell, or the state of being under one.
An enchantress is a woman who enchants — meaning she draws people under her powerful influence, either through literal magic or through the magic of her personality, beauty, or charm.

To encipher something means to take a readable message and deliberately scramble or transform it — following a specific set of rules — so that it becomes unreadable to anyone who doesn't know how to reverse the transformation. The goal is always secrecy.
To encircle something means to go all the way around it, forming a complete ring or circle. When something encircles something else, it surrounds it on every side, leaving no gap or opening.
An enclave is a distinct territory, community, or area that is completely — or largely — surrounded by something meaningfully different from itself.

To enclose something means to surround it completely on all sides, or to place it inside something else so that it is contained within it. Both ideas share the same heart: a boundary is created, and something ends up inside that boundary.
An area surrounded by a fence or wall, as in "an animal enclosure." It can also mean something placed in an envelope along with a letter.

To encode something means to convert it from one form into another form by following a specific set of rules — so that the information can be stored, transmitted, processed, or understood in a particular way.
Something is encomiastic when it is full of high, glowing, enthusiastic praise — the kind of praise that doesn't just compliment but lavishes admiration on a person, work, or idea.
An encomium is a formal, elaborate, and enthusiastic piece of praise — spoken or written — for a person, a thing, or an achievement.
It means to include or contain a wide range of things within something, in a way that is complete and total, leaving nothing important outside.

When you describe something as encompassing, you are saying it is so wide in its reach, so complete in its coverage, that it takes in everything — every part, every angle, every aspect — all at once, leaving nothing outside.
To encourage someone means to give them the confidence, support, or motivation they need to do something — to make them feel that they can do it, should do it, or that it is worth doing.
Encouragement is the act, words, or support that gives someone the confidence, hope, or motivation to do something — to start it, continue it, or push through when it gets hard.

To encroach means to gradually move into, take over, or interfere with something that belongs to someone else — or something that is beyond your proper boundary — typically without permission and often in a slow, creeping way.

Encroachment is the act of slowly and gradually moving into, taking over, or interfering with something — a place, a right, or a boundary — that belongs to someone else, without having the right or permission to do so.
To encrust something means to coat or cover its surface with a hard, solid layer of material — a layer that sticks tightly to the surface, like a crust.

To encrypt means to take readable information and deliberately scramble it into a form that is completely unreadable — and then allow only the right person (or system) to unscramble it again using a special secret called a key.
The process of converting information into a scrambled code so that only someone with the right key can read it.
To encumber something or someone means to burden or weigh them down in a way that makes movement, action, or progress difficult.
If something is encumbered, it is weighed down, restricted, or burdened by something that gets in the way of its free use, free movement, or full potential.
An encumbrance is anything that burdens, restricts, or gets in the way — something that weighs you down, holds you back, or makes free movement and action more difficult.
An encyclopedia is a collection of knowledge, written and organized so that anyone can look up information about almost any topic.
Very comprehensive and detailed, covering a wide range of knowledge like an encyclopedia, as in "an encyclopedic knowledge of history."

To be at the end of one's tether means to have reached the absolute limit of your patience, energy, or ability to cope. You are so exhausted, frustrated, or overwhelmed that you genuinely cannot take any more.

When we say something has reached "the end of the road," we do not mean an actual road. We mean: A point has been reached where something can no longer continue. It is finished. No further progress is possible.
To endanger something or someone means to put them in a situation where they could be harmed, hurt, or destroyed. It means you are exposing them to danger or serious risk.
To endear someone to others means to make that person loved, liked, or cherished by them. It's about creating a feeling of warmth and fondness in people's hearts toward someone (or something).

Something is endearing if it causes people to feel warm affection or fondness — it makes you like or love a person, animal, or thing more. When a quality, habit, or behavior is endearing, it wins people's hearts.

An endearment is anything — a word, a phrase, or an action — that expresses love, affection, or tenderness toward someone. When you use an endearment, you are showing that you care about someone deeply, that they are dear (precious, beloved) to you.
An endeavour is a serious, determined, and sustained effort to achieve something — especially something difficult, challenging, or worthwhile.
To endeavour means to try seriously and sincerely to do something, especially something that is difficult, important, or requires sustained effort. That is the heart of it.
The word endemic describes something that is naturally and consistently tied to a specific place or group — it originates there, it belongs there, and it stays there.
An endgame is the final stage of something — the point where a long process, struggle, or plan is heading toward its conclusion, and where the most important, decisive actions take place.
Endive is a leafy vegetable — a plant whose leaves you eat. It belongs to the chicory family, which means it's related to other slightly bitter greens like radicchio and chicory itself.
Endogenous means originating or produced from within a system, organism, or body — as opposed to coming from the outside.

To endorse something or someone means to publicly declare your support, approval, or agreement with it. When you endorse something, you are essentially saying, "I back this. I stand behind it. I am putting my name and reputation on it."
An endorsement is an act of publicly declaring your support, approval, or backing for someone or something — and that declaration carries weight because it comes from someone whose opinion matters.
To endow means to provide someone or something with something valuable — either a natural quality or a material gift — in a way that is generous, significant, and lasting.
Endowed means having something — a quality, talent, ability, or resource — that was given to you, either by nature, by circumstance, or by another person or institution.
Endowment means something given or provided that continues to give value over time — whether it's money, property, or a natural quality. The word carries the sense of a gift that keeps on giving.

To endue someone with something means to provide them with, invest them with, or equip them with a quality, ability, power, or characteristic — especially one that comes from an outside source rather than something they developed on their own.
Endurance means the ability to keep going through something hard, painful, or tiring — for a long time — without giving up or breaking down.
To bear something painful or difficult without giving up, as in "she endured hours of surgery." It can also mean to last for a long time, as in "their friendship endured."
Enduring means lasting for a very long time, often despite the passage of time, changing trends, or difficult circumstances.
To energize something or someone means to fill them with energy, making them active, lively, powerful, or ready to act.

To enervate someone means to drain them of strength, energy, or vitality — to leave them feeling weakened, listless, and depleted. When something enervates you, it doesn't just make you ordinarily tired. It empties you out.
Enervating describes something that drains your energy, strength, and vitality, leaving you feeling weak, limp, and depleted. It describes the cause of that drained feeling — not the feeling itself.
Enervation means a profound state of weakness, depletion, and drained vitality — physical, mental, or both.

"Enfant terrible" is a French phrase that English borrowed directly and uses as its own. In French, enfant means "child" and terrible means "terrible" or "dreadful." So the literal translation is simply "terrible child" or "dreadful child."

To enfeeble something or someone means to make it weak, frail, or less capable than it was before. When something enfeebles a person or a thing, it strips away strength, power, or vitality — leaving behind a diminished, fragile version of what once existed.
Enfeebled means made significantly weak — reduced in strength, power, or energy to a point where functioning properly becomes difficult.
When you fold something around an object so that the object is enclosed inside, you are enfolding it.

To enfranchise means to grant someone a right, freedom, or power that they were previously denied. It is about letting people in — into a system, a process, or a society — after they had been locked out of it.
Enfranchisement means the act of granting someone full rights, freedoms, and membership in a society or community — particularly rights they were previously denied.
Engage means to make an active connection — with a person, an activity, an idea, or even a machine. Think of two gear wheels locking into each other and starting to work together.
Engaged always means being actively connected to, involved with, or locked into something or someone — not passively, but with real commitment or absorption.
Engagement always carries the idea of a connection — being drawn into something, linked to something, or committed to something. That one thread ties all its meanings together.

When something or someone is engaging, it means they are so interesting, attractive, or charming that they naturally pull your attention in — and then hold it there. You don't want to look away. You don't want to stop. You are drawn in.

To engender something means to cause it to come into existence — to bring about a feeling, a condition, a situation, or an attitude. Think of it this way: something happens, and as a direct result, something new is born or develops from it.
Engineering is the practical use of scientific, mathematical, and technical knowledge to design, build, and improve things that solve real-world problems.
To engrave means to cut or carve a design, letters, words, or a picture into a hard surface, so that the marks go into the material and become a permanent part of it.
"Engraving" can refer to the skill, craft, or technique of cutting designs into hard surfaces. In this sense, it names a profession or an area of artistic practice.

When something engrosses you, it captures your attention so completely that the rest of the world fades away. You are not just interested — you are fully locked in. You might forget to eat, not notice time passing, or fail to hear someone call your name.
When someone is engrossed, they are so deeply focused on something that the rest of the world around them seems to disappear.

When something is engrossing, it means it is so deeply interesting and compelling that it takes over your full attention completely. You become so absorbed in it that you forget the world around you — the time, the noise, the people nearby.

To engulf something means to completely surround, swallow, or overwhelm it — so entirely that whatever is being engulfed is totally consumed, covered, or taken over, with no part of it left free or untouched.
To enhance something means to make it better, stronger, or more noticeable than it already is.
When something is described as enhanced, it means it has been made better, stronger, more powerful, or more impressive than it originally was.
An enigma is something — or someone — that is deeply mysterious and very difficult to understand or explain, no matter how hard you try.
When you call something or someone enigmatic, you mean they are mysterious, puzzling, and difficult to fully understand or explain.
To formally order or strongly urge someone to do something. In law, to enjoin someone from doing something means to forbid them from doing it by court order.
To enlighten someone means to give them knowledge, understanding, or clarity about something they did not know, understand, or see clearly before.

When we call a person, a society, or an idea enlightened, we mean that the darkness — of ignorance, prejudice, cruelty, or narrow thinking — has been replaced by the light of knowledge, reason, wisdom, and understanding.
Enlightenment means the state of gaining deep understanding, clarity, or wisdom — especially about something that was previously unclear, unknown, or confusing to you.

To enlist means to actively bring someone — or yourself — into a cause, effort, group, or organization for a specific purpose. The key feeling of the word is that this involvement is deliberate, purposeful, and often involves commitment.
To enliven something means to make it more lively, interesting, energetic, or full of spirit — to inject a spark of life into it.
To enmesh someone means to catch them, trap them, or entangle them in something complex and difficult — in a way that makes it very hard to get out.

Enmity is a noun that means a deep, strong, and lasting feeling of hatred or hostility between two people, groups, or sides. It is the state of being enemies — not just disliking someone, but feeling a serious, rooted opposition toward them.
To ennoble something or someone means to make it more noble — to raise it to a higher, more dignified, more admirable level. Think of it as a kind of moral or spiritual lifting.

Ennui is a deep, heavy feeling of boredom, emptiness, and dissatisfaction with life. It's the feeling you get when nothing around you seems interesting, meaningful, or worth doing — and that feeling lingers. It's not just a passing "I'm bored right now."

"Enormity" refers to the quality of being shockingly, outrageously evil or morally monstrous. It describes not just something big, but something so deeply wrong or horrifying that it goes far beyond normal human behaviour or moral limits.
Enormous means extremely large — so large that it stands out, often surprising or impressing the person who sees, hears, or thinks about it.

To enrage someone means to make them extremely angry — not just a little upset, not mildly frustrated, but filled with a deep, overwhelming, hot anger that is very hard to control. When something enrages a person, it pushes them to the absolute peak of anger.
Enrapt describes a state of being completely and pleasurably absorbed in something — so absorbed that the rest of the world seems to fade away.
To enrapture someone means to fill them with such intense joy, delight, and pleasure that they become completely swept away by the experience.

When someone is enraptured, they are experiencing such intense joy, wonder, or delight that they feel completely swept away by it. Their whole mind and heart are absorbed in the experience — they are not just enjoying something; they are lost in it.
To enroll means to officially join or enter into something — a school, a course, a program, a plan, or an organization — by going through a formal process that puts your name on an official record.
To ensconce means to settle yourself — or someone/something else — into a place in a way that feels comfortable, secure, and snug, as if you are thoroughly tucked in and sheltered from the world.

Ensemble means a group of things or people that belong together and work as one unified whole. The key idea is not just that the parts exist together, but that they combine to create something greater — a single, complete impression or performance.

To enshrine something means to preserve and protect it in a way that treats it as sacred, precious, and untouchable — so that it is formally recognized, deeply respected, and cannot easily be questioned, removed, or changed.
To enshroud something means to cover it completely, wrapping around it so fully that it becomes hidden, obscured, or difficult to see or understand.
An ensign is a flag — but not just any flag. It is specifically an official flag that a ship flies to show which country it belongs to, or which branch of a navy it serves under.
To enslave someone means to take away their freedom completely and put them under the total control of another person, group, or thing.

Enslavement is the act or process of forcing a person — or a group of people — into slavery: a condition where they are completely stripped of their freedom, their rights over their own body and life, and are controlled by another person or group who treats them not as human beings but as property.
To ensnare someone or something means to trap them — usually through clever, cunning, or deceptive means — in a way that makes it very difficult to escape.

Ensorcelled describes a state of being under a spell — completely and powerfully captivated by someone or something, as if by magic. The person (or thing) described as ensorcelled is not just interested or attracted.

To ensue means to happen or take place afterward — as a natural result, consequence, or close follow-up to something that just occurred. It is the word for when one event triggers or flows into another.
When something happens, and then something else happens right after it — especially because of it — that second thing is the ensuing thing.

To ensure something means to make certain that it happens or is the case. When you ensure something, you take deliberate action so that a particular result is guaranteed — you leave nothing to chance.

When one thing entails another, it means the second thing is a necessary, unavoidable consequence or requirement of the first. You cannot have A without B automatically coming along with it. The two are inseparably linked.

When you entangle something, you cause it to get caught up, twisted, or trapped in something else — in a way that makes it very hard to break free. The key idea is not just being "stuck," but being stuck in a complicated, messy, intertwined way.
"Enter into" means to begin something in a serious, committed, or deeply involved way — not just to start it lightly, but to truly step inside it and become part of it.
To enter the fray means to join a fight, argument, competition, or any intense struggle that is already going on.
A business or company. It can also mean a bold or ambitious project, or the quality of being willing to take on new and difficult challenges, as in "a spirit of enterprise."

If someone is enterprising, it means they are the kind of person who spots an opportunity, takes initiative, and boldly finds a way to make something happen — especially when it isn't easy, when others haven't thought of it, or when there's some risk involved.

To enthrall someone means to capture their attention so completely and powerfully that they feel almost unable to look away, think of anything else, or break free from the experience. The person becomes deeply, almost helplessly fascinated.

When someone is enthralled, they are so completely and deeply fascinated by something that their entire attention is captured — almost as if they're under a spell. Nothing else exists for them in that moment.

When something is enthralling, it is so powerfully interesting, exciting, or beautiful that it completely takes hold of your attention — and holds it so tightly that you almost can't break free even if you tried.
To enthrone someone means to officially place them on a throne, making them a king, queen, bishop, or other high ruler.
An enthronement is the formal ceremony or act of placing someone on a throne and officially giving them supreme power or authority.
Enthuse means to express great excitement about something, or to make someone else feel great excitement. Those are its two jobs as a verb, and everything else flows from these two uses.
Enthusiasm is a strong, energetic feeling of interest, eagerness, and excitement about something — combined with an active desire to engage with it.

When someone is enthusiastic about something, they feel strong, genuine excitement and eagerness toward it. They are not just mildly interested — they are actively energized, eager to engage, and openly expressive about it.
To entice someone means to attract them toward something or persuade them to do something by offering or showing them something appealing.
An enticement is something — or the act of doing something — that attracts, tempts, or lures a person toward a particular choice, action, or place by making it seem appealing or desirable.

Something enticing is so attractive and appealing that it creates a strong pull toward it — it makes you want to have it, try it, go to it, or do it. The key idea isn't just that something looks nice; it's that it draws you in and makes it hard to say no.

"Entirety" means the complete whole of something — every single part of it, with nothing left out, nothing removed, and nothing divided. It is not a partial amount, not most of it, not almost all of it — it is every bit of it, fully and completely.
To entitle someone means to give them an official right to something. That right could be to receive something, do something, or claim something.
In this sense, "entitled" means a person has a legitimate, recognized right to receive or do something. The right usually comes from a law, a contract, a rule, or an established agreement.
Entitlement means the right to have, receive, or do something.
