An entity is anything that exists as a distinct, separate, and independent "thing" — something that can be pointed to, recognized, and treated as its own individual unit of existence.
To entomb something means to enclose it so completely, so permanently, and so tightly that it becomes like something sealed inside a tomb — cut off, unreachable, and shut away, possibly forever.

Entomology is the scientific study of insects. As a noun, it names a complete, organized branch of science — a dedicated field of knowledge that investigates insects in a deep, systematic, and rigorous way.

An entourage is a group of people who regularly surround and travel with one important, famous, or powerful central person. The group exists because of that one person — they are there to assist, support, protect, or simply be close to them.

Entrails refers to the internal organs inside the body — most specifically the intestines (the long, tube-like organs that food passes through during digestion), but it can also include the other soft organs packed inside the belly, such as the stomach, liver, and kidneys.
Entrance is about the threshold between outside and inside — the point where you cross from one space into another. The word captures this idea in three closely related ways.

When something entrances you, it captures your attention and fills you with such deep wonder, delight, or fascination that you feel almost as if you are in a trance — completely lost in the moment, unaware of everything else around you. You cannot look away.

When someone is entranced, they are so deeply and completely captured by something — its beauty, wonder, or magic — that they seem to drift into a dreamlike state. Their full attention is locked in. The outside world fades away.

When something is entrancing, it is so beautiful, captivating, or magical that it pulls your entire mind into it — like it has cast a spell on you. You become so absorbed that the rest of the world around you seems to disappear. You don't want to look away.

Entrapment means being lured, tricked, or pressured into doing something — usually something wrong or harmful — by someone who then uses that very act against you. The key element is that you would not have done it on your own.

To entreat someone means to ask them for something urgently, sincerely, and with genuine emotion. It is not just asking — it is asking in a way that carries real weight, deep feeling, and earnestness.

An entreaty is a deeply sincere, heartfelt request — one made with genuine emotional urgency, where a person desperately needs something and is relying entirely on another person's kindness, compassion, or mercy to receive it.
To entrench something means to establish it so deeply and firmly that it becomes very difficult to change, remove, or get rid of.

Something is entrenched when it has become so deeply fixed, settled, or established — usually over a long period of time — that it is very difficult, or sometimes nearly impossible, to change, remove, or challenge.
Entrenchment is the process or state of something becoming so deeply and firmly fixed in place that it resists being moved or changed.
An entrepreneur is a person who starts a new business — usually from scratch — by spotting an opportunity, taking a risk, and building something to make money from it.

When you call something or someone entrepreneurial, you are saying that it has the qualities of a person who creates, builds, and drives something forward — usually a business or a venture — by taking initiative, thinking creatively, and being willing to take risks.

Entropy is a measure of disorder, randomness, or unpredictability in a system. The higher the entropy, the more disordered and chaotic a system is. The lower the entropy, the more ordered and structured it is.
When you entrust something, you place something important or valuable into someone else's care or responsibility — because you trust them to handle it well.
The right to enter or be accepted into a place or group, as in "an entrée into high society." On a menu, it means the main course in North America, but a starter in Britain.

To entwine means to twist, wind, or coil one thing around another — or to twist two or more things together — so that they become closely connected and bound up with each other. It is stronger and more intimate than simply "connect" or "join."

To enumerate means to name or mention things one by one, in an orderly and deliberate way. Think of it as going through a set of items systematically, picking up each one and holding it up for attention before moving to the next.

Enumeration means the act of going through items one by one and naming or counting each of them individually. Think of it as the careful, deliberate process of ticking things off — not in a rush, but methodically, making sure nothing is skipped.

To enunciate means to express something with deliberate, careful clarity — either in speech (saying words clearly) or in thought (stating an idea clearly). Think of it as the opposite of being vague, mumbled, or sloppy.
The way a person pronounces words, especially how clearly they do it. It can also mean a formal statement of an idea or principle.

To envelop something means to surround it completely — on all sides — so that it is fully wrapped up, covered, or enclosed within something else. Think of it as one thing swallowing another thing whole, without leaving any part exposed.
To envenom something means to introduce venom or poison into it — either physically (into a body or weapon) or emotionally (into a relationship, a mind, or a situation).
When something is enviable, it means it is so good, impressive, or desirable that other people naturally wish they had it, could do it, or were in that position themselves.
Envious describes the feeling you have when you see someone else has something you want — and that makes you feel a mix of longing, dissatisfaction, or even a quiet bitterness about it.
To environ something means to surround it completely — to form a ring or enclosure around it on all sides.
An environmentalist is a person who cares deeply about protecting the natural world — the air, water, soil, forests, oceans, wildlife, and climate — and who actively works to prevent harm to it.
Environs means the surrounding areas around a particular place — typically a town, city, building, or any central location.
To envisage something means to form a clear picture of it in your mind — particularly something that does not yet exist, has not yet happened, or is not right in front of you.
To envision something means to form a clear picture of it in your mind — especially of something that doesn't exist yet, or hasn't happened yet.

An envoy is a person who is officially sent by a government, leader, or organization to represent them, carry an important message, or carry out a specific mission — particularly in political or international matters.
Envy is the painful feeling you get when you see that someone else has something — and you want it for yourself, while feeling unhappy or resentful that you don't have it.
An enzyme is a biological molecule — almost always a protein — that speeds up a chemical reaction inside a living organism, without itself being used up or permanently changed in the process.
An eon is an extremely, almost incomprehensibly long period of time. When someone uses it, they are pointing to a stretch of time so vast that ordinary human imagination struggles to grasp it.

An epaulet is a decorative ornament worn on the shoulder of a uniform or garment. Think of it as a special badge or embellishment that sits right on — or just over — your shoulder, rather than on your chest or sleeve.

Ephemera means things that were only meant to last for a short time — things that were here today and gone tomorrow. It's a word that captures the idea of impermanence, of things that were never meant to stick around.

Something ephemeral lasts for only a very short time and then disappears. If something is ephemeral, it exists briefly, fades away, and is gone — often before you've had enough time to fully appreciate it.
When you call something epic, you are saying that it is grand, heroic, and impressively large in scale — the kind of thing that feels bigger than ordinary life.

An epic is a long narrative poem that tells the story of a great hero performing extraordinary deeds on a massive, sweeping scale. It is one of the oldest and most important forms of literature ever created by human beings.
Having characteristics of both sexes, or of neither. Used of a man, it means effeminate. In grammar, an epicene noun is one with a single form for both males and females.
The point on the Earth's surface directly above where an earthquake starts. Figuratively, the centre of an activity or crisis, as in "the epicentre of the outbreak."
An epicure is a person who has developed a refined, educated taste for food and drink — someone who doesn't merely eat to live, but takes deep, thoughtful pleasure in what they eat and how it tastes.
When someone or something is described as epicurean, it means they are devoted to — or associated with — the sophisticated enjoyment of fine food, fine drink, and sensual pleasure in general.
The ancient Greek philosophy of Epicurus, which taught that the goal of life is a calm, simple happiness, free from pain and fear. Today, it can also mean a love of fine food and pleasure.
An epidemic is when a disease spreads rapidly and affects far more people than usual in a specific place and within a relatively short time.

Epidemiology is the study of how diseases and health conditions occur, spread, and can be controlled in groups of people. It looks at populations — meaning large groups — not just individual patients. That's what separates it from regular medicine.
The epidermis is the outermost layer of your skin — the very surface you can see and touch right now. It is your body's first wall against the outside world.

An epigone is someone who comes after a great, original master — a legendary writer, thinker, artist, composer, philosopher, or any other creative or intellectual giant — and works in that master's style, but without their genius, depth, or originality.

An epigram is a short, clever, and memorable statement — or sometimes a short poem — that makes a sharp, surprising point, usually with wit or wisdom. The entire power of an epigram lies in how much it says with how little it uses.
Something is epigrammatic when it says a lot in very few words — and does so cleverly, sharply, and memorably. It's the opposite of rambling. It's language that is tight, witty, and pointed.

An epigraph is a short piece of writing — a quotation, a line of poetry, a proverb, a verse, or any brief passage — placed at the very beginning of a book, an essay, a chapter, or any written work, before the main content begins.

Epilepsy is a chronic (long-term) brain disorder in which a person has a tendency to have repeated, unprovoked seizures — sudden bursts of uncontrolled electrical activity in the brain that temporarily disrupt how the brain works.
A sudden burst of uncontrolled electrical activity in the brain, caused by epilepsy, which can lead to convulsions, loss of consciousness, or unusual sensations.
An epilogue is a separate section placed at the very end of a book, play, or other written work, which comes after the main story has already finished.

Epinephrine is a chemical your body naturally makes and releases into your blood during moments of stress, danger, or excitement. It rapidly prepares your entire body to either fight a threat or run away from it.

An epiphany is a sudden, powerful moment when something becomes deeply and clearly understood — often after a long period of confusion, struggle, or simply not knowing. It is not a slow, gradual realization.

An epiphenomenon (plural: epiphenomena) is a secondary effect — a byproduct — that arises from a primary process, but which is itself causally powerless. It is produced by something, but it produces nothing in return.
"Episcopal" means relating to bishops, or governed by bishops.
Made up of separate, loosely connected parts or episodes, as in "an episodic novel." It can also mean happening only occasionally or at irregular intervals.
Epistemic means relating to knowledge — specifically, to how we know things, how reliable our knowledge is, where knowledge comes from, and where it runs out.

"Epistemological" is an adjective. It means relating to the study or theory of knowledge itself — specifically, how we know things, what counts as real knowledge, what justifies a belief, and what the limits of human understanding are.

An epistemologist is a person — almost always a philosopher — who makes it their life's work to study knowledge itself. Not a particular subject like history or physics, but the very nature, source, and limits of knowledge as a concept.
Epistemology is the branch of philosophy that studies knowledge — what it is, where it comes from, how we can get it, and what its limits are.

An epistle is a letter — but not just any letter. It is a formal, serious, and often lengthy letter, typically one that carries weight, importance, or literary value. Think of it as the opposite of a quick, casual note.
Epistolary is an adjective that simply means "relating to, consisting of, or carried out through letters."
An epitaph is a short piece of writing composed in memory of a person who has died. Its most classic home is a gravestone or tombstone, where it is carved or inscribed for the world to read.
An epithet is a word or short phrase that is attached to — or used in place of — a person's or thing's actual name, in order to describe or highlight a specific quality about them.

"Epitome" means the perfect, most representative example of something. When you call something the epitome of a quality or category, you're saying it represents that thing so completely and perfectly that it could not represent it any better.
To epitomize something means to be the perfect, most complete example of it — so much so that when people think of that quality or idea, they think of you.

An epoch is a significant, distinctive period of time that has a clear identity of its own — a stretch of history defined by something that gives it a character all its own, setting it apart from what came before and after.
So important that it marks the beginning of a new era, as in "an epochal discovery."
An eponym is a person whose name becomes the name of something else — a place, an object, a disease, a concept, or anything at all.
Having the same name as the person or thing that something is named after — as in a band's eponymous first album, named after the band itself.
Calm and even-tempered, not easily upset or annoyed, as in "an equable temperament." Of climate, moderate and steady, without extremes.

When two or more people, groups, or things are on "equal footing," it means they are in the same position, with the same advantages, rights, power, or opportunities — nobody has an unfair edge over the other.

Equanimity means a calm, steady, and balanced state of mind — particularly when things around you are difficult, stressful, chaotic, or uncertain. A person with equanimity doesn't panic, crumble, or get swept away by strong emotions.
If someone is equanimous, it means they are mentally calm, balanced, and steady — especially when life gets hard.
To equate something means to consider two things as the same, or to treat them as equal in value, meaning, or importance.

An equation is a mathematical statement that declares two things are equal. It always contains an equals sign (=), and that sign is the heart of it — it says: "what's on my left and what's on my right are the same value."

An equerry is a personal attendant or aide who serves a member of a royal family or a head of state, helping them carry out their official duties and managing the practical details of their daily royal life.

When something is described as equestrian, it means it is related to the sport, skill, or activity of riding horses. Think of it as a word that connects anything — a person, a place, an event, a statue — back to the world of horse riding.
Equidistant is an adjective that describes something that is at the same distance from two or more things.
Equilibrium means a state of balance — specifically, a balance between two or more opposing forces, pressures, or influences that results in stability.
Equine simply means "of, relating to, or characteristic of a horse or the horse family."
One of the two days each year, in March and September, when the Sun is directly above the equator and day and night are roughly equal in length everywhere.
To equip means to provide someone or something with what they need to handle a particular purpose, task, or situation.
Equipage refers to the complete set of things — objects, people, or both — that outfit, accompany, or make ready a person or group for some purpose.

Equipoise means a state of perfect balance — where two opposing forces, sides, or pressures are exactly equal, so that neither one wins or dominates. Think of a classic weighing scale with both pans sitting at precisely the same level.
Equal in force, power, or effect.

Equitable means fair and just — but it describes a specific, deeper kind of fairness. It means treating people in a way that is right and reasonable for their particular situation, ensuring that everyone gets what they genuinely deserve or need.

Fairness — especially the kind that takes into account people's different needs and circumstances. In finance, equity is the value of the shares in a company, or the value of a property minus what is owed on it.

Equivalence is the state or condition in which two (or more) things are equal in some specific, meaningful way — even if they are not identical, and even if they look completely different from each other.
When two things are equivalent, they are equal in value, amount, meaning, function, or effect — even if they look completely different or work in completely different ways.
An equivalent is something that is equal to something else in a specific, meaningful way — but is not necessarily identical to it.
Something equivocal is deliberately or genuinely unclear in a way that leaves room for more than one interpretation.

To equivocate means to deliberately use vague, unclear, or carefully worded language to avoid giving a direct and honest answer — usually to hide your real opinion, escape a commitment, or create a false impression, all without technically saying something false.

Equivocation is the act of using language that is deliberately vague, unclear, or capable of being understood in more than one way — usually to avoid saying something directly, to dodge a question, or to create a misleading impression without technically telling an outright lie.
An era is a long stretch of time that has a clear identity — meaning it is defined, named, or remembered because of something significant that shaped it.

To eradicate something means to get rid of it so completely that it no longer exists at all. Not just reduce it. Not just push it away temporarily. But destroy it so thoroughly that it is gone — permanently and entirely.

Eradication means the complete and permanent wiping out of something so that it no longer exists anywhere. Not reducing it. Not controlling it. Not pushing it away. Completely destroying it so that it is gone — forever.

Erasure means the act of removing something so that it no longer exists or can no longer be seen or found. It goes one step further than just "removing" something — erasure implies that what was there is now gone, wiped out, or made invisible.
"Ere" means "before" — but only in the sense of time. Every single time you encounter "ere" as a preposition, you can substitute it with "before" and the meaning will be completely preserved.

Erect means to raise something up so that it stands tall and upright, or to build something that will stand firmly in place. Think of it as the action of making something go from "not there" or "lying flat" to "standing tall."
The act of building or putting up a structure, such as a bridge or monument. In anatomy, it means the stiffening and swelling of the penis.
An eremite is a person who deliberately withdraws from society to live completely alone, almost always for religious or spiritual reasons.

Eremophobia is an intense, irrational, and overwhelming fear of being alone or of solitude. The key word here is irrational — a person with eremophobia doesn't just dislike being alone the way most people might after a long, quiet weekend.
"Ergo" means therefore or consequently. It is a word that tells your reader: "Based on what I just said, this conclusion logically follows."

When you describe something as ergonomic, you mean it has been carefully designed to fit the natural shape, movements, and limits of the human body — so that using it is comfortable, efficient, and unlikely to cause pain or injury over time.
Ergophobia is a noun that refers to an intense, irrational, and persistent fear of work. Not just a dislike of work — an actual, deep-rooted psychological fear of it.
The white winter fur of the stoat, traditionally used to trim the robes of judges and royalty. The animal itself is also called an ermine in winter.
To erode means to gradually wear something away, weaken it, or destroy it — little by little, over time.

When something is described as eroded, it means it has been gradually worn away, weakened, or eaten into over time — so that what remains is incomplete, damaged, or reduced compared to its original state.
Erosion is the slow, gradual wearing away, weakening, or removal of something — piece by tiny piece — over time, until it is noticeably reduced, damaged, or destroyed.

Erosive means causing gradual wearing away or destruction of something. If something is erosive, it has the power or tendency to slowly break down, eat into, strip away, or diminish something — little by little, over time.
Erotic describes anything that is related to, or capable of arousing, sexual desire or excitement in a person.
"Err" means to make a mistake — to be wrong in what you think, judge, decide, or do.
Err on the side of caution
When you err on the side of caution, you deliberately choose the safer option when you are unsure about something, even if that means being more careful than you might actually need to be.
An errand is a short trip you make outside your home (or workplace) to complete a specific, practical task — and then you come back.

"Errant" describes something or someone that has gone off the path they were supposed to follow — whether that path is a physical one, a moral one, or a behavioral one. Think of it as a word for things that have strayed.
A list of errors found in a book or document, along with their corrections. "Errata" is the plural; a single error is an "erratum."
Erratic describes something — a person's behavior, a movement, a pattern, a performance — that is unpredictable, irregular, and inconsistent. Something erratic has no steady rhythm or logic to it.

An erratum is an error in a published work — a book, a research paper, an academic journal, or any formal document — that was discovered after the work had already been printed and released to the public.

Erroneous means containing an error or based on an error. When something is erroneous, it is wrong, incorrect, or mistaken — and the wrongness comes from false information, a faulty assumption, or flawed reasoning.
Erroneously means "in a way that is wrong or mistaken."

Ersatz describes something that is a poor, inferior substitute for the real thing. When you call something ersatz, you are saying two things at once: this is not the genuine article, and it is noticeably worse than what it is trying to replace.

"Erstwhile" means former — it describes someone or something that once held a particular role, identity, or status, but no longer does. If someone was once your ally but isn't anymore, they are your erstwhile ally.
To eruct means to belch — that is, to forcefully expel gas from the stomach up through the throat and out of the mouth.
Eructation simply means a burp — the act of expelling gas from the stomach up through the throat and out of the mouth, usually making a sound as it does so.
If someone is erudite, it means they have deep, wide-ranging knowledge — the kind that comes from years of serious study and reading.
Erudition is the quality of possessing a deep, wide, and highly refined body of knowledge — the kind that comes from years of serious, dedicated reading and scholarly study.

When something erupts, it breaks out suddenly and forcefully — usually after pressure has been building up inside or underneath. Think of it as the moment something contained can no longer stay contained, and it bursts free with great energy.

An eruption is a sudden, forceful burst or release of something that has been building up inside — something that was contained, under pressure, or hidden, and then breaks out powerfully and often violently.

To escalate means to increase or intensify, usually gradually and often to a serious or worrying degree. Think of it as something climbing upward — getting bigger, stronger, more severe, or more complicated over time.
Escalation means the process of something becoming bigger, more serious, more intense, or more extreme — usually in a gradual, step-by-step manner, like climbing up a staircase, one step at a time.
An escapade is a wild, adventurous, or mischievous act — something a person does that is spontaneous, a little daring, and outside the boundaries of normal or expected behavior.

When something escapes your notice, it means you failed to see, realize, or become aware of it. The thing happened or existed right there, but your attention simply didn't catch it — it slipped past you.
An escapee is a person — or sometimes an animal — who has successfully gotten away from a place or situation where they were being held, kept, or controlled without permission.

Escapism is the habit of turning to enjoyable activities, entertainment, or fantasy in order to mentally "run away" from real life — especially from things that feel stressful, boring, painful, or overwhelming.

When you call something escapist, you mean it is designed — or at least tends — to help a person mentally escape from the stress, difficulties, boredom, or harsh realities of everyday life. The escape here is not physical.
Escargot means snails — specifically, snails that are cooked and eaten as food.

An escarpment is a long, steep slope or cliff-like face of land that acts like a giant natural "step" in the earth's surface — where the land on one side is dramatically higher than the land on the other side.

"Eschatological" is an adjective that means relating to the ultimate, final end of things — the last chapter, not just of a story or a life, but of history, of humanity, or of the entire world and cosmos.
Eschatology is the branch of knowledge — usually within religion, theology, or philosophy — that deals with the "last things." That phrase, "last things," is the heart of the whole word.

As a noun, escheat refers to two closely related things: the government's legal right to claim property that has no rightful owner, and the property itself that the government acquires through this process.
To eschew something means to deliberately and consciously choose to avoid it — typically as a matter of personal principle, discipline, or strong preference.

An escort is a person or group that accompanies someone or something from one place to another — not just for company, but with a specific purpose. That purpose is usually one or more of the following: protection, guidance, honor, or supervision.
To escort someone means to go with a person from one place to another, on purpose, with a sense of responsibility toward them.

An escrow is a special, neutral holding arrangement in which a trusted third party temporarily holds something of value — money, property, or documents — on behalf of two people who are in the middle of a deal, and only releases that thing once both sides have fully kept their promises.
Something that is esculent is fit to be eaten — safe, suitable, and appropriate as food.
An escutcheon is a shield — but almost always a shield used as a surface to display something, rather than one carried into battle.

Esoteric describes something that is understood, known, or appreciated by only a very small group of people — usually because it requires special knowledge, deep training, or belonging to a particular community or tradition.

"Esoterica" refers to a body of knowledge, details, or subject matter that is obscure, highly specialized, and understood only by a small group of people — usually insiders, experts, or those who have gone unusually deep into a particular subject or tradition.

An espadrille is a type of casual shoe — and its one unmistakable, defining feature is its sole made of braided or woven rope, most commonly rope twisted from a plant fiber called jute (a natural, rough-textured material, like thick string).

An espalier is a plant — almost always a tree or a woody shrub — that has been carefully trained over time to grow completely flat, like a living picture pressed against a wall, fence, or a freestanding framework.

Especial means particularly outstanding, distinguished, or notable above all others of the same kind. It describes something that stands apart from the rest — not just "above average," but singled out as pre-eminent among its peers.

Espionage means the act of secretly spying on someone — usually a government, organization, or country — to steal information that they are keeping private, and then using that information for your own advantage or handing it over to someone else.
An esplanade is a wide, long, flat, open area — usually paved or grassy — where people can walk, stroll, or simply enjoy the surroundings.
To espouse something means to take up a belief, cause, or idea and make it your own — wholeheartedly and openly.

Esprit means a quality of lively, witty, and animated intelligence — a kind of bright mental sparkle that a person has. It is more than just being smart. It combines quickness of mind, cleverness, and a certain spirited energy all at once.
A feeling of pride, loyalty, and shared spirit among the members of a group, such as a team or army unit.

To espy something means to suddenly catch sight of it, especially when it is hard to see — because it is far away, partially hidden, small, or easy to miss. It is the moment your eyes lock onto something that wasn't immediately obvious.

"Esquire" is a title — a word placed next to a person's name to signal their rank, profession, or social standing. Think of it like "Doctor" or "Captain," except "esquire" has a unique twist: it is almost always written after the person's name, not before it.
To essay something means to attempt it — to try doing something, especially something difficult, demanding, or uncertain.
A writer of essays — short pieces of writing that explore an idea, argument, or personal experience from the writer's point of view.
The essence of something is the quality (or set of qualities) that defines it at the deepest level — what it truly is, beneath all surfaces.

Essential means absolutely necessary — something that must be present for a thing to work, exist, survive, or be what it is truly supposed to be. If you remove something essential, something fundamental breaks down, fails, or ceases to exist properly.
"Essentially" points to that core. When you say "essentially," you are saying: "When you look past the minor details and focus on what truly matters, this is what you find."
To establish something means to set it up so that it exists firmly, stably, and is recognized as real or valid.

When we call something established, we mean it has been around for a long time, has proven itself, and is now widely accepted and recognized. It is no longer new, uncertain, or experimental — it has earned its place through time and repeated success.
A business or organization, such as a shop, restaurant, or school. The Establishment means the powerful people and institutions who control a society. It can also mean the act of founding something.
An estate is a large area of land — usually in the countryside — that is privately owned by one person or family.
Esteem is the deep respect, admiration, and high regard you hold for someone — or that others hold for you — based on their character, qualities, or achievements.
To esteem someone means to hold them in genuinely high regard — to consider them worthy of respect, admiration, and appreciation.
Someone who is esteemed is held in very high respect and admiration by others.
The most important meaning of estimable is: deserving of deep respect, regard, and admiration.

An estimate is your best, reasoned answer to a question you cannot answer exactly — not because you are careless or lazy, but because the exact answer is either unknown, unavailable, or impossible to pin down without more time, data, or effort than the situation allows.

Estimation is the act, process, or result of making an approximate judgment about something — such as a quantity, size, cost, time, distance, or value — when you either cannot or do not need to know the exact answer.
Estival simply means of summer, relating to summer, or characteristic of summer. If something is estival, it belongs to summer, happens in summer, or has the feel and quality of summer.

Estoppel is a legal rule that stops you from saying something that contradicts what you said or did before — especially when someone else acted on your original statement and would be harmed if you changed your story.

To estrange someone means to cause them to become emotionally distant, cold, or separated from a person, group, or place they were once close to. It means to turn someone — or yourself — into a stranger in a relationship where closeness once existed.

Estranged describes someone who was once emotionally close to another person — a family member, a spouse, a friend — but is now distant, cold, or cut off from them, usually because of a conflict, a betrayal, or a long silence that never healed.

Estrangement is the state of being emotionally or relationally separated from someone — or something — you were once close to or connected with. It is not simply distance. It is the painful condition of lost closeness.
An estuary is a partially enclosed, sheltered area of water along a coastline where a river flows into the sea, and where the freshwater from that river mixes with the saltwater of the ocean or sea.
"Et al." is a short Latin expression. It is an abbreviation for "et alii" (or its variations et aliae or et alia, depending on grammar), which simply means "and others."

To etch means to cut or carve a mark, design, or image into a surface — not just on top of it, but into it — usually by using acid, a sharp tool, or a laser, so that the mark becomes a permanent part of that surface.
An etching is a piece of artwork — specifically, a picture printed onto paper using a special technique involving a metal plate and acid. The word also refers to the technique itself.
Eternal means lasting forever — with no end, and often no beginning either.

Eternity means time that never ends — or more precisely, existence that is completely beyond the limits of time. It describes a state where there is no beginning, no ending, and no passing of time at all. It is the opposite of temporary.
A colourless, flammable liquid once used as an anaesthetic. In poetry, the ether is the clear upper sky. Informally, it also refers to the airwaves or the internet.
"Ethereal" describes something so delicate, light, and beautiful that it seems to belong to a world beyond our ordinary, physical one. Think of it as the opposite of "heavy," "solid," or "earthly."
An ethic is a guiding moral principle — a belief about what is right, good, or proper — that shapes how a person, group, or society behaves.
Something is ethical when it is in line with what is considered right, good, and fair — based on a set of moral principles about how people should behave toward each other and the world.
Ethics is about one fundamental question: what is right and what is wrong? More broadly, it asks: how should we act, how should we treat one another, and what kind of person should we strive to be?
"Ethnic" describes something as relating to, belonging to, or characteristic of a particular ethnic group — a group of people who share a common cultural identity.

When someone is ethnocentric, they judge other cultures, people, or ways of life by using their own culture as the measuring stick — and they assume, often without even realizing it, that their own culture is the normal, correct, or superior one.

Ethnocentrism is the tendency to view your own cultural group — your ethnicity, nationality, tribe, or society — as the natural center of the world, and to judge all other cultures by the standards and values of your own.
An ethnography is a detailed, in-depth study of a particular group of people, their culture, and their way of life — written from the inside out.
Ethnology is the scientific, comparative study of human cultures — their characteristics, origins, development, similarities, and differences.
The distinctive spirit, character, and values of a group, community, or period, as in "the company's ethos." In rhetoric, ethos is persuasion based on the speaker's credibility.

To etiolate something means to make it pale, weak, and sickly — specifically by depriving it of what it needs to be strong and healthy. Think of it as a slow draining away of color, vitality, and strength.

Etiolated describes something that has become pale, weak, and unnaturally thin because it was cut off from something it needed to grow properly. The word always carries a sense of deprivation as the cause of the weakness.

Etiolation is what happens to a plant when it doesn't get enough light. Specifically, it's the condition in which a plant becomes abnormally pale, weak, and spindly as a direct result of growing in darkness or very dim light.
Etiology means the cause, or the study of causes, of a disease or condition.

Etiquette is the set of rules — mostly unwritten — that tell people how to behave politely and respectfully toward one another in social situations. It is a shared code of "acceptable behavior" within a society, a group, or a specific setting.
Etymological means "relating to or having to do with the origins and history of words."

Etymology is the study of the origin and history of words — where a word came from, what it originally meant, how its meaning changed over time, and how its spelling or form evolved across languages and centuries.

A eucalyptus is a tall, fast-growing tree (or sometimes a large shrub) that originally comes from Australia. It belongs to a large group — there are over 700 different species of eucalyptus, making it one of the most varied tree families in the world.

Eudaemonic means relating to, producing, or conducive to deep and lasting human well-being and flourishing — the kind of happiness that comes not from fleeting pleasure, but from living a life of meaning, virtue, purpose, and full use of your abilities.
Eugenic is an adjective that means relating to the goal of improving the genetic qualities of a human population by controlling who reproduces and who doesn't.

Eugenics is the belief — and the set of practices based on that belief — that the human species can be deliberately improved by controlling who is allowed (or encouraged) to reproduce, and who is not.

When you call something eulogistic, you mean it is full of high, warm, and often formal praise for a person or thing. It describes language, writing, a speech, a tone, or a style that glorifies and deeply admires its subject.
To eulogize someone means to speak or write about them with deep, heartfelt, and very high praise — publicly, and in a formal or serious way.
A eulogy is a formal, heartfelt speech — or sometimes a piece of writing — that praises and honors a person, most commonly someone who has recently died.
A eunuch is a male human being whose testicles have been surgically removed, making him permanently unable to reproduce and, in most cases, unable to engage in sexual activity.

A euphemism is a word or phrase that people use instead of a word or phrase that feels too harsh, too blunt, too embarrassing, or too uncomfortable to say directly. The substitute says the same thing — but more gently, more vaguely, or more politely.

When you describe something as euphemistic, you mean it uses mild, soft, or indirect language to talk about something that is uncomfortable, harsh, embarrassing, or taboo — instead of saying it directly and plainly.
Euphonious means pleasant-sounding — something that is easy, smooth, and agreeable to the ear, almost like music.
Euphonous means pleasant to hear — it describes something that sounds smooth, agreeable, and easy on the ears.

Euphony means the quality of sounding pleasant, smooth, and agreeable to the ear. It refers to sounds — especially in words, phrases, or music — that feel naturally comfortable and pleasing when you hear them or say them aloud.

Euphoria is a feeling of extreme happiness, excitement, and well-being — so intense that it almost feels bigger than you, like your entire body and mind are overflowing with positivity. It is not just "feeling good."
Euphoric describes a feeling of extreme, overwhelming happiness and excitement — so intense that it almost feels bigger than ordinary joy.
An extremely elaborate and artificial style of writing or speaking, full of fancy comparisons and balanced phrases, used where plain words would do better.
When something is eurhythmic, it means it has a rhythm that is not just present, but genuinely pleasing, harmonious, and well-balanced — a rhythm that feels right.

Eurocentric is an adjective that describes any viewpoint, system, curriculum, story, or way of thinking that places Europe — its history, its culture, its values, and its people — at the absolute center of the world.
Euthanasia is the deliberate act of ending someone's life — on purpose, not by accident — in order to stop them from suffering. The key word here is deliberate.
To euthanize something (or someone) means to deliberately and painlessly end its life, usually to prevent it from suffering. It is an act done out of mercy, not malice.
Eutrophication is the process by which a body of water receives too many nutrients, which triggers a chain of events that eventually suffocates the life within it.
To evacuate means to move people away from a place that is dangerous, or to leave such a place yourself. The key idea is always danger or threat — combined with the act of removing or emptying.
Evacuation is the act of moving people (or sometimes things) away from a place that is dangerous — or is about to become dangerous — to somewhere that is safe.
An evacuee is a person who has been moved away from a dangerous place to a safer one, usually because of an emergency.

To evade something means to deliberately avoid it — but not in a simple or straightforward way. When you evade something, you use cleverness, skill, or indirectness to escape it or keep it from reaching you. The key ideas are intention and indirectness.
To evaluate something means to carefully examine it and form a reasoned judgment about its value, quality, effectiveness, or condition.
An evaluation is the careful process of studying something closely and then making a judgment about it — about its quality, worth, effectiveness, accuracy, or condition.
To evanesce is to disappear slowly and gently — so gradually that you can barely pinpoint the exact moment it's gone.
Evanescence is the quality of fading away gently and gradually — the way morning mist dissolves when the sun rises, or the way a dream slips out of your mind moments after you wake up.

Something evanescent fades away or vanishes so quickly and gently that it almost seems to melt into nothing — like morning mist burning off in the sun, or the warm feeling of a dream that slips away seconds after you wake up.

"Evangelical" means relating to the Christian gospel — specifically, the "good news" that Jesus Christ died for humanity's sins and rose from the dead, offering people salvation and a restored relationship with God.
Evangelism is the act of enthusiastically and actively spreading a belief to other people — with the genuine hope that they will come to share it too.
An evangelist is someone who believes in something so strongly that they feel a deep, almost urgent need to spread that belief to other people.
To evangelize means to actively and enthusiastically try to convince other people to believe in or adopt something you strongly believe in yourself.
To evaporate means for a liquid to slowly turn into an invisible gas and disappear into the surrounding air.
Evasion is the act of deliberately avoiding something or someone — especially something you are expected, obligated, or supposed to face.

When someone or something is evasive, they are deliberately avoiding something — a question, the truth, a direct answer, or even physical capture. The most important word here is deliberately. Being evasive is not an accident.

"Eve" means the day or night immediately before a significant event. Think of it as the time right before something important is about to happen. It is that final stretch of waiting — the last moments before a big occasion arrives.
To reach, or to bring something to, a state of being equal, balanced, smooth, or stable — especially after a period of being unequal, unbalanced, rough, or unstable.

Even steven means perfectly equal, with no advantage or debt on either side. When two people, teams, or sides are "even steven," everything between them is completely balanced — nobody owes anything, nobody is ahead, and nobody is behind.
To "even the score" means to retaliate against someone who has wronged you — to pay them back for something unfair or harmful they did to you, so that you feel the situation is balanced again.

Evenhanded means treating all people, groups, or sides of a situation fairly and equally, without favoring any one of them. A person who is evenhanded does not let personal feelings, relationships, or bias push them toward one side.

Evening is the part of the day that comes after the afternoon and before the night. It is the transition — the in-between time when the sun has set (or is just setting) and the world is moving from daylight into darkness, but full night hasn't arrived yet.

Eventful describes a period of time that is full of important, significant, or notable happenings. When something is eventful, a lot happened during that time — things that are worth remembering, talking about, or paying attention to.

Eventide means the evening — specifically, the time of day when the sun has set or is setting, and the day is quietly coming to a close. Think of that gentle, calm stretch of time between late afternoon and the arrival of full night.
Happening at the end of a process or period of time, as in "the eventual winner."
An eventuality is a possible future event or situation, especially one that might be difficult, unpleasant, or uncertain — that you are thinking about or preparing for ahead of time.
Eventually means at some point in time, after a delay or a process — not immediately, but in the end.

Eventuate means to result in a final outcome or to come about as a result of something. The word always points to the end of a process — whatever finally happens after a series of events, a long situation, or a chain of causes.

Everlasting means lasting forever, or lasting for such a long time that it might as well be forever. When you call something everlasting, you are saying it has no end — it keeps going no matter how much time passes.
Evermore means "always," "forever," or "for all time to come."
Every cloud has a silver lining

This expression means that every bad situation has something good hidden inside it — or at least something hopeful. No matter how dark or difficult a moment in life seems, there is always a positive side, a reason to hope, or a lesson to gain from it.

"Every dog has its day" means that everyone, at some point in their life, gets a moment of good luck, success, or recognition — even people who seem unfortunate, ordinary, or overlooked most of the time.
"Every inch" means completely, totally, and in every possible way — without exception.
An everyman is an ordinary, typical person — someone who represents what most regular people are like. Not a celebrity. Not a genius. Not a hero with special powers.
To evict someone means to officially and legally force a person to leave a property — usually a home, apartment, or land — that they have been renting or occupying.
Eviction is the formal, legal removal of a person from a property they are occupying, carried out by someone who has the legal authority over that property — most commonly a landlord.

Evidence is any information, object, or sign that gives you a reason to believe something is true or false. It is the "why" behind a belief — something real that you can point to, observe, or measure, which logically connects to a conclusion.
When "evidence" is used as a verb, it means to show, demonstrate, or prove something clearly — often a quality, a condition, or a fact. The thing doing the evidencing acts as proof.

When something is evident, it is clearly visible, clearly noticeable, or clearly understandable — so much so that you can recognize it without having to look hard, dig deep, or spend much time thinking. It is right there, showing itself openly.
Evidential means relating to, based on, or having the quality of evidence.
Evidentiary simply means "relating to, consisting of, or based on evidence."

Evil (as a noun) means deep, serious moral wrongness or harm — the opposite of good, but not just in a mild or ordinary sense. It refers to something profoundly wicked, destructive, or morally corrupt.
The evil eye is a curse — a form of supernatural harm — that is believed to be sent to someone through a powerful, envious, or hateful stare.

An evildoer is a person who deliberately does evil — meaning they commit acts that are deeply harmful, wicked, or morally wrong. The word is built from two simple parts: evil (something bad, wicked, or harmful) and doer (a person who does something).
To evince something means to show or reveal a quality, feeling, or characteristic clearly through outward signs — your behavior, actions, words, or manner — in a way that makes it obvious to others.

To eviscerate something means to remove its internal organs or guts. Think of a surgeon cutting open a body and taking out what's inside, or a hunter cleaning an animal after a kill by pulling out its entrails.
Evisceration means the act of removing the internal organs — the guts — from a living creature or a body. Think of it as "gutting" something completely.
Evocation is the act of calling something forth in the mind — a feeling, a memory, an image, a mood, or even a spirit — without directly stating it or physically producing it.

When something is evocative, it has the power to call up feelings, memories, or mental images in the person experiencing it — almost like unlocking something that was already inside them. The key idea is calling forth.
To evoke something means to bring it out — to call forth a feeling, a memory, an image, or a response from somewhere inside a person (or a group of people). Think of it like a key unlocking a door.
Relating to evolution, the gradual development of living things over many generations. It can also mean developing gradually rather than suddenly, as in "evolutionary change."
An evolutionist is a person who accepts and supports the theory of evolution — the scientific explanation for how all life on Earth came to be the way it is today.
To evolve means to change and develop gradually over a long period of time, usually becoming more complex, more advanced, or better suited to a situation.
A ewe is a female sheep that has reached adulthood — or at least sexual maturity, typically around 6–8 months of age or older, depending on the breed.

A ewer is a type of pitcher or jug — a container designed to hold liquid (most commonly water) and pour it out. But a ewer is not just any pitcher. It has a specific look and a specific history that set it apart.
With full official authority. In Catholicism, when the Pope speaks ex cathedra on matters of faith, his statement is considered infallible.
Ex gratia describes something — almost always a payment — that is given voluntarily, out of goodwill, when the person or organisation giving it has no legal duty to do so.

When someone holds a position, role, or membership ex officio, it means they have that role automatically and solely because of another position they already hold — not because they were specifically elected, appointed, or invited for that particular role.

"Ex officio" is a Latin expression. Ex means "from" or "out of," and officium means "duty," "office," or "position." Put together, it literally means "by virtue of one's office" or "from the office itself."
In law, done on behalf of one party only, without the other side being present or informed, as in "an ex parte hearing."
Done or made after the fact, with retroactive effect. An ex post facto law punishes actions that were legal when they were committed.
To exacerbate something means to make a bad situation even worse.
Exacerbation means the worsening of something that was already bad. It is not about something going from good to bad — it is specifically about something that is already bad, becoming worse.
When you call something exact, you mean it is perfectly correct, with zero error, zero deviation, and zero approximation. There is no "almost," no "roughly," no "about."

To exact something means to successfully demand and obtain it — usually through power, authority, pressure, or force. The critical thing to understand is that this word contains two ideas fused into one: demanding something AND actually getting it.
Demanding a very high standard of effort, care, or precision, and refusing to accept anything less.

Exaction means the act of forcefully demanding and obtaining something from someone — usually money, a payment, labor, or compliance — through the use of power or authority, often in a way that is harsh, unjust, or beyond what is rightfully owed.
Exactitude is a noun that means the quality of being perfectly exact, precise, and accurate in every detail — leaving absolutely no room for error, vagueness, or approximation.
To exaggerate means to describe, represent, or show something as being more than it actually is — bigger, worse, better, funnier, more dramatic, more extreme — in a way that goes beyond the truth.

When something is exaggerated, it means it has been made to seem larger, stronger, more extreme, or more important than it actually is. The truth is there — but it has been stretched, blown up, or overstated beyond what is real or accurate.

An exaggeration is a statement that describes something as bigger, worse, better, more extreme, or more significant than it actually is. It stretches the truth — not necessarily to lie, but to create a stronger impression.

To exalt means to raise something or someone up — either in rank and importance, or in praise and glory. Think of it as lifting something to the highest possible level, whether that's a person's status in society or a person's reputation in words.
Exaltation is about being lifted high — either in feeling, in status, or in glory. Everything this word does, it does with intensity and grandeur.

When used to describe a person's position or role in society, exalted means they hold a place of great importance, honor, and prestige — far above the average person. It suggests the kind of status that commands deep respect, even awe.
To examine something means to look at it very carefully and thoroughly so that you can understand it, find out the truth about it, or check whether something is right or wrong.
To exasperate someone means to make them feel intensely frustrated, annoyed, and completely out of patience — particularly through behavior that is repeated, ongoing, or impossible to easily stop.

When someone is exasperated, they are feeling a deep, worn-out mix of frustration and irritation — usually because their patience has been stretched and tested for too long. It is not simple, sudden anger.
If something is exasperating, it means it is deeply irritating and frustrating — the kind that wears you out emotionally.

Exasperation is a strong feeling of frustration and irritation that has been pushed to its limit. It is what you feel when something — or someone — has tested your patience so much that you feel like you simply cannot take it anymore.
To excavate means to dig into the earth and remove material from it — such as soil, rock, or sand — in order to achieve a specific goal.
Excavation means the act of carefully and deliberately digging into the ground to remove earth, rock, soil, or other material — or the resulting hole or site that is created by that digging.
To exceed something means to go beyond a set point, limit, level, or standard — to be more than it, greater than it, or past it.
To except means to deliberately exclude or leave out a specific person or thing from a general statement, rule, group, or situation that otherwise applies to everything or everyone else.
An exception is something that does not follow the general rule, pattern, or expectation that applies to everything else in its group.
An idiom meaning that an exception to a rule confirms the rule exists — for example, a sign saying "parking allowed on Sundays" implies that parking is not allowed on other days.

"Exceptionable" means open to objection — that is, something people could reasonably object to, criticize, disapprove of, or find inappropriate. If something is exceptionable, it is the kind of thing that deserves complaint or refusal.
"Exceptional" means standing apart from what is normal — either because it is remarkably, outstandingly good, or because it is a rare case that doesn't follow the usual rule.

An excerpt is a piece taken directly from something larger. Think of it like cutting a single slice from a whole loaf of bread — the slice is real bread, it came from the loaf, but it is not the whole loaf.
An excess is the amount of something that is more than what is needed, allowed, expected, or considered appropriate. It is the part that goes over the limit — the overflow.
Anything — such as emotional burdens, unnecessary people, or past experiences — that weighs you down and slows your progress.
Excessive means more than what is needed, reasonable, or acceptable. It describes something that has gone beyond a normal, appropriate limit.
Excessively means to a degree that goes beyond what is acceptable, normal, or needed.

In its most fundamental sense, an exchequer is a government's treasury: the official system or department that receives a nation's income (taxes, duties, fees), holds it, and controls how it is spent.
An excise is a special kind of tax that a government places on specific goods or activities — not on everything, but on a chosen list of particular things.
To excise something means to deliberately cut it out and remove it from something it was a part of.
Excision means the deliberate act of cutting something out and completely removing it from a larger whole.

Excitable describes a person (or animal) who gets emotional, worked up, or stimulated very easily and very quickly — often more than the situation really calls for. It is about how readily and intensely someone reacts to things around them.
To exclaim means to say something suddenly, and with strong feeling.
An exclamation is a word, phrase, or sentence that bursts out of a person because of a strong, sudden feeling.
Exclamatory is an adjective. It describes anything that expresses, contains, or has the nature of an exclamation — a sudden, strong outburst of emotion or feeling.
An exclave is a part of a country's territory that is physically detached from the main body of that country, with the land of one or more other countries lying in between.
To exclude means to deliberately keep someone or something out of something — a place, a group, a list, a category, a conversation, or any situation where they could otherwise be present or belong.
Exclusionary describes something that keeps certain people or things out — away from a place, group, activity, opportunity, or right.
Available only to a select few, as in "an exclusive club." It can also mean belonging to only one person or group, or not shared with others, as in "an exclusive interview."
"Exclusively" means only, and nothing or no one else. It draws a hard line around one specific thing, person, or group — and shuts everything else out completely.
Exclusivity means the state of being limited to only certain people, places, or things — and deliberately kept away from everyone else.

To excogitate something means to think it out carefully and thoroughly — to work something out in your mind through deliberate, focused, and sustained mental effort, usually arriving at a solution, plan, or idea as a result.

To excommunicate someone means to officially expel them from a religious community — cutting them off from membership, its rituals, and its spiritual benefits — usually as a punishment for doing something seriously wrong or for violating core beliefs.
Excommunication is the official act by a religious institution of expelling one of its members as the most severe form of punishment that institution can impose.
To criticize someone or something extremely harshly. In medicine, it means to scrape or rub away the skin.
When something — a review, a speech, a report, a letter — is described as excoriating, it means it is severely and harshly critical. Not just a little critical. Not just a firm disapproval.

Excoriation means the act of stripping, scraping, or tearing away the surface of something — most often skin — or the resulting damage left behind. Think of it as removal by force: something being scraped off, scratched off, or worn off from a surface.

Excrement is the solid or semi-solid waste that a human or animal body pushes out after digesting food. In plain terms, it is what comes out when you go to the toilet to "poop." When you eat, your body absorbs everything useful — nutrients, water, energy.

An excrescence is an ugly, abnormal outgrowth — something that has grown or been added onto something else in a way that is unwanted, out of place, and makes the whole thing worse. Think of it as an "ugly extra bit that doesn't belong."
To excrete means to push out or discharge waste substances from the body.
The process by which a living thing removes the waste products produced by its body's chemical reactions, such as urine and sweat.
Excruciating means so intensely painful that it is almost unbearable.
To exculpate someone means to clear them of blame, guilt, or responsibility for a wrongdoing.
Exculpation is the act of clearing someone of blame, fault, or guilt — or the result of that process, meaning someone has been fully relieved of responsibility for a wrongdoing they were accused of.
Exculpatory describes something that clears a person of blame, fault, or guilt — or at least helps to do so.

An excursion is a short journey or trip that you make for a specific purpose — usually for pleasure, curiosity, or exploration — and then return from. The "return" part is important. An excursion is never a one-way journey or a permanent move.
Tending to wander away from the main subject, especially in thought, speech, or writing.

An excursus is a focused, detailed discussion that an author deliberately inserts into a written work to explore a related topic — one that is relevant to the main subject but too involved to weave neatly into the main text.
Excuse means to let someone off — from blame, from judgment, or from a duty. Think of it as giving someone a free pass. That one idea runs through all its different uses.
Execrable means extremely and shockingly bad — so bad, in fact, that it provokes a strong feeling of disgust or moral outrage in the person describing it.
To execrate something means to feel or express an intense, deep hatred or loathing toward it — not ordinary dislike, but a powerful, overwhelming revulsion.

Execration means the deepest, most intense form of hatred — the kind so fierce and overwhelming that it doesn't stay quiet inside a person but erupts outward as a curse, a furious denunciation, or a public damning of someone or something.

Execute means to carry something out — to actually do it, complete it, and bring it to its finished state. It is not about planning, thinking, or intending. It is about the doing itself, and doing it fully, from start to finish.
Execution means the act of carrying something out — fully, completely, from start to finish. It is what happens when something moves from being a plan, an idea, or an order into reality.

An executioner is a person whose official job is to carry out the killing of someone who has been condemned to death. The key word here is official — the executioner acts on behalf of an authority, such as a government, a court of law, or a ruler.
An executive is a person who holds high-level authority in an organization — someone who has the power to make important decisions and the responsibility to make sure those decisions actually happen.

An executor is simply a person (or thing) that carries out, performs, or puts into effect a task, a plan, or a set of instructions. Think of the word "execute" — it means to do something, to carry it out. An executor is the one who does that carrying out.

Exegesis means a careful, detailed, and scholarly explanation or interpretation of a text. The whole point of exegesis is to dig into a piece of writing and pull out its true, intended meaning — meaning that already exists inside the text itself.
If you analyze a text slowly, deeply, and carefully — going word by word, line by line — to figure out exactly what it truly and originally means, your work is exegetical.

An exemplar is something or someone that is such a perfect, outstanding representative of a quality, category, or standard that others look to it as the model — the gold standard — of what that thing should look and feel like.

When you call something exemplary, you are saying it is so outstandingly good that it works as a model — a shining example that other people should look up to and try to copy. It is not just "good" or even "very good."

Exemplification means one of two closely related things: 1. The act of showing or explaining something through an example, or 2. A thing (a person, object, event, or case) that perfectly represents or illustrates something.
To be a typical or perfect example of something, as in "Gandhi exemplifies peaceful resistance." It can also mean to illustrate something by giving an example.
"Exempt" means officially freed from a rule, obligation, duty, or responsibility that applies to other people.
To exempt someone or something means to officially free them from a rule, duty, requirement, or obligation that normally applies to everyone else.

An exemption is an official freedom from a rule, duty, tax, or requirement that normally applies to everyone else. When someone has an exemption, they are legally or officially excused from something they would otherwise be obligated to do, pay, or follow.
To exert something means to actively bring it into use and direct it toward something or someone with intention and effort.

Exertion means the act of using a significant amount of physical or mental energy to do something. It is what happens inside you — and to you — when you push yourself to do something that takes real effort.
To exhale means to breathe out — to push air from your lungs outward through your nose or mouth.
Exhaustion means the state of something being completely used up or emptied out — with nothing left. Think of a battery that has been drained to zero. That zero-state is exhaustion.
Exhaustive means complete, thorough, and covering absolutely everything — leaving nothing out.
Exhibition means a public display of things or skills, organized so that people can come and see them.
Behaviour that is intended to attract attention to oneself. In psychology, it is a disorder in which a person exposes their genitals to strangers for sexual gratification.
A person who behaves in a way intended to attract attention to themselves; a show-off. In psychology, someone who exposes their genitals in public.
To exhilarate means to fill someone with a powerful feeling of joy, excitement, and energy — all at once. When something exhilarates you, it doesn't just make you happy.

When someone is exhilarated, they feel a rush of joy and energy at the same time. It's not calm happiness — it's the kind of happiness that makes your heart beat faster, puts a big smile on your face, and makes you feel like you could do anything.
When something is exhilarating, it makes you feel intensely alive, joyful, and full of energy — all at the same time, and usually very suddenly.
Exhilaration is a powerful, electric feeling of intense joy, excitement, and energy that surges through you during or after something thrilling, freeing, or deeply stimulating.
To exhort someone means to strongly and earnestly urge them to do something, usually because you genuinely believe it is important, right, or necessary.

An exhortation is a strong, sincere, and earnest urging — spoken or written — that tries to move someone to take action, behave in a certain way, or sometimes to stop doing something harmful. It is more than casual advice.
Exhumation is the act of digging up a dead body — or other buried remains — that was previously placed underground.
To exhume something means to dig it up from the ground after it has been buried.

Exigence means an urgent need, demand, or pressing requirement that arises from a specific situation. Think of it as what a situation forces upon you — the unavoidable call to act, respond, or address something because the circumstances make it critical.
An exigency is an urgent, pressing situation or need that demands immediate attention or action. It is something that cannot wait — the circumstances make it critical that you act now.
Requiring immediate attention or action, as in "exigent circumstances." It can also mean making heavy demands on someone.
Exiguous means extremely small in amount, size, or degree — so small that it is barely enough, or not enough at all.
The state of being forced to live away from your home country, as in "living in exile." An exile is also a person who lives this way.
To exile someone means to forcibly send them away from their home country — and ban them from ever returning — usually as a punishment or to remove them as a threat.
Eximious means remarkably distinguished, excellent, or eminent — describing someone (or something) that stands far above the ordinary, in a way that is genuinely worthy of recognition and admiration.
Existential simply means "relating to existence" — specifically to the very fact or experience of being alive and real, or to the survival of something.
Existentialism is a philosophical movement — a school of thought — that places the individual human being at the absolute center of all philosophical inquiry.

An existentialist is a person who accepts and lives by the ideas of a philosophy called existentialism — a school of thought centered on one big, bold claim: you are not born with a fixed purpose. You create your own meaning through the choices you make.
An exit poll is a survey conducted with voters immediately after they have cast their vote and are walking out ("exiting") of the voting station.
An exit strategy is a carefully thought-out plan for how you will leave, end, or get out of something — before you even fully commit to it.
In linguistics, describing a compound or phrase whose meaning is not contained in any of its parts — for example, "redhead" is not a kind of head.
An exodus is when a large number of people leave a place all at once, usually because of something bad — danger, hardship, war, oppression, or a crisis of some kind. It is not just any departure.
Exogenous means coming from outside a system, body, or model — as opposed to being generated, caused, or created from within it.

To exonerate someone means to officially declare — usually backed by evidence or authority — that a person is not guilty of a wrongdoing they were accused of. It means their name is cleared. The blame is lifted. They are free from the accusation.

When someone is described as exonerated, it means they have been officially and formally declared free of blame or guilt for something they were accused of. The accusation existed. The suspicion was real.
Exoneration is the act of officially clearing someone of blame, guilt, or wrongdoing — formally stating that they are not responsible for something they were accused of.
Exorbitance means the quality or state of being far beyond what is reasonable, fair, or acceptable. It is not just "a lot" — it is "way, way too much, to the point where it becomes wrong or unjust."
Exorbitant means unreasonably and shockingly excessive — far beyond what is normal, fair, or acceptable.
To exorcise something means to drive out or expel something harmful, evil, or deeply troubling — either from a person, a place, or even from your own mind.

An exorcism is a formal religious or spiritual ritual performed to drive out an evil spirit, demon, or supernatural force that is believed to be inhabiting and controlling a person, a place, or an object — against that person's will.

An exorcist is a person who performs a ritual — called an exorcism — with the goal of expelling an evil spirit, demon, or supernatural force that is believed to have taken control of a person, place, or object.

An exordium is the opening section of a formal speech or piece of writing — specifically, the introductory part that comes before the main body of the work and is designed to prepare the audience or reader for everything that follows.
Quite literally, an exoskeleton is a skeleton on the outside of the body, rather than on the inside.
Exoteric describes something that is open, accessible, and intended for the general public — anyone can engage with it, regardless of their background, training, or level of expertise.
Exothermic is an adjective used to describe any process, reaction, or change that releases energy — primarily in the form of heat — into its surroundings.

Exotic means strikingly unusual, fascinating, or different — especially because it comes from a faraway or foreign place. It is the feeling of encountering something that feels far outside your everyday, familiar world.
Expand means to become larger, wider, or more extensive — or to make something larger, wider, or more extensive.
When you expand on something, you take a topic that has already been briefly mentioned and say more about it — you add detail, depth, and fuller explanation.
An expanse is a large, open, unbroken stretch of something — usually something you can see spreading out widely before you or around you. Think of standing at the edge of a beach.
Expansionism is the belief, policy, or practice of growing — usually a country, empire, or organization — by taking over more land, resources, people, or influence, often at the expense of others.

Expansionist describes a desire, tendency, policy, or attitude that is strongly focused on growing bigger, wider, or more powerful — and actively pushing to make that happen, especially by taking over or absorbing things that were outside one's original boundaries.
Covering a wide area, as in "an expansive garden." Of a person, friendly, open, and willing to talk freely.
To expatiate means to speak or write about something at great length and in thorough detail, going well beyond a surface-level explanation.
An expatriate is a person who is living in a country that is not their home country — the country where they were born or of which they are a citizen.

To expatriate means to remove a person from their native country, or to leave one's own country to settle somewhere else. The action always involves a person separating from their homeland — either by force or by their own choice.
Expatriation means leaving your home country to live in another country, or more formally, giving up your ties — and sometimes your legal citizenship — to your native country.

Expectancy means the state or feeling of waiting for something you believe is going to happen. It's the inner experience of anticipation — a kind of alert, emotionally charged readiness directed at something you think is coming.

When someone is expectant, they are in a state of waiting — but not ordinary, passive, emotionless waiting. It is waiting that comes with a feeling. That feeling is a charged, alert, eager sense that something is about to happen.

An expectation is a belief that something will happen, will be true, or will be a certain way — before you have actually seen it occur. It lives in your mind, pointed toward the future (or toward something you haven't yet experienced).
To expectorate means to cough up material — usually mucus or phlegm — from your throat, airways, or lungs, and spit it out through your mouth.
Expedience means doing or choosing what is convenient and practically useful right now — especially when that choice comes at the cost of doing what is right, fair, or principled.
Expediency means choosing what is convenient, practical, or personally advantageous in a given situation — especially when that choice comes at the cost of what is honest, fair, or morally right.

Something is expedient when it is the most practical and convenient thing to do in a given situation — but the word quietly hints that it might not be the most honest, fair, or principled thing to do.
To expedite something means to make it happen faster than it normally would.
An expedition is an organized journey made for a specific, serious purpose — usually to explore, study, discover, or accomplish a mission in a place that is distant, remote, or difficult to reach.

An expeditionary force is a military force sent out from its own country to operate in a foreign or distant place. The word carries several powerful ideas packed together: It is deployed far from home. The force travels outward, beyond its own borders.

Expeditious means quick and efficient — done without unnecessary delay and done properly at the same time. It is not just about being fast. It is about getting something done fast and well, without wasting time or effort.
Expeditiously means in a way that is both fast and efficient — getting something done quickly without wasting time, effort, or resources.

To expel something or someone means to force them out — out of a place, an organization, or a body — usually with authority, pressure, or official power. The key feeling behind the word is that the exit is not voluntary.

To expend something means to use it up — to put it toward a purpose in a way that depletes or reduces your supply of it. Think of it like drawing water from a tank: every time you use some, there is less left.
