"Fit" means right for a particular purpose, role, or situation. Think of a key and a lock — when the key is the right one, it fits. Everything else branches from this central idea.

"Fit as a fiddle" means to be in excellent health and physical condition. When someone says a person is "fit as a fiddle," they mean that person is very healthy, full of energy, and feeling great — like there is absolutely nothing wrong with them.
A sudden display of irritation or offended pride, usually because someone feels ignored or disrespected, as in "he stormed out in a fit of pique."
"Fit out" means to provide a person, place, or vehicle with everything it needs to be ready for a specific purpose — all the right equipment, furniture, clothing, supplies, or tools.

When something or someone "fits the bill," it means they are exactly what is needed for a particular purpose or situation. They meet all the requirements, match all the expectations, and are perfectly suitable.

Fitful means happening in short, irregular bursts — starting and stopping repeatedly, rather than flowing smoothly and continuously. Something fitful is unsteady, broken up, and unpredictable in its rhythm.

When something is fitting, it is exactly right and appropriate for a particular situation. It belongs there. It matches the moment perfectly — not just in a "good enough" way, but in a way that feels natural, proper, and just as it should be.
To arrange a date for someone. It can also mean to provide someone with something they need, such as a place to stay, or to repair or decorate something.

Fixate means to focus on something so intensely and persistently that you struggle to pull your mind — or eyes — away from it. It's not just paying attention. It's when your attention becomes locked, almost like a hook catches something and won't let go.

"Fixation" is about being stuck — mentally, emotionally, or physically attached to something in a way that doesn't move or change. Think of a pin that holds a butterfly in place on a board. That's the underlying image: something held firm, unable to move on.
To fizzle means to make a weak, sputtering, hissing sound — like the sound a wet match makes when you strike it, or a dying spark.
A fjord is a long, narrow, and very deep arm of the sea that cuts into the land, with steep rocky walls or cliffs rising high on both sides.
To flabbergast someone means to shock or astonish them so deeply and completely that they are momentarily left speechless, frozen, or unable to respond normally.
Flabbergasted means being so extremely surprised and shocked that you are left completely stunned — often speechless, wide-eyed, and unable to react or respond normally, even if just for a moment.

Flabby describes something that is soft, loose, and lacking firmness — when it should ideally be tight, toned, or strong. Think of flesh that jiggles, wobbles, or sags when it moves. That is the image the word "flabby" paints.
"Flaccid" describes something that lacks firmness, tension, or strength — something that is soft and limp when it should be (or once was) firm and strong.
A flag is something that marks, signals, or represents — but what exactly it looks like and what it does changes quite a bit across different uses. Here is every major meaning explained clearly.

When you flag something, you mark it — physically or digitally — so that it stands out and doesn't get missed or forgotten. The idea is simple: you are placing an invisible "look at this!" sign on something.

To flagellate someone means to whip or beat them repeatedly — usually with a whip, a rod, a strap, or a similar instrument. It is not a casual or accidental act. The word always implies a deliberate, forceful, repeated striking.
Flagging describes something that is losing its strength, energy, or enthusiasm — something that was once going strong but is now noticeably weakening or slowing down.

Flagitious means deeply, outrageously, and shockingly wicked or criminal. It describes something so morally corrupt and villainous that it causes genuine horror or disgust in anyone who witnesses or hears about it.

A flagon is a large container used for holding and serving liquids — almost always an alcoholic drink like wine, beer, or cider. Think of it as a big jug built specifically for drinking occasions, whether at a tavern table, a feast, or a gathering.
When something is flagrant, it means it is so obviously wrong, bad, or unacceptable that it is impossible to miss or ignore. It screams at you.
Literally, a flagship is the most important ship in a naval fleet — the one that carries the commander and flies the identifying flag. Every other ship in the fleet follows the flagship's lead.

A flail is a tool — or sometimes a weapon — made of two sticks connected by a flexible joint (like a hinge, a leather strap, or a chain). The key feature is that the two parts are not rigidly attached.
Flail means to move or wave wildly, without control — often in a frantic or desperate way. The key idea hiding inside this word is loss of control combined with frantic effort.

"Flair" describes something special — a quality that goes beyond ordinary. It suggests that something is done (or possessed) in a way that feels natural, impressive, and a little bit extraordinary. It is always a compliment.
Strong criticism, as in "the government took a lot of flak for the decision." Literally, anti-aircraft fire.
To flake out means to fail to do something you had already agreed or promised to do, usually at the last minute and without a good reason.
Flamboyance is the quality of being strikingly showy, bold, extravagant, and attention-commanding — in the way someone looks, behaves, speaks, or presents themselves to the world.
Boldly and dramatically showy in appearance, behaviour, or personality, in a way that is impossible to ignore.
A flame is the hot, glowing, flickering stream of burning gas that you see when something is on fire.
To flank something or someone means to be at the side of it, or to move to the side of it. The word is all about the side — not the front, not the back, but the side.

A flapper is a word that has one very famous, dominant meaning — and that is the one nearly everyone thinks of first: a young woman of the 1920s who deliberately broke away from the traditional rules of how women were supposed to look, behave, and live.

When something flares, it does one of two things (sometimes both at once): It suddenly becomes more intense, bright, or active — like a small flame that suddenly roars up. It spreads outward from a narrow point — like the bottom of a bell-shaped skirt.
When something such as violence, anger, or an illness flares up, it suddenly becomes more intense or worse. Literally, a fire flares up when it suddenly burns more strongly.
A flare-up is a sudden, often unexpected outbreak or worsening of something — usually something bad — that happens quickly after a period of calm or control.

A flash flood is a sudden, very fast, and powerful rush of water that overwhelms an area in a very short time — typically within a few minutes to around six hours. The word "flash" is key here: it signals speed and surprise.
A "flash in the pan" is something — a person, a product, a trend, a moment of success — that starts with a big, exciting burst but quickly fizzles out and amounts to nothing lasting.
A flashback is a sudden, vivid return to the past — a moment when something from an earlier time is brought sharply into the present, either in someone's mind or within a story.
A place or situation where violence or conflict is likely to break out, as in "the region is a flashpoint." In science, it is the lowest temperature at which a liquid's vapour can catch fire.
When something is flashy, it is designed or intended to attract attention — usually through bright colors, expensive looks, bold style, or impressive skill. It says: "Look at me. Notice me."

The flat look is a visual design style where everything appears two-dimensional, clean, and simple — like a sticker on a flat piece of paper. It deliberately avoids any effect that makes things look three-dimensional, textured, or physically real.

"Flat out" is an informal English expression that generally signals something done to its fullest, most extreme degree — whether that's maximum speed, maximum effort, absolute directness, or complete exhaustion.
Caught unprepared and unable to react quickly, as in "the news caught them flat-footed." Literally, having flat feet with little or no arch.
To die, as shown by a flat line on a heart monitor. Figuratively, to stop growing or developing, as in "sales have flatlined."

To flatter someone means to praise them in a way that is more generous, more enthusiastic, or more exaggerated than the truth really warrants — often to make them feel good, or to get something in return.

Flattery is excessive, insincere praise given to someone — not because you truly mean it, but because you want to get something from them, make them like you, or make them feel good for your own benefit.

Flatulent is an adjective that describes anything to do with gas that builds up inside the digestive system — the stomach and intestines — and eventually needs to escape from the body, either as a burp from the mouth or as gas passed from the rear end.
To flaunt something means to display it very openly and deliberately so that other people notice it — usually out of pride, and often in a way that feels excessive or showy.
A flavoring is any substance that is added to food or drink specifically to give it a taste, to change its existing taste, or to make its taste stronger.
A flaw is an imperfection — something that is wrong with, or missing from, a person or thing, which prevents it from being as good, strong, or perfect as it should be.
A flaw is an imperfection — a mistake, a crack, a weakness, or anything that makes something less than perfect. So flawless simply means: having zero flaws. Not one. Not even a tiny, hidden one.

Flaxen describes a very specific shade of pale, light yellow — soft, gentle, and slightly washed-out. Picture the color of dry straw, ripe wheat stalks in a field, or dried corn silk. That delicate, creamy pale-yellow is exactly what "flaxen" means.

To flay means to strip or peel the skin off a body — human or animal — usually with a knife or a sharp instrument. The skin is not merely cut or wounded; it is removed, peeled away from the flesh underneath.
A fleck is a tiny, small mark, spot, or fragment of something — usually one that stands out visually against a background or surface.
Flection means the act of bending something, or the state of being bent. Think of it as a word that captures bending — as an action or as a condition.
When fledgling is used as an adjective, it describes something — or someone — that is new, undeveloped, and still in the early stages of growth or existence.

A fledgling is a young bird that has recently grown its first real feathers and has just left its nest, but is still in the process of learning to fly and survive on its own. It is no longer a helpless, freshly-hatched chick.
To flee means to run away from someone or something — quickly and urgently — because of fear, danger, or threat. It is not ordinary leaving.

A fleece is the full coat of wool that naturally grows on a sheep's body. Think of it as the sheep's built-in "sweater" — a thick, dense, soft layer of woolly fibers covering almost the entire animal.

To fleece someone means to cheat them out of their money — usually a lot of it — through dishonesty, trickery, or by charging an outrageously unfair price. The person being fleeced doesn't realize what's happening, or realizes it only when it's too late.

To fleer means to mock or laugh at someone with open contempt and scorn. It's not a gentle tease or a friendly joke — it's a sharp, sneering kind of mockery that is meant to make the other person feel small, foolish, or inferior.
A fleet is a group of vehicles — especially ships, but also aircraft, cars, or trucks — that belong to the same owner or organization and are used together for a shared purpose.
Something fleeting lasts for only a very short time and disappears quickly — so quickly, in fact, that you can barely hold onto it before it's gone.

When you call someone "your own flesh and blood," you mean they are your biological relative — your child, parent, sibling, or another blood relation. It emphasizes that you share the same blood, the same biological origins.
To flesh out means to add more detail, depth, and substance to something so that it becomes fuller and more complete.
Relating to the body and its physical desires, especially sexual ones, rather than the mind or spirit.

A fleur-de-lis (plural: fleurs-de-lis) is a specific, highly recognizable decorative symbol that looks like a stylized, three-petaled flower — most commonly described as a lily or iris. It is not a photograph or a realistic drawing of a flower.
"To flex" means to bend or to tighten. But depending on the context, it takes on quite different shades of meaning.
Flexibility is the quality of being able to change, adapt, or adjust easily — without breaking, failing, or resisting too much.
A quick, light, sharp movement, as in "a flick of the wrist." Informally, a flick is a film, and "the flicks" is the cinema.

Flick means to make a quick, light, snapping movement — usually with your fingers, wrist, or a thin object. Think of the motion you make when you snap a crumb off a table. That's a flick. It's fast, it's light, and it involves a small, sharp jerk of movement.
"Flick through" means to turn the pages of something — like a book, magazine, or newspaper — quickly and casually, without reading everything carefully.
To flicker means to move, shine, or appear in a quick, unsteady, and repeated way — going back and forth between being there and almost not being there, never quite settling into one steady state.

A flighty person is someone who is unreliable, unfocused, and hard to pin down. They jump from one idea, mood, plan, or interest to another very quickly, without much thought, and without following through. They are not grounded or steady.
A flimflam is a trick designed to deceive someone — usually to cheat them out of their money, their trust, or something else valuable.

Flimsy means not strong enough for what it needs to do. It describes something that is too weak, too thin, or too unconvincing — something that fails to hold up when pressure is applied to it, whether that pressure is physical force or logical scrutiny.
To flinch means to make a small, sudden, involuntary movement — usually pulling back or tensing your body — as an automatic reaction to something painful, frightening, shocking, or deeply unpleasant.
A short, casual romantic or sexual relationship. It can also mean a brief period of indulging in something enjoyable, or an attempt at something new.
Hard, cold, and unyielding, as in "a flinty stare" or "flinty determination." Literally, made of or like flint stone.

Flip means to turn something over quickly with a sharp, light motion. Think of the action — fast, clean, often with a flick of the wrist. A pancake flips when it spins in the air and lands on its other side.
To make an offensive gesture at someone by raising the middle finger.
To suddenly lose control of your emotions, especially from anger or panic. It can also mean to become wildly excited.
The most common, everyday meaning of "flip-flop" is a simple, flat, open sandal.
When someone flip-flops, they completely reverse their position or opinion on something — and then often reverse it again, or do so repeatedly.
Flippancy is the quality of treating something serious, sensitive, or important as though it is trivial, amusing, or not worth genuine care.
When someone is flippant, they treat a serious or important matter as if it is trivial — with a casual, breezy attitude that clearly does not belong in the situation.

When you flirt with someone, you behave toward them in a way that hints you find them attractive — but you do it lightly, playfully, and without full seriousness. It's like sending a signal of romantic or sexual interest without actually declaring it openly.
To flit means to move quickly and lightly from one place to another — and then move on again, without staying anywhere for long.

To flitter means to move rapidly in a light, restless, back-and-forth or darting way — like something that can't quite stay still. Think of a candle flame in a breeze, or a butterfly that keeps zipping from flower to flower.
To float an idea means to suggest an idea in a tentative, exploratory way — not as a final plan or firm decision, but as a gentle proposal to see how others respond to it.
Floccinaucinihilipilification is the act of deciding — or the habit of deciding — that something is worthless or has no value at all.
Soft, fluffy, and woolly in appearance, like tufts of cotton. In chemistry, describing a precipitate that forms loose, fluffy clumps.

A floe is a large, flat sheet of ice that floats on the surface of the sea or another large body of water. Think of it as a natural raft made entirely of ice — not something someone built, but something the ocean itself created by freezing.
When you flog someone, you beat them hard and repeatedly — usually with a whip, a cane, a rod, or a strap — most often as a form of physical punishment.
To "flog a dead horse" means to waste your time and energy on something that is already finished, hopeless, or impossible to change. You are putting in effort where no effort can make any difference.

A flood is water covering land that is normally dry. It happens when water — from rain, rivers, seas, melting snow, or broken dams — rises beyond its usual boundaries and spreads over ground where it does not normally exist.
A floodgate is a large, heavy gate or barrier built into a dam, canal, reservoir, or river channel. Its job is simple but powerful: to control the flow of water.
A floorboard is one single, long, flat, and narrow strip of wood that is used to build a floor. Think of it like a wooden plank — not too thick, not too wide, but quite long.

To flop means to fall, drop, or land in a heavy, loose, and uncontrolled way — without grace or stiffness. Think of a rag doll being dropped: it doesn't land neatly or upright. It just collapses in a soft, floppy heap. That's the spirit of "flop."
Flora refers to all the plant life found in a particular place or time. It is a collective noun — meaning it refers to an entire group as a single idea, not just one plant.

Floral means of, relating to, or resembling flowers. Think of it as the adjective form of "flower." Whenever something is connected to flowers — its appearance, its smell, its taste, or its scientific study — you can describe it as floral.

Florescence means the state, act, or period of flowering — the time when a plant produces its flowers and is in full bloom. It describes both the process of coming into flower and the condition of being in flower.
Florid means excessively elaborate, showy, or overdone. Something florid has gone beyond what is tasteful, simple, or necessary — it is too much, too loud, too decorated.
When something is described as floriferous, it means it produces many flowers, or is abundantly full of them.
A flotilla is a group of small ships or boats that travel or operate together. Think of it as a team of small vessels moving as one unit, usually for a shared purpose.

Flotsam refers to pieces of a wrecked ship, or the goods and cargo from that ship, that are found floating on the surface of the sea — having ended up there by accident, typically because the ship sank, broke apart, or was destroyed by a storm.
Odds and ends of floating wreckage from a ship. Figuratively, worthless or unimportant things, or people who have been rejected or abandoned by society.

To flounce means to move in a way that is deliberately dramatic and exaggerated, usually to show that you are angry, offended, or displeased. It is not just about how you move — it is about why and what that movement is communicating.
When a person or thing flounders, they are struggling in a messy, confused, uncontrolled way — trying to cope or move forward but failing to do so with any grace, clarity, or success.
Flourish means to grow, develop, and do very well — not just to survive, but to truly thrive in the fullest, most vibrant sense possible.

When something is described as flourishing, it is not just alive, okay, or even simply "doing well." It is growing, developing, and functioning in a way that is healthy, vigorous, and abundant — reaching its full potential.

To flout something means to openly and deliberately disobey or disregard a rule, law, norm, or convention — and to do so in a way that shows you simply don't care about it, or even hold it in contempt.

A flowchart is a diagram that shows a process, system, or workflow as a series of steps connected by arrows. It turns something that happens over time — a sequence of actions and decisions — into something you can see all at once on a single page.
Of language, using too many fancy or elaborate words and phrases. Literally, full of flowers or decorated with flower patterns.

To flub something means to perform it badly or incorrectly, especially when you were expected — or had prepared — to do it well. It is about making a noticeable, often embarrassing mistake in the middle of doing something.
To fluctuate means to keep changing repeatedly — going up and down, or back and forth — over a period of time, without settling at one fixed, stable point.
A fluctuation is a change in something that goes up and down repeatedly, without settling into one stable level. It is not a single, one-time change.

A flue is a channel — a hollow passage — through which smoke, hot gases, steam, or hot air travels from a source of heat to the outside world. Think of it as a dedicated escape route for heat and harmful gases produced by burning something.

Fluency means the quality of doing something — most often speaking or writing a language — in a way that is smooth, easy, natural, and effortless. When someone has fluency, they do not struggle, pause unnecessarily, or have to work hard to express themselves.

"Fluent" describes something that flows smoothly, naturally, and without interruption. Think of a river — water doesn't stop, stutter, or struggle. It moves effortlessly from one point to the next. That image of smooth, unbroken flow is the soul of this word.

When something is fluffy, it is soft, light, and airy — and it usually has fine, loose fibers, fur, or feathers that stand up slightly and spread out, giving it a full, rounded, cloud-like appearance.
Fluidity means the quality of being able to flow, change, adapt, or move smoothly without being fixed or rigid.
A fluke is something good that happens not because of skill or planning, but purely by chance — a stroke of luck that you couldn't repeat even if you tried.
Empty, meaningless talk or flattery that sounds pleasant but has no real substance. It is also an old-fashioned sweet, soft pudding.
To flummox someone means to confuse them so completely and suddenly that they are left totally frozen — not just unsure, but with absolutely no idea what to say, do, or even think next.

If you are flummoxed, you are so completely and suddenly confused that you don't know what to think, say, or do next. Your mind essentially goes blank. It is not mild confusion — it is the kind of confusion that stops you in your tracks.
To flump means to drop, fall, or sit/lie down heavily — with your full weight — in a clumsy, graceless way, usually making a soft, dull thudding sound in the process.
A flunky is a person who blindly does whatever a more powerful person tells them to do — without questioning, without thinking, and often without dignity.
Something is fluorescent when it absorbs invisible light (or other radiation) and immediately converts it into visible light, making it appear to glow or shine with unusual brightness.
A flurry describes a sudden, brief burst of many things happening at once. Think of it as a moment where things suddenly rush in together — quickly, intensely — and then calm down just as fast.

When two surfaces are flush, it means they sit at exactly the same level — one does not stick out or sink in compared to the other. There is no bump, no gap, no ridge, no step between them. They form one single, seamlessly flat, continuous surface together.
To become red in the face, from embarrassment, heat, or emotion. It also means to clean something with a rush of water, as in "flush the toilet," or to drive someone or something out of hiding.
To force someone or something out of hiding. It can also mean to clean something by forcing liquid through it.
Having a red face, from heat, exercise, or strong emotion. Flushed with something means excited and elated by it, as in "flushed with success."

A fluster is a state of nervous confusion and agitation. When someone is in a fluster, their mind feels scrambled and unsettled — they are mentally overwhelmed, anxious, and unable to think or act calmly. It is not a gentle kind of confusion.

To fluster someone means to make them feel nervous, confused, and mentally scattered all at once, usually because of sudden pressure, surprise, or too many things demanding their attention at the same time.
When someone is flustered, they are in a state of being confused, nervous, and agitated all at once — so much so that they cannot think clearly or act calmly.
A flute is a long, thin, tube-shaped wind instrument that produces sound when you blow air across a small opening near one end.

Flutter describes a quick, light, and slightly irregular movement — something that moves rapidly back and forth or up and down, but in a delicate, wavering way. Think of a butterfly's wings, or a piece of paper caught in a gentle breeze.
Fluvial is an adjective that means "of, relating to, produced by, or found in a river or rivers."
At its deepest level, flux captures the idea of flow or continuous change. Think of a river — water is always moving, never the same from one moment to the next.
To fly in the face of something means to openly go against it, defy it, or contradict it — especially when that thing is widely accepted, well-established, or considered obvious.
"Fly off the handle" means to suddenly become very angry, lose control of your emotions, and react in an explosive, unreasonable way — often over something small or without much warning.
When someone says "I wish I were a fly on the wall," they mean: "I wish I could secretly observe that situation without being seen or without affecting what happens."

To "fly the coop" means to escape or leave a place, especially when that place feels limiting, restrictive, or confining. It often suggests that the departure is sudden, secretive, or done out of a desire for freedom.

When you call something or someone fly-by-night, you mean they are untrustworthy, unreliable, and not serious — the kind that appears suddenly, cannot be depended on, and may disappear just as quickly as they showed up, usually after causing some damage or taking your money.
A foal is a baby horse — specifically, a horse that is one year old or younger. The moment a horse is born, it is a foal. It stays a foal until its first birthday.
Focal means "relating to, or situated at, a focus."
"Focus" as a noun means a central point — either a precise point in physical space where things converge, or a point in the mind where attention gathers.

Fodder means material that is used up to feed or fuel something else. Think of it as the "input" that keeps something going — whether that something is an animal, a conversation, a war, or a media cycle.

A foe is an enemy — someone who is against you, who opposes you, or who actively tries to harm, defeat, or work against you. If someone is your foe, they see you as their enemy, and you see them as yours. It is a two-sided, hostile relationship.
A fogey is a person — almost always older — who is stuck in the past. They strongly dislike change, cling to old habits and old ideas, and often disapprove of anything modern or new.
A foible is a small, harmless weakness in someone's personality or character — the kind of flaw that makes you shake your head and smile, not the kind that makes you angry or disgusted.
A person or thing that makes another stand out by contrast, as when a calm character acts as a foil to a hot-headed one. Foil is also very thin sheet metal, or a light fencing sword.
To foil someone means to stop them from succeeding at something they were actively trying to do. You step in, and their plan or attempt falls apart.

To foist something on someone means to push or pass something off onto them — usually through tricks, pressure, or deception — when they would likely refuse it if they knew the full truth or had a real choice.
"Folderol" means nonsense — specifically, things that are silly, trivial, and a waste of your time or attention. It's a word people use when something has no real value, substance, or seriousness.
Foliage means the leaves of a plant or tree — but not just one leaf. It refers to all the leaves together, seen as a single, unified mass of greenery.

"Folie à deux" is a French phrase. "Folie" means madness or lunacy. "À" means of or for. "Deux" means two. So the phrase translates literally to "madness of two" — a shared madness between two people.

Folklore is the collection of traditional stories, beliefs, customs, practices, sayings, songs, and art that a community — a group of people who share something in common, like a culture, religion, region, or ethnicity — passes down from one generation to the next.

A folktale is a traditional story that originally belonged to the ordinary people of a community — the "folk" — and was passed down from generation to generation by word of mouth, long before anyone wrote it down. Nobody knows who first made up these stories.
Follow means to come after something or someone. But "after" can mean after in place, after in time, after in logic, or after in influence.

"Follow suit" means to do the same thing that someone else has done — to copy or imitate someone else's action, often because their action sets an example or creates a kind of pressure for others to do the same.
To follow through means to complete something fully — not just start it, but see it all the way to the end.

At its most essential level, a follower is someone who comes after, goes behind, or orients themselves according to another person, idea, or force. The word always implies a relationship — there is always something or someone being followed.
Folly means serious foolishness — the kind that comes from a lack of wisdom, judgment, or good sense. It's not just a small slip or honest mistake.
To foment means to deliberately stir up, encourage, or keep alive something negative — most often unrest, conflict, hatred, or rebellion — usually in a slow, sustained, and somewhat secretive way.

"Fond of" means to have a warm, gentle, and deep liking for something or someone. When you are fond of something, you don't just casually like it — you have a soft, affectionate feeling toward it that has settled comfortably in your heart.
Fontina is a type of cheese — specifically, a semi-soft to semi-hard cow's milk cheese that originated in the Aosta Valley, a small mountainous region in northwestern Italy near the Alps.

A food court is a large, open area — usually inside a shopping mall, airport, or similar building — where many different food stalls or small restaurants are grouped together in one place, and all of them share a single common dining area with tables and chairs where customers sit and eat.
Food insecurity is the condition in which a person or household does not have reliable, consistent, and adequate access to enough safe, nutritious food to maintain a healthy and active life.
"Fool's gold" is the popular nickname for a naturally occurring mineral called pyrite (its scientific name is iron pyrite, with the chemical formula FeS₂ — meaning it is made of iron and sulfur).
Foolhardy means being boldly reckless — taking dangerous risks without thinking them through, in a way that shows poor judgment rather than true courage.

When you call something foolproof, you mean it is so well-designed, so simple, or so reliable that it is impossible — or nearly impossible — to fail at it, mess it up, or make it go wrong, even if the person using it is completely careless, clumsy, inexperienced, or not paying attention.
To "foot the bill" means to pay for something — usually something expensive, or something paid on behalf of other people.
The word footage is a noun that has two main areas of meaning — one tied to video and film, and one tied to measurement in feet.
A footfall is the sound that a foot makes when it touches the ground as someone walks.
A secure position from which further progress can be made, as in "the company gained a foothold in the market." Literally, a place where a foot can be placed safely when climbing.
All the meanings of footing grow from one central image: how firmly and securely something is placed on the ground it stands on.

Footling means trivially unimportant, pointlessly silly, or ridiculously minor. When you call something footling, you are saying it is so small, petty, or foolish that it is barely worth your attention — and yet, annoyingly, it is demanding it anyway.
If someone is footloose, they are free — free to go wherever they want, live however they please, and make choices without being held back by responsibilities, commitments, or obligations.
Footsore describes a person whose feet are sore, aching, and exhausted — specifically because they have been walking or standing for a very long time.

A fop is a man who is obsessively, ridiculously vain about his appearance — his clothes, his hair, his accessories, and his overall image — to the point where it defines him entirely and makes him look foolish in the eyes of others.

Foppery means excessive, ridiculous vanity about one's clothes, appearance, and manners — combined with a shallowness that makes a person care more about looking impressive than about anything of real substance.

Foppish means being excessively, obsessively, and ridiculously concerned with one's own appearance, clothing, and personal style — in a way that comes across as vain, silly, and superficial. It almost always describes a man.
"For all intents and purposes" means in every practical way that matters or in effect, even if not technically or officially true.
Despite all of his outward show of confidence or boldness — suggesting that the confidence was not quite real.
"For good" means permanently — something that will last forever, with no going back.
When someone does something "for good measure," it means they do something extra — something beyond what was strictly needed or expected — just to make things more complete, safe, or thorough.
"For what it's worth" is a phrase you say before sharing your opinion, suggestion, or information when you are not sure how useful or important it will be to the other person.
To forage means to go out and actively search for food, especially by looking around in your natural surroundings, exploring different spots, and gathering what you find.

A forager is a person or animal that searches for and collects food from the wild — from nature itself — rather than farming it, raising it, or buying it. The food is simply out there in the environment, and the forager goes looking for it.
Foraging is the act of going out into the natural world to search for and collect food.

A foray is a venture into unfamiliar or challenging territory — a bold step into something new, different, or outside your usual world. Think of it as dipping your foot into waters you have never swum in before.

To forbear means to consciously hold yourself back from doing something — especially something you feel tempted to do, want to do, or even have the right to do — out of patience, self-control, or consideration for others.
Forbearance means choosing to hold back — deliberately stopping yourself from doing something you have every right or reason to do, and doing so with patience and calmness.

A forbearing person is someone who stays calm, patient, and restrained — especially in situations where most people would get angry, complain, or hit back. They hold themselves back from reacting harshly, even when they have every reason to.
To forbid something means to officially or authoritatively tell someone that they must not do it. It is a command — not a request, not a suggestion — that says: this is not allowed.
When something is forbidden, it means it is not allowed — and not just casually not allowed, but actively and deliberately prohibited by some rule, authority, law, or strong social/moral code.
When something is described as forbidding, it means it has a harsh, threatening, or deeply unwelcoming quality that makes you instinctively feel like you should stay away from it.
To force something means to make it happen despite resistance — by applying pressure, power, or compulsion strong enough to overcome whatever is pushing back.

Force majeure refers to an extraordinary event or circumstance that is completely outside anyone's control — something so unexpected and powerful that it makes it impossible for a person or organization to fulfill a promise, duty, or legal obligation.
"Force of habit" means doing something automatically, without thinking, simply because you have done it so many times before that your mind or body just does it on its own.

To force someone's hand means to put someone in a situation where they have no real choice but to act, decide, or reveal something — often earlier than they wanted to, or in a way they weren't planning.
Strong, powerful, and effective in a way that is hard to ignore or resist.
To ford something means to cross a body of water — a river, stream, or creek — by walking, riding, or driving through it, rather than using a bridge or a boat.
Fore as an adverb means at the front or toward the front — specifically of a ship, boat, or aircraft.

Your forearm is the part of your arm located between your elbow and your wrist. It is the lower section of the arm — the part you see when you stretch your arm out in front of you, from where it bends in the middle all the way down to where your hand begins.
A forebear is an ancestor — a person who lived before you in your family, from whom you or your family descended.

A foreboding is a feeling — deep inside you — that something bad is going to happen. Not something bad that is happening right now, and not something bad that has already happened. It points forward, toward the future.
When you forecast something, you look at existing information and then make a careful, reasoned statement about what will happen in the future.

To foreclose means to permanently shut off a right, a possibility, or an option — cutting it off so completely that it can never be recovered or pursued again. Think of it as closing a door and sealing it shut for good, not just for now.

Foreclosure is the legal process by which a lender — usually a bank — takes ownership of a property from a borrower who has stopped making the agreed loan payments. It is both the process of taking that property back and, once complete, the event itself.

A forefather is a person who lived before you — in an earlier generation — and whose life, actions, or decisions have had a meaningful impact on your life, your community, your country, or the world you live in today.
The leading or most important position, as in "at the forefront of research."

When you forego something, you make a deliberate, conscious decision to skip it, abstain from it, or not take it — even though you had the option to. The key is that it is always a voluntary choice, never a forced one.
"Foregoing" means previously mentioned or stated earlier in the same text or speech.
The part of a picture or view that is nearest to the viewer. Figuratively, the most important or noticeable position, as in "issues in the foreground of the debate."

To foreground something means to deliberately place it at the centre of attention — to make it the most prominent, visible, and important thing in a piece of communication, a work of art, a discussion, or an argument.
Foreknowledge means knowing that something will happen before it actually happens.

A forelock is a lock of hair — meaning a tuft, strand, or section of hair — that hangs down over the forehead. The word is built simply: fore means "front" or "in front of," and lock here means a strand or bunch of hair.

A foreman is a person who is in charge of a group of workers and supervises their work. They are not the top boss of a company — they sit in the middle: above the ordinary workers but below the higher management.
Most importantly, used mainly in the phrase "first and foremost," as in "she is first and foremost a teacher."
Forensic means "connected to or used in the process of establishing facts for legal or official purposes — especially through careful, scientific investigation."
The use of scientific methods to investigate crimes and gather evidence that can be used in a court of law.
The scientific methods used to investigate crimes. In schools and colleges, forensics is also the study and practice of formal debate.

A forerunner is a person, thing, or event that comes before something else and has a direct, meaningful connection to it — either by preparing the way for it, being an early version of it, or signaling that it is coming.
To foresee something means to know or sense that it will happen before it actually does — not through magic, but through your thinking, experience, or reasoning.
Foreseeable describes something that can be predicted, anticipated, or expected using your current knowledge and reasonable thinking.
To foreshadow something means to give an early hint or clue that something is going to happen later — without directly saying it outright.

Foreshadowing is a hint, clue, or warning placed early in a story that quietly prepares you for something that will happen later. It's a signal from the author — dropped in advance — that something significant is coming.
Foresight is the ability to think ahead — to imagine what might happen in the future and then prepare for it wisely, before it actually happens.
To forestall something means to prevent it from happening by acting before it can occur. The single most important word in that definition is before. You are not reacting to something.
A foretaste is a small, early experience of something that is yet to come — one that gives you a genuine sense of what the full thing will feel like, even though you're only getting a fraction of it.
To foretell something means to say or indicate that something will happen in the future, before it actually happens.
Forethought means careful thinking or planning that you do before something happens — not during it, not after it, but before.

To forewarn someone means to warn them about something before it happens — especially something unpleasant, dangerous, or difficult — so that they have enough time to prepare, protect themselves, or simply not be caught off guard.
If you know about something in advance, you are better prepared to deal with it.

A forewarning is a warning that arrives before something bad actually happens. It is an advance signal — something that tells you a danger, a difficulty, or bad news is on its way, giving you time to prepare or respond before it reaches you.
A forfeit is something you lose — or are forced to give up — specifically because you broke a rule, failed to meet an obligation, or did something wrong.

To forfeit something means to lose it — or be forced to give it up — as a direct consequence of something you did wrong, a rule you broke, an obligation you failed to meet, or a right you failed to use in time.
To forfend means to prevent something bad from happening, or to ward off something undesirable. Think of it as actively keeping something terrible at bay — pushing it away before it can occur.
To create something strong through effort, such as a relationship or agreement. It also means to shape metal by heating and hammering it, or to make a fake copy of a document or signature.
To forge ahead means to move forward with determination and effort, especially when things are difficult.
Fake and made to deceive, as in "a forged signature." It can also mean shaped by heating and hammering metal, or created through hardship, as in "a bond forged in war."
Forgery means making a fake version of something — usually a document, signature, piece of art, or official paper — with the deliberate intention of deceiving someone into believing it is real.

Forgetful means having a tendency to forget things — often, easily, or more than is considered normal. When you describe someone as forgetful, you are saying that their memory regularly fails them. It is not about forgetting something once by accident.

To forgive someone means to make a conscious, deliberate decision to let go of the anger, resentment, or desire for revenge that you feel toward a person who has hurt or wronged you — and to stop holding that wrongdoing against them.

Forgiveness is the conscious, deliberate act of letting go of resentment, anger, or the desire to punish someone who has wronged you — even if they don't deserve it, haven't apologized, or have never changed.
To forgo something means to deliberately choose not to have it, do it, or enjoy it — even when you could.
To fork out means to pay money, especially when you feel reluctant, forced, or unhappy about paying it. The amount is usually something you consider too much, or something you didn't plan to spend.
"Forlorn" describes a very specific kind of sadness — not just ordinary unhappiness, but a sadness that comes from feeling lonely, abandoned, and without hope.
Formal means following established rules, conventions, or proper procedures — whether in behavior, language, clothing, situations, or thinking.

Something that must be done because of rules or custom, but has little real importance, as in "the interview is just a formality." It can also mean correct, polite behaviour that follows strict rules.

To formalize something means to make it official, structured, or recognized through a proper, accepted process. You take something that already exists in a loose, casual, or unofficial way — and you give it a solid, formal shape.
"Formally" means in a formal way — that is, following proper rules, official procedures, accepted conventions, or strict definitions.
"Formation" comes from one simple root: the verb form, meaning to make, create, shape, or develop something. When that action becomes a noun, it gives you "formation."
Something "formative" is something that actively shaped or molded a person, idea, or thing into what it eventually became — leaving a deep, lasting mark on its development.
"Former" means used to be, but no longer is. It tells you that something was true in the past, but that situation has changed. The person or thing has moved on from that state.
"Formerly" is an adverb. It means in the past — but with one critical addition: it always carries the silent message that the situation has since changed.
When you call something formidable, you are saying it is so powerful, impressive, or difficult that it fills you with a sense of awe, respect, or even fear.

Something is formulaic when it follows a fixed, ready-made pattern so closely that it ends up feeling mechanical, predictable, and unoriginal — as if it was made by filling in the blanks of a template rather than through any real, fresh thinking.
To formulate something means to carefully create, develop, or express it — usually an idea, plan, strategy, or theory — in a clear, deliberate, and well-organized way.

The act of carefully creating or expressing an idea, plan, or rule, or the way something is expressed. It is also a mixture of ingredients prepared for a purpose, as in "a new formulation of the drug."

To forsake someone or something means to deliberately leave them behind, give them up, or turn away from them — especially when they needed you, or when you had a duty, bond, or deep connection to them.
When someone or something is forsaken, it has been completely abandoned — left behind, given up on, and stripped of any care, love, or support, often in a way that feels total and permanent.
Forsooth is an adverb that means "in truth," "truly," or "indeed."

To forswear something means to solemnly and seriously commit to giving it up, renouncing it, or having nothing more to do with it — often permanently. When you forswear something, you are not simply deciding to stop doing it.
Your forte is the thing you do exceptionally well — your single greatest strength, the area where you naturally shine above everything else.
About to happen or appear soon, as in "her forthcoming novel." Of a person, willing to share information. Of help or money, ready and available when needed.

When we say someone is forthright, we mean they are open, direct, and honest in the way they communicate. They say what they think and what they know — clearly, confidently, and without hiding anything. They don't beat around the bush.

Forthwith means immediately — right now, without any pause, delay, or hesitation. When something must be done forthwith, it must be done straight away. There is no "I'll do it later," no asking for more time, and no acceptable reason to wait.

Fortification means the act of making something stronger, tougher, or more resistant — and also the result of that strengthening. Think of it as "adding strength where it is needed most, to hold against a threat or weakness."
Fortified means made stronger, more secure, or more capable of withstanding something difficult.
To fortify something means to make it stronger, tougher, or more resistant — specifically in a way that prepares it to face something difficult, threatening, or depleting.

Fortitude is the inner strength of mind and spirit that allows a person to face pain, hardship, danger, or suffering — and keep going — without falling apart, giving up, or losing hope. It is quiet, steady, internal toughness.
A fortnight is a period of exactly two weeks, or 14 days.
Fortuitous means happening by chance — something that occurs accidentally, without anyone planning or intending it. It describes events that simply happen on their own, as if by luck of the draw.

A fortuity is something that happens purely by chance — not because anyone planned it, caused it, or intended it. It is an event, circumstance, or result that comes about through random luck rather than through design, effort, or reason.

When you describe someone or something as fortunate, you mean they have been favored by luck or chance — something good happened to them, or they are in a good situation, often without fully earning it or without it being guaranteed.
A forum is a place — physical or virtual — where people come together to discuss, debate, or exchange ideas on a particular topic.
Forward means in the direction of what is ahead — toward the front, toward what comes next, toward progress. It is the opposite of backward.
Forward-looking means focused on the future rather than the past or the present.

A fossil is the naturally preserved remains or traces of a living thing — an animal, a plant, or any other organism — that died a very long time ago, usually thousands to millions of years in the past, and whose existence has been recorded in rock or similar material in the Earth.
The word "fossilized" always carries one central idea: something that was once alive or active, but has now become permanently hardened, fixed, and frozen in place — unable to move, change, or grow.
When "foster" is used as an adjective, it describes a family relationship that exists because of care and nurturing, not because of biology or blood.

To foster something means to actively care for it and help it grow or develop over time. You're not forcing it to exist — you're creating the right conditions so that it can naturally develop and strengthen.
A foster home is a private home where a trained, approved adult (or couple) temporarily raises a child who cannot live with their own family, under the supervision of a government agency.

"Foul" describes something that is deeply unpleasant, offensive, or seriously wrong — whether to your senses, your moral values, or a set of rules. It's important to understand from the start that "foul" is not a mild word.
"Foul play" means dishonest, unfair, or criminal behavior — especially actions that involve violence, deception, or breaking rules to harm someone or gain an unfair advantage.
"Foul up" means to make a serious mistake that ruins, spoils, or badly damages something — usually through carelessness, poor judgment, or incompetence.

Foul-smelling means having a very bad, deeply unpleasant, or disgusting odor. It describes anything that gives off a smell so offensive that it makes people want to turn away, cover their nose, or leave the area.

Foulmouthed describes a person who regularly and habitually uses offensive, vulgar, or crude language — such as swear words, obscene expressions, and deeply inappropriate words — especially in situations where such language is considered shocking or disrespectful.
To establish an organization or institution, as in "founded in 1850." To be founded on something means to be based on it. "Found" is also the past tense of "find."

Foundation means the base or support that everything else is built upon or depends on. It is the thing that comes first, sits underneath, and holds everything else up. If the foundation is weak or missing, whatever rests on it will collapse or fail.
So basic and essential that everything else is built on it and depends on it, as in "a foundational principle."

A founder is a person who creates something — brings it into existence from nothing — and establishes it as a lasting entity. The "something" is typically an organization, institution, company, movement, city, or nation.
To founder means to sink, collapse, or fail completely — and almost always permanently. It describes something that doesn't just hit a rough patch, but actually goes under and is finished.
A foundry is a factory or workshop where metal is melted into liquid form and then poured into molds to create solid metal objects of specific shapes.

A fount is a source — specifically, a rich, generous, and seemingly endless source from which something flows. Think of it like a spring of water that never runs dry. Whatever flows from a fount flows naturally, abundantly, and from a deep origin.
The original source from which something springs and spreads, as in "the fountainhead of modern science." Literally, the spring where a river or stream begins.

A fowl is a bird — but not just any bird in any situation. The word is almost always used for birds that are closely connected to humans, particularly birds that are kept, raised, or hunted for food (their meat or eggs) or sometimes for their feathers.
To trick or outwit someone cleverly. It can also mean to baffle or confuse someone, as in "the question foxed everyone."
A foxhole is a small hole dug into the ground by a soldier during a battle or war, used as a hiding place and protection from enemy fire.
A foyer is the first room or area you enter when you walk into a building — the space that sits right at the entrance, between the outside world and the rest of the interior.

"Frabjous" means wonderfully joyous and delightful — describing something so good, so exciting, and so celebratory that it fills you with a feeling of pure, triumphant happiness. It's not ordinary, quiet contentment.
A fracas is a noisy, chaotic, disorderly disturbance — usually a quarrel or a minor fight — that happens suddenly and involves a messy mix of shouting, confusion, and sometimes physical scuffling.
Fracking is a method of drilling deep into the Earth to extract oil and natural gas that are trapped inside hard rock formations underground.

A fraction is a way of expressing a part of a whole, or more precisely, a division of one quantity by another. The word "fraction" has two main lives — one in mathematics (its primary and most detailed meaning), and one in everyday general language.
Fractious describes something — or someone — that is irritable, quarrelsome, and difficult to manage or control.
To fracture something means to break or crack it — but not just anything. Fracturing specifically happens to things that are hard, rigid, and solid, like bones, rocks, glass, ice, or concrete.

Fragile describes something that breaks, cracks, or gets damaged very easily. If something is fragile, it cannot handle rough handling, pressure, or stress — even a small amount of force or disturbance is enough to damage or destroy it.

Fragility is the quality of being easily broken, damaged, or destroyed — whether physically, emotionally, or in a more abstract sense. When something has fragility, it means it cannot withstand much pressure, stress, or force before it falls apart.
A fragment is a small, broken-off, or incomplete piece of something that was — or is meant to be — a larger whole. The word has two closely connected uses, both built on the same central idea.
Made up of small, scattered, disconnected pieces of a larger whole, with much of it missing, as in "fragmentary evidence."
The process of something breaking apart into smaller, disconnected pieces, or the broken-up state that results, as in "the fragmentation of the party."

Fragrant describes something that has a pleasant, sweet smell. When you say something is fragrant, you are telling people that it produces a nice aroma — one that is agreeable and enjoyable to breathe in.
Frail means weak in a way that makes something or someone easily hurt, broken, or overwhelmed. It is not just any kind of weakness — it is a delicate, fragile kind of weakness.

Frailty means the state or quality of being weak, delicate, and easily damaged or broken. Think of something fragile — a thin piece of glass, a dried leaf, an old photograph — and frailty is the name for that condition of fragility.
A frame is the rigid structure that goes around the edges of something to hold it, protect it, or display it.

"Frame of mind" refers to your mental and emotional state at a particular moment in time — basically, the way you are thinking and feeling right now, which shapes how you see things, react to situations, and make decisions.
An effect predicted by Einstein's general relativity, in which a massive rotating object such as the Earth twists the fabric of spacetime around it as it spins.
A framework is a foundational structure — physical or abstract — that gives shape and support to something larger, while leaving space for the details to be filled in.
A franchise is a right or privilege that one party officially grants to another.
Frangible means capable of being broken; easily broken or shattered into pieces.
When you describe a person as frank, you mean they say exactly what they think — openly, directly, and honestly — even when the truth is uncomfortable or unwelcome.
Frankincense is a natural, aromatic resin — a hard, gum-like solid — that comes from the bark of certain trees belonging to the Boswellia family.
Frankness is the quality of saying what you truly think or feel, directly and openly, without hiding it — even when it might be uncomfortable, awkward, or difficult to hear.
Frantic describes a state where a person is so gripped by fear, worry, or urgency that they lose their calmness and act in a wild, rushed, and uncontrolled way.
Frantically means doing something in a way that is fast, desperate, and slightly out of control — driven by panic, fear, or extreme urgency.
"Frat" is simply a short, informal word for fraternity — a type of social club or brotherhood that exists at colleges and universities, mainly in the United States.
A party held at a college fraternity house — typically loud and crowded, with plenty of drinking.
Fraternal means of, relating to, or befitting brothers. Think of it as the adjective form of the word "brother."
Fraternity means a feeling of brotherhood — a deep sense of friendship, loyalty, and togetherness between people, as if they were all brothers in the same family.

To fraternize means to socialize with someone in a warm, familiar, and friendly way — like a close friend or a brother would. When people fraternize, they are not just being politely civil to one another.
Fratricide means the killing of one's own brother. That's the single clearest, most direct definition. Everything else about this word grows outward from that center.
Fraud means deliberate deception to gain something at someone else's expense.
Fraudulence is the quality or condition of being deliberately deceptive — of being dishonest in a calculated, intentional way, usually to gain something at someone else's expense.

Something is fraudulent when it involves deliberate deception — meaning someone has intentionally lied, faked, or tricked others — usually to gain money, power, or some other benefit they are not honestly entitled to.

"Fraught" means heavily loaded with something difficult, dangerous, or distressing. Think of it as a container that is completely packed — not with good things, but with trouble, risk, tension, or anxiety.

A fray is a situation of intense conflict — a fight, a battle, a heated argument, or a fierce competition. Think of it as a scene where multiple parties are clashing hard, whether with fists, weapons, or words.

To fray means to slowly come apart at the edges — or to cause something to do so. The key idea is that something which was once solid, intact, or held together begins to weaken, unravel, and fall apart, bit by bit, from the outside in.
Frayed describes something that has worn down at its edges or surface until it starts to come apart — usually with loose, ragged threads, fibers, or strands sticking out untidily.
To frazzle someone means to exhaust them completely — not just physically, but also mentally and emotionally, all at once.
A "freak of nature" refers to a person, animal, or thing that is so far outside the boundaries of what is normal, expected, or possible that it seems almost impossible to explain.

A freckle is a small, flat, harmless spot on the skin that is darker than the skin surrounding it. It sits level with the skin — it does not bump out or rise up. You can feel nothing when you touch it.

"Free rein" means giving someone complete freedom to do whatever they want, in whatever way they choose, without restrictions, rules, or interference. When someone is given free rein, nobody is controlling them, limiting them, or telling them what to do.

Free verse is a type of poetry that does not follow fixed rules about rhythm or rhyme. The poet is free to write each line however they feel is right — any length, any sound, any structure — without obeying a set pattern.
When a man free-balls, he wears no underwear beneath his outer clothing — his pants, shorts, trousers, or whatever he has on his bottom half.
A free-for-all describes a situation where there are no rules, no control, and no order — and everyone is involved, often all at once.
A freebooter is a person who roams around — on sea or land — stealing, looting, and plundering purely for their own personal gain, with no loyalty to any ruler, nation, or cause.
When you describe something as freeing, you mean that it gives you a powerful sense of release, liberation, or relief — as if a weight has been lifted off you, or a cage around you has been opened.
A freeloader is a person who enjoys the benefits of something — money, food, services, hospitality, effort — without contributing anything in return, and often without any intention of ever doing so.

A freeway is a special type of road built for fast, uninterrupted travel. When you drive on a freeway, you won't find any traffic lights, stop signs, or crossroads cutting through it. Traffic moves continuously — no stopping, no waiting.
To freewheel means to coast along without using an engine or pedals, letting momentum do the work. The vehicle keeps moving, but no active power is being applied to it.

Freewheeling describes a person, a style, or a way of doing things that is free from rules, restrictions, or outside control — moving through life (or through a situation) in a loose, independent, go-where-the-wind-takes-you manner.
Freight refers to goods or cargo that are being transported from one place to another, especially in large quantities, and usually for a commercial or business purpose.

Frenetic means wildly fast, intensely busy, and barely controlled. When something is frenetic, it is moving or happening at such a rapid, chaotic pace that it feels almost out of control — like everything is happening at once, too fast, with too much energy.

Frenzied describes something — a person, their behavior, a crowd, an activity, or a situation — that is wildly out of control due to extreme emotion or urgency. That emotion could be excitement, panic, anger, or desperation.

A frenzy is a state of wild, uncontrolled excitement or activity in which a person — or a group of people — becomes so overwhelmed by emotion, urgency, or desire that they lose their usual calm and clear-headedness.

A fresco is a painting made directly on a wall or ceiling — but not just any wall painting. What makes a fresco unique and special is how it is made: the paint is applied onto wet plaster, not a dry surface.
A freshet is a sudden, powerful surge of water that causes a stream or river to rise dramatically and overflow.

To fret means to worry — but not in a casual, passing way. When you fret about something, you worry about it persistently, anxiously, and somewhat restlessly. Your mind keeps returning to the problem, circling it, unable to let it go.

Fretful describes someone who is in a state of mild but persistent distress — a mixture of worry, irritability, and restlessness that makes them difficult to calm or please. A fretful person isn't simply sad, and they aren't simply angry.

Fretwork is ornamental decoration made by cutting or carving an interlaced, repeating pattern into a material, most often leaving deliberate open spaces (holes or gaps) alongside the solid portions that form the design.

A Freudian slip is when you mean to say one thing, but accidentally say something completely different — and that "accident" secretly reveals what you were actually thinking or feeling deep down, even if you didn't realize it consciously.
Friable means easily crumbled into small pieces or powder with very little effort.
To fribble means to behave in a silly, frivolous, and pointless way — or to waste something valuable (especially time, money, or opportunities) on things that don't matter.
At its most essential, friction is resistance. It is the force or tension that arises when two things push against each other, slow each other down, or refuse to move past each other easily.

"Friendly fire" refers to a situation where a person, group, or military unit is accidentally attacked, wounded, or killed by their own side — by the very people who are supposed to be protecting them or fighting alongside them.

A frieze is essentially a long, horizontal decorative band or strip. Think of it as a ribbon of decoration stretched across a surface — usually a wall or a building — that is meant to be looked at and admired.
A frigate is a type of warship — a military vessel built to fight at sea. But what kind of warship, and how it differs from others, has changed significantly over centuries.

Frigid means intensely and uncomfortably cold. Not just a little chilly — think of the kind of cold that bites at your skin, makes your breath visible, and stops you in your tracks. It is a strong, emphatic word.

A frill is a strip of fabric, lace, or paper that is gathered or folded tightly along one edge — causing it to bunch up into small, tight folds — while the other edge hangs free and loose, creating a soft, wavy, ruffled effect.
Frilly describes something that is decorated with frills — or more broadly, something that looks or feels excessively ornate, dainty, and over-decorated in a soft, fussy way.

The outer edge of an area or group, or the people and ideas furthest from the mainstream, as in "the fringes of society." It is also a decorative edge of hanging threads, or hair cut to hang over the forehead.
An extra benefit an employer gives an employee on top of their salary, such as a company car, health insurance, or a gym membership.

Frippery means things that are showy, unnecessary, and have little or no real value. The key combination here is: something looks fancy or elaborate on the outside, but when you think about it honestly, it adds nothing meaningful.

When someone frisks another person, they run their hands firmly over the outside of that person's body and clothing to check whether anything is hidden — usually a weapon, drugs, or other illegal items.
Frisky describes a kind of cheerful, bouncy, playful energy — the sort that makes you want to run around, jump, or fidget with excitement. It is not calm, not serious, and not still.
A frisson is a sudden, brief wave of excitement or thrill that washes over you — one that you actually feel in your body, not just in your mind.
A fritter is a piece of food — fruit, vegetable, meat, seafood, or almost anything — that is coated in a thick, wet batter and then deep-fried in hot oil.
To fritter something means to waste it — but not in just any way. It means to waste something valuable gradually, in small amounts, on unimportant or trivial things, until eventually it is all gone.
To fritter away something means to waste it gradually by spending it on small, unimportant, or foolish things — until it is all gone.
Frivolity is the quality of not being serious — of treating things lightly, wasting time on silly or unimportant things, or behaving in a way that lacks purpose or depth.
Something frivolous is something that has little to no real importance, value, or seriousness — yet it is being treated as though it deserves attention, time, or effort.

A frock is a garment — a piece of clothing. Depending on the context, it refers to one of a few different types, but at its heart, it always means a loose, flowing piece of clothing that covers the body.
To frogmarch someone means to forcibly move them from one place to another against their will, by physically gripping them and pushing or propelling them forward.

A frolic is a cheerful, playful activity full of fun and laughter — the kind where people (or animals) move around freely, laugh, and enjoy themselves without any serious purpose. It's pure, carefree enjoyment.
To frolic means to play in a joyful, energetic, and carefree way — moving your body freely while feeling happy and light-hearted.

Frolicsome means full of playful, carefree, lively joy. It describes someone — or something — that loves to play, act silly, and have fun in a light-hearted, energetic way, without a worry in the world.
"From here on out" means starting from this moment and continuing into the future, with no planned end.
"From pillar to post" means being moved, sent, or pushed from one place to another — repeatedly, without clear purpose, and usually without getting the help or result you actually need.
When you do something "from scratch," it means you start it from the very beginning — from zero — with nothing prepared beforehand, no shortcuts, and no pre-made help.

When you get information "from the horse's mouth," it means you are getting information directly from the original source — the most reliable, firsthand person who actually knows the truth about something.
"From time immemorial" means from a time so far back in the past that no one knows, remembers, or can trace when it actually began.
A frond is a large leaf — but not just any leaf. It is specifically the kind of large, often feathery, divided leaf that grows on ferns, palm trees, and a few related plants.
A frontrunner is a person, team, organization, or thing that is currently leading a competition and is considered most likely to win it.
"Frore" means frozen or intensely, bitterly cold. When something is described as frore, it is not merely chilly or cold in an ordinary sense — it is cold in a total, gripping, penetrating way.
Frost is a thin, white layer of tiny ice crystals that forms on surfaces — like grass, leaves, car rooftops, and windows — when the air gets cold enough and moisture is present.
Frostbite is a serious injury to your skin and the tissue beneath it, caused when part of your body literally freezes due to extreme cold.
Very cold, with frost forming, as in "a frosty morning." Figuratively, cold and unfriendly, as in "a frosty reception."
Full of or covered with froth, as in "a frothy cappuccino." Figuratively, light, entertaining, and lacking serious substance, as in "a frothy romantic comedy."

Froward means stubbornly refusing to do what is right, expected, or asked — not out of confusion or ignorance, but out of a deep, habitual tendency to resist and go against what is reasonable or good.
A frown is a facial expression. Specifically, it is the look on a person's face when their eyebrows pull together and move downward, causing lines or wrinkles to appear on the forehead.
Frowzy describes something — or someone — that is untidy, stale-smelling, and generally neglected in appearance or atmosphere. It carries a sense of mustiness, dirtiness, and a lack of care.

To fructify means to bear fruit, or to cause something to bear fruit — either literally (as in plants and trees) or, far more commonly, figuratively (as in efforts, plans, ideas, or investments producing good results).
When you describe someone as frugal, you mean they are careful and deliberate about how they spend money and use resources. A frugal person does not waste.

Frugality is the quality of being careful, intentional, and wise about how you spend money and use resources. A frugal person avoids waste, avoids overspending, and tries to get the most value out of what they have.

The "fruit of one's labours" means the results or rewards that a person receives from their hard work and effort. In other words, it refers to what you gain — or what comes back to you — because of the effort you put into something over time.

Fruitful means producing something good and valuable. When something is fruitful, it doesn't just do something — it delivers real, worthwhile results. Think of a fruit tree that is loaded with ripe, good fruit.
Fruition means the successful realization of something that was hoped for, planned, or worked toward. It is the moment — or the state — when an idea, a goal, a dream, or a plan finally becomes real.

Fruitless means producing no useful result, benefit, or success — despite effort being made. When something is fruitless, you tried, you worked, you invested time or energy, but in the end, you got nothing worthwhile out of it.
When you call someone frumpy, you are saying that they look unstylish, dull, and unflattering in the way they dress and present themselves.
To prevent a plan or effort from succeeding. It also means to make someone feel annoyed and helpless because they cannot achieve what they want.

When you are frustrated, you feel upset, irritated, and helpless because something is blocking you from getting what you want or doing what you are trying to do. You have a goal. You are trying to reach it.

Something is frustrating when it blocks you from achieving what you want, makes your efforts feel wasted, or keeps you stuck — and as a result, it causes a feeling of irritation, helplessness, or discouragement in you.
Frustration is the feeling you get when you want something to happen — but something keeps blocking you from getting it.
As a noun, "fuchsia" has two closely connected meanings — a plant and a color.

A fuddle is a state of mental confusion — a muddled, foggy, disoriented condition of the mind where a person cannot think clearly, cannot organise their thoughts properly, or cannot make sense of what is happening around them.

A fuddy-duddy is a person who strongly dislikes change, clings to old habits and old ways of thinking, and tends to disapprove of anything new, modern, or different. In short, they are stuck in the past — and they are quite comfortable being stuck there.
To fudge something means to be slightly dishonest or deliberately vague about it — usually to avoid trouble, hide an uncomfortable truth, or escape giving a clear, direct answer.
When someone fudges the issue, they deliberately avoid dealing with a problem or question in a clear, honest, and direct way.
To fuel something means to give it the energy, power, or force it needs to keep going — or to grow stronger.
The quality of passing away quickly; fleetingness. In chemistry, it is a measure of how strongly a substance tends to escape from a mixture, used in place of pressure for real gases.
Quick, fleeting, and hard to hold onto, as in "a fugitive glance" or "fugitive thoughts." It can also mean running away or escaping, especially from the law.
A fugitive is a person who is running away from someone who is trying to catch them.
A fugue is a type of musical composition (or a self-contained section within a larger piece) built around a single short melody.
A rare mental condition in which a person loses their memory of who they are, often wanders far from home, and may take on a new identity, with no memory of it afterwards.
A fulcrum is the fixed point on which a lever rests and pivots.
To fulfill something means to take something that was expected, required, promised, or hoped for — and actually make it happen, completely and properly.
A deep sense of satisfaction and purpose from doing something meaningful or using your abilities fully. It can also mean the completion of a promise, duty, or order.

Fulgent means shining with an intense, dazzling, and powerful brightness. When something is fulgent, it doesn't just glow softly or look shiny — it blazes with a brilliance that is striking, overwhelming, and hard to ignore.
Dark and sooty, like thick smoke or soot. Figuratively, gloomy and murky.

When you say someone is "full of beans," you mean they are bursting with energy, enthusiasm, and good spirits. They are lively, cheerful, and very active — almost like they have too much energy to sit still.

"Full steam ahead" means to move forward with maximum effort, speed, and determination, without slowing down or stopping. When someone says this, they mean: go as fast and as hard as you can, without hesitation.
"Full tilt" means at maximum speed, force, or energy — with absolutely nothing held back.
When something is full-blown, it means it has reached its complete, most developed, most extreme state. Nothing is missing. Nothing is partial. It has gone all the way.

Full-fledged means completely developed, fully qualified, or having everything it needs to be a true and complete example of what it is. Nothing is missing, nothing is partial, and nothing is still in progress — it has reached its final, whole, real form.
Expressed with total commitment, openly and without holding back, as in "full-throated support." Literally, loud and powerful, using the full voice.
