To fulminate means to protest or condemn something loudly, angrily, and with great force — usually at length. When someone fulminates, they are not simply complaining. They are thundering. They are ranting with passion, moral outrage, or fury.
A fulmination is a fierce, loud, and angry verbal attack — specifically one that is full of moral outrage and forceful condemnation. It is not just criticism. It is criticism delivered with thunder.
"Fulsome" means praise or flattery that is so excessive, so over-the-top, that it starts to feel fake, hollow, or even uncomfortable to witness. It is not a compliment.

To fumble means to do something with clumsy, unsteady, poorly-controlled hands — or to handle a situation badly and without confidence. Fumble is about losing control — of an object, of words, or of a situation.
To feel or show intense anger, often silently, as in "she was fuming." Literally, to give off smoke, gas, or strong-smelling vapour.

To fumigate means to fill a space — such as a room, a building, a ship, or even soil — with toxic or disinfecting chemical gases in order to kill pests, germs, or other harmful living organisms inside it.
A funambulist is a tightrope walker — a person who walks, balances, and performs skilled movements on a thin rope or wire that is stretched tightly between two points, usually high above the ground.
A function is the specific purpose or role that something is designed to perform, or the job it naturally carries out.

Functional means working properly and serving its intended purpose. If something is functional, it does what it is supposed to do. If it is not functional, it has broken down or failed to perform its role.

A functionary is a person who holds an official position in an organization — particularly a government, political party, or large institution — and whose job is to carry out specific, assigned duties that keep that organization running.
So basic and essential that everything else depends on it, as in "a fundamental right." It can also mean affecting the very core of something, as in "a fundamental change."

Fundamentalism is the strong, unwavering belief that a particular set of core principles — usually from a religion or ideology — must be followed exactly as they were originally stated, without any change, reinterpretation, or compromise, regardless of how the world changes around them.

A fundamentalist is a person who believes in a strict, literal, and completely uncompromising reading of the core principles of a belief system — and refuses to water them down, reinterpret them, or allow them to be changed, no matter what.
"Funerary" is an adjective that means relating to, used for, or associated with death, burial, and the rituals around them.
Funereal means having the feel, mood, or atmosphere of a funeral.

Something is fungible when one unit of it can be swapped for another unit of the same thing, and the swap makes absolutely no difference. Every unit is perfectly interchangeable with every other unit.

A fungus is a living organism — a life form that is neither a plant, nor an animal, nor a bacterium. It belongs to its own separate kingdom of life, called the Fungi kingdom. The plural of fungus is fungi, though "funguses" is also acceptable.
"Funk" has a few quite different meanings depending on context. Here they are, one by one.

"Funky" is a surprisingly versatile word. It can be a compliment, a complaint, or a warning — and the same person might use it in all three ways in a single day. Here's every important meaning, explained clearly.
To funnel something means to direct or channel it from a wider, spread-out place into a narrower, more specific path or destination — in a controlled and deliberate way.
To furbish something means to clean, polish, or restore it so that it looks bright, fresh, and as good as new again — especially after it has become dull, worn, or neglected over time.
Furious means extremely and intensely angry — not just a little upset, not simply annoyed, but overwhelmingly, powerfully angry. It sits at the far end of the anger scale.
Furiously means doing something with extreme force, energy, or anger — to a very intense, almost uncontrolled degree.
To furl something means to roll or fold it up tightly and neatly around a pole, rod, or central support — and often to secure it there so it stays compact and doesn't unravel.
A furlong is a unit of distance — a way of measuring how long a stretch of land or a path is.

A furlough is a temporary, approved period of time away from a duty or job, where the person is expected to come back after that period ends. The single most important word here is temporary. A furlough is never permanent.
Furnish means to provide or supply something — usually something that is needed, requested, or expected. Think of it as a deliberate, purposeful act of giving, not a casual one.
A furore is a sudden, intense wave of public outrage, controversy, or excitement — triggered by a specific event, statement, or decision — that sweeps through a large number of people all at once.

A furrow is a long, narrow groove or trench — a channel cut into or pressed into a surface, with slightly raised edges on either side. Think of dragging a stick through wet mud: the sunken line it leaves behind is essentially a furrow.
To furrow something means to cut, press, or scrunch something into deep lines, grooves, or channels. Think of dragging your finger through soft clay — it leaves behind a long, narrow trench.
Furtherance means the act of helping something move forward toward a goal.
Furtive means acting in a secretive, sneaky way — doing something quietly and carefully so that nobody notices you, usually because you know you're doing something wrong, forbidden, or embarrassing.

Furtively means doing something in a secretive, sneaky way — usually because you are afraid of being caught, or because you know what you're doing is wrong, forbidden, or something others would disapprove of.
Fury is extreme, violent, and overwhelming anger — anger so powerful that it feels like it could burst out of a person and destroy everything around them. It is not just being "upset" or "annoyed."

Fuscous means a dark, dull, grayish-brown color — murky and shadowy, like something that has had all its brightness drained away. Think of it as brown and gray mixed together, then dimmed down further so it looks almost dusky or smoky.
A fuselage is the main body of an aircraft — the long, central structure that holds everything together and carries people, crew, and cargo.

A fusillade is a sudden, rapid burst of many things all at once — so many, coming so fast, that they feel like a storm or a flood. The word captures not just quantity, but the overwhelming, rapid-fire nature of that quantity.

Fusion means the joining of two or more separate things so completely that they merge into a single, unified whole. The result is something new — something that wouldn't exist if the parts had stayed apart.
Fuss means unnecessary excitement, worry, or activity — especially about something that is not important enough to deserve all that attention.
"Fuss over" is a phrasal verb that means to give someone or something a lot of attention, care, or worry — usually more than is really needed.

A fusspot is a person who makes a big fuss — a lot of unnecessary worry, complaints, or fiddling — about small, unimportant things. They treat minor issues as if they are major problems, and they are very hard to please or satisfy.

"Fussy" describes someone or something that is too difficult, too particular, or too complicated — going beyond what is normal or reasonable. It always carries a sense of excess. Something is not just careful — it is overly careful.

When you call something fustian, you are saying that it sounds grand, important, and impressive on the surface — but when you look closer, it is hollow, empty, and says very little of real value. It is all dressed up with no place to go.

Fustian is a type of thick, rough, coarse cloth, made from a blend of cotton and linen (or sometimes just cotton). Historically, it was a cheap, hard-wearing fabric — the kind worn by laborers and poor people, not by the wealthy.
Stale and musty-smelling, like a room that has been shut up for a long time. Figuratively, old-fashioned and out of touch, as in "fusty attitudes."
Futile means producing no useful result — something that is certain to fail or come to nothing, no matter how much effort is put into it.

Futility is the quality of being completely useless or pointless — the state of something having no chance of working, no hope of success, and no meaningful result, no matter how much effort you put in.
The quality of being in the future; the future time itself. It can also mean a future event, or relevance to or concern for the future.

Fuzzy describes something that is soft, unclear, or not sharp — either in a physical, visual, or mental sense. Think of it as the opposite of crisp, clear, and precise. If something is fuzzy, its edges, details, or boundaries are blurred or hard to pin down.
When you gab, you talk casually and freely with someone for a fairly long time, usually about light, everyday topics — things that don't really matter much.

When someone gabbles, they talk very fast and in a way that is hard to understand. It is not just about speed alone, and not just about being unclear alone — it is both things happening at the same time.
A gable is the triangular section of a wall that appears at the end of a building where two sloping roof surfaces meet at a peak.
"Gad about" means to go from place to place frequently, usually for fun, socializing, or pleasure, without any serious or fixed purpose.

A gadabout is a person who is constantly going out and moving from place to place, always chasing fun, entertainment, excitement, or the company of others — rather than staying home or tending to their responsibilities.
A person who persistently annoys and challenges people in power or authority with criticism and awkward questions, to provoke them into thought or action. Literally, a fly that bites livestock.

A gadget is a small, physical device or tool that is designed to do a specific, practical job — and that usually has an element of cleverness, novelty, or ingenuity about it. It is almost always something you can hold in your hand or carry around.

"Gaff" is one of those words that wears many different hats depending on context. It has distinct meanings across fishing, sailing, British slang, and a few more specialized areas. Here's a full breakdown, one meaning at a time.
A gaffe is an embarrassing mistake you make in a social situation — usually by saying or doing something inappropriate, offensive, or clumsy, without meaning to.

To gag means to experience a sudden, involuntary tightening of the muscles in your throat — the kind your body produces when it is trying to forcefully reject something. Your stomach heaves, your throat contracts, and you make a choking or retching sound.

A gaggle is a group of geese — but with one important condition: the geese must be on the ground or on water, not flying. The moment that same group of geese takes to the air, they are no longer called a gaggle. In flight, they become a skein or a wedge.

Gaiety is a lively, bright, outward joy — the kind of happiness that doesn't stay quietly inside a person but spills out through laughter, energy, and cheerful behavior. It is the state of being merry, light-hearted, and full of high spirits.
When someone does something gaily, they do it in a cheerful, bright, and carefree way — with a light, happy spirit and no sense of heaviness or worry.

Gainful means producing money, profit, or a worthwhile benefit. If something is gainful, it gives you something valuable in return for your effort — and most of the time, that "something valuable" is money.
Gainfully means in a way that produces income, profit, or a meaningful benefit. It describes doing something that earns you something valuable in return — most commonly, money.

To gainsay something means to deny it, contradict it, or speak against it — essentially to say "that is not true" or "I oppose that." When you gainsay something, you are challenging or pushing back against a claim, a fact, or a statement.
Your gait is the specific way you move on your feet — the particular pattern, rhythm, and style of your movement.

A galaxy is a massive system in outer space made up of an enormous number of stars, along with gas, dust, and a mysterious invisible substance called dark matter — all held together by the force of gravity.

A gale is a very strong, powerful wind — strong enough to make it hard to walk, bend trees, rattle windows, and knock over lightweight objects. It is not just a breeze, and it is not just a "strong wind" in a casual sense.
Bold, rude confidence; nerve, as in "she had the gall to ask for more." It is also another word for bile, a feeling of bitterness, or an abnormal growth on a plant.

To gall someone means to deeply irritate or annoy them — but not in a simple, lightweight way. The irritation that "gall" describes has a particular sting to it. It's the kind of annoyance that wounds your pride, makes you feel bitter, or feels deeply unfair.
Brave and noble, especially in a dignified, honourable way. Of a man, being especially polite and attentive to women.
"Gallantly" describes how someone does something — specifically, it describes doing something with a combination of bravery, grace, and a noble, generous spirit.
Gallantry is a noun that describes a quality in a person — specifically, a quality that combines bravery and nobility in a graceful, admirable way.
A galleon is a large, powerful sailing ship that was widely used from roughly the 1500s to the 1700s.

A galley is a long, narrow, flat-bottomed warship that was powered mainly by rows of oarsmen — people sitting in rows on benches and rowing with oars. It sometimes had one or two sails as well, but oars were its primary source of power.

A gallimaufry is a confused, jumbled mixture of many different things that don't obviously belong together. Think of it as a random pile-up — a chaotic, disorganized collection of mismatched things thrown together with no clear order or unifying theme.
Something galling is more than just annoying or frustrating.
To gallivant means to go from place to place purely for fun, pleasure, or excitement — often with no serious purpose or plan.

A gallows is a wooden structure built specifically for the purpose of executing someone by hanging them until they die. It is a tool of capital punishment — meaning a device used by authorities (governments, courts, rulers) to carry out the death penalty.
Gallows humour is making a joke about something that is very dark, frightening, or terrible — especially about death, suffering, disaster, or hopeless situations — as a way of coping with it.

Galore means in large, plentiful, often impressive quantities. When something exists galore, there is a lot of it — more than enough, an abundance of it. Think of it as a stronger, more vivid way of saying "plenty of" or "lots and lots of."
To galumph means to move in a heavy, awkward, and often noisy way — but with energy and enthusiasm, sometimes even with a kind of cheerful self-satisfaction.
"Galvanic" is an adjective that describes anything related to electricity produced by a chemical reaction.
To shock or excite people into taking action, as in "the speech galvanized the crowd." Literally, to coat iron or steel with zinc to protect it from rust.

A gambit is a calculated opening move — in a game, a conversation, a negotiation, or any competitive situation — where you deliberately give something up or take a risk early on, with the plan of gaining a bigger advantage later.
To gambol means to run, jump, and move about in a light, playful, and carefree way — purely for the sheer joy of moving. There is no purpose behind it, no destination, and no urgency.
Gamely means doing something with courage, willingness, and a positive spirit — especially when it is difficult, painful, or when the odds are against you.

Gamesmanship is the practice of using clever psychological tricks and tactics to gain an advantage over an opponent in a competition — without technically breaking the rules, but often going against the spirit of fair play.
Gamut means the complete range of something — every point from one extreme all the way to the other, with nothing left out.

Just like how a male duck is called a drake and a female duck is a duck, the goose species has its own gender-specific names: the female is called a goose, and the male is called a gander. The young of both are called goslings.
"Gang up on" means when two or more people join forces together to oppose, attack, criticize, or pressure one single person or group.

Gangly is an adjective that describes a person who is tall, thin, and physically awkward — someone whose arms and legs appear too long for their body, and whose movements look loose, clumsy, and uncoordinated as a result.
Gangrene is the death of living body tissue, caused either by a loss of blood supply, a serious bacterial infection, or both happening together.
A gangway is a narrow passage or walkway that allows people to move from one place to another — particularly in tight or constrained spaces, or across a gap between two things.
A gaol is simply a place where people are locked up as a punishment or while they are waiting to be tried in court. In other words, it is a prison or a jail.
A gap is an empty space, an opening, or a missing piece that exists between two things — where there should be something, but there isn't.
To stare open-mouthed in surprise, shock, or wonder. Of a hole or wound, to be wide open.

"Garb" means clothing or dress — but not just any clothing. It specifically refers to a particular style or type of clothing that is strongly associated with a certain group, profession, role, culture, or period in history.

To garble something means to take a piece of information, a message, or speech — something that was originally clear and correct — and reproduce or pass it along in a confused, jumbled, or distorted way, so that it becomes hard to understand or no longer accurately reflects the original.

Garbled describes something — almost always a message, piece of information, sound, or signal — that has been so distorted, scrambled, or corrupted during the process of transmission or retelling that it becomes difficult or impossible to understand correctly.
Gargantuan means enormously, almost unimaginably large. When you call something gargantuan, you are not just saying it is big, or even very big.
A gargoyle is a carved stone figure of a strange, often frightening creature — built into the outside of a building, usually sticking out from a high point like a rooftop or ledge.

Garish means unpleasantly bright, flashy, or overdone in a way that assaults your eyes or offends your sense of good taste. It describes something that is trying so hard to be noticed that it ends up looking cheap, vulgar, or just plain ugly.
A garland is a decorative strand or loop made by weaving, threading, or linking together flowers, leaves, greenery, or other ornamental items.
A garment is a single, individual piece of clothing.
To garner something means to gather, collect, or accumulate it — but specifically something valuable, significant, or desirable — usually as a result of effort, merit, or an action you have taken.

A garnet is a naturally occurring mineral — a solid, crystalline substance formed deep inside the Earth. It belongs to a group of closely related minerals that all share the same internal crystal structure but differ slightly in their chemical makeup.

The verb garnish has two entirely separate meanings — one used in everyday cooking and food, and one used in law and finance. They share the same word but mean completely different things, so it's important to know both.
A garret is a small room at the very top of a building, sitting directly under the roof. Think of it as an attic that someone actually lives in — cramped, dim, and often uncomfortable.
A group of soldiers stationed in a town or fort to defend it. It can also mean the place where such soldiers are stationed.
To garrison a place means to station a group of soldiers there permanently or for a long period of time, so that those soldiers can defend that place or maintain military control over it.
To garrote someone means to kill or disable them by tightly squeezing their throat with a wire, rope, cord, or similar thin, flexible material looped around the neck.
Garrulity means the habit or tendency of talking too much, especially about things that are unimportant, trivial, or pointless.
Garrulous means excessively talkative, especially about unimportant or trivial things, in a way that is tiresome or annoying to others.

If someone does something garrulously, they do it while talking excessively, endlessly, and about things that don't really matter — rambling on and on in a way that eventually tires out the people listening.
Gasconade means extravagant, over-the-top boasting — the kind of bragging that is loud, exaggerated, and hollow at its core. It is not just ordinary pride or confidence.
Gaslighting is a form of psychological manipulation in which one person — called the gaslighter — systematically causes another person to doubt their own memory, perception, feelings, and judgment.
A gasp is a sudden, sharp breath taken in through the mouth — quick, brief, and usually audible. It is almost always involuntary, meaning your body does it on its own, without you deciding to.
Gastronomic means relating to the art and deep pleasure of eating fine, high-quality food.

Gastronomy is the art, science, and culture of understanding, appreciating, and enjoying high-quality food and drink. It is not just about eating — it is about eating well, eating thoughtfully, and understanding why something tastes the way it does.

To gatekeep means to control who is allowed access to something — a group, a hobby, a community, an identity, or information — often by deciding whether someone meets a certain standard, and turning them away if they don't.

A gatekeeper is anyone — a person, an organization, or even a system — that controls access to something. Picture a real gate in a wall. On one side is something valuable or important. On the other side is someone who wants to reach it.
Gatekeeping is the act or practice of controlling who gets in, what gets through, or who counts as legitimate — in any situation involving access, membership, or identity.
"Gather" means to bring things or people together from different places into one place — or to come together yourself. Think of it as the opposite of "spread out" or "scatter."
Gauche means socially awkward or tactless — specifically in a way that reveals a lack of polish, refinement, or awareness of how to behave appropriately in a given social setting.
Gaudy describes something that is too bright, too colorful, too decorated, or too showy in a way that looks cheap, tasteless, or excessive.
An instrument that measures something, such as fuel or pressure. It can also mean anything that indicates how something is, or a standard measure of thickness or width, as of wire or railway track.
To gauge something means to carefully assess, estimate, or judge the extent, level, or degree of something — often when you cannot measure it directly or precisely.
Gaunt means extremely thin and bony in a way that looks unhealthy, worn out, or suffering. It is not just "thin."
To "throw down the gauntlet" means to issue a challenge; to "run the gauntlet" means to face a series of attacks or criticisms. Literally, a gauntlet is an armoured glove.
Thin, light, and see-through, like gauze, as in "gauzy curtains." Figuratively, hazy and dreamlike.
A gavel is a small, hard mallet — essentially a miniature hammer — used by a person in authority to signal control, make announcements, or formally confirm a decision during official proceedings.
To gawk means to stare at someone or something in a way that is obvious, prolonged, and slightly rude or foolish-looking — often with your mouth hanging open or a dazed expression on your face.

Gawky describes someone who is physically awkward and clumsy — especially in the way they move or hold their body. A gawky person looks ungraceful. Their movements seem uncoordinated, stiff, or just "off."
To gaze means to look at something or someone steadily, continuously, and for a long time — usually with a strong feeling behind it, such as wonder, admiration, love, sadness, or deep thought.

A gazebo is a small, freestanding outdoor structure that has a roof but open sides — meaning it has no walls. It is a place where people can sit outside while being sheltered from the sun or light rain.
A gazette is an official or formal publication — think of it as a kind of journal or newspaper — used to make important announcements to the public in an authoritative, recorded way.

To gazump someone means to betray a buyer in a property deal by either: accepting a higher offer from a different buyer after already agreeing to sell to the first buyer, OR raising your own asking price on the same buyer after they have already accepted your original price.
"Gear" refers to things that help you do something — whether those things are equipment you carry, mechanical parts inside a machine, or settings you switch between.
"Gear up" means to prepare yourself — mentally, physically, or with the right tools and equipment — for something that is about to happen, especially something challenging, exciting, or important.
"Gedanken" is a German word that simply means "thought" or "thoughts." So a Gedanken experiment — or Gedankenexperiment in German — is, word for word, a "thought experiment."
A geek is a person who has an unusually deep passion and knowledge about a specific subject.

When we call something or someone geeky, we mean they show a very deep, enthusiastic, and often all-consuming passion for a specific subject — especially one that is technical, intellectual, or niche (meaning not everyone is into it).
To gel means to come together into a unified, stable whole — either physically (a substance thickening and setting) or figuratively (people, ideas, or plans clicking into place naturally).

Gelatinous describes something that has the texture, consistency, or appearance of gelatin — that wobbly, jiggly, semi-solid substance you know from Jell-O or gummy bears. If something is gelatinous, it is soft, thick, and somewhat jelly-like.
Gelid means extremely cold — not just a little chilly, and not merely "cold" in the ordinary sense. It describes a cold so intense it feels sharp, biting, and almost punishing.

A gemstone is a piece of mineral crystal — or occasionally a certain type of organic material — that is considered rare, beautiful, and durable enough to be treasured, collected, and used in jewellery or decorative objects.

The state of being male, female, or another identity, especially in terms of social and cultural roles rather than biology. In grammar, gender is a class of nouns, such as masculine, feminine, or neuter.

Gender dysphoria is the significant psychological distress, discomfort, or unease that a person experiences when their internal sense of their own gender does not match the sex they were assigned at birth.
Gender identity is a person's own, deeply internal sense of who they are in terms of gender — whether they feel themselves to be a man, a woman, both, neither, or something else entirely.
A gene is a specific, discrete segment of DNA that carries the instructions for producing a functional molecule — usually a protein, but sometimes a functional RNA molecule.
Relating to the study and tracing of family histories and lines of descent, as in "genealogical records."
Genealogy means the study and tracing of who came before you in your family — your parents, their parents, and all the ancestors going back as far as records allow.
A generalist is a person who has knowledge, skills, or experience across many different subjects or areas, rather than being deeply focused on just one.
A vague or general statement that lacks specific details, as in "he spoke only in generalities." It can also mean the quality of being broad or widely applicable, or the majority of a group.
A generalization is a broad statement, rule, or conclusion that you form by looking at several specific cases and then applying what you learned to a much wider group or situation.
To generate something means to cause it to come into existence — usually through some kind of process, activity, or action.

All the people born and living at about the same time, as in "the younger generation," or the average time in which children grow up and have children of their own. It can also mean the production of something, as in "electricity generation."
Generative means having the power to produce, create, or bring new things into existence.
Generic means belonging to a general group or class, rather than being specific, individual, or distinctive.

When someone is generous, they give freely and willingly — more than what is strictly required, and often more than what others would normally give. They don't hold back. They don't calculate every penny or every minute.

Genesis means the origin or beginning of something — specifically, how something came into existence. It refers to the very point at which something is born, formed, or created, and often includes the process or circumstances that led to that creation.
Genetic means relating to genes — the tiny biological units inside every living cell that carry instructions for building and running an organism.
Genetics is the branch of science that studies genes — what they are, how they work, how they are passed from one generation to the next, and why living things differ from one another.

When you call a person genial, you mean they are warmly friendly, cheerful, and genuinely pleasant to be around. A genial person radiates natural warmth that makes others feel welcome, comfortable, and at ease.
Geniality is the quality of being warm, friendly, and cheerful in a natural, easy way.

When someone does something genially, they do it in a way that is warm, friendly, and cheerful — all at the same time. It describes a manner that makes the people around them feel comfortable, welcome, and at ease.
Exceptional intelligence or creative ability, or a person who has it ("Einstein was a genius"); also a special natural talent for something.
Relating to genocide — the deliberate attempt to destroy a group of people because of their race, ethnicity, religion, or nationality — or intending to commit it.

Genocide is the deliberate, planned attempt to wipe out — or severely destroy — a specific group of people, simply because of who they are as a group. The key word here is deliberate. It is not an accident. It is not a side effect of war.
A genre is a category — a named group that creative works belong to because they share important things in common.
"Genteel" describes someone — or something — that is refined, polished, and proper in a way that signals belonging to a cultured, respectable social class.
A gentile is a person who is not Jewish.
The quality of being polite, refined, and upper-class in manners and lifestyle. It can also mean an exaggerated show of refinement, or the upper class itself.

Gentle means mild, soft, and careful — not harsh, rough, or forceful. When something or someone is described as gentle, there is an absence of violence, sharpness, or unnecessary pressure. The effect of something gentle does not hurt, shock, or overwhelm.

Gentrification is the process by which a poor or run-down urban neighborhood gradually transforms into a wealthier one — attracting richer residents, modern businesses, and rising property prices — often at the cost of pushing out the people who originally lived there.

When a place — almost always a neighborhood or urban area — is described as gentrified, it means that place has gone through a dramatic transformation: it has shifted from being a poor or working-class area into a wealthier, more expensive, more polished-looking one.

To gentrify a place means to transform a poor, run-down, or working-class neighborhood into a wealthier, more expensive, and more "polished" one — in a way that pushes out the people who originally lived there.
Gentry is a collective noun — it refers to a group or class of people, not a single individual.
To genuflect means to briefly lower one knee to the ground — and then rise back up — as a deliberate act of showing deep respect, reverence, or worship toward someone or something.
A genuflection is the act of briefly bending one knee down toward the ground — and then standing back up — as a sign of deep respect, reverence, or submission toward someone or something.
Something genuine is real — not fake, not forced, not put on for appearances. It is exactly what it claims or appears to be, with no deception involved.
"Genuinely" means in a way that is real and authentic — not fake, not pretended, not performed.
A genus is a group that contains things closely related to each other, but not so similar that they are the same thing.

A geochronometer is a natural "clock" found in the Earth — a physical or chemical process built into rocks, minerals, or other natural materials that ticks forward at a known, steady rate, allowing scientists to measure how much time has passed since a certain geological event occurred.
Geometric means "of, relating to, or having the qualities of geometry." Geometry is the branch of mathematics that studies shapes, lines, angles, and space.

Geopolitical is an adjective. It describes things that involve the connection between geography (the physical world — land, borders, oceans, mountains, resources) and politics (the exercise of power between nations and governments).
Geopolitics is the study of how geography shapes the power, decisions, and relationships of countries.
Geothermal describes anything that relates to, comes from, or is powered by the natural heat stored deep inside the Earth.
A gerbil is a small, furry animal — a mammal belonging to the rodent family, which also includes mice, rats, squirrels, and hamsters.
Geriatric means relating to old age, elderly people, or their medical care.
Geriatrics is the branch of medicine that specializes in the health care of older people.

A germ is a microscopic living thing — so small that thousands of them could fit on the head of a pin, and you cannot see even one with your naked eye. Certain germs can enter your body and cause disease.
The very first beginning of an idea, which has the potential to grow into something larger — just as a seed's germ grows into a plant.

Germane means closely and meaningfully relevant to the specific topic or matter being discussed. Something is germane when it fits so well into the conversation or subject at hand that it genuinely helps — it doesn't just loosely connect, it belongs there.
In the earliest stage of development but containing the potential for future growth, as in "germinal ideas." In biology, relating to the germ cells that produce eggs or sperm.
To germinate means to begin to grow or develop. Think of it as the very first moment something goes from being still and inactive to being alive and moving forward. It is the spark of a beginning.
Gerontology is the scientific study of aging — what it is, how it works, what it does to people, and how society responds to it.

To gerrymander means to deliberately redraw the boundaries of a voting district in a way that is designed to give one political party an unfair advantage over another, rather than to fairly represent the people who live there.

Gerrymandering is the deliberate manipulation of the boundaries of voting districts to give one political party an unfair advantage in elections — essentially, it is the art of choosing your voters before they choose you.
A gestalt is a unified whole that has qualities no individual part contains on its own. The whole is greater than — and different from — the sum of its parts.
To gestate means to slowly develop something from within — carrying it through a quiet, hidden process over time — until it is ready to emerge fully formed.
The process of a baby or young animal developing inside its mother's womb, or the period this lasts. Figuratively, the slow development of an idea or plan before it is ready.
To gesticulate means to move your hands, arms, or body in an expressive or animated way, usually while you are speaking — or sometimes instead of speaking.
A gesticulation is a body movement — almost always of the hands, arms, or head — that a person makes, usually while talking, to express or emphasize what they are saying.
A gesture is a meaningful movement or action that communicates something to another person — without using words, or sometimes alongside words to reinforce them.

To gesture means to make a deliberate movement — usually with your hands, arms, or head — to communicate something to another person. This movement can express a feeling, point something out, or send a silent signal.
An informal way of telling someone to calm down, control their emotions, and stop overreacting.
"Get a move on" means to hurry up, to start moving faster, or to stop wasting time and begin doing something.

When you cannot get a word in edgeways, it means you cannot say anything during a conversation because someone else is talking so much, so fast, or so loudly that there is simply no moment of silence for you to speak.
To "get ahead of oneself" means to think, plan, or act too far into the future before the present situation is ready for it.
The good news is there is a loose connecting idea: "get along" generally suggests moving forward smoothly — whether that's in a relationship, in life, in a task, or through time.

To "get back at someone" means to take revenge on a person who has harmed you, wronged you, or treated you unfairly. You do something negative or harmful to them in return — because they did it to you first.
"Get cold feet" means to suddenly become nervous, scared, or lose confidence about doing something that you had already decided or agreed to do.

When someone "gets off scot-free," it means they escape punishment, blame, or consequences entirely — even though they deserved to face them. They walk away without any penalty, payment, or suffering at all.
To get one's act together means to start behaving in a more organized, responsible, and effective way — especially after a period of being messy, careless, lazy, or confused.
Get one's ducks in a row
To "get your ducks in a row" means to organize everything properly and be fully prepared before starting something.

"Get one's own back" means to take revenge on someone who has harmed, cheated, or wronged you — to do something back to them that makes you feel that justice has been served. It is about evening the score.
To get one's back up means to become angry, irritated, or defensive about something. When someone's back is up, they feel annoyed and are ready to push back or argue.
To get the better of someone means to defeat, overcome, or gain an advantage over someone or something.
Get the wrong end of the stick

When someone "gets the wrong end of the stick," it means they have completely misunderstood a situation, a message, or what someone said. They heard or saw something, but walked away with the wrong idea about it.
To "get to grips with" something means to make a serious effort to understand, deal with, or take control of something that is difficult, unfamiliar, or challenging.
To annoy or irritate someone deeply and persistently. It can also mean to affect someone so deeply, often romantically, that they cannot stop thinking about it.
To get wind of something means to hear about or find out about something — especially a piece of information that was secret, private, or not meant for you.
Get-up-and-go means the natural energy, drive, and enthusiasm inside a person that pushes them to start things, take action, and keep going without needing someone else to push them.

A getaway is an act of escaping — moving away from a place or situation, usually quickly. The word captures the feeling of getting away from something, whether that's a crime scene or the stress of your daily life. It always involves leaving something behind.

A gewgaw is a small, decorative object that looks appealing, shiny, or impressive — but is actually cheap, worthless, and serves no real practical purpose. It is all surface and no substance. Think of it as a "pretty nothing."
A geyser is a natural hot spring that, from time to time, suddenly shoots a powerful jet of hot water and steam high up into the air, then stops, and later shoots again.
Ghastly means causing a feeling of horror, shock, or disgust. It describes things that are not just bad, but shockingly, disturbingly terrible — the kind of terrible that leaves a mark on you.
Ghee is a type of pure, clarified fat made from butter — most commonly cow's butter — that has been slowly cooked until all its water has evaporated and all its milk solids have been removed.

A ghetto is a section of a city — a specific neighborhood or district — where people from a particular group (defined by race, religion, or ethnicity) live together, separated from the rest of the city's population.

To ghettoize means to separate, isolate, or push a group of people — or even a type of idea, art, or culture — into a confined space, a lower category, or a marginalized position, usually in a way that is unfair and harmful to their opportunities and standing in society.
A ghost is the spirit or soul of a dead person that is believed to have remained in the world of the living instead of moving on after death.
To ghostwrite something means to write it on behalf of another person, who then presents it to the world as if they wrote it themselves. You, the writer, stay completely invisible — like a ghost.

A ghostwriter is a person who is hired to write something for someone else, and who agrees to remain completely invisible — meaning the work is published or presented under the hiring person's name, not the ghostwriter's.
A ghoul is an evil, monstrous being — found in folklore, horror stories, and fantasy — that is most famous for one deeply disturbing habit: feeding on the dead.

Ghoulish simply means "like a ghoul" — anything that reminds you of that creature, or feels connected to it in some way. Think of it as a stamp you put on something to say: "This belongs to the dark, disturbing world of death and horror."

To gibber means to speak very fast in a way that is impossible — or nearly impossible — to understand. The sounds coming out of someone's mouth when they gibber are jumbled, confused, and senseless. It is not simply speaking quietly or mumbling.
Gibberish is language — or something that pretends to be language — that makes no sense to the person hearing or reading it. It fails at the one job language has: communicating a clear meaning.

A gibbet is a wooden structure — essentially a tall post with a projecting arm sticking out from the top at an angle — that was used in past centuries to publicly display the dead bodies of executed criminals.
"Gibbous" is an adjective that describes something rounded and bulging outward — like a dome, a hump, or a swollen shape that pushes out beyond a flat or curved surface.
A gibe is a mocking, taunting remark — something said specifically to ridicule or belittle someone.
To gibe means to make sharp, scornful remarks at someone in order to mock them, belittle them, or make them feel foolish and small.

Giddiness is a noun that captures two closely related but distinct experiences — one physical, one emotional — and both are united by a single idea: a pleasant but unstable, spinning, slightly-out-of-control feeling.
The word giddy is built around one central sensation: a spinning, unsteady, out-of-control feeling — either in your body or in your emotions.
A gig is a single live performance by a musician, band, comedian, or any entertainer — especially one that is booked for a specific event or venue.
To giggle means to laugh in a light, soft, high-pitched way — usually in short, quick bursts — in a way that is hard to control.

To gild something means to cover it with a thin layer of real gold, or with something that looks like gold — a gold-colored paint or coating. Think of an old painting with a shiny golden frame, or a decorative statue with a golden surface.
To "gild the lily" means to add something unnecessary to something that is already perfect, complete, or beautiful. It means overdoing something that didn't need to be done in the first place.
Gilded means covered with a thin layer of gold, or made to look golden and beautiful. The key word here is covered — not made of gold, but dressed up in gold on the outside.
A gilded cage refers to a situation where someone lives in luxury or comfort, but lacks true freedom. It looks wonderful from the outside, but on the inside, it is still a prison.
Gilt means covered with a thin layer of gold, or made to look as if it were.
Of the highest quality and extremely reliable. In finance, gilt-edged securities are very safe investments, especially government bonds. Literally, having pages with gold edges.

A gimcrack is a small object that looks attractive, interesting, or even impressive — but is actually cheap, poorly made, and completely useless. It is all show and no substance. The moment you look closely or try to actually use it, it disappoints you.
Gimlet-eyed describes a person whose gaze is sharp, intense, and deeply penetrating — the kind of look that seems to cut right through a person or a situation and miss absolutely nothing.

A gimmick is a trick, device, or clever scheme that is mainly designed to grab people's attention or get them interested in something — but which relies more on novelty or cleverness than on real, genuine value.

Gimmickry means the use of clever tricks, flashy devices, or eye-catching tactics to impress, attract attention, or sell something — usually in a way that lacks real substance, genuine quality, or honest intention.

Something is "gimmicky" when it uses a clever trick, flashy feature, or eye-catching novelty to grab your attention — but that trick is the main thing it has going for it. Strip the trick away, and there is little real quality or substance left underneath.

Ginger ale is a sweet, fizzy, non-alcoholic drink that is flavored with ginger — a spicy, warm-tasting root plant. Think of it as carbonated (bubbly) water combined with sugar and the flavor of ginger.
Gingerly means doing something with extreme care and caution — specifically the kind of care that comes from fear of causing pain, damage, or a negative reaction.

Gingham is a type of cloth — specifically, a cotton fabric defined by its clean, cheerful, checkered pattern. Think of the classic red-and-white tablecloth at a pizza restaurant, or Dorothy's blue-and-white dress in The Wizard of Oz. That is gingham.

Gingivitis is a medical and dental noun used to describe the inflammation of the gums — the soft, pink tissue that surrounds and holds your teeth in place. In simpler words, it means your gums are irritated, swollen, and unhealthy.

Ginormous is an adjective that means extremely, overwhelmingly large — so large that ordinary words like big or large feel completely inadequate to describe it. It sits at the very top end of the size scale, beyond huge, beyond enormous, beyond gigantic.
Gird means to wrap around, encircle, or surround something tightly — and by extension, to prepare yourself firmly for something hard that is coming.
"Gird one's loins" means to prepare yourself for something difficult, challenging, or demanding that is about to happen. It is a way of saying "get ready" — not just physically, but mentally too.
A girder is a large, strong, horizontal beam — typically the most important load-bearing beam in a structure.
A girdle is anything that goes all the way around something, like a ring, band, or belt encircling an object. Think of it like a hug that wraps completely around a thing.
A girl is a female human being who is young — typically a child or a teenager who has not yet become an adult. This is the word's most basic and straightforward use.
Girth is used to describe the size of something by measuring around its widest or thickest point. It tells you how big around something is.

Gist means the central meaning or most important point of something — the core of what is being said, written, or communicated, once all the details, examples, and surrounding information have been stripped away.

Give means to transfer something from yourself to someone else, voluntarily. That "something" can be a physical object, an experience, an action, information, or even something abstract like love or hope.
"Give a hoot" means to care about something.
To give a wide berth to someone or something means to deliberately stay far away from them — to avoid them carefully and by a comfortable distance.
Give as good as one gets

When someone gives as good as they get, it means they respond to whatever is done to them — an attack, a criticism, a challenge, a competition — with equal strength, skill, or force. They don't shrink back. They don't stay silent.
To give credence to something means to believe it, or to accept it as true and worthy of trust.

To give free rein to someone or something means to allow complete freedom — to let a person, feeling, idea, or process go in any direction it wants, without controlling, limiting, or interfering with it.
To give ground means to back down, yield, or retreat from a position you were holding — whether that position is physical, in a debate, in a negotiation, or in any kind of conflict or disagreement.
"Give rise to" means to cause something to happen, to exist, or to appear — especially something new.
To give short shrift to something or someone means to dismiss it quickly, with very little time, care, or serious attention — as if it barely deserves to be considered at all.

"Give someone a holler" simply means to contact someone or get in touch with them. It is used when you want someone to reach out to you, or when you plan to reach out to them. Think of it as a casual, friendly way of saying "contact me" or "let me know."
Give someone a run for their money
When you give someone a run for their money, it means you compete against them so strongly and impressively that they have to work very hard to beat you or stay ahead of you.

To "give someone the cold shoulder" means to deliberately ignore someone or treat them in an unfriendly, distant way — usually on purpose, and usually as a way of showing that you are upset with them, disapprove of them, or simply don't want anything to do with them.
To "give someone the slip" means to escape from someone cleverly and secretly, especially when that person is following you, chasing you, or watching you closely.

When you give the devil his due, you are being fair enough to admit something good or praiseworthy about a person you strongly dislike, distrust, or consider your enemy — even when it's the last thing you want to do.
To "give the lie to" something means to prove it is false.

"Give up the ghost" means to die, or more broadly, to stop working or functioning permanently. The key idea is always finality — something or someone has come to a complete and permanent end, with no return.
"Give vent to" means to express or release a strong emotion that has been building up inside you — especially when you finally let it out openly.
To give voice to something means to express it, say it out loud, or put it into words — especially when that thing was previously unspoken, hidden, or difficult to communicate.

"Give-and-take" describes a process where both sides of a relationship, discussion, or situation give something up and receive something in return. Neither side gets everything they want. Neither side walks away empty-handed.
When "given" is used as a preposition, it means "taking into account" or "considering."

When someone is "given to" something, it means they have a deep, habitual tendency or inclination toward that thing. It describes a characteristic that someone keeps showing, again and again — almost like it is built into them.
Having a habit of exaggerating things for effect, making them sound much bigger, better, or worse than they really are.
The core meaning is simple: glabrous means naturally smooth and completely free of hair, fuzz, bristles, or any tiny hair-like outgrowths on a surface.
Extremely slow, as in "progress was glacial." It can also mean very cold and unfriendly, or literally relating to glaciers and ice ages.
Extremely slowly, like the movement of a glacier, as in "the case moved glacially through the courts." It can also mean in a cold, unfriendly way.
Glaciate means to cover land with glaciers or ice sheets, and/or to erode, carve, and reshape that land through the movement of glaciers.
A glade is an open, sunlit patch of ground — usually grassy or covered with low plants and wildflowers — found inside a forest.

Glamor is a kind of dazzling, almost magical attractiveness that makes something or someone seem thrilling, special, and deeply desirable. It's not plain beauty. It's beauty plus excitement plus mystery — all wrapped into one powerful, captivating quality.

To glamorize something means to make it appear more exciting, attractive, romantic, or desirable than it truly is — often by focusing only on its appealing side while hiding or ignoring its ugly, dangerous, or boring realities.

Glamorous describes someone or something that has a powerful, exciting, and almost irresistible attractiveness — one that feels luxurious, polished, and larger-than-life. It is the kind of appeal that makes people stop, stare, and wish they were part of it.

A gland is an organ or a group of cells in a living body whose main job is to produce and release a specific substance. That substance is then used somewhere in the body — or expelled from it entirely.

A glare is a long, fixed, and hostile look that one person directs at another. It is not a quick glance. It is sustained, deliberate, and loaded with strong negative feeling — usually anger, disapproval, contempt, or warning.
Glare means to look at someone with intense, angry eyes — OR for light to shine in a way that is extremely bright and harsh.

When light is described as glaring, it means it is so intensely bright that it is uncomfortable, even painful, to look at or be in. It is not just bright — it is aggressively, overwhelmingly bright. It forces you to squint or look away.
Glaringly means in a way that is so obvious, so clear, and so hard to miss that it is almost impossible to ignore — like something is forcing itself into your attention whether you want it to or not.
Glass refers to a hard, smooth, see-through (or mostly see-through) solid material that is made by melting sand at very high temperatures along with other substances.
An invisible barrier that prevents women or minorities from rising to the top jobs in an organization, even though no official rule stops them.
Smooth, shiny, and still, like the surface of glass, as in "a glassy lake." Of eyes, looking fixed and blank, without expression.
A glaze is a smooth, shiny coating or surface layer — usually thin — that sits on top of something else.
To coat something with a thin, shiny layer, as in "glazing a ham" or "glazing pottery." It also means to fit glass into a window. Of the eyes, to become dull and blank, as in "his eyes glazed over."
Of eyes, looking dull, blank, and lifeless, from boredom or tiredness. Of food or pottery, covered with a thin, shiny coating. Of a window, fitted with glass.
A gleam is a soft, brief, gentle flash or beam of light — especially one that appears quietly, often reflected off a smooth surface, and usually in a dim or dark setting.
When something gleams, it shines with a soft, smooth, and clean-looking light. It is not a harsh, blinding brightness — it is a gentle, pleasant glow that catches your eye without overwhelming it.
Gleaming describes something that shines with a smooth, bright, and steady light — almost always because its surface is very clean, very polished, or very new.

To glean means to gather information, knowledge, or understanding slowly and carefully, piece by piece — often from indirect sources, scattered clues, or hints rather than from something stated to you plainly.

Glee is a feeling of great joy and delight — but not just any ordinary happiness. It is happiness that is lively, excited, and bubbling over. When someone feels glee, they are so happy that the feeling almost can't be contained.
Gleeful describes a person — or their expression, behavior, or mood — who is filled with intense, lively, bubbling-over joy. It goes well beyond simply feeling "happy" or "pleased."

Gleefully means doing something with obvious, lively, and uncontained joy. When someone does something gleefully, they are not just happy — they are bubbling over with happiness, and that happiness is clearly visible to everyone around them.
A glen is a narrow valley nestled between hills or mountains, usually with a stream or small river running along its floor.

Glib describes someone who speaks too smoothly, too easily, and too confidently — but without real thought, care, or depth behind their words. It means the words come out slick and effortless, but there is something hollow or dishonest underneath.
When someone does or says something glibly, they do it in a way that is too smooth, too easy, and too quick — revealing a lack of genuine thought, depth, or sincerity.
Glibness is the quality of saying things too easily, too smoothly, and too quickly — in a way that sounds confident and convincing, but actually lacks honesty, depth, or genuine thought behind it.

A glimmer is something that is present but barely so. Whether it is light or an abstract feeling, a glimmer is always at the edge of being noticeable — faint, soft, and often uncertain. The key idea behind this word is smallness and subtlety.
To glimmer means to shine with a light that is faint, soft, and unsteady. It is the opposite of a bright, bold, fixed light like a spotlight or the midday sun.
To glimpse something means to see it briefly, partially, or by chance — in a way that is quick or incomplete, so you don't get a full, clear view of it.
A glint is a tiny, sharp, brief flash of light — the kind that appears for just a moment when light bounces off a smooth or shiny surface.

When something glints, it catches light and produces a sudden, sharp, brief flash of brightness. It happens in an instant — like a blink — and then it's gone. The key ideas packed into this one word are: small, quick, intense, and reflected light.

To glisten means to shine softly because of wetness or moisture on a surface. When light hits something that is wet, damp, or moist, it bounces off in a gentle, sparkling way. That soft, shimmery shine is what we call glistening.

Glistening describes something that shines with a soft, wet, or bright light — most often because its surface is moist, smooth, or reflective. It is a gentle, continuous kind of shine, not a harsh flash or a blinding glare.

A glister is a sparkling, shimmering light — the kind that flashes and dances when something bright catches your eye. Think of sunlight hitting the surface of a lake, or the way a diamond seems to throw tiny bursts of light in every direction.

A glitch is a small, sudden, unexpected malfunction or error — something that briefly goes wrong in a system, process, or machine, often without a clear explanation, and often fixing itself or disappearing on its own.
To glitch means to suddenly and briefly malfunction or behave in an unexpected, incorrect way — especially a machine, electronic device, piece of software, or any digital system.

Glitter is the quality of shining with many small, quick flashes of bright light. Think of how a diamond catches sunlight and throws off tiny sparks of brightness in all directions — that dancing, sparkling effect is glitter.
Glitterati is a word used to describe the group of people who are famous, wealthy, glamorous, and highly visible in public life.

Glitzy means something that is glamorous, flashy, and visually dazzling — the kind of showy, sparkling, eye-catching quality you associate with bright lights, luxury, and showbiz. If something is glitzy, it looks expensive, exciting, and extravagant.
Gloaming means the soft, dim light that fills the sky shortly after the sun has set — that quiet, in-between moment when the day is ending but true darkness hasn't yet arrived.

To gloat means to feel or show a deep, self-satisfied pleasure — but specifically the kind that comes from either your own success or someone else's failure. It is smugness turned into a feeling or an action.

Globalization is the process by which the world's countries, economies, cultures, and peoples become increasingly connected, interdependent, and integrated with one another — as if the entire world were slowly merging into one giant, shared system.
To globalize something means to make it extend across, operate across, or spread across the entire world — rather than staying confined to a single place, country, or region.
Globular means shaped like a globe or a ball — roughly spherical, round, and compact, bulging outward fairly equally in all directions.
A globule is a small, round ball or drop of a substance — typically a liquid, but sometimes a soft or semi-liquid material. Think of it as a tiny sphere.
To glom onto something means to grab it or attach yourself to it eagerly (informal American). It can also mean to steal something.
When a place is not completely dark, but not bright either — dim, shadowy, heavy with low light — that atmosphere is called gloom.
"Gloom and doom" describes a deeply negative, pessimistic attitude or outlook — the belief that everything is terrible, getting worse, and likely has no good ending.

Gloomy describes something — a place, a person, a feeling, or a situation — that is dark, sad, or without hope or brightness. It carries a heavy, oppressive quality, like a weight sitting over something.

Glorification is a noun. It means the act of making something or someone appear more wonderful, admirable, noble, or praiseworthy than they truly are — OR — the act of giving great honor and praise to something or someone who genuinely deserves it.
Made to seem grander or more important than it really is, as in "the restaurant is just a glorified canteen."

To glorify something or someone means to present them in a way that makes them look extraordinary, admirable, or even sacred — to lift them up in the eyes of others, whether through praise, portrayal, or description.

Glorious means something so impressive, magnificent, or worthy of admiration that it fills you with a sense of awe, joy, or deep pride. It is the kind of word you use when "good," "great," or even "wonderful" simply feel too small.
The word "gloss" has two completely separate families of meaning. They look and sound the same, but they come from different ideas.
To gloss over something means to treat it very quickly and superficially, avoiding full, honest attention to it — usually because it is uncomfortable, embarrassing, inconvenient, or problematic.

A glossary is a collected list of special or unfamiliar words related to a specific subject, along with their clear explanations or definitions. Think of it as a mini-guide to the language of a particular topic.
Glossophobia is the intense, irrational, and persistent fear of public speaking or speaking in front of an audience.

Glossy describes a surface that is smooth, shiny, and reflects light clearly. When light hits a glossy surface, instead of scattering in all directions, it bounces back in a way that makes the surface look bright, sleek, and almost mirror-like.

When someone says "the gloves are off," it means that people have stopped being polite, careful, or restrained — and are now ready to fight, argue, or compete as hard as they possibly can, with no holding back.
When something glows, it produces or shows a soft, steady, warm light — usually from within itself or from deep inside it.

To glower means to stare at someone (or something) with a look of anger, hostility, or deep displeasure. It is not a passing glance — it is a fixed, sustained gaze loaded with negative emotion, communicated entirely through the eyes and face.
Glowering means having a look — or giving off a feeling — that is deeply angry, dark, and threatening, usually in a silent, brooding way.
Full of enthusiastic praise, as in "a glowing review." It also means giving off a steady, warm light, or looking healthy, bright, and radiant.

Glum means quietly sad, downcast, or unhappy — in a way that shows on your face and in your body. A glum person is not screaming or crying dramatically. Instead, they are silent, withdrawn, and visibly low in spirit.

A glut means an extremely large supply of something — so much of it that it far exceeds what people actually need or want. Think of it simply as: too much of something, more than can reasonably be used or absorbed.
To glut something means to fill it far beyond what it needs or can handle — to flood it with an overwhelming excess until it is completely stuffed, saturated, or overwhelmed.
When you describe something as gluten-free, you are saying that it does not contain gluten, or that it contains only a trace amount of gluten so tiny it is considered safe to ignore.
Glutinous means sticky, thick, and glue-like in texture — the kind of stickiness where something clings to your fingers, stretches when you pull it, and resists coming off cleanly.

A glutton is a person who eats or drinks far more than what is normal or necessary — not simply someone with a big appetite, but someone who consumes in an excessive, greedy, and unrestrained way. The key idea is not just quantity but lack of control.

When you call someone "a glutton for punishment," you are saying that this person willingly and repeatedly takes on pain, hardship, difficulty, or unpleasant situations — almost as if they enjoy it, or at least don't mind it at all.

Gluttonous describes someone (or something) that consumes far more than what is needed or reasonable — driven by greed and a total lack of self-control. It is an intensely negative word. It does not just mean "eating a lot" or "wanting more."
Gluttony is the habit of eating or drinking in excessive, uncontrolled amounts — far beyond what a person actually needs. It is not simply eating a large meal.

A glyph is any single visual mark, symbol, or shape that carries meaning or serves as a unit of written communication. Think of it as one distinct visual "piece" that you read or interpret — not a whole word, not a sentence, but one individual symbol.
To twist, bend, and distort something into a rough, knotted, irregular shape — or to become twisted and knotted in that way. The twisting isn't clean or smooth.
Gnarled means twisted, knotted, and bumpy in a way that looks rough, uneven, and distorted — usually because of old age, hard use, or the long, slow pressure of time and struggle.
"Gnarly" is an adjective with two distinct lives: a literal meaning and a slang meaning. To truly own this word, you need to understand both.
To gnash means to grind, strike, or scrape your upper and lower teeth against each other with force. It is not a gentle pressing — it is a hard, tense, often audible grinding or clenching of the jaw.
To feel and express intense anger, frustration, bitterness, or anguish — especially the kind where you feel powerless to do anything about the situation.

Gnashers is an informal word for teeth — plain and simple. When someone says "gnashers," they are talking about the teeth in a person's mouth. This includes both natural teeth and false teeth (dentures).
A gnat is a very small, flying insect with two thin wings. Think of it as a tinier, weaker cousin of the common housefly.
To gnaw means to bite or chew on something repeatedly and persistently, usually using your front teeth, in a way that slowly damages, wears down, or works through it.

When something is gnawing, it means it is a persistent, uncomfortable feeling or sensation that keeps slowly eating away at you from the inside — quietly, continuously, and in a way that is very hard to shake off or ignore.
A tiny, bearded, old man from folklore who lives underground and guards treasure, or a small statue of one placed in a garden. A gnome is also a short, wise saying.
Short, wise-sounding, and often hard to understand, like a riddle or proverb, as in "a gnomic remark."

A gnu is a large wild animal native to Africa. It belongs to the antelope family, though it looks nothing like the slim, graceful antelopes most people picture. It goes by another equally well-known name: wildebeest.
"Go against the grain" means to act in a way that feels unnatural, uncomfortable, or contrary to what is normally expected — either by your own inner nature or by the norms of society.

"Go awry" means that something — usually a plan, a situation, or an effort — does not turn out the way it was supposed to. Instead of going smoothly and as expected, it goes wrong, gets out of control, or moves in an unintended direction.

To "go ballistic" means to suddenly become extremely angry — so angry that you lose control of yourself. It describes a powerful, explosive emotional outburst, usually triggered by something specific.

"Go belly up" means to fail completely and totally — usually with no chance of recovery. It most often describes a business that has collapsed, but it can also describe any plan, project, or situation that has fallen apart beyond saving.
To fall, sink or decrease ("Prices went down"); to happen ("What went down last night?"); or to be received in a certain way ("The joke went down well").
Go down like a lead balloon
When something goes down like a lead balloon, it means it was received very badly, completely failed to impress, or was totally unwelcome.

To "go for broke" means to risk everything you have — all your energy, money, effort, or resources — in one bold attempt to achieve something. You hold nothing back. You commit completely, knowing that if you fail, you could end up with nothing.
"Go it alone" means to do something entirely by yourself, without any help, support, or partners.

When someone goes off on a tangent, they suddenly abandon the main topic they were discussing and start talking about something else — something that may only be loosely related, or sometimes completely unrelated.

"Go overboard" means to do something too much, more than what is necessary or reasonable. It means to go to an extreme — to put in way more effort, emotion, money, or action than the situation actually calls for.

When something "goes pear-shaped," it means it has gone wrong, failed, or turned into a mess — especially when it was supposed to go well. Think of a situation that started out fine but then suddenly took a bad turn.

To "go the extra mile" means to do more than what is expected or required. It means putting in additional effort, time, or care — beyond the basic minimum — to achieve something better or to help someone more.

When someone "goes through the motions," it means they are doing something — performing the required actions — but without any real effort, genuine feeling, or true engagement. Their body is doing the task, but their heart and mind are simply not in it.
To "go to extremes" means to do something in an excessive, over-the-top, or exaggerated way — far beyond what is considered normal, balanced, or necessary.

When someone "goes to great lengths" to do something, it means they try extremely hard and are willing to put in a lot of effort, time, energy, or resources to achieve a goal — often more than what is normally expected.
"Go to pot" means to deteriorate, decline, or fall into a state of ruin or neglect.
To become shabby, neglected, or less attractive through lack of care, especially as you get older. Literally, a plant goes to seed when it stops flowering and produces seeds.
"Go to the wall" captures the idea of reaching an extreme endpoint — either total failure, or total commitment.
Of a business, to fail and go bankrupt. It can also mean to sink below the surface of water, or to lose consciousness, especially under anaesthesia.
A go-ahead is an official or informal permission given by someone in authority that allows a person, group, or project to start or continue moving forward with something.

A go-between is a person who sits in the middle of two other parties and helps them communicate, exchange information, or reach an agreement — especially when those two parties are not talking to each other directly, or simply find it difficult or uncomfortable to do so.

A go-getter is a person who is highly ambitious, energetic, and driven to achieve their goals. The key idea is that they don't sit around waiting for good things to happen to them — they actively go out and make things happen.
A go-slow is a form of protest by workers in which they deliberately do their jobs at a much slower pace than usual — but without stopping work entirely.
When you call something your "go-to," you mean it is your most trusted, most relied-upon choice for a specific purpose — the one you reach for first, almost automatically, because you know it works.
A goad is something that pushes or forces a person (or animal) into action — usually action they would not have taken on their own, and often through pressure, pain, or irritation.

To goad someone means to pressure, provoke, or push them into doing something — especially something they are reluctant to do, or something they end up doing out of frustration, anger, or wounded pride.
A goat is a medium-sized, four-legged animal with hooves, a short tail, and usually a pair of horns (both males and females can have them). Many males also grow a small beard.
A goatee is a style of facial hair where a man grows hair specifically on his chin — and only the chin — while keeping the rest of his face (cheeks, jawline, neck) clean-shaved.

To gobble something means to eat it extremely fast and in large amounts, usually without any care for manners. Think of someone who is very hungry (or very greedy) — they don't chew properly, they don't pause, they barely breathe.
Gobbledygook is language — spoken or written — that is so confusing, so unnecessarily complicated, or so full of meaningless words that it becomes almost impossible to understand.
A goblin is an imaginary creature — meaning it does not exist in the real world — that appears in folklore, myths, fairy tales, and modern fantasy stories and games.

Gobsmacked is an adjective that means so completely and utterly shocked or astonished that you are left speechless. It describes that moment when something is so unexpected, so stunning, that your mind goes blank and words fail you entirely. Your jaw drops.
When you say "God forbid," you are reacting to the thought of something bad, scary, or unwanted — and expressing that you wish, with great intensity, that it never comes true.

"Goddamn it" is a strong exclamation used to express sudden, intense negative emotions — most commonly frustration, anger, disappointment, or shock. It is one of the most emotionally charged expressions in the English language.
A man who promises at a child's baptism to take an interest in their religious upbringing. It also means the head of a Mafia family, or a man who founded or inspired something.
When you call something godforsaken, you are saying it is so bleak, miserable, and cut off from anything good that it feels as if even God has turned His back on it and walked away.
"Godly" is an adjective that means relating to God, or behaving in a way that reflects God's qualities — particularly deep religious devotion combined with moral goodness.
A godsend is something — or someone — that helps you greatly, arrives at exactly the right moment, and feels like a precious, almost miraculous gift.

To goggle means to stare at something with your eyes opened very wide — often so wide that your eyes appear to be bulging slightly outward — because you are shocked, amazed, or can't believe what you're seeing.
A thorough examination or inspection. It can also mean a severe beating, or a harsh scolding.
Goings-on means activities, events, or things that are happening — especially ones that seem strange, suspicious, morally questionable, or at least worth talking about.
A person who forms a romantic relationship with someone mainly to get their money. Literally, a person who digs for gold.
A golden age is a period in history — or in any field — when things are at their absolute best. It is a time of great achievement, creativity, prosperity, and progress.

A golden handshake is a large, generous financial payment given to a senior executive or employee when they leave a company — whether they are fired, forced to retire, or choose to leave as part of a deal.
A very large payment promised to a top executive in their contract if they lose their job, especially after their company is taken over.

A golem is an artificial creature — most often shaped like a human — that has been brought to life through magical or mystical means, rather than through natural birth. It is not born; it is made and then activated.
The word gondola refers to several distinct things in English, but there's a quiet thread connecting most of them: a container or compartment that is carried, suspended, or floated.

"Gone are the days" means that a certain time, era, or situation that once existed no longer exists. It is a way of saying that something which used to be true, common, or normal in the past has now ended — it belongs to history, not to the present.

"Goo-goo" as an adjective describes two closely related things: a look of silly, dreamy infatuation, and anything resembling the soft, meaningless sounds a baby makes. Both meanings share the same feeling — something unguarded, sweet, and a little silly.
The soft cooing sounds a baby makes before it can speak. In American political history, a "goo-goo" was a mocking name for a reformer who campaigned for good government.
A "good egg" is a person who is genuinely kind, honest, trustworthy, and reliable.

"Good grief!" is an exclamation — something you say out loud as a sudden, spontaneous reaction to something. It expresses emotions like surprise, shock, frustration, disbelief, or exasperation (that feeling of "I can't believe this is happening again").
Good offices literally means good or helpful services — specifically, services rendered by a neutral party to help two quarreling parties come together.
"Good riddance" is something you say when you are happy and relieved that someone or something is finally gone.
A "good Samaritan" is a person who helps a stranger in need, without expecting anything in return — not money, not praise, not a favour back. The help is purely out of kindness and compassion.
Good-natured describes a person who has a naturally kind, cheerful, and pleasant disposition.

"Goodly" means impressively large in size or amount, or in older usage, attractive and pleasing to look at. It always carries a sense of approval — like you're not just describing something, you're quietly admiring it.
