"Goodness knows" is an idiom used in two closely related ways: First, it means that something is completely unknown, uncertain, or impossible to say with confidence. It signals that the speaker has no idea about something, or that the answer is a mystery.
Goodwill means a sincere, warm, and positive feeling or attitude toward other people — a genuine desire to be kind, helpful, or friendly, without wanting anything in return.
A goody is something that is desirable, pleasing, or enjoyable — something that makes you happy to receive or experience. It is most often used in the plural form: goodies.

A goody-goody is a person who always behaves in an extremely well-mannered, rule-following, and morally "perfect" way — but does so in a way that feels fake, excessive, or done purely to impress others, especially people in authority (like teachers, parents, or bosses).
"Goof off" means to waste time by avoiding your responsibilities — doing nothing useful, playing around, or acting silly when you are supposed to be working, studying, or doing something important.

A goofball is a person who is silly, playful, and a little foolish — someone who acts in a goofy, clownish, or absurd way, often just to get a laugh or simply because that is their natural personality.
"Goofy" means silly, playful, or mildly ridiculous in a completely harmless, lighthearted way.
A violent man hired to intimidate or hurt people (informal). It can also mean a silly or foolish person.
Gore refers to blood — but not just any blood. It specifically means blood that has been shed from a wound, often blood that is thick, dark, and clotted (i.e., partially dried or congealed).

To gore means to pierce or stab someone with a horn or tusk. When an animal uses its sharp, pointed horn or tusk to thrust into a person's or another animal's body, that animal is said to have gored them.
A gorge is a narrow, deep passage cut into the earth, with steep — often nearly vertical — rocky walls rising up on both sides, and usually a river or stream running through the bottom of it.
To gorge means to eat a huge amount of food in a greedy, uncontrolled, almost desperate way — far beyond what is normal or needed. It is not simply eating a lot.

Gorgeous means extremely and strikingly beautiful — so beautiful that it immediately catches your attention and makes you feel something. It is not just "nice-looking" or "pretty." It sits at the very top of the beauty scale.

To gormandize means to eat greedily and excessively — to stuff yourself with food in a way that shows very little self-control or restraint. When someone gormandizes, they don't eat because they are simply hungry.
Gormless means stupidly unaware, blank, and lacking any common sense or mental sharpness.

Gory describes something that involves a large amount of blood, brutal violence, or the disturbing, graphic physical aftermath of injury or death. When you call something gory, you are saying it is not just violent — it is visually and viscerally graphic.
When someone says something is "the gospel truth," they mean it is absolutely, completely, and without any doubt true. Not probably true. Not mostly true. 100% true — with zero room for questioning.

When you call something gossamer, you are saying it is extremely thin, light, and delicate — so fine that it is nearly see-through, and so weightless that it seems like it could float away or vanish at any moment.
Very fine, silky threads spun by small spiders, often seen floating in the air or on grass. Figuratively, anything extremely light, thin, and delicate, as in "a gossamer veil."

Gossip is talk or information about other people's personal lives — especially when that talk happens behind those people's backs, often involves unverified or private details, and is shared mainly out of curiosity, entertainment, or social bonding rather than any serious purpose.
To gossip means to talk about other people — their personal lives, relationships, problems, secrets, or behavior — usually when those people are not present in the conversation.

A gossipmonger is a person who loves to collect, spread, and share rumours, secrets, and private information about other people — especially information that is unverified, personal, or potentially damaging to someone's reputation.

Relating to a style of fiction with dark, mysterious, gloomy settings and supernatural or horrifying events. It also describes a medieval style of architecture with pointed arches, or the ancient Goths.
Gouache is a type of paint — and also the name for a painting made using that paint.
A deep scratch, cut, or hole in a surface. A gouge is also a woodworking chisel with a curved blade.

Gouge means to dig into or scoop out material by force, or to unfairly take something from someone (usually money). Both meanings share a common thread: something is being forcefully extracted — either from a surface or from a person's pocket.
To dig or force something out violently, especially an eye, leaving a hole or wound behind.
Goulash is a word with two distinct meanings — one very specific, one more general.
A gourd is a fruit that grows on a vine. It belongs to the same plant family as cucumbers, pumpkins, melons, and squash — so it is a close cousin of all of these.
A gourmand is a person who loves food deeply and eats it enthusiastically, often in large amounts.

When you use gourmet as an adjective, you are describing something food-related — a dish, an ingredient, a restaurant, a meal, or an experience — as being of an exceptionally high standard, crafted with great skill and care, and intended for people with a refined, educated sense of taste.

A gourmet is a person who has deep, refined knowledge and appreciation of fine food and drink. Not just someone who enjoys eating — almost everyone does — but someone who has developed expert-level taste and judgment.

To govern means to control, direct, and manage something — especially with authority and through a structured system of rules or decisions. When someone or something governs, they are the force that determines how something behaves, operates, or runs.
Governance is the way a group, organization, or society is directed, controlled, and held accountable.

A governess is a woman who is hired by a wealthy family to live in their home and privately teach their children — particularly their daughters — as well as supervise and guide them in their daily lives.
Smooth, effortless elegance in movement or manner. It can also mean polite decency, extra time allowed to pay or do something, or, in Christianity, the free and undeserved love and mercy of God.
To grace something means to make it more special, beautiful, or dignified simply by being part of it or appearing in it.

Graceful describes something — a person, a movement, an action, or even a way of behaving — that is smooth, elegant, and beautiful in a way that feels natural and effortless. The key feeling it creates in the observer is one of ease and harmony.
Gracefully means doing something in a smooth, elegant, and seemingly effortless way — without awkwardness, strain, harshness, or unnecessary fuss.
Graceless is the direct opposite of all that. It means lacking grace entirely — moving, speaking, or appearing in a way that is clumsy, rough, and unrefined.
"Gracious" describes a person (or behavior) that is kind, warm, and generous in spirit — in a way that goes well beyond just being polite.

Graciously means doing something in a way that shows kindness, warmth, and dignity — especially when you are in a position where you could have acted selfishly, harshly, or rudely, but you chose not to.

Graciousness is the quality of making people around you feel genuinely welcome, valued, and comfortable — and doing so with warmth, generosity, and quiet dignity, without any visible effort or expectation of something in return.

A grackle is a type of bird — specifically, a medium-to-large songbird found mainly across North and Central America. It belongs to a family of birds called Icteridae, which also includes blackbirds, orioles, and cowbirds.

Gradation is the process of changing from one thing to another gradually, smoothly, and in ordered steps, where each step is a natural continuation of the one before it. There are no sudden jumps. No sharp breaks.

Grade inflation is what happens when grades at a school or university rise steadily over time, not because students are genuinely getting smarter or working harder, but because the grading has simply become more generous.

A gradient is a gradual, smooth change in some measurable quantity — going from one value to another across a distance or space. It is not a sudden jump or a sharp boundary. It is a continuous, steady transition.
Slowly, over a period of time, in small stages, as in "the noise gradually faded."
"Graduate" means to move from one level or stage to a higher, more complete, or more advanced one — officially, with recognition.

When something is described as "graduated," it means it is organized into a series of clear, ordered steps or levels that increase or change in a regular, structured way — moving through defined stages, one at a time, from one end of a scale to the other.
Graffiti is writing, drawings, letters, symbols, or images made on a surface — almost always in a public place — without the permission of the person who owns that surface.
Hard work, as in "years of hard graft" (British). It also means the dishonest use of power for personal gain, a piece of plant joined onto another plant, or a piece of tissue transplanted in surgery.

To graft means to take a part of one plant — usually a shoot, a bud, or a small branch — and carefully attach it to the cut stem or root of a different plant, so that the two grow together and eventually become a single, unified plant.

When someone says there is "a grain of truth" in something, they mean that something — a story, a claim, a rumor, or a statement — is mostly false, exaggerated, or misleading, but contains one tiny, small element that is actually true.
Following the rules of grammar correctly, as in "a grammatical sentence." It can also simply mean relating to grammar, as in "grammatical rules."
A granary is a building or storehouse built specifically to store grain — crops like wheat, rice, corn, barley, oats, or millet — after they have been harvested.

A grandee is a person of the very highest rank, power, or social importance — someone who sits at the very top of a hierarchy and is treated with enormous respect and deference by everyone around them.

Grandeur is the quality of being impressively magnificent, vast, or noble — in a way that fills you with awe and admiration. When something has grandeur, it feels larger than ordinary life. It stops you. It makes you feel a deep sense of wonder.
A grandfather clause is a rule that says: "New rules apply to everyone new, but people or things that already existed under the old rules get to keep following the old rules."
Grandiloquence is the habit of using language that is far more grand, pompous, and showy than the situation actually calls for.
Grandiloquent describes a style of speaking or writing that is deliberately overly grand, showy, and inflated — language that sounds far more impressive than what it's actually saying.

When something is grandiose, it appears or claims to be extremely grand, impressive, or important — usually on a very large scale — but with a key catch: it is almost always more show than substance. There is a sense of exaggeration baked into the word.

Grandiosity is the quality of having, or appearing to have, an inflated and exaggerated sense of one's own importance, power, or greatness — a sense that goes far beyond what is actually true or justified. The key word here is "exaggerated."
When someone grandstands, they say or do something — not because it's genuinely useful or sincere — but because it looks impressive to others.

Grandstanding is behavior — usually speech or action — that is performed primarily to impress an audience and make yourself look good, rather than to actually get something done or address a problem honestly.

A grange is a farm — but not just the fields. The word refers to a farm as a whole unit, meaning the farmhouse, the barns, the stables, and all the other buildings that make a working farm function, all grouped together in one place.
Granite is a type of rock — specifically, a very hard, natural rock that forms deep inside the Earth from molten material (called magma) that cools down extremely slowly over millions of years.

A grant is something — most often money, but sometimes land, rights, or permission — that is given officially and formally by one party (usually a powerful or authoritative one) to another, for a specific purpose.

When you grant something, you officially give it, allow it, or agree to it — especially when the person receiving it had to ask for it, or when the giver has some kind of power or authority to give it.
Very detailed, broken down into small individual parts, as in "a granular analysis." Literally, made up of grains or small particles.
Granularity means the level of detail that something has — how finely or coarsely something is broken down, measured, or described.

To granulate means to break something down into, or cause something to form into, small grains or grain-like particles. It can also mean the reverse — when a substance naturally forms small grains on its own.

A granule is a small, individual particle — a tiny, solid piece of a substance that has been broken down or naturally formed into a compact, grain-like unit. Think of it as something bigger than a fine powder but smaller than a noticeable chunk.
The informal spread of news and rumours from person to person, as in "I heard it through the grapevine." Literally, the climbing plant on which grapes grow.
Graphic means making something fully visible — either literally through images, or figuratively through description so vivid and detailed that it feels like you're seeing it with your own eyes.

A graphic novel is a book that tells a story through a combination of sequential artwork (drawings or illustrations) and written text — both working together as partners, not one decorating the other.

When someone describes something graphically, they describe it with so much detail and realism that the listener or reader can almost see it happening in their mind, as if they are watching it rather than just hearing about it.

Graphite is a naturally occurring solid mineral made entirely of carbon — the same element that forms diamonds and coal. It is one of the softest minerals found in nature, with a dark gray to black color and a shiny, almost metallic appearance.
To struggle to deal with or understand a difficult problem, as in "grappling with grief." Literally, to wrestle or fight with someone at close range.
A person's understanding of something, as in "a good grasp of maths." It can also mean a firm hold with the hand, or the power to achieve something, as in "victory was within her grasp."

Grasp means to take firm hold of something — either physically with your hand, or mentally with your mind. Think of it as the act of truly securing something — not loosely, not halfway, but completely and firmly.
When someone grasps at straws, they desperately try things that have very little chance of working, simply because they are in a bad situation and have almost run out of options.
To "grasp the nettle" means to deal with a difficult, unpleasant, or uncomfortable situation boldly and decisively, instead of avoiding it or handling it in a weak, hesitant way.

When someone is described as grasping, it means they are intensely and selfishly greedy — always hungry for more money, wealth, power, or possessions, and willing to act unfairly or take advantage of others to get it.
When something is described as grassroots, it means it comes from ordinary, everyday people — not from powerful leaders, big institutions, governments, or wealthy organizations.
When you grate something, you rub it back and forth against a rough, sharp surface (called a grater) to break it down into tiny shreds or pieces.
To grate on someone's nerves means to irritate or annoy someone, often continuously or repeatedly, until that person feels frustrated, uncomfortable, or mentally worn out.
When someone does something good for you — helps you, gives you something, shows you kindness — and you feel a warm, heartfelt sense of appreciation toward them because of it, you are grateful.
Gratification is the feeling of pleasure and satisfaction you experience when a desire, need, or wish is fulfilled.

To gratify someone means to give them a deep sense of pleasure or satisfaction. When something gratifies you, it doesn't just make you happy for a second — it fulfills a desire, a need, or an expectation you had, and that fulfillment feels genuinely good.
When something is grating, it irritates you — it scrapes against your patience, your nerves, or your senses in a way that is unpleasant and hard to ignore.

A grating is a rigid framework made of parallel bars, rods, or crossed bars arranged in a grid-like or striped pattern, fixed over an opening. The key feature that defines a grating is its gaps — the spaces between the bars.

Gratis means provided at no cost, requiring no payment whatsoever. When something is described as gratis, it means you receive it completely free — no money leaves your pocket, no fee is charged, and no payment is expected, now or later.
When used as an adverb, gratis means without any payment, charge, or cost whatsoever. It describes how something is given or done — specifically, that it costs the receiver absolutely nothing.

Gratitude is a warm, positive feeling you experience inside yourself when someone has done something good for you — or when life itself has given you something valuable — and you recognize it as a gift, not something you automatically deserved.
Gratuitous means unnecessary and unjustified — especially when something goes beyond what is needed, appropriate, or acceptable, and its presence feels unwelcome or offensive as a result.

When something is done gratuitously, it means it is done without a good reason, without any need, and without being asked for — and usually, it causes some kind of harm, offense, or discomfort in the process.

A gratuity is money that you give someone voluntarily, on top of what you are already required to pay them, simply to say "thank you" for their service or effort. It is not a part of the official price. Nobody forces you to give it.

Grave means deeply serious in a way that carries real weight or danger. When something is described as grave, it means it is not just important — it is the kind of serious that demands your full attention, because the consequences could be very bad.
A grave is a hole dug in the ground in which a dead person's body is buried.
Gravel is a loose, natural material made up of small pieces of broken rock and stone.
Seriously, to a worrying or dangerous degree, as in "gravely ill." It can also mean in a solemn, serious manner, as in "he nodded gravely."
The graveyard shift is a work shift — a scheduled block of work time — that takes place during the late night and early morning hours. It typically runs from midnight (12:00 AM) to about 8:00 AM.
Gravitas is the quality of being deeply serious, dignified, and weighty in a way that naturally makes people respect and pay close attention to you.
To gravitate means to be naturally pulled or drawn toward something or someone — as if an invisible force is moving you in that direction.

Gravity is the invisible force of nature that pulls objects with mass toward one another. On Earth, this means everything — you, a book, a drop of rain, even air — is being constantly pulled toward the center of the Earth.
A gravy train is a situation, job, deal, or system that gives someone a lot of money, benefits, or rewards very easily — with little real effort, skill, or risk involved.

A gray area is a situation, topic, or case that is not clearly right or wrong, not clearly allowed or forbidden, not clearly defined by rules or facts. It's a middle zone where things are uncertain, vague, or open to different interpretations.
Of animals, to eat grass in a field. Informally, to snack on small amounts of food throughout the day. It also means to scrape the skin lightly, or to touch something lightly in passing.
Grazing is the activity of animals eating grass and other low-growing plants directly from the ground, while moving slowly across open land.

To grease someone's palm means to bribe someone — to secretly give a person money (or something valuable) so they will do something for you, usually something they are not supposed to do, or to make them do their job faster and in your favor.
"The great unwashed" is a phrase used to describe ordinary, common people — especially those from the lower or working classes — in a condescending, snobbish way.
Greedy means wanting more than you need, more than is fair, or more than is reasonable — and usually being unwilling to share what you have with others.
A green card is an official document issued by the United States government that proves a person who is not a U.S. citizen has been granted permanent legal residence in the United States.

A green light means official permission or approval to begin or continue something. When someone or something "gets the green light," it means they have been authorised to go ahead with a plan, project, or action.

The "green-eyed monster" is a way of referring to jealousy — the painful, uncomfortable feeling you get when you want something that someone else has, or when you fear losing something (or someone) you love to another person.
When you green-light something, you officially give permission for it to begin or go ahead.
A greenhorn is a person who is completely new to something and doesn't yet have the experience, knowledge, or skills to handle it well.
Relating to the trapping of heat in the Earth's atmosphere by certain gases, as in "greenhouse gases" and "the greenhouse effect."
A greenhouse is a structure built primarily of glass or clear plastic, specifically designed to grow plants inside a controlled environment.

Greenwashing is when a company, brand, or organization makes itself appear more environmentally friendly than it actually is — through misleading claims, deceptive marketing, or empty promises — in order to win the trust, loyalty, and money of people who care about the planet.
Gregarious means genuinely loving the company of other people and actively thriving in social situations.
To act gregariously means to act in a way that is openly, warmly, and enthusiastically social — enjoying the company of others and making that enjoyment visible through your behavior.
Gregariousness is the quality of being naturally and enthusiastically drawn to the company of other people.

A gremlin is an imaginary, mischievous little creature that people invented — mostly as a joke or a superstition — to explain why machines suddenly stop working or behave strangely for no obvious reason.
A situation or question that is not clearly right or wrong, legal or illegal, because the usual rules do not apply clearly to it.

A grey eminence is a person who holds enormous real-world power and influence behind the scenes, without any official title or public position — someone who quietly shapes decisions and events while another person stands in the spotlight and takes the credit (or the blame).

Grey matter is the part of your brain and spinal cord where the actual thinking, processing, and controlling happens. If your nervous system were a computer, grey matter would be the processor — the part that does all the real work.

A griddle is a flat, smooth cooking surface used to cook food by direct heat. Think of it as a wide, thick, metal plate — completely flat on top, with no walls or raised edges (or only very slightly raised edges at the border).

Gridlock means a situation where everything is so completely stuck that absolutely nothing can move forward — not even a little bit. It is a total standstill. Not a slowdown. Not a delay. A full, helpless freeze.

Gridlocked means completely and totally stuck — not just slow, not just delayed, but frozen. Nothing is moving. Nothing is progressing. Everything has come to a full stop, and the situation cannot fix itself because every direction is equally blocked.
Grief is the deep, intense emotional suffering you feel when you lose something or someone that truly mattered to you.
Grief-stricken is an adjective. It describes a person who is deeply, overwhelmingly overcome by grief — meaning they are suffering through a powerful feeling of sadness caused by a serious loss.
A grievance is a feeling — or a specific reason for that feeling — that arises when someone believes they have been treated unfairly, wrongly, or unjustly.

To grieve means to feel deep, heavy sadness — the kind that comes from losing something or someone that truly mattered to you. It is not ordinary, everyday sadness. It is a profound, often overwhelming sorrow that sits with you for a long time.

Grievous means extremely serious, severe, or causing great pain and suffering. When something is grievous, it isn't just bad — it is deeply, heavily, painfully bad. It carries a strong sense of weight and sorrow.

When something happens grievously, it happens in a way that is deeply serious, severely harmful, or intensely distressing — not just a little bad, but bad in a weighty, grave way. Think of it as the adverb that carries heavy burden with it.
A griffin is a legendary creature from ancient mythology — meaning it is not a real animal, but an imaginary beast that people invented and told stories about for thousands of years.
A grifter is a person who cheats others out of money or valuables — not by stealing directly, but by tricking them.
A device for cooking food over or under direct, intense heat. A grill is also a framework of metal bars, such as a grille on a window, or a restaurant serving grilled food.

When you grill food, you cook it by exposing it directly to a powerful heat source — no pot, no water, no covering. The heat hits the food straight on, and the result is a browned, slightly charred, flavourful exterior.
An intense and lengthy period of questioning, as in "the minister faced a grilling from reporters." It is also a way of cooking food over or under direct, intense heat.

Grim describes something that is harsh, serious, and deeply unpleasant — with no softness, no comfort, and no hope in sight. It is the feeling you get when you look at something dark and difficult and think, "This is bad, and there's no escaping it."
The Grim Reaper is a legendary, symbolic figure that represents death itself.
A grimace is a facial expression — but not a pleasant one. It is a brief, twisted, scrunched-up look on someone's face that signals something negative: pain, disgust, discomfort, or displeasure.
To grimace means to twist or distort your face in a way that shows you are feeling pain, discomfort, disgust, or something deeply unpleasant.

Grime is a specific, nastier kind of dirt. Not just any dust or mud — grime is dirt that is thick, dark, and deeply stuck onto a surface. It builds up gradually over a long time and refuses to come off with a simple wipe.
"Grimly" describes doing something in a way that is serious, harsh, and without any warmth, lightness, or joy — often in the face of something difficult, painful, or dark.

Grimy describes something — or someone — that is covered in grime, which is a layer of thick, stubborn, deeply embedded dirt. Think of the kind of dirt that doesn't just sit on a surface lightly but has settled in, built up over time, and sticks.

To grin is to smile very widely, usually showing your teeth. It is not a small, polite, or gentle smile — it is a big, open, full smile. When someone grins, the corners of their mouth stretch back and upward, their cheeks lift, and their teeth become visible.
Hard, tiring, and boring work or routine, as in "the daily grind." It can also mean a harsh, scraping sound, or the act of crushing something into small pieces.
When something grinds to a halt, it slows down gradually and then stops completely — often in a difficult, struggling, or labored way.

When you describe something as "grinding," you're saying it is severely difficult, never-ending, and slowly wears a person down — the way a millstone wears grain into dust. The key is that it doesn't just happen once.
A grindstone is a large, thick, round, flat stone — shaped like a wheel or disc — that spins on a rod through its center. Its surface is rough and coarse, like sandpaper but made of natural stone.

A griot is a traditional West African figure who serves as a living keeper of history, memory, and culture. Think of them as a combination of historian, musician, storyteller, and cultural guardian — all rolled into one person.

A gripe is a complaint — but a very specific kind of complaint. It's typically something minor, personal, and recurring that irritates you, and that you keep bringing up or venting about. It's not a crisis.
To gripe means to complain repeatedly about something, usually in a whiny, irritated, or nagging way.
"Grippe" is an old-fashioned English word for influenza — what people today call simply the flu.

When you describe something as gripping, you mean it is so intensely interesting and exciting that it holds your complete attention from start to finish. You cannot look away. You cannot stop. Your mind is fully locked in.

Grisly describes something that is shockingly horrifying or disgusting, almost always because it involves death, violence, blood, or the kind of physical suffering that makes most people recoil. It's not just "unpleasant" or "scary."
"Grist to the mill" means anything that can be used to your advantage, turned into something useful, or made to work in your favour.
Gristle is the tough, rubbery, chewy stuff you sometimes find in meat that refuses to break down no matter how hard you chew it.
Courage, determination, and the strength of character to keep going despite difficulties. Literally, very small, hard particles of sand or stone.

To grit means to press your upper and lower teeth tightly together — clamping your jaw shut with firm, locked force. It's not a grinding motion that damages your teeth; it's more of a tight, tense, muscular clench.
To endure a difficult, painful, or unpleasant situation with determination and self-control, without complaining.
Showing the harsh, unpleasant realities of life without making them seem nicer, as in "a gritty drama." It can also mean brave and determined, or literally, covered in or containing grit.

Grizzled describes hair — or fur — that has turned partly or fully gray, especially in a way that looks streaked or mixed: the original dark color still showing through, but clearly overtaken or threaded through by gray.

To groan means to make a deep, low sound — usually one that comes from your throat or chest — that expresses something heavy, painful, or unwelcome. It is almost always an involuntary sound, meaning it escapes from you without you really deciding to make it.
To struggle under a heavy burden of something, as in "a system groaning under the weight of debt."

Groggy means feeling physically weak and unsteady, and mentally foggy and confused, all at the same time — as if your body and mind are both running at a very low power. You are awake, but you are not functioning the way you normally would.
The most common use of groom is to refer to a man on his wedding day — or in the days just before and after it.

When you groom someone (or yourself, or an animal), you are making their body look clean, neat, and presentable. This includes actions like combing hair, washing, trimming fur, brushing a coat, clipping nails, and so on.

Grooming is the act of cleaning, tidying, and carefully preparing something — whether that's a person, an animal, or even a situation — so that it looks good, functions well, or is ready for a specific purpose.
A groove is a long, narrow channel or cut made into a hard surface. It runs along the surface — like a trench or valley — rather than going straight through it.

To search blindly or uncertainly by feeling with the hands, as in "groping for the light switch." Figuratively, to struggle to find something, as in "groping for words." It also means to touch someone sexually without their consent.

"Grope for" means to search for something with great difficulty and uncertainty, either with your hands (when you cannot see) or with your mind (when you are struggling to find the right word, idea, or answer).

When someone gropes for words, it means they are struggling to find the right words to express what they are thinking or feeling. Their mind is searching, but the words are not coming easily or quickly.
When something is "gross," it triggers a strong feeling of disgust — it offends your senses, makes your stomach turn, or makes you want to look away.

When something is grotesque, it is not just ugly, strange, or wrong. It is all of those things pushed so far that it becomes deeply unsettling — disturbing, shocking, even a little nauseating. The word carries a feeling that is hard to shake off.

A grotto is a small, cave-like space — either a natural cave or a man-made structure designed to look and feel like one. Think of it as a snug, sheltered hollow, often associated with something scenic, mysterious, or special.
To grouch means to complain or grumble in a bad-tempered, sulky, and discontented way.
A ground crew is a team of workers whose job is to support an aircraft, spacecraft, or similar vehicle — but they themselves stay on the ground. They never fly.

"Groundbreaking" describes something so new, original, and significant that it marks a clear turning point — a moment where things shift from the old way to a new way, permanently. It doesn't simply mean "new" or "impressive."
Emotionally stable, sensible, and secure, not easily shaken by life's ups and downs. It also means forbidden from going out as a punishment, or of an aircraft, not allowed to fly.
Something is groundless when it has no evidence, facts, or logical reason to support it. It exists — as a claim, a fear, a belief — but there is simply nothing real holding it up.
The word groundswell describes something that builds up slowly and powerfully from the bottom, eventually becoming a large, unstoppable force.

Groundwork is the essential preparation, effort, or work that is done before something bigger, more important, or more complex can begin or succeed. It is the deep, foundational work that makes everything else possible.

Group therapy is a structured form of psychological treatment in which one or more trained therapists work with a small group of people — typically between 5 and 15 — at the same time, in the same space, during the same session.
A complaint or grumble, especially about something minor. As a verb, to grouse means to complain repeatedly in a low-level, grumbling way. A grouse is also a game bird.

To grovel means to act in an extremely humble, desperate, and self-demeaning way toward someone — almost as if you are making yourself small and worthless in front of them — in order to gain their forgiveness, approval, or mercy.

Groveling describes behavior that is excessively and pathetically submissive — where a person completely abandons their self-respect and dignity in order to please, appease, or avoid angering someone else, especially someone more powerful.

To growl means to make a low, rough, threatening sound that comes from deep inside the throat. The sound is continuous and rumbling — not sharp or sudden, but vibrating and sustained. It signals danger, anger, or a warning.
Growth means the process of becoming more — more in size, more in number, more in maturity, more in capability, or more in strength — over a period of time.
"Grub" has two completely distinct meanings as a noun. You need to know both, because they come up in very different situations.

Grubby means dirty in a way that has built up over time through carelessness, hard use, or neglect — not just a fresh accident like a coffee spill. It suggests that something or someone looks unwashed, dingy, and unkempt.

A grudge is a strong feeling of lasting anger, bitterness, or resentment that you carry inside toward a specific person or group because they wronged you, hurt you, or treated you unfairly at some point in the past.
When someone does something, says something, or gives something grudgingly, they do it unwillingly — not freely, not happily, not openly.

When you do something grudgingly, you do it — but you really, truly don't want to. You feel inner resistance, resentment, or bitterness about it, yet you go ahead anyway, usually because you feel you have to or have no real choice.

Gruel is a very thin, watery food made by boiling a small amount of grain — usually oats, barley, wheat, or rice — in a large amount of water or milk. Think of it as porridge's weak, runny, barely-there cousin.

Grueling describes something that is severely exhausting and extremely demanding — something that pushes you to your absolute limit, drains every drop of your energy, and tests how much you can endure before you break.

Gruesome describes something so shockingly horrible, violent, or disgusting — usually involving blood, death, or serious injury — that it disturbs you deeply, makes your stomach turn, or is simply very hard to look at or think about.

Gruff describes someone (or something) that is rough, low, and harsh — either in the way they sound or the way they behave. It carries the feeling of something that is blunt, coarse, and unwelcoming on the surface.

When someone does or says something gruffly, they do it in a way that is rough, low-voiced, and blunt — not gentle, not warm, not soft. The word almost always describes how someone speaks or responds.
A grumble is a complaint — but not just any complaint. It is a quiet, low, muttered expression of dissatisfaction, usually about something small or mildly annoying.

To grumble means to complain in a low, quiet, and unhappy way — usually about something that bothers you but isn't a huge crisis. It is the kind of complaining where you are not screaming or crying or making a big scene.
If something is grungy, it looks, feels, or smells dirty, grimy, and run-down — in a way that suggests it has been neglected for a long time. It's not just "a little dusty" or "needs a quick wipe."
A grunt is a short, low, rough sound made from deep in the throat. It is not a word, not a sentence — it is just a raw, unpolished noise. It takes almost no effort to make, but it carries feeling.

To grunt means to make a short, low, rough sound from deep in the throat — the kind of sound that requires almost no effort to produce and even less thought. It is raw, unpolished, and animal in nature.

When someone "grunts an apology," it means they say "sorry" in a very reluctant, half-hearted, mumbled, or insincere way. The apology is technically spoken, but it sounds more like a rough, low, dismissive noise than a real, heartfelt admission of wrongdoing.

Grunt work refers to tasks that are tedious, repetitive, unglamorous, and often exhausting — but necessary for something larger to get done. It's the kind of work that nobody really wants to do, but somebody has to do it.

Guacamole is a thick, creamy, green-colored food made primarily from mashed ripe avocados, mixed with other fresh ingredients. It is one of the most well-known foods in Mexican cuisine and is now popular all over the world.

When a person is described as guarded, it means they are cautious, closed-off, and careful not to reveal too much about themselves. They don't open up easily. They think carefully before speaking. They keep their feelings and thoughts tightly under control.

When someone does something guardedly, they do it carefully and with deliberate restraint — holding something back on purpose, whether that's information, emotion, enthusiasm, or full commitment — because they want to protect themselves from risk, embarrassment, or being wrong.
A guardrail is a physical barrier or an abstract rule that exists for one purpose: to stop something from going somewhere dangerous or unacceptable. Think of it as a safety boundary.
Gubernatorial is an adjective that means relating to a governor or to the office and role of a governor.
A guerdon is a reward — something given to a person in return for their service, effort, or merit. Think of it as the prize or recompense a person earns through what they have done.

A guerilla is a fighter who is not part of an official army but who wages war anyway — usually against a much more powerful enemy — using surprise, speed, and secrecy instead of open, face-to-face battle.

A guerrilla is an irregular fighter — someone who wages war without being part of an official, uniformed army. The word almost always appears in the context of "guerrilla warfare," which is the style of fighting these individuals use.
Guff means nonsense — specifically, talk or ideas that are empty, foolish, or simply not worth taking seriously.

A guffaw is a sudden, loud, and completely unrestrained burst of laughter — the kind that explodes out of you when something strikes you as powerfully, almost overwhelmingly funny. It is not a polite laugh. It is not a quiet, controlled laugh.
Guidance means the help, direction, or advice that someone gives you so that you can make better decisions, stay on the right path, or handle something you are unsure about.
A guiding light is a person, idea, belief, or principle that helps you find your way — especially during difficult, uncertain, or confusing times.

A guild is an organized group of people who share the same trade, craft, or profession, and who join together to protect and support one another, maintain quality standards, and advance their common interests.

Guile means clever and cunning deception. A person who uses guile tricks others not through brute force or obvious lying, but through carefully crafted, sly, and indirect means — often so smoothly that the victim doesn't even realize they've been manipulated.

Guileful means cleverly deceptive. It describes someone (or something) that uses smart, sneaky tricks and calculated dishonesty to get what they want — all while hiding their true intentions behind a calm, often charming surface.

Guileless means completely free from deception, trickery, hidden motives, or manipulation. A guileless person is exactly what they appear to be — open, honest, and transparent, with nothing hidden underneath.

A guillotine is a machine designed to execute a person by cutting off their head swiftly and cleanly with a heavy falling blade. It was built to kill quickly — in a fraction of a second — so that the person condemned to death would feel little to no pain.

To guillotine someone means to execute them by beheading — specifically using a machine called the guillotine, which drops a heavy, angled blade to sever the head from the body in a single, swift motion. The action is immediate and total.
Guilt is the feeling you get when you believe you have done something wrong — something that hurt another person, broke a rule you believe in, or violated your own sense of right and wrong.
Guilt-ridden means being so deeply and powerfully consumed by guilt that it dominates your thoughts, emotions, and inner life.
An outward appearance that hides the true nature of someone or something, as in "fraud under the guise of charity."

A gulag is a forced labor camp — a place where people are imprisoned and made to perform extremely hard physical work, often under brutal conditions, not primarily as punishment for ordinary crimes, but as a tool of political control by an authoritarian government.
A large difference or gap between people, groups, or ideas, as in "the gulf between rich and poor." Literally, a large area of sea partly enclosed by land.

A gull is a medium-to-large seabird, commonly known by the informal name seagull — though bird experts and naturalists prefer just gull, since many of these birds also live far from the sea, near lakes, rivers, farmland, and even cities.

To gull someone means to deceive or trick them — but not just any ordinary trick. The word carries a specific, important flavor: it means to fool someone by exploiting their innocence, trust, or naivety. The person doing the gulling is cunning and deliberate.
Gullet is a noun with a few related meanings, all sharing the idea of a channel or passage.
Gullibility is the quality or tendency of a person to believe things too easily — particularly things that are untrue, exaggerated, or unproven.
Gullible describes a person who is too quick to believe what others say, without stopping to think about whether it's actually true. A gullible person is easily fooled, tricked, or deceived.
A gully is a narrow, steep-sided channel or trench cut into the ground by flowing water. Think of it as a small, deep groove that water carves into the earth over time.

Gumbo is a famous dish from Louisiana, a state in the southern United States. Think of it as a rich, thick, deeply flavored stew — somewhere between a soup and a stew in consistency — that is always served over white rice.
Gumption is a quality a person has when they combine practical common sense with the courage and drive to actually act on it.

To gun for someone or something means to actively and determinedly pursue a target — either to harm/defeat a person, or to eagerly try to achieve a goal. Think of a hunter going out into the field with a loaded gun. They are not wandering around aimlessly.

When someone is gun-shy, they are unusually nervous, hesitant, or reluctant to do something — specifically because a past experience hurt them, scared them, or went badly wrong. The key ingredient is always that prior painful experience.

Gunboat diplomacy is a foreign policy strategy in which a militarily powerful nation uses the visible display or implicit threat of military force — without necessarily going to war — to pressure a weaker nation into compliance with its political, economic, or territorial demands.

If someone is gung-ho, they are extremely enthusiastic, eager, and motivated about something — often to the point where they dive in headfirst without stopping to think carefully. It describes a burning, energetic desire to act, achieve, or push forward.
A gunwale is the top edge — or the reinforced strip running along that top edge — of the side wall of a boat or ship.
To gurgle means to make a soft, bubbly, broken sound — the kind that happens when a liquid moves through a narrow or restricted space, or when air and liquid mix and push against each other.
A gurney is a narrow, wheeled bed used to carry a person who cannot walk — usually because they are injured, ill, unconscious, or have just had surgery.
A guru is a teacher — but not just any ordinary teacher. A guru is someone who possesses deep, mastered knowledge or wisdom and passes it on to a student.

A gush is a sudden, strong, and large outpouring of something — all at once, not gradually. Think of the difference between water dripping from a tap and water bursting out of a broken pipe. The burst? That's a gush.
To flow out suddenly, rapidly, and in a large amount, usually from an opening.

To gush over someone or something means to express great admiration, excitement, or affection in a very enthusiastic, emotional, and sometimes over-the-top way — usually through a flood of compliments, praise, or excited words.

When a person is gushing, they are expressing admiration, praise, or excitement in a way that is excessive, overflowing, and hard to contain — often to the point where it feels embarrassing or too much.

A gust is a sudden, short-lived burst of strong wind — not a steady wind that blows continuously, but a quick, powerful rush of air that arrives without warning and disappears almost as fast as it came.
Gustatory means relating to the sense of taste.

Gusto means enthusiastic, energetic, and wholehearted enjoyment. When someone does something with gusto, they don't just do it — they throw themselves into it with visible energy and obvious pleasure, holding absolutely nothing back.
Gusty describes wind — or weather — that does not blow in a smooth, steady stream, but instead arrives in sudden, sharp bursts called gusts. These bursts come and go unpredictably.
When "gut" is used as an adjective, it means instinctive — something that comes from your deepest inner feelings, automatically, before your mind has had any chance to think about it.

To gut something means to remove or destroy what is on the inside, leaving behind only an empty shell. Think of it like scooping out the insides of a pumpkin — the outer skin remains, but everything within is taken out or destroyed.

A gut feeling is a strong inner sense that something is true, right, wrong, safe, or dangerous — even when you cannot explain why you feel that way. It arrives instantly, without any visible logical reasoning.
Gut-wrenching describes something that causes such intense emotional pain or distress that it almost feels physical — like something is twisting and pulling hard at the inside of your body.
Gutless means lacking courage — specifically, the courage to do something difficult, risky, or morally right when it truly matters.
Courage and determination, as in "it takes guts to speak up." Literally, the intestines and other internal organs, or the stomach.
Gutsy means showing boldness, courage, and determination — especially when the situation is risky, difficult, or scary, and most people would hesitate or back down.
Extremely disappointed or upset, as in "I was gutted to miss the final" (British informal). Literally, having the insides removed or destroyed, as in "a building gutted by fire."
A gutter is a channel, groove, or trough that collects and carries away something unwanted — usually water, waste, or filth.
"Gutter press" refers to newspapers or media outlets that care more about shocking, scandalous, and invasive stories than about truth, fairness, or public decency.
Guttural describes a sound — usually a voice, a word, or a language — that is harsh, rough, and seems to come from deep in the throat, almost like a growl or a rasp.
When you say guys (plural), something interesting happens: the word becomes gender-neutral. It no longer means only men. It refers to any group of people — all men, all women, or a mix.
To guzzle means to drink something quickly, greedily, and in large amounts — often all at once or in rapid, continuous gulps, with little care or restraint.

A gynecologist is a medical doctor who specializes in the health of the female reproductive system. This includes the organs and body parts that are unique to people born female — such as the uterus, ovaries, fallopian tubes, cervix, and vagina.

To gyrate means to move in a continuous, wide, circular or spiral motion around a fixed central point. Picture a spinning top twirling on a table — it keeps looping around and around a center point in a sweeping, curving path. That is gyrating.
A gyration is a circular or spiral movement around a central point or axis.
A gyre is a large, circular or spiral pattern of movement — most commonly used to describe a massive, slow-spinning system of ocean currents that loops continuously around a vast area of the sea.

A gyroscope is a device that contains a wheel or disk spinning at high speed, mounted inside a frame that allows the wheel to rotate freely in any direction. The spinning wheel is the heart of the device.
"Habeas corpus" is a Latin phrase. Latin was the language of law and scholarship in medieval Europe, and many legal terms still come from it.

A habit is a behavior — an action, thought, or response — that you do regularly and automatically, almost without thinking, because you have done it so many times before that your brain has put it on "autopilot."
Habitable means suitable or fit to live in. A place is habitable when it provides the basic conditions that allow a person — or a living thing — to survive and exist there.
A habitat is the natural place where a living thing — an animal, a plant, a fungus, or any other organism — normally lives, grows, and finds everything it needs to survive.

Habitation carries two closely connected meanings that flow naturally from one another: 1. The act or state of living in a place — the ongoing process of people occupying and residing somewhere. 2. A place where people live — a home, a dwelling, a shelter, or a settlement.

When something is habitual, it means it is done so regularly and so repeatedly that it has stopped being a conscious choice and has become a natural, automatic part of who someone is or how they behave.
When someone does something habitually, it means they do it so regularly and so consistently that it has become a fixed part of their behavior — almost like second nature.
To habituate means to gradually get used to something through repeated exposure — so much so that your reaction to it becomes weaker or even disappears over time.
A habitué is a person who visits a particular place so regularly and so often that they become a familiar, recognized presence there — almost like they belong to that place.
A writer, especially a journalist, who produces dull, unoriginal work for money. It can also mean a clever trick or shortcut, an act of breaking into a computer system, or a rough cut.

When you "hack" something, you cut it with heavy, repeated strokes — not cleanly or precisely, but aggressively. Think of someone using an axe or a large knife to chop through something thick and tough.
To comb out flax or hemp fibres by pulling them through a board of sharp metal teeth, to clean and straighten them before spinning.

Hackles are the hairs (or feathers, in birds) that run along the back of the neck — and sometimes down the spine — of certain animals. Think of a dog, a cat, a wolf, or a rooster. That strip of fur or feathers sitting on the back of their neck?
Something is hackneyed when it has been used so many times that it has completely lost its freshness, power, and impact.
When you describe someone as haggard, you mean they look extremely exhausted, worn out, and unwell — and it shows clearly on their face.

A haggle is a prolonged, back-and-forth negotiation between two people — usually over the price of something — where each side pushes and pulls, trying to get a deal that works in their own favor. Neither side simply accepts the other's first offer.
To haggle means to negotiate the price of something by going back and forth with another person — each side pushing for a deal that favors them — until you either agree on a price or give up.
A haiku is a very short poem — always three lines — that captures a single, fleeting moment, usually from the natural world.

Hail is precipitation — something that falls from the sky — but unlike rain (which is liquid water) or snow (which is soft, fluffy ice crystals), hail is made of solid lumps of ice. These lumps are called hailstones.
When you "hail" someone, you call out to them loudly, or make a visible signal to get their attention — usually because they are at a distance from you, or moving away.

"Hail from" simply means "to come from" or "to originate from" a particular place. When you say someone hails from somewhere, you are telling people where that person was born, grew up, or considers their original home.
"Hair-raising" describes something so frightening, dangerous, shocking, or intensely thrilling that it makes you feel as though the hairs on your body are literally standing up.

Hairsplitting is the act of focusing on extremely tiny, almost invisible differences between things — differences so small that they are usually unnecessary, pointless, or distracting from what actually matters.
Hajj is the sacred pilgrimage that Muslims make to the city of Mecca, located in present-day Saudi Arabia.

"Halal" is an Arabic adjective that means permissible or lawful. When something is described as halal, it means that thing is allowed — it is acceptable to use, consume, do, or engage with it according to Islamic religious law.

When you describe a time or period as halcyon, you mean it was peacefully, happily golden — a stretch of life that felt calm, carefree, and blissfully good. Think of it as the emotional opposite of turbulent or troubled times.

A halcyon is a legendary bird from ancient Greek mythology — most commonly identified with the kingfisher, a small, vividly colored bird known for diving into water to catch fish. But what made the halcyon extraordinary wasn't its appearance.
"Hale" means strong, healthy, and physically vigorous. But it's not just ordinary good health — it suggests a robust, thriving kind of health, the kind that fills a person with energy and vitality.
A half measure is an action or a solution that is incomplete — one that only partly deals with a problem instead of solving it fully.
When you describe something as half-baked, you are saying it is poorly thought out, incomplete, or not ready to be taken seriously.
When someone is half-hearted about something, they are doing it, but not really meaning it.
When you do something half-heartedly, you do it without real effort, genuine interest, or full commitment. Your actions are there, but your heart — your true desire and energy — is not fully in it.

A halfway house is a place that sits in the middle — between where someone was and where they are trying to get to. It is a bridge. A temporary stop. Not the beginning, not the end, but somewhere in between.
A halibut is a type of fish — specifically, a large, flat fish that lives in cold ocean water.
Halitosis is the formal, medical word for bad breath — an unpleasant or offensive odour that comes from a person's mouth when they breathe or speak.

A hallmark is a feature or quality that is so strongly and consistently associated with someone or something that it becomes the thing by which you recognize and identify them. It is not just any quality — it is a defining one.
A hallow is a saint — a holy person. Plain and simple.
Hallowed means deeply sacred, holy, or worthy of the highest possible reverence and respect.
To hallucinate means to experience something through your senses that does not actually exist in the real world.
A hallucination is when a person perceives something — sees it, hears it, smells it, tastes it, or feels it — that does not actually exist in the real world. It is a false sensory experience.
A hallucinogen is a substance — usually a drug — that, when taken into the body, profoundly alters how a person perceives reality.
Hallucinogenic is an adjective that describes something capable of causing hallucinations — meaning it has the power to make a person's mind experience things that are not actually real.
The halo effect is a type of cognitive bias, which means it's a predictable, systematic error in the way human brains think and judge. It's not a character flaw. It's not stupidity.

To halt means to stop — but not just any kind of stop. When something halts, the stopping feels deliberate, abrupt, and complete. There is a sense that something which was actively moving, running, or progressing has been brought to a standstill.

A halter is a set of straps or a rope fitted around an animal's head — most often a horse, but also cattle, goats, or donkeys. It is used to lead the animal from place to place or to tie it to a post so it stays in one spot.

When someone's speech is halting, they speak with frequent pauses, struggle to find words, restart their sentences, or sound deeply uncertain about what they are saying. The words don't flow — they come out in broken pieces.
A famous problem in computer science, proved by Alan Turing to be unsolvable: it is impossible to write a program that can always tell whether any other program will eventually stop or run forever.
Meat from the upper part of a pig's hind leg, usually preserved by salting or smoking. A ham is also an actor who overacts, or an amateur radio operator.

A hamlet is an extremely small, rural human settlement — a cluster of a few houses and maybe a handful of other buildings, tucked away in the countryside. Think of it as the tiniest kind of place where people live together.
Very drunk (informal). It can also mean shaped or textured by hitting with a hammer, as in "hammered copper," or badly beaten or defeated.

To hamper something means to make it harder for it to happen, move forward, or succeed. When something hampers you or your efforts, it doesn't necessarily stop you completely — it gets in your way, slows you down, or restricts your freedom to act.
Your hamstring is a group of three muscles running along the back of your thigh — the area between your buttock and your knee. Think of the back of your leg.

To hamstring someone or something means to seriously damage or destroy their ability to act, move, or function effectively — to cripple them, not necessarily physically, but in terms of their power, freedom, or capability.
To pass something on to a younger person or the next generation, as in "a tradition handed down over centuries." It can also mean for a court to officially announce a decision or sentence.
Closely connected, so that one usually comes with the other, as in "poverty and poor health often go hand in hand." Literally, holding each other's hands.
"Hand over fist" means rapidly, in large and continuous amounts — usually referring to gaining or losing something, most often money.

A hand-me-down is something — most often a piece of clothing, but also any object — that one person used to own or use, and then passed on to someone else to use after them, instead of throwing it away or selling it.
When something or someone is hand-picked, it means they were carefully and personally chosen by someone — not randomly, not automatically, but with full deliberate thought and intention.
Having only just enough money or resources to survive, with nothing left to save, as in "a hand-to-mouth existence."
A handgun is a small firearm — a gun — compact and light enough to be held and operated with one or both hands, without needing to rest it against your shoulder or mount it on any surface.
A handicap is anything that puts you at a disadvantage — something that makes it harder for you to do something, succeed at something, or compete fairly against others.
"Handily" is an adverb with two main meanings that are somewhat related but feel different in practice. Understanding both will give you complete mastery of the word.
Handiwork means something that someone made, did, or caused — especially when you want to point to that person as the one responsible for it.
To handle someone with kid gloves means to treat a person with great care, gentleness, and sensitivity — usually to avoid upsetting them, offending them, or making a difficult situation worse.

A handover is the act of giving something — control, responsibility, power, a task, or an object — to another person or group, so that they can take over completely. The most important thing to understand is that a handover is not just giving.

"Hands down" has two closely related meanings that almost always go hand in hand: 1. Easily, without much effort — When someone wins or achieves something hands down, they do it with zero struggle. There is no close contest.
When you describe something as hands-off, you mean that a person, organization, or system chooses not to get directly involved in controlling, managing, or interfering with something.
Involving direct, practical participation rather than just watching or reading, as in "hands-on experience." Of a manager, closely involved in day-to-day work.
A handsel is a gift, token, or payment that marks the very start of something — and that start is meant to be lucky or meaningful.

Handsome means attractive in a strong, clean, and dignified way. It is a compliment about how someone or something looks — but it carries a particular flavour that makes it different from words like beautiful, pretty, or cute.

When something "hangs by a thread," it means it is in an extremely fragile, dangerous, or uncertain situation — so unstable that even the smallest push could cause it to fail, collapse, or end completely.
When something "hangs in the balance," it means the outcome of that thing is completely uncertain — it could go well, or it could go badly. Nothing has been decided yet.
"Hang in there" means to keep going even when things are hard, and not give up.

To "hang on someone's every word" means to listen with total, intense, and fascinated attention to everything a person says — not missing even a single word. When you hang on someone's every word, you are completely absorbed in what they are saying.
To hang someone out to dry means to abandon someone and leave them alone to face a difficult or dangerous situation, especially when you could have helped them but chose not to.

"Hang tight" means wait patiently and stay where you are. When someone tells you to hang tight, they are asking you to be calm, stay put, and not worry — because help is coming, the situation will be resolved, or something is about to happen soon.

A hang-up is something inside a person's mind — an emotional block, a deep insecurity, or a mental fixation — that gets in the way of them thinking or behaving freely and naturally in a certain area of life.

A hangar is a very large building designed specifically to shelter, store, maintain, or repair aircraft — such as airplanes and helicopters. Think of it as a garage, but built for aircraft instead of cars.
A hanger-on is a person who stays close to someone rich, famous, or powerful — not out of genuine friendship, but purely for personal benefit.

A hangover is the unpleasant collection of physical and mental symptoms a person experiences after drinking too much alcohol, typically felt the morning after — or several hours after — the drinking has stopped.
To hanker means to have a strong, persistent, restless desire for something — especially something you don't currently have, something from your past, or something that feels just out of reach.
A hankering is a strong, deep, and persistent desire or longing for something. It's that feeling when you really, genuinely want something — and the want doesn't go away easily.

To hap means to happen — specifically, to come about by chance, luck, or fortune, rather than by planning or intention. It's an older, more literary way of saying "to happen by chance" or "to come to pass."

When something is haphazard, it has no plan, no system, and no order behind it. It happens — or is done — in a completely random way, with no thought given to how things fit together, what comes next, or whether there is any logic guiding the process.

Haphazardly means doing something without any plan, order, or careful thought. It describes an action carried out in a random, disorganized, and careless way — as if no one stopped to think about how it should be done properly.
Haphephobia is an intense, irrational, and persistent fear of being touched by another person.
Hapless describes someone who is persistently unlucky — a person who, no matter what they do or how hard they try, always seems to end up on the wrong side of fate.
Happenstance means an event or situation that happened purely by chance — something that was not planned, not intended, and not caused by anyone on purpose. It just happened, randomly, on its own.
A happy medium is a middle point between two extremes that is just right — not too much of one thing, and not too much of the other.

If someone is happy-go-lucky, they are cheerful, carefree, and not worried about what might happen in life. They take each day as it comes, without stressing about problems, the future, or things going wrong.

When something is described as haram, it means it is strictly forbidden under Islamic religious law. This is not a casual "you probably shouldn't" — it is a hard prohibition, the strongest level of "not allowed" that exists in Islam.

A harangue is a long, forceful, and emotionally charged speech delivered at a person or group — most often to scold, criticize, or passionately persuade them. The key word here is at. A harangue is not a conversation.

To harangue someone means to speak to them at length in a forceful, aggressive, and often angry way — usually to criticize them, scold them, or push a strong opinion on them — while they have little choice but to sit there and take it.
To harass someone means to repeatedly and persistently bother, disturb, or attack them in a way that causes them stress, fear, or discomfort — and to do so against their will.

When you describe someone as harassed, you are saying that they are in a state of visible stress, exhaustion, or distress — caused by being repeatedly disturbed, pressured, or troubled, either by too many demands at once or by another person who keeps bothering or mistreating them.
Harassment is unwanted behavior directed at a person that disturbs, upsets, threatens, or causes them distress — and it typically keeps happening again and again.
A harbinger is something — a person, a thing, or a sign — that signals or announces that something bigger is on its way. Think of it as a messenger from the future.

A harbor is a sheltered area of water where ships and boats can stay safely — protected from strong winds, rough waves, and storms. Think of it as nature's (or humanity's) way of giving vessels a calm, safe resting place near the coast.
To keep a feeling or thought in your mind for a long time, as in "harbouring a grudge." It can also mean to hide and protect someone, especially a criminal, or to carry something, such as germs.

"Hard and fast" means fixed, absolute, and impossible to change or break. When a rule, boundary, or line is described as "hard and fast," it means there are zero exceptions — it applies in every single case, no matter what.

If someone feels "hard done by," they feel that they have been treated unfairly or harshly — by a person, a situation, or life in general. They believe they deserve better than what they have received.
Hard feelings are the negative emotions — such as bitterness, resentment, hurt, or lingering anger — that a person feels toward someone else after an unpleasant situation.
"A hard nut to crack" means something that is very difficult to deal with, solve, or understand — or someone who is very difficult to know, persuade, or get along with.
A hard pass is a firm, clear, and definitive refusal or rejection of something — an offer, an idea, an invitation, a suggestion, or an opportunity.

A hard sell is an aggressive, high-pressure attempt to persuade someone to buy something or agree to something — where the person doing the persuading pushes very hard, refuses to take "no" for an answer easily, and makes the other person feel a sense of urgency or obligation.
"Hard to come by" means something is difficult to find, get, or obtain. When you say something is "hard to come by," you're saying it is rare, scarce, or not easily available.
"Hard up" means not having enough of something you need — and most of the time, that something is money.
Tough, unsentimental, and cynical from hard experience, as in "a hard-boiled detective." Literally, of an egg, boiled until both the white and the yolk are solid.

When something is hard-earned, it means two things at the same time: 1. You have it — you achieved it, you got it, you own it. 2. It did not come easily — it required serious effort, struggle, sacrifice, or a long time.

"Hard-fought" describes something that was achieved only after tremendous effort, struggle, and strong opposition. It means the outcome — whether a victory, a right, a deal, or any kind of result — did not come easily.
Practical, realistic, and not easily swayed by emotion. It can also mean stubborn and unwilling to change one's mind.
Direct, forceful, and powerful, especially in dealing with difficult or uncomfortable truths, as in "a hard-hitting report."

When you describe someone or something as hard-line, you are saying that they hold a position — a belief, a rule, a policy — with absolute firmness, and they refuse to soften, compromise, or budge from it, no matter the pressure or circumstances.

Hard-nosed describes a person who is tough, practical, and unsentimental — someone who focuses strictly on facts, results, and logic, and refuses to let emotions, sympathy, or outside pressure change their thinking or decisions.

Under great pressure and struggling, especially from a lack of time, money, or resources. To be hard-pressed to do something means to find it very difficult, as in "you'd be hard-pressed to find a better deal."
Something that is hard-wearing is strong, tough, and built to last through a lot of use — without breaking down, falling apart, fading, or losing its quality quickly.
The word hard-wired means built in so deeply and permanently that it cannot be easily changed, removed, or reprogrammed.
A tough, aggressive, ruthless way of dealing with people, especially in politics or business, as in "to play hardball." Literally, a baseball.
When you call a person "hardcore," you mean they are so deeply and intensely committed to something that they have left casual territory far behind. They don't do things halfway. They are all in.
Firmly fixed in bad habits or ways, and unlikely to change, as in "a hardened criminal." It can also mean emotionally tough and no longer easily affected, or physically made hard or stronger.
When something is hardscrabble, it means it involves exhausting, relentless struggle just to survive — and barely even that.

Hardship means a condition of life — or a specific situation — that causes serious suffering, difficulty, or deprivation. It is the experience of struggling to cope with something that is genuinely painful, harsh, or unfair, especially over a period of time.
Hardtack is a type of extremely hard, dry, plain cracker or biscuit — so hard that if you try to bite into a dry piece without preparation, you could easily chip or break a tooth.

"Hardy" describes someone or something that is tough enough to withstand difficult conditions — whether that means harsh weather, physical hardship, or adversity — and come through unharmed or unbroken.

Harebrained means foolish, reckless, and not carefully thought through. When you call something harebrained, you are saying it is a wildly impractical idea that someone rushed into without using proper judgment or common sense.
Hark means to listen — but not in a casual, half-paying-attention way. It means to listen carefully, alertly, and with your full attention. Think of it as "listen, and really mean it."

"Hark back to" means to return to, recall, or remind you of something from the past. When something "harks back to" an earlier time, idea, event, or style, it means it has a strong connection to — or resemblance to — that older thing.

A harlequin is a classic comic character from traditional theatre — a witty, mischievous, and acrobatic trickster whose entire purpose on stage was to cause lovable chaos, play pranks, and make audiences roar with laughter.
Harm means any negative effect — physical, mental, emotional, financial, social, or otherwise — that is caused to a person, animal, object, relationship, or situation.

When something vibrates — a guitar string, a column of air in a flute, a vocal cord — it doesn't vibrate in just one simple, single way. It vibrates in several ways at the same time, all layered on top of each other.

Harmonious describes a situation where multiple different things — sounds, people, colors, ideas, or elements — come together and fit so well with each other that the result feels balanced, pleasing, and free from conflict. The key word here is together.
To bring different things together so they fit or work well together, or to be in agreement with each other. In music, to sing or play notes that combine pleasingly with a melody.
Harmony means a pleasing combination of different things that fit together so well that the whole feels balanced, complete, and unified.

A harness is a structured arrangement of straps, belts, or bands that are fastened securely around a body — human or animal — or bound around a set of components, for the purpose of control, attachment, safety, or support.
To harness something means to take a powerful force or resource that already exists, bring it under your control, and direct it toward a useful purpose.
A harp is a large musical instrument that you play by plucking its strings with your fingers.
To harp on something means to talk about the same thing again and again, usually in a way that other people find boring, annoying, or unnecessary.
A harridan is a woman — typically an older one — who is harsh, bad-tempered, bossy, and fond of scolding or nagging others.
Harried describes a person who is stressed, rushed, and overwhelmed — someone who feels like they are being pulled in too many directions at once and can barely keep up.
A harrow is a farming tool — a heavy frame fitted with sharp metal teeth, spikes, or rotating disks — that a farmer drags across plowed soil to prepare it for planting.### The problem it solves
To harrow means to cause intense mental distress or torment — to disturb someone deeply, in a way that feels wrenching and painful.
Something harrowing causes you intense emotional pain, anguish, or distress — the kind that shakes you deeply and stays with you.
To harry someone means to trouble them repeatedly and relentlessly — attacking, pressuring, or pestering them again and again, without giving them a moment of peace or rest.
Harsh means something that is unpleasantly strong, severe, or rough — to the point where it causes discomfort, pain, or distress. Think of it as the opposite of gentle, soft, or mild.
Harshly means in a way that is rough, severe, or unkind — often more than seems fair or necessary.
Harshness is a noun that names a quality — the quality of being rough, severe, or unpleasantly intense in a way that causes discomfort, pain, or distress. It is the noun form of the adjective harsh.
To harvest something means to collect or gather something that has grown or built up over time, at the right moment when it is ready.
To hash something means to chop or break something down into smaller pieces. Everything else this word does — across cooking, conversation, and computers — flows from that one idea.
To "hash out" something means to discuss a topic thoroughly and in detail — going back and forth — until you reach a final decision, agreement, or solution.

A hassle is a situation, task, or experience that is more difficult, annoying, or exhausting than it should be — especially when it wastes your time, demands unnecessary effort, or frustrates you with complications and obstacles along the way.

To hassle someone means to repeatedly bother, pressure, or annoy them — often to make them do something they aren't doing, or simply because you want something from them and you won't leave them alone until you get it.

Haste means doing something very quickly because you feel a strong urge or pressure to get it done fast. But it is not just any kind of speed. Haste is speed that is driven by urgency — a feeling that you must move fast, that there is no time to slow down.
