When someone says or does something "in no uncertain terms," it means they communicated their message in a way that was completely clear, direct, firm, and impossible to misunderstand.
"In one fell swoop" means doing something all at once, in a single quick action, especially when that action affects many things at the same time.
"In one's cups" means to be drunk — that is, to have consumed enough alcohol that it has visibly affected a person's behavior, speech, or judgment.
"In someone's/something's stead" means "in the place of someone/something" — acting as a substitute or replacement for them.
"In perpetuity" means forever — with absolutely no end date, ever.
"In perpetuity" means forever. Without end. For all time.
"In point of fact" means "in reality," "actually," or "the truth is."
"In short order" means very quickly, without delay, and without wasting any time.
"In situ" means in the original place — right there, where something already is, without moving it or taking it somewhere else.

When you are "in someone's bad books," it means that person is unhappy, disappointed, or angry with you. They have a negative opinion of you right now, usually because of something you said or did (or forgot to do).
When you are "in someone's good books," it means that person likes you, approves of you, or thinks highly of you at a particular moment. You have their respect, goodwill, or positive regard.

"In spades" means in very large amounts, to a very great degree, or more than enough. It is used to intensify or emphasize whatever it is describing — almost like adding the words "a whole lot" or "big time" to a sentence.
Despite something; without being prevented by it, as in "they went out in spite of the rain."
"In tandem" means two or more things working together, cooperating closely, or happening at the same time in a coordinated way to achieve a shared result.
If someone or something is "in the ascendant," it means they are rising in power, influence, or importance — they are becoming stronger, more popular, or more dominant than before.

When someone or something is "in the doldrums," it means they are in a state of sadness, low energy, or sluggishness — or they are stuck and making no progress. Think of a person who feels gloomy and unmotivated, or a business that has stopped growing.
"In the final analysis" means "when everything has been fully thought through and considered, this is the most important truth."

"In the fullness of time" means eventually, when the right moment arrives naturally. It tells you that something will happen — but only after enough time has passed and conditions are truly ready. It is not just "someday."
If someone is "in the know," it means they have special, private, or inside information about something that most other people don't have. They are well-informed.

To be "left in the lurch" means to be abandoned by someone at the worst possible moment — when you needed them most, when everything depended on them, and when it's too late for you to easily fix the situation on your own.
When something is "in the offing," it means it is likely to happen soon — it is coming in the near future, and there are already signs or reasons to expect it.
When someone is "in the public eye," it means they are widely known and constantly watched by the general public.
When someone says or does two things almost at the same time, especially when those two things seem to contradict each other or feel surprising together, we say they did it "in the same breath."

When you say something is "in the same vein," you mean it shares the same style, tone, spirit, character, or nature as something else. It is a way of saying that two things are similar in feel or approach, even if they are not identical.
"In the teeth of" means directly facing, or acting despite, something powerful, hostile, and dangerous — whether that is a storm, strong opposition, or evidence that contradicts you.

When someone is "in the thick of things," it means they are deeply involved in the busiest, most intense, most active part of a situation. They are not on the sidelines watching. They are not at the edges.

To be "in the throes of" something means to be in the middle of an intense, powerful, and often painful or overwhelming experience or process — one that grips you so strongly that it's hard to think about anything else or break free from it.
"In the wake of" means following something significant, as a result of it, or in the aftermath of it.
When something or someone is "in the wings," it means they are waiting nearby, ready to appear or act when the right moment comes.
"In toto" is a formal adverb that means completely, entirely, as a single whole — with nothing left out, nothing excluded, and nothing only partially included.

When something is "in train," it means it has been properly set up, arranged, and is now moving forward as planned. It describes a process or plan that is organized and underway — things are in motion, progressing step by step in the right order.
One after another, in order, as in "each student spoke in turn." It can also mean as a result of something, as in "the drought raised prices, which in turn hurt farmers."

"In vain" means without success or without achieving any result. When you do something in vain, you put in effort, time, or energy — but nothing comes of it. The work was wasted. The goal was not reached.
Inability means the state of not being able to do something. When someone — or something — simply cannot do a particular thing, that lack of power or capacity is called an inability.
Inaccessible means not able to be reached, entered, used, or understood.
Inadequacy is the state of not being good enough, not being sufficient, or not meeting the level that is needed or expected.
Something is inadequate when it does not reach the level that is needed or expected. There is a gap — a shortfall — between what exists and what is required.
"Inadmissible" is an adjective that means "not allowed," "not acceptable," or "not permitted to be received or considered" — particularly in a formal or official setting.
Inadvertence means a lack of proper attention or care that causes something to happen — without the person meaning for it to happen.
Inadvertent means something that was done without intention and without realising it — usually because the person involved was not paying close enough attention.
"Inadvertently" means doing something without intending to do it, and often without even realizing you are doing it — or without realizing the effect it would have.
Inalienable describes something that cannot be taken away, sold, surrendered, or transferred — no matter what. It belongs to you permanently and completely.

An inamorata is a woman who is deeply loved by someone — she is the object of a person's romantic love. Simply put, she is someone's beloved, his sweetheart, his love. The word always refers to a woman specifically.
Something inane is so completely empty of sense, meaning, or intelligence that it barely qualifies as thought at all. It's not just wrong, not just unhelpful — it's vacuously foolish.

"Inanimate" means not alive. When you describe something as inanimate, you are saying it has no life — no heartbeat, no breath, no ability to grow, feel, or reproduce on its own. It simply exists as matter.
Severe weakness and exhaustion caused by lack of food and nourishment. Figuratively, emptiness and lack of vitality or purpose.
Inanity is the quality of being utterly empty of sense, intelligence, or meaning.
Inapplicable is an adjective that describes something — usually a rule, law, principle, method, or standard — that does not fit or cannot be applied to a particular situation, person, or case.
Something is inapposite when it simply does not fit the situation — it's out of place, beside the point, or unsuitable for the specific context it's being used in.
Something is inappropriate when it does not fit the situation it is used in, said in, or done in.

"Inapt" means not fitting, not suitable, or not appropriate for a particular situation, purpose, or context. When something is inapt, it simply doesn't match or belong where it has been placed or used.
Something is inarguable when it is so clearly and obviously true that no reasonable person can dispute it. It sits completely beyond debate. There is simply no valid argument to be made against it.
Inarticulate means unable to express thoughts, feelings, or ideas clearly through words.
A formal way of saying "to the extent that" or "because," as in "he is guilty, inasmuch as he knew about the plan."
Inattentive means not paying attention — failing to focus on, notice, or properly observe something or someone that deserves your attention.
Something is inaudible when it cannot be heard. If a sound exists but you are unable to hear it — for any reason — that sound is inaudible.
When something is described as inaugural, it means it is the very first of its kind — but not just any ordinary "first."
Inaugurate means to officially begin something important — usually with a formal ceremony or public event.

An inauguration is a formal, official ceremony that marks the beginning of something important — either the start of a person's role in a powerful position, or the official opening of something significant like a building, institution, or program.

Something is inauspicious when it gives off bad signs — when the early conditions, signals, or circumstances suggest that things are not going to go well. It points toward failure, misfortune, or trouble ahead.
Inauthentic means not genuine — not truly what it claims or appears to be. Something inauthentic is putting on a false front.
When we say something is inborn, we mean it is a quality, ability, or characteristic that a person is naturally born with. It was not taught, practiced, or picked up from the outside world.

The word inbred describes something that is so deeply rooted in a person, animal, or group that it seems to have been there from the very beginning — either because it was literally born that way, or because it was absorbed so early and so thoroughly that it feels completely natural and inseparable.

Inbreeding is the process of reproduction between two individuals who are closely related to each other — meaning they share one or more recent ancestors. The word refers to this practice or phenomenon itself, whether it happens in animals, plants, or humans.
Incalculable describes something so enormous, so vast, or so far beyond any scale that no number can capture it — even if you tried your hardest to measure it, you simply couldn't.
Incandescence is the production of light from heat. It is the glow that an object emits when it has been heated to an extremely high temperature.
Extremely angry, as in "she was incandescent with rage." It can also mean dazzlingly brilliant, or literally, glowing with light because it is extremely hot.
An incantation is a set of words — spoken aloud, chanted, or sung — that is believed to have magical power.
Incantatory describes something that resembles an incantation — something that has the quality, feel, or effect of a magic spell being cast.
Incapable means not having the ability, skill, or power needed to do or experience something.

To incapacitate someone or something means to take away their ability to function, act, or perform as they normally would. It is to make something — a person, a body, a machine, or a system — unable to do what it is supposed to do.

When someone is incapacitated, they have been rendered unable to function normally — to move, work, think clearly, make decisions, or take care of themselves — because some condition has stripped away their normal ability to do so.
When something incapacitates you, it takes that capacity away — it prevents you from functioning normally. So incapacitating (the adjective) describes whatever is doing that.
Incapacity means the state of being unable to do something — specifically because of a lack of ability, power, strength, or legal right to do it.
To incarcerate someone means to officially lock them up and confine them in a prison or jail, taking away their freedom of movement as a consequence of the law.

When someone is described as incarcerated, it means they are currently being held inside a prison or jail by legal authority — they are physically confined and cannot leave freely. It describes a state of being locked away as a consequence of the law.
Incarceration means the state of being locked up inside a prison or jail by the authority of a legal system — in other words, it is what happens to a person when they are officially imprisoned.
Incarnadine is a color word. As an adjective, it describes something that is flesh-pink or blood-red in color — somewhere in the warm spectrum between a soft, pale pink and a deep, vivid crimson.
When something abstract — like an idea, a quality, or a spiritual being — takes on a physical, bodily form (especially a human body), it is said to be incarnate.
To incarnate something means to take a thing that is abstract — an idea, a quality, a spirit, a feeling — and give it a real, physical, bodily form.
Incarnation means the act of something invisible, abstract, or spiritual taking on a real, physical, living form — especially a human or bodily form.
Incautious means not careful enough about possible dangers, risks, or bad consequences. A person who is incautious acts or speaks without pausing to think about what could go wrong.

"Incendiary" describes something that ignites — either literally (fire) or figuratively (emotions, controversy, conflict). Think of it as the adjective form of "setting something on fire," whether that something is an actual building or a conversation.
A person who deliberately sets fire to property. It can also mean someone who stirs up conflict or violence, or a bomb designed to start fires.

Incense is a substance that produces a pleasant, fragrant smell when it is lit and burned. The scent doesn't come from the flame itself — it comes from the smoke that slowly rises as the material burns. That fragrant smoke is the whole point of incense.
To incense someone means to make them extremely angry — not just mildly upset or a little bothered, but genuinely furious.

Incensed means extremely angry — not just a little annoyed or mildly upset, but filled with intense, burning fury. When someone is incensed, their anger has reached a high, almost uncontrollable level.
An incentive is anything that encourages or motivates a person to do something — or to do it better, faster, or more often. It is a reason to act.

To incentivize something means to deliberately set up a reward, benefit, or advantage that motivates people to take a specific action they might not otherwise take — or to take it more eagerly than they otherwise would.
Inception means the beginning or starting point of something — specifically, the moment when something is first created, established, or set into motion.
Inceptive means "of, relating to, or marking the very beginning of something."
Incessant means continuing without stopping, pausing, or taking a break. When something is incessant, it just keeps going and going, with no rest in between.
Incessantly means without stopping, without any break, and without any pause — going on and on and on. When something happens incessantly, it never lets up, even for a moment.
Incest is a sexual relationship or marriage between two people who are very closely related by blood or family.
Involving sexual relations between close family members. Figuratively, describing a group whose members are so closely connected that they exclude outsiders, as in "the incestuous world of politics."
Inchmeal means inch by inch — progressing in extremely tiny steps, so slowly and so gradually that each bit of movement is almost too small to notice.
Inchoate describes something that has begun to exist but hasn't taken shape yet — something raw, early, and not yet fully formed or developed.
Incidence means how often something happens, or the rate and extent to which something occurs or affects people and things.
An incident is simply something that happens — an event, an occurrence. But it's not used for just any event.
Happening as a minor or secondary part of something else, rather than being the main thing, as in "incidental expenses." Incidental to something means naturally accompanying it.
By the way, used to introduce an extra remark or side point, as in "Incidentally, did you see the news?" It can also mean as a side effect, not deliberately.

In its most common noun form, incidentals (almost always used in the plural) refers to minor expenses that are secondary to the main cost of something — small charges that come up alongside a bigger, more important purchase or activity.
To incinerate something means to destroy it completely by burning it — at such extreme heat that the object is reduced to nothing but ash, smoke, and gases.

Incineration is the complete burning of something — usually until nothing is left but ash, smoke, and gases. The key word here is complete. It doesn't mean something is slightly charred or partially burned.
Incipient means just beginning to exist or develop — in its very earliest stage.
To incise something means to cut into a surface deliberately and precisely, leaving a mark, groove, or opening behind.

An incision is a deliberate, clean cut made into something using a sharp instrument. The most important word here is deliberate — an incision is not an accident. It is a cut made on purpose, with precision and control.
Sharp, clear, and direct, getting straight to the heart of a matter, as in "an incisive analysis."
An incisor is a type of tooth — specifically, one of the flat, sharp-edged teeth located at the very front of your mouth. Their primary job is to cut and bite into food.
To incite means to deliberately stir someone up and push them toward doing something — usually something aggressive, harmful, or disruptive.
Incivility means rude, disrespectful, or discourteous behavior or speech toward others. It is the act — or the general pattern — of treating people without basic politeness or consideration.

Inclement means harsh, severe, and unpleasant — especially when describing weather, but also sometimes people or their actions. Think of it as the opposite of "mild" or "gentle." When something is inclement, it is rough, merciless, and difficult to endure.
A natural tendency or desire to do something, as in "she has no inclination to travel." It can also mean a slope or angle, or a slight bow of the head.

Whether used physically or mentally, incline always means the same thing at its core: to lean in a direction. Think of a tree that doesn't stand perfectly upright — it leans, it angles toward one side.

Inclined means having a natural leaning toward something — whether that's a feeling, an opinion, a desire, or a tendency. Think of it like a ramp: just as a physical ramp leans in one direction, your mind or personality can "lean" toward something.

Inclusion means the act of bringing someone or something in, or the state of being brought in. It is the noun form of the verb "include," which means to make someone or something a part of a group, a place, a list, or a situation.
Including everyone or everything, without leaving anyone out, as in "an inclusive society." Of a price, including all charges.

Inclusivity is the quality or practice of making sure that everyone is welcomed, valued, and able to participate fully — especially people who are often left out, overlooked, or treated as "less than" by society.
If someone is incognito, they are deliberately hiding who they really are — concealing their true identity so that other people do not recognize them.
When you do something incognito, you do it while deliberately hiding your true identity so that the people around you do not recognize you or know who you really are.

Incoherent means not fitting together in a clear, logical, or connected way. When something is incoherent, its parts don't link up. Ideas jump around, logic breaks down, and the overall picture becomes impossible to follow or make sense of.
"Incommensurable" describes two (or more) things that share no common measure — no single yardstick, scale, or standard exists that can meaningfully measure, compare, or rank both of them together.
Out of proportion with something else, as in "a punishment incommensurate with the crime." It can also mean impossible to compare because there is no common measure.
"Incommodious" means causing discomfort, inconvenience, or difficulty — most often because a space or place is too small, cramped, or poorly suited for comfortable use.

When a person is incommunicado, they are in a state of complete communication blackout with the outside world. They cannot send or receive any messages, calls, letters, or visits. No one can reach them, and they cannot reach anyone.
Incomparable means so exceptionally good, beautiful, or impressive that nothing else can be compared to it.
When two or more things are incompatible, it means they fundamentally cannot exist, work, or be combined together in a successful or peaceful way.
Incompetence means the lack of ability, skill, or knowledge needed to do something properly — especially something that a person is expected or supposed to be able to do.
Incompetent describes someone (or something) that lacks the skill, ability, or knowledge needed to do a job or task properly — to the standard that is reasonably expected of them.

Incomprehensible means impossible, or nearly impossible, to understand. When something is incomprehensible, your mind cannot grasp it, process it, or make sense of it — no matter how hard you try. Understanding simply breaks down.

Incomprehension means the state of not understanding something. It is the experience of encountering something — a word, an idea, a situation, a person's behaviour — and simply being unable to make sense of it.

"Inconceivable" describes something that is impossible — or nearly impossible — for the human mind to imagine, picture, or grasp. If something is inconceivable, you simply cannot form a clear idea of it in your mind. It lies beyond your mental reach.
Not leading to a clear, definite answer or result.
Incongruence is the state of two or more things not fitting together — not matching, not belonging with each other, not being in harmony.

Something is incongruent when it does not fit, match, or belong with something else. There is a mismatch — a noticeable clash — between two things that should ideally be compatible, consistent, or in harmony with each other.

Incongruity means a lack of harmony or compatibility between things that exist together or are being compared. It is the quality of things being mismatched, out of place, or inconsistent with each other or with their surroundings.
Something is incongruous when it feels deeply out of place — when it doesn't fit, doesn't belong, or clashes with everything around it.
An unknown person; a stranger. In Canada and Alaska, an inconnu is also a large freshwater fish related to the whitefish.
Inconsequential means not important enough to matter or make any difference.
"Inconsiderable" means too small, too slight, or too unimportant to be worth any serious attention. If something is inconsiderable, it is so minor that it barely registers — it is beneath notice.
Inconsiderate describes a person, action, or behavior that shows a lack of thought or care about other people's feelings, needs, comfort, or wellbeing.
A situation where things that should match or agree do not, as in "inconsistencies in his story." It can also mean the quality of changing in an unreliable way, as in "the team's inconsistency."

Inconsolable means being so deeply sad or distressed that nothing can comfort you. No words, no hugs, no actions — nothing works. The pain is simply too overwhelming to be eased by anything anyone says or does.

Something is inconspicuous when it does not attract attention — it blends into its surroundings so naturally that people either don't notice it at all, or barely register that it exists. It doesn't stand out. It doesn't make you stop and stare.

Inconstancy is the quality of being unreliable, unstable, or untrustworthy — specifically because of frequent, unpredictable, and unjustified change. When someone or something shows inconstancy, you cannot depend on them to remain the same.
Inconstant means not staying the same — it describes something or someone that keeps changing in a way that makes them unreliable or impossible to depend on.

Incontestable means impossible to argue against, challenge, or dispute. When something is incontestable, it is so clearly true, so solidly proven, or so firmly established that no reasonable challenge to it can succeed.
Incontinence means the inability to control something that should be under your control — most often, your own body's release of waste, but sometimes your own emotions or impulses.
Incontinent describes someone or something that cannot hold back or fails to contain something that is supposed to be kept in.

Something is incontrovertible when it is so completely and solidly true that it is impossible for anyone to argue against it, dispute it, or deny it. There is no debate to be had. There is no "but what if...?" The matter is simply closed.

An inconvenience is something that causes you trouble, difficulty, or discomfort — but in a mild to moderate way, not in a serious or life-threatening way. It is an obstacle or disruption that makes your life harder than it needs to be.
When "inconveniencing" is used as an adjective, it describes something or someone that is actively causing trouble, disruption, or discomfort to another person.
Something is inconvenient when it causes difficulty, trouble, or disruption — but not serious harm. It sits in the space between "perfectly fine" and "a real problem."

"Incorporate" means to take something and make it a real, merged part of a larger whole — not just placing it alongside something, but blending it in so that it genuinely becomes part of the bigger thing.
The process of including something as part of a whole, as in "the incorporation of new ideas." In law and business, it is the legal process of forming a company.

Incorporeal means having no physical body, no material substance, and no matter. Something incorporeal exists — but not as a thing made of flesh, bone, atoms, or any physical stuff you could ever touch, hold, see with your eyes, or weigh on a scale.
So set in their bad habits or ways that they cannot be changed or corrected, as in "an incorrigible liar." Often said affectionately, as in "an incorrigible flirt."
Impossible to corrupt — something or someone that cannot be spoiled, bribed, or made to go bad, no matter what.
"Incredibly" means to a degree that is very hard to believe — or to an extremely great degree.
Incredulity is the feeling — or state — of being unable or unwilling to believe that something is true, especially because it seems too surprising, shocking, outrageous, or strange to simply accept.
If you are incredulous, it means you find something so hard to believe that you simply cannot — or will not — accept it as true.
Incredulously means in a way that shows you cannot believe something — that you find it too strange, surprising, or absurd to accept as true.
An increment is one single step of increase — a measured amount by which something goes up. It is not the total you reach; it is the specific amount of the rise itself.
"Incremental" describes anything that happens or grows in small, gradual steps — one piece at a time, over a period of time — rather than all at once or in one big, dramatic leap.
Incrementalism is the idea that change happens — or should happen — through a long series of small, careful steps rather than in one big, sweeping move all at once.

To incriminate someone means to make that person appear guilty of a crime or wrongdoing. You do this by presenting evidence, making a statement, or doing something that directly links them to the crime.
Something is incriminating when it makes a person look guilty of a crime or wrongdoing — it points a finger at them.

Incrustation refers to a hard, solid layer or crust that has formed over the surface of something. Picture leaving a kettle unused for months in a place with hard water — a white, chalky, rigid coating slowly builds up on the inside walls.
To incubate something means to keep it in the right conditions, protected and undisturbed, so that it can slowly develop into something more complete.
Incubation refers to a period of quiet, hidden development — a time when something is growing, changing, or being carefully nurtured, even if you can't see much happening on the outside.

An incubus is something that presses down on you — physically, mentally, or spiritually — causing distress, dread, or suffering. That single idea of oppressive, crushing weight is the heart of this word, and it runs through all of its meanings.

To inculcate means to fix a belief, value, habit, or principle firmly into someone's mind — not by telling them just once, but by teaching it repeatedly and persistently over time, until it truly sinks in and becomes a part of how they think or behave.

Inculcation is the process of repeatedly and persistently teaching an idea, belief, value, or habit to someone until it becomes deeply fixed in their mind — so deeply fixed that it feels like a natural part of who they are.
To inculpate someone means to make them appear guilty of a crime or wrongdoing — by pointing blame at them, presenting evidence against them, or saying something that ties them to a fault.
The state of currently holding an official position, especially in politics, or the period during which it is held.
Currently holding an official position, as in "the incumbent president." Incumbent on someone means it is their duty or responsibility, as in "it is incumbent on us to help."
An incumbent is the person who currently holds an official position or office.

To incur something means to bring a negative consequence upon yourself as a direct result of something you did. Think of it this way: your action is the cause, and the bad outcome is the effect — and crucially, you are the one responsible for triggering it.

"Incurable" describes something that cannot be cured, healed, corrected, or made to go away — permanently. When something is incurable, no medicine, treatment, effort, or solution in existence can fix it completely.

Incurious means having no desire to learn, explore, or ask questions. A person who is incurious doesn't wonder about things. They don't dig deeper. They encounter something new or interesting and feel no pull to understand it better.
An incursion is when a person, group, or force enters a place where they are not welcome, not supposed to be, or have no right to be — especially doing so in a sudden, aggressive, or forceful way.
Indebted means owing something to someone — either money, or a sense of deep gratitude and obligation for help you received.

Indecency is the quality or state of being indecent — meaning behavior, appearance, language, or content that violates accepted standards of what is proper, modest, or morally acceptable in a society, especially in relation to the body, sex, or nudity.
Offending accepted standards of decency, especially by being sexually offensive or improper. It can also mean inappropriate or unacceptable, as in "indecent haste."

When something is indecipherable, it means it cannot be decoded, read, or understood — no matter how hard you try. The thing is right in front of you (you can see it, hear it, or observe it), but its meaning or content simply cannot be worked out.
Indecision is the state of not being able to make up your mind. It is the condition of being stuck — caught between two or more choices — without being able to commit to any one of them.
Indecisive describes someone — or sometimes something — that fails to reach a clear, firm conclusion or choice. Think of it as the inability to say "yes, this one" and stick with it.
Indecorous describes behavior, speech, dress, or manner that violates the unwritten rules of what is considered appropriate, dignified, or polite in a given situation.
"Indefatigable" is an adjective that describes a person, effort, or spirit that cannot be worn down by tiredness, difficulty, or repeated setbacks.

Something that is indefeasible is so firmly and permanently established that it cannot be cancelled, taken away, defeated, or made invalid — by anyone, under any circumstances, ever. It represents an absolute, unbreakable security against any challenge.

"Indefensible" means something is so wrong, so unreasonable, or so weak that no valid argument, excuse, or justification can rescue it. You simply cannot defend it. If you try, every attempt will fall apart.
Something is indefinable when it is real and noticeable, but no words can fully or precisely capture what it is.
Lasting for an unknown or unlimited time, as in "postponed indefinitely." It can also mean vague or unclear. In grammar, "a" and "an" are indefinite articles.
Indefinitely means for a period of time that has no fixed, stated, or known end.
Indelible means impossible to remove, erase, or forget. It describes something so permanent that no amount of effort, time, or force can wipe it away.
Indelicate means lacking the sensitivity, tact, or refinement that a social situation calls for — particularly in a way that causes discomfort, embarrassment, or a sense that a line has been crossed.

Indemnification is the act of protecting someone from financial loss or legal responsibility, or the compensation paid to someone who has already suffered a loss — with the goal of restoring them to exactly where they stood before.
To indemnify someone means to protect them from financial loss — either by preventing them from bearing that loss in the first place, or by paying them back after the loss has already happened.
Indemnity means protection from loss or harm, or compensation that makes up for a loss or harm that already happened.
To start a line of text further in from the margin than the others. In British English, to indent for something means to make an official order or request for it.

An indentation is a space, gap, notch, or hollow that goes inward — into a surface, an edge, or a line of text. It is the result of something being pushed in, cut into, or set back from the surrounding area.
An indenture is a serious, formal, legally binding written contract — but with a very specific character. It's not just any casual agreement.
Something is indescribable when it is so extreme, so powerful, or so overwhelming that no words — in any language — can fully capture or explain it.
Indestructible describes something that cannot be destroyed, broken, damaged, or ruined — no matter how much force, effort, or time is applied to it.
Something is indeterminable when it is impossible — or at least practically impossible — to figure out, measure, calculate, or settle with certainty.
Indeterminacy is the state or condition of being not determined — meaning not fixed, not settled, not pinned down to a single clear answer, outcome, or meaning.
Not clearly defined, not fixed, or impossible to pin down with precision.

An index is something that helps you find, measure, or point to something else. Think of it as a guide or a marker — it doesn't contain the full information itself, but it leads you to it or represents it in a simplified way.

The verb "to index" means to create or establish a connection between something and a reference point, so that the thing can be found, tracked, or adjusted using that reference. Think of an index as a bridge — "to index" means to build that bridge.
An Indian summer is a period of unusually warm, sunny, and dry weather that arrives in late autumn — after cold weather has already set in for the season.
Indicate means to point toward something — to make something known or clear, either by directly showing it or by being a sign of it.

An indication is a sign, signal, or piece of information that points you toward something — something that exists, is likely to happen, or should be done. Think of it as a pointer. It says, in effect: "look here" or "this is what's going on."
When something is indicative, it works like a clue or a signal — it points toward something and suggests it is likely true, without being an absolute, definitive proof.
An indicator is something that shows, points to, or signals the state, condition, or existence of something else — usually something you cannot see directly or measure easily on its own.

To indict someone means to formally and officially accuse them of a crime through a legal process. It is the legal system's way of saying: "We have enough evidence against this person to take them to trial."
Of a crime, serious enough to be formally charged and tried by a judge and jury. Of a person, liable to be charged with such a crime.

An indictment is a formal, official accusation that a specific person has committed a crime. It is a legal document — or the act of issuing that document — that says, in effect: "There is enough evidence against this person to put them on trial."

Indifference is the state of having no interest, concern, or feeling about something or someone. It means something simply does not matter to you — not in a good way, not in a bad way — just not at all.

When someone is indifferent to something, they simply do not care about it. Not positively, not negatively — just nothing. No interest, no emotion, no concern. A blank feeling, like a wall staring back at you.
Indigence means a state of extreme poverty — a condition in which a person seriously lacks the money and basic necessities needed to live with even a minimum level of dignity and comfort.

Indigeneity is the state or condition of being indigenous — of being the original, ancestral inhabitants of a particular land, with roots in that place that stretch back far before anyone else arrived.

Indigenous describes something — a person, a group of people, an animal, a plant, or even an idea — that originally comes from a particular place and has been there naturally, from the very beginning, without being brought in from somewhere else.

The adjective indigent describes someone who is extremely poor — so poor that they lack the very basics of life: food, shelter, clothing, and the money needed to meet their daily needs. It doesn't simply mean "not rich" or "struggling financially."
Difficult or impossible for the body to digest. Figuratively, too complex or dull to be easily understood or absorbed, as in "an indigestible report."

Indigestion is a noun that refers to the physical discomfort or pain you feel in your stomach — and sometimes in your chest — when your body is struggling to break down the food you have eaten properly.

When someone is indignant, they typically feel two things at once: anger and a sense of righteous self-belief — meaning they are firmly convinced they are in the right. An indignant person isn't confused or guilty. They're sure.
In a way that shows anger at being treated unfairly or disrespectfully, as in "'I did not!' she replied indignantly."

Indignation is a strong feeling of anger that arises specifically when something feels unfair, unjust, or morally wrong — especially when you or someone else has been treated in a way they don't deserve.
Treatment that makes a person feel humiliated, disrespected, or ashamed, as in "the indignity of being searched in public."
The word indigo as a noun carries two closely connected meanings — a color and a natural dye — and understanding both together gives you the full picture.

Indirection means achieving something by a roundabout route rather than going straight at it — whether in speech, action, or thought. There is always a middle step, a detour, between you and the destination. Something is not said, done, or reached head-on.

Something is indiscernible when it cannot be noticed, detected, or told apart — either because it is too faint and subtle for your senses or mind to pick up, or because it is so similar to something else that you cannot tell the two apart.
Indiscipline is the condition in which a person, group, or institution fails to maintain the expected standards of behavior, order, and self-control.
Careless about what you say or do, especially by revealing things that should be kept private or behaving in a way that causes embarrassment.
Careless behaviour or speech that reveals something private or causes embarrassment. An indiscretion is also a minor wrongdoing, especially a secret love affair.
When something is indiscriminate, it is done without care, thought, or selectivity — treating all things as if they are the same, with no attention paid to the important differences between them.
To do something indiscriminately means to do it without making any distinction between the people, things, or situations involved — without selecting, filtering, or evaluating.

If something is indispensable, it means you absolutely cannot do without it. It is so necessary, so critical to a situation, that removing it would either make things fall apart or make the task impossible.

The word indisposed carries two related meanings, both of which share a common thread: something is preventing a person from doing what they might otherwise do. That "something" is either a mild physical ailment, or a simple unwillingness.
Indisputable means something that is so clearly and completely true that no one can argue against it, question it, or deny it — not even someone who really wants to.
Impossible to break, end, or undo; permanent, as in "an indissoluble bond." It can also mean impossible to dissolve in a liquid.

Something that is indistinct is not clear, not easy to make out, or not easy to tell apart from its surroundings. You can sense it — you can see it, hear it, or feel it — but you cannot perceive it sharply or precisely.

When two or more things are indistinguishable, it means you cannot tell them apart. No matter how carefully you look, listen, taste, or examine them — they appear exactly the same. You find zero difference between them.
To indite something means to compose or write it — to put thoughts, feelings, or ideas into words and form them into a piece of writing or speech.

Individualism is the belief that the individual person is the most important unit in society — that your rights, your freedom, your choices, and your personal goals matter deeply and should be protected, often above the demands of any group, government, or collective.

An individualist is a person who believes that the individual human being — the single, separate person — is the most important unit in society, and who strongly values personal freedom, independent thinking, and self-reliance above conforming to group expectations, traditions, or authority.

Individualistic describes anything — a person, a behavior, a culture, a way of thinking — that places the individual at the center, above the group. It emphasizes personal freedom, personal choice, personal identity, and self-reliance.

Individuality is the quality of being distinctly and uniquely yourself — the total collection of traits, characteristics, preferences, values, quirks, and ways of thinking and behaving that make you you, and no one else.
To individuate something means to single it out as a unique, distinct individual — to separate it, in your mind or in reality, from the larger group or mass it belongs to.
Individuation means the process by which something becomes a distinct, separate individual — unique and whole in itself, clearly set apart from everything else around it.
Indivisible means something that cannot be divided, split, or separated — either into parts, or from something else it is deeply connected to.

To indoctrinate someone means to repeatedly teach them a fixed set of beliefs, ideas, or values in a way that makes them accept those beliefs without question — and without ever encouraging them to think critically, explore other viewpoints, or ask "but is this actually true?"
Indoctrination is the process of repeatedly teaching a person or group a fixed set of beliefs in a way that discourages questioning, doubt, or independent thinking.
Indolence means a deep, habitual laziness — a strong tendency to avoid effort, work, or activity, and to be perfectly comfortable doing so.
Indolent means habitually lazy — having a deep, settled dislike for work, effort, or activity. An indolent person is not someone who is just having a lazy Sunday or who is tired after a long week.
Indomitable means impossible to defeat, suppress, or discourage — no matter how hard anyone tries, or how difficult the situation becomes.
Indoors means inside a building. When you do something indoors, you are doing it within an enclosed structure that has walls and a roof — like a house, school, office, gym, restaurant, or mall.
Indubitable means so obviously true and certain that it cannot be doubted. Not "hard to doubt." Not "very likely true." But genuinely, completely, and absolutely beyond all reasonable doubt.
Indubitably means without any doubt at all — completely, certainly, and unquestionably.

Induce means to cause something to happen, or to cause someone to do something, usually through some kind of influence, pressure, or trigger — not by force, and not by accident, but through a deliberate or natural process that leads to a result.
An inducement is something offered to a person — from the outside — to make them willing to do something, or to tip their decision in a particular direction.
To induct means to formally bring someone into a group, position, or organization through an official process or ceremony.

An inductee is a person who has been formally and officially brought into a group, organization, position, or place of honor — typically through a special ceremony or structured process called an induction.
The process of formally introducing someone into a job or group. In logic, it means reasoning from specific examples to a general rule. In medicine, it means artificially starting labour.

Inductive means "moving from specific observations or examples toward a broader general conclusion or principle." Think of it as building upward — collecting individual pieces and assembling them into a bigger picture.
Inductive reasoning is the process of observing specific things and using those observations to draw a general conclusion.

To indulge means to allow yourself or someone else to enjoy something pleasurable — especially something you normally wouldn't, something considered a treat, or something that goes a little beyond what is strictly necessary.
To indulge in something means to allow yourself to enjoy a pleasure, often one that feels a little extra, a little luxurious, or one you don't normally let yourself have.
Indulgence means allowing yourself or someone else to enjoy something pleasurable — especially something that goes a little beyond what is strictly necessary, responsible, or moderate.
Allowing someone, or yourself, to have or do what they want, especially when this is not good for them, as in "indulgent parents." It can also mean generously lenient, as in "an indulgent smile."
Relating to industry — the large-scale manufacture of goods in factories, as in "an industrial area." It can also mean very large or intense, as in "industrial quantities."

Industrialism is a noun that describes a type of society and economy in which large-scale, machine-powered manufacturing becomes the central, defining force — shaping not just how goods are made, but how people live, work, organize their cities, divide into classes, and even think about the world.

An industrialist is a person who owns or controls a large industrial business — meaning a business that manufactures or produces things on a massive scale. Think of giant factories, steel mills, oil refineries, coal mines, automobile plants, or railways.
To industrialize means to transform a place, economy, or process from one based on simple, manual, or agricultural work into one driven by factories, machines, and large-scale manufacturing.
If someone is industrious, they are hardworking and consistently put strong, dedicated effort into whatever they do.
Industriousness is the quality of consistently working hard, staying focused, and putting in steady, purposeful effort — not just once in a while, but as a regular habit.
When you take all the companies, workers, products, and activities that are involved in the same type of economic work and group them together, that entire group is called an industry.

An inebriate is a person who is drunk — and more specifically, a person who is habitually or repeatedly drunk. Think of it as a formal, serious-sounding label for someone who drinks alcohol to excess so often that it defines them or their condition.

To inebriate someone means to make them drunk — to bring them to a state where alcohol (or occasionally another substance) has impaired their senses, judgment, and control over their own mind and body.
Inebriated means being in a state of drunkenness — when a person has consumed enough alcohol that it has visibly and significantly affected how they think, speak, and move.
Producing a powerful, intoxicating feeling of excitement or pleasure, as in "the inebriating scent of jasmine." Literally, causing drunkenness.

Inebriation is the state or condition of being drunk. It names what happens to a person's mind and body after they consume enough alcohol for it to noticeably affect how they think, speak, feel, and move.

Inebriety means the state or condition of being drunk — specifically, the condition a person is in when alcohol (or sometimes another intoxicating substance) has impaired their mind and body to the point where they can no longer think clearly, behave normally, or control themselves properly.
Inedible describes something that cannot or should not be eaten — either because it is physically harmful to consume, or because it is so unpleasant that eating it is practically impossible.
Ineffability is the quality of something being impossible — or nearly impossible — to express in words.
Ineffable means too great, too overwhelming, or too extraordinary to be captured or expressed in words.

If something is ineffaceable, it is impossible to erase, remove, or wipe away. It is so deeply embedded — in the mind, in history, in a person's heart — that no amount of time, effort, or will can make it disappear. It stays. Permanently.
Something is ineffective when it is supposed to do a job, but it fails to do that job. It tries, but it doesn't work — or at least, doesn't work well enough to count as success.
"Ineffectual" means failing to produce the desired result, or describing a person who lacks the ability or power to get things done.

Inefficacious means failing to produce the result it was supposed to produce. It describes something that was meant to work — designed, intended, or expected to achieve a goal — but simply doesn't deliver that outcome.
Inefficacy means the inability of something to produce the result it is supposed to produce.
Inelegance is the quality of being clumsy, awkward, unnecessarily complicated, or lacking in grace and refinement — whether in appearance, movement, language, thinking, design, or behavior.
Lacking grace, refinement, or style; awkward and clumsy, as in "an inelegant solution."

When someone or something is ineligible, it means they do not qualify — they cannot participate in something, receive something, or be chosen for something, because they fail to meet a required condition or rule.

Ineluctable means impossible to escape, resist, or struggle free from. When something is ineluctable, no effort, cleverness, or willpower can stop it. It is going to happen — or it is simply true — no matter what you do.
Inept means lacking the skill, ability, or good judgment to do something well — especially something you are expected or supposed to be able to handle.
Ineptitude means a lack of skill, competence, or ability — the state of being consistently bad at doing something, or doing it in a clumsy, ineffective, and often embarrassing way.
Inequality is a noun that describes the condition of not being equal — when two or more things, people, or groups differ in a way that matters: in size, amount, value, rights, power, or opportunity.
Inequitable means unfair or unjust — particularly in the way something is distributed, applied, or decided among people.
Inequity means unfairness or injustice — a situation where people are not treated fairly, or where something is distributed or decided in a way that is morally wrong.
Ineradicable means impossible to get rid of, remove, or wipe out completely — no matter how hard or how long you try.
Inerrancy means the state or quality of being completely free from errors — of being incapable of being wrong.
Inert describes something that has no power to act, move by itself, or cause a reaction. It just exists — quietly, passively, doing absolutely nothing and affecting nothing around it.
Inertia is the natural tendency of something to resist change — to keep doing what it is already doing, or to keep being what it already is, unless something forces it to be different.

Something is inescapable when it is completely impossible to avoid, ignore, or get away from — no matter what you do, how hard you try, or where you go. You are forced to face it, accept it, or experience it. There is no exit, no workaround, and no way out.

Inestimable describes something so great, so valuable, or so important that it simply cannot be measured, calculated, or estimated. The word is essentially saying: "This is beyond the reach of any measurement."
Inevitability means the state or quality of something being certain to happen — and impossible to avoid, stop, or escape, no matter what anyone does.
Something is inevitable when it is absolutely certain to happen and there is no way to stop it, avoid it, or escape it. It will happen — no matter what anyone does.
Inevitably means in a way that cannot be avoided, prevented, or escaped — no matter what anyone does.

Inexact means not perfectly accurate, not perfectly precise, or not completely correct in every detail. Something inexact is close to the truth, but it falls slightly short of being fully, perfectly right.
An inexactitude is a statement, claim, or piece of information that is not fully accurate, precise, or correct — something that misses the mark of truth, either a little or a lot.
Something is inexcusable when it is so wrong, so harmful, or so unacceptable that no reason, explanation, or excuse can make it okay.
Something is inexhaustible when it cannot be used up, no matter how much you draw from it. It keeps going. It keeps giving. You cannot drain it dry.

"Inexorable" describes something — or someone — that cannot be stopped, changed, or persuaded, no matter what. It is completely and absolutely unstoppable. More than that, it is also unmoved by any appeal.
"Inexorably" means in a way that cannot be stopped, slowed down, or changed — no matter what anyone does.

Something is inexpedient when it is not a wise or practical choice in a given situation — not because it is morally wrong or forbidden, but because it simply will not work out well, will cause problems, or will go against your own interests given the current circumstances.
Something is inexpensive when it does not cost a lot of money. Its price is low.
Inexpert means not having the skill, knowledge, or experience needed to do something well.
Something that is inexpiable is so terribly wrong — so deeply sinful or harmful — that it can never be fully atoned for, made right, or forgiven, no matter what is done to correct it.
Something is inexplicable when it cannot be explained — not just when it hasn't been explained yet, but when no satisfying explanation seems to exist, or when every attempt to explain it falls short.

When something happens inexplicably, it means it happened in a way that cannot be explained — no one knows why, and often, no matter how hard you try to figure it out, you simply cannot find a reason that makes sense.
Inexpressible describes something so powerful, deep, or overwhelming that words simply cannot capture it. No matter how hard you try, language fails you.
"Inexpressive" means not showing feelings, emotions, or thoughts outwardly — or showing very little of them.
Something inextinguishable is something that cannot be put out, stopped, destroyed, or ended — no matter what you do, no matter how hard you try.
"Inextricable" means impossible to separate, untangle, or escape from.
Inextricably means in a way that is impossible to separate, untangle, or escape from.
Infallibility is the quality of being absolutely incapable of making a mistake or being wrong.
Infallible means incapable of being wrong, making errors, or failing — ever.
Infamous means widely known for something bad, evil, or morally wrong.

Infamy is the state of being widely known for something evil, wicked, or deeply shameful. Think of it as the dark twin of fame. Fame means being well-known for something great. Infamy means being well-known for something terrible.

Infancy means the earliest, most undeveloped stage of something. That "something" can be a human life, or it can be anything else — a company, a technology, an idea, a movement. The word always points to a beginning that is fragile, new, and still growing.
An infant is a very young child, typically from the moment of birth up to about one year of age, though in some contexts the word stretches to include children up to two years old.
Infanticide means the deliberate killing of a very young child — almost always a newborn or a baby in the earliest months of life.
Childish and immature in a way that is inappropriate for an adult, as in "infantile behaviour." In medicine, it simply means relating to infants, as in "infantile reflexes."
Childish behaviour or characteristics that persist in an adult. In medicine, it is a condition in which an adult's physical or mental development remains like that of a child.

To infantilize someone means to treat them as if they are a child — even though they are not. It means you act toward them as if they are less intelligent, less capable, or less mature than they actually are.
Infantry refers to the soldiers of an army who fight primarily on foot, and also to the branch of an army to which those soldiers belong.

When you are infatuated with someone, you have an extremely intense, all-consuming feeling of attraction toward them — but one that is based more on how you imagine them to be, rather than who they truly are.
Infatuation is an intense, overwhelming feeling of attraction or passion toward someone — but one that is based more on imagination and fantasy than on truly knowing that person.
Infeasible means not able to be done or carried out in practice.

To infect means to enter something living and cause harm by spreading inside it. Think of it as an unwanted, harmful thing getting into a body — or anything else — and then doing damage from the inside out.

An infection is what happens when tiny, harmful living things — too small to see — enter your body, survive there, multiply, and cause harm. These tiny invaders are called pathogens (a word simply meaning "things that cause disease").
Infectious describes something that has the power or tendency to spread — from one person, place, or thing to another.
Infelicitous means poorly suited, inappropriate, or badly chosen for the occasion or context — especially when it comes to words, remarks, or expressions.
An awkward or inappropriate word, phrase, or remark, as in "the speech was full of infelicities." In older use, it means unhappiness or misfortune.
To infer means to reach a conclusion through reasoning, based on evidence, clues, or information you already have — rather than being told something directly.

An inference is a conclusion you reach through reasoning — not because someone told you directly, and not because you saw it happen, but because you looked at the available evidence and figured it out.

Relating to or based on inference — reaching a conclusion by reasoning from evidence rather than from direct observation. In statistics, inferential methods draw conclusions about a population from a sample.
Inferior means lower in quality, value, rank, or importance compared to something or someone else.
Inferiority is the noun that describes the state or condition of being lower, lesser, or worse than something or someone else — whether in quality, rank, ability, or value.
A deep, persistent feeling of being less capable or worthy than other people, which can lead to shyness or to overcompensating with arrogance or aggression.
The word infernal is rooted in the concept of hell — the place of fire, punishment, and evil that appears in many religions and mythologies.
An inferno is a massive, raging, out-of-control fire — one so large, so intense, and so destructive that it feels almost alive, as if it has a will of its own. It is not just a "big fire."

"Infertile" describes something or someone that is unable to produce new life or growth. The central idea is a missing or blocked ability to create something new — whether that is a baby, an animal's offspring, or a plant growing from the ground.

When something infests a place, it means a large number of harmful, unwanted, or troublesome creatures (or things) have moved into that place, spread all through it, and are now a serious problem there.

An infestation is when a large number of harmful, unwanted, or destructive creatures — such as insects, rodents, or parasites — are present in a place in numbers big enough to cause real damage, danger, or serious discomfort.
An infidel is a person who does not believe in a particular religion — specifically, the religion that the speaker or the labeler considers to be the one true faith.

Infidelity means unfaithfulness — the act or state of breaking a promise of loyalty, especially when that promise is deeply important and built on trust. The word carries real emotional weight. It is not a light word.

Infighting means conflict or struggle that happens inside a group — between the very members who belong to it — rather than against someone or something on the outside. The fight is not directed outward at an enemy or competitor.
To infiltrate something means to enter it secretly, gradually, and without being detected — usually to gain information, cause damage, or gain control from the inside.
Infiltration means the process of gradually and secretly entering or getting inside something — whether that "something" is a place, a group, an organization, a body, or even a material like soil.
Infinite means having no end, no limit, and no boundary — ever.
If you sat a monkey at a typewriter and let it randomly press keys forever, it would eventually type out the complete works of Shakespeare — word for word, perfectly.

An infinite regress happens when every answer you give to a question demands another question of the exact same kind — and that answer demands yet another — endlessly, with no stopping point, no foundation, no final resting place.
Something infinitesimal is so unimaginably, vanishingly tiny that it is almost — but critically, not quite — nothing at all.
The basic form of a verb, usually with "to" in front of it, as in "to eat" or "to run," not tied to any particular person or time.
Infinitude means the state, quality, or condition of being infinite — that is, the condition of having absolutely no end, no limit, and no boundary whatsoever.
Infinity means endlessness — a quantity, size, or extent that has no limit and cannot be exhausted, no matter how long you keep going.
Infirm describes a person who is physically weak and frail — someone whose body has lost its strength and ability to function well, usually because of old age or long-term illness.
An infirmary is a room or small medical facility where sick or injured people can go to receive basic medical care.

An infirmity is a weakness or ailment — a condition that makes a person physically or mentally less capable than they would normally be. Think of it as something that limits a person, something that holds them back or makes life harder to manage.
Inflame means to make something more intense — to heat it up, to make it stronger, more extreme, or more dangerous than it was before. Think of throwing fuel onto an existing fire.
Inflammable means easily capable of catching fire and burning. If something is inflammable, it means that it can ignite — often quickly and intensely — when exposed to a flame, spark, or enough heat.
Inflammation is your body's alarm system going off — and then your body's emergency crew rushing in to deal with the problem.

The word inflammatory describes something that inflames — that is, something that makes a situation, emotion, or physical condition worse, hotter, or more intense than it already is. Think of pouring fuel on a fire. That's the image at the heart of this word.
Inflate means to make something bigger by filling it with air or gas.
Inflated means made larger, greater, or more important than is natural, real, or justified. Something inflated has been puffed up — either literally with air, or figuratively with exaggeration.
A general rise in prices over time, which means each unit of money buys less than before. Literally, the act of filling something with air or gas, as in "tyre inflation."
"Inflationary" is simply the adjective form of "inflation." It describes anything that causes inflation, contributes to inflation, or characterizes a time when inflation is happening.

To inflect means to change or modify something — specifically, the form of a word or the sound of a voice — in order to express a different meaning or feeling. Think of it as bending something slightly from its base form without completely replacing it.
The rise and fall in the pitch or tone of someone's voice. In grammar, it is a change in the form of a word to show tense, number, or case, as in "walk" becoming "walked."
A moment when significant change happens, or a turning point, as in "an inflection point for the industry." In maths, it is the point where a curve changes the direction in which it bends.
Something inflexible does not bend, change, or adapt. It stays exactly as it is, no matter what.
To inflict means to cause something bad, painful, or harmful to be experienced by someone or something else.
Infliction is the act of causing something harmful, painful, or burdensome to fall upon someone else.

The word inflow is built from two simple parts: "in" (meaning into something) and "flow" (meaning a smooth, continuous movement). Put them together, and you get the core meaning: Inflow = the movement of something into a place, system, or container.
Influence is the power that a person, thing, or force has to shape or change how someone else thinks, feels, behaves, or develops — without directly commanding, forcing, or controlling them.
To influence something or someone means to have an effect on them — to cause a change in the way they think, feel, decide, or behave — without directly forcing them.
The corrupt practice of using your connections with people in power to get favours for someone else in exchange for money or other benefits.

When you describe someone or something as influential, you mean that they have the power to affect, shape, or change the way other people think, feel, behave, or make decisions — or to change the course of events in a significant way.

Influenza is a contagious disease that attacks your respiratory system — meaning your nose, throat, and lungs. It is caused by a family of viruses called influenza viruses. In everyday speech, people almost always call it "the flu."

An influx is the arrival of a large number of people, things, or a large amount of something — all flowing into a particular place or system, usually within a notable or relatively short period of time. Think of it almost like a river flowing into a lake.

An infomercial is a long television advertisement that is deliberately designed to look and feel like a regular TV program — such as a talk show, a cooking show, or a documentary — but whose real and only purpose is to sell you a product or service.
Inform means to pass knowledge into someone's mind — to make them aware of something they didn't know before. Think of it as filling a gap in someone's understanding.
When you "inform on" someone, you are going to a person in power — like the police, a teacher, a boss, or a government official — and giving them information that gets the other person into trouble.
Informal means relaxed, casual, and free from strict rules, official structure, or ceremony.
Informality is the quality, character, or state of being relaxed, casual, and free from strict rules, official ceremony, or rigid structure.

An informant is a person who gives information to someone else — usually to a person or organisation that has a specific reason to want or collect that information. The key idea is that an informant is a source. They know something, and they share it.
When you describe something as informative, you mean that it gives you useful, meaningful knowledge or understanding about a subject — knowledge that genuinely adds to what you already know.
"Informed" means having knowledge that is based on real facts, reliable sources, or actual experience — not guesses, assumptions, or ignorance.

Informed consent means that a person voluntarily agrees to something — a medical procedure, a research study, a legal action — after being given all the important information they need to make that decision wisely.

An informer is a person who secretly tells the authorities — such as the police, a government, or military officials — about the activities or wrongdoings of other people, usually people from their own group, community, or circle.

Infotainment is content or a system that blends information with entertainment — so that while you're being informed (taught facts, news, or knowledge), you're also being entertained at the same time.

Infra dig means beneath one's dignity. When something is described as infra dig, it means that thing is considered too low, too common, or too demeaning for a person of a certain status, class, or self-image to do or be associated with.

An infraction is the act of breaking a rule, law, or agreement. When someone does something they are not supposed to do — something that goes against an established rule — that act of breaking the rule is called an infraction.
Infrangible means impossible to break. But this word doesn't just mean "very hard to break" or "extremely strong."
Relating to infrastructure — the basic systems and structures a society needs to function, such as roads, power supplies, and water networks.

Infrastructure refers to the fundamental, underlying systems and structures that a society, organization, or any complex setup needs in order to function. Think of it as the hidden backbone — the essential groundwork that makes everything else possible.
Infrequent means not happening often. When something is infrequent, it does happen — but only sometimes, with noticeably long gaps of time between each occurrence.
To infringe means to cross a boundary that you are not supposed to cross — whether that boundary is a law, a rule, an agreement, or someone's rights.
To infringe on something means to cross a line that you are not allowed to cross — in a way that damages, limits, or takes away something that belongs to, or is protected for, someone else.

Infringement means the act of breaking or violating a rule, a law, or a right — especially one that belongs to someone else or exists to protect someone. Think of any boundary that has been set by law or agreement.
To infuriate someone means to make them extremely angry — so angry that they can barely stay calm or in control. It goes far beyond simply annoying or upsetting someone.

When someone is infuriated, they are extremely angry — not mildly upset, not just annoyed, but deeply and intensely furious. The feeling is sharp and overwhelming. It is anger at close to its highest point.

If something is infuriating, it causes a strong, intense feeling of anger — not just mild annoyance, but a deep, burning frustration that can feel hard to control. The word comes from "fury," which means extreme, fierce anger.

To infuse means to slowly and thoroughly fill something with something else — whether that's a flavor, a quality, a feeling, or a liquid substance — in a way that spreads throughout and becomes deeply part of it. It's not a quick, surface-level addition.
An infusion is what you get — or what happens — when one thing is gradually introduced into another, causing the second thing to absorb the qualities of the first.
Ingenious describes a person, idea, plan, device, or method that shows clever, original, creative thinking — especially when it solves a difficult problem in a surprisingly smart or elegant way.

An ingenue is a young woman (or a girl on the edge of womanhood) who is genuinely innocent, pure, naive, and inexperienced in the ways of the world — and who shows all of this openly, without any pretense or hidden agenda.
Ingenuity is the ability to think of clever, creative solutions to difficult problems — especially solutions that are surprisingly simple, unexpected, or brilliantly resourceful.

Ingenuous describes a person who is genuinely open, honest, and innocent — someone who has no hidden motives, no cunning, and no suspicion of others. They say exactly what they think. They trust easily. They haven't learned to be guarded or calculating.

Ingenuousness is the quality of being open, honest, and innocent — free from any deception, hidden motives, or cunning. A person who has ingenuousness says exactly what they think and feel, trusts people naturally, and doesn't play games or manipulate others.

To ingest something means to take it into the body — most often through the mouth, by swallowing. It is the formal, precise word for what happens when you eat food, drink water, take a pill, or accidentally swallow something you didn't mean to.
An inglenook is a cozy, sheltered seating area built into the wall beside or around a large, open fireplace.

Something is inglorious when it brings shame or dishonor instead of pride and respect — or when it passes through life completely unnoticed and unrecognized, without leaving any mark of greatness behind.

An ingot is a solid block of metal that has been melted down and poured into a mold to harden into a simple, convenient shape — usually a rectangle or a bar — so it can be stored, transported, or processed further.

To ingrain something means to fix a habit, belief, attitude, or way of thinking so deeply into a person's mind or character that it becomes a permanent part of who they are — almost impossible to remove or change.
When something is ingrained, it means it has become so deeply fixed into a person's mind, character, or way of life — or into a culture or society — that it is very hard to change or get rid of.

An ingrate is a person who receives kindness, help, generosity, or favors from others but shows no gratitude in return. They take what is given to them and act as though it was owed to them, or as though nothing was ever done for them at all.

To ingratiate yourself means to deliberately make someone like you or approve of you — usually through flattery, excessive helpfulness, charm, or pleasing behavior — often because you want to gain something from them, like power, money, a promotion, or social acceptance.

When you describe something — a person's behavior, smile, tone, or manner — as ingratiating, you mean that it is clearly, and often too obviously, designed to make someone feel pleased, flattered, or charmed, so that the person doing it can gain favor, approval, or advantage in return.

Ingratiation is the act of deliberately trying to make yourself liked or favored by someone — usually someone who has power, influence, or something you want. In the simplest terms, it is the calculated effort to get into someone's good books.
Ingratitude is the failure to feel or show thankfulness toward someone who has done something kind, helpful, or generous for you.
An ingredient is any individual item that you combine with other items to create something new.
Ingress means the act of entering, the right to enter, or the point through which entry is made. Think of it as a formal, precise way of describing anything related to "going in" or "coming in."

To inhabit a place means to live in it, exist in it, or make it your home on a regular, ongoing basis. It is not about a quick visit or passing through — it means that a place is where someone or something genuinely is, consistently and over time.

An inhabitant is a living being — most often a person, but sometimes an animal or any other creature — who lives in a particular place on a settled, regular basis. That place could be a city, a country, a region, an island, a planet, or any defined area.
Inhalation is the act or process of breathing air — or any gas, vapor, fume, smoke, or fine mist — into your lungs, through your nose or mouth.
To inhale means to breathe air — or any other substance — into your lungs.
Inharmonious means not fitting together well — creating a sense of clash, conflict, or unpleasantness when two or more things are combined or placed alongside each other.
To exist as a permanent, essential, and natural part of something — not added from outside, but built into the very nature of the thing itself.

When a quality is inherent in something, it means that quality is a natural, permanent, built-in part of that thing's very nature. It is not added from the outside. It is not temporary. It is not caused by special circumstances.
As a natural, permanent, and inseparable part of something's core nature.
To inherit something means to receive it from someone who came before you — without having to buy it, earn it through your own effort, or actively seek it out.

Inheritance means something passed down from one person (or thing) to another, usually across generations or time. The thing being passed down can be physical, like money or a house, or intangible, like a personality trait or a cultural tradition.

An inheritor is a person who receives something that was previously owned, held, or possessed by someone else — usually passed down from a person who has died, from a previous generation, or from a source that came before them.

To inhibit something means to hold it back, slow it down, or restrain it from happening freely or fully. Think of it as putting a brake on something — not always stopping it completely, but limiting it, suppressing it, or making it harder for it to happen.
"Inhibited" describes a person who is held back from expressing themselves freely and naturally — not by an outside force, but by something inside them.

Inhibition means the act of holding something back, suppressing it, or preventing it from happening freely. Think of it as an internal brake — something that slows down, blocks, or restricts an action, feeling, process, or reaction.
Of a place, harsh and difficult to live in or survive in, as in "an inhospitable desert." Of a person, unfriendly and unwelcoming to guests.
Extremely cruel and lacking in compassion, as in "inhuman conditions." It can also mean not human, or not having human qualities.
