Languidly means doing something slowly, with little energy, and without any sense of urgency — in a way that feels relaxed, soft, and almost effortless.

To languish means to exist in a prolonged state of weakness, suffering, or neglect — with little or no improvement, and often with no clear way out. It is never a sudden event. It is always slow, drawn-out, and ongoing.

Languor is a state of gentle, dreamy weakness — a heavy, slow tiredness of the body or mind that feels more like drifting than suffering. The key thing that separates languor from ordinary tiredness is that it often carries a sweet, almost pleasant quality.
Languorous means pleasantly slow, dreamy, and relaxed — in a way that feels almost delicious rather than dull or frustrating.

Lank hair is straight, flat, and lifeless — it just hangs down without any volume, curl, or energy. Think of hair that lies completely flat against the head, perhaps slightly greasy or thin, with no bounce or movement to it.
"Lanky" describes a person who is tall and thin, but in an ungainly, loose-limbed way.
A lanyard is a strap or cord that you wear around your neck (or sometimes your wrist) to hold or carry a small object.
When you sit down, your upper legs (thighs) become roughly flat and horizontal, creating a natural upward-facing surface. That surface is your lap.
A lapdog is a small, domestic pet dog — one that is tiny enough to sit comfortably on a person's lap. These dogs are typically kept purely for companionship. They don't guard homes or herd sheep.
A lapel is the folded-back flap of fabric on the front of a jacket or coat, on either side of your chest.
Of language, elegant, concise, and precise, as if engraved in stone, as in "lapidary prose." Literally, relating to the cutting and polishing of precious stones.

A brief failure of concentration, memory, or judgement, as in "a lapse in concentration." It also means a period of time passing, as in "after a lapse of five years," or the ending of a right or agreement because it was not renewed.
To gradually pass into a different, usually worse, state, as in "lapse into silence." Of a right, policy, or agreement, to end because it was not renewed. Of time, to pass.

Larcenous means of, relating to, characterized by, or involving theft. It is the adjective form of the noun larceny, which is the legal term for the deliberate, wrongful taking of someone else's property with the intention of keeping it permanently.

Larceny is a legal word for theft. More precisely, it means the act of unlawfully taking someone else's personal property, without their permission, with the intention of keeping it away from them permanently.

Lard is a type of fat used in cooking, and it comes specifically from pigs. More precisely, it is the fat that has been extracted and purified from a pig's body. It is not the meat of the pig — it is purely the fat.

A larder is a cool, dedicated space — either a room or a cupboard — used for storing food. Think of it as a food storage area, specifically one that is kept cold or at least cool, designed to keep food fresh before it is cooked or eaten.
Largesse means generous, open-handed giving — especially of money, gifts, or privileges. But it's not just any kind of giving.

A lariat is a long rope with a sliding loop at one end. That loop is the defining feature — when the rope is pulled, the loop tightens around whatever it has caught. This makes it perfect for one job: catching animals, particularly cattle and horses.
Something done for fun or as a joke, as in "they did it for a lark." A lark is also a small brown songbird that sings while flying high in the sky.
To lark about (also said as "lark around") means to behave in a silly, playful, and carefree way — fooling around, joking, doing fun or mischievous things without any serious purpose.
A baked Italian dish of flat pasta sheets layered with meat or vegetables, tomato sauce, and cheese. It is also the name for the wide, flat pasta sheets themselves.
Lasagne has two closely connected meanings: it refers both to a specific type of pasta (the flat noodle itself) and to the famous baked dish made using that pasta.
Lascivious means showing or expressing strong sexual desire in a way that is open, shameless, or inappropriate. It is almost always a negative, judgmental word — not a neutral description.
Almost every sense of "lash" carries the idea of something sudden, sharp, and forceful — a quick, hard strike; a violent beating; a sudden snap.
To lash out means to suddenly attack someone — either physically or with words — usually because you are angry, frustrated, scared, or in pain.

Lassitude means a state of deep, heavy weariness — a draining of both your physical energy and your mental drive — that leaves you feeling sluggish, listless, and utterly reluctant to do anything at all.
A lasso is a long rope with a large, adjustable loop at one end. The loop is designed to tighten when pulled — so when you throw it over something and tug, it grips and holds.
A "last resort" is something you do — or use — only when every other option has failed or is unavailable. It is your final choice, the one you turn to when nothing else works.
"The last straw" means the final small problem that causes someone to lose patience or reach their breaking point — after they have already been tolerating many problems before it.

A latch is a simple mechanical device that holds a door, gate, window, lid, or similar object in a closed position. Think of it as a "holder" — its one job is to keep something shut until a person deliberately opens it.
To latch on to something means to seize on it or cling to it eagerly, as in "the press latched on to the story." It can also mean to fasten a door or gate with a latch.
"To latch onto" means to grab hold of something — physically, mentally, or emotionally — and not let it go.
Lately means in the recent period of time leading up to now.
Latency is the delay between when something is triggered and when the result actually shows up. It is the invisible waiting time baked into a process — the gap between a cause and its effect.
Latent describes something that genuinely exists but is hidden, dormant, or not yet visible — and has the potential to come out or become active under the right conditions.
Hidden aggressive feelings or impulses that are present beneath the surface but are not openly expressed.

Lateral means of, at, toward, or from the side. That single idea is the beating heart of the word. If something is lateral, it has to do with the side — not the front, not the back, not the top, not the bottom — specifically the side.
A lathe is a machine that shapes solid material — like wood or metal — by spinning it rapidly and pressing a sharp cutting tool against it.
To understand "lather" as a verb, you first need to picture what lather is: the thick, white, creamy foam that forms when you rub soap or shampoo with water.
Latitude always refers to a measurable range of space or freedom in one direction — either physically on Earth (or in the sky), or figuratively in how freely a person can act.
A latke is a small, flat, pan-fried pancake — most commonly made from grated potatoes. Think of it as a crispy potato patty, golden-brown on the outside and soft on the inside. The plural is latkes.
When you mention two things in a sentence, and then want to refer back to the second one, you use "the latter."

Latterly means in the more recent period of time — either the recent past in general, or the later part of a specific stretch of time. It is a formal adverb, used mostly in writing, and is more common in British English than American English.
A lattice is a framework made of strips, bars, or lines that cross over each other at regular intervals, forming a repeating pattern with gaps or openings between the crossings.

To laud someone or something means to praise them highly, enthusiastically, and openly. It goes well beyond a casual "good job." When you laud something, you are expressing strong admiration — the kind that feels significant, heartfelt, and often public.
Laudable means deserving to be praised. When you call something laudable, you are saying it is worthy of admiration and approval — that it is the kind of thing people should recognize and applaud.
Laudatory means expressing praise or strong admiration for someone or something.
When someone or something is described as lauded, it means they have received a great deal of enthusiastic, public praise — often from many people, or from respected and influential voices.

A laughingstock is a person (or sometimes a thing) that everyone laughs at, mocks, or ridicules — usually because they have done something embarrassing, foolish, or have some quality that others find deeply amusing or pathetic.

The verb to launder means to clean something — but not just physically. It carries a deeper sense: making something look acceptable, respectable, or legitimate when it originally wasn't. This idea runs through both its literal and figurative uses.
A laundromat is a business — open to any member of the public — that contains rows of washing machines and dryers that customers pay to use themselves.
A laureate is a person who has been officially and formally honored for outstanding achievement — usually by a prestigious institution, government, or organization.
Lava is molten rock — rock so incredibly hot that it has melted into a thick, flowing liquid — that has erupted from a volcano and reached the Earth's surface.
To lave means to wash or bathe something — typically with water, and typically in a gentle, careful, flowing way.
A small plant with narrow leaves and sweet-smelling purple flowers, used in perfumes and oils. It is also the pale purple colour of these flowers.

Lavish means more than enough — and done with richness, generosity, or luxury. Whenever you see or use the word "lavish," it is pointing at something that goes beyond the ordinary or the necessary, usually in an impressive or extravagant way.

To lavish something on someone means to give it generously, in very large amounts, and often without holding back. When you lavish something on a person, you are not giving just a little — you are pouring it on them abundantly, even excessively.

A lawn is a flat stretch of ground that is covered with grass and is kept short and neat by regularly cutting it. Think of the green, carpet-like patch of grass you often see in front of or behind a house. That is a lawn.
Lax means not strict, not careful, or not tight enough — especially when strictness or care is required.

Laxity means the state of being too loose, too slack, or not strict/careful enough. Think of a rubber band that has been stretched out so many times that it no longer snaps back tightly — it has lost its tension.
The adjective "lay" means not belonging to a profession or a specialized group — especially not having formal, expert, or official training in a particular field.
Lay means to put or place something down, usually with care or purpose.
When someone "lays down the law," they are telling other people very firmly and clearly what the rules are, what is and is not acceptable, and what will happen if those rules are broken.
To "lay it on thick" means to exaggerate something — especially praise, flattery, or emotion — far beyond what is natural or true.
The current situation or state of affairs, as in "get the lay of the land before deciding." Literally, the shape and features of an area of land.
A layer is a single, relatively flat sheet or thickness of something that lies on top of, or beneath, another sheet or thickness of the same or a different material. It is one level in a stack.
A layman is a person who is not an expert or specialist in a particular field. Think of it as the opposite of a professional or trained specialist.
To laze means to spend time relaxing in a slow, effortless, and pleasantly idle way — deliberately doing nothing much, or very little, and enjoying it.

To laze about means to spend time in a relaxed, idle way — doing nothing useful or productive, just resting or lounging around without any real purpose. The person is not busy, not working, and not making much effort at all.
To leach means for a liquid to pass through a solid material and, in doing so, dissolve and carry away substances from that material — draining them away gradually.
Lead someone up the garden path

To lead someone up the garden path means to deliberately deceive or mislead someone, usually by giving them false hope, false promises, or incorrect information — causing them to believe something that is not true.
Dull, heavy, and slow, as in "leaden prose" or "leaden steps." It can also mean dull grey, as in "a leaden sky," or literally made of lead.

A leaflet is a small, lightweight sheet of paper — sometimes folded — printed with information, and meant to be given out to many people. It is typically free, easy to carry, and designed to communicate one clear message quickly.
A leafstalk is the small, slender stalk that connects a leaf to the stem or branch of a plant. Think of it as the "bridge" between the leaf and the rest of the plant's body.

A league is a group of people, teams, organizations, or countries that have formally come together — usually by agreement — to work toward a shared goal, protect shared interests, or compete under shared rules.

Thin and fit, with little fat, as in "a lean athlete." Of meat, containing little fat. Of an organization, efficient with no waste. Of a period, difficult because there is little money or success, as in "lean years."
When something or someone leans, it means they are not perfectly upright or straight — they tilt, slope, or rest their weight in a particular direction. Everything else grows from this core idea.
A leap is a jump — but not just any jump. It is a big, powerful, and deliberate jump.
To leap means to push yourself off the ground — or any surface — with force and travel through the air, usually covering a meaningful distance or height in a single movement.

When "learned" is used as an adjective, it means having a deep, rich store of knowledge that was built up through serious, dedicated study over a long period of time. It is not just about going to school or knowing some facts.

Learning means the process by which a person (or any living being) acquires something new — new knowledge, new skills, new understanding, new habits, or new ways of thinking or behaving — that they did not fully have before.
A leash is a long, narrow strap, cord, or chain that connects an animal — most often a dog — to a person, so the person can control where the animal goes.

When someone says they will "leave no stone unturned," it means they will try every single possible method, explore every option, and use every available resource to achieve a goal or find something — until nothing is left unexplored.
To not include someone or something, as in "she left out the most important detail." It can also mean to leave something out of its usual place, or to exclude someone socially.

A leave-taking is the act of saying goodbye — but not just any goodbye. It is a deliberate, conscious farewell, the moment when someone formally parts from another person, a place, or a stage of life.

Leaven is any substance that makes dough rise — that is, any ingredient you add to a mixture of flour and water (dough or batter) that causes it to puff up, become lighter, and grow in volume before or during baking.

To leaven something means to add an element that gradually works its way through a larger whole and transforms it — typically making it lighter, more interesting, more alive, or more enjoyable than it would have been on its own.

Lecherous is an adjective used to describe a person — or a person's behavior, expression, or gaze — that is driven by an excessive, shameless, and often predatory desire for sexual pleasure. It goes far beyond simply finding someone attractive.
Lechery means excessive, shameless, and uncontrolled sexual desire or behavior — especially when it is habitual, offensive, and widely considered immoral.

A lectern is a tall, freestanding stand with a slanted top surface, built to hold books, notes, or papers at a comfortable height for someone who is standing and speaking or reading aloud to an audience.
A lecture is a formal, prepared talk given by one person — usually someone with knowledge or expertise — to an audience who is there primarily to listen and learn.

A lede is the opening sentence or paragraph of a news article or any piece of writing. Its entire job is to deliver the most critical information — the heart of the story — right at the very beginning, before the reader has gone anywhere else.

A ledger is a book — or today, a digital file or software — in which financial transactions are recorded in a permanent, organized, and systematic way. It is the central record-keeping tool in accounting and finance.
A person who clings to others and takes advantage of them, especially for money. Literally, a blood-sucking worm that lives in water.
To leech means to continuously take something valuable from a person or thing — without giving anything back in return.

A leer is a specific kind of look — a slow, unpleasant stare directed at someone, usually with the eyes slightly narrowed, often accompanied by a smug or twisted expression on the face. It is not a quick, innocent glance.
To leer at someone means to look at them in a way that is unpleasant, inappropriate, and makes them feel uncomfortable or unsafe. It is not a quick, innocent glance.
Leery means cautious and suspicious at the same time — specifically because something feels off about a person, situation, or thing, even if you can't fully prove why.
Leeward means on the side that is sheltered from the wind — or more simply, facing away from the wind.
Towards the side that is sheltered from the wind; in the direction the wind is blowing.
Leeway means freedom to act, move, or decide within certain limits — essentially, extra room that you have before you cross a boundary or break a rule.
Leftovers are the portions of something — most often food — that remain unused or unconsumed after the main activity is over.
A legacy is something that comes from the past and continues to exist, matter, or have an effect in the present — and often long into the future.
Legalese is the special style of language used in legal documents — things like contracts, laws, court rulings, terms and conditions, and official legal notices.
Legalism is the attitude or belief that following rules and laws strictly and literally — without exception, without flexibility, without asking why — is the most important thing.
Legality means the state or quality of being allowed, permitted, or valid according to the law.
A legate is an official representative — a person sent by a figure of great authority (like a ruler, a government, or the Pope) to act on their behalf somewhere else.
When something is described as legato, it means smooth, connected, and unbroken — with no gaps or interruptions between one moment and the next.

The most foundational meaning of "legend" is a story from the past that has been passed down through generations — usually about a real or semi-real person, place, or event — that is widely believed but cannot be fully proven as historical fact.
"Legendary" comes from the word legend — a story, usually about an extraordinary person or event, that gets passed down through generations and becomes larger than life in the telling.
Legerdemain means skillful trickery or deception — the kind that is so clever and so smoothly executed that the person being fooled doesn't even realize it's happening.
Legible means clear enough to be read.

A legion means a vast, overwhelming multitude — a number so large it feels almost too big to count. Think of it as a word that captures not just "many," but staggeringly, impressively many. It carries a sense of organized power within that enormous number.
To legislate means to make or pass a law — or a set of laws — through an official, formal process.

Legislation means written law — a formal, official rule that a government creates and enforces for the people living under it. Think of it as society's rulebook, written down and made official by people who have the authority to do so.
A legislator is a person who is officially empowered to create, change, or remove laws on behalf of a group of people — typically the citizens of a country, a state, or a region.
A legislature is the official group of people within a government whose primary job is to make, change, and repeal (cancel) laws for a country, state, or region.
Legitimacy is the quality of being recognized as rightful, valid, and acceptable — by people, by law, by society, or by established rules and standards.
Allowed by law or rules, as in "a legitimate business." It can also mean reasonable and justifiable, as in "a legitimate concern," or, of a child, born to married parents.
To legitimise something means to make it accepted, valid, justified, or recognized as proper — either by law, by authority, or by society.
A lei is a garland — a loop or string of flowers, leaves, or other natural materials — worn around the neck like a necklace.
When something is leisurely, it is done slowly, calmly, and without any rush — because there is plenty of time and absolutely no pressure to hurry.
When you do something leisurely, you do it slowly, calmly, and without any rush — as if you have all the time in the world and nothing is pressuring you to hurry.

A leitmotif is a recurring element — a melody, phrase, image, or idea — that keeps reappearing throughout a work of art, and that is consistently linked to a specific character, emotion, place, or concept.

Lemonade is a cold drink made by mixing lemon juice, water, and sugar together. The sourness of the lemon and the sweetness of the sugar balance each other out, making it a refreshing drink, especially in hot weather.
To lend something means to give it to someone temporarily, expecting that they will give it back to you later.
Lengthy means long — but not just ordinarily long. It means longer than what feels comfortable, convenient, or necessary.

Leniency means being gentler or less strict than you could be — especially when someone has made a mistake or broken a rule, and you have the power to punish them but choose to go easy on them instead.
Lenient describes someone — or something — that is not strict or harsh when dealing with mistakes, misbehavior, or rule-breaking.
Lenity means the quality of being gentle, mild, and merciful, especially when someone in power deliberately chooses not to be harsh, even when they could be.

When you call something leonine, you are saying it resembles a lion, or that it has the qualities strongly associated with a lion — power, majesty, strength, courage, and a commanding, almost regal presence.
A leper is a person who has leprosy — a serious, long-lasting bacterial disease that attacks the skin, nerves, and sometimes the eyes and nose.
Leprosy is a serious, long-lasting infectious disease caused by a very slow-growing type of bacteria called Mycobacterium leprae.
A lesion is any area of tissue or organ in your body that has been damaged, changed, or made abnormal — whether by injury, disease, infection, or any other harmful process.
A lessee is the person (or company) who rents something from someone else under a formal agreement called a lease.
To lessen something means to make it smaller in degree, strength, or intensity — not in physical size, but in how much or how strongly something is felt, experienced, or exists.

When you are stuck choosing between two bad options, and you pick the one that is less bad — the one that will cause less harm, less trouble, or less suffering — you are choosing "the lesser of two evils."

A lessor is a person or organization that owns something — a property, a vehicle, a piece of equipment, or any other asset — and allows someone else to use it for a defined period of time, in exchange for regular payments.
"Lest" means "so that something bad does not happen" — or, put another way, "for fear that" or "in order to prevent."
"Let on" means to reveal or disclose something that was hidden, secret, or not obvious — especially something you know, feel, or think, but are choosing to keep to yourself.
To become less intense or severe, as in "the rain let up." It can also mean to stop pressing hard on someone, as in "the coach never let up on them."
If something is lethal, it causes death, or it is capable of causing death. That is its sharp, central meaning — nothing more, nothing less.
Lethargic describes a state of being unusually slow, heavy, and lacking the energy or desire to do anything at all — physically and mentally. A lethargic person doesn't just feel tired.

Lethargy means a state of having very low energy, extreme tiredness, and a deep reluctance — or even an inability — to do anything. When someone is in a state of lethargy, both their body and their mind feel slow, heavy, and unresponsive.
A letup is a pause, a slowing down, or a reduction in the force or intensity of something that has been going on continuously — especially something demanding, relentless, or overwhelming.

Leukemia is a type of cancer of the blood and bone marrow, in which the body produces a large number of abnormal, non-functioning white blood cells that gradually crowd out and replace the healthy blood cells your body needs to survive.
A levee is a long, raised bank or wall built along the side of a river, lake, or other body of water to stop the water from spilling over onto the surrounding land.
Levelheaded describes a person who stays calm, thinks clearly, and makes sensible decisions — especially when the situation around them is stressful, difficult, or emotionally charged.
A lever is a rigid bar or rod that pivots around a fixed point to help you move or lift something heavy with far less effort than you'd need without it.
Leverage is the ability to get a bigger result than your raw effort alone would produce — by using something to multiply your power.
To leverage something means to use a resource, advantage, or strength you already have — in a smart, strategic way — to achieve a bigger or better result than you could have achieved without it.

A leviathan is something so enormous, so powerful, and so overwhelming that it feels almost impossible to challenge or control. Think of the biggest, most unstoppable thing you can imagine — a leviathan is that thing.
To levitate means to rise, float, or hover in the air — or to cause something or someone to do so — in a way that defies gravity and seems to have no physical explanation or support.
Levitation is the act or phenomenon of a person, animal, or object rising and floating in the air — with no visible support holding it up, and apparently defying the force of gravity.

Levity means lightness in attitude or behavior — specifically, treating something with humor, playfulness, or a lack of seriousness, especially at a time or in a situation where seriousness would normally be expected.

A levy is an official, mandatory charge or payment that an authority — almost always a government or legal body — forces people or organizations to pay. The single most important thing to understand about a levy is that it is not optional.

To levy something means to officially impose it and enforce its collection by authority. Think of it as a powerful, formal act — one that only those with recognized authority (like a government, court, or institution) can perform.
Lewd means sexually crude, vulgar, or explicit in a way that is inappropriate, offensive, or indecent.
A lexeme is the abstract, core unit of meaning in a language — the single concept that exists beneath all its surface forms.
Lexical means "relating to words" — specifically, the individual words that make up a language.
A lexicographer is a person whose job is to write, compile, or edit dictionaries.
Lexicography is the art, craft, and discipline of writing and compiling dictionaries.

Lexicology is a branch of linguistics — the scientific study of language — that focuses specifically on words: what they mean, how they are structured, how they relate to each other, and how they function as part of the total vocabulary of a language.
A lexicon is a collection of words — but whose words, and which words, depends on the context. Think of it as an inventory or a treasure chest of words belonging to something or someone.
LGBTQ+ is an acronym — a word made from the first letters of several other words.
"LGBTQI" is an acronym — a word made from the first letters of other words.
LGBTQIA is an acronym — a word formed from the first letters of other words.
Liability means responsibility for something — especially when that responsibility comes with a cost, a risk, or a legal obligation.
Legally responsible for something, especially for paying for damage or loss, as in "liable for the costs." Liable to do something means likely to do it, as in "liable to break."
To liaise means to communicate, cooperate, and share information with someone — especially as the connecting link between two separate groups, teams, or organisations.
When two separate organizations, departments, or groups need to work together, they establish a liaison — meaning a working connection, a line of communication, a coordinated relationship.

A libation is a drink — most often an alcoholic one — that is deliberately poured out as an offering. Not drunk. Poured out. The purpose is to honor something or someone: a god, a spirit, an ancestor, or the memory of a person who has died.
Libel is a false statement of fact, written or published in a permanent form, that damages someone's reputation.
To libel someone means to publish a false statement about them, in written or some other permanent form, that damages their reputation.

Libelous is an adjective used to describe a statement, piece of writing, image, or publication that unfairly and falsely harms someone's reputation — and does so in a way that could expose the person who made it to legal consequences.
Open to new ideas and respectful of other people's opinions and freedoms. In politics, favouring individual rights and social reform. It can also mean generous, or not strictly literal.

A liberal is a person whose political and social beliefs place strong importance on individual freedom, equality, and the idea that society should continuously improve to become fairer for all people.
Liberalism is a belief system — a set of ideas about how society should be organized — built on one foundational value: individual freedom.
To liberalize something means to make it less strict, less controlled, and more open or free. It is always about loosening or relaxing rules, restrictions, or limitations that existed before.
To liberate something or someone means to set them free — specifically from something that was holding them back, controlling them, oppressing them, or trapping them.
Liberation means the act or process of being set free from something that was restricting you, controlling you, or causing you suffering — and arriving at a state of freedom as a result.

A libertarian is a person who believes that individual freedom is the most important value in politics and society, and that the government should be as small and limited as possible to protect that freedom.

When you describe someone or something as libertine, you are saying that the person has deliberately thrown away conventional moral rules — especially those related to sex and personal conduct — and lives purely according to their own desires and pleasures.
A libertine is a person who pursues pleasure — especially sexual pleasure — freely and without feeling bound by moral rules, religious teachings, or social expectations.

Liberty means the freedom to live, think, speak, and act without being unfairly controlled or restricted by others — especially by a government, a ruler, or any powerful force that has the ability to control you.
Libidinous means having very strong, often excessive, sexual desire — and showing it in your behavior, thoughts, or attitude.

Libido means sexual desire — the internal urge, drive, or appetite that a person feels toward sexual activity or intimacy. Think of it as the mental and emotional "hunger" for sex, similar to how hunger is your body's drive to eat food.
A libretto is the complete written text of an opera or a similar large-scale musical vocal work. It contains all the words that are sung — and sometimes spoken — by the performers on stage.
A license is official permission to do something that you are not automatically allowed to do.
Licensing is the process of granting or receiving official permission to do something, use something, or operate something — under a specific set of agreed conditions.
Licentious means having no moral restraint, especially when it comes to sexual behavior or pleasure.
Licentiousness means behavior that is morally unrestrained, especially in a sexual way, with total disregard for rules, decency, or the rights of others.
A lichen is not a single living thing. It is two (sometimes three) completely different organisms living together so intimately that they look and function as one.
Something is licit if it is permitted — allowed by law, rules, or accepted standards. If an action or thing falls within what is officially or morally authorized, it is licit.
When someone is licking their wounds, it means they are taking time to recover — emotionally, mentally, or physically — after a painful defeat, failure, embarrassment, or setback.
A lickspittle is a person who is deeply, embarrassingly eager to please someone powerful — so eager that they lose all dignity doing it.

Licorice is a plant — and also the name given to several things that come from that plant: its root, the extract made from that root, and the candy flavored with it. Think of the word as having a few connected meanings that all trace back to the same plant.
In the feudal system, a lord or ruler to whom loyalty and service are owed, as in "my liege." It can also mean a vassal or subject who owes such loyalty.
A lien is a legal right that one person or organization holds over someone else's property, as security for a debt or obligation that hasn't been paid yet.
"Lieu" means place or stead — as in, the position something occupies. Think of it as a slot that something fills.
A lieutenant is someone who officially acts in place of, or directly assists, a person of higher authority.
A life cycle is the complete sequence of stages that something goes through from its beginning to its end — and often, back to a new beginning again.

"Life-deprived" is an adjective that describes something — or someone — that has been stripped of life, or that completely lacks any trace of life. It signals a total absence of the living quality, energy, or vitality that life brings.
Lifeless means without life — or more broadly, lacking the qualities that we associate with being alive: movement, energy, warmth, spirit, and responsiveness.
Lifelike means: so closely resembling something real — especially a living person, animal, or a scene from real life — that it could almost be mistaken for the actual thing.
A ligament is a tough but slightly flexible band of tissue inside your body that connects one bone to another bone at a joint.

A ligature is something that ties, binds, or joins. This single idea — connection through binding — runs through every use of the word, whether you encounter it in a hospital, a book, or a music class.

"Light up" means: something dark, dull, or inactive suddenly becomes bright, alive, or filled with energy. That single idea — a sudden shift from dim to bright, from flat to alive — is the thread running through every meaning of this phrase.
Lightweight means not heavy — weighing less than what is normal or expected for its kind.
Ligneous means of, like, or resembling wood — or having the qualities that wood typically has.
Like a deer in the headlight

When someone is described as being "like a deer in the headlights," it means they are suddenly frozen with shock, fear, or confusion — unable to think, speak, or act, even when they urgently need to respond.

"Like a shot" means very quickly or immediately, without any hesitation. When someone does something like a shot, they do it instantly — either because they are moving fast, or because they are so willing and eager that they don't pause even for a second.

Likelihood means the chance or probability that something will happen, or that something is true. It describes how likely — how probable — an event, outcome, or situation is, based on what we know or what we can reasonably expect.
To liken something means to compare it to something else in order to point out that the two things are similar.
Likeness is about looking like something or someone.
In the same way; similarly, as in "she bowed, and he did likewise." In conversation, it means "the same to you," as in "Nice to meet you." — "Likewise."
When you call something lilliputian, you mean it is extremely, almost absurdly small — so tiny that it seems almost unreal or laughable in its smallness.

A lilt is a gentle, pleasing, rhythmic rise and fall — like a small wave that moves smoothly and repeatedly up and down. It's the quality of something that sounds (or occasionally moves) in a light, musical, swinging way.

When something is described as lilting, it means it has a pleasant, musical, rhythmic quality — with a gentle, flowing rise and fall. Imagine the way a cheerful melody moves: it goes up a little, comes down a little, bounces along lightly and smoothly.
A lima bean is a type of edible seed that grows inside a pod on a plant. It belongs to the legume family, which is the same family of plants that includes peas, lentils, chickpeas, and kidney beans.
An arm, leg, or wing. It is also a large branch of a tree. To be "out on a limb" means to be in a risky or isolated position.

Limber means able to bend and move easily, smoothly, and without stiffness. If something or someone is limber, they are highly flexible — they stretch, twist, and flex without resistance, without strain, and without the risk of snapping or breaking.
Limbic means relating to the limbic system — a group of tightly connected brain structures that together govern your emotions, emotional memories, and survival instincts.

An uncertain state of waiting, in which nothing can progress until something is decided, as in "the project is in limbo." In Catholic theology, Limbo is a place on the edge of Hell for unbaptized souls. It is also a dance under a lowered bar.
The focus of public attention, as in "she shunned the limelight." Literally, a bright stage light once used in theatres.

Limerence is an intense, involuntary, and often painful state of romantic obsession with a specific person — where your happiness feels almost entirely controlled by whether or not that person shows interest in you.
A limerick is a short, funny poem that always has exactly five lines, following a fixed pattern of rhyme and rhythm. When read aloud, it has a bouncy, skip-along feel — almost like a musical jingle.
Limestone is a type of rock.

Liminal means existing on the threshold between two states, places, or conditions — being in the "in-between." It describes something that has already left one state behind but has not yet fully arrived at the next one.
A limitation is anything that acts like a wall or a fence — it marks the point beyond which you cannot go, or the point at which something stops working, stops being possible, or stops being allowed.
Limitless means having no limits at all — no boundaries, no restrictions, no point where something stops or runs out.
To limn means to depict or portray something — either through visual art (painting, drawing) or through language (writing, description).

A limner is a visual artist — specifically, a painter. But it's not just any painter. The word refers to a particular kind of painter tied to specific historical roles, and understanding those roles is what makes the word truly click.
A limousine is a large, luxurious car — one that is noticeably bigger, fancier, and more comfortable than an ordinary car.
Soft and floppy, lacking firmness, as in "limp lettuce." Figuratively, lacking energy, force, or enthusiasm, as in "a limp handshake" or "a limp excuse."
A limp is an uneven, irregular way of walking — where a person or animal cannot walk smoothly and puts noticeably more weight on one leg than the other.
To limp means to walk in an uneven, labored way because one leg or foot is hurt, weak, or painful.
Limpid means perfectly clear, transparent, and free from anything that would cloud or disturb it. It is a stronger, more beautiful, and more precise word than simply saying "clear."

A linchpin is the single most important person or thing in a system, plan, group, or situation — the one that holds everything else together. If you remove a linchpin, the entire thing collapses, fails, or falls into chaos.

Line dancing is exactly what its name implies: people dancing in lines to music. More precisely, a line dance is a choreographed dance in which a group of people dance along to a repeating sequence of steps while arranged in one or more lines or rows.
When someone talks about your lineage, they are talking about where you come from, who your people were, and the unbroken biological thread that connects you to them.

"Lineal" describes something that exists in a direct, unbroken line of descent — meaning it relates to the straight-line connection from an ancestor down through their child, that child's child, and so on, generation after generation.
A lineament is a distinctive line or outline that defines the shape of something — most often a person's face or body — in a way that gives it its individual, recognizable character.
Progressing step by step in a straight, logical sequence, as in "a linear narrative." It can also mean arranged in a straight line, or in maths, forming a straight line on a graph.

Linen is a natural fabric — a type of cloth — made from the fibers of a plant called flax. Think of it as similar to cotton, but coming from a completely different plant and having its own distinct feel and character.
To linger means to stay somewhere, or to continue existing, longer than expected or longer than necessary — often slowly, and often reluctantly.
Lingo means a type of language or a set of special words and expressions that a particular group of people use — words that outsiders might not easily understand.
A common language used for communication between people who speak different native languages, as English is in international business.
A person who scientifically studies language and how it works. More casually, a person who speaks several foreign languages well.
Linguistics is the scientific study of language — what it is, how it works, how humans use it, and why it behaves the way it does.
A liniment is a medicated liquid or semi-liquid preparation that you rub directly onto your skin to relieve pain, soreness, or stiffness — particularly in your muscles and joints.
Every meaning of "link" shares one central idea: a point of connection between two things. Think of it as a bridge, a joint, or a bond that holds two separate things together or in relation.
A connection or link between things, as in "the linkage between poverty and crime." It can also mean a system of linked parts in a machine, or the tendency of genes to be inherited together.

Linoleum is a type of flat, smooth material used to cover floors. Think of it as a tough, thin sheet — almost like a very firm, dense mat — that gets laid down on top of a floor's surface to protect it, make it easier to clean, and make it look nicer.
A lintel is a horizontal beam placed across the top of an opening — such as a door, a window, or a gate — to support the weight of the wall (or structure) above that opening.
To lionize someone means to treat them as a very important, famous, and admirable person — to shower them with public praise, attention, and admiration, often to an extreme degree.
Lippy means being rude, cheeky, or disrespectful through the things you say — especially by talking back, arguing, or saying things you have no business saying in that situation.

To liquefy means to change something into a liquid, or to become a liquid. Whether something is made liquid by an outside force, or whether something turns liquid on its own, the word "liquefy" covers both.

A liqueur is a sweetened, flavored alcoholic drink. Those two qualities — sweet and flavored — are what define it and set it apart from every other alcoholic drink in the world. If you remember nothing else, remember those two things.
Liquidate means to clear something away completely — whether that's turning an asset into cash, shutting down a business, wiping out a debt, or even eliminating a person or group.
Liquidation means converting something into cash by getting rid of it — and then using that cash to settle what is owed, with nothing left behind afterward.

The word liquidity comes from the idea of liquid — something that flows freely. Liquidity always means: how easily, quickly, and without losing value can something be converted into usable cash, or how much ready cash is available?
A speech habit in which "s" and "z" sounds are pronounced like "th," as in "thun" for "sun." Lisp is also the name of an early computer programming language.
To speak with a lisp, pronouncing "s" and "z" sounds as "th," as in "thnake" for "snake."
Lissome is an adjective that describes a person (or sometimes an animal) who is slender, supple, and graceful — all at once.

A list is a collection of separate items — names, words, numbers, tasks, or anything else — written, typed, or spoken one after another. The whole point of putting things into a list is to record them, organize them, or communicate them clearly.

Listless means having no energy, no desire, and no interest in doing anything. A listless person feels completely flat — not excited, not motivated, not even curious. They don't want to start anything, finish anything, or engage with anything.

A litany is a long, repetitive series of things said one after another — usually complaints, problems, requests, or accusations — that feels overwhelming, exhausting, or tedious because of how many there are and how they keep piling up.

Literacy means the ability to read and write. A person who can read a book, a sign, or a message — and can also write words and sentences — is said to have literacy. It is the skill of working with written language.
When something is literal, it means exactly what it says — no hidden meaning, no exaggeration, no symbolism. Just the plain, direct, face-value truth of the words.

In a literal manner; exactly as stated, not in a figurative way, as in "the building was literally falling apart." It is also often used informally for emphasis, even when something is not literally true.
"Literary" is an adjective built from the word "literature," and it means of, related to, or having the qualities of literature.
Literate means able to read and write. A person who is literate can pick up a book and read it, and can put a pen to paper and write words that make sense.
Literati refers to a group of people who are highly educated, deeply knowledgeable about literature, and are considered the intellectual and cultural elite of a society.
Written works, such as novels, poems, and plays, that are valued for their artistic merit. It can also mean all the writing on a particular subject, or printed information such as leaflets.
Lithe describes a body — or a person or animal — that is flexible, graceful, and moves with effortless ease.

Lithium is a noun that refers to a chemical element — one of the fundamental building blocks of matter found in nature. It is a metal, but unlike the metals most people picture (iron, gold, copper), lithium is strikingly unusual.
A litigant is any person — or organisation — who is directly involved in a lawsuit in a court of law. If you are part of a legal case being fought in court, you are a litigant.
To litigate means to take a legal dispute to a court of law and go through the official legal process to resolve it.
Litigation is the process of taking a legal dispute to court to get it resolved by a judge (and sometimes a jury).

Litigious describes someone who is excessively or unreasonably eager to take people to court, or who sues others far more than necessary. It can also describe a culture or society that relies too heavily on lawsuits to settle disputes.
Litotes is a figure of speech — a deliberate rhetorical device — in which you express a point by denying the opposite of what you actually mean, rather than stating your meaning directly.

Litter refers to pieces of waste — wrappers, bottles, cans, food packaging, cigarette butts, plastic bags, or any other rubbish — that people have carelessly dropped or thrown in a public space instead of putting them in a bin.
To scatter rubbish in a public place. To be littered with something means to be filled or scattered with it, as in "an essay littered with errors."
When we say a place or thing is littered, we mean it is covered with or full of many things that are spread around in a messy, disorganized, or excessive way.

The adjective littoral means relating to, located on, or existing along the shore of a sea, lake, or other large body of water. More specifically, it describes the zone where land and water meet and interact — the shoreline region.
"Liturgical" is an adjective that means relating to liturgy — the formal, structured, and publicly performed acts of religious worship that a religious community follows together.
A liturgy is the official, fixed, structured order of worship that a religious community follows during its public services.

To live down something means to succeed in making people forget about something embarrassing, shameful, or humiliating that you did or that happened to you — usually by waiting for time to pass and by behaving well afterward.

A livelihood is the means by which a person earns money or obtains what they need to survive — food, shelter, clothing, and other basic necessities. In the simplest terms, it is how someone makes a living.

When something or someone is lively, they are full of energy, activity, and spirit. Think of the opposite of dull, flat, or lifeless. Something lively feels alive — it moves, buzzes, sparks, and engages you.
The distinctive colours and design used on an organization's vehicles or aircraft, or the special uniform worn by servants or officials. A livery stable is where horses are kept or hired out.

Livestock refers to animals that are raised by humans on a farm or ranch for practical or economic purposes. These are domesticated animals kept not as pets, but as a resource — to produce food, materials, or labor.
Extremely angry; furious. As a colour, dark bluish-purple, like a bruise.
Living rent free in someone's head
To be constantly in someone's thoughts, especially in an annoying way, without that person getting anything in return — like a tenant who pays no rent.
A lizard is a type of reptile — a scaly, cold-blooded animal. It is one of the largest groups of reptiles on Earth, with over 6,000 known species.

A loafer is a person who avoids work and spends their time doing nothing useful. They are idle, unproductive, and unwilling to put in effort. Think of someone who lies on a couch all day, skips their responsibilities, and lets others carry the load.
Loam is a type of soil — but not just any ordinary soil.

To loan something means to give it to someone temporarily, with a clear understanding that they will return it to you later. You still own the thing. You are simply allowing someone else to use it for a period of time.
A loanword is a word that one language permanently takes from another language and begins to use as its own.

Loath means deeply unwilling to do something. When you are loath to do something, you have a strong inner resistance to doing it — it goes against your nature, your principles, or your feelings, and you would really rather not do it.
To loathe something or someone means to feel an intense, deep disgust combined with strong hatred toward it.
Loathing is a feeling of extremely strong and deep disgust or hatred toward someone or something. It is not just a mild dislike — it sits at the very far end of negative feelings.
When something is loathsome, it causes an intense feeling of disgust, revulsion, or hatred in the person who sees, hears, smells, or thinks about it. It does not just mean "bad" or "unpleasant."
When you lob something, you throw or hit it in a slow, high, curving arc — the object rises up into the air first, then gently comes back down.

A lobby is the first room or area you enter when you walk into a large building — before you reach the main part of the building. Think of it as a "welcome zone" or a buffer between the outside world and the interior of the building.

When you lobby someone, you are trying to persuade a person in power to make a decision that benefits you or your cause. You are not just asking once, casually — you are making a deliberate, organized, and persistent effort to influence their decision.

A lobbyist is a person whose job is to influence the decisions of government officials — typically politicians, lawmakers, or regulators — on behalf of someone else, usually a group, company, or organization that has a strong interest in those decisions.

A lobe is a rounded, slightly bulging section or division that forms part of a larger structure. Think of it as a distinct "chunk" or "segment" that sticks out or is clearly set apart — but is still attached to, and part of, the whole thing.

A lobotomy is a surgical operation performed on the brain in which a doctor deliberately cuts, destroys, or removes connections in the front part of the brain — specifically a region called the prefrontal cortex — with the goal of changing a person's behavior or relieving severe mental illness.

A locale is a specific place — but not just any place. The word carries with it a sense of the character, atmosphere, or particular conditions of that place. When you use the word "locale," you're not simply pointing to a dot on a map.

Locality means a specific, identifiable place or area — typically a relatively small, bounded patch of the world that you can point to and think of as a distinct unit. Think of it as "a particular spot or zone that has its own sense of hereness."
To restrict something to a particular area, as in "the infection was localized." It can also mean to pinpoint where something is, or to adapt a product for a particular country or language.
To locate something means either to find where it is, or to place/establish it somewhere. These are its two distinct meanings, and they are both used very commonly.

The Loch Ness Monster is a legendary, giant creature that many people believe lives in a large, deep lake called Loch Ness in the Scottish Highlands, Scotland. "Loch" is simply the Scottish word for "lake."

A locket is a small decorative case — typically made of metal like gold or silver — that opens and closes like a tiny book, revealing a hidden compartment inside. It is almost always worn as jewellery, hanging from a necklace chain close to the heart.
Locomotion is the act or ability of moving from one place to another. It refers to the process of traveling through space — shifting your whole body, or an entire object, from point A to point B.
The adjective "locomotive" means relating to movement from place to place, or having the ability to produce or enable such movement.
Locus simply means a specific place, point, or position — the exact location where something exists, happens, or is centered.

A locution is a particular word, phrase, or expression — especially one that is characteristic of a specific person, group, time period, or language. Think of it as a "unit of speech" that someone uses to say something.
A lode is a vein of metallic ore running through rock underground.
A lodestar is something — a star, a person, an idea, or a principle — that guides you and gives you a sense of direction, especially in a steady and reliable way.

A lodestone is a naturally occurring rock that has a remarkable property: it is naturally magnetic. That means it can pull iron and other magnetic metals toward itself all on its own — without any human process or artificial treatment.
A lodge is a place of shelter — but not just any shelter. It carries a specific feeling: something smaller, simpler, and set apart from the main building or the busy center of life.

To make a formal complaint, appeal, or claim to an authority, as in "lodge a complaint." It can also mean to become firmly stuck somewhere, as in "a bone lodged in his throat," or to stay somewhere as a paying guest.
A lodger is a person who pays money (rent) to live in a room inside someone else's home — while the owner of that home also lives there at the same time.
Loess is a specific type of fine, powdery, yellowish-brown deposit of soil material that was carried through the air by wind and then settled on the land over thousands of years.
A room or space directly under the roof of a building, used for storage or living. It can also mean a large open-plan flat in a converted warehouse, or a gallery in a church or hall.
Noble and idealistic, as in "lofty ambitions." It can also mean proud and superior in manner, as in "lofty disdain," or impressively high, as in "a lofty ceiling."
An official record of events, especially on a ship or aircraft, or a record of activity kept by a computer system. A log is also a thick piece of tree trunk or branch.

To log something means to officially record it in an organized, ongoing way — not just jotting a quick note, but entering information into a system, register, or record that tracks things over time. Think of it as deliberate, formal, repeated documentation.
Logic is the study of correct reasoning — the rules and principles that separate good thinking from bad thinking. When you reason logically, your thinking is orderly, consistent, and trustworthy.
Something is logical when it follows naturally and correctly from reasoning, evidence, or facts — without contradiction, without arbitrary jumps, and without relying on emotion or guesswork.
Logical symbolism is the practice of replacing the words of ordinary language with precise, standardized symbols in order to express and analyze logical reasoning.
A logician is a person who studies, practices, or is an expert in logic — the science of correct reasoning.
Logistical means relating to the practical coordination and management of resources, people, movement, and timing needed to make something complex actually happen in the real world.

A logistical nightmare is a situation where the practical coordination and planning required to make something happen is so overwhelmingly complex, messy, or full of obstacles that it causes serious stress, confusion, failure, or chaos.

Logistics means the careful planning, coordination, and management of how things — goods, people, resources, or information — move from one place to another, arrive at the right time, and are stored properly along the way.

A logjam is a situation where everything has come to a complete standstill — where progress is totally blocked because things have piled up, gotten tangled together, or because people simply cannot agree on a way forward. Nothing can move. Nothing can happen.
A logo is a unique visual mark that stands for something — usually a company, organization, product, team, or person.
A logophile is a person who deeply loves words.
Logorrhea means an excessive, unstoppable, and often uncontrollable outpouring of words — whether in speech or in writing. Think of it as a verbal flood that just won't stop.

Logos is a Greek word that carries one big central idea: reason expressed through words. It sits at the intersection of two things — thinking and speaking — because the ancient Greeks believed you couldn't truly separate them.
The word loins refers to a specific region of the human (or animal) body.
To loiter means to stand, wait, or hang around somewhere for no clear or obvious reason, often for an uncomfortably long amount of time.

To loll means to rest or move in a way that is loose, heavy, and relaxed — without any tension or effort in the body. Think of the way a person sinks deep into a sofa on a lazy Sunday, or the way a dog's tongue hangs out of its mouth on a hot day.
To lollop means to move with big, loose, bouncy, and clumsy movements. It's the kind of motion where the body seems to flop and roll along rather than move in a smooth, controlled way.

To lollygag means to waste time in a slow, lazy, and aimless way — doing nothing useful, or taking far too long to do something simple. When someone lollygags, they are not purposefully resting or relaxing.

"Lone" means single, solitary, or without others. It describes a person, animal, or thing that is the only one present, or that stands apart from a group — isolated, unaccompanied, or without support.
Lonesome describes a feeling of sadness that comes from being alone or from lacking the company of others. It is not simply the state of being alone — it is the emotional pain that can come with it.
"Long for" means to have a deep, heartfelt wish for something — especially something you don't have right now, something you've lost, or something that feels out of reach.
"Long in the tooth" is an idiom that simply means old or getting old.
"A long shot" means something that has a very small chance of succeeding. It is an attempt, a hope, or a possibility that is unlikely — but not completely impossible.
Long-winded describes someone or something that uses far more words than necessary to say something.
Longevity means the state or condition of living, existing, or lasting for a notably long time. It is the quality of being long-lasting.
Longing is a deep, persistent feeling of wanting something or someone that you do not have — and often cannot easily have, or cannot have at all. It is not just a casual wish.
Longitude is a way of measuring how far east or west a particular location on Earth is, using these imaginary lines as a reference system.
Longstanding describes something that has existed, continued, or been in place for a long time — and is still going on or still relevant right now (or at the time being spoken about).

A longueur is a stretch or passage within a book, film, play, speech, or piece of music that feels tediously slow and dull — a section that drags on, loses your attention, and makes you feel like time is crawling.

To look at someone blankly means to stare at a person with absolutely no expression on your face — no smile, no frown, no raised eyebrow, nothing. Your face looks completely empty, like a blank sheet of paper with nothing written on it.

Lookout is about watching — specifically, watching carefully for something that might be coming, whether danger, opportunity, or anything else worth noticing. The word carries a sense of alertness and anticipation.
A loom is a device — a frame or machine — used to weave threads into cloth. It is the fundamental tool of fabric-making.

When something looms, it appears — or is about to appear — in a way that feels large, unclear, and threatening. The word always carries a sense of weight and unease. Whatever is looming feels bigger than you, darker than you'd like, and difficult to escape.

When something looms large, it means it appears very big, important, threatening, or dominant — either in reality, or in someone's mind. It gives the feeling of something that is impossible to ignore because it feels so huge and overwhelming.

When you call someone or something loony, you mean they are crazy, mentally unbalanced, or wildly foolish. It describes behaviour, ideas, or people that seem far outside the boundaries of normal, rational thinking.
A gap or ambiguity in a law, rule, or contract that allows someone to avoid its intended purpose while technically staying within it, as in "a tax loophole."
A loose cannon is a person who is unpredictable, uncontrollable, and likely to cause trouble — often without meaning to, and often in a way that embarrasses or damages the group they belong to.
Loosen means to make something less tight, less firm, or less restricted — or to become that way on its own.

To loot means to steal things from a place — usually in large quantities and openly — during a time when normal law and order has collapsed or broken down. Think of war, a riot, a natural disaster, or any crisis where police are overwhelmed or absent.
When something is described as looted, it means it was violently or forcibly taken away — stolen during a moment of chaos, disorder, or overwhelming power. The thing didn't go missing quietly.

A looter is a person who steals goods from shops, homes, or other buildings during a time of chaos, crisis, or disaster — especially when normal law and order has broken down and there are few or no police around to stop them.

To lop means to cut something off — usually with a single, clean, decisive stroke. The key idea is removal by cutting. You're not just making a small nick or scratch; you're cutting something away so that it's completely separated from the main body.

A lope is a specific way of moving — a relaxed, smooth, easy, rhythmic, bounding stride. It sits comfortably between a casual walk and a full-speed run. It is not rushed or urgent, but it is not slow either.
To lope means to move — usually run — with long, smooth, easy, flowing strides at a relaxed, steady pace. It's not a slow walk, and it's not a desperate, straining sprint.
When something you can see or touch is uneven, not straight, or not symmetrical, it is lopsided.
Loquacious means talking a lot, often more than what the situation really calls for.

Loquacity means the quality of talking too much or at excessive length. It is the noun that describes a person's habit or tendency to be extremely talkative, often going on and on well beyond what the situation requires.
Proud and arrogant, as if you were superior to others, as in "lordly disdain." It can also mean grand and magnificent, fit for a lord.
Lore means a body of knowledge — a rich collection of stories, beliefs, traditions, and wisdom — about a particular subject, place, or group of people.

A lorgnette is a pair of eyeglasses — or sometimes a small pair of binoculars — that are mounted on a decorative handle, so that you hold them up to your eyes to see through them, rather than wearing them on your face.

To no longer have something, because you cannot find it or it has been taken away, as in "I lost my keys." It also means to fail to win a game or contest, or to have less of something, as in "lose weight."

When something is "lost on someone," it means that person completely fails to understand, notice, or appreciate it. The thing — a joke, a hint, a lesson, a warning, a compliment, beauty, sarcasm — simply does not reach their mind or heart.
"Lot" carries the idea of a portion, a share, or a group — something divided up, assigned, or collected together. This single idea runs through all its different meanings.
A lothario is a man who deliberately and repeatedly charms, flatters, and seduces women — not out of genuine love or care, but purely for his own pleasure and ego.

A lotion is a smooth, liquid or semi-liquid substance that you apply directly onto the surface of your skin (or sometimes your hair or scalp). You do not swallow it — it is always used externally, meaning on the outside of your body.

A lottery is a system or event in which winners are chosen purely by chance — not by skill, knowledge, effort, or merit. People enter by buying a ticket or registering their name, and then a random draw decides who wins a prize.

Louche describes someone or something that is morally questionable or disreputable, but in a way that carries a strange, seductive charm. It's not pure condemnation. It sits in a fascinating middle ground — shady, yet glamorous. Dubious, yet magnetic.
A lounge is a comfortable room or area designed for relaxing, waiting, or socializing in a calm and unhurried way.

To lounge means to sit, lie, or stand in a very relaxed, lazy, and comfortable way — without doing much of anything. It is the kind of relaxation where your body goes loose and limp, your posture is casual and droopy, and your mind is not focused on any task.

Lousy means very bad, of poor quality, unpleasant, or deeply unsatisfactory. It is an informal word — meaning it belongs to everyday spoken and casual written English, not formal writing like official reports or academic essays.
A lout is a person — almost always a man or a boy — who is rude, aggressive, ill-mannered, and socially unrefined.
Lovable describes a person, animal, or thing that has qualities which naturally and easily make others feel love, deep warmth, or strong affection toward them.

A love-in is a gathering of people that is centred on expressing love, peace, goodwill, and togetherness. Think of it as the opposite of a fight or a protest — it is a coming-together in a warm, harmonious, and affectionate spirit.
The word "low" essentially means not reaching far up — close to the bottom, the ground, or the minimum point of something. This single core idea stretches across all its uses.

Low-key means understated, calm, and without unnecessary fuss or drama. Something that is low-key does not try to impress, does not demand attention, and does not go to extremes. It stays in the background.
To lowball means to deliberately give someone a number — a price, a quote, an estimate, an offer — that is intentionally lower than what is realistic or truthful, usually to gain an advantage.
When you call something lowbrow, you mean it is simple, unsophisticated, and does not require much intellectual effort or cultural knowledge to enjoy.

"Lowering" as an adjective describes something that looks dark, heavy, gloomy, and threatening — as if something bad is about to happen. It paints a picture of a world that feels oppressive, menacing, and about to turn dangerous.
Lowery describes a sky — or the weather in general — that is dark, cloudy, and threatening, as if a storm is about to break out. It means something that is dark, gloomy, and threatening.

A lowland is an area of land that lies at a low elevation — meaning it doesn't sit very high above sea level. It is typically flat or gently rolling, and it is usually surrounded by, or positioned next to, higher land such as hills, mountains, or plateaus.

Lowly means low in rank, status, or importance. It describes a person, position, or thing that sits near the bottom of a social, professional, or moral hierarchy — not powerful, not prestigious, not highly valued by society.
Loyalty is a strong, steady commitment to stand by someone or something — not just when it's easy and convenient, but especially when it's difficult or costly.
A lubricant is any substance that you place between two surfaces that touch and move against each other, in order to make that movement smoother, easier, and less damaging.

To lubricate something means to apply a slippery substance — like oil, grease, or any similar material — to a surface or moving part, so that friction is reduced and movement becomes easier, smoother, and less damaging.
Showing or intended to arouse sexual desire in an offensive way; lewd. Literally, smooth and slippery.
Lewdness or sexual offensiveness. In science and engineering, it is the ability of a substance to reduce friction, as an oil does.
Lucent means glowing with light or allowing light to pass through in a soft, radiant way.
Lucid means clear — but a very specific kind of clarity: the kind that cuts through confusion, fog, or disorder and makes something immediately easy to understand or perceive.
Lucidity is a noun that means the quality of being perfectly clear — clear in thought, clear in expression, or clear in consciousness.

Lucrative describes something that makes a large amount of money or profit. When you call something lucrative, you are saying it is not just slightly profitable — it is significantly and notably rewarding in financial terms.
Lucre simply means money or financial gain. But here's the thing — it's never just a neutral word for money. It always carries a strong sense of moral disapproval.

Lucubration means deep, hard, painstaking mental work — the kind of serious, effortful studying or thinking that demands your full concentration, often stretching deep into the night. It is not casual reading or light thinking.

A Luddite is a person who opposes, distrusts, or resists new technology. The word is used to describe someone who is deeply uncomfortable with modern technological advances and either refuses to adopt them or actively speaks out against them.

Ludic means relating to, or having the character of, play. When something is ludic, it carries the essential spirit and qualities of play — imagination, spontaneity, freedom, and an exploratory openness where the process matters more than any fixed goal.
Ludicrous means so absurd, so unreasonable, or so wildly out of touch with reality that it almost makes you laugh — even when the subject is serious.

A lug is a small part that sticks out from the surface of an object. It is usually a flat tab, a ridge, a knob, or an ear-like protrusion. Its purpose is to help you grip, fasten, carry, or connect the object to something else.
To lug something means to carry or move it with great physical effort, usually because it is heavy, bulky, or awkward. The word isn't just about carrying — it's about the struggle of carrying.
Luggage refers to the bags, suitcases, and other containers that a person uses to carry their personal belongings while traveling.
Lugubrious describes something or someone that appears excessively sad, mournful, or gloomy — often to a degree that feels overdone, theatrical, or far greater than the situation actually calls for.
Only slightly warm, as in "lukewarm tea." Figuratively, lacking enthusiasm, as in "a lukewarm response."
A lull is a brief, temporary period of calm, quiet, or reduced activity that occurs in the middle of — or between — periods of greater intensity, noise, or turbulence.

When you lull someone, you calm them — you ease them out of a state of alertness, worry, or restlessness into a state of peace, comfort, or sleep. The central idea is bringing something tense or active to a gentle, quiet stillness.
A lullaby is a soft, gentle song sung to a baby or very young child to help them fall asleep. That is its heart and soul in one sentence.
Lumber is wood that has been cut from trees and shaped into usable pieces — like long flat boards, thick beams, or planks — so that people can build things with it.

When something lumbers, it moves in a way that is slow, heavy, and clumsy — but also powerful. Think of a massive animal, like a bear or an elephant, walking. It doesn't move gracefully or quickly. Its huge body shifts from side to side with every step.
The SI unit for measuring the total amount of visible light given out by a source. In anatomy, a lumen is the hollow space inside a tube-shaped organ, such as a blood vessel or the gut.
A person who is greatly admired and influential in a particular field, as in "a luminary of modern physics." Literally, a natural body that gives off light, such as the Sun or Moon.
Something is luminescent when it emits light on its own, without needing heat to do so.

Luminiferous is an adjective that means producing light, carrying light, or transmitting light. If something is luminiferous, it either generates light on its own or acts as a medium through which light travels.
Luminosity means the quality or amount of light that something gives off. It describes how much light a source actually produces and emits into the world around it.
Something is luminous when it produces, gives off, or appears to be filled with a beautiful, glowing light. But here is the important thing — luminous does not simply mean "bright."
A lummox is a clumsy, awkward person — someone who moves without grace, often bumping into things, dropping objects, or stumbling around.
A lump is a piece of a solid substance that has no particular or tidy shape — just a chunky, rough, irregular mass of something.
When you lump things together, you treat several different things as if they are all the same — you group them together, often in a way that ignores the real differences between them.
"Lumpen" describes people — or things connected to people — who are at the very bottom of society: uneducated, crude, poor, and completely disconnected from mainstream social and working life.
Lunacy means extreme foolishness, wildly irrational thinking, or behavior so reckless and absurd that it seems like madness.
Lunar means "of or relating to the Moon."

When you use lunatic as an adjective, you are describing something — a plan, an idea, a decision, a piece of behavior, or a person's actions — as wildly irrational, completely unreasonable, or so reckless and foolish that it seems to defy all common sense.
A lunatic is a person who is considered to be mentally ill, completely out of their senses, or who behaves in an extremely irrational, wild, and uncontrollable way.

A luncheon is a midday meal, but not just any midday meal — it is a formal or special one, usually organized for a particular occasion or purpose. Think of it as the dressed-up, sophisticated version of an ordinary lunch.
A luncheonette is a small, informal eatery — a type of modest restaurant — that serves simple, light meals, most commonly lunch and breakfast.

To lunge means to make a sudden, forceful movement forward — toward something or someone. It is not a slow, calm step forward. It is not a gentle reach. It is a burst of motion — quick, powerful, and directed at a specific target.
Lupine means wolf-like — relating to, resembling, or characteristic of a wolf. That's the definition in its purest form.
A lurch is a sudden, heavy, off-balance movement — like a jerk, a sway, or a stumble — that happens without warning and feels unstable or clumsy.

To lurch means to make a sudden, sharp, uncontrolled movement — usually sideways, forward, or both at once. It's the kind of movement that feels like a brief loss of balance or control, as if something (or someone) was jolted off course without any warning.
A lure is something that attracts or tempts a person or animal toward it, usually by appearing desirable, rewarding, or appealing. Think of it as a magnet for desire.

To lure someone means to deliberately attract them toward something — a place, a person, a situation, or an action — by offering or showing them something they desire, often with a hidden or self-serving purpose behind it.

"Lurid" means shockingly graphic, disturbing, or sensational — especially when something describes or presents dark subject matter (violence, sex, crime, scandal) in explicit and excessive detail. The word doesn't just mean "dark" or "explicit."
To lurk means to be somewhere in a hidden, quiet, or unnoticed way — staying in the background on purpose, without drawing attention to yourself.
