Luscious means richly and deeply pleasing to the senses — in a way that feels almost overwhelmingly satisfying, indulgent, and luxurious. It's not just "nice" or "good." When something is luscious, it gives you a flood of sensory pleasure.
Of plants, growing thickly, richly, and healthily, as in "lush green fields." It can also mean luxurious and sumptuous, or, in British slang, very attractive or delicious.
Lust means an intense, urgent, and often overwhelming desire — a craving so strong that it tends to override your reason and self-control.
Luster is the soft, smooth glow that a surface gives off when light reflects off it gently. It is not a harsh, blinding brightness. It is not a wild sparkle.

To lustrate something means to purify or cleanse it — but not in the ordinary, physical sense of washing it with water. It means to cleanse something of a moral, spiritual, or symbolic stain through a formal, deliberate act.
Lustrous means having a smooth, rich, beautiful glow or shine.
Lusty means full of strong, healthy energy and enthusiasm. Think of a person who is bursting with life — strong, lively, vigorous, and eager. That person is lusty.

A lute is a plucked string instrument — meaning you make sound by pulling or striking its strings with your fingers, rather than drawing a bow across them (like a violin) or blowing into it (like a flute).
Luxe means luxury — but not just any kind of luxury. It refers to a specific, refined, elegant kind of luxury. Think of it as luxury that has taste, artistry, and a polished sophistication to it.

Luxuriance means the quality of being abundantly rich, full, and overflowing — usually referring to something growing, flowing, or existing in a way that feels almost excessive in its richness and vitality.
"Luxuriant" means growing, existing, or produced in such rich, thick, and abundant quantities that it creates a sense of overflowing fullness and vitality.
To luxuriate means to take great, deep, unhurried pleasure in something — to fully and indulgently give yourself over to enjoying it.
Luxurious describes something that is far above ordinary — something that is extremely comfortable, very expensive or high-quality, and gives a deep sense of pleasure or indulgence.

Luxury means something that gives you great comfort, pleasure, or elegance — but that you don't actually need. It goes beyond the basics of life. You can survive, and even live perfectly well, without it. But having it feels exceptionally good.

A lycanthrope is a human being who transforms — or is believed to transform — into a wolf. In plain terms, it is simply a more formal, scholarly word for a werewolf. The two words point to the same creature.

Lye is a powerfully alkaline, corrosive chemical substance used in soap-making, food preparation, and industrial cleaning. It is one of the strongest bases (the chemical opposite of an acid) you can commonly encounter.
To lynch someone means to kill them as an act of punishment — carried out by a private group of people, outside any court of law, and without a fair legal trial.
A lyre is an ancient stringed musical instrument — one of the oldest in human history. Think of it as a small, handheld harp held upright, with strings you pluck to make music.
Expressing deep personal emotion in a beautiful, imaginative way, as in "lyrical prose." To "wax lyrical" means to talk about something with great enthusiasm.
Lyricism is the quality of expressing deep personal feelings and emotions in a beautiful, flowing, and almost musical way — through words, music, or other forms of art.
The full name of LSD, a powerful synthetic hallucinogenic drug that causes dramatic changes in perception, thinking, and mood.
Macabre describes something that is deeply unsettling or disturbing because it involves death, corpses, decay, or the gruesome physical reality of dying.

A heavy club with a spiked metal head, once used as a weapon. A mace is also a ceremonial staff carried as a symbol of authority, a spice made from the outer covering of nutmeg, or a spray used for self-defence.
To macerate something means to soften it by soaking it in liquid. The liquid slowly works its way into the material, breaking down its structure and making it soft, tender, or even mushy.
A machete is a large, heavy cutting tool that looks like a very big knife. It has a long, wide, flat blade — usually made of steel — with a sharp edge on one side and a dull back on the other.

If you call a person or their behavior Machiavellian, you mean they are cunningly clever, deeply manipulative, and willing to use deceit and ruthless tactics to get what they want — usually power, control, or personal gain — without any guilt or moral concern.
Machiavellianism is the practice of getting what you want by being calculating, deceptive, and manipulative — treating other people as tools to be used rather than as human beings to be respected.
To machinate means to secretly plot or scheme against someone, usually with the intention of causing them harm or gaining an unfair advantage over them.

A machination is a secret, cleverly designed plan to trick, manipulate, or harm someone — usually to gain power, control, or personal advantage. It is never an innocent plan. It is always sneaky, and almost always morally wrong.

Machismo is a strong, often exaggerated belief that men are superior to women — and that this supposed superiority must be displayed through attitude and behavior. It is not just confidence or pride in being a man. It goes further than that.

When you call a man "macho," you are saying he strongly — and usually very visibly — displays what many cultures consider to be traditionally male qualities: toughness, physical strength, fearlessness, dominance, and emotional hardness.
A macrocosm is a large, complete system or world — the "big whole" — especially when you are thinking about it in contrast to something smaller that exists within it or reflects it.
Maculate means spotted, stained, or blemished — either physically (covered in marks or blotches) or morally (tainted, impure, corrupt).

"Mad as a hatter" means to be completely insane or out of one's mind. When you call someone "mad as a hatter," you are saying they are so crazy, confused, or wildly eccentric that they seem to have lost their grip on reality.

When someone says a person is "mad as a March hare," they mean that person is behaving in a wildly crazy, erratic, and unpredictable way — completely out of their mind, as if they have lost all sense of reason or control.

Madame is a word used to refer to or address a woman — but not just any woman. It carries built-in respect, and often implies that the woman in question holds some kind of dignity, authority, rank, or social standing.

Madcap describes something — a plan, an idea, an adventure, a person's behavior — that is wildly impulsive, reckless, and unplanned, but in a way that is fun, exciting, and amusing rather than dark or dangerous.

If something is maddening, it causes such intense frustration, irritation, or confusion that it feels like it could drive you crazy. That word — crazy — is the key. "Maddening" comes from the idea of making someone go mad (another word for crazy or insane).
Madness refers to a state where normal reasoning, sanity, or order has completely broken down — in a person's mind, in someone's behavior, or in a situation.

A madrigal is a song written for multiple voices singing together — typically without any instrumental accompaniment — where each voice carries its own distinct melody, and all these melodies interweave to create a rich, layered sound.

A maelstrom is a situation — or in its most literal sense, a body of water — that is violently chaotic, overwhelming, and feels like it is spinning wildly out of control, pulling everything around it into its center.

A maestro is a person who has reached the absolute highest level of mastery in their field — someone so skilled, so accomplished, and so deeply knowledgeable that others look up to them with genuine admiration and respect.
A maggot is the baby form — more precisely, the larval stage — of a fly.
Magisterial means having or displaying impressive authority, supreme confidence, and commanding mastery — especially in knowledge, skill, or expression.
A magistrate is an official of the law who holds the authority to judge, enforce, or administer legal matters.

Magma is molten rock — that is, rock that has been heated to such extreme temperatures that it has melted into a hot, thick, flowing liquid — found beneath the Earth's surface, deep inside the planet.
Magnanimity is the quality of being noble and generous in spirit — especially toward someone who has wronged you, opposed you, or someone over whom you have power or advantage.
If someone is magnanimous, they are generous and forgiving in spirit — especially in situations where most people would be tempted to be petty, spiteful, or resentful.

A magnate is a person who is extremely wealthy, powerful, and influential — especially because of their success in business or industry. Think of someone who doesn't just run a company, but who dominates an entire field or sector of the economy.

Magnetic Resonance Imaging — or MRI — is a medical scanning technology that creates detailed pictures of the inside of your body using powerful magnets and radio waves. Unlike X-rays or CT scans, it uses absolutely no radiation.
"Magnificent" describes something so impressively grand, beautiful, or excellent that it immediately fills you with admiration and awe.
To magnify means to make something bigger, greater, or more powerful — either in reality, in appearance, or in how it is perceived.

Magniloquent describes a style of speaking or writing that is extravagantly lofty, boastful, and overblown — full of big, impressive-sounding words and sweeping phrases that make ordinary things sound extraordinarily grand.

Magnitude means the size, scale, or degree of something — specifically, how large, powerful, or significant it is. It answers the questions: How much of it is there? How serious is it? How great is it?
A magnum opus is the greatest, most important work of a person's life or career — the one piece of work they are most remembered for, or the one they themselves consider their crowning achievement.
A noisy black-and-white bird of the crow family. Figuratively, a person who collects things, especially random or shiny objects, or who chatters a lot.

When used as an adjective, mahogany describes a deep, rich, reddish-brown color — the color of polished mahogany wood. It is not a plain, flat brown. Think of it as brown that has been warmed up with a clear reddish or burgundy glow running through it.
Mahogany is, first and foremost, a tree — a large tropical tree that grows mainly in Central America, South America, and the Caribbean islands.
A maiden is a young unmarried woman. In its fullest traditional sense, the word carries an extra layer: she is not only unmarried, but also a virgin — a woman who has not had sexual relations.

To maim someone means to injure them so severely that a part of their body is permanently destroyed, lost, or disabled — but they survive. The person lives on, but they are left fundamentally and irreversibly altered.

A mainstay is the single most important source of support that something or someone depends on to keep going. It is the central, indispensable element — the one thing that, if removed, would cause everything else to weaken or fall apart.
Most of the water flows through the center — that central, dominant flow is the mainstream. Water at the edges trickles in smaller, separate streams. The mainstream is where most of the action is.
Maintain means to keep something the way it is — through active, continued effort. It is about preventing something from changing for the worse, stopping, or disappearing.

Maintenance means the work of keeping something in good condition so that it continues to function properly — or the ongoing effort to preserve a state, situation, or standard so it doesn't deteriorate.

When you call something majestic, you are saying it produces a powerful feeling of awe, grandeur, and deep respect — the kind of feeling where you stop, stare, and feel slightly humbled by what you're looking at or experiencing.
"Make a killing" means to make a very large amount of money in a short period of time, usually through a business deal, an investment, or some kind of sale.
Make a mountain out of a molehill
When someone makes a mountain out of a molehill, they are treating a small, minor problem as if it were a huge, serious one. They are exaggerating how bad or difficult something actually is.
To "make a scene" means to behave in a loud, emotional, or embarrassing way in a public place — especially in a way that attracts unwanted attention from people around you.

To "make ends meet" means to have just enough money to pay for your basic needs — things like food, rent, electricity, and transport — without much or anything left over after all your bills are paid.
Make hay while the sun shines
To take advantage of a good opportunity while it lasts.
"Make it up to someone" means to do something good or kind for a person in order to compensate for a wrong, a mistake, or a disappointment you caused them in the past.

To "make light of" something means to treat a serious, difficult, or painful matter as if it is not important — to downplay it, joke about it, or act as though it doesn't really matter, when in reality, it does.

When someone makes no bones about something, they say it or do it openly, directly, and without any hesitation or embarrassment. They don't hide their feelings. They don't soften their words. They don't beat around the bush.

To "make one's mark" means to achieve something significant, to become recognized or respected in a particular field, or to leave a lasting impact on the world — or on a smaller part of it, like a community, a company, or even a single person's life.

To "make short work of" something means to finish, deal with, or defeat something very quickly and easily. When you make short work of something, you handle it with so much speed and efficiency that it barely takes any time or effort at all.

To "make one's blood boil" means to cause someone to feel extremely angry, furious, or deeply outraged. When something makes your blood boil, it does not mean you are slightly annoyed or mildly upset.
"Make the cut" means to reach the required standard or level of quality needed to be chosen, accepted, or allowed to continue.
To cause trouble or controversy by challenging the way things are, as in "don't make waves." It can also mean to make a strong impression or attract attention.

A makeover is a complete and noticeable transformation of someone's appearance, or something's look and condition, with the goal of making it better, fresher, or more appealing. The key word here is complete — a makeover isn't a small touch-up or a minor fix.

When something is makeshift, it means it is a temporary substitute — put together quickly from whatever materials or resources happen to be available — because the proper, correct, or ideal thing is not available at that moment.
When you say someone is maladjusted, you mean that they have failed to adapt properly to the world around them — to its social rules, expectations, relationships, and everyday demands.

Maladministration means handling responsibilities badly. Specifically, it refers to the way an organisation, authority, or official manages its duties — and doing so in a way that is wrong, unfair, careless, or dishonest.
Maladroit means clumsy or lacking skill — either in how you physically move and handle things, or in how you handle situations, words, and relationships with people.

A malady is a disease, illness, or disorder — something that is wrong with a person's body or mind, making them unwell. Think of it as a more formal, serious-sounding way to say "sickness" or "ailment."

Malaise is a vague, general feeling of being unwell or uneasy — one that you can clearly sense, but cannot easily name, explain, or pin down to a single cause. It's the feeling that something is "off," without being able to say exactly what.

A malapropism is when someone accidentally uses the wrong word in place of a similar-sounding word — and that wrong word makes the sentence ridiculous, confusing, or unintentionally funny, because it means something completely different from what was intended.
When something is malapropos, it means it is out of place, poorly timed, or unsuitable for the moment — something said or done that simply does not fit the situation at hand.

Malaria is a serious infectious disease — one that can be life-threatening — caused by tiny, microscopic parasites. These parasites are not bacteria or viruses; they belong to a group of single-celled organisms called Plasmodium.
Malarkey means nonsense — talk, ideas, or claims that are foolish, untrue, exaggerated, or simply not worth taking seriously.

Malcontent describes a person who is deeply and persistently dissatisfied — not just with one small thing, but with the overall situation they are in, especially regarding authority, leadership, society, or the way things are being run.
A malcontent is a person who is persistently and deeply dissatisfied — not just with one thing on one bad day, but habitually and as a defining part of their character.

A malediction is a curse — a deliberate, intentional spoken (or written) wish that evil, harm, or misfortune will befall a specific person. When someone delivers a malediction, they are not simply venting anger or using a bad word.

A malefactor is a person who does something wrong, harmful, or criminal. Simply put, it is someone who commits a bad act — whether that is a crime, a moral wrongdoing, or a harmful deed done against others.
Malefic means causing harm, evil, or misfortune — or having the nature or power to do so.
Maleficent means causing harm or evil, especially in a deliberate, active, or deeply wicked way.
Malevolence means a deep, deliberate desire to cause harm or suffering to others. It is not just disliking someone — it is actively wishing bad things upon them, or taking pleasure in their pain.

Malevolent means having a deep, active desire to cause harm, pain, or suffering to others. A malevolent person doesn't just do harmful things by accident or out of anger in the moment — they want others to suffer. The desire itself is the heart of the word.
Malfeasance means intentional wrongdoing by someone in a position of power or trust — particularly when that wrongdoing is illegal or a serious violation of their duties.
A malformation is an abnormal or irregular structure in something — most often a body part or organ — that came about because it did not develop or form the way it was supposed to.
A malfunction is when something stops working the way it is supposed to work.
Malice is the desire to cause harm, pain, or suffering to someone — and crucially, doing so on purpose, with full awareness and intention.
Malicious means having a strong, deliberate desire to harm, hurt, or cause damage to someone — and often taking pleasure or satisfaction in doing so.
Malign means evil, harmful, or having a deeply threatening influence.
To malign someone means to say false, unfair, or harmful things about them — especially to damage how others see them.

Malignance is the quality or state of being deeply, actively harmful — not in a mild or passing way, but in a way that is serious, dangerous, and often relentless. Something that has malignance doesn't just cause small trouble; it causes real, severe damage.
Malignant describes something that is deeply harmful by its very nature — and not just harmful in a passive, accidental way, but harmful in an active, spreading, and hard-to-stop way.
Malignity means a deep, powerful, and active quality of evil or intense ill will — either in a person's character, or in the dangerous nature of a disease.

To malinger means to pretend to be sick, injured, or unable to function — or to deliberately exaggerate a real illness — in order to get out of a duty, responsibility, or obligation you simply don't want to do.

A malingerer is a person who deliberately pretends to be sick, injured, or mentally unwell — or exaggerates a real but minor condition — in order to avoid a duty, responsibility, or unpleasant task, or to gain some unfair benefit.

A mall is a large building — or a group of connected buildings — that houses many different shops, stores, restaurants, and sometimes entertainment facilities like cinemas or game arcades, all gathered under one roof or within one enclosed space.
Malleable means capable of being shaped, bent, or molded — without breaking.
Malnutrition is a condition in which a person's body does not receive the right nutrients — in the right amounts — that it needs to grow, function, and stay healthy.
Malodorous is a formal adjective used to describe anything — a place, object, substance, or even a person — that has a bad, unpleasant, or offensive smell.

Malpractice means serious professional misconduct — a failure so significant that it falls below the minimum acceptable standard of skill, care, or honesty that a professional in that field is expected to maintain.

Malversation means corrupt or dishonest conduct by someone who holds a position of trust or authority — especially a public official, government employee, or anyone entrusted with managing other people's money or resources.
A mammal is a type of animal. More specifically, it is a warm-blooded, air-breathing animal with a backbone that has hair or fur on its body and feeds its young with milk produced by the mother.
Mammon means wealth, money, or material riches — but not in a neutral way. It specifically refers to the greedy, obsessive, or morally corrupt pursuit of money and material things.

"Mammoth" means extremely and impressively large — so large that the sheer scale of something is hard to ignore or overlook. This is not just another word for "big" or "large." It sits near the very top of the size scale.
A mammoth is a large, extinct animal that looked a lot like an elephant — because it actually was related to elephants. It walked the Earth thousands of years ago and no longer exists today.
A man is a fully grown male person — as opposed to a boy (who is young) or a woman (who is female).

A manacle is a metal restraint — a rigid cuff or ring — that is locked around a person's wrist to prevent them from moving freely or escaping. Think of it as the old, heavy, historical version of what we today call a handcuff.

To manacle someone means to restrain them — to lock, bind, or chain them so that they cannot move freely. Think of a prisoner whose wrists are locked in heavy metal rings connected by a short chain. Those rings are manacles. The act of putting them on?

"Manage" means to exercise control or skill over something that has some difficulty, complexity, or resistance to it. Whether you're running a company, surviving a tough situation, or somehow getting a difficult thing done — "manage" is the word for it.
A large, heated pool or tank where injured, sick, or orphaned manatees are cared for during rehabilitation, or where manatees that cannot be released are kept permanently.
The official standard language of China. A mandarin is also a powerful senior official, originally in imperial China, or a small, loose-skinned citrus fruit.
A mandate is an official instruction, order, or authority given to someone — or a group — to carry out a specific task, role, or policy.
To mandate something means to officially require it, using the power of authority.
When something is mandatory, it means you must do it. You have no choice. It is required by a rule, a law, or an authority — and failing to do it usually brings a consequence.

The Mandela Effect is a phenomenon where a large group of people — sometimes millions — all share the exact same false memory. They all remember something that never actually happened, or remember a detail differently from how it truly was.
A mandible is a jaw or jaw-like structure — a hard, movable part near the mouth that an animal uses to bite, chew, grip, or process food.
The two rounded knobs at the top of the lower jaw, which fit into the skull just in front of the ears to form the jaw joints.
The word mandolin refers to two completely different things depending on the context — a musical instrument and a kitchen tool. Both are common, so knowing both meanings matters.

A mane is the long, thick growth of hair found on the neck — and sometimes the surrounding areas — of certain animals. Think of the flowing hair that frames a lion's face, or the strip of hair that runs along the top of a horse's neck. That is a mane.
A maneuver is a deliberate, skillful action or movement done to achieve a specific goal, especially when that goal involves some challenge, obstacle, or opponent to deal with.
To maneuver means to move or guide something — or yourself — carefully and skillfully, especially when the situation is difficult, tight, or requires clever thinking.
Manga refers to a comic book or graphic novel that is made in Japan, following a distinct Japanese style of visual storytelling.
Mange is a serious, contagious skin disease that affects animals — primarily mammals like dogs, cats, foxes, wolves, horses, and rabbits.

A manger is a long, open box or trough used to hold food — such as hay or grain — for farm animals to eat from. Think of it as a bowl or dish, but designed for large animals like horses, cows, donkeys, and sheep.

To mangle something means to damage or destroy it so badly — through tearing, crushing, twisting, cutting, or very rough handling — that it ends up looking, sounding, or functioning completely unlike how it was before.
A mangrove is a tree or shrub that grows in coastal tropical and subtropical regions where land meets the sea — in places like tidal mudflats, river mouths, lagoons, and shallow coastal waters.
Mangy is an adjective used to describe something — or someone — that looks dirty, diseased, worn out, and in a pitiful or disgusting condition.
To manhandle something or someone means to handle or move them using rough physical force. The key feeling in this word is roughness — it is never gentle, never careful, and never polite.
Mania means an extreme, intense, and overwhelming fixation on something — a state where a person's interest, excitement, or energy goes far beyond what is normal or controllable.
A maniac is a person who behaves in a way that is wildly out of control — either dangerously reckless, obsessively extreme, or both at once.
Maniacal describes behavior, energy, or an attitude that has crossed far beyond the normal limit of reason and control — so far that it looks mad, unhinged, or dangerously obsessive.
Manic describes a state of extreme, frenzied, out-of-control energy or excitement — the kind that feels too intense, too fast, and too overwhelming to be normal or sustainable.

When something is manifest, it means it is so completely clear and obvious that it simply cannot be denied, hidden, or argued against. It is right there, in plain sight, for anyone to see or understand without any effort.
The verb "manifest" means to make something visible, real, or clear — to bring something out into the open so that it can be seen, felt, or understood.
"Manifest" means something that is obvious, clear, and undeniable. If something is manifest, there's no doubt about it. You can see it plainly.
A manifestation is something that makes a hidden, inner, or abstract thing visible, real, or obvious to the outside world. It is the outward form of something that exists internally.
A manifesto is a written document in which a person, group, or organization publicly declares what they believe, what they stand for, and — most importantly — what they intend to do about it.
"Manifold" means many, and of many different kinds. It bundles two ideas into one word: there are a lot of them, and they are varied — not all the same type.
To manipulate something or someone means to handle or control it skillfully and with clear intention — either physically (an object) or psychologically (a person or situation).
Manipulation is the act of controlling, influencing, or handling something or someone — but how it is done is what gives the word its meaning.
An unexpected and very welcome gift or benefit, as in "manna from heaven." In the Bible, manna was the food that God provided to the Israelites in the desert.
A mannequin is a full-sized, three-dimensional model shaped like a human body. It is not alive — it is an artificial, inanimate object, typically made of materials like plastic, fiberglass, or foam.

Mannered means artificially stylized or affected — when something (or someone) is so self-consciously performed, so deliberately styled, that it feels unnatural, forced, and exaggerated rather than genuine and spontaneous.
A distinctive habit or way of speaking or moving that is typical of a particular person. In art, Mannerism is a 16th-century style marked by elongated figures and exaggerated poses.
"Manqué" describes a person who had the potential, the desire, or the inner spirit to become something — but never actually became it. It points to an identity that could have been, and wasn't.
A manservant is a man who is employed to personally serve another person, usually by working in or around that person's home.
A mantel is the shelf — and sometimes the entire decorative frame — built around and above a fireplace.
A mantelpiece is the decorative shelf — and often the entire decorative frame — that sits above and around a fireplace.

An important role or responsibility passed from one person to another, as in "take on the mantle of leadership." It is also a loose, sleeveless cloak, or the layer of the Earth between the crust and the core.

A mantra is a word, phrase, or sound that someone repeats over and over — either out loud, in a whisper, or silently in their mind — because it carries deep meaning or power for them. Repetition is the soul of a mantra.
A manual is a document — a book, booklet, or guide — that tells you how to do something, how to use something, or how something works.
Manumission is the formal, deliberate act by which a person who owns an enslaved person officially sets that enslaved person free.

To manumit someone means to formally release a person from slavery, making them legally free. When an owner manumits a slave, they are granting that slave their freedom — officially, deliberately, and permanently.
A manuscript is a piece of writing in its original, unpublished form — whether handwritten by a person or typed out — that has not yet been formally printed and distributed to the public.
An interpretation of quantum mechanics which holds that every possible outcome of a quantum event actually happens, each in its own separate, branching universe.
A maquette is a small, three-dimensional model that an artist, sculptor, or designer builds before creating the real, full-sized version of a work.
To mar something means to damage or spoil it in a way that makes it less good, less beautiful, or less enjoyable than it was or could have been.
To maraud means to move through an area in search of things to steal or people to attack — like a predator hunting for prey. It's not about one single theft or attack in one place.
A marauder is a person who moves around from place to place, attacking people, stealing their belongings, and causing destruction wherever they go.
A mare is an adult female horse. Specifically, the word applies once the female horse reaches four years of age or older.
A margin is always a gap, edge, or extra space between something and its boundary, limit, or a point of comparison. That one idea runs through every single use of this word.

Very small or minor, as in "a marginal improvement." It can also mean on the edge of something, or of people or groups, not part of the mainstream. In politics, a marginal seat is one won by a very small majority.
Marginalia are the notes, marks, drawings, symbols, or any other written additions that a reader has made in the blank spaces — the margins — of a book, manuscript, or document.
To marginalize someone means to push them to the edges of society — to treat them as if they are unimportant, powerless, or don't fully belong.
When we say someone is marginalized, we mean they have been pushed to the edges of society — treated as less important, less valued, or less deserving than the main, dominant group.

A marina is a managed waterfront facility — a specially built place along the edge of a body of water (the sea, a lake, a river, or a bay) where small recreational boats are kept, parked, and taken care of.
A marine biologist is a scientist who studies life in the ocean and other saltwater environments. The word "marine" means "of the sea," and a biologist is someone who studies living things.

A marionette is a type of puppet — a small figure made to look like a human being, an animal, or a fantasy creature — that is moved and controlled by strings or thin wires attached to different parts of its body.
Marital is an adjective that means relating to marriage — specifically, anything that belongs to, comes from, or is connected with the state of being married or the relationship between spouses.

Maritime means relating to the sea — but specifically to the human relationship with the sea. It describes things connected to the ocean in the context of travel, trade, work, law, and life near or on the water.
Clearly noticeable, as in "a marked improvement." A marked man or woman is someone singled out as a target for attack or punishment.

"Marking" as a noun connects to a single simple idea: something that marks. But "marking" can refer to either a visible mark itself (something you can see and point to) or the activity of making marks.
Marmoreal means resembling marble — in how something looks, feels, or even how a person behaves.

The most common meaning of maroon is a dark, dull red color — like the color of dried blood, dark red wine, or the skin of a ripe dark cherry. It sits somewhere between red and brown, with the brightness of red toned down and darkened.

To maroon someone means to leave them stranded in a remote, isolated place where they cannot escape and cannot easily get help. The person who is marooned is completely cut off — from other people, from rescue, and from any way out.
If someone is marooned, they are completely cut off from help, from people, or from the ability to leave — stuck in a place with no easy way out, usually against their will.
When marquee is used as an adjective, it means the biggest, most prominent, most celebrated person or thing in a particular field or group.
A marquee is a large, often elegant tent that is set up outdoors to host an event — a wedding reception, a corporate gathering, a garden party, a festival, and so on. It is not a small camping tent.

Marquetry is the art of decorating a surface by fitting together small, carefully cut pieces of thin material — usually different types of wood — to form a picture, pattern, or design, much like assembling a very flat, precise jigsaw puzzle.

Marred means damaged, spoiled, or made imperfect in a way that reduces beauty, quality, or value. When something is marred, it has been harmed — not necessarily destroyed, but noticeably lessened from what it was or what it could have been.
The word marrow has a few distinct meanings. The most important one is biological, but it also has a powerful figurative use and a separate meaning as a vegetable.
A marshal is a person in a position of authority whose role is to manage, control, direct, or maintain order — whether in the military, in law enforcement, in a courtroom, or at an event.
To marshal something means to carefully gather, organize, or arrange things — or people — in a deliberate, purposeful, and orderly way, usually in preparation for something important.
A marsupial is a type of mammal — a warm-blooded animal with a backbone that breathes air, has hair or fur on its body, and feeds its young with milk.

Martial means relating to war, soldiers, combat, or the military. When you call something "martial," you are saying it belongs to the world of fighting, armies, and warfare — or that it carries the spirit of that world.

A martinet is a person in authority who demands strict, unquestioning obedience to rules and who enforces those rules with rigid, often excessive harshness — showing little or no flexibility, compassion, or common sense.
A martyr is a person who suffers deeply — or even dies — for something they believe in so strongly that they refuse to give it up, even when they are threatened, punished, or persecuted for it.
Martyrdom is the suffering or death that a person willingly accepts rather than give up something they deeply believe in — a faith, a cause, a truth, or a principle. It is not just any suffering.

To marvel means to feel a deep, almost overwhelming sense of wonder or amazement at something — usually because it seems extraordinary, beautiful, impressive, or almost too good or strange to be real.
Marvelous describes something that is extraordinarily good, impressive, or wonderful — so good that it fills you with a sense of wonder or delight. It goes far beyond "nice" or "good."
Marzipan is a smooth, soft, sweet paste made from ground almonds and sugar. Think of it as edible modeling clay — sweet, nutty, and pliable enough to shape with your hands.
Masala means a mixture or blend of spices. But the word carries quite a bit more nuance depending on how it's used, and understanding the full picture will serve you well.
A mascot is a person, animal, or object that a group officially adopts as their symbol, representative, and bringer of good luck.
Masculine means relating to, or having the qualities typically associated with men or boys. It is the opposite of feminine, which relates to qualities associated with women or girls.
To mash something means to press or crush it with force until it loses its original shape and becomes a soft, flat, or pulpy mass.
Masochism is the act or tendency of finding pleasure, satisfaction, or gratification in one's own pain, suffering, or humiliation.
A masochist is a person who gets pleasure, satisfaction, or a sense of reward from their own pain, suffering, discomfort, or humiliation.
A mason is a skilled craftsperson whose job is to build or create structures using hard materials like stone, brick, or concrete.

Masonry means the skilled work of building things using solid, individual units — like bricks, stones, or concrete blocks — stacked and joined together, usually with a sticky binding paste called mortar, which hardens like cement and holds everything in place.

A masquerade is about hiding the truth — either literally, with a physical mask at a party, or figuratively, through deliberate deception in real life. Both uses share one core idea: the real thing is being concealed behind a false appearance.
To masquerade means to pretend to be something or someone you are not — especially in a way that is meant to deceive others. It is always about hiding your true identity or nature behind a false one.
A large amount or number of something, as in "a mass of people." In physics, mass is the amount of matter in an object. In Christian churches, Mass is the service of the Eucharist.
A massacre is the killing of a large number of people — especially people who are helpless, defenseless, or unable to fight back — in a way that is brutal, cruel, and unjust.

To massacre means to kill a large number of people in a brutal, cruel, and deeply unjust way — particularly when the victims are helpless, unarmed, or have little to no chance of defending themselves.
When you massage something, you press, rub, and knead it with your hands — usually a part of someone's body — in a slow, controlled, rhythmic way.

When something is massive, it is very large, and that largeness feels weighty, solid, and imposing. Think of a massive boulder sitting in the middle of a road — it's not just big, it has bulk, density, and a physical presence that commands attention.
A masterpiece is a work — something created by a person — that stands at the highest possible level of skill, quality, and excellence. It is not just very good or impressive.
Mastery means having complete, expert-level command over something — a skill, a subject, a craft, or a situation. It is the highest level of knowledge or ability a person can reach in a given area.
To masticate means to chew food. More precisely, it means to use your teeth and jaw to bite, crush, and grind food into smaller, softer pieces before you swallow it.
A mat is almost always something flat, laid down, and meant to serve a practical purpose — whether on a floor, on a table, under an object, or around a picture.
Matcha is a very fine, bright green powder made from whole green tea leaves. You use it to make a drink — or to flavor and color food. That's the simplest version.

Matchless means so exceptionally good that nothing else can equal it. When something is matchless, it stands completely alone at the very top — there is no rival, no competitor, and nothing that can be compared to it on the same level.

The belief that money and possessions are the most important things in life. In philosophy, it is the view that only physical matter exists, and that everything, including the mind, can be explained in terms of it.

When we call someone or something materialistic, we mean that they place too much importance on owning physical things — money, luxury goods, expensive possessions — and treat these as the most meaningful or worthwhile things in life.
To materialize means to become real — to go from something that exists only as a thought, plan, hope, or possibility, into something that actually exists or actually happens in the real world.
Maternal means "of, relating to, or like a mother."
Maternity means the state or condition of being a mother — everything that comes with it: the experience of carrying a child, giving birth, and taking on the role of a mother.
A matinee is a live performance or film screening that takes place during the day — most commonly in the afternoon — as opposed to one held in the evening.
A matriarch is a woman who holds the highest position of authority, respect, and power within a family, group, or society.

Matriarchal is an adjective. You use it to describe something that belongs to, comes from, or is characteristic of a system where women — especially mothers — hold the primary power, authority, and leadership.
The act of killing one's own mother. A matricide is also a person who kills their own mother.
To matriculate means to formally enroll at a university or college — specifically, the act of officially registering and becoming a recognized member of that institution.
Matriculation is the formal, official process of being enrolled into and accepted as a full member of a university, college, or other higher education institution.
Matrimonial is an adjective that means "relating to or connected with marriage."

Matrimony means the state of being married — that is, the condition in which two people are legally and/or officially joined together as spouses. It refers to marriage itself, both as a bond between two people and as the formal act of entering into that bond.
A matrix is a structured container, environment, or substance that holds, shapes, or gives rise to something else.

Matron refers to a woman who commands authority, dignity, and respect — typically because of her age, experience, or an official role she holds. The word is almost always associated with a woman who is mature (middle-aged or older), not a young girl.

"Matronly" describes a woman who has the looks, manner, or style typically associated with a respectable, older, motherly woman — one who is past her youth and carries herself (or dresses herself) accordingly.

Matte describes a surface or color that has no shine, no gloss, and no reflection. A matte surface looks completely flat and dull when light hits it. It does not sparkle, gleam, or mirror anything around it.

"Matted" describes something — usually made of strands, fibers, or hair — that has become so tangled, twisted, and pressed together that it forms a dense, clumped, flat mass. The individual strands are no longer separate or free.
When someone is matter-of-fact, they deal with things in a plain, calm, and straightforward way — without showing emotion, drama, or excitement.
Matutinal simply means of, relating to, or occurring in the morning. If something is matutinal, it belongs to the morning — it happens there, lives there, or is characteristic of that time of day.

Maudlin describes a state of being excessively and weakly sentimental — where emotions spill out in an overdone, tearful, or self-pitying way that others find embarrassing or uncomfortable to witness. The key word here is excessive.

To maul means to attack someone or something in a violent, savage, and uncontrolled way — causing serious physical harm, usually by tearing, clawing, biting, or striking repeatedly. The key quality of "maul" is that it is brutal and messy.
To talk in a slow, rambling, aimless way. It can also mean to move or act in a slow, idle, aimless manner.
A mausoleum is a grand, impressive building specifically constructed to hold the remains of a dead person or multiple dead people above ground.
Mauve is a specific color — a soft, dusty, muted pinkish-purple. Think of purple that has been quietly blended with pink and slightly faded, like a gentle bruise or the petals of a dying rose.
A maven is a person who has deep, thorough knowledge in a specific subject — and who is also genuinely passionate about that subject and loves sharing what they know with others.

When you use maverick as an adjective to describe a person, you mean they are independently minded and unconventional — someone who consistently refuses to follow the accepted rules, norms, or beliefs of the group they belong to, and instead thinks and acts according to their own judgment.

A maverick is a person who thinks and acts independently — someone who deliberately refuses to follow the rules, norms, or accepted ways of doing things that everyone else in their group follows without question.
The mouth, jaws, or throat of a hungry animal. Figuratively, something that seems to swallow things up, as in "the maw of the city."
Mawkish means excessively and artificially sentimental in a way that feels weak, overdone, and slightly disgusting.

A maxim is a short, carefully worded statement that expresses a general truth, a rule of behavior, or a guiding principle — the kind of thing worth remembering and applying to real situations in life.
To maximize something means to make it as large, great, or effective as it can possibly be — to push it to its highest possible level.
A thought experiment by physicist James Clerk Maxwell, imagining a tiny being who sorts fast and slow gas molecules between two chambers, seemingly breaking the second law of thermodynamics.
A law in physics describing how the speeds of molecules in a gas are spread out at a given temperature — how many move slowly, how many quickly, and how many in between.
Violent, dangerous chaos and disorder, as in "the protest descended into mayhem." In law, it is the crime of deliberately maiming or disfiguring someone.

A mea culpa is a deliberate, open admission that you were wrong or that something was your fault. When someone issues a mea culpa, they are publicly or formally accepting blame for a mistake, failure, or wrongdoing — saying, in effect: "I did this.
A meadow is an open piece of land covered with grass and wild plants, especially wildflowers. It is a natural, quiet, outdoor space — not a forest, not a farm, and not a city park.

"Meager" describes something that is so small or so little that it is not enough — it falls short of what is needed, expected, or deserved. It is almost always a negative word. You use it when something is disappointingly insufficient.

The word mealy comes from "meal," which means coarsely ground grain — think flour, cornmeal, or oatmeal. When you hold a handful of flour or dry cornmeal, it is soft, dry, powdery, and slightly grainy.
A mealy-mouthed person avoids saying what they really mean by wrapping their words in so much vagueness, hedging, and excessive caution that the honest message disappears entirely.
To mean well means to have good intentions. It means a person genuinely wants to be helpful, kind, or supportive — even if what they actually do or say doesn't turn out well.
To meander means to move, travel, or progress in a slow, winding, indirect way — with no urgency, no straight line, and often no fixed destination.
"Meandering" describes something that follows a winding, curving, indirect path — moving slowly and without urgency, bending and turning rather than going straight.
Measles is a serious infectious disease. "Infectious" means it is caused by a tiny germ — specifically a virus — that gets inside your body and makes you sick.

"Measly" means pitifully, insultingly, or disappointingly small — especially when compared to what was expected, needed, or deserved. It's not just a description of size. It's a judgment. It says: "This is so little that it's almost offensive."
To measure up means to reach a required standard or level of quality — to be good enough for something or someone.
When you describe something as measured, you mean it is carefully controlled, deliberate, and restrained — not too much, not too little, and never impulsive.

A mecca is a place that people with a particular passion, interest, or purpose feel powerfully drawn to — because it is considered the most important, most celebrated, and most defining center of that thing.

Every time a ball rolls down a slope, a planet orbits the sun, water flows through a pipe, or an electron spins around a nucleus — some form of mechanics describes what's happening. It is the science of the physical behavior of matter and energy in motion.
To mechanize something means to replace human or animal effort with machines, or to convert a process so that machines do the work instead of people.
A large, decorative medal worn on a chain around the neck, or given as an award. It is also a round or oval decorative design, or a small, round piece of meat.
To meddle means to get involved in something that is not your business — especially when no one asked you to, and when your involvement is not welcome.
Meddlesome describes a person who involves themselves in other people's business, affairs, or decisions — especially when they have not been asked to and when their involvement is not welcome.
"Median" as an adjective simply means of, relating to, or situated at the middle.

The middle value in a list of numbers arranged in order. In geometry, it is a line from a corner of a triangle to the middle of the opposite side. In the US, a median is a strip of land dividing the two sides of a road.
A major nerve that runs down the arm into the hand, controlling some hand muscles and providing feeling to the thumb and first fingers. Pressure on it at the wrist causes carpal tunnel syndrome.
To mediate means to step in between two conflicting parties and help them reach an agreement. The single most important concept locked inside this word is "between."

Mediation is the process in which a neutral, independent third party helps two or more people or groups who are in disagreement to talk through their conflict and reach a peaceful, mutual agreement — without forcing a decision on anyone.

A mediator is a neutral, independent person who steps between two or more parties who are in conflict, disagreement, or who simply cannot communicate well on their own — and helps them reach a peaceful, mutually acceptable resolution.

Medieval is an adjective that means relating to or characteristic of the Middle Ages — a long period in European history that lasted roughly from the 5th century AD to the late 15th century AD (approximately 400 AD to 1500 AD).

Mediocre means just average — not good, not bad, but sitting uncomfortably in the middle. It describes something (or someone) that is neither impressive nor terrible. It is ordinary in a disappointing way.

Mediocrity means the quality or state of being just okay — not bad enough to fail, but not good enough to impress. It lives right in the middle: below excellence, above failure. Think of a scale from 1 to 10.

To meditate means to engage your mind in a slow, deliberate, and focused way — either inward (on your own mental state) or outward (on a topic or idea). The word carries a sense of intentional stillness and purposeful depth.

Meditation means the act of giving your full, focused attention to something — either inward (your own mind) or to a subject you're thinking deeply about. It is always a deliberate, intentional mental act. You choose to do it. It doesn't happen accidentally.
Meditative describes anything that has the quality of deep, calm, quiet reflection — a quality of being absorbed in thought, turned inward, still, and unhurried.
A medium is something that sits in the middle — between two things — and connects them, carries something between them, or balances them.

A medley is a collection of different, varied things brought together as one. The most important quality of a medley is variety — the items in a medley are noticeably different from each other, yet they exist together under one roof, so to speak.
A meed is a deserved reward or recompense — something given to a person in return for their service, effort, or merit. Think of it as "what you rightfully get for what you did."
Meek describes a person who is quiet, gentle, and unlikely to argue, fight back, or stand up for themselves — even when they have a perfectly good reason to.

When someone does something meekly, they do it in a quiet, gentle, and submissive way — without putting up a fight, without raising their voice, and without demanding anything for themselves. There is a sense of soft, passive acceptance in the action.
Meekness is the quality of being gentle, patient, and humble — especially when you could be forceful, aggressive, or proud, but you choose not to be. It is quietness of spirit.
When someone meets their match, they encounter a person who is just as good as them — or even better — at something they are usually very good at.

To meet someone halfway means to compromise — to agree to give up part of what you want so that another person also gives up part of what they want, and both of you can reach an agreement that works for everyone.

A megalith is a very large stone that ancient people deliberately chose, moved, and placed — either on its own or together with other large stones — to build a monument, a tomb, a temple, or some kind of ceremonial structure.

Megalomania is a state of mind in which a person has a dangerously exaggerated belief in their own power, importance, or greatness — often far beyond what is real or reasonable. It is not just confidence taken too far.

A megalomaniac is a person who is consumed by two things working together: an obsessive craving for power and control over others, and a wildly inflated, often delusional belief in their own greatness, importance, or abilities.
A megaphone is a device you hold up to your mouth to make your voice louder and direct it forward, so that a large group of people — or people far away — can hear you clearly.
Melancholia is a deep, heavy, lingering feeling of sadness, gloom, and unhappiness. It sits in your chest like a quiet weight. It makes the world feel dull, colorless, and distant.
Melancholic means feeling, showing, or causing a deep, quiet, lingering sadness — a sadness that is thoughtful and gentle rather than sharp or overwhelming.
Melancholy is a deep, quiet feeling of sadness — but not the sharp, intense kind. It is a gentle, lingering sadness that sits with you softly, often without a single clear cause.
Melatonin is a natural hormone your body produces to signal that it is time to sleep.

To meld means to combine two or more things so smoothly and completely that they become one unified whole — where the original pieces blend into each other seamlessly, and the boundaries between them soften or disappear.

A melee is a confused, chaotic situation — most often a noisy, disorganized fight involving many people at once, where everyone seems to be clashing with everyone else and no clear order or structure exists.

Mellifluous means smooth, sweet, and richly pleasing to the ear. It describes a sound — most often a voice or music — that flows so effortlessly and beautifully that it feels like a pleasure just to listen to it.

To mellow out means to become calm, relaxed, and at ease — especially after a period of stress, tension, excitement, anger, or anxiety. Think of it as the process of "coming down" from a high-energy or high-stress state into a peaceful, comfortable one.

Melodic means having the quality of a melody — it describes something that sounds like, relates to, or resembles a tune. When you say something is melodic, you are saying it has a flowing, musical, pleasing quality to the ear, like a song you could hum.

Melodious means pleasantly musical and sweet-sounding. When you call a sound melodious, you are saying it is smooth, tuneful, and genuinely delightful to listen to — the kind of sound that feels effortless and beautiful on the ear, almost like a gentle song.
Melodrama means emotional exaggeration — feelings, events, or reactions that are blown far out of proportion compared to what the situation actually deserves.
Melodramatic describes someone or something that is far more emotional, dramatic, or intense than the situation actually calls for.

A sudden and complete collapse, as in "a financial meltdown," or a moment when someone loses emotional control, as in "the toddler had a meltdown." Literally, the overheating of a nuclear reactor, causing the fuel to melt.
Just like a gene is a unit of biological information that gets copied and passed from parent to child, a meme is a unit of cultural information that gets copied and passed from mind to mind.

A memento is a physical object that you keep specifically because it reminds you of a particular person, place, or moment in your life. That's the heart of it — it's not just any object, but one that carries a memory inside it, at least for you.
Memento mori is a Latin phrase. Latin was the language of ancient Rome, and it is still used in philosophy, science, law, and religion today.

A memo is a short, official written message used to communicate information within an organization — a company, a government office, a school, or any institution. People inside that organization write memos to other people inside the same organization.
A memoir is a true story, written by a real person, about their own life — or a meaningful part of it. The person writing it is also the main character in it. They are not making anything up.
Memorabilia is a plural noun that refers to objects collected and kept because they are connected to a memorable person, event, place, or period in time.

A memorial is anything — an object, a structure, a ceremony, or even a place — that is created specifically to help people remember someone who has died, or to remember an important and often painful event from the past.

To memorialize someone or something means to do something deliberate and lasting that keeps their memory alive for the future. It is an act of saying, "This person, or this moment, mattered — and we are going to make sure it is never forgotten."
Menace means a threat — or something/someone that is threatening.

To menace means to threaten someone or something in a way that is frightening, serious, and makes danger feel close and real. It's not a casual or empty threat — when something or someone menaces, they create a genuine atmosphere of fear.
Something is menacing when it makes you feel that danger, harm, or something bad is about to happen — even if it hasn't happened yet.

A menagerie is a collection of wild, exotic, or unusual animals that are kept in cages or enclosures — not roaming free in the wild — so that people can look at them. Think of it as an old-fashioned, often private version of a zoo.
To mend something means to fix or repair it — to take something that is broken, torn, damaged, or not working properly, and bring it back to a good condition.

Mendacious means deliberately lying. A mendacious person is someone who tells falsehoods not by mistake, not out of confusion, but knowingly and on purpose. A mendacious statement is one that is false and was crafted to deceive.
Mendacity means the habit, practice, or quality of being a liar — the tendency to tell untruths deliberately and repeatedly.
A mendicant is a beggar — someone who survives by asking other people for money, food, or other necessities, rather than earning a living through work or owning property.
"Menial" describes a task or type of work that is low in skill and low in social status — work that is considered beneath educated or capable people.
A menorah is a multi-branched candle holder (or oil lamp holder) that holds deep religious significance in Judaism.

A mentor is a person who is more experienced or knowledgeable in a particular area, and who guides, advises, and supports someone who is less experienced — not as a job or for pay, but out of genuine care for that person's growth and success.

To mentor someone means to guide and support a less experienced person over time, helping them grow — in their career, skills, knowledge, or personal development — by sharing your own wisdom, experience, and honest advice.

Mercantile is an adjective that means "relating to trade, commerce, and the buying and selling of goods." Whenever something has to do with merchants, markets, profit-making, or the exchange of goods and money, you can describe it as mercantile.
Mercantilism is an economic theory and system of policy that dominated much of the world — especially in Europe — from roughly the 1500s to the late 1700s.
When we say someone is mercenary, we mean they are motivated purely and entirely by money or personal gain — and nothing else.
A mercenary is a person who fights in a war or armed conflict — but not for their own country, not out of loyalty, and not out of belief in a cause. They fight purely and simply for money.
Merchandise means goods — physical products — that are bought and sold. If something is made, stocked, and traded for money, it is merchandise.
A merchant is a person who buys goods and then sells them to make a profit. A merchant doesn't usually make the things they sell — they are in the business of trading them.
Merciful describes someone (or something) that chooses kindness, forgiveness, or gentleness — when they had every right or power to be harsh, strict, or punishing.
Mercifully simply means in a merciful way — but in real usage, it carries a rich emotional weight that goes far beyond that dry definition.
If someone or something is merciless, it shows absolutely no mercy — no kindness, no pity, no softening, no stopping. It is completely, relentlessly harsh.
Cruelly and without pity, as in "they teased him mercilessly."

If you describe someone as mercurial, you mean that their moods, emotions, or behavior change very quickly, very dramatically, and very unpredictably. One moment they are warm and cheerful; the next, without warning, they are cold and irritable.

Mercurochrome is the brand name of a once-popular liquid medicine — a reddish-pink antiseptic solution — that was applied directly onto small wounds like cuts, scrapes, and scratches to kill germs and help prevent infection.
Mercy is the act of choosing kindness, compassion, or forgiveness toward someone — even when you have the power to punish them, harm them, or simply leave them to suffer.
"Mere" means "nothing more than" or "only." It draws attention to the fact that something is small, limited, or insignificant — or that something small is enough to cause an effect.
"Merely" means only or nothing more than. When you use it, you are saying: this thing is exactly what it is — limited, small, or simple — and nothing beyond that.
Something meretricious looks impressive, attractive, or valuable on the outside, but is actually hollow, cheap, or false underneath.
To merge means to combine two or more separate things so completely that they become one single, unified thing — and the boundary between them disappears.
A merger is when two separate companies combine and become one single company.
A meridian is a line or a point that marks the highest position or the central dividing point of something.
Meringue is a light, sweet, white, foamy mixture made by beating egg whites with sugar until the mixture becomes thick, glossy, and holds its shape. It is used widely in baking and dessert-making.
Merit means genuine worth — the quality of something (or someone) that makes it truly good, valuable, or deserving of recognition, reward, or approval.
To merit something means to deserve it — because the thing, person, situation, or action is good enough, serious enough, or important enough to justify that response.
A meritocracy is a system — a society, an organization, a government, or a workplace — where people succeed, earn rewards, and gain power or positions based purely on their merit.
"Meritocratic" describes any system, process, organization, or society that rewards people based on their actual abilities, effort, and achievements — and nothing else.
Meritorious means deserving of praise, recognition, or reward because of genuine quality, effort, or excellence.

Merriment means cheerful, lively fun — the kind filled with laughter, noise, and a light-hearted spirit. It describes the happy excitement that happens when people enjoy themselves freely and playfully, usually together.
Merry means cheerful, lively, and full of joy — especially the kind of joy that shows itself openly and is shared with others.
A mesa is a landform — a natural feature of the Earth's surface. Specifically, it is a hill or raised piece of land that has a flat, level top and steep, almost vertical sides (like cliffs).
To mesh means to fit together smoothly and work well as a unit — like pieces that interlock perfectly and function without friction.

If something is mesmeric, it holds your attention so completely and so powerfully that you feel almost as though you are under a spell. You can't look away. You can't think about anything else. You are totally, helplessly drawn in.

A historical healing method based on the belief that an invisible magnetic force flows through living things and can be used to put people into a trance. Today it also means the power to hold someone completely spellbound.

To mesmerize someone means to grab their attention so completely and powerfully that they can barely look away, think of anything else, or even react normally. It is more than just "interesting" or "enjoyable."
When you are mesmerized by something, your attention is so completely and intensely locked onto it that everything else around you seems to fade away.

"Mesmerizing" describes something — or sometimes someone — that captures your attention so completely and powerfully that you feel almost unable to look away, think about anything else, or break free from the experience.
Messianic is an adjective that means relating to, resembling, or characteristic of a Messiah — a savior figure believed to be specially chosen to rescue, redeem, or transform people.
A mestizo is a person of mixed European and Indigenous American ancestry.
To metabolize something means to chemically process it inside a living body — transforming it from one substance into another through a chain of reactions happening inside your cells.
Metacognition is your ability to think about your own thinking. It is the mental process of stepping back and watching, judging, and controlling how your own mind works.
Metallurgical simply means "relating to metallurgy." So to understand this adjective fully, you first need to understand what metallurgy is — and once you do, the adjective will be completely clear.

Metallurgy is the science and technology of metals — it is the study of how metals are found in nature, how they are extracted and purified, how their inner structure determines their behavior, and how they are shaped and used to build things.

To metamorphose means to go through a complete and profound transformation — a change so deep and thorough that what comes out the other end is essentially a fundamentally different version of what went in.

Metamorphosis means a profound, complete, and often dramatic transformation — a change so deep and thorough that what exists after the change looks, behaves, or functions fundamentally differently from what existed before it.
Metanoia means a deep, total transformation of a person's mind, heart, and way of being. Not a small update in thinking. Not a tweak in attitude.

A metaphor is a figure of speech where you describe something by saying it is something else — not because it is literally that thing, but because the two things share a meaningful quality, and saying it this way creates instant understanding or impact.
Metaphorical means "not literally true, but used to describe something by comparing it to something else in order to make the meaning clearer, more vivid, or more powerful."

If something is metaphysical, it belongs to a world beyond the physical — beyond what you can see, touch, weigh, measure, or test in a laboratory. It lives in the realm of pure thought, abstract reality, and fundamental existence.

Metaphysics is a branch of philosophy that investigates the most fundamental questions about the nature of reality. Not how reality works — science handles that — but what reality is, at its deepest possible level. It asks questions like: What exists?

To metastasize means to spread from one place to other places in a harmful way, taking root and growing in those new places. It is almost always used about disease — especially cancer — and sometimes used figuratively about the spread of harmful things.
As a noun, mete means a boundary, a limit, or a boundary marker — specifically, a fixed point or line that marks where a piece of land ends.
To mete out something means to give or deliver something to someone — especially a punishment, a reward, or a form of treatment — in a deliberate and decided way.

Metempsychosis is the belief that when a living creature dies, its soul does not die along with it. Instead, the soul survives death, exits the old body, and enters a brand new body — beginning a fresh life.
A meteor is the bright streak of light you see flashing across the night sky — what most people casually call a "shooting star" or "falling star." It is not a star at all.
Extremely rapid and spectacular, like a meteor streaking across the sky, as in "a meteoric rise to fame." Literally, relating to meteors.
A meteorite is a natural, solid object from outer space that has traveled through Earth's atmosphere and landed on Earth's surface.
A meteorologist is a scientist who studies the atmosphere — the layer of air and gases that surrounds the Earth — in order to understand, explain, and predict weather.
Meteorology is the scientific study of the Earth's atmosphere — meaning the layer of gases that wraps around our planet — with a focus on understanding and predicting weather.
A meter is the standard, basic unit for measuring length or distance in the metric system — the system of measurement used by virtually every country in the world and by all of science.

Methane is a gas — meaning it floats invisibly in the air, like oxygen or carbon dioxide. It has no colour, no smell, and no taste. Under normal conditions on Earth, you cannot see it, smell it, or detect it with your senses at all.

When someone has "method in their madness," it means that their behavior — which looks crazy, chaotic, or completely illogical to others — is actually guided by a hidden, clever, and well-thought-out plan.
Methodical describes a person, action, or process that follows a clear, step-by-step plan — done in an orderly, careful, and systematic way, without skipping steps or rushing ahead.
A methodology is a complete, organized system of principles and methods that guides how you approach a task, solve a problem, or conduct research.
Meticulous means giving very careful, thorough attention to every small detail — making sure that nothing is wrong, nothing is missed, and everything is done as perfectly as possible.
When you do something meticulously, you do it with extreme care and close attention to every tiny detail — nothing is overlooked, nothing is left to chance, and nothing is done carelessly.
Metonymy is a figure of speech where you refer to something not by its own name, but by the name of something closely associated with it in real life.
Relating to or written in poetic metre, the regular pattern of stressed and unstressed syllables in poetry. It can also mean relating to measurement.

A metronome is a device that produces a steady, repeated beat at a precise, adjustable speed. Musicians use it as a timing reference — a reliable "pulse" to follow while practicing or performing, so they don't accidentally speed up or slow down.
A metropolis is a very large, very important city — one that acts as a major center of life, activity, and influence for a country or a large region.

Metropolitan means relating to a large, important, and influential city — the kind of city that is not just big in size, but also powerful in terms of economy, culture, and population. Such a city is called a metropolis.

Mettle is the strength of a person's character — specifically the courage, determination, and resilience they show when things get hard. It's what's inside someone that keeps them going when a situation is difficult, scary, or demanding.
If someone is mettlesome, they have a strong, fiery spirit — the kind that makes them face challenges with courage, energy, and determination rather than backing away.
The soft, high-pitched cry of a cat or kitten. A mew is also a type of gull, or a cage in which hawks are kept while they moult.
A mewl is a weak, thin, high-pitched, whimpering cry — the kind of sound that is too faint and feeble to be called a proper cry, yet too distressed to be called silence.
To cry in a weak, feeble, thin little way — like a newborn baby or a tiny kitten.
Mewling describes a sound — specifically a weak, thin, soft, feeble cry. Think of a newborn baby or a tiny kitten making those small, helpless little sounds.

Mewling refers to the act — or the sound — of making a weak, thin, feeble cry or whimper. Think of the tiny, helpless noise a newborn baby makes, or the soft, pitiful sound a kitten or puppy makes when it's cold, hungry, or separated from its mother.
A mews is a row of small homes or apartments that were originally built as stables — places to keep horses and horse-drawn carriages.

A mezzanine is a partial floor — or an intermediate level — that sits between two main floors of a building. It is a level inserted into the vertical space between one floor and the next, rather than being a complete, full-sized floor of its own.
A miasma is a cloud or mass of something deeply unpleasant — something foul, toxic, or suffocating — that seems to hang in the air and wrap around everything it touches.
Foul, heavy, and polluted, like poisonous air rising from a swamp. Figuratively, describing an unpleasant, oppressive atmosphere that seems to spread and infect everything.

A microaggression is a brief, everyday statement, action, or environmental signal that communicates a negative or demeaning message to a person because of their membership in a marginalized group — such as their race, gender, sexual orientation, religion, disability, or national origin.
A microbe is any living organism so tiny that you cannot see it with your naked eye. To observe one, you need a microscope — a device that magnifies objects thousands of times.

A microchip is a tiny, flat piece of silicon — roughly the size of a fingernail or smaller — that contains millions or billions of miniaturized electronic components all packed together and working as a complete, self-contained electronic circuit.
A microcosm is a small thing that contains within it all the key features, qualities, and complexities of something much larger.
A micron is a unit of measurement for length — specifically, an extremely tiny length. It is exactly one millionth of a meter.
Middling means neither good nor bad — just somewhere in the middle. It describes something (or someone) that is average, moderate, or ordinary. Not impressive, but not terrible either. Just... okay.

A midget, historically, referred to a human being who is very small in height, but whose body is proportionally normal — meaning all body parts (arms, legs, torso, head) are small but shaped and sized in the same ratio as an average person's body.

Midnight is the exact moment when the clock shows 12:00 at night. It is the precise point that divides one day from the next — the last second of today dies, and the first second of tomorrow is born, all in the same instant.
Midriff refers to the middle section of the human torso — the part of your body that sits between your chest and your hips.
Midst means the middle or interior of something — not the edge, not the beginning, not the end, but the very heart of it.

The adverb "midway" means at or to the middle point — the point that is equally distant from both ends, or roughly in between two things. Think of it as sitting exactly (or nearly exactly) at the centre of something.

A midwife is a trained healthcare professional whose entire focus is on pregnancy, childbirth, and the period immediately after birth. The word almost always refers to a woman in practice, though men can hold the role too.
To midwife something means to help bring it into existence — to guide, support, and assist something new and significant through its difficult process of coming into being.
Mien refers to the total outward impression a person makes — the unified picture of how they look, how they carry themselves, and the general atmosphere or "air" they radiate.

To miff someone means to cause them to feel slightly annoyed or mildly offended. It's a gentle, low-level emotional disturbance — not deep anger, not rage, not serious hurt — but a small sting of annoyance or feeling slighted.

Miffed means feeling mildly annoyed and slightly offended at the same time — a combination of the two. It describes a quiet, low-level displeasure that sits well below anger, but carries just a small sting of feeling slighted or disrespected.
A migrant is a person who moves from one place to another to live or work there. The defining feature of a migrant is movement — leaving one place and going to another.
To migrate means to move from one place to another — usually over a long distance — and to settle there, at least for a significant period of time.

Migration means the movement of someone or something from one place to another — usually over a meaningful distance, for a specific reason, and often as part of a larger pattern rather than a single random event.
