Migratory is an adjective that describes anything connected to the act of moving regularly from one place to another — and usually back again. It comes from the noun migration, which is that very act of movement.
A milestone is a significant event or achievement that marks an important stage in a journey, a process, a project, or a person's life.

Milieu means the social and cultural environment that surrounds a person — the entire human world they live within: the kinds of people around them, the social class they belong to, the values and norms that feel "normal" in their world, and the cultural atmosphere of their community or era.

Militancy is the state or quality of being fiercely, aggressively, and uncompromisingly active in pursuing a cause — and being willing to fight hard for it, even through confrontational or extreme means.

When you call someone or something militant, you are saying they pursue a cause or belief in a way that is aggressively forceful, confrontational, and absolutely uncompromising — often going far beyond what most people would consider normal or acceptable.

A militant is a person who believes strongly in a cause and actively fights for it — but in a way that is aggressive, forceful, confrontational, or sometimes violent. The word is not just about what someone believes.

Militarism is the belief that a country's military power should be the most important thing it has — and that building, glorifying, and using that power is the best way to solve problems, gain respect, and achieve national goals.

Militaristic describes a strong, often excessive belief that military power is the most important tool a nation, person, or group can have — and that it should be used aggressively, proudly, and often, even in situations where peaceful solutions exist.

To militate means for something to act as a powerful force that works against (or occasionally for) a particular outcome. Think of it as a circumstance or factor that pushes hard in one direction — usually against something happening or succeeding.

A militia is a group of ordinary civilians — regular people from society — who are organized and armed to function as a military or fighting force. They are not professional soldiers. They do not belong to a country's official, permanent army.
A milking stool is a small, low, lightweight seat that dairy farmers traditionally used when hand-milking a cow, goat, sheep, or similar animal.

The verb mill has one central idea running through all its uses: working material through mechanical force to transform it. From that core, it branches into five distinct meanings — from grinding grain to a crowd of confused people.
A millennium is a period of exactly 1,000 years. It is a unit of time — a way humans measure and talk about very long stretches of history.

A milliner is a person who designs, makes, and/or sells hats — particularly women's hats. If you walked into a shop 150 years ago to buy a decorated hat, the skilled person behind the counter who made it and could fit it to your head was a milliner.
A milquetoast is a person who is so timid, meek, and spineless that they cannot — or simply will not — stand up for themselves. They are, in the most vivid sense, a human doormat.

A mime is a performer — and also the art form that performer practices — in which a person tells a story, expresses emotions, or creates a scene using only their body: movements, gestures, posture, and facial expressions. No words. No sounds.
Mimesis means imitation or representation — but not in the shallow sense of mere copying.
Mimetic simply means relating to, involving, or based on imitation.
To mimic something means to closely copy or imitate it — the way it looks, sounds, moves, or behaves — in a way that produces a strong resemblance to the original.

Mimicry is the act of closely copying or imitating someone or something — their appearance, sounds, movements, or behavior — often so accurately that the copy can be mistaken for the original, or at least strongly resembles it.
A minaret is a tall, slender tower built as part of a mosque — the Islamic place of worship — from which Muslims are called to prayer.

Something is minatory when it carries a threat. It signals danger, warns of harm, or communicates — often without words — that punishment, violence, or something bad is coming. In a single phrase: minatory means threatening or menacing in nature.
To cut food into very small pieces. "Not to mince words" means to speak bluntly. To mince can also mean to walk with short, dainty, affected steps.
When we call something or someone mincing, we mean they are being artificially delicate, overly dainty, or excessively careful in a way that looks or feels put-on — not natural.
Mind-boggling describes something so extreme, so vast, or so astonishing that your mind struggles to fully grasp or process it.
Mindfulness is the state of being fully and calmly aware of what is happening right now — in your own mind, body, and surroundings — without judging it as good or bad.
A mindset is the collection of beliefs, attitudes, and assumptions that a person holds about themselves, others, and the world — beliefs that shape how they think, feel, and behave.
A situation or subject full of hidden dangers or difficulties, as in "a legal minefield." Literally, an area of land or water in which explosive mines have been laid.
A miner is a person whose job involves extracting something valuable that is hidden — usually deep underground or within a large mass of material — by digging, drilling, or using machines.
Mingle means to come together and mix, without completely losing individual identity.
Miniature describes something that is much smaller than the usual or standard size of that thing, while still having the same shape, details, and features as the original.
Something is "minimal" when it is as small, as little, or as simple as possible — reduced to the lowest level that still counts as something.

When you call something minimalist, you mean it has been stripped down to only what is essential — nothing extra, nothing decorative, nothing unnecessary. Every element that exists serves a clear purpose.
To minimize something means to make it as small or as little as possible — or to treat it as if it is smaller or less important than it really is.

A minion is a person who blindly follows and obeys a more powerful person, doing whatever that person says — no questions asked, no pushback, no independent thinking. Think of a minion as a human puppet whose strings are pulled by someone more powerful.

A minister is someone who holds an official position of authority and acts on behalf of a larger body — whether a government, a church, or a country. The word has two major areas of meaning: government and religion.
"Ministerial" has two distinct lives depending on context — one in government and religion, and one in law and administration. You need to understand both to fully own this word.
Ministration means the act of giving care, help, or service to someone, especially to a person who is in need — someone who is sick, suffering, weak, or vulnerable.

"Ministry" always carries the idea of dedicated, organized service — usually in one of two very different worlds: government or religion. In both, there is a sense of duty, responsibility, and purpose.

A minnow is a very small fish — typically no longer than your finger, and often even tinier. Minnows live in fresh water: streams, rivers, ponds, and lakes. They are among the most common fish in the world, found on almost every continent.
"Minor" means lesser — lesser in importance, seriousness, size, or degree, especially compared to something bigger or more significant.
A minority is a group that is smaller in number compared to a larger group that it exists alongside.
A minstrel is a performer — specifically a travelling musician, singer, poet, or storyteller — who entertained people during the Middle Ages (roughly 500–1500 AD).
Minuscule means extremely small — so small that it barely seems to register, or so small that it makes you stop and notice just how tiny the thing actually is.

When "minute" is used as an adjective, it means extremely, almost unimaginably small — so small that it barely registers, or might even escape notice entirely. It goes far beyond simply saying something is "small."
A minute is a unit — a fixed, agreed-upon chunk used to measure something. Depending on the context, it measures either time or angles.

When you do something minutely, you examine, describe, or study it so thoroughly that even the smallest, most trivial details are noticed and accounted for. Nothing — however tiny — escapes your attention.
Minutia means a very small, fine detail — the kind of tiny, specific piece of information that exists within a larger subject, but which most people might overlook or consider unimportant.
Minutiae means the very small, fine, or minor details of something — the kind of details that are so tiny that a general overview of a topic would completely skip them.
A minyan is a group of at least 10 adult Jewish people whose presence together is required before certain Jewish religious activities — most importantly, communal prayer — can take place.
A miracle is an event that is so extraordinary, so beyond what is normally possible, that it fills people with awe and wonder.

Something is miraculous when it is so extraordinary, so far beyond what anyone would normally expect, that it seems almost impossible — as if it could only have happened through some power greater than nature or human ability.

A mirador is a structure — or a designated place — built with one specific purpose in mind: to give you a wide, clear, unobstructed view of the surrounding landscape. Everything about a mirador exists to serve the act of looking out.

A mirage is a naturally occurring optical illusion — something that looks completely real to your eyes, but isn't actually there. It is an image that light creates by bending through layers of air at different temperatures. You are not imagining it.

A mire is deep, thick, wet, muddy ground — the kind that sucks you in and won't let you go easily. Think of a swamp or a bog, not a shallow puddle. It is heavy, sticky, dark, and deeply unpleasant to be trapped in.
To mire something means to cause it to get stuck in deep, wet mud or boggy ground. The subject (a person, animal, or vehicle) becomes unable to move because the ground is swallowing it.

As an adjective, mired describes a person, group, organization, or situation that is deeply stuck in something difficult, unpleasant, or complicated — so deeply stuck that moving forward or getting out is very hard.
Mirth is a feeling of great happiness and amusement that shows itself through laughter, giggling, or cheerful noise.
Mirthful means full of great joy, cheerfulness, and laughter.
Without real joy or amusement, as in "a mirthless laugh."
Miry describes something that is full of, covered in, or resembling deep, thick, clinging mud — the kind that sucks at your feet and doesn't let go easily.

A misadventure is an unfortunate accident or an unlucky incident — something that goes wrong unexpectedly, often while a person is doing something or going somewhere. The single most important idea here is this: nobody planned for it to happen.
Misandry is a deep-seated hatred, contempt, or strong prejudice directed at men or boys simply because they are men.
A misanthrope is a person who has a general dislike, distrust, or contempt for other people — not just one specific person, but humanity as a whole. The key word here is general.
A misanthrope is a person who dislikes, distrusts, or even despises human beings — not just one particular person, but people in general, as a whole.
"Misanthropic" is an adjective that describes a general distrust, dislike, or hatred directed at people as a whole — not at any one specific person or group, but at humanity in general.
Misanthropy is a deep hatred, distrust, or contempt for human beings — not for any one particular person, but for humanity as a whole, or for human nature in general.

A misapprehension is a wrong understanding of something — a false picture that someone has formed in their mind about a fact, a situation, or what someone meant. The person isn't confused or unsure; they are confident.
To misattribute something means to wrongly credit it to — or wrongly link it to — the wrong source, person, or cause.

To misbehave means to act in a way that is considered wrong, rude, disruptive, or unacceptable — by breaking a rule, ignoring expected standards of conduct, or acting against what a situation or authority figure requires.
To miscalculate means to make an error in working something out — whether that "something" is a number, a distance, a cost, or even a real-life situation.
A miscarriage of justice is when the legal system produces a deeply wrong or unfair outcome — most commonly, when an innocent person is convicted and punished for a crime they did not commit.
Miscegenation is a noun that refers to the mixing of people from different racial groups — specifically through marriage, romantic relationships, sexual relations, or having children together.
Miscellaneous describes a group, collection, or set of things that are of many different kinds — things that are varied, mixed, and don't all belong to one single, neat category.
A miscellany is a collection of various, different things — things that are mixed together and don't all belong to the same type or category. The single defining quality is variety.
Mischance means bad luck, or an unfortunate event that happens by chance — not by anyone's fault, not by design, but simply because luck went the wrong way.

Mischief is behavior, actions, or conduct that causes trouble, annoyance, or harm — but with a crucial twist: it almost always carries a sense of intentionality and often a dash of playfulness or cunning.
Mischievous describes someone who enjoys causing small troubles, playing tricks, or behaving in a naughty way — often for fun, and usually without serious intent to harm.
A misconception is a belief that someone genuinely holds to be true, but which is actually false.
Misconduct means behavior that is wrong, improper, or unacceptable — especially when it breaks an established rule, a professional standard, or a moral expectation. It is not just any bad behavior.
To misconstrue something means to interpret it incorrectly — to take the wrong meaning from it.
A miscreant is a person who does wrong — someone who behaves in a wicked, criminal, or deeply immoral way.
A misdeed is a bad or wrong action that a person deliberately commits — something they do that is considered morally wrong, harmful, dishonest, or against accepted rules of good behavior.
A misdemeanor is a crime — but a relatively minor one. It sits in the middle of a scale of criminal offenses. It is more serious than a petty violation, but less serious than the most severe crimes.

When something is misdirected, it means it was aimed, sent, or focused toward the wrong target, person, place, or purpose — when it should have gone somewhere else, or served a different purpose entirely.
A miser is a person who is obsessed with saving money and absolutely hates spending it — even when they have plenty of it, and even when spending it would directly benefit themselves.
Miserable describes a state of deep, heavy unhappiness or suffering — the kind that weighs on you, that you cannot easily shake off. It is far stronger than simply "sad" or "unhappy."
Miserly means being extremely and selfishly unwilling to spend money, even when you have plenty of it.
Misery means a state of deep, intense suffering — the kind that weighs heavily on a person and makes life feel very hard to bear. It is not just sadness or discomfort.

Misfeasance is a legal noun that means the improper or negligent performance of a lawful act. In plain words: you were allowed to do something, you went ahead and did it, but you did it badly or wrongly, and that caused harm.
A misfit is a person who does not fit in with the people, group, or environment around them. The word itself tells you everything: mis- means "wrongly" or "badly," and fit means to match or belong.
Misfortune means bad luck, or a specific event caused by bad luck that brings difficulty, pain, or loss to someone.
A misgiving is a feeling of doubt, worry, or unease — especially about whether something you are doing, about to do, or have decided is actually right, safe, or wise.

When you describe someone or something as misguided, you mean they are acting, thinking, or moving in the wrong direction — based on wrong beliefs, poor judgment, or a flawed understanding of a situation.
To mishandle something means to deal with it, treat it, or manage it in a wrong, careless, or incompetent way — typically causing a bad or worsened outcome.

A mishap is a small, unfortunate accident or an unlucky event — something that goes wrong unexpectedly, but is not serious. It causes minor trouble, inconvenience, or mild embarrassment, but it does not cause major harm or lasting damage.

A mishmash is a disordered, random collection of different things that don't naturally fit together — things that seem like they were thrown in together carelessly, with no clear plan or logic connecting them.
To misinterpret something means to understand it in the wrong way — to get the wrong meaning from it.

To misjudge something or someone means to form a wrong opinion or assessment about it. You look at something, you think about it, you come to a conclusion — but your conclusion is incorrect. That's misjudging.
To mislay something is to put it down somewhere and then forget where you put it, making it temporarily difficult to find.

To mislead someone means to cause them to believe something that is wrong or to take them in the wrong direction — whether through false statements, incomplete information, confusing language, or misleading actions.

When someone is misled, they have been caused to believe something wrong or false — not because they were careless, but because a person, a statement, an image, or a situation pointed them in the wrong direction.

Mismatched goes further. It means the two things conflict or clash when combined. There's a sense of wrongness or awkwardness about the pairing. It's not just that they're different; it's that the combination doesn't work.

A misnomer is a name, word, or label that is wrong or misleading for the thing it is supposed to describe. It's when something gets called by a name that doesn't actually fit it — and that name sticks around and gets used widely, even though it's inaccurate.
Misogamy is a strong dislike of, or deep aversion to, the institution of marriage itself — not to any specific person, but to the idea or practice of getting married.
A misogynist is a person who hates, dislikes, or has a deep prejudice against women.

Misogyny is a strong hatred of, contempt for, or deep prejudice against women — specifically because they are women. That last part is crucial. It is not about disliking a particular woman for something she personally did.
"Misprision" is primarily a legal word. It describes the crime of knowing that a serious crime has happened — and deliberately saying nothing about it. Think of it as the crime of guilty silence.

Misrule means the act or condition of governing, controlling, or managing something badly. The word is built on a simple logic: "mis-" means wrongly or badly, and "rule" means governing or controlling.
"Miss the boat" means to lose an opportunity because you were too slow, too late, or not paying enough attention.

Misshapen describes something that has the wrong shape — a shape that is abnormal, irregular, or distorted compared to what it is supposed to look like. The key idea is that something has a shape, but that shape has gone wrong in some way.
A self-propelled weapon that flies through the air towards a target, often guided. More generally, any object thrown or fired at a target.

A mission is a purposeful task or set of tasks that someone is sent to do, or feels called to do — usually something important, serious, and goal-oriented. The word carries a sense of weight and intention. A mission is never casual or accidental.

When you use "missionary" as an adjective, you are describing something that relates to the act of going out into the world to spread beliefs and convince others to adopt them — most often religious beliefs, but sometimes any deeply held cause or ideology.
A missionary is a person who is sent somewhere — usually to a foreign place or an unfamiliar community — with a specific mission to spread a belief, faith, or cause to others who don't yet hold it.

A missive is a letter — but the word carries a bit more weight than just "letter." When someone uses the word missive, they usually mean a letter that is formal, official, lengthy, or important in some way. Think of it as a step up from a casual note.

To mistrust someone or something means to feel that you cannot fully trust, rely on, or believe in them. When you mistrust someone, you carry a quiet suspicion or inner doubt about them — a feeling that they may not be honest, reliable, or safe to depend on.
To misuse something means to use it in a way that is wrong, harmful, or not what it was meant for.
A mite is a very small creature — so small that most mites are nearly invisible to the naked eye. They belong to the same family as spiders and ticks (they have eight legs, not six like insects).
To mitigate something means to make a bad thing less severe, less harmful, or less painful — without necessarily removing it completely.
Mitigated means made less severe, less harmful, or less harsh than it originally was.

A mitigating circumstance is a fact, condition, or situation that makes a wrongdoing less severe in the eyes of those judging it — not enough to say "the person did nothing wrong," but enough to say "the person deserves a lighter punishment than they otherwise would."
Mitosis is the process by which a single cell copies itself and splits into two cells that are genetically identical to each other and to the original cell.

A mix-up is a situation where something goes wrong because of confusion, a mistake in identity, or a failure in communication — usually between two or more people, things, or pieces of information. The confusion is almost always accidental, not deliberate.

A "mixed bag" refers to a collection of things, people, or results that are not all the same — some are good, some are bad, and some are in between. It describes something that has no single, consistent quality.
A mixed blessing is something that has both good sides and bad sides at the same time. It is not purely good, and not purely bad — it is a combination of both.
Mizzle is a specific kind of weather. It means very fine, light rain — so fine and so thin that it barely feels like rain at all. Think of it as the awkward middle ground between mist and drizzle.

When you describe something as mnemonic, you are saying that it is specifically designed or intended to help a person remember something. "Mnemonic" is a word that lives entirely in the territory of memory.
A mnemonic is a memory tool — something you deliberately create or use to help you remember information that is hard to recall on its own.
A moat is a deep, wide ditch dug around the outer walls of a castle, fort, or fortified town — usually filled with water — whose entire purpose is to protect what's inside from attackers.

A mob is a large group of people who have come together in a disorderly, uncontrolled way — usually driven by a shared strong emotion like anger, excitement, or fear. The word almost always carries a negative or at least cautionary feeling.
Mobile means able to move, or able to be moved easily — especially from one place to another.
Mobility is the quality or state of being able to move — or to be moved — freely, easily, and without restriction.
To mobilize means to bring something or someone from a state of rest or inactivity into a state of readiness and action — usually for a specific purpose.
A moccasin is a soft, flat, flexible shoe that wraps around the foot like a glove. It is one of the simplest shoe designs in the world.
Mochi is a Japanese food made from rice — but not ordinary rice. It is made from a special type of short-grain rice called glutinous rice (also called sticky rice).
To mock someone means to treat them with open scorn or contempt — to make them look foolish, ridiculous, or worthless, usually in front of others or with full intent that they feel it.
Mockery means making fun of someone or something in a way that is cruel, contemptuous, or dismissive. It is not gentle teasing between friends.
When something is described as mocking, it means it expresses contempt and ridicule — it communicates, underneath everything, "I think you are foolish, weak, or beneath me."
A mocktail is a drink that looks, feels, and tastes like a cocktail — but contains absolutely no alcohol.
Mode means a particular way, form, or state in which something exists, works, or is done.
Moderate means not too much, not too little — sitting comfortably in the middle.

Moderation means the quality or practice of avoiding extremes — not going too far in any direction, staying within reasonable and sensible limits. Think of it as the middle ground between "too much" and "too little."
A modest person is often described as unassuming — they don't assume they deserve special attention, even when they do.
Modesty is the quality of not making a big deal out of yourself — your abilities, your achievements, your looks, or your possessions — even when you have every reason to.
A modicum of something means a small amount of it — specifically, the bare minimum that is still worth mentioning. Not a lot. Not even much. Just enough to count.

A modification is a change made to something that already exists — a change that adjusts, improves, or adapts it, but does not replace it entirely or make it unrecognizable. The original thing is still there; it has simply been altered in some way.

A modifier is anything that changes, limits, or adds detail to something else. The word comes from "modify," which simply means to adjust or describe. So a modifier is the thing doing that adjusting or describing.

Modish means fashionable, trendy, or stylish in a way that reflects the current moment. When something is described as modish, it means it is very much "of the moment" — it fits perfectly with what is popular, admired, or considered cool right now.

When you describe something as modular, you mean it is designed and built out of separate, self-contained units — called modules — that can be independently understood, used, added, removed, or swapped without breaking the whole thing.
To modulate something means to adjust or vary it in a deliberate, controlled way — usually in response to a situation, need, or goal.
Modulation means a controlled, purposeful change or variation in something — not a random or chaotic change, but a deliberate adjustment to achieve a specific effect.

A module is a self-contained unit that forms part of a larger system. It is designed to do a specific job on its own — completely and independently — but it is also built to connect or work together with other modules to make up something bigger.
A person's or group's characteristic way of doing something, especially a criminal's habitual method. It is often shortened to "M.O."
A basic rule of logic: if "P implies Q" is true and P is true, then Q must also be true. For example, "If it rains, the ground gets wet. It is raining. So the ground is wet."
A basic rule of logic: if "P implies Q" is true and Q is false, then P must also be false. For example, "If it rained, the ground would be wet. The ground is not wet. So it did not rain."
A practical arrangement that allows people or groups who disagree to live or work together peacefully.

A mogul is someone who has reached an extraordinary level of power, wealth, and influence — usually within a specific industry. The word implies that this person doesn't just work in their field; they dominate it.

A mohel is a specially trained Jewish religious official whose specific job is to perform ritual circumcision — the surgical removal of the foreskin of the penis — on Jewish males, as required by Jewish religious law.

Moiety means one of two parts that something is divided into. It is the formal, precise word for "one half" — though the two parts don't always have to be perfectly equal. The word simply names one portion when a whole is split into two.
To molder means to slowly rot, decay, or crumble away — bit by bit — especially when something is left alone, unused, or forgotten.

A small, furry animal that lives underground and digs tunnels. A mole is also a spy who works secretly inside an organization, a small dark spot on the skin, or, in chemistry, a unit of quantity of a substance.
A molecule is the smallest particle of a pure substance that still holds the complete chemical identity of that substance.
To mollify someone means to calm them down when they are angry, upset, or hostile — to make their strong negative feelings softer, gentler, and less intense.
A mollusk is a type of soft-bodied animal that belongs to one of the largest and most diverse groups of animals on Earth.
To mollycoddle someone means to protect and pamper them so excessively that you actually end up doing them harm — by preventing them from ever facing difficulty, discomfort, or failure on their own.
To molt means for an animal to shed, or cast off, a part of its outer body covering — such as its skin, feathers, shell, or exoskeleton — so that a new one can grow in its place.

When certain solid materials are exposed to extremely high heat, they stop being solid and turn into a thick, flowing liquid. While they are in that liquid, superheated state, we describe them as molten.
A moment refers to time — but the word is flexible. It can mean a tiny slice of time, a fixed point in time, or even importance. Understanding which meaning applies depends on the context around it.
Something is momentary when it lasts for only a very brief instant — a fleeting moment — and then it's gone. It emphasizes extreme shortness of time, usually just a second or two at most.
Momentous means of great importance, especially because of the serious and lasting consequences it carries.
Momentum is the power that a moving thing carries with it, and it depends on two things: how heavy the thing is and how fast it is moving.
Monarchical is an adjective. It means relating to, belonging to, characteristic of, or resembling a monarch or a monarchy.
The political belief that a country is best governed by a monarch, such as a king or queen, who usually inherits the role for life rather than being elected.
A monarchist is a person who believes that a country should be ruled — or at least headed — by a monarch: a king, queen, emperor, or empress.

A monarchy is a system of government in which a single person — usually called a king, queen, emperor, or empress — holds the highest position of power in a country, and that position is typically passed down through a family bloodline rather than decided by a public election.

Monastic is an adjective that means relating to monks, nuns, or the kind of life they live. It describes anything connected to the world of monasteries — the places where monks and nuns live — or anything that resembles that way of life.
Monasticism is the practice of leaving ordinary society behind and dedicating one's entire life to spiritual or religious purposes, usually by following a strict set of rules and disciplines.

A mondegreen is a word or phrase that you hear incorrectly — specifically in a song, poem, or speech — and replace with a different word or phrase that sounds similar but has a completely different meaning.
Monetary simply means "relating to, or involving money."

"Money plant" is not the name of one single plant. It is a popular nickname — a common name — that people around the world use for several different plant species. This is the single most important thing to understand about this term.
A monger is a person who deals in something — either as a seller of a product, or as someone who actively spreads or stirs up something, usually something harmful.

A mongrel is something — most often a living creature — that comes from a mix of different origins, rather than from one single, pure, or clearly defined source. Think of it as the opposite of "purebred" or "pure." The central idea is always mixed origin.

Monies is the formal plural of the word money. It refers to distinct, separate sums of money — amounts that come from different sources, belong to different categories, or are set aside for different purposes.

A moniker is simply a name that someone or something is known by — but with a particular flavor: it's usually an informal, distinctive, or descriptive name rather than an official one given at birth or registration.

Monism is a philosophical belief that says all of reality is, at its deepest level, one single thing — one substance, one principle, or one fundamental "stuff" that everything in the universe is made of or reduces down to.
A monist is a person who believes that all of reality — everything that has ever existed or could exist — ultimately comes down to one single, fundamental type of thing. That's the whole idea.
A monition is a formal warning — a serious, official alert given to someone, telling them to stop doing something wrong, to fulfill an obligation, or to be aware of a danger or consequence.
A monk is a man who has made a lifelong commitment to religious devotion — and as part of that commitment, he steps away from ordinary life.

A monkey wrench is a hand tool used to grip, tighten, or loosen nuts and bolts. What makes it special is that it is adjustable — meaning one single tool can fit many different sizes of nuts and bolts, rather than needing a separate tool for each size.
Monochromatic means consisting of, or involving, only one single color.
Something is monochrome when it involves only one single color — or only different shades (lighter and darker versions) of that one color.
A monocle is a single, small corrective lens worn in one eye only, used to help a person see more clearly.
Monogamous means being in a romantic or sexual relationship with only one person at a time.
Monogamy is the state or practice of having only one romantic or sexual partner — one spouse, one mate, one person — rather than multiple. Think of it as the "one-and-one" principle in relationships.
A monogram is a design made by combining two or more letters — usually a person's initials — into a single, unified symbol or mark.
A monograph is a piece of scholarly writing — usually a book or a long, detailed document — that focuses deeply on one single, specific subject. Think of it as the opposite of a general overview.
A monolith is a single, massive block of stone — typically one that stands upright, towers over you, and was either formed naturally or shaped by human hands.
Very large, solid, and uniform, like a single huge block of stone. Of an organization or system, rigid, unified, and hard to change.
A monologue is a long, uninterrupted speech given by one person — while others are silent and listening (or while the speaker is completely alone).

Monomania means an extreme, all-consuming obsession with one single thing — one idea, one goal, one subject, one grievance — to the point where it takes over a person's entire mental life and squeezes out nearly everything else.

Monomaniacal describes someone (or something, like a pursuit or focus) that is so intensely and obsessively fixated on one single thing that it crowds out nearly everything else in their life, thinking, or behavior.
To monopolize something means to take complete control over it — so much control that others are either pushed out, shut out, or simply have no chance to participate.
A monopoly is a situation where one single seller or provider completely controls an entire market for a product or service — with no real competition.
Of speech, very brief and curt, especially using short words in a way that seems rude or unfriendly, as in "monosyllabic replies." Literally, having only one syllable.
Monosyllabically means in a way that uses very short, minimal words or responses — often just one-syllable words like "yes," "no," "fine," or "sure."

Monotheism is the belief that there is exactly one God — and only one. Not two, not many, not none. One single divine being who created everything and governs all of existence. That is the foundation of the whole idea.

A monotone is a single, unvarying pitch — most commonly referring to a voice that speaks at one flat note, with no rise or fall whatsoever. Every word comes out at the exact same level. The voice is completely flat.
Monotonous describes something that is so uniformly the same — so lacking in variety — that it becomes dull, tiring, and mind-numbing to experience. The heart of the word is the absence of change.
Monotony is the dull, draining experience of too much sameness — when things repeat in such a predictable, unchanging way, for so long, that life begins to feel flat, lifeless, and exhausting.
Monstrosity means something that is shockingly, deeply wrong — whether in its appearance, its size, or its moral nature. It goes far beyond "ugly" or "bad."
"Monstrous" is a powerful, emotionally loaded word. It means something is so extreme — in size, ugliness, or wrongness — that it feels unnatural, shocking, or deeply disturbing.
A montage is a single unified work created by deliberately combining many separate pieces together.
Montane means of, relating to, or living/growing in mountainous regions — specifically the middle and upper slopes of mountains where conditions are cool, moist, and often forested.

A Monte Carlo simulation is a way of solving complex problems — especially ones involving uncertainty or randomness — by running a huge number of random experiments on a computer and observing what tends to happen on average.

A monument is something — most often a physical structure — that is created or preserved specifically to be remembered. It exists to say: "This person, this event, or this idea mattered. Don't forget it."
When you call something monumental, you are saying it is so extraordinarily large, important, or impressive that it rises far above the ordinary. It belongs in a category of its own.

A person's temporary state of mind or feeling, as in "in a good mood." It can also mean the atmosphere of a place or artwork, or, in grammar, the form of a verb showing whether it is a statement, command, or wish.

Moodiness is the tendency of a person to experience frequent, unpredictable shifts in their emotional state — often for no clear or obvious reason, and often in ways that affect the people around them.
To pass time in a relaxed, aimless, dawdling way, which can sometimes lead to creative ideas.
Illegally made strong alcohol, especially whisky. It can also mean foolish talk or ideas, or, in poetic use, moonlight.

To moor means to secure a floating vessel — a boat, a ship, a yacht, a houseboat, or anything that floats — so that it stays in one place and doesn't drift away. Think of it as the water-world equivalent of parking a car and putting on the handbrake.
The ropes, chains, and anchors that hold a boat in place, or the place where it is tied up. Figuratively, the values or principles that keep a person stable, as in "cut loose from his moorings."
If something is moot, it either has no practical consequence (the most common modern use), or it is open to debate (a secondary, older use).

To moot something means to raise or introduce a topic so that it can be discussed, considered, or debated. When you moot an idea, you are essentially putting it on the table for others to think about.
To mope means to feel sad, gloomy, and sorry for yourself — and to just sit with that feeling without doing anything about it. When someone mopes, they are not actively crying or dramatically upset.

A moped is a small, motorized two-wheeled vehicle — something in between a bicycle and a motorcycle. It is built for short-distance travel on roads, runs on a very small engine, and moves at low speeds.
Mopey describes a person (or even an animal) who is in a state of quiet, low-energy sadness — someone who is gloomy, downcast, and withdrawn, often showing little interest in the world around them.
Moral means relating to the distinction between right and wrong, and to whether human behavior is good or bad.
Moral hazard is the tendency for people to take greater risks, or to be less careful, when they are protected from the consequences of their own behavior.

Moral objectivism is the philosophical position that says: moral facts are real and exist independently of what any person, culture, or society thinks or feels about them. Moral truths aren't just opinions. They aren't just cultural preferences.

Moral realism is the philosophical view that moral facts exist independently of what anyone thinks or feels about them — meaning statements like "slavery is wrong" are objectively true or false, not just matters of opinion.
The view that there are no universal moral truths, and that right and wrong depend on a particular culture, person, or framework.
Morale is the overall level of confidence, spirit, hope, and enthusiasm that a person or a group of people feels — especially when facing a challenge, a long task, or a difficult situation.

When we call someone or something moralistic, we mean they are excessively and self-righteously focused on judging what is right and wrong — especially when it comes to other people's behavior — often in a way that feels preachy, lecturing, or superior.

Morality is the set of beliefs, principles, and standards that a person, group, or society uses to judge whether actions, intentions, and ways of living are right or wrong, good or bad, fair or unfair.

To moralize means to talk or write about what is right and wrong — especially in a way that lectures or judges others, as though you are the authority on good behavior and they need to be corrected or reminded.

A morass is a dangerous, muddy swamp — a stretch of wet, soft ground that looks like it might hold your weight but doesn't. The moment you step in, your feet sink. The mud grips you. The harder you struggle to pull yourself free, the deeper you go.

A moratorium is an official, temporary pause on an activity — a deliberate decision to stop something from happening for a set period of time, usually made by someone or a group with the authority to do so.
Morbid means unhealthily focused on dark, disturbing, or unpleasant things — especially death, disease, decay, and suffering. The key word here is unhealthily. It's not just "dark" or "sad."
A natural urge to know about or look at things that are disturbing or unpleasant, especially those related to death, violence, or suffering.

Morbidity means the state or condition of being sick, diseased, or unhealthy. Think of it as the "being ill" side of health problems. If someone has a disease, an injury, or a disability that affects their quality of life, that is morbidity.
Mordant means sharply cutting and darkly biting — used to describe a kind of wit, humor, or criticism that is clever enough to sting and dark enough to unsettle.

"More than meets the eye" means that something — or someone — is more complex, significant, or interesting than it appears at first glance. What you see or notice on the surface does not tell the whole story.
More than someone can shake a stick at
This idiom simply means a very large, almost uncountable amount of something — so many that it is hard to keep track of or even wrap your head around. It expresses overwhelming abundance.
Mores are the deeply held moral beliefs, values, and unwritten rules that a society or group considers absolutely essential to its way of life.
The adjective morganatic almost always appears in one specific phrase: morganatic marriage.

A morgue is a place — usually a room or a building — where the bodies of dead people are kept temporarily. The key word here is temporarily: a morgue is not a final resting place. It is a holding place.
On the verge of dying, or no longer active or effective, as in "a moribund industry."
A moron is a person who is considered very stupid, foolish, or lacking basic intelligence or good judgment.
Morose describes a person who is gloomy, sullen, and bad-tempered in a quiet, withdrawn way.
In a gloomy, sullen, and unsociable way, as in "he stared morosely out of the window."
To morph means to change or transform from one form, shape, or appearance into another.

A morpheme is the smallest unit of meaning in a language. It is the most fundamental building block of words — the point at which, if you break things down any further, the meaning disappears completely.
Morphine is a powerful painkilling drug that comes from the opium poppy plant (Papaver somniferum).
Morphology is the study of the shape, form, and structure of something — and also refers to the actual shape, form, and structure that results from that study.
A morsel is a very small piece or amount of something — most often food, but also used for other things in everyday English.
Mortal means "subject to death." If something is mortal, it will die — it cannot live forever. The word is most commonly used as the opposite of immortal (which means living forever, never dying).

A mortal is a human being — but not just any ordinary reference to a person. The word specifically highlights one defining truth about humans: we will all die someday. That is the entire point of the word.

A mortal enemy is a person, group, or force that is in deep, total, and unrelenting opposition to you — one whose hostility toward you is so extreme that it is considered permanent and absolute. It is not just someone who dislikes you or disagrees with you.
Mortality is the word that names one of the most fundamental truths about life: every living thing will eventually die. No human, animal, or plant lives forever.

A mixture of cement, sand, and water used to hold bricks or stones together. A mortar is also a short cannon that fires shells high into the air, or a bowl in which substances are crushed with a pestle.
A mortgage is a loan you take out to buy property — most commonly a house — where the property itself acts as the bank's guarantee that you'll pay the money back.

To mortgage something means to formally pledge something valuable you own as a guarantee for a loan or obligation — while knowingly accepting that if you fail to meet that obligation, you risk losing the thing you pledged.
A mortician is a trained and licensed professional whose job is to prepare the bodies of deceased (dead) people and to help families arrange and carry out funerals.

A feeling of great embarrassment and shame, as in "to her mortification, she tripped on stage." In religion, it means controlling bodily desires through self-discipline. In medicine, it is the death of body tissue.
If you feel mortified, you feel extremely embarrassed or ashamed — so deeply that you wish you could disappear, hide, or make that moment stop existing.

To mortify someone means to make them feel so embarrassed or ashamed that they almost wish they could disappear. It is not mild awkwardness. It is a burning, sinking, wanting-to-hide feeling — embarrassment turned up to its highest volume.

When something is mortifying, it causes a feeling of intense, overwhelming embarrassment or humiliation — the kind that makes you wish you could disappear, sink into the floor, or turn invisible on the spot.
A mortuary is a place — either a room or an entire building — where the bodies of dead people are kept, cared for, and prepared before they are buried in the ground or cremated (burned to ashes).
The adjective mosaic describes something that is made up of many distinct, individual parts — parts that are different from each other — but which together form a single, unified whole.
A mosaic is a picture, pattern, or image that is built by fitting together many small, separate pieces — each piece being a distinct unit on its own, but together forming a larger, unified whole.

To mosey means to walk slowly and casually, with no rush and no particular urgency. When someone moseies somewhere, they are taking their time, completely relaxed, as if they have all the time in the world.

A mosque is a building where Muslims — followers of the religion of Islam — go to worship God (whom they call Allah in Arabic). It is the central place of religious life for Muslims, much like a church is for Christians or a temple is for Hindus.

Moss is a type of plant — but a very simple and ancient one. Unlike the trees, flowers, and bushes you are probably familiar with, moss is tiny, soft, and grows extremely low to the ground, usually forming a thick, cushion-like carpet or mat.
A mote is an extremely tiny particle — so small it can float weightlessly in the air. Think of a single speck of dust. That is a mote.
To mothball something means to deliberately stop using it for now, while keeping it in a safe, preserved condition so it could be brought back into use later if needed.
A mother lode is the single richest, most abundant, and most important source of something — the ultimate jackpot, the grand central supply from which everything else comes.

Mothman is the name given to a legendary creature — a large, dark, winged, humanoid figure with glowing red eyes — that was reportedly seen by dozens of people in and around Point Pleasant, West Virginia, USA, between November 1966 and December 1967.

A motif is a recurring element — an image, sound, idea, symbol, or pattern — that appears again and again throughout a creative work, and through that repetition, builds up meaning or creates a recognizable effect.
Motility is the biological ability of a living thing — a whole organism, an organ, or a single cell — to generate and control its own movement, from within itself, using its own energy.
To motivate someone means to give them a reason, a desire, or an inner push that makes them want to act. When you motivate someone, you are not forcing them.
When someone is motivated, they have a strong inner drive — a force pushing them to act, work, try, or pursue a goal.
Motivation is the why behind human action — the reason a person does something, and the inner force that gets them moving and keeps them going.
Motivational means relating to motivation — and motivation is the internal force that makes a person want to do something, keep doing it, or push harder at it.
Motley means made up of many varied, different, and oddly mismatched parts — a random mix of things that don't obviously belong together.
When you mottle something, you mark or cover its surface with irregular patches, blotches, or spots of different colors or shades — mixed together in a random, unordered way.
Mottled describes a surface that is covered with patches, spots, or blotches of different colors or shades, arranged in an irregular, uneven way.

A motto is a short, carefully chosen sentence or phrase that expresses the most important belief, value, or guiding principle of a person, group, organization, or country. It is meant to answer the question: "What do we stand for?" or "What guides us?"
A moue is a pout — but a very specific, deliberate, and refined kind of pout.

A furry growth of fungus on old food or damp surfaces. A mould is also a hollow container used to give shape to something poured into it, as in "a jelly mould." Figuratively, a type or character, as in "cast in the same mould."

A small pile or heap of earth, stones, or other material, as in "a burial mound." Figuratively, a large pile of something, as in "a mound of paperwork." In baseball, it is the raised area where the pitcher stands.

A mountebank is a person who deliberately deceives people — usually through a flashy, persuasive performance — in order to gain something, most often money. Think of it as a supercharged, theatrical version of a con artist or a fraud.
To mourn means to feel and/or express deep sadness because of a loss — most commonly, the death of someone you loved.

Mournful means deeply and heavily sad — the kind of sadness that comes from grief, loss, or longing. It describes something (or someone) that is filled with sorrow and expresses it, either through appearance, sound, or feeling.

Mourning is the experience of deep sadness and sorrow that a person goes through after losing someone or something they loved or valued deeply. It is most commonly associated with the death of a person, but it can apply to any significant loss.

A moustache is the hair that grows on a person's upper lip — the area sitting right between the bottom of the nose and the top of the mouth. It is a type of facial hair, and it refers only to that specific strip of hair on the upper lip.
Of hair, a dull light brown colour. Of a person, shy, quiet, and unremarkable.
A mouthpiece is something — either a physical object or a person — that acts as the outlet or channel through which sound, breath, or a message travels outward.

When someone says they will "move heaven and earth" to do something, it means they will try absolutely everything in their power to make it happen. They will spare no effort, give up no obstacle, and stop at nothing to succeed.
When someone says they can "move mountains", they mean they can achieve something that seems completely impossible through sheer determination, effort, or strong belief.
"Move the goalposts" means to unfairly change the rules, requirements, or conditions of something after someone has already started working toward the original goal.

A moveable feast is something (or someone) that is rich, enjoyable, and nourishing — but that changes, shifts, or doesn't stay fixed in one place or time, yet keeps its essential value and pleasure wherever it goes.
When you are moved, you feel a deep, strong emotion in response to something — usually something that touches your heart.
"Movement" means the act or process of moving — a change in position, place, or state. Whenever something shifts from where or what it was, that is movement.
Moxie means the guts, energy, and clever determination to face something hard without flinching — and to push through it with spirit.
"Muck about" is a British English idiom. It has two closely related but distinct meanings, and knowing both will help you use it correctly in any situation.
To muckrake means to actively search for and publicly expose wrongdoing, corruption, or scandalous behavior — especially by powerful people, politicians, businesses, or institutions.
A muckraker is a person — almost always a journalist, writer, or reporter — who digs deep into society's darkest corners to expose corruption, injustice, wrongdoing, and abuse of power.

Muckraking is the practice of digging deep into powerful institutions, corporations, or governments to uncover hidden wrongdoing, corruption, or injustice, and then bringing that information to the public's attention.

A muddle is a state of confusion, disorder, or mess — where things (or thoughts) are all mixed up, tangled together, and hard to make sense of. Think of it as a situation or a mental state where nothing is clear, organized, or in its right place.
To confuse someone or mix things up, as in "you've muddled the dates." To muddle through means to manage somehow without a clear plan. In cocktails, it means to crush ingredients together.

"Muddle through" means to manage to complete something or survive a difficult situation, but without a clear plan, proper skill, or organization. You get through it — but in a messy, confused, disorganized way.
Muddle-headed describes a person — or a person's thinking — that is confused, mentally disorganized, and unclear. A muddle-headed person cannot think in a sharp, logical, or orderly way.
To muffle something means to make a sound quieter, duller, and less clear — as if the sound is being swallowed up or absorbed by something thick sitting in the way.
When a sound is muffled, it is quieter, duller, and less clear than it should be — as if something is standing between the sound and your ears, blocking part of it from reaching you fully.
A mug is a large, sturdy cup used for drinking hot or cold beverages.

A mugger is a person who attacks a stranger in a public place — such as a street, park, alley, subway station, or parking lot — with the goal of stealing their money, phone, jewellery, bag, or other valuables.

A mugging is a crime in which a stranger suddenly attacks or threatens you in a public place — on a street, in a park, in a subway, etc. — and steals your valuables (money, phone, wallet, bag, jewellery, and so on).

Muggy is a word used to describe weather — specifically air or atmospheric conditions — that are warm and very damp (full of moisture) at the same time, in a way that feels heavy, sticky, and deeply uncomfortable.
A mugwump is a person who refuses to commit to one political side — someone who stays deliberately independent, switches allegiances, or simply refuses to pledge loyalty to any group.
A mulct is a fine — a sum of money that someone is forced to pay as punishment for breaking a rule, law, or regulation.

To mulct someone means to take money from them — either as a punishment or through unfair, deceptive means. Think of it as being forcibly relieved of your money, whether by an authority figure or by a swindler.
Mulish means being stubbornly and unreasonably unwilling to change your mind, your decision, or your behavior — even when you are presented with perfectly good reasons to do so.
When you mull something, you take your time turning it over in your mind, examining it from different angles before reaching a conclusion or decision.
A mullet is a type of fish. When people use this word in a fishing, cooking, or marine context, this is almost certainly what they mean.

Multiculturalism is the belief that many different cultures — including different ethnicities, religions, languages, and ways of life — can and should exist together within one society, and that each of these cultures deserves to be genuinely respected, preserved, and valued, not just tolerated.
Multifaceted means having many different sides, aspects, or dimensions.
Having many parts, kinds, or aspects that are all different from one another — richly and impressively varied.
Multiform means having or occurring in many different forms, shapes, types, or appearances.

Multilingual means involving, using, or able to use multiple languages — specifically, more than two languages. When you describe something or someone as multilingual, you are saying that three or more languages are part of the picture.
Multiplicity means a large number or a wide variety of different things existing together — or the state or quality of being many rather than one.

Multitude means a very large number of people or things. But it's not just about quantity. The word carries a feeling of vastness — a number so large that it becomes difficult to fully grasp or count.
Multitudinous means consisting of, or made up of, a very large number of things or people — so many that it feels vast, overwhelming, or almost impossible to count individually.

A multiverse is the theoretical collection of all possible universes — including our own — that may exist simultaneously. The "multi-" means many, and "verse" comes from "universe." So: many universes.

When someone mumbles, they speak in a way that is low, unclear, and difficult to understand. The person does not open their mouth fully, their lips barely move, and the sounds they make kind of blur into each other instead of coming out as sharp, clean words.
"Mumbly" describes something or someone that mumbles — meaning their words come out in a low, unclear, and difficult-to-understand way.
Mumbo jumbo means language, ideas, or practices that sound impressive or serious but are actually meaningless, confusing, or nonsensical.
To mummify means to preserve a dead body by drying it out so completely that it stops decaying (rotting) and stays intact — sometimes for thousands of years.
The word mummy has two quite different meanings depending on the context. One is about a preserved dead body. The other is a warm, everyday word for a mother.
A person who stubbornly sticks to a mistaken belief or practice even after being shown it is wrong. It can also mean the mistaken belief or practice itself.

At its most common and everyday meaning, mundane describes something that is ordinary, routine, and lacking any special excitement or interest. It is the opposite of thrilling, remarkable, or extraordinary.
"Municipal" is an adjective that describes anything belonging to, run by, or related to the local government of a city or town.

A municipality is an officially recognized area — like a city, town, or village — that has its own local government. That government has the legal authority to manage the everyday affairs of the people living within that area.
Munificence means exceptional, large-scale generosity — the quality of giving in a way that is remarkably lavish, open-handed, and impressive in its scale. It is not just being generous.
Munificent means impressively and lavishly generous — generous to a degree that goes far beyond what anyone would normally expect.
A munition is any material, supply, or weapon used in fighting a war — particularly things that are fired, launched, thrown, or exploded to cause damage or destruction.
A mural is a large work of art — almost always a painting or image — created directly on a wall, ceiling, or other large, fixed surface.
Murkiness is the noun that describes the quality or state of being murky — that is, the quality of being dark, cloudy, thick, or hard to see through.

"Murky" describes something that is dark, dirty, and unclear in a way that makes it hard to see through — or to understand. Picture a pond where someone just stirred up all the mud at the bottom. The water instantly becomes dark, thick, and cloudy.

A murmur is a soft, low, gentle, and continuous sound — one that is quiet enough that you have to pay attention to hear it, and often indistinct enough that you cannot make out every detail clearly. Think of it as sound that flows rather than hits you.

A murmuration is the word for a flock of starlings — a common type of bird — when they gather in enormous numbers and move together through the sky in sweeping, swirling patterns. This isn't a handful of birds.
A murrain is a deadly, fast-spreading disease — essentially a plague — that strikes animals, especially farm animals like cattle, sheep, horses, and pigs.
A muse is a source of creative inspiration — a person, place, or thing that stirs something deep inside an artist, writer, musician, or poet and makes them want to create.
To muse means to think about something in a slow, quiet, and deeply reflective way — without any rush, and often without trying to reach a specific answer or decision.

As a food term, mush refers to a grain or cereal — most often cornmeal or oats — cooked with water or milk until it becomes a thick, soft, paste-like mass. Think of the texture of oatmeal, grits, or very soft polenta. These are all mush.
When mushroom is used as a verb, it means to grow, spread, or increase very rapidly — often in a way that feels sudden, large-scale, or hard to control.
Mushy means soft and without firm shape — either physically or emotionally.
When something is "music to one's ears," it means that what you heard (or read, or were told) was extremely pleasing, welcome, or exactly what you were hoping to hear.
A musing is a quiet, slow, reflective thought — the kind of thought you have when your mind is gently wandering and exploring an idea on its own, without being in a hurry to reach a conclusion.

Musky describes a particular kind of smell — one that is warm, rich, heavy, and slightly animal-like. It is a deep, lingering scent, not sharp or fresh. Think of it as the opposite of something crisp and clean-smelling.

Muslin is a type of cotton fabric. More specifically, it is a plain-woven cotton fabric — meaning the threads are woven in the simplest possible way: one thread goes over, then under, then over, then under the threads running across it.

To muss something means to make it untidy, messy, or dishevelled — to disturb its neat, orderly state. Think of it as the act of lightly ruffling or rumpling something that was previously smooth and in place.

To muster means to gather things or people together, or to bring something out from within yourself. Think of it as pulling scattered things into one place — whether those "things" are soldiers, animals, people, or even feelings like courage and energy.
Musty describes a smell — and sometimes a taste — that is stale, damp, and unpleasant. It is the smell of something old, closed-off, and slightly wet that has had no fresh air for a long time.
Mutability is the quality of being able to change, or the tendency and likelihood that something will change over time.

Something that is mutable is capable of being changed, altered, or modified. It is not fixed, not permanent, not locked in place. If something is mutable, it can shift — either naturally over time, or because someone deliberately changes it.
To mutate means to change in a deep, structural way — so that the thing that comes out is noticeably different from what it was before.

A mutation is a change — but not just any ordinary change. It specifically refers to a change that alters the fundamental nature, form, or structure of something, resulting in a version that is noticeably different from the original.
Mute means making no sound, or producing no sound when sound is expected or possible. That is the central thread running through every use of this word.
To mute means to silence or significantly reduce a sound — to make something quieter, or to cut it off entirely. Think of it as a decisive action you take against sound: you choose to suppress it.
Softened or reduced in intensity, as in "muted colours" or "a muted response." Of sound, quieter and dulled.
To mutilate something means to damage it severely — usually by cutting, tearing, or forcibly removing a part of it — so that it is left in a disfigured, incomplete, or unrecognizable state.

Mutilation is the serious, severe, and often permanent damaging or destruction of a body — human or animal — in a way that cuts off, tears away, or badly disfigures a part of it. The damage is not minor.
A mutineer is a person who openly rebels against the authority of their leader or commander — specifically from within an organized, structured group like a military unit, a ship's crew, or a prison.

When you describe someone or something as mutinous, you are saying they are openly defying, resisting, or rebelling against a figure of authority over them — and not just quietly grumbling or feeling unhappy, but doing so in a bold, forceful, and potentially dangerous way.
A mutiny is when a group of people who are supposed to follow orders from a commander or authority figure openly refuse to obey — or violently turn against — that very authority.

Mutism is the state or condition of being unable or unwilling to speak. A person experiencing mutism either cannot produce speech or does not speak, even though they may be fully capable of understanding language and thinking clearly.
A mutt is a dog that is a mix of two or more different breeds — or whose breed is simply unknown. It does not belong to any single, recognized dog breed.
To mutter means to say something in a very low, quiet voice that is hard for others to clearly hear or understand.
Mutton is the meat of a fully grown, mature sheep — typically one that is at least two years old — prepared and eaten as food.
Felt or done by each of two or more people towards the other, as in "mutual respect." It can also mean shared by two or more people, as in "a mutual friend."
"Mutually" is an adverb. It modifies a verb, adjective, or another adverb to express that something involves two (or more) parties equally — each toward the other, or both sharing the same thing.
The word muzzle has three distinct, well-established meanings.
To muzzle something or someone means to forcibly stop them from speaking, expressing themselves, or communicating freely — especially by using power or authority.

Myopia means the inability to see or think beyond what is immediately in front of you — whether that is a physical object close to your eyes, or a problem right in front of you in life. It is the opposite of having a broad, far-reaching view.
Lacking foresight; focused only on the short term without considering the future, as in "a myopic policy." Literally, short-sighted, unable to see distant things clearly.

Myriad means countless, or so many that they cannot be easily counted. When you call something myriad, you are saying there are a vast, overwhelming number of those things — so many that trying to put an exact number on them almost feels pointless.
"A myriad of" means an extremely large number of things — so large that counting them all feels impossible. Think of it as a stronger, more vivid, more expressive way of saying "a huge number of."

A myrmidon is a person who carries out someone else's orders without question, without hesitation, and without any moral judgment of their own. They simply do what they are told — even if those orders are cruel, unfair, or harmful to others.

Myrrh is a natural resin — a thick, sticky, gum-like substance — that seeps out of certain small trees when their bark is cut or wounded. Once exposed to air, this oozing liquid slowly hardens into small, rough, reddish-brown lumps.
Something is mysterious when it is difficult or impossible to fully understand, explain, or know — and this difficulty creates a feeling of curiosity, wonder, or unease in the person encountering it.
Mystic describes anything that belongs to, or has the quality of, mysticism — the belief and practice of seeking a direct, personal experience of God, the divine, or ultimate spiritual reality.

A mystic is a person who believes that the deepest truth about reality — often called God, the Divine, the Universe, or Ultimate Reality — cannot be fully understood through reading, thinking, or reasoning alone.
Mystical describes something that belongs to — or feels like it belongs to — a realm beyond what ordinary human senses and reasoning can fully grasp or explain.
The belief that a person can directly experience God, ultimate reality, or the deepest truth of existence through spiritual insight rather than ordinary thought or the senses.
The state of being completely puzzled or baffled. It can also mean the deliberate act of making something seem more mysterious or complicated than it really is.
When someone is mystified, they are deeply and completely puzzled — so confused that they simply cannot find an explanation, no matter how hard they try. It's not just ordinary confusion.

To mystify someone means to leave them completely confused and unable to explain or understand something. The confusion it describes isn't mild — it's deep, total, and often feels almost magical in its intensity.
Something mystifying is so difficult to understand or explain that it leaves you feeling completely baffled and puzzled — even after you've thought hard about it.

Mystique is the special quality of mystery, fascination, and allure that surrounds a person, place, group, or thing — making it feel powerfully attractive, deeply interesting, and impossible to fully understand or explain.

In its older and most important sense, a myth is a traditional story from a particular culture that tries to explain something deep and important — the origin of the world, the nature of the gods, why humans exist, why we die, or how something in nature came to be the way it is.
Larger than life, legendary, or heroic, as in "a figure of mythic proportions." It can also mean relating to myths, or imaginary and not real.
Mythical means belonging to, or resembling, a myth.

To mythologize something means to take something real — a person, an event, a place, even an entire era — and, through stories, retellings, and accumulated imagination, gradually transform it into something legendary.

Mythology refers to a collection of traditional stories that belong to a particular culture, religion, or group of people. These stories — called myths — were passed down through generations, often long before written language existed.
The set of beliefs, stories, and values that shape a group, culture, or fictional world, as in "the Star Wars mythos." It can also mean a whole body of myths belonging to a culture.
A mélange is a mixture of several different, often quite varied things existing together in one place, one moment, or one thing.
A sexual or romantic relationship involving three people who live together.
A mésalliance is a marriage between two people of very different social classes, especially when one person is considered to be far "above" the other in terms of rank, wealth, or social standing.

A métier is the field of work, type of activity, or domain in which a person has not just experience, but exceptional natural skill — the thing they were seemingly built to do. It is their area of highest competence and deepest fit.
A nabob is a person of enormous wealth and power — not just comfortably rich, but extravagantly, almost obscenely rich.
Nacre is the smooth, shiny, rainbow-like substance found on the inside surface of certain seashells.
Nacreous means looking like, or having the qualities of, mother-of-pearl.
The lowest or worst point of something, as in "the nadir of his career." In astronomy, it is the point in the sky directly below an observer.
"Naff" is a British English adjective used to describe something that is lacking in taste, style, or quality — in a way that makes it feel a little embarrassing, cringe-worthy, or simply uncool.
To nag someone means to repeatedly ask, remind, or criticize them about something, usually in a persistent and irritating way. The key idea is repetition — it is not just asking once.
In Greek mythology, a female water spirit who lives in and guards a river, spring, or lake. In biology, a naiad is the water-living young of an insect such as a dragonfly.

A naif is a person who is innocent and inexperienced in the ways of the world — someone who hasn't yet learned how complicated, deceptive, or harsh life can be, and who therefore tends to see things in an overly simple or trusting way.

When you call someone naive, you are saying that they lack real-world experience, and because of that, they think in an overly simple or overly trusting way. They see the world as more straightforward, more honest, and more fair than it actually is.

Naivete is the quality of being naive — it describes a state of mind where a person lacks the experience, knowledge, or critical awareness needed to understand how the world truly works, especially its complexities, hidden motives, and dangers.
If you call someone or something namby-pamby, you mean they are weak, feeble, and lacking the strength, boldness, or firmness that the situation demands. It is a word of mild but clear disapproval.

To namedrop means to casually mention the name of a famous, powerful, or influential person in conversation — not because it's truly necessary or helpful — but to make yourself look important, well-connected, or impressive in the eyes of others.
Napalm is a highly dangerous, sticky, jelly-like substance that burns intensely and is used as a weapon of war.
The nape is the back of your neck — specifically the lower, soft area at the back, right where your neck meets the base of your skull.

Naphtha is a flammable liquid derived mainly from crude oil (petroleum), and it belongs to a category of substances called hydrocarbons — meaning it is made up of molecules that contain only hydrogen and carbon atoms.
A pattern of behaviour in which a person who feels inferior, classically because of being short, overcompensates by being aggressive, bossy, or power-hungry.
Narcissism is an excessive, consuming focus on oneself — one's own importance, appearance, needs, and desires — paired with a deep lack of genuine concern for others.

A narcissist is a person who is so excessively focused on themselves — their own importance, their own needs, and their own image — that they consistently fail to recognise or care about the needs and feelings of others.

When you describe someone or something as narcissistic, you mean that it shows an extreme, unhealthy focus on oneself — one's own importance, appearance, abilities, or desires — combined with a deep need for others' admiration and a striking inability to care about other people's feelings.

Narcolepsy is a chronic (long-lasting, lifelong) neurological disorder — meaning it is a condition caused by the brain not working the way it should. Specifically, the brain loses its ability to properly control when a person is awake and when they sleep.

If something is narcotic, it dulls, numbs, or sedates — it pushes the mind and body toward a state of sleep, numbness, or stupor. Stupor means a heavy, foggy, barely-conscious condition where you're alive but deeply unresponsive to the world around you.

A narcotic is a powerful substance — a drug — that does two things at once: it kills pain and makes you sleepy or unconscious. Think of it as a substance that "numbs" your body and mind. That is its defining character.

A narcotic drug is a substance that acts on the brain and nervous system to relieve pain, produce a deep sense of calm or sleepiness, and create a powerful feeling of pleasure or well-being (called euphoria).
A narrative is a story — but more specifically, it is a connected, ordered account of events or experiences that is told in a way that creates meaning.
A narrator is the person — or voice — who tells a story.

A narwhal is a real, living whale — not a mythical creature, though it has inspired many legends. It is a medium-sized whale found only in the cold Arctic Ocean, mainly around Canada, Greenland, Norway, and Russia.

"Nary" means "not a single" or "not even one." It expresses the complete absence of something — with emphasis. It doesn't just say something was absent; it stresses that even the tiniest, smallest, single unit of it was absent.
Nasal simply means of, relating to, or involving the nose.
Nascence means the process or state of something coming into existence for the very first time — its birth, its earliest emergence, its first moments of taking shape.

Nascent means just beginning to exist or develop. It describes something that is in its earliest, most raw stage — it has only recently come into being and is not yet fully formed, established, or mature.

"Natal" is an adjective meaning of or relating to birth. When you place it in front of a noun, you are signalling that the noun is somehow connected to the event, moment, or circumstance of being born.
Natant simply means swimming or floating on water. It is an adjective, so it describes something — usually a living thing — that is either resting on the surface of water or moving through it.
Natation simply means swimming — the act of moving through water using the movements of the body.
