Nationalism is the belief that people who share a common identity — such as a language, culture, history, religion, or ethnic background — form a "nation," and that this nation deserves to have its own political power, often in the form of its own government or state.
"Native" means originally belonging to or naturally arising from a particular place or condition.

A "native" is someone — or something — that originally and naturally belongs to a place. Not just someone who lives there, but someone who comes from there in the most fundamental sense. Think of it as the opposite of an outsider, a newcomer, or a foreigner.
A policy of favouring people born in a country over immigrants. In philosophy and psychology, it is the theory that certain ideas or abilities are inborn rather than learned.

Nativity means the event or circumstances of someone's birth — not just the fact that a person was born, but everything surrounding that birth: the time, the place, the conditions, and the manner in which it happened.
To natter means to talk casually and at length about things that don't really matter much — light, informal, relaxed conversation between people, usually friends or people who know each other well.
Natty describes someone who looks neat, smart, and stylish — particularly in the way they are dressed.

Existing in nature and not made or caused by people, as in "natural resources." It can also mean normal or expected, as in "a natural reaction," or relaxed and unaffected, as in "a natural smile." A natural ability is one you are born with.
Naturalism is built on one belief: the natural world is all there is, and everything that happens can be explained by natural causes. No gods are needed. No spiritual forces. No magic.

A naturalist is a person who studies, observes, and learns about the natural world — especially living things like plants, animals, birds, insects, and fungi — by watching them in the wild, in their real, natural surroundings.
Naturalistic means relating to, or resembling, what actually exists or happens in the natural world — without idealization, exaggeration, or supernatural explanation.
Naturalization means the process by which something that was once foreign, external, or "not originally from here" becomes fully accepted, established, and treated as if it naturally belongs.

To naturalize something (or someone) means to take something that is foreign, outside, or artificial, and make it fit into a new place so completely that it starts to feel like it naturally belongs there.

"Naught" simply means nothing — a complete absence, an empty result, zero. It is the word you use when you want to say that something does not exist, did not work out, or produced absolutely no result.
Nausea is the deeply uncomfortable, queasy feeling in your stomach — and sometimes your throat — that makes you feel as though you are about to vomit (throw up).
To nauseate someone means to make them feel sick — either physically sick (like wanting to throw up) or deeply disgusted in an emotional or moral sense.

Nauseated means experiencing nausea — that deeply uncomfortable, unsettled, queasy feeling in your stomach where you feel like you might vomit. If you are nauseated, the feeling is happening to you, inside you.
When something is nauseating, it means it causes a feeling of nausea — that horrible, churning sickness in your stomach that makes you feel like you are about to vomit.

Nauseous relates to nausea — that deeply uncomfortable, queasy feeling in your stomach that makes you feel like you might vomit. The adjective "nauseous" describes something that is connected to that feeling, either by causing it or by experiencing it.
Nautical means relating to sailors, ships, or navigation on water. If something is nautical, it belongs to — or has a connection with — the world of the sea, seafaring, and sailing.
The long central part of a church, where the congregation sits. The nave is also the central hub of a wheel.

When something is navigable, it means it can be traveled through or moved across safely and successfully. Think of it as describing a route or path that is usable — one that is open, clear, and physically possible to get through.
To navigate means to find your way through something — carefully, purposefully, and with skill.
Used to add a stronger or more accurate word, meaning "or rather" or "even," as in "it was difficult, nay, impossible." In old or formal use, it simply means "no."
A naysayer is a person who says something will not work, is not possible, or is a bad idea — often before giving it a real, fair chance.
Nazism is a political ideology — a complete, structured system of beliefs about how a country and its society should be organized and governed — that was born in Germany in the early 20th century.
A ne'er-do-well is a person who consistently fails to be useful, productive, or responsible in life — and who, importantly, makes little or no genuine effort to change.

A neap (usually used as neap tide, or in the plural, neaps) is a type of ocean tide that is unusually weak — meaning the sea rises less than normal during high tide and falls less than normal during low tide.
Close to something in distance or time, as in "near the station" or "near the end of the year." It can also mean close to a particular state, as in "near tears."
A nebbish is a person who is so timid, weak, and ineffectual that they almost seem to disappear into the background wherever they go.

A nebula is a vast cloud of gas and dust floating in outer space — not within a planet or a star, but in the space between stars. The gas is mostly hydrogen and helium (the two lightest and most abundant elements in the universe).

Nebulous means something is unclear, hazy, or not well-defined. It describes things that are hard to pin down — ideas, plans, feelings, or situations that exist in a kind of mental fog, where the edges are blurry and the details are hard to grasp.
"Necessarily" means "as a result that must happen / that cannot be avoided."

"A necessary evil" is something that is bad, unpleasant, or harmful in some way, but is still accepted and tolerated because it is seen as unavoidable or essential to achieve something important — or to prevent something even worse.
To necessitate something means to make it necessary — to force it to happen as a result of something else.
Necessitous describes someone — or a situation — marked by extreme, urgent need, especially the lack of basic things required to live, such as food, shelter, clothing, or money.

When two people, teams, or things are neck and neck, they are so close to each other in a competition or race that it is almost impossible to say who is winning. Neither one has a clear lead. They are essentially tied, matched point for point, step for step.
"Neck of the woods" is an informal noun phrase that means a specific area, region, or neighborhood — particularly the one where a person lives, comes from, or is currently in.
A necrology is a list or record of people who have recently died, usually within a specific time period or within a specific group — such as a religious community, an institution, or a profession.

A necromancer is a person who is believed to communicate with the dead — and often to control them — using supernatural or magical power. The entire identity of a necromancer revolves around one thing: the dead.

Necromancy is a type of magic — specifically, magic that involves the dead. Necromancy means using supernatural power to either communicate with the spirits of dead people, or to raise and control dead bodies.
Necrophilia is a noun that refers to a sexual attraction to, or sexual activity with, dead bodies (corpses).
A necropolis is a large, ancient burial site — essentially a vast city built for the dead. Think of it as a cemetery, but on a much grander, more elaborate, and historically significant scale.
Necrosis is the death of living tissue inside a living body, caused by something going wrong — not as part of a natural, planned process.

"Necrotic" is an adjective that describes something as being in a state of, relating to, or caused by necrosis — the localized death of tissue or cells inside a living body. That last part is crucial.

When you needle someone, you deliberately irritate or provoke them — usually through repeated, pointed remarks or persistent teasing that gets under their skin. Think of the noun: a needle is thin and sharp.
Needless means not needed — something that did not have to happen, did not have to exist, or did not have to be done, because there was no good reason for it and it could have been avoided.
Nefarious means deeply wicked, criminal, or evil — especially in a way that is deliberate, scheming, and morally repulsive.

To negate something means to completely cancel it out, make it have no effect, or make it no longer true. Think of it like a mathematical negative sign. When you put a "−" in front of something, it reverses or destroys the value.
Negation means the act of saying "no" to something, or the result of that act. More precisely, it is the act of denying, rejecting, or cancelling something — or the state that results from doing so.

The single thread running through every use of "negative" is this: it points to the opposite side, the absent side, or the unfavorable side of something. Think of a coin — one face is positive, the other is negative.

Negativity is the state, quality, or atmosphere of being negative — meaning the presence of pessimism, discouragement, hostility, or a persistent focus on what is wrong, bad, or unlikely to succeed, rather than what is good, possible, or hopeful.

To neglect something or someone means to fail to give them the care, attention, or effort they need and deserve — either because you chose not to, or because you were too busy, distracted, or careless to do so.

Negligence is the failure to take the care that a sensible, responsible person would reasonably take in a given situation — when that failure causes harm, or creates a serious risk of harm, to someone.
Negligent describes a person (or their behavior) that fails to take the reasonable care that the situation requires — and because of that failure, harm, damage, or risk results (or could result).
Something is negligible when it is so small, so minor, or so unimportant that it can be safely ignored without making any real difference.
Open to discussion or change, as in "the price is negotiable." It can also mean able to be passed over or travelled through, or, of a cheque, able to be transferred to another person.

To negotiate means to have a back-and-forth discussion with one or more people in order to reach an agreement that everyone can accept — especially when those people have different or conflicting interests.
Negotiation is a conversation between two or more parties who have different interests or needs, with the goal of reaching an agreement that all of them can accept.
A neigh is the loud, distinctive vocal sound that a horse makes.
"Neighboring" means "located next to or very close to something else."
When someone says something is "neither here nor there," they mean it is irrelevant — it does not matter, it does not change anything, and it has no real connection to the main point being discussed.

A nemesis is someone or something that brings about another person's downfall, defeat, or ruin — and crucially, this downfall is usually deserved. Think of it as the universe's way of evening the score.
Describing a style of architecture, especially of the 19th century, that deliberately revives the Gothic style of medieval cathedrals, with pointed arches and soaring spires.
"Neoclassical" means inspired by, reviving, or built upon the style and ideas of ancient Greece and Rome, but applied in a later era.

A neologism is a word, phrase, or expression that is newly invented and has recently entered a language. It can also be an existing word that has been given a brand-new meaning that it never had before.
Neonatal is an adjective used in medicine and science. It describes anything that relates to a newborn baby during the very first phase of its life — specifically, the first 28 days after birth.

A neonate is a newborn human baby that is no more than 28 days old — counting from the very day of birth up to and including the 28th day of life. The moment a baby turns 29 days old, it is no longer called a neonate.
A neophyte is a person who is brand new to something — a skill, a subject, a job, an organization, or a belief system. They have just started and have little or no real experience yet.
Neoteric simply means new, modern, or of recent origin.
Nepenthe means a drug, drink, or — more broadly — anything that makes you forget your pain, grief, or sorrow.
Nephritic is a medical adjective that means relating to, caused by, or characteristic of nephritis — where nephritis is inflammation of the kidneys.

Nepotism is the practice of using your power or position to give unfair advantages — such as jobs, promotions, contracts, or other opportunities — to your family members or close friends, not because they deserve it, but simply because of who they are to you.

A nerd is a person who has a deep, intense, and passionate interest in a specific subject — usually one that is intellectual, technical, or academic in nature — and who dedicates a significant amount of their time and energy to it.

At its most literal, a nerve is a thin, thread-like structure inside your body. Your body contains billions of them. They run from your brain and spinal cord to every single part of you — your fingers, your toes, your eyes, your skin.
When you feel nervous, you feel a mix of worry, unease, and tension — usually about something that is coming up or something you are not certain about.
In American English, bold and cheeky, as in "a nervy move." In British English, nervous and easily agitated.

Nescience means the state of not knowing something — a complete absence of knowledge or awareness about a particular thing. It is simply the condition of being without knowledge, whether about a specific subject, a fact, an event, or anything else.

Nescient simply means "not knowing" or "lacking knowledge." If someone is nescient of something, they do not know it — they exist in a state of ignorance or unawareness about it. It describes a gap: the space where knowledge could be, but isn't.
A nest egg is a sum of money you save over a long period of time — money you set aside carefully and do not touch — so that it can grow and provide you with financial security in the future.

To nestle means to settle into a position that is snug, warm, and sheltered — a position that feels just right, like fitting perfectly into a cozy little space. The key feeling the word carries is one of comfort, closeness, and gentle protection.
When something is described as nestled, it is sitting snugly, comfortably, and securely within or among the things that surround it — in a way that feels sheltered, tucked in, or partly hidden.
Nether means lower or situated further down, particularly when referring to something beneath the surface, underground, or at the bottom of something. Think of it as the opposite of "upper."
Netherworld means a place that exists below or beneath — hidden from the normal, visible world above. Think of it as the opposite of the bright, open world you live in.

A neti pot is a small container, shaped roughly like a tiny teapot or a genie lamp, designed specifically for rinsing the inside of your nose with a saline (saltwater) solution. The long, narrow spout is shaped to fit snugly into a nostril.

A nettle is a common wild plant — a weed, really — that is most famous for one thing: it stings you when you touch it. This single quality has shaped everything about how the word is used, both literally and figuratively.

To nettle someone means to irritate or annoy them — but not in a vague, general way. It's a very specific kind of irritation: the sharp, stinging kind that gets under your skin and is hard to shake off.

When someone is nettled, they are feeling mildly but sharply irritated or annoyed — typically because of something someone said or did. It is the feeling you get when a comment, a remark, or a situation pokes at you in a way that is hard to ignore.
Something nettlesome is irritating, annoying, and difficult to deal with — all at once. It describes things (and sometimes people) that get under your skin and give you trouble at the same time.
Neuralgia is a noun that refers to sharp, intense pain that follows the path of a nerve — pain that originates within or along a nerve itself, rather than in a muscle, a joint, or an organ.
A neurologist is a medical doctor who specializes in diagnosing and treating diseases and disorders of the nervous system.
Protein molecules on the surface of nerve cells that receive chemical messages from neurotransmitters, allowing nerve signals to pass from one cell to the next.

A neurosis is a mental or emotional condition in which a person experiences persistent, excessive psychological distress — such as anxiety, fear, obsessive thoughts, or irrational feelings — that disrupts their day-to-day life, but without them losing touch with reality.
Excessively anxious, worried, or obsessive, in a way that is out of proportion to the situation. In older psychology, relating to neurosis.

Neuroticism is a personality trait that describes how emotionally sensitive, reactive, and unstable a person tends to be — particularly when it comes to negative emotions like anxiety, fear, sadness, guilt, anger, and frustration.
Neurotypical describes a person whose brain develops and functions in the way that is considered standard or typical for most people in society.

"Neutral" means not taking either side — or more broadly, not leaning in any particular direction. Picture a perfectly balanced scale, the needle pointing straight to the middle, touching neither left nor right. That middle position is what neutral means.

Neutralize means to cancel out the power, effect, or danger of something — to bring it to zero. When you neutralize something, you don't simply reduce it. You eliminate its ability to affect you entirely.
Nevermore means "never again" — that something will not happen at any point in the future, from this moment onward, for all time. It signals a permanent, absolute end to something.
"Nevertheless" means "in spite of that" or "even so." You use it to say that something is true or happened despite a reason that would make you expect the opposite.

"New" points to a break from the past. Something is new when it did not exist before, was not present before, or was not known before — and has only recently come to be, to arrive, or to be encountered.

When someone gets a new lease on life, it means they have been given a fresh chance to live, enjoy, or experience life with renewed energy, hope, and enthusiasm — usually after going through something difficult, dangerous, or exhausting that made them feel like their time or happiness was running out.
The large post at the top or bottom of a staircase that supports the handrail. It is also the central pillar around which a spiral staircase winds.

Newfangled describes something that is recently invented or newly introduced, but the word carries an important extra layer: the person using it is skeptical, suspicious, or mildly disapproving of it.
Newfound describes something that you have recently discovered, gained, or experienced — something that wasn't part of your life before, but now is.
"Next" means immediately following — the one that comes right after, with no gap and no skip.
Next of kin refers to a person's closest living relative — the family member (or members) who are most closely related to them by blood, marriage, or in some cases, legal adoption.

Nexus means a connection or link between two or more things — but not just any ordinary connection. It implies a connection that is meaningful, important, and often central to understanding how things relate to each other.

The most well-known meaning of nib is the small, pointed metal tip at the front end of a fountain pen — the type of pen that holds liquid ink inside it. The nib is the part that actually touches the paper when you write.
A nibble means a small, gentle bite — not a big chomp, not a full mouthful, but a tiny, light bite taken from something.
A fine or subtle detail or distinction, as in "the niceties of the law." It can also mean a small, polite social custom, or great precision, as in "judged to a nicety."
A niche is a specific, well-fitted space — carved out with purpose, where something belongs perfectly.
Nickel is a naturally occurring metallic element found in the earth's crust. It is hard, shiny, and silvery-white in color — similar in appearance to silver.
A nicker is the soft, gentle, low-pitched sound that a horse makes — often described as a rumbling or vibrating sound coming from deep in the throat, with the mouth closed or barely open.
When a horse nickers, it makes a soft, low, gentle sound — a quiet, rumbling call that comes from deep in its throat. Think of it as a horse's version of a warm, hushed greeting.
To nictitate means to blink or wink — specifically, to rapidly close and reopen an eye. If your eye nictitates, it blinks.
A nidus is a place where something begins, takes hold, and grows — a focal point of origin. Think of it as a "home base" from which something spreads or develops.

"Nifty" is an informal adjective you use to say that something is cleverly made, impressively effective, or attractively stylish — in a way that makes you genuinely appreciate it. Think of it as a warm little compliment.

A niggard is a person who is extremely unwilling to spend money or give anything away — even when they can clearly afford to. Think of someone who clings to every single penny with almost irrational tightness.
Niggardly means extremely and unpleasantly unwilling to give, spend, or share.

To niggle means to persistently bother, annoy, or worry — but only in a small, minor way. Think of it as a tiny itch you can't quite scratch, or a small stone stuck inside your shoe. It's not serious. It's not overwhelming.
Small but persistent and annoying, as in "a niggling doubt" or "a niggling injury." It can also mean overly concerned with small details.
Nigh simply means near or close. If something is nigh, it is not far away — either in distance or in time.
Nightfall means the time when night begins — the moment, or the brief period, when daylight finally fades and darkness takes over the sky.
Nightmarish means having the qualities of a nightmare — that is, something so deeply unpleasant, frightening, chaotic, or disturbing that it feels like a bad dream you cannot escape.
A nightshade is a plant. More specifically, it refers to plants that belong to a large botanical family called Solanaceae — commonly known as the nightshade family.
Nihilism is the philosophical belief that life, existence, and the universe have no inherent meaning, purpose, truth, or value.
The belief that life has no meaning or purpose and that moral values are baseless. It can also mean the rejection of all religious and moral principles, or the belief that nothing can be known.

A nihilist is a person who believes that life has no inherent meaning, no real purpose, and no objective moral truth — and that everything humans consider deeply important (justice, God, love, success, right and wrong) is simply something we invented, not something we discovered.

Nihilistic describes a person, attitude, belief, work of art, or behavior that reflects the view that nothing has any real meaning, purpose, or value — that life is pointless, morality is a fiction, and there is no truth worth standing for.
Nimble means quick, light, and precise in movement or thought — and making it look effortless.
A halo or circle of light around the head of a holy figure in art. In weather, a nimbus is a dark rain cloud. Figuratively, an aura surrounding a person or thing.
Nimiety means excess — the state of having, doing, or saying too much of something, past the point of what is needed, appropriate, or useful.

A nincompoop is a foolish, silly, or stupid person — someone who consistently shows a lack of good sense, clear thinking, or basic competence. It describes a person who does or says things that make others think, "How could anyone be that clueless?"

A nine days' wonder is a person, event, or thing that creates enormous excitement, attention, or buzz — but only for a very short time. After a brief period, everyone quickly loses interest and moves on, as if it never happened.
Nip means to make a sudden, sharp, small action — usually involving biting, pinching, cutting, or moving. Think of it as something quick and precise, not slow and heavy.
To go somewhere quickly and briefly, as in "I'll just nip in to the shop" (British informal). It can also mean to take in a garment to make it tighter at the waist.
A state of perfect happiness or peace, as in "a chocolate lover's nirvana." In Buddhism, it is the final goal of enlightenment, in which suffering, desire, and the cycle of rebirth come to an end.
A nit is the tiny egg laid by a louse — a small, wingless parasitic insect that lives on the human body, usually in hair.
Nitid means bright, lustrous, and polished-looking — the kind of smooth, clean shine you see on a surface that reflects light beautifully and evenly.
To nitpick means to find and point out very small, minor faults or errors in something — usually when those faults are so tiny that they barely matter, or don't matter at all in the bigger picture.

A nitwit is a stupid or foolish person — someone who lacks good sense, clear thinking, or basic intelligence. When you call someone a nitwit, you are saying they did or said something noticeably silly, dim-witted, or lacking in judgment.
Niveous means resembling snow — specifically, having the pure, bright, clean white color of fresh snow.
To nix something means to firmly say no to it, reject it, cancel it, or put a complete stop to it. When someone nixes something, they shut it down — often with authority and finality.
"No cap" simply means "I'm not lying" or "I'm being completely serious."
"No cigar" means you almost succeeded, but you didn't quite make it. It is used when someone comes very close to a goal but falls just short of actually achieving it.
"No shit" is a vulgar, informal English expression. It is used to say: "That is completely obvious. I already knew that."

The No-Cloning Theorem states that it is physically impossible to make a perfect copy of an unknown quantum state. This is not a technological limitation — it is a hard law of nature, as fundamental as gravity.

The no-hair theorem says this: No matter what a black hole is made of, no matter how complex or rich the history of everything that fell into it, a black hole can be completely and perfectly described by just three numbers: its mass, its electric charge, and its spin (angular momentum).
To tamper with a racehorse to stop it from winning. It can also mean to bribe or threaten someone to influence them, to secretly ruin a plan, or to catch someone's attention (British informal).
"Nobility" carries two distinct but connected meanings. Understanding both will cover every use of this word you will ever encounter.
Noble means elevated above the ordinary — and this idea of elevation runs through every meaning of the word.

Noblesse oblige is the idea that people who hold great privilege — whether through wealth, power, rank, or social status — have a moral duty to act with generosity, honor, and responsibility toward those who have less.

Noctilucent is an adjective that describes something that glows or shines at night — specifically, something that is visible and luminous during the darkness of night, either by reflecting light from another source or by emitting its own glow.

Nocturnal is an adjective that simply means "of, relating to, or happening during the night." When you describe something as nocturnal, you are saying it belongs to the night — it happens at night, it exists at night, or it comes alive at night.
A nocturne is a work of art — most commonly a piece of music, but sometimes a painting — that captures the feeling, mood, and atmosphere of the night.

Nocuous means harmful — capable of causing damage, injury, or hurt. When something is described as nocuous, it poses a real threat to health, safety, wellbeing, or morals. It is not just unpleasant or annoying — it actively has the potential to do harm.
A nodule is a small, rounded lump or solid mass — a little knot-like bump that stands out from the material or tissue surrounding it.

Noetic means of, relating to, or based on the intellect — specifically the mind's capacity for pure thought and direct knowing — as distinct from what you learn through your senses, your emotions, or your body.
A person's head or brain (informal), as in "use your noggin." A noggin is also a small measure of alcohol, or a small mug.
Extremely unpleasant and disgusting, especially in smell, as in "a noisome stench." It can also mean harmful to health.
A nom de plume is a made-up or assumed name that a writer uses to publish their work instead of their real name. Think of it as a writer's "fake name for the public."

A nomad is a person who has no fixed, permanent home and moves from place to place as a way of life. The most important idea here is that the movement is not temporary — it is not a vacation or a brief trip. For a nomad, moving around is their normal life.

Nomadic describes a way of life, a pattern of behavior, or a characteristic of a person, group, or animal that involves constantly moving from place to place rather than settling in one fixed location permanently.
Nomadism is a way of life in which a person or a group of people has no permanent home and instead moves from place to place on a regular basis.

Nomenclature means a system of names or terms used within a specific field, subject, or activity. It is the organized, often officially agreed-upon way that a particular community of people names and refers to the things within their area of knowledge.

Nominal means "in name only." When something is nominal, it officially carries a label, title, or number — but that label does not fully reflect reality. There is a gap between what something is called and what it actually is.

Nominalism is the philosophical position that abstract concepts and general categories do not exist as real, independent things in the world. They are merely names — labels we attach to groups of similar individual things.
A nominalist is a philosopher who believes that abstract categories and general concepts — things like redness, beauty, humanity, or justice — do not exist as real, independent entities in the world.

"Nominally" means "in name only." When something is described as nominally being a certain thing, it means the label, title, or official description says one thing — but the reality tells a different story.

To nominate someone means to officially put their name forward as a candidate — for an award, a position, a role, or a responsibility. Think of it as formally raising your hand and saying, "This person should be considered."

A nomination is the formal act of putting someone forward as a candidate — as someone who should be considered for a position, role, honour, or award. It is a proposal that says: "This person deserves to be in the running."
A nominee is a person who has been officially named or put forward by someone — a person, a group, or an organization — for a specific purpose.

A non sequitur is a statement, conclusion, or response that does not logically follow from what came just before it. There is a broken — or completely absent — logical connection between what was said and what comes next.

When something is non-negotiable, it means it is completely fixed and final. It cannot be changed, discussed, adjusted, or bargained about — no matter what. There is zero room for argument, compromise, or flexibility.

Nonage means the state or period of being not yet fully grown, legally capable, or mature — either as a young person who hasn't reached the legal age of adulthood, or more broadly, as anything (a person, an idea, an institution, a civilization) that hasn't yet reached its full, developed form.

A nonagenarian is a person who is between 90 and 99 years old — not a day younger than 90, and not yet 100. The moment someone turns 90, they become a nonagenarian. The moment they turn 100, they are no longer one.
"For the nonce" means for the present time or for this particular occasion. A nonce word is one made up for a single occasion. In British prison slang, it is an offensive term for a sex offender.
Nonchalance is a calm, relaxed, completely unbothered attitude toward something — as if nothing is a big deal, nothing is stressing you out, and you are totally at ease.
Nonchalant describes a person who appears calm, cool, and completely unbothered — especially in a situation where most people would feel nervous, excited, surprised, or stressed.
In a calm and casual way, as if not worried or interested, as in "he shrugged nonchalantly."

When someone is noncommittal, they deliberately avoid giving a clear, direct answer, opinion, or decision. They don't say yes, they don't say no — they say something vague in between that keeps everyone guessing.

To comply means to follow or obey a rule, instruction, standard, or requirement — to do what is expected or demanded of you. Noncompliant simply means the opposite: not following, obeying, or meeting that expectation.
A nonconformist is a person who refuses to follow the accepted rules, customs, beliefs, or ways of behaving that most people in a society or group follow.
Behaviour or thinking that does not follow accepted customs, rules, or beliefs. Historically in Britain, it meant refusal to follow the practices of the Church of England.
Nondenominational means not belonging to, not affiliated with, and not restricted to any specific denomination.
Nondescript describes something — or someone — that is so plain, so ordinary, and so lacking in any standout quality that it leaves almost no impression on you.
A nonentity is a person who is completely insignificant, powerless, unimportant, and forgettable. They have no status, no influence, and no real impact on the world around them.
"Nonetheless" means "in spite of that" or "even so."
Something is nonexistent when it simply does not exist — it has no presence, no reality, and no being anywhere. It is not just hard to find or rare. It is completely and utterly absent from reality.
Nonfeasance means the failure to do something that you were legally required or obligated to do.

Nonpareil means having absolutely no equal. When you describe something or someone as nonpareil, you are saying: this is so extraordinary, so superior, so uniquely excellent that nothing else — past or present — can match it.

A nonpareil is a person or thing so exceptional, so superior, that nothing else in existence can be placed beside it as an equal. Not just "one of the best" — but the best, standing completely alone, with no rival and no match.

Nonpartisan means not supporting or favoring any particular party, side, or group. When something or someone is described as nonpartisan, it means they are trying to be neutral, fair, and independent — not pulling for one team over another.

A nonplus is a state of complete and total bafflement — a mental standstill where a person is so thoroughly confused or bewildered that they genuinely cannot figure out what to think, what to say, or what to do next. They are, in a word, stumped.

To nonplus someone means to surprise and confuse them so completely that they are left at a total loss — unable to speak, respond, or even think clearly about what to do next. The person is not just a little puzzled. They are mentally stopped in their tracks.

Nonplussed means so surprised, confused, or puzzled by something that you are momentarily at a complete loss — you don't know what to say, how to react, or what to do next. It describes a state of being mentally frozen or thrown off by something unexpected.
When "nonprofit" describes an organization, it means that organization does not exist to make money for its owners or investors.
A nonprofit is an organization that exists to serve a purpose or a cause — not to make money for its owners.
Nonsectarian means not connected to, not limited to, and not favoring any particular religious group, denomination, or sect.
Nonsense means anything — words, ideas, behavior, or reasoning — that has no real meaning, makes no logical sense, or is too foolish and wrong to deserve serious attention.

Nonsensical describes something that has no logical meaning, makes no rational sense, or is so absurd and unreasonable that it cannot be taken seriously. When you call something nonsensical, you are saying it fails to hold up to basic reason or logic.
A nonstarter is something — an idea, a plan, a proposal, a suggestion, a request, or a deal — that has absolutely no chance of being accepted, approved, or working out.
Nonverbal means not using or involving words.

Nonviolence is the practice and philosophy of refusing to use physical force, harm, or threats to resolve conflicts — and actively choosing peaceful means instead. It is not merely the absence of violence.

A nook is a small, tucked-away corner or space that feels somewhat hidden, sheltered, or set apart from the rest of a larger area. The key idea is that it is small, partly enclosed, and separate from the open space around it.
"Noonday" means the middle of the day — noon, or 12 o'clock in the daytime. It refers to that moment when the sun has climbed to the very highest point in the sky.
Noontide means the middle of the day — noon, or the time closely surrounding it.

A noose is a loop made in a rope, cord, or wire that has one very special and defining feature: the loop automatically tightens when pulled or when something pulls against it. This is what separates a noose from a regular loop.

Norepinephrine (also called noradrenaline) is a chemical your body naturally produces that acts as both a hormone (a chemical messenger carried in your blood) and a neurotransmitter (a chemical messenger in your brain and nerves).

The word "norm" always comes back to one central idea: a reference point — something used as a baseline for what is considered typical, expected, or standard. Every meaning of this word in English grows from that core idea.

Normalcy means the state or condition of being normal — a time or situation where life is ordinary, stable, and uninterrupted. Nothing unusual. Nothing alarming. Just things running the way they are supposed to run, the way they usually run.
To make something seem normal or acceptable that was not before, as in "normalizing violence." It can also mean to return to a normal state, or for countries to resume normal relations.
Relating to a standard or rule of what should be done, rather than describing what actually is, as in "normative ethics."
A nosegay is a small, compact bunch of flowers — and sometimes fragrant herbs — tied together into a neat little bouquet that you can hold in one hand.

Nosh means food or a snack — something you eat, usually casually and with enjoyment. It is always an informal, everyday word. You would say it to a friend, never write it in a business email or a formal essay.
Nosology is the branch of medical science that deals with the systematic classification of diseases.

Nostalgia is a warm, tender longing for the past. It is the feeling you get when you remember a person, a place, a time, or an experience that once made you feel happy, safe, or at home — and you wish, with a quiet ache, that you could go back to it.
When you feel nostalgic, you are experiencing a warm, tender longing for something from your past — a time, a place, a person, or an experience that you miss deeply.

A nostrum is a fake, unproven, or overly simplistic "cure" or "solution" — something presented with great confidence as if it will fix a serious problem, but which has no real evidence or credibility behind it.
If someone is nosy, they are too interested in other people's private lives, business, or affairs — in a way that is unwanted and intrusive.
"Not the foggiest" means you have absolutely no idea about something. Not a little confused. Not slightly unsure. You know nothing at all about it — zero, blank, complete ignorance.
Notability is the quality of being worthy of notice — of being remarkable, significant, or well-known enough that people naturally pay attention to you, talk about you, or remember you.

When something is notable, it means it is worth noticing and worth remembering — it stands out from the ordinary in a way that deserves your attention. Think of it this way: out of a hundred things happening around you, most fade into the background.

To notarize a document means to have it officially certified by a specially licensed official called a notary public, so that the world — including courts, banks, and government offices — can trust that the document is genuine.

A notary — most commonly referred to as a notary public — is a person officially appointed or licensed by a government to act as an impartial, trusted witness for important legal documents and transactions.

A notary public is an officially licensed, government-appointed person whose job is to act as a neutral, trusted witness when important documents are signed — and to verify that the signing was real, voluntary, and done by the right person.
Notation means a system of symbols, signs, or marks used to represent something — ideas, quantities, sounds, movements — in a clear, compact, and agreed-upon written form.

A notch is a small cut, groove, or indentation made into the surface or edge of something. Think of it as a deliberate bite taken out of an object — usually shaped like a V or a U, going into the material rather than sticking out of it.

Within this meaning, there are a few flavours worth knowing: A personal note is a short, informal message written to someone you know — a thank-you note, a note of apology, a note left on someone's desk.
When something is noteworthy, it means it is worth noticing and paying attention to — because it stands out from the ordinary in some meaningful way.
A notion is a vague, general idea or belief that exists in someone's mind — one that is often loosely held, not fully worked out, and not necessarily proven to be true.
Existing only in theory or on paper, not in reality, as in "a notional sum." It can also mean based on estimates or guesses rather than exact figures.
Notoriety is the state of being widely known — but specifically for something bad, wrong, shameful, or scandalous.
Notorious means widely known for something bad.
When "notwithstanding" is used as an adverb, it means "in spite of that" or "even so" or "all the same."
The number zero, as in "nought point five" (British). In old or literary use, it means nothing, as in "all our efforts came to nought."
"Noumenal" is a philosophical adjective that describes things as they truly and independently exist — completely apart from how any human mind perceives or experiences them.
In the philosophy of Immanuel Kant, a thing as it is in itself, independent of how our senses perceive it — something that can be thought about but never directly experienced.

To nourish means to provide something — or someone — with what it needs to live, grow, stay strong, and thrive. Think of it as feeding, but in the deepest, most caring, most sustaining sense possible.

Nourishment is anything — food, drink, or other substances — that a living being takes in to survive, grow, and stay healthy. When you eat a meal, the vitamins, proteins, fats, carbohydrates, and minerals in that food are the nourishment your body receives.
Practical good sense and intelligence, as in "she had the nous to save early" (British informal). In philosophy, nous is the mind or intellect, the faculty of reason.
A nouveau riche is a person who has recently become wealthy — and who tends to show off that wealth in a very loud, excessive, or tasteless way.

A nova is a star that suddenly becomes explosively brighter — sometimes tens of thousands of times brighter than it normally is — and then gradually fades back down over weeks, months, or sometimes years.

When "novel" is used as an adjective, it means new, original, and strikingly different from anything that existed or was done before. It describes something that feels genuinely fresh — not just new in time, but new in its nature, approach, or form.
A novel is a long, fictional story written in prose — meaning it is written in ordinary sentences and paragraphs, the same way you are reading right now, as opposed to verse or poetry.
A novelist is a person who writes novels. That's the simple one-line answer.

A novella is a work of written fiction — meaning it tells a made-up story — that sits right in the middle ground between a short story and a full-length novel. Think of it as the "middle child" of prose fiction.
Novelty means newness — either the quality of being new and fresh, or something that is new, unusual, or different from what you've seen or experienced before.
A novice is a person who is new to something and has little or no experience in it.
A novitiate is a period of being a beginner — a trial phase that a new person must go through before they are fully accepted as a proper member of a group or community.

Noxious means harmful to health, life, or wellbeing — often in the way that a poison or toxic substance is harmful. When something is noxious, it doesn't just bother you; it actively hurts you or has the real potential to do so.
A nuance is a very small, subtle difference — a slight shift in meaning, feeling, tone, color, or quality that is not immediately obvious, but that matters when you look or think carefully.
Something is nuanced when it recognizes that reality is complex — that most things in life can't be fairly described as simply "good or bad," "right or wrong," or "true or false."

When you dig past all the surrounding details, arguments, noise, and complexity of a topic, and you arrive at the single most essential point — the thing that everything else depends on — that is the nub. Think of it as the seed inside a fruit.
Of a young woman, sexually attractive. In older use, of marriageable age.

To nudge means to gently push or encourage someone or something — either with a light physical touch, or through subtle, mild persuasion. The word always carries the idea of gentleness and small movement. A nudge is never forceful, aggressive, or dramatic.
A nudnik is a person who is a boring, tiresome pest — someone who annoys you not through aggression or malice, but through sheer, relentless tedium.
Something nugatory is so insignificant, worthless, or ineffective that it produces no meaningful result — it might as well not exist.
A nuisance is anything — a person, a thing, a situation, or a behavior — that causes annoyance, inconvenience, or trouble, especially in a persistent or repeated way.
Null means having no value, no force, or no existence at all — amounting to absolutely nothing.
The act of cancelling something or making it legally invalid, as in "the nullification of the contract." In US history, it was a state's claimed right to refuse to obey a federal law.
To nullify something means to completely cancel it out, wipe out its effect, or strip it of all power and validity — so that it becomes as if it never existed or never mattered at all.

Nullity means the state of being absolutely nothing — not just unimportant or weak, but having no existence, no power, and no effect whatsoever. It is the noun form of "null," which means zero, void, or nonexistent.

Numb describes a state in which the ability to feel has been lost or significantly reduced — either in the body or in the mind. Think of it as a kind of "switched off" state. Something that is normally sensitive and responsive has gone quiet.

To numb something means to take away its ability to feel. When something is numbed, it loses sensation — it can no longer feel pain, temperature, touch, or emotion. Think of it as "switching off" the feeling in something, usually temporarily.
When something is numbing, it means it causes you to lose feeling — physically, emotionally, or mentally. It takes away your ability to sense, feel, or react normally.
Numeracy is the ability to understand, use, and think clearly with numbers in everyday life. Think of it as "number literacy."
A numeral is a written symbol — or a spoken or written word — that represents a number.
Able to understand and work confidently with numbers and basic mathematics.
Numeric means "relating to, involving, or consisting of numbers."
"Numerical" means relating to numbers, or expressed in the form of numbers.

Numerology is the belief that numbers have a hidden, mystical meaning that can reveal deep truths about a person's character, life, destiny, and the world around them. A person who practices or studies this belief system is called a numerologist.

Numerous means existing in a large quantity; made up of many individual things or people. When you call something numerous, you are saying there is a big, notable count of it — not just a little, and not just "a few," but genuinely many.

Something is numinous when it makes you feel the overwhelming presence of something divine, mysterious, and far greater than yourself — filling you with awe, reverence, and a kind of trembling wonder all at once.
Numismatics is the study and collection of coins, paper money, and related objects like medals and tokens.
A numismatist is a person who collects, studies, and deeply understands coins, paper money, and related objects like medals, tokens, and ancient currency.
A nuncio is the official diplomat sent by the Pope — the head of the Roman Catholic Church — to represent the Vatican in a foreign country. Think of it simply as the Pope's ambassador.
Nuncupative means spoken aloud rather than written down. When something is nuncupative, it exists as spoken words — declared out loud, in front of other people — instead of being put on paper.

A nunnery is a place — a building or a group of buildings — where nuns live together as a community. Think of it as a dedicated home, workplace, and place of worship, all rolled into one, exclusively for nuns.
Nuptial simply means relating to marriage or a wedding.
"Nuptials" means a wedding — specifically, the ceremony and celebrations that mark the formal union of two people in marriage. When you see or hear this word, think: wedding event.
A nurse is a person who is professionally trained to take care of people who are sick, injured, or in need of medical help.
When you nurse something, you give it careful, gentle, sustained attention — because that thing is either fragile, precious, wounded, or needs time to develop.
A nursery is always a place specifically set aside for caring for, growing, or developing something young — whether that is a baby, a young child, a young plant, or a young animal.
Nurturance is the warm, caring support that a person gives to someone else to help them grow, feel safe, and thrive — emotionally, mentally, and physically.
To nurture something means to care for it consistently and lovingly over time so that it can grow, develop, and become the best version of itself. It is not a single action you do once.
A nutcase is an informal word for a person who behaves in a crazy, irrational, or mentally unstable way.

A nutjob is an informal word for a person who is seen as crazy, mentally unstable, or wildly irrational — someone whose thinking or behavior strikes others as so bizarre, extreme, or unhinged that they cannot be taken seriously.
Nutmeg is a spice — a flavoring used in cooking and food preparation. It comes in two forms: Whole nutmeg: a hard, oval-shaped seed, roughly the size of an apricot pit, with a rough brownish surface.
A nutrient is any substance that a living thing — a human, an animal, a plant, or even a microscopic organism — takes in from its surroundings and uses to stay alive, grow, and function properly.
Nutrition is the process by which a living being takes in food, breaks it down, and uses the useful parts of it to survive, grow, stay healthy, and function properly.

"Nutritious" describes food or drink that is rich in nutrients — the substances your body needs to survive, grow, stay healthy, and function properly. Nutrients include things like proteins, vitamins, minerals, healthy fats, carbohydrates, and fiber.
When you call something nutritive, you are saying one of two closely related things: either that it provides nourishment to the body, or that it relates to the process of nutrition.

A nutter is an informal word — mostly British — for a person who behaves in a crazy, irrational, or wildly eccentric way. When you call someone a nutter, you are saying they think or act in a way that seems completely detached from normal, sensible behavior.
To nuzzle means to gently press, push, or rub your nose, snout, or face against someone or something — almost always as an expression of love, affection, or the desire for comfort.
Nyctophobia is an intense, irrational, and overwhelming fear of darkness or the night.

In Greek and Roman mythology, a beautiful female spirit who lives in nature, such as in a river, tree, or mountain. In biology, a nymph is the young form of insects such as dragonflies and grasshoppers.
A nymphet is a young girl — typically between about 9 and 14 years old — who is perceived by an older man as being mysteriously, unnervingly attractive or seductive.

An oaf is a person who is clumsy, stupid, or socially awkward — or all three at once. It's almost always used to describe a man or boy. The word paints a picture of someone big, lumbering, and blundering through the world without awareness or grace.
An oasis is a small, fertile area found in the middle of a desert — a place where water exists beneath or on the surface of the ground.
An oath is a serious, formal promise — one that carries much more weight than an everyday promise.
Oatmeal starts with oats — a type of cereal grain grown as a crop. Raw oat grains in their whole, unprocessed form are not very easy to eat or cook with directly.

Obduracy is the quality of being stubbornly, almost unmoveably resistant — either to changing your mind, or to feeling guilt and compassion — even when every reason in the world is telling you that you should.

If someone is obdurate, they are stubbornly and completely unwilling to change their mind, attitude, or behavior — even when faced with very good reasons, emotional appeals, or moral arguments to do so.
Obedience is the act of following instructions, rules, commands, or laws given by someone or something with authority over you — and doing so willingly, consistently, and without resistance.
Deep respect or submission shown to someone or something, as in "pay obeisance to the king." It can also mean a gesture of respect, such as a deep bow.
An obelisk is a tall, narrow, four-sided stone pillar that slowly gets thinner as it rises, and ends at the very top in a small pyramid shape.
Obese describes a person who has accumulated so much excess body fat that it poses a serious risk to their health. This is not simply a matter of looking "big" or carrying a few extra pounds.
To obfuscate something means to make it deliberately unclear, confusing, or difficult to understand — usually to hide the truth or avoid giving a straight answer.

Obfuscation means the act of making something unclear, confusing, or difficult to understand. It refers to any process — whether done on purpose or by accident — that muddies, hides, or clouds something that could otherwise be straightforward.

If something is obfuscatory, it makes things harder to understand, see clearly, or figure out. It clouds, muddles, or hides the truth — like throwing a thick fog over something that could otherwise be seen plainly.
An obituary is a written announcement that a person has died, published in a newspaper, magazine, or website.

To object means to express that you are against something — that you disagree with it, disapprove of it, or find it wrong, unfair, or unacceptable. The critical thing to understand is that objecting is not just a feeling you have privately inside your head.
To objectify someone means to treat them as an object — as a thing — rather than as a full human being.
An objection is a reason you give — or a statement you make — to express that you disagree with, disapprove of, or have a problem with something.
Something is objectionable when it is offensive, inappropriate, or unacceptable enough that people have a legitimate reason to oppose or disapprove of it.
When something is objective, it is based entirely on facts and reality — not on personal feelings, personal opinions, or personal biases.
An objective is a specific thing you want to achieve. It is your target — the clearly defined endpoint you are working toward.
Objectively means in a way that is based on facts, evidence, and observable reality — without being shaped by personal feelings, emotions, preferences, or biases.
Objectivity means seeing or judging something as it actually is, based on facts and evidence — not based on your personal feelings, opinions, preferences, or biases.
To objurgate someone means to criticize or scold them in a way that is sharp, severe, and driven by strong disapproval.

An objurgation is a harsh, sharp, and severe scolding directed at someone for something they have done wrong. It is a strong verbal expression of disapproval, criticism, or blame — delivered with force, frustration, or even anger.
An oblation is a gift, offering, or sacrifice presented to God or a divine being as an act of worship or devotion.

To obligate someone means to bind them to do something — through a law, a contract, a promise, a moral duty, or a social pressure — in such a way that they feel or are compelled by a sense of responsibility to follow through.

When someone is obligated to do something, they are bound by a duty or responsibility to do it — meaning they are not fully free to simply skip it or ignore it without some kind of cost or consequence.
An obligation is something you are required to do — not just something you want to do or choose to do freely, but something that binds you to act in a certain way.
If something is obligatory, it means you must do it. You have no real choice in the matter. It is required of you — either by a rule, a law, a duty, or a strong social expectation.
To do something helpful for someone, as in "she was happy to oblige." It also means to require or force someone to do something, as in "the law obliges drivers to carry a licence."

When "obliged" is used as an adjective, it describes a state of feeling compelled to do something — not by physical force, but by an inner sense of duty, conscience, gratitude, or moral/social pressure.
When you describe someone as obliging, you mean they are willing and eager to help — they do what others need or ask without making a fuss, and they do it with a pleasant, cooperative attitude.
Indirect, not stated plainly, as in "an oblique reference." It can also mean slanting, neither vertical nor horizontal, as in "an oblique line."

"Obliquely" means not directly — either in a physical direction (not in a straight line, but at an angle) or in the way something is said or done (not plainly, but through hints, suggestions, or a roundabout approach).

Obliquity means the quality or state of not being straight. Think of a straight line going perfectly horizontal or vertical. Anything that tilts, slants, or deviates from that straight path has obliquity.
To obliterate something means to destroy it so completely that nothing — or almost nothing — is left behind. Not just damaged. Not just broken. Gone. Wiped out entirely.
Obliteration means the act of wiping something out so completely that virtually nothing of it remains — no trace, no sign, no evidence it ever existed. It is total, absolute destruction or erasure.

Oblivion means a state of being completely and totally gone — either gone from someone's memory, or gone from one's own awareness of the world. Think of it as the ultimate form of "nothing left." Not a little forgotten. Not almost gone.
Oblivious means being completely unaware of something that is happening around you, or failing to notice something that is fairly obvious or important.

When you call something oblong, you are saying it has an elongated shape — it is noticeably longer in one direction than in the other. It is not a perfect square, and not a perfect circle. One dimension (length, width, or height) clearly dominates the other.
Strong public criticism or abuse, or the disgrace that results from it, as in "he faced obloquy for his betrayal."
Obnoxious describes someone or something that is so unpleasant, irritating, or offensive that it actively bothers the people around it.
When something is obscene, it is so deeply offensive to people's sense of decency and morality that it shocks or disgusts them.
An obscenity is anything — a word, image, gesture, act, or piece of content — that is considered deeply offensive, disgusting, or morally unacceptable by a society or community.

Obscurantism is the deliberate practice of keeping people confused, ignorant, or in the dark — either by blocking the spread of knowledge, or by making things unnecessarily difficult to understand. The key word here is deliberate. It is never an accident.
Not well known, as in "an obscure poet." It can also mean hard to understand, or hard to see clearly.

To obscure something means to make it harder to see, notice, or understand. Picture placing a frosted glass pane in front of something — the thing still exists behind it, but now it's blurry, hidden, or blocked.
Obscurity means the state of being hidden from attention — either because something is unknown, unclear, or dark. Think of it as the opposite of being in a spotlight.
Obsequies means the formal ceremonies and rituals performed for a person who has died — in other words, a funeral in its full, ceremonial sense.
Excessively eager to please or obey someone, especially a powerful person, in a fawning, insincere way.

Observant describes someone who is very good at noticing things — things that many others would miss, overlook, or simply never register. An observant person keeps their eyes, ears, and mind actively open.
Observation refers to the act of carefully watching or noticing something — and it can also mean the remark or comment you make as a result of that noticing.

An observatory is a place — usually a building or a facility — specially built and equipped for observing and studying things that are far away, most commonly objects in the sky like stars, planets, the Moon, and galaxies.

To obsess means to think about something — or someone — so constantly, so intensely, and so uncontrollably that it takes over your mind. The defining feature isn't just that you think about something a lot. It's that you can't stop, even when you try.
When someone is obsessed with something or someone, it means that thing has taken over their mind.

An obsession is a thought, idea, feeling, image, or desire about a particular person, thing, or subject that keeps returning to your mind repeatedly, is very hard to control or stop, and takes up far more mental space than is normal.

Obsessive describes something — a thought, a feeling, a behavior, or a person — that is driven by an unusually intense, persistent, and hard-to-control fixation on something. When something is obsessive, it goes far beyond normal interest or concern.
Obsidian is a naturally occurring glass — not made by humans, but produced by volcanoes.
Something is obsolete when it is no longer used, no longer needed, or no longer relevant — because something newer, better, or more suitable has taken its place.
An obstacle is anything — a thing, a person, a situation, or even a feeling — that stands in your way and makes it harder or impossible to move forward, reach a goal, or complete something.
An obstetrician is a medical doctor who specializes in pregnancy, childbirth, and the period of time right after a baby is born.
Obstinacy is the quality of stubbornly refusing to change your opinion, decision, or behavior — even when there are very good, clear reasons to do so.
Obstinate means stubbornly and unreasonably refusing to change your opinion, decision, or behavior, even when there are strong and sensible reasons to do so.
Obstreperous means noisy, unruly, and difficult to control — all at the same time.
To obstruct something means to get in its way and stop it — or make it much harder — from moving forward, passing through, or succeeding.

To obtrude means to push something — or yourself — forward into a place, a conversation, or someone's attention when it is unwanted, uninvited, or inappropriate. The thing being obtruded doesn't slip in quietly.
Something obtrusive forces itself on your attention in a way that feels unwanted, excessive, or out of place.
Annoyingly slow to understand something, or deliberately pretending not to. In maths, an obtuse angle is one between 90 and 180 degrees.

The simplest way to understand obverse is this: it is the front face of something, specifically the face that is considered the principal, more important, or more prominent side — as opposed to the back.
To obviate something means to remove a problem, risk, or need entirely — usually by doing something in advance — so that the issue never has to be dealt with at all.

Something is obvious when it is so easy to see, notice, or understand that it requires almost no mental effort at all. It is right in front of you — clear, immediate, and unmistakable. You do not have to search for it, think hard about it, or analyze it.
Obviously means in a way that is easy to see, understand, or notice — so clear that it needs no explanation.

Occam's Razor is a principle that says: when you have two or more explanations for something, the simpler one is usually the better one. In other words, don't make things more complicated than they need to be.
Occasion simply refers to a particular time or instance when something happens — a specific, identifiable point you can look back on or refer to.
Sometimes, but not often or regularly, as in "we occasionally eat out."
Occidental means relating to the West — specifically, the Western world and everything associated with it: its countries, its cultures, its people, and its traditions.

To occlude something means to block it, close it off, or seal it shut — usually completely, so that nothing can get through or past. Think of it as a more precise, technical way of saying "to block" or "to shut off."
Occlusion is the blocking, closing off, or shutting of something — a path, opening, passage, or view — so that what normally flows, moves, or passes through it cannot do so anymore.
Occult means hidden — specifically, hidden from ordinary understanding, ordinary sight, or ordinary access.
Beliefs and practices concerned with hidden, mysterious, or supernatural forces, such as magic, astrology, and spiritualism, that lie beyond ordinary science and religion.
"Occupation" refers to something that fills up space, time, or control. This one core idea branches into four distinct meanings. Let me walk you through each one carefully.
An occurrence is something that happens — any event, incident, or situation that takes place in the real world. It can be big or small, planned or unplanned, good, bad, or completely neutral.
A natural earth pigment, coloured by iron oxide, used for thousands of years to make paints. It is also the yellowish-brown or orange colour of this pigment.

Ocular means of, relating to, or involving the eye or eyesight. When something is described as "ocular," it is directly connected to the eye — either as a physical organ or as the means by which you see things.
An oculist is a medical professional who specializes in the eyes — someone you visit when you have a problem with your vision or your eye health.
"Odd one out" means a person or thing that is different from all the others in a group — one that does not belong, does not fit in, or stands apart from the rest.
An oddment is a small leftover piece or item that doesn't quite belong to a complete set — something remaining after the main bulk has been used up, sold, or taken away.
"Odds" means how likely or unlikely it is that something will happen. It is a way of measuring or expressing chance.
Odds and ends refers to a group of small, miscellaneous things that are left over, unimportant on their own, and don't easily fit into any neat, specific category.
An ode is a poem. But not just any poem — it is a poem that is written in honor of or in deep admiration for something.
"Odious" describes something — or someone — that is so deeply unpleasant, offensive, or morally repugnant that it deserves strong hatred or contempt. It goes far beyond "bad" or "unlikeable."
Odium means a deep, strong hatred or disgust — but not just any hatred.
Odoriferous means having or giving off a strong smell. If something is odoriferous, it produces a smell that is powerful enough to be clearly noticed.
Something that is odorous has a noticeable smell — strong enough that you can detect it easily. The word simply means "having an odor" or "giving off a smell."
An odyssey is a long, eventful journey or experience filled with many adventures, challenges, and unexpected turns — one that tests the person going through it and often changes them by the end.

The Oedipus complex is a theory by the psychologist Sigmund Freud that says young children go through a phase where they feel deep emotional attachment — including unconscious sexual desire — toward the parent of the opposite sex, and rivalry or jealousy toward the parent of the same sex.
An oenophile is a person who has a deep love, admiration, and passion for wine — not just as something to drink, but as something to genuinely understand, explore, and appreciate.
Oeuvre means the complete body of creative work produced by a single artist over the course of their career or lifetime.
"Of one's own choosing" means something that a person selected, decided, or brought about freely — by their own will — without being forced, pressured, or pushed into it by anyone or anything else.
To be "of two minds" about something means to be undecided or torn between two conflicting thoughts, feelings, or opinions about that thing.
When you say someone is "off their rocker," you mean they are crazy, mentally unbalanced, or acting in a very irrational and foolish way.
"Off the beaten path" means something or somewhere that is uncommon, unusual, or away from the popular, crowded, well-known places or ways of doing things.
"Off the cuff" means doing or saying something spontaneously, without any preparation or planning beforehand.

When someone is "off the hook," it means they have been released from a responsibility, duty, punishment, or blame that was previously placed on them. They no longer have to face consequences or deal with something difficult.
When someone says something "off the record," they mean: "What I am about to tell you is private. Please do not repeat it, write it down, quote me, or share it with others."
Off the top of one's head
When someone says something off the top of their head, it means they are giving an answer, idea, or piece of information immediately, without stopping to think carefully, research, or double-check.

"Off the wall" means something that is strange, bizarre, or wildly unconventional — so unusual that it surprises you, makes you raise an eyebrow, or makes you laugh because it was completely unexpected.
When something is off-kilter, it is out of its proper position, balance, or expected state. Think of it as something that should be straight, even, or normal — but isn't.
The internal organs of an animal, such as the liver, kidneys, and heart, used as food. It can also mean waste or rubbish.

If something is offbeat, it is unusual, unconventional, or different from what most people expect or consider normal. It doesn't follow the typical, predictable path that the majority of people follow.

To offend someone means to cause them to feel hurt, upset, or resentful — not because you caused them physical harm, but because you said or did something that violated what they value, believe in, or consider respectful and acceptable.
"Offensive" has two distinct, well-established meanings. Understanding both clearly is the key to mastering this word.

The part of a Christian church service when bread and wine are offered at the altar, or when money is collected from the congregation. It can also mean the money collected, or music played during this time.
When something is described as offhand, it means it happened spontaneously, off the top of someone's head, without careful thought beforehand.

When you call something official, you are saying it comes from, is authorized by, or belongs to a recognized authority — a person, organization, or institution that has the formal power and right to make decisions, issue statements, or set rules in a particular area.

Officialdom refers to officials as a whole group — all the people in positions of authority within governments, institutions, or large organizations — along with the entire world they operate in: their rules, their systems, their habits of thinking, and their way of doing things.
When someone officiates, they perform the official, formal duties of a recognized role at an event — usually a ceremony or a competitive game. The most important word here is official.
When someone is officious, they are annoyingly eager to give orders, offer help, or enforce rules — even when nobody asked them to, and even when it's not really their place to do so.
The word "offing" has two connected meanings — one literal and one figurative. Understanding both will give you a complete picture.

To offset something means to counterbalance it — to reduce or cancel out its effect by placing something else against it. Think of a weighing scale. If one side dips down because of weight, you add something to the other side to level it out.
An offshoot is something new that has grown out of, or developed from, something that already existed.

To ogle someone means to stare at them in a way that is very obvious, prolonged, and driven by strong desire — usually sexual or romantic desire — in a way that makes the other person feel uncomfortable or objectified.

An ogre is a large, frightening, man-eating monster from folklore and fairy tales. It is not a real creature — it lives in stories, myths, and legends. Think of it as a nightmare made into a character: a beast that walks like a human but acts like a predator.
Oilcloth is a type of cloth or fabric that has been coated on one side with a waterproof layer — traditionally oil, and in modern times usually a plastic-like substance called vinyl or PVC.

An oink is the sound that a pig makes. It is that short, grunting noise — somewhere between a grunt and a squeal — that comes from a pig's snout, typically when the pig is eating, resting, moving around, or just communicating.

An ointment is a thick, greasy, semi-solid substance that you spread on your skin — usually to heal, protect, soothe, or treat it. Think of it as a medicated or therapeutic paste that sits on top of your skin and does its job slowly from there.
The puzzle of why the night sky is dark: if the universe were infinite and filled evenly with stars, every line of sight would end on a star and the whole sky would blaze with light.

When someone calls something "an old chestnut," they mean it is a story, joke, claim, or idea that has been repeated so many times that it has become stale, predictable, and overly familiar. It has lost its freshness because everyone has heard it before.

"Old habits die hard" means that behaviors, routines, or patterns a person has practiced for a long time are extremely difficult to stop or change — even when the person wants to change, or even when the habit is no longer useful or helpful.

When you call something "old hat," you mean it is outdated, no longer new, or so familiar that it has lost its freshness and excitement. It describes something that used to be new or impressive but is now considered ordinary, behind the times, or stale.
When you call something old-fashioned, you are saying: "This belongs to the style, way, or thinking of an earlier time — and the world has mostly moved on from it."

An old-timer is a person who has been part of a particular place, job, community, or activity for a very long time — long enough that they have deep familiarity with how things work and how things used to be.
Excessively flattering and insincere in a smooth, oily way, as in "an oleaginous salesman." Literally, oily or greasy.
Olfactory means relating to the sense of smell. Whenever you see this word attached to something, it is telling you that the thing it describes has to do with smelling.
One of a small group of extremely rich and powerful people who control a country or a large part of its economy and politics.

"Oligarchic" describes anything that relates to, resembles, or is characteristic of a system where a small, exclusive, and powerful group of people hold control — while the vast majority are effectively shut out of real power.

An oligarchy is a system of government — or control over a country, organization, or institution — where power is held by a small, select group of people, rather than by the public at large or by a single ruler.

When someone extends (or offers) an olive branch, they are making a peaceful gesture to end a conflict, argument, or period of tension with another person. It means they are trying to make peace, show goodwill, or open the door to reconciliation.
An ombudsman is an official whose sole job is to protect ordinary people against unfair treatment by powerful organizations — typically governments, companies, or institutions.
An omen is a sign or event that people believe predicts something that will happen in the future.
Ominous means giving a strong, dark signal that something bad is about to happen.
In a way that suggests something bad is going to happen, as in "the sky darkened ominously."
An omission is something that has been left out — or the act of leaving something out.
To omit something means to leave it out — to not include it when you could have, or should have.

"Omnibus" as a noun refers to something that brings many separate things together under one roof — one vehicle, one book, one law, one broadcast. Think of it like a big bag that holds many different items instead of just one.

Omnipotence means having complete, unlimited power — the ability to do absolutely anything, with no limits, no boundaries, and no force in existence that can stop you. If you are omnipotent, nothing is beyond your ability.
Omnipotent means having unlimited, total power — the ability to do absolutely anything, with no restrictions whatsoever.

Omnipresence is the state or quality of being present everywhere at the same time, with absolutely no exceptions. Not "in many places." Not "in most places." Everywhere — all places, all at once, simultaneously, without any gap.
Omnipresent means present everywhere, at all times, with no exceptions.
