Omniscience is the state of knowing everything — absolutely everything — with no limits, no gaps, and no exceptions. It is total, complete, and perfect knowledge.

If someone or something is omniscient, it means they know absolutely everything — every fact, every secret, every thought, every event that has ever happened, is happening right now, or will ever happen in the future.
An omnivore is a living organism — almost always an animal — that eats both plants and other animals as regular parts of its diet. It doesn't restrict itself to just one food source.
Omnivorous is an adjective that means eating or consuming both plants and animals.
Everything about "on" flows from one core idea: contact.
When something ends on a low note, it means it finishes in a disappointing, sad, or unsatisfying way. The ending feels heavy, gloomy, or like a letdown.
To do something "on a shoestring" means to do it with very little money.
"On a whim" means doing something suddenly, without planning, and without a strong reason — just because the idea popped into your head at that moment.
"On account of" is a phrase that acts as a single preposition. It means "because of". Its only job is to introduce the reason why something happened, didn't happen, or was done a certain way.
If someone or something is on an even keel, it means they are in a stable, calm, and balanced state — functioning smoothly without any major problems, disruptions, or extreme ups and downs.
When someone or something is "on borrowed time," it means they are continuing to exist, survive, or function even though they were expected to have already ended, stopped, or died.
"To be on edge" means to feel nervous, anxious, or tense — as if something bad could happen at any moment. A person who is "on edge" feels restless, unsettled, and worried.
Continuing with almost no energy, money, or resources left, like a car running on an almost empty tank.

To be "on tenterhooks" means to be in a state of nervous anticipation, anxiety, or suspense. You feel it when you are waiting for something important to happen and you don't know yet how it will turn out.
"On the back burner" means that something has been set aside temporarily. It is not forgotten, but it is not a priority right now.

When you say someone is "on the ball," you mean they are alert, quick to understand things, efficient, and competent. A person who is "on the ball" pays close attention, reacts quickly, doesn't miss details, and handles things well.

To be "on the fence" means to be undecided, uncertain, or neutral about something. When you are on the fence, you have not yet made up your mind — you are neither clearly for something nor clearly against it.

"On the fly" means doing something quickly, without stopping what you're already doing, and without planning ahead. It describes an action that happens in the middle of movement or activity — spontaneously, in real time, as things are happening.
On the horns of a dilemma

When you are on the horns of a dilemma, you are stuck in a situation where you must choose between two options, and both options are bad, painful, or cause a problem. No matter which choice you make, something goes wrong. You lose either way.
When you say someone or something is "on the level," you mean they are honest, genuine, and trustworthy. There is no trickery, no hidden agenda, and no deception involved.

"On the mend" means that someone or something is getting better after a period of being bad, broken, or damaged. It describes the process of recovery and improvement — not the final, complete recovery, but the journey toward it.
"On the nose" means exactly right, perfectly accurate, or precisely correct. When something is "on the nose," it hits the target with zero error — no more, no less.
When two or more people are "on the same wavelength," it means they understand each other very well.
When you say someone is "on the warpath," it means they are very angry and actively looking for a confrontation.

"On thin ice" means you are in a risky or dangerous situation, especially one where your actions, words, or behaviour could cause serious trouble for you — and one wrong move could make things much worse.
"Once bitten, twice shy" means that if someone has been hurt or had a bad experience doing something, they will be very careful — or even avoid it completely — the next time.

When you call something once-in-a-generation, you are saying it is so rare and so remarkable that it comes along only one time within the span of an entire generation — meaning most people alive today will likely never see anything quite like it again in their lifetime.

A once-over is a quick, brief look or check of someone or something. The key idea baked into this word is speed — you are not studying something carefully or deeply. You are glancing over it just one time, quickly, to get a general sense of it.

Oncology is the branch of medicine devoted entirely to cancer — its study, diagnosis, treatment, prevention, and the care of people living with it. A doctor who specialises in this field is called an oncologist.

When someone calls something "one for the ages," they mean it is so extraordinary, memorable, and impressive that it will be remembered and talked about for a very long time — possibly forever, or at least for many generations to come.

"One's swan song" refers to a person's final performance, work, or act — especially one that is seen as their greatest, most memorable, or most significant. It marks the end of a career, a creative life, or sometimes life itself.
Something is oneiric when it has the quality of a dream — when it feels like it came from a dream, belongs in a dream, or works the way dreams work.
Onerous means something that is extremely burdensome, demanding, or oppressively difficult — especially in terms of the effort, responsibility, or obligation it places on you.

An onomatopoeia is a word whose sound is its meaning. In other words, it's a word that imitates, echoes, or resembles the actual sound of the thing it describes. When you say the word out loud, it sounds like the very thing it's referring to.

Onset means the beginning of something — but not just any beginning. It specifically refers to the point at which something begins to arrive, take hold, or set in, especially something that will then continue, grow, or develop over time.
An onslaught is a sudden, powerful, and overwhelming wave of something — usually attacks, forces, or things — that hits a person, place, or thing all at once, with great intensity and force.
Ontological is an adjective that means relating to the nature and fact of existence itself.
Ontology is the study of what exists and what it means to exist. It is a branch of philosophy that asks the most fundamental question imaginable: What is real?

Onus means a burden of responsibility — specifically, a duty or obligation that falls on someone to act, prove, explain, or deal with something. Think of it as a weight that lands on a particular person or group, making it their job to handle something.

"Oomph" means a quality of energy, power, or forcefulness that makes something feel exciting, impressive, or highly effective. It's the special punch or kick that takes something from ordinary to wow.
When something oozes, it moves or comes out slowly, steadily, and in a thick or sticky way — usually through a small opening, a crack, a wound, or a surface.
An opinion article in a newspaper, written by someone who is not on the paper's staff. The name comes from its place opposite the editorial page.

Opacity is the quality of something that blocks — blocks light, blocks your vision, or blocks your understanding. The more opacity something has, the less you can see through it (literally or figuratively). Think of it as the measurement of "blockingness."
A precious gemstone prized for its shifting play of many colours, which seem to change as the stone moves or the light falls on it differently.
Showing soft, shifting, milky colours like those of an opal, as in "opalescent glass."

Opaque means "impossible to see through or understand." Whether you're talking about a physical object or an idea, if something is opaque, it blocks you. You cannot see past it, into it, or through it.

Not closed or locked, as in "an open door." It can also mean not covered or enclosed, as in "open country," honest and willing to share, as in "open about her feelings," willing to consider new ideas, or available to everyone, as in "an open competition."
To suddenly allow a large number of things or people to come in, often after holding them back, as in "the ruling could open the floodgates to lawsuits." It can also mean to release pent-up emotion.

An open-and-shut case is a situation — most commonly a legal matter, but also any problem or argument — where the answer, decision, or conclusion is so clear and obvious that it requires almost no deliberation, investigation, or debate.
Describing software whose source code is freely available for anyone to use, study, change, and share.
Extremely dramatic, emotional, or grand, like an opera, as in "an operatic tantrum." Literally, relating to opera.

Operation refers to the act of something being done, carried out, or made to work. It can describe a machine functioning, a procedure being performed, an organized effort toward a goal, or a mathematical action on numbers.
The adjective operative revolves around one central concept: something that is active, working, and actually having an effect in the real world.
Requiring a great deal of tedious effort, as in "an operose task." Of a person, hard-working and industrious.
When "opiate" is used as an adjective, it means having the qualities of an opiate — that is, something that numbs, dulls, sedates, or produces a stupor-like state, either physically or mentally.

An opiate is a drug that comes directly from opium — a thick, milky substance found naturally inside the seed pods of a plant called the opium poppy. Think of opium as the raw source material, and opiates as the specific drugs extracted or processed from it.
To opine means to express or state your personal opinion on something — to openly declare what you think or believe about a subject.
If someone is opinionated, it means they hold strong opinions about things — and they hold onto them firmly.
Opium is a powerful, naturally occurring drug extracted from a specific poppy plant. It relieves pain intensely, creates a dreamlike sense of happiness, and is highly addictive.
An opponent is a person (or a group) who is against you in a contest, competition, argument, debate, or any situation where two sides are clearly divided.
"Opportune" describes something that happens or is done at exactly the right time — a time that is perfectly suited to a purpose, a need, or a situation.

Opportunism is the habit or practice of spotting a favorable situation and grabbing it for personal gain — but doing so without caring much about whether it's fair, ethical, or consistent with your own stated beliefs and values.

An opportunist is a person who spots a situation that could benefit them and quickly acts on it — usually without worrying too much about whether it is fair, ethical, or consistent with what they previously believed or promised.
Opportunistic describes someone (or something) that takes advantage of a situation as soon as it arises — not because of careful planning or strong principles, but simply because the chance is there.

To oppose something means to be actively against it — not just in your mind, but through your words, stance, or actions. When you oppose something, you push back against it, resist it, or try to challenge or stop it.
Opposition means being against something or someone — a force, action, or position that pushes back, resists, or stands on the opposite side.

To oppress someone means to use power over them in a cruel, unjust, or suffocating way — keeping them trapped in a condition of suffering, hardship, or helplessness, with little or no ability to escape or fight back.

Someone who is oppressed is being treated cruelly and unjustly by a more powerful person, group, or system — in a way that strips them of their freedom, rights, or dignity, and leaves them with little power to resist or escape.

Oppression is the cruel, unjust, and prolonged use of power by one person or group to control, harm, or suppress another person or group — taking away their rights, freedoms, or dignity, and forcing them to live under conditions that are unfair or unbearable.
Something oppressive presses down on you — heavily, relentlessly, and in a way that is hard to escape. It makes you feel crushed, suffocated, or trapped.
An oppressor is a person, group, or system that uses power — unfairly and often cruelly — to keep others down, control them, or prevent them from living freely.
If something is opprobrious, it either expresses or causes deep, public shame and disgrace. The word sits at the intersection of two ideas: scorching contempt and public humiliation.
Opprobrium means harsh public condemnation combined with the deep disgrace that comes with it — specifically when someone has done something widely considered morally shameful or dishonorable.
An opsimath is a person who begins to learn seriously — or discovers a deep love of learning — late in life.

To opt means to make a deliberate, conscious choice between two or more available options. When you opt for something, you are actively deciding in favor of it — not by accident, not randomly, but on purpose.
"Opt in" means to actively choose to participate in something.
To opt out means to choose not to participate in something that you are already part of, or that assumes your participation by default.

An optician is a trained eye care specialist whose job is to help people see clearly — not by examining your eyes or diagnosing problems, but by creating, fitting, and providing the corrective lenses (eyeglasses or contact lenses) that fix your vision.
The way a situation or action appears to the public, as in "the optics of the decision were bad." In science, optics is the branch of physics that studies light and vision.
Optimal means the best possible given the specific situation, goal, or constraints you are working within.

Optimism is a mental tendency — a general way of thinking — in which a person expects that things will go well, that good outcomes are more likely than bad ones, and that even difficult situations can be overcome or improved.

An optimist is a person who naturally tends to expect good things to happen — in their own life, in situations they face, and in the world in general. When something is uncertain or unknown, an optimist leans toward believing it will turn out well.

When you describe someone (or something) as optimistic, you mean they expect good things to happen — that the future will turn out well, that a situation will improve, or that things will generally go in a positive direction.
To optimize something means to make it work as well as it possibly can — not just better than before, but as close to the best possible version of itself, given your real-world situation.

When you describe something as optimum, you mean it is the best possible given the specific situation, conditions, or goal you have in mind. Not just "good" or "very good" — but the exact point where things work as well as they possibly can.
Option means a choice — or more precisely, it means one of the things you can choose from, or the freedom you have to choose.

When something is optional, it means you are free to choose whether to do it or not. No one is forcing you. No rule demands it. You will not face a penalty or a problem if you skip it. The decision is entirely yours.

An optometrist is a trained healthcare professional whose entire job revolves around your eyes — specifically, examining them, figuring out how well you see, identifying problems, and helping fix or manage those problems.
Opulence means great, impressive, and visibly displayed wealth and richness.

Opulent means richly and visibly luxurious — so luxurious that the wealth practically jumps out at you. It describes something (or someone) that doesn't just have wealth but shows it in a full, grand, and abundant way.

An opus is a creative work — most often a piece of music, but also a book, a painting, a film, or any other serious artistic creation. Think of it simply as a work produced by a creator. The word carries a sense of weight and significance.
An oracle is a source of special, authoritative, or divinely-inspired knowledge — someone or something that people turn to when they need answers that ordinary people cannot provide.
Mysterious and wise-sounding but hard to interpret, like the pronouncements of an ancient oracle. It can also mean claiming great authority or certainty.
The word oral has one root idea: the mouth. All of its meanings branch out from this single idea.
An oration is a formal, carefully prepared speech delivered in public — especially on an important or ceremonial occasion — with great skill, eloquence, and often emotional power.

An orator is a person who is exceptionally skilled at speaking in public — and not just competent at it, but genuinely talented. An orator can stand before an audience and deliver a speech that is clear, compelling, and powerful enough to move people.

An oratorio is a large-scale musical work composed for an orchestra, a choir, and solo singers, built around a dramatic story — almost always drawn from religious or sacred texts, most often the Bible.
Oratory is the skill, art, or practice of speaking in public in a way that is powerful, eloquent, and persuasive. It is not just speaking — it is speaking with great skill and effect.

An orb is a perfect sphere — a completely round, three-dimensional shape that is equally curved in every direction, with no flat sides, no edges, no corners. Think of a marble, a soap bubble, or a planet drifting through space.
An orbit is the curved path that one object follows as it travels around another object in space, due to the force of gravity pulling them together.
To orchestrate something means to carefully plan, arrange, and coordinate all the different parts of a complex activity so that they work together smoothly and produce a specific, intended result.
Ordain means to officially establish, command, or appoint something or someone through a position of high authority.

"Ordained" describes something (or someone) that has been officially established, decreed, or made legitimate by a recognized authority — whether that authority is a religious institution, fate, God, or a governing body.
An ordeal is a very painful, difficult, or exhausting experience that truly tests a person's strength, patience, or ability to cope.
"Order" is about deliberate structure — things being arranged, controlled, directed, or put in place on purpose. Its many meanings all connect to this central idea, just in different situations.
As a noun, "orderly" refers to a person in a supporting, helper role who carries out practical tasks under someone else's authority. The word is used in two main settings: hospitals and the military.
An ordinance is an official rule or law created by a local government — such as a city, town, or county — that everyone within that area must follow.

Ordinary means normal, usual, and standard — exactly what you would expect from something, and nothing more. When you call something ordinary, you are saying it doesn't stand out in any way. It is not special, not impressive, not surprising.

Ordination is the official ceremony or process by which a person is formally recognized and granted the authority to serve as a member of the clergy — a priest, minister, deacon, pastor, bishop, rabbi, or similar religious leader.
Ordnance is a collective noun for military weapons, ammunition, and explosives — essentially, the things soldiers use to destroy, damage, or kill.

At its most direct, ordure means excrement — the solid waste that passes out of the body of a human or an animal after digestion. Put simply, it is a formal word for feces, dung, or filth of that kind.

An organ is a distinct, self-contained part of a living body — whether human, animal, or plant — that carries out a specific, vital function. Each organ is made up of different types of tissues (groups of cells) working together to perform that one job.

"Organic" is one of those words that seems to mean something specific until you realize it shows up in completely different situations — food labels, chemistry class, business reports, and casual conversation — each time meaning something slightly different.
Organza is a type of fabric — a specific kind of cloth used in clothing, fashion accessories, and decoration.
Wildly unrestrained and frenzied in pursuit of pleasure, sensation, or excess, like an orgy, as in "orgiastic celebrations."

Orgy describes something done in an extreme, wild, and completely unrestrained way — well beyond normal limits. The word carries a strong sense of excess: too much, too intense, involving too many people or things, with no self-control or moderation.
"Orient" means to position or align something in relation to a reference point — to establish where it stands, where it's pointing, or what it's aimed at, so that everything makes sense in context.

The direction in which something faces or is positioned. It can also mean a person's beliefs or interests, as in "political orientation," or a course of introductory information for newcomers, as in "student orientation."
An orifice is a hole or opening through which something can pass in or out. Think of it as a doorway — not a room, not a tunnel, just the actual opening itself.
Origami is the art of folding paper into decorative shapes, figures, and sculptures. It originated in Japan and has been practiced there for centuries.
In Christian theology, the sin of Adam and Eve's disobedience to God, believed to be inherited by all humans at birth. Figuratively, a fundamental flaw from which other problems arise.
An orison is simply a prayer — a heartfelt, often spoken appeal directed to God or a divine being.

Ornamentation refers to two closely related things: 1. The act or process of decorating something — the doing of it. 2. The decorative details themselves — the things added to make something more beautiful, elaborate, or interesting.
Something is ornate when it is covered in a lot of elaborate, intricate decoration — far more than what is simply needed. It is the opposite of plain, simple, or minimalist.
Ornery means bad-tempered, stubbornly difficult, and uncooperative — almost as if a person enjoys being unpleasant or going against what others want.
An ornithologist is a scientist who studies birds — not casually as a hobby, but professionally and systematically, as their core area of expertise.

Ornithology is the branch of science that is dedicated entirely to the study of birds — all birds, from the tiny hummingbird to the giant ostrich, from the common house sparrow to the rare and exotic birds of remote rainforests.
When you describe someone's voice as orotund, you mean it is round, deep, powerful, and impressively full.
To orphan means to cause someone to become an orphan — that is, to deprive a child of one or both parents, most often through death.

When something is orthodox, it means it follows the established, accepted, and traditional way of thinking or doing things — the way that most people in a group, society, or field have agreed is correct.
Orthodoxy means the officially accepted, mainstream, or approved set of beliefs, ideas, or practices within a particular group.
Orthogonal means at a perfect right angle — that is, exactly 90 degrees — to something else.

Orthography is the standardized, correct way of writing a language. It is the complete set of rules and conventions that determines how words must be written — which letters to use, in which order, with which capitalization, and with which punctuation.

When something is described as orthopedic, it means it relates to — or is designed for — the correction, treatment, or support of problems involving the body's structural and movement system: bones, joints, muscles, tendons, and ligaments.

To oscillate means to move back and forth repeatedly between two points or two states. The movement is not random. It goes one way, then the other way, then back again — over and over, like a pattern.
An oscillation is a repeated back-and-forth movement around a central point.
Osmosis is the movement of water through a special kind of barrier, flowing from a side that has more water toward a side that has less water, until both sides reach an equal balance.
Osseous simply means "of, relating to, or made of bone." If something is described as osseous, it either is bone, consists of bone, or has the qualities of bone. That's the whole idea.
The process of becoming rigid and unable to change or develop, as in "the ossification of the system." Literally, the process by which cartilage or other tissue turns into bone.

When you call something ossified, you mean it has become so rigid, fixed, and set in its ways that it can no longer change, adapt, or grow. It is completely stuck — hardened beyond the point of flexibility.
To ossify means to turn into bone, or to become as hard and rigid as bone. Everything else about this word grows from that one image: bone — solid, inflexible, and set in its shape permanently.
An ossuary is any place or container used to store human bones.
Appearing or claimed to be true on the surface, but possibly not the real truth underneath.
Ostensibly means "on the surface" or "apparently — but possibly not in reality."
Ostentation is the deliberate, exaggerated display of wealth, knowledge, achievements, or abilities — done specifically to impress others, draw their admiration, or make them feel inferior.

Ostentatious means doing something in an excessively showy way, specifically to impress other people or to draw attention to yourself. It describes a kind of display that screams "Look at me! Look at what I have! Look at how great I am!"

An osteopath is a trained healthcare professional who diagnoses and treats health problems by working with the body's physical structure — mainly the bones, muscles, joints, and connective tissues (like tendons and ligaments).
Ostracism is the act of deliberately and collectively shutting someone out from a group, a community, or society.
To ostracize someone means to deliberately exclude a person from a group and treat them as if they no longer belong — cutting them off from social interaction, acceptance, and belonging.
Otiose means serving no useful purpose — something that is there, but contributes nothing. It is pointless, unnecessary, redundant, or ineffective.
A low, cushioned seat or footstool with no back or arms, often with storage space inside. It is also a type of heavy ribbed fabric.
To oust someone means to forcefully push them out of a position of power, authority, or control — usually against their will.
An ouster is the act of forcibly removing someone from a position of power, authority, or a place they hold or occupy — especially when that person did not choose to leave on their own.
Out of control, as in "the party got out of hand." To reject or dismiss something "out of hand" means to do so immediately, without proper consideration.

"Out of keeping with" means not fitting, not matching, or not belonging with something. When something is "out of keeping with" its surroundings, situation, or context, it clashes — it creates a sense that something is wrong, misplaced, or inconsistent.
"Out of kilter" means that something is not working properly, not in its correct state, or not in balance the way it should be.
When something or someone is "out of line," it means they have gone beyond what is acceptable, proper, or expected.
"Out of one's depth" means to be in a situation that is too difficult, too advanced, or too complex for your current level of knowledge, skill, or experience.
When someone is "out of sorts," it means they are feeling slightly unwell, irritable, or not quite like their usual self. It is a mild, vague feeling — not a dramatic or serious one.

When something happens "out of the blue," it means it happened suddenly and completely without warning. There was no sign, no hint, and no reason to expect it. It simply appeared from nowhere and caught everyone off guard.
Out of the frying pan into the fire
This idiom means escaping one bad situation only to land in an even worse one. The key idea is that your attempt to get away from a problem does not help you — it actually makes things worse.

If someone is "out of the loop," it means they do not have the latest information about something that other people already know. They are unaware, uninformed, or left behind in a conversation, decision, or situation.
"Out of the ordinary" means something is unusual, exceptional, or different from what is normal — something you don't encounter every day.

When you say something is "out of the question," you mean it is completely impossible, not allowed, or not even worth considering. It is a firm, final rejection of an idea or request. There is no room for debate, negotiation, or hope.
"Out of the woods" means that a person, situation, or thing is no longer in danger, difficulty, or trouble. It means the worst part is over and things are now safe or stable.

"Out of thin air" means something appears, is created, or is produced suddenly — from nowhere, with no visible source, no preparation, and no clear explanation for where it came from. It describes something that seems to come from absolute nothingness.

"Out of whack" means that something is not working properly, not in its correct state, or not in the right balance. It describes anything that has gone wrong, become misaligned, broken down, or stopped functioning the way it should.

When someone is "out on a limb," it means they are in a vulnerable or risky position, usually because they: Said or did something bold that others might not agree with or support, OR Took a risk — in a decision, a prediction, a business, or a relationship — without a guarantee of safety or support.
An outbreak is the sudden beginning and rapid spread of something harmful — something that affects not just one person or place, but many people or a large area, usually in a short amount of time.
An outburst is a sudden, forceful release of something strong — usually an emotion, sound, or intense activity — that comes out quickly, powerfully, and often without much warning or control.
An outcast is a person who has been pushed out of a group, a community, or a society — and is no longer accepted, welcomed, or treated as a belonging member of that group.
An outcome is the final result that comes from a situation, process, event, action, or decision. It is what ultimately happens — or what you end up with — after everything plays out.

An outcrop is a mass of rock that is visible at the surface of the Earth — rock that has broken through or been uncovered, so you can actually see and touch it, rather than it being hidden under layers of soil, grass, or sand.
In the simplest terms: an outcropping is a mass of rock that sticks up or out from the surrounding ground or hillside, like the tip of something much larger hiding beneath.

An outcry is a strong, loud expression of anger, protest, or shock — usually from many people at once — in reaction to something that feels wrong, unfair, or deeply troubling. Think of it as the collective voice of people who are upset and want to be heard.

Something is outdated when it was once current, useful, or accepted — but is no longer so, because the world has moved on. It belongs to a past moment that has now been replaced by something newer, more accurate, or more suitable.

To outdo someone means to do something better than they did — to surpass them in performance, quality, achievement, or effort. When you outdo someone, you do not merely match them; you go beyond what they accomplished.

The word outfit at its heart means a complete set of things that belong together. Whether it's clothes, equipment, or even people — an outfit is never just one thing. It's a collection that forms a whole.
To outflank someone means to go around their side in order to gain an advantage over them — whether on a real battlefield or in any competitive situation in life.
To outfox someone means to defeat them or get the better of them by being smarter and more cunning than they are. It is about winning through your mind — not through strength, luck, or resources.

When you describe a person as outgoing, you mean they are naturally comfortable and enthusiastic around other people. They enjoy socializing, meeting strangers, starting conversations, and being part of a group.
To outgross something or someone means to earn more money in total revenue than another thing or person, typically in a competition or comparison.
To grow too big for something, as in "he outgrew his shoes." It can also mean to lose interest in something as you mature, as in "she outgrew her childhood fears."
An outgrowth is something that comes out of, develops from, or emerges from something else. It is connected to its source — it didn't appear randomly, it grew from it.
An outie is a type of belly button (also called a navel — the small mark on your stomach) that sticks outward, like a small bump or knob that pokes out from your skin.
"Outlandish" means so strange, bizarre, or different from what is normal that it almost feels like it doesn't belong in the real, familiar world.

An outlaw is a person who has broken the law and lives or operates outside the accepted rules of society — someone the legal system is looking for, or someone who openly defies and ignores the law as a way of life.
When someone outlaws something, they make it officially illegal — forbidden by law.
An outlay is an amount of money that is spent or paid out for a specific purpose.

An outlier is something — or someone — that stands far apart from everything else in a group. It does not fit the usual pattern. It is the odd one out, but in a more extreme, measurable, and meaningful sense than just being "a little different."
This single image is the heart of "outlook." Every meaning of this word is a variation of that act of looking out.
To outmaneuver someone means to gain an advantage over them by being smarter, more strategic, or more skillful in your actions — especially in a competitive or challenging situation.
When something is outmoded, it means it is no longer suitable for the present time because something better, newer, or more fitting has replaced it.
To outpace something or someone means to move, grow, or progress at a faster rate than them — and to keep doing so over time.
A sudden, powerful expression of strong emotion, as in "an outpouring of grief." It can also mean a large amount of something flowing out.

Outrage is a feeling of intense anger that comes with a strong sense that something is deeply wrong — morally wrong, unjust, or indecent. It is not ordinary anger. It is anger that burns with moral force.

To outrage someone means to cause them to feel a powerful combination of shock and deep moral anger — the kind of anger that rises specifically when something feels not just unpleasant, but fundamentally wrong, unfair, or indecent.
When someone is described as outraged, they are feeling an extreme, intense form of anger — but it is a very specific kind of anger. It is not just anger.

Outrageous means something has crossed a line — it has gone so far beyond what is normal, acceptable, or expected that it causes a strong reaction in people. That reaction could be anger, disbelief, shock, or sometimes even laughter or delight.

Outré means so bizarre, exaggerated, or unconventional that it goes beyond what most people consider acceptable or normal — often to the point of being shocking, eyebrow-raising, or just wildly "too much."
Outset means the beginning or the very start of something — the earliest point in time when something begins.
To outshine someone or something means to be so much better, more impressive, or more brilliant that the other person or thing looks dull or less significant by comparison.
When "outside" works as a preposition, it always sits directly before a noun or noun phrase. Its job is to tell you that something is beyond the boundary of that noun — not within it.

An outside chance means a very small but real possibility that something will happen. When you say someone has an "outside chance," you mean they are unlikely to succeed — but it's not completely impossible either.

"Outskirts" refers to the outer areas or edges of a city or town — the parts that sit at the boundary between the main urban area and the open land (or countryside) beyond it. Think of a city as a circle.
When someone is outspoken, they say what they truly think — directly, boldly, and without holding back — even when their opinion might be uncomfortable, unpopular, or controversial.
When something is outspread, it is stretched wide open or extended outward to its full extent — spread out in all directions, or to both sides, from a central point.
To outstay something or someone means to stay longer than you should, or longer than someone else does.

To outstrip something or someone means to go beyond them — to exceed them, surpass them, or leave them behind. The "beyond" here can mean ahead in speed, ahead in size, ahead in growth, or ahead in degree.
When A outweighs B, it means A is more significant than B — not just a little more, but enough to tip the scale in A's direction. Both A and B have some weight (some importance), but A's is stronger.

To outwit someone means to defeat them or get the better of them by being cleverer than they are — not by being stronger, richer, or more powerful, but purely through smart thinking, clever strategy, or a cunning trick.

An ovation is a loud, enthusiastic show of appreciation — most commonly in the form of clapping, cheering, or both — that an audience gives to someone who has just performed, spoken, or done something impressive or admirable.

Above or higher than something, as in "a lamp over the table." It also means across, as in "a bridge over the river," more than, as in "over 50 people," during, as in "over the weekend," or about, as in "arguing over money."
"Over and above" means in addition to something that already exists, or beyond what is normally expected or required.

"Over the moon" means to be extremely happy or delighted about something. Not just a little happy — very, deeply happy. Think of the biggest smile you've ever had on your face. That's the feeling this idiom describes.

"Over the top" means too much, excessive, or exaggerated beyond what is normal or necessary. When something is "over the top," it goes further than it needs to — in terms of drama, effort, emotion, spending, decoration, or behavior.

Overarching describes something that is so broad and important that it covers, includes, and connects everything else beneath it — like a master idea, a top-level goal, or a grand framework that all other things belong to or serve.

To overawe someone means to impress or intimidate them so powerfully — through your authority, skill, reputation, beauty, or sheer presence — that they feel deeply overwhelmed and unable to act freely, speak up, or resist you.
Overbearing describes a person who is so excessively controlling, domineering, and forceful that they suffocate the freedom, opinions, and comfort of the people around them.
"Overblown" means too much. Something overblown has been puffed up, inflated, or stretched beyond what is true, appropriate, or necessary.
Over the side of a ship or boat into the water, as in "he fell overboard." To go overboard means to do something too much or with too much enthusiasm.

When something or someone is overburdened, it means they are carrying or dealing with far more than they can reasonably handle. The load — whether physical, emotional, or work-related — has crossed a limit.

When we say the sky is overcast, we mean it is completely — or almost completely — covered by a thick blanket of clouds. The clouds spread across the entire sky, hiding the sun and turning everything a dull shade of grey.
Not done, paid, or returned by the expected time, as in "an overdue library book." It can also mean something that should have happened much earlier, as in "these changes are long overdue."

To overegg the pudding means to overdo something — to add more than is needed, usually to make something seem better, more impressive, or more dramatic than it really is. The result of this "overdoing" is that things actually get worse, not better.
To overestimate something means to think it is more than it actually is — bigger, stronger, better, longer, harder, or more important than it truly is in reality.

To overhaul something means to examine it completely and carefully, find everything that is wrong, broken, outdated, or inefficient, and then fix, replace, or improve all of those things — so that in the end, the whole thing works properly or significantly better than before.

Overkill means doing, using, or applying far more than what is actually needed to achieve a goal. It is the act or result of going well beyond what is necessary — to a degree that becomes wasteful, absurd, or unnecessary.
Something is overlapping when two or more things share a common part, area, or portion — while each thing still has its own separate parts as well.

To overlay means to place or spread something on top of something else so that it forms a layer — a new surface that covers the thing below, either completely or partially. The original thing doesn't go away; it stays right there underneath.
When you overlook something, you miss it by mistake. It was right there, but your eyes or your mind passed over it without catching it.
To overrate something means to judge it as better, more important, more talented, or more valuable than it actually is. Your opinion of it is higher than the truth supports.

Overrated means something — a person, place, thing, or idea — has a better reputation than it deserves. People praise it, admire it, or think highly of it more than they should, based on how good it actually is.
To try to do more than you are able or permitted to, and fail as a result, as in "the government overreached." Literally, to stretch too far when reaching for something.

An override is what happens when something with more authority steps in and cancels, replaces, or takes precedence over something that was already in place — a rule, a decision, an automatic process, or a setting that was previously running things.
To override something means to use your authority, power, or position to step in, cancel what was already in place, and replace it with something else — your own decision, setting, or action.
When you call something overriding, you are saying it is the most important thing — so important that everything else becomes secondary to it. It is not just very important.
To oversee something means to watch over it, be in charge of it, and make sure it is being done properly.
An overseer is a person whose job is to watch over other people while they work and make sure the work is being done correctly, on time, and up to the required standard.
To make someone or something seem less important or successful by comparison, as in "his brother overshadowed him." It can also mean to spoil the mood of an event, or to cast a shadow over something.
In this sense, "oversight" means the act of carefully watching over something or someone to make sure everything is being done correctly, safely, and responsibly.

To overstate something means to describe it as bigger, more important, more serious, better, or worse than it actually is. You are stating something over (beyond) what is true — you are crossing the line of accuracy and going too far.
Overt means done openly, without any attempt to hide it. If something is overt, it is clearly visible, obvious, and out in the open — anyone watching can see it happening.
To overthrow something means to remove a powerful ruling authority by force or through a drastic, aggressive action — ending their power suddenly and completely.
A subtle quality or implication that is suggested but not stated, as in "the speech had political overtones." In music, an overtone is a higher, quieter note heard along with the main note.
An overture is an opening move — something that comes first, before the main thing begins, and signals or prepares you for what is coming next. Think of it as a door being opened.

"Overturn" means to flip something over, or to completely reverse and destroy something that was standing, in place, or in power. It is always about a drastic, forceful change — not a gentle shift, but a complete undoing.

"Overweening" means excessively arrogant or conceited — but with a very specific flavor. It describes someone whose sense of their own importance, ability, or superiority has gone so far beyond what is reasonable that it becomes offensive, even absurd.

To overwhelm something or someone means to come upon them with so much force, quantity, or intensity that they cannot handle it, resist it, or function normally. The key idea is too much — more than can be managed or processed.

When something is overwhelming, it is so large, so strong, or so intense that it goes beyond what a person can easily handle, process, or resist. Think of it this way: imagine a bucket that can hold 5 litres of water.

When a person is overwrought, they are in a state of intense, raw emotional tension — anxiety, distress, nervousness, or agitation that has built up to a point where they can barely hold themselves together.
To understand "overzealous," you first need to understand the word it's built on: zealous.

Ovine simply means relating to, belonging to, or characteristic of sheep. If something is described as ovine, it has a connection to sheep — it either comes from sheep, pertains to sheep, or resembles sheep in some way.
Looking serious, wise, or studious, like an owl, especially because of large, round glasses or wide eyes.

"Own up" means to honestly admit that you did something wrong, made a mistake, or are responsible for something bad. It is about telling the truth when part of you might want to stay quiet or hide it.

An oxymoron is a figure of speech where two words — or a short phrase — are deliberately placed together even though they seem to directly contradict each other. The key word is "deliberately." An oxymoron is never an accident.

Pabulum means bland, undemanding, intellectually empty content — the kind of material that is so watered-down, so deliberately unchallenging, that it feeds your mind the way a lump of tasteless mush feeds your stomach.
Every use of "pace" as a verb connects to one core concept: controlled, measured movement or speed.

A pachyderm is a large, hoofed mammal with an especially thick, tough skin. The word is most commonly used to refer to elephants, but historically it has also been applied to animals like rhinoceroses and hippopotamuses.
A pacifist is a person who believes that war and violence are never — or almost never — justified, and who is personally committed to resolving conflicts through peaceful means instead.
To pacify means to make someone calm and peaceful, especially when they are angry, upset, or agitated. Think of it as "turning down the heat" on someone's emotions.

A pact is a serious, deliberate agreement between two or more parties — whether individuals, friends, organizations, or entire countries — in which everyone involved mutually commits to doing something, or to not doing something, together.
A paddock is a small, enclosed piece of land — fenced in on all sides — that sits next to or near a stable (a building where horses are kept).
The word paddy has two completely separate meanings that have nothing to do with each other. Context always makes it clear which one is being used.
A padlock is a portable, detachable lock — meaning it is not built into a door, gate, or any object. You can carry it around, attach it to something to secure it, and remove it whenever you want.

"Padre" is an English word used to refer to a Christian clergyman — someone who is an ordained priest, minister, or chaplain. It has two closely related but distinct uses, and knowing both will give you the complete picture.

A paean is an enthusiastic, joyful expression of praise — something said, written, sung, or created to celebrate a person, a thing, an idea, or an achievement with great warmth, admiration, and delight.

Paella is a famous Spanish rice dish. It comes from Valencia, a sunny region on the eastern coast of Spain, and it is considered one of Spain's most iconic and beloved foods. Today, it is enjoyed all over the world.

When you call something pagan, you are saying it belongs to, relates to, or is characteristic of a religion or spiritual tradition that stands outside the three major Abrahamic faiths — Christianity, Islam, and Judaism.
A pagan is a person whose religious or spiritual beliefs fall outside the three major Abrahamic faiths — Christianity, Judaism, and Islam.

A pageant is a grand, elaborate, and visually impressive public event — something designed to dazzle, celebrate, or entertain through ceremony, spectacle, costumes, and performance. It is always big and theatrical.

A pagoda is a type of tall tower, most commonly associated with the religious and cultural traditions of Asia — especially Buddhism. It is one of the most recognizable structures in Asian architecture.
A pail is a container used for holding and carrying things — most often liquids like water or milk, but also loose materials like sand or paint.

A pain point is a specific, recurring problem or frustration that someone experiences — something that makes their life, work, or experience harder, more annoying, or less efficient than it should be.
Painful means causing or involving pain — something that hurts, distresses, or makes you suffer in some way. The pain can be felt in your body, in your mind, or both.
"Painfully" is an adverb. Adverbs describe how something happens or to what degree something is true. So "painfully" tells you in what way or to what extent something is the case.

If you do something in a painstaking way, you give it extreme care and attention. You check everything. You miss nothing. You don't rush, you don't cut corners, and you don't settle for "good enough."

When someone does something painstakingly, they do it with extreme care, great effort, and very close attention to every small detail — often spending a lot of time to make sure nothing goes wrong and nothing is missed.
A paisley is a specific decorative shape — and also the name of a repeating pattern built from that shape, and also the name of fabric that carries that pattern.
A pal is a friend — but not just any friend. It specifically suggests someone you are close to, comfortable with, and genuinely enjoy spending time with.

A palanquin is a covered box or enclosed seat — big enough for one person to sit or lie inside — that is carried from place to place by other people. There are no wheels, no animals, and no engine involved.
Palatable means acceptable, agreeable, or pleasing enough — something you can receive, experience, or go along with without strong objection or discomfort.
"Palate" has two layers of meaning — one physical, one experiential — and both are worth knowing fully.
Palatial means resembling a palace — in terms of size, grandeur, luxury, and impressiveness.

Palaver means unnecessary fuss, bother, or complication — or long, pointless talk. Think of it as a single word that captures the feeling of "why is this so much more complicated and exhausting than it needs to be?"

"Paleolithic" is an adjective. You use it to describe something that belongs to, relates to, or is characteristic of the Old Stone Age — the earliest and by far the longest chapter of human prehistory.
Paleontology is the scientific study of ancient life on Earth — life that existed long before humans started keeping written records, and often long before humans existed at all.
A palette is always about a range or selection of colors — either as an object that physically holds them, or as a concept describing which colors (or options) are available.

Something that has been changed or reused over time but still shows traces of its earlier forms, as in "the city is a palimpsest of history." Literally, a manuscript written over earlier, partly erased writing.
A palindrome is a word, phrase, number, or any sequence of characters that reads exactly the same whether you go from left to right (forward) or from right to left (backward).

A palisade is a tall, strong fence made of a row of wooden stakes (thick, sturdy poles) that are sharpened to a point at the top and driven firmly into the ground, one right next to the other, in a continuous line.

"Pall" describes something heavy and dark that covers something else — creating a feeling of gloom, dread, or heaviness. Picture a thick, dark cloud quietly settling over a scene. That image is the soul of this word.
A pallbearer is a person who carries — or helps carry — the coffin at a funeral.
The word pallet is a noun with several distinct meanings. They are unrelated to each other — the word just happens to be used in different fields to mean different things.
To palliate something means to make a bad thing feel or look less bad — without actually fixing it.
Palliation means the act or process of making something painful, harmful, or severe feel less intense — without actually removing or solving the underlying cause.
Something palliative is something that reduces or relieves pain, discomfort, or the impact of a problem — but does not cure or solve it at its root.
Pallid means pale, drained of color, and lacking the brightness or vividness that something normally should have.
Pallor means an unusual, noticeable paleness in a person's skin — especially the face — that signals something is wrong. It's not simply having a naturally fair or light complexion.
The word palm has two completely separate meanings as a noun. They look and sound identical, but context always makes it clear which one is meant.
Prosperous, flourishing, and successful, as in "the palmy days of the empire." Literally, full of palm trees.
A palomino is a horse. More specifically, it refers to a horse with a particular, very distinctive coloring — and that coloring is what makes a palomino a palomino.

The word palpable describes something so strong, clear, or obvious that it almost feels physical — as if you could reach out and touch it, even though it isn't something you can actually hold in your hands.
To palpitate means to beat rapidly, irregularly, or unusually strongly — so much so that you actually notice it happening. It is almost always used to describe the heart.

A palpitation is the strange, often unsettling feeling of becoming suddenly and intensely aware of your own heartbeat — noticing it flutter, pound, race, or feel irregular in a way that is not normal for you in that moment.
Palsy is a noun for a medical condition in which a person loses normal control over the muscles of some part of their body, due to a problem in the nervous system — the brain, spinal cord, or nerves.

To palter means to deliberately mislead someone — not by telling an outright lie, but by being evasive, using half-truths, or choosing words so carefully that they technically say one thing while making the listener believe something else entirely.
Paltry means something is so small in amount, so weak in quality, or so worthless in value that it deserves to be looked down upon or dismissed with contempt.
Paludal means of, relating to, or produced by a marsh or swamp.

To pamper someone means to treat them with excessive comfort, care, and indulgence — giving them far more luxury, attention, or pleasure than what is normal or necessary. The key word here is excessive. Regular care is not pampering.

A pan is a shallow, open container — typically made of metal — that is used to hold, cook, or collect something. That idea of "shallow and open" is the thread connecting nearly every meaning this word carries.
To criticize something harshly, as in "the film was panned by critics." It also means to swing a camera from side to side, or to search for gold by washing gravel in a pan.
A panacea is something — a solution, a treatment, a plan, or an idea — that people believe will fix ALL problems or cure ALL illnesses at once. Think of it as a magical "cure-all" or "fix-all."

Panache is the quality of doing something with impressive style, boldness, and effortless flair — especially when what you're doing is difficult or important. It's not just about what you do, but the brilliant, confident way you do it.

When pandemic is used as an adjective, it describes a disease — or sometimes another condition — that is spreading across a very large geographic area (multiple countries, entire continents, or the whole world) and is actively affecting a very large number of people at the same time.

A pandemic is a disease that has spread across a very large part of the world — typically many countries or even the entire globe — and is actively infecting a large number of people at the same time.
Pandemonium is a state of wild, overwhelming chaos, disorder, and noise — especially when many people are involved and everything seems to have completely broken loose all at once.

To pander means to give people exactly what they want — especially when what they want is something shallow, base, or not genuinely good for them — usually because you want to gain something from doing so, like their approval, money, votes, or attention.
Pandiculation is the act of stretching your body — especially the involuntary, full-body kind you do right after waking up, often paired with a yawn.

When you call something panegyric, you mean it expresses lavish, formal, and extravagant praise — the kind of praise that is so glowing, so one-sided, and so overflowing with admiration that it goes far beyond an ordinary compliment.

A panegyric is a formal, elaborate piece of praise — spoken or written — that glorifies a person, group, institution, or thing in an enthusiastic, often lavish way. Think of it as praise that has been dressed up in its finest clothes and put on stage.

Paneling refers to a collection of panels fitted together to cover or line a surface — most commonly walls, ceilings, or doors. It is the system or material formed when multiple panels are joined together.

A pang is a sudden, sharp, and brief feeling of physical pain or emotional distress. Think of it like a quick stab — it hits you all at once, feels intense for a moment, and then fades. It is not a slow, building feeling.
A pangolin is a real, living animal — a mammal — and one of the most extraordinary creatures on Earth.
A narrow strip of land that sticks out from a larger area, like the handle of a pan, as in "the Florida panhandle." Literally, the handle of a cooking pan.

To panhandle means to sit or stand in a public place and ask strangers for money or food, usually because you are very poor or in financial hardship. You offer nothing in return — no goods, no service, no work.

Panoply means a complete, wide, and impressively magnificent collection or array of things. Not just "a lot of things" — but a full, dazzling spread of them, the kind that feels grand and leaves an impression.
Panoptic means all-seeing, or relating to a system where everything can be observed at once.
A panopticon is a structure or system designed so that one person (or a small group) can watch everyone else — but the people being watched can never know when exactly they are being watched.
A panorama is a wide, sweeping, unobstructed view of a large area, seen all at once from a single point.
Panoramic describes something that is wide, sweeping, open, and complete — where you can see or understand a large expanse all at once, with nothing blocking or hiding any part of it.

When you pant, you breathe in short, rapid, shallow bursts — quick little gasps of air, one after another. It is not calm, slow breathing. It is fast, laboured, and often audible. You can hear someone panting.

The most fundamental meaning of pantheon is the complete set of gods that a particular religion or culture worships. Think of it as the full, official lineup of a religion's gods — every single one of them, taken together as a group.
A pantomime is a performance that uses the body — gestures, facial expressions, and movement — to tell a story or express something, with little or no spoken words.
A pantry is a dedicated storage space — either a small room or a large, deep cabinet — located in or very close to the kitchen, used specifically for storing food, drinks, and kitchen supplies.

The papacy is the office, position, and authority held by the Pope — the leader of the Roman Catholic Church. Think of it this way: the Pope is the person, but the papacy is the role itself — the seat of power that the Pope occupies.

A paparazzo is a freelance photographer who makes a living by secretly or aggressively photographing famous people — celebrities, politicians, royalty, athletes, socialites — without their permission, and then selling those photos to tabloids, gossip magazines, and entertainment news outlets.
A paper tiger is a person, group, organization, or thing that looks powerful, dangerous, or threatening from the outside — but is actually weak, ineffective, or harmless on the inside.
A tall water plant that grows along the Nile, or the paper-like writing material that ancient Egyptians made from its stems. A papyrus is also an ancient document written on this material.

"Par" means a standard, expected level — a fixed reference point that things are measured against. Think of it as a benchmark: a line in the middle that represents "normal" or "equal." Everything else is either above it, exactly at it, or below it.

"Par for the course" means something is exactly what you'd expect — typical, normal, and unsurprising. It's used when something happens and your reaction is basically: "Well, of course. That's just how things usually go here."

A parable is a short, simple story — always realistic and set in everyday life — told not for the story's own sake, but to teach a deeper moral, spiritual, or ethical truth. The story is fictional, but it could plausibly happen in real life.

A parabola is a smooth, curved line that is shaped like the letter U (or an upside-down U). It is perfectly symmetrical — if you draw a vertical line right down the middle of it, both sides are exact mirror images of each other.
A paraclete is someone who comes alongside another person to help, support, defend, or comfort them — someone who is called in specifically because that person needs help.

A parade is an organized, public procession — a structured line of people, and often vehicles, floats, bands, and animals — moving together along a set route (usually a street), while a crowd of spectators watches from the sides.
A paradigm is a model, pattern, or framework — a way of understanding or doing something that a group of people treats as "the standard" or "the normal way things work."
Paradise means a place, situation, or state of perfect happiness, beauty, and peace — the best possible existence you can imagine, with no suffering, no worry, and no imperfection of any kind.
Paradisiacal means so beautiful, peaceful, and perfect that it feels like paradise itself.

A paradox is a statement, situation, or idea that seems impossible or self-contradictory at first — but when you examine it more carefully, it either reveals a surprising truth, or it leads you into a genuine logical dead-end that no amount of reasoning can escape.
Something is paradoxical when it seems to contradict itself or defy logic at first glance — yet, on closer inspection, it turns out to be true, meaningful, or at least reasonable.
A paragon is a person or thing that is considered the perfect example of a particular quality — not just a good example, but the best possible example.
A parakeet is a type of bird — specifically, a small to medium-sized parrot with a long, pointed tail. The long tail is actually the single most important feature of a parakeet.
"Parallel" describes two or more things that run alongside each other, always staying the same distance apart, never getting closer and never drifting farther away — no matter how far they extend.
To park a vehicle in a line with other parked vehicles, parallel to the side of the road, usually by reversing into a space between two cars.
Parallelism means the state or quality of two or more things being parallel — existing, running, or developing alongside each other in a similar, matching, or corresponding way.
When something or someone is paralyzed, they are in a state of being completely unable to move or act — not just struggling, not just slow, but genuinely frozen and non-functional.
A paramedic is a highly trained emergency medical professional who provides advanced medical care to patients before and during transport to a hospital.
A parameter is a value, condition, or boundary that defines how something behaves or is described — without being the main thing you're studying or producing itself.
Paramount means more important than everything else. Not just very important — but the most important, sitting above all other concerns. When something is paramount, nothing outranks it.

A paramour is a person's secret romantic or sexual partner — someone they are involved with outside of their marriage or committed relationship. In the simplest terms, a paramour is the person someone is having an affair with.

Paranoia is a state of mind in which a person has strong feelings of suspicion, distrust, or fear — believing that others are out to harm, deceive, or persecute them — even when there is little or no real reason to believe so.

A paranoiac is a person whose mind is held in a persistent grip of irrational suspicion — someone who is deeply, unshakeably convinced that others are out to harm them, deceive them, watch them, or conspire against them, even when there is no real evidence for this.

When you describe someone as paranoid, you mean that person believes — without any real, solid evidence — that others are secretly out to get them, are watching them, are plotting against them, or are trying to harm them in some way.
When we describe something as paranormal, we are saying it falls beyond the reach of what science can currently explain or confirm.

A parapet is a low, protective wall or barrier built along the edge of something elevated — such as a roof, a bridge, a balcony, a terrace, or a military fortification — to either stop people from falling off or to shield them from danger.
Paraphernalia means a collection of miscellaneous items, tools, accessories, or equipment associated with a particular activity, person, or purpose.
A paraphrase is a restatement of something someone said or wrote, using different words, while keeping the exact same meaning.

When you paraphrase something, you take an idea that was expressed in someone else's words (or your own earlier words) and restate it in a fresh way — using different words and a different sentence structure — while keeping the original meaning completely unchanged.
A parasite is a living thing that survives by feeding off another living thing — without giving anything back in return, and often while causing harm in the process.
A parasol is a portable, umbrella-shaped device designed to block sunlight and provide shade. Think of it as a "sun umbrella" — its entire purpose is protection from the sun, not from rain.
A paratrooper is a soldier who is trained to jump out of an aircraft with a parachute and land in a combat zone to fight.
To parboil something means to partially cook it in boiling water, then stop before it is fully done.
A parcel is something singled out and treated as one complete, self-contained unit — whether it's a wrapped package, a piece of land, a batch of goods, or a group of things.
To parch means to make something extremely dry through intense heat — or to become extremely dry because of it.

Parched means extremely dry — so dry that it desperately needs water or moisture. The key word here is extremely. "Parched" is never used for something that is just slightly dry. It describes a serious, intense, almost painful lack of moisture.

Parchment is a thin, flat sheet made from the treated skin of an animal — most commonly a sheep, goat, or calf — that people historically used as a surface for writing. Think of it as nature's version of paper, invented long before paper existed.

A pardon is an act of official forgiveness — specifically, forgiveness that removes or cancels a punishment. It is not just any forgiveness between people; it is always granted by someone in a position of authority, and it has real, formal consequences.
To pardon someone means to choose not to hold something against them — to release them from blame, punishment, or resentment, even when a wrong has genuinely occurred.

To pare means to carefully cut away or remove the outer layer of something, usually with a blade or knife. Think of someone sitting at a kitchen table, slowly running a knife along the skin of an apple, removing just the thin outer layer — that is paring.
Paregoric is a specific type of liquid medicine that contains opium as its main active ingredient.

Something parenthetical is extra. It is information added into a sentence or a piece of writing as a side note, an aside, or a small detour — information that is useful or interesting, but not essential. The main sentence can stand perfectly well without it.
A parfait is a dessert. But here's the interesting thing — the word actually refers to two quite different desserts, depending on whether you're talking about French cuisine or American cuisine.
A pariah is a person — or sometimes a group, organization, or country — that is completely rejected, shunned, and avoided by the people or society around them.

A parish is a small, defined local community and the geographic area it occupies, managed or cared for by a specific authority. That authority is either a church (in the religious sense) or a local government (in the civil sense).

Parity means equality — the state of two or more things being equal, equivalent, or on the same level. Think of it as a scale perfectly balanced on both sides. When two sides are in parity, neither one is ahead or behind, higher or lower, stronger or weaker.

Parkinson's disease is a progressive brain disorder that gradually robs the body of its ability to move smoothly, automatically, and effortlessly. The word progressive is important — it means the condition doesn't appear all at once.
Parlance means the particular way a specific group of people use language — the special words, phrases, and expressions that belong to a certain field, profession, community, or context.
To parlay something means to take something you already have and use it cleverly to gain something bigger or more valuable. It always moves in one direction: upward.

A parley is a formal face-to-face discussion between two opposing sides — usually enemies — where they agree to temporarily stop fighting in order to talk and negotiate. Picture two armies locked in battle. One side raises a white flag.

When you parley with someone, you meet with an opponent or enemy — face to face — to have a direct conversation aimed at reaching some kind of agreement. Not to fight. Not to deceive. To talk, negotiate, and try to work things out.
A parlor is a room or place set aside for a specific, usually social or personal, activity — somewhere a little more special or designated than just any general space.
Parlous means dangerously uncertain, precarious, or in a bad and risky state — a condition where things could easily fall apart or get much worse.
Narrow-minded, with interests limited to your own small area or community, as in "parochial attitudes." Literally, relating to a church parish, as in "a parochial school."

Parochialism is a noun that describes a narrow, limited way of thinking in which a person, group, or institution only cares about, or only pays attention to, their own small corner of the world — and as a result, ignores, dismisses, or simply fails to consider anything beyond that small circle.

A parody is a creative work — a piece of writing, a song, a film, a TV show, a drawing, or any other form of expression — that imitates another well-known work, person, or style, but in an exaggerated or distorted way, usually to make people laugh or to make a point about the original.

The verb to parody means to imitate something — a person, a style, a song, a movie, a speech, or really anything recognizable — in a deliberately exaggerated and comic way, so that the imitation makes people laugh, and often makes a quiet but pointed comment in the process.

Parole is the conditional early release of a prisoner from jail or prison, before they have finished serving their full sentence. "Conditional" is the key word here — it means the person is not completely free.
A paroxysm is a sudden, intense burst or fit of something — an emotion, a physical symptom, or an activity — that erupts with great force, usually without much warning, and then passes.

The most famous parquet pattern is called herringbone — rows of rectangular blocks placed at 90-degree angles to each other, creating a zigzag effect that resembles the bones of a fish (hence the name).

Parquetry is the craft of creating decorative surfaces — most commonly floors, but also tabletops and furniture panels — by fitting together small pieces of wood cut into precise geometric shapes, arranged so they interlock and form a repeating pattern.
The act of killing one's own parent or a close relative. A parricide is also a person who commits this act.

To parry means to skillfully deflect or ward off something coming at you — whether that's a physical blow or a verbal challenge like a tricky question or criticism. The key word here is skillfully. You don't just run away from it. You don't absorb it either.
To parse something means to break it down into its parts and analyze what each part means and how they all fit together.

Parsimonious means excessively unwilling to spend money or share resources — to a degree that is unreasonable or even mean. It describes someone who holds onto their money (or anything of value) so tightly that it becomes a fault, not a virtue.
Parsimony means extreme and excessive unwillingness to spend money or use resources — going so far beyond careful budgeting that it becomes a fault.

A part is a piece of something larger — something that, together with other pieces, makes up a whole. Think of a pizza: each slice is a part of the pizza. The pizza itself is the whole; the slices are its parts.
To "part with" someone or something means to give up, let go of, or separate from someone or something — and it almost always suggests that doing so is difficult, sad, or unwanted.

To partake means to take part in something or to have a share of something. Think of the word itself — it's almost hiding its own meaning: part + take. You take a part of something. You step into something and become a part of it.
When something is partial, it is not the whole thing. It is a piece, a portion, a fraction — but not all of it.
"Partiality" has two distinct but related meanings. Understanding both — and how they connect — will give you a complete picture of the word.

To participate means to take active part in something — to be involved in an activity, event, process, or situation in a way where you are actually doing something, not just watching or being present.

A participle is a verb that has been modified so it can do the job of an adjective — that is, it describes or modifies a noun. At the same time, it still looks like a verb and retains some verb-like qualities. Think of it as a verb wearing an adjective's hat.

A particle is an extremely small piece or portion of something — so small that it's often difficult or impossible to see with the naked eye. Think of it as the tiniest meaningful unit or fragment of a substance.
Specific, as opposed to general, as in "this particular book." It can also mean especially great, as in "of particular importance," or fussy and demanding, as in "particular about food."
"Particularly" means especially or to a special/notable degree. It signals that something stands out — either above other things in a group, or above what is normal or expected.
When something is described as partisan, it means it is strongly in favor of one particular side, group, or cause — and is NOT neutral or balanced.

A partisan is a person who strongly and loyally supports a particular political party, cause, leader, or group — and does so in a way that is often one-sided, where they favor their own side regardless of whether it is right or wrong.

Partisanship is the strong, loyal support of a particular group, party, or side — combined with a tendency to favor that group over others, often at the expense of fairness, balance, or objective thinking.
The division of a country into separate states, as in "the partition of India." It can also mean a light wall or screen dividing a room, or, in computing, a separate section of a hard drive.
Parturition is the formal, scientific word for the act of giving birth. It refers to the complete physical process by which a pregnant female — human or animal — delivers her offspring from her body.

A parvenu is a person who has recently risen to wealth, power, or a high social position — but who is not fully accepted by the people already at that level. The world around them sees them as an outsider pretending to belong somewhere they don't truly fit.

A pasquinade is a piece of writing — most often a poem, verse, or short text — that viciously and publicly mocks a real, specific person or group, usually someone powerful, such as a politician, a religious leader, a judge, or a public institution.
"Pass" is about movement or transfer — something or someone moves from one point, person, place, or state to another.

"Pass off" is a phrasal verb — a verb combined with a small word ("off") that together create a meaning quite different from the words on their own. "Pass" alone means to move or go by. But "pass off" opens up into four distinct, separate meanings.

To ignore someone when choosing a person for a promotion or reward, as in "she was passed over for promotion." It can also mean to ignore or leave out a topic, or literally to move across or above something.
The most important and most common meaning of passable is: Something that meets the minimum acceptable standard — it's not bad enough to reject, but it's not good enough to praise or be impressed by.
A narrow corridor or path that connects places. It can also mean a short section of a book or piece of music, a journey, especially by sea, the passing of time, or the approval of a law.
A passel simply means a large group or a large amount of something. Think of it as a more colorful, informal way of saying "a whole lot of" or "a large bunch of."
