A plaudit is an enthusiastic expression of praise or approval — a strong, open, and often public show of admiration for something someone has done. Think of it as praise that is loud in spirit, whether spoken out loud, written, or shown through applause.
Plaudits means enthusiastic praise, admiration, or approval that someone receives — usually from many people — for something they have done well.
Something is plausible when it seems reasonable, believable, and likely to be true — based on the information available — even though it has not been proven to actually be true.
To try to reach the same level or progress as others, after falling behind.
To play hooky means to stay away from school, work, or any obligation you are supposed to attend — without a real, legitimate reason, and usually without permission.
To play possum means to pretend to be dead, asleep, unconscious, or unaware in order to trick someone or avoid a difficult situation.
"Play up" is a phrasal verb — that means it's the word "play" combined with the word "up" to create a meaning that is different from just "play" alone.
A playbill is a printed document — either a small booklet or a single sheet — that is connected to a theatrical performance (a play, a musical, an opera, a ballet, etc.).

Playfulness is the quality of being playful — the natural tendency to approach things in a light, fun, and spirited way, without taking everything too seriously. It is a noun that names a state of mind or a personality trait.
A plaything is something — or someone — that is used purely for amusement or entertainment, and is not taken seriously.
A playwright is a person who writes plays — stories designed to be performed live on a stage by actors, in front of a real audience, in real time.

Playwriting is the art, craft, and practice of writing plays. It refers to the entire creative process of composing a piece of dramatic writing that is designed to be performed on a stage by live actors in front of an audience.

A plea is a sincere, heartfelt request — one made with emotion, urgency, or desperation. It is not a casual ask. When someone makes a plea, they are appealing to another person deeply, often from a position of need, vulnerability, or helplessness.

Plead means to speak with urgency and emotional intensity to persuade, appeal to, or formally address someone — either by begging desperately, arguing a case, making a formal legal declaration, or offering an excuse.

A pleasantry is a polite, light, and friendly remark made in a social situation — not because you have something important or serious to say, but simply to be warm and agreeable. Its whole purpose is to make an interaction feel smooth, comfortable, and human.

When you feel pleased, you feel a quiet, comfortable sense of happiness or satisfaction because something good has happened, someone has done something you like, or a situation has turned out the way you wanted.

A pleat is a deliberately made fold in a piece of fabric, where the fabric is doubled over onto itself and then held in place at one point — usually stitched down at the top — while the rest of the fold is left free and open.

When you call something or someone plebeian, you are saying it belongs to, or is typical of, ordinary, common people — not the upper class, not the elite, not the refined and sophisticated. It's the opposite of aristocratic, exclusive, or high-class.

A plebeian is an ordinary, common person — someone who belongs to the general, lower, or working-class population, as opposed to the elite, noble, or privileged class of society. Think of it as the opposite of a "VIP."

A plebiscite is a direct vote in which all eligible citizens of a country or region are asked to answer one specific, major question — usually one that will determine the fundamental future of that place or its people.

A pledge is a serious, sincere promise — but not just any ordinary promise. It is a promise made with a strong sense of commitment, often in a formal or solemn setting. When someone makes a pledge, they are not casually saying "I'll try."

When you pledge, you make a serious, solemn promise — one that is stronger, more deliberate, and more binding than an ordinary, everyday promise. It carries a sense of deep personal commitment, and often a sense of public accountability.
Plenary means complete, full, and absolute — with nothing left out and nothing held back.

When something is described as plenipotentiary, it means it carries full, complete, and unrestricted authority to act, decide, and make binding commitments on behalf of someone else — with no need to ask permission or check back before acting.

A plenipotentiary is a person who has been given complete, total authority to represent someone else — almost always a government, a head of state, or a powerful organization — and to make binding decisions on their behalf, without needing to pause and check back for approval at every step.
Plenitude means a state of fullness, abundance, or completeness. It describes a situation where there is a great amount of something — often so much that nothing feels missing or lacking.

Plenteous means existing in a large, generous, and richly satisfying amount — more than just "enough," but so much that there is a sense of fullness and abundance. It describes something present in great supply, leaving no shortage whatsoever.

A pleonasm is when you use more words than you need to express a meaning — specifically, when the extra word(s) you add don't contribute any new information, because that information is already contained in the other word(s).

A plethora means an amount that is excessively large — not just a lot, but more than enough, and often more than you can comfortably handle. Think of it as a surplus so great it almost overwhelms you.
Pliable means easily bent, shaped, or molded without breaking. If something is pliable, you can press it, twist it, or reshape it, and it will give way without cracking or snapping.

Pliant means easily bent or shaped without breaking, and by extension, easily influenced or led without resistance. Think of it as describing something — or someone — that gives way smoothly under pressure instead of snapping back or refusing to move.
A plight is a bad, difficult, or unfortunate situation that someone is trapped in — one that is serious enough to make others feel concern or sympathy. It's not just any bad situation.
A plinth is a flat, solid block — usually square or rectangular — that sits at the very bottom of something, supporting it from below.
When you plod, you move — or work — in a way that is slow, heavy, and requires steady effort. It is not elegant, not fast, and not exciting.
A plot is a small, clearly defined area of land that has been measured and set apart, usually for a specific purpose.
A plover is a type of bird — specifically, a small to medium-sized shorebird found on nearly every continent on Earth.
A ploy is a clever trick or strategy that someone uses to get what they want — usually by being sneaky, misleading, or manipulative toward another person.
The most important and widely used meaning of pluck as a noun is courage — but not just any kind of courage.

Pluck means to pull something sharply and quickly — usually to remove it from where it is attached, stuck, or held. Think of it as a confident, deliberate little tug that separates something from its place.
Plucky means brave and determined, especially when the situation is hard, the odds are against you, or you are clearly at a disadvantage — and yet you refuse to give up or back down.
Plumage means all the feathers on a bird's body, taken together as a whole.
When we say something is "plumb," we mean it is exactly, perfectly vertical — straight up and down, with zero tilt, lean, or slant in any direction.
To explore or examine something in great depth, as in "plumbing the depths of despair." Literally, to measure the depth of water using a weighted line. It also means to install water pipes.

A plumber is a skilled, trained professional whose job is to install, connect, repair, and maintain the systems of pipes inside and around buildings that carry water, gas, and waste from one place to another.
A plume is not just any feather. It specifically refers to a large, soft, showy feather — the kind that is visually impressive and often used as decoration.
To feel proud of yourself for something, as in "she plumed herself on her calm." Of a bird, to preen its feathers. Of smoke, to rise in a tall column.

To plummet means to fall or drop extremely fast, extremely steeply, and usually by a very large amount — all at once. It is not a slow, gradual drop. It is a sudden, dramatic, almost violent downward movement.

Plump describes something — or someone — that is rounded, full, and softly fleshed out. Think of a shape that is nicely filled up, not thin or flat, but also not enormous. It sits in the comfortable middle: more than slim, less than fat.
When you plump something, you shake it, pat it, or squeeze it gently so that it puffs up and becomes full and soft again.
Plunder refers to goods, valuables, or property that have been stolen by force, typically on a large scale — especially during a war, invasion, raid, or attack.
To plunder means to forcefully and greedily steal a large amount of valuables from a place or people, especially when the thief has power or an unfair advantage over the victim.

To fall or move suddenly and forcefully downwards, especially into water. It also means to decrease suddenly and greatly, as in "prices plunged," or to throw yourself into an activity with energy, as in "plunging into work."

Pluralism means the peaceful and legitimate coexistence of many different things — different groups, beliefs, values, religions, cultures, or sources of power — within a single society or system, where no single one of them completely dominates or wipes out the others.
Describes a society or system in which many different groups, beliefs, and cultures exist side by side, without any single one dominating the others.
Plurality means "the state of being more than one" — the condition of being many rather than single. It's the opposite of singularity (which means being just one, alone, or unified).
"Plush" captures two closely linked qualities at the same time: deep softness and luxury. Understanding both will give you the full picture.
Plutocracy refers to a system of government or society in which the wealthiest people hold the most power and control.
A plutocrat is a person who uses their extreme wealth to gain and exercise political power or control over society.
Plutomania is a noun that refers to an extreme, abnormal, and consuming obsession with wealth. At its most straightforward, it means an excessive or abnormal desire for wealth.

Pluvial simply means of, relating to, or caused by rain. If something is described as "pluvial," rain is at the center of it — either as its cause, its defining feature, or its context. That's the word's fundamental job.

To do your job or trade steadily, as in "plying their trade." It also means to keep offering someone food, drink, or questions, as in "plied with wine," or for a ship or bus to travel regularly along a route.
"Pneumatic" describes anything that involves air or gas — almost always compressed air (ordinary air that has been squeezed under high pressure).
Pneumonia is a medical condition in which one or both of your lungs become inflamed and infected, causing the tiny air pockets inside them to fill up with fluid or pus instead of air.
A lung disease caused by breathing in very fine silica dust, such as volcanic ash. It is famous as one of the longest words in English, coined deliberately as a curiosity.
To cook food gently in simmering liquid, as in "poached eggs." It also means to hunt or catch animals illegally, or to take workers or customers away from a rival.

A poacher is a person who hunts, catches, or takes animals, fish, or plants illegally. That single word — illegally — is everything. It is the only thing that separates a poacher from an ordinary hunter or fisherman.

Podgy means slightly fat in a soft, round, compact way. When you call someone or something podgy, you are saying they look chubby and rounded — not severely overweight, but noticeably fleshy and a little squat.

A podium is a raised platform — a surface that is higher than the ground or floor around it — that someone stands on top of so that others can see them clearly. Think of it as a small stage built for one person (or a small group).

A poetaster is someone who writes poetry badly — and yet either believes they are a good poet, or shamelessly presents themselves as one. Think of it as a fake poet, or more precisely, a failed poet who doesn't know (or won't admit) that they have failed.

Poetic justice is when something happens to a person that feels like a perfectly fitting punishment or reward — especially when life itself seems to step in and give someone exactly what they deserve, in a way that feels almost too perfect to be a coincidence.

A pogrom is an organized, violent attack carried out by one group of people against another group — typically a minority — with the specific aim of killing, injuring, terrorizing, or driving them away. It is not just a riot or a fight.
Poignancy is the quality of making someone feel a sharp, deep emotional pain — but one that is mixed with beauty, tenderness, or meaning. It is not plain sadness.
Poignant describes something that produces a deep, sharp emotional feeling — usually a mixture of sadness and tenderness happening at the exact same time.
A particular way of thinking about or judging something; an opinion, as in "from my point of view." In storytelling, it is the perspective from which a story is told.

"Point-blank" always carries one central idea: no distance, no gap, no doubt. Whether used literally or figuratively, it describes something that hits you straight on — close, direct, and impossible to dodge or soften.
When you do or say something point-blank, you do it in the most direct, straight, and immediate way possible — with zero distance, zero softening, and zero beating around the bush.
Pointillism is a technique in painting where an artist creates an entire image using nothing but tiny, separate dots of pure, unmixed color placed side by side on a canvas.
Poise is about being steady — both in your body and in your mind — especially when the situation is difficult, high-pressure, or socially demanding.
To poise means to hold something — or yourself — in a carefully balanced, still position, usually right before taking action.
Calm, confident, and composed, as in "a poised young woman." Poised to do something means ready to do it, as in "the company is poised to grow." It can also mean balanced or held steady.
To poke around means to search or explore something casually, without a strict plan, often out of curiosity.
Relating to the North or South Pole, or the areas around them, as in "polar ice." It can also mean completely opposite, as in "polar opposites."
Polarity means the state of having two opposite extremes. Wherever something has two ends, two sides, or two qualities that are completely opposite to each other, you can say it has polarity.
To polarize something means to cause it to split into two strongly opposing sides or extremes — with little or no middle ground left in between.
A polemic is a piece of writing or speech that launches a fierce, passionate, and one-sided attack against something — an idea, a belief, a policy, an institution, or a person.
When you call something polemical, you are saying that it is aggressively and passionately arguing against something — an idea, a belief, a policy, a person, or a group.

To polemicize means to argue against something — an idea, a belief, a policy, a practice, or a person — but with exceptional force, aggression, and passion. It's not casual disagreement. It's not a polite back-and-forth.

A policy is a set of principles or rules that a person, organization, or government intentionally creates to guide how decisions will be made and how people will act — not just once, but consistently over time.
A highly infectious viral disease that attacks the nervous system and can cause paralysis, mainly in young children. Its full name is poliomyelitis, and it is prevented by vaccination.
If someone does something politic, it means they made a cleverly wise and well-judged choice — especially in a sensitive, tricky, or socially complicated situation.
Relating to the government or public affairs of a country, as in "political parties." It can also mean relating to power and status within an organization, as in "office politics."

A politician is a person who is actively involved in politics — that is, someone who seeks, holds, or works toward a position of power in government, or who makes it their career to shape how a country, state, or city is governed.

A politico is a person who is deeply involved in politics — typically a politician or a political insider who knows how to navigate the often complicated, strategic, and sometimes cynical world of political power.
Politics is the activity of making shared decisions for a group of people — especially decisions about power: who has it, how it is used, and who benefits from it.
A polity is any group of people that is organized under a political structure — meaning the group has some system of governance, authority, and rules that control how it runs itself.
A polling place is an official, physical location where eligible voters go to cast their votes during an election.
To pollute something means to make it dirty, harmful, or impure by introducing something that does not belong there — something that causes damage or makes it unsafe.

A poltergeist is a type of ghost or supernatural spirit that is believed to cause physical disturbances in the real world — things like moving objects, making loud noises, breaking things, or switching lights on and off.

A poltroon is a person who is a complete and utter coward — not just a little nervous or hesitant, but someone who is shamefully and contemptibly cowardly. The word does not describe someone who simply feels fear. Fear is human, and everyone feels it.
A polygamist is a person who is married to more than one spouse at the same time.

Polygamy is a noun. It refers to the practice of being married to more than one spouse — a husband or a wife — at the exact same time. It is the opposite of monogamy, which means being married to only one person at a time.

When polyglot is used as an adjective, it means "involving, using, or expressed in several languages." It describes anything — a person, a place, a book, a community — that operates across multiple languages at once.

A polyglot is a person who knows and can use multiple languages — typically defined as three or more. The key word here is use. A polyglot doesn't just recognize a few phrases from a foreign movie or remember some words from a class years ago.

A polygon is a flat, closed shape made entirely of straight lines. Every polygon lives on a flat surface (like a piece of paper), is completely closed with no openings or gaps, and has sides that are perfectly straight — no curves allowed.

A polymath is a person who has deep knowledge and skill across many very different fields of study or areas of human activity — not just a passing interest or surface-level awareness, but a genuinely high level of understanding and ability in each of those areas.
A polymer is a very large molecule made up of many smaller units called monomers, bonded together in a long, repeating chain.
Polytheism is the belief in, and often the worship of, multiple gods — not just one, but many. That's really the heart of it.
The simplest way to say it: Pomade is a thick, greasy or waxy substance that people apply to their hair to style it, hold it in place, and often make it look shiny.
To pommel someone means to hit them hard, repeatedly, with your fists — or sometimes with a blunt object. It's not a single punch. It's a flurry of sustained, forceful blows.
Pomp is a grand, impressive display of ceremony and magnificence — especially in public, and especially to show power, importance, or high status.
A pompadour is a type of hairstyle.

Pomposity is the quality of behaving or speaking as though you are far more important, impressive, or knowledgeable than you actually are — and doing so in a showy, overblown way that comes across as silly or irritating to others.
Pompous describes a person who behaves as if they are far more important, intelligent, or impressive than they really are — and who makes sure everyone around them knows it.
To ponder something means to think about it slowly, carefully, and deeply. It is not a quick or casual thought.

"Ponderous" is an adjective that describes something overwhelmingly heavy, slow, or laborious — and importantly, heavy in a way that feels oppressive, clumsy, or graceless. It is almost always used with a negative or critical tone. It is never a compliment.
A pontiff is a word used to refer to a high-ranking religious leader, specifically within the Christian tradition.
Pompously dogmatic and self-important, as if speaking with absolute authority. Literally, relating to a pope or bishop, as in "a pontifical Mass."

To pontificate means to speak about something in a way that is overly confident, long-winded, and self-important — as if you are the ultimate authority on the subject — often without giving others a real chance to respond, disagree, or even ask questions.

A pony is a small horse — specifically, a horse that belongs to a breed that is naturally and permanently small. This is perhaps the single most important thing to understand about the word: a pony is not a baby horse.
A pop quiz is a short, surprise test given by a teacher in class without any prior warning to students.

A popinjay is a person who is vain, showy, and self-important — someone who is excessively concerned with their own appearance, constantly talks about themselves, and loves being the center of attention, but who has very little real substance or depth beneath all that display.
Populace means the general body of people living in a particular place — a country, a city, a region, or any defined area. It refers to people collectively, as one large group.
Populism is a style of politics built on one simple, powerful idea: society is divided into two groups — ordinary, decent people on one side, and a corrupt, self-serving elite on the other.

A populist is a political leader, activist, or public figure who builds their entire identity around one central claim: "I am on the side of ordinary, everyday people — and I am fighting against a corrupt, powerful elite that has been cheating those people for too long."
Populous means having a very large number of people living in a place.
Porcelain is a hard, white, smooth material made by shaping a special type of fine clay and then baking it in a furnace at extremely high temperatures.
Porcine simply means "of, relating to, or resembling a pig." If something is porcine, it either has a connection to pigs, or it reminds you of a pig in some way.
A pore is a tiny opening or hole in a surface — so small that you often need a magnifying glass, or even a microscope, to see it clearly.
To pore means to read, study, or look at something with deep, sustained, and careful attention — so focused that you are almost entirely absorbed in it.
Something is porous when it is full of tiny holes — so many small gaps in its structure that liquid, gas, or other substances can seep in, pass through, or be absorbed into it.

Porphyry is a type of hard, igneous rock (rock formed from cooled magma) that has a very distinctive look: it contains large, visible crystals scattered throughout a much finer-grained background material.

A porpoise is a small, warm-blooded sea animal that breathes air through a blowhole on top of its head. It is a mammal, just like you — meaning it gives birth to live young, nurses its babies with milk, and breathes air rather than water.
Porridge is a warm, soft, thick food made by slowly cooking a grain (like oats) in water or milk until it turns into a smooth, creamy mush.
In its most essential form, portage means the act of carrying a boat, canoe, or cargo overland between two stretches of navigable water, when the water route between them is blocked or impassable.
A portal is a point of entry that leads you into something beyond — something larger, different, or significant.
A portcullis is a heavy, gate-like barrier that slides straight up and down — like a sliding door, but vertical — to either block or open the entrance of a castle, fortress, or fortified building.
To portend something means to act as a sign or warning that something — usually something significant or bad — is going to happen in the future.

A portent is a sign or signal that warns you something major — usually something dark, threatening, or earth-shaking — is about to happen. It is the world's way of raising a red flag before a great event unfolds.

When something is portentous, it acts like an ominous signal — a sign that something momentous, serious, or threatening is on its way. The thing itself may seem ordinary, but it carries a heavy, foreboding feeling about the future.
"Porter" is a word with four distinct meanings that are essentially unrelated to each other. You need to know all four, because which one is meant always depends on context.

A porthole is a small, round window built into the wall (called the "hull") of a ship or other vessel. If you've ever seen a ship and noticed those small circular glass openings on the side — those are portholes.
A portico is a covered entrance to a building, where the roof overhead is held up by a row of columns (pillars), and the sides between those columns are left open to the air.
A portion is a part of something larger — a piece that has been separated, divided, or set aside from a whole. Think of a big pizza. If you take one slice, that slice is your portion of the pizza.
"Portly" is an adjective that describes a person who is noticeably overweight, with a round, heavy body — especially a large, protruding belly.
A word made by blending parts of two other words, as "brunch" comes from "breakfast" and "lunch." In old use, a portmanteau was a large suitcase that opens into two halves.
A portrait is a carefully made image of a specific person — created to show what that person looks like, and often to reveal something about who they are.
Running through all meanings of pose is one central thread: to deliberately put something in front of others — a body, a problem, a question, or even a false identity.
A poseur is a person who pretends to be something they are not — usually to impress other people or to seem more interesting, cool, sophisticated, or talented than they actually are.
"Posh" describes something or someone that is luxurious, elegant, and strongly associated with wealth and high social class.
To posit something means to put it forward as true, or as a starting point for thinking, so that you can then reason, argue, or build on top of it.
Positivism is the belief that the only real, reliable, trustworthy knowledge is knowledge that comes from things we can directly observe, measure, test, or scientifically verify.
A posse is a group of people who come together — usually around one central person or for one shared purpose. The members of a posse are connected by loyalty, shared interest, or a common goal.

Possession means the state of having something — holding it, controlling it, or being in charge of it. It describes the relationship between a person and a thing they have with them or under their authority.
A possibility is something that can happen, can exist, or can be true — it has not been ruled out, but it also has not been confirmed.

Posterity means all the people who will live after us in the future — every generation that comes after the current one. It refers to future human beings as a whole group, not any one specific person.
Posthumous is an adjective that describes something that happens, is given, or comes into existence after a person has died.
"Posthumously" means after the death of the person it concerns. When something happens posthumously, it happens after a specific person has died — and that thing is directly connected to that person.
A postmaster is a person who is officially in charge of a post office. Think of them as the manager — the person responsible for making sure everything inside a post office runs smoothly.
The adjective postmortem means "occurring after death" or "relating to something done or examined after death."

A postmortem is an examination or analysis that happens after something has ended — most often after a death, or after an event has concluded. The key idea is: it always happens after the fact, looking backward to understand something more fully.
To postpone something means to move it to a later time than originally planned.
A postponement is the act of moving something from its original, planned time to a later time — intentionally, by someone's decision.
Postprandial is an adjective that simply means "happening after a meal."
A postulate is a statement that everyone agrees to accept as true without proof, so that reasoning, mathematics, or a theory can get off the ground.

To postulate something is to put it forward as true — as a claim, an assumption, or a starting point — especially when you don't yet have full proof for it, and you intend to use it as a foundation for further thinking, argument, or theory.
Posture means the way something is held, positioned, or arranged — whether that is a physical body, a person's attitude, or an organization's stance toward the world.
When someone postures, they are deliberately performing a certain attitude, stance, or behavior — not because they genuinely feel it, but to create an impression on others.

Posturing is a type of behavior — or speech — where someone deliberately presents themselves in a way that is designed to look impressive, strong, confident, or principled, but the behavior doesn't reflect what they truly feel, believe, or intend to do.
Potable means safe and suitable for drinking. When something — almost always water — is described as potable, it means a person can drink it without getting sick.

Potent means powerfully effective. When something is potent, it doesn't just have strength — it has the kind of strength that produces a strong, noticeable impact. Think of it as power that actually does something, and does it forcefully.
A potentate is a person who holds supreme, commanding power over a country or large group of people.
When you use "potential" as an adjective, you are saying that something could exist, happen, or become real in the future — but hasn't yet.

"Potentially" means in a way that is possible but not yet confirmed or actual. It tells you that something has the right conditions, the capacity, or a real chance to happen or to be true — but it hasn't been proven or realized yet.
A pothole is a hole — a hollow, bowl-shaped depression — that forms in the surface of a road or path. Think of it as the road's surface suddenly "caving in" at a spot, leaving a rough, open dip.
A potion is a liquid that you drink, or sometimes apply to your body, to produce a special or powerful effect.

A potluck is a meal or gathering where each person invited brings one dish of food, and together all the dishes form the entire meal. No single person — not even the host — is responsible for cooking everything.
A mixture of dried petals and spices placed in a bowl to perfume a room. Figuratively, a varied mixture of things, as in "a potpourri of styles."
A potsherd is a broken piece or fragment of pottery — a chunk that has snapped, chipped, or cracked off from a clay vessel like a pot, jar, bowl, jug, or vase.
A potshot is a quick, careless, and often unfair attack — either a literal shot fired without proper aim, or a criticism thrown at someone casually and from a position of safety.

A potter is a person who makes objects out of clay — things like bowls, cups, plates, mugs, vases, pots, and decorative pieces. These clay objects, once shaped and hardened, are called pottery or ceramics. So a potter is simply the maker of pottery.
A pouf is a large, soft, stuffed cushion that sits directly on the floor and is used as a seat or footrest. It has no legs, no back, and no armrests.

A poultice is a soft, moist, paste-like mass that you spread onto the skin — or onto a cloth pressed against the skin — and leave there for a period of time to treat a medical problem. It is always used externally.

To pounce means to jump at something suddenly and with force — usually to catch it, grab it, or attack it. Think of a cat sitting perfectly still, watching a mouse move across the floor, and then — in one sharp, explosive burst — leaping onto it.
To pour means to cause a liquid — or anything that moves like one — to flow steadily and continuously from one place to another, usually by tilting a container.
Sulky and showing displeasure by pushing out the lips, as in "a pouty expression." Of lips, full and pushed out, often considered attractive.
Poverty means the state of being very poor — a condition in which a person or group of people lacks enough money, resources, or basic necessities to live a decent life.
A dangerous and tense situation that could explode into violence at any moment. Literally, a barrel of gunpowder.

A powwow is a ceremonial gathering held by Indigenous peoples of North America — primarily Native American tribes in the United States and First Nations peoples in Canada. It is one of the most significant traditions in Indigenous culture.

Practicable means able to be done — capable of actually being carried out in the real world, given the current situation, resources, and conditions. When you call something practicable, you are making one single claim: this can actually be done.
"Practical" means connected to real action, real use, and the real world — as opposed to ideas, theories, or things that exist only in the mind or on paper.

A practical joke is a trick that one person plays on another person in real life, designed to make the victim look foolish, feel surprised, or experience a moment of confusion or embarrassment — usually for the amusement of the prankster and any onlookers.

Practical judgement is the ability to figure out the right thing to do in a real, specific situation — by reading that situation carefully, thinking it through wisely, and acting in a way that fits the moment.
When you say "practically," you mean that something is so close to being true that the tiny remaining gap barely matters.
A practitioner is a person who actively does something as their regular work or serious commitment — especially something that requires skill, training, or specialized knowledge.
Pragmatic means focused on what actually works in real life, rather than on theories, ideals, or emotions.

Pragmatism is the belief that the value of any idea, plan, or action should be judged by whether it actually works in the real world — not by whether it sounds beautiful in theory, follows a strict rule, or lines up with a cherished ideal.
A pragmatist is a person who cares most about what actually works in real life, rather than what sounds perfect in theory, what sticks to a rigid rule, or what matches a lofty ideal.
A prairie is a large, open stretch of land that is covered mostly by grasses and wildflowers, with very few trees or sometimes none at all.
When you praise someone or something, you express — out loud or in writing — that you think they are good, worthy, or admirable. You are openly showing approval and admiration.
A pram is a small, four-wheeled vehicle designed to carry a baby. A parent or caregiver pushes it from behind using a handle while walking.
To prance means to move with high, springy, bouncy steps in a way that is lively, energetic, and often showy or self-important.

Prandial means relating to a meal — that is, anything connected to the act of eating, the time of eating, or what happens around a meal. If something is described as "prandial," it is linked in some way to a meal.

A prank is a planned trick that one person plays on another — a deliberate act of deception designed to surprise, startle, fool, or embarrass someone, usually for the purpose of humor. The person doing the trick (the pranker) finds it funny.
To prate means to talk on and on — at great length — about things that are trivial, foolish, or unimportant, usually without realizing (or caring) that you are being a bore or a nuisance to others.
A pratfall is a fall in which someone lands hard on their buttocks — their rear end, their bottom. That's the simplest, most direct definition.
To prattle means to talk continuously about things that are trivial, foolish, or unimportant — in a way that goes on and on, without really saying anything meaningful or worthwhile.
"Prattle on" means to talk continuously about unimportant or trivial things, in a way that is childish, senseless, or annoying to the listener.
A prawn is a small, water-dwelling creature with a hard shell on the outside of its body. It belongs to a group of animals called crustaceans — the same broad family as crabs and lobsters.
Praxis means practice — the actual doing of something, as opposed to merely thinking or talking about it. If you spend a year reading books about cooking, you have culinary theory.

A preamble is an introduction that comes before the main content of something — a document, a speech, a law, or even a conversation. Its job is to set the stage: to explain the background, the purpose, or the reasoning before the actual main message begins.
Something is precarious when it is unstable, uncertain, and could easily go wrong or fall apart — especially because you are not fully in control of what happens next.
Precariously means in a way that is dangerously unstable, uncertain, or unsafe — where things could go wrong, collapse, or fail at any moment with very little warning.
A precaution is an action you take before something bad happens, specifically to stop it from happening — or at least to reduce the harm if it does happen.

Precede means to come before something or someone. Whatever precedes something else is earlier, first, or in front. It can express "before" in four different ways: in time, in order, in physical position, and in rank or importance.
Precedence means the right or condition of being considered more important, coming first, or being ranked higher than something or someone else.
A precedent is something that happened before — a past action, decision, or event — that becomes the accepted guide or example for how similar things should be handled in the future.
"Preceding" means coming before something else — in order, position, or time.

A precept is a rule or principle that tells you how you should behave, think, or act — especially in a moral, ethical, or practical sense. It is a guiding instruction meant to be followed consistently throughout life or within a particular field.
The slow, circular wobble of the axis of a spinning object, such as a spinning top or the Earth, caused by an outside force such as gravity.
A precinct is an officially defined area or zone that has been deliberately carved out and set apart from the larger space around it — usually for a specific purpose or under a specific authority.
Preciosity means excessive, over-the-top refinement — especially in language, writing, or style — that has crossed the line from genuine elegance into something artificial, affected, and strained.
Precious means having great value. But that value can be of two very different kinds — the kind you can measure in money, and the kind you can only measure in your heart.
A precipice is a very steep, almost perfectly vertical face of a cliff or rock — the kind of drop where if you took one more step forward, you would fall a terrifying distance almost straight down.

When something is described as precipitant, it means it is excessively hasty and lacking in careful thought — done or happening so suddenly and rapidly that proper care, judgment, or consideration has been thrown out the window.

When you call something precipitate, you are saying it happened too fast — so fast that important steps like thinking, planning, or waiting for the right moment were skipped. And because of that speed, the result was harmful, risky, or at least unwise.

To precipitate something means to cause it to happen suddenly, abruptly, and often sooner than it naturally would have — usually with a loss of control over the consequences. It's a formal, serious word, and it carries more weight than simply saying "cause."
Precipitation, in weather, means any form of water — liquid or solid — that falls from the sky and reaches the ground.
Precipitous means dangerously or dramatically steep — like something that drops away sharply, almost straight down, giving you that stomach-lurching feeling of a sudden, sheer fall.

"Precipitous" (the adjective this adverb comes from) originally described something physically very steep — like the sheer face of a cliff that doesn't slope gently away but drops almost straight down.

A précis is a short, faithful summary of a longer piece of writing — one that captures all the essential ideas of the original, in your own words, without adding anything new or leaving out anything important.
When something is precise, it is exactly right — not roughly right, not almost right, but sharply and perfectly accurate, with zero room for vagueness or guesswork.

"Precisely" means exactly — with complete accuracy, sharp focus, and zero room for vagueness or error. When something is done or described "precisely," it means it matches the truth, the target, or the standard perfectly.
To preclude something means to make it impossible, or to prevent it from happening — not by physically stopping it in the moment, but by creating a condition that rules it out entirely.
Precocious describes someone — almost always a child — who displays abilities, knowledge, or maturity that are far more advanced than what you would normally expect from someone their age.
Precocity is the quality of being more mentally or behaviorally advanced than is normal for one's age — especially in a child.

Precognition is the claimed ability to know or sense something that is going to happen in the future — before it actually happens — without using any logical reasoning, past experience, or information gathered through the normal five senses.
A preconception is a belief, opinion, or idea that you form about something before you have actually experienced it, learned enough about it, or examined it carefully.
A precursor is something that comes before something else and has a meaningful connection to it.
Predation is the act of one living creature hunting, catching, killing, and eating another living creature for food.
A predator is a living creature — usually an animal — that hunts, catches, and kills other living creatures in order to eat them and survive. The creature that a predator hunts is called its prey.
Predatory means acting like a predator — hunting, targeting, and harming something weaker in order to benefit yourself.
A predecessor is someone or something that held a particular position, role, or place before the current one — and has since been replaced by it.

Predestination is the belief that the ultimate fate or outcome of a person — most often, whether they will be saved or condemned in a religious sense — has already been decided in advance, before they were even born, by a higher power (usually God).
To predestine something or someone means to decide or determine what will happen to them before it actually happens — often long before, sometimes even before they are born or before events begin.
Something is predestined when it was already decided — before it happened — that it would happen, and nothing could have stopped it.
To predetermine something means to decide, settle, or establish it before the relevant event, process, or moment actually takes place.

A predicament is a situation that is difficult, unpleasant, or troubling — and most importantly, one that is hard to get out of. It is not just any ordinary problem. What sets a predicament apart is the feeling of being stuck.

To predicate something means to establish it on a specific foundation — to say that one thing rests on, depends on, or is made valid by something else. That foundation isn't optional background. It is the very thing the first thing requires in order to stand.

To predict something means to say what you think will happen in the future, before it actually happens. You look at what you know right now, you think it through, and you make a statement about what is going to happen later.
Predictability is the quality of something — a person, a thing, a situation, or an event — that makes it possible to know or expect what it will do, say, or be, before it actually happens.
A predilection is a strong, personal preference for something — a deep, settled liking that feels natural to who you are. It is not a passing interest or a casual choice.
To predispose someone to something means to make them more likely — in advance — to think, feel, behave, or develop in a certain way.
If you are predisposed to something, it means you already have a built-in tendency, lean, or readiness toward it — before you even encounter it directly.

A predisposition is a natural tendency or inclination that exists before something actually happens. It means you are already leaning in a certain direction — toward a particular behavior, reaction, outcome, or condition — even before it occurs.
"Predominantly" means mostly, mainly, or above all else — with a clear emphasis on one thing being the biggest, most common, or most powerful element in a situation.
To predominate means to be the strongest, most noticeable, most numerous, or most powerful element among a group of competing elements.
Preeminent means the very best, most important, or most distinguished — standing clearly above everyone or everything else in a particular area.
To preempt something means to act before it can happen, in order to stop it, replace it, or beat it to it.
Done to prevent something from happening, or to act before others can, as in "a preemptive strike."

Preen means to groom or tidy oneself, and to feel very pleased with yourself about it. Think of it as grooming + vanity rolled into one word. The word is used in two main contexts: for birds and for people.

A preface is a short piece of writing placed at the very beginning of a book, before the main content starts. Think of it as the author's personal note to you, the reader, written before you step into the actual book.

When you preface something, you say or write a few words of introduction before getting to your main point. Those introductory words are meant to prepare the listener or reader for what is coming next.
Serving as an introduction to something, as in "prefatory remarks."

A prefect is a person who has been placed in a position of authority or oversight — someone officially put in charge of something, whether that's a place, an institution, a group of people, or a specific function.
To prefer means to like one thing more than another — to feel that one option is better, more suitable, or more desirable than another when you are comparing two or more things.

"Preferably" means "if possible, this option would be better." It tells the listener that you have a first choice — a favourite among the available options — but you are not making an absolute demand.
A preference means liking one thing more than another. It is the feeling or judgment that makes you lean toward one option when you have more than one to choose from.
To prefigure something means to be an early version, sign, or symbol of something that will come later — to represent it in advance, before it fully exists or happens.

The most common meaning of pregnant is: a female who has a developing baby growing inside her body. When a woman (or female animal) is pregnant, she is carrying a baby that will be born in the future.

Prehensile describes a body part that is naturally built and adapted to grasp, grip, or hold onto things by curling or wrapping around them. It is almost always used to describe a part of an animal's (or human's) body.
Prehistoric describes anything that existed, happened, or was made before humans started writing things down.

Prejudice means forming an opinion about someone or something before you have enough facts, real experience, or solid evidence to justify it. Think of it as judging in advance — your mind is already made up before giving the subject a fair chance.
The word prelapsarian is an adjective. It describes a state of perfect innocence, purity, and harmony that existed before something went terribly wrong and ruined everything.
A prelate is a senior, high-ranking official in a Christian church who holds formal, official authority over others.
When something is preliminary, it means it comes before the main thing and helps prepare for it.
A prelude is something that comes before something else — and not just accidentally before it, but in a way that introduces, prepares, or leads into what follows.
Premature means happening too early — before the right time, before things are ready, or before enough time has passed.
Prematurely means before the right time — specifically, before something is ready, fully developed, or supposed to happen.
To premeditate something means to think about it, plan it, or decide to do it ahead of time — before it actually happens.

If something is premeditated, it means it was planned and thought about in advance, before it actually happened. The person who did it didn't act suddenly or by accident — they made a deliberate decision ahead of time and then carried it out.
Premier means the very best, the most important, or the highest-ranking among all others in a particular group, field, or category.

A premiere is the very first time a creative work — such as a film, a play, a TV show, a ballet, an opera, or a musical composition — is shown or performed to an audience. It is the opening moment of that work's public life.
A premise is a starting point — a statement, assumption, or idea that is accepted as true before anything else is built on top of it.

A premonition is a strong inner feeling that something — usually something bad or significant — is going to happen in the future, even though you have absolutely no logical reason, evidence, or information to believe so.
Premonitory is an adjective that describes something which warns you — in advance — that something else is about to happen, usually something significant, serious, or unpleasant.
Prenatal means existing, happening, or relating to the time before birth — specifically the period from the moment a baby is conceived (created inside the womb) until the moment it is born.

A preoccupation is something that takes over your mind and keeps pulling your attention toward it — often at the cost of other things. Your mind is "already occupied" by it before you engage with anything else.

When someone is preoccupied, their mind is so deeply caught up in a particular thought, worry, or concern that they are not fully "present" in the current moment. Their body is there, but their mind is somewhere else — busy with something else entirely.
To preoccupy someone means to fill their mind so completely — so dominantly — that they struggle to think about or pay attention to other things.

To preordain something means to decide or determine that something will happen — before it actually happens. And not just to plan it, but to fix it so firmly in advance that it is certain and unavoidable.
Preponderance means the larger, heavier, or more dominant share of something — whether that's numbers, evidence, power, influence, or importance.

Something is preponderant when it is so much greater — in power, influence, number, or importance — than everything else it is being compared to, that it clearly tips the balance in its favor. Think of an old-fashioned weighing scale.
When something preponderates, it is greater — in weight, number, influence, or importance — compared to everything else in that situation. It tips the balance. It holds the dominant position.
A preposition is a word that shows the relationship between two things in a sentence — usually between a noun (or pronoun) and some other part of the sentence.
Prepossessing means creating a good or attractive impression right away — usually at first sight or first encounter, before you've had time to get to know someone or something deeply.

Something is preposterous when it is so wildly unreasonable, so contrary to common sense, or so absurd that it almost doesn't deserve to be taken seriously. It's not just wrong — it's outrageously, almost laughably wrong or unreasonable.

Preppy is an adjective used to describe a person, a style of clothing, a place, or an overall atmosphere that strongly reflects the look, values, and lifestyle of wealthy, privileged, upper-class America — particularly the kind associated with elite private schools and old-money families.
A prerequisite is something that must be fulfilled, completed, or obtained before something else can happen or be allowed to proceed. It is a mandatory condition that comes first.
A prerogative is a special right or power that belongs exclusively to a particular person, group, or institution — usually because of who they are, what position they hold, or what role they play.
A presage is a sign or a feeling that warns you something is going to happen — usually something important, and very often something dark or threatening.

To presage something means to be a sign that it is about to happen — usually something important, and often something dark or troubling. When one thing presages another, it acts like an early signal from the future, visible in the present.

Presbyopia is a natural, age-related condition in which the eye gradually loses its ability to focus clearly on things that are close up — like a book, a phone screen, or a menu. It is not a disease. It is not an injury.
Prescience means the ability to know what will happen in the future before it actually happens.
Prescient means having the ability to correctly know or sense what is going to happen in the future, before it actually happens.
Prescind means to deliberately set something aside in your mind — to consciously choose to leave something out of your thinking so you can focus more clearly on something else.
To officially tell someone what must be done, used, or followed — with the authority to make that decision.
Something is prescriptive when it tells you what should be done, what must be done, or what the "correct" way of doing something is — based on a set of rules, standards, or authority.
A prescriptivist is someone who believes that language has a set of correct rules, and that everyone should follow those rules strictly.

When something or someone is presentable, it means they are in a good enough condition to be seen by other people, shown to others, or brought into a social situation — without causing embarrassment or disapproval.

A presentiment is a vague, uneasy feeling that something — usually something bad — is about to happen, even though you have no logical reason to believe it. It is not a thought you arrive at through reasoning. It is not based on facts or evidence.

"Presently" is an adverb that has two accepted meanings, and which one is intended depends on the context and where in the world the speaker is from. This is the single most important thing to understand about this word.
A preservative is a substance added to something — most often food, medicine, or a cosmetic product — to prevent it from going bad, spoiling, or becoming unsafe over time.
To preserve something means to keep it safe from harm, decay, or loss — to make sure it continues to exist in its original or good condition, despite things that could damage or destroy it.
To preside means to be the person officially in charge of a formal event, proceeding, or institution — and to actively direct how it runs.
Prestidigitation means the skill of performing magic tricks using fast, clever hand movements to create illusions and deceive an audience.

Prestige is the deep respect, admiration, and high regard that a person, institution, brand, profession, or object earns in the eyes of other people. It is how much others look up to something — how much weight, value, and importance the world places on it.
When something is prestigious, it means it is widely respected, admired, and highly regarded by people in society.
Presto means quickly, immediately, or all at once — but with a very specific flavor. It doesn't just mean "fast" in a plain, boring way.
Used to say that you think something is likely to be true, although you are not certain, as in "presumably she's already left."

"Presume" carries two distinct but related ideas. One is about believing something is true without having certain proof. The other is about daring to do something — often in a way that oversteps a boundary.

"Presumption" is about taking something for granted — either a belief you haven't fully proven, or a right or permission you haven't actually been given. These two directions of meaning look quite different on the surface, but they share that same core idea.
Presumptive means based on reasonable inference or probability, but not yet fully confirmed or proven.

Presumptuous describes a person who acts as if they have a right, permission, or authority that they do not actually have — and does so without asking, without being invited, and often without even realizing they're overstepping.
To presuppose something means to silently treat it as already true before you even begin saying what you actually want to say.

To pretend means to behave or speak as if something is true when you know it is not true. You know the reality, but you deliberately show a false picture — through your actions, expressions, or words.
A pretense is a false show — it's when someone makes something appear to be true, real, or genuine when it actually isn't. Think of it as a mask worn over reality.
Pretension is about claiming something you don't truly have — or acting as if you're more important, more skilled, more cultured, or more sophisticated than you actually are.
When something or someone is pretentious, it means they are trying to appear more important, impressive, intelligent, or sophisticated than they actually are.

To pretermit something means to pass it over — to leave it out, skip it, or set it aside, whether deliberately or through neglect. Think of it as intentionally (or carelessly) stepping around something instead of engaging with it.
"Preternatural" means beyond what is normal or natural — but in a way that feels so extreme, so far outside the expected range, that it's difficult to fully explain.
A pretext is a false or made-up reason that someone gives for doing something, while their real reason stays hidden.
"Pretty much" means almost entirely — so close to being completely true or completely done that the small remaining gap barely matters.

A pretzel is a type of baked snack food made from dough, most famous for its unique, knotted shape — like two loops intertwined, resembling someone crossing their arms over their chest. It's one of the most recognizable food shapes in the world.

To prevail means to succeed or win — but not just any ordinary winning. Prevailing always carries the sense that there was a real struggle, resistance, or difficulty involved. When something or someone prevails, they come out on top despite the challenge.
Prevalence means how widespread or common something is — among a group of people, within a place, or across a period of time.

Prevalent means something is widespread and commonly found within a specific group, place, or period of time. It describes something that exists in large enough numbers or frequency that it stands out as a dominant feature of that context.
To prevaricate means to deliberately avoid telling the truth clearly and directly — not by making up outright lies, but by being evasive, vague, or misleading.
Prevarication is the act of deliberately avoiding the truth — not necessarily by telling a flat-out lie, but by being evasive, vague, or misleading on purpose.
If something is preventable, it means it did not have to happen — because there were actions available that could have stopped it before it occurred.
Intended to stop something bad, such as illness, from happening, as in "preventative medicine."
Prey is any living creature that is hunted, caught, and eaten by another creature.

To prey on someone means to take advantage of or harm vulnerable people, as in "fraudsters prey on the elderly." Literally, of an animal, to hunt and kill another for food. It can also mean to trouble someone's mind constantly.
A small, sharp jab or the tiny hole it leaves ("a pin prick"); also a vulgar insult for a contemptible man.
To prick means to make a tiny hole or wound in something using a sharp point, or to cause a sharp, brief, stinging sensation — the kind you feel from a needle, a thorn, or a pin.
Pride is a feeling — specifically, a warm, satisfying feeling of being pleased with someone or something because of how good, worthy, or impressive it is.

When you pride yourself on something, it means you feel a strong sense of personal pride about a particular quality, skill, or ability that you believe you have — and you consciously work to maintain it as part of your identity.

Prideful means having too much pride — an excessive, stubborn sense of your own importance that gets in the way of how you think, behave, and treat others. It almost always carries a negative meaning.
A prig is a person who is convinced that they are morally better than everyone else, and who makes sure people around them know it.
A priggish person believes they are morally better than everyone around them — and they make sure you know it.
Stiffly proper and easily shocked by anything improper or rude, as in "prim and proper." Of appearance, very neat and formal.
A very proper, strait-laced person who insists that rules and correct behaviour be followed exactly.

In an opera company, the prima donna is the leading female singer — the star of the show. She is the most celebrated, most important, most skilled woman in the production. She gets the biggest role, the most stage time, and all the glory.

When you describe something as prima facie, you are saying: "This appears to be true, valid, or real based on a first look — and that first-look appearance is strong enough to be accepted as fact, unless someone proves otherwise."
When you use "prima facie" as an adverb, it means "on the face of it" or "at first sight" — that is, based on the immediate evidence in front of you, before any deeper digging.
Primacy means the state of being the most important, most powerful, or ranked highest above everything else.
"Primal" means first — but not first in a numbered list. It means first in the deepest sense: first in time, first in origin, or first in importance.
"Primary" is an adjective built on one simple idea: first. Not just first in a line, but first in the sense that truly matters — first in importance, first in order, or first as the original source.
A member of the group of mammals that includes humans, apes, monkeys, and lemurs. In the Church, a primate is the most senior bishop of a country or region.

Prime means first — not necessarily first in order, but first in rank, first in quality, or first in importance. Think of it as a stamp you put on something to say: this is at the top, above everything else.

"To prime" means to prepare something or someone in a specific, targeted way in advance — creating the right conditions so that what follows can work, succeed, or land with full effect. Priming is always the step before the main action.

A primer is always something that comes first to prepare the way for something else. That single idea connects all its meanings — whether you're painting a wall, learning a new subject, firing a bullet, or running a biology experiment.
"Primeval" describes something that belongs to — or feels like it belongs to — the very earliest age of the Earth or the universe. Not just old. Not just ancient.
"Primitive" means belonging to or resembling the earliest, simplest, or least developed stage of something. Think of it as the opposite of "advanced," "refined," or "modern."

Primogeniture is a system of inheritance — and the legal right that system creates — in which the firstborn child of a family automatically inherits everything from their parent: the land, the wealth, the titles, and any political or social power attached to them.

Primordial describes something that existed at the very beginning — not just "a long time ago," but from the absolute earliest point of time, before most other things came into being. It points to the deepest, oldest layer of existence.

To primp means to spend time carefully adjusting and tidying your own appearance — fixing your hair, touching up your makeup, straightening your clothes, checking yourself in a mirror — with a lot of small, fussy attention to how you look.
Every use of the word principal as a noun points to the same underlying idea: the one who is first in importance, authority, or responsibility in a given situation.
A principle is something that sits at the foundation of something else — a fundamental truth, a basic law, or a core belief that everything else is built upon or flows from.
To prink means to dress, groom, or decorate yourself very carefully and in a showy way — usually because you want to look impressive or attractive to others.
"Prior" means coming before something else — in time, in order, or in importance. It's a formal, precise way of saying "earlier" or "before."
To prioritize something means to decide that it is more important than other things, and therefore to give it your attention, time, or effort first — or more than you give to other things.
Priority means the state of being more important than something else, and therefore deserving attention, effort, or action first.
Prissy means excessively proper, prim, and fussy — especially about things like manners, cleanliness, or correct behavior — in a way that is annoying or slightly ridiculous to the people around you.

Pristine describes something that is in a perfect, unspoiled state — either because it has never been touched or harmed, or because it has been cared for so well that it still looks and feels exactly as it did when it was brand new.

The word private describes something — a thing, a place, a piece of information, or a feeling — that is not open to everyone. It belongs to, or is meant for, only a specific person or a specific group.

Privation means the state of being without the things you need to live a decent, dignified human life — things like food, clean water, warmth, shelter, clothing, and safety. It describes a condition of severe, painful lack.
A privilege is a special advantage, right, or benefit that belongs to a particular person or group — but not to everyone.

"Privileged" describes someone or something that has a special advantage, right, or benefit that most other people do not have. Think of a privilege as a bonus — something extra that puts you in a better position than the average person.
When you are privy to something, you have been let into the knowledge of something that is private, secret, or restricted — something that most other people don't know about or don't have access to.

A prize is something desirable that you get as a result of winning, competing, or being exceptionally lucky or skilled. It is something that doesn't just come to you freely — there is an element of earning it, winning it, or capturing it.

When the word pro bono describes something — a piece of work, a service, a case, a project — it means that professional work is being done completely free of charge, as an act of public service, for someone who cannot afford to pay for it.

When something is described as pro forma, it means it is done as a formality — to satisfy a rule, convention, or expectation — but without any real substance, genuine intent, or meaningful deliberation behind it.
Pro rata means proportional to a specific share or factor.
Representing yourself in a court case without a lawyer. The Latin phrase means "for oneself."

Proactive means acting in advance — doing something before a problem happens, before you are forced to, or before a situation gets out of control, rather than waiting and responding only after something has already gone wrong.
Probability is a number that measures how likely something is to happen.
The official legal process of proving that a dead person's will is valid and dealing with their property, debts, and possessions.

To probate means to put a deceased person's will — or their entire estate — through an official court process that legally validates, settles, and closes out everything the person left behind after death.

Probation means a trial period during which someone must prove themselves — by following rules, meeting standards, or demonstrating good behaviour — before they are fully accepted, trusted, or given complete freedom.
Having the power or tendency to prove something, or to help establish whether something is true.
A probe is something that goes into a place that is difficult, hidden, or hard to reach — in order to find out what is there.
To probe means to examine something very carefully and deeply, especially when the thing you are trying to understand is hidden, unclear, or hard to reach. It is not a casual or surface-level look.

Probity means the quality of having strong, reliable, and proven moral principles — particularly honesty, uprightness, and decency. A person of probity does the right thing consistently, not just when it's convenient or when someone is watching.

"Problematic" is an adjective that describes something carrying problems within it — something that causes difficulty, raises serious concerns, or comes with issues attached to it that cannot be ignored.
A proboscis is a long, tube-like or trunk-like flexible organ that sticks out from the head or front of an animal's face.
Relating to procedure — the official steps or rules by which something is done, as in "a procedural error."

"Proceed" means to move forward or continue — either physically, in an action, or in a sequence of events. Think of it as the act of going ahead with something, especially in a deliberate and purposeful way.

The noun proceeding refers to a formal, official action or series of steps — something that happens within a structured, rule-governed framework, such as a court of law, an official meeting, or an organized institution.
Proceeds means the money that comes in from a sale, an event, or any activity where something is exchanged for money.
When you process something, you put it through a series of deliberate steps in order to handle, transform, or deal with it in a systematic way.
A procession is a group of people — and sometimes vehicles — moving forward together in an organized, orderly line, usually as part of a formal or ceremonial occasion.
To proclaim something means to announce it publicly, confidently, and with a sense of importance.
A proclamation is an official, public announcement made by someone in authority, declaring something important for everyone to know.
A proclivity is a strong, natural tendency — built into a person's character — to repeatedly behave in a certain way or to be consistently drawn toward certain things.
To procrastinate means to delay or put off doing something you know you should do — not for a good reason, but simply because you don't feel like doing it right now.
A procrastinator is a person who keeps delaying or postponing tasks — especially important ones — and does them much later than they should, or sometimes never at all.

To procreate means to produce offspring — that is, to bring new life into existence through biological reproduction. When a living being procreates, it creates one or more new members of its own kind: a baby, a calf, a pup, a chick, and so on.
When you proctor something, you officially watch over it to make sure everything happens fairly and according to the rules.

To procure means to obtain or secure something through deliberate effort. It is not just "getting" something passively — it carries the idea that you actively worked, planned, or arranged in order to make it happen.

Procurement is the complete process through which an organization obtains the goods or services it needs — from first recognizing the need, all the way through to the final delivery and payment. It is not just the act of buying something.

To prod means to push, poke, or jab at something — either literally with your finger or an object, or figuratively to get someone to do something. Think of it as applying a small, sharp pressure — physically or mentally — to get a reaction or a result.
Prodigal means wastefully and recklessly extravagant — spending or using far more of something (usually money, resources, or time) than is wise or reasonable, without care for the consequences.
Prodigality means the quality or habit of spending money — or using any valuable resource — in a reckless, excessive, and wasteful way, often to the point of causing real harm to yourself.
When you call something prodigious, you're saying it is so vast or so much that it goes far beyond what is normal or expected.

A prodigy is a person — almost always a child or very young person — who possesses an extraordinary, almost unbelievable level of ability or talent in a particular area. We're not talking about someone who is simply "good" or even "very good."

A prodrome is an early symptom — or a cluster of early symptoms — that appears before a disease or medical episode fully takes hold. Think of it as your body's advance warning signal: a quiet, early message that something bigger is on its way.
Produce means fresh fruits and vegetables, especially ones that are grown on a farm and sold for people to eat.
Showing disrespect for God or sacred things, as in "profane language." It can also mean coarse and full of swearing, or in neutral use, secular rather than religious.

To profane something means to treat something sacred, holy, or deeply revered with disrespect or irreverence — to violate its sanctity, to defile it, to drag it down from its special status into something ordinary, base, or contemptible.

Profanity is a noun that refers to language — words, phrases, or expressions — that society widely considers offensive, rude, vulgar, or deeply disrespectful. In everyday life, people also call it "swearing," "cursing," or "foul language."
To claim something, often falsely, as in "he professed to know nothing about it." It can also mean to openly declare a belief or feeling, or to practise or follow a religion.
To proffer something means to offer it to someone, usually by holding it out or putting it forward for them to take, accept, or consider.
Proficiency means a high level of skill or ability in something — the kind of skill that lets you do something well, smoothly, and reliably, without struggling through it every time.

When someone is proficient at something, it means they are genuinely skilled at it — they can do it well, comfortably, and consistently. They have practiced and learned enough that the task no longer feels difficult or uncertain.

A profile is a view or description that captures the key features of something from a specific angle — not the full picture, but enough to clearly identify or understand it. Think of it as a clear, focused snapshot.
A profiteer is a person who makes unfair, excessive profit by taking advantage of a difficult or desperate situation — usually at the expense of ordinary people who have no other choice.
Profligacy means wild, shameless, reckless excess — specifically in spending money or using resources, but also in moral behavior.
Profligate means recklessly, shamelessly excessive — going so far overboard with something that it becomes harmful and morally wrong. It always carries a tone of strong disapproval.
Every meaning of "profound" comes from a single central idea: going very deep. Not deep in a physical sense, but deep in terms of meaning, feeling, understanding, or impact.
"Profoundly" means to a very deep, intense, and far-reaching degree. It does not just mean "very much."

Profundity means depth — but not physical depth, like the depth of a swimming pool. It means depth in a more powerful sense: depth of thought, depth of meaning, depth of feeling, or depth of understanding.

Profuse means existing, flowing, or being produced in very large — often overwhelming — amounts. When something is profuse, there is so much of it that it almost seems to pour out or overflow. Think of it as abundance cranked up to a high level.
"Profusely" means in a very large amount — so much that it is hard to ignore, hard to control, or even hard to stop.

A profusion of something means a very large, rich, and almost overflowing amount of it — so much that it feels almost extravagant or lavish. It's not just "a lot." It's a generous, abundant outpouring that impresses or overwhelms the senses.
A progenitor is the original source — a person, organism, or thing — from which others of its kind directly descend or develop. It is the very first link in a chain of descent or development.
Progeny means the children or descendants of a person, animal, or plant — essentially, whoever or whatever is born from or produced by something else.
Prognathous is an adjective that describes a face — human or animal — in which the jaw (or jaws) protrude noticeably forward, beyond the normal vertical line of the face.

A prognosis is an informed, expert prediction about how something — most often a medical condition — is expected to develop or turn out in the future. It answers the question: "What is likely to happen from here?"
To prognosticate means to predict or forecast what will happen in the future, typically by carefully studying current signs, patterns, evidence, or symptoms.
A prognostication is a prediction or forecast about the future — but not just any casual guess.
A program is a structured plan or set of things arranged in an organized way — either to guide actions, inform people, or instruct a machine.
To "program" something means to give it a set of instructions so that it behaves in a specific, predictable way.
Progression means the process of moving forward through a series of connected stages, one step following another in an ordered way.
"Progressive" means moving forward, developing gradually over time, or favoring change and improvement.
To prohibit something means to officially forbid it — to declare, through a rule, law, or authority, that something must not happen or must not be done.

When something is prohibited, it means it is officially and formally not allowed. There is a rule, a law, or an authority figure who has deliberately decided that this thing must not happen — and that decision carries real weight.
