The word "prohibitive" describes something that acts as a practical stopper — a barrier so extreme that it either outright forbids you from doing something, or makes doing it so unrealistic that almost nobody can proceed.
A project is a piece of planned work that has a clear goal, a beginning, and an end.
"Projected" means something that has been extended or thrown forward — either into the future (as an estimate or plan), onto a surface (as an image), or onto another person (as a feeling).
A projectile is any object that has been thrown, shot, kicked, or launched into the air and then travels on its own — freely, with nothing continuing to push or pull it along the way.
Every meaning of "projection" shares one underlying concept: something is extended or cast outward from a source — outward in space, outward in time, or outward from the mind.
In rhetoric, answering an objection before your opponent raises it. In storytelling, a flash-forward to a future event. In grammar, describing something as if it had already happened.
Belonging to or typical of the working class, people who earn wages through manual or industrial labour and own little property.

A proletarian is a person who does not own factories, land, machines, or any other tools of production, and who must therefore sell their ability to work — their time, their physical effort, their skills — to an employer in exchange for wages, in order to survive.
The proletariat is the working class — the large group of people in society who survive by selling their labor (their time, physical effort, and skills) to others in exchange for wages.
To proliferate means to increase rapidly and spread widely in large numbers.
Proliferation means a rapid, large-scale increase in the number of something — especially when that thing spreads outward in many directions at once, almost like it is multiplying on its own.
When you call someone or something prolific, you mean they produce a large amount of something — and usually, produce it consistently over time.

Prolix describes something — or someone — that uses far more words than necessary to express an idea. It means excessively long and wordy, in a way that becomes tedious or tiresome to the reader or listener.
Prolixity is the quality of using far more words than are needed to say something.
A prologue is a separate opening section that comes before the main body of a story, play, film, or other creative work.

To prolong something means to make it last longer than it would have naturally, normally, or originally been planned to last. You are stretching something out in time — pulling its ending further into the future.

A prom queen is a female student who is voted by her peers (fellow students) to be the most popular and admired girl at the prom. She is essentially given the title of the "queen" of the event — the most celebrated female student of the night.

A promenade is about leisurely, unhurried movement through a public space — either as an activity (the act of walking) or as a place (a path built for walking). Think of it as the opposite of rushing somewhere.
Prominence is the state of being easily noticed, standing out, or being well-known. The word captures the idea of being in front — not hidden, not in the background, but visible and recognized.
Prominent means standing out — something that is easy to notice because it rises above, projects beyond, or is more important than the things around it.

"Promiscuous" means not selective — engaging with many things or people without care, discrimination, or restriction. The single idea running through every use of this word is: no filter, no boundaries, accepting or doing things indiscriminately.

A promise is a serious statement in which you tell someone that you will (or will not) do something in the future. When you make a promise, you are giving that person your word — meaning they have every right to trust and depend on what you said.
A promontory is a high, raised piece of land that juts out boldly into a body of water — such as a sea, ocean, or lake — or that rises dramatically above the lower land around it.

"Promote" means to actively push something or someone forward — upward, ahead, or into greater prominence. Every use of this word, no matter the context, carries this same core spirit: something is being given a boost, lifted up, or moved forward.
"Promotion" always involves moving something or someone upward — or pushing something forward so it gets more attention, more support, or a higher status.

When something is prompt, it happens without unnecessary delay — right when it should, or even a little earlier. There is no dragging of feet, no keeping people waiting, no hesitation when action is clearly needed.
To prompt means to cause something to happen, or to cause someone to do or say something.
Promptitude means the quality of being prompt — that is, the habit or characteristic of acting quickly, efficiently, and right on time, without unnecessary delay or hesitation.
Promptly means doing something without unnecessary delay — at the right time, or as soon as it is needed or expected.
Promptness is the quality of doing something without unnecessary delay — acting, responding, or arriving at the right time, when it is expected or needed.
To promulgate something means to make it officially and formally known to a large number of people, especially through an authoritative announcement.

Promulgation is the official, formal act of making something — usually a law, rule, decree, or important decision — publicly known so that everyone is now bound by it or aware of it. It is the moment an authority declares: "This is now official.
When you say someone or something is prone to something, you mean they naturally tend to experience it, suffer from it, or do it — and it is almost always something undesirable or negative.

A prong is a thin, pointed spike that sticks out from a larger object. It is usually one of several such spikes that project outward from a shared base — though a single spike can also be called a prong.
A pronoun is a word that stands in place of a noun — a noun being any word that names a person, place, thing, or idea. Instead of repeating a noun again and again, you swap it out with a pronoun.

When you pronounce a word, you use your mouth, tongue, and lips to produce the sounds of that word. Every word in a language has a correct way of being spoken — a specific combination of sounds — and pronouncing it means producing those sounds accurately.

When "pronounced" is used as an adjective, it means so clearly noticeable that it is impossible to ignore or miss. It describes something that stands out strongly and leaves no doubt in the mind of the observer.

Pronto means right away, immediately, or without any delay. When you tell someone to do something pronto, you are telling them to stop wasting time and do it this very moment. There is a strong sense of urgency packed into this single word.
A pole or object used to support something or hold it up. Figuratively, a person or thing that gives support. A prop is also an object used by actors in a play or film.

Propaganda is information — or a mix of information, ideas, and images — that is deliberately created and spread to influence what a large group of people think, feel, or do, usually in favor of a particular cause, group, leader, or ideology.

A propagandist is a person whose job or goal is to spread propaganda — which is carefully crafted information designed to push people toward a particular belief, opinion, or action. The key is that a propagandist doesn't simply share information.

To propagandize means to deliberately spread biased, one-sided, or misleading information to push people toward a particular belief, attitude, or course of action — not to inform them honestly, but to shape how they think and feel.
To spread an idea, belief, or piece of information widely, as in "propagating rumours." It can also mean to grow new plants from a parent plant, or for a wave of energy to travel through something.
Propagation means the act of something spreading, multiplying, or being transmitted outward from a starting point — reaching more places, more people, or more things over time.

To propel something means to cause it to move forward — or in a specific direction — by applying force or power to it. That force can be physical (like an engine, a wind, a push) or non-physical (like an emotion, an ambition, a circumstance).
A propellant is any substance that pushes something else forward — or more precisely, any material that produces the force needed to drive an object through space.

A propensity is a natural, deep-seated tendency in a person (or thing) to behave in a certain way — especially one that shows up repeatedly and consistently, almost as if it is built into their character.

A prophecy is a statement that claims to reveal what will happen in the future — but it's not an ordinary prediction. What makes it a prophecy is its source: it is believed to come from God, gods, or some higher supernatural power.
To prophesy means to declare or announce what will happen in the future, often with a strong sense of authority, certainty, or divine inspiration.
A prophet is a person who is believed to speak on behalf of a god, a divine power, or a higher truth — delivering messages, warnings, or guidance that ordinary people cannot access on their own.
Something is prophetic when it turns out to have accurately predicted, hinted at, or foreshadowed something that happens in the future.
Intended to prevent disease or harm before it happens, as in "a prophylactic dose of antibiotics."
Propinquity means nearness — but it's a rich, layered kind of nearness. It can describe nearness in space, nearness in time, or nearness in relationship.

To propitiate someone means to do something — give a gift, make a sacrifice, or perform an act of submission — in order to calm the anger of a more powerful person or being, and win back their goodwill or mercy.

Propitiation is the act of satisfying the righteous anger of an offended party — usually by offering a sacrifice, a payment, or something of real value — so that their wrath is turned away and goodwill is restored.

Propitious means favorable — but in a specific, meaningful way. Something is propitious when it creates the right conditions for a good outcome, or when it strongly suggests that success, happiness, or good fortune is likely to follow.
A proponent is a person who openly supports, defends, or argues in favor of a particular idea, belief, policy, theory, or cause.

Proportion is about relationship — specifically, how one thing compares to another in terms of size, quantity, or importance. It answers the question: How much of one thing is there relative to something else?

When two things are proportional, it means they are related to each other in a consistent, balanced way — so that when one changes, the other changes in a matching, predictable manner, keeping the same ratio between them.

Proportionate means correctly matched in size, degree, or amount relative to something else. The key phrase here is "relative to something else" — this word is never used in isolation. Something can only be proportionate to something.

A proposal is a suggestion, plan, or offer that someone presents to others for their consideration — meaning, the other person or group gets to think about it, discuss it, and then either accept it, reject it, or modify it.
When you propose something, you bring an idea, plan, or suggestion forward — you put it in front of others so they can think about it, discuss it, or decide whether to accept or reject it.

A proposition is something that is put forward — an idea, a statement, an offer, or a plan that is placed in front of someone for them to consider, accept, reject, or respond to. Think of it as anything someone "puts on the table."
To propound something means to put forward an idea, theory, question, or belief for others to consider, examine, or discuss.
Proprietary means belonging to, or controlled by, a specific owner — and because of that ownership, others cannot freely use, copy, share, or access it without permission.
A proprietor is a person who owns something — most commonly a business, a shop, or a piece of property. Ownership is the single most important idea packed into this word.
Propriety means correct and appropriate behavior — the kind of behavior that a society, a group, or a particular situation considers proper, fitting, and acceptable.
Propulsion is the act or process of driving, pushing, or thrusting something forward — and also refers to the force itself that makes this happen.

Propulsive describes something that drives things forward — with energy, force, and momentum. Think of a rocket engine or a ship's motor: it propels — it pushes forward. When something has the quality of doing that, it's propulsive.
To prorogue a parliament means to officially end its current working session without shutting it down entirely.

Prosaic means dull, ordinary, and unimaginative — lacking any spark, beauty, or special quality. When you call something prosaic, you're saying it is flat and uninspired, the kind of thing that makes no impression on you whatsoever.
In its most widely used modern sense, the proscenium is the large structural arch or framed opening that separates the stage from the audience.
To proscribe something means to officially forbid it — to declare that it is not allowed and must not happen.
Prose is ordinary language — the natural way humans speak and write every day. When you write a letter, a text message, a school essay, a news article, or a novel, you are writing in prose.
To prosecute someone means to officially take them to court and try to prove they committed a crime.
Prosecution is the formal legal process in which an authority — usually the government — officially accuses a person of committing a crime and tries to prove that accusation in a court of law.
A prosecutor is a lawyer who works for the government and whose job is to take accused criminals to court and prove that they are guilty of the crime they are charged with.
A proselyte is a person who has converted from one religion, belief system, or set of ideas to another — especially after being persuaded by someone else.

To proselytize means to actively try to convince other people to adopt your beliefs, religion, ideology, or cause. It's not just believing something strongly yourself — it's going out of your way to spread that belief to others and win them over to your side.
Prosody is the study of the musical and rhythmic qualities of language — the patterns of sound, stress, and rhythm that give speech and poetry their texture, flow, and feel.
The possibility that something will happen, as in "little prospect of success." It can also mean a person likely to succeed, a potential customer, or an extensive view of a landscape.
The word prospective means expected or likely to be or become something in the future.

A prospectus is an official, formal document prepared by an organization — such as a company, a university, or a fund — that gives detailed information about what that organization is, what it offers, and what a person can expect if they choose to get involved with it.
To prosper means to grow, succeed, and do very well — especially over a period of time.
Prosperity is the state of doing very well in life — especially financially — where you have more than enough of what you need, things are going your way, and life feels abundant and secure.

Prosperous means thriving and doing very well — especially in terms of money, wealth, and overall living conditions. When you describe someone or something as prosperous, you're saying they have abundance, comfort, stability, and success.

Prostrate means lying flat on the ground, stretched out face downward. Picture someone lying completely flat with their body pressed to the floor, their face turned toward the ground. That physical image is the heart of this word.
To lie flat on the ground face down, especially in worship or submission, as in "they prostrated themselves before the king." To be prostrated means to be completely overcome, as by grief or illness.

Prostration means the act of lying flat on the ground — specifically, face downward — usually before someone or something far greater than yourself. It is what your body does when your spirit wants to say: "I am nothing before you."
A protagonist is the central character of a story — the person (or being) that the story is primarily about and mostly built around.
Capable of taking on many different forms, roles, or qualities — constantly changing, remarkably versatile, and hard to pin down.
A protectorate is a territory or country that is officially under the control and protection of a stronger, more powerful country — but without being fully absorbed into it.

A protest is an open, deliberate act of expressing strong disagreement with something a person — or a group of people — believes is wrong, unfair, or unjust. What separates a protest from a private opinion is that it is outward.

To protest means to express strong disagreement or opposition to something, especially something you feel is wrong, unfair, or unjust. It is not a quiet or mild disagreement — the word carries a sense of force, urgency, and conviction.

A protestation is a strong, emphatic statement — a declaration made with force and conviction, either to insist that something is true (especially one's innocence, sincerity, or feelings), or to formally object to something.
Protocol always means the same thing across all its uses: A set of rules, steps, or conventions that have been agreed upon in advance, so that a process runs smoothly, correctly, or safely.
A prototype is the first, original version of something — created specifically to serve as a model, a test, or a standard for everything that comes after it.
To protract something means to stretch it out in time — to make something last longer than it normally would, or longer than it needs to.
When something is protracted, it means it lasts much longer than expected, necessary, or desirable. It is drawn out over a long period of time — often painfully or tediously so.
To protrude means to stick out or push outward beyond a surface or boundary, in a way that is clearly noticeable.

Protruding describes something that sticks out from a surface or from the rest of a body or object. Imagine you're running your hand along a flat wall, and suddenly your fingers hit a nail that is slightly pushed out. That nail is protruding.

A protuberance is a part of something that sticks out or bulges outward beyond the surface around it. It is a raised, jutting section — something that projects out from the main body of an object, a surface, or a living thing.
Something is protuberant when it bulges or swells outward from a surface — when it sticks out in a rounded, bump-like way instead of lying flat.
A protégé is a person — usually younger or less experienced — who is actively guided, supported, and sponsored by someone more powerful, experienced, or influential in a particular field.
To prove means to establish that something is true — not just to suggest it, not just to believe it, but to demonstrate it in a way that removes reasonable doubt.
Provenance means the origin and documented history of something — where it came from, who owned or held it over time, and how it ended up where it is today.

Provender is dry, stored food given to animals — especially large working animals like horses, donkeys, mules, and cattle. Think of things like oats, hay, corn, barley, straw, or a mix of grains that farmers keep in a barn or stable to feed their animals.
A proverb is a short, well-known sentence that expresses a general truth or a piece of wisdom about life.
Referring to something from a well-known saying or expression, as in "the proverbial needle in a haystack." It can also mean so widely known as to be famous, as in "his proverbial generosity."
To provide something means to make it available for someone who needs or can use it. The heart of the word is this: there is a need, and you are meeting it.
The protective care and guidance of God or a higher power, as in "trust in providence." It can also mean being careful and wise in planning for the future.
Provident describes someone who carefully thinks ahead and prepares for the future — especially by wisely managing their money, resources, or energy now, so they are not left struggling later.
When something is described as providential, it means it happened as if a higher power — God, fate, or the universe — quietly arranged it on purpose.
A province is a large, officially defined region that a country is divided into for the purpose of governance and administration.
Narrow-minded and unsophisticated, with limited interests and old-fashioned views, as in "provincial attitudes." Literally, relating to a province or to regions outside the capital.

Provision is about making something available to meet a need — whether that "something" is food, a service, a rule, or money set aside for the future. It always involves someone thinking ahead and ensuring that what is needed is there when it is needed.
When something is provisional, it means it is arranged for now, but not yet final.
In motor racing, the fastest qualifying time set so far, which puts a driver at the front of the starting grid unless someone else beats it before qualifying ends.

A proviso is a condition or qualification that is attached to an agreement, statement, permission, or law. It essentially says: "This is allowed / agreed / true — but only under this specific condition."

A provocateur is a person who deliberately stirs things up — who intentionally says or does things to make other people react with anger, outrage, conflict, or strong emotion. The key word here is deliberately.

A provocation is anything — an action, a remark, a gesture, or a situation — that causes someone to react, especially with anger, aggression, or strong emotion. It is the trigger that produces a response in another person.

Provocative means causing a strong reaction. When something is provocative, it stirs something up inside people — strong emotions, sharp opinions, heated debate, or intense desire. It provokes, meaning it pushes people out of a neutral, calm state.

To provoke means to cause a strong reaction — either in a person or in a situation. That reaction is almost always intense: anger, excitement, debate, conflict, curiosity, or a physical response like an allergic reaction.
A provost is a person who holds a senior position of authority and oversight — someone placed in charge of managing an institution, a community, or a group of people.
A prow is the front end of a ship or boat — the pointed, forward-facing part that pushes through the water as the vessel moves ahead. Think of it as the "nose" of a ship.

Prowess means an exceptional, impressive level of skill or ability in a particular area. It's not just being good at something — it's being remarkably good, in a way that earns respect and admiration from others.
To prowl means to move around quietly, slowly, and secretly — usually because you are searching for something or waiting for an opportunity. The key idea is stealth with purpose.

A prowler is a person who moves around quietly, secretly, and stealthily — usually in or around a place where they are not supposed to be — with a suspicious or harmful intention. The word almost always carries a sense of danger and threat.

Proximal means nearest or closest to a specific point of reference. That "point of reference" is the key idea — proximal always describes something's position in relation to something else, usually a central point, an origin, or a point of attachment.
Proximate means nearest or most immediately connected. It describes whatever is closest to something — in a chain of causes, in a sequence of events, or in a series of goals.

Proximity means nearness — the condition or state of being close to someone or something. When two things are in proximity, a small amount of space, time, or distance separates them. When they are not in proximity, a large gap exists between them.
A proxy is a person, thing, or system that is officially authorized to stand in for someone or something else — to act, speak, decide, or operate in their place, as if they were the original.
A person who is easily shocked or offended by anything to do with sex, nudity, or crude humour, even when most people would find it normal.

Prudence is the quality of thinking carefully and wisely before you act — especially by considering what might happen in the future as a result of your choices today. A person who has prudence does not rush into decisions.
Prudent means showing careful, wise judgment — especially by thinking ahead, weighing consequences, and avoiding unnecessary risks before making a decision or taking an action.

"Prudential" means relating to, arising from, or guided by careful, practical wisdom — the kind of wisdom that helps a person, organization, or system think ahead, weigh risks, protect interests, and make sensible long-term decisions rather than impulsive or reckless ones.

Prudery is the attitude or behavior of being excessively and unnecessarily strict about what is considered proper, decent, or moral — especially when it comes to anything related to sex, the human body, romance, or language that others might consider mildly rude or casual.

Prudish describes a person who is easily shocked, offended, or uncomfortable when anything related to sex, the human body, nudity, or "improper" behavior comes up — and who strongly disapproves of it, often making their disapproval very visible.
When you prune something, you carefully cut away certain parts of it — not to damage it, but to make it better. The parts you remove are the ones that are dead, unnecessary, excessive, or harmful.

Prurient describes an excessive, unhealthy, or shameful interest in sexual matters — particularly the kind that feels indecent, obsessive, or voyeuristic (like a peeping-tom's curiosity). It carries a strong moral judgment.
To be too curious about other people's private affairs, as in "I don't mean to pry." It can also mean to force something open or apart, as in "prying the lid off a can."
A psalm is a sacred poem or song written to praise, thank, worship, or speak to God.

Psephology is the scientific study of elections and voting. More specifically, it is the careful, data-driven analysis of how people vote, why they vote the way they do, and what the patterns in voting tell us about society and politics.

Pseudo means falsely claiming to be something, or appearing to be something without actually being it. Think of it as a mask — it looks like the real thing on the outside, but underneath, the real substance is missing.

A pseudonym is a made-up name that a person uses in place of their real name. It is not the name they were born with or legally registered under — it is a name they have chosen for themselves, usually for a specific purpose or audience.
To psych someone out means to mess with someone's mind on purpose so that they feel nervous, lose their confidence, or start doubting themselves — and as a result, they perform worse or give up.
Psyche means the totality of a person's inner world — their mind, soul, and spirit considered as one whole thing. It is the complete inner life of a human being.
Producing intense, dream-like changes in perception, as certain drugs do; or describing art with swirling shapes and vivid, clashing colours.
Psychiatric is an adjective that simply means "relating to psychiatry."

A psychiatrist is a medical doctor who specializes in mental health — meaning they are trained to understand, diagnose, and treat conditions that affect a person's mind, emotions, thoughts, and behavior.
A psychic is a person who claims to have special mental powers that go far beyond what ordinary human senses can do.

A psychologist is a trained professional who studies the human mind and behavior — and uses that knowledge to help people understand themselves, solve mental and emotional problems, and live better lives.
Psychology is the scientific study of the human mind and behavior.

A psychopath is a person who has a deeply ingrained personality pattern marked by an almost complete absence of empathy, guilt, and genuine emotion — combined with a strong ability to charm, manipulate, and exploit others, all while feeling no real remorse for the harm they cause.
Psychopathic is an adjective that describes a set of personality traits — specifically a deep, persistent pattern of coldness, manipulation, and a near-total absence of genuine empathy or conscience.
Psychosis is a serious disruption in a person's mental state in which they lose touch with reality.

Psychosomatic is an adjective used to describe a physical symptom, illness, or bodily condition that is caused or worsened by a person's mental or emotional state — rather than by a purely physical cause like a virus, injury, or disease.
A condition in which a person strongly believes they are pregnant and shows real physical signs of pregnancy, such as a swollen belly and missed periods, although there is no baby.
When you call something psychotic, you are saying it relates to, involves, or is caused by a condition called psychosis — a serious state of mind in which a person loses touch with reality.

A psychotic (plural: psychotics) is a person who is experiencing psychosis — a severe mental state in which the person has lost touch with reality. That phrase, "lost touch with reality," is the heart of the word, so it's worth unpacking carefully.
A mental illness in which a person loses touch with reality, often hearing or seeing things that are not there or holding false beliefs.
A pterodactyl is a type of flying reptile that lived millions of years ago and is now completely extinct. Think of it like a giant lizard with wings — something like a dragon, but real.
Pubescent is an adjective that primarily means going through puberty or having recently reached puberty.
"Publication" is all about one central idea: making something available to the public. Everything this word means connects back to that idea.
Publicity means attention from the public. When people — a large number of them — notice, talk about, or are made aware of someone or something, that is publicity.
To publicize something means to deliberately spread information about it so that a large number of people become aware of it.

To publish means to take something private and make it available to the public. That's the single most important idea behind this word. The moment you publish something, it stops being just yours and becomes something others can access, read, see, or hear.

To pucker means to draw, gather, or squeeze something together into tight wrinkles, folds, or a small, rounded shape. Think of it as the opposite of being flat and smooth — something that puckers bunches up, tightens, and creases.

The word "puckish" means playfully mischievous — in a light, charming, and completely harmless way. When you call someone puckish, you're saying they love to tease, play tricks, and stir up gentle mischief, but with absolutely no cruelty in it.

Pudding is a soft, cooked food. Whatever form it takes, it is always soft in texture — never crunchy, never dry. But beyond that single shared quality, the word means very different things depending on where you are in the world.

Pudgy describes someone (or something) that is short and round in a soft, chubby way. Think of a body — or a body part — that looks compact, a little overweight, and gently rounded, not angular or lean.

Pueblo means a town, village, or community — a place where a group of people lives together. This is its everyday meaning in Spanish, where it is used the way an English speaker would use "town" or "village."
Puerile means childishly silly, immature, or trivial — but specifically in a way that is embarrassing and unbecoming of an adult.

Puerility means childishness — specifically, the quality of thinking, speaking, or behaving in a way that is silly, trivial, or immature, especially when the person doing it is old enough to know better.
A puffball is most commonly a type of fungus — a living organism similar to a mushroom — that grows in a perfectly round or ball-like shape, almost like a small white balloon sitting on the ground.

A pugilist is a person who fights using their fists — in other words, a boxer. If someone is described as a pugilist, it means they box, whether as a professional sport, a trained skill, or their way of life.

Pugnacious means having a strong, habitual tendency to argue, fight, or pick confrontations. A pugnacious person doesn't just get into fights occasionally — they actively seek them out, or are so quick to react that conflict seems to follow them everywhere.

Pugnacity is the quality or character trait of being eager, ready, and inclined to fight or argue. A person who has pugnacity doesn't wait for conflict to come to them — they lean toward it, sometimes actively seek it out, and rarely back down from it.
Puissance simply means great power or mighty strength.
Puissant means extremely powerful, mighty, or commanding in strength and authority.
Pulchritude means physical beauty — specifically, the quality of being strikingly and outwardly beautiful, usually when referring to a person.
Pulchritudinous simply means physically beautiful. When you call someone or something pulchritudinous, you are saying they possess striking, remarkable physical beauty — beauty that you can see.

To pule means to cry or whine in a weak, thin, and feeble way — a sound that is soft, high-pitched, and helpless. Think of the tiny, pitiful whimpering of a sick kitten, or a child sniveling and complaining under their breath rather than crying out boldly.
To "pull out all the stops" means to do everything you possibly can to achieve something — to use every resource, every skill, and every effort available to you, without holding anything back.

To "pull strings" means to secretly use your personal influence, contacts, or connections with powerful people to get something done — often in a way that skips the normal rules or processes that others have to follow.

Pullulating describes something that is teeming, swarming, and multiplying at an overwhelming rate — usually referring to living things packed densely together while actively reproducing or spreading.
"Pulmonary" means relating to, involving, or affecting the lungs.
A pulpit is a raised, enclosed platform — like a tall box or stand — found inside a church or other place of religious worship.
To pulsate means to expand and contract repeatedly in a steady, rhythmic pattern — like a heartbeat.
Pulse refers to a regular, rhythmic beat or throb — something that rises, falls, and repeats in a steady pattern, like a living rhythm.
To pulverize something means to crush, grind, or pound it with such force and thoroughness that it is completely reduced to powder or dust.
Pumice is a type of rock — but it's unlike most rocks you'd think of. It's a very light, rough, and sponge-like rock that comes from volcanoes.

To pummel something or someone means to hit them hard, again and again, repeatedly — usually with your fists. It is not a single punch or a gentle tap. It is a sustained, forceful, relentless series of blows.

If someone is punctilious, it means they pay extremely careful attention to rules, codes of conduct, etiquette, and formalities — and they follow them with almost zero tolerance for mistakes or shortcuts.
Punctiliousness is the quality of being extremely careful and precise about following rules, proper procedures, codes of conduct, or etiquette — right down to the tiniest detail.

If someone is punctual, it means they do things exactly at the time they are supposed to. Most often, it means arriving somewhere or completing something on time — not late, and not so early that it causes inconvenience.
Punctuality is the quality of being on time — consistently and reliably. It means doing what you said you would do, when you said you would do it.
To punctuate something means to mark it, interrupt it, or break it up at certain points — often in a way that adds emphasis, clarity, or a noticeable pause.

A pundit is a person who is seen as an expert in a particular subject and who publicly shares their opinions and analysis about it — most commonly through media like television, newspapers, radio, or the internet.

When something is pungent, it has a smell or taste (or sometimes a quality of language) that is so sharp, strong, and piercing that it almost forces itself upon you. You can't ignore it. It hits you immediately and powerfully.

To punish someone means to make them experience something unpleasant, painful, or difficult because they did something wrong. The unpleasant thing they experience is the punishment — it is the direct consequence of their wrongdoing.
When we say something is punishing, we mean it is so difficult, harsh, or demanding that it feels like a form of punishment — even if nobody intended it that way.
Punitive means relating to punishment, or intended to punish someone.
A long, flat-bottomed boat pushed along with a pole; in sport, a kick of a ball dropped from the hands; informally, a bet or gamble.
"Puny" describes something — or someone — that is both small and weak, to the point of being noticeably inadequate or unimpressive.

A pup is simply a young dog. It means exactly the same thing as "puppy" — just a shorter, slightly more informal way of saying it. When a dog gives birth, the babies are called pups. They are small, dependent on their mother, and not yet fully grown.
A child or young person being taught at school, or a person taught by a particular teacher. The pupil is also the dark, round opening in the centre of the eye that lets in light.
A puppet is something — or someone — that is controlled by another. That single idea of control from the outside is the heart of this word, and it runs through every way the word is used.
Purblind means having a dim, limited, or foggy perception — either of the world through your eyes, or of reality through your mind.
To purchase means to obtain something by paying money for it. In other words, it means to buy.

In the Catholic Christian tradition, Purgatory (written with a capital P when used in this sense) is a state — or sometimes described as a place — that certain souls enter after death. It is not Heaven, and it is not Hell.

A purge means the act of removing or clearing out something — people, things, or substances — that are considered unwanted, harmful, impure, or dangerous. The word carries a strong sense of thoroughness and urgency. It's not a gentle tidying up.
To purge means to forcefully and completely remove something that is unwanted, harmful, or impure — from a place, a system, a body, or a group.
To purify something means to remove everything in it that does not belong — everything harmful, dirty, unwanted, or foreign — so that only the clean, true, or good version remains.
A purist is a person who believes that something should be kept in its original, traditional, or "correct" form — and who strongly resists any changes, mixtures, shortcuts, or modifications to it.

A person with very strict moral or religious views, especially one who disapproves of pleasure and enjoyment. Historically, the Puritans were English Protestants of the 16th and 17th centuries who sought to simplify the Church.
The area surrounding a place; its outskirts, as in "the purlieus of the city." It can also mean a place where someone spends a lot of time; their haunt.

To purloin something means to steal it, but in a quiet, sneaky, sly way — without force, without confrontation, and often without the victim noticing right away. Think of a pickpocket silently lifting a wallet, not a robber demanding it at gunpoint.
Purport means the main meaning, substance, or overall message that something conveys — especially a document, statement, letter, or speech.
To purport means to claim or appear to be something — but with a built-in hint of doubt about whether that claim is actually true.

"Purported" means claimed to be something, but not proven, and often doubted. When you put the word "purported" in front of something, you are saying: "Someone has said this is true, but I am not confirming it — and I may even be skeptical about it."

"Purposeful" describes a person, action, or approach that has a clear goal or purpose behind it — and is consciously directed toward that goal with focus and determination. Nothing about it is accidental, random, or aimless.

A purse is a small bag designed to hold money — especially coins. Picture a compact, hand-sized pouch, often made of leather or fabric, with a clasp or zipper to keep it shut. You open it, put your coins in, and close it again.
To purse means to press your lips together tightly so that they form a small, puckered, rounded shape — almost like a tiny knot or a small "o" pulled inward.
"Pursuant" as an adjective lives almost entirely inside one phrase: "pursuant to." Mastering that two-word phrase is all you need.
Pursue means to go after something — with intention, effort, and persistence over time.

Pursuit means actively going after something. Whether you are physically chasing someone, working hard to achieve a goal, or engaging in a regular activity you love — the word "pursuit" captures the idea of ongoing, directed effort toward something.

To purvey means to supply or provide something — but not in a casual, one-off way. It carries the sense of doing so regularly, professionally, or as an established role. Think of it as a more formal, deliberate kind of providing.
A purveyor is someone — a person, a business, or an organization — that regularly supplies or provides something, typically as their main activity or profession.
Purview means the range, scope, or extent of what something — or someone — is responsible for, has authority over, or is legitimately concerned with.
Someone who is pushy tries very hard to get what they want — and in doing so, they pressure, rush, or impose on other people without caring much about how those people feel.
Pusillanimity is the quality of being weak-spirited, cowardly, and timid — especially when a situation calls for courage, decisiveness, or standing up for what is right.

Pusillanimous means showing a shameful lack of courage or willpower — being so weak in character that you avoid anything difficult, risky, or confrontational, even when the situation genuinely calls for bravery or decisiveness.
To postpone something, as in "don't put off your homework." It can also mean to make someone dislike something or lose interest in it, as in "the smell put me off," or to distract someone.
To put one's finger on something means to identify or pinpoint exactly what something is — especially when that thing is unclear, vague, or hard to define.
"Put one's foot down" means to make a firm, final decision and refuse to change it, no matter what. It is about asserting authority or taking a strong stand on something.
When you "put out" a fire, you stop it from burning.

Putative means generally considered or believed to be something — based on common assumption, reputation, or reasonable inference — but not formally proven, officially confirmed, or legally established beyond doubt.

Putrefaction is the process by which dead organic matter — the body of an animal, a piece of meat, a fish, a fallen fruit — breaks down, rots, and gradually falls apart due to the action of bacteria and other tiny microorganisms.
To putrefy means to rot and decay in a way that produces a horrible smell and causes something to completely break down and fall apart.
Putrescent means in the process of rotting — actively decaying, decomposing, and breaking down.

Putrid means rotting, decayed, and producing a disgusting smell. It describes something that was once organic — like meat, food, or a body — that has broken down so badly that it now smells and looks deeply revolting.

A putsch is a sudden, forceful attempt by a small group of people to seize control of a government — overnight if possible — by using violence, the threat of violence, or military force, rather than through elections, laws, or any legitimate political process.

When you use puzzle as a verb, it means to cause someone to feel confused because they cannot understand something — or, from the other direction, to think hard and carefully about something you find difficult to understand.
When you are puzzled, you are confused and uncertain because something does not make sense to you — and your mind is actively trying to figure it out, but the answer isn't coming.
A solid shape with a flat base and triangular sides that meet in a point at the top, like the great stone tombs of ancient Egypt.
A pyre is a large, deliberately built pile of wood — or other burnable material — that is set on fire in order to burn a dead human body as part of a funeral ritual.

A pyromaniac — a person with a compulsion to set things on fire — or, more casually, someone fascinated by fire. It is also short for pyrotechnics, the special fire and firework effects used in shows.
Pyroclastic is an adjective used in geology and earth science. It describes anything that is made of fragments violently blasted out of a volcano during an eruption.

Pyromania is a rare mental health disorder in which a person feels a powerful, uncontrollable urge to deliberately set fires — and experiences a deep sense of pleasure, excitement, or relief from doing so.
A pyromaniac is a person who has a powerful, uncontrollable urge to set things on fire — and who feels deep satisfaction or relief when they do so.

Pyrotechnics refers to the art, craft, and science of creating and using fire-based devices — most famously, fireworks. Think of the spectacular explosions of color you see lighting up the sky on New Year's Eve or Independence Day.
Pyrrhic describes a victory — or any kind of win or achievement — that costs the winner so dearly that the win itself becomes hollow, meaningless, or even a disaster in disguise.
A person who dishonestly claims to have medical skill or knowledge. Informally, any doctor. It is also the harsh sound a duck makes.

Quackery is the dishonest practice of claiming to have medical knowledge, skills, or treatments that you do not actually have — especially to trick people into paying for fake cures or useless remedies.
Short for several words: a quadrangle (a square courtyard), a quad bike, a quadruplet, or the quadriceps muscles of the thigh.

A quadrant is one of four equal parts that you get when you divide something into four sections — specifically by cutting it with two lines that cross each other at a right angle (like a "+" or a cross).
The adjective quadrennial has two closely related meanings, and both are correct and widely used: 1. Happening once every four years; 2. Lasting for a duration of four years.

A quadruped is an animal that walks, runs, or moves on four legs. If an animal uses four limbs as legs to get around on a surface — whether it's a field, a forest floor, or a desert — it is a quadruped.
To quaff something means to drink it — but not in just any ordinary way. It means to drink eagerly, enthusiastically, and in big, satisfying gulps.
A difficult, complicated situation that is hard to get out of, as in "a legal quagmire." Literally, an area of soft, wet, muddy ground that you sink into.
A quail is a small, plump bird. When someone says "quail," they almost always mean this little bird — and everything connected to it (its meat, its eggs).
To quail means to feel a sudden rush of fear that causes you to shrink back, lose courage, or feel helpless in the face of something threatening or overwhelming.

"Quaint" means attractively old-fashioned or charmingly unusual. When you call something quaint, you are saying two things at once: it feels like it belongs to a simpler, older time — and you find it sweet, pleasant, or endearing because of that.
Quaintly means in a way that is charmingly old-fashioned, pleasantly unusual, or attractively strange — especially in a manner that feels like it belongs to a simpler, earlier time.
Quaintness is the quality of being attractively old-fashioned, charmingly unusual, or pleasingly different from the modern world — in a way that makes you feel warmly drawn to it, not put off by it.
To quake means to shake or tremble, but not in a gentle or small way. It describes a shaking that is powerful, uncontrollable, and often caused by a strong force or a very strong emotion.
The subjective, felt qualities of conscious experience — what it is like to see red or taste sweetness — as opposed to the physical processes that cause them.
Having the training or skills needed for a job ("a qualified nurse"); or limited and not complete ("a qualified success").

A qualifier is something that either limits or conditions a statement, or proves that someone or something meets a required standard. These two ideas — limiting and proving eligibility — are the two main lives this word leads.
To meet the conditions needed for something ("She qualified for the final"); or to limit or add conditions to a statement.
The word qualitative means "relating to the nature, characteristics, or type of something" — as opposed to its amount, size, or number.
"Qualitatively" means in terms of nature, character, or qualities — as opposed to in terms of numbers, amounts, or measurements.
A qualm is an uneasy feeling inside you — a nagging sense of doubt or discomfort — about whether something you are doing, or are about to do, is right, wise, or acceptable.

A quandary is a situation where you are stuck and genuinely don't know what to do. It's not just that the situation is hard — it's that you feel mentally trapped, unable to clearly choose a path forward.

Something is quantifiable if it can be measured, counted, or expressed as a specific number or amount. If you can attach a concrete figure to something — a weight, a speed, a temperature, a percentage, a score — then that thing is quantifiable.

Quantification is the act of turning something into a number — the process of measuring, counting, or assigning a numerical value to something so that it can be understood, compared, or analyzed with precision.
A quantifier is a word, phrase, or symbol that tells you how many or how much of something is being referred to — or how broadly a statement applies.

To quantify something means to measure it and express it as a number or an amount. In other words, you take something — an idea, a problem, a feeling, a result, anything — and you figure out how much of it there is, then put that into numbers.

Quantitative means relating to quantity — that is, relating to how much or how many of something there is, expressed through numbers and measurement. If something is quantitative, it can be counted, measured, or calculated. It lives in the world of numbers.
When you do something quantitatively, you are dealing with it through numbers, amounts, or measurements — not through feelings, opinions, or descriptions.
A quantum is the smallest possible, indivisible unit of something — a fixed, discrete packet that cannot be broken down any further.
A theory proposing that consciousness and memory in the brain arise from quantum physical processes, rather than from ordinary chemical and electrical activity alone.
A quantum phenomenon in which two particles become so linked that measuring one instantly affects the state of the other, no matter how far apart they are.
When someone says something is a "quantum leap," they mean it is a sudden, dramatic, and enormous improvement or advancement — a change so big and so fast that it feels almost impossible or magical.

A thought experiment based on the many-worlds theory, suggesting that a person who repeatedly risks death in a quantum experiment would always find themselves in a branch of reality where they survived.
A quantum effect in which a tiny particle passes through an energy barrier that it would not have enough energy to cross according to ordinary physics.

The Quantum Zeno Effect is the phenomenon where a quantum system can be prevented from changing its state by measuring it very frequently. In other words: watching something closely enough, in the quantum world, can freeze it in place.

A quarantine is a period of enforced separation and restriction placed on a person, animal, or object that has been — or is suspected of having been — exposed to a contagious disease, but who is not yet confirmed to be sick.

To quarantine something or someone means to separate them from others and keep them in a controlled, restricted space — typically because they might be carrying a disease, infection, or contamination, and you want to prevent it from spreading to others.
When something or someone is described as quarantined, it means they have been deliberately kept separate and isolated from others — usually to stop something harmful from spreading.
One of the tiny particles that make up protons and neutrons; also a soft, fresh cheese.

A quarrel is an angry, heated disagreement between two or more people. It is not just a calm difference of opinion — it carries real emotional weight. When people have a quarrel, they are upset, frustrated, or angry at each other. Voices may be raised.

To quarrel means to have an angry, heated argument with someone. It is not a calm, peaceful disagreement — it carries a sense of emotional tension, frustration, or hostility between two or more people.

Someone who is quarrelsome is a person who has a strong habit or tendency to argue, pick fights, and disagree with others — very often over small or unnecessary things. A quarrelsome person doesn't always need a real reason to start a conflict.
A person or animal that is being hunted or chased, as in "the police closed in on their quarry." A quarry is also a large open pit from which stone is dug out.

A quarterback is the most important player on a team in American football. Think of them as the captain on the field — the person who touches the ball on almost every single play and decides what the team does next.

A quartermaster is a person in a military or naval organization whose job is to manage and provide essential support — though exactly what that support looks like depends on whether you're talking about an army (land forces) or a navy (sea forces).
Rooms or lodgings where someone lives or stays, especially soldiers or servants ("the officers' quarters"); also more than one quarter.
A quarto is a type of book (or a single document) made by taking a large, full sheet of paper and folding it twice — first in half, and then in half again.

A quasar is an extraordinarily powerful, extremely distant celestial object — the brilliantly glowing core of a very young galaxy, powered by a colossal black hole devouring enormous amounts of matter.

"Quash" means to put a complete and forceful end to something — so thoroughly that it cannot come back. It's not about slowing something down or weakening it. It's about eliminating it entirely, often in a single decisive act.
"Quasi" means almost, but not quite — or more precisely: resembling something, but not truly being that thing in the full, genuine, or official sense.

"Quaternary" is an adjective that revolves entirely around one idea: the number four. Something described as quaternary is either made up of four parts, belongs to a fourth stage in a sequence, or is organized around a group of four elements.
A quatrain is a set of four lines in a poem. The word itself simply means "a unit of four poetic lines."
A quaver is a specific musical note that tells a musician how long to hold a sound. This meaning is standard in British and Commonwealth English (UK, Australia, Canada, etc.).

To quaver means to speak or sing in a voice that trembles or shakes unsteadily, instead of coming out smooth and controlled. Think of it like this: imagine a straight, calm line — that is a steady voice.
When something is described as quavering, it is trembling or shaking in an unsteady, wavering way. The word is used almost exclusively to describe sounds — and most often, the human voice.

A quay is a solid, flat, man-made platform built along the edge of a body of water — such as a harbor, river, or canal — where ships and boats can pull up alongside, tie themselves securely, and stay while cargo is loaded or unloaded, or while passengers get on or off.
The quayside is the area of ground, space, and activity that exists right alongside a quay — the immediate surrounding zone next to it.

Queasiness is the noun that describes an uncomfortable, uneasy, unsettled feeling — most often felt in the stomach — that makes you feel like you might vomit, even if you actually don't end up vomiting. It is the state or condition of feeling queasy.
When you feel queasy, you feel an uncomfortable, unsettled sensation — like something is wrong inside you and your body is protesting it.
Queenly means having the qualities, appearance, manner, or presence that you would naturally expect of — or associate with — a queen.
An old word for strange or odd ("a queer feeling"); today mainly used for people who are not heterosexual, a meaning many have reclaimed with pride.
To queer the pitch means to spoil or ruin someone's plans or chances before they even get a proper opportunity to try.
To quell something means to put a complete stop to it — usually something powerful, threatening, or deeply uncomfortable — through force, authority, or deliberate effort.

Quench means to completely stop, put out, or fully satisfy something that is active, intense, or pressing. Think of it as bringing something that is "going" — burning, demanding, or urging — to a total end or a full sense of relief.

Quenching means the act of completely stopping, satisfying, or cooling something down — usually something that was intense, active, or overwhelming. Think of it as bringing something powerful to a sudden end.
Quenchless means impossible to stop, put out, or satisfy — no matter what.
Querulous describes a person (or someone's voice, tone, or manner) that is constantly complaining — especially in a whiny, grumbling, and irritable way, often about small or unimportant things.
When someone does something querulously, they do it in a complaining, whining, or grumbling way — usually with a voice or attitude that sounds fretful, irritable, and dissatisfied.
Querulousness is the habit or tendency of constantly complaining, whining, or grumbling, usually about things that are small, unimportant, or beyond anyone's control.

A query is a question — but a specific kind. It's a question that seeks precise information, asks for clarification, or expresses a doubt about something. Think of it as a purposeful, targeted question, not just casual conversation.
To query means to ask a question — but not just any casual question. When you query something or someone, you are asking with a specific purpose: to check, verify, or express doubt about something.
A quest is a long, serious, and deeply motivated effort to find, reach, or achieve something that is very important — and often very difficult to obtain.
To question means either to ask someone something or to doubt something. These two uses look different on the surface, but they share the same spirit: you're not taking something as settled.
Doubtful and not to be trusted, as in "questionable motives." It can also mean open to doubt or debate, as in "it is questionable whether this will work."
A queue is an ordered line of people or things that are waiting — waiting for their turn to be served, processed, or dealt with.

"Qui vive" is almost always used in the fixed phrase "on the qui vive." In this form, it means a state of keen, active watchfulness — being sharply alert, on the lookout, and mentally ready to notice or react to whatever might happen next.
A quibble is a small, minor objection or complaint — one that focuses on a tiny, unimportant detail rather than the main point of something.
To quibble means to raise objections or argue about something small and unimportant, especially when the bigger point is obvious and fair.

A quibbler is a person who argues about small, unimportant details — especially to avoid admitting that the bigger point is correct, or to seem clever and critical without actually engaging with what truly matters.

Quibbling is the act of raising petty, minor objections or making unnecessarily fine distinctions — especially to avoid addressing the real, central point of a discussion, or simply to find something to argue about, even when there is no genuinely important reason to do so.
A quiche is a savory, baked dish that looks like an open pie. It has a crispy pastry shell on the bottom and sides, and is filled with a creamy, egg-based mixture that is baked until firm.

"Quick" describes something that takes little time or happens without delay. It points to speed — either of movement, action, or thought. When something is quick, it doesn't linger. It happens and it's done.

If someone is quick-witted, it means their mind works very fast and very smartly at the same time. They can understand a situation in an instant and respond to it in a clever, sharp way — almost without pausing to think.

Quicken means to make something faster, more alive, or more intense — or to become those things. Think of it as a word that carries energy. When something quickens, it either speeds up, springs to life, or sharpens into a more active state.

Quicksand is a type of ground that looks solid and safe to walk on, but isn't. The moment you step on it or apply weight to it, it behaves like a thick liquid and you start to sink into it. It traps whatever stands on it.

Quicksilver is the old, common name for mercury — a naturally occurring metallic element. When scientists and textbooks talk about "mercury," everyday language and literature often call the very same thing "quicksilver." They are two names for one thing.

A quid pro quo is a mutual exchange — a deal where one person gives something to another person specifically because they are receiving something in return. It means: "I give you this, and you give me that."
The essential nature of something, the qualities that make it what it is. It can also mean a trivial point or a quibble.
A quidnunc is a person who is obsessively, restlessly curious about the latest news, gossip, and other people's business — and who can't help but talk about it constantly.
Quiescence means a state of being still, quiet, calm, and inactive — especially when that stillness is temporary, and activity is expected to return at some point.

Quiescent means temporarily still, calm, or inactive — but in a way that carries an important hidden message: the stillness is not permanent. Whatever is quiescent has the capacity for activity, but it is resting, paused, or suppressed for the time being.

Quiet describes something that produces little or no noise, or something that is free from disturbance, activity, or attention. It is about the absence of something — sound, movement, busyness, or commotion.

Quietism means a deliberate attitude of stillness, passivity, and withdrawal — a conscious choice to not act, not resist, and not engage with the world around you, but instead to remain inwardly calm and quiet.
Quietude means a state of complete calm, stillness, and peace — in a place, in a situation, or within a person's mind.
Death, or something that brings about death, as in "the final quietus." It can also mean a final end to something, or a release from a debt or duty.

A quiff is a hairstyle — or the front section of a hairstyle — where the hair at the very front of the head, just above the forehead, is swept upward and often slightly backward, forming a thick, voluminous wave, curl, or peak that rises visibly from the head.

A quill is most fundamentally a large feather from a bird — specifically the kind with a long, stiff, hollow tube at its base. Think of the big feathers on the wing or tail of a goose, swan, or eagle. That thick, hard tube you see at the bottom of a feather?
A quilt is a thick, warm bed covering made of three layers of fabric stitched together.

Quinoa is a food — specifically, the tiny seed of a plant that grows in South America, primarily in the high-altitude mountain regions of Peru and Bolivia. People all over the world cook and eat these seeds, treating them much like rice or oats.
The most perfect or typical example of something, as in "the quintessence of elegance." In ancient philosophy, the fifth element, thought to make up the heavenly bodies.
"Quintessential" means the most perfect, most pure, most complete example of something.
"Quintessentially" means in a way that represents the purest, most perfect, and most complete example of something.

A quintet is a group of exactly five — five people, five things, or a piece of work made for five. The word almost always implies that these five belong together, work together, or form a single unit.
A quip is a short, clever, witty remark — usually said quickly and spontaneously — that is meant to amuse, impress, or make a sharp point in a light-hearted way.

When someone quips, they say something short, clever, and funny — usually in the middle of a conversation or situation, almost without pausing to think. It's a quick flash of wit, delivered casually, not as a prepared speech or a long joke.
A quipster is a person who is known for making quick, clever, witty remarks — someone who always seems to have a sharp, funny comeback or a smart, humorous observation ready to go.

A quirk is something small, unusual, and a little unexpected — something that makes a person, thing, or situation stand out from what is considered normal. It's the kind of detail that makes you think, "Hm, that's a bit odd — but interesting."
Quirkiness is the quality of being unusual or different from what is normal — but in a way that is interesting, charming, or endearing, rather than disturbing or bad.

When you call something or someone quirky, you mean they have small, unusual, or unexpected qualities that make them stand out from what is considered normal — but in a way that is charming, interesting, or at least harmless, rather than disturbing or wrong.
A quisling is a traitor who actively helps an enemy that has taken control of their own country.
A formal release from a debt or obligation, or a document confirming it. In older use, it means repayment or revenge.
A quiver is a long, narrow case or tube designed to hold and carry arrows. Think of it as an arrow's "home."

To quiver means to make very small, rapid, and continuous trembling movements. Think of a leaf on a tree shaking quickly in a soft breeze — that is quivering. The movements are slight and fast, not big dramatic shakes.
To tremble slightly because of strong anger at something unfair or offensive.

Quivering describes something that is making small, fast, repeated trembling movements — tiny vibrations that happen quickly and without stopping, often because of a strong emotion or physical condition.

A quivering is a small, rapid, repeated trembling or shaking movement — one that happens very quickly and usually without much force. It is not a big, violent shake. It is a slight, fast, continuous flutter, almost as if something is vibrating in place.
Quixotic describes something — a plan, a goal, a person, or a mission — that is driven by noble, romantic ideals but is completely impractical and disconnected from reality.

When someone does something quixotically, they are pursuing a noble, romantic, or grand ideal in a way that is wildly impractical or unrealistic — yet they do it anyway, with total sincerity and passion, often ignoring how impossible the goal actually is.
Quixotism is the quality or habit of chasing grand, idealistic dreams that are hopelessly impractical — while being almost blind to the cold, hard realities of the world.
When someone has a quizzical expression, it means their face shows mild confusion or puzzlement — but often with a light touch of gentle amusement or playful doubt mixed in.

When you do something quizzically, you do it in a way that shows you are puzzled, curious, or questioning — but not in a deep or serious way. It's a gentle, mild kind of "I don't quite understand this" or "something seems odd here."
A wooden toy figure whose arms and legs jerk wildly when its string is pulled. Figuratively, a politician who does whatever someone else tells them to do; a puppet.
In medieval universities, a debate in which a scholar had to answer questions on any subject put by the audience. In music, a light-hearted piece that combines different popular tunes.
Quondam means "that once was" or "who was once." It is used to describe someone or something that held a certain role, title, or identity in the past — but no longer does.
Of a meeting, having enough members present to make its decisions valid.

A quorum is the minimum number of members of a group that must be present at a meeting for that meeting to be officially valid — meaning any decisions, votes, or actions taken during that meeting are considered legitimate and binding on the group as a whole.

A quota is a fixed, specific amount, number, or share that is officially set in advance — either as a minimum you must reach, a maximum you must not exceed, or a target you are expected to hit — for a particular person, group, country, or category of thing.
Something is quotable when it is worth repeating — when the words are so well-chosen, striking, clever, or meaningful that people feel the urge to share them, remember them, or cite them.
Quotidian means everyday — both literally (happening every single day) and, more powerfully, in the sense of being so ordinary and routine that it barely registers notice.
A quotient is the answer you get after dividing one number by another.
A rabbi is a Jewish religious leader and teacher who has been officially trained and certified in Jewish law, Jewish scripture, and Jewish thought.

A rabble is a crowd of people that is noisy, disorderly, and out of control — essentially, a mob. Think of a group of people pushing, shouting, and causing chaos, with no sense of organization or discipline. That is a rabble.

A rabble-rouser is a person who deliberately stirs up strong, raw emotions — such as anger, fear, resentment, or outrage — in a group of people, usually to push them toward a strong reaction or action.

When you describe something as rabble-rousing, you mean it is deliberately designed to stir up strong, passionate — often angry — emotions in a crowd of ordinary people, usually to push them toward action, protest, or unrest.

The word rabid essentially means dangerously extreme — either in the very literal sense of being infected with a deadly disease, or in the figurative sense of being so intensely passionate about something that you've lost all sense of reason and calm.

Rabies is a disease — specifically, a viral disease that attacks the brain and nervous system of mammals. Once a person or animal is infected and symptoms begin to appear, rabies is almost always fatal.

Racism is the belief that humans can be divided into groups called races (such as Black, White, Asian, etc.), and that some races are naturally better, smarter, more capable, or more worthy than others — combined with the attitudes, actions, and systems that flow from that belief, which result in people being treated differently and unequally based on their race.

A racket is not just any sound — it is a loud, chaotic, and annoying noise that bothers people or prevents them from focusing. The word bundles together the idea of disorder, unpleasantness, and disruption.
When you use racket as a verb, you are describing movement or activity that is noisy, restless, and energetic — the kind that creates commotion and disturbance around it.

To racketeer means to run or take part in an organized illegal scheme designed to make money — usually through dishonest, corrupt, or violent means. The person doing it is called a racketeer, and the scheme itself is called a racket.
A raconteur is a person who tells stories and anecdotes in an exceptionally skillful, entertaining, and captivating way.
Slightly sexual or suggestive, as in "racy jokes." It can also mean lively and spirited, or, of a car or horse, designed for speed.

Radar is both a technology and the physical device that uses that technology to detect and locate objects — especially objects that are far away, invisible to the naked eye, or hidden by darkness, fog, or distance.
Looking worn out and haggard, with the effects of a hard life or years of excess showing clearly in the face and body.

Radiant means sending out or filled with light, heat, or a quality so strong and visible that it seems to pour outward from a source. Think of the sun — it doesn't just sit there and look bright; it actively sends out light and warmth in all directions.

To send out light, heat, or energy in all directions. Figuratively, to clearly show a strong feeling or quality, as in "she radiated confidence." It can also mean to spread out from a central point, as in "roads radiating from the city."

Radiation is energy or particles traveling outward from a source — spreading in all directions, the way ripples spread from a stone dropped in water, or the way light from a lamp fills the room around it.

"Radical" means going all the way to the deepest level of something — not staying on the surface, not making small tweaks, but reaching down to the very foundation and changing or affecting it completely.
A person who wants complete social or political change. In chemistry, a radical is an unstable molecule or group of atoms. In maths, it is the root of a number, or the root sign (√).

Radical skepticism is the philosophical position that we cannot have any genuine, certain knowledge — especially about the world around us, about reality itself, or sometimes even about our own minds.

When we call something radioactive, we mean it contains atoms that are spontaneously falling apart — releasing energy in the form of radiation — all on their own, without needing any outside push or trigger.
A radius is the straight-line distance from the center of a circle (or sphere) to any point on its edge.
Raffish describes someone (or something) that is slightly disreputable, unconventional, or rough around the edges — but in a way that is oddly charming and attractive.
A raffle is a competition in which people buy numbered tickets for a chance to win a prize. No skill or knowledge is involved — the winner is chosen purely by luck.
One of the sloping beams that hold up a roof; also a group of turkeys.

A rag is a piece of cloth that is old, torn, frayed, or worn out — something no longer useful in its original form. Rags are used for humble, everyday tasks: wiping up spills, cleaning surfaces, polishing shoes, or applying paint or oil.

A rag doll is one of the oldest and most classic children's toys in the world. It is a doll made entirely from soft cloth or fabric, stuffed with cotton, wool, or any soft filling material to give it a body shape.
A ragamuffin is a person — most often a child — who looks dirty, messy, and poorly dressed, typically wearing clothes that are torn, tattered, or worn out.
Rage is an extremely intense, violent form of anger — so powerful that it becomes very difficult or impossible to control.
Rage-bait is content that is deliberately designed to make you angry so that you react, share it, or engage with it — and that reaction is exactly what the creator wanted.
Ragged describes something that is rough, uneven, and lacking smoothness or neatness — whether that applies to cloth, a surface, a sound, a performance, or even a person's condition.

Raggedy means looking worn out, torn, frayed, untidy, or in a generally poor, falling-apart condition. When something is raggedy, it gives you the impression that it has been neglected, used too hard, or never properly taken care of — and it shows.
"Ragtag" describes a group of people — or a collection of things — that is disorganized, randomly thrown together, and made up of mismatched parts that don't really belong with each other.
A rail is a long, rigid bar — usually made of wood or metal — that is fixed in place to support, guide, separate, or protect. That's the central image: a bar that runs along something, doing a job.
To rail means to complain or protest in a loud, angry, and bitter way — especially about something you feel is deeply unfair or wrong.
A railing is a barrier or fence-like structure made of one or more horizontal bars — called rails — that are held up by vertical posts.
Raillery is good-natured, playful teasing — the kind where everyone laughs, including the person being teased.
Clothing or garments (literary), as in "kings in royal raiment."
"It's raining cats and dogs" means it is raining very heavily — not just a light shower or drizzle, but a powerful, intense downpour where water is falling fast and hard.
A rainforest is a thick, dense forest that receives a very large amount of rainfall throughout the year — typically at least 2,000 millimetres (about 79 inches) annually, though many get far more.
"Raise" always means you are causing something to go higher, increase, or come into being. You are the one doing it. Something else is receiving your action.
A garden tool with a row of teeth on a long handle, used to gather leaves; also an old word for a stylish but immoral man.
"Rakish" describes something or someone that looks or feels stylishly bold, dashing, and a little bit rule-breaking — in a way that is often charming or attractive rather than simply bad.

When something or someone is described as rallied, it means they have come back stronger after a period of weakness, struggle, or being scattered — or that they have been brought together with renewed energy and purpose.
The most everyday meaning of rally is a large, organized gathering of people who share a common purpose — usually to show support for something or to express strong feelings about a cause.
To rally means to come back together — or to bring something back — after a period of weakness, confusion, separation, or falling apart.
A ram is a fully grown male sheep. Female sheep are called ewes, and young sheep of either sex are called lambs.

To ramble means to move or progress without a fixed direction, plan, or clear purpose. Whether it's your feet, your words, or even a plant — if it wanders freely without following a straight or organized path, it rambles.
"Rambling" describes something that wanders — it moves, spreads, or flows in many different directions without a clear, straight course or a focused purpose.
Rambunctious describes someone who is bursting with wild, noisy, and uncontrolled energy — so much so that they become difficult to calm down or manage.
Ramen is a Japanese noodle dish — a bowl of wheat-based noodles sitting in a rich, savory broth, topped with various ingredients.
A ramification is a consequence or result — but specifically one that is serious, far-reaching, or complex, often spreading outward in ways that affect many things at once.
