Ramify means to branch out — to divide or spread from a single point into many smaller parts, paths, or consequences, the way branches grow out from a tree trunk, or the way cracks spread across a wall from a single impact point.

A ramp is a sloped surface — a smooth, angled path that connects two places at different heights. Think of it as the alternative to stairs: instead of going up or down in steps, you move along a continuous incline.
To increase the level, speed, or intensity of something, often gradually, as in "ramp up production."
When someone or something rampages, they move through a place in a wild, violent, and uncontrolled way — causing damage, destruction, and chaos as they go.

When something is described as rampant, it means it is spreading or happening in a way that is completely out of control, on a very wide scale, and unchecked — usually because nobody is stopping it or because nobody can stop it.
A rampart is a broad, raised wall or mound of earth and stone built around a castle, fort, or city to protect it from enemy attacks.
Ramshackle describes something that is so poorly built, badly maintained, or loosely held together that it looks like it could fall apart at any moment.
Rancid describes food — especially food that contains fat or oil — that has gone stale and spoiled in a very specific, deeply unpleasant way, producing a sharp, sour, and offensive smell and taste.
Rancorous means full of deep, bitter, long-lasting hatred or resentment. When someone is rancorous, they carry a sharp, poisonous hostility toward another person — and they don't let it go.
Rancour is a deep, long-lasting feeling of bitter hatred or resentment toward someone.
Randiness is a noun that refers to the state of feeling strong sexual desire or arousal.

Random describes something that happens without any pattern, plan, purpose, or predictability. When something is random, no specific outcome was chosen or favored — whatever happened, happened purely by chance.

Randomness is the quality of something happening without any fixed pattern, plan, or controlling rule — where no specific outcome is forced to occur, and no one can know in advance what will happen next.
"Range" refers to the space between two limits — a low point and a high point. Everything within those two limits belongs to that range.

A ranger is someone whose job or role involves moving across, watching over, or operating in a large, often wild or remote area. Think of someone who doesn't sit behind a desk — they roam, patrol, and cover great distances of land.
Rangy describes a body — usually of a person or animal — that is tall, lean, and long-limbed. Think: stretched out, slender, with noticeably long arms and legs relative to the rest of the body.

A rank is a specific position within an ordered system — a particular slot in an arrangement where people or things are placed at different levels based on some quality: authority, importance, skill, experience, or value.

To rankle means to cause a feeling of persistent, slow-burning irritation, bitterness, or resentment — and crucially, that feeling doesn't go away quickly. It lingers. It festers. It keeps coming back.

To ransack a place means to search through it in a rough, hurried, and disorderly way — turning everything upside down — usually to find something valuable or to steal. The key idea is that the search is not careful or gentle.
A ransom is a payment — almost always money — that a criminal demands in exchange for releasing something or someone they have taken and are holding against the owner's will.
When someone rants, they speak (or write) at great length about something that angers, frustrates, or upsets them — in a loud, heated, and often uncontrolled way.
Rapacious describes someone — or something — that seizes and takes things with extreme, aggressive greed. We're talking about money, land, resources, food, or power.

Rapacity is the noun that names an intense, aggressive form of greediness — an overwhelming drive to grab, take, or seize as much as possible (usually money, wealth, power, or resources) with absolutely no concern for fairness, decency, or the harm inflicted on others in the process.
Rapid means happening very quickly or moving at a very high speed — faster than what is normal or expected in that situation.

A rapier is a type of sword — but not just any sword. It is a long, thin, lightweight sword with a very sharp pointed tip, designed almost entirely for stabbing (thrusting the tip into an opponent) rather than slashing or chopping.

Rapine means the violent, forceful seizure of someone else's property — especially on a large scale. Think of an invading army tearing through a city, grabbing valuables, destroying homes, and taking everything they can carry.
To rappel means to descend — slide yourself down — a steep or vertical surface using a rope.
Rapport is the sense of ease, trust, and mutual understanding that makes a relationship feel natural and comfortable.

Rapprochement means the process by which two parties — countries, organizations, or people — who previously had a hostile, tense, or broken relationship, begin to move toward each other again in a friendlier, more cooperative way.

A rapscallion is a person who behaves badly — someone who is mischievous, dishonest, untrustworthy, or generally up to no good. Think of someone who bends the rules, pulls tricks, tells lies for personal gain, or gets into all kinds of trouble.
When someone is rapt, they are so completely absorbed and fascinated by something that the rest of the world seems to disappear.
Rapture means a feeling of extreme joy or delight — so powerful and overwhelming that it feels like it completely takes you over. It is not ordinary happiness.
Rapturous means filled with, showing, or causing an extreme, overwhelming sense of joy or delight — the kind so intense that it almost feels like you've been swept off your feet by it.
Rara avis is a Latin phrase that literally translates to "rare bird."
Rare means something that does not appear, happen, or exist very often. It is something you don't come across easily — you might go a long time without ever seeing or experiencing it.
Belonging to a small, exclusive, intellectual, or upper-class world, as in "the rarefied world of high finance." Literally, of air, thin and low in oxygen, as at high altitudes.

To rarefy something means to make it less dense — to spread it out, thin it down, or make it less concentrated. Think of it as the opposite of compress or condense. When you compress something, you push its parts closer together.
A rascal is a person who behaves in a dishonest, mischievous, or naughty way.
Rash means acting too quickly, or describing an action done too quickly, without stopping to think carefully about what could go wrong.

A rash is an area of your skin that has changed its normal appearance — usually becoming red, blotchy, spotty, bumpy, or irritated — as a reaction to something going wrong inside or outside your body.
To say something in a harsh, rough voice, as in "'Get out!' he rasped." It can also mean to scrape something with a rough tool, or to make a harsh, grating sound.
Raspy describes a sound — almost always a voice or something that sounds like a voice — that is rough, scratchy, and grating rather than smooth and clear.
To ratchet means to move something — a level, an amount, a situation, an intensity — steadily in one direction, in small steps, one after another, in a way that is difficult or impossible to reverse.
To ratify something means to give it official, formal approval — so that it becomes legally valid, binding, and actually in force.

A ratio is a way of comparing two or more quantities to show how they relate to each other in size or amount. It doesn't tell you the exact size of those quantities — it only tells you their relationship.
Ratiocination is the process of thinking through something step by step, using strict logic, to reach a conclusion.

A ration is a fixed, limited amount of something — usually food, water, fuel, or another essential supply — that is officially given to each person, especially when that thing is scarce or needs to be carefully controlled.
When you ration something, you carefully control how much of it each person gets — or how much of it you yourself use — because there is a limited supply and it needs to last.
Rational means based on, guided by, or capable of clear reasoning and logic — rather than emotion, impulse, instinct, superstition, or bias.

A rationale is the logical reasoning that explains why something exists, was decided, or is being done. It is the thinking behind a decision, rule, action, plan, or belief — laid out in a clear, reasoned way.
Rationalism is the belief that reason — your mind's ability to think, analyse, and draw logical conclusions — is the most reliable and important source of knowledge and truth.
Rationalization is the act of constructing seemingly logical reasons to justify a decision, belief, action, or feeling — when, in reality, those reasons were not what actually drove it.

When you rationalize something, you come up with a logical-sounding explanation for something you did or want to do — but this explanation is not your real reason. Your real reason is something you find embarrassing, shameful, or hard to admit.
A rattle is fundamentally about a rapid, repeated series of short, sharp knocking sounds — the kind made when hard objects hit each other again and again in quick succession.
Loud, harsh, and wild, as in "raucous laughter" or "a raucous party."
To ravage something means to cause severe, widespread, and often lasting destruction to it.

When something is described as ravaged, it means it has been severely and extensively damaged — so badly that it looks broken, worn down, or ruined. The key thing to understand is that "ravaged" isn't just damaged.

To rave means to express something in an intense, unrestrained way — either with wild excitement and praise, or with wild anger and madness. In both cases, the person is going well beyond calm, controlled expression.
To tangle something, or to untangle it — the word can mean both. It can also mean to fray or come apart into threads.
Ravening describes a creature that is so savagely, desperately hungry that it becomes wild, frenzied, and violent in its need to hunt and devour prey. It is not simply about being hungry.

Ravenous means extremely hungry — not just a little hungry, not even just "very hungry," but hungry in an intense, urgent, almost uncontrollable way. Picture a wolf that hasn't eaten in days. It isn't calmly waiting for food.
A ravine is a deep, narrow cut in the earth with steep sides, usually formed by running water over a long period of time.
To fill someone with intense delight, as in "ravished by the music." In older use, it means to rape someone, or to seize and carry them away by force.
Ravishing means extremely and strikingly beautiful — so beautiful that it almost overwhelms you the moment you see or experience it. It is not just ordinary beauty.
Raw means: in a natural, unfinished, or unprotected state — something that hasn't been treated, processed, softened, or prepared yet.
Rawhide is the untreated, dried skin of an animal — most commonly cattle — that has been cleaned but has not gone through any chemical process to soften or preserve it further.

To raze something means to destroy it so completely that nothing is left standing. When a structure is razed, it is not merely damaged, not partly ruined — it is brought all the way down to ground level. Flat. Gone.
To reacclimate means to get used to something again — to go through a process of adjustment a second (or further) time, after a gap or change has disrupted an earlier period of being comfortable.

"Reactionary" describes a person, belief, attitude, policy, or movement that not only opposes change, but actively wants to reverse changes that have already happened — to roll society back to an earlier state that they consider better.

A reactionary is a person who believes that society has already changed too much in the wrong direction — and who actively wants to reverse those changes and return to an older way of life or an older political and social order.

To "read between the lines" means to understand a hidden or implied meaning that is not directly stated. It means paying attention to what someone suggests or hints at, rather than just what they literally say or write.
To "read too much into" something means to find more meaning, significance, or implication in something than is actually there.
When you "realize" something, a moment happens in your mind where something that was previously unclear, unnoticed, or unknown suddenly becomes clear to you.

A realm is a defined space or domain — an area that "belongs to" or is governed by something or someone. Think of it as a complete world unto itself, with its own rules, contents, and boundaries (even if those boundaries are invisible or imaginary).

Realpolitik is the practice of making political decisions based entirely on practical considerations — especially power and national self-interest — rather than on moral values, ideals, or principles.

A ream is a standard unit used to measure and sell paper. One ream equals 500 sheets of paper. When you walk into a stationery shop and buy a pack of printer paper, that pack almost always contains one ream — 500 sheets bundled together.

To reap means to cut and collect a crop — grains like wheat, barley, or rice — when it is ready to be harvested. Farmers reap their fields after months of growing. This is the original, literal meaning.
A person or machine that cuts and gathers grain crops at harvest; "the Grim Reaper" is death shown as a robed figure with a scythe.
To reappraise something means to look at it again carefully and form a fresh judgment about it — especially after some time has passed, new information has come in, or circumstances have changed.

Reappraised, in its adjective form, describes something that has already gone through this second evaluation. It is used to describe the subject — the thing, person, idea, or work — that was looked at again and given a fresh verdict.
When you say something is reasoned, you mean it is based on careful, logical thinking — not on gut feeling, emotion, or guesswork.
To reassure someone means to say or do something that removes their worry, fear, or doubt, and makes them feel calm, safe, or confident again.
Rebarbative means so unpleasant, harsh, or off-putting that it repels you — it makes you want to back away, avoid it, or stop engaging with it altogether.
A rebate is a sum of money that is given back to you after you have already paid for something. Think of it as a delayed, partial refund — but not because something went wrong.
A rebel is a person who refuses to accept, obey, or submit to authority, rules, or an established system — and who actively pushes back against it in some way.

To rebel means to actively resist, oppose, or fight against a power, authority, or set of rules that controls you — particularly when you believe that control is wrong, unfair, or simply something you refuse to accept.
Rebellious describes someone (or something) that refuses to accept authority, control, or rules — and actively pushes back against them.
A rebuff is a rejection — but not just any ordinary rejection. It is a sharp, cold, and blunt refusal given to someone who has tried to reach out, connect, offer something, or get closer to you.
To rebuff someone means to reject them, or their request, offer, or approach, in a sharp, blunt, and unfriendly way.
A rebuke is a firm, sharp expression of disapproval directed at someone because they did something wrong, irresponsible, or unacceptable.
To rebuke someone means to tell them clearly and firmly that what they did was wrong. It is a way of expressing strong disapproval directly to a person because of something they said or did.
A rebus is a puzzle — or a way of writing — where pictures, symbols, letters, or numbers are used to represent words or the sounds of words, instead of writing those words out directly.
To rebut something means to argue against it using evidence, facts, or reasoning. When you rebut a claim, you don't just say "that's wrong" — you actively show why it's wrong.

A rebuttal is a response that directly challenges and tries to disprove a claim, argument, or accusation someone else has made — not by simply saying "you're wrong," but by using reasoning, logic, or evidence to show why it is wrong.

Recalcitrance means stubborn, persistent refusal to obey, cooperate, or follow what is expected — especially when someone in authority is asking you to do something. It is the quality of digging your heels in and refusing to budge, no matter what.

Recalcitrant describes someone who stubbornly refuses to obey, cooperate, or be controlled — especially when there is a clear authority, rule, or expectation requiring them to do so, and even when pressure is applied to make them comply.
When you recall something, you actively search your mind and retrieve it — you bring a past experience, fact, name, or event back into your conscious awareness.
To recant means to formally and publicly take back something you previously said or believed — and to declare, openly, that you were wrong to have said or believed it.

To recap something means to go back over the most important points of something that has already happened, been said, or been discussed — briefly and selectively — so that people can remember, understand, or catch up.

To recapitulate means to go through the main points of something again — briefly, clearly, and usually in the same order they were originally presented. Think of it as pressing a "replay highlights" button on a conversation, lesson, argument, or presentation.
A recapitulation is a restatement — a structured, brief going-over of the main points of something that has already been said or presented.
To recast something means to take something that already exists and reshape it, restructure it, or present it in a completely new form.
When something recedes, it moves away from you, pulls back, or gradually becomes less — often in a way that feels slow and steady rather than sudden.
A carefully revised version of an old text, produced by a scholar who has compared all the surviving copies to work out the most accurate reading.
A receptacle is any object — a container, a slot, a holder, or a space — that is designed or used to receive and hold something else.
Reception refers to the act of receiving something, or the way in which something or someone is received. But in everyday life, the word shows up in five clearly different situations.
A receptionist is a person whose job is to be the first point of contact for visitors, clients, or callers at an organization.

When someone is described as receptive, it means they are genuinely open and willing to take in something coming from the outside — a new idea, a suggestion, feedback, information, a feeling, or an experience. It is not just about "not saying no."

A temporary break in the work of a parliament, court, or committee. In school, recess is a break between lessons. A recess is also a small space set back in a wall, or a hidden place, as in "the recesses of the mind."
A period when a country's economy shrinks and business activity, employment, and spending fall. It can also mean the act of moving back or withdrawing, as in "the recession of the floodwaters."

When you describe something as recherché, you are saying it is so rare, unusual, or refined that it feels like it was deliberately hunted down and chosen because it is uncommon or extraordinarily sophisticated.
Recidivism is the tendency of a person to fall back into the same harmful or criminal behavior they had already been punished, treated, or rehabilitated for.
A recidivist is someone who keeps repeating the same bad behavior — especially a crime — even after they have been caught, punished, and given a chance to change.

A recipient is a person — or sometimes a group or organization — that receives something. That's the foundation of the word. Whenever something moves from one party to another, the one on the receiving end is the recipient.
Something is reciprocal when both sides of a relationship give the same thing to each other — what one gives, the other gives back in the same spirit.
To reciprocate means to respond to something someone does or feels toward you by doing or feeling the same kind of thing back toward them. It is about a two-way exchange — a give and a give-back.
Reciprocity means a mutual exchange between two parties, where what one gives, the other gives back in return. It is the principle of "you do something for me, I do something for you."
"Recital" means a formal, deliberate presentation of something — whether that's music, dance, poetry, a detailed story, or even background facts in a legal document.

A recitation is the act of speaking something aloud — from memory or from a prepared text — usually in front of an audience. It is the spoken delivery of something that has been learned, rehearsed, or formally prepared beforehand.

To recite something means to say it out loud — but not just any kind of speaking. What makes reciting special is that you are saying something you have already learned, memorized, or prepared in advance.

Reckless means acting without thinking about — or without caring about — the dangerous or harmful consequences of your actions. A reckless person takes risks carelessly, with no regard for what could go wrong.

"Reckon" is a rich, versatile word that sits at the crossroads of calculating, judging, and believing. The idea behind every use of this word is the same: your mind is working something out and arriving at a conclusion.

Reckoning is about facing the truth of something — whether that means calculating a number, arriving at a judgment, or confronting the consequences of past actions. Think of it as the moment when vague things become definite. When the math is done.
Reclaim means to take something back or make something useful or good again after it was lost, taken away, abandoned, or damaged.

When you recline, you lean or tilt your body backward — away from a straight, upright position — and settle into a more relaxed, angled pose. It is specifically a backward movement, not sideways or forward.
A recliner is a special type of armchair — a padded, cushioned seat with armrests on both sides — designed to let you lean back into a more comfortable, relaxed position.

A recluse is a person who deliberately withdraws from the world and lives in isolation, away from other people and society. The single most important word here is deliberately — a recluse chooses this way of life. It is not forced upon them.
Reclusive describes someone who deliberately withdraws from society and prefers to live in isolation — away from people, social gatherings, and public life.

At the heart of "recognition" is a simple idea: knowing something again. It is the act of identifying, acknowledging, or giving credit to something or someone — whether in your mind, in words, or through an official act.
A recognizance is a formal legal promise — made in front of a court or a judge — that binds you to do something specific, under the threat of a financial penalty if you don't follow through.
Recognize means to encounter something and know it from before. Your mind makes a connection: "I know this. I've experienced this before."

To recoil means to suddenly move backward or pull away — either physically or emotionally — as a powerful reaction to something. Think of it as your body or mind saying "No — away from this, right now" in a sharp, instinctive burst.
To recollect means to remember something, especially by making a conscious, deliberate effort to bring it back to mind from your memory.

A recollection is a memory — something from the past that exists in your mind. It is the mental image, feeling, or awareness of something that happened before, which you are able to bring back into your thoughts.
When you recommend something to someone, you are telling them: "I think this is good, and I think you should choose it or try it."
A recommendation is a statement in which someone tells another person that something — a product, a person, a place, a course of action — is good, suitable, or worth choosing.
Recompense is something given to a person to make up for — or to acknowledge — a loss, harm, effort, or service they have experienced or provided.
To recompense someone means to give them something of value to make up for a loss, harm, or effort they experienced because of you or on your behalf.

"Reconcile" means to bring two things that are in conflict, separated, or out of agreement back into harmony. The two things could be people, ideas, feelings, or numbers. Think of it as making peace between things that don't currently fit together.

When something is reconciled, it means a state of peace has been reached after conflict, tension, or disagreement. The fighting — whether between people, within your own mind, or between two opposing ideas — has settled down.
Reconciliation means restoring a relationship or a state of harmony that was broken.

Recondite describes knowledge, topics, or ideas that are deeply obscure — things that exist so far outside ordinary awareness that only a small number of highly specialized, deeply learned people have ever truly encountered or grasped them.

Reconnaissance is the careful, deliberate act of observing or investigating a place, a situation, or an opponent — done ahead of time, often in secret — in order to gather useful information before making a decision or taking action.
To reconnect means to connect again — to bring back a link, bond, or relationship that existed before but was broken, lost, or weakened.
To reconnoiter means to go and carefully observe a place or situation before taking any major action, so that you can gather useful information and make a better plan.
To reconstitute something means to bring it back to its original form or condition after it has been changed, broken down, dried out, or dismantled.
To reconvene means to come together as a group again after a break or pause — or to cause a group to come together again after that break.
To recount something means to tell someone about a past event or experience in a detailed, organised way — walking them through what happened, usually in the order it occurred.
To recoup means to get back something you previously lost or spent — most commonly money, but also time, effort, or other resources.
Recourse means a course of action you can turn to when you are in a difficult situation and need help, a solution, or a way out.
"Recover" almost always means returning to a good state after a bad one, or getting back something that was lost.

When you describe someone as recreant, you are saying they are cowardly and disloyal — and crucially, that their cowardice has led them to betray something they were supposed to uphold: a duty, a vow, a cause, or a person counting on them.
Recreation means any activity you choose to do in your free time — for enjoyment, relaxation, or to refresh yourself. You are not paid for it. Nobody is forcing you to do it.

The adjective recreational describes anything that relates to, belongs to, or is done for recreation — that is, for enjoyment, fun, relaxation, or pleasure, especially during your free time, as a break from work or serious obligations.

A recreational vehicle, almost always shortened to RV, is any motorized or towable vehicle that is designed primarily for leisure, travel, and temporary living — rather than for everyday transportation like a car, or permanent housing like a house.
A recrimination is a counter-accusation — an accusation you make back at someone who has just accused you of something.
Recrudescence means the return of something bad that seemed to be dying down or going away.
Recrudescent describes something — almost always something bad — that had quieted down, been suppressed, or seemed to be over, but has now broken out again with renewed force.
A recruit is a person who has very recently joined an organization, group, or cause — and because of that, is still new, untrained, or in the early stages of learning how things work there.

To recruit someone means to actively seek them out, choose them, and persuade them to join a group, organization, team, or effort — usually because you need them to fill a specific role or serve a specific purpose.
A recruiter is a person whose job is to find and bring in new people to fill positions — whether in a company, an organization, the military, a sports team, or any group that needs members.
To rectify something means to fix or correct something that is wrong, faulty, or unsatisfactory — and to bring it to the right or proper state it should be in.

Rectitude means moral uprightness — the quality of being consistently honest, just, and principled in how you think, behave, and live your life. A person with rectitude has a deep, reliable inner compass that unfailingly points toward doing what is right.

A rectory is a house — a real, ordinary house — that a church provides for its rector (a type of Christian priest or minister) to live in. Think of it as the official home that comes with the job of being a rector. The rector doesn't own it; the church does.
Recumbent describes something — a person, an animal, or even a plant — that is lying down or reclining, rather than standing or sitting upright.
To recuperate means to gradually return to a normal state of health, strength, or energy after something has drained or damaged you.
Recuperation is the process of returning to a normal, healthy, or functional state after something has weakened, depleted, or damaged you.
To recur means to happen again — but not just any "again." When something recurs, it has already happened at least once before, it stopped or went away for a while, and then it came back.

Something is recurrent when it happens, goes away for a while, and then comes back — and this cycle of appearing, disappearing, and reappearing happens more than once. The heart of the word is the idea of returning.

A recusant is a person who deliberately and on principle refuses to obey or comply with an official authority — especially in matters of religion or law. The single most important thing to understand about this word is that the refusal is principled.

To recuse means to remove yourself from a decision, a case, or a process because you have a personal interest or bias in the outcome — or because a reasonable person looking at the situation from the outside would think you might be biased, even if you believe you aren't.

A red herring is something — a clue, a piece of information, an argument, or a detail — that seems important or relevant but is actually a distraction. It pulls your attention away from the real issue, the real question, or the real answer.

Red tape refers to excessive, rigid, or unnecessary official rules, procedures, paperwork, and bureaucratic processes that make it needlessly difficult and slow to get something done — especially when dealing with governments, large organizations, or institutions.
To redact something means to deliberately remove, hide, or block out specific parts of a document before sharing it with someone else.
Redaction is the act of deliberately hiding or removing specific parts of a document so that certain information cannot be seen by others — while keeping the rest of the document visible.

To redeem something or someone means to rescue, restore, or exchange it for something better — to take something that is lost, broken, failed, or stuck in a bad place and bring it back to good standing or trade it for its rightful value.
To redefine something means to change the way that thing is understood, described, or thought about — often in a deep or significant way.
Redemption means being saved or rescued from something bad — and then returning to a better state because of that rescue.
Redolence means a rich, sweet, pleasant smell — a fragrance so full and strong that it seems to fill the air around you. But here's what makes this word special: it doesn't just mean a smell.
If something is redolent, it is so strongly full of a quality — especially a smell — that it makes you immediately aware of it and often feel something because of it.
To redouble something means to make it much greater, stronger, or more intense than it already is — especially when referring to an effort, commitment, or activity.
A redoubt is a small, enclosed, defensive military fortification — essentially a protected stronghold built so that soldiers can defend themselves from enemy attack on all sides.

Redoubtable describes a person who is so impressively powerful, capable, or formidable that they inspire a mixture of fear and deep respect in others — especially in those who face them or compete against them.

"Redound" means to flow back to produce an effect — specifically, to contribute to or result in something, especially regarding a person's or group's reputation, honor, or standing. Think of it like a wave that goes out and then comes back.
A remedy or compensation for a wrong or injustice, as in "seeking redress for unfair dismissal."
To redress something means to correct or fix a wrong, an unfair situation, or an imbalance — to take action that makes things right again after something unjust has happened.

To reduce something means to make it smaller, fewer, less, or lower than it was before. Think of it as pulling something down from its current level — shrinking it, cutting it, or bringing it to a lesser state.

A reduction is the result or process of making something less — less in amount, size, degree, complexity, or intensity — or bringing something to a simpler, more concentrated, or more fundamental state.

When you call something "reductive," you are saying it takes something complicated and shrinks it down so much that it loses important truth in the process. The simplification isn't just incomplete — it's misleading.
Redundancy means the state of having something extra that goes beyond what is strictly necessary — something that is repeated, duplicated, or present when it doesn't absolutely need to be.
Something is redundant when it is more than what is needed — and that extra part adds nothing new, because the need is already fully met.
Describing a voice or sound that is thin and high, like a reed instrument; or a place full of reeds.
A reef is a long, raised ridge or shelf-like structure sitting in a body of water — usually an ocean or sea — at or very close to the water's surface.
To reek means to give off a smell that is both very strong and very unpleasant — the kind of smell that hits you immediately, fills the air around you, and is hard to ignore or escape.
To stagger or sway as if about to fall; to feel shocked or dizzy ("still reeling from the news"); or to wind something in on a reel.
A "refection" is a light, refreshing meal — food and drink taken primarily to restore your strength and comfort, rather than for the pleasure of a grand feast.

A refectory is a large dining room — but not just any dining room. It's the communal eating hall found inside an institution, especially a religious one like a monastery or convent, or an academic one like a college or university.
A referendum is a direct vote in which ordinary citizens — not politicians or representatives — decide a specific political or legal question by voting on it themselves.

A referral is what happens when someone — usually a person in a position of knowledge, trust, or authority — directs you to another person, place, or service because that other person or place is better suited to help you with something specific.
At the heart of "refined" is one simple idea: something has been taken from a rough, raw, or basic state and improved into something better, purer, or more polished.

Refinement means the act or result of making something purer, better, or more polished — by carefully removing what is rough, impure, or unnecessary, and bringing out what is clean, smooth, and excellent.
To reflect always involves something going back — light going back, sound going back, an image going back, or your mind going back.

Reflection means something that is sent back — whether it's light bouncing off a surface, a thought returning to your mind, or an action coming back to define you. All its meanings branch from this single root idea: something going out and coming back.
Thoughtful and inclined to think deeply ("in a reflective mood"); or able to throw back light ("reflective tape").
A reflex is an automatic, involuntary action your body performs in direct response to a stimulus — without you consciously deciding to do it.
Something is reflexive when it turns back on itself — when the action, relation, or effect loops back to where it started.

Reformation means the act or process of making something better by changing or correcting what is wrong with it. The "something" being changed could be a system, an institution, a law, an organization, a society, or even a person's character or behavior.
To refract means to cause a wave — most commonly light — to bend and change direction as it passes from one substance into another.

Refraction is the bending of a wave — most commonly a light wave — when it passes from one material into a different material. As the wave crosses the boundary between the two materials, it changes direction.
"Refractory" means stubbornly resistant — something that refuses to be controlled, changed, or affected by the forces working on it, no matter how hard those forces push.
A refrain is a line, group of lines, or a section of words that repeats at regular intervals throughout a song or poem. It keeps coming back — almost like a heartbeat running through the whole piece.
To refrain from something means to stop yourself from doing something, especially when a part of you wants to do it.
Something is refreshing when it gives you a pleasant feeling of being renewed — revived, restored, or woken up — after some kind of tiredness, discomfort, dullness, or monotony.
A refuge is a place, person, or thing that gives you safety and protection when you are facing something dangerous, painful, or overwhelming.
A refugee is a person who has been forced to flee their home country because they face serious danger there — and who cannot safely go back.
Refulgence means a powerful, dazzling, awe-inspiring brightness or radiance — the kind of light that is so brilliant it almost overwhelms you.
Refulgent means shining with an intense, brilliant, and magnificent light.
A refund is money that is given back to someone after they have already paid for something.

To refund someone means to give back money that they had paid you earlier. It is always the seller, company, or service provider who refunds — and they do it for the customer or the person who originally paid.
To refurbish something means to thoroughly clean, repair, and improve an old or worn-out thing so that it looks and works like new — or at least much better than it did before.

A refusal is the act — or the fact — of saying "no" to something that was asked, offered, or demanded of you. When someone asks you to do something, or offers you something, and you say no, that "no" is a refusal.

To refuse means to say "no" to something — either to something offered to you, or to something asked of you. But it's not just any "no." When you refuse, you are making a deliberate, conscious choice not to do something or not to accept something.
A refutation is a piece of reasoning, evidence, or argument that proves something is wrong.

To refute something means to prove that it is wrong or false — using evidence, facts, or a solid logical argument. It is a strong, decisive word. When you refute a claim, you do not simply say "that's not true."

Regal means having the impressive qualities that we naturally associate with a king or queen — things like deep dignity, natural authority, graceful composure, and a commanding presence that makes people notice and respect you.
To regale someone means to entertain them greatly, either by telling them fascinating, funny, or exciting stories — or by treating them to wonderful food and drink.
Regalia refers to the special objects, symbols, and ceremonial items that officially represent the power, authority, and dignity of a monarch — a king, queen, or emperor.

"Regard" is about how much mental or emotional weight you give to something or someone — whether that's attention, care, respect, or admiration. The word shifts slightly across different uses, but this thread runs through all of them.

"Regard" means to view or consider something — deliberately and thoughtfully. Whether you're looking at something with your eyes or forming an opinion about it in your mind, the idea of paying careful, sustained attention runs through every use of this word.
"Regardless" means: despite everything; no matter what the conditions, obstacles, or concerns are — the action still happens, or the statement is still true.

A regatta is an organized sporting event made up of a series of boat races held on water. Think of it as a grand competition day (or multiple days) where many boats race against each other, one race after another, in a structured and official setting.

When "regenerate" is used as an adjective, it describes a person (or sometimes a thing) that has been renewed, reformed, or spiritually reborn — someone who was once corrupt, sinful, or morally lost, but has since undergone a deep inner transformation and is now in a better, purer state.

Regeneration means the process by which something that was damaged, lost, destroyed, or in serious decline is fully renewed, rebuilt, or grown back — coming out the other side as functional and vital as before, sometimes even better.
Regenerative means having the power to restore, renew, or rebuild something that has been lost, damaged, or used up.
A regent is a person who temporarily steps in to rule a country or kingdom on behalf of the rightful ruler, when that ruler is unable to perform their duties.
Regicide is a noun with two closely related meanings: 1. The act of killing a king, queen, or any reigning monarch. 2. A person who kills a king, queen, or any reigning monarch.
A government, especially an authoritarian one, as in "a military regime." It can also mean a system or way of doing things, or a planned routine, as in "a fitness regime."

A regimen is a carefully planned set of activities, rules, or habits that a person follows regularly and consistently, with a specific goal in mind — most often to improve or protect their health, fitness, appearance, or performance.

A regiment is a large, organized unit of soldiers that forms part of an army. Think of it as one major building block inside a much bigger military structure — like a chapter inside a book that is itself part of a series.
To regiment something means to organize and control it in a very strict, rigid, and systematic way — usually leaving very little room for freedom, flexibility, or individuality.
A register is a formal, authoritative document or book where important information is recorded and preserved for future reference.
A registrar is an official person whose primary job is to keep, manage, and maintain important records — and to handle the formal processes connected to those records.
Reigning in one's own right, as in "a queen regnant." It can also mean currently dominant or widespread, as in "the regnant ideas of the time."
To regress means to move backward to an earlier, less developed, or worse state — after you had already moved forward from it.
Regression means a movement backward — a return to an earlier, usually less developed, less mature, or less desirable state than where something or someone currently is.
Something is regressive when it moves backward — away from progress, fairness, or maturity — instead of forward.

Regret is the sad, uncomfortable feeling you get when you look back at something from your past — something you did, something you didn't do, or something that happened — and you wish it had gone differently.

To regret something means to feel sad, sorry, or pained about something — usually because you wish it had happened differently, or hadn't happened at all. The feeling comes from looking back at a moment and thinking, "I wish I had done something different."

When something is regrettable, it means it is something that should not have happened — something that causes a feeling of sadness, sorrow, or disappointment because it went wrong, caused harm, or could have been avoided.
When something is regulated, it means it is controlled, managed, or kept within set limits — by rules, laws, or a system designed to prevent it from going too far in any direction.
To regurgitate something means to bring it back up or push it back out — in other words, something that went in is now coming back out, usually without much change to it.
Regurgitation means the act of something flowing backwards — moving in the opposite direction from the way it is supposed to go. Think of it as a "reverse journey."
To rehabilitate something or someone means to restore them to a good condition after they have been damaged, broken, or fallen from an acceptable state.
Rehabilitation is the process of restoring a person, thing, or reputation to a good, healthy, or functional state — after it has been damaged, lost, or diminished in some way.
To rehash something means to take old material — old ideas, old arguments, old information — and present it again, but in a slightly different form, without adding anything genuinely new or valuable.

To reify something means to take an abstract idea, concept, or relationship — something that doesn't physically exist as a "thing" — and treat it as if it were a concrete, real, solid, independent object in the world.
A reign is the period of time during which a king, queen, emperor, empress, or any supreme ruler holds power.

When someone reigns, they hold the highest position of power over a place or people — and that position is officially recognized and unchallenged. Think of a king or queen sitting on a throne. They don't just work there. They are the supreme authority.
To reimburse someone means to pay them back money they already spent — usually because they spent it on your behalf, or because of something you caused.
Reimbursement is the act of paying someone back for money they have already spent on your behalf — or on behalf of an organization you represent.
Control or power over something, as in "she took over the reins" or "keep a tight rein on spending." Literally, a long strap used by a rider to control and steer a horse.
To rein something means to control, limit, or pull back something that is moving too freely, growing too fast, or getting out of hand.

"Reinforce" means to make something stronger, more powerful, or more resistant by adding to it. The most important thing to understand immediately is this: you do not create something from scratch when you reinforce it.
Reinforcement means: making something stronger, more secure, or more likely to continue — or the thing that does this strengthening.
Reins are the long, narrow strips of leather (or rope) that a rider holds when sitting on a horse, or that a driver holds when steering a horse-drawn carriage.
To reinstate something or someone means to put them back into a position, role, or condition that they had before, but lost.
To reintegrate means to bring something or someone back into a whole after a period of separation.
To reinvent something means to change it so deeply and completely that it becomes something essentially new — as if you threw away the old version and created it all over again from scratch.
When someone says "don't reinvent the wheel," they mean: don't waste your time and effort creating something that already exists and works perfectly well.
To reinvigorate something or someone means to restore energy, strength, enthusiasm, or vitality to it — especially after a period of decline, exhaustion, or stagnation.
To reiterate something means to say or state it again — deliberately, and usually for a specific reason. It is not accidental repetition.
To rejigger something means to change, rearrange, or reorganize it — usually something that already exists — in order to make it work better, fit a new situation, or serve a different purpose.
To rejoice means to feel or show great joy and happiness, especially in response to something wonderful or fortunate that has happened.
Rejoicing means a feeling or expression of great joy and happiness — especially because something wonderful, fortunate, or long-awaited has happened. It's not quiet, inner contentment.
A rejoinder is a reply — but not just any reply. It is a sharp, quick, pointed response that someone gives in the middle of an argument, debate, or disagreement.
To rejuvenate something or someone means to bring back a sense of youth, energy, freshness, or strength — especially after a period of tiredness, aging, or decline.

To rekindle something means to bring it back to life after it has faded, weakened, or stopped. Think of it like this: a fire was burning, it slowly died down to cold ash — and then you start it up again. That act of starting it up again is rekindling.
Rekindling is the act of bringing something back to life that had previously existed, then faded away, died down, or was lost.
A relapse is when someone who was recovering from something bad — like an illness, an addiction, or a mental health condition — goes back to that bad state again after a period of getting better.
To relapse means to fall back into a bad or harmful condition after a period of improvement or recovery.
Relativity means the quality or condition of being relative — the idea that something's value, meaning, nature, or measurement cannot be understood in isolation.

Relaxed describes a state of low tension — physical, mental, or in a situation. When something is relaxed, it has let go of tightness, strain, pressure, or stress. It is the opposite of being tense, stiff, rigid, or anxious.
A relay is a middleman that receives something and passes it along — so that it can travel farther, or trigger something bigger, than it could on its own.
To relegate something or someone means to move them to a lower, less important, or less valued position — often in a way that feels like a demotion, a dismissal, or being pushed aside.
Relegation means the act of being moved to a lower, less important, or less valued position. Think of it as a forced downgrade.
To relent means to become less strict, less harsh, or less firm about something — after previously being tough, stubborn, or unyielding about it.

Something is relentless when it never stops, never slows down, and never eases up — no matter what. It keeps going with full force and full intensity, without pause, without rest, and without mercy. It does not respond to resistance.
Relentlessly means in a way that never stops, never weakens, and shows no mercy or softening.

Relevancy is the quality or state of something being directly connected to, or applicable to, the matter at hand. If something has relevancy, it genuinely belongs in the conversation — it has a real bearing on what's being discussed, examined, or decided.
Something is relevant when it is directly connected to the subject, situation, question, or problem being considered — and that connection makes it useful, meaningful, or worth paying attention to.
Something or someone is reliable when they consistently do what they are supposed to do, without failing, and without making you doubt whether they will come through.
Reliance means the state of depending on someone or something — trusting them and counting on them to give you support, help, or something you need in order to function or succeed.
A relic is something from the past that has survived into the present. The single most important idea packed into this word is survival.
Relief means the removal of something unpleasant — a burden, a worry, a pain, or a difficult situation — and the good feeling that follows when that removal happens.

To reduce or remove pain, worry, or a problem, as in "the medicine relieved her headache." It can also mean to take over a duty from someone, or to free someone from a burden, as in "relieved of his duties."
When you are relieved, you feel a sense of calm, comfort, and happiness because a worry, fear, or stressful situation has ended or turned out okay.
Religious means connected to, belonging to, or arising from religion.
To relinquish something means to deliberately and voluntarily give it up, let go of it, or stop holding claim to it.
Great enjoyment, as in "she ate with relish." A relish is also a spicy sauce or pickle eaten with food to add flavour.
To relish something means to enjoy it deeply, fully, and with great enthusiasm. It is not just a casual "I like this."
To relocate means to move from one place to another — and to then set up your life, work, or presence at that new place as your new base.

Reluctance is the feeling of not wanting to do something — an inner pull-back, a kind of resistance inside you. It is the uncomfortable sense that you would rather not do something, even though you might still end up doing it.

Reluctant means you don't want to do something, but you are not completely refusing either. There is a quiet resistance inside you — a feeling that pulls you away from doing something, even if you end up doing it anyway.
"Reluctantly" means doing something without wanting to, but doing it anyway.

To remand means to send someone or something back — but always in a formal, official, or legal context. It is not a word you use casually in everyday life. It almost exclusively appears in legal and judicial settings.

A remark is a comment or statement that someone makes — usually briefly — to share a thought, observation, or reaction about something. It's what comes out when a person notices something and says something about it.
To remark means to say something as a comment or observation — usually something brief that you've noticed and want to express out loud (or in writing).
Something remarkable is so unusual, impressive, or exceptional that it naturally makes people stop, notice it, and want to talk about it. It goes well beyond what is normal or expected.
Something is remediable when it can be fixed, corrected, or put right.

Remedial means designed to fix, correct, or improve a problem, weakness, or deficiency. Think of the word "remedy" — a cure or solution to a problem. "Remedial" is simply its adjective form, describing anything that acts as that cure or corrective solution.

To remediate something means to identify a problem — usually one that is harmful, dangerous, or damaging — and take deliberate, systematic action to fix it, clean it up, or bring it back to an acceptable condition.
A remedy is anything — a medicine, an action, or a solution — that fixes, cures, or corrects something that is wrong, harmful, or painful.
To remedy something means to fix, correct, or improve something that has gone wrong.
To reminisce means to think about or talk about pleasant memories from your past — and to genuinely enjoy doing so. It's not just the act of recalling something. It's the act of savoring it.
A reminiscence is a memory of a past experience that you think about, talk about, or write about with a sense of warmth, fondness, or gentle emotion.
When something is reminiscent of something else, it means it strongly reminds you of that other thing because it shares similar qualities, feelings, or characteristics.
Remiss means failing to give proper care and attention to a duty or responsibility that you were supposed to carry out.

Remission means the reduction, lessening, or cancellation of something that is harmful, burdensome, or negative — a disease, a punishment, a sin, or a debt. Think of it as something pressing down on you that suddenly eases up or lifts entirely.

Your remit is the specific area of work, responsibility, or authority that has been officially assigned to you — and just as importantly, it defines the limits of that responsibility. It tells you what you are and are not supposed to deal with.
To send money as a payment; or to cancel a debt or punishment.
A remittance is money that someone sends to another person — usually across a long distance, and most often across international borders.

A remnant is what is left behind after the main or largest part of something has gone, been used up, destroyed, or taken away. It is the surviving portion of something that was once bigger, fuller, or more complete.

A remonstrance is a serious, earnest protest or objection that someone openly expresses — usually with reasons — aimed at stopping, changing, or drawing attention to something they believe is wrong, unfair, or unwise.

To remonstrate means to protest or object to something firmly and earnestly — and crucially, to do so by presenting reasons. It is not just expressing displeasure. It is making your case. You are not simply saying "I don't like this."

A remonstration is a strong, earnest expression of protest or objection — made directly to the person responsible for something you disagree with or find wrong — with the clear intention of making them reconsider or stop.

Remorse is a deep, painful feeling of guilt and regret that you get after you have done something wrong — something that hurt another person, broke a moral rule, or violated your own sense of right and wrong.
Remorseful describes how you feel when you have done something wrong — something that hurt another person — and you feel deep, painful guilt and sorrow about it. It is not a small or mild feeling.
Showing no regret or pity; cruel and relentless ("a remorseless killer", "remorseless heat").
Far away from towns and people, and hard to reach, as in "a remote village." It can also mean slight, as in "a remote chance," distant in time, or cold and unfriendly, as in "a remote manner."

To remunerate someone means to pay them for work, a service, or an effort they have performed. It is the act of giving a person money — or sometimes other forms of compensation — as a reward for something they have done for you.
Remuneration means the total payment — or the full set of rewards — that a person receives in exchange for work they have done or a service they have provided.
If something is remunerative, it financially rewards you — meaning it pays you money in return for your work, effort, or service.
Renaissance means a rebirth or revival — the return of something that had faded, declined, or been forgotten.
Renascent describes something that is coming back to life, strength, or importance after a period of decline, dormancy, or disappearance.

To rend something means to tear it apart with great, violent force. It is not a gentle or careful tearing — think of something being ripped, split, or wrenched apart suddenly and savagely. The key feeling packed into this word is raw, destructive force.

To cause someone or something to become something, as in "the news rendered her speechless." It also means to provide or give, as in "services rendered," or to represent something in art or another language.
A rendering is either the act of converting or presenting something in a particular form, or the result — the thing that gets produced from that process.

A rendezvous is a planned meeting between two or more people at a specific place and time that was agreed upon in advance. This is the single most important thing to understand about the word: the meeting is pre-arranged.

Rendition means a particular version or expression of something, shaped by the person or group delivering it. Think of it as the answer to the question: "How did this specific person or authority present, perform, or interpret this thing?"
A renegade is a person who abandons a group, cause, belief, or loyalty they once held — and either joins the opposing side or simply breaks away to live by their own rules.

To renege means to go back on a promise, agreement, or commitment you have already made. When someone reneges, they agreed to do something — and then chose not to do it, even though the other person was counting on them.
To renew something means to make it new again or to give it a fresh start. Think of the word "new" sitting right inside "re-new" — the prefix re- means "again."
The word renewable describes something that can be renewed — meaning it can be restored, replenished, extended, or made available again after it has been used up or has come to an end.
Energy from sources that are naturally replaced and never run out, such as sunlight, wind, flowing water and the Earth's heat.

To renounce something means to formally and deliberately give it up, reject it, or turn away from it — often something you previously held, owned, claimed, or believed in. The act is almost always conscious, intentional, and final.
To renovate something means to take something old, worn-out, or outdated — usually a building or a room — and make it look and feel new or significantly better by doing substantial work on it.

Renovation is the process of improving, repairing, or updating something — most often a building or a part of one — that has become old, worn out, damaged, or outdated, with the goal of bringing it back to a good condition, or making it even better than it was before.
Renown means the state of being widely known and admired by many people — specifically because of something impressive, excellent, or worthy of respect.

When you call someone or something renowned, you mean that they are widely known AND deeply respected or admired — specifically because of a particular skill, quality, or achievement. It is not just fame.
A regular payment made to use property, such as a house or land, owned by someone else. In literary use, a rent is also a tear or split in something, such as cloth.
To pay money to use something that belongs to someone else, as in "rent a car." In old use, rent is the past tense of "rend," meaning torn apart violently.
Renunciation is the deliberate, formal act of giving something up — permanently, and usually with a clear declaration. It's not simply walking away from something.
Reorganization is the process of changing the way something is arranged, structured, or managed — in order to make it work better, more efficiently, or simply differently than before.
Reparable means able to be fixed, corrected, or made right.
Reparation means making up for a wrong that was done. It is the act — or the result of the act — of repairing harm, damage, or injustice that one person, group, or nation caused to another.
Repartee is the art of the quick, clever comeback — and the sparkling, witty conversation built from such comebacks flying back and forth between people.
A repast simply means a meal — the food and drink you consume at one sitting. It can be breakfast, lunch, dinner, or any other eating occasion, large or small.
To repatriate means to send someone or something back to the country it originally came from or belongs to. The key idea is always a return — back home, back to the place of origin.
Repatriation is the act or process of returning someone or something back to the country it originally came from or belongs to.

A repeal is the official, formal cancellation of a law, rule, or regulation — removing it completely so it no longer exists or has any legal force. When a law undergoes a repeal, it is wiped out entirely, as if officially erased from the books.

To repeal something means to officially and completely cancel a law, rule, or regulation that was previously established, so that it no longer exists or has any legal effect. Think of it as "officially undoing" a law — wiping it off the books entirely.

Repel means to push something away, or to force something to stay away. Think of it as the exact opposite of attract. Where attract pulls things closer, repel drives them apart or keeps them at a distance.

When something is repellent, it makes you want to pull back, turn away, or stay far from it. It produces a strong feeling of disgust, discomfort, or aversion — a gut-level reaction that says "I don't want to be near this."

To repent means to feel deep, genuine sorrow for something wrong that you have done — and to sincerely wish you had not done it — while also having a strong desire to change your ways and not repeat that wrong.
Repentance is the act of genuinely feeling sorry for something wrong you have done — and, crucially, deciding to change because of it.
When someone is repentant, they feel deep, sincere sorrow for something wrong they have done — and, crucially, they also have a genuine desire to make things right or to not repeat that wrong.

A repercussion is an indirect, usually unwanted effect that is caused by an action or event — one that spreads outward, often affecting people or things that had nothing to do with the original action.
Repertoire refers to the complete set of things a person, group, or system has fully learned, prepared, and is ready to use or perform at any time.
"Repetitious" is an adjective that describes something involving too much repetition — so much that it becomes boring, tiresome, or pointless. It doesn't just mean something repeats.
To repine means to feel quietly unhappy and discontented with your situation, and to dwell on that unhappiness — often with a sense of self-pity, silent complaint, or helpless resentment.

To replace something means to put something else in its position — something that serves the same purpose, fills the same role, or occupies the same spot. The old thing is out; the new thing is now there in its place.

To replenish something means to fill it back up after it has been used up, emptied, or reduced. The key idea is restoration — something was once full or sufficient, it got used or ran low, and now you are bringing it back to that full or sufficient state.
Replete means completely and abundantly full — not just full, but thoroughly, richly, satisfyingly full. Think of it as fullness that has been achieved to a high and impressive degree.
Repletion means the state of being completely and thoroughly full — so full that nothing more can be added or absorbed.
A replica is a carefully made copy of an object that is designed to look as close as possible to the original thing.
To replicate something means to reproduce it with great accuracy — to make or do something again in a way that matches the original as closely as possible.
A verb, such as "said," "asked," or "claimed," used to report what someone said, thought, or wrote.

Repose means a state of deep, peaceful rest or calm — a kind of stillness that feels complete, undisturbed, and dignified. It is not just any rest; it carries a sense of quiet and harmony, almost like the world has paused.
A repository is a place — physical, digital, or even a person — where things are collected, stored, and kept organized so they can be found and used later.

Reprehensible means deserving strong blame, criticism, or moral condemnation. When you call something reprehensible, you are saying it is so wrong, so unacceptable, that it ought to be judged, criticized, and condemned by any decent person.
"Represent" always means that one thing stands in the place of, points to, or acts on behalf of another thing.
Something is representational when it stands for, depicts, or points to something beyond itself — something real that exists outside the thing doing the depicting.
To repress something means to hold it down by force — either by an inner force within yourself, or by an outer force applied onto others.

When something is repressed, it has been pushed down and held back — not expressed, not let out, buried beneath the surface. The word is used most powerfully in the emotional and psychological sense, and that is where it really comes alive.

Repression means the act of forcefully holding something down — keeping it from coming out, being expressed, or gaining power. Something that exists, something that has energy or force behind it, is being kept under control by a stronger power.
Repressive describes something — a government, a law, a system, a regime, a policy, or even a person — that uses power or control to stop people from acting, speaking, thinking, or living freely.
A reprieve is a temporary relief or escape from something bad that was about to happen — or is currently happening.
To reprieve someone means to save them — at least for now — from something bad that was about to happen to them.

A reprimand is a formal, serious statement of disapproval given to someone who has done something wrong. It is an official way of telling someone, "What you did was unacceptable, and this is being noted."

To reprimand someone means to tell them officially and seriously that their behaviour was wrong — usually because they broke a rule, failed to meet a standard, or acted in a way that was unacceptable.
A reprisal is a harmful act done to someone because they first did something harmful to you. It is an act of payback, punishment, or retaliation.

A reprise is a deliberate, meaningful return to something that came before. When something — a melody, a performance, a role, an event — has already occurred once, and then it comes back and occurs again intentionally, that moment of return is the reprise.
A reproach is an expression of disapproval or disappointment directed at someone because they did something wrong — or failed to do something they should have done. It carries a quiet moral weight.

To reproach someone means to express disappointment, disapproval, or criticism toward them because they did something wrong, failed to do something they should have, or fell short of what was expected of them.
Reproachful means expressing blame, disapproval, or disappointment toward someone because they did something wrong, failed to do what they should have, or let you down.

A reprobate is a person of deeply corrupt moral character — someone who behaves wickedly, lives without principles, and crucially, feels little to no shame or desire to change. The word doesn't describe someone who occasionally does something wrong.
Reprobation means a strong, final, and formal condemnation — the act or state of being rejected as morally unacceptable or unworthy. It goes far beyond simple disapproval.
Reproduce means to make something exist again — whether by creating new life, making a copy of something, recreating an experience or result, or playing back a sound or image.
The word reproduction carries one powerful idea: making something exist again — either by producing a new living being, or by making a copy of something that already exists.

A reproof is when someone expresses disapproval of what you said or did, with the intention of correcting you. It is a statement — spoken or written — that communicates: "What you did was wrong, and you should do better."

To reprove someone means to tell them, in a calm and serious way, that what they did was wrong — and that they should not do it again. Think of it as a firm but controlled expression of disapproval aimed directly at a person.

Reprovingly means doing something in a way that communicates clear but controlled disapproval — signaling to someone that what they said or did was wrong, and that they should recognize it and do better.

The adjective reptilian simply means of, relating to, resembling, or characteristic of reptiles. Reptiles are the group of cold-blooded, scaly animals that includes snakes, lizards, crocodiles, turtles, and similar creatures.
Relating to a republic, a country ruled by elected leaders rather than a king or queen; in the US, relating to the Republican Party.

To repudiate something means to firmly and completely reject it — often in a public or official way — while making it absolutely clear that you want nothing to do with it. It's not a quiet disagreement.
Repugnance means a strong, deep feeling of disgust or loathing toward something — a powerful sense that something is offensive, revolting, or deeply wrong. It is not just a mild dislike.
When something is repugnant, it causes a powerful, deeply felt sense of disgust, revulsion, or moral offense. It is not a mild dislike.
To cause someone to feel strong disgust, as in "the smell repulsed me." It can also mean to drive back an attack, or to firmly reject someone's offer or advances.
Repulsion is a noun. It refers to either a strong feeling of disgust and aversion, or a force that pushes things apart. These are its two main senses, and both are in common, serious use.

If something is repulsive, it causes a strong, almost physical feeling of disgust, revulsion, or extreme dislike — the kind of reaction that makes you want to turn away, back away, or escape from it entirely. It is not merely unpleasant.
To repurpose something means to take an existing thing — which was originally made or used for one specific purpose — and use it for a different purpose instead.
When we say someone or something is reputable, we mean they are known and respected for being good, honest, and trustworthy — especially within a particular field or community.

Your reputation is what other people collectively think and say about you — the general opinion that exists about you in other people's minds, based on your past actions, behavior, and track record over time.
Repute means the opinion that people in general hold about someone or something — what a person, place, or organization is known for or thought to be like, in the eyes of others.

To request means to ask for something — but not in the way you'd casually ask a friend. When you request something, you are asking politely and formally, while fully accepting that the other person may say yes or no.

A requiem is a solemn tribute to the dead — specifically, a prayer, ceremony, or piece of music offered for the peace and rest of a person's soul after they have died. The word always carries a mood of deep mourning, solemnity, and reverence.
Require means: something is necessary — it cannot be skipped, ignored, or avoided.
When something is requisite, it means it is necessary and required for a specific purpose, situation, or standard. It is not just helpful or useful — it is genuinely needed.

A requisition is a formal, official request — usually written — made to obtain something that is needed. But it's not just any ordinary request. What makes a requisition special is that it carries authority and weight behind it.
Requital means giving back something in return for what someone has done to you.
To requite something means to return a feeling, action, or treatment that someone gave you first. It's about giving back — matching what you received.
To rescind something means to officially cancel, withdraw, or take back a decision, agreement, law, or order that was previously made — as if it never existed or as if it no longer holds any power.
Rescission is the act of officially canceling, wiping out, or undoing an agreement, contract, or law — in such a way that it is treated as though it never existed in the first place.
A rescript is an official written reply issued by a supreme authority — such as a ruler, emperor, or the Pope — in direct response to a formal question, petition, or legal inquiry submitted to them.
Research is a careful, organized effort to find out the truth about something — or to discover new knowledge about it — by collecting information, studying it, and drawing conclusions from it.

A resemblance is the quality of looking alike or being similar to someone or something else. When two things share noticeable common features — in the way they look, sound, feel, or behave — there is a resemblance between them.

To resemble something or someone means to be similar to them — to share noticeable characteristics with them. Those characteristics can be in appearance, behavior, personality, structure, sound, smell, or any other quality.
To resent something or someone means to feel a lasting, bitter anger toward them because you believe they treated you unfairly, disrespectfully, or in a way you didn't deserve.

If someone is resentful, they carry a deep, lasting feeling of bitterness and anger inside them because they believe they were treated unfairly, wronged, or disrespected — and they haven't been able to let go of it.

Resentment is a deep, lasting feeling of bitterness and quiet anger that you carry inside yourself toward a person, group, or situation — because you believe they treated you unfairly, wronged you, or disrespected you in some way.
A doubt or concern about something, as in "I have reservations about the plan." It is also a booking for a table, room, or seat, or, in the US, an area of land set aside for Native American people.
To reserve means to hold something back or set it aside deliberately — keeping it separate from general use, so it's available for a specific purpose, person, or moment.

A reservoir is a place where a large amount of something — most often a liquid — is collected, held, and stored so that it can be used when needed. Think of it as a "savings account," but instead of money, it stores things like water, oil, or even ideas.

To reside somewhere means to live there as your home — in a settled, established way. It is not about visiting a place or passing through. It means that place is where you actually belong, sleep, and have made your life.
Residence means the place where a person lives, or the fact/state of living in a particular place. It is a formal, slightly official-sounding word.

Residency means the condition or state of living in a particular place. When you are a resident somewhere — meaning you actually live there, not just visit — that act or status of living there is called your residency.
A resident is a person who lives in a particular place — not just passing through, not on a short visit, but actually based there in an ongoing, settled way.
Residential means relating to, used for, or suitable for the purpose of living.
Something residual is what persists, lingers, or remains after the main part has been removed, used up, finished, or dealt with.
Residue is whatever is left behind after most of something has been removed, used up, consumed, or processed.
When someone resigns, they choose to leave a job, a role, or an official position. They make that decision themselves — nobody forces them out.
When a person chooses to leave their job, quit a role, or give up a position they hold, that act is called a resignation.

When a person is resigned, they have accepted something unpleasant, painful, or undesirable — not because they are happy about it, not because they want it, but because they have stopped fighting against it.
To resile means to pull back — either physically (like an object springing back to its original shape) or figuratively (like a person backing away from something they said, promised, or agreed to).
Resilience is the ability to face difficulty, hardship, or damage — and recover from it.
Resiliency means the ability to recover, adapt, and keep going after something hard has happened.
When something is resilient, it means it has the ability to recover from hardship, stress, or damage and return to a good condition — or sometimes even come out stronger than before.
