If something — or someone — is superannuated, it means they are so old that they are no longer useful, effective, or fit for their purpose. The word carries the specific idea of being past one's prime to the point of being left behind by time.

Superb means extremely good — of the highest or finest quality. When you describe something as superb, you are saying it is not just good or even very good, but genuinely outstanding and impressive in a way that is hard to ignore.

When you call something supercalifragilisticexpialidocious, you are saying it is so extraordinarily wonderful, so breathtakingly amazing, and so far beyond ordinary goodness that no regular word in the English language feels powerful enough to describe it.
Supercilious describes a person who acts as though they are far better than everyone around them — and makes sure others feel it.

A theory in physics suggesting that everything in the universe, including the choices scientists make when setting up experiments, is predetermined, which could explain strange quantum results without randomness.
The act of doing more than duty requires; going beyond what is morally expected, as in "an act of supererogation."
Superficial always points to one thing: the surface — the outermost layer of something — and the idea of not going beyond it.
An amount that is more than is needed or wanted; an excess, as in "a superfluity of detail."
Superfluous means more than what is needed, and therefore unnecessary. If something is superfluous, it goes beyond what is required — and removing it would cause no loss whatsoever.

A superhero is a fictional character who possesses extraordinary abilities — powers or skills far beyond what an ordinary human being could ever have — and who uses those abilities specifically to protect others, fight evil, and do good in the world.
To superimpose means to place or lay one thing directly on top of another, in such a way that both remain visible or recognizable at the same time.
A superintendent is a person who is officially in charge of managing, overseeing, and supervising something — whether that's a place, an organization, a group of people, or an ongoing operation.
"Superior" means higher than, better than, or greater than something or someone else.
A superior is a person who holds a higher rank, position, or authority than you in a particular system or organization.
A small structure in the midbrain that helps control eye movements and directs attention towards things we see or hear.
Superiority means the state or quality of being better, higher, or more powerful than someone or something else.
Superjacent means lying directly above something else — specifically, resting on top of, or overlying, a lower thing.

When you describe something as superlative, you are saying it is of the absolute highest quality or degree — so good, so skilled, or so excellent that nothing else equals or surpasses it. It marks the very top of a scale. The peak.
The word supernal describes something that belongs to, comes from, or feels like it exists in a higher realm — above the ordinary world, up in the heavens, or beyond normal human experience.
When you describe something as supernatural, you are saying that it exists, happens, or works in a way that is beyond what nature and its known laws can explain.

A supernova is the colossal explosion of a star — one of the most powerful events that can happen in the entire universe. It is essentially the violent death of a star, happening in a sudden catastrophic burst.

If something is supernumerary, it is extra or surplus — meaning it exists over and above the standard, expected, or officially allowed amount. It is the odd one out that wasn't accounted for, wasn't planned for, or simply wasn't needed.

To supersede something means to replace it — but not just any kind of replacement. It means to replace something because a newer, better, or more relevant thing has come along and made the old thing no longer necessary or valid.
A superstition is a belief that a certain thing, action, or event can cause good or bad luck — even though there is no logical or scientific reason to think so.

If someone is superstitious, it means they believe that certain objects, actions, or events have the power to bring good luck or bad luck — even though there is no logical or scientific reason to think so.
An uneasy feeling that something bad is going to happen, based on superstition rather than reason, such as after breaking a mirror or seeing a black cat.

To supervene means to arrive, occur, or come into existence on top of — or in addition to — something that is already there. The word always implies a relationship between something new and something pre-existing.
To supervise means to watch over someone or something — and to be actively responsible for making sure things go well.
A supervisor is a person who is responsible for watching over and guiding the work of one or more other people, making sure that the work is done correctly, on time, and to the required standard.
Lying flat on the back, face upward. Figuratively, weak, passive, and unwilling to act or resist, as in "a supine government."
To supplant means to take the place of someone or something by pushing them out. The new thing doesn't just arrive — it removes or drives out what was there before and then occupies that exact spot.
Supple means bending or moving with easy, graceful flexibility — without stiffness, without resistance, and without breaking.
A supplement is something that is added to something else in order to improve it, complete it, or make up for whatever it is lacking.

To supplement something means to add something to it in order to improve it, strengthen it, or make up for what it is missing. The original thing stays exactly as it is — you are not replacing it or changing it.
Supplemental means: added on top of something that already exists, in order to complete it, strengthen it, or fill a gap in it.

When you describe someone or something as suppliant, you mean they are showing humble, earnest pleading — a kind of begging that comes from a place of genuine need and submission. It is not ordinary asking.

A suppliant is a person who humbly goes to someone more powerful and earnestly pleads with them for something — mercy, help, forgiveness, a favor, or justice — in a way that makes clear they are fully dependent on that person's goodwill to get what they need.

A supplicant is a person who humbly begs or pleads with someone more powerful than them for something they desperately need — mercy, help, forgiveness, a favor, or anything else they cannot obtain on their own.

To supplicate means to ask for something very humbly and urgently from someone who has power over you. It is not casual asking. It is asking with your head bowed — emotionally, and sometimes literally.
A supplication is a deeply humble, sincere, and urgent request made by someone who has no power to someone who has all the power. It is not a casual ask. It is not a demand. It is not a negotiation.
Supply means the amount of something that is available to be used, bought, or given to people who need it.
To supply means to give or provide something to someone who needs it or has asked for it — in a purposeful, organized way.
An economic theory that growth comes from encouraging production, by lowering taxes and reducing regulation for businesses and investors, rather than by boosting spending.

Support means something that keeps something or someone from falling, failing, or struggling. Think of it as a "helper" — whether that helper is a physical object, a person, money, words, or even an idea.

To give help, encouragement, or approval to someone or something, as in "support a cause." It also means to provide money for someone to live on, to hold up the weight of something, or to help show that an idea is true.

To think that something is probably true, as in "I suppose you're right." It can also mean to imagine something for the sake of argument, as in "suppose it rains." To be supposed to do something means to be expected or required to do it.

"Supposed" is an adjective that signals doubt about a label or claim. When you describe something as "supposed," you're saying: "This is what people believe or claim it to be — but it may not actually be true."
"Supposedly" means: according to what people say or believe — but it may not actually be true.
A supposition is something you assume or believe to be true, but without proof or certainty to back it up.
Something suppositious is something that exists as an assumption or supposition — not as a proven or established fact, but as something imagined, supposed, or hypothetically put forward.
To suppress something means to actively hold it down or block it from happening, being expressed, or becoming known.

Something is suppressed when a force — a person, an authority, or even the mind itself — actively holds it down or back, preventing it from coming out freely. The critical thing to understand is that the suppressed thing still exists — it has not gone away.
Suppression is the act of forcibly stopping, holding back, or preventing something from existing, spreading, being expressed, or becoming known.

To suppurate means to form and discharge pus. When a wound, a sore, or an infected part of the body suppurates, it is actively producing and oozing that thick, yellowish or greenish fluid you see coming out of badly infected cuts, boils, or abscesses.
Supremacy means the state or condition of being the highest power, authority, or position above all others.

"Supreme" means the very highest — the top of everything, with nothing above it and nothing greater. When something is described as "supreme," it sits at an absolute peak: in power, in authority, in quality, or in degree.

Surcease means the ending or stopping of something — particularly something that has been going on for a while and causing difficulty, pain, or distress. When something comes to a surcease, it ceases, it stops, it comes to an end.
To surcease means to stop, to cease, or to bring something to an end.

A surcharge is an extra charge added on top of an already existing price or fee. Think of it as a second layer of cost. You first have a base price — the main cost of something — and then a surcharge sits on top of it like an addition. You pay both.
Completely certain about something, as in "I'm sure she'll come." It can also mean certain to happen, as in "a sure win," or reliable, as in "a sure sign of trouble."
"Surety" is about a guarantee that is solid, serious, and legally binding — either a person who backs someone else's promise, a thing offered as security, or the state of being absolutely certain.
A surface is the outermost layer or face of something — the part you can see, touch, or interact with from the outside. It is not the inside of a thing; it is the outside edge or covering.
A surfeit is an amount of something so excessive that it becomes unpleasant, overwhelming, or causes discomfort. It doesn't just mean "a lot."

To surfeit means to give, supply, or consume something in such excessive amounts that it stops being pleasurable and starts causing disgust, weariness, or a strong desire to have absolutely no more of it.
A surge is a sudden, powerful increase or forward rush of something — usually something that was calm or steady just before, and then abruptly rises or pushes forward with great force.

To surge means to move suddenly, powerfully, and in a large or intense way — like a wave. Picture the ocean for a moment. A wave doesn't quietly inch forward; it builds up force and then sweeps forward with great energy.

Surgery is the medical practice of treating diseases, injuries, or physical conditions by directly working on the inside of the body — cutting it open, removing something harmful, repairing something damaged, or correcting something that isn't working properly.
If someone is surly, they are bad-tempered, rude, and unfriendly in a gruff, hostile way — and they make no effort to hide it or apologize for it.

A surmise is a belief or conclusion that you form in your mind when you don't have enough evidence to be sure. It's your best guess about something — but a thoughtful one, not a random one. You believe it might be true, but you can't prove it.
To surmise means to conclude or decide that something is probably true, without having enough evidence to be fully certain.
To surmount something means to successfully overcome an obstacle, difficulty, or challenge — not just to face it, but to conquer it and come out the other side. The key word is successfully.
To surpass something or someone means to go beyond them — to be greater, better, or more than them in some way.
A surplice is a loose, white garment worn by certain people during Christian religious services. Think of it as a special piece of clothing that signals, "I have a role in this ceremony."
When "surplus" is used as an adjective, it describes something that exists in a quantity greater than what is needed, used, or required.
A surplus is the amount of something that is left over after all the need for it has been met.

To surprise someone means to do something, say something, or appear somewhere at a moment they were not expecting — causing them to feel a sudden jolt of astonishment, shock, or wonder. The one essential ingredient is unexpectedness.

Surreal describes something that is real — it's actually happening — but feels like a dream. Your mind knows it's real, yet something about it refuses to feel real. Reality seems to have bent its own rules for a moment.

Surrealism is a style in art, literature, film, and other creative fields where the normal rules of reality are deliberately abandoned. Things that could never exist or happen in the real world are shown as if they're completely ordinary.
To surrender means to stop resisting and give in — either to a person, a force, a situation, or even a feeling.
Surreptitious means doing something secretly and carefully, specifically because you know that if someone noticed, they would disapprove, stop you, or get you in trouble.
Surreptitiously means doing something in a secret, careful, sneaky way — specifically because you know it is not allowed, or you know that others would disapprove or stop you if they noticed.

When you describe something as surrogate, you are saying it is a substitute — something that steps in and performs the role of another thing or person that is absent, unavailable, or unable to do so itself.

A surrogate is a person or a thing that steps into the role of someone or something else — standing in their place, doing their job, or serving their purpose when the original person or thing is absent, unavailable, or unable to do so.

To surround something means to be — or to go — completely all around it, on every side, forming a closed ring or enclosure around it. The thing being surrounded ends up with no open side; it is completely enclosed by whatever is surrounding it.

Surveillance means the careful, continuous, and deliberate monitoring or watching of a person, group, place, or activity — usually to collect information, detect problems, or control behavior. The single most important word in that definition is continuous.

A survey is a systematic, organised look at something — whether that "something" is people's opinions, a piece of land, or a subject of study. The key word here is systematic, meaning it's not a random glance.

To survey something means to look at or examine something carefully, completely, and from a broad perspective — not just glancing at one part, but taking in the whole picture with attention and purpose.
To survive means to continue to live or to exist after facing something dangerous, difficult, or potentially deadly.
Susceptible means easily affected by something, or likely to be harmed, influenced, or impacted by something.

When you use suspect as an adjective, you are describing something that raises doubt in your mind — something that seems like it might be wrong, false, dangerous, dishonest, or poor in quality. You're not saying it definitely is any of those things.
To believe that something, especially something bad, is probably true without having proof, as in "I suspect he's lying." To suspect someone means to think they may be guilty of something.

To suspend something means to hold it in a state where it is neither freely continuing nor completely finished. It is "kept" — physically, officially, or in time — in a middle position, between two states.

"Suspended" describes something held in a middle state — not resting, not gone, but kept in between. This shows up in two main ways: physically (something hanging or floating) and figuratively (something temporarily stopped).

Suspense is the tense, anxious feeling of not knowing what is going to happen — while caring deeply about the outcome. It is the experience of waiting for an unknown result when something important is on the line.
Suspension means the act of hanging, holding up, or temporarily stopping something — either physically in space, or in time (pausing an activity or privilege).

Suspicion is a feeling or belief that something wrong, bad, or dishonest is happening — or has happened — even though you don't have solid proof of it. It sits in the mental space between "I don't know" and "I'm sure."
"Suspicious" is about doubt and distrust — a feeling that something is wrong, dishonest, or dangerous, even without solid proof.

"Sustain" means to keep something going, alive, or strong — to stop it from fading, failing, or collapsing. It is an act of continuous support. You don't just help something once; you keep supporting it so it can continue to exist or function.
Sustainability means the ability to keep something going for a long time — without using it up, breaking it down, or causing harm that cannot be repaired.
Sustainable means: able to continue for a long time without exhausting itself, causing lasting damage, or destroying the very conditions that allow it to keep going.
Something is sustained when it: 1. Continues for a long period of time, 2. Doesn't stop, restart repeatedly, or fade away, and 3. Keeps its strength or intensity throughout.

Sustenance means food and drink — the things a living being needs to stay alive, maintain energy, and function. It is what keeps the body going. When you eat a meal after a long, tiring day, that meal is your sustenance.
A susurration is a soft, gentle, continuous whispering or murmuring sound — the kind that is low, flowing, and soothing rather than sharp or loud.
Susurrous is an adjective that describes something producing, filled with, or characterized by soft, gentle, continuous, whispering or murmuring sounds.

A suture is a seam — a line where two separate things have been joined together, either by stitching or by natural growth. Think of it like the seam on a pair of jeans, where two pieces of fabric are sewn together. That seam is the "suture."

A suzerain is a powerful ruler or state that holds authority over a weaker ruler or state — but here is the critical nuance: the weaker party is not fully conquered or absorbed. It still has its own ruler and governs itself to a significant degree.
Svelte means slim and elegant at the same time. It describes someone who is slender in a way that looks graceful, attractive, and refined — not just "thin," but beautifully thin.

A swab is a small, soft tool made of absorbent material — usually cotton — attached to the end of a thin stick or handle. Think of it as a tiny, precise mop for cleaning, applying substances, or collecting material from a surface or body part.
To swab means to clean a surface, or to apply or collect something from a surface, by wiping it with a soft, absorbent material — like cotton, a cloth, or a mop-like tool.
To swaddle means to wrap something — most often a newborn baby — tightly and snugly in a cloth or blanket, in a way that holds the arms and legs close to the body.
Informal: stolen goods; free promotional items given away at events; or a confident, stylish manner.

To swagger means to walk, talk, or behave in a way that is loudly confident — bold, self-assured, and almost always performed for an audience. A person who swaggers wants you to notice them. They want you to think they are impressive, powerful, or cool.
"Swaggering" describes a person — or their behavior, style, or movement — that displays bold, showy confidence in an exaggerated, attention-grabbing way.
A young lover or suitor (literary or humorous). In old use, a young man from the countryside, such as a shepherd.
To swallow means to move something from your mouth, through your throat, and down into your stomach. It is the physical act your body performs every time you eat or drink.

A swamp is a type of wet land — a piece of land where water sits on or just below the surface for most or all of the year. The ground in a swamp is not dry and firm like a normal field or forest floor.

To swamp something or someone means to overwhelm them with so much of something that they struggle to cope or keep up. Think of it as being buried under a flood of things — so much that you feel like you're drowning in them.

When someone says they are swamped, it means they are overwhelmed with too much work, too many tasks, or too many responsibilities — so much so that they feel like they can barely manage. They have more things to do than they have time or energy for.

To swan means to move or travel around in a relaxed, carefree, and often self-important way — drifting from place to place without urgency, responsibility, or apparent purpose. Think of how a swan glides on water: smooth, unhurried, effortlessly at ease.

Swanky means impressively luxurious, stylish, and expensive-looking — the kind of thing that immediately signals wealth, elegance, and high social class. If something is swanky, it looks and feels like it belongs to a world of money and refinement.

To swap means to exchange one thing for another — you give up something, and in return you get something else. The defining quality of a swap is this two-way movement: something goes out, and something comes in.
A sward is a stretch of ground that is covered with short, closely growing grass — forming a smooth, carpet-like, green surface. Think of it as a continuous blanket of grass spread across the earth.

A swarm is a large, dense group of small creatures — or things — that are gathered closely together and moving in an active, often frenzied way. The word almost always carries the sense of overwhelming numbers packed tightly and buzzing with energy or motion.
When a large group of people or creatures moves together all at once — especially in a way that feels overwhelming or hard to stop — they swarm.
Swarthy is an adjective used to describe a person who has a noticeably dark skin tone or dark complexion.
To swat means to hit something with a quick, sharp, flat strike — usually with an open hand, a flat object, or anything that works like a paddle.

A swath is a wide, long strip of something. Think of it like the path a lawnmower leaves behind as it moves across a field — a broad band of freshly cut grass stretching from one end to the other. That strip is a swath.

To swathe something means to wrap, bind, or envelop it completely and thoroughly — usually with cloth, bandages, or layers of fabric — in a way that covers it from end to end, leaving little or nothing exposed.
Sway refers to a slow, smooth, rhythmic movement from side to side (or gently back and forth). It is not a sharp shake, a jolt, or a sudden lurch.
"Sway" has two main meanings — one physical, one psychological — and both are connected by the same core image: a gentle, gradual shifting from one position toward another.
Swear is about speaking with the strongest possible weight behind your words — whether that means binding yourself to a promise, expressing strong emotion, or firmly claiming something is true.
A sweatshop is a factory, workshop, or other place of work where people are forced to work under conditions that are unfair, exhausting, dangerous, and very poorly paid.
Sweep describes a smooth, wide, flowing movement — like the arc of a broom.
"Sweeping" means something is very wide, broad, and large in its reach — covering a lot of ground, a lot of things, or a lot of people, all at once.
The original and most fundamental meaning of "sweet" is a flavor — the taste of sugar, honey, ripe fruit, or chocolate. It is the feeling you get on your tongue when you eat candy or a ripe mango.

A sweet tooth is a strong, habitual liking for sweet foods and drinks. If someone has a sweet tooth, it means they love and regularly crave things like chocolate, cake, candy, ice cream, cookies, pastries, or any sugary treat.
To swell means to grow larger, fuller, or rounder from the inside out — as if something is pushing outward. Think of a balloon being slowly filled with air.
To swelter means to suffer from extreme, oppressive heat — to endure heat so intense that it physically overwhelms and drains you. It is not just about being warm or hot.

Sweltering describes heat that is so extreme, so heavy, and so suffocating that it causes real physical discomfort — most notably, sweating. It's not just "hot." It's the kind of hot where you feel drained, sticky, and desperate for relief.
To swerve means to suddenly change direction while moving, turning sharply away from the path you were on. It is almost always a quick, abrupt movement — not a slow, planned turn.

Swift means moving or happening very fast, with ease and smoothness. Think of a hawk diving through the air, or a river rushing powerfully over rocks — that kind of speed, clean and flowing, is what swift captures.

A swig is a large mouthful of a drink taken in a single, bold gulp — usually quickly and without much ceremony. It is not a dainty, careful sip. It is a hearty, generous pull of liquid, often straight from a bottle or flask.
To swindle someone means to cheat or trick them — usually to take their money or something valuable — by using lies, false promises, or clever deception.
A swindler is a person who tricks or deceives someone else in order to take their money, property, or something else of value.
Swine means a pig — the familiar, four-legged farm animal. If someone says "a herd of swine," they simply mean a group of pigs.
A "swing" is a smooth, curved, arching motion — the kind of movement a pendulum makes, a bat slicing through the air, or a child moving back and forth on a playground.
"Swing by" is a casual, informal phrasal verb that means to make a short, unplanned or informal visit to a place — especially while you are already on the move or on your way somewhere else.
When something swirls, it moves in a smooth, curving, circular — or spiral — motion. It flows, spins, and wraps around in loops, often without being fixed to a single tight point.

A device for turning an electric current on or off. A switch is also a sudden change, as in "a switch in policy," a thin, flexible stick, or a section of railway track that moves trains from one track to another.

To switch means to move from one thing to another, or to exchange two things so each takes the other's place. It always involves change — but a specific kind: deliberate, complete, and clear-cut. There is always a clear "before" and a clear "after."
To swivel means to turn or rotate around a single fixed point, while staying attached to that point.
A swivet is a state of extreme nervous agitation, panic, or anxious distress.
At its most literal, to swoon means to faint — to suddenly lose consciousness and collapse, usually because of an overwhelming emotion or physical weakness.
"Swoop" describes a fast, curved, downward movement — almost always through the air. Picture a hawk spotting a mouse from high above. It doesn't fall straight down like a dropped stone.
A sybarite is a person who is excessively devoted to luxury, comfort, and physical pleasure — and who actively arranges their entire life around having these things.
If someone is sybaritic, they are deeply devoted to luxury, physical comfort, and sensory pleasure — and they pursue these things excessively and without much restraint.

Sycophancy is the behavior of saying or doing whatever it takes to please someone powerful or important — not because you mean it, but because you want something from them: approval, favor, protection, a promotion, or simply to avoid their displeasure.
A person who flatters and agrees with someone powerful in order to win favour or gain an advantage, rather than out of genuine respect.
Sycophantic describes a type of behavior where a person is excessively flattering, agreeable, and praising toward someone — but not because they genuinely mean it.
A syllable is a single, unbroken unit of spoken sound that forms part of a word — or sometimes the entire word itself.
A syllogism is a logical argument made of exactly three statements: two starting statements (called premises) and one conclusion that is locked in by those two statements.
A sylph is a mythical being believed to live in, and move through, the air — invisible, weightless, and supernatural. Think of it as the spirit of the air itself given a body and a personality.

Sylphlike describes someone who is slender, light, and graceful — like a delicate, airy spirit floating through the air. It is almost always used to describe a person's physical appearance and the way they carry themselves.
Sylvan means of, relating to, or characteristic of the woods or forest — and it almost always carries a feeling of natural beauty, peacefulness, and serene charm.
Symbiosis is a biological term that describes a close, long-term relationship between two different species that live together or are deeply connected to each other.
When two different things live closely together and depend on each other in an ongoing, meaningful way, their relationship can be described as symbiotic.
A symbol is something that stands for, represents, or points to something else — especially something bigger, deeper, or more abstract than itself.
Something is symbolic when it stands for or represents something else — something bigger, deeper, or more abstract than the thing itself.
To symbolize means: to represent something beyond yourself — usually something abstract — through a visible, concrete, or imaginable thing.
Symmetry is the quality of something having two or more parts that match each other in a precise, balanced way.
Sympathetic describes a person who understands and cares about another person's pain, sadness, or difficulty — and who shows that they care.
Sympathy is the warm feeling of care, sorrow, or concern that you have for someone else who is going through pain, loss, or difficulty — even though you yourself are not going through it.

A symptom is a sign that something is happening inside a person's body or mind — usually something that is wrong, unusual, or out of balance. Think of a symptom as your body's way of sending a message: "Hey, something here is not normal."
Being a sign of a deeper problem, as in "the delays are symptomatic of poor management." In medicine, showing the symptoms of a disease.

A synagogue is a Jewish house of worship — a building where Jewish people gather to pray, study their sacred texts, and come together as a community. Think of it the way a church is to Christians, or a mosque is to Muslims.

A synapse is a tiny junction — a point of communication — between two nerve cells (called neurons), or between a neuron and another type of cell (like a muscle cell). It is the place where a signal from one cell is passed on to the next.
Synchronicity is the experience of two or more events happening around the same time that have no logical cause-and-effect connection to each other, yet feel deeply and meaningfully related.
To synchronize means to make two or more things match up perfectly — in timing, in data, or in action — so that they are always in agreement with each other.

Synchronized describes two or more things that are perfectly coordinated in time, pace, or state — meaning they move together, happen together, or match each other exactly, as though they are operating as one unified whole.
Synchronous describes things that happen at the same time, or that operate in perfectly matched, coordinated timing with each other.
Syncopated describes something — most often a musical rhythm, but sometimes a word — in which the natural, expected pattern of stress or emphasis has been deliberately shifted to an unexpected place.

Syncopation is the placement of musical emphasis on beats or moments that are normally weak or unaccented — the deliberate disruption of a steady, expected rhythmic pattern to create tension, excitement, or groove.
In medicine, syncope means a sudden, brief, complete loss of consciousness caused by a temporary drop in blood flow to the brain — what most people simply call "fainting" or "passing out."

Syncretism means the blending of two or more different — and often originally separate or even opposing — beliefs, practices, religions, cultures, or systems of thought into a single, unified whole. It's not just "being influenced by" something else.

A syndicate is a group of people, companies, or organizations that join forces to achieve a shared goal — especially one that would be too difficult, too risky, or too expensive for any single member to tackle alone.
A syndrome is a group of symptoms, signs, or features that regularly appear together and, as a cluster, point to a specific condition or situation.
A synecdoche is a figure of speech — a special way of using language — where you use one part of something to represent the whole thing, or the whole to represent just a part of it.

Synergy is what happens when two or more things work together and produce a result that is better, bigger, or more powerful than what each of them would have produced on their own — even if you added their individual efforts together.
Synesthesia is a neurological phenomenon in which stimulating one sense automatically and involuntarily triggers an experience in a completely different, unrelated sense.

A synod is a formal, official meeting or council of church leaders — and sometimes ordinary church members — who gather together to make important decisions about how a church should be run, what it should teach, and how its members should live.
A synonym is a word that means the same thing, or nearly the same thing, as another word in the same language.
When two things are synonymous, they are so alike in meaning — or so deeply connected in people's minds — that they can be thought of as the same thing, or as standing for one another.

A synopsis is a short, clear overview of something longer — like a book, film, TV show, play, research paper, or any piece of work — that captures the most important points without going through everything in full detail.
Syntax is the set of rules that governs how units of a language — whether words, symbols, or commands — must be arranged and combined to form something structurally correct.

Synthesis means the act of combining separate things — whether ideas, substances, or information — into a single new, unified whole. The key word is combining. You are not just collecting things side by side.

To synthesize means to take two or more separate things — materials, chemicals, ideas, or pieces of information — and actively combine them to produce something new and unified that did not exist in that form before.

Synthetic means made by humans through a deliberate process, rather than existing in nature on its own. If something is synthetic, it was produced — usually in a lab or factory — by combining or processing raw materials in a controlled way.
A synthetic is something that has been made by humans through chemical processes, rather than something that comes directly from nature.
A syringe is a small, tube-shaped medical and scientific device used to pull liquids in and push liquids out in a controlled, precise way.

A syrup is a thick, sweet, sticky liquid — much thicker than water, but still pourable. Think of how honey slowly drips off a spoon, or how maple syrup flows over a stack of pancakes. That thick, clingy, slow-moving quality is what makes something a syrup.
When something is systematic, it means it is done according to a clear, organized plan or method, step by step, in a logical order, making sure nothing is missed or skipped.
When you do something systematically, you do it by following a clear, organized method — step by step, in a planned order — making sure nothing is missed and nothing is done randomly or haphazardly.
Systemic means relating to, embedded in, or affecting an entire system as a whole — not just one isolated part of it.
Syzygy means the alignment of three celestial bodies in a straight (or nearly straight) line.
A séance is a gathering where a group of people sit together and attempt to communicate with the spirits of the dead.
When "tabby" is used as an adjective, it describes a pattern — specifically, a streaked, striped, or brindled pattern made up of alternating lighter and darker markings.
A tableau is a scene — but not just any ordinary scene. It's a scene that is so visually striking, dramatic, or perfectly composed that it feels like a painting or a photograph frozen in time.
A small pill of medicine; a flat, handheld touchscreen computer; or a flat slab of stone or clay with writing on it.
A tabloid is a type of newspaper. But it's not just any newspaper — it's a specific kind that is defined by both its physical size and the type of content it publishes.

If something is taboo, it is strongly forbidden or considered deeply unacceptable by a society or group — not because of a written law, but because of a powerful, shared social or cultural understanding that it must not be done, said, or even openly discussed.

A taboo is something — a behavior, a topic, an action, or an object — that a group of people considers deeply forbidden, wrong, or off-limits, not because of a written law, but because of a powerful, shared social or cultural belief that it is dangerous, shameful, sacred, or simply unacceptable.
The mind in its original, blank state before experience shapes it, as in the idea that a newborn's mind is a "tabula rasa." It can also mean a fresh start.

When you tabulate something, you take a messy, scattered collection of information — numbers, facts, results, responses — and organize it into a clean, structured, and systematic arrangement so that it becomes easy to read, compare, and understand at a glance.

A tachometer is an instrument that measures how fast something is spinning or rotating. Specifically, it counts and displays the number of complete rotations (full circles) that a rotating part — usually a shaft or engine — makes in one minute.
Tachycardia is a medical condition in which the heart beats faster than it should, specifically faster than 100 beats per minute (bpm) while a person is at rest.
Something is tacit when it is understood by everyone involved — but never actually said out loud, written down, or formally agreed upon.

"Tacitly" means doing something, or expressing something, without using words. When something happens tacitly, it is understood by everyone involved — but it was never actually said out loud or written down.
If someone is taciturn, they are a person of very few words. They don't talk much, don't volunteer information, and tend to stay quiet even in situations where most people would speak up.

A course of action or approach to a problem, as in "try a different tack." A tack is also a small, sharp nail with a broad head, a long loose stitch, or the equipment used in horse riding, such as saddles.
When you tack something, you attach it quickly and loosely — not in a deep, permanent way, but just enough to hold it in place.
"To tackle" means to face something difficult head-on and actively work to deal with it. Think of it as the opposite of avoiding, ignoring, or putting something off.
When a surface is not quite dry yet — sticky enough to cling to your finger if you touch it, but not wet — it is described as tacky.

Tact is the ability to deal with sensitive or difficult situations — especially ones involving other people's feelings — in a way that is honest, thoughtful, and kind, without causing unnecessary hurt or offense.
Tactful describes a person who handles sensitive, delicate, or uncomfortable situations with great care — in a way that gets the message across without hurting, offending, or embarrassing anyone.
Tactfully means doing or saying something in a careful, sensitive way that considers other people's feelings — especially in a situation that could be awkward, hurtful, or uncomfortable.
A tactic is a specific, carefully chosen action you take in order to achieve a goal — especially when you are in a challenging, competitive, or difficult situation.
"Tactical" is an adjective that describes anything related to tactics — the specific, carefully planned actions or moves you make in order to achieve a goal, especially within a larger plan.
A tactician is a person who is highly skilled at figuring out the exact, smart, specific moves to make in a difficult or competitive situation — and then executing them effectively.
Tactile means relating to the sense of touch. If something is tactile, it involves touching, feeling with your fingers or skin, or the physical sensation of contact.
Tactless describes a person, a remark, or a behavior that shows a complete lack of sensitivity to other people's feelings, especially in situations that call for delicacy and care.

Taffeta is a type of fabric — a woven cloth used to make clothing and home furnishings. What makes it stand out from most other fabrics is its combination of three qualities happening all at once: it is crisp, smooth, and shiny.
To drive too close behind another vehicle; or to hold a party around a car's open tailgate before a game.
A tailspin is what happens when a plane loses control and starts falling from the sky — not in a straight line, but in a tight, rapid, spinning spiral.

A taint is a small but damaging trace of something bad — such as corruption, wrongdoing, disease, or moral pollution — that sticks to a person, thing, or reputation and spoils it, even if just slightly.
To taint something means to introduce something bad into something that was clean, pure, or good — corrupting it, spoiling it, or making it untrustworthy as a result.
Tainted means something has been contaminated, corrupted, or spoiled in a way that makes it impure, unsafe, untrustworthy, or morally unacceptable.
To "take a beating" means to suffer serious damage, loss, or defeat. Think of it this way: when someone is beaten up in a fight, they receive many painful blows and come out hurt.
"Take a stab at something" means to try or attempt something, especially when you are not completely sure you will succeed, or when you don't have all the answers.
When something takes a toll, it means it causes gradual damage, harm, or negative effects — slowly wearing something or someone down over time.
"Take a whack at something" means to try something or to attempt something.

To take exception to something means to strongly object to it or to feel offended by it. When you take exception to something, you are saying, "I disagree with this and I find it unacceptable," or "This bothers me and I won't just let it pass."
"Take in a matinee" means to go and watch a daytime performance — usually an afternoon showing of a movie, a play, a musical, or a similar live or cinematic show.
To say goodbye and depart ("He took leave of his friends"); "take leave of your senses" means to act crazily.

When you take your cue from someone, you watch what that person does (or says) and use it as your guide for what you should do next. You treat their behavior as a signal, a hint, or an example that tells you how to act.
To remove something; to take someone on a date or outing; to buy food to eat elsewhere; or, informally, to destroy or kill.
When someone "takes over the baton," it means they accept a responsibility, role, or task from another person and continue it forward.
To take something in stride means to handle a difficult, surprising, or unpleasant situation calmly, without panicking, complaining, or losing focus.

"Take the edge off" means to reduce the intensity of something unpleasant — not to remove it completely, but to make it slightly less painful, less stressful, less strong, or less difficult to deal with.

To take the initiative means to act on your own, without waiting to be told, asked, or pushed by someone else. You see something that needs to be done — or an opportunity worth grabbing — and you go ahead and do it yourself, first, without prompting.
A talisman is a physical object — usually small enough to carry or wear — that a person believes holds a special, magical, or supernatural power.
Believed to have magical power to bring good luck or protection, like a talisman. Figuratively, of a person, so influential that others are inspired by them, as in "the team's talismanic captain."

To talk down to someone means to speak to them as if they were less intelligent than you. It can also mean to calm someone in a dangerous situation, to guide a pilot to land by radio, or to make something seem less important.
To talk someone into something means to persuade or convince a person to do something they were not originally planning to do — using words, reasons, or arguments.
Talk the hind legs off a donkey
This idiom describes someone who talks excessively — so much, so persistently, and for so long that it becomes exhausting just to be around them.
To talk up something or someone means to speak about them in a very positive, enthusiastic way in order to make others think highly of them.

Talkative describes a person who talks a lot — noticeably more than most people do. A talkative person enjoys conversation, starts it easily, keeps it going, and tends to speak at length. They rarely sit in silence when there's someone around to talk to.

When someone says something is "a tall order," they mean it is a very difficult, demanding, or challenging task or request — something that requires a lot of effort, skill, time, or resources to accomplish.

Tallow is a hard, solid fat made from animals — specifically cattle or sheep. It is not the raw fat you see on a piece of meat. It is what you get after that raw fat has been slowly melted down, cleaned, and purified.
When you tally something, you count it carefully — usually item by item — and keep track of the growing total as you go.
A talon is a sharp, curved, hook-like claw found on the foot of a bird of prey — meaning a hunting bird like an eagle, hawk, owl, falcon, osprey, or vulture.

The word tame means lacking wildness. Everything this word does — in every context — comes down to that. Something tame has had its wildness removed, controlled, or simply never had any to begin with.
"To tame" means to bring something wild, powerful, or uncontrolled under your control — to make it calm, manageable, and no longer a threat or a problem.

To tamp something means to press or pack it down firmly into a space, usually by applying steady, controlled downward pressure — often repeatedly — to make it compact, dense, and free of air pockets or gaps.
To tamper means to secretly and wrongfully interfere with something — touching, changing, or messing with it in a way you are not supposed to, often causing damage, dishonesty, or danger as a result.

A tang is a sharp, strong, slightly biting quality that you notice in a taste or a smell. It hits your senses clearly and distinctly — it is never bland or dull. It has an edge to it, a kind of piercing freshness or sharpness that you notice immediately.
A sudden change of subject, as in "she went off on a tangent." In geometry, a tangent is a straight line that touches a curve at one point without crossing it.
Something is tangential when it only barely touches upon a subject — it has a loose, indirect connection to the main topic, but it isn't central or directly relevant to it.
When something is tangible, it is real and concrete — either real enough to literally touch, or real enough to clearly notice, measure, or prove.
A tangle is a messy, disordered mass of things that have become twisted, knotted, or wound around each other — in a way that makes them very hard to separate or straighten out.
Tangle means to twist, intertwine, or knot things together in such a messy, confused way that they become difficult — or sometimes impossible — to separate.
Tangled describes something that has become twisted, knotted, or messily interlocked with itself or with other things — in a way that makes it hard to separate, follow, or sort out.

Tangy describes a taste or smell that is sharp, strong, and pleasantly acidic — the kind that immediately "wakes up" your tongue or nose. It is a vivid, lively sensation. The key ideas packed into this one word are: sharpness, acidity, and pleasantness.

A tankard is a large, tall, sturdy drinking cup — specifically designed for drinking beer or ale — with a single handle on the side so you can grip it firmly. Think of it as the older, more serious cousin of a regular mug.
To tantalize someone means to tease or torment them by showing them something they desperately want — but never actually letting them have it, or always keeping it just barely out of reach.
Something is tantalizing when it is so desirable and attractive that it fills you with a strong longing — but you cannot fully have it, reach it, or satisfy that desire right away.
Tantamount means equivalent in effect, weight, or consequence to something else.

A tantrum is a sudden, intense outburst of anger, frustration, or distress where a person loses control of their emotions and expresses them in a loud, dramatic, or unreasonable way — often in public or in front of others.
To become gradually narrower towards one end, as in "the candle tapers to a point." To taper off means to decrease gradually, as in "sales tapered off."

A tapestry is a piece of thick, heavy cloth that has a picture or pattern built directly into it through weaving. It is not a painting, not a photograph, and not a drawing. It is a work of art made entirely from threads.
A taqueria is a type of restaurant or food stall that specializes in tacos and other traditional Mexican food.

A tarantula is a very large, hairy spider. It belongs to a family of spiders called Theraphosidae, and it is one of the biggest spiders in the world. When most people think of a giant, intimidating spider, the tarantula is usually what comes to mind.

A tarboosh is a type of hat — specifically, a traditional hat worn by men, most commonly associated with the Arab world, North Africa, and the former Ottoman Empire (which once covered a vast region including modern-day Turkey, Egypt, Syria, Lebanon, and more).
Tardy means late — arriving, happening, or doing something after the expected or correct time. When someone or something is tardy, it has not met a time that was set, expected, or understood.
A tariff is a tax that a government charges on goods that are brought into the country from abroad.
A road surface made of crushed stone mixed with tar; also the paved area of an airport where planes park and move.
A tarn is a small mountain lake — but not just any lake that happens to be on a mountain.

To tarnish something means to make it lose its shine, brightness, or clean appearance — either in a physical, literal sense (like metal going dull), or in a figurative sense (like a person's good reputation being damaged).
Tarot cards are a deck of 78 illustrated cards, each carrying its own unique image, symbol, and meaning.

A tarp is a large, flexible sheet made of tough, waterproof material. Think of it as a giant blanket that water cannot pass through. Its entire purpose is to cover things and protect them — usually from rain, sun, wind, or dust.
A tarpaulin is a large, flat, flexible sheet of tough, waterproof (or highly water-resistant) material.
To tarry means to stay somewhere or delay leaving when you probably should move on, or to be slow and unhurried in doing something. Think of it as the opposite of being in a hurry.
When we describe a food or drink as tart, we mean it has a sharp, sour, acidic taste that you feel as a kind of sting or bite on your tongue.
A tartan is a type of woven cloth — a fabric — that displays a very specific, structured pattern made up of colored stripes running in two directions: horizontally and vertically.

A task is a specific piece of work that needs to be done. It has a clear beginning and a clear end. It is something you must do, are expected to do, or have decided to do — and once it is finished, it is finished.

A tassel is a decorative hanging ornament made of a bunch of loose threads, cords, or strings that are all tied or bound together at one end and left to hang freely at the other end. That free, dangling end fans out into a soft, fluffy cluster.
Experiencing the same bad treatment that you have been giving to others. It carries a strong sense of fairness — almost like karma.

When something is tasteful, it means it is done with good judgment about what is beautiful, appropriate, and fitting — without going too far, without being offensive, and without being excessive or flashy.
Having no flavour ("tasteless soup"); or showing poor judgment and offending good manners ("a tasteless joke").

A tatter is a single, small, ragged piece of cloth or fabric that has been torn, worn out, or frayed — hanging loosely from a larger piece of material, or lying separately after having been ripped away from it.
A tatterdemalion is a person who wears torn, ragged, dirty, or worn-out clothing — someone who looks like they're dressed in rags.

Tattered describes something that is badly torn, ripped, and worn out — falling apart in rough, ragged pieces or hanging in loose, uneven strips. When something is tattered, it has not just one small tear.
A taunt is a mean, mocking remark made directly at someone — specifically to hurt, provoke, belittle, or challenge them.
To taunt someone means to say something cruel, mocking, or insulting to them — on purpose — in order to hurt their feelings, make them feel small, or make them react emotionally.
"Taut" describes something that has been stretched or pulled until it is completely firm and tight — with absolutely no looseness, no sag, and no slack anywhere in it.

Tautological describes a statement, argument, or expression that is true purely because of how it is built — not because it tells you anything real or new about the world. A tautological statement gives you zero new information.

A tautology is a statement that says the same thing twice — just using different words — without adding any new information. The second part of the statement doesn't teach you anything you didn't already know from the first part. It just restates it.

Something tawdry is cheap and of low quality, but — and this is the crucial part — it is trying to look impressive or glamorous. The problem isn't just that it's cheap. The problem is that it's cheap and pretending not to be.

Tawny is a color word. It describes a warm, brownish-orange color — the kind that sits somewhere between brown, orange, and gold, but leans toward all three at once. It is a rich, deep, earthy color, never bright or flashy, always natural-looking and warm.
Taxidermy is the art and craft of preserving a dead animal's body — specifically its skin — and mounting it into a lifelike pose so it looks as though the animal is still alive.
Taxonomic means relating to the classification of things into organized, systematic groups.

A taxonomy is a structured system for classifying things into organized groups based on their shared characteristics — and the word can refer either to the act of creating such a system or to the system itself.

A tchotchke is a small decorative object — a little trinket or knick-knack — that sits around your home (or desk, or shelf) mostly just to look nice or to hold a memory. It doesn't really do anything useful.

To tease means to deliberately create a feeling in someone — a feeling of wanting more, feeling bothered, or feeling the sting of being poked fun at — without fully satisfying or resolving that feeling.
A technicality is a small, specific detail within a formal set of rules — one that is technically correct or valid, but which often feels narrow, minor, or beside the real point.
"Technically" means: according to the exact rule, definition, standard, or fact — with the precision of a specialist, not the looseness of everyday conversation.
Huge and far-reaching in effect, as in "a tectonic shift in politics." In geology, relating to the movement of the large plates that make up the Earth's crust.

When something is tedious, it means it is long, slow, and boring — the kind of thing that drains your energy and patience simply because it takes so much time and effort, yet feels like it is going nowhere. It is not just boring in the casual sense.
Tedium is the heavy, dragging feeling of weariness and dullness you experience when something takes too long, is too repetitive, or is too unstimulating to hold your attention.
To teem means to be so full of something that it feels like it's overflowing or bursting. Think of a glass so packed with ice cubes that there's barely room for water. That glass is teeming with ice.

Teeming means overflowing with a large number of living things that are actively moving around. When something is teeming, it isn't just full — it is so densely packed with life and movement that it feels almost restless, buzzing, alive.
To teeter means to balance in an unsteady, shaky way — rocking back and forth on the edge of something, never quite stable, always on the verge of tipping over to one side or the other.
Someone who is teetotal never drinks alcohol at all — not occasionally, not socially, not even "just a sip." Zero. None. Ever.
A teetotaler is a person who never drinks alcohol — not even a single drop, not even occasionally.
A telamon is a sculpted figure of a man — carved from stone — that is used in place of a column or pillar to physically hold up part of a building.
A telegram is a short written message that was sent over long distances very quickly through a system called the telegraph.
Teleological is an adjective that means "relating to purpose, goals, or end results as the reason something exists or happens."
The explanation of things by their purpose or goal rather than by their cause. In philosophy and theology, it is the belief that nature or history is moving towards a purpose.

Telepathic is an adjective that describes something related to — or involving — the supposed ability to send or receive thoughts, feelings, and mental information directly from one mind to another, without using any of the normal physical means of communication.
Telepathy is the claimed or imagined ability to send and receive thoughts, feelings, or mental information directly between two minds — with no physical means of communication involved.
To teleport means to move instantly from one place to another, without physically traveling through the space in between.
Teleportation is the instant transfer of a person, object, or piece of information from one place to another — without physically traveling through the space in between.
A telescope is a scientific instrument — usually shaped like a long tube — designed to make distant objects appear much closer, larger, and clearer than they look to the naked eye.
A philosophical thought experiment that asks: if a machine destroyed your body and built a perfect copy elsewhere, would the copy be you? It explores what makes a person the same person over time.
When you describe something as telltale, you mean that it gives away a hidden truth — it reveals, exposes, or betrays something that was concealed, not obvious, or not meant to be seen.
Telluric is a formal, scientific adjective meaning "of, relating to, or originating from the Earth." Think of it as a more precise and technical version of "earthly."
Temerarious means recklessly or rashly bold — acting with daring or confidence, but in a way that is thoughtless, careless, and disregards the risks or consequences involved.

Temerity means reckless boldness — the kind of confidence or daring that goes too far, either because it ignores real danger, or because it crosses a social line that most people would never dare to cross.
Temper refers to a person's emotional state or mood — specifically how calm, happy, irritable, or angry they are at a given moment, or as a general pattern of character.

To temper something means to adjust it so it reaches the right, ideal state — not too extreme in one direction, not too weak, but perfectly balanced and suitable. Think of it as fine-tuning something.

Temperament is the natural, inborn pattern of how a person emotionally experiences and reacts to the world around them. It is the emotional and behavioral factory setting you are born with — your built-in style of feeling, reacting, and engaging with life.
Having moods that change quickly and unpredictably, as in "a temperamental artist." Of a machine, unreliable and prone to breaking down. It can also mean relating to a person's temperament or nature.
Temperance means the conscious practice of self-restraint and moderation — the ability to control your own desires, impulses, and behaviors so that you never go to extremes.

"Temperate" always means moderate — not going to extremes. Whether it describes weather or a person's behavior, the core idea is the same: staying in the middle, avoiding excess, not being too much of anything.
A tempest is a violent, wild storm — one that is fierce and intense, not just a bit of rain or a gentle breeze.

Tempestuous means wildly stormy, intensely turbulent, and out of control — like the raw, violent force of a powerful storm. Think of a sea with enormous crashing waves, screaming winds, and dark churning clouds.

A template is a ready-made structure, pattern, or model that you use as a starting point — a guide — so that you can create many similar things quickly, consistently, and without building everything from scratch every time.
A building for worship in many religions; also the flat area on each side of the forehead.
Tempo means the speed or pace at which something moves, happens, or progresses. Think of it as the answer to the question: "How fast or slow is this going?"
Relating to worldly affairs rather than spiritual ones, as in "temporal power." It can also mean relating to time, or, in anatomy, relating to the temples on the sides of the head.
Temporality means the quality or condition of being bound by time. It is the state of existing within time — having a past, living through a present, and moving toward a future.
"Temporarily" means: for a limited period of time — not permanently, not forever.
Something temporary exists, works, or is true only for a limited period of time — and is expected to end or be replaced at some point.
To temporize means to deliberately delay taking a clear position or making a definite decision — not out of confusion, but as a calculated tactic to buy yourself more time.

To tempt someone means to create a strong pull or desire in them toward doing something — usually something they are trying to avoid, know they shouldn't do, or hadn't planned to do. It is not about forcing someone. It is not about convincing them with logic.

Temptation is the feeling of being strongly pulled toward doing something — especially something you know you shouldn't do, something that is wrong, forbidden, or something you have already decided to avoid — simply because it looks or feels appealing in that moment.

Tenability is a noun that means the quality of being able to be defended, supported, or maintained. When you say something has tenability, you are saying it can hold up — that it doesn't fall apart when questioned or challenged.
Tenable means able to be defended, justified, or logically held up against criticism.
Holding on firmly and refusing to let go or give up — especially when things are difficult.
Tenaciously means doing something with fierce, unwavering determination — holding on tightly to a goal, a belief, or an effort, and absolutely refusing to let go, even when things get very hard.

Tenacity is the quality of firmly refusing to give up — even when things are extremely difficult, painful, or discouraging. It is the inner grip that keeps a person going when most others would have long since stopped.

A tenant is a person who pays money to use or live in a property that belongs to someone else. The tenant does not own the property — they simply have the right to use it for a period of time, in exchange for regular payments called rent.
To usually do something or be likely to do something, as in "she tends to arrive late." It can also mean to take care of someone or something, as in "tending the garden."
A tendency is a natural leaning or pull toward a particular behavior, action, or outcome — something that happens repeatedly and seems to come from within a person, thing, or situation.

When something is tendentious, it means it is deliberately slanted or biased to push a particular point of view — and it does so in a way that is unfair, one-sided, or at the expense of honesty and balance.
Tendentiousness is the quality of deliberately leaning toward a particular viewpoint or conclusion — and doing so in a way that is not fully fair, balanced, or objective.

The word tender always revolves around one central idea: softness and sensitivity — whether that's physical softness, emotional gentleness, or a kind of fragile vulnerability. Every meaning of this word traces back to that core.
To tender something means to formally offer it or present it officially. It is not a casual word.

A tenderfoot is a person who is new, inexperienced, and unfamiliar with a tough or demanding situation. It refers to someone who has not yet been tested or hardened by real experience — someone who doesn't yet know how things work "in the field."

If someone is tenderhearted, it means they have a gentle, kind, and deeply compassionate nature. Their heart is easily touched by the pain, sadness, or struggles of others — and that feeling naturally moves them to care, help, or comfort.
Tenderly means doing something in a gentle, warm, and deeply caring way.
Gentle, loving care and affection; soreness when touched; or (of meat) softness that makes it easy to chew.
A tendon is a tough, cord-like band of tissue in your body that connects a muscle to a bone.
Tendonitis is a medical condition where a tendon in your body becomes inflamed — meaning it gets irritated, swollen, and painful.

A tendril is a thin, thread-like, curling part of a climbing plant that acts like a tiny grasping hand — it reaches out, coils around whatever it touches (a fence, a twig, a wire, a wall), and holds on.

Tenebrous means deeply and oppressively dark — the kind of dark that feels heavy, shadowy, and thick with gloom. Think of a cave with no light source, a dense forest at midnight, or a long corridor so dim that shapes blur into each other.
A tenement is a large residential building — typically old, poorly maintained, and divided into many small, cramped apartments — where people from low-income backgrounds live.
A tenet is a belief or principle that someone — or a group of people — holds to be fundamentally true and uses as a guiding foundation for how they think and act.

As an adjective, tenfold means ten times as great, as large, or as many as something else. It always describes a comparison between an original amount and a new one — and it tells you that the new amount is exactly 10 times the original.
The general meaning or character of something, as in "the tenor of the conversation." A tenor is also the highest natural adult male singing voice, or a singer with this voice.

Tense describes a state of being tight, strained, and unable to relax. Think of a rubber band being stretched — it is not loose and floppy; it is pulled tight, holding tension, and feels like it could snap. That image captures the soul of this word.
In grammar, a tense is a form that a verb takes in order to tell you when an action, event, or state occurs — specifically, when it occurs relative to the moment of speaking.

Tensed means brought into a state of tightness, strain, or pressure — the opposite of being relaxed or loose. It describes something (a body, a muscle, a person) that is no longer at rest but is instead pulled tight, braced, or under internal stress.
Tensile describes anything related to the force of stretching or pulling.
Tension is what exists when two forces pull in opposite directions — and neither one has won yet.
Tentative means uncertain, not fully committed, and open to change. Think of it as the opposite of something that is firm, final, or confident.
Tentatively means doing something without full certainty, full confidence, or full commitment.
Very weak or slight, as in "a tenuous link" or "a tenuous hold on power." It can also mean very thin.
Tenuously means in a way that is weak, fragile, thin, or barely holding together.

Tenure means the holding of something — specifically, a position, a piece of land, or an office. It captures not just the fact that someone holds something, but also how long they hold it, under what conditions, and sometimes how securely they hold it.
Lacking enthusiasm, as in "a tepid response." Literally, only slightly warm, as in "tepid water."
A tercet is a group of exactly three lines in a poem, set together as a unit.
To tergiversate is to deliberately avoid being clear and consistent — either in what you say, or in where your loyalties stand.
Tergiversation is the act of being deliberately slippery — either in your words or in your loyalties.
A word or phrase with a particular meaning; a fixed period of time ("a school term"); or a condition of an agreement.

A termagant is a woman who is loud, hot-tempered, bossy, and constantly quarrelsome. She scolds, nags, bullies, and dominates — often aggressively — and seems almost impossible to reason with or calm down.
The word terminal as an adjective always carries one fundamental idea: the end — especially an end from which there is no going further.
A terminal is always a point where something ends, begins, or is accessed. Think of the word "terminate" — to stop or end. A terminal is the end point of something.
To terminate something means to bring it to a definitive, complete end. Not a pause. Not a slowdown. A full stop.
Terminology is the complete collection of specialized words and expressions that belong to a specific field, subject, profession, or area of knowledge.
"Terminus" means the end point of something — the very last point, the final stop, the furthest limit something reaches before it goes no further. Everything about this word points to finality.

Terra cotta is a type of hard, earthen material made from natural clay that has been shaped and then baked in a very hot oven called a kiln. The intense heat transforms the soft, wet clay into something solid, strong, and long-lasting.
A terrace is a flat, paved outdoor space attached to a house, apartment, or restaurant, used for sitting, eating, or relaxing outside.
Terrain means the physical character of a piece of land — what it looks and feels like on the ground.
A terrapin is a type of turtle — specifically, a small to medium-sized turtle that lives partly in water and partly on land.
A terrarium is a transparent container — usually made of glass or clear plastic — that holds a small, carefully arranged piece of land: soil, rocks, plants, and sometimes living animals.
Terrestrial means "of, on, or relating to the Earth or land." The word does two jobs depending on context: it can contrast Earth with outer space, or it can contrast land with water.

"Terrible" means very bad or extremely unpleasant — something that goes far beyond ordinary "bad" and causes a strong negative reaction. When something is terrible, it shocks you, distresses you, deeply disappoints you, or makes you feel very uncomfortable.
Extremely good, as in "a terrific job." It can also mean very great in size or degree, as in "a terrific noise," or, in old use, causing terror.

Terrified means experiencing an extreme, overwhelming level of fear — the kind that takes over your whole mind and body. It is not just being a little scared or nervous. It describes fear at its most intense and powerful.
To terrify someone means to fill them with extreme, overwhelming fear. Not mild unease, not everyday nervousness — but the deepest, most powerful kind of fear the human mind can experience.
The word territorial is the adjective form of territory. A territory is a defined area of land or space that someone or something claims, controls, or calls their own.

Territory means a defined area that someone — or something — controls, claims, or is responsible for. Think of it as a piece of the world that has been "assigned" to a particular person, animal, group, or authority, either by force, law, nature, or agreement.

Terror means an extreme, overwhelming form of fear — the kind that grips your entire body and mind so completely that you can barely think or move. It is not ordinary fear. It is fear turned up to its absolute highest level.
Terrorism is the deliberate use of violence — or the serious, credible threat of violence — against people, most often ordinary civilians, in order to create widespread fear.

Terse means using very few words — so few that your message is delivered cleanly and immediately, with absolutely nothing extra attached to it. No warm-up, no softening, no extra detail, no closing remark.
Tersely means: in a way that uses very few words — and in doing so, comes across as cold, sharp, or impatient.
Tertiary simply means third — third in order, third in rank, third in importance, or third in a sequence of levels.

To tessellate means to cover a surface completely with a repeated shape (or set of shapes) that fit together perfectly — with no gaps between them and no parts overlapping. Every inch of the surface is filled.
When something is described as tessellated, it means it is covered with, or made up of, shapes that fit together perfectly — with no gaps and no overlaps — to tile a surface completely.
A tessellation is a pattern of shapes arranged to cover a flat surface completely — with absolutely no gaps between the shapes, and no shape overlapping another — in a way that could go on forever.

Something that serves as clear proof or evidence of something, as in "a testament to her courage." A testament is also a legal will, or one of the two main parts of the Bible, the Old and New Testaments.
Testamentary means relating to a will.
A testator is a person who has written and left behind a valid will — a legal document that explains how they want their money, property, and belongings to be distributed after they die.
To testify means to formally and seriously state that something is true — often because you have seen it, experienced it, or know it firsthand. Think of it as a step above simply "saying" something.
A testimonial is a statement — written or spoken — in which someone shares their personal, firsthand experience with a person, product, or service, usually to praise or recommend it.
Testimony means a spoken or written statement made by someone who has direct knowledge of something, offered as evidence or proof.
If someone is testy, they are easily irritated and quick to snap at people, especially over small things.

Tetchy means being easily irritated, snapping at people, or getting annoyed over small, unimportant things. A tetchy person is like a raw nerve — the slightest thing bothers them, and they react with sharpness, impatience, or bad temper.
A tether is a rope, cord, chain, or cable that ties something — usually an animal or an object — to a fixed point.

When you tether something, you fasten it to a fixed point — a post, a tree, a wall, a peg in the ground — using something like a rope, a chain, or a leash. The crucial thing to understand is this: whatever you've tethered is not completely frozen in place.

When something is tethered, it is attached or connected to a fixed point by some kind of line — a rope, a chain, a cable, or anything that works like one — and because of that connection, it cannot move freely beyond a certain distance.

Text means written words. That's the seed from which all its meanings grow. Whenever you see words written or typed somewhere — on a page, a screen, a sign — that collection of words can be called text.

A textbook is a book written specifically to teach students a particular subject. It is the kind of book a student buys or is given at the start of a school year or college course, and then reads and studies throughout that course to learn the subject.
A textile is any material that is made by joining fibers together into a flexible, flat sheet. In the simplest terms, it is what we commonly call "fabric" or "cloth."
Textual means of, relating to, found in, or based on a text.
Texture is the way a surface or substance feels, looks like it feels, or comes across to your senses. It answers the question: what is this thing like on the surface, or throughout its body?
Dried straw, reeds, or palm leaves used to make a roof. Informally, a thick mass of hair on someone's head.

A thaumaturge is a person who performs — or is believed to perform — miracles or wonders that go beyond the natural laws of the world. Think of it as a single, elegant word for a "miracle-worker" or "wonder-worker."

A thaumaturgist is a person who is believed to perform miracles or supernatural wonders. Think of them as a "miracle-worker" — someone who can supposedly do things that are impossible by ordinary, natural means.
Thaumaturgy means the supposed performance of miracles, magical feats, or wonders that go beyond what is naturally or ordinarily possible.
Thaw means to change from a frozen, solid state back into a liquid or soft state because of warmth. It is the exact opposite of freezing.
The press and news media, regarded as a powerful force that holds the government and those in power to account.

When someone or something is called "the one to beat," it means they are the best, strongest, or most successful in a particular area right now — and because of that, everyone else who wants to win must defeat or surpass them first.
Exaggerated and dramatic in order to attract attention, as in "a theatrical sigh." It can also mean relating to the theatre and acting, as in "a theatrical production."
Theft is the act of taking something that belongs to another person without their permission, with the intention of keeping it or depriving that person of it.
Thematic is an adjective that means relating to a theme, or organized around a theme.
Thenceforth means "from that point in time onward."

A theocracy is a type of government in which a god — or the idea of a god — is considered the supreme ruler of the country, and the people who lead that country are religious leaders who claim to speak, act, or govern in that god's name.
Theodicy is the attempt to defend the idea that God is good, just, and all-powerful, even though the world is full of evil and suffering.
