A theodolite is a precision scientific instrument used to measure angles — both horizontal and vertical — with great accuracy. Everything else about this word builds on that simple idea.
The adjective theological simply means: relating to theology.
Theology is the serious, disciplined study of God — who or what God is, what God does, and how God relates to the world and to human beings.
A theorem is a statement that has been proven to be absolutely, permanently true through a step-by-step logical argument.
Something is theoretical when it belongs to the world of ideas, concepts, and mental models — rather than to the world of direct action, hands-on experience, or proven real-world results.
A theorist is a person who develops, studies, or works primarily with theories — structured, reasoned explanations of how or why something works the way it does.
To theorize means to think carefully about something and form an explanation for it, especially when you do not have complete proof yet.

An idea or explanation that someone thinks may be true but has not been proved. In science, a theory is a well-tested explanation backed by a large body of evidence, such as the theory of evolution. It can also mean the principles of a subject, as opposed to practice.

Theosophy is the belief that human beings can gain direct, personal knowledge of God, the divine, and the deepest secrets of the universe — not through ordinary religious faith, not through science, and not through logic alone, but through a higher form of inner, spiritual wisdom or illumination.
Therapeutic means having a healing or beneficial effect on the body or mind.
A therapist is a trained professional whose job is to help people heal, improve, or manage a problem — whether that problem is in the mind, the emotions, the body, or behavior.

Therapy is a structured, repeated process of treatment — guided by a trained professional — that is designed to help a person heal, improve, or better manage a condition affecting their body, mind, or emotions.

Thereafter means "after that" or "from that point in time onward." When you use "thereafter," you are pointing back to a specific event, moment, or situation that was just mentioned, and signaling that something else happened following it.
"Thereby" means "by doing that" or "through that action" or "as a result of that specific thing."
Therefore means "for that reason" or "as a result of that."

"Therein" means "in that" or "in it." It is a single word that acts as a shortcut — instead of repeating a place, thing, document, or idea you already mentioned, you use "therein" to mean "inside that thing" or "within that matter."

A theremin is a musical instrument — specifically, an electronic musical instrument — and it holds a remarkable distinction: it is one of the very few instruments in the world that you play without touching it at all.
"Thereupon" is a formal adverb. It means "immediately after that" and very often also "as a direct result of that."

Thermal simply means relating to heat. Whenever you see this word, it is telling you that something is connected to heat — it either involves heat, is caused by heat, retains heat, transfers heat, or reacts to heat in some way.
A thermostat is a device that automatically controls temperature. Its entire purpose is one job: keep the temperature at the level you want — without you having to watch it or adjust it constantly.
A thesis is a position you take and are prepared to defend.
When thespian is used as an adjective, it means relating to, or having to do with, acting, drama, or the theater.

A thespian is an actor — a person who performs in plays and theatrical productions. If someone calls you a thespian, they are saying you are a stage performer, someone who acts out dramatic roles in front of an audience.
A thick-skinned person is someone who is not easily hurt, offended, or bothered by what others say or think about them.

A thicket is a dense, tangled mass of wild plants — such as bushes, shrubs, brambles, or small trees — all growing so closely packed together that it becomes very difficult, or even impossible, to walk through them easily.

To thieve means to steal — to take things that belong to someone else, without their permission, and with the intention of keeping those things. Simple as that. If someone is thieving, they are behaving like a thief.
A thimble is a small, hard, cap-like shield that you slip over the tip of your finger — almost always the middle finger — to protect it while you are sewing by hand.
A small change or action that is likely to lead to bigger, more harmful ones.
Thin-skinned describes a person who gets hurt, offended, or upset very easily — especially when someone criticizes them, teases them, or says something negative about them or their work.

A think piece is a written article or essay whose main job is not to report news, but to explore ideas. It asks the reader to slow down, consider a topic from a new angle, and — as the name suggests — think.
To think straight means to think clearly, logically, and in an organized way.

A think tank is an organization whose main job is to research complex problems and produce ideas, recommendations, and solutions — especially on topics like government policy, economics, foreign affairs, national security, technology, or social issues.

"Thinly" is the adverb form of "thin." Its job is to describe how something is done — specifically, in a way that involves very little of something: very little thickness, very little density, very little disguise, or very little genuine feeling.
Scorn or disrespect for someone that is only barely hidden, so that it is still obvious behind a polite manner.
Thither means "to that place" or "in the direction of that place." It always describes movement or direction toward somewhere.
Thorazine is a brand name (a commercial trade name) for a prescription drug whose actual scientific name is chlorpromazine. It is a powerful medication that acts on the brain and nervous system.
Difficult and likely to cause disagreement or trouble, as in "a thorny issue." Literally, covered with thorns.
Thorough means doing something completely and carefully, making sure nothing is missed, skipped, or left half-done.

A thoroughfare is a road, street, or path that is open for people or vehicles to travel through — specifically, one that connects two points and allows passage from one end to the other without being blocked or stopped.
Thoroughly means doing something in a complete, careful, and exhaustive way — going all the way through every part of something, leaving nothing out, skipping nothing, and cutting no corners.
Thoroughness is the quality of doing something completely and carefully, without skipping any step, missing any detail, or leaving any part unfinished.
Not considering other people's feelings; inconsiderate ("a thoughtless remark"); or done without careful thought.

Thrall means a state of complete control, captivity, or power that one person or thing has over another. When someone is "in thrall" to something, they are so powerfully gripped by it that they seem to have lost their own freedom and will.
To defeat someone heavily, as in "they thrashed the other team." It can also mean to beat someone violently, or to move about wildly and violently, as in "thrashing around in the water."
Boastful and bragging, especially about one's own bravery, like the boastful soldier Thraso in an ancient Roman comedy.
A thread is a thin, continuous strand — something long, narrow, and unbroken, whose job is to run through things and hold them together.

Threadbare means so worn out from use that the condition shows openly — either as thin, deteriorating fabric, or as something so overused that it has lost all its strength, freshness, and power to impress.
A threat is something that signals harm that has not happened yet — but could. That idea of potential, future harm is the beating heart of this word.
"Threaten" means to signal that something bad, harmful, or dangerous may happen — either because a person deliberately intends to cause it, or because a situation is naturally moving toward it.
Threatened means: in a state of danger, or perceiving oneself to be in danger.

A threnody is a song, poem, or piece of music created specifically to mourn someone's death. Think of it as grief given artistic form — a structured, deliberate expression of sorrow composed in honour of a person or group of people who have died.
To thresh means to beat harvested grain crops repeatedly in order to knock the edible seeds loose from the parts of the plant you cannot eat — the stalks, husks, and straw.
A threshold is the exact point where you cross from one state into another. It is the dividing line. The tipping point. The moment or place where "before" ends and "after" begins.
Thrift means the careful, wise, and deliberate management of money and resources so that as little as possible is wasted and as much as possible is saved.
Thrifty means being careful and smart about how you spend money. A thrifty person avoids wasting money, looks for good value, and thinks before spending.
A thrill is a sudden, strong, and intense feeling of excitement or pleasure — one that you experience not just in your mind, but physically in your body too.

To thrill means to cause — or to feel — a sudden, powerful wave of excitement, joy, or intense pleasure. It is not a quiet or gentle feeling. It is sharp, immediate, and strong. It hits you all at once.
Thrilling describes something that causes a sudden, sharp rush of intense excitement — the kind that makes your heart beat faster, your breath catch, and your whole body feel electrified and alive.
To thrive means to grow, develop, or succeed in a strong, healthy, and vigorous way — not just to survive or get by, but to do genuinely, actively well.

When something is described as thriving, it means it is doing exceptionally well — growing strongly, full of energy, and succeeding in a sustained, vigorous way. It is not just okay or alive. It is in a state of robust, active flourishing.
To throb means to beat or pulse repeatedly, strongly, and in a steady rhythm — in a way that is clearly felt or heard.
A throbbing is a sensation, sound, or movement that repeats in a steady, rhythmic beat — over and over, in waves — usually felt strongly and continuously over a period of time.

A throe is a sharp, intense, convulsive pang of pain or anguish — the kind that grips you violently and is hard to control. Think of it not as a steady, dull ache, but as a sudden, powerful wave of suffering that seizes you.
A throne is a special, grand, and highly decorated chair made for a king, queen, emperor, empress, or a top religious figure such as a pope or bishop. It is not an ordinary chair in any sense.
A throng is a large, dense crowd of people packed closely together, often with a sense of movement, energy, or activity buzzing through it.

When people throng a place, they move there in very large numbers and pack closely together. It paints a picture of a dense, pressing crowd — not just gathering, but filling a space so completely that it feels almost overflowing.
A throttle is a device — a valve, lever, pedal, or grip — that controls how much fuel or air goes into an engine, which in turn controls how fast and powerfully the engine runs.
To restrict or suppress something, as in "regulations throttling innovation." Literally, to choke or strangle someone. It can also mean to control the speed of an engine by limiting its fuel.
"Throughout" means in every part of something, or during every moment of something. The key idea it carries is completeness — not just some parts, not just most of the time, but all of it.
"Throw in the towel" means to give up, admit defeat, or stop trying at something because you feel you cannot succeed or continue anymore.
To surprise someone with something unexpected that is difficult to deal with — like a baseball pitch that curves at the last moment.
A thrum is a steady, low, humming or buzzing sound — the kind produced by something that vibrates constantly, without stopping.
Thrust means a strong, forceful push directed in a specific direction. It is not a gentle nudge or a vague shove.

To thrust means to push something or someone suddenly, forcefully, and in a specific direction. It is not a slow, gentle, or casual push. It is sharp, quick, and deliberate — the kind of action that has energy and intention behind it.

A thruway is a wide, fast, long-distance highway that is specially built to let vehicles travel quickly from one place to another — without being interrupted by traffic lights, stop signs, or regular street intersections.
A dull, heavy sound, like that of a heavy object falling onto the floor.

A thug is a person who is violent, brutal, and physically aggressive — someone who uses force, threats, or intimidation to harm, frighten, or control others. Think of someone who beats people up, bullies others physically, or commits violent crimes.
A small image that gives a preview of a larger picture or video. A thumbnail sketch is a brief, concise description. Literally, the nail on the thumb.

When you thump something, you hit it hard enough to produce a heavy, dull sound — not a sharp crack or a light tap, but a deep, solid thud. The word itself almost sounds like what it describes. That heavy, muffled impact is the soul of the word.
A thunderbird is a powerful, supernatural bird from the traditional stories and beliefs of many Indigenous (Native American) peoples of North America.

When a sound is described as thunderous, it means it is so loud, so deep, and so powerful that it resembles a clap of thunder. It is not merely "very loud." It suggests a sound that is overwhelming, earth-shaking, and impossible to ignore.
When someone is thunderstruck, they are so overwhelmingly shocked, stunned, or astonished by something that they are momentarily frozen — unable to speak, move, or even think clearly.
To thwart something means to stop a plan, effort, goal, or attempt from succeeding — to block or defeat it before it can be completed. But "thwart" is not just any kind of stopping.
When you desperately want something, work toward it, or try very hard to make it happen — and then something or someone completely stops you from getting there — you are thwarted.
Thyme is a small, low-growing plant used as an herb — meaning it is a plant (or a part of a plant) that people use to add flavour and aroma to food, or for health purposes.

A tiara is a decorative headpiece — a type of ornamental crown — worn on the head, usually by women. Think of it as a small, elegant, jewel-studded "mini crown." It is considered one of the most glamorous and prestigious accessories a person can wear.

A tic is a sudden, quick, repetitive action — either a movement of the body or a sound — that a person makes without consciously choosing to. It just happens, almost like a glitch the body or voice produces on its own.
"Tick" captures the idea of something small, sharp, and repeated — whether that's a sound, a mark, or a moment passing.

To amuse or please someone, as in "the idea tickled her." Literally, to touch someone lightly in a way that makes them laugh. It can also mean to cause a slight itching feeling, as in "the wool tickles."

"Ticklish" describes something — a person, a body part, or a situation — that is sensitive and requires careful, gentle handling. If you handle it the wrong way, even slightly, it produces a strong, uncontrollable reaction.
"Tidal" means relating to, caused by, or affected by tides. It is almost always used before a noun to describe things that are shaped by tidal forces in some way.

A tidbit is a small piece of something that is especially interesting, pleasing, or choice. The word almost always carries a positive feeling — the small thing being referred to is not just any scrap or fragment, but one that is worth having or worth sharing.
A tide is the regular, predictable rise and fall of ocean water levels. Picture standing on a beach in the morning — the water reaches far up onto the sand.
Tidings simply means news — information about something that has happened or is happening, especially when that information is being passed from one person to another.

Tidy means neat, ordered, and well-arranged — the opposite of messy or cluttered. When something is tidy, everything is in its right place, nothing is scattered or disorganized, and the overall result is visually clean and pleasing to look at.

When you tidy something, you make it neat and orderly by putting things where they belong. Imagine a bedroom where clothes are on the floor, books are scattered across the bed, and items are out of place.
A tier is one distinct level within a system that has multiple levels arranged in order.
Tiered means arranged or organized into distinct, separate levels (called "tiers"), where each level is different from the others — usually in rank, quality, privilege, or importance.
A tiff is a small, petty, short-lived argument between two people who are close to each other — such as friends, romantic partners, siblings, or colleagues.

Tiffin refers to a light midday meal — essentially, lunch or a midday snack. Think of it as the food you eat in the middle of the day, especially when it's a packed, home-cooked meal rather than something you buy from a restaurant.

Fitting closely or held firmly, as in "a tight lid" or "tight jeans." It can also mean strict, as in "tight security," with little to spare, as in "a tight budget" or "a tight deadline," or close and loyal, as in "a tight group of friends."
Tight-lipped means deliberately unwilling to speak or share information, especially when others expect you to.

Tighten means to make something tight — or to become tight. To understand "tighten," you first need to feel what "tight" means: something is tight when it has no extra room, no slack, no looseness. It is firm, secure, and held close.
A tightwad is a person who hates spending money — even when they have it, and even when spending it would be the right or reasonable thing to do. It is not just about being careful with money.

To till means to prepare soil or land for growing plants by digging into it, loosening it, and turning it over. It is an agricultural action — something done to the earth before you plant seeds or crops.
A bar or handle used to turn a boat's rudder and steer it; also a machine or person that tills soil.

A tilt is an angle away from the straight or level position — a lean, a slope, a slant. Think of a picture frame hanging crookedly on a wall. It's not straight up-and-down (vertical) and not perfectly flat (horizontal). It's somewhere in between.
To tilt means to move something — or to move yourself — so that one side is higher than the other, creating a slant or an angle instead of staying flat or straight upright.

Timber means wood — but not just any wood. It specifically refers to wood that comes from trees and is meant to be used for building, constructing, or making things. Think of it as "useful wood" or "working wood."

Timbre is the unique character or "personality" of a sound — the quality that makes one sound different from another, even when they are the same pitch (how high or low a note is) and the same volume (how loud or soft it is).
A state of matter in which particles repeat a pattern over time, moving in a regular cycle without using up energy — just as an ordinary crystal's atoms repeat a pattern in space.

A timeline is a way of arranging events in the order they happen — from the earliest to the most recent, or from the present into the future. The idea comes from imagining time as a straight line, where the past sits on one end and the future on the other.
When something is timely, it means it happened at the right moment — not too early, not too late, but exactly when it was needed or most useful.
Timeworn means showing the effects of a long passage of time — either through physical wear and aging, or through overuse and repetition.

A timid person lacks courage and confidence. They are easily scared, hesitant, and tend to avoid anything that feels risky, threatening, or uncomfortable — even when the "threat" is small or not real at all.

Timidity is the state of being timid — that is, the tendency to feel afraid, nervous, or lack confidence when facing people, situations, or challenges, especially ones that feel uncertain or threatening in some way.

Timorous means easily frightened, nervously fearful, or lacking the courage to act boldly. It describes someone — or something related to someone — that is habitually or deeply hesitant and afraid, even when the situation may not truly call for such fear.
Timpani are large, tunable drums used mainly in orchestras and other classical music ensembles.

A tincture is a small amount of one thing dissolved into, mixed into, or present within something else — so subtly that it flavors or colors the whole, but never overwhelms it. Think of a drop of ink spreading through a glass of water.

Tinder is any dry, light, loosely structured material that can catch fire almost instantly from just a tiny spark or a very small flame. It is the very first thing that burns when you are starting a fire from nothing.
A tine is a single pointed prong — a slim, spike-like projection that sticks out from a larger object. Think of it as one individual "tooth" or "spike" that is part of a group.

A tinge is a very small, faint amount of a color, feeling, or quality that is subtly mixed into something else. It is never the main or dominant thing — it is always a barely-there trace that quietly colors or influences the overall picture.
To tinge something means to add a small, subtle amount of a color or quality to something, just enough to slightly change how it feels or appears — but not so much that it takes over completely.

A tingle is a mild, brief, prickling sensation — a feeling of many tiny, soft "stings" or "pulses" happening quickly in one spot. Think of it like dozens of tiny pins lightly touching your skin at the same moment, but without any real pain.

To tingle means to feel a mild, buzzing, prickling sensation — like hundreds of tiny invisible pins lightly and quickly touching a part of your body from inside or outside. It is not a sharp pain. It is not numbness.

When you tinker with something, you make small, informal, experimental changes to it — usually by trying things, seeing what happens, adjusting, trying again. It is a hands-on, exploratory kind of activity.
Tinnitus is a medical condition in which a person hears sounds — such as ringing, buzzing, hissing, clicking, roaring, or whistling — that have no external source.
"Tinny" describes something that has the unpleasant, cheap, or hollow qualities of thin metal — the kind you associate with a flimsy tin can.
A tint is a color that has been made lighter by mixing it with white.
Tintinnabulation is the ringing, tinkling, or jingling sound that bells make.

"Tiny" means extremely small in size — not just a little small, but noticeably, strikingly small. When something is tiny, its smallness stands out. It is one of the strongest everyday words in English for expressing smallness.
To tipple means to drink alcohol regularly and habitually — not just on a special occasion, but as a steady, repeated habit. It suggests someone who keeps drinking, bit by bit, over time.
Tipsy means slightly drunk — not fully drunk, but not sober either. It describes the mild, early stage of being affected by alcohol.
"On tiptoe" means standing or walking on the tips of your toes with your heels raised, often to be quiet or to reach higher.

When you tiptoe, you walk in a very quiet, careful way — lifting your heels off the ground and moving only on the front part of your feet (the toes and the ball of the foot). The goal is to make as little noise as possible, so that nobody hears you moving.
A tirade is a long, intense, and forceful speech — or piece of writing — in which someone harshly criticizes, attacks, or condemns a person, group, idea, or situation.
To tire means to lose energy or enthusiasm — either physically, mentally, or emotionally. It describes a gradual draining away of something: your strength, your interest, or your patience.
Tired means that your body, mind, or both have used up their energy and now need rest. You feel like you cannot keep going at the same pace. Something inside you is signalling: stop, slow down, rest.
Tireless means having a level of energy, effort, or dedication that seems to never run out — no matter how long, hard, or demanding the task is.

When something is tiresome, it means it causes you to feel a mixture of boredom, mild irritation, and weariness — usually because it is dull, repetitive, overly long, or simply unpleasant to deal with.

A thin, soft paper handkerchief, or a very thin paper used for wrapping. In biology, tissue is a group of similar cells that form a part of the body, such as muscle. Figuratively, a web of something, as in "a tissue of lies."
"Tit for tat" means: you do something to me, I do the same thing back to you.
A titan means something or someone of extraordinary, almost overwhelming power, size, or importance — something so big and mighty that it stands far above everything else of its kind.
Titanic means something that is of an almost unimaginably enormous size, scale, power, or force — so immense that it feels almost beyond what humans or ordinary things can produce or contain.

A tithe is a specific portion of a person's income or goods — exactly one-tenth (10%) — that is given away as a contribution, most commonly to a religious institution. Think of it this way: if you earn $1,000, your tithe would be exactly $100.
To titillate someone means to excite or stimulate them in a pleasant, teasing, and somewhat superficial way.
When something is titillating, it produces a mild, pleasurable sense of excitement — usually of a sensual or slightly provocative nature.

Titillation means a feeling of mild, pleasant excitement — the kind that tingles, teases, or stirs you up a little, but doesn't go very deep. Think of it as a light buzz of pleasure or curiosity, not a powerful, overwhelming emotion.
"Title" means a name or designation officially given to something or someone — to identify it, describe it, or recognize a status or right that belongs to it.

A titter is a short, quiet, suppressed laugh — the kind you try to hold back but cannot fully stop. It sneaks out rather than bursts out. It is not a big, open, hearty laugh. It is small, slightly nervous, and often half-hidden.
To titter means to laugh in a quiet, nervous, and restrained way — a laugh that someone is almost trying to hold back or hide. It is not a big, open, hearty laugh.
When a character or subject shares their name with the title of a book, film, play, or TV show, they are called the titular character or the titular subject.
A tizzy is a state of nervous agitation, anxious confusion, or flustered excitement — usually over something that is not truly serious or catastrophic.
Making mistakes is a natural part of being human.
"To little effect" means that something was done, but it barely worked. The effort or action produced almost no real result, change, or impact.

A toad is a small, four-legged animal that lives both on land and in water. It belongs to a group of animals called amphibians — creatures that are born in water but grow up to spend much of their adult lives on land.
A toady is a person who praises, flatters, and agrees with someone powerful — not because they genuinely mean it, but purely to gain personal benefits.
To toady means to flatter someone — especially someone powerful or important — in a fake, over-the-top way, not because you genuinely admire them, but because you want something from them.
When you take a slice of bread and heat it — in a toaster, under a grill, or over a flame — until it turns golden-brown, dry, and slightly crunchy on the surface, the result is called toast.
When you toast something, you apply dry heat to it until its surface turns golden-brown, slightly crispy, and develops a deeper, richer flavour.
A toboggan is a type of sled — a flat, narrow vehicle designed for sliding down snow-covered slopes for fun or sport.
To toboggan means to slide rapidly down a snow-covered slope on a flat sled called a toboggan.
A tocsin is an alarm bell — or more precisely, the urgent ringing of a bell specifically meant to warn people of danger.
To toddle is to walk with short, unsteady, wobbly steps — swaying a little, moving slowly, without the smooth, confident stride of an adult.
Tofu is a soft, white food made from soybeans. It is also commonly called bean curd. Think of it like cheese — except instead of starting with animal milk, you start with soy milk.
A toga is a large, single piece of cloth that was the official outer garment of ancient Rome. It is one of the most recognizable symbols of Roman civilization.

Toil means hard, exhausting, and long physical work — the kind that drains your body and wears you out. It is not just any work. It is work that feels heavy, relentless, and demanding, the kind that leaves you tired to your bones.
To toil means to work very hard, for a long time, under difficult or exhausting conditions.
A toiler is a person who works very hard — usually in a physically demanding, exhausting, or grinding way — often for long periods of time and without much recognition or great reward.
Toilette refers to the act of grooming and preparing yourself — washing, combing your hair, putting on makeup, dressing up — the entire ritual of making yourself clean and presentable.
Toilsome means requiring a great amount of hard, exhausting, and sustained effort.

When "token" is used as an adjective, it describes something that is done or given at a bare minimum level — just enough to look like a real effort, but not enough to actually be one. It is a gesture that exists mainly for appearances, not for genuine impact.
A token is something small — an object, a sign, or a piece of data — that stands in for, represents, or grants access to something larger or more abstract.

Tokenism is the practice of making a small, symbolic gesture toward including people from underrepresented or marginalized groups — not because you genuinely care about including them, but to look like you do.
"Tokus" is a noun that means the buttocks — the soft, fleshy, rounded part of your body that you sit on. In everyday terms, it's simply another word for your rear end, backside, or bottom.

"Tolerable" means "not so bad that you cannot put up with it." It lives in a middle zone — not good enough to be called great, but not bad enough to be rejected or complained about strongly. Think of it as the language of mild acceptance.

Tolerance is the ability or willingness to put up with something you don't necessarily like, agree with, or enjoy — without letting it overwhelm you or pushing to eliminate it. It implies a kind of patient endurance in the face of discomfort or disagreement.

When someone is tolerant, they are willing to allow something to exist or continue — even if they personally dislike it, disagree with it, or find it uncomfortable — without fighting against it, punishing it, or trying to stop it.

To tolerate something means to allow it to exist or continue, even though you dislike it, disagree with it, or find it unpleasant. You are not stopping it. You are not fighting it. But you are also not happy about it. You are simply letting it be.
A toll is a charge or fee you must pay in order to use a road, bridge, tunnel, or highway. Think of it as "renting" the right to pass through or across something.
Of a bell, to ring slowly and solemnly, especially to announce a death. In law, to toll a time limit means to pause it for a period.
A tomahawk is a type of small, light axe that was originally made and used by the Indigenous peoples of North America — the people commonly called Native Americans.
A tome is a large, heavy, thick book — one that is noticeably bigger and weightier than an ordinary book.
Tomfoolery means silly, foolish, or playful behavior — the kind that is goofy, ridiculous, or lacking in seriousness.
A fine powder used instead of ink in laser printers and photocopiers. In skincare, toner is a liquid applied to the face after cleansing.
Tongs are a tool made of two arms joined together, used to grip, pick up, hold, or move objects — especially when you cannot or should not use your bare hands.
A tonic is any drink, syrup, or medicine that is meant to make you feel stronger, healthier, or more energetic — especially after a period of weakness or illness.
A tonsure is a shaved patch or area on a person's head, created deliberately as part of a religious ritual or ceremony.
A topaz is a naturally occurring gemstone — a hard, shiny crystal that forms deep inside the Earth over millions of years.
Topiary is the art of cutting and shaping living trees or bushes into decorative, often sculpted forms — and it also refers to the sculpted plant itself that is the result of that art.
About things that matter or are in the news right now ("a topical joke"); in medicine, applied to the skin ("a topical cream").

Topographic means relating to the physical shape, layout, and surface features of a piece of land — including its hills, valleys, slopes, rivers, plains, and how high or low different areas are compared to each other.

"Topographical" is an adjective that describes anything related to the physical shape, surface features, and layout of a piece of land — things like hills, valleys, mountains, rivers, plains, cliffs, and lakes — and how all these features are arranged and measured.

Topography refers to two closely linked ideas: 1. The actual physical surface features of a piece of land — its hills, valleys, mountains, plains, and so on — as they exist in the real world. 2. The study, description, or mapping of those physical features.

To topple means to fall over — but not in just any way. It specifically describes something tall, upright, or standing that loses its balance and tips over, usually because it becomes unstable or is pushed.

A torch is a source of portable light or flame. Whether it's a burning stick from ancient times or a modern handheld device, the word always carries the idea of carrying light with you. That single idea connects all its meanings.
To torch something means to deliberately set it on fire in order to destroy it.
Torment means severe, prolonged suffering — either in the body, in the mind, or in the emotions.

To torment someone means to cause them to suffer — deeply, painfully, and usually over and over again. This suffering can be physical (bodily pain), mental (disturbing someone's thoughts), or emotional (hurting someone's feelings at a deep level).
Torpid means being in a state of deep, heavy sluggishness — physically slow, mentally dull, or emotionally lifeless, as if all energy and alertness have been suppressed or switched off.
Torpidity means the state of being torpid, and "torpid" describes something (or someone) that is extremely slow, dull, unresponsive, and mentally or physically inactive.

Torpor means a state of deep sluggishness, inactivity, and unresponsiveness — a condition where a person, animal, or even a group seems to have almost completely "switched off" from the normal activity of life.
Torque is the measure of how much a force causes — or tends to cause — an object to rotate around a fixed point or axis.

A torrent is an overwhelming, fast-moving, and powerful rush of something — originally water, but the word has grown to describe any situation where a large amount of something comes flooding in, all at once, with great force and speed.
Torrential describes something that is so overwhelming in quantity and force that it resembles a torrent — a fast, violently rushing, unstoppable body of moving water.

Torrid is a word that always carries a sense of intense, overwhelming, burning force — whether that force is heat, passion, or difficulty. If something is torrid, it is not mildly warm, slightly romantic, or a little tough. It is scorching.
Torsion is the twisting of an object — or the internal stress that builds up inside an object because it is being twisted.
The main part of the human body, not including the head, arms, and legs. In art, a statue of a body without a head or limbs.
A thin, round, flat bread made from corn or wheat, used in Mexican cooking for tacos and wraps. In Spain, a tortilla is a thick omelette made with potatoes.

"Tortuous" means full of twists and turns. Something tortuous does not go straight. It bends, winds, curves, loops, and doubles back — either physically in space, or figuratively in thought, language, or process.

Torture is the deliberate act of inflicting severe pain — physical, psychological, or both — on a person who cannot freely escape or stop it, usually to achieve a specific goal. The key word here is deliberate. Torture is never accidental.

To torture someone means to deliberately cause them severe, intense pain — whether physical or mental — usually over a period of time. The single most important word in understanding "torture" is deliberately. Torture is never accidental.

A toss is a quick, light, often casual motion — either of throwing something, moving something suddenly, or flipping something. The word captures the idea of something being sent through the air without much force, or something moving in a brief, sharp way.

"Toss" means to throw something — but with a very specific flavor. It is a light, casual, effortless throw, usually over a short distance. It is not a powerful, full-effort throw (that would be hurl or fling).
The most widely understood meaning of "tot" is a very small, young child — typically a toddler or infant.
Describes a government in which one ruler or party holds complete control over every part of society, including the economy, the media, culture, and even people's private lives and beliefs.
Totalitarianism is a system of government in which the ruling power — usually a single leader or a single political party — seeks total, absolute control over every aspect of life in a country.
When people say "a tote" or "a tote bag," they mean a large, open, sturdy bag with two handles that you carry things in.
To tote something means to carry it, usually with your hands, arms, or on your body — and almost always something physical and tangible.

A totem is a natural entity — most often an animal, but sometimes a plant, a natural force (like thunder or wind), or even an object — that a group of people (or sometimes an individual) regards as having a deep, sacred spiritual bond with them.
A totem pole is a tall, carved wooden post created by certain Indigenous (Native) peoples of the Pacific Northwest Coast of North America.

Something is "totemic" when it functions like a sacred tribal symbol — it stands for something much larger than itself, is deeply tied to a group's identity, and is treated with a kind of reverence that goes beyond rational evaluation.
To totter means to move or stand in an unsteady, shaky way — as if you are about to lose your balance and fall at any moment. It is not a fast, dramatic fall.
"Touch base" means to make brief contact with someone — usually just to check in, share a quick update, or stay connected. It's not a deep conversation. It's not a formal meeting.
A touchdown is the most important scoring play in American football. It is worth 6 points — the highest single scoring action in the game.
A touchstone is a reliable standard or criterion by which the quality, value, or genuineness of something is judged.
"Touchy" means easily upset or sensitive in a way that requires careful handling. Think of it like a bruise on your skin — even a light touch causes pain.
"Touché" is what you say when someone makes a point so sharp, so well-aimed, or so clever in a conversation that you have to admit — right there and then — that they got you.

A tough cookie is a person who is mentally and emotionally strong. When someone faces difficult situations — pain, hardship, failure, pressure, or criticism — and does not break down, give up, or get easily hurt, we call them a tough cookie.

A tourney is a tournament — a competition in which many participants (players, teams, or competitors) face off against each other in a series of structured matches or rounds, until one person or team is crowned the winner.
A tourniquet is a device used to stop severe bleeding from a limb — an arm or a leg — by tightly squeezing the limb to cut off blood flow to the wound.

To tousle something means to make it messy, tangled, or disheveled — especially by ruffling it roughly or playfully with your hands. The word is used most often for hair, though it can apply to fur or loose clothing too.

When you tout something, you promote it, praise it, or talk it up enthusiastically — usually to convince other people that it is valuable, impressive, or worth their attention. The key feeling behind "tout" is: eager, public, sometimes pushy promotion.
When something is described as touted, it means it has been loudly and enthusiastically praised, promoted, or recommended — usually by many people, by the media, or by those with influence.
To tow something means to pull it along behind you using a rope, chain, cable, or a rigid bar — while the object being pulled cannot or does not move on its own power.
To tower means to rise or stand dramatically higher than the things or people around it — so much higher that everything nearby looks small or insignificant by comparison.
Extremely tall, as in "towering mountains." Figuratively, of very great importance or quality, as in "a towering figure in science," or very intense, as in "a towering rage."

Toxic means causing harm to whatever it comes into contact with. Think of it as the adjective version of "poison." If something is toxic, it damages, hurts, or destroys — whether that's a living body, a relationship, a workplace, or even a financial system.

A toxin is a poisonous substance that is produced by a living organism. That last part — produced by a living organism — is the single most important thing about this word. It is what separates a toxin from other kinds of poisons.
A trace is something left behind. It could be a leftover mark, a leftover amount, a leftover path, or a leftover record.
To trace something is to follow a line — carefully, step by step.

Traceable describes something that can be traced — meaning you can follow a trail, a path, or a chain of connections backward (or forward) to find its origin, cause, source, location, or the person responsible for it.
The trachea is the tube in your body that carries air from your throat down to your lungs.
A large area of land, as in "a tract of forest." It is also a short leaflet on a religious or political subject, or a system of organs in the body, as in "the digestive tract."
Tractability is the quality of being easy to handle, manage, control, or deal with.
Tractable means easy to manage, control, or deal with. Think of it as describing something or someone that doesn't put up a fight — it cooperates, it yields, it can be handled.
Traction is about grip and resistance that enables movement or progress.
A trademark is a unique sign that a business uses to identify its products or services and to separate them from those of every other business in the market.

A tradition is a practice, belief, custom, or way of doing something that people have been passing down from one generation to the next over a long period of time — and that continues to be followed, observed, or celebrated because of that established history.
To traduce someone means to deliberately say false and damaging things about them to other people, in order to destroy or harm their reputation.

"Traffic" describes the movement of things — most commonly vehicles, people, or goods — through a shared space or along a route. Think of it as a flowing stream of things moving from one place to another, usually in significant numbers or volumes.
A tragedy is a deeply sad and terrible event — one involving great suffering, loss, or death — especially when it feels unnecessary, wasteful, or devastating to witness or experience.
Tragic means deeply, profoundly sad — but not in the ordinary, everyday sense of sadness.
A trail refers to something that is left behind, or a path that has been formed, by something or someone moving through a place.

When something trails, it moves behind, hangs behind, or follows behind something else — often slowly, loosely, or passively. Think of a bride's long wedding dress being pulled along the floor behind her as she walks.
A trailblazer is a person who is the first to do something new, difficult, or important — and in doing so, opens the way for others to follow.

A train of thought is a connected series of ideas that flow from one to the next in your mind. It's the path your thinking takes as you move from one idea to another, step by step, in a natural sequence.
To traipse means to walk somewhere in a way that feels tiring, tedious, or pointless. It is not just any kind of walking. The word carries a built-in feeling of effort, weariness, or mild complaint.
A trait is a specific, lasting quality that belongs to a person, animal, or thing — something that is a consistent, recognizable part of what they are or how they behave.
A traitor is a person who betrays someone or something that trusted them.

When you call someone or something traitorous, you are saying that it involves a deep, deliberate betrayal of trust or loyalty — especially toward someone or something that fully trusted and relied on that person.

A trajectory is the path that something travels through space or time as it moves from one point to another — particularly when that path is shaped by forces acting on it, and when the movement has a clear direction and momentum.
A tram is a passenger vehicle that runs on metal rails (tracks) laid directly into a city street, powered by electricity.
To trammel someone or something means to restrict, confine, or hold back their freedom — to stop them from moving, thinking, or acting as freely as they otherwise could.
A tramp is a person who has no permanent home and no steady job, and who travels from place to place — usually on foot — to survive.
To trample means to step on something heavily and repeatedly, causing damage or destruction in the process.
A trance is a mental state in which a person is not fully conscious of the world around them, yet is not fully asleep either.
A tranche is a distinct, purposefully designed slice of a larger whole — a portion that has been deliberately carved out to serve a specific purpose.

Tranquil describes a state of deep, undisturbed calm and peace. When something is tranquil, it is free from noise, stress, agitation, chaos, or any kind of disturbance. It is not just "a little quiet" — it is a full, settled, gentle stillness.

Tranquility means a state of complete calm, peace, and stillness — free from noise, stress, conflict, or disturbance. It is what you experience when everything that could unsettle you has gone quiet, both around you and inside you.
To tranquilize something or someone means to make them calm, still, and free from agitation, stress, or excitement — either through a drug or through some other calming influence.
To transact means to carry out or conduct a piece of business, a deal, or a formal exchange between two or more parties.
A transaction is a completed exchange between two or more parties, where something moves from one side to the other — and both sides agree to it.
To transcend something means to go beyond its limits — to rise above it, exceed it, or exist at a level that is higher than what is normally possible or expected.
Transcendence means the state of going beyond ordinary limits — beyond what is normal, physical, or expected.

Transcendent means going beyond the usual limits — beyond what is ordinary, beyond what is expected, and sometimes even beyond what can be fully understood or explained. Whatever is transcendent doesn't just surpass things around it.

Going beyond ordinary human experience or understanding, especially in a spiritual sense, as in "a transcendental experience." In maths, a transcendental number, such as π, is not the root of any ordinary equation.
Immanuel Kant's philosophy that we can only know things as they appear to us, shaped by our minds, and never as they truly are in themselves.
A 19th-century American movement of thinkers such as Emerson and Thoreau, who believed that people can find spiritual truth through intuition and nature rather than through established religion.
To transcribe means to take something that exists in one form and faithfully convert it into written text.

A transcript is a written record of something. That "something" is usually either: Words that were spoken (converted into written form), or Important facts and data about a person or event, captured in an official document.
Transcription means taking something that exists in one form and faithfully converting it into written or typed text — either the act of doing that, or the written result itself.

The word transfer refers to the act of moving something — or someone — from one place, person, group, or state to another. A transfer is always about a movement between a starting point and a destination.

To transfer means to move something from one place, person, or system to another. But it's not just any kind of movement. Transfer always carries two ideas together: something leaves one point, and that same thing arrives at another.

Transference means the act of shifting or redirecting something — a feeling, emotion, expectation, or attitude — from one person or situation onto another, often without being fully aware that you're doing it.

To transfigure something means to change its outward appearance so completely and dramatically that it looks almost unrecognisably different — and almost always more beautiful, radiant, or awe-inspiring than it was before.

The single most important thing to understand about "transfix" is this: it means to hold something completely still — either by physically piercing through it, or by stunning it so powerfully that it cannot move.

When someone is transfixed, they are so completely captured by something — something they are looking at, listening to, or experiencing — that they cannot move, cannot look away, and cannot think about anything else. Everything else fades out.
To transform something means to change it so deeply and completely that it becomes fundamentally different from what it was before. This is not a small, surface-level change.
Transformation means a thorough, fundamental change in which something — or someone — becomes so different from what it was that it has, in an important sense, become a new version of itself.
Transfuse means to cause something to pass from one place, person, or container into another — like pouring or moving a substance (or quality) through from one source into a receiver.
A transfusion is the act of transferring a liquid — almost always blood or a blood component — from one source into the body of a person or animal, delivered directly into a vein.
A transgender person is someone whose internal sense of who they are — as a man, a woman, or neither — does not match the sex they were recorded as at birth.
To transgress means to cross a line that you are not supposed to cross — whether that line is a rule, a law, a moral principle, or a social boundary.
A transgression is an act of crossing a line that should not be crossed — breaking a rule, a moral code, a law, or a limit that exists to define what is right or acceptable.

Transience is the quality of not lasting. When something has transience, it means it exists for a while and then it's gone — it passes, fades, or disappears. It is the state of being temporary, fleeting, or short-lived.
Transient means lasting only for a short time before disappearing or passing away. If something is transient, it does not stay. It arrives, exists briefly, and then it is gone.
A transistor is a small electronic component made from semiconductor material that can do two things: switch an electrical current on or off, or amplify a weak electrical signal into a stronger one.
A transition is the process of moving or changing from one state, condition, situation, or place to another.
Transitory means lasting only for a short time and then disappearing or coming to an end. Something transitory does not stay. It passes. It is not permanent.
Translate means to take something that exists in one form and convert it into another form, in a way that preserves its meaning or essence.

Transliteration is the act of taking a word written in one script (one writing system) and rewriting it using the letters of a different script — not to change its meaning, but to represent its sounds as closely as possible.
Something is translucent when light can pass through it, but you cannot see clearly through it. You get light, but not a clear picture.

To transmit something means to send it, pass it, or carry it from one place or person to another. Every use of this word involves three things: a source (where something starts), a receiver (where it ends up), and something traveling between them.

To transmogrify something (or someone) means to transform it into a completely different form — but not in an ordinary way. The change is usually strange, bizarre, grotesque, magical, or comically absurd.
Transmutation means the process of something changing completely from one fundamental nature, form, or substance into something entirely different.

To transmute something means to change it from one form, substance, or nature into something completely and fundamentally different. This isn't a surface-level change, like painting a wall a different color.
A horizontal bar of wood or stone across a window or above a door. A transom window is a small window above a door. On a boat, the transom is the flat back end.
Openness and honesty, with nothing hidden ("transparency in government"); or the quality of being see-through.

Everything about "transparent" comes down to one simple idea: you can see through it. Nothing is hidden. Whether the word is used to describe a piece of glass or a person's behavior, that core idea never changes.

Transphobia is a prejudice — a collection of negative attitudes, feelings, and behaviors — directed at transgender people or at anyone whose gender identity or gender expression does not match the sex they were assigned at birth.
To happen, as in "nobody knows what transpired." In formal use, to become known, as in "it transpired that she had lied." In biology, of plants, to give off water vapour through their leaves.
To transplant something means to take a living thing out of the place where it exists and move it to a new place, where it is then expected to survive and function just as it did before.

Transport means the movement of people or things from one place to another. Think of it as anything that carries something or someone across a distance. This one simple idea branches out into a few different but closely related meanings.
To transport means to move someone or something from one place to another, usually over a distance and usually by some kind of vehicle or system.

To transpose means to move something out of its current position and place it somewhere else — or more specifically, to swap or shift the order of things. The movement isn't random; it's deliberate and structured.

Transubstantiation is a word from Christian theology — specifically Roman Catholic doctrine — that names a very particular and extraordinary belief: that during a sacred religious ritual, ordinary bread and wine are completely and truly transformed into the body and blood of Jesus Christ.
Transverse means lying, moving, or extending across something — typically at a right angle to its length or main direction.
A trap is something that catches, holds, or stops something — usually without warning, and usually in a way that is hard to escape.
To trap means to catch or hold something in a way that makes escape or release difficult or impossible.

"Trappings" refers to the visible signs, symbols, and accessories that are associated with a particular status, role, or lifestyle — the things that you can see and point to that signal what something or someone is, represents, or has achieved.

Trash refers to things that are no longer wanted, useful, or valuable — things that people throw away or discard. Think of an empty juice carton, a broken pen, a torn envelope, or leftover food scraps. These are all trash.

Trauma means a serious wound — one that doesn't just hurt in the moment, but leaves a lasting mark. That one idea runs through every use of this word, whether it's being used in a hospital or in a conversation about someone's difficult past.

The adjective traumatic describes something that causes, involves, or is related to trauma — a wound so deep, whether emotional or physical, that it doesn't simply pass. It leaves a lasting mark on a person.

To traumatize someone means to cause them such severe psychological shock, pain, or fear that it leaves a deep and lasting wound in their mind — not just a momentary upset, but damage that continues to affect them long after the experience is over.
Travail means painful, exhausting, and deeply difficult effort or suffering — especially the kind that drags on over a long period of time.
Traversable means: capable of being crossed, passed through, or traveled across in its entirety.
To traverse something means to travel across it, through it, or over it — from one side to the other.

A travesty is something that is supposed to represent, reflect, or honor something good, serious, or important — but does so in such a distorted, inadequate, or absurd way that it ends up mocking or degrading the very thing it claims to represent.

To trawl means to search through a large amount of something — carefully, slowly, and thoroughly — in order to find what you're looking for. Think of it as a wide, sweeping, drag-everything-in-your-path kind of search.
The simplest definition first: A trawler is a fishing boat that catches fish by dragging a large, heavy net through the water.

"Treacherous" means something — or someone — that cannot be trusted, especially because the danger or disloyalty is hidden or disguised. It's not just about being dangerous or dishonest. The key idea is that the threat is concealed.
"Treacherously" describes doing something in a way that betrays trust through hidden deception — or describes something that is secretly dangerous in a hidden way.
Treachery means the act of betraying someone who trusted you, done in a secret and deliberate way, usually causing them serious harm.
A thick, dark, sticky syrup made from sugar; also speech or writing that is too sweet and sentimental.
The noun tread almost always refers to one of two things: the textured surface of something that makes contact with the ground, or the sound and manner of someone's footsteps.
Tread means to step on something or walk on or over something, with a specific focus on the contact between your foot and the surface beneath you.
Treason is the act of betraying your own country — working against the very nation or government that you belong to and owe loyalty to.
Treasonous means relating to, involving, or constituting treason — which is the act of betraying your own country in a serious and deliberate way.

A treasure is anything that is considered extremely valuable and worth keeping safe. The value can be in terms of money, or it can be deeply personal — something priceless to you, even if the rest of the world doesn't care about it.
To treasure something means to feel a deep, loving appreciation for it — to hold it in your heart as something rare and precious to you, and to make sure you never lose sight of its special value.

The government department responsible for a country's finances. A treasury is also a place where money or valuable objects are kept, or a collection of valuable or delightful things, as in "a treasury of poems."
A treatise is a serious, carefully written piece of writing — usually a long book or document — that explores a specific subject in great depth, thoroughly, and in an organized way.

Treatment means the way something or someone is handled, dealt with, or acted upon. Every single meaning of this word — whether it's about medicine, human behavior, writing, or materials — revolves around this one idea: how something is handled.
A treaty is a formal, written agreement made between two or more countries (or other recognized international bodies) that is legally binding under international law.
A tree line is a natural boundary — a line or zone on the landscape that marks the limit beyond which trees cannot grow. On one side of this boundary, you have a forest or at least some trees.
A trek is a long, difficult journey made mostly on foot, especially through wild, remote, or challenging terrain like mountains, forests, or deserts.
To trek means to travel a long distance, usually on foot, through difficult or challenging conditions. Think of it as being on the harder, longer, more demanding end of the "movement" scale.
A trellis is a frame or flat panel made of thin strips — usually of wood, metal, or plastic — that are arranged in a crisscross pattern, creating a grid of small diamond- or square-shaped openings.
To tremble means to shake with small, fast, and uncontrolled movements. The key thing to understand is that trembling is involuntary — the person or thing doing it is not choosing to shake.

Tremendous means so large, powerful, or great in degree that it almost overwhelms you. It describes something that hits you with force — something you can't ignore or brush aside because of its sheer scale or intensity.

A tremor is a small, involuntary, rhythmic shaking or quivering — something that shakes in a way that cannot be fully controlled, and usually in a repeated, back-and-forth motion rather than just a single jolt.

Tremulous means shaking or quivering with small, rapid movements — and it can describe either something that is literally, physically trembling, or something that is emotionally fragile and unsteady, as if on the verge of trembling.
"Tremulously" means in a trembling, shaking, or quivering manner. It describes how something is done — with a physical or emotional shakiness that the person doing it cannot fully control.

A trench is a long, narrow hole dug into the ground — think of it as a cut in the earth that is much longer than it is wide, and deep enough for a purpose. If you dragged a giant knife along the ground and scooped out the dirt in a line, you'd have a trench.
Sharp, clear, and forceful, as in "a trenchant critique."

When someone does or says something trenchantly, they do it in a way that is sharp, direct, forceful, and cutting — like a blade slicing cleanly through something. There is no softening, no hedging, no dancing around the point.
A trencherman is a person who eats a great deal — someone who has a large, enthusiastic appetite and enjoys food wholeheartedly. The word describes a hearty, vigorous eater.
A trend is a general direction in which something is moving, changing, or developing over a period of time.

A trendoid is a person who follows the latest trends — especially in fashion, style, or culture — in an obsessive, mindless, and excessive way, without any real personal taste or original thought of their own.

Trepidation is a feeling of fear or worry about something that is about to happen or might happen. It is the nervous, uneasy feeling you get when you are uncertain about what lies ahead and suspect it could be unpleasant, difficult, or dangerous.
If someone is trepidatious, they feel a nervous, uneasy kind of fear or anxiety — usually about something that is about to happen or something whose outcome is uncertain.

A trespass is the act of crossing a boundary that you have no right to cross — whether that boundary is physical (someone's land), personal (someone's body), legal (someone's possessions), or moral (God's law or basic decency).
To trespass means to go somewhere you have no right to go, or to do something you have no right to do — especially when it crosses a line that belongs to someone else.

A tress is a long lock or strand of hair — specifically one that hangs loosely or is loosely braided. Think of it as a distinct, flowing portion of hair, not hair in general as a whole lump or mass, but as a recognizable individual strand or section of it.

A trestle is a supporting framework — a structure whose only job is to hold something else up. It doesn't do any work of its own; it simply stands firm so that whatever rests on top of it stays at the right height and doesn't fall.
A triad is a group, set, or unit of exactly three things — three people, three ideas, three objects, or three elements — that are related to each other or work together in some meaningful way.

Triage is the process of sorting people, tasks, or problems into priority order — deciding who or what gets attention first — when you don't have enough time, resources, or capacity to handle everything at once.
The word trial carries one central idea: a test. Whether something is being judged, examined, or put through difficulty — a trial is always about determining something through a process.
To triangulate means to use three separate reference points to locate, confirm, or figure out something more accurately than you could with just one or two.
Tribal is an adjective that means relating to, belonging to, or characteristic of a tribe.
A tribe is a group of people bound together by shared ancestry, shared culture, or both — who see themselves as one united community with a common identity.
Tribulation means a state of great suffering, hardship, or distress — especially one that is serious, prolonged, and deeply felt. It is not about small, everyday annoyances.
A tribunal is an official body of people who have the authority and power to listen to disputes, examine facts, and make formal, binding decisions about them.
A tributary is a river or stream that flows into a larger river or lake, rather than flowing directly into a sea or ocean.
A tribute is something you offer to show that you deeply value, respect, or admire someone or something. It is a way of saying "this person, or this thing, matters — and I want the world to know it."

A trice is an extremely short period of time — so short that it feels almost like no time at all. Think of it as a tiny, barely-there sliver of a moment. We're not talking about a few minutes, or even a few seconds.
Trickery means the deliberate use of clever, dishonest acts or schemes to make someone believe something that is not true, or to gain an unfair advantage over them.
A small, thin stream of liquid, as in "a trickle of water." Figuratively, a small number of people or things arriving slowly, as in "a trickle of visitors."
To trickle means to flow slowly in a thin, gentle stream — in a small amount, little by little, not all at once.
"Tricksy" describes someone — or something — that is full of tricks: clever, crafty, and not quite straightforward.

A trident is a long spear with three sharp points at one end, instead of just one. Picture a regular spear — now imagine three pointed tips sitting side by side at the top, like three teeth of a fork. That is a trident.

Something of little value or importance, as in "a mere trifle." "A trifle" can also mean slightly, as in "a trifle nervous." A trifle is also a British dessert of sponge cake, fruit, custard, and cream.

To trifle means to treat something or someone as if they are less important or less serious than they actually are — to handle them carelessly, dismissively, or with a kind of playful disrespect that the situation simply does not deserve.
To trifle with something or someone means to treat it without the seriousness, care, or respect it deserves.

Something is trifling when it is so small, unimportant, or insignificant that it barely deserves to be noticed or taken seriously. If you call something trifling, you are saying it is too minor and too petty to merit real attention or real concern.
A trigger is something that starts, causes, or sets off something else. Think of it as the first domino that makes all the other dominoes fall. The thing that makes things happen.

To trigger something means to cause it to start or happen, especially by being the direct thing that sets it off. Think of it like a domino effect — your action is the first domino that pushes everything else over.
A trill is any sound produced by a rapid, repeated back-and-forth vibration or flickering motion — creating a fast, trembling effect.

A trilobite is a type of ancient sea creature that is now completely extinct — meaning no trilobites are alive anywhere on Earth today. Every single thing we know about them comes from their fossilized remains, which are found in rocks all over the world.
A trilogy is a set of three creative works — such as books, films, or plays — that are connected to each other and are meant to be experienced as one complete whole.
The word trim describes something — or someone — that looks neat, well-kept, and in good shape, without any mess, excess, or disorder. Think of it as the opposite of "sloppy" or "unkempt."
To trim means to make something better by removing or adjusting the parts that shouldn't be there.
A trimester is a period of three months. More specifically, it refers to one of three equal (or roughly equal) parts into which a stretch of time — usually nine months — is divided.

A trinket is a small object that has little to no monetary value, but is kept or given because it looks pretty, feels special, or holds a memory. Think of it as a little "nothing" object that still somehow means something — or at least catches the eye.
A trio is a group of exactly three — three people, three things, or three parts that are connected and treated together as one unified whole.
To cause someone to make a mistake, as in "the tricky question tripped him up." Literally, to cause someone to stumble and fall.
Tripe refers to the edible stomach lining of a large farm animal — most often a cow, but also sheep or pig. It is sold as meat and cooked in various ways around the world.

When you use "triple" to describe something, you are telling your reader or listener one of two closely related things: that something is made up of three parts, or that something is three times as much as something else.

To triple something means to make it exactly three times as large, as many, or as great as it was before. If something triples on its own, it becomes three times what it was without anyone directly causing it.
A triplet means a group of exactly three things that are closely linked together — usually of the same kind, treated as a single unit, or occurring together.
A triptych is a single work — most often a work of art — that is made up of exactly three parts, where all three parts belong together and are meant to be experienced as one complete whole.
Something is trite when it has been said, done, or expressed so many times that it has completely lost its freshness, power, and meaning. It once had impact. It once felt real and meaningful.

A triumph is a great and decisive victory or success, especially one that was hard to achieve. It is not just any win — it is a win that feels significant, that came after real effort, difficulty, or competition, and that brings a deep sense of joy and pride.
To triumph means to achieve a great victory or success, especially after facing real difficulty, a strong opponent, or serious odds against you. It is not just about winning.
Triumphant means having achieved a great victory or success, and showing or feeling enormous joy and pride because of it.
Triumphantly means in a way that openly shows great joy, pride, and satisfaction because of a victory or success.

A triumvirate is a group of exactly three people who share power, authority, or dominance together. It describes a situation where three individuals — rather than one leader — are jointly at the top, running or controlling something.
A trivet is a small stand or rack designed to hold something up — either to protect a surface from heat, or to lift food above liquid inside a cooking pot.
"Trivia" refers to small, minor facts or pieces of information that are not important to daily life, but that people often find interesting, surprising, or fun to know.
When something is trivial, it means it is so small, minor, or unimportant that it barely deserves any attention or effort. Think of it as the opposite of "serious" or "significant."
"Triviality" means the quality or state of being trivial — that is, being small, unimportant, or not worth serious attention.
To trivialize something means to make it appear less important, less serious, or less significant than it actually is.
Trod is the simple past tense of the verb "tread." So to understand "trod," you first need to understand "tread."
A person who is deliberately ignorant, old-fashioned, or unwilling to accept new ideas. Literally, a person who lives in a cave, especially in prehistoric times.

Troika simply means a group of exactly three. But it's not just any three things — it almost always refers to three people or three organizations that hold power, authority, or responsibility together, as a united unit.
A Trojan horse is something — or someone — that looks harmless, friendly, or beneficial on the outside, but secretly contains a hidden danger, threat, or destructive purpose on the inside.
To post provocative or insulting messages online to upset people; or to fish by trailing a baited line behind a moving boat.

A troop is a group. Specifically, it is a group of beings — people or animals — that are together, either moving as one or assembled in one place. Think of it as a cluster, a pack, a crowd — but with a particular flavor depending on the context.

A trope is a recognizable, recurring pattern — a familiar device, idea, or figure of speech that keeps appearing again and again, in language or in stories, so reliably that people instantly know what it is when they see it.
Trophic means "relating to feeding, nutrition, or the flow of energy through living things."
A trophy is an object that you keep and often display to show that you achieved something great — especially that you won a competition, defeated an opponent, or succeeded at something difficult.

A tropic is an imaginary line drawn around the Earth, parallel to the equator, marking the farthest point north or south where the Sun can shine directly overhead — straight down, at a perfect 90-degree angle — at least once during the year.

Tropical means relating to, belonging to, or characteristic of the tropics. That's the single root idea behind every use of this word. So to understand "tropical," you first need to understand what the tropics are.

Of a horse, to move at a pace faster than a walk but slower than a canter. Of a person, to run at a moderate pace with short steps, or to go somewhere casually. To trot out something means to repeat it tiresomely, as in "trot out the same old excuses."
Troth means a solemn, deeply serious pledge of faithfulness or loyalty — the kind of promise that binds you completely, as a matter of your personal honor.
A troubadour is a poet and musician — specifically one who composes their own songs and performs them. The key idea is that a troubadour is not just a performer who sings other people's work.

Trouble refers to anything that causes difficulty, worry, pain, or inconvenience — whether it is a situation, a person, a thing, or a feeling. Think of it as the opposite of smooth, easy, and peaceful.
To cause someone to worry or feel uneasy, as in "something is troubling her." It can also mean to put someone to inconvenience, as in "may I trouble you for the salt?" or to cause pain or problems.

When something is troublesome, it means it causes problems, difficulty, or annoyance — and usually does so in a persistent or repeated way. It is something that demands more effort, attention, or patience than you would like.
A long, narrow open container from which farm animals eat or drink. Figuratively, a low point, as in "peaks and troughs" in the economy. In weather, a trough is a long area of low pressure.

To trounce someone means to defeat them completely, decisively, and by a very large margin. It is not just winning — it is winning so overwhelmingly that the other side looks almost helpless. Think of a football match that ends 9–0.
A troupe is a group of performers — such as actors, dancers, acrobats, circus artists, or comedians — who work together as an organized unit, usually in a professional or semi-professional setting.
A trousseau is the personal collection of clothes, linens, and other belongings that a bride puts together before her wedding — specifically to take with her into her new married life and new home.
A trout is a type of fish. More specifically, it is a freshwater fish — meaning it lives in rivers, streams, and lakes (not the sea), though a few types can spend time in saltwater too.

A trove is a rich, impressive collection of things that are considered valuable, interesting, or useful — especially one that has been found or uncovered. Think of it as a rewarding discovery of many good things gathered in one place.

A trowel is a small, handheld tool made up of two basic parts: a flat or scooped blade (usually metal) and a short handle attached to it. You hold it in one hand and use the blade to either spread a material onto a surface or dig into the ground.
Truancy is the act of staying away from school without permission and without a good reason.
A truant is a student who deliberately stays away from school without permission and without a valid reason.

A truce is a mutual, temporary agreement between two opposing sides to stop fighting each other. Both sides agree — at the same time — to pause their conflict for a set period or until a certain condition is met. Neither side wins, neither side surrenders.

A truckle is a small wheel or roller — specifically the kind used beneath furniture or objects to make them easy to move. Think of the little wheels attached to the legs of a heavy bed or crate so you can roll it across the floor.

Truculence means the quality of being aggressively hostile, fiercely confrontational, and always ready to fight or argue — not because the situation demands it, but simply because that is how a person naturally carries themselves.
Truculent describes someone who is aggressively hostile, combative, and quick to argue or fight.
To trudge means to walk slowly, with heavy and laborious steps, usually because you are tired, the ground is difficult, or you are doing something you don't want to do.
"Trudge off" means to walk away from somewhere slowly and heavily, usually because you are tired, sad, disappointed, reluctant, or defeated.
A truffle, in its most famous sense, is a type of fungus — a living organism related to mushrooms — that grows completely underground, near the roots of certain trees like oak, hazel, and beech.
