A truism is a statement that is so obviously and undeniably true that saying it out loud adds no real value. Everyone already knows it. It tells you nothing new. It's truth, yes — but truth so plain and self-evident that it barely needed to be spoken.

To trump something means to beat it, defeat it, or override it decisively — by having a stronger authority, a more powerful advantage, or a more important claim. When one thing trumps another, it wins so completely that the losing side has no comeback.
Trumped-up means deliberately invented or fabricated — especially to harm someone or to justify something unfair.
Trumpery refers to things — whether physical objects or ideas/speech — that look impressive or valuable on the surface but are, in reality, completely worthless.
A trumpet is a musical instrument made of metal — usually a shiny yellow metal called brass.
To trumpet something means to announce or promote it very loudly, very publicly, and with great pride or enthusiasm — to make absolutely sure as many people as possible hear about it.
To truncate something means to shorten it by cutting it off at a specific point — and simply leaving out everything that comes after that point.

Truncated means cut short by having a part removed from it. Something truncated is not simply small or brief — it is a version of something that was (or was meant to be) larger, longer, or more complete, but now has a piece missing because it was cut away.

Truncation is the act of cutting something short, or the result of something having been cut short. Something existed in a fuller, more complete form — and then a portion of it, almost always from one end, was removed.

A truncheon is a short, thick, heavy stick used as a weapon — specifically the kind carried by police officers to control or strike people when necessary. Think of it as a handheld club, built for one purpose: hitting and subduing.
To trundle means to move — or to cause something to move — slowly and steadily, rolling along on wheels or in a heavy, rotating fashion.
The thick main stem of a tree. It can also mean the main part of the body, a large box for storing things, the boot of a car in American English, or an elephant's long nose.
To truss something means to tie it up tightly and securely — binding it so thoroughly that it holds a fixed, compact shape or cannot move freely.
Trust is a confident belief that someone or something is reliable, honest, good, or capable — and that you can safely depend on them.
When you call someone or something trusted, you are saying that people have placed their confidence in it — and that confidence has been earned and proven over time.

A trustee is a person — or sometimes an organization — who is given the responsibility of holding and managing something (usually money, property, or assets) on behalf of someone else, not for their own personal benefit.

When you say someone or something is trustworthy, you mean they are deserving of your trust — meaning you can rely on them, believe them, and feel safe depending on them, because they have proven themselves to be honest, responsible, and consistent.
When you call something or someone trusty, you mean they are reliably dependable — and not just in theory, but proven to be so over time. A trusty person or thing has already passed the test of time.

When "trying" is used as an adjective, it describes something — a situation, a person, an experience, or a period of time — that is difficult to deal with because it tests your patience, strength, or emotional endurance.

"Trying times" means a period of life that is very difficult, painful, stressful, or hard to endure. It describes a stretch of time that puts a heavy burden on people — emotionally, physically, or practically.
A tryst is a secret, romantic meeting between two people — usually lovers — that is planned ahead of time and held in a private or hidden place, away from the knowledge of others.
A tsunami is a series of extremely powerful ocean waves caused by a sudden, massive disturbance that displaces a huge volume of water.

Tsuris means troubles, worries, suffering, and aggravation — all rolled into one word. Think of it as pointing to that heavy, draining mix of problems and distress that life sometimes piles onto a person.
A mistake in reasoning where someone dismisses criticism by pointing out that the critic is guilty of the same thing, as in "You smoke too, so you can't tell me to quit."
A tub is an open container that is wider than it is tall, with a flat base and outward-sloping or straight sides. Think of a large bowl — sturdy, wide-mouthed, and meant to hold something inside it.
A tuber is a swollen, fleshy underground part of a plant that stores food — mainly starch — for the plant to use later.
Tuberculosis — commonly shortened to TB — is a serious infectious disease caused by a bacterium called Mycobacterium tuberculosis. "Infectious" means it can spread from one person to another.
"Tuck" means to push, fold, or place something snugly into a tight, enclosed, or small space — usually to make it neat, secure, cozy, or hidden.
A tuckshop is a small shop that sells snacks, sweets, drinks, and light food. In most cases, it is found inside or right next to a school, and it mainly serves students.

A tuft is a small, compact bunch of thin, soft, flexible things — such as hair, grass, feathers, or threads — that are held together or rooted at one end (the base), while the other ends are free and spread outward.
Teaching or instruction, especially given to one person or a small group; also the fee charged for teaching.
Tulle is a type of fabric — but unlike the fabric of a shirt or bedsheet, it is extremely thin, lightweight, and full of tiny holes, like a very fine net or a stiff cobweb.

Tumble means to fall, roll, or move in an uncontrolled, disorderly way. Think of the motion of a person tripping and rolling down a hill — that messy, spinning, out-of-control movement is the soul of this word.
To come out quickly and in a disorganized way, as in "the children tumbled out of the car." Of words or feelings, to be expressed in a sudden rush, as in "the whole story tumbled out."
Tumbledown is an adjective that describes a building or structure that is so old, neglected, and worn out that it looks like it is about to fall apart or collapse.
A drinking glass with a flat bottom and no handle or stem. A tumbler is also an acrobat, part of a lock that must be moved by a key, or a machine that tumbles clothes dry.
A tumbrel is a simple, open, two-wheeled cart — the kind pulled by a horse or an ox — designed so that its body can tilt backward to dump whatever is inside it onto the ground.

"Tumescent" means swollen, or more precisely, in the process of swelling up — particularly when that swelling happens because fluid (most often blood) has rushed into and filled a tissue from the inside, making it enlarged, firm, and turgid.
Of language, pompous and overblown, as in "tumid prose." Literally, swollen, as in "a tumid wound."
An abnormal mass of tissue caused by cells growing and dividing out of control. A tumor can be benign (not cancerous) or malignant (cancerous).
Tumult means a state of loud, chaotic confusion and disorder. Think of a moment when everything around you is noisy, wild, and out of control all at once — that is a tumult.
Tumultuous means wildly chaotic, loud, and disorderly — full of confusion, strong emotion, or violent movement.
A tundra is a large, treeless, freezing cold, and dry landscape where the ground beneath the surface stays permanently frozen.
To tune means to adjust something carefully until it reaches exactly the right state — whether that's the right sound, the right signal, the right performance, or the right setting.

Tuneful means pleasantly musical. When something is tuneful, it has a clear, sweet, agreeable melody that is easy and enjoyable to listen to. Think of it as the opposite of noise — tuneful sounds are organized, melodic, and pleasing to the ear.

A tunnel is a long, enclosed passage that goes through something — most commonly through the earth, a mountain, or under a body of water. It is hollow inside, like a long tube, and it has two open ends: one where you enter and one where you exit.

A turban is a type of head covering made by winding a long piece of cloth around the head. Unlike a hat — which has a fixed shape and is simply placed on the head — a turban has no pre-made shape of its own.

Turbid describes something — most commonly a liquid — that is cloudy, murky, and unclear because it has tiny particles floating and suspended through it. You cannot see through it clearly. It is the opposite of clear, clean, or transparent.

Turbidity is a noun that describes the cloudiness, haziness, or murkiness of a fluid — most commonly water — caused by tiny particles suspended within it. Think of it this way: pure, clean water is transparent. You can see straight through it.

A turbine is a machine that spins when a moving fluid — either a gas (like air or steam) or a liquid (like water) — flows over its blades. That spinning motion is then used to do useful work, most often to generate electricity or to power vehicles.
Turbulence means a state of irregular, chaotic, and unpredictable movement or change. It is the opposite of calm, smooth, and orderly.

Turbulent describes something that is chaotic, unstable, and in a state of disorder — something that is rough, restless, and hard to control, where things are constantly moving in unpredictable or conflicting directions.
A tureen is a large, deep serving dish with a lid, designed to bring soups or stews directly to the dining table so people can serve themselves.
Grass and the layer of soil held together by its roots. Informally, the area or field where someone feels at home or in control, as in "on his own turf." "The turf" is also horse racing.
Of language, pompous, dull, and overcomplicated, as in "turgid prose." Literally, swollen or bloated, especially with liquid.

Turgidity means the state or quality of being swollen, puffed up, or bloated — either physically (as in a body or a cell filled with fluid under pressure) or figuratively (as in language that is inflated, pompous, and unnecessarily complicated).
A Turing machine is not a physical, real-world machine you can touch or buy.
A Turing test is a method for determining whether a machine (specifically, an artificial intelligence) can think and behave in a way that is indistinguishable from a human being.
Turmoil means a state of great confusion, disorder, and disturbance — where many things are going wrong, shifting, or clashing at the same time, and there is no sense of calm, stability, or control.
To turn a blind eye means to deliberately pretend not to notice something, especially something wrong, unfair, or troubling — even though you are fully aware of it.

Every meaning of "turn around" comes from a single core idea: reversal — going the opposite way. Whether it's your body, a journey, a situation, an opinion, or an expectation — something is doing a 180.

A turnabout is a complete reversal — a full 180-degree change from one direction, position, or state to another. Picture someone walking down a path, then spinning around and walking back the way they came.

"Turnaround" captures the image of something literally turning around — going in one direction, then reversing completely. Every meaning of this word flows from that central idea of a full reversal or a full cycle of completion.

A turncoat is a person who abandons the group, side, or cause they once belonged to — and then joins or supports the opposing side. The switch is seen as a betrayal, and the word is always used with a negative, condemning tone.

A turnkey is something — a product, a property, a business, or a system — that is completely finished and fully ready to use the moment it is handed over, with no additional work required from the person receiving it.
A turnoff is a spot on a road where you leave the main path and take a smaller road, a side road, or an exit that branches off in a different direction.
When someone says "turnout," they usually mean how many people showed up — to a vote, a protest, a concert, a match, a meeting, or any public event. It measures attendance or participation.
The word turnover captures one core idea: things cycling out and being replaced. Think of it like a wheel turning — something goes out, something new comes in.
A turnpike is a road — specifically, a major road where you must pay a toll (a fee) in order to use it. The toll is collected at specific points along the road, called toll booths or toll plazas.
A turnstile is a mechanical gate that lets only one person pass through at a time. It is designed to control access — meaning it decides who gets in and how many people enter.
Turpitude means deep, shameful wickedness. It refers to behavior that is so morally corrupt and so fundamentally wrong that it offends the basic values of decent society.
As a noun, "turquoise" refers to two closely related things: a gemstone, and the color of that gemstone.

A turret is a small tower that is part of, or attached to, something larger — not a standalone tower, but one that grows out of a bigger structure. Think of it as a tower's little sibling, always connected to something else.

A tusk is a very long, pointed tooth that sticks out of an animal's mouth and stays visible even when the mouth is closed. Think of it this way — most animal teeth are hidden inside the mouth and are used mainly for chewing.
A tussle is a rough, disorderly struggle between two or more people or groups. It can be physical (bodies pushing and grabbing) or non-physical (a conflict over power, opinions, or resources).

To tussle means to struggle, fight, or compete with someone or something in a rough, active, and energetic way. Think of two people grabbing, pushing, pulling, or wrestling with each other — not in a calm, gentle way, but in a messy, physical back-and-forth.
A tussock is a dense, compact clump of grass — or a grass-like plant such as a sedge or rush — that grows tightly bunched together and stands up as a raised, rounded mound above the ground around it.

To tut means to make a short, sharp sound — or simply say "tut" — to show that you disapprove of something, are disappointed by it, or find it mildly unacceptable. It is a way of reacting negatively to something without saying a full sentence of criticism.

Tutelage means the guidance, teaching, or protection that a more experienced, skilled, or authoritative person gives to someone who needs to learn or grow. Think of it as being formally "taken under someone's wing."
Having the recognized, established role of a guardian or protector over someone or something.
A tutor is a person who teaches someone — but in a very personal, focused way.
To tutor someone means to teach a person privately, giving them focused, one-on-one (or very small group) attention in a specific subject.

A tutorial is a structured, step-by-step lesson that teaches you how to do one specific thing. Its entire purpose is to guide you through a task or skill — from the beginning to the end — in a way that is easy to follow, even if you are a complete beginner.
A tuxedo is a special type of formal suit that men wear to elegant, high-end social events.
Twaddle is talk or writing that is foolish, trivial, and completely without substance — the kind that sounds like words are being said, but nothing real or meaningful is actually being communicated.

When you twang something, you make it produce a sharp, short, ringing, vibrating sound — the kind of sound that happens when something thin and tight (under tension) is plucked, snapped, or released suddenly.

To tweak something means to make a small, careful, precise change to something — usually to make it slightly better, more accurate, or more suitable. It is never a big or dramatic change. It's a minor adjustment.
Excessively cute, sweet, or sentimental in a way that feels artificial or irritating (British).

Tweed is a type of fabric — specifically, a rough, thick, woolen cloth. Think of it as a sturdy textile made from wool, with a noticeably coarse and textured surface. It is not soft and smooth like silk or fine cotton.
Tweezers are a small, handheld gripping tool used to pick up, hold, or pull out objects that are too tiny or too delicate to be handled safely and precisely with your bare fingers.

A twig is a very small, thin, and short piece of a woody plant — specifically, one of the tiny shoots that stick out from the end of a branch. Think of it as the smallest, outermost tip of a tree's or shrub's branching system.
Twilight is the soft, gentle light that fills the sky when the sun is just below the horizon — not fully up, and not fully gone. It is the in-between: the transition between daylight and darkness.

When you use twin as an adjective, you are describing something that is one of a matched pair — meaning there are exactly two of it, and those two things are closely similar, closely connected, or naturally belong together.
A twin is one of two people or things that come from the same origin at the same time and are therefore closely linked as a pair.

A twinge is a sudden, brief, sharp feeling — either in your body or in your emotions. Think of it as a quick jab or flash of feeling that comes and goes in a moment. It is never long-lasting, never overwhelming. It appears, you notice it, and it fades.
A twinkle is a small, brief, soft flash of light — one that appears and disappears quickly, repeatedly, and gently. It is not a strong, steady beam. It is not a harsh glare.
When something twinkles, it shines with a soft light that rapidly and repeatedly turns slightly brighter and slightly dimmer — on and off, on and off — in quick, small, gentle pulses.
To twirl means to spin something — or yourself — around in a smooth, continuous, circular motion. The spinning usually happens quickly, more than once, and in a light or graceful way.

To twitch means to make a small, sudden, quick movement — usually just one tiny part of the body, and often without fully intending to. It is always a brief, sharp, jerky motion. It happens in a split second and then it's over.
Having two parts or approaches working at the same time ("a two-pronged attack"); literally, having two prongs, like a carving fork.
A tycoon is a person who has become extremely wealthy and very powerful through business. Not just successful — but dominantly successful.

To typecast someone means to see them as only fitting one specific "type" of role, character, or job — and to keep putting them in that same mold, over and over, without giving them a chance to do anything different.
Typhoid (also called typhoid fever) is a serious, potentially life-threatening infectious disease caused by a specific bacterium called Salmonella Typhi.

Having the usual features of a particular type of person or thing, as in "a typical British breakfast." It can also mean characteristic of someone's usual behaviour, often in an annoying way, as in "That's typical of him!"
To be a perfect, representative example of something — to have exactly the qualities that people associate most strongly with a particular type, group, era, or idea.
"Typographical" is an adjective. It describes anything that relates to how text looks on a page or screen — its arrangement, its style, and the physical craft of presenting written language visually.
Typography is the art and practice of arranging written text so that it is easy to read, visually pleasing, and effectively communicates a message.
Typology means the systematic study and practice of grouping things into types — organized categories based on shared characteristics.

Tyrannical is an adjective that describes someone — or something — that uses power in a way that is cruel, unjust, and completely unchecked, with total disregard for the rights, feelings, or freedoms of others.
Tyranny means cruel, harsh, and absolute power that someone uses to control other people — with no fairness, no checks, and no mercy.
A tyrant is a person who holds power over others and uses that power in a cruel, unfair, and controlling way — without caring about the rights, feelings, or well-being of the people under them.

A tyro is a beginner — a person who is brand new to something and has very little experience or skill in it yet. Think of someone on their very first day of learning to drive, or a person who has just picked up a paintbrush for the first time in their life.
A u-boat is a military submarine — a warship designed to travel and fight underwater — most closely associated with Germany, particularly during the two World Wars of the 20th century.
Ubiquitous describes something that seems to be everywhere at once, so thoroughly spread throughout the world (or a given context) that it is nearly impossible to go anywhere without encountering it.
Ubiquity means the state or quality of being present or found everywhere, or seeming to be everywhere at the same time.

An udder is the soft, bag-like organ that hangs underneath the belly of certain female animals, from which milk is produced and drawn out. Think of it as a natural milk container built into the animal's body.
To uglify something means to make it ugly — to change it in a way that makes it look worse, less pleasing, or more unpleasant than it was before.
A ukase is a powerful, official decree — an order that comes from an absolute authority and must be obeyed without question, debate, or appeal.

A ukulele is a small, four-stringed musical instrument. It belongs to the family of string instruments and is closely related to the guitar — think of it as a miniature acoustic guitar, though it has its own distinct character and sound.
An ulcer is an open sore that forms on the surface of a tissue inside or outside your body — and crucially, one that struggles or refuses to heal on its own.
Ulterior describes something that is hidden beneath the surface — a true purpose, reason, or intention that someone deliberately keeps secret and does not openly admit.

The word ultimate points to something that is the furthest you can possibly go — in a sequence, in importance, in degree, or in depth. It signals an endpoint: nothing comes after it, nothing exceeds it, and nothing is more fundamental than it.

When you say "ultimately," you are pointing to either: 1. The final outcome — what happened at the end, after a long process, OR 2. The most fundamental truth — what something really comes down to, when you look past everything else.

An ultimatum is a final demand you make to someone, where you clearly state that if they do not meet your conditions, a specific consequence will follow — and that there is no room left for further negotiation.
An ultracrepidarian is a person who confidently gives opinions, judgments, or advice on subjects they know nothing — or very little — about.
The failure of classical physics to explain heat radiation, as it predicted that hot objects should give off infinite energy at ultraviolet frequencies. Solving it led to the birth of quantum theory.
To ululate means to make a long, loud, high-pitched, wavering cry — a sound that rapidly trembles up and down in pitch, giving it a quivering, rippling, almost undulating quality.
An ululation is a long, loud, high-pitched, wavering cry made by a human voice — or sometimes an animal. The key word here is wavering: it is not a steady, flat sound like a regular shout or scream.

Umber is two things at once: a natural earthy substance and the dark brown color that substance produces. These two meanings are deeply tied together — the color is named after the material, and the material is defined by its color.

Umbilical is an adjective that means "relating to, or resembling the connection between a baby and its mother in the womb." Everything this word means — literally or figuratively — flows from that one central image.

Umbra simply means shadow — but not just any vague, fuzzy kind of shadow. When the word "umbra" is used, it almost always points to the darkest, most complete part of a shadow, where light is blocked out entirely and totally.

Umbrage is the feeling you get when you believe someone has disrespected, insulted, or slighted you. It's that sharp, wounded, "how dare they" feeling — a mix of hurt pride and indignation (a kind of hot, self-righteous annoyance).

When you describe something as umbrageous, you are saying that it creates a lot of shade or is filled with deep shadow. It is used to describe things like trees, forests, canopies, or any place that is dense and shady.

Unabashed describes someone who feels no shame, no embarrassment, and no guilt about something — and who shows it openly, without trying to hide it. The person doesn't just feel unashamed on the inside; they act openly and confidently on the outside too.
Continuing with full force, intensity, or strength — without becoming weaker, slower, or less severe.
When something is unabridged, it means it is complete and whole, exactly as it was originally created — with nothing removed, shortened, or left out.
When you use unaccountable to describe a feeling, an event, or a situation, it means that no logical reason can be found for it.
Unadorned means plain and simple, with nothing added to decorate it or make it look more impressive.

Unadulterated means completely pure, with absolutely nothing added, mixed in, or taken away. It describes something in its most original, untouched, total state — exactly as it is, without any interference whatsoever.
When something is exposed to a force, event, or influence — but it stays the same despite that — it is unaffected.
Unalloyed means completely pure — with absolutely nothing negative, doubtful, or imperfect mixed into it.

Something unalterable is something that cannot be changed — not by you, not by anyone, not by anything, not ever. It is fixed, final, and absolute. No amount of effort, time, argument, or power can modify it.

Something is unambiguous when it has only one possible meaning or interpretation — no more, no less. When a word, sentence, signal, or action is unambiguous, anyone who encounters it will understand it in exactly the same way.
Unanimity is the state in which every single person in a group agrees on something — completely, with no one left out and no one disagreeing. Not most people. Not nearly everyone. Every. Single. One.
Unanimous means that every single person in a group agrees on something — not most people, not almost everyone, but all of them, without even one exception.
Unassailable means so strong, solid, or perfect that it simply cannot be attacked, defeated, or successfully challenged.

Unassuaged describes a feeling, need, or pain that has not been relieved, eased, or satisfied — one that remains just as strong, raw, and intact as it was before. Nothing has softened it. Nothing has brought it any comfort or resolution.

When someone is described as unassuming, it means they are modest and quiet about who they are, what they have, or what they can do — even when they have every reason to feel proud. They do not try to impress people.
Unassured means lacking assurance — that is, lacking the settled, confident feeling of someone who is sure of themselves or sure of an outcome.
Unattached means not connected, joined, or tied to something else. The prefix "un-" simply flips the meaning of "attached" (which means fastened, connected, or committed).
Unattainable means impossible to achieve, reach, or get — no matter how hard you try.
Unavailing describes an effort, attempt, or action that produces no result — one that completely fails to achieve the purpose it was meant for, despite being genuinely tried.
Unavoidable describes something that cannot be stopped, prevented, or escaped from, no matter what you do or how hard you try.
Unavowed means not openly declared, admitted, or acknowledged.

Something is unbearable when it is so extreme, so intense, or so overwhelming that a person cannot handle it, endure it, or continue putting up with it. It has gone past the limit of what someone can tolerate.
Something is unbecoming when it does not suit or fit a person — either because it clashes with who they are, the role they hold, or the standards expected of them.
Unbeknownst means not known to someone. It describes a fact, action, or situation that a specific person has no knowledge of — they are completely unaware it exists or is happening.
"Unbelievable" means so extreme, surprising, or unusual that the mind struggles to accept it as true. The logic is simple: if something is believable, you can accept it without much surprise.
To relax and become less formal or stiff, as in "he finally unbent and joined the fun." Literally, to straighten something that was bent.
Fair and impartial; not favouring one side or opinion over another, as in "an unbiased report."
Arising without being asked for or invited, as in "unbidden thoughts" or "tears came unbidden."
Without any flaw or mark, as in "unblemished skin." Figuratively, without any fault or wrongdoing, as in "an unblemished record."
To unbosom means to openly reveal your private thoughts, feelings, or secrets to someone — especially as a way of freeing yourself from the emotional weight of carrying them alone.
"Unbounded" means having no limits, edges, or restrictions of any kind. Something unbounded cannot be contained, stopped, or measured because there is simply no ceiling, wall, or endpoint to it.

Unbridled means completely unrestrained, uncontrolled, and unchecked — with nothing holding it back, limiting it, or keeping it within bounds. When something is unbridled, it is running at full, raw, maximum force, with zero restriction.
To relieve yourself of a worry or secret by telling someone about it, as in "she unburdened herself to her friend." Literally, to remove a heavy load from someone.
Uncanny means strangely beyond what feels normal, natural, or humanly possible — in a way that makes you feel a quiet, unsettling sense of wonder or unease.
Unceremonious means doing something in a way that is abrupt, blunt, and lacking in the politeness, respect, or dignity that the situation normally calls for.

The Uncertainty Principle says that nature itself — not our instruments, not our clumsiness — places a hard, unavoidable limit on how precisely you can simultaneously know certain pairs of properties of a tiny particle, like where it is and how fast it's moving.
Not explored, mapped, or known about, as in "uncharted territory." Figuratively, completely new and unfamiliar, as in "uncharted waters."
Uncivil means rude, disrespectful, or impolite — specifically in a way that violates the basic standards of courtesy and decent behavior that people are expected to show one another in social life.
To uncoil means to take something that is wound up in loops or a spiral and release it, stretch it out, or let it become straight again. Think of it as the undoing of a coil.

"Uncompromising" describes a person, attitude, or approach that refuses to give up any part of what it stands for — even under pressure, even when it would be much easier to give in, and even when bending a little would make things smoother for everyone involved.
If you are unconcerned, it means you are not worried, not anxious, and not troubled about something. You feel calm and relaxed about it — or you simply don't care about it at all.
Without any conditions, limits, or exceptions — absolute, complete, and total.
Shockingly unfair, unreasonable, or morally wrong, as in "an unconscionable delay." In law, describing a contract so unfair that it should not be enforced.

To be conscious means to be awake, aware, and able to experience the world — to think, feel, notice, and respond. Unconscious simply means the opposite: the absence of that awareness, either in a physical sense or in a mental/behavioral sense.
Unconstitutional describes something — a law, a government action, a policy, an order — that goes against, violates, or is not permitted by the constitution of a country.
Not following what is generally done or accepted; unusual and original, as in "unconventional methods."
Unconvinced means: you have heard a claim, argument, or reason — but it has not persuaded you to believe it.
Uncouth describes a person, their behavior, or their manners as being rough, rude, and socially unacceptable — lacking the basic polish and grace expected in social situations.
Excessive, insincere charm or flattery, especially as a manner of speaking. In religion, unction is the act of anointing someone with holy oil, as in "Extreme Unction" for the dying.
Excessively flattering and insincerely polite, in a smooth, oily way, as in "an unctuous salesman." Of food, rich, smooth, and fatty.

"Undaunted" describes a person who faces difficulty, danger, failure, or fierce opposition — and is not discouraged, not frightened, and not stopped by any of it. They press forward with courage and determination, regardless of what is in their way.

Undefiled means not made dirty, impure, corrupt, or contaminated — physically, morally, or spiritually. Something that is undefiled exists in a state of perfect purity, completely untouched and unspoiled by anything that would taint or corrupt it.
Something is undeniable when it is so clearly and completely true that no one can honestly say "that's not true" or "I disagree." It is beyond argument, beyond doubt, and beyond dispute.

"Under one's breath" means to say something very quietly — so quietly that the people nearby can barely hear it, or cannot hear it at all. The person is not quite whispering, but they are definitely not speaking at a normal, clear volume either.
"Under the guise of" means doing something while pretending it is something else. A person hides their real intention, identity, or action behind a fake or misleading front.

When someone says they are "under the weather," it means they are feeling sick, unwell, or not at their best. It is usually used for mild to moderate illness — like a cold, a headache, an upset stomach, or general tiredness and low energy.

"Underactive" describes something that is functioning below the normal, expected, or healthy level of activity. The key thing to understand is that it does not mean something has completely stopped working.
The hidden, unpleasant, or criminal side of a society or place, as in "the city's seedy underbelly." It can also mean a weak or vulnerable point, or literally the soft underside of an animal.

When someone is undercover, they are secretly pretending to be a different person in order to investigate wrongdoing or gather information that they could never get if people knew who they truly were.
In its physical sense, an undercurrent is a body of water (or sometimes air) that flows beneath the surface layer, often in a different direction or at a different speed than what you can see on top.
When a business undercuts a competitor, it charges less money for the same product or service — low enough to pull customers away.
An underdog is a person, team, animal, or group that is widely expected to lose, fail, or be defeated — especially when compared to a stronger, more powerful, or more favored opponent.
To underestimate something or someone means to form a judgment that is lower or smaller than reality — to think something is less than it truly is.
To undergird something means to support or strengthen it from its very foundation — to be the deep, underlying force that holds it together and keeps it stable.

To undergo something means to go through an experience — but with one very important quality: the subject is not the one causing it to happen. Instead, something is happening to the subject, or upon the subject.
"Underground" as an adjective carries one powerful image: something that exists beneath the surface, out of plain sight. In its literal sense, it means physically below the ground.
When underground works as an adverb, it describes where something goes, happens, or exists — specifically, beneath the surface of the earth, or in a hidden, secret place away from public sight.
Undergrowth is the layer of low plants — shrubs, bushes, ferns, weeds, mosses, creeping vines, and small young trees — that grows on or near the ground under the taller trees of a forest or woodland.

"Underhand" describes behavior that is secretive, dishonest, and unfair — something done in a hidden or deceptive way, usually because the person doing it knows it is wrong and would never be accepted if done openly.
Something is underhanded when it is done in a secret, sneaky, and dishonest way — especially to gain an advantage over someone else.
To be the basic cause of or reason for something, as in "the factors that underlie the crisis." Literally, to lie beneath something, as in "rock underlies the soil."
Underlying describes something that exists below the surface of something else — either physically below it, or deeper than what is immediately obvious or visible.
To undermine something means to weaken it gradually, often in a quiet or hidden way, so that it slowly loses its strength, stability, or effectiveness.
Underneath means directly below something that is acting as a cover, layer, or shelter over it.
To support or form the basis of something, as in "the values that underpin our society." Literally, to support a building from beneath by strengthening its foundations.

When used figuratively, underpinning means the fundamental idea, principle, fact, or assumption that supports something else — a theory, an argument, a belief, a system, a policy, a decision, or even a relationship.
"Underprivileged" describes a person or group of people who do not have the same basic advantages, opportunities, and resources that most other people in their society have.

To underrate something means to judge it as less valuable, less important, or less capable than it truly is. When you underrate something, your opinion of it is lower than it deserves. You are giving it less credit than it has earned.
To underscore something means to emphasize it — to draw strong attention to it and make its importance impossible to ignore.

When something or someone is underserved, it means they are not receiving enough of the help, resources, attention, or services that they need — and, importantly, that they deserve or have a right to expect.
"Undersized" means smaller than what something is supposed to be. It doesn't just say something is small — it says something is too small, compared to a standard, a norm, or an expectation.

When the word "understanding" describes a person, it means they are someone who recognizes what you are going through — your feelings, your struggles, your mistakes, or your difficult situation — and responds with patience, empathy, and acceptance rather than judgment, frustration, or harshness.
Understanding means the state of having grasped something deeply in your mind — not just knowing what something is, but knowing why it is, how it works, and what it means.
To understate something means to describe it in a way that makes it sound less than what it truly is — less serious, less extreme, less important, or less impressive than reality.

When we say something is understated, we mean it is expressed or presented in a quiet, restrained, low-key way — without drama, without exaggeration, without shouting for attention. But here is the crucial part: despite being low-key, it still works.
An understatement is a statement that describes something as less significant, serious, extreme, or impressive than it actually is.

To understeer means the car turns less than you told it to. You command a curve, but the car drifts stubbornly toward going straight instead — the front of the car slides toward the outside of the bend, as if it's ignoring you.
An understudy is a person who learns someone else's job or role thoroughly, so that they can step in and do that job whenever the main person is unable to.
Undertake means to take on a task, responsibility, or piece of work — and commit yourself to carrying it through.
An undertaker is a person whose profession is to manage everything that needs to happen when someone dies — particularly preparing the dead body and organizing the funeral.
A task or project, especially a large or difficult one, as in "a major undertaking." It can also mean a formal promise, or the business of arranging funerals.
A hidden feeling or quality that is suggested but not openly expressed, as in "an undertone of anger." It can also mean a low, quiet voice, or a subtle underlying colour.
An undertow is a hidden current of water that flows back toward the sea, beneath the surface, while waves are rolling toward the shore on top.

To undervalue something or someone means to treat it as less important, less worthy, or less valuable than it truly is. Think of it this way: everything — a person, an object, a skill, a contribution — has a certain true worth.
Something is "underwhelming" when it fails to impress, excite, or satisfy — when it simply does not live up to what was expected of it.
To underwrite something is to take on financial risk or responsibility for it — to stand behind it with your money and say: "If this goes wrong financially, I will cover the loss."

An underwriter is a person or organization that studies a risk, decides whether to take it on, and then bears the financial consequences if things go wrong — in exchange for receiving a fee or premium.
"Undesirable" describes anything — a thing, a situation, a quality, or sometimes a person — that is not wanted, not welcome, or considered bad in some way.
Not stopped, discouraged, or put off by something difficult, scary, or discouraging — continuing forward anyway.

The word undeveloped describes something that exists but has not yet been grown, built upon, processed, or brought to its full potential. Think of it as a seed that is sitting in the soil but has not yet sprouted into a plant. The seed is real.
Never changing or turning aside from a course, belief, or standard, as in "undeviating loyalty."
Undifferentiated describes something that has not been divided into distinct types, categories, or specialized forms.
Undignified means lacking dignity — behaving, appearing, or happening in a way that looks embarrassing, improper, or beneath the level of respect and seriousness that a situation or person deserves.
Undiminished means: not reduced, not weakened, not made less in any way. Something undiminished has kept its full original strength, intensity, quality, or size — nothing has taken away from it.
When something is undisclosed, it means it has not been revealed, shared, or made known to other people.
Not showing good judgement or taste; unable or unwilling to tell good from bad, as in "an undiscriminating reader."
When something is undisguised, it means it is not hidden, not covered up, and not masked in any way. It is completely open and visible for everyone to see.

When something is undisputed, it means that nobody argues against it, challenges it, or questions it. Everyone — or at least everyone who matters — accepts it as true, real, or valid. There is zero disagreement, zero pushback, zero controversy surrounding it.

Undistinguished means not special, not remarkable, and not standing out from the crowd. Something undistinguished blends in — it doesn't rise above the ordinary, and nothing about it makes you sit up and take notice.
Undisturbed means left completely alone — not touched, not interrupted, not interfered with, and not upset in any way.

"Undivided" means whole, complete, and not split into parts. If something is divided, it has been cut into separate pieces. If it is undivided, it has stayed whole — nothing taken away, nothing broken up, nothing separated from the rest.
The word undocumented simply means not supported by, recorded in, or proved through official documents.
Undoing means the cause of someone's ruin, failure, or destruction.

When you say something is undoubted, you mean that it is accepted as true, real, or genuine by everyone — no one questions it, no one disputes it, and no one has any doubt about it. It describes something so clear and obvious that it sits beyond argument.
"Undue" means more than what is right, appropriate, or reasonable in a given situation.
"Undulant" describes something that moves — or looks — like waves. Imagine the ocean: the water doesn't jump up and crash down in sharp, jagged bursts.
To undulate means to move in a smooth, continuous, wave-like motion — gently rising and falling, or curving in and out, over and over again in a flowing rhythm. Think of the surface of the ocean.
An undulation is a smooth, wave-like movement or shape — a gentle, flowing rise and fall that repeats in a continuous, rhythmic pattern, like the surface of the ocean moving up and down.
Unduly means to a degree that is more than what is right, fair, necessary, or reasonable.

"Undying" describes something that never ends, never fades, and never weakens — not with the passage of time, and not even in the face of death. When you call something undying, you are making the strongest possible claim about its permanence.
To discover something hidden or secret by searching, as in "unearthing new evidence." Literally, to dig something up out of the ground.

"Unearthing" as a noun refers to the act of bringing something hidden, buried, or forgotten out into the open — either by literally digging it out of the ground, or by discovering something that was concealed, suppressed, or long lost.

Unearthly means so strange, extraordinary, or intense that it seems impossible to belong to the normal, natural world. It describes something that feels as though it has crossed the boundary of what Earth — or ordinary human experience — can produce.

Uneasy describes a feeling of quiet discomfort, tension, or worry — a sense that something is slightly wrong, or that a situation is not fully settled or safe. When you feel uneasy, your mind is not at peace. You are not relaxed.
Uneducated describes someone who has not received formal schooling or training, or who lacks knowledge and understanding about a particular subject.

Something is unencumbered when it is completely free — not weighed down, held back, tied up, or restricted by anything. Nothing is pulling at it. Nothing is claiming it. Nothing is getting in its way.
Unending means having no end — something that continues without ever stopping, finishing, or reaching a conclusion.
To be unenlightened means to lack real knowledge, understanding, or awareness about something — especially in a way that makes your thinking narrow, outdated, or simply wrong.

Unequal means not the same when compared against a standard or against each other. It describes a gap — a difference in size, amount, level, degree, quality, or value between two or more things. The word is always about comparison.

Unequivocal means something is so completely clear and direct that it can only be understood in one single way. There is no doubt. No confusion. No hidden meaning. No "well, maybe they meant something else." It is the opposite of vague or wishy-washy.
Unequivocally means in a way that is completely clear, leaving absolutely no room for doubt, uncertainty, or alternative interpretation.
Unerring means never making a mistake. It describes someone or something that is always accurate, always correct, and always hits the mark — without ever going wrong.
Unethical is an adjective used to describe something — a behavior, action, decision, person, or practice — that goes against what is considered morally right, honest, or fair.
"Uneventful" describes a period of time — a day, a trip, a meeting, a life — during which nothing significant, noteworthy, exciting, or unusual happens.
So good, proper, or correct that nobody can find any fault with it or raise any objection to it.
Unexpectedly is the adverb form. It answers the question: "How did it happen?" The answer: in a way that nobody anticipated.
Unfailing means never failing, never stopping, and never letting you down — not even once.

Unfair describes anything that violates a reasonable standard of equal, honest, or just treatment — something that gives one person or side an advantage over another without a good reason, or that fails to give someone what they rightfully deserve.
"Unfairly" means in a way that is not fair — that is, in a way that is unjust, unequal, or wrong.
Unfaltering means steady, firm, and continuous — without any sign of weakening, hesitating, or slowing down.

To unfasten something means to undo, release, or open a thing that was being held closed or held together by some kind of fastening mechanism — and to bring it back to a free, open, or separated state.
Unfathomable means something that is impossible to fully understand, measure, or explain — because it is too deep, too vast, too complex, or too mysterious for the human mind to completely grasp.
Something is unfavorable when it is not good, not helpful, or working against you — when it makes things harder, less likely to succeed, or creates a bad impression.
Unfazed means: not disturbed, unsettled, or thrown off by something — even when that something is difficult, surprising, shocking, or stressful.
"Unfeeling" describes a person who shows no sympathy, kindness, or concern for the pain and emotions of others.
Unfeigned means genuinely felt or genuinely meant — not pretended, not performed, not faked.
To unfetter something or someone means to remove whatever is holding them back — to set them completely free from restrictions, control, or limitations.

Something that is unfettered is completely free — not controlled, not limited, not restricted in any way whatsoever. It operates, grows, moves, or exists exactly as it chooses, with nothing holding it back or placing boundaries on it.
Unflagging means never losing energy, effort, enthusiasm, or determination — no matter how much time passes or how difficult things get.

Unflappable describes a person who stays completely calm, composed, and in control — no matter how stressful, chaotic, or shocking the situation around them gets. Think of it as: nothing can shake this person.
When someone is unflinching, they do not pull back, hesitate, or show weakness when facing something difficult, painful, frightening, or unpleasant.
"Unfold" means to open something that was folded — or, more broadly, to gradually reveal or develop something that was hidden, compressed, or not yet visible.

Unforeseeable means impossible to predict or know in advance — not just something that wasn't predicted, but something that couldn't have been predicted, even by a careful, thoughtful, well-informed person.
When something is unforeseen, it means nobody saw it coming. It is something that was not predicted, not expected, and not planned for — before it actually happened.
Harsh and allowing no room for mistakes or weakness, as in "an unforgiving climate." Of a person, unwilling to forgive others.
"Unfortunate" describes something bad, unpleasant, or regrettable that happened — especially when it was caused by bad luck or circumstances beyond someone's control.

"Unfounded" describes something — usually a claim, belief, accusation, fear, or rumor — that has no solid basis in fact, evidence, or sound reasoning. If something is unfounded, there is simply nothing real or reliable supporting it.

To unfrock someone means to officially strip a priest, monk, or religious minister of their clerical status — removing them from their position in the Church as a punishment, and taking away all the authority, rights, and privileges that came with it.

To unfurl something means to open it out from a rolled or folded state, allowing it to spread freely and fully. Think of a rolled-up flag being released — it opens outward, stretches out, and flows. That action is unfurling.

Ungainly means awkward and lacking grace — whether in the way something moves or the way something looks. It describes anything that gives you the impression of heaviness, clumsiness, or poor coordination, making it seem out of place or off-balance.

Ungovernable means impossible, or extremely difficult, to control, manage, or restrain. When something or someone is ungovernable, no amount of rules, authority, or force can truly bring them under control. They resist being tamed — completely and stubbornly.
Ungrateful means not feeling or showing thankfulness for something kind, helpful, or valuable that someone has given you or done for you.
An unguent is a soft, smooth, greasy substance that you rub onto your skin, usually to soothe, heal, or protect it.
An ungulate is any mammal that walks on hooves.
Not made holy or consecrated, as in "unhallowed ground." It can also mean wicked or sinful.
Not previously announced or recognized; receiving little attention or praise, as in "an unheralded player who became a star."
To make someone mentally unbalanced or deeply disturbed, as in "the trauma unhinged him." Literally, to take a door off its hinges.
When someone is described as unhinged, it means their mind or behavior has completely broken free from reason, stability, and self-control.

Wicked or sinful, against what is sacred. Informally, dreadful or outrageous, as in "an unholy mess." An "unholy alliance" is a partnership between people who would not normally work together, for a bad purpose.
A unicycle is a vehicle that has only one wheel. The rider sits on top of it and pedals to move forward or backward.

When something is unidentifiable, it means you simply cannot figure out what it is, who it is, or where it came from. No matter how hard you try — no matter what tools, methods, or information you use — it remains unknown, unnamed, and impossible to pin down.
Unification means the act, process, or result of bringing separate things together so they become one single, unified whole.
Uniformity means the state in which everything is the same, with no variation, no difference, and no irregularity.
To unify means to bring separate things together so they become one single, complete whole.
"Unilateral" means done by only one side, party, or person — without the agreement, consultation, or involvement of any other side that is part of the situation.
When someone acts unilaterally, they take action entirely on their own — without asking, consulting, or getting agreement from the other people or parties who are involved or affected.
Unimpaired means fully intact, undamaged, and working at complete strength — with nothing missing, weakened, or reduced from what it should naturally be.
Unimpeachable means so completely reliable, trustworthy, or correct that it cannot be questioned, doubted, or challenged by anyone.
Not blocked, not slowed down, and not interfered with in any way — free to move, flow, or progress without anything standing in the way.
"Unincorporated" simply means: not brought into such a structure; not formally or legally organized as an official body.
Uninformed describes a person — or a person's thought, opinion, or decision — that is lacking the necessary knowledge or facts about a particular subject or situation.
Uninhabited describes a place where no people live. If a place is uninhabited, it has no residents, no settlers, no community — nobody calls it home.
Uninhibited describes a person, a behavior, or a style that is completely free and unrestricted — not held back by fear, shyness, embarrassment, or worry about what others think.
When someone is uninitiated, it means they have not yet been introduced to, trained in, or made familiar with a particular subject, skill, activity, group, or field.
Unintelligible describes something that cannot be understood — not merely difficult to understand, but so unclear, distorted, or confusing that you cannot extract any meaning from it at all.

Something is unintentional when it happens without the person meaning or planning for it to happen. In other words, the person did not do it on purpose. It was an accident, a slip, or simply something that occurred without any desire or decision behind it.
Uninterested means having no interest in something or someone — you simply do not care about it, you feel no curiosity toward it, and you have no desire to pay attention to it.
Uninterrupted means continuing from beginning to end with nothing getting in the way — no breaks, no pauses, no stops, no disturbances of any kind.

Union means the joining of two or more things into one, or the state of being joined together. It captures the idea that separate things have come together to form something combined — and that the result is now, in some meaningful sense, a single whole.
Unique means one of a kind — there is exactly one of something, and nothing else in existence is exactly like it.
"In unison" means happening or done at the same time, as in "they answered in unison." In music, it means singing or playing the same note together.
A unitard is a tight, stretchy, one-piece garment that covers your entire torso and your legs — and sometimes your arms too — all in one continuous piece of clothing.

Unity means the state of being one — or, more precisely, the state in which many things come together to form a single, complete whole. Think of it as the opposite of being broken, divided, or scattered.
"Unjust" means not fair, not right, or not in line with what people deserve. When something is unjust, it goes against the basic principles of fairness and moral correctness.
When something or someone is described as unkempt, it means they look messy, untidy, and neglected — as if they haven't been properly cared for or groomed in a while.
Something is unlawful when the law does not permit it, does not authorize it, or does not recognize it as acceptable. In plain terms: the law says no — or the law never said yes in the first place.
To unleash something means to release it from a state of control or restraint, allowing it to act freely and with full force.

Unlettered describes a person who has not been educated — specifically someone who cannot read or write, or more broadly, someone who lacks formal learning, especially the kind that comes from books and literature.

"Unlikely" describes something that probably will not happen, is probably not true, or does not seem to fit naturally in a given situation. The heart of the word is probability — or rather, the lack of it.

"Unloose" means to release something, set something free, or let something go. When you unloose something, you are removing whatever was holding it back — undoing a knot, opening a cage, dropping a grip, or releasing a powerful force that had been contained.

To unmake something means to reverse the act of making it — to cause something that existed, had a form, or had an identity to lose that existence, form, or identity entirely. Think of it as hitting an extreme undo button on reality.

To unman someone means to cause them to suddenly lose their emotional strength, courage, or self-control — to break them down inside so that they can no longer hold themselves together the way they normally would.
Unmannerly describes a person, or their behavior, that lacks good manners — meaning they act in a way that is rude, impolite, or disrespectful toward others, especially in social situations.
Unmarred means perfectly whole, without any damage, flaw, spoiling, or blemish of any kind.
Better than any other; without equal, as in "unmatched skill." It can also mean not forming a matching pair, as in "unmatched socks."
Something is unmentionable when it is considered so embarrassing, indecent, shocking, or morally offensive that people deliberately avoid naming or talking about it in polite conversation or company.
Unmerciful means showing absolutely no mercy — no pity, no compassion, and no willingness to ease someone's suffering or forgive their mistakes.
Unmindful means not paying attention to something, not thinking about it, or failing to consider it — especially something that you should have been aware of or careful about.

Unmistakable means something is so clear, so obvious, and so distinctly itself that it is impossible to confuse it with anything else. There is zero room for doubt. You recognize it immediately, with full confidence, the very moment you encounter it.

When something is unmitigated, it means it is total, complete, and absolute — with nothing present to lessen it, soften it, or take the edge off it even slightly. It exists at 100%, full force, with zero relief.

When "unmoored" describes a person, it means they have lost the thing that kept them stable, grounded, and oriented in life. They are no longer anchored. They are drifting — emotionally, psychologically, or in terms of their sense of identity and purpose.
Unmotivated means lacking a reason, drive, or force that pushes something forward — either inside a person, or behind an action or event.

"Unmoved" describes a person who is not emotionally affected by something — they feel no sympathy, sadness, pity, admiration, excitement, or any other strong feeling, even when the situation would reasonably be expected to produce one.
To unnerve someone means to make them suddenly feel anxious, unsettled, or afraid — in a way that causes them to lose their inner calm, confidence, or ability to think clearly.
Unobtrusive describes something — or someone — that does not force itself on your attention. It is present, it is doing something, but it does not announce itself.
Unoccupied means not being used, lived in, or taken by anyone or anything at a given moment. When something is unoccupied, it is sitting there with no person present in it, on it, or engaged with it.

"Unofficial" describes something that has not been approved, authorized, confirmed, or recognized by the relevant authority — a government, a sports organization, a company, an institution, or any body that has the formal power to make things "official."

"Unorthodox" describes something — a method, a behavior, a belief, or a style — that goes against what is normally accepted, expected, or traditionally done within a particular area of life or society.
To analyse something complicated in order to understand it, as in "let's unpack that idea." Literally, to take things out of a suitcase, bag, or box.
Unpalatable means something that is unpleasant or difficult to accept. Think of it this way: when food tastes awful and you can barely swallow it, you find it unpalatable.

If something is unparalleled, it means nothing else matches it. It stands completely alone in its level of greatness, quality, or extreme degree — with no equal anywhere. When you try to find something that reaches the same level, you simply cannot.
When something is unpardonable, it means it is so wrong, so offensive, or so serious that it cannot be forgiven or excused — not now, not ever.
Unperturbed means calm, steady, and composed — even when something happens that could reasonably cause worry, stress, or disturbance.

The word unpick means to carefully take something apart, piece by piece, that was previously held together. The "un-" at the start signals reversal — you are undoing something. The key feeling the word carries is one of patience, care, and gradualness.
Something is unpleasant when it causes a bad feeling — in your mind, your body, or your emotions. It makes you feel uncomfortable, bothered, or unhappy in some way.

At the most basic level, "unpolished" describes a surface or object that hasn't been polished — meaning it hasn't been buffed, rubbed, or treated to become smooth and shiny. An unpolished stone looks dull and rough.
Something is unprecedented when it has never happened before in history — not once, not anywhere, not ever.

Unpredictability is the quality or state of being impossible — or very difficult — to predict. When something has unpredictability, it means you cannot know in advance what it will do, how it will behave, or what will happen next.

If something is unpredictable, it means you cannot know or guess ahead of time what it will do, how it will behave, or what will happen with it — no matter how much you try or how much information you have. It keeps surprising you.

If something or someone is unprepossessing, they don't make a good first impression — usually because of how they look. They seem plain, ordinary, or unremarkable at first glance. They don't catch your eye.
Modest, natural, and not trying to impress people, as in "an unpretentious restaurant."
Not guided by moral principles; willing to do dishonest, unfair, or harmful things to get what you want, without letting any sense of right and wrong stop you.
Unproductive means failing to produce useful results, meaningful output, or worthwhile progress.
Unpromising describes something that shows early signs suggesting it will not go well, succeed, or turn out favorably.
Done without any cause or provocation ("an unprovoked attack").
Complete and without any limits, as in "an unqualified success." It can also mean lacking the necessary skills, training, or certificates for a job.
Impossible to satisfy or put an end to, as in "an unquenchable thirst for knowledge." Literally, of a fire, impossible to put out.

If something is unquestionable, it means it is so clearly and completely true, real, or certain that there is no room to doubt it, challenge it, or argue against it. It is beyond all reasonable questioning.
When you describe something as unquestioning, you mean it is completely and absolutely free of any doubt, challenge, or hesitation.
To unravel means to undo something that was twisted, tangled, or woven together — either by pulling it apart physically, or by working through its complexity until it becomes clear.

When you call a person unreasonable, you mean they refuse to listen to logic, evidence, or fair arguments. They won't budge even when given perfectly good reasons to do so. They are stuck in their position in a way that seems irrational or stubborn.
When something is unreasoning, it means it acts or exists with no use of reason whatsoever — not just a little bit of reason, not poor reason, but literally zero reasoning at all.

When something or someone is unrecognisable, it means they have changed so drastically, or are so completely unknown to you, that your mind simply cannot identify them. You look, and you draw a blank. There is no moment of "oh, I know what that is."

When something is unregarded, it means it has been given no attention, no thought, and no importance by people around it. It sits there — existing — but nobody notices it, considers it, or cares about it.

Unregenerate describes a person who has not changed — specifically, someone who stubbornly refuses to reform, repent, or improve, even when they know they probably should, or when the world around them is pressuring them to.
If something is unrelenting, it means it does not stop, does not slow down, and does not become gentler or weaker. It keeps going at full force, with no pause and no softening, no matter what.
If something or someone is unreliable, it means you cannot depend on them to do what they are supposed to do, or to behave the way you expect them to.

Unrelieved describes something that goes on completely without any break, easing, variation, or contrast. Nothing lightens it. Nothing interrupts it. Nothing makes it more bearable. It is total and absolute in its nature, from beginning to end.
When something is unremarkable, it means it is so ordinary, average, and plain that there is nothing about it that stands out, surprises you, or makes you want to say "Whoa, look at that!"
Unremitting means never stopping, never easing up, and never giving relief. When something is unremitting, it keeps going with full force — it does not pause, slow down, or soften at any point.
"Unrepentant" describes a person who does not feel sorry for something wrong they have done — and, crucially, shows no sign of wanting to change or make amends, even after being confronted about it.
Unrequited means not returned or not given back in equal measure — especially when talking about feelings.
Complete and given without any doubts or limits, as in "unreserved support." It can also mean frank and open in manner, or, of seats, not booked in advance.
Not settled or solved, as in "an unresolved issue." In music, describing a chord that has not moved to a harmonious one.
Unrest means a state of widespread dissatisfaction, tension, and agitation — especially among a group of people — where things are far from calm and could easily get worse.
Unrestrained means not held back, not controlled, and not limited in any way.
Not held back, limited, or controlled in any way.

When something is unrewarding, it means that after all your effort, you get nothing meaningful in return. The task, situation, or experience leaves you feeling empty, flat, or as though your effort was wasted.

When something is unripe, it means it has not yet reached the stage where it is fully developed, ready, or fit for its intended purpose. It is still in an incomplete, premature state — somewhere in the middle of its natural journey toward being ready.

Unrivaled means so excellent, powerful, or impressive that nothing else can compete with it or match it. It describes someone or something that stands completely alone at the top — with no rival, no close competitor, and no equal.

To unroll something means to open it out from a rolled-up shape, spreading it flat or straight. Think of a rolled-up poster: when you hold one end and let the rest fall open, you are unrolling it. The result is that it lies flat, fully open, and readable.
Calm and composed, especially in a difficult or stressful situation.

If something or someone is unruly, it means they are very difficult or impossible to control, manage, or keep in order. An unruly person, thing, or group resists discipline, rules, and restraint — either actively or simply by their nature.
When something is unsaid, it means it was thought or felt but never actually spoken aloud or expressed in words. The words existed in someone's mind — but they never made it out into the open.
Morally offensive or disreputable, as in "an unsavory character." Literally, unpleasant in taste or smell.
Morally offensive or disreputable, as in "unsavoury business practices." Literally, unpleasant in taste or smell. This is the British spelling of "unsavory."
Unscathed means not harmed, not hurt, and not damaged — even after going through something dangerous, destructive, or very difficult.
Unschooled means not taught, not trained, or not formally educated — either in life generally, or in a specific subject or skill. The absence of instruction is the central idea.
When something is described as unscrambled, it means it has been restored to a clear, correct, and fully understandable state — after being previously mixed up, disordered, or deliberately hidden.
To unscrew something means to rotate or twist it in the reverse direction to loosen it, detach it, or open it.
Willing to do anything — even dishonest, unfair, or morally wrong things — in order to get what you want, with no guilt or hesitation.

To unseal something means to open it after it has been sealed — that is, after it has been deliberately closed, fastened, or shut tight in a way that prevents easy access, protects the contents, or keeps something hidden or private.
Unseasonable means not fitting or suitable for the time.
To unseat someone means to remove them from a position they are currently holding — usually a position of power, authority, or dominance — and replace them, or at least push them out.
Something is unseemly when it is inappropriate, improper, or unacceptable — specifically because it violates what society, a situation, or common decency considers right, dignified, or fitting.

To unsettle something or someone means to disturb their calm, stability, or sense of order — pushing them from a state of being "settled" (peaceful, steady, composed) into a state of unease, uncertainty, or anxiety.

When a person feels unsettled, they experience a quiet but uncomfortable sense of anxiety or unease — as if something is "off," but they can't always say exactly why. It isn't the sharp, intense feeling of being terrified or furious.
So firm, strong, and deeply rooted that nothing can weaken it, change it, or make it fall apart.

"Unshaken" describes something — most often a feeling, a belief, a confidence, or a person — that has not been disturbed, weakened, or moved despite pressure, difficulty, or a strong reason to feel otherwise.
Unshod simply means not wearing shoes — or, for an animal like a horse, not fitted with horseshoes.
Something unsightly is something that is unpleasant or offensive to look at — something that is ugly, visually messy, or disturbing to the eyes in a way that makes you wish you weren't looking at it.
Unsolicited means not asked for, not requested, and not invited.

Unsophisticated means lacking refinement, complexity, or worldly experience. It describes something — or someone — that is simple, basic, or not fully developed in its understanding, design, or outlook.

Not based on reliable evidence or sound reasoning, as in "an unsound argument." It can also mean physically weak or damaged, as in "structurally unsound," or, in law, mentally ill, as in "of unsound mind."
Harsh and severe, not holding back, as in "unsparing criticism." It can also mean very generous, as in "unsparing in her efforts."

"Unspeakable" describes something so extreme — so far beyond the ordinary — that human language feels completely powerless to capture it. Think of it as a word that says: "Words aren't enough for this."
When something is unspecified, it means it has not been clearly stated, named, defined, or identified.
Unspoken describes something that exists — a feeling, a rule, an agreement, or a truth — but has never been said out loud. It lives in silence.
When something unspools, it comes off that reel. It unwinds. It stretches out. What was compact and coiled becomes long and extended, one part flowing out after another, continuously, in sequence.
Unstinting means giving something fully, generously, and without holding anything back.
When something is unsubstantiated, it means it has not been supported or backed up by solid evidence, facts, or proof.
Unsullied means completely pure, clean, and untainted — not damaged, not stained, not corrupted in any way.
Not praised or recognized, although deserving to be, as in "the unsung heroes of the war."

Unsurpassed means the absolute best — nothing has beaten it, exceeded it, or gone beyond it. When you describe something as unsurpassed, you are making the strongest possible claim about how great it is.
Unsuspecting describes a person (or a group of people) who has no idea that something bad, dangerous, or deceptive is happening — or is about to happen — to them.
Unsustainable means something cannot be kept going the way it is — it will eventually collapse, run out, or cause serious harm if it continues.
Unswerving describes a quality of total, unbreakable steadiness in a person's loyalty, commitment, belief, focus, or determination.
Not showing any understanding or concern for someone's problems or feelings. Of a character in a story, not likeable. It can also mean not in favour of something, as in "unsympathetic to the idea."

Something that is untainted is completely free from any kind of corruption, spoiling, contamination, or negative influence. It has remained in its original, pure, clean state — nothing bad has gotten into it, touched it, or changed it for the worse.

In its most direct sense, untamed describes an animal that has never been domesticated or trained by humans. It lives by its own instincts. It does not follow commands. It has not been made safe or gentle for human interaction.

"Untapped" describes something that already exists and holds real value or potential, but has not yet been used, accessed, or developed. It is sitting there — available and ready — but no one has reached into it yet.

Untenable means something that cannot be defended, justified, or maintained — whether it's an argument, a belief, or a real-life situation. When something is untenable, it has reached a point where it simply cannot "hold up" anymore.
"Unthinkable" describes something so extreme, so shocking, or so far outside the boundaries of what seems acceptable or possible that the mind refuses to seriously consider it as a real option.
"Unthinking" means done, said, or behaved without any careful, conscious thought — or, when describing a person, not in the habit of thinking carefully or critically.
Untidy describes something — or someone — that lacks neatness and order. When things are not arranged properly, are scattered around carelessly, or are in a state of disorder, they are untidy.
Happening too soon or at an unsuitable time, as in "an untimely death" or "an untimely interruption."
Untiring describes someone who keeps going with full effort and dedication, no matter how long, hard, or exhausting the task is — without ever slowing down, giving up, or running out of energy.
Too great or too many to be counted or measured, as in "untold damage." It can also mean not told or revealed, as in "the untold story."
Unexpected and unwelcome or inappropriate, as in "nothing untoward happened."
Untrammeled means completely free from any restriction, limitation, or obstacle — with nothing holding it back, blocking it, or tying it down.

When something is untried, it simply means it has never been tested, attempted, or put into practice. Nobody has tried it yet, so nobody knows how it will turn out. The result is unknown because the experience of doing it simply hasn't happened.
Untroubled means free from worry, anxiety, distress, or difficulty — in a state of calm, with nothing disturbing the mind or the surface of a situation.
An untruth is a statement that is not true. In its simplest sense, it is something said or written that does not match reality or the facts.
Not turned over. It is used almost only in the phrase "leave no stone unturned," meaning to try every possible way to find something or achieve something.

Untutored means not having been formally taught, trained, or guided in something. It describes a person, a mind, a skill, or an ability that is raw and natural — untouched by structured learning or expert instruction.
"Unusually" means: in a way, or to a degree, that goes beyond what is normal or expected.

Unutterable means too extreme or too intense to be expressed in words. It describes something so overwhelming — a feeling, an experience, a quality — that human language simply collapses trying to capture it. Words feel insufficient.
Plain and direct, without any attempt to make something seem better than it is, as in "the unvarnished truth." Literally, of wood, not coated with varnish.
Unveil means to reveal something that was previously hidden, covered, or kept secret — and to do so in a deliberate, often significant moment.
Unwarranted means: not justified, not supported by sufficient reason or evidence, and therefore not deserved or called for.

Unwary describes a person (or sometimes a group) who is not alert, not cautious, and not on guard — especially in a situation where they should be careful because danger, a trick, or a problem is nearby.
Unwavering means not changing, not hesitating, and not weakening — no matter what happens.
Something is unwieldy when it is so large, heavy, bulky, or complex that it becomes genuinely difficult to handle, move, or manage smoothly.
