Wade means to walk through something that slows you down and requires effort to move through — something that pushes back against your body or your progress.

To waffle means to be vague, evasive, or uncommitted — either in what you say or in a decision you make. It always implies a frustrating lack of clarity. The person waffling is dancing around something rather than facing it directly.
To waft means to move something — or to be moved — gently, lightly, and smoothly through the air, as if being carried by a soft, invisible current.
A wage is money that a person receives from an employer as payment for the work they do. When you work for someone and they pay you in return, that payment is your wage.

A wager is an agreement between two or more people where each side risks something of value — almost always money — on the outcome of an uncertain event. The person whose prediction turns out to be correct wins the money that the other person put up.

Waggish means playfully mischievous in a humorous way. It describes a person — or their words, behavior, and expressions — that are full of light-hearted jokes, clever teasing, and a fondness for pranks or wit, all done in a good-natured spirit.
To waggle means to move something — or to be moved — repeatedly from side to side (or up and down) in small, quick motions.
A waif is a person — almost always a child or young person — who is homeless, helpless, and completely alone in the world, with nobody to care for them.

To wail means to cry out in a loud, prolonged, high-pitched sound that expresses deep pain, grief, or distress. Think of it as the sound of overwhelming sorrow that simply pours out of a person — uncontrolled, raw, and impossible to hold back.
Wainscoting is a covering of panels — usually made of wood — applied to the lower portion of an interior wall, stopping partway up and leaving the upper wall bare (or differently finished).

A waistcoat is a sleeveless, button-up garment that covers only your torso — from your shoulders down to roughly your waist or hips. It has no sleeves at all, and it typically has a V-shaped opening at the top (the neckline).
To waive something means to voluntarily choose not to use, enforce, or claim something that you have the right to.
A waiver is the deliberate, voluntary giving up of a right, privilege, or claim that you are legally entitled to.
A shy or unpopular person who stays on the sidelines at a party or social event without joining in. A wallflower is also a sweet-smelling garden plant that often grows on old walls.

A wallop is a powerful, forceful blow or strike — the kind that lands hard and makes an impact you can't ignore. Think of a boxer throwing a punch with everything they have, or a cricket bat connecting with the ball with full force.
To wallop something or someone means to hit them with great, forceful power. It is not a gentle tap, not a nudge, not even a firm smack — it is a heavy, hard, full-force blow.
To wallow means to stay inside something — rolling around in it, soaking in it, letting it completely surround you — without trying to get out.
To wallow in something means to stay in a feeling, emotion, or situation for a long time — absorbing yourself in it deeply, without making any effort to get out of it.
Wan means a pale, weak, and lifeless quality — a kind of faded, washed-out state that quietly signals that something is wrong, missing, or depleted.

To wander means to move around without a fixed destination, without a clear plan, and without being in a hurry. You are not going to a specific place — you are simply going, and wherever you end up is fine.
Wanderlust is a strong, deep desire to travel, explore, and see the world.

The noun wane refers to a gradual process of becoming smaller, weaker, or less significant — a slow, steady decline from a peak toward nothing. It captures that specific phase when something that was once strong, bright, or powerful is quietly fading away.
To wane means to gradually become smaller, weaker, or less intense over time — especially after having been at its biggest, strongest, or most powerful.

To wangle something means to obtain it, or make it happen, through clever, sneaky, or indirect means — usually by bending rules, using persuasion, or exploiting a situation — rather than through straightforward, honest effort.

Waning describes something that is gradually becoming smaller, weaker, or less intense over time — something that is slowly fading away or losing its force after having been stronger or fuller before.

A wannabe is a person who desperately wants to be someone they are not — usually someone famous, cool, powerful, or part of an admired group — and who tries to act, look, or present themselves as if they already are that person, even though they clearly are not.
Wanton describes something done deliberately, for no good reason, and with a total disregard for the damage or suffering it causes.
A wanton is a person who behaves in a morally unrestrained way — especially in a sexual or self-indulgent sense — without shame, guilt, or care for consequences.
To warble means to sing with a flowing, musical sound where the voice moves smoothly and rapidly up and down in pitch — like a river of notes, not a flat, straight line of sound.
To ward means to actively protect yourself or someone else by blocking, deflecting, or preventing something harmful from reaching you or taking hold.
"Ward off" is a phrasal verb. It means to take action to keep something harmful, dangerous, or unwanted away from yourself or someone else.
A warden is a person who has been officially given the authority and responsibility to watch over, guard, and manage a particular place, institution, or group of people.
The most basic and concrete meaning of wardrobe is a large, tall, freestanding piece of furniture used to store clothes.
Ware means manufactured goods — things that people make and, typically, sell or use. It is a word for products of a particular kind.
Warily means doing something in a careful, watchful, and cautious way — because you suspect there might be danger, a trick, or something untrustworthy nearby.
Wariness is a noun that describes a state of careful watchfulness mixed with caution, because you sense that something could be dangerous, harmful, or untrustworthy.
Pleasantly hot, between cool and hot; or friendly and affectionate ("a warm welcome").

A warmonger is a person who actively pushes for war — someone who encourages, promotes, or stirs up armed conflict, often eagerly and repeatedly, even when war is not necessary or when peaceful solutions are available.
Warmongering is the act of encouraging, promoting, or pushing for war — especially when war is not necessary or justified.
To warp means to bend, twist, or distort something out of its original, correct, or natural shape — whether that "shape" is a physical object, a person's mind, or even reality itself.

A warpath is, at its most literal level, a route or path taken by warriors heading out to attack an enemy. Think of a group of fighters marching down a trail toward battle — that trail was called the warpath.
Abnormal, twisted, or perverse in a way that is disturbing, as in "a warped sense of humour." Literally, bent or twisted out of shape, as in "a warped door."
To warrant something means to give sufficient justification for it — to make it reasonable, appropriate, or necessary. Think of it as saying: "There is enough reason for this."
When something is warranted, it means there is a good enough reason, basis, or evidence for it to exist, happen, or be said. The situation, facts, or circumstances justify it.

A warranty is a formal promise or assurance — made by a seller, manufacturer, or service provider — that something meets a certain standard, and that if it doesn't, they will take responsibility for it.
A warren is a network of underground tunnels and burrows where rabbits live together as a community. Think of it as a rabbit city built beneath the soil.
Wary means being carefully watchful and cautious because you sense that something might be dangerous, harmful, deceptive, or risky.
To drink something to help you swallow food or medicine, as in "she washed the pill down with water." It can also mean to clean something with a lot of water.

Washed-up describes someone who was once successful, talented, or important — but is no longer. Their best days are behind them, their glory is gone, and there is little or no hope of them ever returning to their former success.
A complete failure, as in "the party was a washout." It can also mean an event spoiled by rain, or a place where flood water has washed away a road or the ground.
If someone is waspish, they are irritable in a sharp, stinging way — quick to snap at others, make cutting remarks, or respond with biting sarcasm when annoyed.

Wastage is a noun that refers to the amount or portion of something that is lost, used up unnecessarily, or fails to be put to productive use — especially as a natural or expected part of a process, system, or period of time.

A wasteland is a place — or by extension, any situation — that is empty, barren, ruined, and without value or life. It is a space where nothing useful, meaningful, or beautiful exists, and where nothing worth having can grow or thrive.

A wastrel is a person who wastes their life — someone who squanders money, time, talent, or opportunity, and lives in an idle, irresponsible way. They contribute little or nothing of value, either to their own life or to the people around them.

"Watch your six" means "be aware of what's behind you" or, more broadly, "watch your back." It is a warning to stay alert to threats, dangers, or problems that may be sneaking up on you from a direction you cannot naturally see.

A watchword is a word or short phrase that carries special importance — either as a secret signal used to verify identity, or as a guiding principle that defines what a person, group, movement, or era stands for.
"Water down" means to make something weaker, less powerful, less effective, or less extreme — usually in a way that takes away from its original quality or impact.
Something is waterproof if water cannot pass through it — not at all, not even a little bit.

A turning point that marks an important change, as in "a watershed moment." Geographically, a ridge of high land dividing two river systems. In British TV, the watershed is the time after which programmes unsuitable for children may be shown.
So carefully worked out that it cannot be faulted or challenged, as in "a watertight alibi." Literally, sealed so that no water can get in or out.
The distance between one wave peak and the next, as in light or sound; "on the same wavelength" means thinking alike.
To waver means to not stay firm or steady — instead, something shifts back and forth, trembles, or becomes uncertain when it should be solid.
To apply wax to something, as in "waxing the car," or to remove hair with wax. Of the Moon, to appear to grow larger. To wax lyrical means to talk about something with great enthusiasm.
Pale and smooth like wax, especially in an unhealthy way, as in "a waxen face." It can also mean made of wax.
The core meaning in one line: A wayfarer is a person who travels, especially on foot, usually over long distances and through open roads or paths.
To waylay someone means to intercept or stop them — usually by waiting for them — in order to do something to them or with them, often without their consent or at an inconvenient moment.
A wayside is simply the side of a road or path — the strip of land, grass, or ground that runs along the edge of a road, track, or route of travel.
Wayward describes something or someone that stubbornly goes in its own direction — away from what is expected, controlled, or correct. Think of the word "way" hiding inside it.

Wayworn means exhausted from a long journey. It describes a person who is deeply tired — physically drained, worn out, and weary — specifically because they have been traveling a long distance, usually on foot or through difficult conditions.
Weakening refers to the process or act of becoming less strong — or of being made less strong. It describes a gradual slide away from a previous level of strength, power, intensity, or effectiveness.
Weal means wellbeing, prosperity, and happiness — the state of things going well, of people being healthy, safe, and flourishing. Think of it as the opposite of suffering or misery.

Wealthy describes someone (or something) that has a large amount of money, valuable possessions, or financial resources — so much so that they can live very comfortably, afford almost anything they want, and do not have to worry about money in day-to-day life.

To wean means to gradually get a person or animal used to living without something they have depended on — or to get them used to something new in its place. The key word is gradually. Weaning is never a sudden cut-off.
To wean someone off something means to gradually reduce their dependence on it until they no longer need it at all.
Weaponry means weapons considered as a whole group or collection. It is the word you use when you are talking about weapons not one by one, but all together — as a mass, a category, or a system.
Weariness is a noun that describes a deep, heavy feeling of being tired — not just in your body, but often in your mind and emotions too. It is the state of being weary.

Wearisome describes something that makes you feel drained, tired, or fed up — not usually because it is physically demanding, but because it is too long, too repetitive, or too dull to keep enduring with a fresh mind and willing spirit.
Weary means being very tired — but not just any ordinary tiredness. It is a deep, heavy kind of tiredness that comes after a long stretch of effort, stress, difficulty, or waiting.
To weasel out means to escape from a responsibility, commitment, or uncomfortable situation by using sneaky, clever, or dishonest tricks — instead of facing it honestly and directly.
To survive a difficult period safely, as in "weather the storm." Literally, to be worn or changed by long exposure to the weather, as in "weathered stone."

When something is weather-beaten, it means it looks rough, worn, and visibly damaged from being exposed to the weather — sun, wind, rain, cold, and storms — for a long time. Think of the outside of an old wooden boat that has been at sea for decades.

When something is weathered, it means it has been exposed to the forces of nature — sun, wind, rain, frost, heat — for a long time, and those forces have left visible marks on it. The thing looks worn, aged, and changed because of that long exposure.
A wedge is an object that is thick and wide at one end, and narrows down to a thin edge or point at the other end. If you look at it from the side, it looks like a triangle.
Wee simply means very small or tiny. If something is wee, it is small in size — noticeably, often charmingly so.

As a noun, wee means urine — the liquid your body produces and releases when you go to the bathroom. It also refers to the act of urinating — the event of going to the bathroom to release that liquid.

To weep means to cry — to shed tears because of a strong emotion. That emotion is almost always sadness, grief, or sorrow, though sometimes it can be an overwhelming positive feeling like joy or relief.

Weigh means to find out how heavy something is, or to be a certain heaviness. But the word has grown far beyond that — it is used in everyday physical situations, in thinking and decision-making, and in describing emotional burden.
Weight refers to how heavy something is, or the force that pulls something downward.
Serious and important, as in "weighty matters." Literally, heavy.
To weld means to permanently join two or more pieces of material — usually metal — by melting them at the point where they meet, so they fuse together and, upon cooling, become one solid piece.

Welfare means the condition of being well — well in every important sense of the word: healthy, safe, comfortable, happy, and free from suffering. It describes the overall quality of someone's life or existence.
Welkin means the sky — but not in the plain, everyday sense of "it's a cloudy sky today." It refers to the sky as a grand, sweeping, awe-inspiring dome that arches over the entire world.

If someone is well-adjusted, it means they are mentally and emotionally healthy in a balanced, stable way — and they handle the normal demands of life without being overwhelmed, dysfunctional, or constantly struggling.
"Trodden" is the past participle of the verb "tread," which means to walk on something. So "well-trodden" literally means walked on many, many times.
Wellness means the active, ongoing state of being healthy and thriving — across your body, mind, emotions, relationships, and other areas of your life. It's not just the absence of sickness.
A wellspring is a rich, deep, and seemingly endless source of something — a place or thing that keeps producing and supplying, as if it never runs dry.
A raised red mark on the skin left by a blow or lash; also a strip of leather joining a shoe's upper to its sole.
A welter is a large, chaotic, jumbled mass of things — especially when so many things are all mixed together at once that it feels overwhelming and hard to sort through.
A wench is a word used to refer to a young woman or girl, but — and this is crucial — the word carries very different weight depending on when it was used, who uses it, and in what tone.
To wend means to travel or go somewhere — but not in a hurried, straight-line way. It describes movement that is slow, relaxed, and often along a winding or curving path.
If someone is wet behind the ears, it means they are inexperienced, naive, or new to something. They lack the knowledge, skills, or wisdom that only comes with time and practice.

A wet blanket is a person who ruins the fun, excitement, or enthusiasm of others. They do this by complaining, being overly negative, criticizing ideas, or simply refusing to participate and enjoy something.

A wetland is a type of land that is soaked in water — either all the time or for a significant part of the year — and because of that water, it supports a very specific kind of soil, plants, and wildlife.
A whack is a sharp, hard hit — the kind that makes a loud smacking sound.
To whack means to hit something or someone with a hard, sharp, forceful blow — usually a single strike, and usually with something solid like a hand, a bat, a stick, or any flat or rigid object.

A wharf is a solid, flat structure built along the edge of water — such as a sea, river, or lake — where ships and boats can pull up, stop, and either drop off or pick up cargo (goods) and passengers.
An informal way of asking what is happening or why something is the way it is, as in "Why is everyone so quiet? What gives?"

To wheedle is to get someone to do what you want — or to get something from them — not by demanding, threatening, or reasoning logically, but by using charm, flattery, gentle pressure, or sweet talk. There's a soft, sly, almost irresistible quality to it.

A wheelhouse is a physical structure found on a ship or boat. It is an enclosed room or cabin where the steering wheel is kept, and from where the captain or helmsman controls and navigates the vessel.

A wheeze is a sound — specifically, a rough, whistling, or slightly squeaky sound that comes from someone's chest or throat when they breathe. Think of it as the sound air makes when it has to squeeze through a passage that is too narrow or partially blocked.

To wheeze means to breathe with a rough, noisy, whistling or rattling sound — the kind of sound that makes it obvious that breathing is difficult and effortful. It is not silent breathing. It is not even just loud breathing.
"When push comes to shove" means when a situation becomes serious enough that you are forced to act, decide, or face reality — even if you were avoiding it before.
Where do you come down on
When someone asks "Where do you come down on [someone or something]?", they are asking: "What is your final opinion, judgment, or position about this person or topic? Which side do you land on?"
"Whereabouts" means the place where a person or thing is at a particular time — or approximately where they are.
A wherefore is a reason — specifically, the reason why something is the case or happened the way it did. Think of it as a packaged answer to the question "why?"
"Whereupon" means "immediately after which" or "at which point."
Wherewithal means the necessary means to do something — most often money, but sometimes also ability, energy, courage, or other resources needed to get a job done.
To whet someone's appetite means to make them eager for more of something, as in "the trailer whetted my appetite for the film." Literally, to sharpen a blade.
A faint smell, as in "a whiff of perfume." Figuratively, a slight trace or hint of something, as in "a whiff of scandal."
To catch a faint smell of something. In sport, to swing at a ball and miss completely. Informally, to fail badly at something.
A whim is a sudden, unplanned desire or idea that pops into your mind for no strong or logical reason.
To whimper means to make a series of small, soft, weak sounds that come out broken and unsteady — sounds that express pain, fear, sadness, or distress.
Playfully fanciful, imaginative, or quirky in a charming way, as in "a whimsical story." It can also mean acting on sudden impulses rather than reason.
Whimsy is a quality of playful, imaginative creativity that is light-hearted, charming, and delightfully unexpected.
To whinge means to complain repeatedly, in an irritating and petty way, usually about things that are minor or trivial — and often without doing anything to actually fix the problem.
A whinny is a sound — specifically, the soft, gentle, high-pitched, trembling cry that a horse makes.

To whinny means to make the gentle, soft, high-pitched sound that a horse produces. It is the quiet, breathy, slightly trembling cry that a horse lets out — not a loud scream or a roar, but a soft, musical sound that travels through the air.
To whir means to make a continuous, rapid, humming or buzzing sound — the kind of sound that comes from something spinning very fast or moving quickly through the air.

To whirl means to spin or rotate very rapidly in a circular or curving motion — usually with energy, force, or a sense of things moving out of control. It's not a slow, steady spin. It's fast, vigorous, and often a little dizzying.
Happening very quickly and intensely, as in "a whirlwind romance" or "a whirlwind tour."

To whisk means to move something quickly, lightly, and smoothly — like a swift, clean sweep. The movement is fast but not violent or clumsy. Think of how a magician pulls a cloth off a table in one clean, quick motion.
One of the long, stiff hairs on the face of a cat or other animal; a hair of a man's beard; or a very small distance ("won by a whisker").

To whisper means to speak using very little sound — so soft and quiet that only the person right next to you can hear. When you whisper, your voice almost disappears. It becomes a hush, a breath with words inside it.

A whit is the smallest possible amount of something — an amount so tiny that it barely exists, the absolute minimum you can imagine. Think of it as a microscopic speck, a hair's breadth, a single grain of sand on a vast beach.

A white elephant is something — an object, a project, a building, or even a gift — that is: Expensive or difficult to maintain; Of little or no practical use; Hard to get rid of, even though you want to.
A snowstorm or fog so thick that everything looks white and nothing can be seen; also white correction fluid for covering mistakes.

To cover up a mistake or wrongdoing to make it seem less bad, as in "whitewashing the scandal." Literally, to paint something with a white mixture of lime and water. In sport, to defeat an opponent without letting them score.
To whittle something means to shape or reduce it by making many small, repeated cuts or removals — slowly, patiently, bit by bit, until you get what you want.
To gradually reduce something in size or number, as in "whittle down the list of candidates."
A whodunit is a story — a novel, film, play, or TV show — whose central puzzle is a mystery crime (almost always a murder), and whose entire plot is built around the question: who committed it?
Done on a large scale and indiscriminately, as in "wholesale destruction." In business, relating to the sale of goods in large quantities to shops rather than to the public.
Wholesome means genuinely and completely good — good in a way that nourishes you, benefits you, and leaves nothing harmful hiding underneath.
"Wholly" means completely and entirely — 100%, with absolutely nothing left out, left over, or held back. When you use "wholly," you are saying that something applies in full, with zero exceptions.

To whoop means to make a loud, sharp, enthusiastic cry or shout. It is the sound a person makes when they are suddenly overcome with a strong emotion — most often joy, excitement, or triumph. It is not a calm, quiet expression.
Whopping means extremely large — larger than what you'd normally expect, larger than what seems ordinary, and large enough to make someone stop and notice.
A whorl is anything that forms a circular, spiraling, or swirling arrangement around a central point — like a coil, a curl, or a ring that winds around itself or a center.
"Whys and wherefores" means all the reasons, explanations, and justifications behind something.
A sharp, clever, and often slightly naughty or mischievous sense of humour.
Wicker refers to thin, flexible plant stems or twigs that are woven over and under each other — repeatedly, in a criss-cross pattern — to create a solid, sturdy structure.
A widower is a man whose wife has died. It describes a specific marital status — not a divorced man, not a separated man, but a man whose wife is no longer alive.
To wield something means to hold it and use it actively, with control and skill — especially when that thing has power or force behind it.
To wiggle means to move with small, quick, repeated movements — typically from side to side, or in a twisting, squirming way.

A wild goose chase is a search or effort that wastes your time because you are unlikely to find or achieve what you are looking for. The thing you are chasing either does not exist, cannot be found, or simply isn't worth the effort spent trying to get it.
A wilderness is a large area of land (or sometimes water) that exists in its natural, wild state — a place that humans have not built upon, farmed, or significantly changed.

A wildfire is a large, uncontrolled fire that burns across open, natural land — such as forests, grasslands, shrublands, or deserts. The key word here is uncontrolled: nobody planned it, nobody is managing it, and it moves on its own terms.

Wildlife refers to all living creatures — animals, birds, fish, insects, reptiles, and sometimes plants and fungi — that exist and survive in nature on their own, without being domesticated, farmed, or controlled by humans.

A wile is a clever trick or cunning strategy that someone uses to lure, persuade, or manipulate another person — not through force or honest argument, but through charm, deception, or indirect cleverness.

When you wile someone, you draw them toward you — or toward doing something — through charm, cunning tricks, or clever strategies. The verb comes directly from the noun wiles, which means the tricks, charms, or clever moves someone uses to get what they want.

"Wilful" describes two closely related things: an action done on purpose — especially when the person knows it is wrong or harmful — and a person who stubbornly insists on doing things their own way regardless of what anyone else says or thinks.
When someone does something wilfully, they do it on purpose, knowing full well what they are doing — and often knowing it is wrong, harmful, or against the rules — yet they choose to do it anyway.

To "will oneself into" something means to use the pure power of your mind and determination to force yourself into a particular state, condition, or action — especially when it is difficult, when your body resists, or when your emotions are working against you.
Willingness is the state of being ready and open to do something — without anyone forcing you.

A williwaw is a sudden, violent burst of cold wind that sweeps down from steep mountains toward the sea, striking with little or no warning. Think of it as nature losing its temper very briefly but very intensely.
"Willowy" describes a person who is tall, slender, and graceful — someone whose body is lean and whose movements have a soft, flowing, almost bendable quality to them.
Willpower is the mental strength you use to control yourself — to do something hard that you know is right, or to stop yourself from doing something tempting that you know is wrong or harmful.
Whether you like it or not, as in "we were dragged into it willy-nilly." It can also mean in a careless, disorganized, or random way, as in "throwing clothes willy-nilly into the bag."

To wilt means to lose firmness and droop downward because of lost vitality or strength. Think of a freshly cut flower standing tall in a vase — after a day without water, its stem bends, its petals hang down, and it looks limp and defeated.
Wily describes someone who is very clever — but in a particular way. It's not just regular cleverness or intelligence.
A wimp is a person who is seen as weak, timid, or lacking courage — someone who gives up easily, avoids difficulty, or cannot handle challenges that most people are expected to handle.
Wimpiness is the quality of being weak, cowardly, or lacking the courage and determination needed to face difficult situations.
Wimpish is an adjective that describes someone — or something — that shows a lack of courage, strength, or determination in a way that others find weak, unimpressive, or even slightly contemptible.

A wimple is a piece of cloth worn as a head covering by women, designed specifically to wrap around and cover the neck, chin, and the sides of the face, while also covering the top of the head or the hair.
If someone is wimpy, they are weak — not just physically, but in their character, their courage, or their ability to handle difficult situations.
"Win over" means to successfully persuade someone to like you, support you, or agree with you — especially when that person was doubtful, opposed, or not yet convinced before.
To wince means to make a small, involuntary movement of your face or body in reaction to something painful, unpleasant, or uncomfortable — a brief flinch that you didn't consciously decide to make.
To winch something means to pull it, lift it, or drag it from one place to another using a mechanical device (called a winch) that winds a cable, rope, or chain around a rotating drum or spool.
To relax after a period of stress or activity, as in "winding down after work." It can also mean to gradually bring an activity or business to an end.

A windbag is a person who talks a lot but says very little of value. They go on and on, filling the air with words, but when you step back and think about what they actually said, there's not much substance there. It's all air — like a bag full of wind.

A windbreaker is a type of lightweight jacket designed primarily to shield you from the wind. The name says exactly what it does — it "breaks" (meaning blocks or stops) the wind from hitting your body directly.
When you are winded, you suddenly cannot breathe properly — your breath has been knocked out of you, either by intense physical effort or by a blow to your body.
A windfall is an unexpected gain — usually of money — that comes to you suddenly, without you planning for it or working directly for it. It's a piece of good luck that drops into your life.

A windowsill is the flat, horizontal ledge at the very bottom of a window. Think of it as a narrow shelf that is built right into the base of a window opening. It runs the full width of the window, left to right.

Windswept describes something that has been exposed to strong, persistent wind — and shows it. The word is built from two ideas: wind (moving air) and swept (the past tense of "sweep," meaning to pass over a surface forcefully and continuously).
To "wing it" means to do something without any preparation, planning, or practice — you just figure it out as you go, relying on your natural ability, instinct, or quick thinking in the moment.
Charming and attractive, as in "a winning smile." It can also mean gaining victory, as in "the winning team."
To winnow means to carefully separate what is valuable or good from what is worthless or unwanted — and then discard the unwanted part, keeping only what matters.

Winsome describes a person who has a sweet, gentle, and naturally appealing charm — the kind that makes people feel instantly warm and drawn toward them. It is charm that feels innocent, fresh, and effortless.
Wintry means having the qualities, feel, or appearance of winter — or, by extension, anything that resembles what winter feels like, even if it has nothing to do with actual weather.

"Wipe out" means to remove something so completely that almost nothing is left. Think of wiping a whiteboard clean — you don't just reduce what's there, you erase it entirely. That feeling of total removal runs through every use of this phrase.
When a person is described as wiry, it means they are lean and thin, but quietly strong and surprisingly tough.

Wisdom is the ability to consistently make good judgments, take right actions, and understand life deeply — not just by knowing facts, but by knowing what truly matters, how things really work, and what the right thing to do is in any given situation.

A wiseacre is a person who acts as though they are smarter or wiser than everyone else — usually in an annoying, smug, or sarcastic way — but who often doesn't actually have the depth of knowledge or wisdom they are pretending to have.
A wisecrack is a short, clever, witty remark — usually meant to be funny, and often carrying a slight edge, teasing quality, or bit of sarcasm.
When someone wisecracks, they make a quick, clever, witty remark — usually one with a slightly cheeky, teasing, or sarcastic edge to it.

If something or someone is wishy-washy, it means they are weak, vague, and lacking in firmness or decisiveness. There is no clear, strong position — just a blur of "maybe," "sort of," and "I'm not sure."

A wisp is a small, thin, faint, barely-there piece or trace of something. The word carries a strong feeling of delicacy and lightness — of something so small and fragile that it almost doesn't exist. If something is a wisp, it is present, but only just.
Wispy describes something that is thin, light, and delicate — so thin, in fact, that it barely seems to exist at all. It sits right at the edge between "something" and "almost nothing."
Wistful describes a gentle, quiet feeling of longing — mixed with a touch of sadness — usually for something you can't have, something that is gone, or something that never was.
Wistfully means in a way that combines quiet sadness with gentle longing — usually for something you once had, something you wish you had, or something that feels just out of reach.
Wit is the ability to say or write things that are both clever and funny — quickly and precisely.
When someone does something "with flying colours," it means they succeeded at something impressively and outstandingly — not just barely passing, but doing it really well.
At the very heart of "withdraw" is one simple idea: pulling something back from where it was, or pulling yourself back from somewhere or something.

Withdrawal means the act of pulling something back, taking something away, or stepping away from something. Think of it like a hand reaching into a space and then pulling back out. That pulling-back motion — that is the essence of withdrawal.
To wither means to slowly lose vitality, moisture, and strength — until something becomes weak, dry, shrunken, or dead.

Withered describes something that was once alive and full of life or moisture, but has since dried up, shrunk, and lost all its freshness and vitality. The word always carries the idea of a decline from a former, better state.
Intended to make someone feel crushed and humiliated, as in "a withering look" or "withering criticism."
The withers is the highest point on the back of a horse (or similar four-legged animal), sitting right at the base of the neck, between the two shoulder blades.
To withhold something means to deliberately keep it back — to choose not to give it, share it, or reveal it, even though there is often an expectation, a request, or even a right to receive it.
"Within a whisker of" means extremely close to something happening — so close that it almost did happen, but ultimately didn't (or just barely did).
"Without reservation" means completely, fully, and unconditionally — with zero doubts, zero hesitation, and zero holding back.
To withstand something means to remain strong, firm, or intact when something powerful tries to damage, destroy, defeat, or change you — and to succeed in not being broken or overcome by it.
Witless means lacking intelligence, good sense, or the ability to think clearly. Calling a person witless is saying they are foolish or stupid — that their mind doesn't work sharply or sensibly.

A person who sees an event happen, especially a crime or accident, or who gives evidence in court. A witness is also a person who watches a document being signed and signs it too. To bear witness to something means to show that it exists or is true.
To witness something means to see it happen with your own eyes, while being present at that very moment.
To be at one's wits' end means to have completely run out of ideas, solutions, or ways to deal with a problem. You have tried everything you could think of, but nothing worked.
A witticism is a short, clever, funny remark that makes people both laugh and think at the same time.
When you do something wittingly, you do it with full awareness and deliberate choice. You know exactly what you are doing, you understand its nature or consequences, and you choose to do it anyway.
Great skill in a particular activity, as in "technical wizardry." Literally, the art or practice of magic.
To wizen means to shrivel, shrink, and become dry and wrinkled — usually because of age, heat, or the slow loss of moisture over time.
Wizened describes something — almost always a person, a face, or a body part — that looks shrunken, dried out, and deeply wrinkled. Think of how a grape looks when it turns into a raisin.
To wobble means to move repeatedly and unsteadily from side to side (or sometimes back and forth), without fully tipping over or falling.

"Wobbly" describes something that moves unsteadily from side to side, or something that is not firm and stable. When something is wobbly, it shakes, rocks, or tilts in a slightly out-of-control way — not smoothly, but in an uneven, shaky motion.
Woe means deep sorrow, grief, or misery — the heavy, overwhelming kind that sits on your chest and doesn't lift easily. It is not mild disappointment or passing sadness.
Woebegone means looking deeply sad, miserable, and sorrowful — often in a way that is clearly visible on a person's face or in their whole appearance.
Woeful means "full of woe." And woe means deep, heavy sadness or suffering — the kind that weighs on you, not the kind you shake off in five minutes.

Woefully means to a deeply bad, insufficient, or distressing degree. It describes how something is done or how something exists — and it always signals that what is being described falls far, far short of what is needed, right, or acceptable.

A wok is a large, deep cooking pan used on a stovetop. Think of it as a bowl made of metal that you cook food in over high heat. It is one of the most important and versatile cooking tools in the world, especially in Asian cuisines.
A term, often used critically, for an outlook that emphasizes awareness of social injustices such as racism and sexism, and for the political correctness associated with it.

To wolf something means to eat food extremely fast and in large amounts, with almost no pausing, chewing carefully, or enjoying the taste. It's the kind of eating where food practically disappears from the plate within seconds.
To wolf down something means to eat it very quickly and greedily, usually in large amounts, without taking time to taste, enjoy, or properly chew it.
This idiom describes a person who pretends to be safe, kind, or friendly on the outside, but is actually dangerous, dishonest, or harmful on the inside.
At its most precise, a woman is an adult human female.
Wonderment is a feeling — specifically, the feeling of being amazed, deeply impressed, or captivated by something that seems extraordinary, beautiful, mysterious, or hard to fully understand.

"Wondrous" describes something that fills you with wonder — that deep, almost speechless feeling of awe and amazement you get when you witness something so beautiful, so extraordinary, or so magnificent that it feels almost too grand or magical to fully take in.

Wonky means something is not quite right — not working properly, not straight, not stable, or not as it should be. It describes a kind of imperfection that is noticeable and slightly frustrating, but usually not catastrophic.
Wont means a personal habit, custom, or characteristic way of doing something — a behavior so regular and typical of a particular person that it has come to define how they routinely act.

To woo someone means to make a deliberate, sustained effort to win their love, affection, or favor — usually through charm, attention, flattery, or attractive gestures. The key word is effort. You are not passively hoping someone will like you.
Woolgathering is the act of letting your mind drift away into vague, aimless, unfocused thoughts — especially when you are supposed to be paying attention to something else.
Vague, confused, or muddled, as in "woolly thinking." Literally, made of wool or soft and fuzzy like wool, as in "a woolly hat."

Woozy describes a deeply uncomfortable physical and mental feeling where you feel dizzy, unsteady, and confused all at once — as if the world around you is slightly spinning or tilting, your head feels heavy and foggy, and you are not quite in full control of your own body.
A wordsmith is a person who is highly skilled at using words — someone who crafts language with care, precision, and artistry.
Workaday means ordinary, plain, and routine — the kind of thing that belongs to everyday working life rather than anything special, exciting, or elevated.

A workhorse is, literally, a horse kept specifically for doing hard physical work — pulling heavy plows across fields, hauling carts loaded with goods, carrying heavy burdens over long distances. These horses were not bred for speed or beauty.

A workshop is a room or building where someone works with their hands — building, fixing, or crafting physical things. It is a functional space, meaning it exists so that work can actually happen there, not just be discussed.
If someone is world-weary, they are deeply tired — not physically tired, but emotionally and mentally tired — of life itself.
Worldly describes someone or something that belongs to, or is shaped by, the real, everyday world of human experience — especially its practical, social, and material side.
"Worried sick" means to be so deeply and intensely worried about something that the worry starts to feel like a physical illness.

To worship means to show the highest possible level of devotion, reverence, and honor toward someone or something — to place them so far above yourself that your whole being turns toward them in submission, admiration, and love.
To worst someone means to defeat them, to get the better of them in a competition, fight, debate, or any kind of contest.
Worthless means having no value, no use, or no good qualities whatsoever.
Worthy means: having enough genuine value, quality, or merit to deserve something.
Very tense, nervous, or agitated, as in "she gets wound up before exams." To wind someone up means to tease them or make them annoyed. To wind up somewhere means to end up there.

A wraith is a ghost — but not just any ghost. It's a very specific kind: a pale, shadowy, barely-visible spirit of a dead person. Think of it as the ghostly outline of a human being, thin and transparent, drifting silently like mist or smoke.
Wraithlike means: resembling a wraith. When you describe something — usually a person or a figure — as wraithlike, you are saying it has the qualities of that kind of ghost.
To wrangle means to deal with something — or someone — that resists you. That resistance is the key.

When people engage in wrangling, they are not just having a quick disagreement — they are locked in a drawn-out, back-and-forth argument, often over something complicated, where no one wants to back down.
Wrath is an intense, burning anger — but not the mild, passing kind. It is anger at its most powerful, most serious, and often most dangerous.

Wrathful means full of wrath — and "wrath" is not ordinary, everyday anger. It is anger at its most intense, most powerful, and most fierce. Think of it as anger that has grown so large it feels like a storm inside a person.
To wreak means to cause or bring about something harmful, damaging, or destructive. When something wreaks, it does not just do damage — it unleashes or inflicts it, often on a large or severe scale.
"To wreak havoc" means to cause a lot of damage, destruction, or chaos. When something wreaks havoc, it creates a serious mess — things go very wrong, out of control, or fall apart badly.
To wreathe means to encircle, surround, or envelop something — but with a specific quality: the surrounding thing winds, curls, or wraps around its subject, often softly and completely.
To wreck something means to damage or destroy it so badly that it can no longer work, be used, or be what it was before.

Wreckage refers to the broken, scattered, and often twisted pieces that are left behind after something has been badly destroyed or damaged. Think of it as what a "wreck" leaves behind — the physical remains of a disaster.
A wrench is a hand tool — a device you grip in your hand and use manually — designed to turn nuts and bolts.

To wrench means to pull, twist, or turn something with sudden, forceful effort — often in a way that is rough, violent, or causes damage. The key ingredients are always: force, a twisting or jerking motion, and often some kind of harm or difficulty.

To wrest something means to take it away from someone or something by using force or great effort — especially when there is resistance, a struggle, or difficulty involved. It is not a gentle or easy taking.
A miserable, unfortunate person ("the poor wretch"); or a contemptible, wicked one.
"Wretched" describes a state of deep, intense suffering or extreme poorness of quality. It is a word that carries real emotional weight — it is not just "bad" or "sad."
In a very unhappy or miserable way, as in "she sobbed wretchedly." It can also mean very badly or poorly, as in "wretchedly paid."
Unfortunate people in a miserable or pitiful state. Wretches can also be wicked or despicable people.

To wriggle means to make short, quick, twisting movements with your body — the kind of movements a worm makes as it moves across the ground. Picture a fish just caught in someone's hands, twisting and turning rapidly trying to get free. That is wriggling.

To get something from someone with great effort or force, as in "wring a confession out of him." Literally, to twist and squeeze something wet to get the water out. To wring your hands means to clasp and twist them in worry.

A writ is a formal, written command issued by a court or legal authority, directed at a specific person or body, telling them exactly what they must do — or must not do — backed by the full force of law.
To twist and turn your body in a desperate, uncontrolled way — usually because of severe pain, discomfort, or intense negative emotion.

Writhing describes something — usually a living creature, or something that moves like one — that is twisting, curling, and contorting continuously in an uncontrolled, restless way. The movement is not clean or purposeful.

A wrong is an act that is unjust, harmful, or unfair — something that should not have happened because it violates what is right. It is not simply a mistake or an accident. A mistake is something done without bad intent or through carelessness.
Wrongdoing means an action or behavior that is morally wrong, unethical, illegal, or a violation of accepted rules and standards.

Wrongful means unjust, unfair, or done without proper legal or moral justification — especially when someone's rights have been violated or when something should never have been allowed to happen in the first place.

Wrongheaded means having mistaken beliefs or deeply flawed judgment — and, crucially, holding onto them stubbornly or with unwarranted confidence. It is always used as criticism. There is nothing neutral or positive about this word.

Made or shaped with skill and effort, as in "a finely wrought poem" or "wrought iron." Wrought up means very upset or agitated. In old use, it is a past tense of "work," as in "what havoc the storm wrought."
"Wry" describes a particular kind of humor, expression, or tone — one that is dry, ironic, and slightly twisted.

To do something wryly means to express something — usually humor or a remark — in a way that is quietly clever and ironic, often while acknowledging something unpleasant, awkward, or absurd about life.
A wuss is a person who is weak, timid, or cowardly — someone who lacks the courage, toughness, or mental strength to face difficulty, pain, discomfort, or challenge.
A xanthate is a type of chemical compound that belongs to a family of chemicals containing sulfur. More specifically, it is a salt or ester derived from a parent acid called xanthic acid.
Xanthic simply means yellow, or relating to a yellow color. When you describe something as xanthic, you are saying it is yellow, yellowish, or tinged with yellow.

Xanthine is a natural chemical compound found inside the bodies of humans, animals, and plants. It is produced as a waste product when the body breaks down certain genetic building blocks called purines.
A xanthoma is a yellowish, fatty deposit that builds up under the skin, forming a bump, nodule, or flat patch.

A xanthophyll is a natural yellow pigment — a coloring compound — found in plants, algae, and some animals. The word is almost always used in the plural, xanthophylls, because there are many different ones.
Xanthous is an adjective that simply means yellow or yellowish in color. If something is described as xanthous, it has a yellow hue or tone to it.
A xebec is a type of sailing ship — a real, historical vessel that once sailed the Mediterranean Sea.

Xenial is an adjective that describes the warm, generous, and kind relationship between a host and their guests — particularly between a host and strangers or travelers who have come under their care and roof.

When something is described as xenobiotic, it means it is chemically foreign to a living organism — it is not something that organism naturally makes, naturally contains, or naturally encounters as part of its normal biology.

Xenodochial means friendly and welcoming toward strangers or people you don't know. It describes a warm, open, hospitable quality — the opposite of being cold, suspicious, or unwelcoming toward unfamiliar people.
Xenogenesis is the creation, generation, or birth of something — especially a living organism — from a source that is fundamentally foreign, alien, or completely unlike the thing being produced.

A xenograft is a piece of living biological material — such as an organ, tissue, or group of cells — that is taken from an animal of one species and transplanted into the body of an animal of a different species.

A xenolith is a piece of rock that is trapped inside another rock where it clearly does not belong — it's made of completely different material than the rock surrounding it. Think of it as a "stranger rock" locked inside a "host rock."
Xenomorphic is an adjective used primarily in geology and mineralogy.

Xenon is a chemical element — one of the fundamental, pure substances that make up all matter. It has the chemical symbol Xe and atomic number 54, meaning every xenon atom contains exactly 54 protons in its core.

A xenophile is a person who loves, is deeply fascinated by, or feels a strong attraction toward things that are foreign — meaning things that come from other countries, cultures, or peoples that are different from their own.

Xenophilia means a love of, attraction to, or deep fascination with things that are foreign or unfamiliar — particularly people from other countries, their cultures, customs, languages, food, music, art, and ways of life.

A xenophobe is a person who fears, dislikes, or hates people who are foreign — meaning people from other countries, other cultures, or backgrounds different from their own. This isn't based on any real personal experience with those people.
Xenophobia is a deep fear, hatred, or strong dislike of people who are perceived as foreign, strange, or "outsiders."
Someone or something described as xenophobic has — or shows — a strong fear, hatred, or deep distrust toward people who are seen as foreign or outsiders.

To act xenophobically means to act in a way that is driven by fear, hatred, or hostility toward people who are seen as outsiders — especially people from a different country, culture, ethnicity, or background.

Xenotransplantation means transplanting living cells, tissues, or organs from one species into another species. In practice today, this almost always means transplanting biological material from an animal — most commonly a pig — into a human being.

Xeric means characterized by, relating to, or adapted to extremely dry conditions — environments or situations where water is scarce, rainfall is very low, and moisture in the soil and air is minimal.
A xeriscape is a garden, yard, or outdoor landscape that is deliberately designed and built to survive on very little water — or sometimes no extra water at all, relying only on natural rainfall.
To xeriscape means to design, plant, or convert a garden or landscape so that it needs very little water to survive — ideally thriving mostly on natural rainfall alone.
Xeroderma is a medical noun that means abnormally dry skin — skin that is excessively dry, rough, and sometimes flaky in a way that goes beyond ordinary seasonal dryness.

"Xerographic" is an adjective that describes anything related to, produced by, or belonging to a specific dry-copying process called xerography — a method of making copies of documents or images using electricity and fine dry powder, without any wet ink or liquid chemicals.
Xerography is a method of making exact copies of documents or images using static electricity and a dry powder called toner.
Xerophilous describes a living organism — most often a plant, but sometimes an animal or microorganism — that is specifically adapted to survive and thrive in very dry, water-scarce environments.
Xerophthalmia is a serious, progressive disease of the eye caused entirely by a severe lack of vitamin A in the body.

A xerophyte is a plant that has specially developed the ability to survive and thrive in places where water is extremely scarce — like deserts, dry rocky hillsides, and semi-arid scrublands. The key word here is adapted.
Something is xerophytic if it is specially built — structurally and physiologically — to survive in places where water is scarce.

Xerosis is the medical term for an abnormal, pathological dryness of body tissue — most often the skin, but also the eyes or mucous membranes (the moist linings inside the body, like your mouth or nose).
Xiphoid means sword-shaped — that is, flat, elongated, and tapering to a point at one end, just like the blade of a sword.

Xylem is a type of tissue found in plants that works like a network of tiny pipes. Its main job is to carry water and dissolved mineral salts from the roots all the way up to every part of the plant — the stem, branches, and leaves.
Xylene is a colorless, liquid chemical compound that smells somewhat sweet and aromatic — a bit like certain paint thinners or industrial solvents.
A xylograph is a picture, design, or text that has been carved into a flat block of wood, or — more commonly — the printed image you get when you ink that carved wooden block and press it onto paper.
Relating to xylography, the art of carving images or text into blocks of wood and printing from them.
Xylography is the art and craft of carving designs or text into a flat piece of wood, and then using that carved wood as a stamp to print those designs onto paper or fabric.
Xyloid means "resembling wood" or "having the characteristics of wood." If something is xyloid, it looks, feels, or behaves like wood — even if it isn't actually wood.
Xylophagous describes any organism that feeds on wood — meaning it actually eats wood as its food source.
A xylophone is a musical instrument that you play by hitting it.
A xylophonist is a person who plays the xylophone.
Xylose is a simple, naturally occurring sugar found mostly in the cell walls of plants — especially woody plants like trees, corn cobs, and straw.
In ancient Greece, a long, covered walkway used by athletes for exercise in bad weather. In ancient Rome, a garden walk or terrace lined with trees.

To yabber means to talk a lot, quickly, and in a way that is hard to follow — or that sounds foolish, pointless, or confused. Think of it as the verbal equivalent of noise more than meaningful communication.

A yacht is a boat — but not just any boat. It is a boat used specifically for pleasure, leisure, or sport, rather than for work. This single idea — a boat for enjoyment, not labour — is the heart of what "yacht" means.

A yahoo is a rude, crude, loud, and uncivilized person — someone who behaves like a brute. It is a word of contempt. When you call someone a yahoo, you are saying that they are rough and unrefined, lacking basic manners, good sense, or education.
To yak means to talk a lot, often about unimportant or trivial things, and usually for a long time. It captures the idea of non-stop, flowing chatter that doesn't necessarily go anywhere meaningful.

Yakuza refers to organized crime syndicates based in Japan, or to a member of such a syndicate. Think of it the way you'd use the word "mafia" in English — it can mean the criminal organization as a whole, or one person who belongs to it.

A yammer is a kind of noise — specifically, loud, continuous, and annoying noise. It is almost always the sound of complaining, whining, or just relentless, irritating chatter that seems to never stop.

To yammer means to talk, complain, or whine continuously in a way that is loud, repetitive, and deeply annoying to whoever is listening. It is the verbal equivalent of a leaking faucet — it just keeps going, and it drives you crazy.

Yang is one of the two fundamental forces or principles that, according to classical Chinese philosophy, make up everything in the universe. It cannot be fully understood in isolation — yang always exists in relationship with its counterpart, yin.
To yank something means to pull it suddenly and with force. It is not a slow, gentle, or gradual pull. A yank is sharp, quick, and energetic — done in one swift motion.
A short, sharp, high-pitched bark, like that of a small dog. Informally, noisy, foolish chatter, or a slang word for the mouth, as in "shut your yap."
A yard is a fixed unit used to measure length or distance. It equals 3 feet, or 36 inches. To give you a rough sense of size, one yard is just a little bit shorter than one metre.
A length or distance measured in yards. In American football, yardage is the total distance gained by a team or player. It is also the amount of fabric needed for a sewing project.
Either end of a yard, the long horizontal pole on a ship's mast that holds a sail. "The sun is over the yardarm" is a humorous saying meaning it is late enough in the day for an alcoholic drink.
A yardstick is something used to measure or judge how good, how successful, or how correct something is. Think of it as your personal ruler for making comparisons.

A yarmulke is a small, round cap — roughly the size of your palm — that Jewish men wear on top of their head. It sits on the crown of the head (the upper-back part), not pulled down over the ears like a regular hat. It covers only a small portion of the head.

Yarn is a long, continuous, thread-like strand made by twisting together many short, loose fibers. It is the fundamental raw material used to make fabric, clothing, blankets, scarves, and many other textiles.
A yashmak is a type of face veil traditionally worn by some Muslim women, most closely associated with Ottoman Turkey and certain parts of the broader Islamic world.

Yaw is a specific type of rotational movement. It describes the side-to-side swinging of a moving object — its front (nose, bow, or tip) turning left or right around an imaginary vertical axis, like a spinning top rotating flat on a table.

To yaw means to rotate or swing around a vertical axis — that is, to swivel left or right from a fixed heading, like a compass needle spinning on its pivot. The key thing to understand is that yawing is purely a rotational side-to-side movement.
A yawl is a type of sailboat — specifically, a boat with two masts (the tall vertical poles that hold the sails).

To yawn means to open your mouth very wide, breathe in a long, deep breath of air, and then breathe it back out — usually slowly. It often comes with a sound, like a soft moan or sigh, and sometimes your eyes water a little when you do it.
"Yawning" as an adjective means wide open, gaping, and vast — especially describing an opening, gap, or empty space that is so large it feels impossible (or very difficult) to cross or fill.
A yawp is a loud, harsh, raw cry or shout — one that is unrefined, unpolished, and bursting with energy. It is not the clean, controlled sound of someone calling out calmly.
To yawp means to make a loud, harsh, rough cry or shout — the kind of raw, unpolished sound that bursts out with force and wild energy, without any care for being elegant or refined.
Yaws is a disease — specifically, a contagious, long-lasting infectious disease that affects the skin, bones, and cartilage.
"Ye" means "you." Specifically, it means "you" when talking to more than one person — a group. Every time you read "ye," you can mentally replace it with "you" and the sentence will make sense.
Yes, used especially when voting aloud, as in "the yeas have it." In old or literary use, it can also mean "indeed," to introduce a stronger word.
A yea is a vote in favor of something — a formal "yes" vote cast during an official vote or decision.

A yearling is a young animal that is one year old — more precisely, an animal that has passed its first birthday but has not yet reached its second. It is no longer a newborn or a baby, but it is not yet fully grown.
"Yearlong" means lasting for the full span of one year. When you describe something as yearlong, you are saying it continues, runs, or extends across an entire year — from start to finish.

To yearn means to feel a deep, aching desire or longing for something — usually something you don't have, something far away, or something you may not be able to get easily. It is not a quick, casual wish.
To yearn for something means to want it very deeply, with a strong feeling in your heart — especially when that thing feels far away, out of reach, or lost.

A yearning is a deep, powerful, and aching desire for something — something you want so badly that you feel its absence in your heart. It is not just a casual wish. It is not the same as feeling slightly hungry or mildly interested in something.
In a way that shows a strong, deep longing for something, as in "she gazed yearningly at the sea."
"Yeasty" simply means of, relating to, or resembling yeast — in smell, taste, or appearance.
A yegg is a criminal — specifically, a safecracker: someone who breaks into safes to steal the money or valuables inside. This is the word's primary, most precise meaning.

To yell means to produce a very loud sound with your voice — louder than normal talking, and loud enough that people at a distance can hear you clearly. When someone yells, they push a lot of air and force through their voice to make it as loud as possible.
To yelp means to let out a short, sharp, high-pitched cry — the kind that bursts out of you (or an animal) suddenly, usually because of pain, shock, or surprise.

A yen is a deep, quiet feeling of wanting something — a longing or craving that sits inside you, often for something you don't currently have or can't immediately get. Think of it as a pull from within. It's not a fleeting wish.
To yen means to feel a deep, persistent longing or desire for something — especially for something you don't currently have, something distant, or something you haven't had in a long time.

A yenta is a person — traditionally a woman — who is a nosy gossip and a busybody. She talks too much about other people's private lives, pries into things that are none of her business, spreads rumors, and meddles where she isn't wanted or needed.

A yeoman is a free, independent, hardworking, and reliable person — one who owns what is theirs, does their duty without complaint, and earns respect through honest effort rather than noble birth or great wealth.
A yes-man is a person who always agrees with whoever is in charge — a boss, a leader, a powerful figure — even when that person is wrong, making a bad decision, or saying something foolish.
A yeshiva is a Jewish school dedicated to the study of sacred religious texts.
"Yesteryear" means the past — specifically, a time that has gone by and is now being remembered or reflected upon. It almost always refers to an earlier era, not just a specific moment.

A yeti is a legendary, large, ape-like creature said to live deep in the snowy, remote mountains of the Himalayas — the great mountain range stretching across Nepal, Tibet, northern India, and Bhutan, home to Mount Everest, the tallest mountain in the world.

A yew is a type of tree — or sometimes a large shrub — that grows in many parts of the world, especially across Europe, Asia, and North America. It belongs to a group of very ancient plants that have existed on Earth for millions of years.

"Yield" as a noun means the amount that something produces, delivers, or gives out. It always refers to output — the result of a process, effort, or investment. Think of it as the answer to one simple question: How much came out of this?

To produce or give something, such as crops, profit, or results, as in "the research yielded new insights." It can also mean to give way to pressure or demands, to surrender, or to let other traffic go first.
Soft and giving way under pressure, as in "yielding mud." Of a person, willing to give in to others' wishes. It can also mean producing a result, as in "high-yielding crops."

Yin is one half of a pair. It is the quiet, dark, cool, soft, and receptive side of existence — and it only makes sense when understood alongside its partner, yang, which is the bright, warm, active, and outward side.

The yips is a condition in which a skilled athlete — someone who has practiced and perfected a specific physical movement for years — suddenly and unexpectedly loses the ability to perform that one particular movement, especially under pressure.
Ylang-ylang is a tropical flowering tree — and, more commonly, the word refers to the fragrant flowers it produces, as well as the precious essential oil extracted from those flowers.

A yob is a British slang word for a young man — usually a teenager or someone in his early twenties — who is loud, rude, aggressive, and behaves in a way that is unpleasant or threatening to others around him.

"Yobbish" describes behavior — or a person — that is rude, loud, aggressive, and completely lacking in manners or consideration for others. It paints a picture of someone who acts in a coarse, loutish, and often threatening way, especially in public.

A yobbo is a rude, loud, and aggressive person — typically a young man — who behaves in a coarse, unpleasant, and antisocial way. He has no manners, no regard for others, and no sense of how to behave in civilised company.

A yodel is a special kind of singing call — a sound a human voice makes by rapidly and repeatedly flipping back and forth between two very different vocal registers: your normal, deeper "chest voice" and a higher, lighter "head voice" (also called falsetto).

To yodel means to sing in a special way where you rapidly and repeatedly jump back and forth between two very different voice registers — your normal voice and a much higher, lighter voice — creating a distinctive, warbling, fluctuating sound.

Yogic simply means "relating to, of, or characteristic of yoga." Whenever something belongs to, comes from, or is connected with yoga — whether its practices, its philosophy, its mindset, or its traditions — you can describe it as yogic.

Something that oppresses or burdens people, as in "under the yoke of tyranny." Literally, a wooden bar fitted across the necks of two animals, such as oxen, so they can pull a plough or cart together.

To yoke something means to join or bind two things — or two people — together, usually in a way that ties them to a shared task, burden, or fate. The joining is almost never casual or light. It carries weight.
A yokel is a person from the countryside or a small, isolated town who is seen as unsophisticated, naive, and out of touch with the wider world — especially with city life and modern ways of living.
To yomp means to march or walk a long distance, over difficult or rough terrain, while carrying a heavy load — typically in a physically demanding and exhausting way.
"Yon" means "that [thing] which is over there — at a distance, but still visible to you."

When "yonder" is used as an adjective, it tells you two things about a noun at the same time: that the thing is far away from the speaker, and that it can still be seen from where the speaker is standing.
"Yonks" means a very long time. That's its entire job as a word.
"Yoo-hoo" is a friendly call you make to get someone's attention. You use it to say, in effect: "Hey, I'm here — notice me!" or "Is anyone there?"

"Yore" means the distant past — a time long, long ago, well beyond living memory. Think of it as pointing to a far-gone era: not last decade, not your grandparents' time, but a much earlier, older time — the kind that feels almost legendary.
You can't teach an old dog new tricks
It is very hard to get people to change their habits or learn new ways, especially when they are older.
"If I were not here to help you, you would be completely and badly defeated."
Youthful means having the qualities, energy, or appearance that we typically associate with being young.
Youthfully means in a way that shows the qualities of youth — the qualities we typically associate with being young.
Youthfulness is the quality or state of being youthful — that is, having the characteristics, energy, spirit, or appearance that we normally associate with being young.
To yowl means to make a long, loud, wailing cry that sounds raw and miserable. It's the kind of cry that signals real distress — pain, fear, or deep unhappiness. The sound is not short or sharp.

A yuan is the basic unit of money in China. It is to China what a dollar is to the United States, or what a rupee is to India. When you buy something in China, you pay in yuan. When you see a price tag in a Chinese shop, the number on it is in yuan.

A yucca is a type of plant — specifically, a whole group (genus) of flowering plants known for their stiff, spiky leaves and tall, dramatic flower stalks. Think of it as a tough, dramatic-looking plant built to survive in harsh, dry conditions.

Yule is an old, poetic word for Christmas or the Christmas season. When someone says "Yule," they essentially mean the same festive period that we today call Christmas — the midwinter holiday celebrated around December 25th.
Yuletide is a word for the Christmas season — that warm, festive stretch of time centered around Christmas.

A yuppie is a young, well-educated, city-dwelling person who works in a high-paying professional job and spends their money freely on expensive, fashionable things — and who tends to care a great deal about status, success, and appearance.
The process by which a neighbourhood or place is changed by an influx of wealthy young professionals, often pushing up prices and driving out poorer residents.
To yuppify something means to transform it so that it appeals to, caters to, or reflects the tastes and lifestyle of yuppies — making it upscale, trendy, polished, and expensive in the process.

A yurt is a circular, portable home — a sturdy, tent-like dwelling that has been used for thousands of years by nomadic peoples across the vast grasslands and steppes of Central Asia, particularly in places like Mongolia, Kazakhstan, and Kyrgyzstan.

Zaftig is an adjective used to describe a woman who has a full, rounded, and pleasantly plump body — curvy and soft, with a well-rounded figure that suggests richness and abundance rather than slimness.
Zanily means doing something in a way that is wildly silly, amusingly eccentric, and comically unpredictable — like a clown, but not in a creepy way. In a delightfully off-the-wall, over-the-top way.
Zaniness is the quality of being wildly silly, absurdly funny, and unpredictably ridiculous — all at the same time, and in a way that is clearly meant to entertain. It's not just being funny.

When something is zany, it is funny in a wild, silly, and wonderfully unpredictable way. It is the kind of funny that feels a little crazy, a little over-the-top, and full of energy — but always in a harmless, lighthearted way.

Zeal is a powerful, energetic, and wholehearted dedication to something — a cause, a belief, a goal, a job, or a person. It means you don't just care about something; you actively, eagerly, and forcefully pursue it with great energy and enthusiasm.
A zealot is a person who believes in something so intensely and so unshakeably that their passion has crossed the line into unreasonable, rigid, and often intolerant territory.
Zealotry is extreme, blind, and often harmful devotion to a cause, belief, or idea — so intense that the person stops thinking rationally and becomes intolerant of anyone who disagrees.
Zealous describes a person who is intensely passionate, deeply dedicated, and actively hardworking toward something they care greatly about — a cause, a belief, a goal, or a duty.
When someone does something zealously, they do it with an intense, burning eagerness — not just willingness, but a kind of driven passion that pushes them to go all-in, without holding back.

Zealousness is the quality of being deeply and intensely devoted to something — a cause, a belief, a goal, a person, or an activity. It describes a state where your enthusiasm isn't just mild or casual, but burning and driven.
An external cue, such as daylight, meals, or temperature, that resets the body's internal 24-hour clock each day.
Zeitgeist means the defining spirit, mood, or feeling of a particular period in history — the invisible cultural "air" that everyone living in that era breathes, whether they realize it or not.

Zeitgeist is the general set of ideas, beliefs, values, feelings, and attitudes that are "in the air" during a particular time in history — shared unconsciously by most people living through that era.

A zenana is the part of a home — in certain South Asian and Persian households — that was set aside exclusively for women. Think of it as the "women's section" of a house, physically walled off from the rest of the home where men lived and moved freely.
Zenith means the highest possible point — the absolute peak, the very top, the farthest something can go before it must start coming back down.
Relating to the zenith, the point in the sky directly overhead. Figuratively, at the highest point of something.
A zephyr is a soft, gentle, and light breeze — the kind of wind that barely grazes your skin and feels almost like a whisper of air rather than a true wind.
Something described as zephyrous is gently and pleasantly breezy — soft, light, and airy in the way a calm, mild wind feels on your skin on a warm day.

A zeppelin is a type of large, powered aircraft that floats through the air — not by using wings like an airplane, but by being filled with a gas that is lighter than air, the same basic principle that makes a helium balloon float upward.
To zero in on something means to focus your full attention very precisely and directly on one specific thing — especially after searching, thinking, or narrowing down possibilities.
Great enthusiasm and energy, as in "a zest for life." In cooking, zest is the thin outer layer of the peel of a citrus fruit, grated to add flavour.

Zestful means full of energy, enthusiasm, and a genuine delight in what you are doing. When someone is zestful, they don't just do something — they dive into it with excitement, liveliness, and a sense of joy.
Zestfully means doing something with great enthusiasm, energy, and genuine enjoyment — all at the same time.

Something described as zetetic is characterized by open, ongoing inquiry — a commitment to questioning, observing, and investigating in order to find truth, rather than accepting conclusions handed down by authority or tradition.

A zeugma is a figure of speech in which a single word — usually a verb or adjective — is applied to two or more other words in the same sentence, but in a different way, or with a different meaning, for each one. That one word does double (or triple) duty.

To zhuzh something means to make it more interesting or attractive by changing it slightly or adding something to it. Think of it as giving something a creative little boost — a sprinkle of flair, personality, or polish — so it goes from "fine" to "great."

Zibeline can refer to the fur of the sable — a small, sleek, weasel-like creature native to the cold forests of Siberia and northern Asia. This fur is considered one of the most precious in the world.

A ziggurat is a massive, ancient tower built in a staircase-like shape — wide and large at the bottom, narrowing as it rises, with a series of clearly defined flat platforms (called terraces or tiers) stacked one on top of another, each slightly smaller than the one below.
A zigzag is a shape, line, or path that repeatedly changes direction in sharp, angled turns — first going one way, then sharply turning and going the other way, then turning back again, and so on.

To zigzag means to move in a path that keeps sharply turning — first to one side, then to the other, then back again — over and over, instead of going in a straight line. Think of the letter Z or the letter N.
Zilch means absolutely nothing. Zero. Not a single thing.
